title: Operationalizing Multi-Domain Electronic Health Record Data for Acute Hospital Rehabilitation Research: A Learning Health Systems Approach.
abstract: Introduction Hospital-based rehabilitation therapy electronic health record (EHR) documentation is uniquely rich in social and environmental content, yet has received little systematic attention in health services research. These EHR data encompass pre-admission living situation, household composition, home accessibility, discharge barriers, and post-acute care recommendations. Our technical report describes a systematic approach to operationalizing this multi-domain data for acute hospital research within a Learning Health System (LHS) framework. Methods Working within an LHS embedded researcher model at Intermountain Health, we describe the data governance, pre-data stakeholder engagement, and variable creation computational pipeline applied to acute hospital encounters. We negotiated a data use agreement for a limited dataset and engaged with inpatient therapists to map EHR documentation structures before submitting the data request. Sequential cleaning steps operationalized variables across seven analytic domains: clinical complexity, functional status, social and environmental factors, home environment, therapy delivery, procedures, and discharge planning. We processed the therapy documentation file (1 032 359 submissions across 41 form types) using a form prioritization algorithm, crosswalk harmonization across heterogeneous form vocabularies, and regular expression matching to classify free-text entries. Results The pipeline produced a dataset of 156 557 hospital encounters between September 2022 and August 2023 and operationalized 74 analytic variables spanning clinical, functional, social, and environmental domains. Key structured variables included: Activity Measure for Post-Acute Care (AM-PAC) 6-Clicks functional assessment scores (at least one assessment present for all 156 557 encounters); pre-admission living situation across 10 harmonized categories (95.0% complete); barriers to safe discharge across 10 clinically grouped indicators (70.1% of encounters); post-acute therapy recommendations (91.9% complete); and time to first therapy visit (mean 25.5 h; 99.7% complete). A master data dictionary documents all variables with technical specifications and plain-language descriptions. Conclusion This work demonstrates that high-completeness analytic variables spanning clinical, functional, social, and environmental domains can be systematically derived from heterogeneous multiform rehabilitation therapy EHR documentation at scale. The data cleaning scripts, crosswalk tables, and master data dictionary provide a transferable foundation for rehabilitation researchers and health systems seeking to leverage therapy documentation for outcomes research and quality monitoring as an LHS.

Stress-induced alterations in neurodevelopment in iPSC-Derived i n vitro model systems.
abstract: Psychological stress is common in women during pregnancy and after childbirth, showing a prevalence of up to 15.6% in pregnant women in developing countries. Clinical and pre-clinical studies have implicated their role in negatively affecting pregnancy outcomes and have been linked to adverse child outcomes. Yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood, specifically the signatures associated with their effect on human fetal development. Thereby, impairing our further understanding of the effects of therapeutics used to treat these disorders in expecting mothers. This study proposes the use of human iPSC-derived embryoid bodies (EBs) and forebrain-specific organoids as complementary human developmental models to investigate the effects of exposure to prenatal stress (mediated by glucocorticoids) across distinct stages, in vitro. Our findings suggested that excessive glucocorticoids altered early lineage specification in an exposure-dependent manner. This was evidenced by a brief increase in pluripotent and neural progenitor populations, with mild alterations in proliferative dynamics without a net change in proliferative capacity. Changes in lineage-associated markers were observed in ectodermal and meso-endodermal layers of EBs. Particularly, focusing on neurogenesis (forebrain-specific organoids) to understand the impact of stress on neurodevelopment, we saw concentration-dependent changes in progenitor maintenance and neuronal- glial differentiation. Furthermore, the activation of inflammatory and oxidative stress responses can be implicated as signalling mechanisms responsible for the differences observed. Together, these results suggest that glucocorticoid signalling linked to prenatal stress can alter developmental trajectories by modifying cellular states rather than directly altering proliferation or survival during early development.

3D Gaussian Digital Twins for View-Robust 3D Visuomotor Policy Learning on Articulated Objects
abstract: Single-view 3D visuomotor policies based on point-cloud observations, such as 3D Diffusion Policy, often suffer from limited viewpoint generalization due to partial observability and occlusion. This is particularly challenging for articulated objects whose internal motion induces geometry changes. To address this problem, we propose an articulation-driven digital twin augmentation approach that couples reconstruction, online articulation-state estimation, and observation generation within a shared 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model. Offline, we reconstruct an articulation-aware 3DGS part model and parameterize the articulation. Online, we optimize joint states through differentiable rendering conditioned on the base pose, then transform pre-sampled part point clouds using the estimated configuration. Fusing the object point cloud with robot geometry enables real-time augmentation from partial to global observations using single-camera input during execution. Experiments on the complete pipeline in simulation and the real world demonstrate accurate articulation tracking and improved viewpoint generalization of 3D Diffusion Policy.

title: AI Agents as Digital Employees in the Travel Industry: Challenges and Prospects
abstract: The article considers the possibility of introducing digital employees in the form of AI agents in the tourism sector. The author considers the features of AI agents as a new technology, summarizes and highlights seven key problems of implementing AI agents and provides a description of a typical AI agent architecture. The promising roles of AI agents in the tourism sector are highlighted separately and five potential areas of their application are described. Special emphasis is placed on the need to review the current business processes of travel companies in favor of adapting to the digital capabilities of AI agents as a promising technology. The article may be useful for entrepreneurs and government officials responsible for automating business processes in the tourism sector.

title: Operations research model for inventory optimization through statistical demand analysis and linear programming
abstract: Efficient inventory management requires integrating demand uncertainty, costs, and replenishment decisions within a quantitative framework. This research develops an Operations Research model for inventory optimization by integrating statistical analysis, demand forecasting, ABC classification, Economic Order Quantity [EOQ], Safety Stock [SS], Reorder Point [ROP], and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming [MILP]. The procedure uses historical data to estimate demand parameters and establish differentiated replenishment policies. These parameters are subsequently incorporated into the mathematical model to determine order quantities and periods while minimizing relevant inventory costs. The results reveal a significant economic concentration among priority items and an approximate 46% reduction in relevant inventory costs compared with the baseline policy. Sensitivity analysis confirms the stability of the proposed model under the evaluated variations in demand, holding costs, and safety stock. Overall, the integrated framework provides a reproducible quantitative approach for connecting predictive analysis with prescriptive optimization and supporting cost-efficient inventory and logistical decision-making.

title: Visión artificial para la detección de plagas en cultivos de tomate: revisión sistemática de la literatura
abstract: Phytosanitary monitoring is an essential activity for reducing production losses caused by pests in tomato crops grown under protected agriculture conditions. In recent years, computer vision and deep learning methods have gained relevance as tools capable of automating agricultural image detection and analysis processes. Despite these advances, there is still a need to determine which techniques have been used, under what conditions they have been evaluated, and what performance they have reported, particularly in protected agriculture and small-scale production contexts. This study aims to examine research published on these technologies and assess their potential incorporation into participatory agricultural monitoring schemes. To this end, a systematic review of scientific literature published between 2020 and 2026 was conducted following the methodological guidelines proposed by Kitchenham. The review was developed through the stages of planning, study search and selection, and information synthesis, considering previously established inclusion and exclusion criteria. As a result, fifty studies related to image processing, artificial intelligence, and phytosanitary monitoring were selected and analyzed. Among the main findings of the review, several studies reported high-performance levels for deep learning models in tasks involving the automatic identification of symptoms associated with pests and other crop-related conditions. The synthesis identified the main techniques, data, application contexts, and reported performance levels, providing reference elements for assessing their potential incorporation into participatory agricultural monitoring schemes.

title: Critical Issues in Building Information Modeling (BIM) Workflows: A Multi-Case Study Review
abstract: Building Information Modeling (BIM) is increasingly used in structural and infrastructure engineering as a digital environment supporting design, construction, and asset management processes. However, the application of BIM to complex infrastructures still presents several critical issues, particularly when dealing with non-standard geometries, existing structures, and heterogeneous information flows. This paper presents a technical synthesis based on six case studies developed by the authors through BIM-based approaches applied to different structural and infrastructural fields, including bridges, road infrastructures, underground utility networks, and complex structural systems. The study analyzes the main issues encountered during the modeling, coordination, and data exchange phases, highlighting the strategies adopted to address them. The identified challenges mainly concern the geometric modeling of irregular or existing structures, interoperability issues between BIM software and structural analysis software, the management of point clouds and survey-derived data, as well as the definition of appropriate Levels of Development and Information. The paper provides a technical overview of recurring issues and offers useful indications for improving BIM workflows applied to structural and infrastructure engineering.

A Human-Centric Decision Framework for Selecting Artificial Intelligence Collaboration Strategies Under Uncertainty in Industry 5.0
abstract: Effective collaboration between humans and artificial intelligence (AI) in industry 5.0 demands technological systems with human social-cognitive processes, such as trust calibration and shared mental model. This study introduces human-centric decision-making framework for configuring human-AI collaboration in smart manufacturing systems. As Industry 5.0 evolves, finding the best synergy between human intelligence and collaborative robots (cobots) becomes crucial for enhancing adaptability, safety, efficiency, and sustainability. The proposed methodology uses neutrosophic Z-numbers (NZN) to capture uncertainty with three components: truth, indeterminacy, and falsity with their associated reliabilities, and the NZN weighted arithmetic averaging (NZNWAA) operator to combine individual preferences of decision-makers. Afterward, the criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC) method is used to objectively determine the importance of each criterion by analyzing contrast intensity and inter-criteria correlation. The ranking of alternatives is then obtained using the compromise ranking of alternatives from distance to ideal solution (CRADIS) method. This hybrid NZN-CRITIC-CRADIS approach is applied to a real-world case study of BMW manufacturing systems, assessing four human-AI collaboration strategies: full AI automation, partial cobot integration, human-led AI-assisted assembly, and hybrid multi-agent collaboration, across four critical criteria. The results of the study show that the AI-assisted assembly emerges as the most suitable solution, balancing technological capability with human-centric design. The effectiveness of the proposed approach has been further validated through a sensitivity analysis and a comparative assessment with existing decision-making techniques, where our model consistently demonstrated superior performance in handling uncertainty and maintaining objectivity. Ultimately, this study offers a reliable human-centered framework that emphasizes socially intelligent manufacturing.

Regional variation in taste profiles and non-volatile metabolites of raw Anhua dark tea revealed by metabolomics and machine learning.
abstract: Raw Anhua dark tea (RADT) from different production regions has its own unique flavor characteristics, this study systematically investigated taste differences and their metabolic basis in RADT from key four production regions in Anhua County. Sensory evaluation and electronic tongue (E-tongue) analysis revealed distinct regional variations in taste characteristics. Non-targeted metabolomics identified 269 non-volatile metabolites, including 31 differential metabolites mainly comprising amino acids, phenolic acids, flavonoids, and flavonoid glycosides. Correlation analysis indicated that EGCG, ECG, and epigallocatechin 3-O-(3-O-methylgallate) were primarily associated with bitterness, aftertaste-A, and richness, whereas flavonoid glycosides and kaempferol derivatives were positively correlated with the E-tongue sweetness response and astringency modulation. Phloridzin and carbohydrates, including sucrose and trehalose, were also potentially associated with regional taste variation. Machine learning models further demonstrated the feasibility of discriminating RADTs from different production regions based on metabolic profiles, with random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and k-nearest neighbor (KNN) showing better classification performance. These findings reveal the metabolic basis of regional taste differentiation in RADTs and deepen the understanding of how metabolites contribute to tea taste formation.

title: Quantifying Vernacular Window Geometry via CNNs for Simulation-Oriented Analysis: An Iranian Architecture Case Study
abstract: Environmental performance is a key concern in contemporary architectural design, as buildings significantly affect energy consumption and contribute to climate change. Iranian vernacular architecture, particularly traditional window types, incorporates passive design strategies associated with thermal comfort regulation and daylight modulation. Decoding these window typologies can reveal climate-responsive design principles rooted in environmental and cultural contexts, with continued relevance to current sustainability goals. However, the geometric and formal complexity of traditional Iranian window systems has limited the systematic analysis of these systems using conventional methods. Existing research has primarily relied on visual, descriptive, or syntactic approaches, with limited emphasis on extracting quantitative, simulation-oriented data. This study proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based visual framework for automated classification of traditional window typologies and extraction of architectural parameters from façade images. Fine-tuned CNNs are employed to identify window types and derive key geometric descriptors commonly used in environmental performance modeling, including window-to-wall ratio, frame depth, and perforation density. The extracted parameters are organized into structured, simulation-oriented data sets intended for downstream use in energy and daylight modeling workflows, including tools such as EnergyPlus and Radiance. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping is used to verify that the model focuses on morphologically meaningful features, while statistical analysis (Kruskal–Wallis, P < 0.001) confirms significant typological differentiation in the extracted parameters. While environmental simulations are not conducted in the present study, the resulting parameter sets are explicitly designed to be compatible with established simulation platforms, enabling downstream use in performance evaluation workflows. Although developed using traditional Iranian window typologies, the proposed framework provides a transferable methodology for linking visual data with simulation-oriented architectural parameterization.

title: Intelligent Prediction of Rock Mass Classification Using TBM Multivariate Time Series and Multichannel Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: In tunnel boring machine (TBM) operations, a large volume of feedback data related to the excavation process is collected in real time, which directly reflects the interaction between the TBM and surrounding rock. The key challenge in ensuring efficient and safe tunneling is to accurately extract sensitive features from vast, fluctuating, and complex multidimensional time series data to understand the geological conditions ahead of the cutterhead. In this study, a novel intelligent recognition method for TBM rock mass classification is proposed, based on piecewise aggregate approximation (PAA) and a multichannel one-dimensional convolutional neural network (MC-1D-CNN). The method effectively maps the interaction between the TBM and surrounding rock to the associated rock classes information ahead of the cutterhead. Five tunneling parameters are selected as input features. First, the PAA technique is applied to transform the multidimensional, raw TBM time series data, which exhibit different scales, into fixed-length one-dimensional feature vectors. This process reduces dimensionality and fuses the data along spatial channels. Then, a MC-1D-CNN model is constructed, which takes the multichannel PAA sequence matrix as input for training. Through multilayer nonlinear mappings and dynamic optimization, the model automatically learns the features of univariate time series within each channel, further reducing the dimensionality and extracting high-order features more strongly correlated with the rock classes. Additionally, to enhance the feature extraction ability and generalization capability of the model, a MC-1D dilated CNN (MC-1D-DCNN) is developed by incorporating dilated convolutions. The method is validated using TBM monitoring data from the second section of the Yinchao project, demonstrating its capability to accurately classify the rock classes. Comparative analysis with several ensemble machine learning models based on key tunneling parameter time series statistical features shows that the proposed TBM surrounding rock level intelligent method PAA-MC-1D-CNN has better feature mining ability and higher recognition accuracy and robustness.
journal: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering

title: Data-Driven Differentiated Analysis of Construction Accident Causes Using Hybrid Knowledge Graphs and Bayesian Networks
abstract: Construction accidents are characterized by a high level of risk and are typically caused by the combined effects of multiple interacting factors. However, systematic investigation into the causes of construction accidents is lacking in current research, and differentiated analysis of accident types has not been provided, which renders the formulation of targeted prevention strategies challenging. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multilevel analytical framework to explore the underlying causes of construction accidents. First, accident reports of various types were collected and analyzed to extract causal factors, and a construction site accident knowledge graph (CSAKG) was established to visualize their interrelationships. Second, the decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory method was applied to simplify the complex interrelationships among causal factors within the CSAKG and to identify the key influencing elements. These elements were subsequently incorporated into a four-layer hierarchical Bayesian network (BN) model, which was developed based on the human factors analysis and classification system framework. Finally, differentiated causal pathway analyses were performed using the BN model to identify the critical causal factors and clarify their interaction mechanisms. The results demonstrate significant variations in key causal factors and their interaction pathways across different accident types, each exhibiting distinct causative logics and evolutionary characteristics. The identified pathways were further validated through tolerance design, thereby confirming the robustness and reliability of the proposed model. Overall, the proposed analytical framework effectively addresses the shortcomings of traditional approaches, offering precise, multilevel, and practical decision-support for construction safety risk management.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Tail-Dependent Price Escalation Risk in Road Projects: A Hybrid LSTM-Gumbel Copula Model for Probabilistic Contingency Estimation
abstract: Road and bridge projects are exposed to escalation in key construction inputs such as diesel, cement, structural steel, and construction steel, where common shocks can generate jointly adverse price movements and weaken fixed-percentage contingency practices. Prior construction cost-forecasting studies have largely emphasized single-series point accuracy and often rely on independence or linear dependence assumptions, leaving a gap in contingency sizing that explicitly accounts for multivariate co-movement in escalation shocks. This study proposes a hybrid framework that couples multivariate long short-term memory (LSTM) forecasting of monthly input-index log-returns with copula-based dependence modeling of strictly out-of-sample forecast innovations. The workflow follows a blocked walk-forward design, using separate validation and test blocks for dependence calibration and final evaluation, respectively. A Monte Carlo engine integrates the trend component and dependent residual shocks to generate joint escalation scenarios and produce decision-grade cost percentiles. Using official Peruvian monthly indices from 2013 to 2025, the empirical results show heterogeneous dependence across inputs, with the strongest positive rank association observed between structural steel and construction steel ( τ = 0.9394 ), while several other pairwise links are weak or negative. In this context, the Gumbel copula is used as a conservative upper-tail benchmark, yielding θ ˆ = 16.5000 and λ ˆ U = 0.9571 . For the analyzed material basket, the benchmark tail-dependent model yields contingency requirements of 1.72% at the 90% confidence level and 3.99% at the 95% level above 50th percentile ( P 50 ). The results show that dependence assumptions materially affect high-confidence cost thresholds and that contingency reserves are better treated as confidence-based governance choices than as fixed deterministic add-ons.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Contrasting Local Ecosystem Water and Energy Balances with a Regional Land Surface Model in the Southeastern United States
abstract: Land use and land cover changes, especially urbanization, can strongly alter coupled water and energy cycles, intensifying urban heat island effects, stormwater runoff, and flood risk. Process-based land surface models provide an important tool for quantifying these interactions in heterogeneous landscapes with mixed urban, grassland, and forest cover where direct observations are limited. However, few studies have evaluated how models designed for regional-scale applications perform across scales from small watersheds to a broader urban–rural interface. Here, we diagnostically assessed the upgraded Common Land Model -Urban (CoLM-U) parameterization in the Nashville metropolitan area in the State of Tennessee, southern United States. We integrated local precipitation observations, streamflow records from five small watersheds, and remote sensing-derived evapotranspiration (ET) products from 2000 to 2020. CoLM-U reproduced the broad magnitude of annual ET and runoff but showed substantial watershed-to-watershed and seasonal discrepancies. At the monthly scale, runoff root mean square error ranged from 14.4 to 27.4 mm month −1 and Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency ranged from 0.3 to 0.6. The model generally underestimated winter runoff and overestimated summer runoff, reflecting the combined effects of precipitation forcing uncertainty, growing-season ET underestimation, and limitations in representing soil water storage and runoff generation. Long-term ET estimated by CoLM-U was broadly consistent with watershed water balance estimates, while remote sensing ET was generally over estimated ET, especially over forested areas. CoLM-U modeling results indicated that forests exhibited the highest ET and lowest sensible heat fluxes during the growing season, whereas urban cores showed lower ET and higher sensible heat. This study demonstrates what a regional land surface model can and cannot capture of ecohydrological processes at local watershed-to-regional scales. Improved local model climate input data and refined soil parameterizations are essential for accurate application in estimating the environmental effects of land cover change.

title: Evaluation of the Corrosion Resistance of Welded Joints of Stainless-Clad 304/Q235B Bimetallic Steel Rectangle Tubes and 304 Stainless-Steel End Plates
abstract: Stainless-clad bimetallic steel, which can balance corrosion resistance and economy, is becoming a new research hot spot in high-performance steel structures. This study focuses on rectangular tube components fabricated from stainless-clad 304/Q235B bimetallic steel plates (with 304 stainless cladding on the outer side) and closed by welding with 304 stainless-steel end plates. This design is to isolate the carbon steel base from corrosive media, achieving corrosion resistance close to that of all-stainless-steel structures. Three welding process schemes are proposed, and mechanical tests and indoor salt spray accelerated corrosion tests were conducted to evaluate the joints. Mechanical property tests show that the maximum hardness value of each joint does not exceed 280 vickers hardness (HV), and their microhardness meets engineering requirements. The joint with the process combination of shielded metal arc (SMA) welding + E309-16 electrode has the best mechanical properties, while the joint with the combination of tungsten inert gas (TIG) welding + ER308 welding wire has the best corrosion resistance. The indoor salt spray accelerated corrosion test indicates that welds promote the occurrence of corrosion, and the intersections of welds are the most susceptible parts to corrosion in tube joints. The weight loss fitting curve shows a power function characteristic, with the fitting coefficient R 2 > 0.98 and the exponent n < 1 , which indicates that the rust layer or passive film plays a partial protective role on the base material. The corrosion prediction model for the welded joints of stainless-clad 304/Q235B bimetallic steel rectangle tubes and 304 stainless-steel end plates in the marine atmospheric environment of Qingdao, China, is as follows: t = 34.9876 T 0.4441 . These findings provide a reference for promoting the application of stainless-clad steel plate structures.
journal: Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering

title: Prediction Model for the Indirect Tensile Strength of Engineered Emulsion-Stabilized Cold Recycled Materials for Efficient Quality Assurance Practices
abstract: The growing use of cold recycling for flexible pavement rehabilitation offers a compelling approach to advancing sustainable infrastructure developments. Despite its many advantages, one of the challenges hindering broader implementation of cold recycling is the lack of real-time methods to quickly assess as-constructed material properties, which are essential for evaluating construction quality and to ensure compliance with the original material design. Integrating fast and efficient methods for determining as-constructed material properties can greatly enhance quality assurance and design processes on a wider scale. This study leveraged advanced statistical modeling techniques to develop a robust predictive model for estimating the indirect tensile strength of engineered emulsion-stabilized cold-recycled materials. A comprehensive database of laboratory-produced mixtures which incorporates material attributes such as varied engineered emulsion contents, the presence of chemical additives, gradation characteristics, and density, replicating as-constructed conditions, was utilized to train and validate predictive models, using the support vector regression (SVR) and self-validating ensemble modeling (SVEM) techniques. Among the advanced statistical modeling techniques explored, SVR consistently demonstrated better predictive accuracy, based on a range of statistical error metrics assessed. Model sensitivity analyses identified coarseness and mixture density as the most influential variables for the prediction of the indirect tensile strength. The resulting model was incorporated into a user-friendly Microsoft Excel–based prediction tool, developed to aid engineers and practitioners in quality assurance by enabling rapid estimation of as-constructed mechanical properties, thereby minimizing dependence on extended laboratory testing and support pavement design processes.

title: CD49f identifies stem-like memory T cells with enhanced therapeutic potency.
abstract: The efficacy of adoptive cell therapies depends on the presence of T cells with durable self-renewal, proliferative capacity, and differentiation potential, yet heterogeneity within starting cell populations remains a major barrier to consistent clinical outcomes. Here, we identify CD49f as a marker of a unique subset of human memory T cells with stem-like characteristics. CD49fHi memory CD8+ and CD4+ T cells exhibited transcriptional and phenotypic features associated with T cell stemness, including elevated LEF1, TCF1, CCR7, CD27, and CD28, while CD49fLo cells exhibited effector-like transcriptional programs. Clinical evaluation of solid-organ transplant recipients treated with virus-specific T cells for cytomegalovirus complications demonstrated that autologous T cell therapies manufactured from CD49fHi-enriched T cells were associated with superior immune reconstitution and greater in vivo expansion of CMV-specific T cells. Functional assays further revealed that CD49fHi memory T cells possessed enhanced proliferative capacity and transcriptional plasticity following activation. Consistent with these findings, CD19 CAR T cells engineered from CD49fHi memory T cells demonstrated improved persistence and conferred superior survival in a preclinical lymphoma model. Together, these findings establish CD49f as a marker of a stem-like memory T cell subset with enhanced therapeutic potential and identify CD49fHi enrichment as a practical strategy to improve the consistency, durability, and clinical efficacy of both virus-specific and CAR T cell therapies.

title: Modified Fangji Huangqi Decoction ameliorates IgA nephropathy by enriching Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans to rebalance Th17/Treg.
abstract: BACKGROUND Abnormalities in mucosal immunity caused by gut microbiota dysbiosis are one of the key factors in the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Modified Fangji Huangqi Decoction (MFHD) is an effective treatment for IgAN, but it remains unclear whether its therapeutic effect is mediated by modulating the gut microbiota and thereby influencing mucosal immunity. METHODS The chemical composition of MFHD was analyzed using UPLC-MS/MS. The renoprotective effects of different doses of MFHD on IgAN mice were evaluated by examining renal pathology and laboratory parameters. Additionally, a combination of metagenomics, flow cytometry, ELISA, and Western blot techniques was used to evaluate the effects of MFHD on the gut microbiota-mucosal immune axis. Potential functional bacterial species were identified through correlation analysis, and their effects were validated through strain transplantation experiments in a pseudo-germ-free mouse model. RESULTS MFHD reduces urinary protein and improves renal pathological damage in IgAN mice. MFHD significantly increases gut microbiota diversity, enriches beneficial bacteria, and reverses the Th17/Treg immune imbalance, thereby reducing IgA+ plasma cells and serum IgA and IgG levels. Correlation analyses and strain transplantation experiment further confirmed that intestinal colonization by Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans restores the Th17/Treg balance and inhibits the differentiation of IgA+ plasma cells, thereby exerting a renoprotective effect. Additionally, both MFHD and Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans increase the expression of occludin and ZO-1, thereby improving histopathological damage in the small intestine. CONCLUSION MFHD improves IgAN by regulating the gut microbiota-particularly by enriching Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans-thereby restoring the Th17/Treg immune balance and reducing IgA secretion.

canSAR 2026-an update to the public drug discovery knowledgebase.
abstract: canSAR (https://cansar.ai) serves as the world's largest public platform for cancer drug discovery and translational research. It serves as an exploration and hypothesis generation platform for drug discovery through (i) fully integrating large, multidisciplinary data from public resources, as well as bespoke curated data, creating a connected, navigable drug discovery knowledge map; and (ii) applying a suite of machine learning and AI tools to generate novel insights. We share the latest updates to canSAR highlighting growth across all data, enhancements to the predictive algorithms, and continued improvements to the user experience. We leverage our latest open science chemical handling and druggability prediction tools to provide traceable insights. An increased focus of the platform is to provide "in-line" support and guidance to drug discovery exploration. We report the first incarnation of our high-fidelity, agentic-AI-generated, context-specific summaries, which we provide across the website for all human proteins to further aid users in synthesis and distillation of key information.

title: P – T – n H2O constraints on transcrustal magma evolution: Phase equilibrium modeling and binary endmember optimization of Neoproterozoic granitoids from the Ailaoshan region, southwestern China
abstract: Continental crustal differentiation in subduction zones transforms primitive mafic material into intermediate to felsic compositions through partial melting and magma interaction. The Neoproterozoic Jinping Complex in the Ailaoshan region, southwestern China, preserves an exceptional record of transcrustal magma evolution spanning ca. 783–697 Ma that provides quantitative constraints on crustal melting within the MASH (melting, assimilation, storage and homogenization) framework. Using binary melt mixing tools, this paper explains how a range of distinct magmatic rocks formed within crust exposed to prolonged mantle magma intrusion and heat transfer. Mantle sources metasomatized by slab-derived melts and fluids are inferred to have generated a compositional range of juvenile mafic lower crust. Melting of these rocks with residual garnet at ≥1.2 GPa, with best-fitting endmembers at 800–950 °C and H2O amounts of 1.0–1.3 wt.%, produced high Ba–Sr porphyritic granites with juvenile isotopic signatures. In contrast, muscovite-poor Group B monzogranites are best explained by the mixing of melts generated at 0.6 and 1.4 GPa, 875–950 °C and H2O amounts of 1.0–1.3 wt.% from mafic crust derived from slab-melt-modified mantle. For both suites, mixing melts from different protoliths improves the fit more than varying the melting conditions of one protolith. Gneissic granites record magma mixing, with their isotopic signatures indicating a contribution from evolved crust. Their felsic members are best reproduced by mixing melts generated at 0.6 and 1.2 GPa and 950 °C, with H2O amounts of 1.3 and 3 wt.%, respectively. Muscovite-rich Group A monzogranites, by contrast to the other rocks, reflect reworking of intermediate to felsic crust. Combining the constraints on the source composition and melting conditions for these different rock types reveals how repeated mantle magma intrusion and heating drove crustal melting of a variety of rocks and magma interaction.

title: Rethinking audits in the age of ESG
abstract: This study aims to systematically examine the core themes and boundaries of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) assurance, identifying prevailing research hotspots and dominant scholarly conversations. Furthermore, this study seeks to uncover emerging areas and critical gaps that offer opportunities for future research to address current and evolving challenges in ESG assurance. Based on 148 peer-reviewed articles (after rigorous screening), the authors use bibliometric techniques, including network analysis, clustering and co-citation analysis, to synthesise the field’s evolution and reveal underexplored areas. The review identifies five priority directions for future inquiry: the professionalism and evolving role of ESG assurers, ESG assurance quality and firm performance, the influence of governance mechanisms and stakeholder pressures, the implications of Audit 4.0 technologies (e.g. artificial intelligence, blockchain and data analytics) for assurance legitimacy and impact of agentic AI on assurance providers and ESG reporting readability and its consequences for assurance outcomes. By highlighting persistent tensions, contradictions and unresolved debates, this study reconceptualises ESG assurance as an evolving, multidisciplinary domain. This study may fully rely on Scopus, which limits the scope by potentially excluding relevant studies from other databases. Further, this paper addresses the key challenges found by International Federation of Accountants (IFAC, 2021), in determining the scope of an assurance engagement, exercising professional scepticism and judgment and obtaining the necessary competency and skills. This study advances the emerging field of ESG assurance by identifying underexplored research areas, highlighting key research gaps and outlining promising directions for future inquiry. Beyond mapping the existing literature, this study also discusses the possible theoretical contributions that can strengthen the conceptual development of this domain. The review highlights key practical issues, including the role of governance, AI adoption and assurer professionalism in enhancing the credibility and transparency of ESG assurance. This study offers useful insights for researchers, practitioners, standard setters and regulators aiming to strengthen the quality and reliability of ESG assurance. This study’s insights can enhance transparency and accountability in ESG reporting, fostering trust among stakeholders such as investors and regulators. Improving ESG assurance practices encourages companies to adopt more responsible and sustainable approaches, benefiting society at large. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first multi-disciplinary systematic literature reviews to study potential future avenues in the ESG assurance area with a holistic view. This study introduces diverse significant areas to meet current challenges in ESG assurance practices.

title: Appearances may mislead: explicit and implicit consumer responses to virtual anchors' form realism in live-streaming commerce
abstract: As virtual anchors become increasingly humanlike in live-streaming commerce, it remains unclear whether higher form realism consistently elicits more favorable consumer responses. This study examines how virtual anchors' form realism shapes consumer responses across explicit, implicit and neurophysiological levels. Two laboratory studies compared human anchors with virtual anchors varying in form realism. Study 1 combined self-reported evaluations with an affective priming measure of implicit evaluation, whereas Study 2 combined self-reports with electroencephalography to examine neurophysiological processing. Across both studies, high-form-realism virtual anchors received more favorable explicit evaluations than low-form-realism anchors and did not differ significantly from human anchors. In Study 1, however, high-form-realism virtual anchors received less favorable implicit evaluations than human anchors, while low-form-realism anchors did not differ significantly from either group. Study 2 revealed differentiated neurophysiological responses: human anchors elicited greater frontal theta power than high-form-realism virtual anchors and greater frontal gamma power than both virtual-anchor types, whereas low-form-realism virtual anchors elicited greater central and parietal theta power. Grounded in the associative–propositional evaluation model, this study develops an explicit–implicit evaluation framework for virtual anchor design. By demonstrating that increasing form realism does not uniformly enhance consumer responses, this study provides a more differentiated understanding of consumer responses to AI-mediated social agents.
journal: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing

title: End-to-End Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Activity Cable-Driven Hip Exoskeleton Assistance
abstract: Most learning-based methods for generating exoskeleton assistance profiles rely heavily on real-world human-in-the-loop data collection. This approach remains highly challenging for tracking arbitrary movements and often suffers from convergence issues due to large parameter scales. To address these challenges, this letter proposes a Behavior Foundation Model for Exoskeleton Assistance (BFM-EXO), in which a Universal reinforcement learning (RL)-based generalist motion-tracking policy is first trained as the Behavior Foundation Model (BFM) and then used to train a task-specific exoskeleton assistance policy, enabling real-time assistance across diverse motions. Specifically, we first develop the BFM, a generalist skeleton-level tracking policy capable of tracking a wide spectrum of daily activities. Building upon this, a two-stage training process is employed to derive BFM-EXO, an exoskeleton control policy that acts as a local joint-assistance compensator and simultaneously reduces biological joint torques and improves motion-tracking performance. Finally, we deployed this strategy on a physical hip exoskeleton. Both quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate a substantial reduction in the wearer's metabolic cost, validating the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Vision-Based Ergodic Control for Robotic Defect Detection
abstract: Efficient detection of surface defects is a critical component of quality control in manufacturing; however, standard robotic inspection methods typically rely on uniform coverage strategies and do not explicitly plan inspection trajectories based on available prior information about defect locations. This letter proposes a closed-loop active sensing framework based on ergodic control to address these limitations. Our approach leverages prior knowledge of the manufacturing process to prioritise exploration in regions with a higher likelihood of defects. We model the target distribution as a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) and employ a Kalman filter to recursively update the belief state based on incoming measurements. Simulation and experiments with a vision sensor mounted on a UR5 robot validate the proposed method.

title: Design, Modeling, and Control of a Fully Actuated Quad-Thopter With Wing Thrust Vectoring Mechanism
abstract: Flapping-wing micro air vehicles (FWMAVs) have attracted increasing attention in recent years, especially in dense agricultural environments such as greenhouses because they are safe around delicate crops and robust against collisions. However, existing FWMAVs are underactuated, limiting their ability to approach and reach downward-facing targets, such as drooping flowers, while maintaining a tilted attitude. Thus, in this study we propose a fully actuated FWMAV that enables independent position and attitude tracking, a capability unavailable to conventional underactuated FWMAVs. To this end, a quad-thopter configuration equipped with thrust-vectoring mechanisms for each pair of wings is designed to achieve full actuation. Furthermore, a full-pose tracking control framework for flapping-wing flight is developed based on a time-averaged thrust model. Experimental results obtained with the quad-thopter prototype demonstrate accurate full-pose tracking, alongside a unique tilted perching maneuver. This work provides a potential pathway toward omni-directional flight using flapping-wing platforms.

title: TR-MOTS: End-to-End Multi-Object Tracking and Segmentation for Autonomous Field Robots
abstract: Autonomous agricultural robots depend on temporally consistent perception to support reliable monitoring and intervention in dense crop scenes. However, homogeneous agricultural settings lead to incorrect plant localization and trigger ineffective robot actions in long-term operations. Conventional tracking-by-detection pipelines decouple detection from association, allowing error propagation between these two stages. Transformer-based frameworks address this by modeling detection and association in an end-to-end manner through persistent queries. However, existing methods cannot establish and preserve sufficiently discriminative query representations in dense homogeneous scenes. To address these limitations, we propose TR-MOTS, an end-to-end multi-object tracking and segmentation (MOTS) framework tailored for autonomous agricultural robots. TR-MOTS integrates instance segmentation and robust query initialization to improve object localization and reduce temporal fluctuation in densely cluttered scenes. By jointly optimizing detection, segmentation, and association within a unified architecture, TR-MOTS improves spatial separation in dense scenes and maintains consistent identities under partial occlusions. We evaluate TR-MOTS on two challenging robotic perception settings in agriculture, AppleMOTS for aerial orchard-scale monitoring, and LettuceMOTS for ground-robot field operation. TR-MOTS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art MOT and MOTS methods, achieving $51.61\%$ HOTA on AppleMOTS, and $83.08\%$ HOTA on LettuceMOTS. These indicate that robust detection and segmentation within end-to-end tracking frameworks substantially improves perception robustness for autonomous field robots.

title: Contrasting Fire‐Driven Erosion Processes Mobilise Distinct Organic Carbon Pools in Forest Landscapes
abstract: Wildfires can substantially alter organic carbon (C) cycling in forest ecosystems beyond immediate emissions from fuel combustion. Among these post‐fire effects, lateral C mobilisation by water erosion is an important but poorly quantified flux, rarely incorporated into fire‐related C budgets. Here, we quantified and characterised C mobilised by hillslope erosion and channel erosion by debris flows in highly fire‐prone eucalypt forests in southeastern Australia. We monitored suspended and bedload C export from headwater catchments across fire severities until erosion returned to background levels, quantified C mobilisation from colluvium by debris flows, characterised C chemical recalcitrance in ash, soils, eroded sediments and colluvium, and constrained colluvial C age using radiocarbon measurements. We then upscaled these fluxes to the area affected by the 2009 Beechworth Fire. Over the three‐year post‐fire perturbation period, hillslope and channel erosion mobilised 15,866 t C (0.78 t C ha −1 ). Hillslope erosion accounted for 91% of this landscape‐scale flux, compared with 9% from debris flows. The two processes mobilised contrasting C pools. Hillslope C export was dominated by young wildfire ash derived from incompletely combusted vegetation and the surface organic soil horizon. In contrast, debris flows generated substantial localised C pulses by eroding deeper colluvial deposits, with 2%–20% of mobilised C older than 6000 years. Chemically recalcitrant and highly recalcitrant forms accounted for 47%–60% of C in fire‐affected hillslope sediments and 43%–74% in colluvium, highlighting the potential importance of these lateral fluxes for long‐term C dynamics. Post‐fire erosion mobilised C equivalent to only approximately 4% of direct fire C emissions, but the C mobilised during the three‐year post‐fire period was equivalent to approximately 210 years of background (unburnt) erosion. Thus, lateral erosion represents an additional and compositionally distinct pathway of fire‐driven C redistribution that should be considered in fire‐prone forest C budgets.

title: SeqA-mediated sister loci cohesion regulates the efficiency and fidelity of DNA double-strand break repair across the E. coli genome
abstract: In Escherichia coli , SeqA-mediated cohesion at snap loci on the right replichore persists longer, but its role in DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair remains untested. Here, we show that site-specific DSBs at snap loci confer higher cell survival than nonsnap loci. With perturbations affecting sister cohesion [Δ seqA , topoisomerase IV overexpression (T4-OE)], this survival advantage was progressively reduced, with the combined Δ seqA T4-OE strain retaining only a transient advantage. The increased survival correlates with faster repair, reflected by rapid restoration of locus copy number and shorter-lived, thinner RecA–green fluorescent protein filaments. Consistent with more accurate repair, snap loci exhibited lower mutation accumulation under normal and antibiotic stress conditions. Comparative genome analysis of E. coli strains revealed higher GATC motif counts and higher sequence conservation. Together, these findings suggest that the chromosomal organization associated with prolonged sister cohesion at snap loci promotes efficient homologous recombination–mediated DSB repair and contributes to genome conservation.

title: Evolution of MEIS transcription factor activity during metazoan neural development—born to be wild
abstract: Meis TALE-class proteins pattern vertebrate neural tissue, inducing hindbrain and neural crest in Xenopus laevis embryos. Meis orthologs have two conserved regions: (i) Meis-specific domain and (ii) Meis-specific TALE homeodomain. Meis homeodomain proteins are present in “ancient” metazoans-eucaryotes like cnidarians, placozoans, and protozoans. We asked: When during metazoan evolution did Meis proteins acquire functionality to induce neural pattern? Using structure-function analysis in Xenopus , we show that the Meis-specific and Meis homeodomains suffice to induce the spinal cord but not the hindbrain. Meis proteins share a functionally conserved carboxyl-terminal transcription activation domain inducing the hindbrain. Ancient Meis proteins from Trichoplax and chlorophyte algae have a conserved Meis homeodomain, but lack the Meis-specific domain. Unexpectedly, these ancestral proteins robustly induce hindbrain and neural crest in Xenopus , unlike metazoan proteins requiring the Meis-specific domain. Thus, in early eukaryotes, Meis prototypes were “born to be wild,” having the intrinsic capacity to induce vertebrate structures like hindbrain and neural crest, despite predating them.

title: Structural basis of Anopheles mosquito salivary protein complexes implicated in malaria transmission
abstract: Successful malaria transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes depends on Plasmodium development within the mosquito midgut and subsequent sporozoite invasion of its salivary glands. Salivary proteins, notably Saglin and likely salivary gland surface proteins (SGS4 and SGS5), were suggested to play roles in these processes, but the lack of their structures has hindered our understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, we carried out biochemical and mass spectrometry analyses of salivary gland extracts and demonstrate that Anopheles gambiae SGS4 and SGS5 bind Saglin and other SG1 (salivary gland 1) proteins. Cryo-EM structure of the Saglin-SGS4 complex reveals that Saglin homodimerizes through coiled-coil interactions and disulfide bonds and engages longitudinally with SGS4. Comparisons among SG1-SGS complexes show that SG1 proteins share a conserved architecture, and SGS proteins adapt conformationally to bind different SG1 partners of varying lengths. To our knowledge, our findings uncover the first native mosquito salivary protein complexes that likely facilitate malaria transmission and highlight potential vector targets for blocking malaria transmission.

title: Psychedelics shift decision strategies and reconfigure orbitofrontal dynamics
abstract: Psychedelics such as psilocybin and ketamine are attracting renewed attention as rapid-acting therapeutics, yet how they reshape cognitive computations remains poorly understood. To address this, we trained mice on a free-response perceptual decision-making task that disentangles bias-driven from sensory-guided strategies. Acute administration of psilocybin or ketamine slowed decision times while improving accuracy. Behavioral modeling combining drift diffusion and GLM-HMM approaches revealed that these effects were driven by increased decision thresholds and a shift toward sensory-engaged states. Whole-brain c-Fos mapping identified modulation of distributed task-related networks, including the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC). Calcium imaging showed that OFC population dynamics were reorganized under psychedelic conditions, with preserved task selectivity but altered temporal structure and shifted population correlations. Together, these findings indicate that psychedelics shift decision-making toward greater reliance on sensory evidence while reshaping cortical population dynamics, providing a system-level account of their effects on perceptual decisions.

title: Self-assembly of bacterial volumetric patterns directed by a synthetic reaction-diffusion circuit
abstract: Reaction-diffusion (RD) has long been proposed as a mechanism underlying biological pattern formation. However, quantitative frameworks linking circuit design to spatial organization remain limited. Here, we engineered a synthetic gene circuit, MINPAC, that couples gene expression regulation (reaction) with bacterial colony expansion and quorum sensing (diffusion) to guide bacterial cells to self-organize into periodic volumetric patterns across multiple scales, from single cells to three-dimensional colonies. The patterns exhibit robustness against environmental variations and size-dependent complexity. Mathematical modeling supports a clock-and-wavefront mechanism, where oscillatory gene expression interacts with outward expanding diffusions to generate these periodic spatial structures. Topological analysis reveals that specific network architecture is essential for pattern formation. Guided by model predictions, we further show that pattern complexity can be systematically tuned by gene dosage, with lower expression levels favoring multiple rings through faster dynamics. This work establishes a framework uniting circuit engineering and mathematical analysis for programming multicellular self-organization through RD mechanisms, with potential applications in regenerative medicine and biomaterials.

title: Immune infiltrate predicts response to αPD1/αCTLA4 but not αPD1 and distinguishes programs of primary resistance in metastatic melanoma
abstract: While immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized treatment of metastatic melanoma, the identification of robust biomarkers to predict the relative efficacy of single versus combination ICB has been challenging. We performed a meta-analysis of eight cohorts of patients treated with anti–PD-1 ( n = 290), anti–CTLA-4 ( n = 175), and combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 ( n = 51) with pretreatment tumor sequencing and clinical annotations. Surprisingly, the increased response rate to combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 compared to anti–PD-1 monotherapy was observed only in highly immune infiltrated tumors, and not in immune-low tumors. Stratifying tumors by high or low frequency of immune cells also distinguished context-dependent programs of primary resistance to single and combination ICB. Notably, hypoxia-related pathways were enriched in nonresponders to anti–PD-1 ICB in immune-high, but not immune-low, tumors. Using an independent cohort of patients with scRNA-seq data, we observed that correlates of hypoxia were associated with increased stromal tumor receptor-ligand interactions. As proof of concept, selective inhibition of HIF-2α, a component of the hypoxia pathway and highly expressed in endothelial cells and fibroblasts, in combination with anti–PD-1, controlled tumor growth in mouse models of highly immune-infiltrated tumors but not poorly immune-infiltrated tumors. Our work demonstrates how stratification by tumor immune characteristics and clinical features can lead to the rational discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

title: Roseburia intestinalis counteracts TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis
abstract: Interactions between serum metabolites and vascular endothelial cells directly influence atherosclerotic lesions. It is essential to identify and understand the effects of the complex profile of serum metabolites on vascular pathology. In this study, we found that coronary lesion severity positively correlated with serum levels of the organophosphate ester tris (2-butoxyethyl) phosphate (TBEP), while TBEP levels inversely correlated with gut Roseburia intestinalis abundance. Western diet supplemented with TBEP substantially exacerbated atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E −/− ( ApoE −/− ) mice. We found that TBEP enhanced AMP-activated protein kinase α (AMPKα) phosphorylation, reduced nuclear translocation of active sterol regulatory element–binding protein 1c (SREBP1c) fragments, suppressed Patatin-like phospholipase domain–containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) protein expression in endothelial cells, and increased lipid deposition. Oral R. intestinalis supplementation reduced fecal and serum TBEP levels and attenuated TBEP-driven atherosclerotic lesions. We highlight that TBEP aggravates endothelial lipid accumulation and atherosclerosis, suggesting that targeting gut microbiota may serve as a promising strategy against TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis.

title: A membrane-guided strategy for optimizing proton exchange membrane fuel cells via spatially controlled acid distribution
abstract: Efficient regulation of phosphoric acid (PA) distribution is vital for advancing high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. PA migration from the membrane into the catalyst layer (CL) enhances proton accessibility but compromises membrane conductivity, highlighting the need to balance acid distribution within the membrane electrode assembly. Here, we propose a membrane-guided strategy enabling systematic evaluation of PA distribution effects and identification of a favorable acid content range. By designing side chain–grafted polybenzimidazole (PBI) membranes with abundant acid-binding sites, we achieve tunable acid doping levels and regulate PA partitioning through acid-polymer interactions. To compare PA accumulation, we introduce the mass ratio of phosphorus to platinum in the CL (PA CL /Pt CL ) as a semiquantitative descriptor of CL acid content and use distribution of relaxation times analysis to decouple its influence on ohmic resistance, oxygen reduction kinetics, and oxygen transport. We identify a favorable PA CL /Pt CL range of approximately two to three under the present conditions, while the nearly twofold enhancement over OPBI highlights coordinated control of membrane transport and the CL acid state.

title: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) binds talin and is anchored at the postsynaptic density by direct PDZ interactions
abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) is a serine/threonine kinase essential for brain development and function. Mutations in CDKL5 cause CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD), a severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathy associated with impaired synapse formation and function. However, how CDKL5 mutations disrupt synaptic function remains unclear. Here, we show that the major neuronal isoform of CDKL5 contains a C-terminal PDZ domain–binding motif that mediates direct binding to PSD-95 and SHANK PDZ domains and recruits CDKL5 to the postsynaptic density. Disrupting this motif mislocalized CDKL5, reduced dendritic spine density, and impaired spine maturation. We also show that the CDKL5 kinase domain binds the R8 rod domain of the mechanosensitive scaffold talin. Mutation of the talin-binding interface or reduced cellular contractility altered CDKL5 positioning relative to focal adhesions. These findings define how CDKL5 is targeted to synapses, suggest that talin mechanoswitching may position CDKL5 kinase activity, and highlight the importance of C-terminal anchoring for interpreting pathogenic truncations.

title: THERM-D uncovers distinct neural mechanisms separating morning and evening body temperature rhythms in Drosophila
abstract: Animal body temperature rises throughout the day and peaks in the evening, a pattern conserved across diurnal endotherms and ectotherms. However, the mechanisms driving the robust body temperature rhythms (BTRs) remain largely unclear. Here, we developed a machine learning–based platform, Temperature Homeostasis Evaluation of Rhythmicity in Model Drosophila (THERM-D), enabling continuous, high-throughput analyses of BTR. Using THERM-D, we identified robust BTR patterns reflecting flies’ morning and evening behaviors and revealed the function of CRYPTOCHROME (CRY)–negative clock neurons. About half of all clock neurons lack CRY, yet their functions are only partially understood. Gal4 drivers targeting CRY-negative neurons demonstrated that these neurons control the morning temperature rise. We further show that separate clock circuits regulate morning and evening BTRs. Thus, THERM-D elucidated the role of CRY-negative clock neurons in BTR and provides a powerful platform for uncovering mechanisms underlying circadian temperature homeostasis.

title: Dynamic nuclear pores dictate the emergence of lamina-associated domains and UV protection during embryogenesis
abstract: Lamina-associated domains (LADs) are large heterochromatin domains tethered to the nuclear periphery. LADs organize genome architecture, replication, repair, and transcription, but their formation during development is not well understood. Here, we use DamID and single-cell imaging to analyze embryonic LAD biogenesis in Caenorhabditis elegans . In early embryos, abundant nuclear pore components prevent heterochromatin formation at the lamina, and DNA positioned there is transcriptionally active. Over time, pore components decline, enabling LADs to form; auxin-mediated pore depletion induces precocious LADs. Nuclear basket component npp-21 /Translocated Promoter Region is not required, distinguishing embryonic LAD biogenesis from LADs in differentiated cells. Functionally, LADs confer protection against UVB radiation: Older embryos concentrate DNA damage at the nuclear periphery and survive UVB, whereas early embryos accumulate damage throughout nuclei and die, unless shielded by their mothers in utero. Within the embryo, damage is concentrated in upper, ultraviolet-facing cells, while underlying cells are shielded, suggesting that the Bodyguard effect operates at the organismal level. These findings identify embryonic dissipation of nuclear pores as a key step in embryonic LAD biogenesis, enabling older embryos to withstand environmental challenges.

title: Subclonal evolution can shape the transition toward a sarcomatoid phenotype in pleural mesothelioma
abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

title: Disulfiram inhibits pyroptosis and apoptosis through multiple complementary mechanisms
abstract: Gasdermins (GSDMs) execute pyroptosis by forming lytic pores in the plasma membrane that release IL-1 cytokines and promote cell swelling and membrane rupture. Their key roles in infection, inflammation and cancer make GSDMs attractive therapeutic targets. Here we systematically investigate how disulfiram, an approved drug for treating alcoholism, inhibits pyroptosis and identify multiple complementary mechanisms. First, disulfiram inhibits processing of procaspase-1 to caspase-1. Second, disulfiram inhibits caspases from processing human GSDMD to release the lytic N-terminal domain (GSDMD Nterm ). Third, disulfiram structurally modifies GSDMD Nterm . Fourth, disulfiram partitions into membranes, where it remains embedded, changes membrane properties and prevents GSDMD Nterm insertion. Similarly, disulfiram blocks intrinsic apoptosis by inhibiting procaspase-3 activation, caspase-3 cleavage of human GSDME, and GSDME Nterm pore formation. Furthermore, we show that two other GSDMD inhibitors, necrosulfonamide and dimethyl fumarate also inhibit GSDM-induced cell death through multiple complementary mechanisms. These multilevel inhibitory mechanisms deepen our understanding of strategies to target GSDM-mediated cell death pathways.

title: Platelet glycoprotein Ib shapes the immune response during lung injury
abstract: The acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening, inflammatory disease state of the lung. Self-propagating inflammation within the alveolar space and excessive infiltration of neutrophils into the pulmonary airspace are the main mechanisms underlying the dysfunction. A role of platelets in the pathogenesis of ARDS is suggested, but the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. We hypothesized that platelet glycoprotein (GP)Ib is an important contributor of platelet activation in this context. To highlight the contribution of the GPIb to the acute phase of experimental ALI in mice, we exposed mice genetically lacking functional GPIb ( GPIb-IL-4tg ) and wild-type (WT) mice injected with a function blocking anti-GPIb antibody to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) inhalation. GPIb-IL-4tg mice as well as anti-GPIb–treated mice displayed reduced neutrophil infiltration of the alveolar space in response to LPS. GPIb-IL-4tg mice as well as anti-GPIb–treated WT mice showed reduced interactions of platelets with neutrophils in comparison to controls, resulting in reduced platelet-neutrophil complexes and mitigated formation of neutrophil extracellular traps. Since these mechanisms are important for defense against external invasion of pathogens, we exposed GPIb-IL-4tg mice to Klebsiella pneumoniae and found reduced survival with increased bacterial load in these animals. Last, translational evaluation of biosamples of patients with ARDS showed that patients with low plasma levels of the shed GPIbα ectodomain (glycocalicin) exhibited higher mortality and worsened overall outcome. Together, our study shows that GPIb is a central mediator of neutrophil migration into the alveolar space and the defense mechanisms against the external invasion of pathogens.

title: An all-magnonic neuron with tunable fading memory
abstract: Magnonics offers nanometer-scale wave propagation and strong nonlinearities, making it attractive for neuromorphic applications such as artificial neurons. Yet, magnonic elements with interconnections solely within the magnonic system remain challenging, preventing the realization of interconnected magnonic neurons to date. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an all-magnonic neuron that reacts to magnon inputs with thresholded, amplified magnon firing and subsequent self-reset, enabling all-magnonic operation and cascading. Our approach is based on micro-antenna excitation on an ultralow damping garnet with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, where we exploit the positive magnon frequency shift to realize nonlinear activation. Using Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy, we uncover a transient neuron response with tunable fading memory: A 25% change in pump power results in a three-order-of-magnitude tuning in memory time, which we harness, demonstrating temporal integration of up to 50 magnon pulses. Last, we realize neuron triggering in a cascade of three neurons, highlighting its potential for connected magnonic circuits.

title: Clearance of erythrocytes after subarachnoid hemorrhage: Cranial lymphatic and dural pathways
abstract: The clearance of toxic blood products from the brain after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is critical for neurological recovery, yet the precise anatomical pathways and cellular mechanisms responsible for this process remain poorly defined. Using murine models of both arterial perforation and low-rate intracisternal injection, we have mapped a comprehensive, multifaceted network of red blood cell (RBC) distribution and clearance. We found that, while RBCs accessed peripheral lymphatic vessels via cranial nerves, an extensive distribution of extravasated erythrocytes could also be observed sequestered within nonendothelial, collagen-lined interstitial channels flanking the major dural venous sinuses. By day 2 post-SAH, regional macrophages actively cleared some trapped erythrocytes. These findings provide a detailed spatiotemporal framework of SAH blood clearance, revealing promising anatomical and cellular targets to accelerate stroke recovery.

title: LONP-1 deficiency causes dysregulated protein synthesis within mitochondria that is suppressed by mitoribosomal mutations
abstract: Mitochondrial homeostasis is maintained by molecular chaperones and proteases located within the organelle. The mitochondrial matrix-localized protease LONP-1 degrades oxidatively damaged or misfolded proteins. Importantly, LONP-1 also regulates mitochondrial DNA replication. Here, we show that mutations in C. elegans that impair LONP-1 function cause dysregulation of mitochondrial DNA replication, mitochondrial RNA transcription and protein synthesis within the mitochondrial matrix. LONP-1 deficient worms had reduced levels of oxidative phosphorylation proteins despite increased mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis. Via a forward genetic screen, we identified three mutations that restored mitochondrial function and the rate of development in lonp-1 mutants to levels comparable to those in wildtype worms. Interestingly, all three suppressor mutations were found in genes encoding mitochondrial ribosome proteins. A point mutation in the mitochondrial ribosome protein MRPS-38 restored oxidative phosphorylation in lonp-1 mutant worms. Combined, our results suggest that LONP-1 regulates mitochondrial translation and that suppressor mutations within mrps-38 or mrps-15 can enhance oxidative phosphorylation complex assembly when LONP-1 function is diminished.

title: PEG-free tunable poly(2-oxazoline) lipids modulate mRNA-LNP biodistribution and expression in vivo
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed drug delivery, enabling the stabilization and efficient intracellular delivery of nucleic acids. Current LNP platforms, including those used in clinical COVID-19 vaccines, rely on polyethylene glycol (PEG) to stabilize the nanoparticle. However, anti-PEG antibodies are ubiquitous in the population and are a major cause of anaphylaxis and reduced therapeutic efficacy by accelerating the blood clearance of PEGylated products. Here, we report the development of poly(2-oxazoline) (POx) lipids as alternatives. POx polymers are poorly immunogenic and mitigate accelerated blood clearance. Upon varying polymer hydrophilicity and molecular weight, we screened transfection efficiency in multiple cell lines and evaluated top candidates in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that POx-lipids incorporating short hydrophilic oxazoline chains enhance target transfection while mitigating liver expression. These POx-lipids boost expression in key extrahepatic tissues, including lymph nodes and spleen. This marks a notable advancement toward replacing PEG in LNP therapies and provides a clear path to optimizing POx-lipids for targeted vaccine and therapeutic applications.

title: Complex IV maturation coordinates postnatal mitochondrial and metabolic development
abstract: The perinatal heart undergoes a rapid metabolic transition from glycolysis to fatty acid oxidation that requires extensive mitochondrial remodeling, yet the molecular checkpoints that coordinate this process remain poorly defined. Using temporally resolved proteomics and complexome profiling of developing mouse hearts from late gestation through early postnatal life (E18.5 to P10), we identify a discrete developmental window in which respiratory chain architecture is remodeled to enable metabolic commitment. Complex IV (CIV) emerges as a central structural determinant of this transition, undergoing isoform-specific reassembly and transient suppression at birth before incorporation into mature respiratory supercomplexes. We identify the CIV subunit COX7C as a developmentally regulated determinant of CIV maturation, with its abundance increasing during maximal respirasome assembly and the switch to fatty acid oxidation. Loss of COX7C impairs terminal CIV maturation, prevents incorporation of heart-specific isoforms, and destabilizes the respirasome organization. Notably, this defect causes a selective secondary failure of complex I completion, demonstrating that respirasome formation is required for catalytic CI maturation in vivo. Consequently, cardiac-specific COX7C deficiency fails to complete the perinatal metabolic transition, leading to the collapse of fatty acid oxidation, activation of nucleotide and serine–glycine–one-carbon metabolism, attenuated activation of the mitochondrial integrated stress response, and a metabolically and structurally compromised state unlikely to support the increasing energetic demands of the postnatal heart. Together, these findings define a developmentally timed, CIV-dependent assembly step that couples respiratory chain assembly to postnatal cardiac metabolic fate and provide a temporal framework for mitochondrial maturation in the developing heart.

title: Geophysics-informed hydrologic modeling reveals contrasting regolith and bedrock responses of headwater catchments to warming
abstract: Predicting how warming reshapes headwater streamflow requires distinguishing shallow and deep subsurface contributions, which remain difficult to constrain in catchment-scale models. We use seismic P-wave velocity to partition the critical zone into regolith and fractured bedrock domains within a three-dimensional physically based model and develop a particle-based attribution method to quantify their streamflow contributions and source-water ages across realizations spanning diverse hydraulic configurations. Across these realizations, warming produces contrasting subsurface hydrologic responses: Regolith-sourced streamflow generally becomes slightly younger, whereas fractured bedrock-sourced streamflow generally ages. This contrast arises because warming increases evapotranspiration and alters snow accumulation and melt timing, reducing effective recharge and lowering fractured-bedrock saturation. Declining recharge slows water transit and shifts fractured-bedrock-sourced water toward longer flow paths. Our results suggest that warming may reduce fractured-bedrock water renewal, with implications for the buffering role of bedrock water storage and for prolonged retention of legacy contaminants.

title: SMAD4 loss drives cancer chromosomal instability through transcription-replication conflict–associated replication stress
abstract: Cancer chromosomal instability (CIN) drives tumor evolution through generating structural and numerical chromosome aberrations. However, its molecular determinants remain poorly characterized. Here, we uncover a yet unrecognized role for the tumor suppressor SMAD4 as a key regulator of chromosomal stability. Mechanistically, loss of SMAD4 causes replication stress by promoting transcription-replication conflicts (TRCs) and induces subsequent mitotic errors, leading to the concomitant emergence of structural and numerical CIN. While the tumor suppressor function of SMAD4 has been predominantly attributed to transforming growth factor–β signaling, we find that its role in genome maintenance operates via bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling and its transcriptional target gene ID3 . Consequently, inhibition of BMP signaling mimics the loss of SMAD4 , while reexpression of SMAD4 or ID3 in SMAD4 -deficient colorectal or pancreatic cancer cells suppresses TRCs, replication stress, and mitotic errors. Our findings reveal a TRC- and replication stress–driven mechanism by which loss of BMP-SMAD4 signaling causes cancer CIN.
