title: Interfacing ultrafast single-photon-level fields with an atomic ensemble
abstract: Ultrafast photons—with pulse durations on the order of 100 femtoseconds—are typical of high-rate, high-purity, entangled photon-pair sources. Efficient, coherent mapping between these states and matter-based quantum systems is an important problem in quantum optics and could enable applications in quantum frequency conversion, bandwidth conversion, and local quantum information processing at gigahertz speeds. This coherent mapping is also the initial storage step in matter-based photonic quantum memory, which can enhance multiphoton rates and allow for synchronization in quantum repeaters. Here, we use a collisionally broadened neutral atomic barium ensemble to demonstrate a quantum-compatible light-matter interface with storage efficiency of 95.6 ± 0.3%, total internal efficiency of 31 ± 1%, and noise contributions of <10 −4 photons per pulse. Using the simultaneous efficiency, bandwidth, and noise performance of this interface, we perform a full amplitude and phase reconstruction via spectral interferometry of single-photon-level fields retrieved from the interface.

title: Targeting METTL3 protects against acetaminophen-induced liver injury through HAPTOGLOBIN/CD163 macrophage axis
abstract: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is the most common cause of drug-induced liver injury (DILI), with limited treatment options. N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) is the most abundant internal epitranscriptomic modification in eukaryotic RNAs and is involved in various physiological and pathological processes, serving as a potential therapeutic target for many diseases. However, little is known about the role of m 6 A in DILI. Here, we found that intrahepatic expression of Methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3), the core catalytic subunit of RNA m 6 A methyltransferase complex, was elevated in patients with DILI and mouse DILI models. Hepatocyte-specific knockout of METTL3, achieved via either Alb-Cre ERT2 –driven recombination or adeno-associated virus (AAV)–mediated delivery of Cre, significantly protected from APAP-induced hepatotoxicity in both male and female mice. Mechanistically, hepatic METTL3 deficiency reduced m 6 A deposition on acute-phase protein haptoglobin ( Hp ) transcripts and promoted Hp transcription and translation in hepatocytes. Increased HP secreted by hepatocytes bound to its receptor CD163, expressed explicitly on macrophages, and induced highly phagocytic and anti-inflammatory polarization of macrophages, finally reducing APAP-induced hepatic injury. Moreover, two different METTL3 inhibitors, JNJ64619178 and STM2457, effectively alleviated APAP-induced liver injury. Our study thus demonstrated that hepatic inhibition of METTL3 protected against APAP-induced liver injury by promoting the cross-talk between hepatocytes and macrophages through HP/CD163, underscoring the potential of targeting METTL3 as a promising therapy for APAP overdose.

title: Anisotropic field suppression of charge order reveals orbital-selective Kondo hybridization in UTe 2
abstract: UTe 2 is a rare correlated quantum material where unconventional density-wave orders, Kondo physics, spin-triplet pairing, and reentrant superconductivity coexist. Because superconductivity emerges from a strongly correlated normal state, identifying and controlling intertwined normal-state orders are essential for understanding the electronic landscape where superconductivity arises. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy in a vector magnetic field, we uncover a staggered charge density wave (CDW) in high-quality UTe 2 crystals. This CDW exhibits a strong directional field response: It is completely quenched by a modest 1.7-tesla magnetic field along the quasi–one-dimensional uranium-chain direction while remaining robust against fields along other crystallographic axes. This anisotropy suggests an orbital-driven field-tuned quantum phase transition. Unexpectedly, the same field orientation concurrently suppresses the 5f Kondo resonance. Modeling indicates a switch in the dominant hybridization channel from Te 5 p- U 5 f to U 6 d- U 5 f coupling, suggesting an intimate interplay between CDW and the Kondo effect.

title: Dissecting the molecular triggers of early and late long-term potentiation
abstract: The brain stores information by changing the strength of its synapses, a process that has at least two phases: Late long-term potentiation (L-LTP) is thought to result from the consolidation of early LTP (E-LTP), just as long-term memory requires the prior establishment of short-term memory. Recently, inhibitory avoidance experiments under CaMKII inhibition have challenged this notion, demonstrating long-term fear memory without measurable short-term memory. Here we use optogenetic activation and inhibition of CaMKII during induction of spike-timing-dependent potentiation (tLTP) to dissect the signaling pathways. While CaMKII activation in CA1 neurons was sufficient to induce E-LTP, growth of the postsynaptic density and spine neck expansion, we found that CaMKII-induced LTP does not give rise to L-LTP. Conversely, inhibition of CaMKII during tLTP induction prevented E-LTP, but FOS and L-LTP were still expressed, driven by CaMKK and PKMζ. Thus, both long-term memory and L-LTP form in the absence of CaMKII activation.

title: Predictive model for nanoparticle incorporation into crystals reveals essential role of interfacial solution structure
abstract: Control of interfacial phenomena remains limited by incomplete understanding of molecular-scale solution structure at solid-liquid interfaces. We address this challenge by developing and validating a comprehensive analytical model for nanoparticle incorporation during crystallization. Using atomic force microscopy (AFM) probes surface functionalized to be “particle proxies” combined with three-dimensional AFM and force spectroscopy, we measure nanoparticle-calcite crystal binding energies and kinetic barriers associated with interfacial hydration layers. These measurements, together with diffusivities, parameterize a predictive model that is corroborated using surface-functionalized fluorescent silica nanoparticles incorporated into calcite. We show that surface chemistry governs incorporation by reshaping the energy landscape, with amine groups particularly favoring incorporation. Applying this approach to nanoparticles with different topologies further supports our finding that kinetic barriers play a pivotal role in incorporation processes. This synthesis science framework links interfacial solution structure, particle dynamics, and crystallization kinetics, identifying kinetic barriers as a key design principle for engineering bioinspired nanocomposites beyond empirical approaches.

title: Dual-modality photoacoustic and optical coherence tomography imaging simultaneously tracks transplanted stem cells and their viability
abstract: Monitoring transplanted cell viability in vivo, noninvasively remains a considerable challenge. By using multiwavelength photoacoustic microscopy powered by a reactive oxygen species (ROS)–responsive contrast agent, we can relatively and semiquantitatively assess and longitudinally monitor the viability of human-induced pluripotent stem cell–derived retinal pigment epithelium (hiPSC-RPE) cells in vivo. The contrast agent comprises colloidal chain-like gold nanoparticle (CGNP) clusters conjugated with IR775c, a heptamethine cyanine dye that undergoes selective oxidative quenching under elevated ROS conditions associated with cellular death (CGNP-IR775c). Dual-wavelength photoacoustic microscopy at 620 and 775 nanometers provides self-calibrated ratiometric measurements that enable relative viability assessment, distinguishing healthy from nonviable cell populations. In vitro studies demonstrated that CGNP-IR775c exhibited biocompatibility and showed dose-dependent ROS sensitivity across physiologically relevant H 2 O 2 concentrations. hiPSC-RPE cells labeled by CGNP-IR775c were subretinally transplanted into living rabbit eyes and longitudinally monitored for 2 weeks, showing that laser-induced oxidative stress produced measurable photoacoustic signal changes that were consistent with the viability status of the transplanted cells. The imaging technology developed here provides a practical solution for noninvasive, longitudinal, and semiquantitative assessment of the transplanted cell viability in vivo, and may contribute to ophthalmology cell-based therapy in both preclinical and clinical settings.

title: Flexible megahertz low-power complementary circuits based on nanoscale organic transistors
abstract: The stringent low-power requirements of wearable electronics systems can be met only by combining p-channel and n-channel transistors in a complementary circuit topology. For circuits based on organic thin-film transistors (TFTs), this calls for improvements in n-channel TFT performance. We report on flexible low-voltage nanoscale n-channel organic TFTs fabricated using a recently developed high-performance small-molecule semiconductor. The TFTs have on/off current ratios greater than 10 8 and subthreshold swings below 200 millivolts per decade. Nanoscale n-channel and p-channel organic TFTs were integrated into inverters that display small-signal gains up to 175, noise margins up to 80%, static power consumption as low as 10 −12 watts, and characteristic signal-delay time constants as short as 60 nanoseconds (at 3 volts). These are the best-performing flexible organic TFT–based complementary inverters reported to date.

title: ModuFold: Semantic Authoring of Origamic Architecture
abstract: Designing origamic architecture requires coordinating a three-dimensional form with its deployed panel structure and planar fabrication pattern. We present ModuFold, an authoring environment that connects these representations through a shared semantic design model. Makers compose parameterized architectural modules using familiar 3D interactions, while supported edits in the conventional modeling, deployed kirigami, and template views update the same underlying design. A Rhino-based geometry engine converts supported compositions into panels, hinges, openings, and an A4 cut-and-fold pattern. By preserving module identities and parameters across this process, ModuFold supports a continuous workflow from architectural construction to physical fabrication.

title: iTPMS: Interactive Inverse Design of Spatially Varying TPMS Metamaterial Fields
abstract: Spatial material design requires control over deformation and local structure. iTPMS maps sparse displacement targets to triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) fields through differentiable mechanics and response-aware regularization. Examples include deformation-aligned interfaces, inverse reconstruction, interpolation, and a Gyroid–Schwarz P pillow. For the pillow, prescribed head and neck families enforce morphology contrast while density and transition mixtures are jointly optimized using periodic unit-cell elasticity. The resulting connected three-dimensional mesh combines distinct pore patterns with continuous transitions between the prescribed regional families. Its displacement response is evaluated with a homogenized two-dimensional model.

title: Computational Dip Coating
abstract: Dipping an object in diluted paint leaves a tone that varies with surface geometry. We learn a differentiable model of this process from photographs of dipped relief plates, and predict tone with a correlation of 0.57. Inverting the model turns a grayscale image into a relief that reproduces it when dipped, which we demonstrate on ten fabricated plates.

title: Process modelling and optimization of the removal of biophile metals from Nigerian bitumen driven by phosphonium-based ionic liquid
abstract: This study explored the process modelling and optimisation of the removal of biophile metals from Nigerian bitumen using a hydrophobic phosphonium-based ionic liquid. Bitumen extraction from oil sands was performed using a Soxhlet extractor with toluene as the solvent. Metal removal was achieved through biphasic solvent extraction employing trihexyltetradecylphosphonium chloride as the extractant, chosen for its high thermal stability, low volatility, and strong affinity for metal ions. Metal concentrations of Cu, Mn, Zn, Co, Fe, and Cr were quantified via Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometry (Model Alpha Star 4). The optimisation process utilised Response Surface Methodology (RSM), with model validation through diagnostic plots generated by Design Expert Stat-Ease software. ANOVA results (p<0.005) confirmed the model’s significance. Consistent R 2 and adjusted R 2 values indicated a good fit to the experimental data. Diagnostic plots showed a near-perfect linear fit, reinforcing the model’s accuracy. Interaction effects studied through 2D contour and 3D response surface plots indicated that increasing input variables reduced metal concentrations. Optimal conditions determined were 50 °C temperature, 60-min reaction time, and 3 % w/v ionic liquid, achieving complete Mn removal and removals of 56 %, 61 %, 51 %, 43 %, and 36 % for Cu, Co, Cr, Fe, and Zn, respectively. These findings demonstrated the significant potential of trihexyltetradecylphosphonium chloride for the multimetal demetallization of bitumen under mild conditions.

title: When linguistic assistance becomes authoritative judgement: a multilevel framework for generative AI in higher-education language practices
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can suggest wording, explain language, and increasingly contribute to feedback and assessment. The central issue is not only what these systems generate, but when learners, teachers, and institutions begin to treat their outputs as reasons for judging language. Existing research addresses language ideology, distributed agency, algorithmic normativity, trust, assessment, and AI governance, but these literatures use different concepts for influence, authority, and institutional power. This article develops a multilevel framework of linguistic authority escalation through a critical integrative review focused primarily on English-dominant higher-education writing and assessment. In the framework, authority in the strict sense refers to attributed epistemic or normative standing; operational uptake is causal influence, and regulatory consequentiality is institutional power. The framework differentiates the initiator, subject, decision-maker, and accountable actor, and represents the source of authorisation, the subject’s degree of meaningful choice, and the durability of system embedding as co-occurring configurational conditions rather than alternative routes. It also distinguishes epistemic warrant, procedural legitimacy, substantive linguistic justice, and assessment validity as different standards for evaluating AI-mediated judgement. A literature-grounded worked case shows how the same model suggestion can remain optional assistance or acquire institutional force depending on these relations. The framework helps educational linguists identify when GenAI support preserves evaluative control and when opaque linguistic norms become difficult to contest, directing pedagogy and governance towards norm-explicit feedback, meaningful alternatives, task-specific evidence, appeal, and clear answerability.

title: Demonstratives as Emergent Definiteness Markers in Mongolian
abstract: This study investigates the functional differentiation of demonstratives in Mongolian and their extension beyond spatial deixis into discourse- and definiteness-related functions. Although Mongolian lacks a grammatical article system, its demonstrative paradigm exhibits systematic variation in referential function and is analysed as a grammaticalization continuum ranging from lexical deixis to emergent definiteness marking. The analysis draws on two complementary datasets: The Secret History of the Mongols (13th century), examined through its Spanish translation as a cross-linguistic interpretive probe, and a contemporary spoken Mongolian corpus comprising 32,598 sentences and 15,254 annotated noun phrase tokens, including 4,358 demonstrative occurrences. The historical data provide evidence for earlier stages of demonstrative usage, while the spoken corpus reveals synchronic distributional and discourse-functional patterns in natural language use. Integrating frameworks of deixis (Fillmore, C. J. 1982. “Towards a Descriptive Framework for Spatial Deixis.” In Speech, Place, and Action, edited by R. J. Jarvella and W. Klein, 31–59. Wiley; Levinson, S. C. 2004. “Deixis.” In The Handbook of Pragmatics, edited by L. R. Horn and G. Ward. Blackwell), definiteness (Lyons, C. 1999. Definiteness. Cambridge University Press; Himmelmann, N. P. 2001. “Articles.” In Language Typology and Language Universals, edited by M. Haspelmath, et al. 831–41. De Gruyter), and grammaticalization theory (Hopper, P. J., and E. C. Traugott. 2003. Grammaticalization, 2nd ed. Cambridge University Press; Diessel, H. 1999. Demonstratives: Form, Function, and Grammaticalization. John Benjamins), the study identifies four functional stages: spatial deictic forms (ene, tere), discourse-anaphoric extensions (tere), recognitional forms (önööh, mönööh), and near-determiner forms (el, tus). These stages instantiate a stratified system reflecting graded degrees of deictic and definiteness force. The findings support a gradient model of definiteness encoding and suggest that Mongolian demonstratives participate in an ongoing grammaticalization pathway from deixis toward definiteness, while not developing a dedicated article system.
journal: Mongolian Diaspora. Journal of Mongolian History and Culture

title: Influence of Irrigation Regimes on Genotypes of Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) for Grain Yield, Straw Yield and Yield-contributing Traits
abstract: Background: Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) is one of the most important cereal crops for global food security, but its productivity is strongly influenced by water availability and irrigation management. Evaluating irrigation regimes together with genotype performance can help identify combinations that maintain higher productivity under irrigated conditions. The present study evaluated the effects of three irrigation regimes on grain yield, straw yield and selected yield-contributing traits of five wheat genotypes. Methods: A two-year field experiment was conducted during the rabi seasons of 2023-24 and 2024-25 at the Instructional-cum-Research Farm, Department of Agronomy, Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, India. Five wheat genotypes (HI 1572, HI 3000, MP 3288, MP 3332 and Lok-1) were evaluated under one (I1), two (I2) and six (I3) irrigations in a factorial randomized block design with three replications. Grain yield, straw yield, grains per spike, spikes m-1 and spike length were recorded and pooled analysis was performed over the two seasons. Result: Irrigation regime significantly affected grain and straw yield, with I3 recording the highest pooled grain yield (4618.4 kg ha-1) and straw yield (7038.4 kg ha-1), compared with 3546.0 and 5330.7 kg ha-1, respectively, under I1. MP 3288 recorded the highest pooled grain yield (4490.7 kg ha-1) and straw yield (7187.7 kg ha-1), although its differences from MP 3332 were smaller than the corresponding critical differences. For yield-contributing traits, I3 recorded 48.05 grains spike-1, 261 spikes m-1 and 8.5 cm spike length. MP 3288 recorded the highest numerical grains spike-1 (47.75) and spike length (9.5 cm), whereas HI 1572 recorded the highest spike density (290.5 spikes m-1).

title: Beyond Correlation: A Causality-Driven Machine Learning Framework to Climate-Crop Yield Data Using Transfer Entropy and Lag Optimization Approaches
abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens agricultural production globally by altering growing seasons, precipitation and temperatures. Understanding and predicting crop yields under these changing conditions is critical for food security. However, traditional climate-crop yield models rely on correlational approaches that are incapable of distinguishing causality or identifying optimal temporal lags. These correlational approaches result in spurious predictions and limited mechanistic understanding. We designed a three-stage machine learning framework that integrates causal analysis, lag optimization, and ensemble modelling to predict maize ( Zea mays ) and soybean ( Glycine max ) yields using county-level data from Ohio from 1981–2020. Transfer Entropy (TE) analysis was applied to 24 climate variables from stage 1, including monthly minimum, maximum, and mean temperatures and monthly precipitation (May through October). We also selected the 10 features with the highest causal strength for each crop, based on dual significance criteria (p < 0.05 or TE > 0.01). The results showed high causal relationships: maize (mean TE = 1.62, range: 1.54–1.74) and soybean (mean TE = 1.36, range: 1.29–1.47). Stage 2 used univariate lag-effect analysis, testing lags of 0–3 years for each selected feature using R 2 maximization. It showed that the temporal patterns of maize features were different, 50% of which had no lag (lag-0) and 20% had a 3-year lag (lag-3). Soybean responded with 50% immediate (lag-0) features and 30% lagged (lag-3) features. Maize is the best performer with minimum temperature in June (R 2 = 0.10, 3 years lag); while the soybean predictions are best with maximum minimum temperature in October (R 2 = 0.11, direct effect). In the Stage 3, four machine learning algorithms were evaluated with optimally lagged features. Random Forest performed better: maize (R 2 = 0.75, RMSE = 0.83 Mt/ha) and soybean (R 2 = 0.72, RMSE = 0.27 Mt/ha). Temperature extremes at key growth stages became primary drivers and not just correlates of the causal drivers. This TE-LO framework goes beyond just spurious correlations in agricultural forecasting, going so far as to incorporate mechanistically significant relationships.

title: Differentiable Route Optimization in Prescribed Tunnel-Fire Fields: Computational Cost and Observation Age
abstract: Route guidance during a tunnel fire requires feasible paths to be compared within the time available between control updates. Reducing the cost of this calculation can improve the search, although the resulting exposure also depends on whether the observed fire field represents conditions encountered during traversal. This study examines these computational and information constraints through a differentiable route calculation in JAX. Reverse-mode automatic differentiation propagates sensitivities through bounded motion, field interpolation and exposure integration. Its performance is compared with coordinate finite differences within Adam and bounded quasi-Newton optimization under matched elapsed-time allowances, with Sobol search as a derivative-free reference. Fixed, translating and laterally switching analytical hazards distinguish the effects of control dimension and temporal freedom. Prescribed Fire Dynamics Simulator fields are then used to vary observation age while retaining the physical trajectory clock, common motion bounds and a fixed-centre reference. Evaluating frozen and evolving fields along the same executed path separates forecast error from realized exposure; derivative, dose-integration and field-resolution checks establish the numerical scope of these comparisons. Automatic differentiation benefits higher-dimensional Adam searches, but faster low-dimensional optimization does not consistently reduce exposure. Older observations increase forecast error without a monotonic exposure response. The computational benefit of differentiation therefore depends on the control problem and the fire information supplied to it.

title: Clinical AI agents: a short narrative review
abstract: Clinical artificial intelligence (AI) agents represent an emerging generation of AI systems. They extend conventional clinical decision support through goal-directed planning, tool interaction and adaptation of actions to intermediate results. Memory may support these functions but is not essential in every implementation. Human oversight is a safeguard for clinical deployment rather than an intrinsic capability. This short narrative review summarizes current evidence regarding the core architectural features, representative clinical applications, and primary implementation challenges of clinical AI agents. Recent studies indicate promising applications in diagnostic decision support, workflow automation, patient communication, and evidence synthesis. However, existing evidence remains largely based on technical validation studies, proof-of-concept systems, and conceptual frameworks, with relatively limited prospective evaluation in routine clinical practice. Key challenges include establishing reliable evaluation frameworks, ensuring process-level safety, developing effective governance structures, and generating robust clinical evidence to support implementation. Although technological progress is rapid, widespread adoption will require not only further technical advances but also rigorous clinical validation, transparent governance, and successful integration into healthcare workflows. Clinical AI agents may become useful components of multidisciplinary healthcare workflows, provided that future research addresses the remaining methodological and implementation challenges.

title: UAV Thermal Screening of Landfill Gas Networks: Detection Limits, Matched Controls and Georeferencing Requirements
abstract: Leaks from above-ground landfill gas pipelines are hard to locate with point-based methods. This study tested whether unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) thermography can identify potential leak zones on the gas network in a site of central Italy. Two thermal surveys (November 2023 and 2024) were processed into 8 cm thermal orthomosaics, co-registered to a median offset of 22 cm and checked on 29 RTK GNSS points. The 147 thermal anomalies identified from the ground in 2023, only one of which had measurable gas, were compared with random, distance-matched and on-pipe controls, using a local thermal metric on all pixels and on soil only. Anomaly sites were warmer than random points (AUC 0.77) but not warmer than matched or on-pipe controls once spatial dependence was considered, and showed no excess soil heat in any of 176 parameter settings. Synthetic warm spots were detected in 80% of cases above 15 °C on the pipe and 10 °C on the adjacent soil, and became undetectable with position errors of 2 m. The study thus evaluates the thermal signature of ground-identified anomalies, not leak detection rates; UAV thermography can support screening only with matched controls, accurate co-registration and gas verification.

title: Reconstruction of Paleo-Channels Around the Tang Wang Cheng Site in Xinjiang, China, Discerned from Multi-Source Remote Sensing and OSL Dating
abstract: The development of drainage systems is essential for sustaining oasis vitality and human habitation in arid and semi-arid regions. The Tang Wang Cheng Site (TWCS) is located in the desert-oasis ecotone at the northwestern edge of the Taklamakan Desert. Archaeological evidence from reclamation zones and irrigation channels at the site indicates a substantial historical reliance on water resources, in sharp contrast to the current arid conditions. However, the processes of paleo-drainage reorganization and associated environmental evolution around the TWCS remain poorly understood. In this study, paleo-channel traces were mapped through geomorphological interpretation of multi-source remote sensing data, supported by field investigations, geomorphological surveys, and archaeological excavations. Sedimentary stratigraphic analysis and optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating were used to investigate local changes in depositional conditions. The results reveal numerous paleo-channel traces west of and within the TWCS, indicating a high concentration of former channel features around the site. Five OSL ages from a natural profile approximately 11 km northwest of the TWCS constrain local depositional changes between approximately 1500 and 710 yr B.P., including a transition from gravel-dominated to sand-dominated sedimentation. Excavated channel deposits within the site provide evidence of fluvial activity during its occupation. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating historical satellite imagery and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-derived terrain data for mapping paleo-channel traces in arid archaeological landscapes and provide a basis for further investigation of hydrological change and settlement dynamics in southern Xinjiang.

title: Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for design in emerging creative environments
abstract: The study, titled From Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for Design in Emerging Creative Environments, aims to determine the competencies linked to the use of Artificial Intelligence in the training of designers, as well as to examine its impact on the professional environment. The advancement of AI has reconfigured not only the tools for design practice, but also the essential dynamics of the creative process. In emerging human-AI collaboration [HAIC] scenarios, these systems operate as cooperative agents and not merely as support tools. However, even though design students are progressively incorporating these technologies into their practice, a gap persists in the development of fundamental competencies for establishing effective interaction with these systems. Therefore, the need to strengthen disciplinary training through competencies that integrate critical interpretation, collaborative interaction, ethical and metacognitive reflection, in addition to specialized technical mastery is recognized. Based on the above, this research is structured around a comprehensive review of scientific literature, analysing studies retrieved from specialized databases in both design and higher education. The methodology will adopt the PRISMA [2021] systematic review protocol, which will ensure a rigorous process for the identification, selection, and synthesis of emerging competencies. The findings will be presented through graphic visualizations, and the discussion will incorporate relevant case studies. Ultimately, the study aims to offer an in-depth theoretical and methodological framework for future lines of research, highlighting the strategic role of AI competencies in the academic achievement and professional development of designers. These competencies are essential for overcoming limitations related to the originality, quality, and coherence of creative proposals, indispensable elements for competitive performance in educational and professional contexts.

title: dMoT v1.0: A Differentiable Library of 36 Conceptual Hydrological Models for Large-Sample Modelling
abstract: Conceptual hydrological models represent alternative hypotheses of catchment behaviour, yet their diverse numerical implementations complicate gradient-based, large-sample modelling. We present dMoT v1.0, a PyTorch-based library implementing 36 established lumped rainfall-runoff models within a common differentiable framework. Drawing on MARRMoT formulations, dMoT retains model-specific storages, fluxes, and routing processes while adopting explicit sequential state updates and GPU-parallel computation. We evaluate numerical reliability, automatic differentiation, computational efficiency, and scalability. Water-balance tests met their prescribed tolerances, and automatic-differentiation gradients agreed with finite-difference estimates under the evaluated conditions. Compiled GPU execution achieved a median 2.89-fold forward-execution speed-up over single-threaded CPU execution across the 36 models. We further demonstrate independent calibration and differentiable parameter learning across 531 CAMELS-US catchments. The two approaches achieved median model-level test scores of 0.624 and 0.612, respectively, using a numerically stabilised Kling-Gupta efficiency metric on temporally held-out data from the training catchments. These results establish dMoT as a computational framework for applying contrasting conceptual model structures under different parameter-estimation strategies. By combining a documented model library with automatic differentiation, numerical verification, and scalable execution, dMoT supports reproducible large-sample hydrological modelling and systematic comparisons of model structures and learning approaches.

title: Decorrelation and Deformation: Sentinel-1 InSAR Analysis of the March 2025 Earthquake in Central Myanmar and along the Sagaing Fault
abstract: A moment magnitude (Mw) 7.7 earthquake, as reported by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), struck central Myanmar on 28 March 2025. Its epicenter was situated near the Sagaing Fault, a major right-lateral strike-slip fault system that accommodates the relative motion between the Indian and Sunda plates. As one of Southeast Asia’s most active tectonic structures, the Sagaing Fault has a history of producing destructive earthquakes, and this event caused significant ground displacement and surface rupture particularly across the Mandalay and Sagaing regions, which lie directly along its central segment. Using Sentinel-1 satellite imagery and advanced Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) techniques, the co-seismic deformation was mapped and quantified with high precision, revealing clear patterns of displacement. Interferometric phase analysis indicated a reported maximum line-of-sight (LOS) pixel displacement of 52.0 cm, which requires coherence and phase-unwrapping validation before it can be interpreted as ground displacement concentrated near the fault trace while coherence analysis showed localized areas of signal decorrelation corresponding to intense ground disturbance. To refine rupture mapping, the Normalized Coherence Change Index (NCCI) was applied for the identification of severely damaged zones. Spatial analysis further indicates that as the distance from the epicenter increases, the deformation amplitude gradually decreases, which is consistent with the typical elastic strain release of strike-slip faults. Quantitative assessments were conducted by dividing the affected area into multiple zones for the evaluation of displacement gradients and rupture extent. The results provide new insights into the mechanics of active fault systems in central Myanmar and reveal the spatial patterns of ground movement associated with large-magnitude seismic events. These findings identify regions of high seismic vulnerability and highlight the importance of remote sensing combined with ground-based observations for hazard assessment, infrastructure resilience planning and earthquake preparedness.

title: Explaining Organizational Decoupling through Informal Governance: A Latent Mediation Model of Academic Discipline
abstract: This study examines how Informal governance is associated with Organizational decoupling among Chinese university students, with Academic discipline proposed as an explanatory mechanism. Drawing on self-determination and self-regulated learning perspectives, a conditional process model was specified and evaluated using a synthetic dataset of 486 cases. The simulated measurement model demonstrated acceptable reliability (composite reliability = 0.84) and fit (CFI = 0.95, TLI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.049, SRMR = 0.046). Structural estimates suggested that Informal governance was positively associated with Academic discipline (β = 0.35, p < .001) and with Organizational decoupling (β = 0.25, p < .001). The standardized indirect effect through Academic discipline was 0.15, with a synthetic 95% bootstrap interval excluding zero. Together, the modeled predictors explained 42% of the variance in Organizational decoupling. The paper contributes a concise mechanism-based account of adaptive learning and demonstrates an empirical structure aligned with The Journal of Interactive Social Sciences. Because all results are simulated, the findings are illustrative and require validation with ethically collected data.
journal: The Journal of Interactive Social Sciences

title: Impulsive and Planned Life Strategies as Factors of Life Success and Subjective Well-Being
abstract: The aim of the study was to investigate the relationship between Impulsive and Planned life strategies and their association with subjective well-being and perceived life success. The methodology included theoretical analysis, conceptual modeling, a semi-structured interview, subjective success rating scales, the Subjective Well-Being Diagnostic Method, content analysis, and non-parametric statistical analysis using the Mann-Whitney U test. The theoretical framework was based on the conceptual differentiation of Impulsive and Planned life strategies according to their characteristics in time perspective, decision-making, motivational orientation, attitudes toward professional activity, leisure organization, and responses to stressful situations. Based on these criteria, an original semi-structured interview was developed to identify the dominant life strategy and examine its relationship with subjective success and psychological well-being. The interview lasted between 1 and 1.5 hours and was followed by respondents’ self-assessment of success across major life domains and completion of a standardized subjective well-being questionnaire. The empirical study involved 25 middle-aged participants. Statistical analysis demonstrated that 64% of respondents exhibited a predominance of the Impulsive life strategy, whereas 36% were characterized by the Planned life strategy. At the same time, no participant represented a purely impulsive or purely planned type, as all respondents demonstrated characteristics of both strategies in different proportions. The findings further indicated the absence of statistically significant differences between the two groups across the examined indicators of subjective well-being and perceived success. These results support the assumption that both life strategies may contribute to successful psychological adaptation and life satisfaction through different mechanisms. The Impulsive strategy appears to facilitate success through flexibility, rapid adaptation, intuitive decision-making, and openness to change, whereas the Planned strategy promotes comparable outcomes through systematic planning, self-regulation, persistence, and long-term goal orientation. The findings also provide a basis for considering life strategies in relation to meaning in life, particularly the role of personally significant goals, values, and temporal orientations in understanding how different patterns of life organization may support subjective well-being and life satisfaction.

title: Technological Innovation and Green Process Innovation: A Serial Mediation Model of Information Quality and Green Work Engagement
abstract: Growing environmental concerns and increasing sustainability expectations have encouraged manufacturing organizations to adopt technological innovations that support environmentally responsible production processes. However, the mechanisms through which technological innovation enhances green process innovation remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the direct effect of technological innovation on green process innovation and examines the serial mediating roles of information quality and green work engagement in Malaysian manufacturing organizations. Drawing upon the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) framework, a conceptual model was developed and empirically tested. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among employees of manufacturing organizations in Malaysia, and 391 responses were collected using a convenience sampling technique. The collected data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings indicate that technological innovation positively influences information quality and green process innovation. Information quality significantly enhances both green work engagement and green process innovation, while green work engagement positively contributes to green process innovation. Furthermore, the results support the mediating role of information quality and the serial mediating effects of information quality and green work engagement in the relationship between technological innovation and green process innovation. These findings highlight the importance of integrating technological capabilities with high-quality organizational information and employees' environmental engagement to achieve sustainable manufacturing practices.

title: Cadmium, Chromium, and Nickel Toxicity in Crop Plants: Mechanisms, Crop Responses, and Mitigation
abstract: Cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), and nickel (Ni) are persistent contaminants of agricultural soils and irrigation systems. Their plant toxicity depends on chemical speciation, soil properties, concentration, exposure duration, crop genotype, and interactions with nutrients and other metals. Cd is a non-essential and highly toxic element that can enter plants through transport systems for iron, zinc, and manganese. Cr toxicity is strongly controlled by oxidation state: the relatively mobile and oxidising Cr(VI) species generally cause greater phytotoxicity than Cr(III), although both can impair growth. Ni is an essential micronutrient at low concentrations but becomes toxic when homeostasis is exceeded. Across crop species, the principal effects include inhibited root and shoot growth, nutrient imbalance, chlorophyll loss, impaired photosynthesis, membrane damage, reactive oxygen species accumulation, and reduced yield. Plants respond through antioxidant enzymes, chelation by phytochelatins and metallothioneins, vacuolar sequestration, cell-wall immobilisation, transporter regulation, hormonal signalling, and rhizosphere interactions. Recent studies show that silicon, selenium, zinc, molybdenum, nitric oxide donors, beneficial microbes, biochar, and genotype selection can reduce metal accumulation or oxidative injury, but field-scale effectiveness remains variable. This review compares Cd, Cr, and Ni toxicity in crop plants, synthesizes recent crop-specific findings, and identifies priorities for food-safe and climate-resilient remediation.

Modelling pesticide residues and ecological risks in Kilombero Valley, Tanzania: a SWAT + approach
abstract: Thorough pesticide use in tropical agricultural catchments threatens surface and groundwater quality, yet long-term pesticide transport and ecological risks remain poorly understood in data-scarce regions. This study assessed the long-term distribution and ecological risks of chlorpyrifos, profenofos, cypermethrin, and lambda-cyhalothrin in the Kisawasawa catchment, Kilombero Valley, Tanzania, from 2005 to 2035 using the Soil and Water Assessment Tool Plus (SWAT + ). By integrating SWAT + modelling with satellite-derived land use data, global soil datasets, NASA climate records, laboratory-derived pesticide concentrations, and ecological risk assessment, this study provides a long-term spatial assessment of pesticide transport and ecological risks in a tropical, data-limited agricultural catchment in Tanzania. High-risk HRUs for chlorpyrifos, cypermethrin, and profenofos increased from 21% to 41% in 2005 to 63% to 100% in 2035 in surface water, indicating a substantial expansion of ecologically at-risk areas. In groundwater, high-risk HRUs increased from 0–47% to 55–89%, reflecting progressive pesticide migration and persistence in subsurface environments. In contrast, lambda-cyhalothrin declined slightly from 12.7% to 10.4% in surface water, suggesting relatively stable spatial ecological risk. The measured concentrations reached 2.00 µg/L for chlorpyrifos and 0.42 µg/L for profenofos. Ecological risk assessments based on these concentrations revealed risk quotient (RQ) values ≥ 1 at most monitoring sites. Although cypermethrin and lambda-cyhalothrin had concentrations as low as 0.005 µg/L, they still posed significant ecological risks. These results demonstrate the usefulness of SWAT + for projecting long-term pesticide transport trajectories and provide a scientific foundation for targeted mitigation efforts and sustainable water resource management in tropical agricultural catchments.

Evaluation of RGB sensor system for nondestructive detection of salinity stress in arugula
abstract: Purpose Salinity stress silently erodes crop yields long before symptoms appear, making early, non-invasive detection essential for precision agriculture. Methods We evaluated a low-cost RGB sensor platform, with possible integartion of wireless networking, for real-time phenotyping of hydroponically grown arugula ( Eruca sativa (Mill.) Thell.) under 0, 40, and 80 mM NaCl. Results The sensor captured reflectance across seven spectral channels, generating leaf color metrics in situ. Principal component analysis, canonical correlation and clustering analysis confirmed tight coupling between RGB channels and ion ratios. Physiological, CIELAB, and optical datasets were fused using DIABLO, (Data Integration Analysis for Biomarker discovery using Latent components), achieving exceptional performance (mean error rate = 0.083 for component 1; zero for component 2) with only three features per block. High-stability variables (Na⁺, Na⁺/K⁺, Na⁺/Mg2⁺, b*, Chroma, White, Green, Red) tracked a clear dose-dependent stress gradient, linking ionic imbalance to possible pigment degradation and reflectance shifts. Particularly, sensor-derived indices detected spectral shifts preceding visible chlorosis, enabling early diagnosis. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that compact RGB-based sensing, empowered by integrative analytics, can deliver rapid, non-destructive, and biologically grounded stress diagnostics. The approach is readily deployable in controlled or open-field systems, providing a scalable pathway for precision stress monitoring before yield losses occur. Graphical abstract Optional description: Optical sensor module, connected to Arduino mega 2560 along with a Wi-Fi module, is capturing reflectance of arugula leaves under salinity treatments. The sensor setup is shown measuring leaves grown at 0, 40, and 80 mM NaCl in a deep water culture system. Physiological, CIELAB, and sensor-derived data were integrated and analyzed using multivariate approaches and the DIABLO framework to validate the sensor’s potential for early, non-destructive detection of salinity stress.,

title: Automated Multi-Horizon Forecasting of Hourly Reference Evapotranspiration Using Statistical, Tabular, Ensemble, Deep-learning and Foundation Models
abstract: Accurate short-term forecasting of reference evapotranspiration (ET0) is important for irrigation scheduling and agricultural water management. However, hourly multi-horizon ET0 forecasting remains relatively underexplored, particularly using automated forecasting frameworks and emerging time-series foundation models. This study develops a univariate multi-horizon framework for hourly ET0 forecasting using statistical, tabular, ensemble, deep-learning, and pretrained foundation forecasting paradigms implemented through AutoGluon TimeSeries (AG-TS). Hourly ET0 was computed using the ASCE Penman–Monteith equation from meteorological observations collected between October 2015 and September 2023. The forecasting performance of the evaluated models was assessed at 1-h, 6-h, 24-h, and 168-h horizons using mean absolute scaled error (MASE), revealing clear horizon-dependent variation. Chronos2 achieved the best performance at 1-h and 168-h, with MASE values of 0.096 and 0.723, respectively, whereas WeightedEnsemble performed best at 6-h and 24-h, with corresponding MASE values of 0.800 and 0.647. Horizon-wise and temporal analyses further showed that forecast agreement generally weakened at longer lead times, while the characteristic diurnal ET0 pattern was broadly retained. Chronos2 also exhibited moderate computational requirements, whereas Temporal Fusion Transformer required substantially greater fitting time. Overall, the results demonstrate the value of horizon-specific model evaluation and highlight the potential of pretrained time-series foundation models for capturing temporal patterns in historical hourly ET0 observations.

Governing Agentic AI: An Onto-Relational-Sophic (ORS) Framework for Deployment-Sensitive Governance
abstract: Agentic AI systems now act, rather than merely advise, within social and institutional settings. The persistent gap lies less in principles than in deciding which obligations a deployment should attract as the relationships around it change. Risk-based regulation classifies by declared intended purpose and does not register the dependence that forms around a system once it is in use. We propose the Onto-Relational-Sophic (ORS) framework, whose core contribution is to treat that dependence, rated as social embedding, as a trigger for reclassification. A system-in-deployment is rated on autonomy, social embedding, and moral relevance; each rating triggers a module of obligations on providers, deployers, and institutions; nine explicit rules govern assignment, conflicts, and reclassification, including the rating of multi-agent ensembles as wholes and the prospective rating of systems designed to induce dependence; and categories serve as summary labels. Two supporting pillars, grounded in Cyberism, structure the framework: a Cyber-Physical-Social-Thinking ontology that organises the evidence for each rating, and Cybersophy, an axiology that applies a reversibility priority when principles conflict. Three scenarios and a structured comparison with existing EU law show where ORS converges with current obligations and where it adds to them, most clearly when people come to depend on one certified system in different ways. No legal personality is conferred on any system. The rating scales and rules are proposed rather than validated: the social-embedding instrument has not been tested for inter-rater reliability, and the worked classifications rest on the authors’ own ratings. A reliability study should precede regulatory use.

title: A reference architecture for governed cognitive enterprises combining knowledge memory and decision intelligence with agentic AI under continuous assurance
abstract: Enterprises increasingly combine large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and autonomous software agents with existing enterprise architecture, knowledge management, and analytics investments, yet these capabilities are commonly adopted as isolated point solutions without a shared architectural foundation for organizational knowledge, decision reasoning, human accountability, or continuous assurance. This fragmentation leaves organizations unable to explain how an automated recommendation was produced, to bound what an autonomous agent may do, or to demonstrate governance to auditors, regulators, and boards. This paper asks how enterprise knowledge, decision support, agent execution, and governance can be structured as one coherent architecture. Using a literature-grounded conceptual synthesis across enterprise architecture, knowledge management, retrieval-augmented generation, decision intelligence, agentic artificial intelligence, and artificial intelligence governance, the paper derives a consolidated research gap and proposes the Governed Cognitive Enterprise Architecture: six integrated layers, a human accountability boundary, a structural formal representation, an operational lifecycle, and a maturity model, the Cognitive Enterprise Readiness Index, for organizational self-assessment. The architecture is evaluated conceptually against explicit criteria for completeness, capability integration, and governance alignment, and is compared with the reviewed literature through a source-referenced framework rather than an experimental benchmark. The principal contribution is an integrated architectural vocabulary and structure that treats human accountability and continuous assurance as first-class concerns alongside knowledge and decision capability. As a conceptual reference architecture it has not been empirically validated in an operational enterprise; expert evaluation, case-study, and quantitative validation are specified as future work.

title: An empirical evaluation of image preprocessing techniques for transfer learning-based multicrop classification
abstract: The accurate and correct classification of leaves as healthy is quite necessary in advanced precision agriculture. However, more work on the effects of preprocessing in machine learning is needed. The study worked on evaluating the various preprocessing techniques on five classes of healthy leaves, the dataset consisting of apple, blueberry, grape, cherry, and corn leaves. The dataset was split into train, test, and validation parts, then the train images were augmented with horizontal and vertical flips. Later preprocessed with five various approaches, i.e., raw data as a baseline, gamma enhancement, Sobel edge detection, histogram equalisation, and lastly, a brightness-adjusted preprocessing technique. Trained on various deep learning and transfer learning techniques, i.e., CNN-based architecture, AlexNet, DenseNet, InceptionV3, MobileNetV2, ResNet-50, and VGG-16, maintaining consistent splits and maintaining uniformity. Here, a total of 35 hybrid architectures are explored. Performance is being assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, MCC, F1 score, and AUC-ROC. AlexNet performed the best of the bunch with Raw images, sitting at 99% test accuracy, and MobileNet with a 99% accuracy on the Gamma-enhanced dataset, with a significant drop in Sobel edge detection-based datasets for certain models like Inception-V3 and the custom model. The findings of this study highlight how various preprocessing techniques affect training and the selection of appropriate preprocessing techniques to optimize deep learning models for excellent agricultural image classification, giving strong insights for automated crop species detection systems.

Evaluation of Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (IR BiotyperⓇ) for Rapid Serotyping of Streptococcus pneumoniae: A Prospective Validation in a Public Health Reference Laboratory.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To validate an expanded Artificial Neural Network (ANN) classifier for S. pneumoniae serotyping using FT-IR spectroscopy and assess its prospective performance in a routine public health reference laboratory. METHODS A diagnostic accuracy study was conducted at the Central Public Health Laboratory of Paraná - Brazil, based on the acquisition of 1,603 spectra, corresponding to 27 target groups/serotypes for training models and 70 independent routine clinical isolates (2025-2026) for prospective blind validation. RESULTS The ANN classifier achieved 100% cross-validation accuracy across 27 target serogroups/serotypes in the derivation dataset. In prospective blind testing (N = 70 clinical isolates), the FT-IR/ANN workflow demonstrated 98.6% overall serotype concordance (69/70) with Quellung reaction (reference method), correctly differentiating high-priority vaccine-escape strains (19A, 3, and 6C). High-reliability classification (≥ 80.0) was obtained for 90.0% of isolates, with a mean Isolate Score of 94.6% (median 100.0%, IQR: 98.2-100.0%). An untested non-target serotype (35F) was flagged by a low Isolate Score (34.2), serving as a preliminary internal quality control indicator requiring confirmation by reference methods. CONCLUSION FT-IR spectroscopy combined with ANN provides a rapid, accurate, and scalable alternative to the Quellung reaction for pneumococcal serotyping, supporting its use in routine public health laboratory surveillance.

title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
abstract: This work investigates how defect engineering and nanostructuring via severe plastic deformation influence electrical and thermal transport in the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi. High-pressure torsion (HPT) for up to N = 4 turns produces a hierarchical defect structure, including deformation twins at low strains, dislocations and Lomer-Cottrell locks at intermediate strains, and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries at large strains. While hardness naturally increases and saturates at ~520 Hv, both electrical and thermal conductivity exhibit an unusual increase upon HPT processing (from 0.953 MS m-1 and 10.3 W m-1 K-1 after homogenization to 1.003 +- 0.005 MS m-1 and 14.4 W m-1 K-1 after N = 4). Analysis based on the Wiedemann-Franz law indicates a modest increase in electron transport (~5%) and a significant increase in phonon transport (~100%) after HPT processing. The phonon mean free path remains small on the order of 0.6-1.1 nm, and comparison with the Cahill-Pohl model shows that heat transport occurs near the minimum thermal conductivity limit, where vibrational modes are strongly scattered. This suggests that the enhancement in thermal transport is not governed by conventional defect scattering, but it is hypothesized that modifications in atomic-scale disorder, such as deformation-induced short-range ordering, are responsible for this unusual behavior. Specific heat capacity increases after HPT, consistent with stored defect energy. The linear thermal expansion exhibits a non-monotonic behavior, decreasing initially due to internal stresses and relaxation effects, and increasing at higher strains due to grain boundary-induced anharmonicity. These findings highlight the complex interplay between defects, atomic-scale disorder, and nanostructure in governing the electrical and thermal properties of severely deformed high-entropy alloys via electron and phonon scattering.

title: Interpretable machine learning for seasonal nitrate and total phosphorus concentrations integrating hydrologic, land-use, and ecological indicators.
abstract: Diffuse nutrient pollution remains difficult to assess because nutrient concentrations reflect interacting watershed, hydrochemical, ecological, and hydrologic conditions that vary across space and time. Although machine-learning models incorporate multiple environmental predictors, the contribution of different predictor domains can be difficult to distinguish when all variables are evaluated simultaneously. This study developed an interpretable machine-learning framework to predict seasonal nitrate and total phosphorus concentrations across seven watersheds in southeastern Pennsylvania using observations from 2002 to 2024. Physicochemical, land-cover, ecological, climatic, and hydrologic information were progressively integrated through four predictor scenarios, allowing the added predictive value of each domain to be evaluated. Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models were independently optimized for each scenario. Predictive performance improved as broader environmental information was incorporated, with the largest gain occurring after land-cover variables were added to the physicochemical baseline. The environmental-only M4 XGBoost models achieved test R2 values of 0.858 for nitrate and 0.770 for total phosphorus, with RMSE values of 0.624 and 0.170 mg L-1, respectively. Repeated site-stratified validation of the nitrate M4 model yielded a mean test R2 of 0.834 ± 0.026, indicating stable performance across alternative partitions. SHapley Additive exPlanations identified forest cover, developed land cover, and specific conductance as dominant predictors for both nutrients, while discharge contributed more strongly to nitrate and dissolved oxygen to total phosphorus prediction. These reveal that land-cover composition offers significant prognostic insights beyond in-stream conditions, whereas hydrochemical and hydrologic factors aid in differentiating nutrient-specific trends. The framework could guide the prioritizing of watershed monitoring and the evaluation of nutrient dynamics.

title: Checkpoint Inhibition during primary hepatitis E virus infection alters memory development of virus-specific T-cells in humans.
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS HEV infection is an underappreciated differential diagnosis in patients presenting with acute hepatitis during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. As T-cells are the key targets of ICIs, particularly through blockade of inhibitory immune checkpoints such as PD-1, this intervention is likely to influence the dynamics and differentiation fate of de novo primed virus-specific T-cells during primary HEV infection. We therefore aimed to examine how PD-1 blockade during primary HEV-infection influences expansion, contraction, and memory formation of virus-specific CD8+ T-cells. METHODS HEV-specific CD8 and CD4+ T-cells were analyzed by applying a reverse phenotyping approach combined with single-cell transcriptomics and TCR sequencing, as well as multiparameter flow cytometry with MHC class I tetramers. We characterized HEV-specific T-cell responses in patients receiving ICI and in untreated patients during acute-viremic infection and after viral clearance. RESULTS Under ICI, de novo primed HEV-specific CD8+ T-cells showed enhanced clonal expansion, cytotoxicity, and terminal differentiation. Rather than transitioning into classical memory subsets, these cells retained a cytotoxic transcriptional program and acquired features of long-lived effector-like T-cells (LLEC). While HEV-specific T-cells remained detectable over > 2 years, their functional recall responsiveness declined in ICI-treated patients. CONCLUSIONS Collectively, our findings demonstrate that PD-1 blockade during the formation of a primary immune response reshapes the fate of the antiviral CD8+ T-cell pool, favoring terminally differentiated effector states over conventional memory formation, with potential implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies. LAY SUMMARY Our study represents the first demonstration in a human model that PD-1 blockade during primary antigen exposure reshapes antiviral CD8+ T-cell effector formation and memory differentiation. By identifying PD-1 signaling during a primary immune response as a regulator of antiviral CD8+ T-cell fate, our findings establish a conceptual framework for understanding how immune checkpoint blockade influences the development of primary antiviral T-cell responses, with implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies.

DNNGP-Pro: A multi-omics data integration platform for predictive modeling of complex traits and crop hybrid breeding.
abstract: Accurate prediction of complex agronomic traits poses a long-standing challenge for hybrid crop breeding, which may be resolved by integrating multi-omics data with shared-parent relationship information among hybrids. To accelerate variety development, we constructed the DNNGP-Pro platform for predictive modeling of complex hybrid traits in large-scale populations. In preliminary steps, the pipeline extracts local features from omics data via convolutional neural networks, then employs graph convolutional networks to integrate these single-omics features with hybrid shared-parent graph (HSPG), and captures long-range dependencies across multi-omics features using a Transformer module. Exhibiting comparable performance to DNNGP model on single-omics data, incorporating the HSPG with individual genomic (G), metabolomic (M), or transcriptomic (T) datasets respectively improved prediction accuracy by 2.98%, 5.54%, and 4.75%, for 13 traits across four hybrid populations. Dual-omics models (MT, GT, or GM) demonstrated 5.33%-9.23% higher accuracy than single-omics models across 10 traits, whereas the incorporating all three omics data (GMT) with the HSPG enhanced accuracy by 2.95%, 1.71%, and 4.39%, respectively. To demonstrate DNNGP-Pro application for breeding high-yield rice varieties, we conducted trait prediction in the Rice26040 population, training on 1,040 screened hybrids and validating predicted candidates through multi-location trials. The model identified the superior indica hybrid, Chunliangyou825, within this massive candidate pool, which demonstrated 23.62% and 8.01% increases in grain yield in Hangzhou, and 7.70% and 16.15% higher yields in Pingxiang, over control varieties Tianyouhuazhan and Fengliangyou4, respectively, which we verified through regional testing and submitted for variety certification. The present study demonstrates the prediction power and analytical versatility of DNNGP-Pro in accelerating hybrid development through large-scale complex trait prediction from multi-omics data and shared-parent relationship information among hybrids.

Landscape genetics reveals the role of watercourses in driving gene flow in Chioglossa lusitanica
abstract: Riparian ecosystems are increasingly affected by human activities that alter habitats and reduce landscape connectivity. Riparian amphibians are particularly vulnerable because they depend on both aquatic and terrestrial environments. In this study, we examined how landscape features influence genetic connectivity in Chioglossa lusitanica, an endemic stream salamander from the western Iberian Peninsula, using a high-resolution watershed-scale landscape genetic approach in the Ceira River basin. Microsatellite data from 248 individuals sampled at 88 sites were analysed to evaluate isolation-by-distance and isolation-by-resistance models incorporating environmental, geographical, and topographic variables. Genetic analyses identified two main genetic clusters with extensive admixture in the Lousã Mountains, revealing fine-scale genetic structuring within a single drainage system. Patterns of genetic differentiation were strongly associated with the river network, indicating that watercourses play a key role in maintaining connectivity across the watershed. However, the observed genetic structure likely reflects the combined influence of contemporary connectivity and historical population processes. Lowland areas were associated with increased landscape resistance, consistent with reduced habitat suitability in human-modified landscapes. These findings highlight the importance of riparian landscapes for population connectivity and suggest that conservation efforts should prioritize the maintenance and restoration of riparian corridors, particularly in mountainous regions, to support long-term persistence of C. lusitanica and other riparian-dependent species.

title: Model-Based Low-Order Wavefront Sensing and Control with a Fully Physical Digital Twin on MagAO-X
abstract: Context. Residual low-order aberrations and post-AO tip-tilt jitter are major drivers of stellar leakage in small-inner-working-angle coronagraphs and limit high-contrast imaging performance. Aims. The aim of this work is to develop a fully physical and differentiable digital twin for the focal plane low-order wavefront sensor on MagAO-X. This digital twin can be used to provide accurate non-linear and fast linearised wavefront sensing and control to deal with low-order aberrations. Methods. We build a physics-based optical model of the focal plane low order wavefront sensor (FLOWFS) system and calibrate it using laboratory and on-sky measurements. The calibrated model is used for non-linear phase retrieval, deriving a model-based linear reconstructor, and generating the corresponding reference image for real-time control. Results. The calibrated digital twin accurately reproduces the sensor response and recovers the dominant low-order aberrations. In the laboratory, non-linear reconstruction achieves residual floors of about 6 to 7 nm over the pupil, compared with about 11 nm for the linear reconstructor, and the same digital-twin framework transfers across different coronagraph and wavelength configurations. On-sky, the model can be recalibrated with limited changes, achieves reconstruction performance close to the residual atmospheric floor, and provides a linear reconstructor that enables stable closed-loop low-order control at kHz speed. Conclusions. A fully physical digital twin can unify accurate low-order wavefront reconstruction, fast linearised control, and transfer across observing configurations and from lab to on-sky operation within a single interpretable framework.

title: Clinical Factors Associated with Progression-Free Survival after Radioiodine Therapy for Pulmonary Metastases from Follicular Cell-Derived Thyroid Carcinoma: A Japanese Single-Center Study
abstract: Objectives This retrospective study aimed to identify clinical factors associated with progression-free survival (PFS) after radioiodine therapy (RAI) in Japanese patients with differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) and pulmonary metastases. Materials and Methods We included 74 patients with DTC and pulmonary metastases who underwent RAI at our institution between 2015 and 2023. Baseline clinicopathological, laboratory, and imaging variables at the initial RAI for pulmonary metastases were evaluated. Statistical Analysis PFS and overall survival (OS) were estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method. Because 27 PFS events were observed, associations with PFS were evaluated using Firth's penalized Cox regression. The primary multivariable model included the maximum pulmonary metastasis diameter, iodine-131 avidity, and extrapulmonary distant metastases. Results The cohort included 64 patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma, 7 with follicular thyroid carcinoma, and 3 with poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma. During a median follow-up of 21.1 months, 27 patients experienced disease progression or death, and 10 died. The median PFS and OS were 46.3 and 76.0 months, respectively. In the primary multivariable model, a larger maximum pulmonary metastasis diameter (hazard ratio [HR] per 10-mm increase, 1.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.20–2.73; p = 0.006) and absence of iodine-131 uptake (HR, 6.15; 95% CI, 1.73–37.55; p = 0.003) were associated with poorer PFS. The association between extrapulmonary distant metastases and PFS was not statistically significant in this model. Conclusion Larger pulmonary metastases and absence of iodine-131 uptake were associated with poorer PFS after RAI. These findings require cautious interpretation and validation in larger independent cohorts.

title: Study on the Dynamic Response Characteristics and the Damage Constitutive Model of Magnetite Based on the Energy Dissipation Method
abstract: In underground metal mining operations, pillars are often subjected to dynamic loads induced by blasting. To investigate the response characteristics of pillar rock mass under dynamic loading conditions and to propose a damage constitutive model based on energy dissipation to describe the mechanical behavior of magnetite, dynamic triaxial tests were first conducted on magnetite, and its energy evolution characteristics were analyzed. Subsequently, a damage variable based on energy dissipation was introduced, and a modification factor was proposed based on energy evolution parameters, thereby developing a new damage constitutive model. Finally, the fitting results of the proposed model were compared with those of the conventional damage constitutive model based on the Weibull distribution and with the experimental data. The results indicate that the energy evolution characteristics of magnetite during the loading process are closely related to the loading method, the loading process, and the development of damage. Energy evolution indicators, such as the proportion of elastic energy, can be used to quantitatively characterize and distinguish the elastoplastic evolution process of rock during loading. It is feasible to employ energy evolution indicators as modification factors for the damage constitutive model, and they possess clear physical significance, thus outperforming modification factors derived from statistical approaches. The proposed damage constitutive model accurately describes the response characteristics of rock under dynamic loading conditions and it performs particularly well in capturing the yielding and residual characteristics of the rock.

title: Impact of Subway Passenger Flow–Built Environment Interaction on Road Congestion around Subway Stations Using Machine-Learning Models
abstract: To alleviate urban traffic congestion, metro systems have become critical urban transportation infrastructure. While effectively relieving pressure on long-distance commutes, the areas surrounding metro stations often emerge as congestion-sensitive zones due to the transient aggregation of feeder traffic and the high-density land use patterns concentrated there. This study focuses on road networks within a 500 m radius of stations along six metro lines in Kunming, China. It integrates four categories of multisource heterogeneous data: metro smart card transactions; point of interest (POI) data; meteorological data; and the Amap Road Congestion Index. Employing an innovative integrated modeling framework combining light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) interpretability analysis, this research dissects the complex interactive relationships underlying traffic congestion around metro stations. The research results indicate that the LightGBM model can effectively identify road traffic congestion conditions around metro stations, and SHAP can effectively analyze the nonlinear relationship of the interaction between metro passenger outflow and POI facility density on road traffic congestion around metro stations. The study found that, when the density of pedestrian facilities exceeds 60 / km 2 , as the density of pedestrian facilities increases, its impact on road traffic congestion becomes positive, with an effect value above 0. When the density of government institutions exceeds 120 / km 2 and passenger outflow is greater than 120 people/10 min, the interaction between the two further exacerbates road traffic congestion. When company density is around 50 / km 2 , the SHAP value spikes sharply, reaching a maximum exceeding 0.6, indicating that, in areas with moderate company density but extremely high passenger flow, the interaction between the two generates a substantial positive predictive driving force for traffic congestion. When the density of business residential areas is low, it exerts an inhibitory effect on road traffic congestion; however, as its value increases, this inhibitory effect weakens and gradually transitions to a positive contribution. Further, regarding whether it is a peak period, the influence of off-peak periods on road traffic is compactly clustered around zero; however, once entering a peak period, the feature contribution exhibits a stepwise increase. These findings enhance the understanding of the causes of traffic congestion near urban metro stations, providing a robust empirical basis for optimizing functional zoning around stations, implementing differentiated facility allocation, and enabling precise traffic control strategies.
journal: Journal of Transportation Engineering, Part A: Systems

title: Mapping Coastal Resource–Environment Carrying Capacity in an Intensively Developed Coastal Area: Evidence from Rui’an, China
abstract: Coastal zones are dynamic land–sea interfaces where development pressures often approach ecological and environmental limits. Here, we operationalize a pressure–condition–response (P–C–R) framework to deliver a customized, high-resolution ( 30 × 30 m ) assessment of coastal resource–environment carrying capacity (RECC) for Rui’an (Zhejiang, China) using 2017 multisource geospatial, environmental, socioeconomic, and planning data sets. GIS-based spatial overlay and index modeling produce a composite coastal carrying capacity index (CAI) that ranges from 0.5 to 2.1, revealing strong spatial heterogeneity and a persistent “higher pressure north of the Feiyun River–lower pressure south of the river” pattern. Overload hotspots occupy ∼ 10 % of the coastal zone and cluster along the northern urban shoreline belt, whereas near-saturation dominates ( ∼ 78 % ), indicating widespread proximity to threshold conditions where incremental disturbances could shift local areas into overload. The cooccurrence of high pressure and constrained condition aligns with carrying risk concentrated where intensive human use coincides with limited buffering capacity; intensive land reclamation and shoreline artificialization are prominent contributors associated with this pattern. These outputs provide zoning-ready evidence to support differentiated governance pathways, including constraining additional development intensity and reducing loads in overloaded areas, institutionalizing capacity assessment index (CAI)-based early warning and adaptive controls across near-saturation belts, and maintaining ecological bottom lines in undercapacity areas.
journal: Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management

title: The sound of persuasion: Using generative AI to identify gender gaps in political influence.
abstract: Women often experience a deficit in persuasive influence, particularly in contexts like politics, where expectations about women's behavior may conflict with gendered expectations about the domain and role. In spite of this widespread pattern, the mechanisms behind the gender gap in persuasion are difficult to isolate and test in dynamic political conversations. Women may be less persuasive simply because role-based expectations prompt others to afford women less authority when speaking about politics generally or about some political topics. Alternatively, women may be less persuasive because they tend to use linguistic patterns or rhetorical strategies that are less effective. Using an original AI-based approach, we put 4,300 human subjects into realistic, real-time phone conversations with an AI agent. These agents were randomly assigned either a masculine or feminine gendered conversation topic and a male- or female-sounding voice, allowing us to manipulate topic and perceptions of speakers' gender while holding constant other elements of rhetorical content and strategy. After validating the experimental treatments, we find no direct effects of perceived gender of the AI agent, as cued by voice. However, gender affects other important aspects of the persuasive interaction. Research subjects were more likely to be persuaded about the masculine topic (defense spending) than the feminine topic (aid to the poor). Additionally, women research subjects were, on average, more persuaded than men. To the extent that men and women emphasize different topics in political conversations and have different discussion partners, these dynamics are likely to shape women's political persuasive influence.
