title: Reassessing the link between stomatal anatomy and conductance across operating states: implications for crop water use and modelling

authors.name: Yazen Al-Salman
authors.affiliation: Centre for Crop Systems Analysis, Wageningen University & Research , P.O Box 430, 6700 AK, Wageningen ,

abstract: Background Intrinsic leaf water use efficiency (iWUE), defined as a single point ratio of photosynthesis (An) to stomatal conductance (gs), is a key target trait for improving crop productivity without increasing water use. However, a single An/gs measurement does not fully describe how leaves regulate carbon gain and water loss across changing environmental states. Because stomatal anatomy influences gs, variation in stomatal density (SD), size (SS) and pore geometry may help explain differences in stomatal behaviour and water-use strategy among genotypes. Scope I develop a quantitative framework in which stomatal anatomy defines the operating space within which physiological regulation determines realised gs. I use stomatal allometry to examine how contrasting stomatal SD-SS configurations govern the range and responsiveness of gs, and couple these responses to C3 and C4 photosynthesis models to show how these constraints interact with physiological regulation to shape water-use strategy across operating states. Published datasets are used to assess whether observed anatomical and gas-exchange relationships are consistent with the framework. Finally, I examine how anatomy-informed differences in stomatal response could be represented in crop models through sensitivity coefficients and anatomically derived gs limits. Conclusions Stomatal anatomy does not determine stomatal behaviour, but constrains the gs space within which that behaviour occurs. Different SD-SS configurations can therefore generate distinct gs vs An trajectories across operating states, while photosynthetic pathway, aperture regulation and other physiological processes determine where leaves operate within that space. The compiled crop data show partial consistency with these expectations but also highlight regulatory and biochemical compensation that cannot be inferred from anatomy alone. Viewing stomatal anatomy as a partial contributor to water-use strategy provides a more mechanistic basis for interpreting variation in iWUE and for constraining stomatal-response parameterisations in crop models.

title: DeepFlav: an integrated resource and computational platform for flavonoid biosynthesis gene analysis
abstract: Flavonoid metabolism determines fruit coloration, nutritional quality, and stress adaptation in horticultural crops, making identification of biosynthetic components essential for synthetic biology and precision breeding. However, sequence-homology-based annotation methods remain prone to missed and incorrect annotations, particularly for modifying enzymes with low sequence similarity. To address this limitation, we developed DeepFlav ( https://cbi.gxu.edu.cn/KPGF/html/), a comprehensive resource and integrated computational platform for flavonoid biosynthesis gene analysis. DeepFlav integrates high-quality genome and proteome data from 1,031 plant species and annotated records for 630,951 genes encoding enzymes associated with flavonoid biosynthesis. Systematic analysis reveals a hierarchical evolutionary pattern in flavonoid pathways, with broadly conserved core enzymes and continuously expanding modifying enzymes. Differences among plant lineages are reflected in both the number of related genes and branch-specific pathway reconfiguration. Unlike conventional databases, DeepFlav does not rely solely on homology searches but implements an prediction framework based on the ESM-2 protein language model, AlphaFold-based three-dimensional structure modeling, and initial docking screening with AutoDock Vina. This design establishes an integrated annotation paradigm connecting sequence, structure, and function. The platform also reconstructs an interactive flavonoid metabolic network through literature mining. Using DeepFlav, we identified candidate genes with low sequence similarity to known flavonoid tailoring enzymes but high prediction confidence. In vitro validation of three candidate glycosyltransferases by LC-MS/MS confirmed their catalytic activity, demonstrating the reliability of DeepFlav for discovering low-homology flavonoid glycosyltransferases. DeepFlav provides a systematic resource and scalable framework for investigating plant flavonoid metabolism evolution, discovering functional modifying enzymes, and developing high-value natural products through synthetic biology.

title: Lipid evolution in early land plants: from structural barriers to signaling networks.
abstract: Lipid metabolism played a pivotal role in enabling the transition of plants from aquatic to terrestrial environments. Early land plants evolved complex lipid networks that supported the formation of protective surface barriers, membrane remodeling, energy storage, and lipid-mediated signaling in response to desiccation, ultraviolet radiation, and nutrient limitation. This review integrates biochemical, genetic, and evolutionary insights to trace how these lipid pathways diversified across plant lineages and laid the foundation for the structural and physiological complexity of modern plants. By examining three interconnected themes involving the formation of cuticular and membrane lipids, metabolic remodeling under stress, and the emergence of signaling and trafficking systems, we highlight how early lipid features and pathways underpinned terrestrial adaptation. Special attention is given to bryophytes as model systems that bridge ancestral and derived traits, offering mechanistic and evolutionary insight into lipid functions that continue to shape plant-environment interactions. Advances in lipidomics and genetic tools now make it possible to resolve these networks in greater mechanistic detail, opening new directions for understanding plant evolution and harnessing ancient lipid traits for sustainable agriculture and biotechnology.

title: Chronic high-fat diet disrupts the homeostatic and differentiation potential of megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitors.
abstract: Chronic obesity induced by a high-fat diet (HFD) profoundly alters systemic metabolism; however, its impact on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) lineage commitment, particularly erythroid differentiation, remains poorly understood. To address this question, C57BL/6 mice were fed an HFD for 16 weeks to establish an obesity model. HFD induced significant weight gain, hyperlipidemia, and increased bone marrow adiposity, accompanied by a marked elevation in total bone marrow cellularity. Peripheral blood analysis revealed increased white blood cell counts, together with elevated red blood cell counts and hemoglobin levels despite reduced circulating reticulocytes. Flow cytometric analysis further demonstrated a significant expansion of HSPCs and downstream progenitor populations in the bone marrow. However, despite this progenitor expansion, megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitors (MEPs) from HFD-fed mice exhibited impaired colony-forming capacity and reduced erythroid output, indicating compromised erythroid differentiation potential. Consistently, HFD markedly promoted splenic extramedullary hematopoiesis. Although HFD increased HSPC abundance, competitive transplantation assays revealed no improvement in long-term hematopoietic reconstitution capacity. Mechanistically, transcriptomic analysis revealed dysregulation of erythroid regulatory networks in MEPs, characterized by reduced expression of the lineage regulators Fli1 and Gata2, accompanied by altered expression of erythroid-associated transcriptional programs. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that HFD-induced obesity disrupts hematopoietic homeostasis by expanding HSPC pools while suppressing erythropoiesis through MEP dysfunction and transcriptional remodeling.

title: Supporting SDG4 through immersive learning technologies design: a self-directed learning approach in higher education
abstract: This study aims to examine the redesign of a traditional higher education course using principles of self-determination theory and self-directed learning (SDL). The course integrates immersive learning technologies (ILT) within a flipped classroom model to promote learner autonomy, competence and digital competence aligned with SDG 4. This study adopts an action research approach. The study collects quantitative data through student questionnaires and applies partial least squares structural equation modelling to examine the relationships among perceived teacher autonomy support (PTAS), self-determination factors, SDL and learning outcomes. The study also analyses qualitative data from classroom observations and semi-structured interviews using thematic analysis to provide contextualised insights into students’ learning experiences and digital competence development. Students reported high levels of learning autonomy, while PTAS was positively associated with autonomy and relatedness. Competence was the only psychological need significantly associated with SDL, which was positively associated with students’ satisfaction, perceived learning outcomes and digital competence. Students with higher competence and greater proactivity reported more positive learning experiences, whereas less proactive learners required substantial guidance to meet learning expectations. The findings highlight the importance of supporting students’ competence when designing autonomous, technology-enhanced learning environments. Higher education courses integrating ILT should provide differentiated scaffolding to help less proactive or lower-performing learners participate more successfully. The study offers insights for institutions seeking to strengthen digital competence and advance SDG 4 implementation through curriculum innovation. This study offers context-specific empirical insights into how integrating ILT within a flipped, autonomy-supportive curriculum may support SDL and digital competence development. Its principal contribution is to identify competence as a possible enabling condition through which students can translate autonomy into effective SDL in technically demanding ILT design tasks.
journal: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education

title: Transformational leadership, psychological safety, and work engagement in family businesses: the indirect roles of resilience and job satisfaction
abstract: This study examines how transformational leadership is associated with work engagement in family businesses through interconnected relational, personal and attitudinal pathways involving psychological safety, resilience and job satisfaction, while also assessing the complete sequential indirect association among these constructs. Data were collected from 800 employees working in Portuguese family businesses and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement and structural models, direct and indirect associations, predictive performance and potential endogeneity were assessed. Transformational leadership was positively associated with psychological safety and work engagement. Psychological safety was positively associated with resilience, job satisfaction and work engagement, while resilience was positively associated with job satisfaction and work engagement. Job satisfaction was also positively associated with work engagement. Furthermore, several statistically significant indirect associations linked transformational leadership with work engagement through psychological safety, resilience and job satisfaction. The complete sequential indirect association was statistically significant but very small in magnitude (ß = 0.005), indicating that the findings are better characterised by multiple interconnected pathways, with the complete sequential indirect association representing only one component of this broader pattern. Family businesses may support employee engagement by attending to transformational leadership, psychological safety, resilience and employees' evaluations of their jobs. These implications should not be interpreted as evidence of causal intervention effects. The study extends family-business research beyond the established transformational leadership–psychological safety–engagement relationship by integrating relational, personal and attitudinal components within a broader pattern of direct and indirect associations. In doing so, it applies Conservation of Resources theory to provide a more differentiated explanation of employee engagement in family businesses.

title: Caring in rural territories: trajectory of self-care decline and hybrid care regimes in rural Russian aging
abstract: This study aims to analyze how care for older people is organized in rural Northwest Russia, tracing the trajectory of self-care decline and the emergence of hybrid care regimes that combine self-care, family, substitute and professional support. It seeks to identify which actors and interactions shape models of care in these contexts and how these models are transformed under conditions of infrastructural scarcity and a “crisis of care.” The research is based on qualitative analysis of 51 interviews with older adults, 13 interviews with social workers and paramedics and 12 interviews with caregivers in remote villages across three Russian regions. Data collection was complemented by thick descriptions of nine villages, including housing and local infrastructure, and interviews were thematically coded, with the aid of an AI tool, to construct visual care matrices that map the “mix” of agents and practices in different cases. The analysis reveals four interrelated care models: “Self-care,” “Family care,” “Substitute care” and “Professional care,” which combine into layered hybrid regimes over the life course. As health and mobility decline and infrastructural barriers intensify, the space of self-care contracts from village and yard to house and body, while family, neighbors and local professionals (social workers and paramedics) successively take on care functions, often extending their roles beyond formal job descriptions and engaging in reciprocal exchanges with older adults. The identified trajectory of gradual self-care decline highlights how infrastructural deficits, migration and changing family roles reconfigure care responsibilities and push rural households toward hybrid combinations of formal and informal support. These findings suggest the need for social policies that recognize and bolster hybrid rural care regimes by integrating long-term care services with support for family caregivers, neighborhood initiatives and community-based “substitute” care arrangements.

title: Contactless Estimation of Respiratory Frequency Using 3D-CNN on Thermal Images
abstract: Monitoring physiological parameters such as respiratory rate ($f_R$) is essential for diagnosing and managing various pathological conditions. Thermal imaging offers a promising contactless alternative to traditional methods, which often rely on partially invasive sensors or obtrusive wearable systems. However, existing approaches for $f_R$ estimation from thermal signals typically require extensive pre-processing and manual or semi-automatic region-of-interest (ROI) tracking, limiting their practical applicability. This study proposes a deep learning-based method for estimating $f_R$ directly from thermal videos, eliminating the need for complex pre-processing and ROI tracking. A 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) is developed to operate on raw thermal video data. To address challenges related to small datasets, the model is trained using data augmentation and transfer learning from synthetic datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a validation $R^2$ score of approximately 0.61 on both pre-processed and raw thermal videos. By simplifying the workflow, this method holds promise for enhancing the feasibility of thermal imaging in real-world applications, such as remote healthcare and driver monitoring in automotive applications.

title: Deep Clustering of fMRI with Global-Local Feature Extraction for Functional Brain Activity Analysis.
Instantaneous-Value Modeling of DC–DC Converters: From Switched System Models to Smooth Continuous-Time Models
abstract: Switched system models of DC–DC converters cannot be directly analyzed or controlled using conventional continuous-time system theory. To address the problem, we propose a smoothing-based modeling approach in which sigmoid functions are employed based on a generalized switched-system formulation. First, logical variables are defined to represent the mode-switching conditions of the converter, enabling the construction of a logical switched dynamical model. Next, smooth and continuous sigmoid functions are introduced to approximate these logical variables. This approach was used to develop smooth continuous-time models for single-ended primary-inductor, Zeta, Cuk, and interleaved parallel DC–DC converters. Simulation and experimental results of single-ended primary-inductor converter and interleaved parallel buck converter reveal that the proposed models accurately capture the instantaneous behavior of the converters. This modeling method provides a unified framework for representing multimodal switching behavior and various circuit phenomena across different operating modes, thereby improving the accuracy, applicability, and generality of converter models. The proposed smooth and differentiable model was used for stability and dynamic analysis, providing guidance for parameter selection and the development of more effective control strategies to optimize the system operating performance.

title: Integrating Landscape Genomics and Ecological Niche Modeling to Characterize Climate-Associated Copy Number Variation and Future Climatic Suitability in Sheep (Ovis aries) From the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau.
abstract: Livestock, including sheep, are central to global food systems and rural livelihoods, yet their productivity is increasingly threatened by climate change. Characterizing genetic variation associated with local climatic conditions and evaluating changes in climatic suitability under future climate scenarios may support sustainable management. Here, we integrated copy number variation (CNV) data from whole-genome resequencing of 121 wild and domestic sheep with environmental variables to characterize CNV patterns, population structure, and genetic signals potentially associated with climatic variation. Ecological niche modeling was used to project potential shifts in climatically suitable areas under future climate scenarios. A total of 24 026 CNVs were identified, and population-specific copy number variation regions (CNVRs) were generally more numerous in wild than in domestic populations. Population structure analyses showed clear genetic differentiation between wild and domestic groups. Genes overlapping CNVRs in wild sheep were mainly enriched in functions related to metabolic homeostasis and cellular transport, whereas those in domestic sheep were mainly annotated to energy metabolism and circulatory regulation. Genotype-environment association (GEA) analyses identified 38 candidate genes associated with climatic variables. Among them, PIK3C2G and TACR1 were detected by both GEA and VST-based population differentiation analyses. Ecological niche modeling indicated heterogeneous future climatic suitability patterns among plateau sheep populations. Kazakh sheep, Oula sheep, Minxian Black Fur sheep, Gansu Alpine Merino, and Mongolian sheep were projected to show net reductions in climatically suitable areas, whereas Lanzhou Large-Tailed sheep, Tan sheep, Tianhua Mutton sheep, and Tibetan sheep showed projected increases or temporally dynamic changes. Together, our study provides candidate genomic and climatic evidence for population differentiation, environment-associated genetic variation, and population-specific climatic responses in plateau sheep.

title: Differentiating between cognitive impairment and patient non-adherence: the utility of Hospital-in-the-Home for optimisation of diabetes mellitus care.
A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress
abstract: Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to–central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transforms early-life stress into female-specific vulnerability to chronic pain and anxiety-like avoidance.

title: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects
abstract: Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.

title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
abstract: Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. With a few qubits, we illustrate quantum contextuality with the magic square game and quantify it through a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality violation. To examine many-body contextuality, we implement the N -player Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger game and separately solve a two-dimensional hidden linear function problem, advancing the state of the art on fidelity and system size in both tasks. Our work introduces benchmarking of quantum processors using contextuality-based algorithms.

title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation
abstract: Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron–containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose balance controls mitochondrial function and, when perturbed, leads to neurological diseases.

title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
abstract: Turbulence is chaotic, yet its fluctuations follow a structured, nonequilibrium energy cascade unconstrained by the equilibrium theorems that limit passive energy extraction from molecular gases. Here, we introduce turbulence shelters: hollow shells with a single aperture that filter eddies by scale, sustaining gradients in fluctuation intensity that drive directional particle transport despite zero mean fluid flux. Across three orders of magnitude in size, shelters establish particle concentration contrasts between their interior and the surrounding flow, with selectivity controlled by particle geometry, inertia, thermal fluctuations, and electrostatic forces. At the microscale, shelters discriminate particles differing by tens of nanometers independently of material composition. These results establish a design principle for selective filtration: Geometry that compartmentalizes turbulent fluctuations can harness ambient eddies to direct particle transport.

title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
abstract: Wernicke’s area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke’s area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke’s area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces
abstract: Ultrasound imaging relies on soft interfaces that transmit sound efficiently between a device and the body. Conventional gel couplants provide low acoustic loss but contain mobile liquid phases that can dry, flow, or leach during extended use. By contrast, mobile phase–free elastomers are more stable but generally attenuate megahertz ultrasound strongly, limiting their use as couplants. We report an interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer molecularly designed to overcome this trade-off. A densely grafted backbone lowers the shear modulus without increasing shear loss, whereas well-packed sidechains reduce bulk compressibility, jointly suppressing acoustic attenuation in a soft elastomer. The resulting elastomer combines soft tissue–like mechanics with low-loss acoustics, providing a durable couplant for soft ultrasonic interfaces.

title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year −1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year −1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year −1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

title: Angular momentum transfer from an optical vortex to an atomic rotor
abstract: Light carries angular momentum in two forms: spin, associated with polarization, and orbital, associated with helical wavefronts. Whereas spin angular momentum underlies well-known atomic selection rules, the role of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in light-matter interaction continues to be discussed in the literature. In this work, we investigate OAM transfer from a vortex laser beam to a trapped-ion quantum rotor using rotational sidebands of the electric quadrupole transition of 40 Ca + . We directly observe coherent transfer of optical OAM into quantized rotation and identify distinct selection rules for different rotational sidebands. This observation provides experimental evidence for a scale-dependent separation of angular momentum transfer pathways in light-matter interactions. Further, our work elucidates the previously reported modified selection rules in trapped-ion experiments, establishing a unified framework for twisted light–matter interactions.

title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells
abstract: The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours of maximum power point operation at 85°C and 98% after 5000 hours of dynamically varying light-intensity day-night cycling.

title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists
abstract: The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo–electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor’s ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanisms for protein and small-molecule agonists of RXFP1.

title: Quaternary carbon–guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles
abstract: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

title: Meso–microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels
abstract: Aluminosilicate zeolites offer exceptional size and shape selectivity but suffer from diffusion limitations imposed by subnanometer micropores. Intrinsically meso–microporous zeolites integrate mesopores with micropores to create interconnected pathways that accelerate diffusion while preserving selectivity, yet their synthesis remains challenging. In this study, we report NJU120-5 and NJU120-7, intrinsically meso–microporous aluminosilicates that integrate micropores with mesopores enclosed by two-T-atom-thick walls containing 10-ring channels, forming a fully interconnected three-dimensional pore network. Their plausible framework models were established on the basis of advanced electron ptychographic imaging, revealing representative quasi-rectangular mesopores in calcined NJU120-5 with a uniform width of ~12 angstroms and lengths from 41 to 162 angstroms. Both materials exhibit high porosity, strong Brønsted acidity, and enhanced performance in heavy-oil cracking, delivering high yields of valuable fuels with suppressed coke formation.

title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling
abstract: Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved with specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sampling. In this study, we introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach uses light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical reactions relevant to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, including photochemical and electrochemical systems, providing access to reaction kinetics under native operating conditions with subsecond temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, and mechanistic investigation and will accelerate data-driven reaction discovery. By embedding analytical functionality directly within reaction vessels, reaction telemetry establishes a general framework for information-rich observation of chemical processes across research, development, and education.

title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme
abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((k cat /K M )/k w ) of up to 3 x 10 13 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

title: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules
abstract: Reliable, strong, and low-loss interfaces are needed for durable perovskite photovoltaics. We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. This device architecture achieves a power conversion efficiency of 22.7% for 900–square centimeter (cm 2 ) submodules (aperture area: 655 cm 2 ) and 21.3% for 7200-cm 2 standard modules (aperture area: 6380 cm 2 ). The champion 7200-cm 2 standard module maintained consistent performance during 105 days of outdoor testing, as independently measured by the Photovoltaic Accelerator for Commercializing Technologies (PACT) center.

title: The scientific record is never finished
abstract: The scholarly scientific record has always been a work in progress. From the earliest days of scientific publishing, new findings would come along that changed the way earlier findings are understood. When research journals were published only in print, occasional errors would be reported by the authors or found by others, and papers would be retracted or corrected. When publishing became digital, many more people could quickly access and scrutinize data and images for accuracy. Now, in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), it is possible for machines to do these examinations more expeditiously and at a larger scale. All of this has added an important new layer to the publishing process and put more responsibility on authors, who must update their work if new issues arise. In response to this need, Science is improving the ways in which it will flag and notate papers that require adjustment or where changes are under consideration. Our Editorial Policies now reflect these updates.

title: Toward a Science of AI Agent Societies
abstract: AI agents are rapidly evolving from isolated personal assistants into networked actors that interact with one another at scale. We envision the emergence of AI agent societies, with their own social and economic dynamics, as a new research frontier. We argue that AI agent societies should be studied as a distinct object of inquiry: neither simply larger collections of individual agents nor merely simulations of human society. To formalize this perspective, we propose four core properties that a valid AI agent society should satisfy: individualized objectives, rules and governance, autonomy, and scale and complexity. Building on this framework, we identify four classes of societal behaviors worth studying in AI agent societies: economic behaviors, behaviors under conflict-of-interest, unsafe and unethical behaviors, and system-level behaviors. We then outline key technical challenges--including property parameterization, parameter balancing, and robust implementation--and argue that progress on these challenges could enable scientifically informative and practically useful models of AI agent societies. Finally, we revisit existing multi-agent systems through the lens of the proposed core properties, show that they instantiate only subsets of them, and discuss implications for platform design, evaluation, and governance.

title: Planet Falconia: Mission Possible Using Immersive Visualization to enable Digital Twin of Remote Sensing Data
abstract: Planet Falconia: Mission Possible is a months-long project for 10th graders in the Science, Mathematics, and Computer Science magnet program at Poolesville High School, in which students design and build remotely operated rovers, analyze simulated remote sensing data, and explore a physical model of a fictional exoplanet through immersive 3D visualization. Students progress from hands-on data collection to processing data in ParaView and to virtual reality walkthroughs of a LiDAR scan of the model, enabled by NIST’s Immersive ParaView. A ceiling-mounted Raspberry Pi camera tracks live rover positions and overlays them on the 3D terrain in near real time, bridging physical rover navigation and virtual planetary exploration.
journal: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Educator's Forum

title: Grounding Gaussian Splatting Geometry with Stochastic Solids
abstract: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) excels in novel view synthesis, extracting high-fidelity surfaces remains challenging. Standard 3DGS updates transmittance discretely through primitive-wise alpha compositing, leading to jagged depth profiles and weak multi-view consistency. We address this by reinterpreting 3DGS through the lens of stochastic geometry. To compute continuous depth, we model each Gaussian as a continuous stochastic opaque solid. Leveraging the ‘Objects as Volumes’ formalism, we show that a single Gaussian under the splatting formulation admits a unique continuous occupancy function whose volumetric rendering matches the original splat. This formulation transforms the step-wise transmittance into a smooth, differentiable curve. Using the volumetric nature of stochastic geometry, our method efficiently renders high-quality depth maps for fine-grained geometry extraction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art surface reconstruction accuracy and smoothness among 3DGS methods, without compromising optimization efficiency. Code: https://github.com/HKUST-SAIL/Gaussian-Splatting-with-Stochastic-Solids.
journal: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers

title: Generative Whimsy Jigsaws
abstract: Unlike conventional jigsaw puzzles which partition an image into a predefined set of rectangular pieces, “whimsy” jigsaw puzzles depict a variety of objects, such as animals, vehicles, and characters, through the outlines of the pieces themselves. Although skilled artists have created visually compelling and playful puzzles within this framework, designing whimsy jigsaws remains highly challenging—creators must simultaneously partition a given outline into multiple interlocking pieces while ensuring that each piece conveys a recognizable visual concept. This difficulty limits accessibility, preventing casual creation by less experienced users, particularly when designing puzzles with many pieces and concepts. To address this challenge, we present a computational framework for automatically designing whimsy jigsaws from a loosely specified set of visual targets, each assigned to an individual piece. Specifically, we take a set of text prompts as input and use differentiable optimization to refine the geometry of each piece, guided by a pre-trained diffusion model. Since naive formulations suffer from a fundamental tension in whimsy jigsaws between geometric validity and recognizability, this paper develops a representation for planar partitioning that guarantees the partitioning of the domain into a specified number of connected pieces, while allowing for highly flexible geometric evolution. The key component is the scalar slowness field, which is used to compute a warped geodesic distance field given a point source by solving the Eikonal equation. Given distance fields from multiple sources, we can compute warped Voronoi cells that define pieces of a puzzle. The representation is fully differentiable, with gradients computed via adjoint sensitivity analysis, and the slowness field is represented as a neural implicit field. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework generates diverse, thematically consistent jigsaw puzzles across a wide range of user prompts, enabling the automated design of puzzles with complex, figurative pieces.
journal: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers

title: RISE: Reconstructing Interactive 3D Scene from a Single Image
abstract: Interactive 3D scenes serve as the foundational infrastructure for embodied AI, digital twins, and immersive metaverses, providing the essential physical and semantic substrate for realistic agent-environment interaction. While recent advances have made single-image 3D reconstruction increasingly feasible, existing methods still fail to directly reconstruct interactive scenes with part-level articulated structures for fine-grained physical interactions. The primary challenges lie in integrating fine-grained, interactable object modeling with holistic scene layouts, and in recovering detailed interactive properties from limited supervision. To bridge this gap, we introduce the task of Single-Image 3D Interactive Scene Reconstruction, which aims to synthesize physically interactive 3D scenes directly from a single image. By unifying fine-grained object articulation with holistic scene synthesis, this task enables the efficient derivation of simulation-ready environments from real-world observations, representing a pivotal step toward the scalable creation of interactive digital worlds. To solve the task, we propose RISE, a unified framework that extends the coarse-to-fine 3D reconstruction pipeline into an interactive paradigm. The coarse stage reconstructs rough object geometry and scene layout, while the fine stage refines object geometry and appearance. To infer interactive properties, we introduce a Generative Articulation Estimation (GAE) module between the coarse and fine stages. By extracting articulation parameters directly from compact coarse-stage representations, GAE efficiently recovers interactive properties while decoupling joint reasoning from entangled geometry. Furthermore, by reformulating articulation estimation as a 4D generative task, GAE leverages 3D priors to ensure geometric- and motion-aware predictions. To evaluate reconstructed interactive scenes, we further introduce three sets of metrics that comprehensively assess scene reconstruction and interactive property recovery. Experiments on both holistic interactive scene and single articulated object reconstruction demonstrate that our method generates high-quality interactable assets. We further validate that the interactive scenes reconstructed by our framework significantly expand the data scaling capacity for downstream embodied AI applications.
journal: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers

title: WildAnySplat: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting in the Wild
abstract: We present WildAnySplat, a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that enables robust novel-view synthesis from in-the-wild multi-view images. Unlike controlled captures, real-world images often contain multi-view inconsistencies caused by transient occluders, illumination changes, and camera ISP, which degrade the quality of existing feed-forward reconstruction methods. To address this challenge, we introduce a student–teacher framework that learns transient-robust and appearance-consistent 3D representations. A teacher network operates on clean images, while a student processes the corresponding in-the-wild inputs. The teacher provides clean supervision to guide the student toward a consistent canonical representation. Since paired clean and in-the-wild data are scarce, we use a hybrid data strategy, combining real paired captures, synthetic augmentations, and pseudo-clean labels generated from optimization-based reconstructions, bridging the domain gap between synthetic and real-world data. We adopt a transformer architecture with dedicated DPT heads for camera pose, depth, and Gaussian prediction. We additionally predict per-view transient masks to reweight photometric supervision and suppress unreliable Gaussians. To account for cross-view appearance variation, we incorporate a bilateral grid module that models per-image color transformations and enables recovery of a canonical radiance representation. Experiments on challenging in-the-wild benchmarks show that WildAnySplat improves robustness to transient occlusions and appearance variation while retaining the fast inference of feed-forward Gaussian Splatting.
journal: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers

title: Neural Surrogate-Driven Inverse Design of Nonlinear Heterogeneous Metamaterials
abstract: Mechanical metamaterials enable a wide range of effective properties, including anisotropic stiffness and nonlinear stress–strain behavior. While prior work has largely focused on periodic structures, many applications require heterogeneous materials with spatially varying properties. Designing such materials remains challenging due to the highly nonlinear inverse mapping from target behavior to spatially varying microstructures. We present a fully differentiable, surrogate-driven approach for the inverse design of heterogeneous metamaterials with spatially varying mechanical properties. As the key ingredient, we propose a neural surrogate model that predicts the homogenized nonlinear response of local microstructures, which are composed to form globally varying materials. We combine this surrogate with a material space based on star-shaped-distance Voronoi diagrams, enabling smoothly varying structures with diverse mechanical properties. Together with an annealed Langevin optimization scheme, our method supports arbitrary differentiable objectives encoding spatially varying target properties. We demonstrate the versatility of our method on a range of inverse design problems, showcasing nonlinear and spatially varying behavior. We validate the results through full-scale FEM simulations and physical testing on 3D-printed prototypes.
journal: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers

title: StructSVG: Tree-Graph Guided Multi-Agent Text-to-SVG Generation
abstract: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) is a resolution-independent and fully editable graphic format widely adopted in UI design, art, and web development. Inherently a hierarchical semantic structure, SVG organizes geometric primitives in a document tree where element hierarchy and drawing order directly determine both visual appearance and editability. However, most of the existing text-to-SVG methods either treat SVG as flat token sequences lacking structural awareness, or rely on optimization-based differentiable rasterization with prohibitive computational costs, resulting in outputs that lack meaningful semantic hierarchy and editable structure. Inspired by the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) and agent-based frameworks, which have demonstrated strong capabilities in structured reasoning and multi-step planning, we propose StructSVG, a training-free, structure-aware multi-agent framework for text-to-SVG generation. StructSVG constructs an explicit Tree-Graph intermediate representation: the semantic tree hierarchically decomposes the prompt into editable visual components with semantic identifiers and spatial information, while the topology graph models inter-element rendering order and spatial relationships, providing a structured blueprint for LLM-driven generation and refinement. Five specialized agents collaborate across three stages to perform structured planning, component drafting, and refinement and selection. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, and we showcase diverse applications highlighting its generality and practical utility. Code and data for this paper are at https://github.com/sealost/StructSVG.
journal: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers

title: Beyond Rigid Bodies × Newton for Robotics: Open GPU Physics, Differentiable Simulation, and Multi-Solver Ecosystems for Physical AI and Embodied Robotics
abstract: How can physics developed for graphics become reliable infrastructure for robot learning? This full-day workshop follows one path from programmable physics to research questions, solver choices, and policy evaluation. An NVIDIA Warp introduction and interactive demonstration establish a shared contact-and-manipulation example. The Taiwan-led Beyond Rigid Bodies organizing team then leads research clinics and group exercises on non-rigid fidelity, differentiability, Real2Sim2Real, and world models, with contributions from four invited speakers. Participants turn those lessons into explicit modeling assumptions and validation requirements. Closing Newton and Isaac Lab sessions use these requirements to examine multi-solver interfaces and robot-learning workflows through demonstrations, comparisons, and group review. Academic and industry participants jointly produce a task-to-solver decision record, an evaluation checklist, and prioritized open questions. The program welcomes alternative engines, critical comparisons, and negative results; software demonstrations provide concrete evidence for discussion throughout the day.

title: NKTR-255, a polymer-conjugated IL-15, enhances CAR T cell therapy by engaging endogenous antitumor immunity.
abstract: CAR-T cells have yet to show widespread efficacy in solid tumors due in part to poor persistence and dysfunction in the tumor microenvironment. Further, heterogenous expression of target antigens can lead to escape of antigen-null tumors that resist CAR-T killing. Strategies to cooperatively boost both CAR-T and endogenous antitumor immunity may be critical for achieving durable efficacy in cancer patients. NKTR-255 is a polymer-conjugated IL-15 with extended half-life that can boost endogenous T and NK cells, as well as CD19 CAR-T cells in B cell malignancies. However, whether NKTR-255 is sufficient to overcome CAR-T dysfunction in the suppressive solid tumor microenvironment, and how NKTR-255 and CAR-Ts together re-shape endogenous antitumor immunity, is not known. Using mouse models of ROR1+ lung adenocarcinoma, we show that NKTR-255 significantly boosted accumulation and function of tumor-infiltrating CAR-T cells targeting ROR1. Compared with NKTR-255 or CAR-T treatment alone, combination of NKTR-255 and CAR-T therapy increased endogenous tumor-specific T cells that preserved a PD-1+Tcf1+ stem-like phenotype. Consequently, NKTR-255 and CAR-T combination therapy completely eliminated ROR1+ tumor cells and significantly improved survival, with enhanced tumor control dependent on both CAR-Ts and endogenous T cells, though all mice ultimately succumbed to progression of ROR1- tumor. Compared to IL-15-armored CAR-T cells, systemic NKTR-255 induced greater accumulation and reduced terminal differentiation of endogenous tumor-specific T cells, resulting in superior tumor control. Thus, combining NKTR-255 with CAR-T therapy is a promising strategy to enhance both CAR-T and endogenous antitumor immunity to promote coordinated control of aggressive tumors.

title: Serial vaccination establishes and refines the human CD4+ T cell memory repertoire.
abstract: CD4⁺ T cells coordinate protective immunity against pathogens. However, how human CD4⁺ T cell memory is established and evolves following primary and repeated vaccinations remain incompletely understood. Using COVID-19 mRNA vaccination as a model, we tracked 50 distinct antigen-specific populations directly ex vivo with peptide-MHC class II tetramers in eight SARS-CoV-2-naïve individuals from pre-exposure baseline through memory time points after three mRNA doses. We showed that primary vaccination established the architecture of antigen-specific memory. Initial vaccination leveraged pre-existing memory while preferentially recruiting high-avidity T cells, establishing an immunodominance hierarchy dominated by a small subset of precursors. Booster vaccination refined both the magnitude and quality of T cell memory. It increased select populations and enhanced differentiation of subdominant CD4⁺ T cells. Populations that did not become more abundant after boosting retained their polyfunctional potential. Beyond establishing memory to the ancestral spike, vaccinations recruited cross-reactive T cells and increased the breadth of CD4+ T cell memory. Collectively, these findings reveal how human T cell memory evolves through sequential immunizations to generate a functionally diverse and broadly responsive memory repertoire against future viral challenges.

title: Multiple-Camera Tracking of Rigid Objects
abstract: In this paper we describe a method for tracking rigid objects using one or several cameras. The tracking process consists of aligning a 3-D model representation of an object with image contours by measuring and minimizing the image error between predicted model points and image contours. The tracker behaves like a visual servo loop where the internal and external camera parameters are updated at each new image acquisition. We study in detail the Jacobian matrix associated with this minimization process in the presence of both point-to-point and point-to-contour matches. We establish the minimal number of matches that are needed as well as the singular configurations leading to a rank-defficient Jacobian matrix. We find a mathematical link between the point-to-point and point-to-contour cases. Based on this link we show that the latter has the same kind of singularities than the former. Moreover, we study multiple camera configurations which optimize the robustness of the method in the presence of single-camera singularities, bad, noisy, or missing data. Extensive experiments done with a complex ship part and with up to three cameras validate the method. In particular we show that the tracker may well be used as a camera calibration procedure.

title: The structural resilience capacity of agricultural supply chains in China–ASEAN: the role of digital infrastructure and spatial spillovers
abstract: Agricultural supply chains in integrated developing regions face growing climate volatility, market uncertainty, and coordination challenges. In the China–ASEAN context, digital transformation has reshaped cross-border production and coordination networks. This study examines the structural resilience capacity of agricultural supply chains, hereafter referred to as structural ASCR. Structural ASCR captures long-term system capacity rather than high-frequency recovery following a specific disruption. Using a balanced country-level panel covering China and ASEAN countries from 2000 to 2023, this study employs a two-way fixed-effects Spatial Durbin Model. The model estimates the association between digital infrastructure and structural ASCR, including direct and cross-regional spillover associations. Digital infrastructure is positively associated with structural ASCR in the full sample, and the estimated indirect effect is also positive. Higher digital governance is associated with a more favorable DigInfra–ASCR relationship through local and spatial channels. Digital-trade development conditions the local and spatial channels differently, with positive moderation concentrated in spatial transmission. By combining spatial interdependence with these contextual moderators, the study provides macro-level evidence relevant to interoperable digital infrastructure, digital regulatory conditions, and regional coordination.

title: Sustainable food choice in a multilabel rice market: green signal jamming and the limits of traceability labels
abstract: Competition between certified traceability and weakly verified eco-friendly claims may complicate sustainable food choices in multilabel markets. Drawing on signaling theory, this study examines whether Taiwan’s government-certified Traceable Agricultural Products label retains its distinctiveness when consumers are simultaneously exposed to ecological claims that may generate green halo effects. Using a two-study quantitative design, we combine e-commerce retail prices with consumer survey data. Study 1 applies descriptive price comparisons and a hedonic price model to assess market-side differentiation, whereas Study 2 uses partial least squares structural equation modeling and an exploratory probit classification to examine consumer interpretation and purchase orientation. Traceability-only products show a positive but smaller price association than ecological-claim-only products. On the consumer side, traceability retains perceptual and attitudinal relevance, but this recognition does not consistently translate into value-for-money judgments. Overall, the market-side and consumer-side findings provide complementary and convergent evidence of a recognition–reward gap. Formal traceability remains relevant, but its standalone distinctiveness and market reward appear attenuated in a noisy multilabel environment in which weakly verified green cues attract similar consumer recognition. This pattern is consistent with informational interference and diminished signal salience, underscoring the importance of food-label governance in preserving certification credibility and supporting sustainable food choices.

title: Ellagic acid, gut microbiota, and urolithins in bone metabolism: microbial transformation, human exposure, and preclinical evidence
abstract: Ellagic acid (EA) and its gut microbiota-derived metabolites, particularly urolithin A (UA), have attracted attention because of their potential involvement in the regulation of bone remodeling. However, most available evidence comes from in vitro and animal studies, and the clinical relevance of these findings to the prevention and treatment of osteoporosis remains unclear. This review summarizes the evidence from three perspectives: gut microbial transformation, compound-specific bone effects, and human exposure and clinical evidence. The gut microbiota can convert ellagitannins and EA into a variety of structurally distinct urolithins, but the production profiles differ markedly among individuals. The urolithin metabotype refers to an individual’s overall pattern of urolithin production, and to date it still cannot be used to predict skeletal responses. In preclinical models, including in vitro and animal studies, EA and some urolithins can influence processes related to bone remodeling, such as RANKL-dependent osteoclastogenesis, osteogenic differentiation, and inflammatory and oxidative stress responses. As for the mechanisms involving Wnt signaling, the NF-κB/MAPK pathway, and antioxidant responses, the evidence likewise comes from preclinical studies; the effects vary with the compound and the experimental model, making it difficult to extrapolate directly to other urolithins or to the human skeleton. Another notable issue is that circulating urolithins exist predominantly as conjugated metabolites, whereas many in vitro studies have used the free aglycone. Whether these compounds can accumulate in human bone tissue to levels sufficient to produce biological effects remains undetermined. Existing human studies have mostly focused on pharmacokinetics, short-term safety and tolerability, and some non-skeletal endpoints, and the limited bone-related evidence is insufficient to demonstrate that EA or urolithins prevent osteoporosis or fractures. The EA–gut microbiota–urolithin metabolic axis provides clues for understanding the link between microbial metabolism and skeletal health; however, whether it exerts bona fide skeletal effects in humans remains unconfirmed. Tailoring supplementation regimens according to urolithin metabotype, modulating the gut microbiota, or implementing individualized dosing are promising but still unvalidated research directions. Future studies should incorporate actual human exposure characteristics, take into account the etiology of secondary bone loss and various confounding factors, and conduct randomized controlled trials with skeletal outcomes as primary endpoints in addition to standard anti-osteoporosis therapy, so as to clarify the true clinical value of this axis.
journal: The Egyptian Journal of Internal Medicine

title: Plasma Steroid Profiling for Differentiating Cushing's Disease from Ectopic ACTH Syndrome.
abstract: CONTEXT Bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) remains the gold standard for differentiating Cushing's disease (CD) from ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) syndrome (EAS), but its invasiveness and limited availability pose clinical challenges. We developed a blood-based adjunctive model using LC-MS/MS-based plasma steroid profiling. METHODS We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 128 patients with ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome, including 95 with CD and 33 with EAS, evaluated at Peking Union Medical College Hospital between November 2020 and July 2025. Plasma concentrations of 23 quantifiable steroids were analyzed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection, followed by classification and regression tree (CART) modeling. Apparent discrimination and classification performance of the CART model were evaluated, while calibration and decision curve analyses were performed using a separate logistic regression model incorporating the same LASSO-selected predictors, with 1,000 bootstrap resamples used for calibration correction. RESULTS LASSO analysis identified four key predictors: androstenedione (A4), LC-MS/MS cortisol, age, and sex. The exploratory CART model showed high apparent discrimination in the development cohort, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.986 and an overall classification accuracy of 96.9% (124/128). CONCLUSION LC-MS/MS-based plasma steroid profiling combined with basic demographic information may provide an exploratory blood-based adjunct for differentiating CD from EAS. A4 was the splitting variable at the root node, with subsequent splits based on age, sex, and LC-MS/MS cortisol. However, the model and its cohort-derived thresholds require independent external validation before clinical implementation.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

title: Education Research: A Novel Clerkship-Level Approach to Disability Education: Integrating Patient and Professional Identity Through Adaptation and Inclusion.
abstract: Background and Objectives Persons with disabilities experience inequities in health care, partly driven by clinicians' limited training in disability-competent communication and accommodations. Disability education remains heterogeneous, with few framing disability as both a patient and physician identity. We developed a clerkship-level curriculum to address this gap. Learner objectives were to differentiate the medical and social models of disability; describe disability-inclusive communication; recognize disability as both a patient and physician identity; identify accessibility barriers and accommodations; and support disability-inclusive care. Methods A multidisciplinary team developed a disability curriculum within a required third-year neurology clerkship. Students completed asynchronous preparation and observations, followed by a workshop incorporating team-based simulation and structured debriefing. Anonymous preworkshop and postworkshop surveys assessed understanding, attitudes, and comfort. Quantitative comparisons and exploratory thematic analysis evaluated learner outcomes. Results All 267 enrolled third-year medical students completed the preworkshop survey; 204 completed the postworkshop survey, with attrition reflecting clerkship absences. Significant improvements were observed in understanding of the medical and social models of disability (24.7%-98.5%; +73.8%; 95% CI 67.7%-78.7%), comfort discussing disability with patients (53.6%-98.0%; +44.4%; 95% CI 37.9%-50.6%), discussing accommodations (63.3%-98.0%; +34.7%; 95% CI 28.4%-40.8%), and comfort supporting colleagues with disabilities (35.2%-97.1%; +61.9%; 95% CI 55.1%-67.6%) (all p < 0.0001). Attitudes toward physicians with disabilities were favorable at baseline and remained high (97.0% vs 99.0%; +2.0%; 95% CI -0.9% to 4.9%; p = 0.20). Respondents rated the curriculum excellent or very good (95.6%; 95% CI 91.8%-97.7%). Students agreed that the workshop would benefit future practice (99.0%; 95% CI 96.5%-99.7%) and improve patient outcomes (99.5%; 95% CI 97.2%-99.9%). Exploratory thematic analysis identified 5 themes: open communication and active listening, individualized accommodations, collaborative adaptation, structural accessibility, and the value of time in inclusive care. Discussion The curriculum improved attitudes, comfort, and recognition of disability as both patient and physician identity. Key lessons include the value of experiential, team-based learning; explicit framing beyond deficit-based models; and clinical observation integrated with structured reflection. Future studies should examine longitudinal retention and transfer to clinical practice.

title: Müllerian duct maintenance is promoted by GATA2: Evidence from genetic mouse studies and two human cases of Müllerian duct agenesis.
abstract: The paradigm of sexual differentiation holds that female embryos retain the Müllerian ducts, the precursor of the female reproductive tract, by default in the absence of anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH). However, whether Müllerian duct maintenance requires active signaling remains unknown. Here, using mouse genetic models, we discover that deletion of mesenchymal Gata2 causes selective regression of the cranial Müllerian duct, the precursor of the oviduct. This regression is not driven by ectopic AMH signaling but may instead result from the loss of region-specific NRG1 signaling. Deletion of mesenchymal Gata2 also causes uterine hypoplasia and vaginal atresia, whereas epithelial Gata2 is specifically required for uterine gland differentiation. These genetic mouse studies reveal a Gata2-dependent, region-specific program that actively maintains the Müllerian duct and promotes female reproductive tract differentiation. Extending these findings to humans, we report two individuals with GATA2 deficiency who exhibit utero-vaginal agenesis or hypoplasia, consistent with Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome. Collectively, our results identify Gata2/GATA2 as a critical regulator of Müllerian duct development, providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying female reproductive tract development and Müllerian anomalies.

title: Exploring EFL students’ critical AI literacy in generative AI-assisted essay revision: insights into profiles and trajectories
abstract: This study examines how English as a foreign language (EFL) students demonstrate and develop Critical AI Literacy (CAIL) in generative AI-assisted essay revision. Drawing on the APSE model, which conceptualizes CAIL across four dimensions (awareness, positionality, interaction strategies, and evaluation), we conducted a longitudinal case study of three focal students across four writing tasks throughout a semester. Data sources included student-AI interaction logs, think-aloud protocols, stimulated recall interviews, and both initial and revised essay drafts. Qualitative analyses were conducted to trace patterns and changes in students’ CAIL. Findings show that all three students demonstrated CAIL across the four dimensions, although critical evaluation and critical positionality emerged as the most salient dimensions. Students selectively integrated AI feedback based on rhetorical fit, linguistic appropriateness, and factual accuracy, demonstrating various levels of agency. Over time, two students became increasingly selective and context-sensitive in their engagement with AI, whereas the third demonstrated strategic engagement from the outset but showed substantial task-to-task variation in feedback uptake. Overall, the students’ trajectories were heterogeneous and task-dependent rather than uniformly progressive. These patterns challenge linear models of AI literacy and highlight its situated nature in EFL writing contexts. Pedagogically, the study calls for differentiated instruction that fosters evaluative judgment and self-representation alongside prompt design. The findings contribute to a growing body of research advocating for more nuanced, learner-centered approaches to AI integration in foreign language writing.
journal: International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching

title: Development of Public Control Institutions: A Model for Individual Voter Vote Tracking in Elections in the Russian Federation
abstract: This article examines the problem of ensuring trust in the electoral process and its results in the context of digital transformation. The author proposes a comprehensive model for the modernization of the electoral system of the Russian Federation, based on the introduction of a mechanism for personal voter control of the fate of their vote. The technical, organizational and legal aspects of the implementation of this model for all existing forms of voting are considered: face-to-face, remote electronic and postal. Special attention is paid to preserving the principle of secrecy of voting, minimizing administrative risks and increasing transparency at all stages of the election campaign, including the stage of nomination and registration of candidates. A comparative analysis with foreign analogues is carried out, the potential risks and benefits of implementing the system are considered. The conclusion is made about the potential positive impact of the proposed innovations on the legitimacy of government and the legal awareness of citizens.

title: Benchmarking CNN, Transformer, Hybrid, and Foundation Models for Multi-Label Bronchoscopic Finding Classification on the BERD Dataset
abstract: Background: Automated classification of bronchoscopic findings is hindered by severe class imbalance, visual similarity between findings, and scarce expert-annotated data. This study benchmarked convolutional, Transformer, hybrid, and foundation models for multi-label bronchoscopic finding classification. Methods: ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B3, ViT-B/16, Swin-T, and Hybrid-EffSwin (average-pooling fusion of EfficientNet-B3 and Swin-T) were trained on 23 finding categories of the Bronchoscopy Examination Report Dataset (BERD) using identical hyperparameters and patient-level data splits. ConvNeXt-T and two foundation models (DINOv2 ViT-B/14 and BiomedCLIP ViT-B/16) served as additional baselines. Ablations examined fusion strategy, loss function, and decision thresholds. Models were compared using patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs) and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests on patient-level summaries. Results: On the independent test set (316 images, 180 patients), Hybrid-EffSwin achieved the highest macro F1-score (0.376), Matthews correlation coefficient (0.339), and area under the ROC curve (0.803). Across three training seeds, Hybrid-EffSwin ranked first in every run (macro F1 = 0.363 \((\pm)\) 0.013); its advantage over ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 was significant in all runs, over EfficientNet-B3 in one of three, and over Swin-T in none (\((\Delta)\)F1 = +0.020 to +0.025).Among additional baselines, DINOv2 performed comparably to Hybrid-EffSwin (Hybrid-EffSwin minus DINOv2: \((\Delta)\)F1 = +0.013; 95% CI \((-)\)0.025 to 0.052) and achieved the best exact-match accuracy and calibration, whereas ConvNeXt-T was significantly inferior; a late-fusion ensemble of separately trained EfficientNet-B3 and Swin-T performed close to Hybrid-EffSwin. Average-pooling fusion performed at least as well as residual-projection and concatenation fusion, and validation-selected thresholds changed macro F1 only modestly. Conclusions: Hybrid CNN-Transformer, hierarchical Transformer, and self-supervised foundation models formed the strongest tier for multi-label bronchoscopic classification and could not be distinguished on the current test set. Multi-institutional validation is warranted.

title: Study on Quantitative Modeling of Task Completion Probability in AI Agents Using DAG and State-Machine
abstract: Autonomous AI agents increasingly decompose user instructions into task lists, but widely used approaches (AutoGPT, BabyAGI, MetaGPT) generate simple linear, ID-ordered sequences that cannot express conditional branching or parallel execution. Newer orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph, the LLM Compiler, and the Claude Agent SDK add DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) or state-machine execution control for non-linear workflows, yet none provides a quantitative, probabilistic estimate of how likely a plan is to succeed, or how much a redundant (alternative) path improves that likelihood. This study integrates DAG-based dependency modeling, prompt engineering for conditional branching, and a state-machine execution engine, and formulates the resulting task-completion probability P(Goal) with reliability engineering. The model is generalized to 1-out-of-n (parallel) path redundancy and to general DAG topologies with parallel branching and AND-joins, and a cost-constrained redundancy-allocation problem and a Beta-prior estimator of path success probabilities from execution logs are given. Assuming independent task outcomes, Monte Carlo simulations (10,000–100,000 trials) of a retrieval-and-summarization task (72.7% completion for the linear model, 84.4% with redundancy) agree with the closed-form predictions to within 0.18 percentage points across 24 parameter combinations and within 1 point under all conditions. Redundancy at the bottleneck stage yields about 3.9 times the gain at the most reliable stage, as the marginal-utility formula predicts. Alternative paths help most when failures are persistent; correlated failures reduce the gain. With a real LLM agent (100 runs), completion rates predicted from probabilities estimated on half the runs fell within the 95% intervals observed on the other half.
