title: Diagnostic Performance of Radiomics-Based Machine Learning in Differentiating Glioblastoma From Brain Metastasis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Glioblastoma (GBM) and brain metastasis (BM) are the most common malignant intracranial tumors in adults. Noninvasive differentiation between them remains challenging, as they frequently share similar imaging features. Although radiomics-based machine learning (ML) models show promise, systematic evidence of their performance remains limited. OBJECTIVE We aimed to systematically estimate the diagnostic performance of radiomics-based ML models in differentiating GBM from BM and to explore multiclass classification involving primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL), thereby assessing their potential for clinical use. METHODS We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library databases from inception to January 22, 2026, for studies reporting the diagnostic performance of radiomics-based ML models for differentiating GBM from BM. Multiclass studies involving PCNSL were also retained. Methodological quality was appraised via the Radiomics Quality Score 2.0. Binary diagnostic accuracy was pooled using a bivariate random-effects model, stratified by internal and independent external validation. Multiclass sensitivities and specificities were pooled using separate joint generalized linear mixed models. Physician assessments were evaluated as an exploratory benchmark. RESULTS A total of 39 studies (31 binary and 8 multiclass), involving 11,558 patients, were included. For binary classification, pooled sensitivity and specificity were 88.9% (95% CI 84.1%-92.4%) and 83.0% (95% CI 76.8%-87.9%) in internal validation, and 83.8% (95% CI 77.4%-88.7%) and 80.7% (95% CI 71.1%-87.7%) in external validation, respectively. In multiclass analyses, pooled sensitivity was 84.4% (95% CI 72.4%-91.8%) for GBM, 70.6% (95% CI 54.4%-82.8%) for BM, and 75.0% (95% CI 62.7%-84.3%) for PCNSL, with corresponding specificities of 82.5% (95% CI 70.1%-90.4%), 88.8% (95% CI 81.9%-93.3%), and 94.4% (95% CI 88.4%-97.4%), respectively. CONCLUSIONS Radiomics-based ML models could distinguish between GBM and BM in the included cohorts. However, due to methodological limitations and scarce evidence, their generalizability and clinical utility remain unclear. Further multicenter prospective studies should conduct independent external validation in consecutive patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION PROSPERO CRD420261295269; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261295269.

title: Agentic AI: A Review and Proposed Framework
abstract: Chatbots built on large language models (LLMs) are good at producing text, but most of them stop at the reply. They cannot look up an order, run a test or update a record unless someone connects them to tools and tells them how to use those tools safely. Agentic AI is the name given to systems that close this gap: an LLM is placed inside a loop where it makes a plan, calls a tool, reads what came back and decides what to do next. This paper reviews the main building blocks of such systems, namely planning and reasoning, tool use, memory and state, and human oversight, and places them in the recent literature on ReAct-style agents, tool learning, reflection, multi-agent conversation and agent benchmarks. Building on this review, we propose a modular agent pipeline made of a tool registry with permissions, a planner, a permission check, an optional human approval gate, tool execution with observation, result checking and an audit log. We also describe how such a pipeline should be evaluated, using task success, tool errors and injection resistance, and time and cost. The paper is a review with a proposed design and does not report new experiments. It closes with open problems, including reliable planning over long tasks, defence against prompt injection, and fair evaluation of agents that behave differently on every run.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: SmartKrishi-AI: A Survey of AI-Integrated Agriculture Decision Support and Farm Resource Management
abstract: Agricultural choices depend heavily on a complex mix of environmental variables, including soil properties, fluctuating weather patterns, crop compatibility, market dynamics, pest threats, and the availability of vital farming resources. Most contemporary digital services target only one of these factors, forcing growers to manually gather data from multiple disconnected websites and local contacts. This paper reviews recent developments related to SmartKrishi–AI, a conceptual, integrated platform designed for agricultural decision-making and asset coordination. Our analysis evaluates several vital domains, including crop recommendation frameworks, weather forecasting networks, commodity price models, plant disease diagnostics, public welfare discovery, equipment leasing, and labor scheduling. We analyze recent research from 2023 to 2026 indexed across major venues such as IEEE, Elsevier/ScienceDirect, and MDPI, exploring their mathematical approaches, dataset constraints, evaluation methods, and practical challenges. Based on these insights, we introduce a conceptual multilayer architecture that connects data-driven analytical models with verified institutional channels and peer-to-peer resource exchange workflows. Because the proposed ecosystem serves as a structural blueprint rather than an experimentally fieldtested software tool, no project-specific crop yield or predictive precision increases are claimed. Finally, we highlight persistent open challenges in this sector, such as data quality gaps, geographic adaptation limits, model interpretability, forecast volatility, system interoperability, regional language support, and the necessity for rigorous field trials.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: ETHNO-STEAM INTEGRATION USING KASONGAN POTTERY IN SCIENCE LEARNING (A Study in Bachelor of Islamic Elementary School Teacher Education)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the potential application of an Ethno-STEAM approach based on the local wisdom of Kasongan pottery in science learning within the Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Teacher Education (PGMI) Program at UIN Sunan Kalijaga Yogyakarta. The study employed a qualitative method, with data collected through the analysis of instructional documents, particularly the Semester Lesson Plan (Rencana Pembelajaran Semester/RPS) for the science course. The findings indicate that Kasongan pottery possesses relevant characteristics and strong potential for integration into Ethno-STEAM–based science learning. These characteristics include the use of clay as a natural material representing the physical and chemical properties of matter, pottery-forming processes that involve principles of force, pressure, and balance, and firing processes that demonstrate physical and chemical changes resulting from high temperatures. In addition, activities involving dimensional measurement, size comparison, and volume estimation in pottery making reflect the application of mathematical concepts in real-world contexts. In conclusion, an Ethno-STEAM approach based on the local wisdom of Kasongan pottery has strong potential to be developed as a contextual and meaningful science learning model in pre-service Madrasah Ibtidaiyah teacher education, as it effectively connects theoretical concepts with authentic local cultural practices.

title: Global Surface Coal Mine Segmentation with Multi-Spectral Sentinel-2 Imagery: Overcoming Spectral Dilution using Geospatial Foundation Models
abstract: Surface coal mines are a diffuse, undermonitored source of methane, whose reduction could deliver measurable near-term climate benefit. A lack of precise spatial boundaries and reliance on global emission inventories (based on point coordinates with kilometer-scale spa- tial uncertainty), limit their continuous spaceborne attribution and monitoring. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Global Surface Coal Mine (GSCM) Polygons dataset, obtained by spatially match- ing the Global Coal Mine Tracker to the Global Mining Footprint and linking candidate polygons to cloud-free Sentinel-2 imagery. We benchmark semantic-segmentation models from convolutional, vision-transformer, and geospatial-foundation-model families. On spatially isolated test tiles containing mine pixels, a pre-trained Prithvi-EO-2.0 model with six visible and infrared bands obtains the best mine recall (0.6975) and mIoU (0.6971). In contrast, adding channels to an ImageNet-pretrained SegFormer causes mine IoU to fall to 0.0094 at 15 bands. We term this spectral dilution. While the positive-only evaluation does not establish global mine discovery or operational readiness, the results support a practical baseline for delineating known surface mines.

title: Developing Financial Intelligent Investment Methods Using an Improved-PPO Algorithm
abstract: In the context of dynamic financial markets and the limitations of traditional and existing intelligent methods in balancing risk and return, this study targets the poor generalization and weak risk resistance of investment strategies in dynamic stock market environments. It proposes a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)–based investment model that integrates a deep sequence-encoding module and a dynamic, risk-adjusted advantage mechanism. The model employs a hybrid encoder that combines Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architectures to process multi-granularity time-series data (minute, daily, weekly), effectively compensating for deficiencies in state observations. Meanwhile, a dynamic risk adjustment advantage function is introduced, in which a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) generates dynamic penalty coefficients to enhance risk control, working synergistically with the actor–critic structure of PPO to optimize decisions. Experimental results show that incorporating the deep sequence encoding module yields the fastest convergence in ablation studies, achieving an average round reward of 1.7. In cross-industry Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) portfolio management, the model achieves a cumulative return of 35.85% and a 99% risk tolerance of –2.50%, outperforming comparable models. During simulated high-volatility periods, peak volatility is capped at 5.5%, and the dynamic risk penalty coefficient closely tracks market fluctuations. This research provides a scientific and practical tool for A-share stock timing and portfolio management, enriches methodologies for financial time-series processing, and promotes the practical application of deep reinforcement learning in intelligent finance.
journal: Journal of Engineering, Project, and Production Management

title: Enterprise Data Governance Combining Federated Transfer Learning and Security Audit
abstract: Due to the problems of dispersed business data, inconsistent regulatory interpretations and limited cross-domain modeling at the enterprise level, this paper puts forward a data governance model based on federated transfer learning and security auditing. The preprocessing stage adds salted pseudonymization, entity masking, rare-category pooling, 30-minute window aggregation, and lineage/access-log feature construction to ensure reproducibility without revealing raw records. The method builds metadata, lineage, access behavior and rule-hitting features locally in each business domain and achieves cross-domain knowledge transfer via transfer gating and alignment loss. At the same time, it records summary hashing, responsible parties, policy consistency and lineage continuity in audit quality scores, adds a risk-suppression aggregation mechanism, and synchronously links the model update process to the governance traceability process. Experiments are based on financial, procurement, logistics, sales and compliance data from a large local group from January 2024 to December 2025. According to the results above, the proposed method achieves an AUC of 0.957, a macro-F1 score of 0.912, a recall of 0.926, and an audit trace completeness of 0.987. It is 2.1 and 2.3 percentage points higher than the best-performing comparative method. Extra imbalance, threshold-sensitivity and edge deployment tests show that the transfer gate reduces negative transfer in a 1:50 class imbalance, and audit-suppressed aggregation maintains real-time latency below 160ms under the tested edge configuration. Thus, cross-domain risk identification and strategy implementation can be achieved in a closed-loop manner without aggregating raw data, and a technical path for enterprise data governance that balances accuracy, compliance, and feasibility has been provided. A separate public HDFS log benchmark supplies a limited proxy stress test; it does not validate enterprise audit completeness or reproduce an accuracy advantage over FedAvg.
journal: Journal of Engineering, Project, and Production Management

title: Regional artificial intelligence development and agricultural ecological efficiency: evidence from Chinese provinces
abstract: Existing studies have primarily focused on the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) on productivity and carbon emission efficiency, while systematic evidence on whether and through which mechanisms AI improves agricultural ecological efficiency (AEE) remains relatively limited. Using provincial panel data from China for the period 2005 to 2023, this study employs the entropy weighting method to measure regional AI development and a slack-based measure (SBM) model incorporating undesirable outputs to evaluate AEE. A two-way fixed effects model is further constructed to examine the effects of AI on AEE and the underlying mechanisms. AI is conceptually distinct from general digitalization, automation, precision agriculture, and information technology development, as its defining feature lies in leveraging machine learning, intelligent sensing, and algorithmic decision-making to achieve more advanced data processing and intelligent decision-making capabilities. The results indicate that a 0.1-unit increase in regional AI development is associated with an average increase of 0.01078 units in AEE. Mechanism analysis suggests that AI can indirectly improve AEE by promoting green finance development and industrial structure upgrading. Furthermore, agricultural technological innovation exhibits a significant threshold effect, with higher levels of technological innovation strengthening the positive effect of AI on AEE. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the positive effect of AI on AEE is more pronounced in eastern regions, regions with lower levels of urbanization and agricultural modernization, and non-major grain-producing regions. Further analysis identifies positive spatial spillover effects of AI on AEE in neighboring regions, contributing to coordinated green agricultural development across local and neighboring regions. This study provides evidence on the effects, transmission mechanisms, and threshold conditions through which AI improves AEE, offering new empirical insights into the role of AI in facilitating the green transformation of agriculture and extending the analytical perspective of agricultural sustainability research.

title: Exploring Machine- and Deep-Learning Algorithms for Hybrid Crop Prediction
abstract: Genomic selection (GS) offers a practical route for identifying superior hybrid combinations before extensive field testing, but predictability (PA) may depend jointly on the genomic representation and the prediction algorithm. We used 18 trait–population combinations across five crop hybrid public datasets including maize, wheat, rice, strawberry, and pumpkin. Six predictor sets were compared: all genome-wide markers, 2000 Spearman-selected markers, and eigenvectors of additive (G), dominance (D), and additive-by-additive epistatic (G#G) relationship matrices. Seven conventional, machine-learning (ML) and deep-learning (DL) models were evaluated. PA was assessed by random cross-validation and three parent-aware schemes (T2, T1, T0), in which both, one, or neither parent of a hybrid was represented in training. Across datasets, PA ranged from 0.39 to 0.93. Adding dominance or epistatic information to additive predictors gave little consistent improvement and occasionally reduced PA. Genomic best linear unbiased prediction (GBLUP) showed the most stable performance, whereas ML and DL models varied more; support vector regression and multilayer perceptron excelled for specific traits, and Anchored Genomic NETwork (AGNET) was competitive but did not consistently outperform GBLUP. Under the parent-aware schemes, PA declined from T2 to T0, with tree-based models most affected. Overall, tailoring prediction strategies to specific traits and populations remains essential.

title: STELLA: A Connectivity Representation for Lane Marking Detection from Satellite Imagery
abstract: High-definition (HD) maps for autonomous driving store each lane marking as a separate polyline. Satellite imagery covers wide areas at low cost, but current methods cannot turn it directly into such polylines. The reason is that no existing output representation suits polyline detection. Segmentation masks do not tell which line a pixel belongs to, and they merge lines that meet or cross. Existing cell-wise connectivity representations tie their output slots to fixed angular sectors. Their training target therefore changes discontinuously at sector boundaries. We propose STELLA, an output representation suited to polylines, and a method to train it. At each grid cell, STELLA predicts one self-slot and two unordered connection slots. During training, these slots are matched to the ground-truth (GT) connections at minimum cost. One line thus becomes one chain of cells, and post-processing only cleans up overlapping lines. We also propose AI-CCQ, an asymmetric instance-level metric for thin, long lines. It gives credit to a partly drawn line but rejects a line that switches to a neighboring marking. On the SEED-MAP test set, STELLA reaches an AI-CCQ F1 score of 0.4483, against 0.3005 for a segmentation-based method and 0.3551 for the Sat2Graph representation.

title: LightMaskMamba: A Near-Ground Remote Sensing Object Detection Network with Visible–Infrared Fusion
abstract: Visible–infrared fusion is a main route to all-weather object extraction in near-ground remote sensing, but single-band RGB remains unstable under occlusion, clutter, and low light and illumination variation. This study presents LightMaskMamba, a lightweight visible–infrared object detection network for near-ground remote sensing. Public benchmarks test fusion quality across scenes, and the self-built near-ground wampee field dataset is for deployment-oriented field validation. The core of the network is a lightweight mask-guided Mamba fusion architecture. Its key module, the Lightweight Mask Mamba Fusion Block (LMMFB), uses an object-related mask to drive shallow-to-deep VIS–NIR feature fusion, focuses computation on object regions, and reduces scan redundancy. Dual-band detection therefore stays light enough to run at the edge. On the self-built wampee dataset, LightMaskMamba-v11s reaches 97.4% mAP50 and 52.0% mAP50:95. Relative to single-band YOLOv11s, mAP50 is 2.3 and 4.6 percentage points higher on IR and RGB. Parameters rise by 3.7M, from 8.8M to 12.5M. The same model is likewise effective in detection accuracy, and lighter, on public multimodal object-detection datasets. On a Jetson Orin NX Super, TensorRT INT8 mixed-precision inference reaches about 17.3 FPS, or 58 ms per image.

title: RS-DeCLIP: Gated Dual-Source DeCLIP Adaptation with Side-Branch Query-Based Local Fusion for Remote Sensing Image–Text Retrieval
abstract: Remote sensing image–text retrieval requires diverse textual supervision and fine-grained visual representations. Redundant captions limit linguistic diversity, while rewriting can introduce semantic drift. A single global image descriptor may also underrepresent small objects and local spatial arrangements, limiting fine-grained discrimination. To address these challenges, we propose RS-DeCLIP, a two-stage retrieval framework. Stage 1 adapts a RemoteCLIP ViT-B/32 dual encoder with DeCLIP-style multi-view supervision using official captions and captions polished by a large language model. A semantic consistency gate downweights text self-supervision (TSS) between less consistent original and rewritten captions. Similarity-aware negative downweighting and text-to-image weighting address ambiguous negatives and directional imbalance, while training-only fine-grained alignment strengthens detail sensitivity. Stage 2 targets the fine-grained visual information underrepresented by the global descriptor. Five learnable visual query vectors, conditioned on the global image embedding and guided by soft spatial preferences, attend to a dense P2 feature map to extract local evidence. Consistency-gated orthogonal residual fusion integrates this evidence into the frozen global image embedding. These visual queries are distinct from the user’s text query: image feature extraction and fusion do not use the retrieval text, so fused image descriptors can be precomputed and compared with independently encoded text vectors. On the Remote Sensing Image Captioning Dataset (RSICD), Stage 1 improves mean recall (MR) from 35.26% to 38.54%, and Stage 2 further increases MR to 39.27%. On the Remote Sensing Image–Text Match Dataset (RSITMD), Stage 2 improves MR from 50.90% to 52.58%. The final model exceeds the reported GeoRSCLIP-FT (RET-2) results by 0.40 and 0.77 percentage points on RSICD and RSITMD, respectively, and the Representation Discrepancy Bridging (RDB) method by 1.18 and 0.54 percentage points.

title: OMEGA-Avatar: One-shot Modeling of 360° Gaussian Avatars
abstract: Creating high-fidelity, animatable 3D avatars from a single image remains a formidable challenge. We identified three desirable attributes of avatar generation: 1) the method should create avatars from a single image in a one-shot setting without per-identity network optimization, 2) model a 360° full-head, and 3) produce animation-ready results. However, current works address only two of the three points simultaneously. To address these limitations, we propose OMEGA-Avatar, the first framework for one-shot reconstruction of animatable, 360°-complete full-head avatars. Starting from a one-shot animatable avatar framework, we achieve 360° full-head avatar generation with two novel components. First, to overcome poor hair modeling in full-head avatar generation, we introduce a semantic-aware mesh deformation module integrating multi-view normals to optimize a FLAME head with hair while preserving its topology. Second, to enable effective feed-forward decoding of full-head features, we propose a multi-view feature splatting module constructing a shared canonical UV representation from features across multiple views through differentiable bilinear splatting, hierarchical UV mapping, and visibility-aware fusion. This approach preserves both global structural coherence and local high-frequency details across all viewpoints, ensuring 360° consistency without per-instance network optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OMEGA-Avatar achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming baselines in 360° full-head completeness while maintaining competitive cross-view identity consistency.
journal: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers

title: Now You See Me Now You Don't: A Framework To Detect and Reduce Proxy Capacity
abstract: In regulated domains such as lending, the two most salient fairness concepts are disparate impact and disparate treatment: disparate impact is generally defined by differential rates of adverse outcomes between demographic groups, while disparate treatment is generally defined by the use of demographic information or proxies to issue decisions. There already exist established methods to quantitatively detect and mitigate disparate impact; however, there has been less research on doing the same for disparate treatment. From a practitioner's perspective, the manner in which a conditional independence test is formulated and operationalized to identify proxies is nuanced and underexplored. As Machine Learning (ML) systems increase in scope and application in regulated domains, practitioners need a defensible framework to identify proxies at scale. Current disparate treatment frameworks typically rely upon some combination of quantitative and qualitative review of models' inputs to identify proxies. Features that are identified as proxies are then typically removed from the model in practice, and predictive performance degrades in favor of fairness through unawareness. Here, we propose a two-part framework that reduces the disparate treatment risk of a feature and keeps the predictive performance that removal of the feature loses. First, we propose a quantitative test for proxy capacity that identifies whether some of a feature's values reveal membership in a particular demographic group. Second, we propose a pre-processing methodology that adjusts those proxy features to reduce their proxy capacity. We show empirically on synthetic and public datasets that this framework identifies features that proxy for demographic information and reduces their proxy capacity while the adjusted feature retains task-relevant signal (i.e. improves predictive performance versus removal).

title: Pro$^2$ Agent: Scientific Problem Probing for Autonomous AI R&D
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can now autonomously conduct AI research by writing code and running experiments. They typically do so by iteratively optimizing a codebase, while ignoring the problem structure behind the task. This formulation is effective on simpler tasks, but on difficult problems it often gets stuck in the wrong solution region because the agent never explicitly represents its understanding of the problem. We introduce Pro$^2$ Agent, which shifts the primary state of autonomous AI research from a codebase state to a Problem State: an explicit structure of what problems prevent success and which solutions are likely to address them. Pro$^2$ Agent initializes the Problem State through comprehensive analysis of available resources and constraints. It then performs targeted research to relate the identified problems to candidate solutions. Through controlled hypothesis testing, the agent updates the importance of a suspected problem or the benefit brought by a candidate solution. On the complete MLE-Bench, Pro$^2$ Agent matches the best reported medal rate (70.7%) under the standard 24-hour budget and reaches 76.0% with a 48-hour budget, the highest medal rate reported on the complete benchmark. It also achieves competitive performance on PostTrainBench. In addition, it produces research notes for each task that make the research process transparent and reusable by human researchers.

title: AppSci-Bench: Can LLMs Build AI Agents and Make Them Better?
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used not only to power AI agents but also to build them. While many benchmarks assess the quality of LLM- powered agents, few ascertain how good LLMs are at building them. To this end, we introduce AppSci-Bench, where we construct a setting akin to how human Applied Scientists build agents for businesses - through eliciting task requirements from stakeholders, exploring the business's infrastructure, and scientifically improve the target agent by designing experiments and internal benchmarks. AppSci-Bench features seven realistic domains - five new ones (Slides Generation, Order-to-Cash, Compliance Review, Customer Call Insights, and CRM Insights) and two domains recast from tau3-bench (Yao et al., 2024; Shi et al., 2026b)(Airline and Banking) - each with a held-out evaluation suite customized for that task. We evaluate seven frontier models and find AppSci-Bench challenging: the best model, Claude Opus 5.0, only reaches a mean-minimum score of 59.1% across 3 build attempts; other models do significantly worse. Models struggle with eliciting task requirements (only 65% for Opus 5.0), build representative internal evaluations (models saturate their own evaluation 65% of the time but fail to solve the held-out task), presenting challenges for future research. The benchmark code is available here: https://github.com/sanjari-orb/appsci-bench.

title: Incorporating argumentation frameworks for LLM decision-making: Task-specific design and evaluation
abstract: Argumentation frameworks (AFs) provide explicit, formal mechanisms for representing and resolving conflicts and thus have been incorporated into large language model (LLM) decision-making. The benefits vary and depend on how arguments and their relations are constructed, evaluated, and incorporated into the decision process. {We abstract a workflow consisting of four stages based on existing argumentation-augmented methods} and investigate their design choices over tasks of debate-based decision-making and retrieval-based fact verification. Our evaluation with recent LLMs shows that existing methods do not consistently improve performance across the considered tasks. Motivated by this observation, we develop two task-specific methods. The first is called Qnt-Arg, which organizes arguments around the original speakers in debate materials and aggregates model-estimated argument strengths and candidate-answer priors under gradual semantics. The second is Qlt-Arg that uses credibility estimates to establish preferences between conflicting evidence items and applies grounded semantics to select acceptable evidence for subsequent LLM inference. We examine the roles of generative and decision models within the two methods. In the debate setting, Qnt-Arg consistently outperforms other argumentation-augmented methods across matched configurations; Qlt-Arg improves retrieval-based fact-verification performance compared with the baselines. These findings demonstrate the value of combining formal argumentation and LLM while highlighting the importance of aligning with tasks in argumentation construction, model selection, and the role of formal semantic reasoning.

title: Differentiable Hydrodynamics for Whole-Body MPC of Underwater Robots
abstract: Underwater vehicle-manipulator systems distribute actuation across thrusters and joint motors. Whole-body model predictive control (MPC), rather than separate vehicle and arm controllers, can coordinate both to extend the workspace and exploit the system's full kinematic capability. Doing so, however, requires a hydrodynamic model and derivatives throughout the prediction horizon. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) captures geometry-dependent forces and moments for such a model, but is too expensive to evaluate online. We present a differentiable analytical hydrodynamic model combining smooth spherical-harmonic force and moment fields with a coupled added-inertia matrix identified from CFD. It compactly represents velocity and acceleration-dependent loads and provides their derivatives in closed form. These derivatives are propagated through free-floating vehicle--manipulator dynamics for whole-body trajectory optimization and receding-horizon control, jointly optimizing thruster forces and joint torques for reaching and continuous tracking. Held-out CFD tests validate the principal translational-force and rotational-moment fields and the added-inertia response. The analytical Jacobians evaluate faster and avoid the step-size sensitivity of central finite differences. Closed-loop Stonefish experiments demonstrate whole-body MPC in an independent marine simulator. By making geometry-dependent hydrodynamics directly available to gradient-based control, the model incorporates water forces and their sensitivities into motion allocation between the vehicle and arm, rather than treating them only as disturbances.

title: Zero to Four Views: Unified Panorama Generation and Preference RL for Unobserved Regions
abstract: Panoramas can serve as shared scene backgrounds for multi-shot video generation, but most existing panorama generators take text alone or a single input image. We present a single model that generates a full equirectangular panorama from a text caption and K in {0,...,4} perspective conditioning views taken by a four-camera rig at one viewpoint. We fine-tune a pretrained text-to-image rectified-flow transformer in two stages. In the first stage, each conditioning view is appended to the token sequence together with the ID of its camera slot, and the number of views varies during training, so one set of weights serves every input setting. In the second stage, we improve the region not covered by any conditioning view. Supervised training computes its loss on noisy latents of the ground truth and never scores a panorama the model has generated and decoded, so we propose Uncovered-Region GRPO (UR-GRPO), a reinforcement-learning recipe that rewards the candidates a vision-language model prefers in pairwise comparisons on crops around this region. Because the slot ID alone does not tell the model which way the rig points, we also offer an optional variant that writes each view's camera direction into its position encoding, which lets the user decide where each view appears in the output. With one conditioning view, our model outperforms the previous state of the art, 360Anything, trained on the same data and evaluated with the same code, on Laval Indoor and gives mixed results on an indoor subset of SUN360; the second stage improves the results for every number of conditioning views.

title: AI-Native Industrial Control Systems: An Agent Architecture for the Control System Lifecycle
abstract: Industrial control systems increasingly use AI for perception, control, and engineering, while available control functions and execution environments are typically established in advance. This paper proposes an AI-native industrial control system in which collaborating agents determine the capabilities required by a task, construct the control application, and prepare its execution environment. System-level agents coordinate device-level agents within configured resource and permission constraints. A physical sorting workstation illustrates two forms of adaptation. In the first case, controller and robot agents construct a sorting application on a prescribed Raspberry Pi target. In the second, a camera agent adds inspection on an edge node, and the controller associates inspection results with downstream pickup decisions. A subsequent revision enables selective sorting using the same agents and deployment arrangement. The trials demonstrate the feasibility of task-driven construction and evolution on the workstation. Commissioning also reveals limitations in the traceability of design decisions, adherence to delegated responsibilities, diagnostic reasoning, and verification of physical behavior.

title: Instance-Optimal Moment Estimation in the Add-Remove Model of Differential Privacy
abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of estimating empirical means, variances, and covariances under pure differential privacy in the add-remove model. While existing mechanisms achieve optimal worst-case error, they may not be optimal for individual datasets. To measure the performance of mechanisms on individual datasets, we introduce instance-dependent error metrics and prove sharp lower bounds on them. Then, we design mechanisms that achieve these lower bounds and demonstrate that they achieve asymptotically better utility compared to existing methods.

title: A fast and accurate model for gradient-based inverse design of multimode waveguides
abstract: Multimode photonic inverse design requires fast, accurate computational models that provide geometry gradients. Based on coupled-mode theory (CMT), we propose a differentiable surrogate model. Its parameter-extraction method uses a change of modal basis to obtain coupled-mode parameters from cross-sectional mode data. We also provide a complete, easy-to-implement propagation and optimization workflow. Using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation data as a common reference, we compare the prediction accuracy of our model and forward dataset-based eigenmode expansion (EME) for randomly generated thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) waveguide profiles that traverse modal coupling regions. Using identical modal libraries, the model reduces the maximum per-mode mean absolute transmission error by 17-37% compared with forward EME. We demonstrate a spot-size converter design that preserves the fundamental TM$_0$ mode in its hybridization region with the first-order TE$_1$ mode and obtain nine structures, each with FDTD-verified transmission above 98%. These tests demonstrate the model's utility for large-scale photonic inverse design, enabling rapid exploration of the design parameter space by combining gradient information with improved prediction accuracy.

title: RoCoKV: Accelerating LLM Inference Serving through Uncertainty and Redundancy Aware KV Cache Compression
abstract: KV cache compression is critical for large reasoning models, where most of the cost comes from long generated reasoning traces rather than the input prompt. These traces often contain redundant and low-utility tokens due to looping, self-verification, and corrections. However, such tokens may still receive high attention scores, making it difficult to remove them without harming the reasoning process. We propose RoCoKV, a KV cache compression method designed for large reasoning models. RoCoKV introduces two key components. First, uncertainty-guided adaptive pruning adjusts the compression strength based on the model's confidence, allocating more memory during uncertain phases and applying stronger pruning when the model is confident. Second, redundancy-aware token selection reduces the impact of tokens that are highly similar to recent reasoning content, encouraging the model to retain more informative and diverse tokens. Beyond the algorithm, we co-design RoCoKV with the serving stack: we develop fused three-phase CUDA decode kernels and integrate them into vLLM as a drop-in plugin that preserves its paged KV layout and CUDA graph capture, turning algorithmic savings into real end-to-end speedups. Extensive experiments across three reasoning benchmarks and two reasoning models demonstrate that RoCoKV consistently improves reasoning accuracy under constrained KV cache budgets, achieving higher accuracy compared to state-of-the-art KV cache compression methods. For DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B in vLLM, RoCoKV achieves a 1.27X speedup and 38% higher throughput on AIME25, the most challenging evaluated reasoning benchmark, and a 1.43X speedup and 45% higher throughput on the long synthetic benchmark, compared with Full-KV.

title: An explicit domain-preserving projected Milstein scheme with strong order one for stochastic systems
abstract: A variety of domain-preserving numerical schemes have been developed for scalar stochastic differential equations and for several classes of multidimensional systems, including those defined on hyperrectangles and positive orthants. To accommodate more general domain constraints, we consider stochastic systems on bounded or unbounded open convex polyhedral domains, where coefficients may exhibit boundary singularities and polynomial growth. Under local regularity, growth and boundary assumptions, we establish well-posedness and integrability estimates for the exact solution. Then we construct an explicit projected Milstein scheme that preserves the domain by applying a Euclidean projection onto a step-size-dependent interior set after each Milstein update. For systems driven by multidimensional commutative noise, we prove strong order-one convergence for the maximum grid error in Lp, for suitable p > 1 and sufficiently small step sizes under additional weighted regularity and stability conditions. The proof combines these integrability estimates with local Milstein consistency, localization and weighted stability, without requiring a priori step-size-uniform moment or boundary inverse-moment bounds for the numerical approximation. Applications to constrained stochastic models and numerical experiments illustrate the observed first-order convergence behavior.

title: RemoteVLPG: How to Obtain a Specific VLM for Language-Guided Path Generation on Remote Sensing Images?
abstract: We study how to obtain a task-specific Vision-Language Model (VLM) for language-guided path generation between start and end points on remote sensing images. We explore this question from three aspects. First, we implement three widely used architectural approaches and compare their performance. Second, we design a scalable method for constructing pre-training data and build an effective pre-training dataset with a degree of diversity. Methods trained on this dataset achieve promising zero-shot performance. Third, we construct three benchmarks that support stratified evaluation and design three metrics for path generation. We investigate this problem through extensive experiments. The results show that the zero-shot performance of methods trained on the constructed pre-training dataset can exceed that of some advanced commercial VLMs. Code and Dataset can be available at https://github.com/jzdang/RemoteVLPG

title: SR-Agent: An Advanced Intelligent Agent for Seismic Data Restoration
abstract: Field seismic data often suffer from multiple degradations, including noise contamination, incomplete geometry, low-frequency loss, and reduced spatial resolution, requiring different restoration operations. Existing methods mainly address individual degradations, while sequential application of task-specific models often relies on human experience. Although all-in-one models integrate multiple restoration tasks, they face a trade-off between generalization and task-specific accuracy. To address this issue, we propose a SR-Agent (Seismic Restoration Agent) containing three sequential stages: classification, restoration, and evaluation. For the first two stages, we design an intelligent classifier based on ResNet to identify the degradation types presented in low-quality seismic data, and the classification results are used as task instructions to activate the corresponding restoration models in a pool, which contains dedicated networks for different restoration tasks. For the last stage, SR-Agent can dynamically schedule the activated models and explore an optimal restoration path, rather than relying on a predefined processing pipeline. Specifically, we first develop a no-reference restoration-performance evaluation measurement by combining four parameters: seismic trace coherence, energy distribution in F-K domain, spectral smoothness, and high-frequency energy ratio. Second, the evaluation measurement is applied to quantify the restoration performance of different candidate restoration paths. Finally, the path with the highest evaluation score is automatically selected and then applied to input seismic data. The results show that, when multiple degradation mechanisms coexist, SR-Agent can effectively plan an optimal restoration path, achieving accurate and intelligent restoration of degraded seismic data.

title: A Wolf in Sheep's Pixels: Visual Camouflage Attacks via HDR Gain Maps
abstract: An image can pass automated safety checks while showing harmful content to its human viewer. We introduce DRJanus, a visual camouflage attack that exploits the gap between standard dynamic range (SDR) processing and high dynamic range (HDR) display. Automated systems often read only an image's SDR base, whereas HDR viewers reconstruct its appearance using an auxiliary gain map. DRJanus inverts this reconstruction to embed two independently chosen color images in a single JPEG, without querying or optimizing against the target model. It preserves the chosen SDR base exactly and reconstructs HDR targets at an average PSNR of 43.03 dB across 400 images. On a benchmark of 100 sexual-content images, DRJanus evades detection by all six tested commercial moderation services and nine vision-language models. Across five agents, each evaluated on 120 task cases per threat setting, attack success ranges from 31.67% to 100% for moderation evasion and from 95% to 100% for task manipulation. We also explore cross-view consistency checks as a mitigation. These findings expose a gap in visual trust: securing what a machine reads does not secure what a user sees. A demo is available at https://qshen0629.github.io/DRJanus/

title: ToolPulse: Side-Channel Eavesdropping on Tool-Using LLM Agents
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as agents that translate user requests into sequences of local tool invocations. While prior cache-based side-channel attacks target the locally deployed models, they typically require the adversary to share model-related components or hardware resources with the victim's inference process. These assumptions do not apply to the predominant agentic settings, in which commercial LLMs execute on vendor-controlled infrastructure. We show that agentic execution exposes a more practical attack surface: although inference remains remote, tools are executed on the user's machine and commonly rely on shared system libraries. In this paper, we first systematically evaluate Flush+Reload and Prime+Probe for monitoring agentic tool invocations. Our evaluation across three hardware platforms shows that Flush+Reload enables accurate, real-time tool monitoring, whereas Prime+Probe, despite supporting cross-VM attacks, incurs prohibitive monitoring overhead and suffers from cache-set aliasing. We present ToolPulse, a cache-based side-channel eavesdropping framework against tool-using agents. We first design the Tool Recovery Attack to reconstruct an agent's tool-execution workflow. We evaluate the Tool Recovery Attack on 11 LLMs across Codex and Claude Code. It consistently reconstructs tool workflows, with the lowest F1 score exceeding 93%. We further demonstrate two attack scenarios enabled by the recovered traces. Task Profiling Attack infers user intent across two Terminal-Bench task categories and the Trigger Localization Attack identifies sensitive tool calls in encryption/decryption and model training/inference workloads. Even under substantial system noise on a server shared by approximately 20 users, both Task Profiling Attack and Trigger Localization Attack maintain high accuracy.

title: SegAnyFruit: Learning Generalizable and Edge Deployable Fruit Instance Segmentation at Scale
abstract: Deploying fruit instance segmentation in real agricultural settings requires generalizing across unseen species, orchards, and imaging conditions under strict onboard compute and annotation budgets. We introduce SegAnyFruit (SAF), a data construction and progressive training framework that distills foundation-model priors into lightweight, prompt-free segmenters. SAF combines generic mask pre-training, broad mid-training on automatically annotated web imagery from our curated WebFruits dataset, and human-verified agricultural refinement post-training on PaperFruits, together spanning 733K images and 9.66M whole-fruit masks across 165 fruit types. Across seven benchmarks, zero-shot SAF-RF-DETR-XL reaches 69.06 average mask AP50:95 (+4.76 over SAM 3) while remaining deployable on edge devices. SAF initialization also boosts few-shot to full-shot adaptation across five agricultural domains while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Finally, we systematically analyze training stages, data scale, model capacity, and generative augmentation, and validate our pipeline's transferability to underwater, cell, and human segmentation. We will release our datasets, code, and SAF models.

title: LingSante MedGuard Technical Report
abstract: As medical AI is increasingly used for patient consultation and clinical decision support, identifying harmful, non-compliant, or ethically problematic responses is essential for responsible deployment. Assessing these risks requires checking clinical claims against relevant evidence, verifying calculations, and applying medical requirements under their intended conditions. We introduce LingSante MedGuard, a capability-enhanced guardrail that integrates supervision from a medical guardrail teacher model and six specialized medical capability experts into a unified model. The guardrail teacher supervises risk decisions and explanations across medical safety, compliance, and ethics, while the capability experts support medical rule understanding, numerical reasoning, multimodal hallucination detection, agentic safety verification, risk localization, and multimodal entity understanding. We consolidate these sources of supervision through offline supervised fine-tuning on teacher-generated demonstrations, followed by multi-teacher on-policy distillation using feedback on student-generated responses. We further introduce LingSante MedGuardBench, a benchmark comprising 11 risk-detection subsets spanning medical safety, compliance, and ethics. At 4B, 9B, and 27B scales, LingSante MedGuard achieves mean benchmark F1 scores of 82.3%, 82.4%, and 87.4%, respectively. The 4B model also achieves 73.9% mean accuracy across MedHallu and MedHALT-NOTA under retrieval-enabled evaluation. Additional evaluations of the verification components show improvements in evidence-supported consistency, source traceability, and rule-guided rationale quality across model scales. These results support the integration of specialized medical capabilities into a unified guardrail for medical risk assessment and evidence-based medical safety verification.

title: Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models
abstract: Estimating the score function of a distribution plays a central role in statistics and machine learning, with applications in distribution estimation, sampling, and score-based generative modeling. However, learning scores from sensitive data raises privacy concerns. These concerns are particularly pronounced in score-based generative modeling, where trained models may memorize individual training examples and expose sensitive information through membership inference and data extraction attacks. Although non-private score estimation has been extensively studied, the statistical limits of its private counterpart remain less understood. In this work, we study score estimation under $(α,β)$-differential privacy for $d$-dimensional sub-Gaussian distributions with locally $γ$-Hölder-continuous scores. We develop a sampling-based private score estimator using quadratic B-splines and the exponential mechanism, and we implement our proposal through projected Langevin Monte Carlo with runtime polynomial in the sample size $n$. The proposed estimator satisfies $(α,β)$-differential privacy, and achieves expected density-weighted squared error $\mbox{polylog}(n) \max(n^{-2γ/(d+2γ+2)},\,(nα)^{-2γ/(d+γ+1)})$. We also establish a nearly matching private minimax lower bound, thereby characterizing the privacy-accuracy trade-off for score estimation. As an application, we construct a differentially private diffusion model whose privacy guarantee is independent of the number of denoising steps. We show that, with an appropriate discretization scheme, the resulting diffusion model attains nearly minimax optimal expected total variation error among all private distribution estimators. We validate our theoretical findings through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

title: Reinforcement-Aligned Probabilistic Weather Forecasting with Discrete Tokens
abstract: Global medium-range weather forecasting must not only generate ensembles efficiently to characterize uncertainty in future states, but also serve downstream applications such as extreme-event warnings and cross-sphere coupled simulations. We introduce WeatherCraft, a framework that unifies probabilistic generation and reinforcement learning alignment through discrete weather tokens, bringing the GPT-style pretraining--post-training paradigm to global medium-range weather forecasting. A multiscale tokenizer represents atmospheric states as a coarse-to-fine token hierarchy, while a Transformer models causal dependencies across time and scale and predicts tokens within each scale in parallel. Direct sampling generates diverse ensembles, and exact token log-probabilities enable Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to maximize downstream task rewards without differentiating through evaluators or coupled models. On the ERA5 benchmark, WeatherCraft's eight-member ensemble mean reduces day-15 normalized RMSE by 17.6% relative to the strongest evaluated deterministic baseline and, with KV caching, achieves an approximately $18\times$ inference speedup over GenCast. Direct fair-CRPS adaptation improves ensemble probabilistic skill, while reward-based post-training improves forecasts of persistent land temperature extremes and coupled ocean heat extremes. This work establishes discrete autoregressive modeling as a general foundation for scalable, task-alignable Earth system foundation models.

title: Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise as predictors across various tasks, benefiting from their ability to use information from unstructured context. However, when predictions serve as parameters of downstream optimization problems, higher prediction accuracy does not necessarily translate into lower decision costs. We propose decision-focused reinforcement learning (DFRL), a framework for post-training LLMs to predict optimization parameters using negative downstream decision regret as reward. DFRL trains LLM predictors to minimize the costs of the decisions induced by their predictions, without requiring downstream convexity or differentiability, and integrates readily into existing RL post-training frameworks. To address expensive reward evaluation, we develop two approaches. Heuristic warm-starting uses inexpensive approximate rewards during an initial phase before switching to refinement with exact rewards. Reward correction combines inexpensive estimates with randomized exact evaluations, preserving the expected policy gradient while reducing the expected number of exact solves per update. Experiments on three synthetic optimization problems demonstrate improvements over prediction-loss baselines, while a larger knapsack experiment shows faster early improvement under short training budgets. On inventory planning with H&M transactions and product descriptions, our best configuration, in which the LLM reasons before predicting, reduces regret by 31.4% relative to the SFT baseline and 12.4% relative to the strongest evaluated conventional forecasting baseline.

title: Tether: Verified Stateful Policy Engine for System-Level Monitoring of Agents
abstract: Autonomous AI agents are increasingly deployed for long-running tasks that execute arbitrary shell commands or programs. However, these actions can result in unauthorized network requests or persistent, malicious changes to the user's file system, processes, or privileges. Existing defense mechanisms rely on either LLM-based monitors, which lack provable safety guarantees, or stateless policy enforcement layers, which miss multi-step data flows and execution side-effects unmodeled by the policy language (e.g., network calls initiated inside a Python script). We introduce Tether, a framework for runtime enforcement of stateful security policies over the observed side-effects of an agent's actions. Tether executes each proposed action in an ephemeral, isolated sandbox, inferring abstract action semantics from observed system calls. Tether then enforces stateful policies over these inferred semantics, permitting actions to proceed only if they comply with the policy. Policies and action semantics are defined in an embedded DSL in Lean 4 capable of expressing diverse constraints, including information flow control (IFC), access control, and network security policies. Because actions can propagate labels from sources to destinations, a single rule can enforce fine-grained IFC policies across multi-step execution flows of arbitrary length. Expressing policies in Lean enables formal verification that they satisfy global security invariants (e.g., preventing network access after reading a sensitive file). We evaluate Tether on realistic coding-agent benchmarks across both benign and adversarial trajectories. With a single policy shared across all tasks, Tether blocks 100% of in-scope attacks while maintaining a benign false-positive rate under 5%.

title: Cyber-Physical RSI for AI-RAN: A Case Study
abstract: Learned models for radio access networks (RANs) are often developed using simulation, yet their predictions can shift when exposed to physical propagation conditions, protocol behavior, and equipment implementations. This paper presents a cyber-physical recursive self-improvement (RSI) framework for AI-RAN that connects a task-oriented student model, an experiment-planning coach agent, a calibratable virtual environment, and a physical host agent. Physical measurements are organized as evidence for both model adaptation and subsequent experiment planning. We examine an implementation of the physical-feedback pathway using ping-pong handover as a case study. The system completes 12 physical executions organized into six baseline--candidate pairs, updates the student from measured outcomes, and evaluates the revised model on reserved physical configurations. In the observed short-window tests, increasing the time-to-trigger from 320 to 1280\,ms changes the ping-pong count from three to zero. The updated student achieves a grouped-validation mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.673 round trips/min, while a common three-configuration physical evaluation yields MAEs of 1.240 and 1.601 round trips/min for the pre-feedback and post-feedback models, respectively. These results characterize both the operational feedback loop and the parameter-dependent generalization behavior revealed by new physical experiments.

title: Tenon: A Unified Programming Framework for Retargetable PIM Compilation
abstract: Processing-in-memory (PIM) is emerging as a building block of heterogeneous systems for memory-bound workloads, and commercial prototypes now span near-bank SIMD engines, bank-level GDDR accelerators, programmable DRAM cores, and bit-level in-SRAM processors. Their programming stacks are fragmented: no abstraction or compiler is shared across vendors, and per-device models range from instruction sequences to C-like languages. Data layout further complicates the problem: tight compute-memory integration makes data layout a first-order optimization, yet existing PIM compilers lack a unified way to represent and optimize it. A key observation is that PIM compilation targets can be modeled as nested grids of compute and storage units connected by legal data-transfer paths. We present Tenon, a unified programming framework for retargetable PIM compilation. It decouples workload, compilation target, and cost specifications, so a workload is expressed once and compiled through a unified programming framework. Tenon generalizes the $\mathbb{F}_2$ linear layout algebra from GPU compilers to map logical work and data onto these compute and storage grids. It automatically constructs a minimum-movement data layout given a workload and a target specification. We evaluate Tenon on six PIM backends: five commercial backends and AttAcc, a state-of-the-art academic HBM-based PIM architecture. Across the commercial backends, it matches or outperforms vendor, expert, and compiler baselines, with geometric-mean speedups of up to $1.20\times$ and individual speedups up to $3.65\times$. For end-to-end GPT-13B decoding on AttAcc, Tenon-compiled workloads run $1.2$--$1.3\%$ faster than those compiled by DCC, a state-of-the-art PIM compiler, across all three batch-4 configurations. Together, these results demonstrate Tenon's performance portability across diverse PIM target families.

title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction
abstract: Fast and accurate prediction of adsorption energies is critical for high-throughput computational catalyst screening, existing methods compromise either on evaluation speed (full-graph machine learning potentials) or geometric sensitivity (coordination-based models like the alpha-scheme). Here, we present AdsNet, an equivariant graph neural network that directly predicts adsorption energies in a single forward pass, which operates on a local graph restricted only to adsorbate atoms and its immediate surface neighbors within a cutoff radius. This local graph formulation decouples computational complexity from total system size while encoding continuous geometric features (interatomic distances and directional vectors) enabling sensitivity to subtle variations in local bonding environments. AdsNet adopts a message-passing architecture with scalar and vector node features over multiple interaction layers. Trained on AdsTraj, a dataset of 33,920 density functional theory (DFT) calculated structures spanning 26 transition metals and 6 adsorbates (H*, C*, O*, CO*, OH*, HOCO*), the model achieves an adsorption energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.032 eV and a force RMSE of 0.047 eV/A. Analytic forces obtained via automatic differentiation enable structure relaxation through a projected gradient descent algorithm with adaptive line search, eliminating entire geometry optimizations. Additionally, AdsNet uniquely decomposes predicted adsorption energies into contributions from individual atoms within the local adsorbate graph - an interpretability feature unattainable with conventional machine-learning potentials. AdsNet thus establishes an accurate, highly efficient, and interpretable framework for large-scale adsorption energy prediction and local interface relaxation across various material surfaces.

title: GNetSS: Towards Learning GNSS Corrections without Ground Truth
abstract: We present GNetSS, a self-supervised GNSS position correction framework that improves the robustness of single point positioning (SPP) without requiring ground-truth locations for training. GNetSS combines a transformer-based network with a deterministic differentiable positioning solver. The network predicts satellite-wise pseudorange corrections by modelling inter-satellite geometry and temporal context, while the solver converts these corrected measurements into receiver position corrections under GNSS geometry and optional motion constraints. Unlike supervised GNSS correction methods that rely on ground-truth, GNetSS derives its training signal directly from GNSS measurement consistency. Experimental results show that GNetSS improves robustness across open-sky, urban, and forested environments. The method is particularly effective at suppressing large-error outliers, reducing the maximum 3D positioning error by over 50% compared with SPP. These results demonstrate the potential of self-supervised pseudorange correction for scalable and robust GNSS positioning in real-world autonomy applications. Code and the in-house dataset will be released upon acceptance.

title: Ask in the Crowd: Differentially Private LLM Inference via Dummy-Augmented Shuffling
abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as LLM-as-a-Service (LLMaaS), where user queries are sent to remote LLMs for inference, raising severe privacy concerns about the exposure of sensitive user inputs. Differentially private inference mitigates these risks by injecting noise into input embeddings. However, existing methods struggle to balance privacy and utility, as stronger privacy protection often leads to substantial accuracy degradation in LLM inference. In this work, we propose DP-SPD, a differentially private LLM inference framework that protects user queries by hiding the real query among client-generated dummy queries. All queries are randomly shuffled before being sent to the server, preventing direct identification of the user's true intent. To improve inference efficiency, we exploit the shared-prefix structure among queries and reuse transformer key--value (KV) caches during decoding. We analyze the privacy guarantee of DP-SPD and evaluate its utility on classification and generation tasks, as well as its privacy protection under QIA, EIA, and GPT-based attacks. Experimental results show that our method achieves strong inference-time privacy protection and near-plaintext utility while improving inference efficiency through shared-prefix KV-cache reuse.

title: Verifying Before Enhancing: Target Evidence Chain Verification for Infrared Small Target Detection
abstract: Infrared small target detection is essential for early warning, surveillance, remote sensing, and space-based target perception. However, infrared small targets are typically tiny, weakly textured, and boundary-blurred, making them difficult to distinguish from complex backgrounds. Moreover, target-like background structures can produce salient responses across multiple scales, making response strength alone insufficient for reliable target discrimination. To address this challenge, we propose VBE-UNet, a Target Evidence Chain Verification Network that assesses candidate reliability beyond response magnitude through complementary evidence cues. Specifically, counterfactual background explanation models local target evidence, while joint evidence verification integrates cross-scale support and perturbation-based contribution verification to guide feature recomposition. The resulting reliability estimates guide selective feature refinement, promoting target-relevant responses while reducing unsupported background activations. Extensive experiments on IRSTD-1K, NUDT-SIRST, and NUAA-SIRST demonstrate that VBE-UNet achieves superior detection accuracy and lower false-alarm rates compared with state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies and evidence reliability analysis further validate the effectiveness of the proposed verification framework.

title: What's in the box? Revealing Object Layouts Inside Opaque Boxes via Contactless Vibration Excitation and Sensing
abstract: Can we reveal what is inside an opaque box by observing its surface vibrations? Objects inside a box alter its mechanical response, providing cues about their hidden locations. We introduce a method that uses these cues to predict a box's 2D occupancy layout entirely remotely. A nearby speaker excites vibrations, which we measure on one visible wall using a grid of laser points and a camera measuring each point's speckle-pattern shifts. Our model, WhisperBox, learns to encode these vibrations into a latent representation and decode it into an occupancy map of the box's contents. The method requires no physical contact to excite or sense vibrations. We demonstrate layout recovery across various boxes and single- and multiple-object scenes, with generalization to unseen object instances, positions, orientations, and weights, as well as changes in laser placement and excitation source. Our analysis reveals that informative frequency bands need not coincide with the box's resonances and that the learned latent space captures object placement and supports arithmetic operations. These results demonstrate the potential of remote vibration sensing to infer spatial layouts hidden from view.

title: Scattering by Small Ice Crystals in Turbulence: From Orientation Statistics to Retrieval Biases
abstract: Ice-cloud retrievals from polarimetric radar, lidar and submillimeter radiometry commonly assume random orientation, horizontal alignment or a prescribed flutter angle. We link the orientation dynamics of ice crystals to their scattering. Fluid-inertial torque turns small settling crystals broadside on, and turbulent velocity gradients turn them away, so their orientation depends on the dissipation rate. We combine a closed-form orientation distribution for overdamped spheroids, including rotational diffusion and turbulence intermittency, with orientation-averaged Rayleigh, Rayleigh--Gans, T-matrix and specular scattering. Turbulence enters the scattering only through the Legendre moments of the orientation distribution. In the Rayleigh regime the specific differential phase follows crystal alignment, so assuming perfectly horizontal crystals biases ice-water-content retrievals low. Combining the specific differential phase with differential reflectivity limits this bias to $25\%$ for a single size of the shapes studied. For size distributions that span the alignment transition the bound can fail, because the two observables weight sizes differently. Depolarization adds sensitivity to higher-order moments and to intermittency. At finite size the second orientation moment mainly controls the scattering cross sections and the asymmetry parameter, and for optically soft crystals its contribution vanishes $54.7^\circ$ from the vertical. Specular returns from partly aligned plates should persist for lidars pointed $3^\circ$ from nadir. An exploratory analysis of EarthCARE lidar data finds a weakly depolarizing, low-lidar-ratio signature most frequent near $-11^\circ$C, where plates grow. Degree-scale tilt widths inferred from glints and lidar require larger crystals, near or beyond the validity range of the model.

title: Intelligent Imaging of Thermal Transport in Nanostructures
abstract: The ability to measure thermal properties and visualize heat transport processes with high spatial resolution is becoming increasingly important for materials discovery, next-generation electronics, and advanced manufacturing. As critical dimensions and architectures of novel materials and high performance electronics shrink and become more heterogeneous, thermal transport is no longer governed by bulk material properties alone, but by local variations in microstructure, such as interfaces and defects, while the operating conditions can also play a role. With the development of non-contact pump-probe thermoreflectance techniques, specific heat, thermal conductivity, and interface conductance can be mapped either through wide-field thermos-reflectance images or by scanning technique. However, key challenges remain such as the balance between imaging throughput and measurement accuracy, the extraction of multiple parameters with high confidence, and non-intrusive subsurface characterization, etc. This Review highlights recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI)-assistance in high-throughput data processing, visualizing interfacial thermal transport, and nonintrusive subsurface analysis, and offers outlooks for future research directions such as spectral mapping of heat carriers, three-dimensional property mapping, and AI-agentic experimental designs. We anticipate this Review will motivate future efforts in combining AI with experimental techniques to achieve unprecedented capabilities for thermal characterization of nanoscale materials and device characterization, facilitating materials discovery and electronics revolution.

title: From Attention to Semantics: Detecting and Mitigating Sound Event Hallucinations in Large Audio-Language Models
abstract: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) excel at diverse audio tasks, yet remain prone to hallucinating sound events absent from the input. Prior work links such hallucinations to insufficient audio attention. However, we find that real and hallucinated events can receive comparable audio attention mass while attending to different audio positions. To examine whether the attended representations support the generated events, we adapt LatentLens to retrieve neighboring contextualized text representations. The retrieved contexts reveal semantic support for real events, but a semantic mismatch between hallucinated events and their attended audio representations. Directly masking the corresponding audio regions can suppress hallucinated events at the cost of real content. We are motivated by these findings to introduce an explainable and training-free detect-then-mitigate framework for effectively hallucination detection and mitigation that aggregates semantic support and applies differential audio masking to protect regions associated with events predicted to be supported. Extensive experiments on three LALMs and two datasets demonstrate that our method significantly improves hallucination detection and hallucination mitigation performance.

title: Personalized Privacy-Aware MARL Offloading in the Edge-Cloud Continuum
abstract: Task offloading in End-Edge-Cloud computing enables resource-constrained User Devices (UDs) to execute computation-intensive applications with reduced latency and energy consumption. However, existing task offloading schemes generally overlook the heterogeneous privacy requirements of users, leading to inefficient privacy-aware offloading decisions. In this paper, we propose a personalized privacy-aware task offloading framework, where the privacy requirement of each task is quantified through a User-Centric Privacy (UCP) model that considers task sensitivity, user privacy preferences, and task urgency. The task offloading problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to jointly optimize the offloading ratio and the target computing server while minimizing the long-term system cost under latency, energy, and privacy constraints. To efficiently solve the resulting high-dimensional continuous optimization problem, we develop an Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithm under the Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves lower average system cost, lower energy consumption, and higher task success rate than representative baselines under diverse privacy requirements.

title: Helices at Twisted Ferroelectric Interfaces
abstract: We report that twisted interfaces, formed between two ferroelectric lithium niobate single crystals, contain arrays of coherently bonded and elastically deformed nanoscale structural helices, separated from one another by screw dislocations. The helices generate remarkable contrast in four dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM) and through related differential phase contrast (DPC). Such images have been successfully rationalised by modelling the trajectory of electrons that channel along helical pathways as they traverse the interface, but the structural helices implied have also been directly imaged using electron ptychography. Importantly, as lithium niobate is a uniaxial ferroelectric, the torsional strain in these structural helices necessarily also causes dipolar helices to form, inferred through consideration of pertinent piezoelectric tensors and flexoelectric coefficients. Helices are topologically distinct from the more commonly reported vortices and, importantly, they are chiral. Helical (and hence chiral) character was confirmed by observing that DPC images were identical before and after the sample was inverted. Chirality was also established through second harmonic optical circularly-polarised dichroism measurements, in which unusually large interfacial signals were seen. It must be stressed that the arrays of helices observed are distinct from moiré patterns; they facilitate lattice rotation combining plastic and elastic deformation and are not simply a superposition of lattices, twisted with respect to one another. Thus, intimately bonded twisted oxide interfaces will have distinctly different characteristics from those of twisted stacks of two-dimensional van der Waals materials, opening up a new and distinct kind of twistronics.

title: LINEAGE: A Benchmark for Empirical Lineage Retrieval in AI Scientific Literature
abstract: Current research agents are moving beyond academic search toward literature synthesis and experiment planning. These workflows increasingly rely on literature retrieval systems, which serve as standalone systems or as components of research agents. However, existing scientific literature retrieval benchmarks mainly evaluate these methods using topical relevance or citation links as supervision, which cannot capture which prior methods are used for empirical comparison. To address this gap, we introduce Lineage, a benchmark for empirical lineage retrieval in AI scientific literature. An empirical lineage relation links a prior paper to a source paper that explicitly uses its method as an empirical comparison baseline. These relations form lineage graphs whose multi-hop neighborhoods provide retrieval ground truth for structural evaluation. To construct these graphs at scale, we develop Lineage-Constructor, which converts heterogeneous paper records and full-paper empirical baseline evidence into calibrated lineage graphs. Built from 121,048 papers across 17 top AI venues from 2018 to 2025, Lineage contains 3,950 graph components, 67,502 paper nodes, 164,948 lineage edges, and 80,000 multi-facet retrieval queries. Experiments with 19 representative retrieval systems show that empirical lineage retrieval remains challenging. Performance drops sharply with lineage distance, while structural metrics reveal that isolated retrieval hits often fail to recover closely connected empirical comparison neighborhoods.

title: Generalist Meets Specialists: An Evolving Multimodal Agent with Persistent Tool Orchestration for Traffic Scenario Understanding
abstract: Traffic scenario understanding requires combining fine-grained visual evidence with spatial and temporal reasoning. Tool-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) can use specialized perception tools, but effective collaboration faces two challenges: terminal rewards provide limited guidance for intermediate decisions and error recovery, while repeated planning adds unnecessary cost across similar tasks. Echoing the fast-slow dichotomy of human cognition, we propose StarTV-Agent, which combines policy learning with experience evolution to support adaptive reasoning when needed and efficient reuse of prior experience when possible. During training, Role-Sensitive Process Optimization (RSPO) combines process advantages with terminal advantages, while Weakness-Driven Demonstration Learning (WDL) provides validated teacher demonstrations targeting the student's weak questions. During inference, Lightweight Adaptive Workflow Reuse (LAWR) enables a fast path by selecting suitable workflows and binding task-specific arguments and resource references, while a slow ReAct-based path handles tasks without suitable workflows. We further design label-free feedback based on execution completion, workflow adoption, and cost savings to guide workflow reuse and memory updates. Across three challenging benchmarks, StarTV-Agent achieves up to 8.0% relative performance improvement, while reducing token consumption by up to 52.1%.

title: Trustworthy Geospatial AI Workflows: Reproducible Maritime Analytics and Forecasting on Open-Source AIS Data
abstract: Publicly available geospatial data provide increasing opportuni- ties for data-driven maritime analytics and predictive modelling.
