ProtoDiffusion jointly denoises the prototype and a fixed set of candidate slots, conditioned on an image or text, with bounding boxes as optional layout guidance. The model leaves unneeded slots empty and determines the number of layers and, in absence of boxes, their layout, requiring neither as input. The same architecture supports both image-to-design and text-to-design. ProtoVAE achieves high-fidelity reconstruction from its compact shared latent representation, reaching 40.43 dB PSNR on layer crops. On the LayerD evaluation split, image-to-design achieves RGB L1 scores of 0.040 with bounding boxes and 0.057 without, with box-guided alpha soft IoU (0.850) comparable to the strongest fine-tuned baseline (0.871). On merged images, text-to-design reaches 66.41 FID versus 86.84 for FLUX.2 [klein], achieves a 0.860 text-accuracy score, and runs $19.1\times$ faster than the same-backbone generation-then-decomposition cascade.

title: A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
abstract: Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact. In particular, we explain how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes. We distinguish equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep. We examine the existence and uniqueness of motion and contact forces, including the solver's role in selecting among multiple solutions. We then compare first-order and Newton-based methods, explain regularization and proximal strategies, and discuss trade-offs between computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity. Connections to widely used simulators, optimal control, and differentiable simulation help readers interpret simulation results, choose suitable formulations and solvers, and develop their own contact dynamics routines.

title: BRUCE (Bayesian Rio Urban Climate Estimator): spatiotemporal interpolation of air temperature from heterogeneous sensor networks for operational heat monitoring
abstract: Accurate characterization of intra-urban temperature variability is essential for heat-health surveillance, yet official monitoring networks are too sparse to resolve fine-scale gradients, particularly in Global South cities. We present BRUCE, a Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model, fitted with the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA) and a Stochastic Partial Differential Equation (SPDE) spatial component, that fuses four heterogeneous temperature sources for Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: official weather stations, low-cost IoT sensors, citizen-science personal weather stations and ERA5-Land reanalysis. The model accounts for class- and station-specific measurement bias and estimates a continuous spatial field that evolves day to day through an autoregressive (AR1) structure. Fitted independently to nine monthly windows (January, June, November; 2023--2025), the elevation coefficient was significant in all windows and of consistent magnitude in eight ($-$1.08 to $-$1.38 \textdegree{}C per SD). In leave-region-out cross-validation against LCZ4r, accuracy was comparable (RMSE differences within station-level bootstrap uncertainty in all three windows), while BRUCE produced predictions at every held-out station, including those where LCZ4r is masked, and preserved finer-scale spatial structure than LCZ4r's discrete zone classification. Applied to 241 primary care territories, BRUCE's posterior exceedance probabilities allowed 96 to be classified with high confidence (model-based classifications), whereas a constant-width interval derived from LCZ4r cross-validation errors supported confident classification of none. The framework offers a statistically principled, operationally viable basis for intra-urban heat monitoring in data-heterogeneous settings.

title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
abstract: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.

title: Posterior Matching Distillation
abstract: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

title: Digital Agriculture and Plant Genomics for Predictive Breeding
abstract: Digital sensing, genomic prediction and increasingly accessible computational methods are changing how crop breeders observe environments, characterise genetic variation and prioritise candidate varieties. Yet the central question is not whether more data improve predictive fit, but whether combining information sources produces reliable, timely and economically worthwhile selection decisions outside the circumstances in which models were trained. This critical narrative review examines the convergence of plant genomics, field phenomics, environmental characterisation and artificial intelligence in predictive breeding. Peer-reviewed research and methodological literature published from 2001 to 11 September 2026 were critically selected through accessible scholarly sources and citation tracing, with attention to empirical comparisons, validation design and translational relevance. Genomic prediction provides a well-established foundation, whereas phenomic and environmental covariates yield more conditional benefits. Contrasting wheat studies illustrate that spectral and thermal information can improve prediction in some settings but can also introduce noise or fail under forward validation. Environmental descriptors become more informative when aligned with developmental stage and the target population of environments; flexible machine-learning architectures do not consistently outperform appropriately specified statistical baselines. Structural variation, pangenomes, multi-omics and genomic language models broaden the biological information available to breeders, although evidence of additional realised genetic gain remains limited for several emerging approaches. Major weaknesses include information leakage, unrepresentative validation partitions, incompatible field metadata, uncertainty neglected during selection, and scarce evaluation of operational costs and varietal delivery. The review develops a decision-centred framework in which data collection, model complexity and evaluation are governed by the breeding decision and the information genuinely available at that point. The strongest near-term opportunities lie in prospective multi-environment validation, careful phenomic measurement, stage-aware environmental modelling and interoperable datasets. Predictive breeding is therefore best understood as a disciplined integration of biological understanding, field experimentation and statistical evidence, not as a replacement for them.

title: Coordinated Use of Large Language Models in Academic Research
abstract: This study proposes a methodological framework for the coordinated use of multiple large language models in academic research. Its central argument is that involving more models does not in itself guarantee more reliable results; what matters is how cognitive and verification operations are organised. The framework is based on seven principles (procedural independence, functional allocation, the diagnostic value of divergence, the diagnostic value of convergence, external verification, proportionality of checking, and human epistemic responsibility) and sets out a non-linear multi-LLM protocol in which independently obtained results are compared, critically examined and, where necessary, verified against external sources. The approach is illustrated through real-world cases drawn from research practice. The study concludes that moving from a single language model to a coordinated multi-LLM process represents a change in the organisation of research, in which the researcher makes the final decisions and bears scholarly responsibility.

title: Model Terpadu Pemberdayaan Desa Berbasis Green Economy melalui Hilirisasi Nilam dan Perlebahan di Desa Lambadeuk, Aceh Besar
abstract: Lambadeuk Village, Aceh Besar Regency, possesses patchouli and linot (stingless bee) honey potential that remains underutilized for economic value addition. Partner groups face challenges such as limited processing technology, absent SOPs, low capacity, weak business governance, and restricted market access. This community initiative aims to establish a green economy-based empowerment model through appropriate technology, capacity building, and product downstreaming. Carried out with the Benteng Makmur Farmer Group and KTH Lestari Alam, activities employed a participatory method spanning problem identification to evaluation. Benteng Makmur was facilitated with a stainless-steel steam distillation unit and patchouli processing SOPs, while KTH Lestari Alam received additional linot bee colonies and harvesting SOPs. The initiative improved community capacity, production self-reliance, and value-added opportunities. The added colonies are targeted to increase honey production by up to 50%, while the distillation unit underpins high-value patchouli oil development. Integrating appropriate technology, standardization, and green economy principles effectively supports sustainable village-level enterprises.

Ecological Responses of Intertidal Microalgal Communities to Repeated Freshwater Inundation
abstract: Intertidal ecosystems are characterized by frequent environmental changes caused by tidal dynamics, precipitation, river runoff, and coastal hydrology. Frequent inundations of fresh water constitute one of the environmental disturbances that change salinity, nutrient status, sediments, and physiological processes affecting the intertidal microalgae. Intertidal microalgal communities, especially benthic diatoms, play an important role in primary production, nutrient recycling, sediments stabilization, and energy flows in coastal ecosystems. The present conceptual study attempts to identify the possible ecological reactions of intertidal microalgal communities to repeated flooding by integrating hydrologic disturbance, physiological adaptation, community reorganization, and ecosystem function into one framework. Inundation frequency, duration, intensity, and recovery periods are recognized as main environmental factors affecting community reactions. Osmoregulation, salinity tolerance of individual taxa, community structure, functional diversity, photosynthesis, and microbiological interactions are all emphasized. The theoretical model suggests that the continuous flooding with freshwater may lead to various effects based on the level of disturbance frequency, salt content of the ecosystem, nature of sediments, availability of nutrients, and adaptation mechanisms in microalgae. In addition, the conceptual framework emphasizes the value of making a distinction between short-term physiological response and long-term community reorganization. The framework serves as a basis for future experimental work and the development of microalgal indicators for hydrological disturbances.

title: Seasonal Variation in Seagrass Epiphyte Communities and their Contribution to Coastal Primary Productivity
abstract: Seagrass ecosystems are significant coastal ecosystems where biodiversity, nutrient cycles, carbon sequestration, and primary production processes are carried out. Epiphytic communities living on seagrass leaves play a significant role in photosynthesis and ecological interactions in seagrass ecosystems. The biomass and productivity of epiphytic communities are influenced by seasonal changes in temperature, nutrients, penetration of light through water, and biological interactions. In the current study, seasonal variation in seagrass epiphytes is studied, and their contribution to coastal primary productivity is evaluated using simulation-based research method. Four seasons, namely pre-monsoon, monsoon, post-monsoon, and winter, were taken into consideration to study seasonal changes in environmental factors, biomass of epiphytes, and primary productivity. A simulated data set of 120 samples was constructed based on predetermined seasonal factors and variability of ecological factors. Mathematical models have been used to determine the biomass density, photosynthetic productivity, and relative importance of epiphytes in the overall ecosystem productivity. The simulations show that the biomass and productivity of the epiphytes are not consistent throughout the year; the post-monsoon season shows the greatest biomass and photosynthetic productivity. Availability of nutrients and underwater lighting influence the development of epiphytes, while environmental suitability influences their productivity dynamics. This leads to the creation of a mathematical base that explains the significance of epiphytes in relation to seagrasses ecologically and serves as a foundation for further research on coastal ecosystems productivity.

title: Ecological Interactions Between Mangrove Leaf Litter and Detritus-Feeding Coastal Organisms
abstract: Mangrove ecosystem is essential in preserving coastal ecological equilibrium by means of nutrient recycling, organic matter decomposition, and creation of habitats. The leaf litter of mangroves is one of the important sources of organic carbon and nutrients required for detritus feeders such as crabs, amphipods, molluscs, polychaetes, and microorganisms. Nevertheless, the quality of leaf litter, rates of decomposition, environmental conditions, and preferences of diet affect the effectiveness of the ecological interaction. The necessity of the present research emerges due to the increase of coastal disturbances and insufficient knowledge about the influence of characteristics of mangrove leaf litter on food web of the detritus. The uniqueness of the present research project is connected with the creation of the ecological model that links leaf litter production, its decomposition, microbial modification, and feeding behavior of detritivores. The methodological approach suggested is based on comparative ecological assessment of litter production, decomposition experiments, taxonomic classification of organisms, their feeding behavior, and physicochemical properties of water and sediments. This review attempts to explore the impact of litter quality and environmental variability on the detritivores' feeding process as well as the movement of organic material among different mangrove sites. It is believed that the suggested framework will help better understand the role of detritivores in nutrient cycling, sedimentation, and food-web dynamics within the mangrove ecosystems.

title: Mapping Ecological Connectivity among Isolated Freshwater Habitats Using Landscape-Based Spatial Analysis
abstract: Ponds, tanks, wetlands and small lakes are examples of freshwater ecosystems which house aquatic diversity. However, agriculture, urban development and drainage systems continue to cause fragmentation of these ecosystems. In this study, a spatial methodology based on a landscape approach that employs remote sensing, GIS, landscape metrics, least cost path analysis and graph theory was developed to map connectivity between isolated freshwater habitats in a 100 km² landscape. A total of 24 patches amounting to 3.84% of the total landscape were mapped, while 58.33% were found to be isolated. There were nine least cost corridors and habitat patches H03 and H10 were identified as important corridors. An ecosystem restoration scenario increased the Probability of Connectivity from 18.60% to 31.40%. The framework supports corridor restoration and conservation prioritization.

title: A Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Real-Time Cyberattack Detection in Internet of Things Networks
abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) networks introduces significant cybersecurity challenges because connected sensors, gateways, and embedded controllers operate with limited memory, processing capacity, and energy. Conventional intrusion detection solutions may impose computational costs that exceed the capabilities of these devices, while cloud-only analysis adds latency and creates privacy concerns. This narrative review develops a conceptual lightweight deep learning framework for real-time cyberattack detection at the IoT edge. The proposed architecture combines flow-based feature extraction, selective preprocessing, a compact one-dimensional convolutional network, calibrated risk scoring, and adaptive response at the gateway. It discusses feature selection, class imbalance, model compression, data drift, adversarial resilience, and deployment constraints. An illustrative design chart compares qualitative trade-offs between model classes; it does not represent measured experimental findings. The article outlines an evaluation protocol using reproducible train-test separation, device-aware latency measurement, and cross-dataset validation. The central conclusion is that practical reliability requires jointly optimizing detection quality, false-alarm burden, inference time, memory use, and operational maintainability rather than accuracy alone.

title: Evaluating Software Quality Through Automated Testing and Predictive Defect Detection Using Machine Learning
abstract: Software quality assurance increasingly depends on the ability to combine automated testing with data-driven estimates of defect risk. Conventional test suites reveal failures in executed scenarios but do not necessarily identify which untested changes are most likely to introduce faults. Machine learning models can prioritize code review and testing by learning associations between historical defect outcomes, code structure, change activity, and process characteristics. This narrative review synthesizes established research on software defect prediction and proposes a transparent evaluation framework integrating data preparation, temporal validation, calibrated prediction, risk-based test selection, and continuous monitoring. It distinguishes test effectiveness from model discrimination and emphasizes precision–recall analysis, operational cost, data leakage prevention, and human oversight. A conceptual graph illustrates how testing effort might be redistributed according to predicted risk; it does not represent measured experimental outcomes. The paper argues that machine learning should supplement rather than replace automated tests, and that deployment claims require prospective, project-specific evidence. Limitations include incomplete defect labels, shifting development practices, class imbalance, and uncertain cross-project transferability

title: A Threshold‐Based Episodic Recharge Component for Semi‐Arid Process‐Based Isotope‐Enabled Hydrological Modelling
abstract: Conceptual isotope‐enabled rainfall–runoff models are used to improve hydrological process understanding, but simulations of sub‐surface recharge are often inconsistent as they conceptualise the process as continuous in time and therefore likely overestimate water fluxes between the soil‐water and groundwater stores. Based on stable water isotope evidence that aquifer recharge happens episodically, once soils are sufficiently wet, here we develop a new episodic recharge component, gated by root‐zone soil moisture, within a combined isotope enabled climate and hydrological model for a semi‐arid catchment of the Eerste River, South Africa. We contrast the impact of the new component on baseflow simulations against a standard hydrological (J2000) model, its isotope‐enabled version (J2000‐iso), as well as the impact on the simulation of the Young Water Fraction ( F YW ) metric. The models are driven by bias‐corrected spatially‐distributed precipitation isotopes from the Regional Spectral Model IsoRSM (10 km). The simulated streamflow across all the models was largely consistent with Nash‐Sutcliffe Efficiencies of between 0.53 and 0.78 for the headwater (24 km 2 ) and downstream (328 km 2 ) calibration and validation periods. Stream isotope simulation performance with Kling‐Gupta Efficiencies of between 0.20–0.29 were better for the episodic recharge model, and with more of the seasonal precipitation isotope signal reaching the stream. Streamflow performance was, however, not sensitive to the new episodic recharge component, but the episodic recharge model simulated different flow components and a higher F YW than J2000‐iso. The new episodic recharge component, whilst relatively simple in nature, changes the simulated flow components relative to the J2000 models.

title: Bullying Situational Cues and Adolescents' Bystander Behaviors: Associations With Empathy and Moral Disengagement.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Bystander defending behaviors are regarded as a key component in preventing bullying among adolescents. Although previous research has primarily focused on individual factors influencing bystander behaviors, less is known about whether the way a bullying episode is presented, and the socio-emotional information available through that presentation, is associated with adolescents' bystander responses. To address this issue, the present study examined how empathy, moral disengagement, and the presentation modality of a traditional bullying episode were associated with bystander behaviors. METHODS In the pre-study, a factor analysis was conducted with 789 students, which revealed four stable bystander behavior dimensions in traditional bullying: aggressive defending, constructive defending, remaining an outsider, and reinforcing the bully. A subsequent behavioral experiment was conducted with an independent sample of 366 students, in which the same bullying episode was presented through three modalities: text, audio, and video. Participants' bystander behaviors, empathy (affective and cognitive), and moral disengagement were then measured. RESULTS Two-part models, distinguishing the occurrence and intensity of each bystander response, showed that presentation modality was associated with several bystander responses. Compared with text, audio and video were associated with a higher likelihood of constructive defending; audio was associated with a higher likelihood of aggressive defending; and audio and video were associated with greater intensity of aggressive defending. Audio was also associated with lower intensity of remaining an outsider and a lower likelihood of reinforcing the bully. Affective empathy and moral disengagement showed differentiated associations across the four bystander response dimensions. CONCLUSION These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing bystander response dimensions and considering how socio-emotional information is presented when examining adolescents' responses to traditional bullying.

title: EncNovo: De Novo Peptide Sequencing With an Encoder-Only Architectures.
abstract: RATIONALE De novo peptide sequencing enables interpretation of tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) data without relying on sequence databases and is valuable for analyzing proteins from unknown species. However, existing Transformer-based approaches may not fully exploit interactions among precursor information, spectral features, and sequence prediction tokens, potentially limiting sequencing performance. METHODS We developed EncNovo, a nonautoregressive de novo peptide sequencing model based on a BERT-inspired encoder-only Transformer architecture. Precursor attributes, spectral peaks, and sequence prediction tokens are jointly encoded within a unified encoder, enabling continuous interaction among the three throughout the encoding process. A residual attention mechanism and a peak mass-difference inductive bias were further incorporated into the self-attention framework to encode amino acid residue mass relationships between spectral peaks. RESULTS Experimental results on the nine-species benchmark dataset demonstrate that EncNovo improves peptide recall at 100% coverage by 5.10 and 4.18 percentage points on average compared with Casanovo and RefineNovo, respectively. The model also achieved higher amino acid recall and demonstrated faster convergence during training. CONCLUSIONS Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed encoder-only framework, combined with residual attention and a peak mass-difference inductive bias, effectively improves peptide recall and accelerates model convergence. Collectively, these advantages make EncNovo a reliable framework for de novo peptide sequencing in proteomics.
journal: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM

title: Factors Affecting the Climate Change Adaptation Strategies of Coffee Farmers: Evidence From Vietnam
abstract: The impact of climate change on agriculture has been recognized as a prominent global issue and has negatively affected the livelihoods of many agricultural households worldwide. This paper aims to explore the factors influencing coffee farmers' behavior in choosing adaptation strategies to climate change in Vietnam, the second‐largest coffee producer in the world. Random Utility Theory and the Sustainable Livelihoods Framework are used to develop the theoretical foundation of the research model. Primary data were collected from 314 Vietnamese coffee farms to conduct this study. Unlike previous results, this study shows that most farmers (93.9%) confirmed that the climate has been changing rapidly, and that the cost of coffee production has increased due to the adoption of adaptation strategies (95.5%). The findings suggest that surplus labor on farms is an obstacle to selecting adaptation strategies due to the currently large household labor size. A large farmland area is a factor that encourages adaptation through technical improvements, including new varieties, planting schedules, and technologies. Moreover, technology and credit services are crucial catalysts for effectively transforming the coffee industry's adaptation to climate change in the future. Farmers' access to updated information on climate change also promotes the adoption of strategies. However, training activities have shown low effectiveness, as farmers who attended climate‐change training classes have not yet implemented appropriate adaptation measures. Finally, the paper provides several policy implications to enhance farmers' adaptation to climate change in the future.

title: eQt Protein Nanocage-Delivered IL-21 mRNA Systemically Reprograms Host Immune Cells Toward Stemness and Maturation to Achieve Anti-Tumor Immunity.
Machine learning interatomic potentials and orientational defects in polymers
abstract: Photopolymerization of acrylated epoxidized soybean oil (AESO) is a convenient model of a self-organizing process in a soft, bio-based material: ultraviolet light starts a free-radical chain reaction, the growing network releases heat, and the mobility of molecular groups changes on several time scales at once. We follow this process from two sides. Experimentally, the real and imaginary parts of the dielectric permittivity of an AESO:VDM (1:0.5) mixture with 3 mol% of the photoinitiator DMPA were recorded at 500-5000 Hz under an intermittent on/off illumination protocol, and the resulting time series were analysed with a sliding-window Shannon entropy and the Grassberger-Procaccia correlation integral. Both measures show that short light pulses at the start of curing trigger strongly correlated, collective relaxation, which fades as the network forms, leaving only localized reorientations active. We describe these reorientations as orientational defects and quantify their energetics with the MACE-OFF23 machine learning interatomic potential, using relaxed dihedral scans of five rotational modes ($α$, $α/β$, $β$, $γ$, $δ$) of an AESO fragment. Compared with density functional theory (DFT) reference profiles, MACE reproduces the shape of all five profiles (Pearson $r=0.95$-$0.98$) and the hierarchy of barriers - from 2.9 eV for the constrained main-chain rotation, through 0.54-0.81 eV for the acrylate rotations, to 0.16-0.18 eV for the methyl and 0.06 eV for the hydroxyl rotation - while underestimating the barrier heights by 3-20%. A simple Arrhenius estimate shows that the acrylate rotations are the modes closest to the frequency window of the dielectric measurement.

title: Optimization of vermicompost and water management for greenhouse tomato in Northeast China based on the CRITIC-VIKOR model
abstract: Protected cultivation plays a dominant role in winter vegetable production. However, long-term continuous cropping in greenhouses can easily lead to soil degradation, which not only reduces vegetable yields and fruit quality but also hinders the sustainable facility agriculture. It is urgent to explore feasible strategies to ameliorate greenhouse soil environments, coordinate high crop yield with superior fruit quality, and advance the sustainable progress of protected horticulture. Therefore, we selected tomatoes—a common horticultural crop, as the subject of our study. Using an ETgage evapotranspiration atmometer to control irrigation and applying different amounts of vermicompost for experimental study. The experimental design was a two-factor randomized block design with three levels of vermicompost application: 150 t ha− 1 (V1), 300 t ha− 1 (V2), 450 t ha− 1 (V3), and three levels of irrigation: 0.6 ETgage (W1), 0.8 ETgage (W2), and 1.0 ETgage (W3). The application of vermicompost could reduce soil bulk density and improve soil water-holding capacity by increasing organic matter content and improving soil aggregation and pore structure. It could also further promote crop growth, leading to improvements in fruit yield, quality, and water productivity. In terms of irrigation impacts, appropriate reductions in irrigation could improve yield, quality, and water productivity of tomatoes, but could reduce the photosynthetic capacity of tomato leaves. The results of CRITIC-VIKOR evaluation model show that V3W1 was the best treatment in terms of overall benefits for greenhouse tomato, with maximum values of soluble sugars (SS), total soluble solids (TSS), sugar-acid ratio (SAR) and water productivity (WP), as well as better yields and organic acids (OA) under this treatment. Compared to V3W3, the greenhouse management method using V3W1 could save 40% of the irrigation amount, with a yield reduction of less than 12%. In addition, comparisons between models indicate that the CRITIC-VIKOR model exhibited better stability and universality compared to EWTOPSIS (Entropy Weight Method and TOPSIS). This study demonstrates that in the cold regions, using greenhouse cultivation of crops, applying 450 t ha− 1 vermicompost and irrigating with 60% ETgage atmometer of water can effectively improve the quality of continuous cropping soil and achieve sustainable development in facility agriculture.

title: Implementation of digital pathology AI in routine clinical breast pathology practice.
abstract: The convergence of whole-slide imaging (WSI), digital pathology, and artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming routine breast pathology practice. Experiences from multiple institutions have demonstrated that successful clinical deployment requires robust digital infrastructure, seamless laboratory information system integration, standardized validation, and close collaboration between pathologists and information technology teams. Following the successful implementation of a digital pathology workflow, AI has emerged as a realistic tool for routine pathology practice. Artificial intelligence applications in breast pathology have evolved from automated detection of lymph node metastases and quantitative analysis of breast biomarkers to diagnostic classification of breast lesions and prediction of treatment response and clinical outcome. Artificial intelligence-assisted workflows can reduce pathologist review time and unnecessary ancillary testing while maintaining high diagnostic performance. Rather than replacing pathologists, AI functions as an intelligent decision-support tool that enhances efficiency, reproducibility, and quality. This review summarizes current strategies for implementing digital pathology AI in routine breast pathology practice, highlights clinically validated applications, discusses practical implementation considerations, and outlines future directions toward foundation models and agentic AI systems that may further automate pathology workflows.

title: Weighing the hazards: body mass index and recurrence in early-onset colorectal cancer
abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC, < 50 years) is rising sharply. The obesity paradox, where overweight correlates with better outcomes despite obesity being a risk factor, has been reported in colorectal cancer (CRC), mainly for overall survival, but its relevance to recurrence and to EOCRC specifically remains unclear. We investigated the association between body mass index (BMI) at diagnosis and risk of recurrence in EOCRC compared to average-onset colorectal cancer (AOCRC, ≥ 50 years). This retrospective cohort study at Sahlgrenska University Hospital included 1821 patients who underwent radical surgery with curative intent for colorectal adenocarcinoma between 2011 and 2019, comprising 158 patients with EOCRC and 1663 with AOCRC. Cox models of recurrence were adjusted for tumour stage and location and stratified by differentiation. BMI was modelled with restricted cubic splines, and overall association and nonlinearity were assessed with likelihood-ratio tests (LRTs). In EOCRC, BMI was associated with recurrence (LRT p = 0.048), with a lower hazard among patients in the overweight range, although the test for nonlinearity was not significant (p = 0.08). In AOCRC, no significant association was observed (LRT p = 0.88). The interaction between BMI and cohort was not statistically significant (p = 0.11). BMI at diagnosis was associated with recurrence in EOCRC but not in AOCRC. The observed pattern may be consistent with an obesity paradox in EOCRC. Larger studies incorporating prediagnostic weight and body composition are needed to confirm these findings.

Math Teachers as Cultural Agents: Motivational Pathways and Gender Differences in STEM Major Choice
abstract: This study examines how teacher-related cultural resources in high school mathematics are associated with students’ subsequent STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) major choices, with attention to gender differences. Mathematics is examined as a foundational subject for STEM learning and a potential gateway to advanced STEM pathways. Drawing on cultural capital, expectancy-value, and identity perspectives, we examine associations among teacher-related resources, students’ mathematics-related motivational beliefs, and subsequent STEM major choice. Using the High School Longitudinal Study of 2009 (HSLS:09), we examined a sample of 11,749 students using exploratory factor analysis and structural equation modeling, including gender-specific models and adjustment for ninth-grade mathematics performance. Supportive mathematics classroom environments were positively associated with mathematics identity, utility, self-efficacy, and interest. Mathematics identity and utility were positively associated with STEM major choice after accounting for mathematics performance, whereas self-efficacy and interest were not significantly associated with this outcome. Identity showed the strongest association among the motivational beliefs. Both identity and utility were associated with STEM major choice for female and male students, without statistically significant gender differences in these paths. Selected teacher-related pathways and the association between mathematics performance and STEM major choice differed by gender. These findings highlight the relevance of supportive mathematics classroom environments and differentiated motivational pathways for understanding subsequent STEM major choice. They offer implications for mathematics teaching and teacher development while underscoring the need for caution in drawing causal conclusions from observational data.
journal: International Journal of Science and Mathematics Education

title: Generative AI-Enhanced STEM-Education: Investigating Teachers’ Experiences from Implementation in Primary School Settings
abstract: This pilot study explores the integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into primary STEM education in Sweden through a structured Teacher Professional Development (TPD) model. While GenAI tools such as ChatGPT and Copilot have rapidly entered educational contexts, empirical research on their pedagogical use in primary schools remains limited. Eleven teachers participated in a six-month TPD programme comprising workshops, collaborative discussions, and classroom implementations. The empirical material consisted primarily of audio-recorded workshop discussions, which were transcribed and analysed, supplemented by a post-intervention questionnaire. Data were analysed using thematic coding informed by the Refined Consensus Model (RCM) and the Digital Promise AI Literacy Framework. Findings indicate that GenAI served primarily as an idea generator, supporting lesson planning and interdisciplinary integration across mathematics and science. Teachers reported opportunities for timesaving, differentiated instruction, and enhanced creativity, alongside challenges related to mathematical inaccuracies, unrealistic time estimates, and the need for contextual adaptation. The TPD model facilitated growth in pedagogical content knowledge and AI literacy, fostering confidence and critical engagement with GenAI tools. These results underscore the potential of structured professional development to bridge the gap between emerging technologies and classroom practice. Future research should extend implementation duration, include student perspectives, and address ethical and equity considerations in AI integration.

title: Differentiated responses of ecosystem service supply and demand to urbanization across urban–rural gradients: a case study of the Yangtze River Delta, China
abstract: Urbanization is closely associated with changes in ecosystem services, but how the relationships between urbanization and ecosystem service supply and demand vary along urban–rural gradients remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the relationships between urbanization and ecosystem service supply and demand across urban–rural gradients and to provide evidence for landscape planning and sustainable management in rapidly urbanizing regions. We assessed the supply, demand, and supply–demand ratios of four ecosystem services—water yield, carbon sequestration, habitat quality, and soil conservation—in China’s Yangtze River Delta region (YRDR) in 2000, 2010, and 2020. Spearman’s rank correlation analysis was used to identify associations between urbanization and ecosystem service supply, demand, and supply–demand ratios across urban–rural gradients. Random forest and SHAP analyses were then used to evaluate the relative explanatory contributions of urbanization indicators and their nonlinear associations. (1) Ecosystem service supply and demand showed marked spatial mismatches across the YRDR. With increasing urbanization, habitat quality deficits deepened and soil conservation surpluses narrowed, whereas the carbon sequestration supply–demand imbalance was alleviated in old urban areas. Water-yield supply–demand patterns were sensitive to the method used to spatialize demand. All urban–rural gradients showed surpluses when sectoral water demand was allocated to the corresponding land-use types. In contrast, supply–demand pressure increased markedly in highly urbanized areas when demand was allocated by population density. (2) Urbanization indicators were generally negatively correlated with ecosystem service supply and supply–demand ratios, with stronger correlations in rural areas. Except for soil conservation, demand for the other three services was mostly positively correlated with urbanization indicators. (3) In 2020, among the seven models that met the spatial predictive-performance criterion, impervious surface proportion had the highest relative explanatory contribution in six. However, conventional urbanization indicators had limited explanatory power in old urban areas and for the supply–demand ratios of water yield and carbon sequestration across most urban–rural gradients. Ecosystem service supply–demand patterns and their associations with urbanization varied with urban–rural landscape context, service type, and the method used to spatialize demand. Landscape planning should consider the spatial configuration of land development and the continuity of ecological spaces, with particular emphasis on development control and landscape connectivity restoration in urban–rural fringes.

title: Ethical and practical challenges of artificial intelligence for sleep and mental health in disability care: a narrative review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored to support sleep and mental health care, yet its role in disability care remains insufficiently synthesised. This narrative review examines the ethical and practical challenges associated with AI applications for sleep and mental health in disability care, with attention to both people with disability and disability support workers. Current applications include wearable and sensor-based sleep monitoring, mood tracking systems, conversational agents, predictive models, and workforce-facing decision-support tools. These technologies may improve early detection, continuous monitoring, personalised support, and care coordination. However, the literature identifies substantial barriers to safe and equitable implementation. Practical challenges include poor accessibility, limited inclusive usability, workflow disruption, variable digital literacy, weak external validation, and concerns about reliability across diverse disability groups. Ethical concerns include privacy and data governance, meaningful informed consent, algorithmic bias, lack of transparency, intrusive surveillance, and the risk of dehumanising care. The evidence base is also limited by overreliance on general mental health AI literature, minimal focus on disability support workers, a lack of longitudinal and implementation research, and insufficient co-design with people with disability. Overall, AI may offer meaningful benefits in disability care, but responsible implementation requires disability-specific evidence, inclusive design, strong governance, human oversight, and sustained commitment to person-centred and rights-based care.

title: Neither human nor machine alone: why the next step in AI needs an ethics core with the last word, and a receipt that proves it holds
abstract: Who is accountable for what an AI system does, and how can that accountability be shown rather than asserted? Human sign-off and the autonomous agent both place the last word in a single party. Following a design science approach, we built and used a third arrangement, the verification interface: human, machine and an explicit ethics core form one construct, the core has the last word over both, and every output carries a tamper-evident receipt showing what was checked. The interface has been in daily use since February 2026 and had issued 12,398 receipts by 10 October 2026. In a sealed blind test on 1798 AI answers checked against company records, its verdicts matched the answer key in 97.1% of cases; a human check of 50 answers on which two AI auditors disagreed confirmed the answer key in 44. A check took a median of 1.9 s. We derive seven design requirements, report which the interface meets, and connect the approach to EU2122, a public content profile for receipts published as an IETF Internet-Draft. The economic hypothesis, that verification per output removes the review bottleneck of AI adoption and raises speed, quality and operating margin together, is stated but not tested. The interface assumes neither that AI is conscious nor that it has moral standing. All evidence comes from one system and is reported by its developer; it shows feasibility and measured accuracy in one domain, not effectiveness across organisations.

Impact of altitudinal climate variability on fruit productivity in the Kumaun Himalaya
abstract: Climate change is altering horticultural productivity in mountain ecosystems, yet region-specific assessments of altitudinal climatic shifts and their impact on fruit yields remain limited. This study examines the long-term climatic trends (1990–2025) across three elevation zones in the Nainital district of the Kumaun Himalaya: Foot Hill ( 1200 m). Climate variations were assessed using the ERA5-Land datasets; we quantified variations in temperature, rainfall, surface latent heat flux, and solar radiation. Analysis revealed significant altitudinal variations, with a consistent warming trend of 0.34 °C per decade observed in the Foot Hill zone. Horticultural data for seven primary crops (Apple, Apricot, Citrus, Mango, Peach, Pear, and Plum) revealed high inter-annual yield volatility, particularly for stone fruits in the Mid-Hill zone (CV% > 100%). Statistical modeling using Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) indicated that climatic variables serve as suggestive drivers, explaining between 13 and 41% of yield variance across different crops, though these models lacked statistical significance (p > 0.05). The remaining variance suggests the substantial influence of non-climatic drivers such as orchard management and physiological stressors. Time-lagged correlation analysis further identified that climatic conditions during the preceding year's bud differentiation period significantly influence subsequent yields. The findings suggest that shifting climatic baselines are eroding traditional fruit belts, necessitating adaptation strategies such as the introduction of low-chilling varieties and enhanced moisture conservation. This research provides a systematic framework for sustainable horticultural planning in the Central Himalayan region.

Bergenin attenuates osteoclast-mediated bone loss by modulating the SIRT1/NF-κB p65 signalling axis.
abstract: Current pharmacological treatments for osteoporosis are often accompanied by clinically significant adverse effects, highlighting the need for safer therapeutic strategies. Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) suppresses inflammatory responses and osteoclast differentiation, suggesting its therapeutic potential. Bergenin is known to activate SIRT1, although its effects on osteoporosis and the underlying mechanism remain unclear. Hence, we aimed to identify a mechanistic rationale for the therapeutic application of bergenin in the treatment of osteoporosis. We first examined SIRT1 expression in femoral tissue from patients with osteopenia and osteoporosis. The role of SIRT1 and efficacy of bergenin were then investigated using myeloid cell-specific SIRT1 knockout (SIRT1fl/fl-LysMCre) mice, ovariectomised models, and osteoclastogenesis in bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) following RANKL stimulation. SIRT1 expression was reduced in osteoporotic femoral tissue, while myeloid cell-specific SIRT1 deficiency aggravated ovariectomy (OVX)-induced bone loss. Bergenin preserved bone microarchitecture and inhibited osteoclast differentiation in OVX mice; these effects were weakened by the SIRT1 inhibitor, EX527. Mechanistically, bergenin activated SIRT1, diminished both the phosphorylation and acetylation of NF-κB p65, prevented NF-κB pathway activation, and suppressed osteoclast differentiation. To our knowledge, this study provides the first clinical evidence linking SIRT1 to osteoporosis in human bone specimens. These findings suggest that bergenin acts through the SIRT1/NF-κB p65 pathway and provide a rationale for developing bergenin as a naturally derived therapy for osteoporosis and related osteoclast-driven skeletal disorders.

Morphogenesis, differentiation, and robust multi-scale organization of the honeybee nest revealed by a novel 4D atlas.
abstract: Morphogenesis is the emergence of structured form. As with cells during embryo development, social insects may follow similar developmental principles when constructing their nest. Here, we present the first four-dimensional (4D) "atlas" of honeybee nest development at per-cell resolution. Colonies showed specialization at the cell and comb scales, analogous to the differentiation of cell types and tissues in embryos. Across colonies, nests had consistent patterns of organization that varied seasonally: cell contents were clustered and stratified with pollen accumulating on one side of the nest and nectar on the other. The directionality of this protein-carbohydrate polarization was reliably predicted by nest initiation point. By the season's end, nests had undergone an organizational metamorphosis, from asymmetrical polarization to a centralized layout. To test the functional importance of this sequenced organization, we experimentally manipulated nest architecture in a subset of colonies (n = 6 of 12) by weekly shuffling the order and orientation of all combs. Shuffled colonies changed what their cells contained more frequently, had more uniform comb-level organization, and lost their nest-level organization but maintained colony-level performance in key metrics (nest contents, worker population, and nest size). Autoregressive modeling showed that intact three-dimensional structure was necessary to accurately predict cell contents from spatial context, and this predictability collapsed under shuffling, suggesting informational benefits of intact architecture. This work shows how developmental principles apply beyond the organismal form to the extended phenotype, offering resilience in collective systems.

Peripheral blood CD99hiPD-1+ T-cell expansion distinguishes early systemic lupus erythematosus.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To investigate CD99- and programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1)-associated T-cell subsets in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and evaluate their clinical relevance and diagnostic potential for early disease detection. METHODS Peripheral blood samples were obtained from 37 newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve patients with SLE and 33 healthy controls, and 24 patients with pSS as a disease-control group. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were isolated and analyzed by flow cytometry using antibodies against CD3, CD4, CD8, CD99, PD-1, CCR7, and CD45RA to characterize CD99- and PD-1-defined T-cell subsets and differentiation states. Correlations between T-cell subsets and clinical indicators were assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed to evaluate diagnostic performance for early SLE detection. RESULTS Circulating T cells from early SLE patients showed preferential co-expression of CD99 and PD-1, with significantly higher PD-1 levels in CD99hi than in CD99int T cells. CD99hiPD-1+ cells were enriched in effector memory compartments and were least frequent in naïve T cells.Patients with SLE exhibited a broad expansion of CD99hiPD-1+ T cells across multiple CD4+ and CD8+ differentiation states. CD99/PD-1-defined subsets correlated with serological indicators of disease activity, including autoantibodies and complement consumption. ROC analysis demonstrated moderate diagnostic performance of individual subsets (area under the curve [AUC] 0.54-0.78), whereas a multivariable logistic model integrating 12 subsets improved discrimination for early SLE (AUC 0.867). CONCLUSION CD99hiPD-1+ T cells are expanded across multiple T-cell subsets in SLE and correlate with serological indicators of disease activity, suggesting potential value as immunological markers for early diagnosis.

title: Anthropogenic restructuring of urban wetland ecological networks: Differentiated source-corridor responses and management priorities in a lake-rich megacity.
abstract: Urban wetland ecological networks (WENs) are increasingly affected by rapid urbanization and spatially uneven anthropogenic pressures. However, international literature remains constrained by cross-sectional analyses and generalized disturbance indicators, missing the spatiotemporal non-stationarity and differentiated responses of ecological sources versus potential corridors. This study couples WEN reconstruction with MGWR-based spatial non-stationarity analysis by tracking two decades of network restructuring in Wuhan, China, using a multidimensional anthropogenic driver indicator set, MSPA-Conefor-Linkage Mapper modeling, Spearman correlation, OLS regression and MGWR. The results showed that although the number of source areas increased from 86 to 108, the total area decreased from 690.42 km2 to 615.98 km2; In contrast, the length of the corridor increased from 653.23 km to 769.77 km, but the network structure indicators(α,βandγ) decreased from 0.63, 2.21, and 0.75 to 0.44, 1.84, and 0.63, highlighting the increasing dependence of WENs on lengthy and inefficient alternative paths. Crucially, the MGWR analysis unveils highly differentiated source-corridor response pathways to anthropogenic drivers across space and time. Population density and agricultural expansion act as persistent global background pressures diminishing network capacity. At the local scale, however, ecological sources are primarily degraded by localized industrial encroachment, whereas ecological corridors exhibit high sensitivity to linear transportation barriers, outward urban boundaries, and nighttime human activities. MGWR improved adjusted R2 from 0.518 to 0.550 to 0.644-0.838, indicating spatial non-stationarity. These findings highlight the differentiated responses of ecological sources and corridors to anthropogenic pressures, suggesting that source protection should prioritize industrial land encroachment, while corridor conservation should focus on transportation barriers and urban expansion. By distinguishing persistent global pressures from localized and stage-specific associations, this study provides a basis for targeted WEN management in rapidly urbanizing, lake-rich cities.

title: Machine learning based mesh movement for non-hydrostatic tsunami simulation
abstract: This study investigates the use of machine learning based mesh movement method, specifically the Universal Mesh Movement Network (UM2N), with depth integrated non-hydrostatic shallow water models. Motivation for this comes from the need for models which balance efficiency and accuracy for use in probabilistic coastal hazard assessment. Implementations are built on the discontinuous Galerkin finite-element (DG-FE) based software, Thetis, which leverages the partial differential equation (PDE) framework Firedrake for automated code generation. Verification on benchmark test cases and validation against laboratory measurements of coastal hazards, focusing on tsunami propagation, run-up, and inundation is performed. In these tests, the UM2N-driven meshes help resolve key non-hydrostatic dynamics including wave refraction over a conical shoal, run-up with wetting-drying on a conical island, and tsunami inundation in the Monai Valley laboratory benchmark, and yield numerical solutions in close agreement with reference fine-mesh computations and measured data. Notably, in the Monai Valley case, UM2N achieves a ~91% reduction in wave-peak error at the nearshore gauge compared with ~74% for the conventional Monge--Amp\`ere (MA) mesh movement, both relative to the coarse fixed mesh. The UM2N surrogate based approach accelerates the conventional mesh movement step, achieving a ~32% reduction in total runtime and ~2 times speed-up in mesh movement step time over the MA solver on GPU, while offering a significant improvement in robustness over long integration periods and under strongly nonlinear wave conditions.

Targeting T follicular helper (Tfh) Cells for Improved Vaccine Efficacy: Lessons from Diverse Disease Models.
abstract: Despite remarkable progress in vaccinology, many vaccines fail to generate durable and broadly protective immunity against rapidly evolving and deadly pathogens. Conventional vaccine strategies often rely on quantifying antibody titers or neutralizing antibodies, but accumulating evidence suggests that humoral responses alone may not ensure long-term protection. An effective vaccine must engage multiple components of the immune system, harnessing intricate cellular interactions to generate durable immunological memory. Among these, CD4+ T follicular helper (Tfh) cells have emerged as central players in orchestrating germinal center (GC) dynamics, where they provide essential signals to B cells for affinity maturation, class switching, and differentiation into memory B cells and long-lived plasma cells. Tfh cells thus directly shape the magnitude and quality of vaccine-induced antibody responses. Clinical and experimental studies across infections such as influenza, HIV, HBV, and SARS-CoV-2 highlight that robust Tfh responses correlate with effective immunity and reduced disease severity. However, most licensed vaccines elicit suboptimal or short-lived Tfh activation, underscoring a critical limitation in current vaccine design. This review provides a comprehensive overview of vaccines targeting Tfh cells across various diseases, elucidating their mechanistic contributions to vaccine-induced immunity, and how their modulation could improve next-generation vaccine strategies. By harnessing Tfh biology, future vaccines could achieve durable, high-quality antibody responses, offering improved protection against emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases.

title: BT-115386, a MAT2A inhibitor, targets MTAP-deficient nasopharyngeal carcinoma via c-Myc and p53 modulation.
abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is an aggressive malignancy lacking targeted therapies. By screening 200 NPC specimens, we identify homozygous deletion of methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP) in 37.5% (75/200) of cases, ranking NPC as the second most common cancer type harboring MTAP loss. To target this therapeutic vulnerability, we develop an orally bioavailable methionine adenosyltransferase 2α (MAT2A) inhibitor, BT-115386, which significantly suppresses tumor growth and prolongs survival in mouse models of MTAP-deleted NPC. In MTAP-deleted NPC, BT-115386 treatment reduces protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) activity, thereby enhancing p53 activity through aberrant splicing of MDM4 and inducing c-Myc degradation through abolishment of arginine symmetric dimethylation. Loss of c-Myc thus reduces stemness and lipogenesis but induces cellular differentiation and EBV lytic cycle, indicating that BT-115386 causes MTAP-deleted NPC cell death through multiple pathways. Pharmacological inhibition of MAT2A/PRMT5 is a promising precision therapeutic strategy for MTAP-deficient NPC.

title: From Crop Residue to Groundwater: Quantifying the Transport Potential of Genetically Modified Crop-Derived Antibiotic Resistance Genes and RNA Interference Constructs in Soil
abstract: The mobility of extracellular transgenes derived from genetically modified crops remains inadequately characterized following release into nonsterile soil environments, despite their potential to alter microbial ecology and propagate antibiotic resistance. This study quantified breakthrough behavior and phase partitioning of two model constructs, the antibiotic resistance gene nptII and the silencing RNA Sbe1, in saturated soil columns under continuous synthetic rainwater infiltration. While quantitative PCR and fluorometric mass balance analyses demonstrated retention of >70% of the introduced nptII (initial loading: 1015.19 copies; peak effluent: 1011.38±0.34 copies/mL) and greater than 90% of the total RNA within soils (initial loading: 1016.73 copies; peak effluent: up to 1014.65±0.21 copies/mL), effluent concentrations indicate off-site transport potential. Columns inoculated with Pseudomonas putida (107 CFU/g) exhibited delayed breakthrough, with nptII delayed by up to 3.3 PV (p = 0.0012) and Sbe1 breakthrough absent. Inoculation increased soil-associated DNA mass by up to 35%, suggesting enhanced bio-mediated losses. Modeling with the phase exposure-dependent exchange (PhEDEx) framework suggests that DNA retention is governed by a sorption timescale of 0.17 min from the pore fluid, residence time-dependent desorption, and concentration threshold-activated sequestration. The findings underscore the long-term transport potential of extracellular nucleic acids in agroecosystems.

title: Inflammation-Targeted Multifunctional Nanoparticles Remodel the Spinal Cord Injury Microenvironment to Promote Neurovascular Repair.
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by interconnected inflammation, oxidative stress, vascular dysfunction, and impaired neural regeneration, while insufficient lesion-directed delivery further limits the efficacy of systemic therapy. Here, we developed macrophage membrane-camoufl11aged Sr-PDA/Fasudil/MnO2 nanoparticles (MM-NPs) that were designed to integrate inflammation-targeted delivery with complementary immunomodulatory, redox-regulating, and repair-supporting functions. Macrophage membrane camouflage reduced nonspecific phagocytic uptake, enhanced recognition of inflammatory endothelium, improved delivery in an in vitro endothelial barrier model, and increased lesion accumulation in vivo. The formulation provided sustained fasudil release and was designed to combine Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) inhibition with redox regulation and bioactive support. MM-NPs consequently attenuated microglial inflammatory activation and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, improved endothelial migration and angiogenic responses, and alleviated inflammation-induced impairment of neural stem cell differentiation. In a rat SCI model, MM-NPs reduced lesion cavitation and fibrosis, improved the inflammatory microenvironment, enhanced vascular, axonal, and myelin-associated repair, and promoted neurological recovery. Transcriptomic profiling and quantitative spinal cord immunoblotting supported treatment-associated changes in ROCK-associated and NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling. Collectively, MM-NPs couple inflammation-targeted delivery with coordinated immune, redox, vascular, and neural regulation, providing a microenvironment-centered strategy for neurovascular repair after SCI.

title: Humidity-Regulated MOF-Kirigami Passive Flyer.
abstract: While passive flyers have gained increasing attention as an energy-efficient alternative to active unmanned aerial vehicles, they are challenged by limited flight time, high energy consumption, and large-scale deployment issues caused by heavy batteries and complex electronics. The dandelion seed, a natural passive flyer for wind-borne dispersal, has inspired the design of synthetic biomimetic counterparts that similarly leverage airflow for sustained locomotion. However, existing designs lack adaptive mechanisms to respond to diverse environmental conditions such as humidity variation, limiting their functionality in real-world atmospheres. Thus, a humidity-regulated passive flyer was presented here which integrates a ZPF-2-Co metal-organic framework (MOF)-polymer composite humidity actuator into a dandelion-seed-inspired kirigami structure. This flyer is capable of altering its flight position based on ambient humidity, enabling adaptive dispersal. A theoretical model about descent of a dandelion seed was established, using fluid dynamics simulations to analyze the flow field and pressure distribution. It is revealed that a vortex ring formed above the pappus increases drag and slows descent, while a restoring torque stabilizes the attitude and enables gliding upon tilt. Flight tests under seven humidity conditions reveal that the flyer descends vertically below 70% RH, transitions into stable gliding between 70% and 80% RH for controlled long-distance dispersal, and loses gliding stability due to flipping when RH exceeds 84.6%. The passive flyers developed in this work validate the humidity-regulating functionality of MOFs and their potential implementation in flexible devices, providing a foundation for future applications such as smart agriculture, distributed environmental sensing, and pollution tracking.

title: A bio-digital circular framework for sustainable duck feed production using agro-industrial side-streams and aquatic biomass
abstract: The poultry sector faces increasing environmental and economic pressures associated with agro-industrial by-product accumulation, dependence on conventional feed ingredients, and feed-supply logistics. This study developed the SHIREEM framework, a bio-digital circular approach for the valorization of Snack Food Industry By-products (SFIB) and aquatic biomass (Azolla pinnata and Spirulina platensis) in poultry feed production. The framework integrates IoT-assisted process monitoring, computational feed optimization, machine-learning prediction, and circular resource-utilization principles. An IoT-assisted pelleting system incorporating a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and real-time sensors was used to monitor and control processing conditions, while a Python-based Least-Cost Ration (LCR) model optimized feed formulations under predefined nutritional and economic constraints. Under the simulated conditions, the optimized formulation reduced the estimated feed production cost from approximately 22,000 to 12,450 EGP ton⁻¹ (43.4%) and reduced logistics-related CO₂ emissions by 93.8% within the defined assessment boundary. Machine-learning models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, with Gradient Boosting providing the best prediction of body weight and Extra-Trees providing the best prediction of feed conversion ratio among the evaluated models. Feature-importance analysis indicated that age and metabolizable energy were major predictors of growth-related performance, whereas Azolla inclusion showed a greater contribution to feed conversion ratio than to body weight prediction. In addition, 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation indicated that the economic performance of the optimized system remained feasible across the majority of the simulated uncertainty scenarios, with SFIB cost and transportation expenditure identified as important cost drivers. Overall, the results support the potential of SHIREEM as an integrated computational framework for circular feed-resource utilization and localized production. However, the findings represent a computational proof-of-concept and require experimental and commercial-scale validation before biological, environmental, and economic performance can be generalized to practical poultry production systems. To support regional adoption, agricultural policymakers could consider developing appropriate quality-certification frameworks for bio-based feed resources and supportive policy mechanisms that facilitate the responsible upcycling of locally available agro-industrial residues into animal feed.

title: The Digital Future of Road Maintenance: An MCDM for Evaluating Data-Driven Road Maintenance Strategies for the M-30 Highway
abstract: Road maintenance is essential to preserve road quality and service standards. However, adopting a maintenance strategy depends on multiple factors. The digitalization of infrastructure provides better insights into its condition, allowing resources to be allocated more efficiently. Evaluating the implementation of digitalization-focused measures is a complex task. Therefore, a multicriteria analysis using a hybrid approach based on the expert-adjusted entropy method was carried out to compare the different road maintenance strategies. This evaluation has been applied to a case study, the M-30 urban ring highway, whose management is carried out through an integrated maintenance contract regulated by key performance indicators. These quality indicators have been the basis for defining functional criteria, which, along with other sustainability criteria, make up the proposed multicriteria method. The results show that the proposed framework supports the comparative evaluation of alternative road maintenance strategies by integrating operational, social, and economic criteria within a structured decision-making process. The study contributes to the body of knowledge by demonstrating how building information modeling (BIM)-based infrastructure data can be systematically incorporated into multicriteria decision-making models to support more transparent and informed maintenance planning in road asset management.

title: Optimal temperature windows of mild hyperthermia in tissue regeneration: from bone to skin and beyond.
abstract: BACKGROUND Mild hyperthermia (MHT) has emerged as a promising biophysical approach for promoting tissue repair and regeneration. Controlled, sub-ablative heating can stimulate regenerative cellular responses while preserving tissue viability. However, the optimal thermal conditions vary across tissues and remain incompletely defined. OBJECTIVES This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the regenerative effects of MHT across bone, skin and wound tissue, skeletal muscle, cardiovascular tissue, peripheral nerves, and neural cell models. Particular emphasis is placed on tissue-specific temperature windows, underlying biological mechanisms, heat-delivery technologies, and clinical translation. RESULTS MHT supports tissue regeneration and repair-related responses through coordinated regulation of heat-shock responses, immune polarization, angiogenesis, cellular metabolism, progenitor-cell activity, and pro-regenerative signaling pathways. Evidence from bone, skin, and skeletal muscle models demonstrates enhanced osteogenesis, wound repair, myogenic differentiation, vascularization, and functional recovery. Cardiovascular and neural studies further suggest that controlled heating can support repair by improving cell survival, reducing oxidative and inflammatory injury, and creating a microenvironment favorable for recovery. The principal 39-42 °C range provides a practical framework for regenerative MHT, although effective conditions depend on tissue type, exposure duration, treatment frequency, perfusion, heating modality, and the regenerative endpoint assessed. Advances in targeted heat-delivery, real-time thermometry, and regenerative biomaterials are expanding the potential for precise, tissue-adapted treatment. CONCLUSION MHT represents a versatile and promising adjunct to tissue regeneration. Establishing tissue-specific temperature-time protocols and integrating precise thermal control with regenerative technologies may enable its translation into individualized therapies for diverse injuries.
