title: Utilizing LSTM networks for LaBr 3 :Ce scintillators RUL prediction under extreme gamma irradiations
abstract: Cerium-doped lanthanum bromide (LaBr ₃ :Ce) scintillation detectors are widely deployed in harsh radiation environments, such as space exploration, radioactive monitoring in nuclear facilities, and high energy physics. Cumulative radiation damage introduces lattice defects and radiation-induced absorption (RIA), which results in progressive degradation of optical transmittance and light yield. Previous investigations have been largely confined to post-irradiation characterizations of light output and transmittance. Therefore, predictive methods for estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of LaBr ₃ :Ce scintillators remain absent, especially under extreme gamma irradiation. This paper presents a prognostic method based on multiphysics simulation, utilizing a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to estimate the RUL of LaBr ₃ :Ce crystals. A kinetic multiphysics platform is constructed to simulate the spatiotemporal evolution of radiation damage across multiple working conditions with varying source activities and crystal geometries, generating multi-condition EWLT sequences. A geometry-dependent optical threshold is then established to define the condition-specific failure state. A single LSTM network is trained jointly on the pooled sequences and compared with GRU, vanilla RNN, and exponential fitting methods under strict chronological splits. Results demonstrate that the LSTM achieves the lowest forecasting errors across the evaluated conditions, with group-mean RMSE values of 1.47×10 ⁻⁴ and 2.71×10 ⁻⁴ for the activity and geometry conditions, respectively. This method provides a data-driven approach for the predictive maintenance of radiation detectors.

title: An antagonistic DlFT1 – DlFT2 module underlies potassium chlorate-induced off-season flowering in longan ( Dimocarpus longan Lour.)
abstract: Flowering time is critical for yield stability and production scheduling in fruit trees. Longan (Dimocarpus longan Lour.), an economically important fruit tree in Southeast Asia, supports year-round production through well-established practice of KClO₃-induced off-season flowering, providing an ideal model for studying chemical-induced flowering. However, the molecular mechanisms by which KClO₃ is perceived and converted into flowering signals remain unclear. Here, we show that KClO₃ application via either root drenching or foliar spraying consistently induced off-season flowering in the ‘Shixia’ and ‘E-daw’ cultivars. Comparative transcriptomic analyses of leaves, which are early KClO3-responsive organs and major sites of FT-derived florigen production, identified a conserved heat-stress-like module comprising heat shock proteins and stress-responsive transcription factors. Among these transcription factors, DlDREB1C, DlWRKY3, and DlWRKY35 directly bound to the promoter of the FT-like gene DlFT2, linking KClO₃-induced stress signaling to flowering control. Functionally, DlFT1 acted as a florigenic activator, whereas DlFT2 functioned as a floral repressor by forming a ternary complex with DlGF14-1 and DlSVP9 to inhibit DlFT1 transcription. KClO₃-mediated repression of DlFT2 weakened this complex, thereby relieving repression of DlFT1 expression. Together, these findings reveal a KClO₃-responsive DlFT1-DlFT2 antagonistic module involved in off-season flowering in longan, providing new insights into the chemically induced flowering in perennial crop production.

title: B cell-intrinsic TLR7 and TLR9 signatures define clinical phenotype and therapeutic response in lupus nephritis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES This study explores the expression of intracytoplasmic TLRs across diverse B cell subtypes in lupus, their association with renal activity, and their prognostic value. METHODS We compared TLR7, TLR9, and MyD88 expression across peripheral B cell subtypes by flow cytometry, along with 29 cytokines serum levels from 28 LN patients and 26 lupus patients with extrarenal activity (NLN). After induction therapy, TLRs/MyD88 expression was reanalysed according to treatment response in LN. RESULTS LN patients were characterised by higher frequency of MyD88+ B cells (86.5% vs 52.65%, p 0.04), predominantly in transitional cells (97.7% vs 58.7%, p 0.03). Treatment-adjusted analysis revealed the association of TLR7⁺ naïve B cells (OR 1.02, p 0.01) and TLR9 mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) in transitional B cells (OR 1.008, p 0.004) with LN. The latter, together with eotaxin (OR 1.01, p 0.01), constitute the proposed LN association model (OR 1.006 and 1.01 p 0.01, respectively). At 6-month follow-up, the responder group showed persistently elevated expression of TLR7 and TLR9 in naïve and atypical B-cell subsets, including double-negative (DN) and age-associated B cells (ABCs). The association model for renal response included TLR7 MFI in naïve B cells (OR 1 p 0.05) and TLR9 MFI in ABCs (OR 1.001 p 0.03). CONCLUSION In LN, increased MyD88 and TLR7/TLR9 expression in early B-cell stages may promote autoreactive cell survival and differentiation into autoantibody-secreting cells, contributing to immune complex deposition and eotaxin-sustained renal inflammation. In contrast, higher TLR9 in TLR7-dependent subsets may exert a regulatory effect that, alongside induction therapy, favours nephritis resolution.

title: Governing attention, triggering fatigue: how social media intrusiveness and regulatory focus shape perceived overload
abstract: This study uses the attentional sovereignty perspective to examine how social media intrusiveness (presenteeism, anonymity, and flexibility) relates to perceived information overload, perceived social overload, and social media fatigue, and how regulatory focus moderates feature-overload relationships. Survey data from 386 social media users in China are analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling and hierarchical regression. Presenteeism is positively associated with both types of perceived overload, whereas anonymity and flexibility show negative associations. Perceived information overload and perceived social overload mediate relationships between intrusive features and fatigue. Promotion and prevention focus exert feature-specific moderating effects, some of which differ from the hypothesized directions. Platforms can reduce fatigue by offering simple, reversible controls over notifications, availability, audience visibility, and interaction timing rather than assuming that all intrusive features are harmful. This study advances the fatigue literature by integrating the attentional sovereignty lens, differentiating two overload mediators, and revealing the moderating mechanism of regulatory focus in users' responses to social media intrusiveness.

title: Unraveling the differentiated strategic pathways linking network tie strength and product innovation performance
abstract: Drawing on social network theory and open innovation theory, this study explores how network tie strength influences product innovation performance through different product innovation strategic paths in open collaborative innovation contexts. Specifically, this study examines the mediating roles of technology-push, market-pull and design-driven product innovation strategies, as well as the moderating role of network closure. Using survey data collected from 275 Chinese manufacturing firms, this study constructs and tests a moderated mediation model through factor analysis, correlation analysis, multiple regression analysis and Bootstrap analysis. The study investigates the relationships among network tie strength, product innovation strategies, network closure and product innovation performance. The results indicate that network tie strength has a significant positive effect on product innovation performance. Network tie strength also positively affects technology-push, market-pull and design-driven product innovation strategies. Furthermore, market-pull and design-driven product innovation strategies play significant mediating roles between network tie strength and product innovation performance, whereas the mediating effect of technology-push product innovation strategy is not statistically supported. In addition, network closure positively moderates the relationships between network tie strength and both market-pull and design-driven product innovation strategies, while its moderating effect on technology-push product innovation strategy is insignificant. This study extends existing research by integrating social network theory and open innovation theory into a unified analytical framework and revealing how network tie strength affects product innovation performance through heterogeneous strategic innovation paths. However, this study relies on cross-sectional survey data and self-reported perceptual measures, which may raise concerns regarding common method bias and reverse causality. Future research could employ longitudinal or multi-source data to further validate the causal relationships identified in this study. The findings suggest that manufacturing firms should strengthen long-term collaborative relationships within innovation networks and adopt differentiated product innovation strategies according to specific innovation objectives. In particular, firms should emphasize design-driven and technology-push innovation capabilities while dynamically balancing network openness and closure to improve collaborative innovation efficiency and product innovation performance. This study develops an analytical framework of differentiated strategic pathways linking network tie strength, product innovation strategies, and product innovation performance. It reveals the differentiated mechanisms through which network relational resources are converted into product innovation performance, further extends the application of social network theory and open innovation theory to product innovation research in the manufacturing context, and provides a new theoretical perspective for firms' product innovation strategy selection in complex innovation network environments.

title: ConDiST: Context-Conditioned Spatiotemporal Diffusion for Traffic Anomaly Detection.
abstract: Traffic anomaly detection is critical for urban safety. Existing methods struggle to capture context-dependent normal patterns, often confusing routine fluctuations with true anomalies and causing high false positives. While diffusion models show promise, most treat contextual information as mere auxiliary inputs and fail to achieve componentwise, context-differentiated conditioning. To address these limitations, we propose ConDiST, a context-conditioned spatiotemporal diffusion framework that takes external temporal features and long-term trends as explicit conditioning signals. In the temporal domain, we design a context-conditioned temporal modeling module that uses wavelet decomposition to let each frequency band evolve along a context-dependent path, mitigating cross-scale coupling. In the spatial domain, we develop a context-conditioned spatial modeling module that anchors on fixed geographic priors as a stable basis while learning context-driven structural evolution, enabling dynamic reconfiguration of spatial dependencies. Building on these, we introduce an anomaly scoring method that multiplicatively couples deterministic prediction errors with diffusion-based uncertainty for synergistic enhancement. Extensive experiments on NYC, Chicago, and PeMS benchmarks demonstrate that ConDiST achieves the highest mean AUC on all three datasets, outperforming the strongest baseline by 0.72, 0.88, and 2.21percentage points on NYC, Chicago, and PeMS, respectively.

TRIM28-mediated SUMOylation of ERG at K389 conveys PARP inhibitor resistance by inhibiting 53BP1 expression in CRPC
abstract: Both intrinsic and acquired resistance to poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPis) have emerged as a formidable challenge in clinical practice. Here, we report that the transcription factor E-twenty-six (Ets)-related gene ( ERG ) was highly expressed in PARPi-resistant prostate cancer and was correlated with PARPi resistance in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) cells. ERG was posttranslationally modified by tripartite motif-containing 28 (TRIM28) as SUMOylation at lysine 389 (K389), which promotes DNA homologous recombination repair (HRR), thereby weakening the efficacy of PARPis. Mechanistically, the SUMOylation of ERG (K389) inhibited protein degradation mediated by the SPOP-mediated ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, thereby stabilizing the protein. Concurrently, this posttranslational modification increased HRR capacity by inhibiting 53BP1 expression, which in turn reduced PARPi sensitivity. Blockade of ERG K389 SUMOylation can effectively impair DNA repair efficacy and overcome PARPi resistance. These findings suggest that TRIM28-mediated ERG SUMOylation conveys resistance to PARPis by inhibiting 53BP1 expression; combined TRIM28/ERG targeting and PARPi therapy may improve outcomes for ERG-positive CRPC patients.

title: Auditory cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulations is sufficient to support perceptual categorization of speech and music
abstract: Auditory processing is typically described as hierarchical, culminating in neural representation of abstract categories. However, it remains unclear whether category-selective responses in auditory cortex require representational mechanisms beyond the coding of acoustic features or whether the acoustic representations already available in the auditory cortex are sufficient to account for categorization. Here, we test whether cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulation (STM) features is sufficient to support speech-music categorization by combining human intracranial recordings with continuous behavioral judgments of a naturalistic soundtrack in which speech and music occur both separately and simultaneously. We show that temporal and spectral modulation patterns largely characterize speech and music, respectively, and that cortical auditory regions robustly track these features over time, with distinct oscillatory frequency bands preferentially encoding temporal and spectral modulations. Critically, cortical representations of STMs predicted perceptual categorical judgments gathered in an independent sample. Last, speech- and music-related STM representations showed stronger tracking of category-specific acoustical features in left versus right cortical auditory regions, respectively. These findings indicate that the efficient neural coding of acoustical features provides a sufficient basis for the categorical distinction between speech and music and that the temporal and spectral components of this representation are implemented through distinct oscillatory mechanisms.

title: Ribosome-associated vesicles promote activity-dependent local translation in neurons
abstract: Local protein synthesis in axons and dendrites underpins synaptic plasticity. However, the composition of the protein synthesis machinery in distal neuronal processes and the mechanisms for its deployment to local translation sites remain unclear. Here, we employed multi-scale imaging that combines cryo-electron tomography, volume electron microscopy, and live-cell imaging to identify endoplasmic reticulum-derived KDEL-positive vesicles, a subset of which are decorated with ribosomes (Ribosome-Associated Vesicles, RAVs) in neurites. We demonstrate that neuronal stimulation triggers compartment-specific responses: dendrites accumulate stationary KDEL-positive vesicles at sites of enhanced translation, while axons accelerate vesicle transport. cLTP stimulation additionally increases the proportion of KDEL-positive vesicles that carry ribosomes, expanding the local RAV pool. Real-time imaging of translation at single mRNA resolution reveals that RAV-associated translation sites exhibit ∼30% greater nascent-peptide signal amplitude compared to periods without RAV association, indicating that RAVs boost local translation output. These findings establish RAVs as specialized platforms that integrate activity-dependent signals with local protein synthesis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how neurons achieve precise spatiotemporal control of translation.

title: Unblockable communication with gravity
abstract: All modern wireless communication technologies are based on electromagnetism. However, electromagnetic signals are readily susceptible to screening and blocking, so their availability cannot be guaranteed in adverse environments. This raises a fundamental question: Can information be transmitted through an unblockable channel? Here, we show that gravity, under physically realistic conditions, offers such a path. We propose and implement a wireless communication protocol in which a broadcaster encodes a binary message by moving a mass, while a receiver detects the resulting gravitational signal with a gravimeter. We validate this scheme experimentally, successfully transmitting a gravitational message a distance of ≈0.7 meters through a brick wall at a rate of 1 bit per minute. These results establish gravity as a viable platform for practically unblockable communication.

title: Machine-learning-driven identification of cooperative descriptors for polysulfide conversion on spinel oxides
abstract: Spinel oxides have emerged as promising catalysts for polysulfide conversion, yet a comprehensive design strategy that elucidates the underlying structure–property relationship across diverse spinel oxides remains elusive. The complex multistep conversion processes make single descriptors insufficient to capture the full catalytic behavior, whereas identifying cooperative descriptors introduces additional complexity that challenges manual analysis. Here, we employ a machine-learning–assisted approach to uncover universal cooperative descriptors and accelerate the discovery of high-performance spinel catalysts. We reveal that the intrinsic polysulfide conversion efficiency of spinel oxides is cooperatively governed by two structural features. Further screening of promising catalysts is conducted using the extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) algorithm, achieving rapid and accurate prediction of these features on spinel oxides. The model identifies Fe 2 CoO 4 and Fe 2 NiO 4 as superior catalysts, which are experimentally validated to exhibit excellent performance. This work provides deep mechanistic insights and a powerful data-driven framework for the rational design of spinel catalysts, with potential extension to other applications.

title: Intestinal BMP SMADs impart the mid-villus pattern through a transcription factor cascade mechanism
abstract: Differentiated cells of the intestinal villus are not a monolith of equivalent cell types, but an exquisitely patterned continuum of transdifferentiated cells with evolving functions. Villus patterning requires BMP signaling; however, the transcriptional regulators downstream of BMP are unclear. We find that SMAD1 and SMAD5 are necessary for middle villus pattern. Spatial transcriptomics reveal a homeotic-like shift in the villus pattern of SMAD1/SMAD5 mutants, with the villus bottom and tip domains expanding at the expense of the middle. Disruption of mid-villus patterning corresponds to decreases in lipid uptake and runted pups in SMAD1/5 mutants. Unexpectedly, SMAD1/5 is not required for regulation of villus tip identity, which is dependent on SMAD4. Epigenomics approaches reveal a mechanism in which SMAD1/5 directly activate some mid-villus genes and control others via a transcription factor hierarchy, including TBX3. An intestine-specific TBX3 mutant phenocopied the SMAD1/5 mutant. These findings contribute mechanistic details to intestinal villus patterning.

title: Cortical population codes for embedding sensory inputs into the prior context
abstract: According to theories of the brain as a predictive network, perceptual decisions result from integrating incoming sensory inputs with prior experience. A neuronal population implementing this form of computation must not only retain information about past events but also combine this information with current sensory evidence. To examine how this integration occurs, we recorded extracellular activity from both primary sensory cortex and a target frontal region in rats performing stimulus categorization. Psychophysical analysis showed that judgments were history dependent. Sensory cortex represented the current stimulus largely independently of prior stimuli and failed to account for the history dependence seen in behavior. In contrast, frontal cortex embedded current input within a representation of prior sensory information, with the two variables aligned along partially overlapping coding dimensions. This mechanism predicted choice bias in the behavioral data and involved a disproportionate contribution from putative fast-spiking units. These findings suggest distinct contributions of sensory and frontal cortical regions to predictive processing and point to frontal cortex as a potential site where sensory history may be integrated with incoming evidence to influence perceptual decisions.

title: Structure and dynamics of the cellular belt driving bacterial gliding motility
abstract: Various bacteria move on solid surfaces through a process known as gliding motility. Gliding bacteria of the phylum Bacteroidota are major ecological players in a wide variety of niches, as commensals or as pathogens. They use the type IX secretion system (T9SS) to transport adhesins to the cell surface, which then travel in a helical pattern to propel the cell. Here, we purified the filament that drives adhesin helical movement and uncovered its structure by cryo–electron microscopy. Live imaging showed that this outer membrane–associated periplasmic belt, built from T9SS core components, is powered by T9SS molecular motors. This structure functions as a moving walkway that conveys outer membrane β barrel protein–adhesin complexes, therefore coupling motor activity to directional surface translation. This study reveals a unique machinery coupling protein secretion with rapid directed movement of membrane-embedded protein complexes.

title: Seasonal effects of simulated marine heatwaves on temperature-dependent growth performance
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly longer and more frequent globally, but the cumulative impacts of multiple events on organism performance remain poorly understood. Using thermal performance models, we simulate the effects of simple seasonal MHW scenarios on the predicted growth of 36 mariculture species across the western Pacific Ocean. Simulations suggested that winter MHWs could generally benefit growth, while summer MHWs produced generally negative impacts, especially at higher latitudes where species experience summer growth periods. When combined, winter and summer MHW scenarios indicated a cumulative negative effect for most species. Vulnerability was highest at the warm- and cold-range edges of species’ distributions. These simulations suggest that temperature-dependent growth may be closely linked to the seasonal timing and frequency of extreme events, with multi-season MHWs posing potential challenges for mariculture species in the future. Our simulations highlight the importance of considering multi-season impacts in climate adaptation strategies.

title: Small and large earthquakes driven by inelastic deformation in weak fault zones
abstract: Earthquakes manifest across a wide range of magnitudes, corresponding to a diversity of rupture sizes and amounts of slip. Classical earthquake models consider rupture processes solely on the fault plane, but the surrounding fault zone rocks can host inelastic deformation. Here, we show, via a dynamic seismic cycle model incorporating spontaneous fault zone evolution through damage and healing, that both small and large earthquakes on a single fault emerge naturally from the interplay of fault slip and fault zone inelastic deformation. Our simulations reproduce key observations: frequency-magnitude distribution consistent with the Gutenberg-Richter law, magnitude-invariant static stress drop, and the dual-regime scaling of fracture energy density with earthquake magnitude. The results underscore the coevolution of earthquakes and fault zone damage as a fundamental mechanism governing earthquake behavior in nature. Fault zone deformation causing multiscale seismicity indicates that continuous monitoring of fault zone material properties may reveal fault stress states and earthquake potential.

title: TLR5 drives metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis through lipid- and flagellin-induced hepatocyte injury signaling
abstract: Liver fibrosis is a strong predictor of clinical outcomes in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Fibrosis is a consequence of persistent liver cell injury and inflammation in which Toll-like receptors (TLRs) play a key initiating role. Here, we test the hypothesis that TLR5 is involved in the development of MASH and fibrosis using a combination of clinical data from multiple independent patient cohorts, single-cell liver transcriptomics, and human in vitro and ex vivo models. Hepatic TLR5 expression, but not TLR2 or TLR4, is associated with liver fibrosis and mortality. Plasma levels of TLR5’s cognate ligand flagellin are increased in MASH with advanced fibrosis and fall with liver disease improvement. Mechanistically, we identify two parallel TLR5-mediated routes to hepatocyte injury: one elicited by flagellin and the other indirectly by lipid injury. Furthermore, hepatocyte TLR5 inhibition abrogates paracrine activation of hepatic stellate cells to suppress collagen production. This is also seen ex vivo in patient-derived precision-cut liver slices where TLR5 inhibition significantly reduces lipid-induced collagen deposition. These findings reveal a new role for TLR5 signaling, specifically in the development of advanced MASH fibrosis and may offer a novel disease-specific therapeutic approach.

title: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict
abstract: To survive, animals must balance opportunity and risk, yet how internal motivational state biases this trade-off remains poorly understood. Here, we show that hunger gates avoidance of a noxious stimulus in Drosophila to enable food approach under conflict. Using a behavioral assay in which flies must cross an electric shock barrier to reach food, we find that starvation promotes shock tolerance only when food-related olfactory cues are present. This state- and context-dependent behavioral shift is mediated by a defined neuromodulatory circuit. Leucokinin neurons encode hunger and convey this information to PV5K1 lateral horn output neurons, which integrate internal state signals with food odor cues and suppress shock-responsive FB2B neurons in the ventral fan-shaped body. Accordingly, electric shock-evoked activity in FB2B neurons is suppressed in starved flies exposed to food cues. These findings identify a circuit mechanism by which motivational state gates aversive processing to bias action selection towards goal-directed behavior.

title: Somatostatin 6, a master maternal mRNA driving early development
abstract: Vertebrate genomes contain six somatostatin (SST) gene family members, of which only SST1 and cortistatin (CORT or SST2) are present in mammalian genomes. These genes encode peptides that predominantly exert inhibitory effects on growth, metabolism, reproduction, and the immune system. However, their roles in nonmammalian vertebrates remain poorly understood. Here, we examined zebrafish sst6 ( sst6.2 ) loss of function and discovered that maternally inherited sst6 mRNA is vital for embryonic cleavage and gastrulation. Its absence impaired calcium release from stores, calcium wave propagation, F-actin assembly, furrow ingression, and overall embryonic development. Moreover, maternal sst6 mRNA is crucial for degrading maternal mRNAs, for calcium-dependent phosphorylation of Stat3 and Smad1/5, and for activating zygotic gene transcription, including pou5f1 , nanog , and sox2 , as well as downstream pluripotency factors. This suggests that maternal sst6 mRNA acts as a master regulator of early development, a function likely conserved in other vertebrates.

title: Membrane-confined self-assembly enables localized bioorthogonal prodrug activation and selective cancer therapy
abstract: Bioorthogonal prodrug activation offers a promising approach for site-specific drug release, significantly reducing the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. However, challenges remain in precisely controlling prodrug activation at the target site while maintaining optimal selectivity, reactivity, and potency. Here, we report a dual-targeting peptide, TzFFY p HH, that integrates on-membrane enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) with bioorthogonal chemistry to enable selective chemotherapy. Exploiting the overexpression of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) on cancer cells, TzFFY p HH selectively anchors and self-assembles on the cancer cell membrane, enriching tetrazine (Tz) handles that act as bioorthogonal reactors to activate a trans -cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrug (TCO-Dox) for precise drug release. Upon topical administration, TzFFY p HH forms a hydrogel at subcutaneous tumor sites, enabling in situ prodrug activation for effective tumor inhibition. Notably, this localized chemotherapy elicits a potent antitumor immune response, which, when combined with anti-programmed death-1 antibody (αPD-1), synergistically potentiates therapeutic outcomes. By coupling supramolecular self-assembly with bioorthogonal reactivity on the cell membrane, this work establishes a chemically programmable platform for spatiotemporally controlled prodrug activation and provides a general strategy for integrating localized chemotherapy with immunotherapy.

title: A floss-based platform for native gingival crevicular fluid analysis enables noninvasive systemic and oral health monitoring
abstract: Gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) is a serum-derived biofluid in the gingival sulcus, offering access to systemic metabolic signals and localized oral inflammation. However, its diagnostic utility remains underutilized because native submicroliter volumes cannot be analyzed without specimen pooling and reagent-mediated dilution. We overcome this barrier using a floss-based platform that enables on-demand GCF analysis during routine flossing. The device integrates a dual-fiber system exploiting shear-dependent property for efficient mobilization, liquid-bridge retention, a pyramidal microfluidic sensor stack, and real-time electrofluidic volume correction. This architecture supports multiplexed electrochemical quantification of glucose, uric acid (UA), pH, and H 2 O 2 from native GCF within minutes. In human studies, GCF glucose and UA correlated with capillary blood (glucose: r = 0.89, UA: r = 0.78). Site-specific pH and H 2 O 2 levels differentiated inflamed from healthy periodontal sites, correlating with probing pocket depth. By converting a daily hygiene practice into a dual tool for systemic and oral health monitoring, this platform advances comorbidity management for chronic disease populations.

title: USP8 inhibition suppresses prostate tumorigenesis via promoting RICTOR degradation to inhibit mTORC2 signaling
abstract: RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3–based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived SPOP mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression. Furthermore, we identify USP8 as its upstream deubiquitinase, and inhibition of USP8 specifically suppresses RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1. As such, the USP8 inhibitor induces RICTOR degradation concomitant with marked tumor suppression in vivo. Hence, these findings reveal an SPOP-USP8-RICTOR regulatory circuit that underlies PrCa tumorigenesis and provides a rationale for targeting RICTOR via USP8 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for patients with PrCa.

title: Pten regulates neurogenic radial glia lineage progression and tunes neocortical astrocyte production in Mapk1/3 -dependent pathway
abstract: The cerebral cortex consists of immense numbers of diverse cell types derived from radial glial progenitor (RGP) cells. How RGPs generate appropriate quantities of distinct cell types to safeguard a brain of correct size is not well understood. However, genetic aberrations in human, including mutations in PTEN , lead to cortical malformation such as macrocephaly, albeit with unknown etiology. Here, we used mosaic analysis with double markers (MADM)–based clonal analysis and single-cell phenotyping to decipher the role of Pten in RGP lineage progression during cortical ontogeny. Although neurogenic RGP lineage progression was altered and projection neuron production doubled in the absence of Pten , cortical astrogenesis was drastically increased. Through epistasis experiments, we show that the loss of Pten uncouples astrogenesis from essential growth factor signaling hubs, funneling into MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase). Collectively, our results suggest that Pten regulates RGP lineage progression with distinct sequential functions in corticogenesis to safeguard the emergence of a correctly sized cortex.

title: Engineering interfacial nucleation and growth for long-life, ultrahigh-rate anode-free sodium batteries
abstract: The practical application of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs) is limited by the poor reversibility of sodium plating and stripping on current collectors. Here, we show that conventional graphite unexpectedly regulates sodium plating and stripping through a dynamic, interactive interface that enables multidimensional charge transport. This behavior arises from the combination of ultrafast mixed ion-electron transport, reversible ether solvent cointercalation, and the anisotropic flake architecture of graphite, which together promote efficient charge exchange and edge-dominant nucleation. The resulting adaptive interface forms an ultrathin, mechanically robust SEI that stabilizes sodium plating and stripping across a wide current density range (1C to 10C). Ampere hour–level anode-free pouch cells based on this design exhibit an initial Coulombic efficiency of 92.3%, retain 84.9% capacity after 1100 cycles at 3C, and display exceptional safety characteristics, including minimal temperature rise at high rates and no thermal runaway during nail penetration. These results establish a platform for controlling interfacial metal nucleation and growth in AFSBs.

title: Posttranscriptional regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 controls the transcriptional program enforcing T cell quiescence
abstract: Immune protection against infections relies on long-term maintenance of a highly diversified naïve T cell repertoire. Transcription factors cooperate to enforce T cell metabolic quiescence and maintenance. However, less is known about the posttranscriptional networks that preserve naïve T cells. Here, we describe the RNA binding proteins T cell antigen 1 (TIA1) and TIA-like 1 (TIAL1) as key promoters of CD4 and CD8 T cell quiescence. T cells deficient in TIA1 and TIAL1 undergo premature T cell activation, exhaustion, and death in the absence of cognate antigens. Mechanistically, TIA1 and TIAL1 promote the messenger RNA translation of quiescence-associated transcription factors such as forkhead box P1, lymphoid enhancer factor 1, and T cell factor 1 to restrain homeostatic T cell proliferation and activation. In summary, our study highlights a previously unrecognized dependency on posttranscriptional gene regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 for implementing the quiescent transcriptional programs for long survival of T cells.

title: In vivo screening reveals new regulators of natural killer cell development and functional response to acute cytomegalovirus infection
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical innate immune effectors in antiviral and antitumor responses. However, the factors governing NK cell development and function remain incompletely understood. To address this, we adopted an in vivo screening approach, generating a panel of mice deficient in genes differentially expressed across NK cell maturation stages or following viral infection. We performed a combinational screen comprising baseline immunophenotyping and mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) challenge. We identified regulators of NK cell development, including transcriptional regulators and proteins with putative trafficking functions. MCMV challenge studies additionally identified proteins that affected antiviral immunity independently of NK cell phenotypes, including a previously undescribed regulator of NK cell degranulation, synaptotagmin-like protein 3. Identified genes exhibited a trend toward reduced tolerance to loss of function in large-scale human sequencing studies and evidence for reduced NK cell numbers in a cohort of patients with immunodeficiency. Together, these findings provide a resource of NK-expressed genes important for NK cell maturation and function, with relevance to human health.

title: Spheroid-laden hydrogels with dual biomimetic intra- and perispheroidal niches for enhanced bone healing
abstract: Stem cell spheroid–hydrogel platforms offer promise for bone defect repair, but implantation-associated oxidative stress, poor vascular ingrowth, and insufficient osteogenic cues limit their clinical translation. Here, we developed dual-NICHE (dual niche-instructive construct for bone healing and engraftment), a gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel containing human adipose–derived stem cell spheroids with spatially distinct intra-/perispheroidal niches. Within a single construct, these two niches provide complementary functions to simultaneously address the key bottlenecks in bone regeneration. The intraspheroidal niche incorporated bone morphogenetic protein-2–immobilized fibers to promote osteogenic differentiation, whereas the perispheroidal matrix contained Sr 2+ –tannic acid nanoparticles (NPs). Upon implantation, the NPs mitigated oxidative stress and supported vascular infiltration. Concurrently, the osteogenic cue promoted differentiation, while the NPs facilitated mineral nucleation and growth, as further supported by molecular dynamics simulations. Together, this spatial integration enhanced vascularized bone formation with a bone volume fraction of ∼13.5% using only 5208 cells per defect in a mouse calvarial model, providing a potentially translatable framework for bone regeneration.

title: Dynein-dependent positioning of multiple organelles regulates adaptive gene expression during oxidative stress
abstract: Cells respond to environmental insults through well-characterized changes to their transcriptome and proteome. The contribution that reorganization of intracellular architecture makes to the adaptive stress response is much less understood. Here, we reveal a conserved spatial response to oxidative stress in which the microtubule motor dynein enhances perinuclear clustering of multiple membrane-bound organelles. These events are triggered by reactive oxygen species and protein kinase C and occur without increased association of dynein with its activator dynactin, pointing to a noncanonical mechanism for stimulating retrograde transport. Using a chemically inducible system for dispersing individual organelles, we show that perinuclear localization of multiple compartments potentiates oxidative stress–induced gene expression, with distinct genes depending on inputs from either combinations of organelles or individual compartments. Together, these findings implicate positioning of multiple membrane-bound compartments in gene expression regulation and identify coordinated organelle trafficking by dynein as an additional regulatory layer in the cellular stress response.

title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
abstract: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation. We report near-unity efficiency quantum frequency conversion over a bandwidth >45 terahertz, which allowed us to measure the state with an electron-multiplying CCD (EMCCD) camera-based spectrometer, at noncryogenic temperatures. The parametric amplification and conversion of >400 frequency modes yielded an overall mean of ∼700 visible photons per shot and photon statistics consistent with squeezing. Our work shows how many-mode quantum states of light can be generated, manipulated, and measured with efficient use of hardware resources, motivating the use of frequency encoding in quantum optics.

title: Spatially multiplexed microneedle biosensors for low-abundance protein biomarker monitoring in dermal interstitial fluid
abstract: Microneedle (MN) biosensors offer a minimally invasive approach for molecular analysis of interstitial fluid (ISF), but multiplexed detection of low-abundance protein biomarkers remains limited by poor spatial functionalization and analytical sensitivity. Here, we introduce a high-resolution transfer-printing strategy that functionalizes individual MNs with distinct biorecognition elements on a single patch, enabling simultaneous capture and on-needle analysis of multiple protein biomarkers. Combined with plasmonic-enhanced ultrabright fluorescent nanolabels, the platform enables sensitive multiplexed quantification of low-abundance immune and kidney function biomarkers in mouse models and human subjects. ISF biomarker concentrations showed strong correlations with corresponding plasma levels, supporting the physiological relevance of MN-based measurements. The MN patch enabled painless, blood-free sampling with rapid skin recovery and no irritation. This scalable platform provides a versatile approach for minimally invasive biomarker profiling and may facilitate frequent disease monitoring and timely clinical decision-making.

title: Postimpact evolution of the South Pole–Aitken basin revealed by Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6
abstract: South Pole–Aitken (SPA) basin has recorded complex geological histories of the Moon. It is a critical region for solving lunar fundamental questions but remained unexplored until the Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6 missions of China. Their in situ measurements and the Chang’e-6 samples provided the first ground truth for the SPA evolution. On the basis of these constraints, we found that the SPA impact occurred ∼4.34 billion years ago, generating a thick melt sheet that differentiated to form moderately magnesium (Mg)–rich norites. They are exposed at the SPA central peaks and currently investigated by the Chang’e-4 mission in Von Kármán crater, transported by the Finsen impact to the site. Highly Mg-rich materials were found within SPA, likely products of Mg-suite magmatism, including those exposed at the Apollo western peak ring. They were initially excavated by the Apollo impact at ∼4.2 billion years ago and delivered to the Chang’e-6 site by the Chaffee S impact. A series of other events occurred in the SPA basin subsequently (e.g., the Orientale impact ∼3.87 billion years ago); all of them shaped the architecture of the Moon’s largest impact basin.

title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors
abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

title: Phylogeny explains differences in the crystal structures and chemistry of vertebrate tooth enamel and enameloid
abstract: A phylogenetically diverse suite of modern tooth enamel/enameloid bioapatite from fishes, mammals, and reptiles from 22 species were chemically and structurally analyzed to establish whether crystal structure and chemistry are phylogenetically correlated. Rietveld refinement analysis of x-ray diffraction data suggests variable crystallographic parameters across vertebrates. Coupled chemical data show correlations between the a -axis of bioapatite and the proportions of sodium substitution for calcium, the introduction of vacancies, and carbonate substituting for phosphate (B-type substitution) or channel anions (A-type substitution). Principal component analysis of all variables suggests that a -axis lengths are highly influenced by the introduction of carbonate in both crystallographic sites. Phylogenetic variations in chemistry and structure of enamel/enameloid crystals show how biomineralization processes have changed through evolutionary time with implications for variation in biomineralization processes across vertebrate lineages. The predominant controls on tooth enamel/enameloid crystal structure are phylogeny rather than primary diet or habitat. Crystal structure variations also influence material properties across organisms, which may control how teeth are fossilized.

title: Discovery of volatile- and Fe-rich melts from low-velocity zones above the mantle transition zone
abstract: Low-velocity layers atop the mantle transition zone (MTZ) are commonly observed and predicted to comprise volatile- and iron (Fe)–rich melts, yet direct evidence from natural samples remains lacking. Nephelinites from eastern China may preserve such signatures. They contain ultradeep peridotite fragments and show anomalously low potassium (K)/uranium (U) and barium (Ba)/thorium (Th) ratios, indicating derivation from recycled crustal materials in the MTZ, with high-pressure liebermannite residues retaining K-Ba. This study investigates Wuxi nephelinites, eastern China, where seismic tomography images a slab fragment in the MTZ (high-velocity anomalies) and an overlying low-velocity layer. Volatile- and Fe-rich melt inclusions [maximum FeO T content and Cl (chlorine)/K ratio of 21.8 weight % and 0.15, respectively] are identified in these rocks, consistent with predicted compositions of low-velocity zone melts. Phlogopite in unhomogenized inclusions further confirms their volatile-rich nature. Calculated densities of these inclusions exceed that of ambient mantle, thus stabilizing melts atop the MTZ. Sustained volatile influx or melt-rock reaction reduces melt density and triggers upward melt migration, forming nephelinites, providing key petrological record verifying the geophysically detected MTZ molten layer.

title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment
abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition–associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type–specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type–enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

title: Steering nanometric reductive-oxidative Fenton-like cycle for PFAS mineralization
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs), known as “forever chemicals,” have highly stable C─F bonds that render them resistant to destruction by conventional water treatment processes. Here, we developed a destructive technology that does not require external photo-, electro-, or heat energy input, relying simply on Fenton-like cycles (peroxymonosulfate activation) under nanometric spatial confinement. Unlike the ordinary activation process, confinement shielded peroxymonosulfate radicals ( S O 5 • − ) from external quenching and enabled them to remain active for reductive defluorination. Coupled with oxidative sulfate radicals ( S O 4 • − ), this process unlocked a synergistic “reduction-oxidation” destruction pathway. Specifically, the catalyst was designed by planting single-atom cobalt on MXene nanosheets, whose interlaminar confinement directed efficient PFAS mineralization via alternating α-carbon defluorination (by S O 5 • − ) and decarbonization (by S O 4 • − ). We further constructed a Fenton bed that allowed highly efficient and cost-effective treatment of PFASs in complex water matrices. Our findings underscore the promising potential of nanoconfinement in driving reductive-oxidative Fenton-like cycles toward efficient PFAS mineralization.

title: Chromatin loci move coherently due to spatially correlated fluctuations
abstract: From enhancer-promoter communication to DNA repair, essential genome functions require chromosomal loci to encounter each other. While live-cell imaging enables direct measurement of pairwise locus dynamics, a quantitative framework for interpreting them is lacking. Here, using imaging data from Drosophila embryos and mouse stem cells, we show that nearby loci diffuse relative to each other far more slowly than expected from polymer chain–mediated effects. We propose that this slowdown is caused by spatially correlated fluctuations (SCFs) which couple loci via the nucleoplasm. We theoretically predict how these fluctuations scale with space, time, and genomic separation and confirm these predictions using live-cell imaging. Using polymer simulations, we demonstrate that while spatially correlated equilibrium noise fails to reproduce the observed SCF scalings, coupling the polymer to actively driven flows recapitulates the experimental statistics. Consistently, we experimentally show that SCFs couple locus motion across chromosomes and that their magnitude depends on adenosine 5′-triphosphate (ATP)–dependent activity and cohesin-mediated loop extrusion. By reducing encounter frequencies while prolonging encounter durations, SCFs generate a trade-off with direct implications for gene regulation. Our results provide a quantitative framework for chromatin dynamics, revealing how nuclear activity governs chromatin encounters in living cells.

title: Beyond metabolites: A wearable biointerface integrating antibody and aptamer probes for the real-time tracking of proteins in vivo
abstract: Continuous monitoring of protein biomarkers could transform the management of acute and chronic diseases. Despite tremendous potential, wearable health monitors have remained largely limited to metabolites and small molecules. A key challenge is the limited availability of biointerfaces that reversibly track low-abundance proteins in vivo without user intervention. Here, we present the Differential Aptalyzer, a minimally invasive hydrogel microneedle platform for continuous monitoring of proteins in skin interstitial fluid. The platform combines high-affinity antibodies for selective target capture with aptamers for reversible electrochemical signal transduction. When integrated into a differential electrochemical chip and pulse-assisted sensor regeneration, this approach enables continuous monitoring of proteins in a wearable format. Using cardiac troponin I (cTnI) as a clinically relevant model analyte, Differential Aptalyzer offers a broad dynamic range (0.003 to 0.640 nanograms per milliliter) and strong specificity against interfering proteins. This platform reliably tracks both rising and falling exogenous cTnI levels injected into healthy mice, as well as endogenously elevated cTnI in a double-knockout mouse model of coronary artery disease, demonstrating its capability in continuous protein monitoring and identifying coronary artery disease cohorts.

title: The interferon-gamma response pathway is a targetable driver of FSHD muscular dystrophy progression
abstract: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is a leading neuromuscular disorder caused by the aberrant expression of the transcription factor double homeobox 4 (DUX4) in skeletal muscle. While DUX4 is normally restricted to early embryonic development, its reactivation in FSHD triggers chronic inflammation and progressive muscle degeneration. However, the precise molecular links between DUX4 and persistent immune activation remain poorly understood. Here, we show that DUX4 induces a viral mimicry-like pathway that is fundamentally uncoupled from canonical type I interferon (IFN) activation. Instead, DUX4 establishes a non-canonical innate immune state dominated by IFN-γ signaling, providing a mechanistic explanation for the non-resolving inflammation characteristic of the disease. We demonstrate that while IFN-γ treatment alone is sufficient to recapitulate key DUX4 pathogenic effects, its inhibition rescues muscle inflammation and halts disease progression in FSHD models. These findings define a “skewed viral mimicry” process driven by a disease-specific transcription factor and identify IFN-γ as a primary therapeutic target for tissue-informed immunomodulation in muscular dystrophy.

title: GenNA: Conditional generation of nucleotide sequences guided by natural language annotations
abstract: Deciphering the mapping between biomolecular sequences and complex biological functions is a central challenge in genomics. While existing generative nucleotide models capture sequence distributions, they lack explicit access to gene-associated biological semantics, limiting semantics-guided design. Here, we present GenNA, a generative nucleotide foundation model guided by natural language annotations. Pretrained on a multimodal nucleotide-text corpus spanning 2221 eukaryotic species (∼416 billion characters), GenNA internalizes relationships between sequence syntax and functional semantics within a unified autoregressive framework. Without explicit rule-based supervision, GenNA yields distinguishable perplexity responses to sequence-annotation mismatches, mutational variants, and species-label perturbations. Furthermore, across diverse generation tasks, GenNA produces statistically plausible nucleotide sequences consistent with target semantics, structural constraints, and species contexts. Overall, GenNA provides a versatile framework for controllable nucleotide generation, establishing a practical route to integrate functional descriptions with sequence design.

title: Interband connectivity and climate shaped Neanderthal extinction and Homo sapiens ’ dispersal
abstract: To what extent Neanderthal extinction was triggered by climate change or the arrival of Homo sapiens , and by which mechanisms, remains unresolved. Here, on the basis of climate-driven changes in habitat favorability for primary and secondary consumers and in net primary productivity, we estimate carrying capacity, herbivore biomass, and intraguild predation pressure during the time Neanderthals and H. sapiens lived in Europe. These spatially explicit estimates were incorporated into an agent-based model simulating human demographic dynamics under various scenarios. Results indicate that carrying capacity changes cannot explain Neanderthal extinction at a continental scale, though they are essential to understanding spatiotemporal distribution patterns of both human species. Conversely, the arrival of H. sapiens remarkably increased Neanderthal extinction likelihood. Because of the successive demographic expansions and contractions, group connectivity emerges as the key factor shaping population stability in both species. These findings support that Neanderthal disappearance and H. sapiens dispersals were interconnected demographic processes.

title: Cross-domain encoding models reveal shared and domain-specific neural representations across language and mathematics
abstract: Whether language and mathematics rely on shared or distinct neural representations remains unresolved in cognitive neuroscience. Here, we combined latent features from a large language model with functional magnetic resonance imaging encoding models to test cross-domain generalization in 32 participants performing sentence comprehension and calculation tasks. Cross-domain prediction identified cortical regions showing partially shared representations, most consistently in the left area 55b, while control analyses suggested that these effects could not be fully explained by low-level visual or task-general factors. Domain-specificity contrasts revealed stronger language-related prediction in the left superior temporal sulcus and angular gyrus and math-related prediction in the left precentral sulcus and bilateral intraparietal sulci. Model-weight analyses revealed distinct weight profiles associated with shared and domain-specific prediction patterns. Cross-domain regions also exhibited task-dependent functional coupling with language- and math-related networks. Together, these findings suggest that language and mathematics involve partially shared neural representations alongside domain-specific cortical organization, helping reconcile previous contrasting views on their neural basis.

title: Bionic skin with hair follicle regeneration capability from acoustic fluids-mediated 3D printing
abstract: Tissue engineering holds substantial potential for constructing normal skin with appendages such as hair follicles, directly restoring skin’s complete physiological functions. The current challenge lies in recreating biomimetic hair follicle organs with high-level cell density and architecture. Here, we developed an acoustofluidic-assisted 3D bioprinting platform to fabricate bionic skins with efficient hair follicle regeneration capability. Pre-formed hair follicle germs, derived from co-cultured epidermal and dermal mesenchymal stem cells, were encapsulated within a hydrogel bioink. Controlled acoustic fields generated flow vortices that directed cell migration and promoted organized cellular assembly from initially disordered states. Guided cell aggregates were then patterned through bioprinting to construct a grid-structured bionic skin. This architecture provided stable 3D support while maintaining high porosity, enabling efficient gas exchange. The printed bionic skin exhibited well-organized spatial cell distribution, high cellular viability, and promising differentiation potential. Further in vivo experiments demonstrated the efficiency of the bionic skin in accelerating mature hair regeneration, showing promise for clinical alopecia treatment.

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl − induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85°C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Hydrogen radical-participating spatiotemporal sequential therapy via hypoxia aggravation for hypoxia-amplified immunotherapy
abstract: The hypoxic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment and endogenous antioxidant defenses compromise the efficacy of oxygen-consuming oxidative therapy, positioning oxygen-free reductive stress as a new paradigm in tumor treatment. Nevertheless, the immunosuppressive characteristics of hypoxia and reductive stress pose significant challenges for advancing reductive stress-induced immunotherapy. Here, we constructed a hydrogen radical (H•) generator synergistically activated by near-infrared light and thiols, and first elucidated that photocatalytic H•-mediated reductive stress can elicit a robust antitumor immune response via the H•-featured mechanism. Nanoplatform HA@UFTL was engineered using lactate oxidase as an ideal H• partner, with the synergistic contribution enabling cross-amplified antitumor immunotherapy. The H•-participating spatiotemporal sequential strategy highlights a triple spatiotemporal sequential cascade, including dual sequential hypoxia exacerbation, sequential oxidative-reductive stress, and sequential organelle damage. By aggravating rather than alleviating hypoxia, HA@UFTL overcomes immunosuppression induced by hypoxia and reductive stress with H• as a universal building block, providing new insights for hypoxia-based immunotherapy.

title: Non-invasive, high-precision, and independently controllable neuromodulation via optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation
abstract: Non-invasive neuromodulation is an important approach in clinical and translational neuroscience, yet existing techniques remain limited in precisely and flexibly targeting spatially distributed brain regions. Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) enabled non-invasive selective targeting; however, conventional implementations lack sufficient spatial focality, steerability, and scalability for network-level modulation. Here, we introduce optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation (omTIS), a computationally optimized framework that achieves high spatial focality, flexible steerability, and scalable control for distributed neuromodulation. Using a multi-electrode architecture, finite element analysis (FEA)–based optimization, and carefully selected multiple carrier frequencies, omTIS generates focal interference envelopes that can be positioned across multiple brain targets, enabling simultaneous and independently controllable multi-focal stimulation with minimal mutual interference. Across simulations, tissue-mimicking phantom experiments, and in vivo mouse studies, omTIS outperformed conventional TIS in spatial selectivity, steering flexibility, and cross-talk-free multi-focal modulation. These results establish omTIS as a scalable platform for precise, non-invasive control of distributed brain networks.

title: Phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization enables record NIR-II-to-visible-light photon upconversion
abstract: Near-infrared-to-visible triplet−triplet annihilation photon upconversion (TTA-UC) enables harvesting low-energy photons; however, extending nanocrystal-sensitized TTA-UC into the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) remains challenging because triplet sensitization is thermodynamically disfavored under sub-triplet excitation. Here, we demonstrate that lead-free AgBiS 2 nanocrystals facilitate phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization, enabling efficient NIR-II-to-visible upconversion. Under the sub-bandgap single-photon excitation, AgBiS 2 nanocrystals exhibit anti-Stokes photoluminescence, suggesting strong exciton−phonon coupling mediated by surface states. When coupled with 5-tetracene carboxylic acid transmitters and rubrene annihilators, AgBiS 2 achieves 980 nm-to-visible upconversion with a record quantum yield of 6.22% (normalized to 100%) and an anti-Stokes shift of 0.95 eV. Time-resolved photoluminescence and ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy support a surface-state-mediated uphill energy-transfer pathway coupled to low-frequency vibrational modes. Our work establishes phonon-assisted triplet sensitization as a strategy to overcome the NIR-II red wall for lead-free photon upconversion.

title: Environment-adaptive molecular neural networks enabled by heterogeneous threshold DNA neuron
abstract: Molecular neural networks enable autonomous information processing in biochemical environments, yet most existing DNA-based implementations operate with fixed connectivity after assembly, limiting their ability to adapt network topology to changing environments. Here, we report an environment-adaptive molecular neural network enabled by DNA neurons with sequence-programmed, heterogeneous activation thresholds. These neurons incorporate triplex-based proton-gated DNA switches with tunable pH-response windows, which regulate the accessibility of toehold and recognition domains to switch pre-encoded weighted connections between inactive and signal-propagating states, thereby reconfiguring network connectivity without changing molecular composition. We demonstrate this principle in a DNA neural network that processes 64-bit inputs, where environmental acidification activates dormant neurons and reconfigures the computational topology from a sparse convolutional neural network for coarse two-class categorization into a fully connected neural network for fine-grained discrimination among four distinct patterns. Our results establish DNA-based neural circuits capable of adapting their computational architecture to environmental cues, offering a framework for molecular information processing in fluctuating biochemical environments.

title: Recovery and resurrection of chiral homogeneous catalysts for closed-loop recycling
abstract: Homogeneous catalysis by transition metal complexes is essential for chemical synthesis; however, these processes remain unsustainable because the catalysts are generally not recovered. We address this problem with a framework for closed-loop catalyst recycling. This approach centers on two chemical processes: stasis, where catalytic activity is selectively halted while retaining molecular integrity; and anastasis, where full catalytic function is restored. We apply this framework to recycle chiral palladium catalysts used for asymmetric allylic alkylation. ortho -Quinone oxidants drive the catalyst to converge on a discrete Pd II complex that is readily recovered, while mild reductants regenerate active Pd 0 precatalysts in a subsequent step. By rendering catalyst deactivation, isolation, and reactivation chemically addressable, this work is an important step toward circular, resource-efficient synthesis.

title: Investigation of anti-SARS-CoV-2 multimeric bicyclic peptide inhibitors in a range of preclinical therapeutic settings.
abstract: The spread of respiratory viruses, such as influenza and SARS-CoV-2, has presented significant challenges over the last 30 years, with few effective therapeutic options available to this day. Bicyclic peptides represent a unique, modular modality in the antiviral armamentarium against future pandemics. This study utilizes tool molecules to provide a deeper evaluation of multivalent bicyclic (Bicycle) molecule efficacy in several preclinical SARS-CoV-2 challenge settings. We explore both pre-exposure prophylaxis and post-exposure therapeutic settings via subcutaneous and intranasal routes of administration. We contextualize this further in bespoke scenarios where the immune system is compromised, as well as viral transmission. Promisingly, in all studies, we observe efficacy, significantly reducing infectious viral burden at each study endpoint. These data further support the candidacy of Bicycle molecules as a differentiated antiviral therapeutic class in the context of pandemic preparedness. IMPORTANCE The COVID-19 pandemic triggered a rapid wave of innovation, accelerating the delivery of new vaccine technology and antiviral treatments. In our first paper, we described the discovery and molecular optimization of Bicycle molecules as a novel drug class for the potential treatment of SARS-CoV-2. Here, we have performed deeper characterization of these tool molecules in established animal models to evaluate scenarios for deployment, simulating SARS-CoV-2 transmission, testing more convenient delivery routes, such as intranasal, as well as looking at immunocompromised animals. The Bicycle molecules demonstrated positive outcomes in each of these studies and suggest that Bicycle molecules, as convenient and effective antiviral treatments, could be an important addition to help future preparedness against new viral pandemics.
