title: Multicomponent Model Cellular System for Studying Molecular Mechanisms of Cytotoxicity of Antileukemic Agents
abstract: Despite recent advances in chemotherapy, over 20% of leukemia patients suffer from a relapse or refractory disease, largely due to leukemic stem cell survival in specialized bone marrow niches. Malignant cell interactions with stromal elements activate compensatory pathways that inhibit apoptosis and differentiation, enhancing cell survival and drug resistance. Overcoming this resistance requires novel therapeutic targets and adequate models for testing their inhibitors. An experimental co-culture model was developed using suspension blood cell lines and HS-5 stromal cells with ectopic expression of the enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP). The model allows efficient separation and analysis of suspension and adherent fractions using flow cytometry. Co-culture with the stroma was shown to promote leukemic cell survival and adhesion. Interestingly, treatment with the cytostatic drug cytarabine enhanced tumor cell adhesion, while hypoxia reduced adhesion. Additionally, contact with HS-5 fibroblasts significantly upregulated expression of key chemokines, their receptors, and cell adhesion molecules in leukemic cells. The model was thus found to provide an attractive tool for studying the mechanisms of stroma-dependent resistance and developing novel approaches to overcoming chemotherapy resistance in leukemia.

title: An Integrated Inversion Framework for Efficient Identification of Groundwater Contamination Source with Deep Learning Tools
Systematic Characterization of Clinically Actionable Antibody-Drug Targets Across Solid Tumors to Advance Precision Oncology.
abstract: The rapid expansion of antibody therapeutics is shifting the clinical bottleneck from drug availability to precise patient selection. We systematically characterize 87 clinically actionable tumor-associated antigens across solid tumors by integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, spatial, and single-cell profiles from more than 32,000 specimens to define expression prevalence, intratumoral heterogeneity, immune contexture, internalization and payload-sensitivity pathways, and translational relevance. We establish ANCHOR, a coordinate reference framework for standardizing patient RNA-seq data, and develop ReSort, a two-tiered scoring system for scalable target prioritization. ReSort enables virtual basket and umbrella trial matching, demonstrates concordance with clinical assays, predicts therapeutic response in patient-derived models, and identifies repurposing opportunities in rare malignancies. We develop an AI-based decision-support agent for antibody trial matching and construct a multimodal feature space integrating tumor- and protein-intrinsic attributes to guide systematic target discovery and prioritization. This work provides a scalable, clinically actionable approach for precision antibody-based therapies and next-generation target development.

title: VEGF-4-1BB Conditional Bifunctional Antibody Drives Tumor-Localized Immunity through Sustained Macrophage and T-cell Activation.
abstract: AMP-410 achieves potent antitumor efficacy with high therapeutic index and favorable tolerability in murine tumor models. It is a conditional bifunctional VEGF-4-1BB biologic designed to simultaneously neutralize VEGF and activate 4-1BB signaling, delivering a localized and dual-action approach to immunotherapy. By leveraging VEGF-dependent activation of 4-1BB, AMP-410 preferentially enhances immune responses within the tumor microenvironment, minimizing systemic toxicity while amplifying innate and adaptive immunity. In human 4-1BB transgenic mice bearing syngeneic tumors (MC38 colorectal carcinoma and B16F10 melanoma), AMP-410 promoted rapid M1 macrophage differentiation and enhanced progenitor-exhausted (Pex) T-cell signatures, suggesting coordinated activation of innate and adaptive compartments. At later stages, AMP-410 sustained macrophage antitumor activity and a continued expansion of Pex cells, consistent with long-term immune engagement. Localized activity was indicated by clonal T-cell expansion within tumors with minimal draining lymph node exchange. Compared with the systemic 4-1BB agonist urelumab in syngeneic tumor models, AMP-410 provided superior long-term protection with reduced exhaustion and improved hepatic tolerability. In head-to-head testing against a VEGF-PD-1 bispecific, AMP-410 achieved robust tumor suppression and survival benefits without systemic IFNγ surges. To establish translational relevance, VEGF concentrations were measured in tumor interstitial fluid from patients with cancer. VEGF levels were consistently two to four orders of magnitude higher in tumors than in matched serum, supporting the clinical opportunity of VEGF-restricted 4-1BB activation. Together, these studies position AMP-410 as a promising next-generation immunotherapy for both monotherapy and combination settings, with the potential to overcome key limitations of existing checkpoint- and 4-1BB-based approaches. SIGNIFICANCE Localizing 4-1BB activity to VEGF-rich tumor microenvironments may expand the therapeutic window of 4-1BB costimulation, promoting strong antitumor immunity while limiting systemic immune activation and liver inflammation.

title: Growth Differentiation Factor 15 as a Body-Brain Stress Signal in Major Depression and Insulin Resistance.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Major depressive disorder (MDD) is linked to insulin resistance, which is associated with increased risk, chronicity, and poor treatment response in depression. Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15), a stress-induced cytokine linking peripheral to central energy metabolism, may mediate this link, but its role in MDD is unclear. The authors assessed associations of MDD and insulin resistance with GDF15; links between GDF15, symptoms, and stress; and whether baseline GDF15 levels predict symptom persistence. METHODS In this preregistered secondary analysis, 190 participants with MDD and 183 control participants provided blood, underwent interviews, and completed questionnaires. GDF15 values were log-transformed and analyzed with linear models. The association between GDF15 and depression severity was validated in an independent cohort of medication-free MDD patients (N=168). RESULTS Both MDD diagnosis and insulin resistance were significantly associated with elevated GDF15 (adjusted for age and sex). Across all participants, elevated GDF15 was significantly associated with greater depressive severity, childhood trauma, and perceived stress. In stratified analyses, the association with depression severity and perceived stress was significant only in healthy control subjects. In MDD patients, baseline GDF15 was associated with persistence of symptoms across time. In the second independent sample of medication-free MDD patients, depression severity was significantly associated with GDF15. CONCLUSIONS GDF15 is elevated in MDD and insulin resistance, indicating convergent stress-energy pathway activation, and in MDD higher GDF15 predicted symptom persistence. These findings position GDF15 as a mechanistic biomarker at the interface of psychiatric and metabolic health and reinforce the need for integrated care of metabolic and mental health.

title: Usability of an artificial intelligence enabled Participation and Environment Measure prototype for family-centered goal setting support in pediatric rehabilitation
abstract: Family-centered care coordination (FC-CC) in pediatric rehabilitation benefits from tools that support caregivers in contributing to personalized service planning for their children. Participation and Environment Measure (PEM) is a digital application that is being further developed to support FC-CC in early intervention (EI). PEM is being further developed to include the Young Children’s Participation and Environment Measure (YC-PEM) electronic patient-reported outcome and a companion PEM-Plus (PEM+) goal setting intervention. This study examined usability of the first artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled PEM prototype. Caregivers from an urban EI program met these eligibility criteria: (1) were at least 18 years old; (2) identified as the parent or legal guardian of a child enrolled in EI services; (3) read, wrote, and spoke English; (4) had internet and telephone access; and (5) had a child 0–3 years old who received EI services for 3 or more months. Participants completed the AI-enabled PEM application with access to a debiased prototypic conversational agent. PEM usability was assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS), and chatbot usability was assessed along four BOT Usability Scale (BUS-11) domains: 1) accessibility of chatbot functions; 2) functional interactive conversation; 3) privacy and security; and 4) timely response. Univariate logistic regression models were used to examine associations between each of the four BUS-11 domains and PEM+ engagement. Eleven female caregivers of children (mean age: 24.5 months) enrolled, 66.7% of whom interacted with the prototypic chatbot during one or more iterations of the PEM+ intervention. Overall PEM usability remained acceptable. While overall chatbot usability was very poor (Mdn = 53.4%, IQR = 50.0, 55.4), caregiver perceptions of chatbot usability were average for accessibility of chatbot functions (Mdn = 3.8, IQR = 3.0, 4.0) and good for privacy and security (M = 3.1, Range = 2.0–5.0). Higher caregiver perceptions of chatbot usability did not significantly increase odds of PEM+ intervention use. Findings indicate that an AI-enabled PEM retains adequate usability. A chatbot integrated within the PEM+ intervention is accessible and secure, though its functional interactive conversation and timely responses could benefit from further development to increase odds of its use in an EI service context. NCT06458959 (Registration date: 2024–06-14)
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Traditional Chinese medicine modulates Notch signaling in inflammatory bowel disease: from restorative inhibition to context-dependent fine-tuning
abstract: The Notch signaling pathway serves as a critical rheostat in intestinal homeostasis, yet its dysregulation in ulcerative colitis (UC) presents a therapeutic paradox: hyperactivation depletes goblet cells and erodes the mucus barrier, whereas inhibition impairs epithelial regeneration. This duality underscores the limitations of indiscriminate pathway blockade and highlights the need for therapeutic strategies that account for disease stage, cell type, and the narrow homeostatic window of Notch signaling. This narrative mechanistic review critically synthesizes preclinical evidence on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM)-mediated modulation of Notch signaling in experimental colitis and proposes an evidence-stratified framework that distinguishes predominant restorative inhibition of excessive Notch/Hes1 activity from less common patterns of pathway activation, node-specific regulation, and stage-dependent modulation. A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CNKI, and Wanfang up to April 2026. Studies were selected if they examined TCM-related interventions in IBD, experimental colitis, or relevant intestinal barrier models and reported Notch pathway components, Notch-associated epithelial or inflammatory outcomes, or mechanistically related pathways. Evidence was narratively synthesized and categorized according to mechanistic level and strength of Notch involvement. Most available evidence was preclinical and derived from UC-like experimental colitis models. Across three hierarchical levels, most characterized TCM interventions were associated with restorative suppression of excessive Notch/Hes1-related activity, accompanied by recovery of Atoh1/Math1 expression, goblet-cell differentiation, and mucus-barrier function. Sinomenine and Qing-Bai Decoction (QBD) were associated with reduced NICD abundance and/or nuclear localization, whereas Wu-Mei-Wan attenuated Notch/NF-κB inflammatory crosstalk. Gegen Qinlian Decoction (GQD) provided the clearest current example of stage-dependent changes in tissue-level Notch-related readouts, with Hes1 suppression in acute colitis and Hes1 elevation in chronic colitis. Current preclinical evidence suggests that TCM-related interventions modulate Notch-associated epithelial and inflammatory networks through heterogeneous mechanisms, most commonly by suppressing excessive Notch/Hes1 activity in acute experimental colitis. The current evidence is strongest for UC-like experimental colitis, while its applicability to Crohn’s disease remains less well established. True context-dependent recalibration of Notch signaling remains an emerging concept requiring further mechanistic and cell-type-specific validation.

title: Sheep grazing within regenerative perennial systems accelerates soil carbon and nitrogen accrual
abstract: Global agricultural intensification and crop-livestock decoupling have reduced soil carbon and nitrogen stocks, weakening terrestrial carbon sinks and altering nutrient cycling. Integrating livestock into cropping systems is a cornerstone regenerative practice, with the potential to enhance carbon and nitrogen storage. However, on-farm research quantifying outcomes of stacked regenerative production models remains limited, and it is unclear how grazing, alone or combined with other practices, affects soil carbon and nitrogen accrual. We assessed carbon and nitrogen stocks (0–60 cm), including mineral-associated and particulate organic matter pools, microbial biomass and plant productivity across 49 California (USA) vineyards spanning conventional to regenerative management, with and without sheep grazing. We evaluated the relative contributions of management practices to carbon and nitrogen pools, accounting for spatial and edaphic predictors, and estimated accrual rates from vineyards with differing management histories (space-for-time substitution). Grazing emerged as the most influential management practice for increasing soil organic matter pool stocks, followed by reduced physical disturbance and permanent ground cover. Other regenerative practices, including organic amendments and avoidance of synthetic insecticides, showed positive but more variable associations with soil organic matter pool stocks. Grazing was strongly associated with approximately fivefold higher nitrogen accrual rates (+ 0.04 ± 0.01 Mg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹), including plant-available nitrogen (+ 0.94 ± 0.30 kg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹), and more than threefold higher soil carbon accrual within regenerative management systems relative to conventional ungrazed systems (+ 0.38 ± 0.13 Mg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹). Grazing was also associated with greater microbial biomass and plant productivity, consistent with enhanced carbon and nitrogen cycling. Under grazing, greater nitrogen availability and more robust plant and microbial communities likely reduced microbial nitrogen limitation while enhancing carbon sequestration and stabilization. Geography and edaphic properties constrained soil carbon and nitrogen accumulation. These patterns proved robust across geographically independent farms, highlighting the value of multi-farm datasets for climate-mitigation assessments. These results demonstrate that integrating grazing within regenerative perennial systems can help meet mitigation targets while building nitrogen stocks and reducing synthetic fertilizer reliance. This underscores the importance of research on commercial operations for translating site-specific results into scalable, climate-smart farming strategies.

title: Differentiable inverse design of Bessel-like beams with tunable focal depth and uniform on-axis intensity
LightTeaNet: SeparableConv-based lightweight CNN with Grad-CAM explainability for tea leaf disease identification
abstract: Global tea production, valued at USD 25.6 billion in 2024, faces annual yield losses of approximately 20% due to foliar diseases, yet existing deep learning-based detection systems remain impractical for real-world deployment due to prohibitive computational requirements and limited interpretability. This paper presents a purpose-built lightweight convolutional neural network architecture for four-class tea leaf disease classification (Brown Blight, Red Rust, Red Spider Mite, and Healthy Leaves) that achieves an exceptional balance between classification accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed model leverages depthwise separable convolutions across four progressive feature extraction blocks, integrated with Batch Normalization, Global Average Pooling, and Dropout regularization to minimize parameter count while maintaining discriminative feature learning. Evaluated on the TeaLeafNet dataset (5,000 balanced images across four categories), the model achieves 98.14% classification accuracy with only 80,959 trainable parameters—representing a 90-fold reduction compared to DenseNet121 (7.3M parameters)—and a model size of merely 0.31 MB, while requiring only 191.29 million FLOPs, approximately 160 × fewer than VGG16 (30.71B FLOPs). The model demonstrates robust per-class performance with F1-scores of 0.97 or higher across all categories and perfect ROC-AUC values of 1.000 for two classes. Grad-CAM visualization, validated through quantitative Insertion (AUC: 0.972) and Deletion (AUC: 0.181) faithfulness evaluation, confirms that the model’s predictions are driven by diagnostically relevant leaf regions, achieving model transparency essential for agricultural adoption. Comparative analysis against nine state-of-the-art architectures—including DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB1—reveals that while DenseNet121 achieves marginally higher accuracy (99.20%), it requires 90 × more parameters and 30 × more computational operations, rendering it unsuitable for edge deployment. The proposed framework offers the most compact architecture among all evaluated models with competitive accuracy, establishing a new benchmark for resource-constrained tea disease diagnosis in precision agriculture systems. By enabling accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient disease detection, this work addresses critical barriers to the practical deployment of AI-driven crop monitoring on mobile devices, unmanned aerial vehicles, and IoT-enabled agricultural sensors.

title: ANALYSIS OF GEOMETRIC ACCURACY OF GAOFEN-7 SATELLITE SCENES
abstract: The aim of this article was to investigate the quality and accuracy of images taken from the first Chinese civilian VHRS Gaofen-7 satellite. Visual evaluation of the images was carried out, in particular, to assess the remote sensing capabilities of objects with sizes comparable to the field size at the sampling distance (GSD). The main part of the experiment was geometric analysis, in which the distribution of errors in the positions of the measurement points relative to the aerial orthophoto was examined, divided by their distance from the sensor, including the imaging angle for forward and backward imaging. Distance measurement errors were also checked by measuring the differences in the length of individual objects in relation to their orientation and the image angle of view. The result was the determination of the average geometric accuracy at approximately this level. 10 m. The measurement accuracy of linear objects was close to the spatial resolution of the imagery, within the limits of the measurement error. The experiments proved that Gaofen-7 satellite scenes have measurement potential that approaches the sensor's spatial resolution, making them useful for the applications for which this system was designed.
journal: Archives of Photogrammetry, Cartography and Remote Sensing

title: An assessment of integrated nutrient management as a climate-smart approach to sustainable soil health and agricultural productivity
abstract: The rapid increase in global population has significantly intensified the demand for food production, necessitating the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices. Integrated nutrient management (INM) combines inorganic fertilisers, organic amendments and biofertiliser inputs to optimise nutrient availability, whereas conventional systems predominantly rely on excessive chemical fertilisers, which compromise long-term sustainability through soil degradation and environmental pollution. This study provides a comprehensive review of existing literature, encompassing field experiments, long-term trials and simulation modelling to evaluate the concepts, objectives and principles of INM across diverse agroecosystems. Studies report substantial reductions in greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions (20 % to over 1300 %) under INM across India, Zimbabwe and China, highlighting its global potential. The integrated application of organic and biofertilisers increased available phosphorus by about 7.5 % over 100 % of the recommended dose of fertiliser (RDF) alone. The highest soil organic carbon (0.894 %) was recorded under 25 % RDF + 75 % poultry manure (10 t ha-1), compared with 0.614 % under sole RDF, while maximum soil microbial biomass carbon was observed with 50 % inorganic N + 25 % farmyard manure combined with dual cropping of Azolla. Findings indicate that INM significantly improves crop yield over conventional practices while enhancing nutrient use efficiency (NUE) and farm profitability by positively influencing the physical, chemical and biological properties of soils. This review highlights that INM is a sustainable, innovative and eco-friendly strategy for managing reactive nitrogen losses, improving soil quality and ensuring global food security.

title: The Development of Breast Apocrine Carcinoma Score That Distinguishes Breast and Cutaneous Apocrine Carcinomas.
abstract: Background Apocrine carcinoma (AC) is a rare cancer that arises either from cutaneous apocrine sweat glands (cutaneous AC) or as breast carcinoma with apocrine differentiation (breast AC). Differentiation between them is clinically critical because their management and outcomes differ significantly: breast AC is treated according to established breast cancer therapies, whereas cutaneous AC lacks standardized systemic treatment and often carries a poorer prognosis. A diagnostic challenge arises when AC occurs in the axilla, where both entities may arise, given their highly similar histology. Methods In this study, we performed a retrospective multi-cohort transcriptomic analysis integrating institutional, multi-institutional, and publicly available datasets to characterize the molecular differences between breast and cutaneous ACs and developed a transcriptomic classifier using differentially expressed genes and a least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression model for tissue-of-origin classification. Results Transcriptomic profiling revealed that breast ACs exhibited higher steroid hormone-related signaling and lower proliferative activity compared with cutaneous ACs, while immune-related features were largely comparable between the two tumor types. These findings suggest that, despite shared apocrine morphology, breast and cutaneous ACs retain distinct biological characteristics reflective of their tissue of origin. Building on this, we further developed a transcriptomic classifier, the Breast Apocrine Carcinoma (BAC) score, which distinguished breast and cutaneous ACs, suggesting that these tumors retain distinct tissue-of-origin transcriptional signatures despite shared apocrine differentiation. Furthermore, application of the BAC score to tumors with unknown primary origin in the axillary region enabled estimation of tissue origin, highlighting its potential clinical utility in diagnostically challenging cases. Conclusions Breast and cutaneous ACs exhibit distinct biological features despite shared apocrine morphology. The BAC score showed promising discriminatory ability for tumors of breast and cutaneous origin, including within AC cohorts, highlighting the potential utility of transcriptomic profiling for improving their classification and diagnostic evaluation.

title: Turbulence-aware free-space optical communication system hybrid CNN–LSTM channel modeling, adaptive prediction, and real-time mitigation
abstract: Atmospheric optical turbulence severely degrades the performance of free-space optical communication. Mitigating these effects without costly additional hardware remains an open challenge. This paper presents a fully machine learning–driven adaptive modulation and coding architecture that combines a first-principles neural surrogate model with a hybrid deep learning predictor to optimize the modulation and coding scheme. A feed-forward neural network, trained on exact Kolmogorov phase-screen statistics, learns the differentiable mapping from the refractive-index structure parameter C n 2 ${C}_{n}^{2}$ to the gamma–gamma channel parameters α and β, bypassing the limitations of standard Rytov approximations. Turbulence forecasting, a systematic ablation study demonstrates that a hybrid convolutional-recurrent architecture with temporal attention achieves a near-perfect coefficient of determination (R 2 = 0.9956) for log 10 C n 2 ${\mathrm{log}}_{10} {C}_{n}^{2}$ , dramatically outperforming standalone CNN (R 2 = −104.42) and LSTM (R 2 = −0.06) models. The predicted channel state drives a threshold-based MCS selector evaluated through exact analytic integrals for outage probability, average bit error rate (BER), and spectral efficiency. When benchmarked against adaptive optics, the predictive scheme achieves a 9.3 % lower average BER and a 10.5 % lower outage probability, corresponding to absolute values of 2.04 × 10−4 and 0.0068, respectively. In fact, a reduction in inference time by 15.7 % in comparison with the CNN-only model, amounting to an inference time of 86.45 ms. The proposed approach, therefore, provides a feasible, low-complexity solution for mitigating atmospheric turbulence in FSO systems.

title: Optimization of Spray Drying Parameters for Producing Red Pitahaya Powder Using Response Surface Methodology
abstract: Research background. Red pitahaya (Hylocereus polyrhizus) is an exotic tropical fruit rich in antioxidants and betalains, but it is characterised by a relatively short shelf life. An effective and safe means of processing this fruit is the production of dehydrated products that can be readily reconstituted. Therefore, this study aimed to optimise the spray drying parameters for producing red pitahaya powder with suitable physicochemical and reconstitution properties. Experimental approach. Response surface methodology based on a central composite design was applied to evaluate the effects of inlet air temperature, feed flow rate and maltodextrin mass per volume ratio. The experimental data were modelled using a second-order polynomial equation to describe and predict the assessed responses: yield, moisture, water activity, hygroscopicity, flowability, cohesion and solubility. In the optimised sample, betalains, total phenols and antioxidant capacity were quantified as complementary quality indicators. Particle size and morphology were analysed using scanning electron microscopy. Results and conclusions. The quadratic models adequately described the main physicochemical responses, including yield, moisture content, water activity, flowability, cohesion and solubility. The selected processing conditions resulted in a powder with suitable physicochemical characteristics and reconstitution properties, including appropriate powder recovery, moisture content, water activity, flowability and solubility. The powder also showed measurable levels of betalains, phenolic compounds and antioxidant capacity. Microscopic observations revealed irregular particles with smooth surfaces and no visible cracks or fractures. Novelty and scientific contribution. The results demonstrate that inlet air temperature, feed flow rate and maltodextrin mass per volume ratio influenced the physicochemical and reconstitution properties of red pitahaya powder. The scientific contribution of this work lies in defining suitable processing conditions for a juice matrix rich in low-molecular-mass sugars and natural pigments, where powder recovery, moisture control, water activity, flowability and solubility must be balanced. These findings provide specific information for the production of red pitahaya powder with suitable technological properties and support its potential use as an ingredient in food formulations.

title: Innovative Approaches to Human Capital Development and Insurance in the Agricultural Sector Based on Digital Technologies and Risk Management
abstract: Agricultural digitalization creates interdependent demands for employee competencies, reliable data transmission, and accountable insurance decisions. This article develops a framework connecting these requirements and reports a reproducible analysis of a workbook supplied by the authors. The authors identify the underlying records as real-world data. The workbook contains 1,220 insurance-related records, a separate set of 540 regression records, 120 technical-run records, and three assumption-based scenarios. Three ordinary least-squares models include country and year indicators and use HC3 standard errors. Standardized digital-skills coefficients are 0.155 for the productivity response, 0.261 for the employment-stability response, and 0.279 for the resilience response. These estimates describe associations within the analyzed records; they do not establish causal effects or population representativeness. Separate technical summaries distinguish a 19.5% difference in computation time from a 61.4% difference in combined transmission and computation time. The scenario values reproduce a 24.7% accuracy-target increase and a 17.0% gap-target reduction through arithmetic applied to stipulated endpoints, rather than forecasting. The contribution is methodological: explicit separation of data provenance, variable construction, statistical association, technical comparison, and managerial interpretation. Training, recruitment, and professional development remain proposed applications rather than measured interventions. Incomplete source-level documentation and measurement validation constrain external interpretation of the results.

title: Bankruptcy Risk Analysis and Estimation of Healthy and Distressed Stocks Using Extended Black-Scholes Model
abstract: The classical Black-Scholes model assumes that stock prices follow a Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM) process, in which stock prices remain strictly positive throughout time. However, this assumption restricts the model’s capability to represent firms experiencing financial distress, where stock prices may gradually approach zero as bankruptcy risk increases. This study employs the Extended Black-Scholes Model (EBSM), which introduces a stoppingtime mechanism that enables stock prices to reach the bankruptcy boundary, to analyze and compare bankruptcy risk characteristics between financially healthy and distressed stocks. Historical adjusted closing price data from Microsoft Corporation (MSFT.US) and Bed Bath Beyond Inc. (BBBY.US) were utilized, with model parameters estimated using quadratic variation and Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) methods. The estimation results revealed different stochastic characteristics between the two stocks, where MSFT.US generated a positive drift parameter of 0.216682, whereas BBBY.US generated a negative drift parameter of −0.248385 along with higher volatility. The bankruptcy risk analysis demonstrated that MSFT.US produced infinite Expected Bankruptcy Time (EBT) and Conditional Expected Bankruptcy Time (CEBT) values, while BBBY.US yielded a finite EBT of 5.113633 years, with CEBT values updated according to the observed stock price conditions. These results suggest that the EBSM framework can effectively differentiate bankruptcy risk characteristics by combining stochastic stock price dynamics with time-to-bankruptcy measures.
journal: CAUCHY: Jurnal Matematika Murni dan Aplikasi

title: AI agents for science and society in 2025: ten representative advances
Configuration selection and matrix-aware optimization for data-efficient atomistic foundation models
abstract: Atomistic foundation models achieve high accuracy by training on very large labeled datasets. However, it remains unclear how much of this data is actually needed. Data-efficient training requires a better understanding of the roles of both data selection and model optimization. Here, we study these two factors separately using MACE-OFF24 as a baseline. We build smaller training sets by selecting configurations to cover diverse local atomic environments and include cases with large teacher-model errors. We then compare AdamW with the matrix-aware Muon optimizer using the same training data. We selected approximately 21% of the available configurations (190,000 for training and 10,000 for validation). Training from scratch produced energy and force root-mean-square errors within 8.1% and 6% of those obtained with the published checkpoint. On the fixed 200k subset, Muon reduced mean energy and force errors by 29% and 6% relative to AdamW. In a single-run comparison of selection rules within a fixed candidate pool at 49k, the 80:20 representative/residual allocation gave the lowest observed energy and force errors. On a separate small test set of approximately 7,000 3BPA conformers, AdamW instead gave the lowest mean relative-energy and energy-span errors. Our results show that data-efficient training of atomistic foundation models is jointly controlled by configuration coverage, optimizer geometry, chemical regime, and target observable. Especially, for training on big datasets, matrix-aware updates can improve broad from-scratch energy-force training.

title: Modelling and Simulation of the Operation and Maintenance Process of Means of Transport in an Urban Public Transport System
abstract: This paper presents a model of the operation and maintenance process of means of transport in an urban public transport system and the results of its simulation. The process is described by a semi-Markov model identified on the basis of source documents and operational tests carried out in a real urban transport system. The model is defined by the transition probability matrix for the operation and maintenance states (among others, those of carrying out transport tasks, servicing and repairs), the distributions of the sojourn times in the states, and the unit revenues and expenditures associated with the sojourn in them. An algorithm and a program have been developed for simulating realisations of the stochastic process, in which the sojourn times in the states are generated from a gamma distribution with parameters determined on the basis of the research results. In the first example, simulation runs were compared for two groups of buses differing in their period of operation. The share of driving time in the total simulation time proved to be significantly greater for the new buses, which is consistent with the observational data. In the second example, experiments were carried out in which the transition matrices and the parameters of the sojourn time distributions were swapped between the two groups, and it was investigated how the mean value of the sojourn time in the state of active use affects the total sojourn times in the individual states and the profit from the operation of the buses. The results confirm the influence of the period of operation of the buses and of the mean sojourn time in the state of active use on the efficiency of the operation and maintenance process. The proposed model can support the assessment of the operating efficiency of the transport system and the making of operation and maintenance decisions and, owing to the generality of its description, it can also be used in systems other than urban bus transport.

title: A Break-Even Threshold Framework for Circular Digital Transitions on Family Farms: Precision Agriculture and Blockchain Traceability in Rural Colombia
abstract: Digital technologies are promoted as enablers of circular agri-food systems, yet family farms lack tools to judge whether such investments pay off, and economic data at this scale are often unreliable. This study develops a break-even threshold framework that evaluates digital investments using only physical and price variables, derives three propositions on entry costs, decision robustness and unreliable data, and applies it to precision agriculture with blockchain traceability on 100 family farms in Sumapaz, Bogotá, Colombia, 50 of them adopters. Three circular dimensions were assessed: the narrowing of resource flows, value retention and chain governance. Adopting farms used 26 to 42% fewer inputs per tonne of output and recorded fewer batch rejections and intermediaries. The investment broke even with a yield gain of 2.51% against an observed differential of 19.95%, and all farms remained viable if only half of that differential were retained, if half of the additional output went unsold or if technology costs doubled. Viability depended on the ratio of investment to farm area, with an elasticity of −0.65, and no price premium for verified origin was found. The framework turns transition narratives into a computable decision rule and identifies entry cost as the main barrier for smallholders.

title: Crop Yield Analysis and Predictions Using Traditional and Machine Learning Models
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in national economies and global food security, yet increasing population demands and climate variability continue to challenge sustainable crop production. Accurate crop yield prediction can significantly support farmers and policymakers by enabling better planning, resource allocation, and risk management. This study presents a machine-learning-based framework for predicting crop yield using key agronomic and environmental attributes, including rainfall, crop type, climatic conditions, cultivated area, fertilizer and pesticide usage, production statistics, and historical yield records. Multiple predictive models were evaluated, including ARIMA, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost regressors, to identify the most effective approach for yield forecasting. Experimental results demonstrate that machine learning models—particularly tree-based methods—achieve strong predictive performance, with the Decision Tree model obtaining the highest accuracy of 99.62% and the lowest error values across MAE, RMSE, and R² metrics. The evaluation confirms that ML models reduce prediction errors and offer interpretable feature contributions, providing actionable insights for stakeholders. Overall, the findings validate the effectiveness of machine-learning approaches in agricultural forecasting and highlight their potential to enhance climate adaptation, optimize resource utilization, and support data-driven strategies for improved food security and sustainable agricultural development.

title: From Generative Models to Autonomous Agents: A Multidimensional Taxonomy of Generative AI Architectures and Operational Autonomy
journal: OAE – Organizational Architect and Engineer Journal

title: Gestational PFOS Exposure Impairs Placental System A (SNAT2)-Mediated Amino Acid Transport and Labyrinth Vascularization in Rats and Differentiated BeWo Monolayers.
abstract: Aim This study investigated mechanisms underlying perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS)-associated fetal growth restriction. Specifically, we asked whether PFOS directly impairs transcellular transfer of substrates representing three major nutrient classes-glucose, long-chain fatty acid, and system A-mediated neutral amino acid transport-across the placental epithelial barrier, and examined the transporters involved. Materials and Methods Syncytialized human BeWo b30 monolayers cultured on collagen-coated Transwell inserts were exposed to PFOS (10 and 50 μM) for 24 h. Transcellular transport of [3H]-2-deoxy-D-glucose, [1-14C]-linoleic acid, and the system A-specific substrate L-[14C]MeAIB was quantified. Transporter expression was assessed by digital PCR and Western blot. Timed-pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats received PFOS (10 or 50 mg/L, corresponding to 1.2 and 6.1 mg/kg/day) in drinking water from gestational day (GD) 4 to 20 (n = 5 dams/group). Maternal intake and body weight, fetal and placental weights, and labyrinth zone SNAT and CD31 expression were quantified. Results In BeWo monolayers, PFOS did not alter transcellular transport of 2-deoxy-D-glucose or linoleic acid but reduced MeAIB transport by 24% (10 μM) and 28% (50 μM). SNAT2 mRNA and protein were dose-dependently downregulated; SNAT1 mRNA was reduced only at 50 μM, with no change in SNAT1 protein, and SNAT4 was expressed at very low levels in this model. In pregnant rats, PFOS reduced fetal weight at both exposures (9% and 15% at 10 and 50 mg/L) and reduced placental and labyrinth zone weights, without altering maternal water intake, feed intake, gestational weight gain, or litter size. Quantitative immunohistochemistry showed dose-dependent reductions in labyrinth zone SNAT2 (60% and 79% at 10 and 50 mg/L) and SNAT1 immunostaining, with no change in SNAT4, together with reduced CD31-positive area (19% and 33%). Conclusions Gestational PFOS exposure impairs placental system A-mediated neutral amino acid transport, as measured with the system A-specific substrate MeAIB, without detectable effects on 2-deoxy-D-glucose or linoleic acid transfer under identical conditions, and is accompanied by downregulation of the stress-responsive syncytiotrophoblast transporter SNAT2. In vivo, this epithelial transport defect coincides with reduced labyrinth zone vascularization. Together, these epithelial and vascular changes describe a plausible route by which a persistent environmental contaminant constrains maternal-fetal nutrient supply.

title: Few-shot semantic segmentation of UAV imagery for plant conservation: A systematic comparison of foundation models for Euphorbia resinifera mapping
abstract: Deep learning has transformed vegetation mapping from UAV imagery, yet state-of-the-art segmentation models require hundreds to thousands of expertly annotated images, creating prohibitive labor costs for conservation applications targeting endangered flora. This study addresses this bottleneck by systematically comparing three foundation models namely: DINOv2 (self-supervised), SegGPT (supervised), and SAM (promptable), for binary segmentation of Euphorbia resinifera, an endemic Moroccan succulent of conservation concern, using patches extracted from a single annotated UAV orthomosaic. A single-image training framework is presented where spatial diversity within one high-resolution orthomosaic substitutes for diversity across multiple images, combined with sliding window inference with vote-based fusion for full-resolution deployment. SegGPT achieved 83.74±2.55% mean IoU across 20 spatially independent test images spanning a 10.5-fold vegetation density gradient (2.01 to 21.11% coverage), outperforming DINOv2 (78.09±6.63%) and SAM (47.03±20.64%). The observed collapse in SAM’s performance, despite billion-mask pretraining, can be attributed to its architectural constraints. SAM’s fixed 1024×1024 input reduced training patches by 76.2%, and its frozen encoder limited trainable parameters to 0.1M versus SegGPT’s 316M. These findings establish that fine-tuned encoders substantially outperform frozen-encoder architectures for specialized vegetation (Euphorbia resinifera) segmentation, and that single-image foundation model training offers a viable paradigm for conservation deployment, reducing annotation costs from tens of thousands to hundreds of dollars. While demonstrated for a morphologically distinctive species, these principles may inform broader conservation remote sensing applications pending validation across diverse plant forms.

title: PCR-based assays for determining mating status in field-weathered Ceratitis capitata with enhanced precision across conventional, quantitative, and droplet digital platforms
abstract: Accurately determining the mating status of the agricultural fruit fly pest Ceratitis capitata , commonly known as Medfly, is essential for timely and effective eradication efforts. To overcome the limitations of subjective DAPI-based staining assessments of females captured in dry Jackson traps and liquid Multilure traps, we developed a multi-tier molecular diagnostic method that unequivocally detects mating status using DNA probes targeting the male-specific Y114 locus on the Y-chromosome of C. capitata . Our protocol integrates morphological evaluation with increasingly sensitive molecular assays through the following steps: (1) A preliminary quality assessment of the specimens’ physical condition, DNA preservation, and mating status using conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) followed by agarose electrophoresis (cPCR); (2) quantification and real-time detection of sperm presence via quantitative PCR (qPCR); and (3) detection of trace amounts of sperm through droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). This PCR-based framework is designed for samples collected in the field, enabling accurate analysis of specimens exposed to adverse environmental conditions and varying levels of preservation after 2 and 3 weeks of weathering in traps. It allows quantitative determination of mating status even when sperm concentrations are extremely low, such as during transient copulation, and achieves detection limits down to approximately 14 spermatozoa in a mated female. By accounting for variable specimen quality and the performance characteristics of each molecular platform, this tiered approach ensures highly sensitive and unequivocal detection of mated females. The methodology can be used to assist eradication efforts across the C. capitata geographic range through the timely detection of mated females, halting their expansion and establishment into novel regions, reducing control and eradication costs.

title: LMAPNet: a lightweight multi-scale attention network for real-time maize disease and pest detection on edge devices
abstract: Accurate detection of maize diseases and pests is essential for targeted crop protection, but field performance is limited by scale variation, weak lesion boundaries, occlusion and background interference. This study proposes the Lightweight Multi-Scale Attention and Path-Aggregation Network (LMAPNet), a compact detector based on YOLO26n. The Adaptive Multi-Scale Initialization (AMSI) module combines parallel depthwise receptive fields with branch-wise channel recalibration to preserve features across target scales. The Multi-Scale Attention Path-Aggregation Network (MSAPAN) uses attention-guided bidirectional fusion to integrate high-level semantics with low-level spatial details. Inverted Residual Mobile Block (iRMB)-based refinement further limits irrelevant background responses. Slide -GIoU Loss (SG-Loss) applies sample-quality-aware classification weighting and provides localization signals for non-overlapping bounding boxes without increasing inference-time computation. On the held-out test set, LMAPNet improved precision and mAP@0.5 by 3.1 and 2.5 percentage points, respectively, while reducing the parameter count by 27.1% relative to YOLO26n. The complete system was deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano with an IMX219 camera, demonstrating the feasibility of on-device field monitoring under the tested conditions. LMAPNet provides a compact solution for real-time maize disease and pest detection on resource-constrained agricultural devices.

title: Early agroecological transition in smallholder vegetable systems in Nepal: a matched observational study of productivity and gross revenue
abstract: Smallholder agriculture in Nepal faces growing challenges from soil degradation, dependence on external inputs, and climate variability. This study evaluated the productivity and gross-revenue performance of a locally adapted agroecological package relative to conventional farming in smallholder vegetable systems during the early stage of agroecological transition. Program data were collected between September 2022 and January 2024, with matched plot monitoring conducted from May 2023 to January 2024 in three contrasting settings: Lalitpur, a market-integrated mid-hill vegetable-producing area; Humla, a remote high-Himalayan area with a short growing season and limited access to external inputs; and Doti, a mid-western hill area with steep terrain and marked climatic variability. The quantitative analysis used 242 complete within-farmer pairs (484 plot-level observations), in which the same farmer managed an agroecological and a conventional plot of the same crop during the same production period. Linear mixed-effects models included farming system as a fixed effect and matched pair as a random intercept and were fitted by restricted maximum likelihood (REML); inference for the within-pair contrast used Student’s t distribution with finite-sample degrees of freedom. A baseline survey ( n = 1,659 farmers) and key informant interviews (KIIs; n = 27) provided contextual evidence. The agroecological package was associated with comparable or higher productivity than conventional farming, although the magnitude varied by crop and site. Productivity was significantly higher for cauliflower in Lalitpur (+3.92 t/ha) and Humla (+3.86 t/ha), tomato (+3.77 t/ha) and potato (+1.95 t/ha) in Humla, and cucurbits in Doti (+0.57 t/ha); no crop–site combination showed a significant productivity disadvantage. Gross revenue was significantly higher in six of the seven crop–site combinations, with Humla tomato as the exception. KII respondents consistently reported lower purchased-input requirements and reduced irrigation needs, whereas perceptions of productivity and market demand differed by location (Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact tests: p < 0.001 and p = 0.016, respectively). These findings represent short-term observational associations rather than causal or long-term effects. Early-transition performance was generally favorable but heterogeneous, indicating that local production, market, cooperative, and institutional contexts may influence outcomes.

title: Years of social media use, information-sharing behavior, and attitudes toward agricultural information sharing among Saudi female gardeners
abstract: Social media is a key channel for exchanging agricultural information. This study examined social-media utilization and attitudes toward agricultural information sharing among Saudi female gardeners, evaluating whether years of social-media use moderated the association between sharing behavior and attitudes. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among Saudi female gardeners registered on the Smart-Garden digital platform ( N = 222). The questionnaire assessed demographics, social-media utilization and experience, sharing behavior, and attitudes toward sharing (five-item, four-point Likert scale). Principal component analysis, Cronbach’s alpha, descriptive statistics, and Spearman’s correlations were utilized. Hierarchical moderated multiple regression was performed with effect-coded sharing behavior and mean-centered years of social-media use, followed by group-specific simple-slope analyses. Participants reported high social-media usage, led by Instagram (93.7%), Snapchat (92.8%), and WhatsApp (88.3%), alongside favorable attitudes toward sharing ( M = 3.526, SD = 0.661). In the full regression model ( R 2 = 0.160, F3, 218 = 13.827, p < 0.001), years of social-media use was positively associated with attitudes ( B = 0.033, β = 0.177, p = 0.005). The interaction between years of social-media use and sharing behavior was significant ( B = −0.067, β = −0.359, p < 0.001), accounting for an additional 12.6% of explained variance (Δ R 2 = 0.126). Simple-slope analyses revealed a positive association between years of social media use and attitudes among non-sharers ( B = 0.100, β = 0.490, p < 0.001), but a negative association among active sharers ( B = −0.034, β = −0.202, p = 0.029). The association between years of social-media use and sharing attitudes varies by sharing behavior, highlighting utilization and active sharing as distinct dimensions of digital agricultural communication. Longitudinal or intervention-based studies examining factors like information credibility and digital literacy are recommended.

title: AgriTrust: an adaptable semantic and geospatial framework for reconciling EUDR and Brazilian regulatory compliance
abstract: The European Union Deforestation-Free Regulation (EUDR), Brazil’s Forest Code (Law No. 12,651/2012), and the proposed National Policy for Digital Transformation in Agriculture (Bill No. 4,132/2025) together create a complex regulatory framework for Brazilian agricultural exports. Although these frameworks share common objectives such as preventing deforestation, ensuring traceability, and promoting sustainable production, they differ in their definitions, thresholds, and verification mechanisms. This fragmentation produces complex compliance requirements and disconnected data systems. We propose AgriTrust, an open technological framework that reconciles these regimes through open semantic web standards and satellite-based monitoring. The framework integrates the Ontology Web Language (OWL) for harmonizing agricultural data semantics, the Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL) for automated regulatory validation, W3C Verifiable Credentials (VC) for portable compliance proofs, Decentralized Identifiers (DID) for cryptographic authentication, the Open Digital Rights Language (ODRL) for machine-executable data contracts, and GeoSPARQL with SOSA/SSN ontologies for integrating geospatial and observational data. By combining Copernicus Sentinel-2 Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) with Brazil’s Rural Environmental Registry (CAR) GeoServer SICAR data, AgriTrust enables unified compliance assessment across multiple regulatory frameworks. The framework supports dual sovereignty: producer sovereignty through an explicit ownership property and national sovereignty through a blockchain-agnostic, multi-provider architecture. The demonstration exercises the EUDR deforestation-free check via Sentinel-2 NDVI analysis and the Forest Code check via CAR registration status, using December 31, 2020 as the EUDR legal cutoff. Seventeen rural establishments across four of Brazil’s six biomes were assessed. Seven were verified and issued VCs; the remaining ten were distributed across five outcome classes, each corresponding to a distinct real-world data condition and to a parametric or configurational adaptation rather than an architectural change. Full spatial validation of self-declared CAR protected areas and the multicriteria composite score remain specified but not exercised, pending additional GeoServer data availability. These results provide functional evidence that the framework’s adaptable engineering can be exercised end-to-end under real-world constraints, and we emphasize the need for public–private partnerships to operationalize it at production scale.

title: Cost structure and grain production stability in China: evidence from provincial panel data
abstract: Grain-output stability is central to sustainable agricultural development. This study examines whether the composition of rice, wheat, and maize production costs provides explanatory information beyond the aggregate production cost burden in China. We analyze 31 Chinese provincial-level regions over 2011–2024 using province and year fixed effects with province-clustered standard errors. The outcome is the negative three-year rolling coefficient of variation of combined rice, wheat, and maize output. The analysis compares aggregate cost-to-output-value ratios and internal cost shares, supported by alternative windows, detrending, fixed crop-area weights, observed-data coverage checks, rice-variety aggregation sensitivity, and meteorological-exposure specifications. The aggregate cost-to-output-value ratio (ACP) has no statistically significant association with output stability, while the material-and-service cost share (MS) has a positive conditional association (coefficient 0.316; p = 0.007). Adding MS and LS increases within R-squared from 0.108 to 0.137 (joint F (2,30) = 4.239; p = 0.024). The MS coefficient remains positive in a seven-year rolling window (0.417; p = 0.018), with fixed crop-area weights (0.294; p = 0.011), and after replacing rice-variety arithmetic means with medians (0.288; p = 0.010 in the ACP-adjusted model). The detrended seven-year estimate is imprecise (0.143; p = 0.192), as is the estimate in the three-crop original-cost subsample. Meteorological interaction models yield no 5%-significant MS-by-exposure effects. Cost composition contributes additional explanatory information about contemporaneous grain-output stability. The positive MS association is supported by several alternative cost and window specifications, with sensitivity to detrending and the concentration of original cost observations. The findings motivate further research on expenditure allocation and stability using disaggregated cost and production data.

title: Breast Ultrasound Classification Under Cross-Dataset Shift: A Multi-Seed Benchmark of Convolutional Networks, a Vision Transformer, and a Self-Supervised Foundation Model
abstract: Deep-learning classifiers for breast ultrasound are usually evaluated on images from their training institution, and self-supervised foundation models are increasingly proposed as more transferable than supervised networks; whether ranking ability, decision thresholds, and probability calibration survive a change in institution has rarely been tested under leakage-controlled conditions. We fine-tuned ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B0, a supervised Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16), and self-supervised DINOv2 under one shared protocol on the official BUS-BRA five-fold partitions, each fold with three seeds, and on three case-grouped hold-out splits, and evaluated every trained model unchanged on the Breast Ultrasound Images (BUSI) dataset. The supervised models largely retained their discrimination externally. ResNet-50 had the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve under the official folds, but no criterion separated it from ViT-B/16, whose small hold-out advantage at the decision threshold did not recur. In every official-fold run, both models labeled a larger share of BUSI than of BUS-BRA images malignant, although prevalence was the same—a shift that temperature scaling cannot correct. Top-label calibration error also understated malignant-class miscalibration. Full-frame DINOv2 did not fit its training data in any run, although exploratory lesion cropping produced good discrimination. External evaluations should report operating-point transport and class-wise calibration alongside discrimination.

title: Integrating Remote Sensing, Management Information, and Satellite Embeddings for Machine-Learning Prediction of Field-Level Maize Yield in Kenyan Smallholder Systems
abstract: Accurate field-level maize-yield estimation in smallholder systems is challenging because plots are small and management is heterogeneous. We analyzed 6016 Kenyan field-years (2017–2020) using conventional Sentinel-2 predictors, climate, soil, terrain, location, survey-based management, and 64-dimensional satellite embeddings. Ten algorithms were compared using random, leave-one-year-out (LOYO), and spatial-block cross-validation, followed by predictor-group comparisons and SHAP analysis. The all-predictor XGBoost model achieved R2 = 0.395, RMSE = 1321 kg ha−1, and MAE = 1010 kg ha−1 under random cross-validation; R2 declined to 0.172 under LOYO and 0.292 under spatial-block validation. Adding management information to conventional remote sensing, climate, soil, terrain, and location raised random-validation R2 from 0.270 to 0.394, with positive gains across all three validation designs. Replacing 252 conventional remote-sensing predictors with 64 embedding dimensions yielded similar accuracy (random-validation R2 = 0.394 and 0.405, respectively) and substantially reduced input dimensionality. These conclusions were broadly consistent with Extra Trees. Because predictors included full-year observations and measurements recorded at harvest, the models provide retrospective, end-of-season yield estimates rather than in-season forecasts. Results highlight management information and compact satellite representations, alongside limitations in transfer to unseen years and locations.

title: From Remote Sensing to Smart Agricultural Decision-Making: A Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence, Crop Models and Data Assimilation
abstract: Remote sensing has become a major information source for smart and Precision Agriculture, enabling non-destructive monitoring of crop and environmental conditions across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Increasingly, its value depends on integration with analytical approaches capable of transforming observations into actionable agronomic information. This systematic review assessed the integration of remote sensing with artificial intelligence (AI), crop simulation models, data assimilation and digital decision-support systems, and their contribution to sustainable agricultural management. Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus-indexed peer-reviewed literature published between 2015 and 2026 was systematically reviewed, with 205 studies included in the final synthesis. AI-based approaches were identified in 71.2% (146/205) of the reviewed studies, crop simulation models were reported in 48.8% (100/205), and data assimilation approaches were identified in 46.3% (95/205). These frequencies describe the representation of the respective approaches in the reviewed literature and do not necessarily indicate their experimental implementation in every publication. The evidence shows a transition from descriptive remote sensing applications towards integrated systems supporting crop monitoring, yield prediction, irrigation and nutrient management, stress detection and resource optimisation. However, challenges remain regarding data interoperability, AI transferability and explainability, crop-model calibration, methodological heterogeneity, uncertainty and operational accessibility. Overall, remote sensing increasingly provides the observation layer of smart agricultural systems, while AI, crop modelling and data assimilation provide the analytical and predictive capabilities required for sustainable agricultural decision-making.

title: Future Climate Change Impacts on Rainfed Wheat Yield in the Northern Zagros, Iran: Integrating CMIP6, DSSAT-CERES-Wheat, and Satellite Indicators
abstract: Rainfed wheat production in the Northern Zagros of Iran is highly dependent on climatic conditions and is therefore particularly vulnerable to future changes in temperature and precipitation. This study assessed the potential impacts of climate change on rainfed wheat yields at three locations, Urmia, Sanandaj, and Hamedan, using an integrated climate–crop modeling framework. Historical climatic and agricultural data for 2000–2024, together with CHIRPS precipitation, MODIS Normalized Difference Vegetation Index(NDVI) and land surface temperature (LST) were analyzed to characterize the environmental and agricultural conditions at the study locations. Future climate conditions were projected using the MPI-ESM1-2-HR model under four CMIP6 Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5) and statistically downscaled using the Statistical Downscaling Model (SDSM). The resulting climate projections were subsequently used as inputs to the DSSAT-CERES-Wheat model to simulate rainfed wheat yields over the 2040–2070 period. Historical results revealed substantial spatial differences in wheat productivity among the three locations, with mean yields of approximately 4859, 2074, and 4670 kg ha−1 in Urmia, Sanandaj, and Hamedan, respectively. Future simulations indicated declining yield across all locations and scenarios, greater reductions under higher-emission pathways. Under SSP5-8.5, simulated wheat yields in 2070 were approximately 29.3%, 40.5%, and 30.6% lower than those in 2040 in Urmia, Sanandaj, and Hamedan, respectively. Sanandaj exhibited the greatest projected yield reduction, whereas Urmia and Hamedan exhibited the greatest projected yield reduction, whereas Urmia and Hamedan showed comparatively smaller, although still substantial, declines. These findings indicate that climate change may impose significant and spatially heterogeneous constraints on rainfed wheat productivity at the three study locations, highlighting the importance of location-specific adaptation strategies.

title: Can Scene-Level NWP Cloud Cover Replace Expert Pixel Labels? A Large-Scale Assessment with ERA5, GFS and CloudSEN12+
abstract: Deep learning cloud detectors require large volumes of pixel-level labels that are expensive to produce. Gridded cloud cover from ERA5 reanalysis and GFS forecasts could serve as freely available weak supervision. We assess this hypothesis through a large-scale comparison of NWP total cloud cover with expert-annotated cloud masks from CloudSEN12+ (Sentinel-2, 10m) over 48,000 globally distributed samples (2017–2022). ERA5 shows moderate agreement (r=0.42, MAE ∼30%), with performance strongly dependent on cloud type. We then train U-Net cloud segmentation models that differ only in the source of their labels, on a region-disjoint partition of the dataset, and evaluate them on 975 held-out expert-annotated patches. Expert labels yield a binary cloud IoU of 0.78 and a scene-level accuracy of 0.92, against 0.47 and 0.71 for ERA5-derived weak labels. Increasing the weak supervision from 200 to 20,000 patches produces no systematic improvement over the tested range, which suggests that, for this label formulation, the limitation lies in what each label expresses rather than in how many are available; 849 expert-annotated patches outperform 20,000 weakly labelled ones. Pretraining on ERA5 labels and fine-tuning on expert masks is worse than training from scratch at every annotation budget that we tested. Training on ERA5 labels does improve on applying the same labels directly as a mask, from 0.38 to 0.47 in binary cloud IoU, and the resulting model remains usable for coarse scene-level screening where no pixel-level annotation exists. Results provide practical guidelines for leveraging NWP products in deep learning training pipelines where expert annotations are scarce.

title: ReSORT: LLM-Guided Policy Selection for New-ID Assignment Under Occlusion in Multi-Object Tracking
abstract: Objects that reappear after occlusion can receive new identities when data association fails, fragmenting trajectories. We present ReSORT, an identity recovery framework that evaluates competing links using motion history, numerical association scores, and selective language-model evidence. Camera-compensated trajectory states are propagated through five motion hypotheses to construct a persistent candidate graph. A numerical ranker scores candidate links, and a frozen Qwen3.5-4B model reviews selected ambiguous cases using image crops and scene context. Candidate-order consistency checks filter the model responses before their relative evidence enters a global one-to-one assignment. Inference does not access ground truth; the numerical ranker is trained with supervision, and the evaluated reassociation uses subsequent observations offline. On seven MOT17 development videos, the complete pipeline produces 243 identity switches, compared with 427 for native ByteTrack and 299 for the historical automatic ReSORT reference, with IDF1 of 85.96% and HOTA of 78.06%. The historical comparison includes changes beyond the final language-model component, whose contribution is assessed separately through matched ablations. Experiments across seven tracker families on MOT17 and MOT20 show tracker-dependent benefits and sensitivity to evidence weighting. The results support selective language-model verification within a constrained association system while identifying limitations in response consistency, computational cost, and development-set evaluation.

title: Source–Load Data-Driven Multi-Objective Siting and Sizing of Distributed Energy Storage in Islanded Microgrids
abstract: The variability of renewable generation and load demand complicates energy storage planning for islanded microgrids, particularly when siting, sizing, operating reliability, and economic performance must be considered simultaneously. This paper proposes a source-load data-driven method for siting and sizing distributed energy storage in an islanded microgrid. An improved grey wolf optimiser-gated recurrent unit (IGWO-GRU) model was developed to forecast photovoltaic output and nodal loads under normal and adverse weather conditions. The forecasts were incorporated into a multi-objective planning model that maximised islanded supply reliability and capacity-normalised discharge throughput while minimising annualised planning and operating cost. Continuous state-of-charge evolution, transitions between grid-connected and islanded operation, nodal-voltage limits, line-loading limits, upstream-grid power exchange, and priority supply to critical loads were explicitly considered. NSGA-III was directly coupled with a pandapower full-chronology AC power-flow model so that every candidate configuration was evaluated from its simulated operating performance. In the synthetic PV–BESS IEEE 33-bus case study, the 1319 h chronological assessment yielded 640 feasible configurations, including 10 non-dominated solutions. For this synthetic case and predefined candidate buses, the results illustrate a chronological planning workflow and quantify conditional trade-offs among annualised cost, islanded supply reliability, and capacity utilisation. They do not establish universal forecasting or optimisation superiority.

title: Effects of Rootstock on Growth, Productivity, and Fruit Quality of Pear (Pyrus communis) cv. ‘Conference’ in an EUFRIN Thematic Orchard Network
abstract: Pear (Pyrus communis L.) production in high-density orchards depends critically on the choice of a size-controlling, precocious and quality-neutral rootstock, yet most comparative information still originates from single-site trials. We evaluated four quince (Cydonia oblonga Mill.) rootstocks—‘Adams’, ‘Sydo’, QR196-9 and QR530-11—under the cultivar ‘Conference’ across five contrasting European environments of the EUFRIN thematic orchard network (Spain, Romania, United Kingdom, Poland and Norway; 41.6–59.7° N), compiling 512 plot-year observations (replicate plots of four to five trees) over up to eight seasons (2018–2025). Vegetative growth (trunk cross-sectional area, TCSA; tree height; annual increment), productivity (yield, yield efficiency, crop load, cumulative yield) and fruit quality (weight, size distribution, firmness, total soluble solids, titratable acidity and their ratio) were analyzed by two-way and per-year ANOVA, linear mixed models (LMM), variance partitioning, Finlay–Wilkinson joint regression and Wricke ecovalence stability statistics, correlation and principal component analysis. Site was the dominant source of variation for all traits (variance components up to 78% for titratable acidity, 52% for TCSA and 36% for yield), whereas the rootstock contribution, although small, was largest for TCSA (≈3%). Across environments, TCSA ranked QR196-9 > ‘Adams’ > ‘Sydo’ > QR530-11 (LMM: QR196-9 +2.77 cm2, QR530-11 −2.83 cm2 vs. ‘Adams’; p = 0.002), and QR530-11 was consistently the least productive (−1.66 kg tree−1 vs. ‘Adams’; p < 0.001). Including the trunk size at planting as a covariate did not change the QR196-9 contrast and only attenuated that of QR530-11, which had the smallest nursery trees. QR196-9 behaved as an environment-responsive genotype (regression coefficient b ≈ 1.15–1.30), whereas QR530-11 was low-yielding, with its below-average slope (b ≈ 0.82) being largely a scale effect of its smaller size (b ≈ 1.0 on the log scale); ‘Sydo’ combined intermediate performance with the highest stability. Titratable acidity was the only trait showing a significant site × rootstock interaction, confined to the Lleida site. A weighted multi-criteria index computed from the site- and year-adjusted mixed-model estimates of eight criteria, including rootstock suckering, ranked ‘Adams’ highest (7.44/10), followed by QR196-9 (5.75), ‘Sydo’ (5.64) and QR530-11 (2.76), and rootstock differences attenuated as orchards approached canopy closure. Because the four rootstocks were compared within one complete multi-site trial rather than at single sites, the mixed-model estimates are site-corrected and the resulting recommendations are transferable across environments: ‘Adams’ and ‘Sydo’ as robust general-purpose rootstocks, QR196-9 for high-potential sites and caution with QR530-11 where yield is the priority.

title: Asymmetric Resilience and Restoration Limits in Degraded Hyper-Arid Fog Desert Systems: A Regime-Dependent Framework
abstract: Land restoration is widely promoted as a response to degradation, yet its feasibility varies across hydrological and geomorphic regimes. This review develops a regime-dependent framework that separates persistence resilience from recovery resilience and defines asymmetric resilience, in which ecosystems maintain function under chronic stress but recover only slowly after disturbance. Focusing on anthropogenically degraded, fog-dependent hyper-arid landscapes, with the Namib Desert as the anchor case and rainfall-supported drylands as comparators, we synthesise evidence on hydrological limitation, pedological legacy effects, biological soil crust dynamics and surface stability. Disturbance frequently removes slow structural variables that regulate roughness, infiltration and moisture retention; reported recovery times for these variables extend from decades to centuries or longer, commonly exceeding management horizons by up to two orders of magnitude. We propose a provisional Restoration Feasibility Index combining water availability, soil fertility and intrinsic recovery time relative to an explicit management horizon; it is a prototype for regime screening that requires calibration, not a validated decision model. Additional post-review analyses of independent dryland datasets illustrate hydrological and restoration-response heterogeneity, including poor cross-site transfer of simple biocrust forecasts; they test component mechanisms, not the full index. Feasibility classes map to a three-tier management pathway: restoration-feasible, where avoidance still comes first, and active restoration is additionally justified; restoration-marginal, with selective staged intervention; and recovery-limited, where avoidance and protection take priority, and degraded units are managed rather than abandoned. Under the compiled parameter ranges, illustrative screenings bound the classes by endpoint: slow structural endpoints yield upper-bound classes that are predominantly marginal for mature composition and predominantly recovery-limited for surface armour under management horizons sampled across 10 to 100 years, low bounds excluding full feasibility and high bounds unable to establish it, while the faster cover endpoint spans all three classes; as framework inference rather than reviewed outcome evidence, this places prevention ahead of restoration wherever slow variables define the regimes.

title: Multitemporal Thermal Imaging for Archaeological Prospection
abstract: Recent technological advances have made drone-based thermal imagery easier to acquire and process than ever before and a growing number of studies demonstrate the potential of aerial thermography to reveal archaeological landscape features. This paper brings together case studies at archaeological sites in New Mexico, Maine, and Oman where thermal imagery collected at different times in the diurnal cycle or under different environmental conditions displays cultural features with varying clarity. To leverage the potential of these multitemporal thermal image series, we experiment with several approaches to processing thermal imagery collected under different temperature and moisture conditions, the results of which can highlight subtle archaeological features and filter background noise. Despite ongoing challenges related to sensor data quality and the co-registration of thermal orthoimage mosaics, our results highlight the possibilities for advanced raster-based analyses of multitemporal thermal imagery to aid in archaeological prospection.
