title: Spatial Dynamics of Population Density Change Around a Planned High-Speed Rail Station in a Secondary Southeast Asian City: XGBoost-SHAP Predictions and Policy Scenarios for Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand
abstract: High-speed rail (HSR) expansion into secondary Southeast Asian cities raises critical questions regarding pre-operational spatial forecasting. This study develops an interpretable machine learning framework to anticipate the spatially differentiated impacts of a planned HSR station in Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand. By integrating two decades of LandScan ambient population data, Sentinel-2 imagery, and network-based accessibility metrics, we trained an XGBoost model interpreted via SHAP analysis. To ensure methodological rigor, we implemented spatial block cross-validation, which yielded a conservative median R2 of 0.699, acknowledging the inherent spatial autocorrelation that often inflates random-split performance. The analysis reveals that recent demographic momentum dominates predictive power (mean |SHAP| = 326.53). However, HSR proximity remains a highly significant localized attractor (mean |SHAP| = 146.08). Placebo tests confirm that this HSR effect is location-specific, outperforming random locations by a factor of 3.85. Furthermore, centrality controls demonstrate that the rail effect persists independently of the existing urban core. Spatially, the station’s influence is non-stationary, with an empirical distance-decay zero-crossing identified at 5723 m. Policy scenario forecasts (2027–2037) project that a Business-as-Usual trajectory yields a modest 0.86% district-wide compound annual growth rate (CAGR). Conversely, a Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) scenario—applying a 9.08% local CAGR within the station catchment—translates to a 4.03% district-wide CAGR, potentially elevating core densities to 837.68 people/km2. These findings underscore that while HSR proximity acts as a catalyst, proactive spatial planning is the decisive factor in capturing long-term demographic dividends.

title: Indigenous Conceptualizations of Plant Sex, Inheritance, and Reproduction: Amazonian Quijos Runa
abstract: Indigenous peoples’ understandings of plant sex, reproduction, inheritance, and variation remain comparatively understudied in ethnobotanical research, which has more extensively documented plant classification, nomenclature, and use. We examine how Quijos Runa farmers in the Ecuadorian Amazon recognize and explain reproductive processes, parent–offspring relationships, and inherited variation, and how these understandings relate to cultivation practices. Drawing on participant observation of 60 adult participants and structured interviews of 30 of these participants, we analyzed coded responses using descriptive frequencies and percentages of the sample for thematic analysis as well as their co-occurrence analysis. Most participants (28/29; 96.6%) recognized male and female plants, frequently distinguishing them through flowering and fruit production. Papaya was the most frequently identified plant that was thought to have male and female individuals, mentioned by 26/30 or 87% percent of participants. However, explanations concerning male reproductive necessity varied: 18/30 (60%) rejected male necessity, 7/30 (23%) affirmed it, and 4/30 (13%) described it as conditional on particular crops requiring males. Participants also described parent–offspring resemblance and variation in vigor, yield, and fruiting characteristics, alongside cultivation practices including plant care, selection, and propagation. Co-occurrence analysis identified recurring combinations of explanations concerning reproductive characteristics, inheritance, and cultivation, illustrating how these understandings were expressed together across participants’ responses. Together, these findings demonstrate that shared recognition of reproductive phenomena can coexist with diverse causal explanations of reproductive processes. We contribute to ongoing efforts to decolonialize science while aiming to advance Indigenous science studies by documenting Runa reproductive reasoning and its potential relevance to cultivation decisions and the management of plant diversity.

title: Perceived Authenticity in AI Afterlife Agents: A Dimensional Conceptualization
abstract: Advances in generative AI have enabled AI Afterlife agents that simulate deceased or absent persons through interactive systems, raising the question of what makes such representations appear authentic to close others. This paper conceptualizes perceived authenticity as the perceived fit between a digital representation and the remembered person and derives seven theoretically grounded dimensions: Traits, Facts, Behavior, Decision Logic, Values, Boundaries, and Style. The dimensions are implemented in a scenario-based prototype with an assessment and simulation phase and explored in a within-subjects study with close others of represented persons. Baseline scenarios were rated highly, while targeted mismatches in Facts and Style reduced perceived authenticity. Facts emerged as particularly relevant, suggesting that factual correctness may function as a basic hygiene factor that becomes salient when violated. The findings support the usefulness of a dimensional approach for designing and evaluating AI Afterlife agents, while also indicating that users may rely on fewer and more immediately recognizable cues when judging authenticity. Given the small exploratory sample and the manipulation of only two dimensions, the full seven-dimensional framework requires further empirical examination.
publisher: Academic Conferences and Publishing International Ltd

title: Designing AI Afterlife Agents: A Socio-Technical Design Space, Lifecycle Model, and Prompt Architecture
abstract: AI afterlife systems transform digital traces of deceased persons into interactive posthumous representations. Current literature describes these systems as griefbots, deathbots, ghostbots, postmortem avatars, digital resurrection, and digital legacy, but the field remains fragmented across information systems, psychology, ethics, philosophy, theology, and anthropology. Using an interdisciplinary conceptual design approach, this paper develops a framework for AI Afterlife Agents as socio-technical systems of posthumous presence. It contributes three linked artifacts: a socio-technical design-space model, a lifecycle model, and a prompt/state-machine architecture. The design-space model explains how identity-corpus construction, interaction modality, user interpretation, psychological and cultural effects, and governance mechanisms jointly shape risks and experiences. The lifecycle model operationalizes these dimensions across data elicitation, directed recognizability training, bereavement use, and decommissioning. The paper argues that responsible AI afterlife design requires traceability between personal data, consent, prompts, safeguards, user boundaries, and retirement procedures. Next steps involve stakeholder validation, prototype-based experimentation, and longitudinal research with data donors and authorized bereaved users.
publisher: Academic Conferences and Publishing International Ltd

title: Benchmarking Problem-Solving AI Agents in a Dairy Farm Digital Twin Against Expert-Derived Reference Solutions
abstract: A digital twin may describe an animal accurately without helping a farmer decide what to do next. This study examines that gap through a blinded benchmark of problem-solving agents in a simulated dairy-farm environment. The benchmark comprises 500 scenarios across 13 classes, covering animal health, farm management, sensor problems and situations in which no intervention is needed. Decisions and the steps leading to them are scored against hidden, deterministic reference solutions written by the authors. Six systems were compared, including conventional decision-support systems (DSS) and three configurations of the same language model: one-shot, ReAct and a digital-twin (DT) agent with action simulation and environmental feedback. In the paired evaluation of 300 scenarios, the DT agent improved the correct action rate from 73.7% for the one-shot model to 85.7%, but did not significantly outperform ReAct on this endpoint. The machine-learning (ML) DSS remained strongest overall within the simulator distribution. The DT agent was comparatively effective in difficult and sensor-related scenarios, yet often intervened when the reference solution required no action. No unsafe decisions were observed for this agent under the benchmark rules, but its more elaborate workflow increased API use. These findings show why decision-support agents should be assessed not only on whether they identify a problem, but also on whether they gather useful evidence, select a proportionate response and recognise when to stop. The benchmark is a research environment, not a validated veterinary system.
publisher: Academic Conferences and Publishing International Ltd

title: PHYSICO-CHEMICAL ASSESSMENT AND FERTILITY EVALUATION OF AGRICULTURAL SOILS FOR SUSTAINABLE NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT IN TELANGANA
abstract: Soil fertility is a critical factor influencing agricultural productivity, nutrient availability, and sustainable crop production. The present study was undertaken to evaluate the physicochemical properties and fertility status of selected agricultural soils and to assess their suitability for sustainable nutrient management. Surface soil samples were collected from representative agricultural fields and analyzed using standard laboratory procedures for soil pH, electrical conductivity, organic carbon, available nitrogen, available phosphorus, and available potassium. The obtained data were interpreted using established soil fertility classification criteria. The findings revealed that the soils were generally slightly alkaline in reaction and non-saline in nature. Organic carbon content ranged from low to medium, indicating moderate soil organic matter status. Nutrient analysis showed that available nitrogen levels were low across the sampled soils, whereas phosphorus status was categorized as medium and potassium availability was high. The results indicate that nitrogen constitutes the primary limiting nutrient affecting soil fertility. In contrast, phosphorus and potassium levels were generally adequate to support crop growth under normal management conditions. The study emphasizes the importance of regular soil fertility evaluation, balanced fertilizer application, and integrated nutrient management practices for maintaining long-term soil productivity. Incorporation of organic amendments and appropriate nutrient supplementation can improve soil health, enhance nutrient-use efficiency, and support sustainable agricultural production. The findings provide valuable baseline information for farmers, soil scientists, and agricultural planners seeking to develop site-specific nutrient management strategies and promote sustainable agriculture in Telangana.
journal: EPRA International Journal of Agriculture and Rural Economic Research

title: ICT, the Real Exchange Rate and Structural Change: Testing for Dutch Disease Effects in Developing Countries in the Post-Covid-19 Era
abstract: Purpose: This paper examined whether the rapid expansion of information and communication technology (ICT) generates Dutch disease effects in developing countries. Methodology: Using an annual panel of 37 low- and middle-income economies covering 2005-2021, the study tested the two channels of the Corden-Neary framework. The spending effect was assessed by estimating the effect of ICT on the real effective exchange rate, and the resource movement effect by estimating the effect of ICT on agricultural, manufacturing and services value added. Estimation moved from fixed effects with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors to system GMM to address endogeneity and persistence and allowed the effects to change after the Covid-19 pandemic through an ICT-Covid interaction. Findings: The results did not support a spending effect: ICT was not associated with real appreciation, and the negative coefficient implied a depreciation of about 2.0 per cent for a 10-percentage point rise in internet use, which was significant only with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors. Higher ICT use was associated with a lower manufacturing share of GDP, but this association was not robust in the dynamic specification and did not operate through the exchange rate. No clear effect was found for agriculture or services, and the effects did not strengthen after 2020. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: The findings suggest that policymakers need not adjust exchange rate policy in response to digital expansion but should support manufacturing competitiveness directly and monitor sectoral structure as digital adoption deepens.

title: Kisan Sahayak: A Smart Agricultural Marketplace for Connecting Farmers, Labourers, and Machinery Providers
abstract: Agricultural activities depend on the timely coordi-nation of land, labour, machinery, information, and local services. In many rural settings, farmers identify workers and equipment through personal contacts and fragmented communication chan-nels. Such methods can make it difficult to discover available service providers beyond an immediate network, communicate work requirements consistently, and maintain a clear record of requests. Agricultural labourers and machinery owners can face a corresponding difficulty in communicating their availability to potential customers. This paper presents Kisan Sahayak, a theoretical, mobile-first agricultural marketplace designed to connect farmers, labourers, and machinery providers through a common web platform. The proposed system is organized around the MongoDB, Express.js, React.js, and Node.js (MERN) stack. Its conceptual capabilities include role-based profiles, location-aware discovery, farmer job postings, direct worker invitations, request acceptance or rejec-tion, wage negotiation, machinery listings, and service-request tracking. An optional artificial-intelligence assistance layer is proposed for multilingual platform guidance and explainable matching based on location, skills, availability, and stated pref-erences. The paper details the system architecture, data model, stake-holder workflows, marketplace rules, AI design, security and privacy controls, deployment considerations, and an evaluation framework. The contribution is an architectural and process model; no field trial, measured performance result, or im-plemented AI capability is claimed. The design is intended to provide a foundation for subsequent implementation and empirical evaluation in agricultural communities

authors.name: Najan Ramesh Somnath Naik Balkrushna Anil
Kolhe Aditya Jalindar Nagargoje Sushant Dattatray

journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

title: Polymorph: Operating System Kernel Optimization Through Artificial Intelligence
abstract: While popular operating systems such as Linux and Windows were originally designed as monolithic kernels, an increasing number of kernel subsystems have become extensible using eBPF. Users can now define custom policies for essential kernel mechanisms, such as the process scheduler, page cache, and network stack, without recompiling the kernel. These mechanisms give developers significant freedom to fit the kernel to their applications' workloads, but the question of which policy to deploy remains open. We study how to use agentic AI to automate kernel policy development, selection, and deployment, focusing on the page cache and the process scheduler as two representative subsystems. We show that existing approaches fall short: evolutionary and agentic search runs offline, is relatively expensive, and often fails to generalize to online workloads, while online knob tuners are encumbered by the knobs' lack of expressivity. In contrast, we propose Polymorph, which learns online: an AI agent writes a generalized, granular policy once, and a user mode tuner adjusts its parameters during runtime, with no LLM in the loop. For the page cache, Polymorph improves throughput over Linux's LRU by 8.4% on unseen data, nearly twice the gain of the best existing policy, while adapting to workload changes at runtime and costing only 16M tokens once, versus 125-240M tokens per workload for agentic offline search. For the process scheduler, it improves on Linux's default by 2.75x across six workloads, versus 2.27x for the best fixed sched_ext policy.

title: Lodestone: Automated Semantic Discovery of Datacenter Hardware Specialization
abstract: Hardware specialization can improve datacenter efficiency. Unfortunately, identifying computations that justify dedicated hardware is difficult. Existing approaches analyze hot functions, instruction patterns, or overheads such as datacenter tax. They can miss fine-grained computations whose aggregate cost is spread across applications and libraries, especially when different pieces of code obscure the same underlying computation. We observe that seemingly unrelated code regions often perform the same computations, creating specialization opportunities that require semantic reasoning. The rise of agentic AI makes it possible to automate this. However, conventional AI agents cannot efficiently and reliably analyze large scale datacenter software. To unlock this opportunity, we present Lodestone, an agentic framework that automatically discovers hardware specialization opportunities by reasoning about what the executed code computes. First, Lodestone extracts hot control-flow regions from execution traces across workloads and organizes them into compact analysis packages that make large workloads tractable for agents. Second, agents describe what each region computes, merge those that perform the same computation into computational families, and check their semantic correctness in a loop. Third, to verify the discovered family, Lodestone runs every piece of code in a family against a set of reference inputs and outputs on recorded executions. Finally, for selected families, Lodestone proposes hardware, e.g., ISA extensions, near-core units, or detached accelerators, and human experts decide which proposals to develop further. We evaluate Lodestone on 20 workloads across six datacenter workload categories. We simulate 30 discovered families in a cycle-accurate simulator and implement them in RTL. These optimizations speed up the workloads by 12.6% on average and by up to 80.2%.

title: Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics
abstract: Autonomous agents that run ML experiments are usually judged by the best score they reach. That score says nothing about how it was reached: whether the agent stayed within the files it was allowed to edit, whether failed trials were kept or silently dropped, and whether each keep or discard decision can be traced to its evidence. We propose evaluating such systems on their experimental process as well as their outcome, and we build a governed harness that makes this possible. A control plane, not the LLM that proposes changes, owns each trial's lifecycle, checks its edit scope, decides keep or discard, and appends one record per trial to an append-only ledger. Governance metrics such as the invalid-action rate, the repeated-bad rate and provenance completeness are computed from that ledger. Across six ML tasks, from synthetic logistic regression to language-model training, and 1,445 trials, the same contract applied unchanged. The ledger exposed failures that a task score hides: a no-memory arm in which all 120 trials failed, a benchmark adapter whose bounded proposals ran out, and a reset failure that reproducibility hashes revealed, after which the affected campaigns were rerun. In a matched counterfactual, a loop that logs only successful trials left no record of 43 of 50 trials, while the governed ledger recorded all 50. Memory ablations show that memory's effect on repeated bad proposals depends on the task. We release the ledgers of all 1,445 trials, so that every number reported for them can be recomputed.

title: Axion: A differentiable, GPU-native finite element framework,demonstrated on phase-field fracture
abstract: We introduce Axion (Autodifferentiable, XLA-compiled, Implicit, On-device Numerics), a differentiable, GPU-native finite element framework written in JAX. The element kernels, Newton and Krylov iterations, bound-constrained updates, staggered coupling of fields, and the loop over load increments are expressed as a single program that is just-in-time compiled and executed on the GPU without host intervention. Consistent tangent operators are obtained by forward-mode automatic differentiation of the element residual, and derivatives of the discrete solution with respect to model parameters are obtained by differentiating the same program. Global operators are applied element by element without assembling a sparse matrix, octree mesh refinement is performed within fixed-size arrays, and a cell-based domain decomposition runs the same program on several GPUs. Phase-field fracture is implemented as the first module because it combines fine mesh resolution, bound-constrained damage, and repeated nonlinear solves over a loading history, which together make it computationally expensive. On two- and three-dimensional single-edge-notched tension benchmarks, a uniformly refined Axion computation completes faster than the corresponding adaptive FEniCSx computation. At identical discretization, the two-dimensional benchmark runs 37.9 times faster on one GPU than a FEniCSx implementation on one CPU. Strong and weak scaling efficiencies on four GPUs are 92% and 96%, respectively. Large-scale demonstrations include hydraulic fracture in a poroelastic medium (0.38M degrees of freedom), fracture of a multi-material premolar under contact loading (0.69M degrees of freedom), and a concrete gravity dam (96M degrees of freedom) on a single GPU. The implementation is available as open-source software.

title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents
abstract: Clinicians reviewing a diagnostic work-up will ask what was considered at each step and why the assessment changed. Agents powered by free text can reach physician-level diagnostic accuracy, but their written reasoning does not always reflect the factors that went into the decision. Here, we present Decision2Care, a decision agent that works up the acutely ill patient without producing any text. A decision model assigns a probability to each permitted EHR action, and fixed rules carry out the most probable one. We evaluated Decision2Care on the records of 546 emergency admissions across 12 diseases. Decision2Care reached a diagnostic accuracy of 86.5%, compared with 86.1% for the MIRA-v2 agent, and required a median of 2.2 s per work-up, compared with 92-100 s. Each work-up tracked which options Decision2Care was considering at each step. In 10 of the 12 diseases, the differential diagnosis changed most at the test on which the guideline bases the diagnosis. Where Decision2Care was most confident after a single work-up, all but four of its diagnoses were correct (98.5%). We traced each of these four errors back to a single imaging report. Three of them were corrected when that report was removed. The same kind of decision was used to select the treatments, and Decision2Care's drug orders were judged guideline-adherent more often than MIRA-v2's. In emergency patients, its prediction of death was comparable to that of three intensivists on the same cases. In five of the eight intensive care cohorts, it exceeded the best of the three 24-h severity scores within 2-6 h of records. Our results show that decision agents can carry out clinical work-ups while recording the options, probabilities, and execution rules behind each action for audit.

title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
abstract: The growing volume of topically similar papers makes it difficult to identify new work that can offer useful research insights or methodological guidance. We present KnowMe Paper Radar, a lightweight discovery tool that combines multiple sources of evidence into personalized reading priorities. Users specify topics, priorities, exclusions and dates; the system brings together topical relevance, recency, author research histories, collaboration paths and direction-specific institutional context. By exposing each score component and its supporting sources, KnowMe helps readers select promising papers for their current questions and discover relevant work beyond familiar authors. Automatic acquisition, version merging and graph-cache reuse keep this workflow convenient without large language model (LLM) inference during ordinary use. Experiments on 174,640 acquired records show more than threefold faster repeated context preparation, while cached abstracts improve normalized discounted cumulative gain at rank 10 (NDCG@10) from 0.412 to 0.598 on expert-judged retrieval tasks. Complementary analyses examine how the same accumulated records support semantic retrieval, research-history modeling and literature-grounded planning. A browser interface and a structured command-line interface (CLI) make these capabilities available to both researchers and research agents, positioning KnowMe as a practical upstream tool for literature-informed recursive self-improvement (RSI) workflows.

title: CoScan: Multi-Scale Content-Adaptive Space-Filling Scans for Causal State-Space Image Restoration
abstract: Selective state-space models (SSMs) have recently shown strong potential for efficient image restoration. A central difficulty, however, is that a 2D feature map typically needs to be linearized into a 1D token sequence for causal state-space updates, making restoration performance highly sensitive to the imposed scan order. Existing deterministic scans follow space-filling principles but remain fixed and content-agnostic, and can yield fragmented or semantically inconsistent contexts under degradations. We propose \textbf{CoScan}, a \textbf{co}ntent-adaptive \textbf{scan}-order design for causal vision SSMs. CoScan learns image-dependent space-filling traversals via differentiable proxy supervision driven by \textbf{scan-quality objectives} that \textit{encourage short-range coherence and causal predictability, while preserving spatial adjacency}. To support hierarchical restoration backbones, we introduce an \textbf{efficient multi-scale scan construction by coarsening a fine-level minimum spanning tree}, producing coherent scans across feature resolutions. In addition, a \textbf{frequency-guided start selection strategy} is designed to \textit{place informative structures early in the sequence prefix to strengthen causal context formation}. Plugged into existing Mamba-based backbones, CoScan yields consistent improvements across several restoration benchmarks with minimal overhead and shows promising results on high-level vision tasks. Code will be released at https://github.com/dongw22/CoScan

title: A Comparison of Heuristic, Human-Sensitive, and Self-Play DRL Policies in Human-Agent Teaming
abstract: Dynamical Perceptual-Motor Primitives (DPMPs) offer a tractable framework for generating human-like movement dynamics in artificial agents (AAs) and have been used to support coordination in human-AI teaming tasks. Traditionally, DPMP controllers rely on heuristic (rule-based) decision policies derived from human behavior to guide goal selection and action sequencing. Although effective in structured tasks, such heuristics can be difficult to generalize to more complex settings, motivating interest in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches for learning decision policies for human-AI interaction. A key challenge, however, is ensuring that DRL policies remain aligned with human strategies, particularly when agents are trained through self-play. To examine this issue, we compared three target-selection policies governing DPMP-based AAs in a first-person herding task: (1) a human-derived heuristic policy, (2) a self-play DRL policy (SP-DRL), and (3) a human-sensitive DRL policy (HS-DRL) trained alongside a heuristic agent. Results showed that heuristic agents most closely matched typical human-human coordination patterns, followed by HS-DRL agents, whereas SP-DRL agents deviated most. These findings highlight the importance of human-informed training when developing DRL-based teammates and suggest that simple heuristic policies may remain an effective approach for designing human-aligned AAs capable of human-AI collaboration.

title: Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents
abstract: Multimodal agents largely rely on generic tools such as cropping, search, and code execution, leaving specialist vision models outside their tool space. However, bringing such a model into an already trained agent is not straightforward. The challenge is to learn each new tool efficiently while retaining the ability to use existing ones. This work proposes COTEX, continual tool-space extension learning, that adds new tools at efficient adapter-level cost. COTEX locates two sets of parameter directions; one triggers a tool call and thereby opens a multi-turn reasoning trajectory, while the other determines which tool is chosen. The adapter of a new tool is restricted to the calling directions that leave earlier tool choices unaffected by orthogonal constraint. We further introduce a protocol that converts specialist models' existing task-specific annotations into verified tool-use trajectories. Experiments on two representative agents and three specialist tools show gains on ten vision-language benchmarks, with at most a 0.3-point drop on existing tools.

title: Sensor Monitoring Towards Industry 4.0: Bridging Concepts on the $C_n$ Multivariate Control Chart
abstract: The main challenge in monitoring multiple sensors is the high dimensionality that a process can easily reach. From a decision-making perspective, converting these multivariate dynamics into an informative visualization is also not trivial. Statistical Process Control (SPC) techniques detect changes in quality characteristics, but they are difficult to apply beyond the normality (Gaussian) assumption. For instance, the most well-known SPC multivariate control chart is based on Hotelling's $T^2$ statistic, which assumes that the process data follow a multivariate normal distribution (which rarely occurs in practice) and that the observations are serially independent. This study focuses on the multivariate case (dimension $d \geq 2$), regardless of the data dependence or marginal asymmetry. We propose a new control chart for change detection in copula-based multivariate processes, called the $C_n$-chart, which is based on a density level-set tolerance region built from a copula function, and we derive its run-length properties. The methodology also quantifies the (not necessarily linear) dependence among the variables. Two case studies are presented, one on water quality control and the other on monitoring brass-steel thermostats, complemented by a simulation study of run-length performance and computational cost. The results show that the proposed methodology captures both the association among variables and the anomalies, and that it accommodates variable selection through conditional (regression) modeling of the margins.

title: Great Listeners, Poor Decision-Makers: Rethinking Agentic Audio AI
abstract: Audio artificial intelligence (AI) now recognizes speech, sounds, and music remarkably well, yet voice agents still act when they should not: they execute commands addressed to others, act on misheard content, and commit before the user finishes speaking. This position article argues that the bottleneck in agentic audio AI has shifted from recognition to decision-making. We propose a reference architecture with an explicit decision layer, separate from perception and reasoning, that chooses whether to act, wait, ask, or remain silent from evidence on addressedness, speaker identity, content confidence, tool reliability, utterance completeness, and action risk. We motivate the design through six recurring decision failures and a decision-theoretic argument that transcript confidence alone is insufficient to justify an action. We implement the layer with fuzzy inference, evolutionary optimization, and sequential decision-making, and evaluate it through simulations, ablations, and recorded audio, including egocentric recordings. Addressedness and speaker evidence matter most, risk-aware gating suppresses costly errors, and well-tuned policies perform similarly, with fuzzy gates more robust to overconfident addressedness estimates. On recorded audio, explicit gating cuts executed side talk from 41\% to 7--10\% while serving 83--85\% of valid requests under successful clarification, outperforming prompting-based baselines. These results support explicit action gating as an architectural requirement for reliable voice agents.

title: RoboBuilder: Agentic Robot Co-Design with Real-world Video Feedback in the Loop
abstract: Can AI agents design robots that work in the real world? We introduce RoboBuilder, a benchmark in which coding agents co-design a robot's hardware and program from standard parts, motors and a custom 3D-printed part, and every design that passes in simulation is built and tested on a physical course. Simulation alone is not enough: under public part data, none of 15 initial passing designs crossed the real course, so an agent learns the simulator from measurements it requests and videos of real runs. Across four frontier coding agents, ten obstacles at three difficulty levels, 16,427 simulations of 12,774 distinct robots and 135 physical robots built in an estimated 240 hours, agents solve nearly all easy obstacles and invent mechanisms our search baselines do not reach, but falter at harder levels, when one robot must cross every obstacle, and in the real world, where 66% of simulated passes hold across all levels. Closing the loop helps: shown a video of its real failure, an agent redesigns the robot, sometimes correcting its simulator, and removes 72% of level-1 and level-2 failures. RoboBuilder measures progress toward agents that engineer real machines. Project Page: https://ghadinehme.com/robobuilder.github.io/

title: Aharonov-Bohm blockade of complete reversal in coupled Rabi cavities
abstract: When a common bias reverses two bistable fields, the system can pass through either of two single-reversal configurations on its way to the favored state. We show that interference between these two orders of reversal can block the final step. In a dimer of coupled quantum Rabi cavities, the four field configurations form a loop, and a complex photon-hopping amplitude threads it with an Aharonov-Bohm flux. Near half a flux quantum, the two paths to complete reversal interfere destructively: in microscopic simulations, a slow uniform sweep reverses one field with probability 0.998, although the final bias favors reversing both. A four-state model calibrated at zero bias predicts how the window of this Aharonov-Bohm blockade narrows with sweep time. The blocked state remains coherent. A differential pulse followed by a return sweep converts the relative phase of the two single-reversal configurations into a fringe in the joint field signs, with contrast 0.95. In a trimer, a phase gradient imprinted between sweeps determines whether the next sweep adds or removes a reversed field: reversing the second of two gradients changes the most probable outcome from three reversed fields to one.

title: Comparing Data-Driven and Numerical Weather Prediction Forecasts of Extreme Weather: A Review
abstract: Data-driven weather forecasting models, chiefly trained on reanalysis data, now match or beat physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) models on most headline scores, but whether this advantage extends to extreme weather is contested. We review peer-reviewed studies that directly compare data-driven forecasts with NWP for extremes, from nowcasting to subseasonal lead times. We discuss grey literature in the outlook but do not include it in the formal review. There is good agreement on the fact that data-driven models mostly outperform NWP on temperature extremes, tropical cyclone tracks and the location of synoptic features across time scales. The evidence is mixed for extreme precipitation and feature-based extreme event detection such as extremes related to atmospheric rivers, while it leans toward better NWP performance for estimating event intensity. For record-breaking events that lie outside the training distribution, the evidence is narrower. Nonetheless, both a systematic global evaluation and several case studies find that physics-based models retain the advantage, with data-driven models underestimating both the frequency and the magnitude of records. Hybrid systems that post-process NWP with machine-learning (ML), or couple data-driven forecasts with physics-based models, deliver some of the largest and most consistent gains. We argue that headline scores, verification choices and case selection explain much of the apparent disagreement in the literature, and provide recommendations for a more trustworthy and interpretable evaluation of data-driven models for extreme and record-breaking weather.

title: Projected Sensitivity of a Differential Torsion Sensor for Tests of the Weak Equivalence Principle
abstract: Tests of the weak equivalence principle (WEP) are among the most sensitive probes of new long-range, composition-dependent interactions beyond general relativity and the Standard Model. We evaluate the potential of a differential torsion sensor, which combines long mechanical coherence times with optical-cavity readout and common-mode rejection, for laboratory WEP tests and fifth-force searches. For a representative configuration based on an existing prototype, with Be-Ti test masses and 180 days of coherent integration, the projected noise-limited sensitivity to the Eötvös parameter is $η\simeq7.5\times10^{-16}$ and $2.4\times10^{-16}$ for signal modulation at 2 and 20 mHz, respectively, below current ground-based torsion-balance limits. For a baryon-coupled Yukawa interaction sourced by the Earth, the corresponding projected sensitivity to the coupling strength is $α\simeq3.1\times10^{-13}$ and $9.8\times10^{-14}$ for ranges $λ\gtrsim10^{7}$ m. We identify the modulation scheme, the material contrast, and the source geometry as the main factors that set the projected reach, and the control of systematic couplings as the main experimental requirement for attaining it. These results indicate that differential torsion sensors are a promising platform for future laboratory WEP tests.

title: A structure-based model of the bacterial chemosensory array reveals how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes sensory responses
abstract: We introduce a structure-based Ising model of the bacterial chemosensory array to investigate how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes signaling responses. The model couples the activity states of core signaling units and of CheW subunits within hexameric rings on a lattice with the structure observed in cryoEM experiments. Recent experiments show that increasing CheW participation in hexameric rings raises response cooperativity in non-adapting cells and sensitivity in adaptation-proficient cells. Our lattice model quantitatively reproduces both effects, while mean-field theory shows that CheW increases the effective coupling between core units, sharpening the response in both cell types. The statistics of CheW placement (complete hexameric rings versus random distribution) substantially alter how responses vary with CheW abundance. Moreover, different coupling strengths can yield the same static response yet markedly different activity fluctuations and dynamics. CheW abundance further controls a crossover from relaxational to oscillatory fluctuations, whose location depends on the spatial distribution of CheW. These dynamical signatures, including oscillations predicted near native CheW levels, are testable by single-cell dynamics measurements. Combined with CheW titration and our modeling results, these measurements can probe the array's assembly dynamics and allosteric couplings. Beyond the chemosensory array, our approach can generalize to other large protein complexes, providing a framework to study the functional role of scaffolding proteins and allosteric interfaces in signal processing.

title: GLIDE: Scalable and Event-Aware Inductive Forecasting over Evolving Logistics Graphs
abstract: Accurate forecasting of order volume at scale-effect hotspots (SEHs), spatially coherent groups of logistics flows that serve as distributed optimization units for real-time many-to-one dispatch, is a prerequisite for efficient order pooling in on-demand food delivery (OFD) platforms such as Meituan. However, real-world logistics networks present unique challenges that render standard spatiotemporal prediction model ineffective. (i) Dynamic Topology: Unlike static road networks, logistics graphs are ephemeral, with hotspot emerging and vanishing continuously; (ii) Scale--Volume Heterogeneity: Graph sizes vary from $10^2$ to $10^4$, while zero-inflated, long-tailed volumes create computational bottlenecks and bias predictions toward inactivity; and (iii) Event-Driven Disruption: Exogenous events (holidays, weather, academic calendars) induce systematic demand shifts that purely data-driven backbones cannot anticipate. In this paper, we present GLIDE, a production-ready framework that models evolving logistics graphs in a scalable latent space while adapting to heterogeneous demand regimes and event-driven shifts. GLIDE introduces a Graph-Guided Latent Aggregation mechanism, which dynamically projects varying physical subgraphs into a fixed-size, semantically stable latent space via a differentiable sparse assignment...

title: SEE: Unlocking the Hidden Perception of Frozen VLMs
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) grasp the overall content of an image but often miss the fine details a question hinges on, such as a small object in a large photo or a number in a dense infographic. Yet even when their answer is wrong, the region they point to often contains the evidence. We introduce Self-Elicited Evidence (SEE), a training-free method that lets a frozen VLM look again where it points. When the initial answer has low confidence, SEE prompts the model to propose regions where the details may appear, answers the question on these enlarged crops, and aggregates the answers with the original prediction through confidence-weighted voting. The model also answers with its own transcript, which helps on text-rich images. SEE needs no detector or OCR engine. Across five backbones, SEE improves every small-object benchmark by 2.3-13.1 points and outperforms five training-free baselines on small objects. With SEE, Qwen3.5-4B surpasses the direct answer of Qwen3.5-9B and matches the 6 times larger Qwen3.5-27B.

title: Probing dimension-six SMEFT operators in heavy-quark sector at future muon collider
abstract: We investigate the sensitivity to the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) operators which define the interactions of heavy-quarks with electroweak gauge bosons and with leptons via the process $μ^- μ^+ \rightarrow Wtb$, followed by leptonic W-boson decays, at a 10 TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of 10 ab$^{-1}$. Signal and background events are generated at leading order using MadGraph5aMC@NLO, interfaced with Pythia 8 for parton showering and hadronization, and passed through Delphes 3.5 for fast detector simulation. The 95% confidence level (C.L.) limits on nine Wilson coefficients are derived using a cut-based method for two $b$-tagging working points (70% and 90% efficiencies). These limits are significantly tighter than those currently reported by the CMS Collaboration; furthermore, these results highlight the advanced potential of a future high-energy muon collider to investigate new physics within the electroweak sector through precise measurements of heavy-quark interactions.

title: A Lie-Group Approach to Alfvénic Turbulence: The SO(3) Rotational p-model
abstract: The inner heliosphere is permeated by fully developed, highly intermittent nonlinear turbulence. Conventional stochastic models synthesize these multiscale fluctuations by injecting additive noise within a flat Euclidean space. However, such approaches fundamentally violate the topological constraints of ideal magnetohydrodynamics, inadvertently breaking the kinetic incompressibility of the plasma and introducing spurious magnetic compressibility. To preserve the exact geometrical invariants of Alfvénic fluctuations, a novel mathematical framework is presented: the rotational p-model. By mapping a multifractal singular measure directly into the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and integrating the associated stochastic differential equations in the Stratonovich sense on the spherical manifold $S^{2}$, the model generates highly intermittent, scale-dependent rotational dynamics. This Lie-group formulation conserves the magnetic field modulus while perfectly reproducing the fractional spectral envelopes and the non-Gaussian directional intermittency observed in space plasmas. Furthermore, by isolating purely directional reorientations, the framework provides exact analytical control over the waiting time statistics of magnetic intermittent bursts and the multifractal scaling exponents of angular deflections, offering a powerful new paradigm for the study of nonlinear turbulent phenomena.

title: Dynamic and Risk-Aware Procurement of Fast Frequency Response from Electric Vehicles and Heat Pumps
abstract: Low-inertia power systems increasingly rely on Fast Frequency Response (FFR) to keep the frequency nadir above under-frequency load-shedding thresholds without oversized Frequency Containment Reserve or synchronous inertia. This paper proposes two complementary methodologies that interface with an existing day-ahead FFR capacity market. On the Transmission System Operator (TSO) side, a dynamic procurement rule maps forecasted kinetic energy and contingency magnitude onto an offline neighborhood-need surface, yielding interval-wise FFR capacity requests rather than constant seasonal or annual volumes. On the aggregator side, a risk-aware, TSO-certifiable bidding strategy quantifies reliable FFR capacity from fleets of electric vehicles (EVs) and heat pumps (HPs) by offering lower conditional quantiles of day-ahead headroom at a prescribed delivery reliability. The resulting requests and offers are cleared through a pay-as-bid capacity auction. A Cyprus 2025 case study shows that dynamic neighborhood-based procurement yields an annual clearing cost of about EUR 476,000, which is 30%-33% lower than the seasonal and annual static rules and also below the UFLS VoLL of EUR 637,500 estimated from the fifteen real 2025 events with fmin <= 49 Hz. EV and HP offers meet their target delivery reliabilities, and RMS validation finds 46 of 50 operating points above 49 Hz at both full and 85% FFR delivery.

title: Algorithmic Market Making Can Lead to Rough Volatility Through the Order Book
abstract: Existing work suggests that markets can show volatility with paths rougher than those of Brownian motion. In theory this can happen when the order flow is close to instability with memory that decays as a power law. However, it is not fully clear how such order flow could arise from the predominantly algorithmic market making that characterizes order book dynamics. We show one such consistent mechanism. We treat each market maker as a desk that uses a first-order gradient rule to move the distances of its orders from the mid price toward target distances provided by an unknown oracle. We assume that distinct desks do not act synchronously in time but act whenever new information relevant to their respective oracles arrives, which each desk samples over its own characteristic lookback horizon. Across all desks the rule therefore takes the form of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with information-driven (mini-batch) noise. In the continuum limit this update rule makes the volume of the order book follow a conservative stochastic partial differential equation (the Dean--Kawasaki equation) whose fluctuations drive the order flow. The distinct horizons of the desks further induce a persistent memory in the order flow that decays as a power law. Standard scaling arguments then lead to rough volatility. We confirm the key predictions of the model on simulated agents and on six months of Binance data with about 790 million orders. In liquid markets governed mainly by market makers, such as the perpetual futures of Binance, the order books are consistent with how our desks change the book.

title: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises
abstract: Agentic AI platforms-systems in which LLM agents plan, invoke tools, retain memory and coordinate to change the state of enterprise systems-are being procured faster than they can be measured. Public agent benchmarks score models in fixed harnesses; enterprises buy integrated platforms whose orchestration, memory, governance and tooling layers dominate outcomes, and they buy them largely on the strength of vendor demonstrations. We report an industrial evaluation programme ("bakeoff") run by the innovation laboratory of a global bank in which ten platforms-spanning open-source frameworks, proprietary products and hyperscaler ecosystems-were assessed by a cross-functional panel on nine capability dimensions across three financial-services workloads: counterparty credit risk, retrieval-augmented generation and process automation. Scores separate the field into three tiers that are stable under alternative weightings, and surface workload-specific strengths that aggregates hide. A secondary analysis, however, finds Cronbach's alpha = 0.98 across nominally distinct dimensions and rank correlations >= 0.93 with the total for eight of nine: a halo effect indicating that demonstration-based scoring measures presentation as much as capability. From these lessons we propose a gate-then-score evaluation protocol with four layers (capability, execution reliability, governance gates, business value), trace-level reliability metrics estimated over repeated runs, an autonomy-readiness scale and a reproducibility protocol. We state precisely what the present evidence supports, and what a controlled harness must add to turn enterprise platform evaluation from structured judgement into measurement.

title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
abstract: Attention has become one of the most widely adopted solutions for estimating the relevance of surrounding objects and interpreting an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions. However, its ability to capture the causal impact of individual input elements on an AI model's output has long been discussed in the literature, particularly in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) domain. This work brings this discussion into the autonomous driving domain by analyzing the accuracy of attention in estimating the impact of an input object on an autonomous vehicle's driving, i.e., its relevance. To this end, we compare different attention-based relevance estimation methods against a causal reference of object relevance obtained through counterfactual analysis. We perform our analysis on more than 80,000 synthetic driving scenes using an autonomous vehicle based on PlanT 2.0, a state-of-the-art Transformer-based model for object-level planning. Results show that attention provides a correlational rather than causal indication of object relevance. Attention-based relevance estimation methods do not consistently identify all relevant objects and tend to incorrectly classify as relevant objects with little or no impact on the vehicle's driving. In particular, results show that attention can effectively identify relevant objects in simple single-lane, straight-road scenarios, but its accuracy degrades in more complex settings, such as multi-lane roads and intersections. These findings highlight the limitations of attention as a proxy for object relevance, calling for novel methods able to accurately capture the causal impact of individual objects on the vehicle's driving and distinguish it from correlational associations.

title: R$^{3}$Sieve: Suppressing Unconditional Information from Attention to Answers for High-Resolution VQA
abstract: High-resolution visual question answering (VQA) requires models to identify question-relevant small objects in high-resolution images and select the correct answer based on what they recognize, demanding fine-grained perception. Previous methods focus on obtaining better visual evidence (image crops), but obtaining it alone is insufficient, using it effectively is equally crucial. Visual evidence should therefore be utilized as effectively as possible throughout inference. We argue that small-target evidence is obscured by unconditional information that remains observable in subsequent processing even after the condition on which it should depend is removed. Such information hinders the effective use of small-target evidence. We propose R$^{3}$Sieve (Residual-Region-Response Sieve), a training-free framework. We divide inference into three stages---localization, cropping, and answering---and introduce distinct counterfactual references to suppress interference at each stage. During localization, the Shared-Subspace Canceller (SSC) uses a generic image description to construct a counterfactual reference and obtain question-relevant attention maps. During cropping, the Unique-Contribution Spotter (UCS) constructs counterfactual references from visual and non-visual features to identify distinctive, complementary crop regions. During answering, the Content-Aligned Voter (CAV) constructs an image-free branch to calibrate answer responses. Experiments on three high-resolution VQA benchmarks show that R$^{3}$Sieve achieves the highest overall accuracy among compared methods across diverse settings, improving base models by up to 21.5 percentage points.

title: Benchmarking Reasoning Reliability,Prior_Evidence Contrast,and Spectral Discrimination in Remote-Sensing Geological Image Interpretation
abstract: Reliable lithology interpretation requires accurate geological recognition and reasoning grounded in visual evidence. Although Multimodal Large Language Models show promise in remote sensing, their reliability in geological interpretation remains unclear. We introduce HyGeoBench, a diagnostic benchmark of 10,000 questions based on hyperspectral imagery across three dimensions: reasoning reliability, prior_evidence contrast, and spectral discrimination. It covers ten task types, with both multiple-choice and open-ended response formats. Integrating hyperspectral satellite imagery with geological annotations and verified evidence, HyGeoBench examines reasoning errors, conflicts between geological priors and visual evidence, and cross-band inconsistencies. Evaluations reveal limitations in fine-grained recognition and evidence-grounded interpretation. To address these challenges, we propose HyGeoAgent, a tool-augmented framework integrating region observation, text knowledge retrieval, same-band image retrieval, and native PCA analysis through adaptive tool use. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over the corresponding base models, improving geological image interpretation across diagnostic dimensions.

title: SemPhys: Semantic-Physical Co-Learning for Humanoid Motion Generation via Differentiable World Models
abstract: In human-robot collaboration, natural language lets people direct a humanoid's whole-body movements without programming joint trajectories. A common approach generates a kinematic reference from an instruction and relies on a tracking controller to execute it. However, as the controller maintains balance under contact constraints, the executed motion can depart from the reference in ways that change the action it conveys. Our central insight is that semantic alignment must be evaluated directly on the complete motion the robot physically executes. Building on this insight, we introduce \textbf{SemPhys}, a framework that trains motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated executions. A differentiable world model and a fixed tracking controller predict a short segment of a recorded execution. SemPhys inserts this prediction at its original position, scores the complete trajectory against the instruction, and backpropagates through the predicted segment. A paired anchoring loss stabilizes adaptation by keeping each generated reference close to its counterpart from the initial generator. On BONES-SEED, SemPhys largely preserves instruction retrieval accuracy from reference to execution and achieves the highest retrieval accuracy on executed motions among the evaluated methods.

title: APS: Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection for Long Video Understanding
abstract: Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) have significantly improved video understanding capabilities, yet processing long videos remains challenging due to the substantial computational cost of extensive visual inputs. Frame selection offers an efficient alternative, but many existing region-based methods rely on fixed or predefined temporal partitions, which may result in suboptimal temporal regions, compromising subsequent budget allocation and frame selection. In this work, we propose Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection (APS), a training-free framework that adapts temporal partitions to local variations in query-frame relevance. Specifically, APS formulates temporal partitioning as a complexity-regularized fitting problem, jointly optimizing partition boundaries and local models through dynamic programming. The resulting adaptive temporal partitions guide frame budget allocation based on query relevance and temporal extent, enabling informative frame selection under limited visual budgets. Extensive experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate that APS consistently improves performance across diverse LVLM backbones, achieving the highest average gains over uniform sampling among competing methods. Further analyses validate the effectiveness of adaptive partitioning and demonstrate its generalizability across model scales, similarity encoders, and advanced LVLMs.

title: Electrostatic and Quantum Transport Engineering of Multilayer Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions for Improved TER and RA Trade off
abstract: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for non-volatile memory and neuromorphic computing, but achieving a high tunnel electroresistance ratio (TER) with a low resistance-area (RA) product remains challenging. In this work, TiN/Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$ (HZO)-based FTJs containing zero to three TiO$_2$ and IGZO-based quantum wells (QWs) are analyzed using the Miller ferroelectric (FE) polarization model integrated with the non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism to examine the effects of QW material and thickness on polarization and transport. TiO$_2$-based structures exhibit higher polarization and TER than IGZO-based structures. At a read bias of 0.1 V, the uniform TiO$_2$ double-QW structure, with 1-nm-thick QW and insulating layer (IL) layers, gives a TER of $2.71\times10^{10}\%$ and an RA product of $5\times10^4~Ω\cdot\text{cm}^2$, compared with $5.95\times10^7\%$ and $2\times10^5~Ω\cdot\text{cm}^2$, respectively, for IGZO. Both uniform and non-uniform TiO$_2$ double-QW structures exhibit resonant tunneling (RT) and negative differential resistance (NDR) associated with QW-confined states. Increasing the first QW thickness to 1.38 nm, while keeping the second QW and both IL layers at 1 nm, shifts the confined-state energies and modifies resonant transport. The selected non-uniform structure achieves a TER of $2.95\times10^{11}\%$ and an RA product of $1.25\times10^3~Ω\cdot\text{cm}^2$ at a read bias of 0.1 V. Elastic scattering changes the amplitude and width of QW resonant-transmission peaks, with a stronger effect on the low resistance state (LRS) than on the high resistance state (HRS). These results show that QW material and thickness optimization can improve the TER--RA trade-off, while electrode screening and elastic scattering further influence polarization-dependent transport in multilayer FTJs.

title: Embodied Graph: A Relational World Model for Long-Horizon Tasks
abstract: Long-horizon tasks in embodied and web environments involve extended decision sequences and delayed feedback, making accurate planning crucial for success. World models tackle this by learning latent dynamics for imagination-based planning. However, existing approaches merely rely on dense pixel-level observations, which forces the model to absorb redundant information while overlooking relations among task-relevant entities. Consequently, small errors may accumulate over long imagined rollouts and gradually corrupt the predictions. In this paper, we explore world models that imagine over sparse state abstractions, which poses two key challenges: 1) how to remove redundant information and form a compact state abstraction; 2) how to incorporate the relational structure to learn reliable long-horizon dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose Embodied Graph, a relational state abstraction that supports structured dynamics modeling and long-horizon imagination, and the Relational World Model (RWM), which performs imagination directly over graph states. RWM consists of (i) a Task-Aware Embodied Graph Constructor that filters redundant details and maintains graph memory through online updates, and (ii) an Embodied Graph Recurrent State Space Model that learns node-wise latent dynamics while capturing inter-node dependencies. The imagined graph states provide predictions of action consequences to guide decision-making. Experiments on Minecraft and Crafter demonstrate the effectiveness of RWM in embodied environments. Notably, in Minecraft, RWM is the only method that obtains diamonds within the given budget. Experiments on web interaction further illustrate the applicability of relational state prediction to the decision making process of web agents.

title: Sharp boundary regularity for planar minimal graphs with analytic Dirichlet data
abstract: We study the boundary behavior of generalized (BV) solutions of the Dirichlet problem for the minimal surface equation over a bounded set \(\Omega\). Such a generalized solution is always the graph of a smooth function \(v\) inside \(\Omega\), but might carry a vertical part over \(\partial\Omega\), which records the gap between the prescribed Dirichlet datum \(g\) and the boundary trace \(h\) attained by \(v\). When \(\Omega\) is a bounded real-analytic planar domain and \(g\) is real analytic we prove that \(h\) is Lipschitz, right and left differentiable at every point, of class \(C^1\) on \(\partial\Omega\setminus\Sigma\), and real analytic on \(\{h\neq g\}\setminus\Sigma\), where \(\Sigma=\{\kappa=0\}\) is the zero set of the curvature of \(\partial\Omega\). Also, at each point \(p\in\Sigma\cap\{h\neq g\}\), the two one-sided branches extend real analytically across \(p\). The proof recasts the vertical part near a contact point as a scalar obstacle problem with a possibly degenerate right-hand side, whose model case is \(\Delta v=H\,\id_{\{v>0\}}\) with \(H\ge0\) a polynomial. These results are optimal: for merely smooth data the trace may be discontinuous, while in the real-analytic case there are examples where corners do occur.

title: How Well Do Generalist CT Foundation Models Differentiate Liver Tumors?
abstract: Generalist CT foundation models detect many findings with high performance, but their ability to differentiate detected lesions remains largely unevaluated. This retrospective study evaluated two generalist models, RADAR and Merlin, for differentiating liver tumors using a public single-institution multiphase CT dataset (517 cases: hepatocellular carcinoma, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, breast and colorectal cancer liver metastases, and hemangioma). The models were evaluated in a zero-shot setting using their existing outputs and with linear probing, in which only a linear classifier was trained on frozen image features (stratified fivefold cross-validation repeated five times). In the zero-shot setting, RADAR achieved an accuracy of 54.4% (95% CI: 49.9, 58.8) and a $\kappa$ of 0.37 for four-class differentiation at the portal venous phase and predicted 31% (129 of 421) of malignant tumors as hemangioma. With linear probing of four-phase features, its accuracy improved to 79.9% (95% CI: 76.6, 83.4) with a $\kappa$ of 0.72, and 1% (five of 421) of malignant tumors were predicted as hemangioma; Merlin achieved an accuracy of 60.9% (95% CI: 56.9, 65.0). Generalist CT foundation models showed limited zero-shot ability to differentiate liver tumors, which improved substantially with linear probing alone.

title: Second-Order Steady-State Approximation of Heterogeneous Mean-Field Models
abstract: Mean-field models provide tractable approximations for large stochastic systems, but second-order steady-state results are largely limited to homogeneous or fixed-dimensional population processes. This paper develops a second-order steady-state approximation for fully heterogeneous mean-field models. Conditioning on the realized agent parameters, we study fixed-dimensional weighted occupancies even though the dimension of the full heterogeneous mean-field system grows linearly with the number of agents $M$. We first establish an $O(M^{-1})$ bound on the mean-field approximation error for stationary expectations of twice continuously differentiable functions of these occupancies. We then characterize the leading term in this error in terms of the stationary mean bias and covariance of the weighted occupancies. A Lyapunov equation for the linearized dynamics yields an approximation to the stationary covariance of the unscaled weighted occupancy with error $O(M^{-3/2})$. Its solution, together with the drift derivatives at equilibrium, also gives an explicit $1/M$ correction to the mean-field prediction of the stationary mean. The corrected mean has error $o(M^{-1})$, which improves to $O(M^{-3/2})$ under a stronger bound on the drift remainder. The resulting covariance and mean-refinement equations have the same structure as the finite-time heterogeneous refined mean-field equations, but our results directly provide steady-state guarantees for weighted occupancies rather than marginal state probabilities of individual agents. The results are illustrated through a heterogeneous power-of-two load-balancing model with buffer size two.

title: MemoSync: Co-Managing Developer-Agent Metamemory Across Contexts
abstract: AI coding agents increasingly manage what context carries across sessions and projects, but developers have limited visibility into what these agents store, retrieve, and apply. This opacity creates a metamemory problem: the developer's meta-level judgments about what should be remembered are separated from the agent's object-level memory operations, disrupting the monitoring and control that keep the two levels aligned. We conducted a formative study with 12 developers and identified what they want to monitor and control across four dimensions of agent memory use. Based on these findings, we designed MemoSync, a co-management system that treats agent memory as a shared, operable representation: the agent proposes memory candidates and reports which items it uses, and the developer reviews, edits, and scopes them. In a between-subjects study (N=132) against two baselines, MemoSync participants achieved significantly higher task performance and the highest mean developer-agent memory alignment. In an exploratory mediation analysis, the alignment advantage was primarily driven by improved monitoring accuracy. Despite performing substantially more monitoring and control actions, participants reported no increase in perceived workload. A week-long deployment with nine developers showed that memory monitoring and control fit into everyday development work. MemoSync is open-sourced at https://github.com/SLEEPYBQ/MemoSync.

title: CounselTraj: Synthesizing Process-Aware Psychological Counseling Dialogues via Dialogue-Act Trajectory Planning
abstract: The growing demand for psychological counseling has motivated the development of LLM-based systems that support human counselors, but training such systems requires large-scale, high-quality dialogue data. Authentic counseling transcripts are difficult to collect and share because of privacy concerns, making synthetic dialogues an important alternative. However, existing synthetic datasets, despite covering diverse scenarios and client profiles, often consist of brief exchanges and fail to capture session-level counseling processes. We propose CounselTraj, a dialogue-act trajectory planning framework for expanding brief synthetic dialogues into process-aware, session-level psychological counseling dialogues. CounselTraj learns dialogue-act patterns from role-play counseling dialogues produced by human counselors, plans coordinated trajectories for clients and counselors, and uses them as flexible guidance for long-form dialogue generation. Experiments across three Chinese synthetic counseling datasets show that CounselTraj produces more complete and coherent sessions with higher-quality counselor interventions than both direct expansion and expansion with randomly sampled trajectories. Based on CounselTraj, we construct CounselTrajD, a dataset containing over 10K process-guided Chinese psychological counseling dialogues, and use it to train CounselTrajLM for counseling response generation. Evaluations at both the response and session levels show that CounselTrajLM outperforms publicly available Chinese counseling models in response quality, therapeutic understanding and intervention, and counseling-process coherence and progress. Our code and model are publicly available at https://github.com/UEC-InabaLab/CounselTraj.

title: Guarding the Kingdom of Skill-Based Agents in the AI Dynasty of Computation: Control-Flow Integrity for Agent Skills
abstract: Control-flow integrity (CFI) confines a program to a control-flow graph fixed ahead of time. Procedural agent skills move this control flow into prompt text, and a large language model (LLM) agent decides at runtime whether each step runs in its reasoning, a tool call, or a script. The procedure's control skeleton survives, but its enforceability depends on where each step runs. Many violations, such as overwriting a file before validation, use only operations the skill requires, so permission allowlists admit them. A deviating or prompt-injected model can also evade a monitor by regime migration, for example by claiming that a check passed. We present SkillCFI, which carries CFI over to skill-based agents. Its compiler confines LLM interpretation to compile time and derives the agent's instructions and an executable contract from one skill. By a formal enforceability criterion, it enforces obligations whose evidence crosses the tool boundary and rejects a skill whose mandatory obligation leaves nothing to check. A deterministic runtime enforcer admits a tool request only on trusted evidence and refuses unmediated channels such as inline scripts, so admitted traces follow the contract whatever the model proposes. On eight self-written skills, no compiled contract permits more than its source under 24 source mutations. In 770 agent sessions, SkillCFI blocks before dispatch all 240 such violations, which an allowlist admits, and normal tasks complete nearly as often as without it. Listing the next legal steps in a refusal raises recovery from 21% to 65%. Checking takes about 2% of task time, and a compact command form cuts session slowdown from 1.32 times to 1.08 times. None of 53 public skills is accepted as written. The compiler's diagnostics point to interfaces rather than workflows and guided seven into enforceable contracts.

title: Worth Another Look:Constrained World-Model Planning for Visual Inspection
abstract: Visual inspection in field robotics and environmental monitoring must localize multiple targets under strict compute and sensing caps. Exhaustive sweeps waste calls on absent classes, while myopic and search-free policies stumble over heterogeneous tariff cliffs or discard viewport edits whose value emerges only after re-querying. We formulate inspection over frozen detectors as neuro-symbolic observation planning under partial observability, decoupling a compact recurrent world model (WM) from exact symbolic feasibility and tariff rules. Receding-horizon beam search with online replanning jointly schedules class queries, crops, enhancements, and termination (stop), paired with slack-aware shadow pricing and legal fallback at larger budgets. Across eight terrestrial, optical, and sonar benchmarks, multi-step lookahead outperforms static schedules and search-free offline RL under tight budgets -- gaining up to 28.4 AP percentage points over static priority on RUOD and 15.1 on ARIS -- while dynamic pricing lifts large-budget performance on all eight domains at 11 ms planning cost. Ultimately, pairing lightweight learned dynamics with exact symbolic constraints turns frozen detectors into adaptive, budget-aware inspection agents without retraining.

title: Stochastic Optimisation for Scalable Ptychographic Image Reconstruction
abstract: X-ray ptychography is a lensless coherent diffraction imaging technique capable of high spatial resolution, in which an image is reconstructed by solving a large-scale inverse problem from highly redundant far-field diffraction measurements acquired under overlapping illumination. Whilst the measurement redundancy created by overlapping illumination is essential for reconstruction fidelity, it leads to computational and memory demands that scale poorly with object size and target resolution when using conventional reconstruction algorithms. This work proposes a ptychographic reconstruction framework that reduces peak memory usage and time to convergence by leveraging stochastic optimisation techniques developed for large-scale machine learning. Specifically, the framework employs stochastic gradient descent with a decaying step size that progressively reduces the effect of gradient noise, referred to here as variance reduction (VR), with gradients that agree with automatic differentiation, to optimise the ptychographic forward model using randomly sampled subsets of diffraction measurements. For an experimental dataset of 200,000 diffraction patterns of $128\times128$ pixels, VR is demonstrated to require $65\%$ of the peak GPU memory and $22\%$ of the reconstruction time of the established maximum-likelihood (ML) algorithm. The VR framework incorporates the Poisson maximum-likelihood formulation and partial coherence within a unified and extensible optimisation setting. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the framework achieves reconstruction quality visually comparable to established methods, with lower peak GPU memory and a shorter time

title: A fully differential charged-particle phase-space measurement of $Z$+jets production in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
abstract: The production of a $Z$~boson decaying to muons in association with hadronic jets is a benchmark process in proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider. It provides a clean experimental signature with high selection efficiency and purity while probing a wide range of Standard Model dynamics. Measurements of this process are typically reported as binned differential cross sections in a limited set of predefined observables, which reduces the information retained and hinders reinterpretation. In this paper, the OmniFold method is used to produce an unbinned and highly differential measurement of the $Z$+jets cross section using 140 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ of $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS detector. This constitutes the first published unbinned, fully differential measurement of a collider cross section, describing the kinematics of individual charged particles within a well-defined region of phase space. This unbinned event representation is used to construct measurements in four example applications that illustrate the broad range of observables constrained with a single measurement, including several that would be difficult or impossible to access using traditional unfolding methods. The measurement is published as particle-level Monte Carlo events together with unfolded event weights, allowing arbitrary observables to be constructed after publication and enabling a broad range of future applications and reinterpretations.

title: Diffusion-Score-Based Joint Topology Identification and Generative Particle Filtering
abstract: Inferring the interaction graph of a networked system while tracking its latent state is central to infrastructure, environmental, and brain networks. Joint identification of interaction topology and latent network states is challenging when observations are intermittent and transition noise is unknown and non-Gaussian. We develop TopoScore-FAF, a diffusion-score-based framework for joint topology identification and generative particle filtering. The graph governs a leaky-diffusion conditional mean, while a frozen diffusion emulator represents the centered transition residual, avoiding the structural ambiguity of unrestricted generative models. First, we establish a score--topology duality that expresses edge-wise transition likelihood gradients as projections of the residual diffusion score. This enables topology learning without evaluating transition densities or differentiating through the generative sampler. Second, we develop diffusion-score-based topology identification with guarantees of identifiability under intermittent observations and invariance of the population minimizer across diffusion noise levels. Sufficient smoothing yields global strong convexity for bounded-plus-Gaussian residuals. As smoothing vanishes, the asymptotic covariance of the state-pair estimator decreases toward the Cram\'er--Rao bound, with a strict advantage over Gaussian quasi-likelihood under an edge-relevant non-Gaussianity condition. Third, we construct a topology-conditioned generative particle filter that combines guided residual sampling with score-driven graph updates. We establish mean-square closed-loop error bounds under a step-size-independent small-gain condition. The resulting framework uses the graph to structure state propagation and the estimated states to refine the graph. Synthetic and real-data experiments demonstrate its benefits under non-Gaussian forcing.

title: Reducing Inference Cost of Coding Agents with Timeout Cascades
abstract: AI coding agents have become one of the most popular applications of large language models. Yet, agentic AI comes at the cost of a tremendous amount of GPU compute resources, which limits its profitability and its viability at scale.
