title: Neural collaborative filtering with compliance gating for AI agent access permissions in smart grid enterprises
abstract: Intelligent agents are now used in smart-grid and distributed-energy enterprises to automate predictive maintenance scheduling, control-loop parameter inspection, dispatch data querying, and cross-department information sharing. When an agent takes any of these actions, it has to access supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) records, fault logs, and control-loop parameters across organizational boundaries—which is exactly where the compliance issue appears. The agent’s access decision has to obey mandatory-deny rules coming from sector-specific regulation and internal governance, without exception, and a purely learned classifier is not enough. Three concrete gaps remain in existing permission models. The first is that no deterministic guarantee is enforced on the mandatory-deny rule set. The second is that the business context is represented in a flat form, so the relational dependencies among tasks, tools, personnel roles, and data types are lost. The third is that the false positive rate on high-variance domains stays high—\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$16.7\%$$\end{document} for the strongest prior hybrid. In order to close the three gaps together, this paper formulates the Compliance-Aware Permission Prediction (CAPP) task and proposes an implementation named NCF-CG. Its learned branch is trained end-to-end and jointly uses a neural collaborative filtering preference estimator, a graph attention encoder over a Business Knowledge Graph, and a compliance-margin loss on forbidden pairs. On top of this branch, a hard compliance gate overrides the learned score at inference time whenever a mandatory rule fires. On a public benchmark of 7563 permission decisions, NCF-CG reaches \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$89.20\%$$\end{document} full-coverage accuracy and \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$11.73\%$$\end{document} false positive rate, surpassing all seven baselines (including four modern deep-learning models) under a paired participant-level t-test (\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$p < 10^{-12}$$\end{document} against every baseline). On the subset of decisions the gate never touches it still leads the prior hybrid by 5.05 percentage points, and a cross-domain transfer probe on 500 expert-reviewed energy-production vignettes returns \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$74.5\%$$\end{document} accuracy on the gate-untouched subset (the subset where domain shift can affect the model output). The framework gives an auditable modelling pattern for AI-agent access control in smart-grid enterprises: deterministic where the rules require it, and learned everywhere else.

title: A quick appraisal of machine learning techniques in different aspects of rice cultivation
abstract: Rice is the most important cereal crop in the world, consumed by more than half of the global population. With the projected world population reaching around 9 billion by 2050, the cultivation of the rice crop becomes important for the food security of the world. Machine learning methods are playing a crucial role in optimising technologies related to rice cultivation. This paper is a quick appraisal of 343 research articles for the comparative utilisation of Machine Learning methods pertaining to different aspects of rice cultivation viz crop improvement, crop monitoring, crop mapping, irrigation management, weed management, disease management, etc. The study indicated that ML methods are used unevenly in different aspects of rice cultivation, where the aspects like disease management, yield forecasting, post-harvest, crop mapping, crop monitoring lead in the utilization of ML methods in comparison to the other aspects like weed management, irrigation management, fertilizer management, etc. both in terms of the quantity and quality of methods utilized.

title: Artificial intelligence, English proficiency, and graduate employability: a narrative review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping English-language learning and digitally mediated work, yet research on AI-supported language development, psychological conditions, AI literacy, and graduate employability has largely developed in separate literatures. This focused narrative review integrates these domains to examine how AI-supported English learning may relate to graduate employability among university students and recent graduates, particularly in EFL and other non-native-English-speaking higher-education contexts. The final evidence base comprises 46 unique sources, including 19 published between 2018 and 2026 and 27 earlier foundational or contextual sources, drawn from empirical studies, reviews, theoretical literature, competence frameworks, and selected authoritative reports. The review examines how specific AI affordances support or constrain language-learning processes and differentiated English outcomes; how functional English communication relates to employability capabilities; how motivation, language anxiety, linguistic and digital self-efficacy, and career confidence operate as distinct antecedents, conditioning factors, or outcomes; and how critical AI literacy intersects with language and professional competence. Its distinctive contribution is a mechanism-based framework linking AI affordances, language-learning processes, English communicative outcomes, employability capabilities, perceived employability, opportunity access, and labor-market outcomes while explicitly distinguishing comparatively well-supported proximal relationships from tentative downstream transitions. The synthesis indicates that AI-supported learning can support feedback uptake, revision, repeated practice, interaction, and selected linguistic and psychological outcomes, but evidence for durable independent proficiency is more heterogeneous and direct evidence for employment, earnings, retention, or career progression remains limited. Benefits are conditional on pedagogical design, independent practice, human interaction, equitable access, and responsible AI use. Accordingly, the framework should be interpreted as a set of mechanism-based propositions rather than a validated causal model linking AI use directly to employability or employment. Because source identification and selection were purposive rather than exhaustive, the conclusions remain subject to selection and publication bias, geographical imbalance, methodological heterogeneity, reviewer judgment, and the rapid evolution of AI technologies. Of the 46 sources, 15 are classified as primary empirical publications, and four provide RQ1-specific direct evidence on AI-supported English-language learning. Two primary empirical publications examine graduate employability-related competencies or perceptions; one additional publication synthesizes earlier empirical assessments. Although some evidence concerns graduates’ employment experiences, no included study directly tests the effect of AI-supported English learning on job attainment or other labor-market outcomes.

title: Multiple intelligences as a pedagogical heuristic for EFL argumentative writing in Ethiopian higher education
abstract: This study examined the effects of Multiple Intelligences Theory (MIT), re-conceptualized as an instructional design heuristic rather than a validated cognitive model, on argumentative writing skills among English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners at an Ethiopian university. A mixed-methods quasi-experimental design assigned 90 undergraduates to an experimental group receiving MIT-as-heuristic instruction (n = 45) or a control group receiving traditional instruction (n = 45). Writing performance was assessed via pre-test and post-test argumentative essays, independently scored by six trained raters using a validated rubric (Intraclass Correlation Coefficient [ICC] = 0.92). Quantitative analyses employed independent-samples and paired-samples t-tests. Qualitative data from 15 semi-structured interviews underwent reflexive thematic analysis. Results revealed statistically significant improvements in the experimental group (pre-test M = 2.33, SD = 0.54; post-test M = 3.58, SD = 0.52; t (44) = 12.29, p < .001), whereas the control group showed minimal non-significant change (M gain = 0.02, p = .061). Between-group post-test comparisons confirmed significant differences favoring the experimental condition, t (88) = 12.28, p < .001, Cohen’s d = 0.80. Qualitative findings indicated that MIT-as-heuristic activities enhanced engagement, self-efficacy, and structural command of argumentation by providing scaffolded entry points into the writing process. When operationalized as a heuristic for designing varied learning tasks, MIT offers a practical, context-sensitive approach to differentiated writing instruction. This study contributes to EFL pedagogy in resource-constrained, large-class settings and recommends integrating such heuristic approaches into teacher education and curriculum development.

title: Iot and machine learning for multi-horizon soil moisture forecasting using leakage-free reconstructed sensor data in precision agriculture
abstract: Smart agriculture has emerged as an important approach for improving crop productivity, resource efficiency, and climate resilience through continuous environmental monitoring and predictive analytics. This study presents an Internet of Things (IoT) edge computing and machine learning framework for multi-horizon soil moisture forecasting in precision Agriculture. The proposed system integrates a Raspberry Pi 5 edge device with soil moisture, temperature, relative humidity, carbon dioxide (CO\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$_2$$\end{document}), and camera sensors to continuously monitor environmental and crop conditions on a cassava farm. Sensor data were processed using an edge-computing architecture and subsequently analyzed using statistical and machine learning techniques. To address prolonged sensor outage, a leakage-free time-series reconstruction methodology was developed that preserves temporal causality by reconstructing missing observations using only historical information available before the outage. Following data preprocessing and feature engineering, four supervised machine learning models including Linear Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), together with Persistence and ARIMA benchmark models, were evaluated for 1-day, 2-day, 5-day, and 7-day soil moisture forecasting. The nonlinear machine learning models consistently outperformed the benchmark approaches, with XGBoost and MLP achieving the highest predictive performance, reaching R2 score of up to 0.94 while substantially reducing forecasting errors. Comparative experiments further demonstrated that leakage-free reconstruction significantly improved forecasting accuracy relative to the non-reconstructed dataset. Feature importance analysis identified cyclical time-of-day information, historical soil moisture observations, and engineered temporal features as the most influential predictors. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of integrating IoT sensing, leakage-free data reconstruction, and machine learning to provide reliable soil moisture forecasting for intelligent irrigation management and sustainable cassava production.

title: Beyond likes and shares: how social media marketing communications build brand equity and drive electronic word-of-mouth in emerging E-commerce markets
abstract: Social media is a primary setting in which consumers form brand judgements and recommend products to others. Yet most studies either examine a single social media communication source or combine firm advertising, peer conversation, consumer reviews and influencer endorsements into one composite construct, so the relative associations of these sources with brand equity are rarely compared within one model. It is also unclear whether perceived performance risk weakens or strengthens the translation of brand equity into electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) intention. Using stimulus–organism–response (SOR) theory as an organising framework, this study models four communication sources social media advertising, social media word of mouth, user-generated content and influencer-generated content as stimuli (S), customer-based brand equity (CBBE) as the organism (O) and eWOM intention as the response (R), with performance risk as a moderator of the CBBE → eWOM path. Survey data from 384 e-commerce consumers in Pakistan were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. All four sources were positively associated with CBBE, with user-generated content showing the largest association (β = 0.432), followed by social media advertising (β = 0.183), influencer-generated content (β = 0.178) and social media word of mouth (β = 0.155). CBBE was strongly associated with eWOM intention (β = 0.695), and, contrary to a simple risk-aversion expectation, performance risk strengthened this association (β = 0.157, p < .001). CBBE transmitted significant indirect effects from each source to eWOM intention; when direct paths were added, the associations of social media advertising, social media word of mouth and user-generated content with eWOM intention were fully transmitted through CBBE (indirect-only mediation), whereas influencer-generated content retained a significant direct association (complementary mediation). Because the design is cross-sectional and the mechanisms proposed to explain the moderation were not measured, the findings are interpreted as associations that are consistent with, but do not establish, an informational-value account. The study contributes a source-differentiated test of the S → O → R chain and identifies perceived performance risk as a condition under which brand equity is more strongly linked to advocacy intention.

title: Crash analysis of highway during full-length rehabilitation: A predictable and interpretable framework.
abstract: Long-term full-length highway rehabilitation significantly alters traffic dynamics, however the heterogeneity in crash mechanisms between work and non-work zones remains unexplored. To address the limitations of conventional models in capturing spatial heterogeneity and the ordinal nature of crash severity, this study proposes a Zone-aware Ordinal Attention-regularized TabNet (ZOA-TabNet) framework. Based on a matched dataset of 920 crash records, a comprehensive crash severity indicator (Z) was constructed via the entropy weight method. Comparative experiments against five benchmarks: two established discrete-choice crash severity models (a correlated random parameter ordered probit model and a mixed logit model with heterogeneity in means and variances) and three gradient-boosting models (XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost) demonstrated ZOA-TabNet's superiority. In work zones, the model achieved average accuracy, recall, F1 and ordinal distance of 0.97, 0.96, 0.96 and 0.03, with the improvements of 2.9 %, 2.2 %, 2.2 % and 54.4 % over the best-performing baseline, respectively. Results show that environmental factors and lane reductions make greater contributions to crash severity in work zones, whereas high-speed operating conditions and passenger-car characteristics are more prominent in non-work zones. These findings offer an insight for differentiated traffic management during highway rehabilitation.

title: A Conventional T1WI-Derived Signal Ratio for Differentiating Granulomatous Prostatitis From Prostate Cancer: A Two-Center Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To evaluate whether a signal ratio derived from conventional T1WI can differentiate granulomatous prostatitis (GP) from prostate cancer (PCa) in patients with overlapping PI-RADS findings. MATERIALS AND METHODS This retrospective two-center study included 29 patients with GP and 58 patients with PCa, all pathologically confirmed. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging parameters were analyzed. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors and construct a combined diagnostic model. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and comparisons were performed using the DeLong test. RESULTS There was no significant difference in PI-RADS scores between patients with GP and those with PCa (p > 0.05), and all patients with GP were classified as PI-RADS 4-5. The T1 ratio was significantly higher in GP than in PCa and showed the best diagnostic performance among individual parameters, with an AUC of 0.769 (95% CI: 0.662-0.876). In contrast, the T2 ratio and ADC ratio showed limited performance, with AUCs of 0.581 (95% CI: 0.447-0.715) and 0.599 (95% CI: 0.469-0.730), respectively. In multivariable analysis including age, T1 ratio, T2 ratio, ADC ratio, neutrophil count, and PSAD, T1 ratio, neutrophil count, and PSAD remained independent predictors for differentiating GP from PCa. A combined model incorporating these three predictors achieved an AUC of 0.873 (95% CI: 0.797-0.949), significantly higher than that of T1 ratio alone (DeLong p = 0.024). CONCLUSION T1 ratio provides independent diagnostic value for differentiating GP from PCa in patients with overlapping PI-RADS findings. Combining T1 ratio with neutrophil count and PSAD further improves diagnostic performance, supporting the potential utility of routinely available clinical and MRI parameters for noninvasive diagnosis.

Co-culture with embryonic renal stromal progenitor cell enhances podocyte differentiation and modulates doxorubicin-induced injury responses.
abstract: Podocytes are specialized epithelial cells that play a central role in maintaining the selective permeability of the glomerular filtration barrier of the kidney. However, conventional podocyte mono-culture systems often lack the cellular microenvironment required to fully support podocyte differentiation. Renal stromal progenitor cells (rSPCs) contribute to glomerular development and give rise to stromal derivatives, including mesangial cells, suggesting that they may provide developmental cues that support podocyte differentiation. Therefore, this study investigates the effect of co-culturing heat-sensitive mouse podocytes (HSMPs) with mouse embryonic rSPCs on podocyte differentiation and function in a membrane-based system. Podocytes were cultured alone or in combination with sorted embryonic rSPCs on porous membranes of different pore sizes (0.4 μm and 8 μm). The results showed that co-culture with rSPCs on 8 μm membranes significantly enhanced podocyte marker expression and promoted podocyte-like morphology, likely due to improved cellular interactions. The co-culture model maintained size-selective permeability and exhibited a distinct dose-dependent response to doxorubicin-induced injury, suggesting that rSPCs modulate podocyte sensitivity to toxic stress. These findings suggest that embryonic rSPCs provide a supportive microenvironment that enhances podocyte differentiation and stability, offering a more physiologically relevant in vitro model for studying glomerular development and injury.

title: A lightweight differentiable method for real-time skin rendering and digitization
abstract: Inverse rendering for skin typically relies on offline path tracing to estimate physical properties, which fail to map directly to the approximate shaders utilized in interactive applications, such as game engines. We bridge this gap by directly estimating subsurface scattering parameters tailored for real-time rendering pipelines. We introduce a differentiable Screen-Space Subsurface Scattering (SSSS) framework that enables the joint optimization of spatially varying base textures and scattering distances. To account for local variations in skin thickness, we estimate these parameters across distinct facial regions, generating a blended profile map ready for production runtime engines. Our pipeline utilizes a low-cost, single-light, single-view capture setup designed for accessible and practical appearance acquisition. Optimization is driven by a masked loss function targeting regions where subsurface scattering effects are dominant. We validate our approach on a real-world dataset of $45$ individuals across the Monk Skin Tone Scale, ensuring demographic generalization. Furthermore, we complement this evaluation with synthetic data, a multi-light setup validating our single-light assumption, and a tilted-view configuration confirming angular consistency. Results demonstrate that our method effectively recovers scattering parameters from lightweight inputs, yielding realistic skin appearance directly compatible with standard real-time shaders.

title: Auditing the adversarial robustness of genomic foundation models with SafeGenes
abstract: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) such as evolutionary scale modeling (ESM) are increasingly applied to variant effect prediction in clinical genomics, yet their adversarial robustness remains underexplored. We present SafeGenes, an evaluation framework combining input-space attacks, a discrete single-nucleotide variant (SNV)-reachable HotFlip attack, and a soft-prompt-triggered backdoor. Across cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia datasets, iterative attacks severely degrade discrimination: projected gradient descent (PGD) reduces the area under the curve (AUC) by more than 30 percentage points, and the false-positive rate at 95% sensitivity collapses to nearly 1.0, misclassifying virtually all benign variants as pathogenic. The backdoor selectively elevates the pseudo-log-likelihood ratio (PLLR) scores of benign variants and transfers across ESM architectures. A single population-observed background substitution inverts pathogenicity ranking below chance, lowering the AUC from 0.76 to 0.39, showing that these vulnerabilities are biologically realizable. SafeGenes provides an open auditing framework for adversarial robustness in genomic AI.

title: Farmers’ perceptions and determinants of the use of botanical pest control in food crop production in Benin (West Africa)
Achievements and current perspectives on nitrate leaching mitigation in German agriculture
Managing for upside in a variable climate: An envirotyping framework for wheat genotype × management strategies
Lentil, chickpea, microalgae, and duckweed proteins in plant-based foods: a food chemistry perspective on composition, processing, functionality, and digestibility.
abstract: Growing demand for alternative protein ingredients has expanded research on lentil, chickpea, microalgae, and duckweed. Cross-source comparison remains difficult because material form, analytical method, processing history, digestibility model, and functional assay often differ among studies. Quantitative primary evidence was evaluated using a material-method-structure-function-matrix approach. Microalgal nitrogen-to-protein conversion factors ranged from 2.53 to 5.77, indicating limitations of a universal factor of 6.25. Processed lentil and chickpea showed fecal-protein-based DIAAS-type values of 44-58 and 78-84, respectively, whereas cooked chickpea showed true-ileal DIAAS values of 67-76. High-pressure homogenization increased lentil protein solubility while reducing particle size. Hydrolysis of Wolffia globosa increased solubility but reduced oil-binding capacity. Evidence remains broader for lentil and chickpea, whereas interpretation of microalgal and duckweed proteins is more condition-dependent. Direct validation in the intended food matrix is therefore more informative than cross-source ranking.

title: How food structure and processing govern metabolizable energy: a critical review of the food-matrix determinants of energy availability and the limits of the Atwater accounting.
abstract: Food energy is usually reported using Atwater factors: composition-based coefficients that treat metabolizable energy as a function of macronutrient mass rather than food structure. Yet a growing food-science literature shows that metabolizable energy can diverge materially from Atwater predictions according to the integrity of the food matrix and the processing applied to it. This review brings energy-accounting and food-structure science into direct contact. It defines where the Atwater system remains useful and where its structural blind spot becomes consequential; clarifies the frequent conflation of digestibility, bioaccessibility, bioavailability and metabolizable energy, and distinguishes physical resistance from chemical inhibition of digestive enzymes while treating the two as coupled rather than independent. It then maps major processing operations to their structural and energetic consequences, and compares methods used to quantify metabolizable energy and nutrient release, including human balance studies, ileostomy and intubation studies, standardised in vitro digestion, dynamic models and in silico approaches. Tree nuts provide the strongest empirical case. Measured metabolizable energy ranges from about 5% below the Atwater value for pistachios to more than 30% below for whole almonds, a divergence that is explained by matrix integrity and lipid encapsulation. Four energetic consequences of matrix disruption are considered: net metabolizable energy, rate of energy release, thermic effect of feeding and colonic salvage. The review concludes that energy values based on composition alone are insufficient for foods whose structure strongly constrains digestion, and that food-composition data, labelling, feeding research and reformulation would benefit from structure-aware measures of delivered energy.

title: Beyond weed control: Herbicide-driven rhizosphere dysbiosis in tropical agriculture.
abstract: Herbicides are essential for tropical agriculture, enabling effective weed control and sustaining the productivity of intensive cropping systems. However, their impacts extend beyond target weeds, influencing the rhizosphere microbial communities that support soil and plant health. Previous studies have focused on short-term toxicity or changes in bulk soil microbiota, often under temperate conditions. Consequently, the ecological processes governing rhizosphere microbiome responses to repeated herbicide exposure remain poorly understood, particularly in tropical systems. In this review, we propose a conceptual model in which herbicides act as ecological filters that may progressively drive the transition from rhizosphere eubiosis to dysbiosis in tropical agroecosystems. This perspective integrates plant-mediated effects, microbial community assembly, interaction networks, and ecosystem functions to explain how repeated herbicide exposure progressively changes rhizosphere resilience. We discuss how herbicide-induced changes in plant physiology and root exudation modify microbial recruitment and community assembly and reshape microbial interaction networks. We further examine how these changes affect candidate keystone taxa, network stability, nutrient cycling, and plant resilience. Building on this ecological perspective, we evaluate emerging strategies to restore rhizosphere eubiosis, including defined microbial communities, in situ microbiome manipulation, regenerative agricultural practices, and microbiome-conscious herbicide management. Finally, we identify critical research priorities, highlighting the need for long-term field experiments, multi-omics approaches, ecological network validation, and microbiome-aware herbicide risk assessment. By integrating ecological theory with rhizosphere microbiome research, this review provides insights into herbicide-driven dysbiosis and offers new perspectives for developing sustainable, microbiome-informed weed management strategies that enhance soil and plant health in tropical agriculture.

title: Percolation-tunable conductive MXene-hydrogel multi-channel conduits promote integrin-mediated peripheral nerve regeneration.
abstract: Peripheral nerve repair is severely hindered by the lack of biomimetic conductive scaffolds that recapitulate native conductive microenvironments to coordinate neuronal differentiation and myelination. Here, we fabricate a multi-channel polyacrylamide/chitosan/MXene hydrogel nerve conduit with concentration-programmable percolative conductivity. A critical percolation threshold at 600 μg/mL establishes an optimal conductive microenvironment, which significantly enhances Schwann cell viability, neurite outgrowth, and neurotrophic factor secretion. Mechanistically, the MXene-mediated conductive cue upregulates myelination- and neuronal differentiation-related genes via activating integrin-dependent PI3K-Akt mechanotransduction and axon guidance signaling pathways. In a rat sciatic nerve defect model, the optimized conduit significantly promotes axonal regeneration and remyelination, with 12-week functional and electrophysiological recovery indicators showing no significant statistical difference from those of autologous nerve grafts. This work demonstrates that percolation-tunable conductive engineering is a reliable strategy to construct biomimetic neural microenvironments, providing a feasible translational scaffold for advanced peripheral nerve regeneration.

title: Dual-phase deep learning recommendation system for radiographic crown lengthening assessment and post selection for the restoration of endodontically treated teeth.
abstract: STATEMENT OF PROBLEM Restoring endodontically treated teeth requires careful evaluation of the supracrestal tissue attachment, ferrule integrity, and post-space dimensions to ensure long-term success. Manual radiographic analysis for crown lengthening indication and post selection is often time-consuming, subjective, and inconsistent, particularly in resource-limited settings where specialist access may be constrained. PURPOSE The purpose of this study was to design and validate an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven system that automated 2 essential restorative planning tasks, evaluating the clinical need for crown lengthening and recommending appropriate post dimensions in endodontically treated teeth, using dental radiographs as the input. MATERIAL AND METHODS Two deep learning pipelines were developed and trained on annotated panoramic and periapical datasets with annotations created under the supervision of dentistry professionals. The crown measurement pipeline employed a U-shaped network (U-Net) model for initial tooth segmentation (assigning unique instance masks to each tooth), then cropping individual teeth and feeding them into a Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN) for precise detection and crown length calculation, facilitating the assessment of parameters such as supracrestal tissue attachment and ferrule height, for identification of potential violations or restoration limitations. The post measurement pipeline utilized Mask R-CNN directly on the original images to detect endodontic posts and measure their length and width, enabling comparison against established prosthodontic criteria. Both models were trained in a graphics processing unit (GPU)-enabled environment (Kaggle; Google LLC) and evaluated using standard metrics including Intersection over Union (IoU), Dice coefficient, and measurement accuracy, with validation involving visual overlays and quantitative comparisons to expert annotations. RESULTS The segmentation model achieved a mean IoU of 0.52 and a Dice coefficient of 0.66, with diagnostic accuracy exceeding 99% in identifying post locations and assessing ferrule presence. The system accurately detected supracrestal tissue attachment violations and provided clinically relevant post dimension recommendations, closely aligning with expert-guided decisions. GPU acceleration reduced model training time by over 70% compared to local central processing unit (CPU)-only workflows. CONCLUSIONS The AI-powered system demonstrated promising performance in automating radiographic evaluations critical to restoring endodontically treated teeth. By identifying crown lengthening requirements and suggesting post dimensions, the integrated pipelines supported objective and reproducible treatment planning. This approach may enhance prosthodontic workflows, especially in settings with limited specialist availability, and holds potential for integration into commercial dental imaging platforms.

title: Decoupling physiological and non-physiological drivers of SIF response to spatial water-salinity stress of Suaeda salsa in coastal wetlands
Toward agentic AI co-practitioners in dermatology.
abstract: Multimodal foundation models have given dermatological artificial intelligence a strong perceptual baseline, although performance on darker skin, rare conditions, and real-world images remains uneven. The next challenge is clinical agency. Here we propose a conceptual framework for agentic co-practitioners: systems in which a reasoning engine orchestrates active sensing, specialized tools, and longitudinal memory to take part in the clinical encounter from referral to management plan. No such system has yet been validated end to end in dermatology. We argue that sustained clinical value requires these systems to co-evolve with their physician users through structured feedback that captures local expertise without retraining. Because the value of a co-practitioner lies in its reasoning process and its effect on clinicians, retrospective benchmarks are insufficient; evaluation must assess complete clinical episodes, including patient-centered and health-system outcomes. We also set out the workforce, cost, liability, and regulatory questions that the framework does not yet resolve.

title: Epigenetic memory meets transcriptional plasticity: Mechanistic perspectives from a chromatin regulatory hub in plants.
abstract: Epigenetic landscapes shape gene expression beyond the genetic code. How is epigenetic memory faithfully transmitted through cell divisions while retaining conditional transcriptional flexibility? In plants, LIKE HETEROCHROMATIN PROTEIN 1 (LHP1), for which the functional nomenclature Polycomb-beyond Composite Regulator 1 (PCR1) was recently proposed, offers a mechanistic lens for interrogating this paradox. Converging evidence, primarily from Arabidopsis thaliana, links LHP1 to DNA replication-coupled chromatin restoration, Polycomb-linked 3D genome organization, and long non-coding RNA (lncRNA)-mediated chromatin switching. Guided by this chromatin hub logic, we synthesize evidence across these interfaces and develop forward-looking models for how Polycomb memory may be maintained while permitting context-dependent transcriptional reconfiguration. We distinguish established mechanisms from cross-study inference and working hypotheses, highlighting key mechanistic gaps that remain unresolved. Across crops and woody perennials, cross-lineage observations suggest recurrent redeployment of LHP1-associated regulatory themes across developmental, environmental, and trait-associated regulatory programs while accommodating lineage-specific variation. Together, these perspectives highlight how a chromatin regulatory factor can help coordinate chromatin memory with transcriptional plasticity.

title: Genomic signatures of divergence and connectivity in the Western Banded Gecko (Coleonyx variegatus).
abstract: Desert ecosystems of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico are characterized by high endemism. Many desert adapted species exhibit phylogeographic patterns that correlate with major desert regions, but the relative contributions of geographic isolation, environmental differentiation, and gene flow to these patterns remain unclear. In this study, we used genome-wide SNP data to measure the genetic diversity of the Western Banded Gecko (Coleonyx variegatus), which spans the Sonoran and Mojave deserts, and the entirety of the Baja California Peninsula. The broad geographic distribution of C. variegatus across these unique ecosystems provides an opportunity to determine how genetic diversity is structured across desert ecoregions, and to investigate the history of gene flow within and between deserts. We conduct population structure analyses to identify population boundaries, use multispecies coalescent models to estimate the species tree and divergence times, and then apply the multispecies coalescent with migration (MSC-M) to estimate rates of gene flow among populations. Our analyses identify geographically and genetically distinct populations that largely align with desert ecoregions. Populations exhibit significant ecological niche differentiation; however, counter to expectations, high levels of gene flow persist, particularly between populations in the Mojave and Sonoran deserts. Species tree inference and divergence dating suggest a recent diversification history, with primary lineages originating during the mid-to-late Pleistocene. These results contribute to a growing phylogeographic framework for taxa spanning the southwestern deserts and highlight the value of comparative analyses across sympatric species for identifying shared drivers of diversification in the region.

title: Tracking human HSCs and MPPs in mice reveals distinct clonal dynamics and responses to pre-transplant conditioning
abstract: Blood and immune cell regeneration is sustained by hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), which form the therapeutic basis of bone marrow transplantation. While the functional hierarchy of mouse HSPC subsets is well characterized, the distinct roles of human HSPC populations remain less well defined, particularly at clonal resolution and in the context of transplantation conditioning. Here, we performed quantitative clonal tracking of purified human HSCs (hHSCs) and human MPPs (hMPPs) in NSGW41 mice across primary and secondary transplantation under no conditioning, and busulfan or irradiation conditioning. We found that hHSC clones generated more blood cells, initiated lymphoid production earlier, and exhibited more robust multilineage differentiation than hMPP clones. hHSC clones were also less sensitive to conditioning, maintaining stable lineage biases. Notably, busulfan and irradiation differentially affected the magnitude, lineage bias, and timing of hematopoietic reconstitution without altering engraftment. During secondary transplantation, hHSCs and hMPPs contributed comparably to hematopoietic reconstitution but with substantially reduced output and increased clonal diversity. Extramedullary hematopoiesis was observed in all secondary recipients. These findings advance our understanding of human hematopoiesis and provide a framework for optimizing experimental models, improving transplantation conditioning strategies, and informing the preclinical evaluation of HSC-based cell and gene therapies.

title: Student mental health patterns in the REALISE cohort show four trajectories over one academic year
abstract: University students experience high levels of psychological distress, often exceeding those observed in other young adult populations. Despite growing evidence that students are at increased risk for psychological distress, its development across the academic year remains insufficiently understood. Additionally, for early identification of highly distressed students, understanding heterogeneous patterns is crucial. This longitudinal study investigated trajectories of psychological distress among N = 458 students from a German university using the Depression, Anxiety, Stress Scale with monthly assessments across one academic year. Latent class growth analysis identified distinct trajectory classes. In addition, a random forest model predicted class membership based on baseline measurements. Four trajectory classes were identified: low psychological distress (36.9%), moderate psychological distress (32.1%), moderate-high psychological distress (23.8%), and high psychological distress (7.2%). The high-distress class showed persistently elevated distress, whereas the other three classes revealed decreasing distress over time. Baseline measures of depression, anxiety, stress, and well-being best predicted trajectory class membership with moderate average accuracy (61.4% [95% CI 56.7, 65.8%]), demonstrating best accuracy for extreme trajectory classes (low and high distress). Including two additional within-year measurement points slightly increased accuracy to 66.4% (95% CI 61.8, 70.7%), but notably improved the differentiation of moderate distress trajectories. These findings suggest that baseline screening enables early risk stratification, whereas subsequent within-year assessments could serve as ongoing monitoring for adaptive risk refinement and targeted resource allocation in university settings.

title: Author Correction: A systematic scoping review of environmental, food security and health impacts of food system plastics

title: Redesigning photoprotection: nature-inspired and synthetic biology strategies to enhance crop productivity.
abstract: Photosynthesis captures solar energy and carbon dioxide to fuel life on Earth by providing food and oxygen. When light intensity exceeds photosynthetic capacity, resulting in the saturation of the electron transport chain, photosynthetic organisms protect themselves by activating photoprotective non-photochemical quenching (NPQ), which dissipates excess energy as heat. Despite the importance of NPQ in plant physiology, its slow activation and relaxation may cause substantial yield losses in field-grown crops. For this reason, qE, the fastest component of NPQ, has become a central biotechnological target for crop engineering. While pioneering approaches, such as the "VPZ strategy" involving the overexpression of both xanthophyll cycle and PSBS proteins, have successfully enhanced field productivity, their efficacy varies across species, highlighting current biotechnological bottlenecks. This review discusses the molecular bases and activation models of qE in different clades, describing the transition from LHCSR- to PSBS-dependent strategies and the central role of the xanthophyll cycle, while highlighting open debates and unresolved questions. Further, it outlines the future of NPQ engineering, exploring nature-inspired solutions, including the heterologous expression of LHCSR or alternative xanthophyll cycles in crops. Finally, this review discusses how CRISPR-Cas9-driven precision breeding and the application of Artificial Intelligence, and de novo protein design will guide future biotechnological intervention toward developing high-yielding, better resource-efficient crops.

title: The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Facial Plastic Surgery: From Education and Research to EHR-Embedded Applications.
abstract: Aims and Backgrounds Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly relevant to facial plastic surgery. This narrative review examines applications in education, research, and clinical workflows, including tools embedded in the electronic health record (EHR), and discusses responsible adoption. Technology Applications include educational content generation, surgical skill assessment, facial measurement, research assistance, preoperative simulation and planning, decision support, chart summarization, ambient documentation, and patient-message drafting. Agentic workflows could coordinate clinical tasks. Current and Future Development Available evidence primarily evaluates feasibility, content quality, measurement agreement, and workflow effects rather than improved clinical outcomes. Hallucinations, readability, privacy, safety, and bias require attention. Priorities include external validation, outcome assessment, and governance with continued monitoring as systems change. Conclusions and Clinical Relevance AI should augment surgeons, with oversight proportionate to clinical risk, protection of patient information, and assessment across patient groups. Its value should be judged by demonstrated improvements in clinical work, patient experience, and meaningful outcomes.

title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. AREAS COVERED This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. EXPERT OPINION AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

title: Enormous enhancement of resistivity in a nanostructured electron-phonon system.
abstract: Recent experiments on nanoclusters of silver (Ag) embedded in a gold (Au) matrix reveal a substantial enhancement of both the residual resistivity and the coefficient of the linear-in-$T$ thermal resistivity with increasing Ag volume fraction. Since bulk Au and Ag are both weakly coupled electron-phonon systems, these observations raise the possibility of an enhanced effective electron-phonon coupling at the Ag-Au interface. In this work, we explore the consequences of such an enhancement for electronic transport in a strongly inhomogeneous system. An important task is to elucidate the origin of the large interfacial coupling via {\it ab initio} calculation. In this paper, we {\it assume} the presence of such a coupling, and focus on its consequences for residual resistivity and finite temperature scattering in this strongly inhomogeneous scenario. To establish the qualitative physics we construct nanocluster configurations for varying $f$ in a two dimensional geometry, and define a Holstein model on it with weak coupling on the `interior' sites and a strong coupling on the interfacial sites. The model is solved through exact diagonalisation based Langevin dynamics. Our calculations reproduce the qualitative trends of the experimentally observed resistivity enhancement, with its magnitude depending on the choice of interfacial coupling. More importantly, we find that interfacial scattering is strongly spatially differentiated, with the zero temperature and thermal scattering arising from different parts of the interface. We confirm the resistivity trends in three dimensions as well through computation at select parameter points.
journal: Journal of physics. Condensed matter : an Institute of Physics journal

title: A regime-based nested CV machine learning model to forecast the magneto-induced mechanical characteristics of a magnetorheological fluid
abstract: Magnetorheological fluid (MRF) is an intelligent fluid that has a lot of promise in the automation industry. It is well established from earlier research that the magneto-induced yield stress primarily determines MRF's load-bearing capacity. However, the existing experimental and theoretical approaches to measure the magneto-induced yield stress of MRF have limitations. Without making any assumptions, a data-driven machine learning model can learn nonlinear relationships between input parameters and observed attributes from data. This method makes it possible to model with accuracy, interpretability, and uncertainty awareness even in situations when there are few experiments and the system is very non-linear. The objective of this study is to generate a hybrid physics-informed data-driven ML model to predict the magneto-induced yield stress with raw and non-linear input features. The experimental findings for the MRF for different material ratios evaluated over the rotational rheometer (Anton Paar) are gathered for the hybrid physics-informed data-driven analysis.Three distinct machine learning (ML) models-Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) -were applied to rheological experimental data of the MRF of different compositions to predict the magneto-induced yield stress of MRF. Using performance analysis, we demonstrated that the ML models can reliably forecast the magneto-induced yield stress of MRF based on material, rheological, and electromagnetic test variable data. It was evident from a comparison of model results that the GPR performed better in predicting yield stress than other ML models. According to a further investigation of permutation feature importance, strong inter-feature correlations and nonlinear interactions seen in magnetorheological systems are reflected in the comparatively large error bars as compared to the mean permutation importance, which shows that the contribution of individual features changes across permutations.

title: Explainable Deep Learning-Based Characterization and Classification of Metallographic Microstructures Using a Multi-Scale Swin Transformer
abstract: Automated classification of metallographic microstructures is challenged by subtle inter-class differences, substantial intra-class variations, and sparse discriminative regions. Conventional convolutional neural networks have limited ability to model long-range dependencies and cross-scale microstructural patterns, whereas vision Transformers may inadequately capture local textures and grain-boundary details. To address these limitations, an explainable multi-scale enhanced Swin Transformer is proposed for complex metallographic microstructure classification. A convolutional information enhancement module and an efficient multi-scale attention module are integrated into the backbone to strengthen the representation of local textures, grain boundaries, and multi-scale morphological features. Generalized mean pooling is adopted in the classification head, while multi-view crop augmentation, focal loss, and five-crop inference are used to improve robustness. Channel-contribution analysis is subsequently performed to identify discriminative channels associated with five microstructure classes. Channel-response maps demonstrate correspondence between the regions emphasized by the network and characteristic microstructural morphologies. The identified channels are preserved during structured pruning, while low-contribution channels are removed. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 98.00%, a precision of 98.01%, and a Cohen’s kappa coefficient of 0.9750. After pruning, the parameter count decreases from 28.096 M to 14.043 M, representing a reduction of approximately 50.0%, while retaining competitive classification performance. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an accurate, interpretable, and lightweight approach for automated recognition of complex metallographic microstructures.

title: Porcupine inhibition alleviates excessive bone formation in osteopathia striata with cranial sclerosis.
abstract: Osteopathia striata with cranial sclerosis (OSCS) is a rare osteosclerotic disorder caused by mutations of AMER1, a negative regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway. These mutations lead to excessive osteoblast activity and bone hypertrophy, often resulting in cranial nerve compression. In the absence of targeted therapies, we explored Wnt inhibition as a potential treatment strategy. This study aimed to (i) characterize the cellular and histopathological features of OSCS human bone tissue, (ii) analyze the skeletal phenotype of an OSCS mouse model, and (iii) evaluate the therapeutic potential of LGK-974, a porcupine inhibitor that blocks Wnt ligand secretion and signaling. Histological analyses and primary osteoblast cultures from bone samples of a patient living with OSCS revealed increased trabecular thickness and reduced bone marrow adiposity, alongside enhanced osteoblast differentiation and mineralization. The OSCS murine model Prx1-Cre+; Amer1flox/Y recapitulated partly the human phenotype, with elevated cortical and trabecular bone mass due to increased bone formation by increasing osteoblast number. Transcriptomic profiling showed upregulation of Wnt & TGF-β signaling. Administration of LGK-974 significantly reduced bone mass and microarchitectural parameters by decreasing both osteoblast number and function, while promoting osteoclastogenesis. Transcriptomic changes included downregulation of Wnt and MAPK target genes, and upregulation of adipogenesis genes. In summary, AMER1 loss-of-function induces bone sclerosis by driving precursor cells toward early osteogenic differentiation. This phenotype results, at least partly, from ligand-dependent Wnt signaling, as demonstrated by the ability of LGK-974 to mitigate the excessive bone formation. Porcupine inhibitors may therefore represent a potential therapeutic strategy for orphan sclerosing bone disorders.
journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research

title: TyCHE enables time-resolved lineage tracing of B cells and other heterogeneously-evolving populations.
abstract: Phylogenetic methods for cell lineage tracing have driven significant insights into organismal development, immune responses, and tumor evolution. While many methods estimate trees with branch lengths representing mutations, time-resolved lineage trees with branch lengths representing calendar time are more interpretable and could relate events like cellular migration and differentiation to perturbations like vaccines and drug treatments. However, in many evolving systems such as B cells, tumor lineages, and hypermutating bacterial populations, evolutionary rates often vary dramatically by genomic background or cell state, significantly biasing existing methods that build time trees using either a fixed molecular clock rate or uncorrelated relaxed clock models without a mechanistic model of molecular clock rate variation. We introduce TyCHE (Type-linked Clocks for Heterogeneous Evolution), a Bayesian phylogenetics package that infers time-resolved phylogenies of populations in which the molecular clock rate is linked to discrete states like genomic background or cell type. We demonstrate that TyCHE improves the accuracy of estimated time trees using a new simulation package SimBLE (Simulator of B cell Lineage Evolution). We use TyCHE to infer patterns of memory B cell differentiation during HIV infection, dynamics of recall germinal centers following influenza vaccination, evolution of a glioma tumor lineage, and progression of a bacterial lung infection, showing the applicability of our model to a wide range of systems and across different scales. TyCHE and SimBLE are available as open-source software packages compatible with the BEAST2 and Immcantation ecosystems.

title: qPTM 3.0: the AI-enhanced knowledgebase for protein post-translational modification dynamics.
abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) are key mechanisms of regulating protein function, yet quantitative PTM data remain fragmented across publications, supplementary datasets, and specialized resources. Here, we present qPTM 3.0, an integrated resource for quantitative PTM dynamics and AI-assisted knowledge discovery. The current release contains 15 652 063 quantitative events on 994 878 modification sites within 49 280 proteins across 3988 conditions, curated from 846 publications and spanning 12 PTM types in human, mouse, rat, and yeast. Raw mass spectrometry (MS) data associated with the curated entries were re using MaxQuant, and each modification site was assigned a five-star reliability score. Detailed annotations of experimental context, protein information, functional regulation, regulators, and inhibitors are also provided. qPTM 3.0 further introduces two AI-assisted modules. The PTM research agent enables natural-language exploration of qPTM 3.0 and complementary resources by synthesizing evidence on PTM regulators, regulatory conditions, and functional consequences. The data collection agent supports database curation through automated literature screening, full-text retrieval, metadata extraction, quantitative table parsing, and raw MS data acquisition within a human-in-the-loop workflow. Together, these features support systematic exploration of quantitative PTM dynamics and evidence-based biological interpretation. The online service is freely available at https://qptm.omicsbio.info/.

title: From anthropomorphic design cues to dual trust: adoption intention toward autonomous delivery robots in Hanoi, Vietnam
abstract: Autonomous delivery robots (ADRs) perform a functional logistics task, yet scenario-based evaluations may depend substantially on whether the robot appears readable and approachable. This study examines how perceived anthropomorphic design cues relate to ADR adoption intention in Hanoi through interaction fluency, instrumental value, social trust and competence trust. A standardised scenario-based online survey of 410 respondents in Hanoi, Vietnam, was analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in AMOS. The original structure and an exploratory extension linking instrumental value to social trust were compared. Latent-model bootstrap contrasts assessed specific and aggregate indirect associations. Perceived anthropomorphic cues are positively associated with adoption intention and interaction fluency. Instrumental value is positively associated with both trust dimensions, whereas the direct interaction fluency–social trust association is unsupported. The aggregate indirect association through social trust exceeds that through competence trust in the bootstrap comparison. Limited measurement fit and construct overlap qualify these findings. Using the stimulus-organism-response framework, the study integrates signaling, Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)-derived appraisal and multidimensional human-robot trust to examine associations between perceived design cues, appraisals and differentiated trust. The exploratory instrumental value-social trust extension identifies a possibly shared appraisal antecedent of the two trust dimensions in scenario-based autonomous delivery robot (ADR) evaluation.
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics

title: Content licensing strategy in AI–publisher coopetition: the role of asymmetric comparative advantages and citation intensity
abstract: This study examines strategic content licensing between a generative artificial intelligence (AI) platform and a digital news publisher in digital news markets, an important issue for understanding where AI platforms rely on publisher content while competing for user attention. It analyzes how citation intensity shapes licensing incentives, pricing, user diversion and welfare. We develop a game-theoretic model of two-dimensional horizontal differentiation in which the AI platform has a comparative advantage in content integration and the publisher has a comparative advantage in factual accuracy. The model examines how citation intensity, hallucination risk, user preference correlation and per-use royalty jointly determine equilibrium outcomes. Licensing between AI platforms and publishers arises from a trade-off between two countervailing forces: entry displacement and engagement expansion. Content licensing requires sufficiently high citation intensity; mutual gains additionally require low preference correlation. The pricing effects of citation intensity are nonmonotonic. Subscription prices can rise or fall depending on the strength of citation relative to royalty costs. User diversion is shaped by the balance between referral traffic expansion and direct substitution. Welfare improves only when engagement expansion dominates entry displacement. This study models AI–publisher licensing in a two-dimensional Hotelling framework of asymmetric comparative advantages, conceptualizing citation intensity as a content-composition variable that shapes output quality, user traffic and royalty payments beyond existing display-level constructs.
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics

title: Robustness in foundation models
abstract: Foundation models have transformed artificial intelligence (AI) by providing general-purpose representations that can be adapted to a wide range of tasks and modalities. As these models become increasingly integrated into real-world systems, robustness can no longer be viewed as a single property evaluated at deployment. Instead, robustness emerges throughout the entire lifecycle of a foundation model, from pretraining and adaptation to deployment, monitoring, and human interaction. This survey presents a unified framework for robustness in foundation models based on three complementary paradigms: a priori robustness, which shapes representations during pretraining; a posteriori robustness, which adapts and aligns models after training; and post hoc robustness, which evaluates and safeguards models during deployment. This study introduces primary and secondary robustness as complementary perspectives on the learning problem and uses them to analyze self-supervised learning, transformers, multimodal fusion, task-specific adaptation, alignment, representation editing, red teaming, explainability, and uncertainty quantification. This study further extends robustness beyond technical model properties to include socio-technical deployment factors such as accountability, fairness, privacy, human–AI interaction, and operational adoption. By organizing existing research through a lifecycle perspective, this study shows that robust foundation models arise not from a single technique, but from the interaction of learning objectives, adaptation mechanisms, transparency tools, and governance processes that collectively support reliable and trustworthy deployment.
