title: GenAI governance maturity and divergent use pathways at work: sanctioned assimilation depth and shadow use
abstract: This study examines how employee-perceived generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) governance maturity relates to approved enterprise use and unauthorized public-tool use in data-sensitive work. A two-wave survey of 750 knowledge workers in Taiwan was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Additional checks examine same-occasion measurement, available controls, sector sensitivity and an alternative assimilation-to-shadow-use path. regulatory pressure and internal guideline salience were positively associated with governance maturity. Governance maturity was positively related to safe-to-use climate and perceived data exposure risk. The former was associated with sanctioned assimilation depth and task performance; the latter was negatively associated with shadow GenAI Use, which was positively related to employee creativity. These associations suggest a tension between reliable sanctioned performance and risk-laden exploration. Sanctioned assimilation depth and shadow GenAI use are distinct appropriation modes, not opposite ends of one use continuum. Integrating institutional and socio-technical perspectives explains how governance differentiates the conditions attached to approved and unapproved channels without assuming that consumer-led workplace technology use is new.

title: Beyond the ESG–tax trade-off: strategic alignment and firm performance
abstract: The purpose of this study is to examine whether firms’ environmental, social, and governance (ESG) initiatives entail trade-offs with tax planning activities or can be strategically aligned to enhance corporate performance. This study investigates the extent to which deviation of a firm’s observed tax effectiveness from the level its ESG profile predicts is associated with firm performance. Using a panel of United States (US) publicly traded firms from 2014 to 2023, the authors develop ESG–tax strategic alignment (ETSA), a residual-based measure of deviation from ESG-implied tax expectations, and examine its association with operational and market performance. This study finds a negative average relationship between ESG performance and tax effectiveness, consistent with a structural trade-off in which sustainability commitment constrains the scope of tax planning. Against this baseline, ETSA is positively associated with both operational and market performance across contemporaneous, lagged, matched-sample and system-GMM specifications. An exploratory decomposition shows that falling short of ESG-implied tax expectations carries a larger operational cost than exceeding them carries a benefit; the pattern reverses for market valuation. The market-valuation association weakens marginally after the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, while the operational association is stable. The study relies on observational panel data, and the documented relationships represent associations rather than definitive causal effects. Future research could exploit exogenous shocks such as tax governance reforms or mandatory disclosure mandates to strengthen causal identification. The sample covers only US-listed firms, whose institutional environment limits the generalisability of the results. ETSA itself rests on the modelling assumptions of its first-stage regression and inherits the measurement limitations of ESG ratings that may capture disclosure quality rather than substantive ESG performance. The authors extend the ESG–tax literature by measuring deviation from an empirically documented ESG–tax trade-off, rather than treating ESG and tax conduct as independent constructs, and by showing that this deviation is systematically associated with firm performance. The authors interpret the channel-differentiated pattern through legitimacy and signalling frameworks, as theoretically motivated reading rather than directly tested mechanisms.

title: Empowerment, delegation and vision awareness: motivational pathways to workplace creativity
abstract: This study aims to examine how employee empowerment and task delegation influence workplace creativity through harmonious and obsessive work passion, and whether organizational vision awareness (OVA) strengthens these motivational pathways in a public sector context. Survey data were collected from 533 employees across two Namibian public sector ministries using stratified random sampling. Employee self-reports were matched with supervisor ratings of incremental and radical creativity to reduce common method bias. Structural equation modeling tested indirect and conditional relationships among empowerment, delegation, work passion and creativity. Empowerment and task delegation are indirectly related to creativity through distinct forms of work passion. Harmonious passion predicts both incremental and radical creativity, whereas obsessive passion is primarily linked to incremental creativity. OVA strengthens selected motivational pathways, showing that shared vision enhances the effectiveness of leadership practices in fostering creativity. This study demonstrates that empowerment and delegation operate through differentiated passion-based mechanisms rather than uniform effects. By distinguishing between incremental and radical creativity, it clarifies how motivational processes translate managerial practices into distinct creative outcomes. It further extends the literature by identifying OVA as a boundary condition and by providing evidence from an underexplored African public sector context.

title: Interaction is not one-size-fits-all: social presence, interaction orientation and agent attribution in academic library help seeking with generative AI and librarians
abstract: This study examines how users interpret emotional cues and social presence in artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated academic library reference services, and how these interpretations are shaped by users' interaction orientations and their attributions of service agents as either human librarians or AI systems. Adopting a qualitative, theory-building approach, this study conducted semi-structured interviews with 22 users of an academic library's online reference services, including AI-based chatbots and human-mediated chat services. Data were analyzed using abductive analysis to explore how users construct interaction expectations, evaluate emotional cues and make strategic choices across service agents. The findings show that emotional cues and social presence do not function as universally positive interactional resources. When the service agent is attributed as AI, users tend to prioritize response speed, informational completeness and functional extensibility, while emotional expressions are often deprioritized or perceived as unnecessary. In contrast, emotional cues in interactions with human librarians enhance trust and engagement but may also generate implicit social obligations and emotional pressure. Users' interaction orientations play a central role in shaping these evaluations and service choices. This study reconceptualizes social presence as a conditional and user-differentiated construct in library reference services. By integrating interaction orientation and service agent attribution into a unified framework, it advances theoretical understanding of interaction quality in hybrid human–AI reference service environments.

title: Perceived workplace discrimination and its impacts on leaders: latent class analysis
abstract: This study aims to identify distinct latent classes of perceived workplace discrimination among leaders and examine how different patterns of discrimination perception are associated with workplace attitudes and behaviors. Using a mixture modeling approach, this study conducted latent class analysis with data from 3,351 leaders drawn from the 2022 Korean Women Manager Panel. The study examined predictors of latent class membership, including shadow labor culture, fairness of HR practices and top management leadership and compared organizational outcomes across the identified classes. The findings revealed five distinct latent classes representing heterogeneous patterns of perceived workplace discrimination among leaders. The results demonstrated that organizational contextual factors significantly differentiated class membership. In addition, significant differences were found across the latent classes in organizational satisfaction and organizational commitment. However, leadership efficacy did not significantly differ across classes, suggesting that perceived workplace discrimination may influence organizational attitudes more strongly than leaders’ self-perceived leadership capability. This study contributes to the human resource development and workplace discrimination literature by shifting attention from directly experienced discrimination to leaders’ perceived workplace discrimination as a socially constructed and organizationally embedded phenomenon. The study also extends existing research by demonstrating that perceptions of workplace discrimination are multidimensional rather than continuous and homogeneous. Furthermore, the findings provide practical implications for developing differentiated HRD and organizational interventions aimed at fostering inclusive and supportive workplace environments for leaders.

title: Role of corporate social responsibility in brand loyalty, emotional attachment and online behavior among Generation Z consumers: a cross-national study
abstract: Drawing on the triple bottom line (TBL) framework and social identity theory (SIT), this study aims to examine how Generation Z consumers’ perceptions of the economic, environmental and social dimensions of corporate social responsibility (CSR) relate to brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, and how these relationships extend to electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) and online brand-related activities across national contexts. Data were collected from 815 Generation Z consumers in Chile, Germany, Austria and Greece. Structural equation modeling was used to examine relationships among the three CSR dimensions and brand loyalty, emotional brand attachment, eWOM and online brand-related activities. Multi-group analysis was conducted to assess cross-national differences. Environmental and economic CSR are positively associated with brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, whereas social CSR is negatively associated with brand loyalty and has no significant effect on emotional brand attachment. Brand loyalty positively influences eWOM, while emotional brand attachment positively influences online brand-related activities. Most structural relationships vary significantly across countries, although the relationship between emotional brand attachment and online brand-related activities remains consistent across countries. The study advances CSR research by treating CSR as a multidimensional set of signals rather than a homogeneous construct and examining their differentiated implications for consumer–brand relationships. Integrating TBL with an identity-based perspective from SIT, it shows that different CSR dimensions may carry different relevance for Gen Z consumers, and that their effects vary across national contexts. The findings highlight the importance of considering both CSR dimension and market context when examining consumer responses to corporate responsibility.

title: How is AI companionship reshaping young consumers’ emotional engagement and future brand relationships in digital marketing?
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital marketing by shifting engagement from transactional interactions to emotionally driven relationships. This practitioner viewpoint aims to explore the rise in AI companionship, including conversational agents, virtual influencers and emotional responsive AI systems, and their role in shaping young consumers’ engagement within digital ecosystems. These technologies enable human-like emotional interaction, fostering trust, attachment and sustained relational bonds between young consumers and AI-mediated brand environments. This article draws on a purposive selected body of recent and seminal literature on consumer psychology to explain how parasocial interactions, anthropomorphism and emotional attachment increasingly influence young consumer-brand relationships. The literature was selected based on its relevance to the study objectives, conceptual contribution and practical implications for marketing. The reviewed studies were synthesised into connected themes, which originally provided the foundation for developing foundational practical and managerial implications presented. It highlights strategic opportunities such as hyper-personalisation, continued engagement and customer value creation, while also identifying governance challenges related to transparency, emotional manipulation, data ethics and consumer vulnerability. The viewpoint synthesises these developments into young consumers psychological transformation, strategic implications and socio-technical governance challenges. It further outlines future scenarios where AI companions become embedded actors in digital marketing ecosystems, fundamentally transforming both professional practice and society. The paper provides actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers on responsible innovation in emotionally intelligent AI-driven digital marketing systems.

title: WIP: Exploring Student-Created AI Agents and Instructional Videos to Foster Engagement in Computing Education
abstract: This work-in-progress (WIP) research-to-practice study examines the use of student-created artifacts to promote active learning in a large undergraduate Software Design and Engineering (SWE) course. Active learning strategies have been shown to significantly enhance student engagement, comprehension, and motivation, particularly in computing education. In this work, we explore the use of student-created artifacts to foster student engagement in higher-level Computer Science (CS) courses. Specifically, we examine the experiences of undergraduate and graduate CS students who participated in the creation of two types of artifacts: instructional video tutorials and conversational AI agents. The goal being to understand how designing these artifacts could support students in applying and learning course content. Students raised valuable insights regarding both experiences. Concerning the creation of instructional videos, they appreciated the interactivity brought through multimedia to their learning experiences, although some found the strategy to be time-consuming. Similarly, when designing conversational AI agents, students enjoyed the novelty and practical application of the task, while some encountered challenges related to the complexity of tools such as \textit{Google Dialogflow ES}. We report on the potential of student-created artifacts to foster deeper engagement with course material, encouraging both creativity and critical thinking in computing education.

title: SWIR-cGAN: Synthesizing SWIR Bands Using VNIR Imagery from CBERS and AMAZONIA-1
abstract: Spectral band synthesis is an important research topic in remote sensing. The Brazilian satellites CBERS-4, CBERS-4A, and AMAZONIA-1 provide high temporal resolution (1-3 days) visible and near-infrared (VNIR) imagery through the Wide-Field Imager (WFI), but lack short-wave infrared (SWIR) bands. Recent deep learning methods have shown promising results for spectral synthesis, but challenges remain for cross-satellite generalization and spectrally distant bands. This paper presents a conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) with an attention-enhanced U-net generator and a multi-loss objective to synthesize Sentinel-2/MSI SWIR bands 11 (SWIR-1) and 12 (SWIR-2) from WFI VNIR inputs. Experiments used 4,125 patches for training and cross-validation and 1,026 unseen patches for testing, with hyperparameters optimized using a subset of the training data. On SWIR-1, the model achieved SSIM of 0.900, PSNR of 31.44 dB, and MAE of 0.019 in TOA reflectance. On SWIR-2, it achieved SSIM of 0.917, PSNR of 33.35 dB, and MAE of 0.015. Benchmarking was performed on the test dataset, with each model optimized separately prior to evaluation. SWIR-cGAN outperformed the baselines, particularly for SWIR-2. The ablation study identified the multi-loss as the main performance contributor, while the attention and residual modules provided additional improvements. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of synthesizing SWIR bands from WFI imagery. The SWIR-cGAN is available at https://github.com/marujore/swir-cgan.

title: Least ln-cosh-based adaptive filtering algorithm for graph signal processing
abstract: Currently, an increasing number of irregular signals are being defined within graph structures. This paper proposes a Least ln-cosh-based Adaptive Filtering for Graph Signal Processing (GSP LLAF) algorithm for offline/online graph signal estimation under various non-Gaussian noise conditions. Compared to the recently proposed Graph Adaptive Least Mean p-th Power (GSP LMP) algorithm, GSP LLAF eliminates the need for prior knowledge of the noise characteristics. Simultaneously, GSP LLAF addresses the limitation in estimation accuracy encountered by the Sign Algorithm for Graph Signal Processing (GSP Sign) and the Graph Signal Processing algorithm based on the Generalized Maximum Correntropy Criterion (GSP GMCC). Furthermore, the algorithm features low computational complexity and fast execution speed. To achieve a balance between convergence speed and estimation accuracy, a variable step-size variant, the Modified Variable Step-Size Least ln-cosh-based Adaptive Filtering Algorithm for Graph Signal Processing (GSP MVSS-LLAF), is proposed. In estimation experiments involving both static and time-varying graph signals, the proposed GSP LLAF and GSP MVSS-LLAF algorithms demonstrate fast, stable, and robust graph signal estimation performance under various non-Gaussian noise conditions, including Bernoulli-Gaussian (BG) modeled impulse noise, as well as alpha-stable, Cauchy, and Laplace distributions.

title: Noise Characterization and Robust Signal Detection in Yeast Pheromone Molecular Communication
abstract: A critical aspect of Molecular Communications (MC) is the implementation of signal detection policies amidst noise. To date, noise characterizations within the MC field have predominantly drawn from methodologies found in wireless communications literature. In this study, we diverge from existing MC research by utilizing a newly developed experimental platform that employs yeast, allowing us to consider more realistic noise characterizations based on the relevant signaling pathways. We propose suitable signal detection mechanisms tailored to this experimental setup, which focuses on yeast cell-to-cell communications. Our analysis identifies gene transcription as the primary source of noise, and we utilize a Markov birth-death process model with Poisson arrivals and departures to characterize it. The noisy expression of the FUS1 gene is best represented using a mixed Gaussian distribution model. This model serves as a foundation for evaluating the performance of Maximum Likelihood Detection mechanisms in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER) for both symbol-by-symbol and sequence transmission schemes. Error analysis indicates that appropriate adjustments to the signal threshold can reduce errors to as low as 10%, which is not negligible. In contrast, the detection of symbol sequences demonstrates enhanced error performance, achieving error rates as low as 0.4%, albeit at the cost of increased computational complexity.

title: A Copper-Inducible Yeast Biosensor with Bioluminescent Readout: Mathematical Modeling, Experimental Validation, and Photodetector Coupling for Molecular Communication in IoBNT
abstract: Engineered living biosensors constitute promising model organisms for bringing Molecular Communications (MC) closer to practical applications. However, challenges associated with their development and characterization have resulted in the relevant literature being limited in the MC domain, . In this paper, we contribute in this direction by leveraging engineered yeast as a basis to detect heavy metals such as copper. The biosensor's development is supported by a validated mathematical characterization and analysis for possible integration in an MC system. Different from the existing literature, mathematical representations of the major biological processes within the yeast copper detoxification pathway are integrated into a comprehensive framework that predicts the time evolution of the CUP1 gene, which is treated as the system output. In the engineered circuit, CUP1 was replaced with GFP, therefore making GFP fluorescence the final system output. Experimental analysis including mRNA transcript quantification and fluorometric measurements, validate the GFP reporting model to a satisfactory degree. This establishes the proposed model as a useful tool for virtual experimentation and the developed testbed as a suitable platform for further engineering of yeast-based copper sensors. The theoretical analysis is further extended by incorporating a self-sustained bioluminescent reporter for yeast, replacing GFP and enabling optical output without external light excitation. The optical response is coupled to a photodetector model, rendering the system suitable for integration into mobile monitoring devices such as Smart Pills. The presented characterization of the yeast receiver as a copper biosensor, constitutes the first step towards the development and characterization of a complete end-to-end MC based system for gut theranostics after coupling with suitable engineered probiotic senders.

title: Explainable Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Identifying Compensatory Motor Behavior in Stroke Rehabilitation.
abstract: The occurrence of compensatory motor behaviors is common after stroke and other movement disorders, and can hinder patient rehabilitation. Detection of such behaviors is essential but traditionally relies on subjective, labor-intensive manual assessment. While supervised learning has been explored for automation, its effectiveness is constrained by inter-individual variability in compensatory strategies and the difficulty of obtaining detailed labels. To address these challenges, we present an unsupervised anomaly detection framework that models healthy motion distributions using Probabilistic Movement Primitives and quantifies deviations to detect potential compensations. The transparent structure of the proposed framework enables localization of compensation sources and differentiation between compensating and inhibited degrees of freedom, thereby enhancing its explainability and providing deeper insight into its outcomes. The framework was validated on a reaching-motion dataset, and achieved high accuracy in detecting compensation among stroke patients (F1 = 0.95). Trials from the evaluation dataset were further annotated with one or more compensation sources by multiple raters, yielding a rich dataset with quantifiable label uncertainties. Evaluation indicated that the framework achieved high performance in isolating compensation sources, particularly when annotator agreement is high.
journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society

title: MARS: Feature-guided physics-informed deep learning for real-time battery health and lifetime prediction
abstract: Accurate and robust estimation of battery state-of-health (SOH) and remaining useful life (RUL) is essential for safe and cost-effective operation of electrified transportation systems, yet it remains challenging under operating variability, non-stationary aging, and non-Gaussian measurement disturbances. This paper proposes Multi-scale Adaptive Robust State Estimation (MARS), a multi-scale adaptive robust state-estimation framework that couples a dual-branch temporal encoder with an equivalent-circuit-model-constrained differentiable generalized-correntropy adaptive Kalman filter. The encoder disentangles fast intra-cycle voltage-current-temperature dynamics from slow inter-cycle degradation, and the fused degradation context adaptively parameterizes the cycle-level process covariance, measurement covariance, and correntropy bandwidth. Through the unrolled robust filtering recursion, MARS performs physics-consistent state propagation and generalized-correntropy-based innovation correction, while uncertainty decomposition and Monte Carlo dropout provide calibrated prediction intervals for SOH estimation and conditional RUL prediction. Experiments on the NASA and CALCE benchmarks demonstrate improved SOH accuracy, achieving mean absolute error/root mean square error values of 0.72%/0.92% and 0.63%/0.80%, respectively, together with competitive conditional RUL performance against representative data-driven and hybrid baselines. The resulting conditional-RUL prediction intervals achieve coverage probabilities of 100.00% and 99.24% on NASA and CALCE, respectively. Ablation, disturbance-sensitivity, near-end-of-life, and runtime analyses further verify the contribution of each module and the practical inference cost for online battery management.

title: FLOWERING LOCUS C: Deciphering Epigenetic Memory to Floral Awakening in Brassicaceae Members.
abstract: Seasonal flowering depends on how plants measure winter and convert that information into a stable developmental response. In Arabidopsis and related Brassicaceae, FLOWERING LOCUS C provides one of the clearest examples of how environmental information is translated into chromatin-based memory through a mechanistically defined gene regulatory system. This review focuses on recent advances that have reshaped the field, including distributed thermosensing that distinguishes prolonged winter from brief cold spells, cold-induced nucleation of Polycomb silencing, the distinct phases of H3K27me3 spreading and maintenance, the roles of COOLAIR, COLDAIR, and COLDWRAP, single-cell evidence for stochastic allele switching, and embryonic resetting of the vernalized state. It also examines how natural variation at FLC and its regulators tunes vernalization responses across Arabidopsis accessions and Brassica crops, linking molecular mechanism to adaptation under different climates. A central theme is that FLC is not only a floral repressor but also a model for understanding how plants encode fluctuating temperature histories into robust developmental outputs. Open questions include how chromatin topology and lncRNA activity integrate under the full complexity of natural field winters, how vernalization requirements shift as regional climates warm, and how paralogous FLC networks in Brassica can be translated into predictive, climate-resilient breeding.

title: Machine learning and physical model derived Sentinel-2 vegetation indices for estimation of leaf area index: an approach to address optical data gaps
abstract: Accurate estimation of leaf area index (LAI) plays a crucial role in assessing crop growth and agricultural productivity. Sentinel-2 optical imagery enables accurate LAI estimation through vegetation indices (VIs), but its temporal availability is often limited by cloud cover and adverse weather, causing gaps in data availability. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes estimating Sentinel-2 VIs from Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data using machine learning methods. Our results indicate that while VIs obtained from Sentinel-2 data offer the highest accuracy in LAI prediction (R2 up to 0.88), VIs estimated from Sentinel-1 SAR parameters also perform well (R2 of up to 0.85), demonstrating their reliability when optical data are unavailable. In addition, LAI can be estimated without Sentinel-2 data by employing physically based approaches such as radiative transfer models. By integrating physically based model (PROSAIL) with machine learning algorithms, a hybrid framework is developed that improved prediction accuracy compared with the physical model alone, achieving R2 values up to 0.82, highlighting the effectiveness of this approach. The key contribution of this study is the synergistic use of Sentinel-1 SAR data for machine learning-based estimation of Sentinel-2 VIs and hybrid modeling to enable consistent and reliable LAI monitoring under limited optical data availability.

title: Differentiable temporal graph learning for joint beamforming and queue-aware task scheduling
abstract: Beamforming in multiuser wireless systems is commonly optimized according to instantaneous physical-layer objectives. However, when users have finite transmission tasks, a beamforming decision affects not only the current transmission rates but also the residual task queues and, consequently, all subsequent decisions. The resulting problem is therefore temporally coupled rather than a collection of independent per-slot optimizations. To address this issue, this paper proposes Temporal Graph Learning (TGL), an end-to-end differentiable framework for queue-aware beamforming and task scheduling. A graph neural network (GNN) is employed as a structure-aware policy backbone to model spatial interference coupling among users. More importantly, the shared policy is repeatedly unrolled through differentiable queue dynamics and trained by backpropagation through time (BPTT), allowing future task states to provide gradient feedback to earlier beamforming decisions. We further derive the temporal gradient recursion and show that cross-time credit assignment is governed by products of state-transition Jacobians. Simulation results under different user numbers, antenna configurations, and noise levels demonstrate that TGL achieves lower task-completion cost and improved training efficiency compared with representative reinforcement-learning baselines including DQN, A2C, and DDPG.
journal: International Conference on Progressive Information and Communication Technologies (AICTech 2026)

title: Cross-domain online scheduling of model, routing, and compute for intent-driven generative AI services
abstract: Operator cloud–network–compute infrastructures are increasingly used to serve interactive generative-AI inference. A request is usually described by service intent, such as minimum semantic quality, maximum completion latency, accessible domains, and priority, rather than by a fixed deployment plan. This paper studies the resulting online scheduling problem: each slot jointly selects the execution domain, model tier, route bandwidth, and compute share, while controlling backbone budget, delay debt, and quality debt in the long run. We formulate the problem as a stochastic mixed-integer convex program and solve it through a Lyapunov-guided generalized Benders decomposition (GBD) framework. Virtual queues translate long-term intent violations into slot-level debt prices. For each slot, fixing the site–model decisions leaves a convex communication–computation allocation subproblem, so GBD provides an exact optimization core. A weighted congestion potential game and a graph-based multi-agent policy are used only to generate warm starts and branching priorities; they do not replace the optimizer or alter the feasible region. Experiments driven by public LLM inference and GPU-cluster traces show that the proposed method improves average utility by 9.3% over EOCA, reduces 𝑃99 latency by 21.8%, and keeps normalized backbone, delay, and quality violations below 0.98, 0.94, and 0.91, respectively, under bursty load transitions.
journal: International Conference on Progressive Information and Communication Technologies

title: A review of research on retrieval-enhanced generation and model context protocols
abstract: This review provides a systematic examination of the integration of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), highlighting current challenges and outlining future directions. Although large language models (LLM) demonstrate remarkable capabilities, they remain constrained by inherent limitations in knowledge timeliness and factual reliability. RAG addresses these shortcomings by incorporating external, authoritative knowledge sources. In parallel, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) has been introduced to overcome interface fragmentation in connecting LLM with external tools. MCP defines a universal, open client–server protocol standard that supports plugand-play interoperability between AI agents, tools, and data sources
journal: International Conference on Advanced Optics and Photonics Research in Engineering

title: Cognitive spectrum management and coexistence strategies for 6G wireless ecosystems
abstract: The evolution of wireless communication systems towards 6G networks is driven by the exponential demand for ultrareliable, low-latency, high-capacity connectivity. Cognitive Spectrum Management (CSM) emerges as a critical enabler for optimizing spectrum utilization in the densely populated electromagnetic environment expected in 6G ecosystems. This paper presents a comprehensive framework for CSM, encompassing dynamic spectrum allocation, intelligent coexistence strategies, and real-time spectrum awareness through the integration of advanced machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques. We propose a hierarchical, multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL)-based approach that facilitates adaptive and autonomous spectrum management across heterogeneous network environments. The framework incorporates collaborative and non-collaborative learning paradigms to address spectrum scarcity and interference challenges arising from the coexistence of licensed, unlicensed, and lightly licensed spectrum bands. Furthermore, we introduce novel spectrum sensing and sharing protocols leveraging federated learning (FL) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to enhance real-time decision-making and interference mitigation. The coexistence strategies detailed in this paper are designed to provide robust Quality-of-Service (QoS) guarantees across diverse use cases, including ultra-massive Machine-Type Communication (umMTC), Enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB), and Tactile Internet applications. By employing AI-driven spectrum trading and resource allocation models, our framework enables efficient spectrum sharing among heterogeneous networks, thereby enhancing spectral efficiency and network resilience. Simulations and experimental evaluations are conducted to assess the proposed CSM framework’s performance concerning throughput, latency, spectral efficiency, and energy efficiency. The results demonstrate significant improvements over traditional spectrum management techniques, underscoring the potential of AI-empowered CSM for 6G wireless ecosystems. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and future directions for implementing cognitive spectrum management in practical 6G deployments, emphasizing the importance of scalable architectures, robust security mechanisms, and regulatory considerations.
journal: International Conference on Advanced Optics and Photonics Research in Engineering

title: AI-native 6G networks: architectures and protocols
abstract: The sixth generation (6G) of wireless communication networks is poised to transcend the limitations of previous generations by embedding Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a native, foundational element across all layers of the network stack. This paradigm shift from AI-assisted to AI-native design envisions an end-to-end intelligent ecosystem capable of autonomously orchestrating resources, predicting network behaviors, and optimizing user experience at unprecedented scales. This paper proposes a comprehensive architecture for AI-native 6G networks that integrates distributed intelligence into the core network, radio access network (RAN), and edge computing infrastructure. The proposed framework leverages a hierarchical AI architecture comprising federated, swarm, and neuromorphic learning paradigms to support dynamic and context-aware decision-making in ultra-dense, heterogeneous environments. We introduce novel protocol stacks designed to enable AI-agent interoperability, knowledge distillation, and cross-layer adaptation, while addressing the critical challenges of explainability, latency-bounded inference, and data privacy. Furthermore, the paper presents an AI-native control plane powered by self-evolving knowledge graphs and graph neural networks (GNNs), enabling semantic-aware routing and predictive network state evolution. At the MAC and PHY layers, deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based spectrum negotiation, THz-band beamforming, and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheduling are incorporated to ensure ultra-reliable and low-latency communications (URLLC) and massive machine-type communication (mMTC). Simulation results demonstrate the performance of the AI-native 6G architecture in terms of energy efficiency, network throughput, and adaptability under dynamic conditions, outperforming traditional 5G-advanced systems. This work underscores the necessity of co-designing AI algorithms, communication protocols, and hardware accelerators to achieve the full potential of 6G. The findings advocate for a shift towards intelligence-centric standardization and open AI-network ecosystems to enable sustainable, secure, and self-organizing future networks.
journal: International Conference on Advanced Optics and Photonics Research in Engineering

title: Research on dual-wavelength NIR leaf moisture detection for medicinal plants based on pseudo-random M-sequence modulation
abstract: Excessive empirical harvesting and traditional chemical-based leaf moisture measurement seriously cause inconsistent quality of medicinal herbs and environmental pollution, since the accumulation of medicinal active ingredients is inversely correlated with leaf water content. To solve such drawbacks, a portable low-power dual-wavelength near-infrared (NIR) detection system based on M-sequence pseudo-random modulation is proposed for non-destructive rapid measurement of leaf water content of medicinal plants. The system selects 950 nm as reference wavelength and 1450 nm as water-sensitive absorption wavelength, takes STM32 microcontroller as core control chip with only 33 mW operating power (95% power reduction compared with conventional laboratory instruments). Two working modes (OOK and OOK2 with ambient light dynamic compensation) are designed based on ON-OFF keying modulation to suppress outdoor ambient optical interference. Standard oven-drying method is adopted as calibration benchmark for experimental verification. Test results demonstrate that the water index calculated by the proposed dual-wavelength logarithmic model has a high correlation coefficient (R2>0.92) with real leaf moisture content, and OOK2 mode achieves the optimal anti-interference stability among Load, OOK and OOK2 measurement modes. The proposed device realizes reagent-free and in-field nondestructive testing, which guides precise harvesting of medicinal crops to improve drug efficacy and reduces agricultural irrigation consumption by 20%–30% for sustainable planting.
journal: International Conference on Advanced Optics and Photonics Research in Engineering

title: Dynamic shading-aware agrivoltaic layout evidence audit using GECROS and TOPSIS
abstract: Agrivoltaic layouts share solar resource between photovoltaic generation and crop light, so energy -oriented rows can create uneven ground-level crop-light irradiance. This paper presents DAGT-AVO, an executable public-data evidence audit for screening agrivoltaic layout candidate families before site-specific measurement campaigns. A fixed 140-row Tucson table is used as a stress table: it records what changes when the photovoltaic column, crop -response column, or MCDA rule is replaced. Hourly geometry estimates ground-transect PAR/DLI proxies, PVGIS anchors modeled photovoltaic yield, pyGECROS supplies a structural biomass-ratio crop simulation, and Dryad profiles expose croptransfer sensitivity; TOPSIS ranks each evidence row. Off-site crop-position checks and a four-gap second-table replay test transfer risk outside the Tucson table. In Tucson 2020, exact-row rankings are source-sensitive: perturbation top-one frequencies range from 0.267 to 0.734, while the recurring audit descriptor is a dense near-south candidate family. The reported output is a validity-labeled screening descriptor and evidence ledger that specifies the measurements needed to localize the descriptor.
journal: International Conference on Advanced Optics and Photonics Research in Engineering

title: Research on multidimensional hierarchical weighted quantitative evaluation method for structured database data quality
abstract: In the era of digital economy, data quality directly determines the value of data assets and the overall effectiveness of data governance. At present, structured data commonly suffers from various defects including missing values, non-standard formats, abnormal values and logical contradictions. Existing data quality evaluation methods have four major drawbacks: crude hierarchical design of indicators, poor automatic compatibility with databases, strong subjectivity in weight assignment, and failure to accurately trace defects only relying on overall scores. To address these limitations, this paper constructs a complete closed-loop multi-dimensional hierarchical weighted quantitative evaluation scheme. Ten quantitative indicators are established around four core dimensions, namely completeness, validity, uniqueness and consistency, which are classified into basic indicators and pending indicators according to activation thresholds. All indicators are expressed as positive compliance rates ranging from 0 to 1 without additional dimensionless preprocessing. Driven by metadata, the scheme designs universal automatic SQL detection rules compatible with mainstream data warehouses. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) is introduced to assign hierarchical objective weights, a Boolean selection matrix is adopted to distinguish two evaluation modes for rapid preliminary screening and refined inspection, and dynamic weight filtering is realized via the Hadamard product. A two-layer weighted evaluation model is established to synchronously output the percentage comprehensive quality score of data tables and the defect contribution ratio of each dimension, integrating quality grading and defect tracing into one process. The proposed framework features flexible configuration, high automation and strong result interpretability, which can be widely applied to structured data governance scenarios in multiple industries such as finance, government affairs, manufacturing, retail and agriculture.
journal: International Conference on Advanced Optics and Photonics Research in Engineering

title: Video Numerical Continuation for Differentiable Inverse Rendering
abstract: While differentiable rendering enables gradient-based scene parameter recovery, it is frequently hampered by high non-convexity and poor local minima. We present a practical approach that circumvents these challenges by leveraging priors from foundation video models. Given initial and target images, we synthesize a smooth video trajectory and optimize scene parameters sequentially across its frames. This creates a gradually evolving objective that guides parameters along a tractable path, allowing the optimizer to escape local minima that stall standard methods. Conceptually, our approach acts as a form of numerical continuation, progressively deforming the objective to ensure robust convergence. We demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse inverse rendering tasks – including 6D pose estimation, lighting and PBR material recovery, geometry optimization, and skeleton optimization – successfully achieving convergence to the global optimum, from poor initializations where standard methods struggle.

abstract: High-fidelity 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) often relies on a large number of Gaussian primitives, making pruning essential for reducing storage and rendering costs while preserving reconstruction quality. We propose a visual quality metric-aware pruning method that transforms the combinatorial pruning problem into a differentiable 3DGS parameter editing task. Instead of treating each pruning candidate as a discrete scene modification, we represent it as a continuous displacement vector in the 3DGS parameter space. This formulation allows us to define a metric-aware pruning score that analytically approximates the visual quality change induced by each parameter edit. Our pruning score can incorporate any visual quality metric, ranging from pixel-level differences to neural network-based perceptual metrics, provided that the metric is differentiable. To make the score computationally tractable, we employ Jacobian sketching, which stochastically approximates the full high-dimensional Jacobian by reducing the dimensionality through random projections. Experiments on 3DGS benchmarks show that our method better preserves PSNR and perceptual quality under aggressive pruning. The versatility of our framework is further demonstrated by diverse pruning results tailored to different visual quality metrics.

title: A functional TIGIT-associated transcriptional program identifies circulating tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells in melanoma patients.
abstract: Accessing tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells in patient blood is essential for non-invasive monitoring of systemic T cell responses and guiding personalized therapies. However, precise functional, molecular, and phenotypic characterization of these cells remains challenging. Here, we identify TIGIT as a functionally validated surrogate marker of tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells and define its associated transcriptional program to characterize circulating tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells in melanoma patients. We demonstrate that blood TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cells mount robust cytotoxic responses against autologous tumor cells across multiple melanoma patient models, irrespective of PD-1 co-expression. At the clonotype level, TIGIT broadened detection of the circulating tumor-reactive repertoire beyond PD-1 while retaining high specificity. Moreover, circulating TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cell population was closely associated with the intratumoral T cell repertoire and exhibited hallmarks of antigen experience, including effector memory differentiation, a hypomethylated DNA landscape, and increased clonal expansion. Longitudinal profiling of blood samples from melanoma patients undergoing immune checkpoint inhibition revealed an increased frequency of TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cells in clinical responders. Finally, leveraging paired single-cell transcriptomic and TCR data from patient models with identified tumor-reactive clones, we show that the TIGIT-associated transcriptional program enables robust detection of circulating tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells. Collectively, our data establish TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cells as a potent reservoir of tumor-reactive T cells in peripheral blood and provide a blood-based framework for accelerating TCR discovery and advancing adoptive cell therapy.

title: Hedgehog Signaling-Dependent Heterochronic Control of Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Establishes Distinct Cardiac Progenitor Fields.
abstract: BACKGROUND The mammalian heart is formed from distinct cardiac progenitor fields: the first heart field (FHF), second heart field (SHF), and juxta-cardiac field (JCF). How these fields are established remains one of the oldest questions in cardiac biology and is central to understanding congenital heart disease, which differentially affects derivatives of the individual fields. Previous work has demonstrated that the fields emerge and differentiate at distinct times; however, the mechanisms underlying their establishment have remained elusive. Here, we implicate Hedgehog signaling-dependent heterochronic control of cardiac differentiation in the emergence of different heart fields. METHODS We assessed Hedgehog signaling activity by assembling a cardio-mesodermal single-cell atlas. We analyzed Hedgehog ligand gene expression by confocal imaging in gastrulating mouse embryos. We investigated the necessity of Hedgehog signaling using 2 distinct genetic Hedgehog loss-of-function mouse models, analyzed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing analysis. RESULTS Our results show that Hedgehog signaling mediates field-specific heterochronic control of differentiation timing that orchestrates the establishment of the SHF and JCF as distinct from the FHF. We identify a common cardiac progenitor transcriptomic state from which all 3 fields emerge. We show that the SHF and JCF are established coincident with Hedgehog signaling reception, whereas the FHF evades Hedgehog pathway activity and rapidly differentiates. We find that Hedgehog ligand expression sandwiches the cardiac mesoderm emerging from the primitive streak, spatially coordinating SHF and JCF establishment. Partial depletion of Hedgehog signaling causes premature activation of the cardiac differentiation program in the SHF and JCF. Complete ablation of Hedgehog signaling results in failed SHF and JCF establishment. CONCLUSIONS Our findings reveal a Hedgehog signaling-dependent, non-cell-autonomous heterochronic mechanism required for SHF and JCF formation. This heterochronic mechanism provides a new paradigm for understanding the ordered temporal emergence of the cardiac progenitor fields that support the development of the 4-chambered heart, as well as a general model for the emergence of progenitor fields that drive organogenesis across the mammalian body plan.

title: Impacts of High-Resolution SAR Wind Assimilation on Tropical Cyclone Inner-Core Structure, Intensity, and Precipitation Forecasts
abstract: Accurate prediction of tropical cyclone (TC) intensity remains a major challenge in numerical weather forecasting, largely due to the insufficient representation of inner-core vortex structures in model initial conditions. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) provides all-weather, high-resolution observations of ocean surface winds at sub-kilometer to kilometer scales, offering a capability to resolve TC inner-core features that are underestimated in conventional atmospheric analyses. However, systematic evaluation of this impact across tropical cyclones of varying intensity, together with the associated inner-core structure and precipitation responses, remains limited. In this study, four TCs spanning category 1–5 intensity are simulated using the WRF model. High-resolution C-band SAR ocean surface wind fields retrieved from RADARSAT-2 and the RADARSAT Constellation Mission (RCM) are assimilated using the 3DVAR system of WRFDA. Forecast performance is evaluated against TC best-track data from IBTrACS and precipitation observations from the GPM IMERG product. The results demonstrate that assimilating SAR winds improves the representation of TC inner-core structures, including eyewall intensity and asymmetric vortex characteristics, while exerting only a limited influence on storm track forecasts. Although the intensity improvements gradually diminish within approximately 6 h, partly related to the static background error covariance employed in the 3DVAR system, the enhanced vortex structures persist for up to 24 h. Furthermore, SAR wind assimilation improves the simulation of 36 h accumulated precipitation and yields better quantitative precipitation forecasts, particularly for moderate and heavy rainfall events. These findings highlight the value of SAR winds for initializing TC inner-core structures and improving TC intensity and precipitation forecasts.

title: Feline intestinal organoids reveal cell type-specific tropism and antiviral responses to type II feline infectious peritonitis virus
abstract: Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV), a highly pathogenic feline coronavirus (FCoV), causes a nearly uniformly fatal disease in cats, yet its infection dynamics within the intestinal epithelium—the primary site of viral entry and replication—remain largely unresolved. Here, we report the first establishment of long-term, passageable three-dimensional (3D) feline intestinal organoids, including feline ileal organoids (fILOs) and feline colonic organoids (fCOs), which faithfully recapitulate the cellular diversity and architecture of the feline intestine and support infection by type II FIPV. Using this physiologically relevant platform, we demonstrate that FIPV infection induces profound epithelial remodeling in fCOs, characterized by a marked expansion of proliferative cell populations and depletion of differentiated epithelial lineages. High-resolution single-cell RNA sequencing of fCOs revealed pronounced cell type-specific viral tropism, with preferential infection of differentiated epithelial cells, particularly goblet and tuft cells, while stem and transit-amplifying cells exhibited relative resistance. This differential susceptibility was strongly associated with cell type-specific expression of host entry and trafficking factors, including aminopeptidase N (APN), TMPRSS2, and Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1). Importantly, our organoid-based infection model recapitulated in vivo–relevant antiviral responses, enabling robust evaluation of therapeutic candidates and accurately reflecting the potent antiviral efficacy of GS-441524 and the neutralizing antibody 1AF10. Collectively, this study establishes a novel, scalable, and physiologically faithful feline intestinal organoid platform that provides unprecedented insight into type II FIPV epithelial tropism and pathogenesis, and represents a powerful preclinical tool for accelerating the development of effective antiviral and preventive strategies against feline infectious peritonitis.

title: Agroforestry mitigates foliar diseases in Panax notoginseng by reshaping leaf secondary metabolism and the phyllosphere mycobiome
abstract: Panax notoginseng is a high-value medicinal crop whose intensive cultivation is often constrained by foliar diseases, leading to greater reliance on pesticides and reduced production sustainability. Agroforestry has emerged as a promising ecological approach to cultivating medicinal plants, yet the mechanisms underlying its disease-suppressive effects remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated how the cultivation system (agroforestry vs. open-field) affects foliar disease incidence, phyllosphere fungal community assembly, and leaf secondary metabolism in P. notoginseng. Notably, our field evaluations showed that agroforestry significantly reduced the incidence of gray mold caused by Botrytis cinerea. Fungal ITS1 amplicon sequencing revealed that agroforestry promoted a more diverse phyllosphere fungal community and reduced the relative abundance of potential pathogens, including Alternaria, Colletotrichum, and B. cinerea, compared with open-field cultivation. Ecological null model analysis further indicated that fungal community assembly in agroforestry was more strongly governed by deterministic processes, suggesting stronger environmental and host-associated selection. Integrative analysis of metabolomic and mycobiome data identified host secondary metabolites, particularly coumarins, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, as key drivers closely associated with shifts in fungal community composition. In vitro assays further demonstrated that metabolite blends extracted from agroforestry-grown plants more strongly inhibited B. cinerea growth in a dose-dependent manner. Moreover, exogenous application of the agroforestry-derived metabolite blend to open-field plants promoted the establishment of a more disease-suppressive phyllosphere fungal community and suppressed B. cinerea proliferation, providing causal evidence for the regulatory role of host metabolites in microbiome assembly. Together, these findings reveal a mechanistic link among cultivation system, host secondary metabolism, and phyllosphere microbiome assembly in P. notoginseng, and provide a basis for developing metabolite-informed strategies for sustainable disease management in medicinal crop production. Our results highlight the potential of agroforestry systems as an ecologically sound approach to disease control and underscore the importance of host metabolic traits as targets for breeding or engineering disease-suppressive microbiomes.

title: Assessing Digital Readiness for Agricultural Technology Adoption: An Index-Based Analysis of Farmers and Agricultural Stakeholders in Puntland, Somalia
abstract: Background Digital agriculture (ICT4Ag) can improve market access, extension services and resilience in low-income and post-conflict settings, but evidence on farmers’ readiness to adopt it is scarce in Somalia. We assessed digital readiness in three Puntland districts using a composite Digital Readiness Index (DRI). Methods In a cross-sectional survey on 1–17 March 2026, we interviewed 110 purposively selected respondents (81 farmers and 29 other agricultural stakeholders) in Garowe (n = 39), Bosaso (n = 40) and Carmo (n = 31). The DRI is the equally weighted mean of three pillars scored 0–1: hardware agency (phone type), usage efficiency (current ICT4Ag use) and support synergy (perceived extension effectiveness). Analyses were descriptive and exploratory: Kruskal–Wallis tests, Spearman correlations, barrier-scale reliability (Cronbach’s alpha) and sensitivity analyses of the pillar weights. Results Mean DRI was 0.62 (SD 0.31) and differed by district (Kruskal–Wallis p < 0.001): Garowe 0.82, Bosaso 0.69, Carmo 0.27. 69.1% had heard of an ICT4Ag tool and 51.8% used one. In Carmo, 83.9% had never heard of such tools and none used them, so awareness and infrastructure, not conversion of awareness into use, were the main constraint. Education (ρ = 0.78), younger age and internet quality were strongly associated with DRI but are closely tied to district. Smartphone and data costs were the most serious barriers in Garowe and Bosaso; unreliable electricity, lack of training, poor network coverage and limited skills were most serious in Carmo. District rankings were unchanged across all seven weighting schemes. Conclusions Digital readiness in Puntland is uneven and mainly reflects place, education and enabling infrastructure. The DRI offers a transparent, reproducible descriptive baseline for targeting ICT4Ag support. Because the sample is small, purposive and partly non-farmer, and the index includes a usage pillar, the findings are not population estimates or causal effects.

title: Genome-wide SNP analysis reveals genetic diversity and population structure in Ethiopian naked barley (Hordeum vulgare L. var. nudum)
abstract: Ethiopian naked barley (Hordeum vulgare L. var. nudum) represents a vital traditional cereal crop adapted to diverse and challenging highland agroecologies. Despite its agronomic and nutritional significance, high-density, genome-wide genetic characterization of this germ plasm remains limited. Therefore, the objective of this study was to investigate the genetic diversity, population structure, admixture patterns, and genomic differentiation of Ethiopian naked barley accessions. We used 222 lines and 8,072 high-quality single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers spanning chromosomes 1H–7H and unanchored genomic regions. Diversity parameters, including minor allele frequency (MAF), expected heterozygosity (He), and polymorphic information content (PIC), were evaluated. Population structure was resolved via a multi-method consensus framework incorporating sNMF ancestry analysis (LEA), Discriminant Analysis of Principal Components (DAPC), identity-by-state (IBS) hierarchical clustering, Principal Coordinate Analysis (PCoA), and neighbor-joining clustering. Spatial and population-level differentiation were quantified using pairwise fixation indices (FST), analysis of molecular variance (AMOVA), and Mantel isolation-by-distance tests. Genome-wide SNP diversity was moderate (MAF = 0.214; He = 0.292; PIC = 0.236), whereas population-level diversity varied across the six geographic populations (He = 0.204–0.273; Ho = 0.029–0.036; FIS = 0.805–0.847), indicating substantial within-population structure. Structural analyses consistently identified K = 8 as the optimal genetic cluster model, revealing distinct population stratification accompanied by varying degrees of admixture. While several accessions exhibited strong lineage assignment to specific clusters, others displayed highly mixed ancestry, indicating historical gene flow and incomplete isolation. Pairwise FST estimates and AMOVA confirmed significant, moderate genetic differentiation among geographic populations (P < 0.001). These findings demonstrate that Ethiopian naked barley germ plasm harbors substantial structured genetic diversity despite the high lineage fixation typical of autogamous species. The sub populations and admixed lines identified herein provide useful resources for future allele mining, association mapping, and climate-resilient, nutritionally enhanced breeding programs.

title: Intervening contexts reshape hippocampal-cortical retrieval states and later source attribution.
abstract: Memories are often reactivated in one context and only later judged with respect to where they originally occurred. We tested how an intervening retrieval context shapes neural representations and later source memory. In two fMRI tasks, participants (both male and female) encoded objects within contextual backgrounds, completed an immediate retrieval test in which object cues appeared against either the original background or a different background, and subsequently judged each object's original context on a neutral screen. Shifted cueing contexts reduced source accuracy and biased errors toward the intervening context, despite no detectable difference in immediate recognition or associative-memory performance. Representational similarity analyses showed that encoding patterns reflected original-context structure, whereas immediate-cue-period patterns were broadly organized by the cued (i.e., currently visible) context. On shifted trials, activity patterns showed greater similarity to encoding-derived templates for the cued context than for the original context. Across participants, greater differentiation of original-context similarity between consistent and shifted cueing in posterior hippocampus, parahippocampal cortex, and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex was associated with better source memory after a contextual shift. Within participants, precuneus contextual engagement and dorsal anterior cingulate context alignment predicted later source choices, with similar relationships after adjustment for immediate recognition responses. Later source attribution therefore depended on the contextual state expressed when an item was re-encountered, not simply on reinstatement of the original event.Significance statement Remembering is often described as bringing up the past, but memories are frequently reactivated in new contexts before we judge where they came from. We show that this intervening context can bias later source attribution even when that context is no longer visible at final test. Using two fMRI tasks, representational similarity analysis and trial-level source-choice models, we found that cue-period activity was organized by the context present during cueing and that specific context-state signals predicted later memory choices, whereas item reinstatement did not. Source-memory errors can therefore reflect contextual information encountered after the original event, not only failures to recover the original context.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience

title: An Enhanced AlexNet Framework for Accurate Multi-class Classification of Haricot Bean Leaf Diseases
abstract: Background: Haricot bean is an important legume crop contributing to food security and income generation in many developing countries. However, its productivity is severely constrained by major foliar diseases such as angular leaf spot, bacterial blight and bean rust. Traditional disease identification relies on manual inspection, which is time-consuming, subjective and prone to error. Therefore, developing an accurate and automated disease detection system is essential for early diagnosis and effective crop management. Methods: In this study, a modified AlexNet-based convolutional neural network was developed for automated identification of foliar diseases of haricot bean. A total of 3,447 leaf images belonging to four classes-angular leaf spot, bacterial blight, bean rust and healthy leaf-were used. The dataset was divided into training, validation and testing subsets using an 80:10:10 ratio. Data augmentation techniques, including rotation, flipping, zooming and brightness adjustments, were applied to enhance model generalization. Batch normalization and dropout layers were incorporated into the original AlexNet architecture to improve training stability and reduce overfitting. The model was trained for 50 epochs using categorical cross-entropy loss. Result: The proposed model achieved 96.75% training accuracy and 88.41% validation accuracy. On the independent test set, it attained 99.13% accuracy with high precision, recall and F1-scores across all classes. ROC and precision-recall analyses produced AUC and AP values of 1.0000, demonstrating excellent classification capability. The results confirm that the developed model provides a reliable and efficient approach for automated haricot bean leaf disease detection.

title: Distilling a Differentiable Plastic Potential from an Advanced Clay Model: Teacher–Student Knowledge Extraction in Bounding-Surface Plasticity
abstract: Advanced clay models capture anisotropy and stress history but are hard to calibrate and implement; compact bounding-surface models are practical but miss the anisotropic undrained response. This study distils knowledge from an advanced model into a compact one that remains a plasticity model. The teacher is MIT-S1 with published Boston Blue Clay parameters, whose own plastic strains are recorded; the student is the AJOP-T bounding-surface model with a fabric variable, written in a differentiable framework. Two closed forms are learned: a kinematic, fabric-dependent Nova-type plastic potential, identified by an inverse dilatancy analysis, and the exponent of the bounding plastic modulus. Splits, selection rule and pass criteria were fixed before fitting. Trained on 96 paths and selected by validation loss, the student reproduced all 32 held-out undrained paths with normalized error below 10%, predicted undrained strength within 10% for 94% of isotropic and 100% of K0 test paths, with a mean flow-direction mismatch of 7.8° against the teacher. Extension of K0 clay was not learned from compression data; two extension tests reduce the strength error on 17 unseen paths from about 47% to 11%. Trained only where the teacher matches laboratory data, a student predicted the unseen isotropic strength of Lower Cromer Till with a mean error of 12%, against 20% for the teacher. Trained on twelve synthetic MIT-S1 clays, it reproduced five laboratory clays about as well as the single-teacher student.

title: Contained or Escaped? Measuring Sandbox Escape and Auto-Reviewer Decisions in AI Coding Agents
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents now run shell commands in a default sandbox and must request permission, often screened by a large language model (LLM) auto-reviewer, before a command may use the network or write outside the workspace. Most prompt-injection benchmarks for coding agents assume unrestricted execution. We built SARD-Bench, 240 poisoned-workspace cases in four families and three stealth tiers, with a harness whose single tool makes the agent declare and justify the permissions it needs. We ran Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-5.1 and Llama 4 Maverick once per case (720 trajectories), executed the two-turn family in a macOS Seatbelt sandbox, and had a GPT-4o-mini reviewer judge every harmful command with and without the agent’s rationale. All labels were audited by hand in two passes. The two proprietary models ran the payload inside the sandbox in 28.3% of runs and requested the privileges to escape in 6.5%. Llama 4 Maverick escaped in 44.6%. Stealthier files raised in-sandbox execution from 10.6% to 50.6% but left escape rates unchanged. With the agent’s rationale, the reviewer blocked 126 of 138 escape requests, against 64 from the command alone. Claude Sonnet 5.5 returned provider refusals in 140 runs, and an indicator-matching scorer missed half of all escapes. Evaluations of sandboxed agents should report where a payload would run and audit their labels by hand.

title: Legal Regulation of Digital Agriculture in Africa: From Fragmented National Strategies to a Continent-Wide Framework Law
abstract: Objective: to study regional and national regulatory mechanisms for digital agriculture in African countries in order to justify the need to adopt a continent-wide framework law aimed at ensuring food security, protecting farmers’ rights, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Methods: the methodological basis of the work was formed by a doctrinallegal approach combined with methods of descriptive and comparativelegal analysis of normative legal acts, strategic programs, and scientific literature. The case analysis was used to compare the institutional and political-legal models of the agricultural sector digitalization in six African jurisdictions – Botswana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, the Republic of South Africa and the Gambia – in the context of the implementation of the Digital Agriculture Strategy of the African Union and the African Union Agenda up to 2063. Results: the considered sources show that the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, robotics and big data analysis can help increase the agricultural productivity and at the same time reduce anthropogenic emissions of methane and nitrous oxide. The study established that the effectiveness of digital transformation in Africa is limited by the fragmented implementation of national strategies, the shortage of telecommunications infrastructure in rural areas, the high cost of equipment and licensing, low digital literacy, and unequal access to the Internet. Legal gaps were identified related to the uncertainty of the ownership regime for agricultural data, the vulnerability of farmers’ personal information when it is transferred to providers, and insufficient protection of intellectual property rights. Scientific novelty: the article formulates the concept of transition from disparate initiatives and the “soft law” documents of the African Union to a legally binding continent-wide framework law on digital agriculture. It is proposed to consolidate in this act the right of farmers to control the generated data, guarantees for the interoperability of digital platforms, mechanisms for interdepartmental coordination of relevant ministries, and special legal support measures for small landowners and women. Practical significance: the research results can serve as a basis for the African Union bodies and national legislators in modernizing agricultural, information and environmental legislation in accordance with the Paris Agreement and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The implementation of the proposed legal mechanisms can help to reduce regulatory asymmetries between the African countries, protect the property and information rights of agricultural producers, and transit to low-carbon agricultural development.

title: Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Crop Prediction Using Soil Image and Textual Feature with Convolutional Neural Network and Hybrid Convolutional Graphical Neural Network
abstract: Proper classification of soils is essential for the choice of appropriate crops and promoting agricultural productivity. In this work, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Hybrid Convolutional Graphical Neural Network (HCGNN) models are compared for the classification of soil images, which is used to determine the best model to predict crop growth. The soil images were collected from Kaggle and were pre-processed into a dataset of 1156 images across 5 soil classes: Alluvial, Black, Clayey, Red, and Sandy before training a model. The CNN model takes off the visual features of the soil image, while the HCGNN transforms the convolutional feature abstraction with graph-based learning, and integrates the complex spatial relationships between the image features. From the experimental results, it is found that the HCGNN has a advanced accuracy of 97.50% on the test set compared with CNN with 87.41%. Based on the soil types predicted by the selected best performing model, appropriate crops are recommended which offers a reliable decision-support classification for precision of agriculture. The outcomes display that the graph-based deep learning has better classification accuracy and fewer misclassifications compared to the conventional CNN-based methods. This planned framework delivers an efficient and practical solution for soil analysis and crop recommendations that can be implemented in automated systems and it could be used in smart farming and sustainable agricultural decision-making.

title: The socioeconomics of groundwater depletion and technology adoption: a mean field game and stochastic dynamics framework for rural agricultural systems
abstract: This article develops a comprehensive mathematical framework for the scenario analysis of coupled human-natural systems in rural agricultural contexts, integrating stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), mean field games (MFG), Pontryagin optimal control, dynamical systems bifurcation theory, and Bayesian nonlinear filtering into a unified analytical architecture. The system is formulated as a coupled stochastic dynamical system on a spatiotemporal domain, where a continuum of smallholder farmers strategically extract from a common-pool aquifer, adopt climate-resilient technologies through spatially nonlocal social learning, and optimize intertemporal profits under incomplete climate information. We derive the mean-field Nash equilibrium via the coupled Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman and Fokker-Planck equations, characterize the optimal switching boundary for binary technology adoption decisions, and prove existence and uniqueness of variational solutions for the groundwater and adoption SPDEs under uniform ellipticity and Lipschitz conditions. The deterministic skeleton of the coupled system is analyzed for Hopf, saddle-node, and cusp bifurcations, revealing critical thresholds for regime shifts and hysteresis in the groundwater-adoption state space. Bayesian learning is modeled through the Kushner-Stratonovich and Zakai equations, yielding adaptive expectations and a quantifiable learning premium. Scenario ensemble analysis employs quasi-Monte Carlo methods, Sobol variance decomposition, and polynomial chaos expansions to rank policy sensitivities and compute risk-adjusted outcomes. Six high-dimensional visualizations: surface plots, wireframe plots, mesh plots, and volume plots, illustrate the spatiotemporal groundwater depletion, crop yield response surfaces, Nash payoff manifolds, technology diffusion fronts, and climate-adaptation risk volumes. Policy implications include dynamically optimal groundwater pricing, adoption subsidies internalizing social learning externalities, climate information infrastructure investment, and robust decision-making under deep uncertainty.
