title: Digital agriculture and institutional transferability
Dialogue, Trust and Collective Action: Women’s Empowerment and Grassroots Leadership in Rural Uttarakhand
abstract: Women’s grassroots leadership in Uttarakhand, India is located within a specific context shaped by geographic isolation, climate risk, long-term migration of men from villages and entrenched inequality. This creates opportunity for women to take on greater responsibility in terms of managing mountain agriculture, and therefore also increases the likelihood that these women will be able to assume roles of local leadership. This paper draws upon Kabeer’s concept of empowerment, Habermas’ theory of communicative action, Putnam’s model of social capital and Ostrom’s theory of collective action, to understand the role of dialogue, trust and collective action in shaping women’s grassroots leadership across a range of development contexts. A qualitative-dominant embedded mixed-methods multi-case study was used to investigate four female leaders in Uttarakhand: Radha Bhatt (education); Basanti Devi (conservation); Kamla Pant (advocacy); and Sunita Kashyap (collective enterprise led by women). Life history interviews with the four leaders were conducted between March – June 2026. In addition to these interviews, primary data were also gathered via survey instruments administered to 130 community member respondents. Data analyses included thematic coding; descriptive statistics; and cross case comparative analysis. Results indicate that dialogue can facilitate articulation of common issues and promote community mobilization. Trust emerged as an essential relational resource for developing credibility and maintaining continued involvement. The collective action strategies adopted by each leader differed significantly based upon each leader’s focus on education, environment, rights and economic development. High levels of assessment were provided by respondent communities regarding behaviors exhibited by the leaders and their level of trust in them. However, because ceiling effects may potentially confound evaluation of differences among cases, it cannot be concluded that assessment levels differ. The results of this study argue that women’s grassroots leadership is more than an output of either institutionally based participation or individually empowered individuals. Rather it is a contextually dependent relational process whereby dialogue, trust and collective action serve to enhance the ability of communities to act. The findings contribute to feminist development studies and participatory communication literature, by illustrating the relational foundation of grassroots leadership and its implications for sustainable community development that is led by women.

title: Rutas estratégicas para el café: un análisis desde la gestión del conocimiento de su ecosistema
abstract: Objective: This study analyzes the knowledge and context of the coffee ecosystem to elucidate the most appropriate ecosystem strategy for the development of the sector in Chiapas, Mexico. Methodology: The knowledge management paradigm was used in terms of its context, its conversion Socialization (S), Externalization (E), Combination (C), and Internalization (I)- and assets, combined with structural equation modeling by least squares (PLS-SEM), involving 35 participants from 13 organizations. Results: variances between variables (R²) are indicated in the flow from S to E (0.120); E to C (0.002), and C to I (0.176); while in the PATH, 0.380 from S to E; 0.067 from E to C; and –0.364 from C to I, in the effect of one on the other. Limitations: insufficient sample size, among others. Conclusions: There is a discontinuity between the SE and CI phases, recommending strategies such as taking advantage of the conditions to continue exploiting the crop, developing plantations with resistant varieties; analyzing areas with excellent production and quality that have not been used; productive diversification; obtaining a greater benefit in coffee production, among others, taking advantage of the openness and desire of the producer to learn in the use of technological innovations.

title: Computer Vision-Based Assessment of Environmental Stress and Fungal Pathologies in Aloe vera within the Churu Agro-Climatic Zone
abstract: The hyper-arid and extreme continental climate of the Churu district in western Rajasthan presents severe environmental challenges for succulent medicinal agriculture. Characterized by shifting sand dunes, low precipitation, high solar irradiance, and extreme thermal amplitude ranging from sub-zero winter nights to summer temperatures exceeding 〖48〗^∘ "C" the Churu microclimate subject’s Aloe vera (Ghritkumari) to chronic abiotic stress. These environmental pressures frequently overlap with or predispose the crop to biotic fungal infections, most notably leaf spot (Alternaria alternata) and basal collar rot. Traditional visual scouting methods are labor-intensive, highly subjective, and frequently fail to distinguish between non-pathological physiological adaptations (such as UV-induced anthocyanin reddening and tip desiccation) and early-stage fungal lesions. This paper introduces a specialized computer vision framework tailored explicitly for field-captured imagery of Aloe vera under unconstrained Churu environmental conditions. By integrating deep convolutional neural network (CNN) feature backbones (ResNet-50) with mathematical spatial descriptors—specifically Box-Counting Fractal Dimension (D), Grey-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture attributes, and CIELAB (L^* a^* b*) color space transformations—the model successfully decouples abiotic stress manifestations from necrotic fungal boundaries. Evaluated on an extensive dataset of 4000 field-verified images collected across diverse rural plots in Churu, the proposed hybrid ensemble framework achieved an overall classification accuracy of 95.8%, outperforming standard baseline vision models by over 5.4%. This research provides a robust, automated diagnostic pipeline for precision agriculture and phyto medicinal conservation in desert ecosystems.
journal: International Research Journal of Computer Science

title: Microfluidic design optimization in the era of AI agents
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to optimize design of microfluidic devices by predicting their performance, reducing the number of simulations, and guiding the search for design configurations with improved performances. However, in most studies, the design problem is still defined by the researcher. The device concept, design variables, parameter ranges, objective functions, and constraints are selected in advance, while AI is used to search within these predefined limits. A key limitation of current approaches is that AI is involved only in a specific step of the workflow, performing a narrowly defined task. The emergence of AI agents may change this workflow more fundamentally. AI agents are autonomous systems capable of coordinating computational processes and adapting their behaviour to achieve a defined goal. In other words, in an agentic design workflow, an AI system could interpret an optimization goal, select computational tools, define or modify the design space, run and analyse numerical simulations, and adjust the optimization strategy based on the physical behaviour of the system. This perspective examines how AI agents could extend microfluidic design optimization beyond fixed, researcher-defined search spaces toward adaptive and physics-grounded workflows. We discuss a spectrum of agentic approaches, ranging from LLM-driven conceptual design to agent-supervised numerical optimization, together with evolving role of human supervision and technical challenges associated with reliable implementation. Moving from fixed optimization workflows towards agent-guided design could enable microfluidic systems to be explored more efficiently and may shift design optimization from simple parameter search towards a more adaptive and reasoning-based process.

title: Dual-task graph attention learning for stress-responsive gene regulatory network inference in Panax notoginseng
abstract: Panax notoginseng is an important specialty crop and geo-authentic medicinal plant vulnerable to multiple stresses, with its stress responses regulated by complex gene regulatory networks. Limited species-specific regulatory evidence and sample size make systematic analysis of transcription factor (TF)-target relationships difficult. We developed a dual-task graph attention network (DTGAT) with a shared graph attention encoder and joint optimization of link prediction and expression reconstruction for regulatory relationship prediction. DTGAT was first evaluated in Arabidopsis thaliana for methodological validation. On the independent test set, link prediction achieved an AUC of 0.9106 and an AUPR of 0.8933, while expression reconstruction achieved an R² of 0.8375 and a PCC of 0.9152; link prediction outperformed the evaluated baselines. DTGAT was then applied to transcriptomic data from stressed P. notoginseng together with a homology-mapped prior network, yielding 55,108 high-confidence candidate regulatory edges. Promoter motif analysis further provided sequence-level support for 22 newly predicted candidate regulatory relationships associated with stress responses. Published experimental evidence supported the biological plausibility of the candidate MYB–CCoAOMT relationship. These findings highlight the utility of DTGAT for prioritizing stress-responsive regulatory candidates in non-model medicinal plants.

title: The psychological value of creatorship in the era of generative AI
abstract: While generative artificial intelligence (AI) can quickly produce appealing work, human involvement in creation may still matter to creators themselves, audiences and those who assign credit. This review examines research across creative, communicative and service domains, including art, literature, music, science, marketing and advice. We organize the evidence by evaluator, by the outcome measured and its timing, and by what was compared, including differences in content, in information about how a work was produced, and in the human role of creation. Outcomes include quality ratings, relational experiences such as feeling heard, and felt ownership. Our framework links specific human activities, such as setting intentions, selecting, revising and verifying, to specific goals. The literature shows that in AI-assisted work, human verification matters for trust in accuracy of the work, their personal input for sincerity, and their choices for the feeling of ownership. The strongest evidence concerns origin-information effects, where labeling the same work as human- versus AI-made can change immediate evaluator ratings. In blinded studies, AI-generated texts were rated higher than human-written texts, yet labeling the text as AI-generated lowered its ratings. These effects vary in size, and sometimes in direction, across contexts and measures. Less is known about the long-term effects of AI-use on creators’ motivation, creative identity, and skills. A well-rated result does not reveal the value of a particular human contribution or the consequences of delegating it to AI. Nor is more human involvement automatically better. Choosing to delegate work or selected work tasks to AI can itself express agency. As AI agents become capable of taking on more creative processes, deciding what to delegate may become a central form of human involvement. This review offers a framework for identifying which contributions matter to whom and for what purpose.

title: Asymmetric and dynamic effects of climate variability on crop and livestock production in Somalia
abstract: Climate variability poses escalating risks to agricultural systems in fragile and climate-exposed regions, yet evidence on asymmetric and dynamic production responses remains limited. This study investigates the short-run and long-run effects of climate variability on crop and livestock production in Somalia using annual data for 1989–2021. Crop and livestock production indices from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) are combined with rainfall and temperature data from the Climatic Research Unit (CRU). A nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag (NARDL) framework is applied to examine asymmetric responses to positive and negative climate shocks, complemented by cumulative climate stress indicators and endogenous structural break controls. Structural instability is addressed using endogenous break tests. The results reveal statistically significant short-run asymmetries in the effects of temperature on both agricultural systems. Negative temperature shocks exert larger and more persistent adverse short-run effects than positive temperature changes, with coefficients significant at conventional levels for both crop and livestock production. In contrast, the long-run coefficients are generally statistically insignificant and imprecisely estimated, providing suggestive rather than conclusive evidence of persistent climate effects. Error-correction estimates provide strong evidence of convergence for livestock production, with approximately 45% of disequilibrium corrected annually ( p = 0.008), but only marginal evidence for crop production, for which approximately 30% is corrected annually ( p = 0.097). Baseline linear models overlook short-run nonlinear responses, emphasizing the need for asymmetric frameworks. The Climate Stress Index shows high-stress regimes have increased in both frequency and duration in recent decades. These findings show that short-run climate impacts on Somalia’s agriculture are asymmetric and system-specific: crop production is more sensitive and recovers more slowly than livestock. This underscores the need for climate-responsive policies, including investment in heat-tolerant crop varieties, improved water management, and adaptive support for pastoral systems in fragile environments.

title: Spatial effects and mechanisms of the digital economy’s impact on agricultural carbon emissions
abstract: To explore the spatial effects and mechanisms of the digital economy in promoting low-carbon agricultural transformation, this paper measures digital economy development and agricultural carbon emissions based on panel data for 31 provinces in China from 2011 to 2023, and analyzes their spatial distribution characteristics. Spatial Durbin and mediating models are employed to investigate the effects and mechanisms of the digital economy on agricultural carbon emissions. The results show that both the digital economy and agricultural carbon emissions present a “high-high and low-low” spatial agglomeration pattern, and agricultural carbon emissions have a significant positive spatial spillover effect. The digital economy significantly reduces agricultural carbon emissions in local and neighboring provinces, with obvious regional heterogeneity. In major grain-producing areas, the digital economy only inhibits local agricultural carbon emissions. In non-major grain-producing areas, the digital economy has a weaker effect on local emissions but can reduce carbon emissions in adjacent areas through cross-regional technology diffusion. From 2011 to 2018, agricultural carbon emissions exhibit a spatial clustering pattern, while the digital economy significantly reduces emissions in both the local and neighboring provinces. By contrast, in 2019–2023, agricultural carbon emissions shift toward a spatially competitive pattern: the direct local reduction effect of the digital economy gradually diminishes and becomes statistically insignificant, while its inhibitory effect on neighboring provinces also weakens. Fiscal support for agriculture strengthens the carbon reduction effect of the digital economy, and a higher level of economic development enhances this inhibitory effect. Rural entrepreneurship vitality and agricultural total factor productivity play significant mediating roles in the process of digital economy-driven agricultural carbon emission reduction. The conclusions provide empirical support for strengthening the role of the digital economy in agricultural carbon emission reduction and guidance for improving the policy system of low-carbon agricultural development.

title: Stochastic Optimization and Machine Learning for Intelligent Water Management in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Efficient irrigation-water allocation requires accounting for climatic uncertainty and heterogeneous crop water requirements. This study develops an integrated framework combining machine learning prediction, climatic scenario generation, crop water-balance modeling, and risk-averse stochastic optimization. The framework is evaluated for four municipalities in Hidalgo, Mexico, using historical meteorological and agricultural records. Reference evapotranspiration and precipitation predictions are incorporated into 200 climatic scenarios, which are propagated through crop-specific water-balance calculations to estimate uncertain net irrigation requirements. A static mean–CVaR optimization model determines crop-level water allocations under exploratory water budgets defined relative to simulated mean demand. The objective minimizes expected weighted irrigation deficits and their upper-tail risk, rather than observed monetary losses or irrigation expenditures. Computational results show that the influence of risk aversion depends on the available water budget. Under the adopted production-value-based priority weights, allocations become concentrated in grain barley as water scarcity increases, and the tested risk-aversion settings yield coincident allocations under more restrictive budgets. Supplementary sensitivity analysis indicates that exclusive allocation to barley depends on the adopted crop-priority criterion. The results provide a reproducible, scenario-based framework for comparing risk-aware irrigation-allocation decisions, while remaining conditional on the climatic scenario, crop–demand assumptions, priority weights, and hypothetical water budgets.

title: Constraints and Drivers of Pest and Disease Control Outsourcing Among Chinese Small Farmers from the Perspectives of Transaction Costs and Farmer Trust
abstract: Small farmers’ extensive and inefficient use of pesticides increases the risk of non-point source pollution and ecological degradation, becoming a key bottleneck for the green transformation of agriculture. Agricultural socialized services offer a feasible path for addressing this issue. However, the promotion of outsourcing pest and disease control is slow, and farmers’ response is insufficient, leading to a noticeable gap between policy expectations and actual outcomes. Therefore, it is necessary to clarify the underlying factors. Based on the perspectives of transaction costs and farmer trust, this study used survey data from 552 households and a Logit-ISM model to identify the key factors influencing farmers’ adoption of outsourced pest and disease control services and their hierarchical association structure. The results showed that (1) land fragmentation, technical training, number of operations, perceived yield reduction risk, and difficulty in accessing information were significantly negatively associated with farmers’ adoption of outsourced pest and disease control services, while participation in cooperatives, pest and disease outbreak frequency, social trust, and local service availability were significantly positively associated with outsourced pest and disease control services adoption. (2) Outsourced pest and disease control services followed a three-level association structure of “deep-rooted causes–intermediate transmission–surface-level direct factors,” with farmer trust as the deep root factor and transaction costs as intermediate and surface factors. (3) The hierarchical structure of influencing factors showed three association paths and two direct factors. The association paths indicated that farmer trust was an important foundation for reducing transaction costs and stimulating outsourcing demand. The two direct factors were the inhibitory effect of land fragmentation and the promoting effect of pest and disease outbreak frequency, which together formed the decision boundary under “endowment constraints” and “risk responses.”

title: Date Fruit Sorting: From Classical Vision to Deep Learning
abstract: Date fruit (Phoenix dactylifera L.) is a major economic and food-security crop across arid and semi-arid regions, with global production around 10 million tons annually, led by [yellow]Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Algeria, Iran, and Iraq. Sorting and grading dates by size, color, maturity, and surface quality remains largely manual, slow, costly, and inconsistent between inspectors, motivating automated systems that meet export-quality standards. This review synthesizes the literature on automated date-fruit sorting by methodological family (classical computer vision, rule-based and fuzzy-logic grading, chemometric classification, and deep learning, including multimodal systems fusing RGB, thermal, weight, and spectral data) and categorizes studies by sensing modality, decision method, and sorting target. [yellow]Reported accuracies span roughly 68% to above 99%, but they were obtained on different tasks, datasets, and evaluation protocols and are not directly comparable; most come from small, single-institution datasets, and physical sorting machines with published mechanical detail remain rare relative to algorithm-only studies. Persistent gaps limit real-world adoption: few public benchmark datasets, narrow varietal coverage, near-absent field validation, inconsistent evaluation protocols, and sensing modalities ([yellow]validated inline internal-quality sensing, acoustic firmness, real-time tracking) still minimally explored on dates despite maturity elsewhere. Closing these gaps is essential for moving automated date sorting from laboratory demonstrations to industry-wide use.

title: MELD-YOLO: A Lightweight Edge-Deployable Model for Maize Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: Maize leaf diseases can reduce crop yield and quality, making timely detection important. However, existing detectors still face trade-offs between detection accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly when further reducing model complexity for edge deployment. MELD-YOLO is developed as a lightweight detector based on YOLO26n. The backbone convolutions are replaced with GhostConv to reduce computational cost, and the parameter-free SimAM module is introduced to enhance disease-related feature responses. Feature Channel Reconfiguration (FCR) adjusts channel widths for maize leaf disease detection. Layer-adaptive magnitude-based pruning (LAMP) then compresses the model, while feature-based distillation during fine-tuning recovers the lost accuracy. Using the Corn Leaf Diseases dataset, MELD-YOLO achieves 98.5% mAP@50 and 91.3% mAP@50-95 with 0.875 M parameters and 2.0 GFLOPs, with 63.4% fewer parameters, 61.5% less computation and a 2.4-point gain in mAP@50-95 over YOLO26n. Pruning and distillation then reduce the model to 0.505 M parameters and 1.5 GFLOPs while retaining 90.4% mAP@50-95. After quantisation, the model achieves 12.38 FPS with 81.05 ms latency and a 0.65 MB model size when running on the Raspberry Pi 5B, compared with 4.19 FPS before quantisation. These results support real-time maize leaf disease detection on resource-constrained edge devices.

title: Low-Cost Alternative for Monitoring Soil Erosion Based on UAV Imagery
abstract: Soil erosion is a major driver of land degradation in tropical agricultural systems, yet repeated field-scale monitoring remains constrained by the cost and operational complexity of conventional surveying techniques. This study evaluated the feasibility of using a consumer-grade, non-RTK RGB unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) for monitoring erosion in a sugarcane-producing area in Paraíba, northeastern Brazil. Twelve approximately biweekly surveys were conducted between July and December 2023 using a DJI Mini 2, producing orthomosaics and digital surface models. Eleven campaigns were suitable for quantitative volumetric analysis. The workflow combined multi-temporal co-registration, fixed analysis polygons, and reconstructed reference surfaces. A field comparison was conducted for selected sections of the main road erosion feature (E1), yielding absolute relative differences between manual and photogrammetric estimates of 0.23% to 8.99%. The analysis indicated alternating loss- and gain-dominated intervals in E1, with cumulative pre-intervention volumetric losses of 30.64 m3 and gains of 32.58 m3. A second erosion feature within the sugarcane field (E2), which became visible after harvesting, exhibited an estimated additional net volumetric loss of 20.82 m3 between the final two surveys. These findings support the operational feasibility of repeated field-scale monitoring using a lower-entry-cost UAV platform. However, limited field comparisons and residual geometric uncertainty do not independently establish the accuracy of the multi-temporal volumetric changes or their equivalence to survey-grade RTK-enabled systems.

title: From Decoupling to Mitigation Bottlenecks: Spatiotemporal Dynamics and Projections of China’s Crop Production Carbon Emissions
abstract: China’s efforts to reconcile crop production with decarbonization, as the world’s largest agricultural producer, offer critical lessons for global environmental governance. Using a balanced panel of 31 mainland provincial level regions from 2005 to 2024, we develop an integrated framework combining an input-based carbon inventory, K-means clustering, Tapio decoupling, Gray Relational Analysis (GRA), Kaya-LMDI decomposition, and a Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN). The inventory covers seven input- and operation-related CO2 sources—chemical fertilizer, pesticides, plastic film, diesel, irrigation, tillage, and machinery power—and reports all results in Mt CO2-eq; soil N2O, soil organic carbon changes, rice CH4, straw burning, and livestock remain outside the system boundary. Three main findings emerge: (1) National emissions followed an inverted-U trajectory, rising from 488.99 Mt CO2-eq in 2005 to a peak of 582.08 Mt CO2-eq in 2015 before declining to 531.52 Mt CO2-eq by 2024 (−8.69%), accompanied by pronounced spatial polarization and a shift from weak to strong decoupling after 2016. (2) Fixed-base Kaya-LMDI decomposition (2005–2024) reveals that agricultural energy efficiency was the dominant mitigating component (contributing approximately −604.3 Mt CO2-eq, or 55.9% of gross cumulative mitigation), reinforced by rural labor out-migration (−366.56 Mt CO2-eq, 33.9%) and declining energy carbon intensity (−110.18 Mt CO2-eq, 10.2%), whereas rising land productivity and per-worker cultivation scale exerted dominant upward accounting pressures on emission trajectories. (3) A BPNN scenario emulator using chronological partitioning (training: 2005–2016; validation: 2017–2019; testing: 2020–2024) projects continued decline through 2040 but a marked deceleration after 2035. Given the 20-year national series, this post-2035 plateau is interpreted as a model conditional warning signal of diminishing returns to conventional input reductions rather than a deterministic forecast, underscoring the need for disruptive energy substitution and spatially differentiated governance.

title: Hybrid Architecture of Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks and XGBoost with a Residual Damping Mechanism for Wind Power Forecasting
abstract: The share of wind energy in global electricity generation is rising, driving demand for accurate and interpretable short-term generation forecast models that combine physical consistency with the ability to capture the nonlinear dynamics of meteorological time series. We propose a hybrid architecture: a physics-informed Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN) paired with an XGBoost-based residual corrector and a residual damping mechanism. The KAN core encodes wind turbine operational constraints—such as the Betz limit, power curve monotonicity, and cut-in/cut-out thresholds—via learnable B-spline activation functions on the network edges and structured loss function terms. XGBoost acts as a weak corrector: it learns from the core’s residual errors and relies on exogenous physical features (ERA5 reanalysis, the Jensen/Park wake model, air density, and inter-turbine wake effects), while a damping coefficient regulates its contribution. The evaluation was conducted on 58,496 hourly records from four wind farms. Two different problem formulations can be considered: one that accounts for lags of the output variable, and another where such lags are intentionally excluded from the set of input data. In our study, we compare the proposed model with baseline models XGBoost and LightGBM. The metrics on the test set for excluded lagged values of the target variable are MAE = 1385 kWh and R2 = 0.846 for XGBoost and MAE = 1460 kWh and R2 = 0.842 for the proposed interpretable hybrid model, where the kernel’s contribution was 91.1% and the MAE of the standalone KAN improved by 6–8%. For the alternative problem formulation that incorporates lagged values of the target variable, the proposed hybrid model yielded MAE = 790 kWh and R2 = 0.947, while XGBoost and LightGBM achieved an MAE of approximately 767–770 kWh and R2 = 0.948–0.949 on the same test set. The proposed model offers greater transparency and interpretability, allows for the inclusion of components based on physical principles, while remaining comparable in accuracy to XGBoost or LightGBM models in both problem formulations. Thus, the proposed architecture offers a controlled trade-off between accuracy and interpretability.

title: Forecasting the Fiscal Balance Through the Joint Dynamics of Government Revenue and Expenditure: A European Union Panel Study
abstract: We investigate whether joint revenue–expenditure dynamics and additional macroeconomic information improve one-year-ahead fiscal-balance forecasts. A revised Eurostat panel of 27 present-day EU countries over 2009–2025 is evaluated at 324 country-year targets in 2014–2025, with an extended 1995–2025 panel used to assess training-history sensitivity. Joint pooled VAR(1) yields a balance MAE of 1.626 percentage points of GDP, compared with 1.725 for persistence, 1.727 for separate component autoregressions, and 1.619 for direct balance AR(1). Its gain is concentrated in 2020–2022, and the two-year block-bootstrap interval for its gain includes zero. Component scores show a small expenditure improvement but no revenue improvement over persistence. Training-window ridge selection improves the penalised comparator, while lagged GDP growth, GDP-deflator growth and interest expenditure do not improve matched-sample accuracy. A separate archived-autumn experiment uses information recorded at each forecast origin and spring-after-target outcomes. Adding the European Commission’s contemporaneously available GDP and price outlook reduces direct-model MAE from 1.875 to 1.769; the Commission’s own balance forecast remains more accurate at 1.637. The contribution is a reproducible separation of cross-dynamics, information timing and regime sensitivity, rather than a claim of universal joint-model superiority.

title: Fuel Cell Voltage Degradation Prediction Based on Residual Learning Under Dynamic Operating Conditions
abstract: Predicting voltage degradation at a fixed operating load from proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) subjected to dynamic load cycling is important for durability assessment and maintenance scheduling. This study develops a hierarchical residual forecasting scheme that combines exponential smoothing (ETS), autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), and iTransformer. For every repeated load cycle, the voltage measured at the same predefined load plateau and within-cycle phase is extracted to form a condition-consistent degradation sequence. Pearson-correlation screening retains four synchronous operating variables. ETS first estimates the slowly changing degradation path, ARIMA represents the autocorrelated component of the first residual, and iTransformer forecasts the nonlinear secondary residual with the selected operating information. The three forecasts are then added to obtain the final voltage estimate. The framework is evaluated using a 1000 h dynamic durability dataset from a single PEMFC. Over the held-out interval from 720 to 1000 h, rolling one-step-ahead forecasts yield an RMSE of 1.51 mV, an MAE of 1.12 mV, and an R2 of 0.9759. Relative to the ablated configurations and the compared deep-learning models, the framework follows recovery behavior and nonstationary fluctuations more closely and produces a tighter absolute-error distribution.

title: Cost Sensitivity-Assisted Net Load Forecast Correction for Day-Ahead Scheduling of Wind–Solar–Coal Systems with Molten Salt Storage
abstract: Wind–solar–coal systems require flexible generation and storage operation to accommodate renewable variability while meeting regional demand and scheduled electricity exports. Coordinating coal-fired units with molten salt thermal energy storage can improve renewable integration and operating economy. However, day-ahead schedules depend on uncertain net load forecasts, and higher forecast accuracy does not necessarily yield lower operating costs. This paper proposes a cost sensitivity-assisted forecast correction framework to improve the economic value of net load predictions. Analysis of the scheduling model links forecast errors to asymmetric balancing costs, equipment state changes, and inter-temporal storage constraints. Starting from a temporal convolutional network forecast, the framework learns cost responses to signed forecast perturbations evaluated through the complete scheduling model. These responses supervise action value differences in the critics of a soft actor–critic agent, guiding joint correction of hourly forecasts to minimize realized daily cost. Tests on the Reliability Test System–Grid Modernization Laboratory Consortium benchmark show a 7.47% reduction in mean realized cost relative to the uncorrected temporal forecast, despite higher forecast error. With identical cost sensitivity inputs, auxiliary critic supervision reduces mean cost by 2.01% compared with ordinary critic training.

title: Evidence-Weighted Monte Carlo Forecasting with Qualitative Scorecards: A Simulation Study and Corporate Illustration
abstract: Financial forecasts often combine numerical assumptions with qualitative assessments whose influence remains difficult to audit. Evidence-Weighted Monte Carlo (EWMC) links a five-point scorecard to bounded changes in downside and upside scenario probabilities. The original experiment evaluates six synthetic evidence conditions, eight procedures and 100 replications per condition. Under informative evidence, EWMC reduces the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) from 6.119 to 5.836. Simpler procedures achieve lower errors in several conditions. The revision separates relative source weighting from total support through a strength attenuation rule and evaluates 16 additional stress conditions with 100 replications each. A rolling calibration and suspension procedure reduces reversal CRPS from 6.991 for the original frozen rule to 6.229, compared with 6.156 for the numerical baseline. Under stable informative evidence, the same safeguard increases CRPS from 5.885 to 5.976. An exponential-tilt comparator supplies a restricted relative-entropy benchmark. A retrospective application uses Apple’s dated 2020 revenue guidance, a subsequent management warning and the reported quarterly outcome. The example demonstrates implementation with real disclosures, with no prospective or independent coding validation. The contribution consists of an auditable procedure, explicit safeguards and reproducible failure tests. The results establish conditional computational behaviour. They provide no general evidence of superior corporate cash-flow forecasts.

authors.name: Alessio Faccia

title: Geospatial Approaches for Assessing Climate Variability Impacts on Agricultural Water Productivity and Irrigation Systems: A Systematic Review
abstract: Climate variability is one of the major challenges to sustainable water management in agriculture due to its effects on water availability, crop productivity, and irrigation systems. This review analyzes how geospatial approaches have been used to assess the impacts of climate variability on agricultural water productivity and irrigation systems. Following the PRISMA guidelines, a search conducted on 10 April 2026, identified 706 records in Scopus and Web of Science, resulting in a final review corpus of 398 publications that were examined through bibliometric and qualitative content analyses. Two major thematic clusters were identified: (i) geospatial and methodological approaches and (ii) climate variability and its impacts on agricultural and irrigation systems. The findings reveal a transition from descriptive monitoring toward predictive and integrated methodologies combining remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), agro-hydrological modeling, machine learning, and cloud computing. Evapotranspiration (ET) emerged as a key link between climate variability, water availability, and Crop Water Productivity (CWP), while Water Use Efficiency (WUE) and water productivity remain central indicators of agricultural sustainability. Persistent challenges include methodological standardization, validation, interoperability, and the integration of climatic, hydrological, agricultural, and socioeconomic information. Overall, integrating geospatial technologies with predictive modeling offers a promising pathway for strengthening adaptive water management, increasing irrigation-system resilience, and promoting sustainable agricultural water use under increasing climate variability.

title: Phenotypic Diversity, PCR Markers, and Inheritance of Resistance to the Causal Agent of Stem Rust in Spring and Winter Hexaploid Triticale
abstract: Stem rust, caused by Puccinia graminis Pers., poses a significant threat to cereal crops, including triticale; however, the genetic basis of stem rust resistance in this crop remains insufficiently studied. In this study, 110 hexaploid triticale genotypes were evaluated for resistance to populations of P. graminis at the seedling and adult plant stages. In addition, PCR screening was performed to identify marker profiles associated with the Sr2, Sr31, Sr50, and Sr1RSAmigo loci, and the inheritance of resistance was analyzed in four F2 populations of triticale. Spring genotypes exhibited resistance to populations of P. graminis f. sp. tritici, whereas winter genotypes exhibited resistance to populations of P. graminis f. sp. secalis (within the tested pathogen set). In most cases, the proportion of resistant plants increased at the adult plant stage, indicating a contribution from age-related resistance. Segregation ratios predominantly consistent with a digenic model were observed in the F2 populations, with a 15:1 ratio. Comparison of marker profiles with phenotypic data showed that the Sr50 and Sr1RSAmigo markers may be informative for selection but do not provide complete predictive accuracy. These results highlight the need to validate resistance markers directly in triticale genetic backgrounds and to combine marker-assisted selection with phenotypic testing against multiple pathogen isolates.

title: False-Positive Scar Control in Scribble-Supervised LGE-CMR Segmentation Using an Asymmetric Intensity Prior
abstract: Background: Scribble-supervised LGE-CMR segmentation can overestimate myocardial scar. Methods: We introduced an asymmetric intensity prior that penalizes predicted scar darker than a scribble-derived reference. We evaluated 36 patient-disjoint test cases using reference myocardium-guided crops and performed separate reference-free central-crop and automatic-myocardial-wall analyses. The main prior-specific comparison matched the 2.5D backbone with and without the prior across three seeds. Results: On the pre-cropped images, mean Dice increased from 0.5328±0.0108 to 0.5472±0.0060, while recall fell from 0.6924 to 0.6399. The predicted-to-reference scar ratio fell from 1.6796±0.1834 to 1.4039±0.1389, and absolute scar-volume error fell from 21.09±5.27 to 14.08±2.47 mL on the common crop grid. However, restriction to the reference myocardial wall increased absolute percent-LV-scar error from 5.55±1.14 to 6.58±0.99 percentage points. With additional healthy-myocardium background points (seed 2022), the matched prior model reduced Pred/GT from 1.5789 to 1.1500 but Dice fell from 0.5441 to 0.5366. With one fixed-rule reference-free central crop and retraining (seed 2022), Dice was 0.4892 without and 0.5047 with the prior. In a paired automatic-wall analysis, the prior did not improve three-seed wall-restricted burden error (6.14 versus 8.16 percentage points). Conclusions: The prior reduced full-output overestimation on the pre-cropped images, but did not improve intramyocardial burden agreement or retain a Dice advantage in the single-seed healthy-background sensitivity analysis. Its effects depend on localization and wall quality and require independent prospective reference-free evaluation.

title: Farmers’ Risk Management Strategies for Climate Change Adaptation in the Nile Delta, Egypt
abstract: Climate change poses profound risks to agriculture, particularly in vulnerable regions such as Egypt’s Nile Delta. This study examines farmers’ adoption of five adaptation strategies—modern irrigation technologies, mixed cropping, intercropping, plasticulture, and planting windbreaks—and explores the socio-economic, institutional, and perceptual factors shaping these decisions. Data were collected from 324 farmers in Kafr El-Sheikh governorate within the Nile Delta and analyzed using a multivariate probit (MVP) model to identify determinants and correlations between the unobserved components of adoption decisions, along with a Poisson regression to assess adoption intensity. Results show that 40.43% of farmers did not adopt any strategy, with windbreaks (10.8%) and intercropping (15.4%) recording the lowest uptake. Perceptions of financial and production risks, higher education, and cooperative membership increased adoption, whereas older farmers and those relying on weather forecasts were less likely to adopt. The econometric analysis indicates positive error term correlations among modern irrigation, mixed cropping, and windbreaks, and a negative correlation between plasticulture and mixed cropping, suggesting potential complementarity and substitutions relationships, respectively. The extent of adopting multiple strategies is positively associated with education and perceptions of production and financial risks, whereas age has a negative effect. These findings align with regional evidence that education, risk perception, and strong institutions encourage climate-smart practices, although market barriers and weak extension services remain major constraints. Policy implications highlight the need to expand credit and insurance access, strengthen cooperatives, and improve extension services to promote integrated adaptation packages.

title: Field Reliability Prediction of Distributed Electromechanical System Components Integrating Regional Clustering and Machine Learning: A Case Study
abstract: Field reliability of components in distributed electromechanical systems exhibits nonlinear, non-stationary patterns across geographic regions, which makes direct prediction difficult. To address this, taking the air-conditioning compressor as an example, a zonal prediction methodology integrating regional clustering and machine learning for the field failure rate is proposed. First, failure mode and effects analysis systematically identifies influencing factors, and a self-organizing map neural network performs regional clustering to yield homogeneous zones. Second, mutual information quantifies correlations between failure rates and influencing factors, identifying key predictors. Third, the discrete wavelet transform decomposes the failure sequence into low-frequency and high-frequency components. The low-frequency part is predicted using the GM(1,1) model based on Fourier series residual correction. For the prediction of high-frequency components, an enhanced rime optimization algorithm incorporating dynamic opposite learning and cyclone foraging is proposed. It optimizes a radial basis function neural network and an extreme learning machine for separate predictions, and a variable-weight projection-resonance method is then used to combine the results. Finally, all component predictions are summed to obtain the final forecast. Applied to the Zhejiang-Jiangsu-Shanghai region in mainland China, the method achieves mean absolute error and root mean square error values of 4.66 × 10−7 and 5.03 × 10−7, respectively, substantially outperforming benchmark models.

title: Multi-Step Stability Selects Sparse Surrogate Models for Economic Greenhouse Climate Control: An in Silico Study of Feature-Library Design and Actuator-Pathway Survival
abstract: Sparse greenhouse surrogates are often selected by prediction accuracy, although their purpose is feedback control. We compare three sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy) libraries and 15 controllers in a GreenLight tomato greenhouse using reanalysis weather. The identification ladder comprises 54 distinct recipes at 20 seeds. Physical features reduce mean one-step temperature root mean square error from 1.86 to 1.68 °C but increase median 24 h error from 2.67 to 23.79 °C; CO2 and humidity show the same reversal. Labelled numerical-completion and planner-cap variants yield a mixed cohort of 1048 full trajectories across four 60-day test seasons. The raw ensemble has the highest reference-setting mean margin (+4.32 EUR m−2), with 4140 climate-corridor variable-steps; the low-threshold intermediate controller achieves +3.07 with 3699, while proximal policy optimisation achieves +0.45 with 1330. Training-selected horizons and price-dependent selection retain the raw ensemble’s largest mean among four principal sparse configurations at all nine prices, without adjusted separation from the nearest comparator at nominal prices. Weather interventions, crop-state continuations and paired coefficient edits assess mechanisms and robustness. The inner model predictive controller predicts climate and resource use, not crop revenue; seasonal margin is evaluated separately. Results support complementary multi-step, interpretability and closed-loop checks within the tested sparse-identification setting.

title: The Past, Present and Possible Future of Thermal Remote Sensing
abstract: The number and diversity of thermal infrared observing systems have grown rapidly. This non-exhaustive review compiles an inventory of 185 named thermal infrared instrument designs spanning 390 historical, operational and planned satellite platform deployments. A status audit identified 83 of these deployments as operational on 18 August 2026. Across this orbital record, the finest reported nominal spatial sampling decreased from 55 km for the Medium Resolution Infrared Radiometer aboard TIROS-2 in 1960 to a provider-reported 3.5 m for the mid-wave infrared imager aboard HotSat-2 in 2026. This reduction of more than four orders of magnitude in nominal spatial sampling does not by itself establish improved effective spatial resolution or radiometric performance. Public continuity missions are now complemented by specialized instruments on the International Space Station, commercial small satellites, aircraft, stratospheric balloons, drones and terrestrial systems. This review links these platform histories to the governing physics of emitted radiation, detector and cooling technologies, calibration, atmospheric effects, emissivity and spatial resolution. It also examines the development from classical machine learning to convolutional, recurrent, transformer, diffusion, foundation and vision–language approaches. The selected examples illustrate different levels of adoption across thermal applications rather than a field-wide measure of uptake. These methods support image interpretation, reconstruction and quantitative retrieval, but model-inferred thermal detail, however visually convincing, is not a direct measurement and must be identified and validated as such. As sensor availability expands, scientific comparability increasingly depends on harmonization, cross-sensor transfer, uncertainty characterization and validation in physical units. We recommend three priorities: (i) open, cross-calibrated thermal archives; (ii) models that preserve the distinct physical meanings of thermal variables; and (iii) validation across sensors, regions and seasons using physical units, independent observations and quantified uncertainty.

title: G3H-GraphSim: A Reproducible 3D GeoHash Cell-Graph Workflow for Semantic LiDAR Analysis
abstract: Reliable infrastructure graph analysis requires transparent links between point-cloud observations, semantic annotations, spatial addresses, and graph decisions. This study evaluates G3H-GraphSim, a reproducible three-dimensional GeoHash cell-graph workflow on five adjacent Gwangju LAS–annotation tiles, using shared-origin metric grids, stage-level computational measurements, and tile-resolved paired routing statistics. Tile-local level-7 cells have unequal physical dimensions and largest-component shares of 26.0–95.1%. In a pooled grid with 4 m × 4 m horizontal cells, six-neighbor largest-component shares are 24.7% at 0.5 m and 26.5% at 1.0 m vertical resolution, showing that common addressing alone does not ensure graph continuity. A noncontemporaneous OpenStreetMap cross-check places 95.3% of retained road-cell centers within 10 m of mapped centerlines, although only 63.5% of selected reference-line length is covered. On the same 150 start–goal pairs, integrated routing reduces pooled mean speed-bump proximity and high-LiDAR-density cell entries by 18.0% and 28.5%, respectively, at a 0.6% increase in mean route length, with appreciable tile-to-tile variation. Stage-level tests show lower amortized batch exact-key lookup time and smaller key-array payload for packed integers than for padded Base32 strings. The results demonstrate traceable sensitivity to spatial resolution, representation, and routing policy, without establishing field-calibrated safety or deployed-system performance.

title: IntentCD: Remote Sensing Change Detection Guided by Implicit User Intent
abstract: Remote sensing change detection (CD) is commonly formulated as pixel-level localization of predefined changes or changes specified by explicit semantic categories. However, practical users often express their requirements indirectly through functional, causal, or consequence-oriented descriptions, creating a semantic gap between natural-language intent and the corresponding spatiotemporal change regions. Our introduces implicit user-intent-guided change detection and proposes IntentCD, an intent-aware multimodal framework that translates indirect user requirements into pixel-level change maps. The key idea is to use a latent change-of-interest representation to bridge intent interpretation and temporal change localization. Specifically, bi-temporal remote sensing images and user instructions are jointly encoded into a multimodal representation, while a pretrained large language model is employed to infer implicit user intent from implicit descriptions. The inferred semantic representation is then used to condition a change-map decoder, which integrates high-level semantic features and multi-scale visual features for pixel-level change localization. Experiments are conducted on the BCDD and SECOND datasets. On BCDD, IntentCD achieves an F1 score of 92.1% for building change detection. In addition, implicit-intent annotations derived from multiple land-cover categories in SECOND are used to evaluate the model under indirect semantic descriptions. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can generate change maps conditioned on both explicit and implicit user requirements while maintaining competitive change detection performance. These findings suggest that incorporating implicit user intent provides a more flexible interface between natural-language requirements and remote sensing change analysis.

title: Sustainability of Agrivoltaic Dual Land Use in the Bajío Region, Mexico: A Techno-Economic, Water-Use and Uncertainty Assessment
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) expansion competes with farmland in the Bajío, a key Mexican agricultural region, creating a food–energy–water trade-off. This simulation study assesses whether an agrivoltaic (AV) system with green chili (Capsicum annuum) in Querétaro can advance sustainable land use, comparing it with conventional PV and open-field chili on the same hectare. Energy was modeled with the System Advisor Model and verified with two alternative models; light under the array was resolved by row position and month, crop water use was estimated with FAO-56, and uncertainty was assessed with Monte Carlo analysis. The system would produce 1286 MWh/ha per year and 78% of open-field chili output, reach a land equivalent ratio of 1.52 (0.52 ha of land saved) and reduce seasonal crop water demand by 27%. At an assumed contract price of USD 0.070/kWh, the net present value is USD 69,500/ha, but the probability of loss is 37%, the value turns negative with taxes, and conventional PV is far more profitable. AV therefore offers measurable land and water benefits for Sustainable Development Goals 2, 6, 7 and 15, but its adoption requires low-cost finance, contract prices above USD 65/MWh, lower structural costs or supportive land-use policy, and field validation.

title: HiFRA-AD: High-Frequency Residual-Aware Sparse Refinement for Unsupervised Industrial Anomaly Detection
abstract: Symmetry and repetitive patterns are common in industrial products, where small defects often disrupt local structural regularity. Fixed-resolution reconstruction can weaken this evidence, while high-resolution cropping changes visual context and anomaly-score distributions. We propose HiFRA-AD, a high-frequency residual-aware sparse refinement framework that couples local feature sensitivity with calibrated evidence aggregation. A fixed-coefficient token-grid residual operator enhances local spatial variation before reconstruction using a frozen DINOv2 encoder. At inference, the global anomaly map selects four peak-suppressed regions for re-evaluation by the shared model. Robust median/quantile alignment and a soft evidence gate convert the local responses into nonnegative residual updates. HiFRA-AD-S achieves P-AP/AUPRO scores of 71.6/95.5, 55.1/96.1, and 46.8/59.8 on MVTec AD, VisA, and MVTec AD 2, respectively. The MVTec AD 2 evaluation uses the official 2045-image TESTpriv partition and AU-PRO@0.30. In backbone-matched MVTec AD comparisons, P-AP improves from 67.5 to 71.6 with ViT-S and from 69.3 to 72.8 with ViT-B. Five paired ViT-S training runs yield a 4.10-point P-AP gain (95% CI [3.95, 4.25]) and a 1.10-point AUPRO gain (95% CI [0.98, 1.22]). With four local regions, ViT-S inference takes 20.8 ms per image on an RTX 4090, compared with 10.0 ms for the global baseline. A defect-subtype analysis records larger paired per-image AP gains for structural disruptions (+4.99 points) than for other anomalies (+2.68 points). These results support selective local refinement for fine-grained industrial anomaly localization.

title: GIS-based drought susceptibility modelling in the Ashanti Region for environmental sustainability management
abstract: Drought is a major environmental hazard affecting agricultural productivity, water availability, and ecosystem stability in many parts of Sub-Saharan Africa. This study evaluates drought susceptibility in the Ashanti Region of Ghana using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and a multi-criteria decision analysis framework based on the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). Seven environmental factors were integrated into the model: temperature, Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), Soil Moisture Index (SMI), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), slope, elevation, and distance to rivers. Spatial datasets were derived from WorldClim climate data (2010–2019), Landsat satellite imagery, Copernicus digital elevation models, and Ghana Lands Commission River datasets. AHP pairwise comparison was used to determine the relative importance of each factor. The derived weights were validated using a consistency test (CR = 0.006), indicating reliable pairwise comparisons. The weighted overlay technique in ArcGIS was applied to produce the final drought susceptibility map. Results show that 2.18% of the Ashanti Region falls within the very high susceptibility class, while 28.98% is classified as highly susceptible. These areas are characterized by high temperatures, low vegetation cover, and reduced soil moisture availability. Model validation was conducted using NDVI drought indicators and historical drought records. The resulting susceptibility map provides valuable information for drought mitigation planning, climate adaptation strategies, and sustainable environmental management in Ghana.

title: An Explainable Agentic AI Framework for Distribution System Load Restoration
abstract: Distribution system load restoration is a sequential decision-making problem in which restoration actions must maximize served load, prioritize critical loads, and preserve power-flow feasibility. This paper proposes an explainable agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for distribution system load restoration. The proposed framework uses multiple large language model (LLM) agents for planner guidance, strategic plan generation, decision arbitration, memory-based feedback, and explanation generation. Unlike unconstrained LLM-based control, the proposed method restricts agent decisions to feasible restoration actions and evaluates all candidate plans using deterministic AC power-flow feasibility checks. The framework is evaluated on IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus distribution feeders, as well as a larger IEEE 118-bus test case, and compared against reinforcement learning and planning baselines. The results show that the proposed agentic framework achieves better restoration performance while producing structured explanations for operator-facing decision support. A direct comparison with a Single-LLM-Agent baseline further shows that the proposed multi-agent decomposition improves weighted restored load and critical-load recovery compared with a monolithic LLM decision structure.

title: Structural functional identifiability of unknown differential equation observation maps
abstract: In many differential equation models of real-world systems, the mechanistic structure of the dynamics is known, but the map from the dynamics to the observations is not. This is potentially problematic, as it can prevent us from e.g. learning model parameter values from data. Examples where this occurs include measuring a fluorescent marker as a proxy for the dynamics of a cellular circuit, and using wastewater measurements to follow the development of an epidemic. The nascent field of hybrid modelling, in which machine learning components (like neural networks) are embedded within mechanistic models, provides the tools to learn such maps. Here, the system's dynamics keep their mechanistic form, while a neural network represents the unknown observation map and is trained alongside any unknown core system parameters. This raises a question of identifiability: when can the true observation map be learnt, and when does one simply learn some map that transforms the dynamics into the available data? Building on previous work, we show how structural functional identifiability analysis can establish whether a model's unknown observation maps and core system parameters are identifiable, i.e. can be uniquely learnt from data. We both prove general results on when models with unknown observation maps are, and are not, identifiable, and demonstrate a general methodology (based on differential algebra) for assessing the identifiability of such models. This paves the way for applying classic differential equation workflows to the many real-world systems that contain such unknown maps.

title: RiDEx: Reward-Informed Directional Exploration for Diffusion Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reward-based diffusion post-training updates model parameters from task rewards. While existing approaches improve sampling and policy optimization, they still rely largely on isotropic random perturbations in a high-dimensional latent space for exploration. Such variation often spends the perturbation budget on changes with little influence on the target reward, making exploration inefficient. We study where diffusion models should explore and how to learn from that exploration. We introduce Reward-Informed Directional Exploration (RiDEx), which concentrates local exploration in reward-relevant subspaces of the denoising velocity field. Conditional residuals or differentiable reward gradients propose the subspace, and equal-and-opposite perturbations at the same generation state measure its terminal reward response. The reward difference supplies signed local supervision in the explored coordinates, while all generated images contribute to global DiffusionNFT learning. RiDEx thereby couples exploration-space selection with feedback about the changes it produces. On Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium, RiDEx attains the highest peak rewards among the evaluated methods on four alignment and preference tasks. Its gradient-direction instantiation achieves 15x and 29x target-attainment speedups over DiffusionNFT on HPSv2 and PickScore, measured in H200 GPU hours. Controlled experiments confirm that reward-aligned directions elicit stronger responses at equal perturbation magnitude, and that applying their measured credit improves curve-average reward across all four tasks.

title: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions
abstract: Tool-using AI agents change files, databases, access rights and public information, yet permission to call a tool does not establish whether a mistake can be undone. We present Reversibility Classes, a declared five-level vocabulary with argument-sensitive rules, conservative defaults and an explicit prior-state capture contract. The pinned implementation and evidence-linked registry cover 536 tools across 20 MCP servers. All 738 rule-case checks conform to declared expectations, while native annotation mapping differs from draft registry labels for 118 of 481 comparable tools. One AI-assisted reviewer approves 148 ratings, 75 matching the registry; this is not independent agreement. On 2,158 recorded runs, the implemented session guard gates the associated action in all 29 attributable attack-positive runs, compared with 18 for a read/write proxy, while adding nine approval points across 1,209 benign runs. Controlled file, Git, SQLite and three-browser experiments show that recovery depends on captured state, later changes, editor storage and recovery route, and expose a Git merge-state exception. The evidence supports making recovery assumptions explicit and testable. It does not establish registry-wide accuracy, reduced production harm or general recovery reliability.

title: ATLAS-Finance: Benchmarking AI Agents in Realistic Banking Environments
abstract: Professional work involves under-specified assignments, where relevant information is spread across workplace applications and may conflict or change over time. To evaluate how well frontier agents can perform economically valuable work in such settings, we introduce ATLAS-Finance, a benchmark of 100 end-to-end investment-banking tasks across 13 simulated firms. As in real banking workflows, agents must search email, chat, calendars, notes, and files to identify requirements, gather information, reconcile conflicts/updates, and then build complex financial models. Tasks were developed by experienced bankers based on their real deal work and take them 15-30 hours to complete. Agent deliverables are evaluated with expert-authored rubrics (median: 124.5 criteria) covering financial rationale and results, spreadsheet construction, completeness, and formatting. Despite completing substantial portions of the requested work, current agents rarely produce correct deliverables. Across today's frontier models, the best ones (Claude Opus and Fable) pass fewer than 11% of tasks.

title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require visual encoders that extract fine-grained visual features while constructing semantically disentangled and discriminative representations. Conventional methodologies encounter a fundamental trade-off: contrastive learning enhances inter-class discrimination by suppressing intra-class variability, whereas generative reconstruction emphasizes perceptual fidelity but lacks explicit comparative supervision. The naive aggregation of these objectives via composite loss functions often induces optimization conflicts and instability due to gradient interference within the shared latent space. To resolve this, we introduce a unified representation-learning paradigm that reformulates generative reconstruction as a discriminative ranking problem within the generative output manifold. Our approach maintains perceptual reconstruction as a supervisory signal and integrates a ranking-based discriminative constraint by systematically ordering matched and mismatched reconstruction outputs. This formulation embeds discriminative information seamlessly into the generative process, alleviating the risk of loss competition. Specifically, we propose AUC Generative Reconstruction (AUCGR), which optimizes the area under the ROC curve (AUC) by ensuring higher scores for matched pairs than for mismatched pairs, and Partial AUC Generative Reconstruction (pAUCGR), which addresses supervision bias by focusing on mismatched comparisons within reliable feature subspaces. The proposed objectives are designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no architectural modifications to existing generative reconstruction frameworks. Theoretical analysis establishes rigorous connections to AUC/pAUC optimization and provides generalization guarantees. Extensive experiments validate that our method advances both discriminative accuracy and fine-grained perceptual representation.

title: DailyBrick: Language-Guided Synthesis of Brick Assembly Instructions
abstract: Generating a LEGO model from a user request is more than a plausible 3D shape generation. LEGO models require physical support per brick, and each brick should be placed unblocked. Current methods address this issue by training an expert large language model. We reduce the problem of generating extremely long context on all brick connections to that of writing a program that builds LEGO models like a human, considering each intermediate step could be executed. We introduce DailyBrick , a multi-stage agentic system that produces a LEGO model together with a brick-by-brick assembly instruction for human building and robot assembly. We design a multi-stage harness with roles to help LLMs generate more effectively. A versioned construction SDK compiles multi-level decisions, from semantic subparts to individual bricks, into canonical operations. An external Meta-Reviewer agent replays and inspects the generated package, verifies the model and its construction process, identifies failures, traces them to the responsible stage, and routes them to bounded repairs or to editable candidates for later skill or tool updates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DailyBrick generates LEGO models based on simple user requests better than recent agentic systems, and show its utility in downstream applications such as robot manipulations on model assembly from instructions and brick sets (https://spatialagentlab.github.io/DailyBrick.github.io/).

title: ReMoE: An Interpretable Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Human Mobility Recovery Forecasting Across Disasters
abstract: Human mobility often declines sharply following disasters and subsequently exhibits complex recovery dynamics. Effective forecasting of this recovery is critical for timely assessment and resource allocation. However, existing approaches are often developed for individual events and operate as black boxes, limiting their transferability and interpretability beyond the events they were trained on. Recent studies have identified recurring post-disaster mobility recovery types across disasters, suggesting that recovery knowledge may be transferable. Motivated by this, we propose ReMoE, an interpretable mixture-of-experts framework for cross-disaster mobility recovery forecasting. ReMoE uses a feature-guided router to adaptively combine specialized experts that learn these heterogeneous yet reusable recovery types, producing a region-specific recovery pattern. It further refines this pattern through residual correction informed by forecasts of future hazard conditions. We evaluate ReMoE on a large-scale mobility dataset covering 18 disaster events spanning hurricanes, floods, winter storms, and wildfires. ReMoE is competitive in-distribution and achieves the strongest performance on unseen events and hazard types, with larger gains under greater distribution shifts. Further analyses show that ReMoE yields interpretable learning outcomes and maintains robust performance under uncertainty. Broadly, ReMoE offers a transferable and traceable forecaster that can support anticipatory post-disaster assessment.

title: Big Brains, Tiny Board: Pupavision, an Agentic Physical AI Instrument for Monitoring Drosophila Pupariation and Lifecycle Transitions
abstract: Many biology experiments are limited by the availability and ease of use of instruments that monitor and record them. For example, the timing of pupariation in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, a widely used model organism, can provide biologically relevant information about growth regulation and is often recorded manually. Here, we present Pupavision, a small physical AI instrument built from a single-board Linux computer and a day/night camera for roughly 45 to 75 US dollars in parts. The key idea is that a frontier coding agent runs its agentic harness directly on the tiny board. The model thinks in the cloud, but the agent works on the device. The agent assists image capture, writes code to repair errors, and checks the experiment every day to keep raw data capture reliable. If recording stops, the researcher gets a ping on their mobile phone. A simple deterministic capture service records one image every ten minutes and never depends on the agent. We report a 26-day pilot in a fly incubator (about 3,580 frames), including eleven days in which the agent was logged out and capture continued, and a 51-hour outage whose cause led to the layered design. A researcher-in-the-loop workflow then produces per-vial pupariation curves by tracing selected pupae backward in time from a late reference frame. Future work will validate the assay for lifecycle tracking accuracy against expert-labeled data and expand real-time computer vision analysis. Pupavision offers a blueprint for do-it-yourself agentic instruments that put frontier intelligence on a tiny board, with deterministic code underneath. We present this as an early case study from a pilot lab deployment and contribute lessons learned toward a future where scientific domain experts are empowered by DIY agentic hardware.

title: AI Agents Executing an RMS and EMT Ride-Through Workflow on a 2,000-Bus Synthetic Texas Grid: A Case Study with Open-Source Tools
abstract: This paper reports a case study of engineer-supervised AI agents executing a predefined RMS and EMT ride-through workflow on the 2,000-bus ACTIVSg2000 synthetic Texas grid with open-source tools. The test case is a 133 MW battery with a co-located 130 MW data-center load, assessed against ride-through criteria fixed before simulation and for loss of synchronism elsewhere in the grid. One agent ran 44 RMS cases and 15 without-project comparisons in ANDES; the other ran a 220-row EMT intake bench and an 84-row system study in DPsim and ParaEMT on a Kron-reduced area. Across the 44 RMS cases, 127 criterion cells fail, including loss of synchronism in all 44. Two findings concern the project plant. The battery keeps absorbing reactive power during sags on the light-load schedule (B3, as low as -19.8 Mvar on S4 T1), and the data-center load returns only at 5.00-5.56 s after long bolted faults (L3), which misses the ERCOT load-return requirement. In 13 of the 15 comparisons, which the authors selected after slips or speed-gate stops, the same machines slip without the project; the other 29 runs have no without-project comparison. RMS and EMT values differ in network, plant model, controls, operating point, and base, and so they are reported as separate, unaligned observations. The paper reports the errors the authors identified in the agent logs, 63 author messages, and 3.8 days from agent start to the integrated study report. The agents executed and documented the predefined ride-through and stability workflow, which covers one part of an interconnection study.

title: Readie: Low-Latency Code Sandboxes for AI Agents
abstract: From quantitative research to personal assistance, AI agents act by iteratively generating and executing code. To decouple the agent harness from code execution, many agents offload execution to dedicated systems called code sandboxes. However, existing code sandboxes suffer from slow startup. Whether they rely on custom snapshots or a single fat image, the root cause is the same: it is hard to build a compact, pre-warmed snapshot that can be shared across diverse agent-generated code while covering nearly all the artifacts (e.g., packages, datasets) it requires. In this work, we propose learned startup snapshots for low-latency code sandboxes. Our insight is that while it is hard for a single snapshot to be both compact and cover most workloads, a set of snapshots can achieve both. Each snapshot is small, initializes quickly, and covers a fraction of agent-generated code; together, the set covers most of it. We learn this set from a large training workload by formulating snapshot construction as an optimization problem and solving it with an approximation algorithm. Planned on 15K public and LLM-synthesized scripts, our system, Readie, reduces startup latency by 3-22$\times$ and end-to-end runtime by 1.3-3.3$\times$ compared to existing approaches at the same storage budget.

title: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
abstract: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density-valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.

title: A Visual Information Extraction System Using Multimodal Large Language Models for Scanned Cognitive and Behavioral Assessments
abstract: Objective. Paper-based assessments are common in patient care, but handwriting and scanning artifacts make these forms difficult to process at scale. This study proposes a modular, multimodal LLM-based system with human oversight for extracting fields and scores. We conducted a qualitative analysis of the use of LLMs for hand-drawing analysis. Materials and Methods. The system processes cognitive assessments (i.e., MMSE, MoCA, Mini-Cog) and the NICHQ Vanderbilt Assessment using two modules: 1) a form classifier that assigns a scanned page to a form type, followed by a corresponding 2) score extractor that extracts fields and scores into a schema. A human-in-the-loop design utilizing dual-model validation engages human annotators when two LLMs disagree, limiting manual review to challenging pages only. Results. End-to-end accuracy for cognitive assessments was 88%, with most form types exceeding 90%. For the NICHQ Vanderbilt, overall accuracy reached 97.5%, with all form types above 96%. The human-in-the-loop design further improved cognitive assessment accuracy to 97.5% while reducing manual work by 63.8%. In the Mini-Cog Clock Drawing task, qualitative analysis showed that 62.3% of all extraction errors stemmed from ambiguous drawing, in which cases the LLM provided reasonable readings. Discussion. Compared to current manual data extraction, our LLM-based system reduces processing time by 10 to 20 times and costs by over 12 times. The modular design allows seamless expansion to additional form types. Conclusion. Our system provides an accurate, scalable, and cost-efficient solution for structuring data trapped in handwritten paper forms for clinical decision support.

title: ST-FateFlow: Continuous Gene-Spatial Reconstruction with Differentiation-Potential Learning from Time-Resolved Spatial Transcriptomics
abstract: Time-resolved spatial transcriptomics provides a powerful view of dynamic biological processes by measuring cellular states together with their spatial organization across time. However, destructive profiling and experimental cost restrict observations to a few discrete time points collected from independent samples, with no known cell pairing across time. This makes it difficult to reconstruct gene expression and tissue organization at unobserved stages and to characterize differentiation-associated dynamics. Here, we introduce ST-FateFlow, a flow-matching framework for continuous gene-spatial dynamics and differentiation-potential learning. ST-FateFlow jointly learns gene-expression and spatial-coordinate velocity fields, enabling interpolation of missing time points and continuous modeling of transcriptional evolution and tissue remodeling. In parallel, it independently learns a time-conditioned differentiation potential, whose values organize cell states along inferred differentiation progressions and support the analysis of differentiation-associated transcriptional changes. Across multiple time-resolved spatial transcriptomics datasets, ST-FateFlow effectively captures coordinated gene-expression and spatial dynamics.
