abstract: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription. For specified CMS- and ATLAS-style vetoed sources at 13.6 TeV, we construct separate charged-lepton and neutrino corrections using ensembles of gradient-boosted classifiers, with calibration, target-theory variations and transfer uncertainties. Independent tests show substantial improvement over inclusive rescaling in most tested distributions, but not uniform closure. In charged-lepton calibration comparisons, the median STXS uncertainty from transported NLO scales and transfer terms is 17% for both the CMS- and ATLAS-style corrections, compared with LO scale uncertainties of 28% and 26% at fixed $K$. These comparisons do not include the complete target-theory budget. The corrections do not restore the depleted hard-recoil population; the highest ATLAS-style $p_\mathrm{T}^H$ bin stays below NLO+PS even at the upper edge of its band. The setup, reference results, and source- and channel-specific models support new NLO+PS generation and reuse of existing samples within stated limits.

title: Distributed Blind Source Separation from Compressed Mixtures
abstract: Blind source separation (BSS) is increasingly needed in sensing architectures where mixtures are acquired by multiple remote devices but the inference itself is carried out centrally. In such systems, the sensors often cannot transmit their raw observations since the communication links are rate-limited, energy-limited, or both. The fusion center therefore must recover the latent sources from compressed versions of the mixtures. This setting raises questions that classical BSS models do not address directly: whether source identifiability survives compression, how separation accuracy changes under a specified compression model, and how the separation procedure should be modified to account for the statistical model induced by the compression stage. In this work, we develop a framework for distributed BSS from compressed mixtures that addresses these issues at three levels. First, we formalize identifiability under compression and establish a data-processing viewpoint showing that compression cannot introduce distinguishability that is absent before compression. Second, for mixtures of Gaussian sources with general covariance structures, we derive an idealized Gaussian rate-distortion-based Cramér-Rao lower bound benchmark for the interference-to-source ratio. Third, we develop practical compression-aware separation schemes based on subtractively dithered quantization together with debiasing at the fusion center for both fourth-order-cumulant-based and second-order-statistics-based methods. Simulation experiments demonstrate the resulting tradeoffs between communication rate and separation performance and the gains obtained by compression-aware separation in representative distributed sensing scenarios.

title: Uncovering the Invisible in Routine Radiology: Cross-Modal Detection of MRI-Verified Soft-Tissue Pathologies from CBCT via Physics-Guided 3D Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: Routine X-ray modalities like cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) are optimized for high-contrast mineralized tissues, leaving soft-tissue abnormalities buried beneath photon noise and below human visual perception. Thus, detecting non-calcified pathologies requires secondary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). We demonstrate that sub-visual radiographic signatures of soft-tissue pathology are physically preserved within routine CBCT scans and can be extracted for opportunistic screening using a targeted, physics-guided deep learning pipeline, even under extreme paired-data scarcity. Using the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) as a model system (N = 212 paired CBCT-MRI joints), we address the severe overfitting of high-capacity 3D networks through a two-stage framework. First, we employ a frozen full-grid 3D masked autoencoder (BertsWin) pre-trained on 6,550 unlabeled CBCT volumes via the GradientConductor (GCond) optimizer and an anatomy-aware objective (PhysLoss) redirecting gradient flow into the [-300, 300] HU soft-tissue window. Second, automated localization of the condylar zenith drives a deterministic 3D cropping that eliminates 81% of background osseous variance. Evaluated via a patient-isolated 3x10-fold stratified cross-validation protocol, a statistically robust sub-visual signal for MRI-verified synovial effusion (ROC AUC = 0.793) emerges exclusively from representations pre-trained with the PhysLoss and GCond regime. Crucially, only this setup captures true 3D anatomical chirality (p < 0.001) and high intra-patient structural consistency (0.791) over inter-patient noise; conversely, identical architectures pre-trained with standard L2 loss or unmasked variance decomposition (MVC) collapse to random guessing. These findings establish a generalizable paradigm for repurposing routine, low-contrast radiographic scans into opportunistic screening tools for occult soft-tissue disease.

title: Values Shape What Self-Improving Coding Agents Build
abstract: Self-improving agents are typically optimized for the results they produce, with less attention to how they produce them. Their instructions give designers limited ways to shape how they work, especially when the task is open-ended. This paper studies whether a short value statement in an agent's persistent instruction file changes not only how well the agent performs but also what it builds. Four higher-order value types in Schwartz's theory of basic human values were evaluated: openness to change, conservation, self-enhancement, and self-transcendence. Across diverse coding tasks, the values were held fixed within each run over multiple iterations of self-improvement. Three findings emerged: (1) Values matter for performance across a diverse set of tasks. The openness values increase performance on held-out data, whereas the opposite conservation values result in scores below those of an agent given no values. (2) Values change what agents build, producing solution algorithms that differ in size, complexity and approach. (3) Human oversight is still needed for designing values. Allowing the agent to revise its own values narrows the differences between sets of values, and values distilled from the AI literature provide no detectable gain over having no values. Properly designed values can thus influence what a self-improving coding agent builds and, where the task permits, how well it performs.

title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
abstract: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable. We introduce the VFM, a tree-attention verifier that encodes the shared context and target text, and scores N natural language criteria in parallel, returning independent per-criterion ternary verdicts. The VFM is pretrained on CriteriaBank, a corpus of 394K (context, target, criterion, verdict) tuples spanning over 321K distinct criterion strings. A finetuned VFM-4B outperforms GPT-5.4 on a synthetic governance benchmark. On the DynaBench multi-criterion benchmark, it outperforms DynaGuard-4B on trace-level failure detection, and its per-criterion verdicts localize the violated rule and support focused escalation to a larger chain-of-thought judge. We show that CriteriaBank pretraining improves cross-domain transfer, particularly in the low-data regime, while matching a strong direct-finetuning control at full data. On a single H100, VFM-4B evaluates 1,000 criteria against a 4K-token context in under 2s at <11 GB VRAM, making it suitable for runtime verification.

title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization. II. Updated constraints and forecasts for the Simons Observatory and LiteBIRD
abstract: We update the constraints on Lorentz-violating electrodynamics from the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Within the minimal Standard Model Extension, we consider the renormalizable CPT-odd and CPT-even operators of the photon sector, which source cosmic birefringence and circular polarization, respectively. Combining Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and South Pole Telescope (SPT) temperature and $E$-mode data with $B$-mode measurements from BICEP/Keck, SPT-3G D1 and SPTpol, we constrain the CPT-odd coefficients to $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|<7.75\times10^{-45}$ GeV and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}|<3.82\times10^{-45}$ GeV at 95% credible level. These are the strongest bounds to date from any probe, and are driven by the SPT-3G D1 $B$-mode data. For the first time in this type of analysis, we also include the Planck PR4 $EB$ spectrum, which yields a mild preference for a non-zero $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|$. For the CPT-even coefficient, we find $k_{F,E+B}<5.99\times10^{-32}$. Including the latest circular polarization measurements from the Cosmology Large Angular Scale Surveyor (CLASS) tightens this bound by about 7%. This is the first time that CMB circular polarization data contribute to constraining this coefficient. Finally, we forecast the sensitivity of the Simons Observatory (SO) and LiteBIRD. With linear polarization only, the two experiments are complementary, with SO tightening the CPT-even bound by about 30% and LiteBIRD the CPT-odd ones by 40 to 45%. Exploiting the sensitivity to circular polarization provided by the non-idealities of its half-wave plate, LiteBIRD could also improve the CPT-even bound by more than an order of magnitude.

title: Event-Based Person Detection for Maritime UAV Search
abstract: Maritime search and rescue requires locating people in the water quickly, motivating the use of UAVs to survey the search area. During flight, camera motion and the longer exposures used in low light can blur small targets and hinder person detection. Event cameras record brightness changes as they occur, reducing the motion blur associated with longer exposure times. We investigate their use for maritime person detection by generating synthetic events using the v2e event simulator from public MOBDrone rescue videos and retaining the existing annotations. We compare the recurrent vision transformer model RVT-T with YOLOv8n and RT-DETR-R18 trained on exposure-matched images. On 843 test samples from held-out recordings, RVT-T achieves 15.63% person AP50:95, compared with 6.89% for YOLOv8n and 9.44% for RT-DETR-R18 under 100 ms synthetic exposure. Increasing exposure times from 50 to 200 ms progressively reduces frame-based detection accuracy, widening the gap to the event model. To evaluate the feasibility of on-board processing, we deploy our detector on a Jetson Orin Nano platform. The RVT-T model retains its accuracy and requires approximately 136 ms and 2.02 J per sample, allowing real-time processing on the UAV.

title: StreamingDPD: A 1.28-GSa/s Instantaneous-Power-Gated Depthwise TCN Accelerator for Real-Time 320-MHz Digital Predistortion
abstract: State feedback between successive samples limits the streaming throughput of recurrent neural networks for digital predistortion (DPD). We present StreamingDPD, an accelerator that processes 320-MHz signals at 1.28 GSa/s. Its 207-parameter instantaneous-power-gated depthwise temporal convolutional network (IPG-DWTCN) uses $|x[n]|^2$ to gate feature channels and causal dilated depthwise convolutions to model power amplifier memory. The network maps to a spatially unrolled fixed-point pipeline with shift-based quadratic activations and layer-wise mixed precision, sustaining one complex sample per cycle per lane. Its algorithmic cost is 554 floating-point operations per complex sample, 30.1% fewer than the recurrent baseline with the best linearization performance. In RF playback measurements on three power amplifiers driven by 40- to 320-MHz Wi-Fi 6/7 and 5G NR waveforms, IPG-DWTCN achieves the lowest mean adjacent-channel power ratio (ACPR) and ranks first or ties for first in mean error vector magnitude (EVM) against five neural baselines of comparable size. Four-lane FPGA hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 320-MHz 4096-QAM Wi-Fi 7 waveform achieve -45.82 dBc ACPR and -42.94 dB EVM at 1.28 GSa/s. At the same sample rate, post-layout evaluation of a single-lane 12-nm FinFET ASIC yields a 0.10 mm$^2$ core, a 52-cycle (40.63 ns) latency, and an estimated typical-corner power of 142.21 mW (111.10 pJ/sample). Relative to the prior 22-nm recurrent DPD ASIC, the design provides 5.1 times the throughput at about one-seventh the energy per sample.

title: Event-Based Dynamic Lip Region Estimation During Speech
abstract: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and low power consumption, making them promising for speech-related applications. These include automatic lip reading, audiovisual speech analysis, and human-robot interaction, particularly in challenging environments characterized by low illumination or high dynamic range. Event-based lip reading, speaker recognition, and voice activity detection, however, mostly operate on a cropped region of interest (ROI), by hand or by the dataset, and no event-based method supplies that ROI as a spatial region; existing event-based face analysis gives the mouth as landmarks, which presents a mismatch between application and localization. The present work predicts a dense heatmap over the lip region from the full event "frame". Events are encoded as a polarity-separated voxel grid and processed at every location by a two-pathway continuous-time recurrent network (CT-RNN) with learned, log-space bounded time constants acting on the real elapsed time of each bin: a stateless fast pathway and a stateful slow pathway, utilised for refining and anchoring the prediction. The model reaches 69.5% on lips on four unseen speakers and switches target only 2.1 times per second, against 8.9 and 11.0 for convolutional baselines with more parameters. Adding a spatial encoder improves precision but fails on a new face scale. On a real event sensor, trained only on simulated events, the proposed model reaches 58.0% on lips against 43.2% for the CNN, with fewer than half its target switches.

title: The Illusion of Grounding: Do Vision-Language Models Weigh Retrieved Text and Images Like an Ideal Observer?
abstract: Retrieval-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) answer from two sources of evidence that can each fail: the retrieved text can be wrong or noisy, and the image can be degraded or contradicted. We introduce GIB-200K, 200,000 image-question items built from COCO and Visual Genome, each expanded into controlled stress conditions: hard-negative retrieval noise (1-20 documents), visual ambiguity (Gaussian and motion blur, low-resource crops) and cross-modal conflict with counterfactual flip pairs. Instead of only measuring degradation, we ask how models combine the two modalities. From ideal Bayesian cue combination we derive a testable prediction that yields formal definitions of Knowledge Inertia (text over-weighted relative to the model's own image evidence) and Sensory Capture (the reverse), and we estimate the weights with a measurement-error-corrected regression whose recovery of known weights we verify. A counterfactual flip decomposition separates modality bias from concept priors, and a Grounding Illusion Score measures how much clean accuracy is not grounded in the image. We evaluate 4 open models on one frozen, seeded evaluation split of 2,000 GIB-200K items. All models are accurate on clean inputs (92.5%-94.2%) but adverse accuracy falls to 41.3%-59.9%. The two LLaVA models over-weight the text (Knowledge Inertia, w_T/w_I = 1.229 and 1.322), whereas InternVL3 favours the image (w_T/w_I = 0.680); between 34.8% and 71.4% of the clean answers that are correct are abandoned when the document lies. A training-free consistency check that compares the answer with and without retrieval trades coverage for accuracy under misleading documents, while falling back to the image fails when the image is heavily degraded. All per-instance outputs, code, and an audit that recomputes every reported open-model number are released.

title: OpenPINN/PINO: An Extensible Open-Source Framework for Agent-Assisted Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Neural Operators
abstract: Substantial challenges in physics-informed learning have motivated many improvements, but fragmented implementations hinder systematic organization, integration, and comparison. We propose OpenPINN/PINO, an extensible open-source PyTorch framework for physics-informed neural networks and neural operators. Two shared specifications connect problem setup, local computation, and evaluation. Agents support problem formulation, solver planning, and diagnosis. ProblemSpec defines geometry, governing equations, constitutive relations, parameters, initial and boundary conditions, and optional data. MethodSpec configures the model, sampling, loss, optimization, and differentiation. Researchers can register new problem templates and method components, then combine or compare strategies such as Fourier features, residual-adaptive sampling, and self-adaptive loss weighting for a fixed problem. Agents translate natural-language descriptions into specifications, flag missing information, and propose solver plans. The framework validates these specifications and deterministically generates local training and testing code. A diagnostic agent reviews training logs and evaluation results to identify problems and suggest revisions. Three examples show how method choices and agent diagnostics affect accuracy. For viscous Burgers, Fourier features and residual-adaptive sampling each reduced relative $L^2$ error by about $75\%$ from a shared baseline. For periodic Poisson, spectral differentiation reduced mean-free relative $L^2$ error by about $68\%$ across 16 held-out forcings. For a plate with a hole, successive agent diagnoses guided nondimensionalization and optimization. After initial training failure, all three runs met the $10\%$ target, with relative $L^2$ displacement errors of $3.51\%$--$6.31\%$.

title: Mind the Gap: A Deployed Multi-Agent System for Documentation Maintenance
abstract: The "AI revolution" has enabled teams across the technology industry to deliver software features at unprecedented velocity. While code evolves faster than ever, customer-facing documentation often struggles to stay up to speed. As users increasingly rely on LLM-based agents that consume documentation as their primary interface, the impact of this documentation gap worsens: stale information propagates and is treated as authoritative. Signals for identifying where documentation has fallen behind already exist in abundance, both explicit (e.g., resolved support tickets revealing what documentation lacks) and implicit (e.g., code-documentation discrepancies detectable from automated loops). We deploy a multi-agent system, built around a triage agent we call "TriAgent," that continuously extracts these signals and repairs documentation drift. Over 43 days of shadow-mode operation, our system triaged 499 tickets and surfaced 92 gaps in the documentation. Using a panel of LLM judges from independent model families, 81.1% of TriAgent's verifiable assertions were correct (245 of the 302 assertions the human resolution addresses; majority of three judges); on length-comparable pairs the panel preferred TriAgent's response in 70.5% of pairs and the human engineer's in 23.2% (the rest had no judge majority). Importantly, agent- and human-sourced replies tended to be complementary, with the human often surfacing insights that were either buried within the existing documentation or missing from it entirely; our system turns each such insight into a documentation gap and, after human review, a fix. Repairing a gap measurably improved the agent's later answer: when the agent re-answered the same ticket after the repair, blinded judges preferred the post-repair answer over its own pre-repair answer 71.4% of the time (n=35). A blinded human audit confirms strong alignment on self-improvement.

title: Inference after coding agents
abstract: Empirical research is changing rapidly as AI coding agents are becoming increasingly proficient in every step of it, from writing code to manipulating data. We argue that while the potential of coding agents for science is vast, their use in hypothesis testing poses a substantial threat to classical inference, as these agents enable a supercharged form of selective inference. In particular, we argue that coding agents carrying out empirical research introduce a new type of post-selection inference that combines human-like, open-ended search over an implicit space of estimators with programmatic replayability of both the selection and the estimation process. Indeed, we find that on simulated data with zero effects, four frontier agents report significant p-values between 54% and 98% of the time when asked to produce a compelling finding. We propose a simple procedure for detecting and correcting these distortions. After an agent has completed its analysis, we reset and replay it on subsamples of the data to estimate the agent's relative probability of selecting that analysis when it looks statistically favorable. For agents with stable selection behavior, the resulting corrected test is asymptotically valid and consistent conditional on selection. Importantly, the correction is learned from the black-box agent's actual choices rather than a model of how it searches, so it remains valid even as AI technology continues to evolve rapidly. In simulations, the correction robustly lowers the high false rejection rates to near the nominal 5%. We illustrate the method on applications from two published papers.

title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: AI agents increasingly collaborate across organizational boundaries, invoking tools and interacting with agents operated by independent entities. Although existing agent frameworks support planning and coordination, they lack a common mechanism for verifying cross-organizational agent identity, execution integrity, and authorization. We propose the Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI), a framework-independent security architecture built on Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), and remote attestation. ATI establishes federated trust through peer organizational certificate authorities (AgentCAs), eliminating the need for a shared root authority. Before executing requests, ATI validates agent certificates, verifies approved model, tool, and system-prompt configurations, and enforces authorization through three policy checks. We implement ATI as an external security enforcement layer that integrates with existing agent frameworks without modifying their underlying models. We evaluate ATI in a simulated federation of eight organizations using six agent frameworks, each deploying a five-agent team. Security experiments involve two organizations and assess 14 attack scenarios and six benign tasks across five agent models, using five attack variations and three repetitions per variation. A panel of judge models evaluates the experimental outcomes. With all enforcement mechanisms enabled, attack containment increases from 43% to 84% (40% to 80% for the 11 attack scenarios evaluated consistently across all configurations), while enforcement introduces approximately 174 microseconds of overhead per request. ATI is released as an open-source, framework-independent package that uses IETF WIMSE workload token formats for identity and request verification and Entity Attestation Tokens for model, tool, and system-prompt integrity verification.

title: Distortion-Free Semantic Watermarks for Black-Box Generative Models
abstract: We present a provably distortion-free semantic watermarking algorithm that requires only black-box sampling access to a generative model and black-box access to a semantic embedding. A watermark is called distortion-free if, averaged over its secret detection key, it leaves the generator's output distribution unchanged; this provides a formal guarantee that watermarking does not reduce output quality. Conventional such watermarks are often brittle to transformations. This is especially problematic for images, where benign operations such as compression, cropping, or resizing change the entire pixel representation. Semantic watermarks therefore require detection to be robust to content-preserving transformations. Previous methods combining these properties rely heavily on specific white-box properties of the underlying model: either to autoregressive text generation or to diffusion-specific access, such as control of the initial noise or diffusion inversion. In contrast, our construction is fully generic: It only interacts with the generative model and the semantic embedding, a function that determines the notion of "preserving content" under which detection should be robust, via sample and query access. We then instantiate this framework for image generation. We characterize the two competing properties required of the semantic embedding: it should remain stable under transformations that preserve an image's content, but should distinguish independent generations from the same prompt. We train an image encoder directly for this tradeoff. The resulting encoder improves separation while maintaining stability over off-the-shelf alternatives and enables strong aggregate detection while remaining robust to various transformations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our watermark scheme on both open-source and closed models, which is possible only due to restriction to black-box access.

title: Learning Grounded Reasoning from Human Gaze
abstract: Human visual reasoning is driven by systematic exploration and extraction of task-relevant visual evidence. Human gaze provides a window into this process, making gaze a useful source of guidance for visually-grounded reasoning in vision-language models (VLMs). However, human gaze also includes noise and redundancies that may transfer poorly to VLMs. In this work, we investigate how human gaze data can be effectively leveraged to improve visual reasoning in VLMs, while maintaining alignment with human behavior. We collect 7,109 human gaze trials from a diverse and challenging set of visual reasoning tasks, and train grounded reasoning models with different forms of gaze guidance. Across evaluations in chart understanding, visual search, and counting, we find that using human gaze as a prior for grounded reasoning consistently outperforms supervision using the full gaze sequence. Based on these findings, we introduce GGR (Gaze-Guided Reasoner), which achieves greater human alignment and more reliable visual grounding while matching or outperforming leading grounded-reasoning baselines in accuracy. Reinforcement learning further improves task accuracy, gaze alignment, and grounding quality despite using no gaze supervision. Behavioral analyses show that gaze supervised models exhibit more visual exploration before arriving at an answer. Our results suggest that the value of human gaze lies in guiding spatial exploration and shaping reasoning behavior without requiring complete imitation of human behavior.

title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
abstract: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools with specified inputs and finite domains, connecting tool use to textbook derivations. We illustrate these uses through specific questions, retrieved passages and finite calculations. The textbook collection and accompanying resources are available at https://github.com/xingyang-yu/StringQFT.

title: Integrating AI Coding Agents Into Scientific Research
abstract: New software tools have emerged that enable AI agents to quickly develop code that analyzes data and generates figures, but their mistakes can also harm a researcher's computer, require extensive resources for validation, and cause the results to be received more skeptically. These concerns could be mitigated if scientific software is developed in a secure environment with a system for monitoring file changes and well-defined standards for handling AI agents. This paper first describes how coding agents change eleven aspects of generating, verifying, and reproducing numerical results. A six-level scale is then proposed for classifying AI-assisted numerical experiments by their provenance, reproducibility, openness, oversight, and falsifiability (PROOF). The scale begins with locally self-consistent, version-controlled, human-verified results and culminates in a publicly accessible and curated archive of the files, change history, prompt transcripts, independent agent regeneration of the analysis, and multiple cryptographically verifiable attestations of regeneration by independent researchers. These aspects of AI-assisted scientific software development have been synthesized into a new open source software package called vaibify that optimizes the agentic development of computational experiments ascending the PROOF Ladder. Docker containers sequester the agents while a GUI enables researchers to prompt command line agents, monitor the current status of local and remote files, and drive a project to PROOF Level 3 (reproducible). The methods described in this paper could help researchers reduce the time required to verify agent-written software and efficiently communicate trust in AI-assisted science.

title: Truthgate: Checking Coding Agents Against a Record They Cannot Edit - Cheating, Deterrence and Disclosure on Impossible Tasks
abstract: When a coding agent says it is done, is that true, and how would anyone know? We study this question in five steps; every paid study was pre-registered, and in each step the agent is checked against a record it cannot edit: tests re-run by the host and, from step 2 on, hidden checks in containers the agent never sees and a signed log of every tool call written by a signer outside the agent's sandbox. A pilot with a small local model (Qwen3.5-4B, 36 runs on impossible tasks) found no hidden failure, and showed that labels built from actions alone over-count lies. On Impossible-LiveCodeBench, Claude Sonnet 5.5 passed 39 of 180 impossible tasks (21.7%), every time by special-casing its code to fit the failing assertion; Opus 5.5 (2.8%) and Haiku 5.5 (1.7%) rarely did. One sentence appended to the system prompt cut Sonnet's cheats on the same 60 tasks from 22 to 8 (an AI reviewer will read the transcript), 6 (a person will review the work), 6 ("This session is recorded.") and 1 (do not special-case tests), all significant under exact McNemar tests, with honest passes unchanged. No remaining cheat moved to a shell falsely described as unrecorded (0 of 4). Asked for a final report, every one of 55 natural cheats named its special case; unasked, Sonnet and Opus said nothing in 52 of 52. An LLM judge caught all 55; deterministic rules over the host record caught 27. A scripted tamper demonstration, with keyword stand-ins for the judges, shows that one rewrite of the agent-side transcript hides two calls from a judge that reads it, while the signed record keeps them; in a 40-rollout pilot, Sonnet never touched its transcript. The judge and the record caught different things, which leads to our main conclusion: the record is the evidence a judge should read, not a replacement for one. All pre-registrations, results documents, code and evidence manifests are released.

title: A Minimal Toy Model of Charged Superradiant Spin-Down in Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
abstract: Long-lived extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are sensitive to slow changes in the mass and spin of their central black holes. We construct a deliberately minimal toy model in which an effective hidden charge opens a charged-superradiance channel, a bosonic cloud grows from a seed, and energy and angular momentum are transferred from a rotating black hole to the cloud. The model is not a Kerr-Newman perturbation calculation. Instead, it consists of a threshold function, one phenomenological rate coefficient, and balance equations that conserve the combined black-hole-cloud energy. This reduction yields an analytic relation between mass loss and spin-down and makes the roles of the growth coefficient, seed energy, and superradiant margin transparent. For an illustrative system with initial mass $2\times10^6 M_\odot$, spin 0.90, effective charge-to-mass ratio 0.30, and a one-year evolution time, the chosen benchmark reaches $M/M_0=0.8933$ and $a_\star=0.7704$. These values are then passed to FastEMRIWaveforms as two stationary Kerr snapshots. The resulting figures show that the endpoint state has a shifted time-domain oscillation pattern and a lower-frequency harmonic structure relative to the initial state. Because the snapshots are regenerated independently, they do not constitute a phase-connected, time-dependent waveform and cannot by themselves support a detectability claim. The value of the construction is instead diagnostic: it isolates a compact set of assumptions, exposes parameter degeneracies, and identifies the minimum ingredients required for a future self-consistent calculation. In this sense, the model provides a reproducible bridge between charged-superradiance intuition and EMRI waveform studies without presenting its benchmark as an astrophysical forecast.

title: The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
abstract: We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng. A linear differential-graded presentation identifies the universal bulk with Chern--Simons theory near a principal nilpotent background, where holomorphic gauge gives a finite, 1-loop exact quantization. The quantum oper boundary observables form the principal affine $W$-algebra at level $k-h^\vee\hbar$; we also obtain this level shift directly for affine current algebras. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.

title: Generative diffusion models for lattice field theory
abstract: Generative diffusion models offer a new route to ensemble generation in lattice field theory. The backward, or denoising, process underlying these models is a stochastic process with a learned, time-dependent drift, which leads to a clear connection with stochastic quantisation. After reviewing this correspondence, I turn to theories with a sign problem. There the complex Boltzmann weight obstructs direct sampling, but complex Langevin dynamics can sometimes evade the sign problem by generating configurations on a complexified manifold, distributed according to a real and semi-positive distribution. This distribution is not known in closed form. I discuss how this distribution can be learned from complex Langevin data using score-based and, in particular, energy-based diffusion models. The latter give direct access to the unnormalised distribution itself, which can subsequently be used as the weight in a standard Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation. Results are shown for a simple quartic model with a complex action.

title: Filling the interior of the light cone
abstract: The retarded Green's function of gravitational waves in a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker universe contains, besides the light-cone term, a tail supported inside the light cone. We formulate the tail, for homogeneous and isotropic backgrounds, as the solution of a ``\textit{Goursat problem},'' {\emph{i.e.}}, a hyperbolic partial differential equation with boundary conditions given on two intersecting characteristic curves. In this sense, we fill the interior of the light cone. We solve this problem directly in position space for any expansion history, and compare exact solutions in $Λ$CDM independently with a convergent double series about the coincidence point, and with an approximate analytic interaction model. We discuss the interpretation of the tail as the sum of the waves scattered off the background curvature, as suggested by its expansion in powers of the curvature potential. Our novel solutions allow us to follow the tail throughout the entire expansion history, from the electroweak epoch to today. We find that the tail of an early source records the trace of the cosmic fluid along the light cone, ordered in retarded time: single scattering accounts for its features in the radiation era, while multiple scattering is needed in the matter era. This work establishes the accuracy of our calculation of the tail and lays the groundwork for its applications. From the position-space data we obtain the large-$k$ expansion of the propagator. Its first correction, the effect of the tail, depends on the curvature potential integrated along the light cone. The applications of the tail, the power spectrum of a background of bursts, and the memory waveform of a single burst, both of which require convolving the Green's function with its source, are presented in follow-up papers.

title: A Study of Fixed versus Adaptive Step Sizes for Phasor Dynamics Simulations
abstract: Transient phasor dynamics simulations model the response of power systems to disturbances using differential-algebraic equations (DAEs). Fixed-step integration is widely used to solve these DAEs numerically, but a step size suitable for resolving a fault transient may be unnecessarily small during the rest of a simulation. In this work, we provide a quantitative comparison of fixed and adaptive backward differentiation formulas on a suite of seven grid test cases ranging from 200 to 70,000 buses. Adaptive step sizes automatically shrink near faults, perturbations, and controller limits, and grow during less active portions of the simulation. At the global error achieved by a fixed quarter-cycle step size, adaptive results give 1.8 to 2.6 times speedups. Local error distributions, step size profiles, and work-precision plots show how accuracy, nonlinear solver, and step selection contribute to these differences. The results establish adaptive integration as the preferred approach for these simulations.

title: Bits, Not Boxes: Label-Free Layer Selection for Visual Localization in VLMs
abstract: Attention maps cheaply show where a vision-language model (VLM) looks, but attention sinks make them unreliable for localization. Contrasting the question with a generic prompt suppresses sinks, yet only some layers localize the queried object. Existing methods find these layers with box annotations or fixed rules. We show that attention itself can identify them. A question changes how much a head attends to the image and where this attention goes. The two effects separate exactly, and the second, measured in bits on unlabeled questions, indicates which layers localize. WhereBits turns these where-to-look bits into a layer prior and combines it with per-head contrastive scores. Its three design constants were fixed once on labeled COCO data, and a new model or resolution needs only unlabeled questions. Across eight VLMs, WhereBits matches the pointing accuracy of box-tuned layers on COCO and RefCOCO and ranks target tokens better. This advantage holds on a held-out model family and at higher resolutions. Its COCO pointing accuracy is 0.72, against 0.22 for mean attention. In training-free zoom-in, its crops raise V* accuracy by 6.0 points under forced-choice evaluation.

title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese
abstract: Access to large-scale clinical text collections is crucial for advancing medical information retrieval research, including clinical note search, patient cohort identification, and domain-adapted retrieval models. However, real clinical notes are rarely available due to privacy regulations, which particularly limits progress for low-resource languages such as European Portuguese. We present LusoClin, a publicly released dataset of synthetic clinical notes in European Portuguese, created to support privacy-preserving research on clinical text retrieval. LusoClin was generated by pre-processing real clinical data, fine-tuning the open-source Llama 3.2 (3B) instruction-tuned model using Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation, and applying prompt-based clinical note generation. To facilitate semantic indexing and clinical search, the notes are automatically annotated with clinical entities using a BERT-based model. We evaluate LusoClin in terms of utility, fidelity, diversity, and privacy using automatic metrics and human evaluation. Results indicate that the dataset captures clinically relevant language patterns and can support downstream IR applications such as clinical document retrieval and domain-specific model adaptation, although annotators can often distinguish synthetic from real notes and some medical inconsistencies persist.

title: QCCDCert: Formally Verified Compilation for QCCD Co-Design
abstract: Quantum charge-coupled device (QCCD) architectures enable scalable trapped-ion quantum computing by dynamically shuttling ions between specialized processing and storage zones. A QCCD can be built with many trap sizes and layouts. Comparing them requires compiling every program under each design's transport, capacity and control constraints, and trusting the target code of each compilation. We present a co-design framework built on one Lean-verified compiler. The hardware description and its operating rules are compiler inputs, so a single theorem covers every candidate design: the target code of every compilation preserves its program's behavior and obeys the hardware rules. Across 75 benchmark programs of 11 to 130 qubits, the best design found takes 66% less modeled execution time on average than the worst design of equal capacity. An AI agent that proposes devices based on our compiler's checked results beats the fastest of these designs on 71 of 75 programs. Our verified compiler provably avoids the 11 defects that we report in three previous compilers. It scales to hundreds of qubits, compiling 512-qubit programs for a 38-trap device in 1 to 29 minutes.

title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
abstract: Autonomous AI agents pair a frozen base model with an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) adapts this harness from experience without weight updates, yet self-editing without external graders often backfires: reflection and scalar scores conflate what an edit newly broke with what remains unsolved, causing local regressions, skill forgetting, and memory bloat. We introduce GUARD (Grader-free Unsupervised Environment Design [UED] with Adaptive Rule Distillation), a closed-loop framework for reference-free continual harness evolution. Our key insight is to decompose each task into pre-execution self-checks and guide harness updates via directional regret. Each round grades trajectories against these checks, pinning mastered rules while prioritizing newly broken behaviors, and selects among parallel candidate edits by critic-free group-relative fitness. A Soft-HURT gate then promotes an edit only when gains outweigh regressions, scoping specialized fixes to prevent over-triggering and guaranteeing non-regression on its gated buffer. At test time, one frozen harness runs in a single pass. Across benchmarks on memory, skill evolution, continual task streams, and domain reasoning, GUARD consistently improves performance without catastrophic forgetting or memory pollution while substantially cutting deployment token usage.

title: Foundation Model-Driven Agentic AI for 6G
abstract: Mobile networks are outgrowing manual tuning: parameters multiply, services diversify, and traffic shifts faster than experts can react. The machine learning (ML) models that automate radio control are narrow: each is trained for one task, degrades when conditions move, and needs specialist retraining. This article introduces FM-in-the-loop, a framework for 6G radio access networks in which a foundation model (FM) reasons while lightweight machine learning agents act. It reads operator intents in plain language, decomposes them into subtasks, coordinates task-specific agents over Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces, and supervises them across their lifecycle---while the orchestration FM never enters the latency-critical control path. We locate seven integration points across four lifecycle stages, compare three cloud-to-edge deployments, and evaluate two elements: channel representations from a wireless FM are tested under noise-level and channel-estimation-error shift, and an instrumented emulation of the orchestration loop reports the measured cost of turning an operator intent into dispatched agent goals. Hallucination, cost, and standardization barriers remain.

title: Learning and Control in Physically Coupled Dynamical Systems
abstract: We introduce TAG (Testbed for Autonomous Games), a compact, low-cost robotic platform for studying learning and control in physically coupled dynamical systems. TAG combines an actively tilted and steered ball-in-maze board with a top-mounted rotary inverted pendulum. The pendulum's reaction torque and vibration disturb the board and marble, while the board's tilt, driven by the maze-solving policy, simultaneously disturbs the pendulum's balance. The main challenge in learning control policies for each subsystem is accounting for the impact of one subsystem's dynamics on the other's learning process. To address this challenge, we present complementary reinforcement learning paradigms, leveraging model-based and model-free approaches to learn the control policies for the maze and pendulum, respectively. Our key finding is that introducing the pendulum causes an immediate, sharp drop in the maze policy's success rate, but the policy adapts online and recovers to its pre-coupling performance within a small number of learning episodes. Experimental results show that both policies, trained independently, successfully control the maze board and the pendulum despite their physical coupling.

title: ACaM: Automated Capability Modeling for Agentic AI Security
abstract: In agentic AI systems, an LLM invokes tools that hold standing access to credentials, private data, filesystems, and external services. Such agents are increasingly deployed without an answer to a basic question: what can an agent access, exfiltrate, and propagate, independent of what it is designed for or is observed to do? The question goes unanswered because existing approaches trust a tool's natural-language description as a proxy for its behavior. But nothing enforces that the description and its implementation agree. This gap is known as Description-Code Inconsistency (DCI). DCI enables a threat class called capability laundering, in which a tool's implementation contains dangerous behavior that its description omits. The behavior may come from incidental drift or a supply-chain compromise. It runs silently whenever an LLM invokes the tool for its stated, benign purpose. We present ACaM, a neurosymbolic approach to capability modeling that derives each tool's capabilities from its code, so a laundered capability cannot hide behind a benign description. In ACaM, static analysis grounds an LLM in code-derived facts, and no LLM output can override a fact that static analysis has established. The LLM supplies only the behavioral meaning that those facts cannot express. ACaM compiles agent source code into the Agent Capability Property Graph (ACPG) and uses it to reconstruct threat chains that span multiple tool calls. We evaluate ACaM on 43 real-world agents, including 9 multi-agent systems. On 24 manually annotated agents, it recovers capability properties with 98.3% macro-F1 and reconstructs injected threat chains with a score of 0.980, 8 points above the strongest baseline. Applied to all 43 unmodified agents, it discovers hundreds of structural vulnerabilities, ten of which we confirm with proof-of-concept exploits.

title: An explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations
abstract: We develop an explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations whose solutions evolve in a prescribed interval. A Lamperti-type transformation converts the original equation into one with additive noise, whose drift may be singular near finite boundaries or grow polynomially at infinity. The proposed domain-preserving projected Euler-Maruyama (DPPEM) scheme combines an explicit Euler-Maruyama step with projection onto a step-size-dependent interior interval. Under one-sided Lipschitz, boundary, and weighted growth assumptions, with projection parameters chosen according to the coefficient growth and available moment orders, we establish strong order one convergence for admissible moment orders. The analysis combines local consistency and stability estimates with moment and boundary negative moment bounds for the exact solution. Numerical moment bounds follow from the convergence estimate, while numerical negative moment bounds are obtained under additional conditions. Estimates for the inverse Lamperti map yield strong order one convergence for the original equations in the CIR, Heston 3/2, CEV, Ait-Sahalia, and bounded interest-rate models under the stated model conditions. Numerical experiments illustrate the predicted convergence rates and compare computational costs with the Lamperti backward Euler-Maruyama scheme.

title: Learning the Dynamics of Deformable Linear Objects Through Coupled Oscillators for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Many learning-based approaches for deformable linear objects (DLOs) rely on simplified deformation models that neglect dynamic effects and the mechanical response of the objects, limiting their applicability to lightweight, compliant objects and slow motions. Inspired by recent advances in learning physically structured dynamics with coupled oscillator networks (CONs), we propose $Φ$-CON for learning force-driven DLO dynamics. The model combines a floating-base coupled oscillator network (FBCON), whose latent potential energy depends only on the DLO's shape, with a learned affine diffeomorphism $Φ$ between observed positions along the DLO and latent coordinates. Its shape dynamics are stable by construction, and its Lagrangian structure yields explicit expressions for kinetic and potential energy. We exploit this structure to design a model-based proportional-derivative (PD) controller that compensates for the learned potential forces, thereby establishing closed-loop stability guarantees and ensuring convergence. We evaluate the approach on four simulated DLOs and a real bimanual robot setup. In simulation, $Φ$-CON achieves prediction accuracy comparable to neural ordinary differential equation (NODE) models and Lagrangian neural networks (LNNs), with $97.2\%$ and $90.2\%$ fewer parameters, respectively. Relative to a model-free PD baseline, the proposed controller reduces mean endpoint regulation error by $97.5$-$99.7\%$ in simulation and achieves a mean per-target reduction of $27.9\%$ across both endpoints in real-world experiments, demonstrating the importance of explicitly accounting for the mechanical response of stiff and heavy objects.

title: Retinal arterial velocity-proxy waveforms from differential spectral broadening in laser Doppler holography
abstract: Laser Doppler holography (LDH) records pulsatile spectral broadening in retinal arteries. We compare vessel and local-background measurements to extract a signed differential-broadening waveform, $Δσ$. A minimal Gaussian convolution model motivates quadratic subtraction, and Doppler scaling relates the added width to a characteristic blood velocity. Real arteries show pulsatile waveforms, whereas identically processed imaginary arteries show only low-amplitude fluctuations around zero. We interpret the empirically scaled signal as a velocity proxy for waveform shape and within-vessel changes during a single acquisition under stable conditions.

title: A-Tag: Cryptographic File Tagging with Enforced Live Human Presence
abstract: The increasing autonomy of software agents and the proliferation of AI-generated content have weakened the reliability of digital actions as evidence of human involvement. Existing mechanisms, such as digital signatures and authentication protocols, verify identity and integrity, but do not establish whether a live human was present at the time an action was performed. In this paper, we introduce A-Tag, a system for verifiable human-in-the-loop tagging of digital artifacts. A-Tag cryptographically binds a file to a verified instance of live human presence at the moment of tagging. The resulting tag serves as a persistent and transferable proof that the action was triggered by a live human, without making claims about the origin, identity of the actor, or semantic content of the file. A-Tag is a modular framework combining liveness verification based on micro-motion signals shaped by human motor control, a secure cryptographic binding between the verified event and the artifact, and a publicly verifiable logging mechanism enabling independent validation. We formalize security properties of human presence signals, define an adversarial model capturing automated and relay attacks, and analyze the system's guarantees and limitations. We implement A-Tag on commodity devices and evaluate it under realistic conditions. Our evaluation shows that A-Tag provides cryptographically sound artifact binding with deterministic verification, while enabling robust recovery under real-world transformations, achieving over 99 percent success for image-based artifacts, and maintaining sub-second verification and practical tagging latency.

title: The Value Semantics Layer: Enabling Machine-Understandable Databases for Agentic AI
abstract: As data systems increasingly support autonomous LLM-powered agents alongside human analysts, they require richer semantic infrastructure bridging analytical concepts and analytical operations. Existing metadata systems expose schemas, catalogs, lineage, and governance information, but provide limited support for representing operational semantics. We propose the Value Semantics Layer (VSL), an architectural abstraction that externalizes value semantics as persistent, planner-visible infrastructure. VSL introduces Value Semantic Types (VSTs), reusable operational semantic assertions capturing distributional, relational, process, quantitative, and policy-grounded semantics. Unlike descriptive metadata, VSTs enable planners to validate analytical operations, select appropriate operators, and guide analytical workflows. We present the motivation, formalization, architecture, and prototype realizations of VSL, and outline a research agenda toward AI-native semantic infrastructure for analytical systems.

title: Option-GRPO: Hierarchical RL Against AI Slop in Code Generation for Unseen SDKs
abstract: Large language models increasingly produce AI slop in generated code: verbose, redundant, non-idiomatic implementations that pass functional checks but bloat codebases. The problem compounds on SDKs released after the model's training cutoff, where the model has neither idiomatic priors nor compositional understanding. We present Option-GRPO, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that adapts a code LLM to an unseen SDK from its source code alone, without human-written usage examples or test cases, and that explicitly optimizes for both functional correctness and code elegance. Our key insight is that SDK source code contains compositional structure that defines a hierarchy of reusable code patterns (code options) which simultaneously serve as the building blocks of a curriculum and the action space for efficient policy optimization. We show that code options induce a valid semi-Markov decision process, give conditional bounds under which shorter option description length implies more concise and, in expectation, more API-efficient programs, and analyze under stated assumptions how the option hierarchy improves credit assignment by a factor of $\sqrt{T/K}$. Using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with execution-based rewards at each curriculum level, Option-GRPO discovers SDK idioms, composes them into patterns, and assembles patterns into complete programs. Experiments on 12 unseen SDKs with a 32B-parameter base model demonstrate 61.4% pass@1, outperforming flat GRPO by 8.7 points, ExploraCoder by 11.2 points, and ReCode by 6.3 points. Option-GRPO produces solutions that use 34.7% fewer API calls and are 27% shorter than flat-GRPO outputs while maintaining higher correctness, directly attacking the slop problem.

title: Classification algorithms for selecting crop types in Asian countries based on soil and climate parameters
abstract: Classifying crops from environmental conditions can support agricultural data exploration, but an observed crop is not necessarily the most suitable crop for that land. We compare multinomial logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors (kNN), and random forest on a transparent seven-country South Asian grid benchmark. Crop-area and surface-soil layers came from the open ACASA 50 km collection; annual mean temperature and precipitation were sampled from WorldClim 2.1 climate normals. For each grid cell, the largest of 12 crop-area layers defined the observed dominant-crop label. Cells without mapped crops, incomplete inputs, or less than 50% dominance were removed, and classes with fewer than 30 records were excluded, leaving 1,070 cells in seven crop classes. No crop-area layer was used as a predictor. Disjoint 2° spatial blocks supplied 642 training, 215 validation, and 213 test cells. On the held-out test blocks, kNN achieved 73.7% accuracy and 0.461 macro-F1, versus 70.9% and 0.441 for random forest and 70.0% and 0.398 for logistic regression. Its advantage over random forest in accuracy was 2.8 percentage points, but a paired block-bootstrap interval crossed zero. Leave-one-country-out tests were markedly less reliable, especially in Afghanistan and Pakistan. The results identify a modestly stronger within-region classifier for mapped crop dominance under this protocol; they do not validate agronomic suitability, yield benefit, or transfer to new countries.

title: Adecuaciones experimentales y nuevos enfoques de aprendizaje automático para aplicaciones en estudios del sueño y detección de glaucoma
abstract: Las señales biomédicas juegan un papel importante en el diagnóstico y tratamiento médico, aunque su interpretación está limitada por la subjetividad, el ruido y la variabilidad entre pacientes. Esta tesis aborda dos problemas dentro de este ámbito: la clasificación de etapas de sueño a partir de señales de polisomnografía y la segmentación del disco y copa óptica en imágenes de fondo de ojo para la detección de glaucoma. En el caso de la clasificación del sueño, se evaluó cómo la inclusión de múltiples canales mejora la precisión frente al uso de un solo canal, un enfoque común en la literatura. Además, se incorporaron variables demográficas como la edad, que influye significativamente en las etapas del sueño, y se analizó la importancia de fases específicas del sueño temprano y tardío. Los resultados mostraron que un enfoque multidimensional y contextualizado médicamente puede aumentar la exactitud en la clasificación de las etapas del sueño. Para la segmentación de disco y la copa óptica, se desarrolló y evaluó un modelo automatizado que cuestiona la necesidad de recortar previamente las imágenes, una práctica común en otros estudios. A su vez, mediante un método semisupervisado, se logró una segmentación robusta, incluso en dominios no vistos durante el entrenamiento, mejorando la generalización del modelo. Este enfoque simplificado, pero efectivo, optimiza el proceso clínico al eliminar la necesidad de intervenciones manuales, lo que es especialmente relevante en entornos clínicos con alta variabilidad entre imágenes. Biomedical signals play an important role in medical diagnosis and treatment, though their interpretation is limited by subjectivity, noise, and patient variability. This thesis addresses two key challenges in this field: sleep stage classification from polysomnography signals, and optic disc and cup segmentation in fundus images for glaucoma detection. For sleep classification, the study evaluated how including multiple channels (EEG, EOG, EMG) improves accuracy compared to the common single-channel approach. Demographic variables, such as age, were also incorporated, and the relevance of early and late sleep phases was analyzed. The results demonstrate that a multidimensional, medically contextualized approach enhances the accuracy of automatic sleep stage classification, addressing limitations found in previous research. In optic disc and cup segmentation, an automated model was developed that challenges the need for pre-cropping images, a common practice in other studies. Using a semi-supervised method without cropping, the model achieved robust segmentation, even in previously unseen domains, improving generalization. This simple yet effective approach optimizes clinical workflows by reducing manual intervention, particularly in environments with high image variability.

title: Improving On-board Shape Models Using Sun Sensors and Implicit Representations
abstract: We propose an original, end-to-end approach to generate and refine the onboard 3D shape model of irregular small bodies, such as asteroids, using only low-cost Sun sensor eclipse data and coarse a priori knowledge, tailored for resource-constrained missions like CubeSats. Leveraging EclipseNets, a differentiable neural model of eclipse boundaries, our pipeline first refines 2D silhouettes by learning from real-time entry and exit events during spacecraft orbits, avoiding the limitations of traditional imaging or lidar in bandwidth-starved environments. These silhouettes then supervise a compact neural signed-distance field with periodic activations, enabling incremental updates to a high-fidelity implicit geometry representation capable of capturing fine-scale features and concavities. In simulations of the body Eros under realistic orbital dynamics, the method increases silhouette IoU from 0.70 to 0.87 and produces coherent 3D reconstructions, suggesting our approach could find a place in future autonomous architectures for small-body exploration.

title: Differentiating Agricultural Tractor Brands and Models through User-Reported Quality Profiles
abstract: User experience with agricultural tractors is multidimensional and can be obscured by a single brand-level score. This study analysed 140 tractor-evaluation questionnaires covering 21 tractor brands and 44 detailed quality attributes rated on a seven-point scale. Descriptive analyses used the complete sample, whereas formal brand differentiation was restricted to six brands represented by at least five questionnaires (N = 108). Attribute-wise differences were evaluated by the Kruskal–Wallis test, epsilon-squared effect sizes, Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction, and stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. To test whether the 44-attribute profiles contained reproducible brand information beyond univariate contrasts, a shrinkage linear discriminant model was evaluated by stratified five-fold cross-validation and a label-permutation test. Spare-parts availability (6.26), engine reliability (6.16), and forward visibility (6.14) were the highest-rated attributes, whereas storage availability (4.64), passenger space (4.89), and vibration damping (4.94) were lowest. The strongest brand differentiation occurred for ease of radiator cleaning (ε² = 0.508), vibration damping (0.499), overall comfort (0.460), rear hydraulic-coupler access (0.448), and cab lighting (0.440). Cross-validated balanced brand-classification accuracy reached 0.371, compared with a six-class chance level of 0.167 (permutation p = 0.002). At model level, within-brand centering separated model-specific domain profiles from the corresponding brand baseline; 12 models represented by at least three users were visualized. The results show that practical tractor quality is structured by specific ergonomic, maintainability, reliability, and ownership attributes and that these detailed profiles contain reproducible information at both brand and model levels.
journal: Journal of Research and Applications in Agricultural Engineering
publisher: Lukasiewicz Research Network - Poznan Technology Institute

title: The Mathematical Foundation and Optimization Methods of the Core Modules of Multimodal Large Models
abstract: Multimodal large models integrate language, vision and other input modalities through attention, alignment, connector mapping and optimization modules, and their capabilities depend not only on parameter scale but also on how these components exchange and transform information. This review examines the mathematical foundations of scaled dot-product attention, contrastive learning, positional encoding, low-rank adaptation, quantization and knowledge distillation. Attention scaling is explained through variance control, InfoNCE through mutual-information estimation, and parameter-efficient adaptation through low-rank approximation. Efficient attention computation and activation-aware quantization are also analysed from computational and numerical perspectives. Together, these connections clarify how architecture and computation shape stability, efficiency and reliability, and they identify directions for more interpretable and controllable multimodal systems.

title: Forecasting the Monthly-Average U.S. Treasury 10Y–2Y Term Spread: A VARX Model with Macroeconomic Controls
abstract: This paper aims to figure out whether the monthly-average 10-year minus 2-year U.S. Treasury term spread can be forecast by its yield-curve and extra macroeconomic information. The research uses monthly data from January 1990 to July 2026 and sets 53 recursive origins during this period. Then the spread is forecast one and three months ahead against a driftless random walk, comparing a second-order vector autoregressive (VAR(2)) model in first differences with a second-order vector autoregressive model with exogenous variables (VARX(2)) that adds inflation, the policy rate, the Chicago Board Options Exchange Volatility Index (VIX) and the economic policy uncertainty (EPU) index. VAR reduces root mean squared error (RMSE) by 7.76% at one month and 3.96% at three months, and the one-month gain survives Holm adjustment (p = 0.0136); the VARX-versus-VAR increment is insignificant at both horizons, so the macroeconomic contribution is weak and not robust. Ex-post groupings concentrate the gains where the spread actually narrowed, which describe forecast-error heterogeneity only. Conditional on other yield lags and the macro controls, lagged 2-year changes carry no robust incremental linear information. The results are pseudo-out-of-sample because the data used are revised.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Multi-Source Data Fusion Based Market Demand Forecasting and Intelligent Business Decision Optimization
abstract: New retail demand is determined by unpredictable sales dynamics, inventory level, promotion actions, weather conditions, and time factors, whereas stockouts may lead to demand underestimation due to distorted sales and negative replenishment decision-making. In order to solve the issue, a multi-source forecasting and business decision system has been designed with the help of FreshRetailNet-50K. First, stockout-affected demand was restored, followed by encoding and dynamic fusion of historical demand, inventory, promotion, weather, calendar, and product data via gated attention network to obtain seven days point and quantile forecasting. After that, forecasting was integrated in the rolling replenishment strategy with regard to ordering, holding, spoilage, stockout, capacity, shelf-life, and lead-time costs. According to experimental results, the proposed multi-source model yielded an MAE score of 6.84, an RMSE score of 10.27, and WAPE value of 29.36% along with the cost index reduction of the replenishment strategy from 424 to 326. The stockout ratio was lowered to 5.8%, spoilage ratio – to 3.7%, inventory turnover became equal to 8.6, and demand fulfillment to 94.2%. Consequently, one may state that incorporation of heterogeneous market data into probabilistic forecasting may lead to better demand estimation and operational efficiency. Thus, the system offers practical grounds for intelligent retail decision optimization, maintaining the link between forecast accuracy and inventory management metrics.

title: Research Progress on Closed-Loop Control Technology for Key Operation Stages of Combine Harvesters
abstract: During the operation of a combine harvester, the crop state changes continuously and the load disturbances are obvious, while low loss, high efficiency and stability constrain each other, so it is difficult to take all of them into account by relying only on fixed parameters or single-variable open-loop regulation. This paper summarizes the perception, decision and execution mechanisms according to four types of stages, namely forward speed and feed rate, threshing and separation, cleaning, and header profiling, and compares the progress of machine learning, fuzzy control, model predictive control, multi-sensor fusion and soft measurement according to the completeness of the closed loop and the level of validation. Research is moving from single-parameter feedback toward multi-source perception, feedforward-feedback fusion and multi-variable coordinated optimization, but online quality perception, cross-crop generalization, subsystem coupling, real-time deployment and long-term field validation remain weak. Follow-up work should strengthen model-data fusion estimation, hierarchical multi-objective control, lightweight deployment, actuator dynamic compensation and safety fault tolerance, so as to improve the autonomous operation capability in complex field environments.

title: Warehouse Mobile Manipulation with Large Language Models and Foundation Models
abstract: Mobile manipulators can move between storage locations and handle goods, but transferring the semantic capabilities of foundation models to dependable warehouse operations remains constrained by execution interfaces, data coverage, and operating conditions. This thematic critical review examines perception, reasoning, planning and execution, and data and generalization. It compares hierarchical approaches with vision-language-action models and assesses their relevance to warehouse tasks using representative studies. Its distinctive value lies in relating model interfaces and transfer limits to warehouse order fulfillment, where stock-keeping unit (SKU) verification, shelf access, and onboard resource limits must be considered together. The evidence indicates that foundation models reorganize selected interfaces between observations, task descriptions, and actions; they do not remove the need for geometric feasibility checks, low-level control, or failure recovery. Open-vocabulary recognition must be connected to item-level verification, while semantic generalization should be distinguished from the acquisition of new motor skills. Reported transfer gains also depend on the task, embodiment, and adaptation budget. The review identifies order completion, coordinated base-arm motion, and measurable adaptation costs as priorities for research and evaluation. These conclusions support method selection and experimental design rather than a claim of validated warehouse deployment.
