title: Evaluating Full-Track Log-Mel Features and a CNN-BiGRU Model for Music Genre Classification Using the FMA-Small Dataset
abstract: Automatic music genre classification is complicated by overlapping genre boundaries and by distribution differences between development and test data. This study evaluates whether expanding temporal coverage and recurrent modeling improves a compact convolutional baseline on the official FMA-small split. All 8,000 thirty-second clips are represented as 128-bin log-Mel spectrograms. The baseline CNN uses a fixed 512-frame excerpt, whereas the proposed system retains the full track, samples random 512-frame crops during training, uses a bidirectional gated recurrent unit after convolutional feature extraction, and averages five deterministic crops at inference. SpecAugment, mixup, class-weighted cross-entropy, AdamW, and cosine learning-rate decay are applied without changing the official 6,400/800/800 train-validation-test partition. The proposed system raises validation accuracy from 46.50% to 62.25% and validation macro-F1 from 43.93% to 59.62%. However, test accuracy changes from 48.75% to 47.63%, while test macro-F1 increases modestly from 45.19% to 47.30%. The resulting 14.62-percentage-point validation-to-test accuracy gap shows that the optimization package improved development-set performance but did not establish stronger overall generalization. The work therefore contributes a reproducible, leakage-aware evaluation and demonstrates why final claims must be based on held-out test behavior rather than validation gains alone.

title: Trauma History Mapping and Family Psychoeducation Protocol(THMFP): A Structured Trauma-Informed Clinical Formulation Framework for Functional Neurological and Psychosomatic Disorders
abstract: Functional Neurological Disorders (FND), dissociative conditions, and psychosomatic presentations remain clinically challenging due to fragmented care pathways, diagnostic uncertainty, and inconsistent integration of psychological and neurological perspectives. This paper presents the Trauma History Mapping and Family Psychoeducation Protocol (THMFP), a structured clinical framework designed to support trauma-informed formulation and psychoeducation in patients with functional and psychosomatic symptoms. THMFP integrates three core components: (1) systematic trauma history mapping, (2) neuropsychological and psychosomatic formulation, and (3) consent-based family psychoeducation. The protocol is grounded in contemporary models of FND emphasizing predictive processing, salience network dysregulation, autonomic nervous system imbalance, and trauma-related emotional processing. The model was developed through retrospective clinical application in a sample of approximately 28 patients presenting with functional and psychosomatic symptoms, alongside a comparison group of 15 individuals with stress-related but non-functional presentations. Observational outcomes suggested improved diagnostic clarity, enhanced patient understanding, and improved engagement with care; however, no standardized outcome measures were applied. THMFP is presented as a structured clinical formulation and psychoeducation framework requiring further validation through prospective and controlled studies.

title: Productivity, cost and energy efficiency in recultivation of short rotation poplar plantations
abstract: Recultivation is an essential task in the management of Short Rotation Forestry (SRF) poplar, which is grown on arable land and is generally integrated within a crop rotation system. This task involves destroying the poplar stumps and tilling the soil down to a depth suitable for establishing a new farm crop. Recultivation can be performed using versatile heavy forestry mulchers that simultaneously mulch the soil and remove stumps. The objective of this study was to develop long-term benchmark performance metrics for industrial mulchers used in the recultivation of SRF poplar. The study involved the collection of long-term data on a forestry mulcher working on 486 ha of harvested SRF poplar stands. Data were collected across 18 sites in Germany and Slovakia by maintaining detailed, site-specific logs for two years. Data recorded included position, time use, and fuel consumption, number of mulcher teeth replaced, soil type, and resprouting class. The data were analyzed using bootstrapping, allowing robust calculation of means, confidence intervals and regression models despite the low number of sites and non-normal data. The results show that mean fuel, time and teeth consumption were 181 L ha-1, 3.26 h ha-1, 0.75 teeth ha-1, respectively. The number of passes and soil type significantly affected fuel consumption, time consumption, and tooth wear. In contrast, resprouting and field size did not significantly affect the same dependent variables. The study's findings provide key benchmark figures for planning and estimating the cost of SRF poplar recultivation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications for Precision Agriculture: Opportunities, Challenges, and Prospects for Smallholder Farmers in Adamawa State, Nigeria
abstract: Precision agriculture represents a paradigm shift in agricultural production, leveraging digital technologies to optimize inputs, enhance yields, and minimize environmental impact. While Artificial Intelligence (AI) has demonstrated transformative potential in advanced agricultural systems worldwide, its adoption among smallholder farmers in Northern Nigeria remains largely underexplored. This study investigates the opportunities, challenges, and prospects of AI applications for precision agriculture among smallholder farmers in Adamawa State, Nigeria. Employing a descriptive survey research design, data were collected from 120 farmers across six local government areas using structured questionnaires and semi-structured interviews. Findings indicate that while 82.5% of farmers expressed strong interest in AI-driven agricultural solutions, actual adoption remains minimal. Key perceived benefits included improved crop yield (M = 4.28), reduced input waste (M = 4.15), and enhanced pest and disease detection (M = 4.09). Major barriers included limited digital literacy (90.8%), high cost of smart devices and data services (87.5%), erratic power supply (85.0%), and limited or no access to internet connectivity (83.3%). The study concludes that AI offers substantial potential for transforming agricultural productivity in Adamawa State, but meaningful adoption requires more than technology transfer. It demands context-appropriate infrastructure development, localized AI solutions, farmer-centric capacity building, and supportive institutional frameworks. Evidence based recommendations are proposed for policymakers, agricultural extension services, and technology developers to facilitate equitable and sustainable AI integration in smallholder agricultural systems.
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory

title: Development of A Cross-Border Regulatory Harmonization Model for African Pharmaceutical Markets: The ARCH-Model Framework
abstract: The fragmentation of pharmaceutical regulatory systems across Africa's 55 nations constitutes one of the most consequential structural barriers to universal health coverage on the continent, generating an estimated USD 2.5 to 3.8 billion in annual avoidable costs through duplicative regulatory assessment processes, delayed medicine registration, proliferation of substandard and falsified medicines, and procurement inefficiency attributable to limited competition in fragmented national markets. Each African country operates an independent national medicines regulatory authority whose technical capacity, dossier format requirements, quality standards, and postmarket surveillance architecture diverge substantially from those of neighboring jurisdictions, collectively requiring pharmaceutical manufacturers seeking pan-African market access to complete 55 separate registration processes with a combined completion timeline of 15 to 25 years and total compliance costs exceeding USD 100 million per product. This regulatory fragmentation directly undermines access to quality-assured essential medicines for Africa's 1.4 billion population and systematically disadvantages African patients relative to counterparts in regulatory harmonization zones where centralized or mutually recognized registration enables continental market access within 12 to 18 months. This paper presents the African Regulatory Convergence and Harmonization Model (ARCH-Model), a four-phase continental regulatory integration framework designed to achieve continental-scale harmonization of pharmaceutical regulatory systems across Africa's Regional Economic Communities within a 15 to 25-year implementation horizon. The four phases are: Phase 1 National Foundation Building, Phase 2 REC-Level Technical Harmonization, Phase 3 Mutual Recognition Architecture, and Phase 4 AMA Continental Governance. The model integrates evidence from WHO regulatory system strengthening initiatives, the African Medicines Regulatory Harmonization programme, the African Medicines Agency treaty, ASEAN and EU harmonization precedents, industrial safety governance and environmental risk management frameworks, supply chain governance, digital platform architecture, healthcare infrastructure capacity assessment, data governance design, and agricultural development policy alignment. The paper specifies phase deliverables, governance standards, REC capacity profiles, digital infrastructure architecture (PARIS), multi-source financing mechanisms, stakeholder engagement frameworks, and an economic analysis demonstrating net present value of USD 24 to 60 billion over 25 years against total investment of USD 1.5 to 2.8 billion.

Keeping Cultivar Values in Their Ecological Type Zones: A Multimedia Knowledge Pipeline for Cultivar Selection and Daily Crop Management
abstract: In China's national variety approvals, each cultivar's growth duration and disease grades are reported under the ecological type zone of its trials. A cultivar approved for several zones carries one set of values for each zone, and these values often disagree between zones. We describe a multimedia knowledge pipeline that keeps the type zone, assessment method and source with every value. Using the official approval descriptions of 5,885 rice and maize registrations and the 2025 announcement, we kept every grade and duration under the type zone that reports it. We then counted cultivar--disease pairs whose grades differ between zones, compared pooled and conservative shortlists with the answer for the intended zone, compared the pipeline's determinacy test with published retrieval policies that decide when to read the source passage, and predicted withheld grades from the cultivar's other zones. For more than a third of the cultivar--disease pairs documented in several zones, the official grades differ between zones, and the documented durations of one cultivar can differ by weeks from zone to zone. Pooling across zones adds unsupported cultivars to the 2025 shortlists, whereas requiring every profile to pass leaves out supported ones. The pipeline answers from stored profiles when the determinacy bounds agree and reads the source passage otherwise, and this rule reproduced every documentary answer in the 2025 workload. On sampled requests with a shared language-model reader, the rule made no errors and read the source passage for only 1.2% of requests. It also used far fewer generation tokens than the adapted retrieval policies we evaluated. In predicting grades across zones, a random forest beat the zone--disease majority grade only slightly, and the cultivar-level sign test did not settle the difference. Keeping the type zone with each value avoids the errors of pooled summaries and ties every answer to the record that supports it.

title: Reliability-Calibrated q-Rung Orthopair Fuzzy Decision Support for Uncertainty-Aware Crop Prioritisation
abstract: Crop prioritisation requires simultaneous evaluation of productivity, production stability, input burden, soil condition, and irrigation dependence under uncertain evidence. This study proposes a Reliability-Calibrated q-Rung Orthopair Fuzzy Distance-to-Ideal method (RC-qROF-DI) for transparent, non-predictive agricultural decision support. Unlike conventional applications that elicit membership, non-membership, and hesitation independently, RC-qROF-DI transforms observed desirability and empirical reliability into an admissible orthopair representation in which unresolved evidence is determined by data quality. The method was evaluated using 10,000 complete observations covering six crops and 20 soil, climate, management, contextual, and yield variables. Six decision criteria were constructed: mean yield, yield variability, fertilizer use, pesticide use, organic carbon, and irrigation dependence. Entropy weights were combined with q-rung orthopair distance-to-ideal ranking. At the primary Fermatean setting, sugarcane ranked first with a closeness coefficient of 0.5747, followed by potato (0.5473), wheat (0.4341), maize (0.4241), cotton (0.4195), and rice (0.4096). The first three positions were preserved across the intuitionistic, Pythagorean, Fermatean, and higher-rung specifications; full-ranking Spearman agreement with the primary model ranged from 0.9429 to 1.0000. All ±10% weight perturbations preserved the ranking. Across 500 stratified bootstrap samples, sugarcane ranked first in 86.4% and potato in 13.4%. The framework provides an auditable link from numerical evidence to fuzzy support, opposition, indeterminacy, and ranking uncertainty. Its output is a within-dataset production-profile prioritisation, not a location-specific agronomic recommendation.

title: Deploying Diffusion Models on Embedded Agricultural Platforms Using Region-Specific Farming Practices
abstract: Agricultural platforms increasingly require intelligent, region-specific data generation and predictive decision-making; however, conventional diffusion models demand substantial computational resources, while existing agricultural generation approaches often emphasize image diversity and disease-detail preservation without explicitly addressing regional farming variations and embedded deployment constraints. These limitations create difficulties in delivering reliable agricultural intelligence across geographically diverse and resource-constrained farming environments. To address these challenges, this paper introduces Region-Adaptive Predictive Intelligence Diffusion (RAPID), an AI-driven methodology integrating regional agricultural feature extraction, predictive intelligence, adaptive diffusion generation, and lightweight embedded optimization. RAPID incorporates soil characteristics, climatic conditions, crop information, and localized farming practices to guide conditional data generation and estimate region-dependent agricultural requirements. Additionally, predictive parameter adaptation and model compression facilitate efficient inference on embedded agricultural platforms. The methodology is evaluated against Noise-Enhanced Conditional Diffusion (NECD), which employs prior condition feature extraction, dual-condition noise enhancement, and self-attention-based memory enhancement for crop disease image generation. Comparative evaluation considers generation quality, regional adaptability, prediction accuracy, computational complexity, and deployment efficiency.
journal: International Journal of Pharmacy with Medical Sciences

title: Validating regional insect pest phenology forecasts using published developmental data
abstract: BACKGROUND Crop losses caused by insect pests are expected to increase under global warming, highlighting the need for accurate phenology forecasts to support integrated pest management (IPM). Arthropod pests, as ectotherms, exhibit temperature-dependent development and phenology that can be described by thermal performance curves (TPCs). For decades, developmental models have predicted pest emergence through thermal accumulation approaches, yet it remains unclear to what extent experimentally derived development models can accurately predict field phenology across spatial and temporal scales. Here, we evaluate whether developmental TPCs and linear degree-day models fitted from published experimental data can predict large-scale pest phenology under a rate-summation approach. RESULTS We compiled published developmental data for the widespread crucifer pest Pieris rapae and fitted several TPCs and linear degree-day models. Model predictions were validated against independent long-term monitoring data from the Catalan Butterfly Monitoring Scheme for mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands. Published experimental data accurately predicted large-scale pest emergence, with prediction errors generally below one week. However, predictive performance depended strongly on the spatial and temporal scale considered, with model rankings changing according to the scale and temperature resolution used. CONCLUSION Published experimental thermal biology data can accurately predict regional insect pest phenology when developmental models are selected according to the intended forecasting scale. These findings provide practical guidance for improving pest alert systems and other decision-support tools, while demonstrating how decades of experimental research can be translated into operational phenology forecasting.

title: Human-Agentic AI Collaboration Workflow for Trend Analysis of ChatGPT Applications in Healthcare
abstract: Background: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT have demonstrated strong potential to transform healthcare research and practice. However, LLMs are probabilistic and generate inherently variable outputs, which create risk and uncertainty in healthcare applications. Therefore, analyzing the current research landscape of ChatGPT applications is imperative to understand applied techniques and related concerns and to facilitate their practical integration into healthcare information systems. Objective: Leveraging LLM-based agentic AI with domain experts to analyze trends in ChatGPT healthcare applications and to examine the collaborative and interpretative capacities of LLM agents in broader contexts beyond narrowly defined topics. Methods: The review used a systematic search of the PubMed and Web of Science databases, following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and focused on ChatGPT applications, associated concerns, applied techniques, and usage factors. To support the review process, an adaptive, iterative LLM-based agentic AI with a human-in-the-loop mechanism was employed for automated metadata extraction, identification, classification, and knowledge synthesis. The extracted information was subsequently used for temporal and thematic analyses, citation network construction, and main-path analysis. Results: Across 192 papers, the review identified 511 ChatGPT application types, 690 concern items, and 368 influence usage factors distinct from traditional IT, achieving a metadata error rate of 1.04%. The human-agentic AI workflow enabled efficient synthesis of contextual information across studies, addressing the growing challenge of timely evidence integration in medical knowledge. The findings provide insights into the evolving trajectories of ChatGPT applications in healthcare and demonstrate the value of an expert-validated human-agentic AI workflow in supporting literature analysis and streamlining review processes. Conclusion: This review provides a comprehensive overview of emerging ChatGPT applications, associated concerns, applied techniques, and usage factors in healthcare. The study further provides meaningful insights into the operational mechanisms of agentic AI, demonstrating the potential of human-AI collaboration for medical informatics research.

title: From connection to co-creation: Human relationships as the foundation for technology-enhanced learning
abstract: This paper explores how sustained collaboration between an academic and an educational technologist can inform human-centred approaches to educational technology and AI integration. Drawing on a seven-year partnership, the authors use retrospective co-generative dialogue to identify relational conditions that supported innovation, including psychological safety, mutual respect, and shared pedagogical purpose. Two key themes emerged: human connection fosters creativity and preserves pedagogical voice, while explicit expectation-setting ensures technology remains subordinate to learning goals. These themes are translated into design principles guiding the development of an AI-powered course agent. The paper argues that the relational infrastructure built through co-generative dialogue is not incidental to innovation, it is the condition that makes responsible, student-centred technology integration possible and that responsible AI integration depends on investing in human relationships as much as technological capability.

title: Bridging the articulation gap: A multi-agent conversational AI platform for compassionate scaffolding of technical interview skills
abstract: Technical job interviews place computing students under pressure to demonstrate algorithmic and communication skills simultaneously under live observation, producing what we term the articulation gap. Existing preparation pathways provide only partial support: coding platforms ignore communication, coaching is economically inaccessible, and current AI simulators remain reactive. We present AIView, a multi-agent conversational platform that scaffolds integrated interview competencies. A LangGraph orchestrator coordinates specialised agents for question delivery and adaptive guidance alongside verbalisation monitors and an affect-aware tone layer, with assessments anchored in the SOLO taxonomy. An evaluation with 31 students showed high usability (SUS = 73.8), strong trust in AI feedback (M = 3.94), and high recommendation intent (M = 4.29). Participants valued personalised, code-aware feedback and a low-pressure learning environment. By fostering compassionate human-AI collaboration that supports creative problem solving and connection in a digital learning environment, AIView represents a step towards democratising access to career preparation through adaptive scaffolding.

title: From short-term gains to deep learning: Designing AI learning agents through productive failure
abstract: This conceptual paper proposes a conceptual framework for designing Productive Failure-informed AI learning agents that function as pedagogical facilitators rather than answer-providing tools. Grounded in Productive Failure (PF), the framework structures AI-supported learning across three interconnected phases: idea generation and exploration, consolidation, and knowledge assembly. Within each phase, it specifies the role of the AI facilitator, the structure of AI–learner interaction, and the cognitive processes intended to support learning. The framework positions AI agents as mediators that activate prior knowledge, encourage multiple solution attempts, support comparison with canonical knowledge, promote recognition of knowledge gaps, and guide the organisation of emerging understanding into generalisable principles. Theoretically, the framework extends PF into AI-mediated learning contexts by translating its underlying mechanisms into interaction design principles. Practically, it provides educators and developers with a pedagogically grounded approach to designing AI-supported environments that prioritise cognitive engagement, conceptual understanding, and knowledge transfer. Future research should empirically examine the framework across disciplinary, learner, and institutional contexts.

title: Where did that student risk model come from? Hidden inference in agentic AI-generated teacher-facing dashboards
abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) coding tools have the potential to democratise the development of teacher-facing learning analytics dashboards by enabling educators to generate complete applications from natural language specifications. In this study we evaluate Claude Code (Fable) and OpenAI Codex (GPT-5.5 High) across three dashboard specifications of increasing complexity using realistic educational datasets typically available to educators. Both AI systems successfully generated functional dashboards that accurately implemented the required visualisations and interactions. However, they also independently introduced additional analytical functionality, including student risk classifications and AI-generated insights, despite these features not being requested. These implicit inferences raise important concerns regarding transparency, bias and student data privacy, particularly where educators may be unaware of the analytical models or external AI services embedded within generated applications. The findings suggest that while agentic AI can significantly reduce the technical barriers for end user educators developing learning analytics tools, careful review of generated analytical logic and data flows is essential to support responsible and trustworthy use in educational settings.

title: Cogniti agents in practice: AI as academic infrastructure in a foundation business course
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly entering universities not only as a student-owned productivity tool but as part of the digital infrastructure through which learning support, feedback and assessment guidance are mediated. This concise paper reports on an exploratory pilot of Cogniti AI agents in an Aotearoa New Zealand foundation business course, with a focus on human-centred learning design. The pilot involved five role-specialised agents: a course buddy for administration support, a case-discussion agent for Maori entrepreneurship learning, and three virtual team members focused on task coordination, relationship management and value-adding contribution. Rather than positioning AI as a generic chatbot, the paper presents a design model for embedding AI agents within the course ecosystem. Drawing on design records, early usage patterns and practice reflections, the paper argues that AI agents can extend human-centred pedagogy when they are co-created with students, shaped by student input, assessment-aligned, and circumscribed by teacher oversight. The contribution is a practical model for integrating AI agents into learning management systems in ways that prioritise connection, mentorship, evaluative judgement, feedback literacy and collaborative learning.

title: Agricultural Knowledge and Innovation Systems (AKIS) and Advi-sory Services in the European Union and Associated Countries: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Achieving the European Union's agricultural sustainability targets depends heavily on reliable advice, coherent system governance and connected innovation networks. Within the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), Agricultural Knowledge and Innovation Systems (AKIS) and Farm Advisory Services (FAS) represent the primary macro-systemic and meso-organizational frameworks for sharing knowledge and supporting farm-level decisions. Peer-reviewed literature indexed in Scopus was systematically searched between 2018 and 2026 following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The initial publication title search yielded 408 records. Applying automated filters for English-language peer-reviewed journal articles, reviews and conference papers narrowed the pool to 190 records. Title and abstract screening excluded 109 records (72 outside the European geographic/policy scope and 37 keyword or acronym collisions), leaving a final sample of N = 81 core studies covering EU Member States as well as European countries associated to Horizon Europe or candidates for EU accession. The synthesis reveals a structural transition away from top-down, linear extension toward pluralistic, interactive innovation networks, structured across five analytical dimensions: (a) Macro-level AKIS governance and CAP integration: Member States are not equally ready to put AKIS into practice in their 2023-2027 CAP Strategic Plans, be-cause they differ in funding capacity and in institutional coordination. (b) Meso-level pluralism and market structure: private advisors respond quickly, but advice tied to input sales creates commercial conflicts of interest. Smallholders also lose out because public-good advice is in short supply. (c) Interactive innovation and brokerage: innovation brokers in EIP-AGRI Operational Groups and Living Labs work across boundaries in ways traditional farm advisors do nοt. (d) Digitalization and smart farming: socio-technical bottlenecks and disconnected networks hold back the uptake of Decision Support Systems (DSS) and algorithmic identity friction adds to the problem. (e) Micro-level advisor competencies, wellbeing and microAKIS: advisors now need to facilitate group processes and direct farmers to psychological support. They also have to communicate in ways that fit farmers’ personal knowledge networks. European AKIS needs permanent funding for innovation brokerage and reform of higher agricultural education curricula. It also needs sustained public investment to keep independent, public-good advice available.

title: Autonomous Agricultural Machinery and Soil Compaction Mitigation: Mechanisms, Technologies, Challenges and Future Perspectives
abstract: The transition from high-mass agricultural machinery towards autonomous vehicles, coordinated fleets and soil-sensitive field operations has renewed debate about whether precision automation can protect soil structure. Mechanical compaction arises from the interaction of applied stress, soil strength, traffic frequency and moisture conditions, rather than machinery mass alone. This critical narrative review integrates soil physics, agricultural robotics, controlled traffic farming, coverage-path optimisation, sensing and farm systems economics. Scholarly evidence published from 2000 to 10 September 2026 was examined, with earlier conceptual work considered where pertinent. Particular attention is given to experiments with lightweight field robots, comparative traffic systems, process-based soil-stress models and recent optimisation methods. The evidence supports reducing unnecessary trafficked area, controlling wheel loads and inflation pressure appropriately, avoiding vulnerable soil moisture states and concentrating recurrent passes on selected lanes. Nevertheless, lower individual wheel loads do not guarantee protection of topsoil when narrow robots make numerous passes, and modelled traffic benefits cannot be equated with observed gains in yield, soil biodiversity or environmental performance. Controlled traffic has a strong mechanistic rationale and useful field evidence, but yield responses vary by climate, soil, crop and management. Emerging algorithms can incorporate spatially explicit compaction costs, yet often rely on simplified soil-strength assumptions and have limited multi-season field validation. Sensor-equipped robotic platforms may improve mapping and adaptive routing, although reliable calibration across moisture states, depths and management systems remains unresolved. The review proposes an integrated assessment of load, cumulative traffic, traffic location, operational timeliness and soil functional recovery. Priority research requires paired machinery–traffic comparisons, repeated measurements over depth and time, transparent benchmarking and whole-farm economic and environmental appraisal. Autonomy should be evaluated as a means of implementing verified soil-protective practices, not as an intrinsically soil-conserving technology.
journal: Asian Journal of Advances in Agricultural Research

title: Factors Associated with Farmers' Choice of Semi Organic Mustard Type in Mataram City, Indonesia
abstract: Background: Farmers practising semi-organic cultivation choose among green mustard, Chinese cabbage and pakcoy, but the factors associated with their choices and the relative priorities of these crops require investigation. Aims: To identify the factors associated with farmers' choice among green mustard, Chinese cabbage and pakcoy under semi-organic cultivation, to rank the three types by priority, and to estimate their priority-weighted revenue (PWR). Methods: A quantitative, descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among 75 purposively selected farmers in Ampenan Sub-district, Mataram City, in late December 2024. Eight candidate variables were examined using three one-vs-rest binary logistic regression models at a 10% significance threshold. Variables significant in at least one model informed the criteria used in the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). PWR was calculated from each crop's AHP priority and mean gross farm revenue. Results: Of the 75 farmers, 27 grew green mustard, 26 Chinese cabbage and 22 pakcoy. Age and farm size were significant in all three models; farming experience (P = .07) in the green mustard model; number of dependants (P = .02) in the Chinese cabbage model; and log revenue (P = .097) in the pakcoy model. McFadden R² ranged from 0.217 to 0.359 and classification accuracy ranged from 76.0% to 78.7%. In the AHP, farm size had the highest criterion weight (0.2718; consistency ratio = 0.0175). Global priorities were 0.3950 for green mustard, 0.3817 for pakcoy and 0.2232 for Chinese cabbage. PWR was Rp1,704,180, Rp1,558,387 and Rp943,333 per cultivated land area, respectively. Conclusion: Farm size and age were the most consistent factors associated with the choice of mustard type. Green mustard had the highest priority and PWR, but its margin over pakcoy was small, and PWR was based on gross revenue rather than profit.
journal: Asian Journal of Agricultural and Horticultural Research

title: An Overview of the Applicability of Artificial Intelligence Learning Techniques for Agricultural Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: Accurate and timely crop yield prediction is essential for ensuring global food security, optimising agricultural resource allocation and informing policy decisions in an era of accelerating climate change. The rapid growth of satellite remote-sensing archives, high-resolution weather and soil datasets, and advances in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have led to new approaches with promise at regional and national scales. This review examines the current state of ML and DL applications in crop yield prediction, covering classical ML; deep learning, including Transformers; transfer learning; hybrid and ensemble models; explainable AI; and uncertainty quantification. Classical ML approaches include Random Forest, XGBoost and Support Vector Machines, while deep learning architectures include CNNs, LSTMs and CNN-LSTM hybrids. Emerging Transformer-based models use self-attention to model long-range temporal dependencies, while transfer learning strategies support adaptation across regions and crop varieties. Explainable AI (XAI) techniques, including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME), attention-based attribution and counterfactual explanations, help bridge the gap between predictive accuracy and agronomic interpretability. Uncertainty quantification methods include Bayesian neural networks, Monte Carlo dropout, quantile regression and conformal prediction. Several shortcomings remain, including the lack of standardised benchmark datasets, inconsistent evaluation practices that may inflate reported performance, and limited provision of calibrated prediction intervals. The unresolved question is not simply which algorithm achieves the highest accuracy on a given dataset, but whether these models can reliably predict yields under challenging climatic conditions. This review outlines directions for benchmarking, uncertainty-aware modelling and the integration of explainability into decision-support tools for agricultural crop yield prediction.

title: Baseline Information on Agriculture Performance and Rural Development Indicators Survey in the First Congressional District of the Province of Northern Samar, Philippines
abstract: Reliable baseline information is important for planning agricultural and rural development activities in Northern Samar. This study established baseline agricultural performance and development indicators in selected municipalities of the first Congressional District of Northern Samar to provide evidence for planning and policy formulation. A descriptive survey design was employed using structured questionnaires and interviews with 180 farmers, fisherfolk and agricultural workers. The study profiled respondents, assessed agricultural activities and government support services, examined technology adoption, and evaluated crop farming practices. Results showed that most respondents were male (67.2%), married (78.9%), and reported varied levels of educational attainment. Farming was the primary source of livelihood for 63% of respondents, while 23% combined farming and fishing as a diversified income strategy. Respondents reported receiving agricultural inputs, training and other government support services, with differing counts across assistance categories. The reported adoption of improved seeds and fertilisers was moderate, whereas the utilisation of digital technologies and mechanised farming remained limited. Reported sales were concentrated in the first half of the year, particularly in the first quarter. The findings indicate the need to strengthen equitable delivery of agricultural services, expand technology adoption, promote integrated farming systems, and enhance post-harvest support to improve productivity and livelihood resilience. The baseline information generated by this study provides a valuable foundation for evidence-based agricultural planning, programme development, and policy interventions aimed at promoting sustainable agricultural development in Northern Samar.

title: WDR76 Drives Hepatocellular Carcinoma Stemness and Progression by Stabilizing CBX5 and Promoting Phase Separation-Dependent Chromatin Remodeling.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by high recurrence, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance, with cancer stem cells (CSCs) contributing substantially to these malignant features. In this study, we identify WD repeat-containing protein 76 (WDR76) as a key oncofetal regulator of liver cancer stemness. Transcriptomic profiling of an in vitro hepatocyte differentiation model revealed that WDR76 is highly expressed in embryonic stem cells, suppressed during hepatocyte maturation, and aberrantly reactivated in HCC. Clinically, WDR76 upregulation correlated with poor differentiation, advanced stage, and reduced patient survival. Functional assays demonstrated that WDR76 enhances CSC-like properties, including self-renewal, invasion, and lenvatinib resistance, while suppressing hepatocytic differentiation. Mechanistically, WDR76 recruits the deubiquitinase USP14 to stabilize the chromatin-binding protein CBX5 by preventing its ubiquitination and degradation. Stabilized CBX5 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation, promoting heterochromatin condensation and chromatin reprogramming, thereby activating stemness-associated genes. Loss-and gain-of-function studies confirmed CBX5 as an essential downstream effector of WDR76 in driving HCC stemness and tumor progression. Finally, siRNA-loaded nanoparticles targeting WDR76 synergized with lenvatinib to suppress tumor growth in preclinical models. Together, these findings establish a WDR76-USP14-CBX5 axis as a pivotal pathway sustaining CSC phenotypes and nominate WDR76 as a promising diagnostic and therapeutic target in HCC.

title: A Credit Risk Assessment Model Based on SVM With a Hypersphere‐Based Adaptive Oversampling Technique
abstract: Credit risk prediction for small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) is challenging under imbalanced data conditions, where the scarcity of high‐risk SME samples undermines the performance of traditional classifiers. However, SME credit risk studies addressing data imbalance have mainly focused on class imbalance, while other performance‐degrading data difficulty factors, such as outliers, small disjuncts, and class overlap, remain underexplored. To address these challenges, we develop a customized credit risk assessment framework, termed DCHO‐SVM, that integrates the DCHO oversampling method for data preprocessing with SVM for classification. The model first employs principal component analysis (PCA) to reduce data dimensionality and derives a compact feature representation from the constructed indicator system. Subsequently, DCHO preprocesses the training data by dynamically constructing hyperspheres, adaptively determining their oversampling weights based on local distribution characteristics to address within‐class imbalance, and then performing oversampling within the hyperspheres to avoid class overlap. Finally, the balanced training set obtained after oversampling is used to train the SVM classifier, which is subsequently utilized for SME credit risk prediction. Empirical analysis on 551 Chinese listed manufacturing SMEs shows that the proposed model outperforms the conventional classifier, with , , , , and improving from 0.741, 0.507, 0.763, 0.602, and 0.455 to 0.924, 0.752, 0.935, 0.920, and 0.734, respectively. In addition, robustness tests on various real‐world imbalanced credit datasets from UCI and Fannie Mae repositories further verify the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed model. These results indicate that DCHO‐SVM provides an effective solution for SME credit risk assessment under complex imbalanced scenarios.

title: Incremental Diagnostic Value of Serum Tumor Markers Beyond Multimodal Ultrasound for BI-RADS Category 4 Breast Lesions: A Retrospective Diagnostic Modeling Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To determine the incremental diagnostic value and potential clinical utility of serum tumor markers beyond multimodal ultrasound for differentiating benign from malignant Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System category 4 breast lesions. METHODS This retrospective diagnostic modeling study included 307 patients with 1 pathologically verified BI-RADS category 4 lesion each. Three nested logistic regression models were evaluated: BI-RADS subcategory alone, multimodal ultrasound comprising clinical and ultrasound variables, and multimodal ultrasound plus normalized serum CA15-3, CEA, CA125, and CYFRA21-1 ratios. Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, integrated discrimination improvement, likelihood-ratio testing, bootstrap internal validation, and decision-curve analysis were assessed. Prespecified analyses evaluated lesions 20 mm or smaller and patients with all 4 markers within reference limits. RESULTS Of 307 lesions, 184 (59.9%) were malignant. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve increased from 0.875 (95% CI, 0.837-0.913) for BI-RADS alone to 0.920 (95% CI, 0.888-0.952) for multimodal ultrasound and 0.953 (95% CI, 0.931-0.976) after addition of serum markers. Relative to multimodal ultrasound, the combined model improved the AUC by 0.033 (95% CI, 0.013-0.055; p = .002), reduced the Brier score by 0.025 (95% CI, 0.011-0.040; p < .001), and yielded an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.103 (95% CI, 0.069-0.138; p < .001). Bootstrap-corrected AUCs were 0.908 and 0.940, respectively. In lesions 20 mm or smaller, AUC increased from 0.934 to 0.970 (p = .003). In the all-marker-negative subgroup, the corresponding increase from 0.912 to 0.930 was not statistically significant (p = .229), although cohort-derived combined-model tertiles showed malignancy rates of 4.0, 24.5, and 89.8% (p for trend <.001). CONCLUSIONS Serum tumor markers provided statistically significant incremental information beyond multimodal ultrasound in this BI-RADS category 4 cohort, with a particularly clear improvement among small lesions. The marker-negative risk-stratification findings are exploratory. External validation and prospective assessment of clinical pathways are required before implementation.

title: Food Havens: Governing Technological Change for Equitable, Sustainable and Healthy Pacific Food Futures
abstract: Background: Global food systems are being reshaped by climate change, nutritional transition and widening health inequities. In Pacific communities, these pressures intersect with colonial legacies and import‐dependent food economies, contributing to a high burden of diet‐related non‐communicable diseases. Since 2018, the Food Havens programme has undertaken community‐based research across Pacific settings, emphasising that food‐related health challenges require systems‐wide approaches rather than health service‐centred interventions. Objective: To examine how rapid technological change may reshape Pacific food systems and health equity, and to identify policy‐relevant directions for socially just food futures. Methods: This paper undertakes a qualitative, conceptual policy analysis. Drawing on Food Havens programme insights, it applies the Honest Food Framework to assess current Pacific food systems and to contrast inclusive and extractive future trajectories. Scenario‐based analysis examines the implications of digital, production and governance technologies across agriculture, food markets and nutrition support. Results: Technological change creates both opportunities and risks. Community‐governed pathways may strengthen food sovereignty, nutrition and resilience, while poorly governed technologies risk deepening dependency and health inequities. Conclusions: Technology alone will not produce equitable food or health outcomes. Policy‐makers should prioritise governance frameworks that embed cultural values, community decision‐making and accountability in food‐system innovation. These findings are relevant for countries seeking to align digital transformation with health equity and resilience.

Incident-wavefront optimization for energy-efficient digital micromirror device projection
abstract: Digital micromirror devices (DMDs) are widely employed in maskless lithography, structured illumination, and programmable optical projection. However, the periodic micromirror array distributes the reflected optical power among multiple diffraction orders, only a fraction of which can be collected by projection optics with a finite numerical aperture (NA). Here, we propose a content-independent incident-wavefront optimization method for enhancing finite-NA energy collection in DMD projection. A physics-based differentiable diffraction model is established to describe the effects of the tilted micromirror aperture, periodic lattice, binary projection pattern, incident phase, and finite collection pupil. The incident wavefront is designed under the all-mirror-active state to redistribute optical energy from diffraction orders outside the pupil toward the NA region. Spectral decomposition and perturbation analysis identify conditions for transferring the all-on optimized wavefront to different binary patterns, enabling a single phase design to be reused across projection targets. Numerical simulations show that the NA collection efficiency increases from 27.33 to 71.20% for the all-on state. Experiments using a conjugate spatial light modulator—DMD system validate the predicted intensity enhancement across representative projection patterns. The proposed method provides a reusable wavefront-control strategy for improving optical-power utilization efficiency in finite-NA DMD projection systems.

abstract: We examine the Bullen estimations for functions twice differentiable within an AG-multiplicative calculus model, as characterized by the fractional Riemann – Liouville operators. First, an identity was established to serve for this purpose. By using this identity, new inequalities are derived and expand the scope of previously established results (obtained with the help of Riemann – Liouville integrals), utilizing the multiplicative absolute value and presuming multiplicative h-convexity in the context that h is a B-function. Furthermore, we obtain similar results for AG-multiplicatively s-convex functions and AG-multiplicatively P-functions.

Where Digitalisation Supports Sustainability: Environmental Gains in the Agrifood Sector
abstract: This paper investigates the role of digital technologies in enhancing environmental sustainability in the agricultural sector. Using microdata from the Italian Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) and counterfactual methods for policy evaluation, we find that digitalised farms exhibit lower GHG emissions. By contrast, we find no significant effects on water use. The potential impact on non-digitalised farms, had they been treated, is estimated to be even larger. The digitalisation of agricultural systems, therefore, holds significant potential for reducing emissions while promoting more effective, sustainable strategies. The paper offers novel and significant policy insights into promoting digitalisation to enhance environmental sustainability across the sector and to support economic actors in making more sustainable decisions.

title: Understanding Circular Economy Adoption in Agriculture: An Integrative and Configurational Perspective on Farm-Level Practices
abstract: Circular Economy is increasingly promoted as a strategy to improve the sustainability of agricultural food systems, yet its implementation at the farm level remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates how Circular Economy practices are adopted in agriculture, analysing whether and how regenerative practices aimed at restoring ecological functions are combined with Standard Circular Economy practices related to Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. Building on a multiple case study of 16 Italian fruit and vegetable farms, the analysis employs cross-case comparison to identify recurring bundles of circular practices, and the configurational Qualitative Comparative Analysis to unveil the conditions associated with the adoption of Regenerative practices in circular farms. The findings show that Circular Economy implementation is best understood as the outcome of bundles of interdependent practices rather than isolated actions. Three distinct recurring practice bundles are identified, i.e. Efficiency-oriented, Hybrid, and Systemic Bundles, reflecting different degrees of integration between standard circular economy practices and regenerative practices. Secondly, the configurational analysis associates regenerative practices adoption among standard circular practices adopters with a combination of institutional, internal, and market-related drivers. Exploratory second-order analyses highlight knowledge and coordination networks and price differentiation and quality segmentation as recurrent lower-order features within their respective models. Barrier configurations indicate that adoption can coexist with heterogeneous constraints. Overall, the study advances an integrative and configurational understanding of Circular Economy in agriculture, emphasizing the importance of practices combinations and contextual conditions in shaping farm-level adoption.

title: Circular Bioeconomy in Organic Waste Management: Maggot Cultivation from Organic Waste and its Utilization for Agriculture, Aquaculture and Livestock in Indonesia
Effect of field characteristics and surrounding landscape composition on abundance of cabbage seedpod weevil and their parasitoids in canola in southern Alberta, Canada
abstract: The cabbage seedpod weevil (Ceutorhynchus obstrictus) is a major invasive species in North America, with limited natural control due to low parasitism rates. Classical biological control is being researched as a potential strategy against these weevils surrounding landscape composition can influence the abundance of insect herbivores and their natural enemies in agroecosystems. This study aimed to assess the influence of landscape structure around canola fields on cabbage seedpod weevil populations and document its native parasitoids and levels of parasitism. Landscape structure was documented by detailed ground truthing within a 2 km radius of each canola field. Digital maps were then created using ArcGIS Pro and landcover proportions were calculated for each landscape. Multiple linear regression analysis was used to understand the impact of different landcover types on cabbage seedpod weevil and parasitoid abundance in canola. Using spatial analysis, we found a positive association between cabbage seedpod weevil abundance and cereal crop cover and non-crop cover at scales of 500 m, 1000 m, and 2000 m in adjacent canola fields. Additionally, habitat richness at a broader landscape scale (2000 m) was also positively associated with cabbage seedpod weevil abundance. Nicremnus tidius was the predominant parasitoid in 2019 and 2021. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating large-scale landscape data when assessing pest populations. We further suggest that agronomic practices should be integrated into landscape-level research to improve the accuracy of pest prediction models. Overall, the results highlight that surrounding landscape plays critical roles in shaping pest dynamics and should be considered in the development of sustainable pest management strategies.

title: Comparative effects of cerabone® plus and cerabone® on the adhesion, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation of human bone marrow–derived mesenchymal stem cells: an in vitro study
abstract: Hyaluronic acid may improve the biological performance of xenogeneic bone grafts, but its effects on human bone marrow–derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMMSCs) remain unclear. This study compared a hyaluronic acid–containing bovine xenograft (Cerabone® Plus) with a hyaluronic acid–free xenograft (Cerabone®) regarding BMMSC attachment, proliferation, mineralization, and osteogenic gene expression. BMMSCs were allocated to Cerabone, Cerabone Plus, negative-control, and osteogenic positive-control groups, with five replicates per group. Initial cell attachment and metabolic activity were assessed by MTS assay 4 h after seeding, and proliferation was evaluated on days 1, 3, and 5. Matrix mineralization was assessed by Alizarin Red S staining, while COL1A1 and SPARC expression was quantified by real-time PCR on days 0, 7, 14, and 21. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Initial MTS-derived metabolic activity differed significantly among groups (p < 0.001) and was higher with Cerabone Plus (0.532 ± 0.017) than with Cerabone (0.412 ± 0.017). Cerabone Plus also showed greater metabolic activity during the proliferation period. Mineralization increased over time, with significantly greater Alizarin Red absorbance in the Cerabone Plus group than in the Cerabone group on day 14; the numerical difference observed on day 21 was not statistically significant. COL1A1 expression was higher with Cerabone Plus on day 7 but was comparable between the two materials on day 14, whereas SPARC expression remained higher with Cerabone Plus at the post-seeding time points. Cerabone® Plus showed more favorable responses than Cerabone® for selected cellular and osteogenic-related outcomes, although these differences were dependent on the endpoint and time point evaluated. These findings warrant further investigation in more comprehensive experimental models.

Soft-sprayed sodium alginate/cellulose nanofibril hydrogel membrane for temporally differentiated curcumin/ibuprofen release and enhanced infected wound healing.
abstract: Infected wound healing requires both effective early infection control and sustained regulation of the inflammatory microenvironment, while conventional prefabricated dressings often provide limited adaptability to irregular wound surfaces. Here, we developed a soft-sprayed sodium alginate/cellulose nanofibril hydrogel membrane (CUR@IC/SA) integrating conformal in-situ formation with temporally differentiated curcumin (CUR) and ibuprofen (IBU) release. CUR was encapsulated in Pluronic F127 nanomicelles and physically confined within the hydrogel network, enabling rapid release for early antibacterial and antioxidant intervention. In contrast, IBU was covalently grafted onto cellulose nanofibrils through hydrolyzable ester linkages, resulting in prolonged hydrolysis-mediated release. The precursor was deposited by low-impetus ultrasonic spraying and rapidly crosslinked by Cu2+ to form a self-supporting hydrogel membrane, which could also be formed directly on irregular wound surfaces. The optimized CUR@IC/SA membrane exhibited favorable porous structure, mechanical flexibility, fluid-management capability, short-term in vitro cytocompatibility, and wet-tissue interfacial stability. In vitro, CUR@IC/SA showed strong antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, with inhibition rates of approximately 99.8%, together with pronounced radical-scavenging activity. In an S. aureus-infected mouse wound model, CUR@IC/SA significantly reduced the early bacterial burden and achieved approximately 97% wound closure by day 13. Histological and immunohistochemical analyses further indicated improved tissue repair and reduced local inflammatory responses. Transcriptomic analysis revealed broad treatment-associated changes in inflammation- and repair-related transcriptional programs, including NF-κB-associated signaling. Overall, this work demonstrates a soft-spray hydrogel platform that couples conformal wound coverage with temporally differentiated therapeutic release for infected wound management.

title: Forecasting international stock market variances
GW9508 suppresses chondrogenic differentiation of BMSCs and attenuates heterotopic ossification without significantly affecting osteogenic differentiation.
abstract: Post-traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a pathological bone-forming disorder characterized by aberrant activation of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and ectopic endochondral ossification; however, effective targeted therapies remain limited. This study investigated the regulatory effects and underlying mechanisms of GW9508, an agonist of free fatty acid receptors GPR40/120, on HO progression. After determining the safe concentration range of GW9508 using a CCK-8 assay, in vitro chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation models were established to evaluate its effects on BMSC lineage commitment through qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and histological staining. A C57BL/6 mouse Achilles tendon transection model was further used to assess in vivo efficacy by micro-computed tomography, histological analysis, and immunofluorescence staining. GW9508 did not affect BMSC proliferation but significantly reduced the expression of chondrogenic markers Sox9, Col2a1, and Acan at both mRNA and protein levels in a dose-dependent manner, accompanied by decreased cartilage extracellular matrix deposition. In contrast, GW9508 showed no significant effects on osteogenic markers Runx2, ALP, and Sp7 or mineralized nodule formation. In vivo, local administration of GW9508 reduced ectopic bone formation and inhibited both early chondrogenesis and subsequent ossification. Collectively, these findings suggest that GW9508 attenuates HO progression by suppressing the chondrogenic differentiation of BMSCs, thereby limiting the subsequent endochondral ossification process. Under the present in vitro experimental conditions, GW9508 selectively inhibited chondrogenic differentiation without causing significant alterations in osteogenic differentiation. These findings provide new insights into potential therapeutic strategies for post-traumatic HO.
