A stochastic developmental framework for maize leaf area dynamics.
abstract: Maize developmental models have traditionally focused on crop growth, biomass production, or architectural traits, whereas fewer studies have integrated leaf development, expansion, and senescence within a single dynamic framework. Here, we present a stochastic developmental framework for the dynamics of the maize leaf area that combines temperature-driven plant development with a dynamic representation of the total, green and senesced leaf area. The framework extends a stage-structured model previously developed by generalizing leaf area development to plants producing between 6 and 29 final leaves, incorporating a structural delay between leaf appearance and full expansion, and introducing a parsimonious two-parameter senescence module. Sensitivity analyses identified distinct roles of the senescence parameters in controlling the timing, magnitude, and persistence of the green leaf area. Simulated senesced leaf-area trajectories were compared with published experimental data for six maize hybrids, capturing the main temporal trends, although the agreement varied among hybrids. The proposed framework provides a parsimonious and developmental description of the dynamics of the maize leaf area. Beyond its relevance for maize development, the model establishes a basis for future ecological applications in which the temporal availability of the green leaf area governs interactions between maize plants and specialized herbivorous insects.

title: Chloride transporters: Regulators of ion homeostasis and plant salt tolerance
A multi-targeted, barrier-penetrating inhalable nanoplatform for simultaneous immunomodulation and antifibrotic therapy in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and fatal lung disorder characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation, myofibroblast activation, and chronic inflammation. Current pharmacotherapies are hindered by modest anti-fibrotic efficacy and poor drug accumulation within fibrotic lesions. Herein, we developed an inhalable, collagenase-modified liposomal nanoplatform co-encapsulating methylprednisolone and pirfenidone (termed CMPNPs) to address these limitations. The CMPNPs exhibited favorable physicochemical properties and retained collagenase activity under atomization-induced shear forces, enabling efficient penetration through collagen-dense barriers and enhanced lung accumulation. In vitro, CMPNPs suppressed TGF-β1-induced myofibroblast differentiation and migration, and shifted macrophage polarization away from pro-fibrotic and pro-inflammatory phenotypes. In a bleomycin-induced IPF mouse model, inhaled CMPNPs improved survival, reduced collagen deposition and fibrotic lesions, and demonstrated superior lung retention and anti-fibrotic efficacy compared to intravenous administration. Collectively, this multi-targeted, barrier-penetrating strategy overcomes key bottlenecks of current IPF therapies and offers a promising translatable approach for treating progressive pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Toward a global snow water equivalent observing strategy
Multimodal Ultrasonography for Preoperative Differentiation of the Tall Cell Subtype of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma: A Dual-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE This study aimed to evaluate preoperative B-mode ultrasound (BMUS) and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) features associated with tall cell subtype of papillary thyroid carcinoma (TC-PTC) and to develop a Bayesian logistic regression model for differentiating TC-PTC from classical papillary thyroid carcinoma (C-PTC). METHODS This dual-center retrospective study included 177 histopathologically confirmed PTC patients, comprising 21 patients with TC-PTC and 156 with C-PTC. BMUS and CEUS features were compared between groups. Variables with a univariable p value <0.10 were considered candidate predictors and were subsequently assessed for redundancy and multicollinearity. Bayesian logistic regression with weakly regularizing normal priors was used to develop the final prediction model. Model convergence was assessed using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) diagnostics. Model performance was assessed using area under the curve (AUC) estimation, posterior predictive checking, and 1000 bootstrap resamples. RESULTS The final Bayesian model included four predictors: isoechoic area, distance to capsule ≤0 mm, isoenhancement and early washout. All showed positive posterior associations with TC-PTC. MCMC diagnostics indicated satisfactory convergence and sampling performance. The posterior median AUC was 0.830 (95% CrI, 0.766-0.859). Internal validation using 1000 bootstrap resamples yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.822. The observed TC-PTC event proportion was consistent with its posterior predictive distribution. CONCLUSION The Bayesian model integrating BMUS and CEUS features showed good discrimination for differentiating TC-PTC from C-PTC. However, caution is advised when interpreting positive predictions given the limited positive predictive value. Further external validation is necessary before routine clinical application.

title: Gut microbiome-derived disease-associated indices for non-invasive detection of chronic diseases.
abstract: Accurate differentiation of chronic diseases remains challenging in precision medicine. Although the gut microbiome harbors disease-associated signatures, their clinical translation remains limited. Here, we introduce a framework that constructs microbial representation indices (MRIs) to aggregate complex microbial variations into phenotype-associated features. Building on these MRIs, we develop specific chronic-disease tracer (SPECTRA), a multi-output random forest model for simultaneous assessment of microbiome-informed risks for multiple diseases. SPECTRA demonstrated robust discrimination among phenotypes, achieving mean one-versus-rest area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.92 (internal validation) and 0.79 (external validation) across 12 and 9 phenotypes, respectively. The model effectively captured shared biological features and generalized to previously unseen diseases, highlighting its scalability. Integrated into the xMICARE (Microbiome-based Indicator for Chronic-disease Assessment and Risk Evaluation) platform, this approach provides interpretable and ranked microbiome-informed risk profiles for individual samples, offering a user-friendly resource for non-invasive disease assessment and potential screening across multiple chronic diseases.

title: Engineering the Organoid Niche: A Biomaterial Perspective.
abstract: Organoids are three-dimensional in vitro models that recapitulate key structural and functional features of native tissues. The process of tissue morphogenesis of the organoid models is regulated by the niche that they reside, which include intercellular signaling and microenvironmental cues. From a biomaterial perspective, the matrix is not only a permitting support for cell proliferation, differentiation, migration, and self-organization, but also provides intrinsic and interactional regulatory functions. In this review, we discuss the biomaterials that are commonly applied for organoid culture, and their material properties. With a focus on the biochemical and biophysical cues for the spatiotemporal guidance of organoid models, we discuss how static and time-dependent properties can regulate tissue morphogenesis, maturation, and model-specific function. Mediated by engineered biomaterials, a variety of external stimulations can be applied to the organoids. Finally, we discuss the future perspectives on biomaterials for organoids with prolonged culture, real-time accessibility and improved standardization.

title: Cytokines in brain development.
High-quality pig pan-genome resources illuminate centromere evolution and enhance genotype-phenotype mapping.
abstract: Pigs are important agricultural resources and valuable biomedical models, necessitating a high-quality pan-genome to comprehensively capture genomic diversity. Here we present an extensive genomic and phenotypic resource comprising 3 telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genomes and 16 high-quality assemblies. This resource enables the construction of the pig pan-transcriptome and pan-metabolome, thereby enhancing genotype-phenotype mapping. Using 12 Y-chromosome assemblies, we resolved centromere repositioning at basepair resolution, establishing centromeres as unique evolutionary markers. Reconstruction of centromeric three-dimensional genomic architecture revealed their role as structural scaffolds that concentrate chromatin interactions. We identified eEF1A1, a transcriptionally active gene consistently located near chromosome 1 centromeres, as a candidate hotspot for karyotype variation. From a pan-structural variation map, we pinpointed AKR1B1 as a key gene underlying hypoxia adaptation. Moreover, a graph-based pan-genome built from T2T genomes improved heritability capture. Together, this work provides a foundation for studies of centromere evolution, adaptive genetics and precision breeding.

title: Maternal and early life obesity programs CD4+ T cell fate to impair vaccine immunity.
abstract: In their first 3 years, children experience an average of 14 infections and receive vaccines against roughly 15 pathogens, yet whether maternal and early life obesity alters adaptive immune responses during this critical period remains largely undefined. Using a mouse model that mirrored the epidemiological link between maternal and childhood obesity, we found that high-fat diet exposure during pregnancy or early postnatal life, but not adulthood, reshaped the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of naive CD4+ T cells and impaired their ability to differentiate into T follicular helper (TFH) cells and support germinal center reactions in response to mRNA-based and protein-based vaccines. Mechanistically, epigenetic repression of the ubiquitin-editing enzyme A20 (Tnfaip3) was a central driver of these defects. Pediatric patients with haploinsufficiency of A20 displayed a marked reduction in circulating TFH cells. Altogether, these findings establish maternal and early life obesity as determinants of adaptive immunity during a critical developmental window.

title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery.
abstract: Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer's blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.

title: Predictive modeling of single-cell transcriptomic dynamics with Dynamo.
Composite approach to quantifying regulating soil-based ecosystem services using multiple indicators
abstract: The spatial evaluation of soil functions and soil-based ecosystem services (SES) is a key challenge and demand nowadays. SES can provide a scientific background to the decision and policy-making. We define them as benefits that humans and the environment derive from soils and their functions. In our studies we presented the first maps of SES on a national scale for Poland. The research was focused on evaluation of regulating SES, which plays a crucial role in the crop production and circulation of matter and processes in the entire environment. Regulating SES contribute to CO 2 fluxes and sequestration, nutrient cycling, water cycle regulation, control of erosion and mass movements, among others. In this research we develop the multi-indicators index, grouping four SES and 11 separate indicators. For this reason, we used geometric means for calculating regulating SES and their final integrated index. For the nutrients provision, and carbon sequestration we used digital soil mapping approach with quantile regression forest algorithm, while for the water regulation and erosion control, mechanistic and empirical models were applied. Our results showed that regulating SES in Polish agricultural areas is relatively low, indicating serious limitations for Polish agriculture. In particular, 84% agricultural soils were classified as having very low or low status of regulating SES especially due to natural limitations, whereas only 2% showed high status, mainly due to the limited capacity for erosion control and high water retention capacity. This is an important step in the agricultural studies indicating the main soil health problems and areas of improvement to increase the natural potential of soils. The presented approach, due to the applied statistical and point bonitation methods, can be applied to other SES evaluation, and also allows to implement different indicators that may be more important for different regions in the world.

title: LCK promotes proliferation while restraining effector differentiation of CD8+ T-cells.
abstract: LCK is an SRC family kinase involved in the initial steps of T-cell receptor signaling and the regulation of thymic T-cell selection. While its role in thymocyte development is well established, its functions in peripheral T-cell responses remain poorly defined. Here, we use whole-body and inducible Lck knock-out models to investigate the responses of LCK-deficient T-cells across three infection models and an autoimmune diabetes model in monoclonal and polyclonal setups. LCK is not essential for primary CD8+ T-cell responses, but LCK-deficient T-cells exhibit reduced antigen-induced proliferation and enhanced effector T-cell differentiation in vivo. LCK deficiency in effector T-cells does not compromise their tissue infiltration or functional capacity. Our results also indicate that LCK deficiency disproportionately impairs NFAT-dependent signaling among downstream T-cell receptor signaling pathways. T-cells deficient in the related kinase FYN also exhibit a modest increase in effector T-cell formation, suggesting that the two kinases may act additively to restrain this process. Our results reveal that LCK has two intrinsic roles in peripheral T-cell responses, namely promoting proliferation of these cells while restraining their differentiation into effector T-cells.

title: Translation and Adaptation of the Hebrew Preschool Screening Instrument for Targeting Educational Risk in Children With Hearing Loss.
abstract: PURPOSE Preschool children with hearing loss (HL) increasingly attend inclusive preschools in Israel. Alongside the lack of validated Hebrew screening tools for this population, this study aimed to translate, adapt, and validate the Hebrew Preschool Screening Instrument for Targeting Educational Risk (HePre-SIFTER). It further examined the questionnaire's ability to differentiate between preschool children with HL and those with typical hearing (TH) across educational and communicative domains. METHOD Participants included 176 children aged 3-6 years (TH: 148, HL: 28) and 77 teachers from public preschools supervised by the Israeli Ministry of Education. Teachers completed the HePre-SIFTER, rating each child's performance across five domains: Pre-academics, Attention, Communication, Class Participation, and Social Behavior. Psychometric analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, internal consistency measures, interdomain correlations, and group comparisons. RESULTS Confirmatory factor analysis supported the original two-factor structure and demonstrated acceptable-to-good model fit. Internal consistency was high overall, although lower values were observed in some domains within the HL subgroup, particularly Social Behavior. Significant moderate-to-high interdomain correlations were found across most domains. Children with TH scored significantly higher than children with HL across all domains. Nearly half of the children with HL were classified as "at risk" in at least one domain. HL severity was negatively associated with Attention scores. CONCLUSIONS The findings provide preliminary support for the validity, reliability, and clinical utility of the HePre-SIFTER as a Hebrew screening tool for identifying functional and educational difficulties among preschoolers with HL in inclusive educational settings. While the questionnaire demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties overall, some domains yielded lower internal consistency values within the HL subgroup, highlighting the need for further validation in larger, more clinically homogeneous samples. Nevertheless, the HePre-SIFTER offers educators and clinicians a practical, time-efficient tool for early identification of children who may require further evaluation, support, or educational accommodations.
journal: Language, speech, and hearing services in schools

title: The Prognostic Value of the Inflammation-Immunity-Nutrition Score in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Undergoing First-Line Immunotherapy: A 3-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE This study preliminarily evaluated the prognostic value of the inflammation-immunity-nutrition score (IINS) in advanced NSCLC patients receiving first-line immunotherapy. METHODS This retrospective, single-center study enrolled 212 patients. Patients were categorized into the death group, survival group, progressive disease (PD) group, and non-PD (N-PD) group. Prognosis analysis employed Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier (KM) survival curves, and ROC curves. Internal validation was performed using the Bootstrap method and a 10-fold cross-validation approach, and calibration curves were plotted. RESULTS High IINS was associated with poorly differentiated tumors, stage IV disease, and ≥2 metastases. Patients with PD or death had significantly higher IINS. After adjusting for available confounding factors, a higher IINS remained associated with PD and death. IINS may aid in the prognostic assessments of PD and death within 3 years, with good model performance in internal validation. High-risk patients showed reduced survival. CONCLUSION Higher IINS correlates with poor 3-year prognosis. Given the limitations of the retrospective, single-center design, the absence of a non-immunotherapy control group, and the failure to adjust for certain key confounding factors, the above conclusions should be regarded as preliminary, hypothesis-generating findings that require external validation through prospective, multicenter studies.
journal: Biomarkers : biochemical indicators of exposure, response, and susceptibility to chemicals

title: Fragment End Motif Analysis of Microbial Cell-Free DNA Improves Detection of Pathogens over Noise from Contaminants and Commensals.
abstract: BACKGROUND Circulating plasma microbial DNA (mDNA) is a promising biomarker for sepsis, but its accuracy is hindered by the low abundance of pathogen DNA and the presence of contaminants and commensals. mDNA enrichment using a selection of short fragments and single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) library preparation can improve pathogen yield but also increases background noise. Since nucleotide representation at mDNA fragment ends is biased by enzymatic digestion in vivo, we hypothesized that analysis of 5' and 3' mDNA fragment end motifs in enriched ssDNA libraries could improve pathogen detection. METHODS We performed deep metagenomic sequencing of size-selected ssDNA libraries from 38 plasma samples, including 20 samples from 5 sepsis patients, 18 samples from 6 patients without infection, and 6 no-template controls. Across these samples, we compared observed-to-expected ratios for end motifs in mDNA fragments from candidate pathogens and contaminants. For each candidate pathogen, we evaluated the accuracy of combining end motifs with microbial abundance for detection of infection. RESULTS mDNA fragments from infection-causing pathogens were biased in the nucleotide motifs at both fragment ends compared with contaminants, with the highest enrichment observed in the GG dinucleotide at the 3' end (P < 0.0001). Integrating microbial abundance with end motif features improved differentiation between clinically significant pathogens and corresponding noise from the same microbes in noninfection samples. For Staphylococcus infections, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the combination model was higher than than that for microbial abundance alone (0.892 vs 0.431, respectively; P = 0.018). CONCLUSIONS mDNA end motif analysis improves signal-to-noise ratio beyond microbial abundance alone and improves pathogen detection in plasma metagenomic sequencing.

title: Diverse Functions of the Phytohormone Cytokinin Across the Plant Kingdom.
abstract: Cytokinin, an adenine-derived compound, is a phytohormone found throughout the plant kingdom, including species ranging from green algae to land plants. Although its importance in algae is not yet clear, cytokinin is a major regulator of growth and development in land plants, playing diverse and sometimes opposing roles in different species and/or organs. The availability of genome sequences across the plant kingdom, coupled with powerful new tools to analyze gene expression and to edit target genes has led to a major expansion in our understanding of cytokinin function across the plant kingdom beyond the previously well studied model Arabidopsis thaliana (Arabidopsis). In this review, we focus on the developmental functions of cytokinin in a range of non-Arabidopsis species. We discuss how cytokinin acts to modulate growth and differentiation, often in concert with other phytohormones and signals, with many species regulating cytokinin metabolism and/or signaling to promote the development of various structures, including shoots, axillary branches, seeds, vasculature, and epidermal outgrowths.

title: RenovaBio, environmental efficiency scores, and the cost of debt: evidence from Brazilian biofuel firms
abstract: This study aims to investigate whether the environmental efficiency scores assigned to Brazilian biofuel firms under the RenovaBio program affect their cost of debt. Specifically, it examines whether a regulated, standardized and externally verified environmental-performance metric can influence creditors’ risk assessments and borrowing conditions in an emerging economy, with particular emphasis on the highly leveraged Brazilian sugar-energy sector. This study uses panel data from Brazilian biofuel-producing firms participating in RenovaBio, covering the 2020/2021, 2021/2022 and 2022/2023 crop years. Financial data were obtained from Balanços Patrimoniais and Valor Pró, while environmental efficiency scores and biofuel information came from the ANP. The relationship between RenovaBio efficiency scores and the cost of debt was estimated using panel regressions, with a random-effects specification as the main model, robust standard errors clustered at the firm level and additional robustness checks using lagged RenovaBio scores. The results show that RenovaBio environmental efficiency scores are negatively associated with the cost of debt, but the relationship is not statistically significant. This suggests that creditors in the Brazilian sugar-energy sector do not yet systematically incorporate these environmental performance signals into lending conditions. Firm size and asset tangibility are associated with lower borrowing costs, while the Selic interest rate increases them. Robustness tests using lagged RenovaBio scores confirm the absence of a statistically significant effect, indicating that traditional financial characteristics remain more influential in creditors’ risk assessments. Broader access to affordable green credit could support investment, preserve jobs and generate positive spillovers in biofuel-producing regions. Audited environmental efficiency scores may also contribute to reducing local environmental harms and improving public health. However, policymakers should prevent the benefits of sustainability-linked financing from being disproportionately captured by large firms. Combining environmental certification with targeted support and capacity-building initiatives for smaller producers may help promote a more inclusive and just transition toward a low-carbon economy. This study provides novel evidence on the financial implications of a regulated, policy-certified environmental-efficiency metric, rather than relying on voluntary ESG disclosures or composite sustainability indicators. By examining RenovaBio’s standardized, externally verified, LCA-based efficiency score and its relationship with borrowing costs, the study extends the literature on environmental performance and corporate finance. It also contributes evidence from the Brazilian sugar-energy sector, offering insights into how climate-related regulatory instruments may interact with credit markets in an emerging economy.
journal: RAE: Revista de Administracao de Empresas

title: The role of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in shaping ecosystem services in agroecosystems
abstract: Intensive agriculture contributes to biodiversity loss, soil degradation and the decline of ecosystem services, creating a need for management strategies that sustain crop production while reducing environmental impacts. Arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi are often proposed as biological tools for sustainable agriculture, but their contribution to ecosystem service provision in agroecosystems remains context dependent and unevenly quantified. Here, we compiled 1390 effect‐size observations from 115 articles published between 1992 and January 2024. Notably, 91.2% of these observations derived from greenhouse studies, with only 123 representing field experiments. We used a multilevel meta‐analysis to assess AM fungal effects on provisioning, regulation and maintenance services classified according to the Common International Classification of Ecosystem Services framework. We also evaluated whether these effects varied with water availability and fertilization level. AM fungi significantly enhanced the accumulation of beneficial substances, buffering against abiotic stress and belowground biomass‐related variables, whereas effects on production, nutrient accumulation and soil retention were not significant in the general model. Water‐retention proxies showed a negative overall response, although this effect was not significant under drought stress. AM fungal benefits were stronger under drought stress, particularly for plant stress‐buffering responses, while high fertilization reduced detectable benefits. These results show that AM fungi can support several ecosystem‐service‐related processes in agroecosystems, but that their effects are not uniformly positive across all services and depend strongly on abiotic context. We conclude that AM fungi should be considered as components of integrated agroecosystem management strategies, especially under resource‐limited conditions, rather than as universal substitutes for external inputs.

title: Transcription Factor StTCP6 Promotes Potato Tuberization and Axillary Bud Dormancy Through FLOWERING LOCUS T and Symplastic Transport.
abstract: In plants that form underground storage organs, assimilate partitioning is central to coordinating above-ground vegetative growth and underground storage organs development. However, how plants balance this specialized source-sink relationship, and synchronize it with storage organ formation, remains largely unknown. Here, using potato shoot branching and tuberization as a model, we show that TCP transcription factor StTCP6 orchestrates branching-tuberization trade-offs by coordinating tuber-forming signals and potentially modulating assimilate distribution to axillary buds. StTCP6 activates the expression of tuberigenic StSP3D and StSP6A, and is genetically dependent on StSP6A to promote tuberization. Notably, StTCP6 also suppresses shoot branching through maintaining axillary bud dormancy. Suppression of StTCP6 in ssp. tuberosum promotes increased branching, later maturity and higher yield, while its overexpression leads to opposite effects. Further investigations demonstrate that under long days, StTCP6 overexpression remarkably induces tuber formation in short-day potato. These findings reveal StTCP6 as a central integrator that coordinates shoot branching and tuberization to optimize plant maturity and tuber yield, providing new insights into how above- and below-ground source-sink relationships are modulated in root and tuber crops.

title: Rotating Polytropic Twins and the Fragmentation Problem
abstract: Polytropic n=1 stellar configurations with strong differential rotation have been considered. The so-called twin configurations: stars having almost identical integral characteristics, but clearly structurally different have been found. Hydrodynamic 3D modeling has been performed for two such structures and has shown that these configurations also differ in the dynamic aspect: one of them remains practically stationary, while the other turns out to be unstable with respect to the development of the bar mode and fragmentation. The gravitational wave signal accompanying the fragmentation process has been calculated.

title: EgoLink: Egocentric Language-Vision Interactive Network Knowledge Challenge Summary
abstract: The EgoLink Challenge at ACM Multimedia 2026 benchmarks egocentric multimodal intelligence linking first-person perception, social reasoning, and interactive action. Unlike benchmarks centered on visible objects and activities, EgoLink evaluates whether models can interpret emotional and social cues, resolve visually grounded references, and convert user requests into verified tool-mediated actions. Its two tracks cover social reasoning in egocentric video and interactive agents that complete service tasks through dialogue, tool use, and closed-loop execution. Together, they test whether perception, reasoning, and decision-making remain coupled under both offline question answering and state-changing interaction. We highlight a multi-stage Track 1 data pipeline for multiple-choice question (MCQ) generation, chain-of-thought generation, automatic quality grading, and video-contribution filtering. We summarize the task design, evaluation metrics, rules, leaderboards, and representative solutions. The benchmark combines objective answer scoring with process- and result-based evaluation, enabling analysis of both final correctness and execution quality. The best Track 1 system achieved 0.9263 accuracy, while the best Track 2 system achieved 0.844 joint success and 0.916 micro accuracy. Participant reports reveal a shared principle: strong systems make intermediate evidence explicit through candidate verification, option-robust reasoning, scenario-aware planning, tool canonicalization, and state-aware correction before answering or acting. These findings highlight the importance of process verification and evidence-grounded reasoning for reliable egocentric multimodal intelligence.

title: Clock Distribution Network with Backside Clock Mesh in BSPDN Architecture
abstract: We propose a clock distribution network (CDN) in which the clock mesh is located on backside metal (BM) layers, while the rest of the network remains on the frontside. Since the backside power distribution network (BSPDN) also uses the BM layers, the clock mesh and power network must share them. We identify an important problem of placing mesh receivers while accounting for keep-out zones (KOZs) between clock- and power-nTSVs. We show that this problem can be solved using a potential-field method (PFM). Machine learning models are developed to place the mesh receivers: a U-Net predicts their initial positions, and an MLP predicts force weights for PFM-guided position refinement. Both models are trained through self-supervised learning by optimizing a differentiable objective that accounts for clock latency, IR-drop, and KOZ violations. Experimental results show that, on average, the proposed CDN reduces maximum local clock latency by 26%, global clock skew by 40%, and mesh switching power by 29% compared with a frontside CDN. On the same backside CDN, ML-guided PFM satisfies KOZ constraints while lowering IR-drop by 33% and requiring 85% fewer iterations than standard PFM.

title: METTL8 orchestrates TFH cell differentiation through m³C-mediated TCF1 regulation in infection and cancer models.
abstract: T follicular helper (TFH) cells are critical for humoral immunity against infections and correlate with immunotherapy efficacy, whereas immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy can drive their aberrant expansion, underscoring the need to understand the regulators controlling TFH cell fate. However, the epitranscriptomic regulation of their differentiation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the 3-methylcytosine (m³C) methyltransferase METTL8 as a key regulator of TFH cell differentiation in both viral infection and cancer. METTL8 was preferentially expressed in CXCL13hi TFH cells, and its deficiency impaired TFH differentiation and germinal center responses in the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus infection model and following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in tumor models. Mechanistically, METTL8 exerted dual functions: it bound and stabilized Tcf7 mRNA through m³C modification, and it interacted with TCF1 protein to regulate chromatin accessibility and 3D genome organization at key TFH-associated loci, including Cxcr5 and Il6ra. Notably, ginkgolic acid treatment suppressed TFH responses without compromising the antitumor efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy, an effect associated with METTL8. Collectively, our findings identify METTL8 as an epitranscriptomic regulator linked to RNA modification, TCF1-associated transcriptional control, and chromatin architecture during TFH differentiation and suggest that modulation of this pathway may provide a strategy to tune TFH-driven immune responses.

title: From Registration to Adoption: A Multi-group SEM Analysis of Farmers’ Digital Market Behaviour on the e-NAM Platform in India
abstract: The rapid digitalization of agricultural marketing in India has expanded farmer registration on the electronic National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), but registration alone does not ensure effective adoption. Effective adoption refers to progression from registration to active use of e-NAM’s digital trading functions, especially e-auctions. This study examines the behavioural factors associated with this transition using an extended technology acceptance model incorporating technology self-efficacy, perceived transparency, trust, perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, attitude (ATT) and behavioural intention. Diffusion of innovation theory provides a stage-based lens for comparing registered physical-auction users and active e-auction users. Data were collected from 600 farmers in e-NAM-linked Agricultural Produce Market Committees in Haryana, with a separate sample of 200 used for exploratory factor analysis. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), measurement invariance of composite models and multi-group analysis show that transparency strengthens trust, while ease of use and usefulness shape ATT and intention directly and indirectly. The findings support stage-specific interventions focused on capability, transparency and institutional trust.

title: Generative AI and the restructuring of criminal opportunity
abstract: Fifty years after Crime as Opportunity (Mayhew et al., 1976), the opportunity paradigm remains criminology’s most productive account of how and where crime happens. This theoretical article asks what generative artificial intelligence (hereafter AI) does to the opportunity structure that the paradigm describes. It argues that AI is not merely another item in the long list of technologies that create new targets; it is a change in the supply of offender capability itself. Distinguishing three criminal uses of AI—expert on demand, producer of synthetic artefacts and autonomous agent—and placing them beside the crime harvests of earlier technologies, the article works through the constitutive dimensions of a criminal opportunity—effort, risk and reward—and the guardianship that bears on them. AI lowers the effort required to offend, weakens the perceived risk of detection and raises the expected yield per attempt, moving previously unprofitable targets across the threshold of viability. These claims are illustrated with recent evidence on AI-assisted phishing, no-code malware, agent-executed extortion and insurgent use of frontier models. The article maps AI mechanisms onto the five families of situational prevention and analyses where guardianship is most efficiently located—at the target, in the channel or in the tool—in a contest in which defenders also hold AI. It contends that the paradigm’s explanatory core survives intact, but that its preventive centre of gravity must move upstream, to the model and platform layer, and closes with a research agenda.

title: Accessory regions shape genome evolution in the cereal pathogen Fusarium poae.
abstract: Fusarium poae is a widespread component of Fusarium head blight (FHB) pathosystems, frequently detected in cereal crops despite limited symptom development during infection. Populations of F. poae comprise closely related lineages with limited evidence of sexual recombination, raising questions about the genomic variation present within this comparatively cryptic pathogen and how it is organized. Here, a genomic analysis of 84 F. poae isolates, including 12 long-read assemblies, was used to characterize population structure and genomic variation within a predominantly contemporary Canadian collection supplemented by isolates from diverse international origins. Long-read assemblies showed that genomes are partitioned into gene-dense core regions and repeat-rich accessory regions (ARs) predicted to encompass entire chromosomes as well as regions near telomeres of core chromosomes. Homologous AR sequences were broadly shared among strains but showed variable organization across the most contiguous assemblies, precluding consistent assignment of discrete accessory chromosome identities. AR-associated loci also exhibited distinct patterns of sequence similarity across distantly related Fusarium species, including unusually high similarity to sequences present in F. langsethiae and F. oxysporum genomes. In addition to genes predicted to be involved in regulation, transport, and metabolism, F. poae ARs encode candidate effectors, secondary metabolite biosynthesis gene clusters, putative antifungal resistance loci, enzymes predicted to be involved in plant host interactions, and an expanded family of hydrophobins. Across long-read assemblies, copy number variation within ARs showed similar locus-specific amplification patterns, consistent with both non-random genome dynamics and shared evolutionary history. Together, these findings support a model of compartmentalized genome evolution in F. poae, in which ARs contribute to genomic plasticity and functional variation in a largely recombination-limited population.

title: Intelligent classification of medically and veterinary important mosquito vectors using self-distillation-enhanced supervised learning
abstract: Mosquito-borne diseases remain a persistent global public health burden, with effective control strategies depending on the accurate and timely identification of mosquito species and estimation of their population density. The current gold standard, morphological identification via microscopic examination, is limited by inter-observer variability and a scarcity of local taxonomic expertise. While highly accurate, molecular techniques like polymerase chain reaction and DNA barcoding are often impractical for widespread field use due to their cost, procedural complexity, and reliance on specialized equipment and technicians. In response to these challenges, this study harnesses the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to develop a robust, accessible diagnostic tool. We introduce an innovative application of the Distillation of knowledge with NO labels v2 (DINOv2-l14) algorithm, a self-supervised learning (SSL) model, for the classification of 30 distinct mosquito species from image data. A key focus was enabling the model to learn effectively from a highly imbalanced dataset, where the number of images per class ranged from 15 to 124. We also investigated the data efficiency of SSL by determining the minimum data partition required to match the performance of a conventional supervised model. Our image processing pipeline involved cropping, padding, and dividing images into 14 × 14 patches before converting them into embedded vectors for classification. The fully trained DINOv2-l14 model significantly outperformed a selected ResNet101 baseline, achieving 99.2% accuracy, 97.7% specificity, an F1 score of 86.1%, and a robust area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.996. Most notably, when fine-tuned on just 20% of the available data (averaging 11–13 images per class), the SSL model achieved performance comparable to the baseline model trained on the entire dataset, demonstrating exceptional data efficiency. Although limitations exist, including dataset imbalance and a lack of standardization for broader application, the model's high performance across five-fold cross-validation and strong Cohen’s Kappa coefficients (up to 0.836) confirm its reliability. This work validates a novel, efficient, and highly accurate AI-driven approach to mosquito identification. By integrating such a model into a mobile application using an embedding AI framework, this technology holds significant promise for empowering field personnel with a practical, powerful tool to enhance vector surveillance and control programs worldwide.

title: Plant disease detection and recognition using hyperspectral remotely sensed data: A review
abstract: Plant diseases are an inevitable challenge in agricultural production, yet timely intervention and effective management practices can significantly prevent crop losses and sustain yield and quality. Conventional diagnostic approaches depend on visual evaluation and labour-intensive, time-consuming physical sample collection, making them inadequate for large-scale crop monitoring and often detecting diseases only after visible symptoms appear, considerably hampering the potential for early disease detection. These limitations necessitate unbiased and automated approaches to disease monitoring and diagnosis. By measuring spectral reflectance across hundreds of continuous wavelength bands in the visible, near-infrared (NIR) and shortwave infrared (SWIR) domains, hyperspectral remote sensing represents a revolutionary technique facilitating non-invasive, spatially comprehensive crop health assessment. Disease-related physiological and metabolic changes such as chlorophyll loss, water stress and pigment alteration generate distinctive spectral signatures detectable by hyperspectral sensors with high resolution. Hyperspectral data analysis employs spectral vegetation indices (VIs), feature selection and machine/deep learning models to enable automated, high-accuracy disease classification, substantially improving detection efficiency over conventional field scouting. However, the technology’s practical deployment is constrained by high sensor costs, large data volumes, spectral redundancy, sensitivity to illumination and calibration variability and the scarcity of large, labelled datasets, which limit model generalisability across crops and environments. Combining hyperspectral data with other complementary remote sensing techniques through multisensor integration enhances the accuracy and spatial resolution of plant disease detection. This review elucidates hyperspectral data acquisition, preprocessing and analytical techniques for plant disease detection, current methodologies, applications and research gaps, positioning hyperspectral remote sensing as a foundational technology for next-generation sustainable agriculture.

title: Age-stratified diagnostic performance of pelvic ultrasound combined with basal LH for differentiating central precocious puberty in girls
abstract: Objectives Central precocious puberty (CPP) requires timely differentiation from benign puberty variants (BPV). While the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test is the gold standard, it is invasive and costly. This study evaluated whether pelvic ultrasound parameters combined with basal luteinizing hormone (LH) could reliably distinguish CPP from BPV. Methods This retrospective study included 153 girls aged 5–9 years (CPP, n=85; BPV, n=68). Multivariate logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis across three age strata (<7, 7 to <8, and ≥8 years), and mediation analysis were performed. Results Basal LH, uterine anteroposterior diameter (AP), and mean antral follicle count (AFC) were independent predictors of CPP. The combined AP+AFC+LH model achieved an AUC of 0.905 (sensitivity 81.2 %, specificity 82.4 %). Age-stratified analysis showed improving accuracy with older age: AUC 0.862 (<7 years), 0.912 (7 to <8 years), and 0.937 (≥8 years). Mediation analysis demonstrated that basal LH partially mediated the effects of both AP and AFC on CPP. Conclusions The combination of uterine AP diameter, AFC, and basal LH provides a robust, minimally invasive screening tool for CPP, with diagnostic accuracy increasing with age. This simplified model may reduce reliance on GnRH stimulation testing, particularly in girls ≥7 years.
journal: Journal of Pediatric Endocrinology and Metabolism

title: From extension to the reconfiguration of the human: artificial intelligence as an environment in media ecology
abstract: Purpose The main objective is to analyze the sociotechnical implications of Artificial Intelligence as it transitions from an assistive model (“copilot”) to an agentic and autonomous model. It seeks to explore how this new environment redefines human identity, authorship, and the autonomy of thought in the face of total technical integration. Method The study employs a theoretical-critical analysis methodology based on Media Ecology as a metadiscipline. It adopts a systemic and longitudinal perspective that traces the evolution of human interfaces from the control of fire to the present. As a primary diagnostic tool, it uses the McLuhan Tetrad to examine what AI enhances, obsolesces, retrieves, and reverses into. Findings AI as an Exocortex: AI functions as an external layer of brain processing that tends to reshape our decisions, tastes, and analyses. Autonomous and Agentic Model: Unlike previous media that functioned as a human reflection, AI contributes to creating an autonomous model capable of generating culture and narratives independently. The “Black Box” Effect: The inscrutable nature of neural networks hinders transparency and oversight in critical areas like justice or healthcare. Displacement of Judgment: There is a progressive “anesthesia” where human critical judgment is displaced toward automated algorithmic processes. Implications Cognitive Amputation: By delegating decision-making and technical labor to machines, humans risk the atrophy of their own critical and creative capacities. Crisis of Truth: AI can “hack” the operating system of civilization (language), creating “reality bubbles” where “truth” becomes a byproduct of the algorithm rather than human dialectics. Dictatorship of Efficiency: The velocity of AI exceeds the response capacity of democratic institutions, potentially rendering “freedom of choice” an obsolete concept in favor of automated efficiency. Value The text provides a critical outlook that moves beyond technical optimism, proposing an “ethics of selective disconnection”. Its value lies in defending human imperfection, ambiguity, and silence as essential non-optimizable elements that must be preserved against the binary logic of AI.

title: Caracterización del uso y cobertura del suelo en los cantones Turrialba y Jiménez, Cartago, Costa Rica, a partir de imágenes satelitales Sentinel-2, para el año 2021
abstract: The characterization of land uses and covers is crucial for the management and monitoring of agricultural territories and natural resources to facilitate decision-making by various entities. This research aimed to provide updated information on the main agroproductive systems using remote sensing techniques to aid decision-making for both governmental and non-governmental entities involved in territory management. The methodology involved adapting computer code in the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform, utilizing Sentinel-2 images from the year 2021 and field survey data. Three classification algorithms were applied to the image mosaic, and their accuracy was validated, with "Random Forest" showing the highest overall accuracy at 82.95%, followed by "Classification and Regression Tree (CART)" at 81.50%, and finally "Minimum Distance" at 57.51%. According to the "Random Forest" results, the main land uses identified were forest cover (136,162.78 ha), followed by pasture classes (25,497.24 ha), sugarcane cultivation (11,081.02 ha), and coffee cultivation (5,512.17 ha). Additionally, two agricultural suitability maps were generated for sugarcane and coffee crops to identify potential and non-potential areas for their development. The research encourages the application of these tools for national-level territory management, benefiting the agricultural sector.

title: Deep-Learning Prediction of Reversed-Phase Liquid Chromatographic Retention Times for Small Molecules and Pharmaceuticals: A Systematic Review
abstract: Predicted retention times can narrow candidate lists in liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC–HRMS). Deep-learning models report errors near the variability between repeated measurements, but their credibility depends on the evaluation design. We reviewed deep-learning retention-time prediction for non-polymeric small molecules in reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RP-LC). Searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science through August 3, 2026, identified 594 records; 33 studies were eligible. Fifteen studies reported mean absolute errors (MAEs) on the METLIN Small Molecule Retention Time (SMRT) dataset across at least seven differently filtered subsets. Among 13 models evaluated under a broad retained-only convention, the spread from best to worst was 18 s, compared to the 36 s mean repeat-measurement variability observed on SMRT reference standards. Unseen chromatographic methods were rarely tested; one model’s error rose from 29.3 s internally to 596.8 s on a held-out gradient. Random molecular partitions remained common, including in studies using cross-validation or transfer-set deduplication. Risk of bias was low in 18 studies for model development and 19 for performance evaluation, but in only seven for leakage control and one for generalizability. Reported accuracy depends as much on benchmark construction as on architecture. To support reliable compound identification, these models need structure-aware and method-aware validation with uncertainty estimates.

title: ECONOMIC POTENTIAL OF BALCONY SOLAR SYSTEMS IN THE NATIONAL ECONOMY OF UKRAINE
abstract: This study develops a transparent framework for discussing the economic potential of balcony photovoltaic systems in Ukraine. Its focus is on three different outcomes: equipment-market turnover, avoided purchases of grid electricity by households, and value added retained domestically. The framework incorporates a technically eligible reference population, an adoption rate, rated photovoltaic capacity, specific energy yield, self-consumption, retail tariffs, and equipment cost. A normalized reference base of 100,000 potentially suitable households is deliberately hypothetical; it is not an estimate of the Ukrainian housing stock. Three illustrative adoption scenarios are separated from the unit economics of a single installation. Payback, break-even tariffs, net present values and one-factor sensitivity are calculated under explicitly stated assumptions. The German plug-in solar experience is treated as an institutional comparison, not as evidence that equivalent grid-connection procedures apply in Ukraine. Official electricity tariffs and primary sources are used where available, while installation prices, local yields, user-load profiles and feasible housing populations require independent empirical validation. The analysis provides a decision framework and a research agenda but does not claim to forecast Ukrainian installations or demonstrate a causal contribution to gross domestic product.
journal: Energy saving. Power engineering. Energy audit.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF AGRICULTURAL INNOVATION SUPPORT INSTRUMENTS IN THE CONTEXT OF GREEN AND DIGITAL TRANSITION
abstract: This study represents the strategic transformation of contemporary agricultural systems through the synergistic integration of digital platforms, innovation infrastructure, venture capital, and green finance mechanisms. Amidst compounding global challenges, including climate instability, natural resource degradation, and tightening decarbonization mandates, the traditional paradigm of agricultural production has proven insufficient. Consequently, the global agri-food economy is undergoing a structural transition toward Agriculture 4.0 and 5.0, underpinned by cyber-physical systems, autonomous robotics, big data analytics, and regenerative resource management. The paper examines the multi-layered architecture of modern agricultural platforms—encompassing physical IoT sensors and geospatial data streams, integration networks, core artificial intelligence analytics, and user-centric applications such as farm management systems and ESG reporting modules. The research also emphasizes the critical institutional role of agrotechnoparks, innovation clusters, and digital innovation hubs in mitigating the high risks of technology adoption and bridging the gap between scientific research and commercial implementation. The study pays special attention to venture capital dynamics in the AgriFoodTech sector, highlighting the post-crisis shift toward upstream technologies, agribiotechnology, field robotics, and dual-use innovations driven by wartime realities. Finally, the study integrates green financial instruments, including carbon farming under Verra standards, sustainability-linked loans, and carbon border adjustment mechanisms, demonstrating that the convergence of digital monitoring and green finance significantly reduces measurement, reporting, and verification costs, mitigates investment risks, and enhances the global competitiveness of agricultural enterprises.
journal: Energy saving. Power engineering. Energy audit.

title: THE USE OF DIGITAL MARKETING TOOLS AND DIRECT SUPPLY CHAINS IN THE COMPETITIVENESS MANAGEMENT OF AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISES
abstract: The article theoretically substantiates, methodologically systematizes, and develops a holistic competitive management model for agricultural enterprises based on the synergistic integration of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems, agricultural e-commerce (Agri-e-commerce), precision digital marketing, and Short Food Supply Chains (SFSC). The research proves that the traditional extensive agribusiness model, which relies on selling undifferentiated raw commodities through long multi-tiered distribution networks, deprives agricultural producers of strategic market power and renders them price-takers. The study analyzes the operational specifics of agricultural CRM systems that serve as analytical processors, calculating and optimizing Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) across B2B and B2C/D2C segments. Furthermore, the strategic advantages of Agri-e-commerce operational models – including corporate D2C portals, B2B/B2C marketplace aggregators, and digital spot exchanges – are evaluated for their ability to reduce transaction costs associated with information search, contract negotiation, and counterparty risk. The role of 3PL and 4PL logistics outsourcing in addressing cold-chain distribution challenges for perishable agricultural goods is clearly demonstrated. The toolkit of precision digital marketing – spanning search engine optimization, content storytelling, and digital traceability via dynamic QR codes and blockchain registries – is presented as a primary vehicle for food decommoditization. The study substantiates the economic superiority of short food supply chains, which allow farmers to capture up to 57 % of total chain value added and command price premiums averaging 72.2 %. Finally, a closed-loop cybernetic governance framework is conceptualized that integrates marketing traffic, e-commerce transactions, short-chain fulfillment, and CRM analytics into a unified strategy. To overcome barriers to investment and digital competence, the institutional model of digital agro-marketing cooperatives is proposed for small- and medium-scale farms.

title: Deep time-series generative/predictive exploratory study of site-specific crop yield using satellite imagery
abstract: Purpose:: Pixel-level crop yield estimation using satellite imagery is a less explored problem with limited comparison of deep time-series models and their generalisability. Reliable prediction is constrained by sparse ground truth, spatial autocorrelation, imbalanced yield distributions, and temporal inconsistencies from cloud removal. We investigate how temporal alignment and feature pruning influence within-field interpolation versus spatial block generalisation. Furthermore, we introduce a new time-series generative augmentation pipeline to address yield imbalance and investigate its impact on prediction accuracy and robustness in a comparative predictive modelling framework. Methods:: Using 20,170 winter wheat pixel-year observations (2017--2021; 19 field-years) at Witzwil, Switzerland, we benchmark Random Forest (RF), a Convolutional Neural Network--Attention--Gated Recurrent Unit hybrid (CNN-A-GRU), and a selective state-space model (Mamba). We compare seven-pass Consistent Timestamps via Single Closest Pass (CTSCP) against 90-day seasonal averaging, prune features from $K=20$ to $1$, and introduce a regime-stratified temporal conditional generative adversarial network (T-CGAN) for extreme yield-bin augmentation. Results:: RF achieved the highest within-field accuracy ($R^2=0.901$), but its performance declined substantially on average across unseen spatial blocks within the same farm ($R^2=0.329$). In contrast, CNN-A-GRU demonstrated stronger average within-farm spatial generalisation ($R^2=0.444$), improving to $0.485$ with T-CGAN augmentation, while Mamba improved from $0.434$ to $0.464$. Consistent temporal sampling improved prediction accuracy across all models ($\Delta R^2\approx+0.022$), while feature pruning maintained competitive performance using only six variables. Conclusion:: High within-field accuracy does not guarantee spatial transferability; sequence models with discrete phenological sampling generalise better on average across unseen blocks within the same farm. Generative augmentation further improves average prediction accuracy under within-farm spatial distribution shift.

title: RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION (RAG) IN ENTERPRISE APPLICATIONS: ARCHITECTURE, APPLICATIONS, CHALLENGES, AND FUTURE RESEARCH DIRECTIONS
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as an important approach for enhancing the capabilities of Generative Artificial Intelligence in enterprise environments. By combining information retrieval with Large Language Models (LLMs), RAG enables organizations to connect generative AI with current, domain-specific, and proprietary knowledge. This article examines RAG from an interdisciplinary perspective, integrating concepts from Computer Science, Commerce, Management, and Business Analytics. It discusses the conceptual foundations and architecture of RAG and examines its applications in knowledge management, customer service, human resource management, finance, marketing, business analytics, and decision support. The article further identifies key business benefits, including improved knowledge accessibility, productivity, response relevance, and managerial support, while examining challenges related to data quality, retrieval accuracy, hallucination, privacy, security, governance, and human oversight. The study also highlights the potential of RAG to support evidence-based enterprise decisionmaking and proposes a conceptual framework linking RAG capabilities, enterprise applications, business benefits, decision support, and organizational outcomes. The article concludes by identifying future research opportunities in secure, explainable, multimodal, domain-specific, and agentic RAG systems.

title: Integrating Organic Fertilized Coco Peat Bricks with Bayesian Generalized Logistic Regression Model for Maximizing Plant Growth Efficiency and Yield
abstract: Modern agriculture is increasingly challenged to meet rising food demands while preserving soil fertility and environmental balance. The excessive reliance on chemical fertilizers has resulted in adverse effects such as soil degradation, nutrient imbalance, water contamination and ecological disruption. The excessive use of chemical fertilizers in agriculture has led to soil degradation, environmental pollution and reduced crop sustainability, necessitating eco-friendly alternatives. This study presents a sustainable approach for enhancing plant growth using organic fertilized coco peat bricks integrated with Bayesian Generalized Logistic Regression Model (CPB-BGLR-PGEY). Initially, plants are cultivated using the prepared coco peat medium and data collection is performed by capturing plant images and recording growth parameters such as plant height, leaf count and soil moisture. The collected data is fed to preprocessing technique, which is used to resizing image, noise removal and normalization to improve data quality. Then, Bayesian Generalized Logistic Regression Model (BGLR) is employed to analyze plant images for classification of plant health and prediction of growth performance. BGLR does not indicate any adaptation of Supercell Thunderstorm Algorithm (STA) that ensures accurate classification of plant health and prediction of growth by determining optimal parameters. Therefore, STA technique is used to enhance hyper parameter tuning of BGLR method, which precisely classifies the plant growth. The efficiency of the proposed approach is evaluated using a number of performance criteria including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, Specificity, F1-score, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) and Computational Time are analyzed. The proposed CPB-BGLR-PGEY approach attains 99.43% accuracy and 98.14% precision compared with existing techniques. The results demonstrate improved plant productivity and provide a reliable, data-driven solution for sustainable and intelligent agriculture.

title: Assessing the transfer-learning performance of foundation models for energetic materials property prediction under low-data conditions
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of off-the-shelf foundation model embeddings provided by CheMeleon, MolCLR, and MACE-OFF to predict energetic material properties from sparse datasets. Models were trained to predict crystal density, heat of formation and impact sensitivity from SMILES strings, with performance benchmarked against molecular representations provided by Morgan fingerprints and hand-crafted descriptors. Overall, the foundation model embeddings were found to be competitive with the hand-crafted descriptors, with MACE-OFF showing the strongest performance in numerical regression tasks. Heat of formation was found to be the most predictable property (R2 = 0.72), followed by crystal density (R2 = 0.54) and impact sensitivity (R2 = 0.47). Testing under more demanding cluster-based data splitting revealed that MACE-OFF retained the strongest performance across representations, suggesting that its learned embeddings generalise more effectively than hand-crafted descriptors to molecules that are more dissimilar to the training set distribution. Predictability for impact sensitivity improved noticeably when recast as a classification task, where CheMeleon emerged with comparable performance to the hand-crafted descriptors. These results show that while foundation model embeddings can provide useful low-input screening tools for energetic materials, they are not yet a competitive replacement for the bespoke models trained on larger datasets.

title: SUSTAINABLE E-LEADERSHIP AND ORGANIZATIONAL TRANSFORMATION: THE ROLES OF FLEXIBILITY, DIGITALIZATION, AND CULTURE IN ENHANCING OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY
abstract: The given paper analyzes the contribution of sustainable e-leadership (SEL) to the efficiency of operations with the help of the mediating variables, such as organizational flexibility (OF) and digitalization (DIG), and the moderating role of digital organizational culture (DOC). Based on the Resource-Based View (RBV), the conceptual framework of the study is sustainable eleadership that is a crucial intangible asset that helps organizations transform flexible structures and digitalized operational processes to effective and reliable performance results in dynamic and highly regulated environments. Data were collected from 300 senior and middle managers across 15 Jordanian commercial banks—a highly regulated sector undergoing intensive digital pressure in an emerging-economy context—using an online survey. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) provided by SmartPLS 4.0 was imposed on the proposed research model. The results indicate that sustainable e-leadership affects both flexibility and digitalization of organizations significantly in a positive manner that leads to improvement in operational efficiency. Besides, organizational flexibility and digitalization can work as independent and sequential mediators exposing a multistage process of capability development in which leadership initiatives are transformed into effective everyday operations. The findings show as well that digital organizational culture reinforces the effect of sustainable e-leadership on flexibility and digitalization, which determines the degree to which digital initiatives are institutionalized into consistent operating patterns, instead of being a solitary technological endeavor. Focusing on the organizational change as the process of increasing efficiency in operations under the leadership, flexibility, digitalization and cultural fit, this research adds the RBV knowledge to the operational segment of digital leadership. The paper makes theoretical contributions by explaining how e-leadership-facilitating capabilities contribute to efficiency-oriented change and offers practical implications to the banking managers looking to increase flexibility, instill digitalization in their operations, and promote a culture that encourages sustainable operational excellence.

title: Machine-learning Crop Classification Under Idealized Temperature and Rainfall Perturbations
abstract: Machine-learning crop recommenders are increasingly proposed for climate adaptation, yet the benchmark data behind them are rarely examined. We audited the public Crop Recommendation Dataset (2,200 records, 22 crops, seven soil and climate inputs), compared eight classifiers in a leakage-controlled pipeline and submitted the fitted models to idealized perturbations of temperature (+1.5 to +4 °C) and rainfall (±10 and ±20%). Each crop occupies fixed-width, uniformly filled ranges, a structure consistent with records generated from predefined intervals. Random Forest reached 99.36% five-fold accuracy, statistically indistinguishable from Extra Trees, while label permutations stayed at chance; thirteen engineered features did not raise accuracy. Rainfall changes reassigned up to 8.0% of records, against at most 0.6% for warming alone; the hottest and driest case reassigned 10.1% and placed 17.2% of records outside the applicability domain. Other classifiers responded more strongly but ranked the perturbations alike. A generic alert flag rose from 15.7% to 18.3%, a value governed by crop composition and threshold choice. The predicted class reproduces benchmark labels, not validated agronomic suitability; the protocol offers a transparent stress test for crop classifiers before they inform climate adaptation. Keywords: random forest; sensitivity analysis; applicability domain; agro-environmental alerts; data provenance.

title: AGRICULTURAL SUPPORT ADMINISTRATION IN POLAND AND ESTONIA: TRANSFERABLE INSTITUTIONAL AND DIGITAL PRACTICES FOR UKRAINE
abstract: The article examines the institutional, procedural and digital organisation of agricultural support administration in Poland and Estonia and identifies practices suitable for Ukraine. The analysis extends beyond paying agencies to the allocation of functions among competent authorities, implementing bodies and territorial offices; applications, verification, decision-making, payment, recovery and review; and the use of registers, electronic services and area-monitoring data. Comparative-legal, formal-dogmatic, systemic and functional methods are applied. The Polish model combines a differentiated institutional structure, statutory identification of authorities responsible for individual cases, controlled delegation and a modular digital environment centred on the Electronic Services Platform. The Estonian model is more compact, yet preserves a distinction between policy direction, accreditation, implementation, registry administration, control and decision-making in individual cases, integrating these functions through e-PRIA, agricultural registers and area monitoring. The article substantiates institutional, procedural and digital coherence as a criterion for evaluating agricultural support administration. It requires correspondence between competence, workflow, authoritative data, the evidentiary status of digital outputs, responsibility for the final decision and means of correction and review. The scientific novelty lies in distinguishing transferable public-law safeguards, organisational arrangements adaptable to national conditions and scale-dependent solutions that should not be copied mechanically. For Ukraine, priority is assigned to a complete map of functions and authorities, interoperable data governance, applicant-oriented electronic services, legally regulated automated processing and phased implementation separating testing from the exercise of public powers. The findings may support legislative approximation, subordinate rule-making and the design of the Integrated Administration and Control System.

title: Machine Learning Based Plasma Proteomic Analysis Identifies Disease Differentiating Biomarkers in Atopic Dermatitis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Inflammatory diseases consist of a diverse group of conditions characterized by immune responses leading to inflammation causing damage and abnormality in function. Atopic dermatitis (AD) and ulcerative colitis (UC) both exhibit aberrant Th2 cell activity, leading to epithelial barrier dysfunction in the skin and gut, respectively. Although both diseases share similar features, differences in their tissue-specific pathology, clinical manifestations, and immune profiles may provide valuable insights into the distinct mechanisms underlying each disease. METHODS We used the high-throughput Olink 384 proximity extension assay platform to profile plasma proteins from 58 patients with AD or UC and 29 healthy subjects. Differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were identified and machine-learning (ML) model using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was conducted to select disease-differentiating biomarkers. Pearson correlation analysis was performed to identify protein modules associated with severity of AD. RESULTS DEP analysis yielded 85 (35 unique) and 99 (49 unique) upregulated proteins in AD and UC, respectively, compared to healthy subjects. We integrated an ML model and selected 24 proteins to distinguish between the diseases, which accurately predicted disease-differentiating biomarkers based on distinctive proteomic signatures and disease severity. Using nested cross-validation approach, we achieved robust classification performance with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.99 ± 0.01. Correlation analysis with disease severity identified upregulated ML-selected proteins such as CCL13, CCL26, CD70, CDON, LY6D and MMP1 in AD, and ITM2A and REG4 in UC. Among these identified proteins, we suggest CDON, CD70, and LY6D, which had highly correlated expression levels, as AD-specific biomarkers. CONCLUSION Our study provides insight into the application of ML algorithms for disease diagnosis, and our model may be expanded to other disease contexts. Our results identify inflammatory protein biomarkers and suggest their relevance in predicting disease severity, monitoring clinical progression and future therapeutic strategies.

title: Identifiability and scaling limits of field sap-flow phenotyping: a two-season case study of the vapour pressure deficit response in maize and grain sorghum
abstract: The limited-transpiration phenotype, a plateau in transpiration above a threshold vapour pressure deficit (VPD), is invoked to explain why grain sorghum conserves soil water better than maize. Most evidence comes from controlled environments, where VPD is imposed, and radiation is held constant. We treat a two-season field dataset as a methodological case study and ask whether such a threshold is identifiable from stem heat balance records. We analysed sap-flow records from 37 plants (18 in 2024, 19 in 2025) of one sorghum hybrid (rainfed) and one maize hybrid (rainfed and irrigated). The records cover a dry and a wet postflowering season in the Pannonian Basin, Hungary. Management differed between seasons, so inference is restricted to contrasts within seasons. Midday flux (09:00 to 17:00) from measured records only was normalised within plant and season and modelled against daily maximum VPD, adjusted for window day and clearness index. No breakpoint was identifiable at day level in five of the six combinations of group and season; the sixth (corrected p = 0.03) sat at the edge of the search grid and did not recur with other integration windows. Bootstrap intervals for the breakpoint covered up to 57% of the sampled range, and a simulation recovered a full plateau in 12%–48% of replicates. The data neither locate a threshold nor exclude one. The adjusted demand slope was positive in every group (0.051 to 0.119 kPa −1 ), lower in rainfed than in irrigated maize in both seasons, and not lower in rainfed sorghum. Reconstructed records changed no slope by more than 0.003 kPa −1 , but the 24-h total gave rainfed slopes near zero, so the integration window is itself an analytical choice. On that total, the interannual amplitude of sorghum flux per plant was 0.1% or 9.3% depending on window alignment, and 33% per unit ground area, so no crop ranking is supported. Density-scaled sorghum flux exceeded reference evapotranspiration and tabulated basal crop coefficients. The instrumented stems were most likely a size-biased subset of a dense stand. We set out the reporting items a field sap-flow record needs before a VPD threshold can be interpreted.

title: Towards verifiable accountability for autonomous AI agents via cryptographic decision anchoring
abstract: As robots increasingly operate under the control of autonomous AI agents in safety-critical and socially sensitive environments, the ability to audit and verify past decisions becomes essential for trust, liability, and post-incident analysis. However, conventional logging mechanisms do not provide guarantees against post hoc manipulation of recorded agent behavior. This paper proposes a lightweight, reproducible framework for tamper-evident logging of autonomous multi-agent decisions, based on cryptographic commitments and blockchain anchoring, as an integrity building block for AI accountability. In the proposed approach, agents record selected decision events off-chain, aggregate them using Merkle trees, and periodically anchor resulting root hashes to an immutable ledger. This design enables efficient storage while ensuring that any modification of committed decision logs after anchoring becomes cryptographically detectable. We implement the framework in an open-source multi-agent robotic simulation and evaluate it under honest and adversarial logging scenarios. Across twelve attack types with 1,000 trials each, every modification of committed decision records was detected against the on-chain commitment, with no false positives in 1,000 honest runs, whereas a local check without the anchor missed every attack once the attacker also rewrote the local commitments. Verification took about 7 µs per recorded decision, a single decision could be verified in about 20 µs with a proof below 1 kB, and each run required one anchoring transaction of 188 virtual bytes, regardless of the number of agents and decisions. The framework guarantees the integrity of what has been committed while keeping the underlying decision records off-chain until an audit requires them. The main contribution is a practical architecture for verifiable decision records of AI agents. It combines selective logging, efficient cryptographic verification, and reproducible experimentation, and lays a foundation for post hoc auditing of autonomous robotic systems.
