Context-aware forecasting of inter-firm competitive dynamics with graph learning and multi-agent reasoning
abstract: The evolution of competitive dominance in technology-intensive industries is shaped by complex interactions among research activity, media visibility, strategic disclosures, public attention, and market signals. Understanding these dynamics is critical for strategic intelligence, yet existing predictive models often treat firms as isolated entities and provide limited support for contextualizing long-horizon firm-to-firm competitive forecasts. Here, we introduce an integrated framework that captures the relational nature of market competition by extending our prior Bayesian Multivariate Time-series Graph Neural Network with a newly designed, post hoc, lookahead-free multi-agent reasoning layer. The framework infers inter-firm relational dependencies endogenously from multimodal signals to forecast latent firm competitiveness and pairwise competitive gap trajectories with quantified predictive uncertainty. To evaluate strategic plausibility, specialized persona-driven language model agents critique the forecasted trajectories across technological, financial, and regulatory lenses using retrieved evidence. Evaluated under a rigorous date-based temporal protocol with strictly withheld test horizons, the framework consistently outperforms competitive structural baselines and yields well-calibrated prediction intervals. When applied to thirty leading AI-oriented technology firms, the framework uncovers asymmetric competitive momentum, contested market leadership, and emerging challenger dynamics. By bridging relational time-series forecasting with structured multi-agent deliberation, this study advances competitive dynamics analysis from purely accuracy-centric prediction toward context-aware, uncertainty-informed strategic intelligence.

title: CD22 loss enhances phagocytosis in myeloid cells and ameliorates Alzheimer's disease-like pathology in mice.
abstract: CD22, an inhibitory receptor canonically expressed in B cells, is also present in microglia of the murine central nervous system. In the human brain, CD22 was predominantly found in oligodendrocytes, but also in a subset of brain-resident myeloid cells from patients with Alzheimer's disease, while it is also expressed in peripheral monocytes and differentiated THP-1 cells. CD22 has been implicated as a negative regulator of microglial phagocytosis. Here, we demonstrate that genetic ablation of CD22 in APPPS1 transgenic mice, a widely used murine model of Alzheimer's disease-like pathology, attenuates amyloid-β pathology and protects parvalbumin-positive interneurons in an age-dependent manner. Mechanistically, microglia and differentiated THP-1 cells lacking CD22 exhibit enhanced activation and phagocytosis following stimulation of the pattern-recognition receptor CLEC7A, mediated by increased SYK signaling. Conversely, activation of CD22 with the agonistic antibody epratuzumab suppresses activation of differentiated THP-1 cells. Our findings identify a CLEC7A-CD22-SYK signaling axis in both human and murine myeloid cells, in which CD22 functions as an inhibitory regulator of CLEC7A-mediated cell activation.

title: Screening Hydrological Boundaries and Identifying Spatiotemporal Response Disparities for Lake Water Level Forecasting in Regulated River–Lake Systems: Evidence from Poyang Lake before and after Three Gorges Regulation
abstract: Reliable water level forecasting for regulated river–lake systems requires systematic screening of external hydrological boundaries with effective, nonredundant predictive information. However, inconsistent criteria for exogenous boundary variable selection in existing studies hinder cross-region and cross-period comparability of water level modeling. Taking the Three Gorges Reservoir (TGR)-regulated Poyang Lake as empirical evidence, this study conducted systematic hydrological boundary screening and identified spatiotemporal disparities in lake water level responses under altered river–lake interactions. Monthly water level data from four representative stations (Xingzi, Duchang, Tangyin, and Kangshan) served as response variables. Candidate predictors include water level and discharge at Jiujiang, Datong, and Hukou, as well as total inflow from the five major tributaries. The study period was divided into pre- and post-TGR regulation phases with 2003 as the breakpoint. Using the well-established seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average with exogenous variables (SARIMAX) model as a unified benchmark, this study adopted a hydrologically informed forward selection framework to quantitatively evaluate the marginal predictive contribution of each boundary variable and diagnose information overlap and redundancy. Results revealed distinct spatial heterogeneity and temporal variations in optimal boundary configurations. Hukou-related variables were consistently included in optimal models for all stations across both periods, with Hukou water level becoming the dominant single predictor after TGR regulation. Jiujiang variables provided complementary predictive information for the northern lake region, and Datong discharge and five-tributary inflow were critical for water level simulation in the central and southern lake areas. The findings demonstrate that no universal boundary configuration can represent the spatially and temporally differentiated water level dynamics of regulated river–lake systems. Instead, a common outlet boundary signal coexists with location- and period-dependent predictive information from mainstream and catchment inflows. This new understanding provides guidance for identifying priority boundary stations, optimizing hydrological monitoring, and selecting parsimonious predictors for water level forecasting in river-connected lakes affected by upstream reservoir regulation.

title: An Innovative Energy-Efficient In Situ Conversion Process of Oil Shale: Numerical Simulation Study of Mechanism and Development Scheme
abstract: The in situ conversion process (ICP) of oil shale has gained significant attention after successful pilot testing in the USA besides having a relatively lower energy input–output ratio. In this paper, a novel method of stored heat recovery and its reutilization during ICP is presented and modeled through a simulator. The actual data of the pilot field project were used to model the complex mechanisms of heat transportation, chemical reactions, fluid generation, and production and heat losses through overburden and underburden geologic formations during the ICP of oil shale. The results of oil and gas generation and production by heating through downhole electrical heaters were validated by the previous model of the same field data. Since the posthydrocarbon production leftover temperature of oil shale was around 370°C, this developed model of ICP was extended to field scale to incorporate the novel concept of stored heat recovery by injecting the fluid. Based on the modeling of the mechanism and the amount of heat energy recovery, a comparative analysis of the same field was carried out and it was found that this proposed method is more energy-efficient with higher energy output. The field development strategy of oil shale through this proposed energy-efficient in situ conversion process was also offered. This research provides novel insights and comprehensive methods for a significantly higher energy output–input ratio for conventional ICP.

title: Two-phase NEUROD1 pioneer activity synchronizes sensory neuronal differentiation and subtype specification.
abstract: Temporal control of neuronal differentiation is essential for establishing stable neuronal identities, yet the transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms underlying this process remain poorly understood. Using auditory neurons as an in vivo model, we investigate the role of the proneural factor NEUROD1 in regulating neuronal differentiation timing and subtype specification. To bypass early neuronal loss in germline Neurod1 deletion mutants, we generated a delayed, self-terminating conditional knockout mouse (Neurod1ST) that permits analysis of later differentiation stages. Integration of NEUROD1 chromatin binding and histone profiling at embryonic day (E) 11.5 with transcriptomic analyses across E11.5, E14.5, and E18.5 reveals a two-phase regulatory program during auditory neuron development that parallels dynamic Neurod1 expression. In the first phase, coinciding with Neurod1 upregulation during early neuronal differentiation, NEUROD1 preferentially binds putative enhancers of neuronal differentiation genes and promotes their transition to active chromatin states, consistent with pioneer factor activity. Loss of Neurod1 disrupts these epigenomic transitions, resulting in persistence of progenitor-like states with premature activation of differentiation and axonogenesis programs. This dysregulation is accompanied by activation of alternative regulatory networks, leading to defective neuronal migration and innervation, progressive identity instability, and apoptosis. In the second phase, marked by reexpression of Neurod1 in developing Type Ib/Ic precursors, Neurod1 deletion selectively impairs Type Ic specification while promoting a Type Ib-like identity. These findings identify NEUROD1 as a temporal regulator that coordinates developmental progression and stabilizes auditory neuron identity through phased regulatory activity, providing a mechanistic framework for how pioneer transcription factors couple chromatin remodeling to developmental timing.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: The AI engagement paradox: algorithmic congruence and its inverted-U effect on tourist experience quality
abstract: Despite widespread adoption of AI agents in restaurant and gastronomic tourism settings across Asia, practitioners consistently observe a counterintuitive pattern: increasing AI service involvement initially enhances but subsequently undermines tourist experience quality. This study aims to term this the “AI engagement paradox” and introduce algorithmic hospitality congruence (AHC), a new second-order construct to theorise and empirically confirm the inverted-U relationship between AI congruence and gastronomic tourist experience quality (GTEQ). A sequential exploratory mixed-methods design was used across three Asian markets (Hong Kong, Singapore, Bangkok). Phase 1 comprised 24 semi-structured interviews using the critical incident technique to develop AHC construct items. Phase 2 involved a quantitative survey (N = 412). AHC was grounded in cognitive load theory (CLT). Polynomial regression with response surface methodology confirmed the inverted-U effect; partial least squares structural equation modelling validated the construct. Common-method-bias mitigation and endogeneity-robustness checks used temporal separation, Harman’s single-factor test with a marker variable and Gaussian copula endogeneity correction. AHC comprising culinary AI precision (CAP), emotional service resonance and cultural contextual fit (CCF) demonstrated robust construct and discriminant validity. AHC exhibited a significant inverted-U effect on GTEQ. Cultural collectivism steepened the negative slope, while digital literacy shifted the tipping point rightward. This study delivers empirically grounded deployment guidance for hospitality operators in AI-integrated gastronomic settings. The validated 15-item AHC scale provides a diagnostic instrument for monitoring AI-experience alignment. Operators are advised to benchmark their AHC composite score against the estimated tipping-point zone (4.18–5.04 on a seven-point scale), differentiate deployment intensity by tourist digital literacy, apply conservative ceiling margins for high-collectivist segments and treat CCF as a foundational design requirement rather than a localisation afterthought. Digital literacy investment is reframed as a direct hospitality revenue strategy. This is among the first studies to theorise and empirically confirm an inverted-U effect of AI congruence in gastronomic tourism. AHC is rigorously differentiated from five related constructs and grounded in CLT from the outset. The findings challenge the linear AI benefit assumption dominant in hospitality AI research and provide indicative deployment guidance for practitioners.
journal: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: External resilience controls as sociotechnical governance: an extension of dynamic capabilities theory under externally driven volatility
abstract: This study examines how organizations construct governance responses to externally driven volatility by embedding external signals into control practices. Focusing on climate exposed agricultural firms, this study extends dynamic capabilities theory (DCT) by developing external resilience controls (ERCs) as a sociotechnical governance construct that illuminates how firms make volatility actionable through formal control routines. Adopting a pragmatic constructivist design science orientation, this study combines six years of financial and operational context (2019–2024) with a longitudinal interpretive content analysis of annual report and sustainability disclosures (2022–2024) from five major agricultural firms. An interpretive design approach enables the systematic synthesis of disclosed organizational practices into a conceptual framework. ERCs emerge as sociotechnical governance arrangements that translate external volatility into organizationally meaningful routines and actionable dynamic capabilities. These arrangements materialize through digital sensing infrastructures, traceability systems, scenario thresholds and board-level oversight that collectively shape how firms interpret and respond to climate anomalies, regulatory shifts and technological change. ERCs reveal resilience as an ongoing process of constructing, stabilizing and legitimizing responses to external volatility. ERCs offer practitioners an analytic framework to operationalize dynamic capabilities by integrating digital tools and governance structures. They show how firms convert external volatility into actionable sensing, seizing and reconfiguring routines, enabling adaptive decision-making without relying on rigid control mechanisms. This study advances qualitative management scholarship by conceptualizing ERCs as sociotechnical governance constructs. It contributes to strategy research by extending DCT, showing how dynamic capabilities are enacted through the interplay of digital infrastructures, institutional pressures, and organizational sensemaking.
journal: Qualitative Research in Organizations and Management: An International Journal

title: Seasonal Asynchrony of Microbial Biomass and Respiration Across Terrestrial Ecosystems
abstract: Soil microorganisms are fundamental drivers of terrestrial carbon cycling, acting both as a major reservoir of carbon through their biomass and as a dominant flux via respiration. While conventional models assume a positive correlation between microbial biomass and respiration at the interannual scale, the seasonal synchrony between these two components remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed seasonal data from 323 studies to assess the synchrony between microbial biomass carbon and respiration, and used site‐level observations to explore the underlying mechanisms. We observed a seasonal asynchrony between microbial biomass and respiration, meaning that periods of higher biomass did not consistently coincide with higher respiration rates. This seasonal asynchrony was consistent with divergent governing mechanisms, in which microbial biomass was associated with plant competition, whereas microbial respiration was closely associated with temperature. Our findings provide correlative evidence to refine microbial‐mediated carbon seasonal dynamics in Earth system models under increasing climatic seasonality.

title: Agricultural and Forested Landscapes Are Associated With Lower Hair Cortisol Concentrations in Male, but Not Female, Sika Deer
abstract: Human‐modified landscapes have been increasing globally, presenting novel challenges to free‐ranging animals and causing behavioral and physiological changes. Many species exhibit avoidance behaviors in response to human disturbances, such as the presence of humans or hunting activities. Conversely, certain environments—particularly agricultural landscapes—may attract wildlife by offering additional resources or decreasing predation pressure. Nevertheless, the physiological impacts of human‐modified landscapes on free‐ranging animals remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of landscape features on long‐term stress in sika deer Cervus nippon in Nagano Prefecture, Japan. We analytically validated a hair cortisol assay and subsequently employed hair cortisol concentration (HCC) as an indicator of long‐term stress. We used AIC‐based model selection with two separate sets of linear models to investigate the effects of landscape features, including grasslands, crop fields, forests, and urban land cover, as well as intrinsic factors, such as age, body condition index (BCI), and crop consumption, on HCC. The results revealed significant negative relationships between male HCC and the areas of grasslands, crop fields, and forests within a 2.0‐km buffer around each hunting location, but not in females. Although no intrinsic factors influenced HCC in males, HCC was positively associated with BCI in females. These findings suggest that agricultural and forested landscapes are associated with lower HCC in male deer. Thus, landscapes composed of multiple habitat types, including human‐modified areas and forests, may not correspond to elevated long‐term stress. Because these landscapes can provide forage resources, breeding sites, and spatial refugia from human disturbance, male deer inhabiting landscapes containing agricultural land and forests may exhibit lower long‐term stress. Furthermore, because cortisol plays a role in regulating energy mobilization, an increase in energy expenditure due to reproductive events, such as pregnancy and lactation, may explain the positive relationship between HCC and BCI observed only in female deer.

title: Socio-Economic Forecast for the Development of Regions of the Russian Federation within the Framework of the Macroeconomic Intersectoral and Regional Model Complex
NARA – NAtural Relationship with Agents: Haptics and Conversational AI as Forms of Communication with Immersive Companions
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) became widely available, enabling the simulation of visual and auditory experiences. However, there remains a lack of sufficient sensory and contextual cues to help users feel fully present, thereby limiting the user experience. We aim to shed light on forms of communication with virtual agents, specifically touch (haptics) and conversational Artificial Intelligence (AI), using a Large Language Model (LLM), within Immersive Virtual Environments. We created a VR setup to compare participants’ subjective perspectives (quantitative and qualitative) regarding a virtual animal companion, represented as the deer Ralph in a winter forest setting. Haptics thereby foster natural interactions, while conversational AI provides context-focused reactions from an LLM. We conducted an empirical study with 30 participants to examine the influence of two main forms of communication (factors) across two conditions (levels) each on participants’ perceptions: Active Haptics and Passive Haptics vs. Verbal AI and Non-Verbal AI. Our results underscore the perspective that Active Haptics and Verbal AI outperform their less sophisticated levels, Passive Haptics and Non-Verbal AI, in interaction qualities, presence, as well as technology-specific characteristics. However, more importantly, each level provides unique advantages for use in the context of a smart animal companion. Active Haptics accelerates realism, while Passive Haptics offers a low-complexity option focused on tactile interactions. In the case of an LLM agent, Verbal AI fosters positive emotions and engagement, while Non-Verbal AI enables subtle interactions and an enhanced perception of responsiveness.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology

title: Reporting Two Feelings at Once: An Empirical Characterization of Dual-Channel Continuous Self-Report in Immersive VR
abstract: Virtual reality enables controlled study of emotional responses to immersive experiences, but little is known about how people manage multiple continuous self-report inputs simultaneously while immersed. We study this interaction behavior in the context of empathic responses to infant crying, where viewers continuously report two co-occurring dimensions, empathic concern (EC) and personal distress (PD), using a deliberately simple VR-embedded interface: two rotary knobs mapped to two visual indicators. In a user study (N = 40), we characterize how people generate, coordinate, and interpret the two channels while viewing a stereoscopic VR180 video. We analyze how these reports changed over time: a linear mixed-effects model shows that both EC and PD increased more during higher-intensity crying segments, with a modestly stronger coupling for PD, suggesting differentiated stimulus-linked use of the two channels at least for this scene and interface. An interval-level analysis reveals heterogeneous coordination strategies, spanning single-dimension input, one-way switching, and back-and-forth alternation. Based on questionnaires, participants learned and operated the instrument with low perceived effort, minimal discomfort, and little disruption to viewing, indicating that the behavior was observed under valid conditions. We contribute an exploratory empirical characterization and feasibility assessment of dual-channel continuous self-report in VR, together with design considerations for such interfaces in future affective-VR research.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology

title: Exploring Cultural Competency in Palliative Nursing Education Using AI-Powered Virtual Agents in VR: An Exploratory Study
abstract: Cultural and spiritual values can shape end-of-life decisions, family roles, and communication, making culturally responsive communication an important part of palliative nursing care. Virtual reality (VR) can offer an immersive setting for practicing conversations involving cultural and emotional concerns. We developed a VR simulation featuring an AI-powered family-member agent in a Hindu end-of-life care scenario and conducted an exploratory study with ten undergraduate nursing students. Conversation logs and interviews were analyzed to examine students’ experiences and interaction patterns. Participants valued opportunities for cultural exposure and family communication practice, while noting limitations in conversational timing. These exploratory findings suggest that VR-based simulations may complement existing educational approaches to culturally sensitive palliative nursing care.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology

title: Two Billion Stories: Scaling Empathy for Conflict-Affected Populations Through Conversational AI and Embodied Immersion
abstract: Globally, an estimated two billion people inhabit conflict-affected regions, underscoring an urgent imperative to develop psychologically informed educational interventions that address the emotional and cognitive sequelae of armed conflict. This study examines the convergent application of immersive virtual reality (VR) and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as a novel pedagogical framework for cultivating cognitive empathy and emotional resilience in conflict-affected populations. In a pilot study, fifteen participants (N = 15) engaged with immersive VR environments via Meta Quest 2 headsets, navigating simulated conflict scenarios situated in a classroom, hospital, and urban setting through naturalistic locomotion while receiving narrative contextualization. Subsequently, participants interacted with agentic virtual humans powered by large language models (LLMs), which embodied first-person lived experiences of military conflict through dynamic, naturalistic dialogue. We investigate how the synergistic integration of immersive spatial presence and interactive GenAI-mediated narrative can facilitate perspective-taking, enhance empathic accuracy, and strengthen psychological resilience. Preliminary findings contribute a theoretically grounded, technology-enhanced framework for conflict education and trauma-informed psychosocial support.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology

title: Shared View, Different Readings: Human–AI Alignment in Place Interpretation for XR Agents
abstract: AI agents in smart glasses and XR devices may share users’ views yet interpret places differently. In this study, we compared interpretations from 12 participants and Gemini 3.1 Pro across twelve places using matched field-of-view recordings. Compared with disagreement among humans, human–AI gaps were larger for place meaning and important cues; no additional gap was detected for place function or activity contexts. AI ratings tracked human patterns across scenes but varied less and showed little correspondence with individual differences within the same scene. These findings position functional judgments as tentative defaults but call for greater care with place meanings, cues, and individual impressions.
journal: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology

title: DeltaBox: Millisecond-Scale Sandbox Checkpoint and Rollback for Stateful AI Agents
abstract: Emerging LLM-powered AI agent workloads, such as test-time tree search and reinforcement learning (RL), require high-frequency state exploration, relying on rapid checkpoint/restore (C/R) of the complete sandbox state, including files and process state. Existing mechanisms duplicate the entire state, causing hundreds of milliseconds to seconds of latency per C/R, which severely bottlenecks deep search and large-scale fan-outs. We observe that consecutive sandbox states between checkpoints differ only marginally. Therefore, instead of full duplication, a sandbox should only duplicate the changes between consecutive checkpoints (Key Insight), yet the lack of OS support makes this hard to realize. We propose a new OS-level abstraction, DeltaState, that delivers change-based C/R for agents through co-designed OS mechanisms. First, DeltaFS checkpoints file state by freezing the writable layer and inserting a new one, turning updates into copy-on-write and rollback into a layer switch. Second, DeltaCR quickly restores process state by forking from a frozen template process. A coordinator pairs the two so each checkpoint is one consistent (filesystem, memory) state. Building on these mechanisms, we present DeltaBox, an agent sandbox with millisecond-level C/R. On SWE-bench, DeltaBox hides its checkpoint work (10.83 ms) under inference and rolls back in a mean 1.86 ms, with the same warm-template fork driving low-cost RL rollout fan-out. DeltaBox is open-sourced at https://github.com/delta-box.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGOPS Annual Technical Conference

title: A Novel AI-Native GPU Kernel Programming Language for Autonomous Kernel Tuning
abstract: Autonomous LLM-driven kernel tuners have proliferated in 2025–2026, yet none produces kernels that match vendor libraries on the operators those libraries target, such as cuBLAS GEMM or cuSPARSELt sparse GEMM on Hopper GPUs. Two critical gaps explain this ceiling. First, every existing system tunes parameters within a human-supplied skeleton, so the agent cannot explore architectural alternatives such as warp specialisation, pipeline topology, or persistence mode. Second, the programming substrates these systems rely on impose compounding obstacles: large per-iteration token footprints, coupled code sites that fan a single structural change into many scattered edits, and absent compile-time feedback when a configuration is infeasible. This paper presents the first AI-native GPU kernel programming language, co-designed with AI tuning to close both gaps. In a six-DSL comparison on the same agent, H800 GPU, and iteration budget, our approach is the only programming substrate whose AI-tuned kernels consistently outperform vendor libraries, averaging 1.23 × across cuBLAS, CUTLASS, and cuSPARSELt on 95 production shapes. Trajectory analysis shows that the breakthroughs stem from structural kernel discoveries (warp specialisation, pipeline staging, TMA) rather than parameter search alone, enabled by two co-design axes. Syntax–context co-design makes structural edits practical: decoupled primitives yield the fewest code sites per feature, cutting the token footprint 1.6 × below equal-expressiveness DSLs and raising compile pass@1 to 85.7% (95.6% pass@5). Compiler–harness co-design amplifies this through compile-time pruning and structured diagnostics, sustaining 82.1% pass@1 on dynamic-shape kernels (Triton 48%) and 82.3% under moderate-capacity models where competing DSLs collapse (Triton 65.8%).

title: Choreographing Suspicion: Staging Legible Embodied AI Deception
abstract: Unfolding Myth in Motion is an installation where nine language-model agents move through an Unreal Engine maze under partial observation. Visitors compare live views, replays, generated evidence panels, and judgment screens routed by a Supervisor. The work asks how proximity, delay, disappearance, and separated viewpoints become evidence of deception. Here, legible deception describes a public attribution produced through spatial trace, media framing, and procedural judgment, not access to hidden intention. A representative reconstruction follows co-presence as it becomes accusation while cause remains unsettled. The paper argues that evidence should remain comparable with its source traces and viewpoints.
journal: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Art Papers

title: Internal Marketing and Service‐Oriented Organizational Citizenship Behavior Among Medical and Nursing Staff in Nursing Homes
abstract: Introduction This study examines the association between internal marketing and service‐oriented organizational citizenship behavior among medical and nursing staff in eldercare institutions and investigates the mediating roles of emotional labor and care‐giving workload. Design A three‐wave time‐lagged survey design. Methods This study included 515 medical and nursing staff from 14 nursing homes in Beijing. Nursing homes were initially selected through random sampling, and data were collected using online self‐report questionnaires. Structural equation modeling and response surface methodology were used to test the hypotheses and examine interaction effects. Results Internal marketing had a significant positive effect on service‐oriented organizational citizenship behavior among medical and nursing staff in nursing homes. Significant indirect effects were observed through both dimensions of emotional labor (surface acting and deep acting). In contrast, the indirect effect through care‐giving workload was not significant, although workload was negatively associated with service‐oriented organizational citizenship behavior. Response surface analysis further revealed a significant curvilinear pattern along the line of incongruence between internal marketing and care‐giving workload. Further response surface analysis indicated a nonlinear joint effect of internal marketing and care‐giving workload on service‐oriented organizational citizenship behavior, with an inverted U‐shaped pattern along the line of incongruence. Conclusion This study broadens the understanding of service‐oriented organizational citizenship behavior among medical and nursing staff in nursing homes by considering employees’ emotional regulation and work demands alongside internal marketing. By distinguishing the indirect associations involving emotional labor from the nonlinear joint relationship involving care‐giving workload, it offers a more differentiated perspective on the association between organizational support and discretionary service behavior. Implication for Nursing Management Nursing home administrators and nursing managers should strengthen internal marketing through effective communication, staff recognition, and professional development opportunities. Emotional support and emotion‐regulation training may help medical and nursing staff manage care‐related emotional demands. Regular workload assessments, appropriate staffing, and reasonable task allocation may further help managers tailor internal marketing practices to employees’ work demands and foster service‐oriented organizational citizenship behavior.

title: Redefining Urban Agriculture Promotion in China: A Communication-Centered Model for Cultural Governance
abstract: Urban agriculture (UA) has traditionally been framed through the functionalist lenses of food security and ecological sustainability. However, such models – largely derived from the developed economies – do not fully address China’s unique urban-rural structure and rich agrarian heritage. This study identifies an underexplored opportunity to connect production-oriented narratives with the emotional and cultural needs of urban residents. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a localized communication-centered model for UA in China. Grounded in the Communicative Cities framework – which conceptualizes the city as a communicative medium of “urbanity” (chengshi xing) – and Communication Infrastructure Theory (CIT), this model establishes UA as a vital form of communicative infrastructure. The framework is built upon three pillars: 1. The Reconstruction of the “Agrarian Imaginary”: Utilizing traditional wisdom – such as seasonal awareness and the ethics of labor – to foster “spiritual cultivation” and restore the emotional “warmth” of the city. 2. Digital Meso-Infrastructure: Leveraging platforms like WeChat and Douyin to foster integrated storytelling networks that connect micro-experiences of the soil to macro-level urban policy. 3. Cultural Governance: Positioning UA as a mechanism for building collective efficacy and social resilience. Importantly, the research highlights UA’s role as a material anchor of truth and reality in an era dominated by artificial intelligence and virtual simulations. By providing a tangible, “unskippable” biological reality, UA serves as a necessary counterweight to digital acceleration. Ultimately, this study advocates for a transcultural synthesis that redefines UA not merely as a site of production, but as a medium of “grounded truth,” fostering a harmonious balance between tradition, modernity, and the human experience in the digital age.

title: Morphological Evaluation and Multivariate Analysis of Fruit Traits in Capsicum annuum L. Genotypes for Breeding Applications
abstract: Capsicum annuum L. is an economically important vegetable crop, and along with the fact that the characterization of Romanian germplasm is essential for broadening the genetic base available to breeding programs, were the base of the present investigation. This study evaluated fruit morphology in 35 C. annuum genotypes representing four horticultural types (gogoșar-round red pepper, bell, kapia and chili pepper), obtained from the Plant Genetic Resources Bank in Buzău, Romania, and grown in a greenhouse at the Horticultural Research Station of UASVM Cluj-Napoca. Genotypes differed significantly within each horticultural type. ‘L78 A1’ had significantly heavier (197.57 g) and longer (98.67 mm) fruits compared with the other gogoșar genotypes studied; 'Savuros' had the heaviest and widest fruits among kapia genotypes (140.72 g; 73.72 mm); ‘L66’ had the widest fruits among chili genotypes (43.24 mm), whereas ‘Royal’, ‘Fideluță’ and ‘Halep’ had the most elongated fruits (L/D 7.96–10.28). Fruit weight and diameter were strongly correlated (r = 0.951), and the first two principal components explained 92.92% of the total variation, separating fruit size from fruit elongation. Hierarchical clustering grouped genotypes mainly by fruit size and did not fully follow the horticultural classification. The results highlight contrasting fruit phenotypes within the collection and identify genotypes that will be subject to further agronomic evaluation as part of breeding programs.
journal: Bulletin of University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine Cluj-Napoca. Horticulture

title: Ways to Develop Protection and Protection of Geographical Indications of Agricultural Products in China and Russia (Using the Example of Chinese Cuisine)
abstract: The article analyzes the protection systems of geographical indications in the People’s Republic of China and the Russian Federation, as well as the specifics of registration of geographical indications in relation to culinary dishes. The authors explore the possibility of obtaining legal protection of Chinese cuisine in the territory of the Russian Federation. The general trends and specific features of the legal protection of geographical indications are identified, and its relationship with the protection of other types of means of individualization is investigated. The authors conclude that the existing geographical indication protection system in China is mainly focused on agricultural products, while the mechanisms of legal protection of geographical indications used in relation to semi-finished products are still insufficiently regulated. To solve this problem, it is proposed to create a multi-level system for identifying geographical indications in relation to processed agricultural products, implement a differentiated system of legal protection depending on the share of raw materials in the market and the degree of technology concentration, establish a transparent labeling mechanism for basic raw materials, use digital technologies in the area of legal protection of geographical indications, strengthen interregional and interdepartmental supervision, promote unification of standards and integration with international procedures.
journal: Legal Science in China and Russia

title: Improvement of Working Capacity of Disks of Ploughshares of Grain Seeders by Welding a Repair Part
abstract: BACKGROUND: During operation, the disks of the ploughshares of grain seeders experience severe friction against the soil, which leads to their active abrasive wear, a decrease in the quality of sowing and yield of grain crops. In this regard, the failure of disks due to wear is decisive and requires frequent restoration of working condition. AIM: evaluation of efficiency of recovery of ploughshare disks by welding of repair part with further electromechanical hardening. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A method and a device are developed for welding a repair part in the form of ring fragments to ploughshare disks with wear along a diameter of 24 mm and more. Welding type, electrode selection, welding modes and repair part material are substantiated on the basis of multi-criteria approach on technical and economic assessment, manufacturability, criteria of modes and strength. A comparative assessment of experimental and serial disks for wear resistance was carried out by bench tests with modeling of operating conditions of disk ploughshares. Control of test parameters - change in the outer diameter, thickness, chamfer length, grinding angle and hardness of the disc material over the test period, equivalent to an average work volume of about 650 hectares. RESULTS: The effect of increasing the operability of the working zone of the disks by welding a repair part with subsequent electromechanical hardening is achieved. The multi-criteria approach when welding repair parts ensured uniform hardness in the zone of the seam and the main material of the restored disk. As a result, the wear resistance after restoration and hardening of worn discs compared to commercially available ones increases by 20.0... 25.0%. Analysis of the results showed a significant effect of welding a repair part with subsequent electromechanical hardening on increasing wear resistance for all evaluated parameters. CONCLUSION: Comparison of the wear of the ploughshare disks during bench tests with the data in operation showed that at an average operating time of 650 hectares, the increase in the durability of the restored hardened disks averages 22.5%, which is equivalent to processing 146 hectares. The technical and economic assessment of the introduction of welding of the repair part with the subsequent electromechanical strengthening of the ploughshare discs shows a decrease in specific operating costs per hectare when using repaired discs by an average of 25.0%.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Deep Learning Framework for Leaf Disease Prediction and Classification
abstract: Recognising plant leaf diseases from images is difficult because symptoms of different diseases often look alike, and expert inspection is not always available to growers. This paper presents a hybrid quantum deep learning framework that predicts both the plant species and the disease of a leaf image in a single pass. An ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 backbone extracts a high-dimensional feature vector, which a small projection reduces to four values that drive a four-qubit variational quantum circuit built from angle embedding and strongly entangling layers. The resulting Pauli-Z expectation values are concatenated with the classical features and passed to separate plant and disease classification heads. The model is compared with a MobileNetV2-only baseline on an identical stratified train–test split covering six crops and twenty disease and healthy classes. The hybrid model scores higher than the baseline on accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score for both tasks, although the margins are modest and come from a single split. The framework is also deployed as a Flask web application that adds blur and leaf validation, leaf segmentation, Grad-CAM explanations and disease-management guidance. The results are therefore presented as preliminary evidence of the value of a compact quantum feature stage rather than a definitive advantage.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Digital Transformation in Shariah-Compliant Agri-Fintech: A Case Study of The Bagh E-Platform
abstract: Agricultural finance in developing markets faces systemic bottlenecks, including collateral dependencies, information asymmetry, and a lack of Shariah-compliant alternatives. Grounded in the Three-Dimensional Fintech Framework and Agency Theory, this study employs a qualitative, desk-based documentary single-case study design to evaluate how the digital architecture of the Bagh-e platform modernizes traditional ethical contracts. The findings demonstrate that Bagh-e automates classical risk-sharing and asset-backed instruments, specifically Salam (forward sales) for working capital and Murabahah (cost-plus) for physical inputs, by integrating cloud databases, predictive AI risk engines, and closed-loop digital voucher routing. This infrastructure satisfies constructive possession (qabd) requirements and systematically mitigates principal-agent conflicts, including moral hazard and greenwashing, without requiring physical property collateral. Ultimately, this study demonstrates how digital agri-fintech aligns with the objectives of Shariah (Maqasid al-Shariah) and Bank Negara Malaysia’s Value-Based Intermediation (VBI) framework, harmonizing commercial viability with social equity and ecological resilience.

title: METHODS FOR CONTROLLING HARDWARE RESOURCE USAGE BY AUTONOMOUS SOFTWARE AGENTS IN MULTI-TENANT CLUSTER ENVIRONMENTS: REVIEW OF APPROACHES AND GAP ANALYSIS
abstract: This study presents a systematic review of methods for controlling hardware resource usage by autonomous software agents in multi-tenant cluster environments, based on 25 sources (2020–2026) selected via the Kitchenham methodology across six search rounds in Google Scholar, arXiv, USPTO, Espacenet, IEEE Xplore, and ACM Digital Library. A chronology of resource control technologies (2007–2026) is presented, from cgroup v1/v2 to eBPF subsystem evolution, agent architectures, and EU regulatory requirements. Four categories of approaches are examined: cgroup v2 limits, application-layer network policies, eBPF instrumentation at the OS kernel level, and cloud platform APIs. A detailed technical analysis of seven eBPF components is provided, being the category closest to solving the problem. A comparative analysis of 14 systems across five criteria (Ring-0 enforcement, zero-gap update, proactive verification, cryptographic attestation, and control-plane protection) against NIS2, DORA, and EU AI Act requirements reveals three structural gaps: absence of zero-gap configuration updates in Ring-0 systems for autonomous agents, absence of a proactive oracle interface for agent action verification, and absence of architectures combining Ring-0 enforcement with a cryptographically verifiable audit chain. The identified gaps define the directions for further research.

title: Constraint Based Diagnosis and Recovery Assessment for Interconnected Chemical Processes
abstract: Diagnosis and recovery in an interconnected process require compatible representations of fault evidence and feasible interventions. We specify a constraint-based architecture, Constraint-based Diagnosis and Recovery (CDDR), that uses a signed process model to generate and rank diagnostic candidates and a steady-state model to assess recovery options. Inclusion-minimal diagnoses are distinguished from minimum-cardinality candidates, and recovery feasibility is treated as an operational assessment rather than a test of whether a diagnosis is true. A reported synthetic campaign comprises an eight-unit plant, 18 measured variables, 16 constraints and 1,000 episodes across five seeds. Reported top-1 unit-plus-fault-type accuracy is 0.573 for CDDR, 0.475 for univariate threshold monitoring, 0.246 for causal reachability and 0.149 for Principal Component Analysis (PCA) contribution analysis. CDDR has a reported false-alarm fraction of 0.015. Recovery validity is reported as 0.5556 for CDDR, 0.3788 for an alarm-driven comparator and 0.8430 for an oracle, with different scoring denominators. These are descriptive results pending verification of episode records, scoring rules and analysis code. CDDR performs poorly on fouling drift (top-1 0.011) and has the lowest accuracy at doubled observation noise (0.033). The campaign does not validate optimal intervention selection, transient safety, performance on the Tennessee Eastman (TE) process or industrial deployment.

title: Fruit Nutrient-Based Classification of Selected Food Crops using Bayesian Multilayer Perceptron Algorithm
abstract: Research on machine learning has focused primarily on the ability to recognise fruit and identify diseases, but there has been little work done on the classification of nutrients. The traditional approaches to fruit classification are based on physical features of fruit, primarily size, shape, color and texture, and little emphasis is placed on nutritional composition. The study is intended to: present an intelligent and automated nutrient-based fruit classification approach that will aid in healthy dietary decisions, precision agriculture and fruits recommendation systems. The main concerns of this study are the classification of fruit nutrient aggregates by utilizing a Bayesian Multilayer Perceptron (BMLP) model which is expected to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of fruit classification based on nutrients. The system developed gets the fruits datasets from the kaggle datasets repository, which includes vitamin, minerals, carbohydrate, protein, fat, dietary fibre, moisture and energy values. It then will be subjected to a pre-processing called Histogram Equalization to enhance nutrients contents and extract relevant features. The extracted features are used for fruit nutrient aggregates classification by using a Bayesian Multilayer Perceptron. To measure the effectiveness of the model, it is evaluated in terms of Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score. The result yielded an accurate performance to the adopted Machine learning used on this research. Bayesian probability theory is incorporated into the model, which is performed excellently in terms of improving the classification accuracy and handling the uncertainty of nutrient patterns well and outperforms conventional classification techniques.

title: Explainable Deep Learning for Prickly Pear Cladode Condition Classification: Reproducible Evaluation and Mobile Deployment
abstract: Prickly pear (Opuntia ficus-indica) cladodes may exhibit physiological differences, abiotic injuries, and tissue deterioration that can affect crop management and product quality. However, their visual assessment is commonly based on manual inspection and may be subjective, particularly when different conditions exhibit similar surface characteristics. This study presents a deep learning framework for multiclass visual classification using RGB images, with emphasis on reproducible evaluation, mobile deployment, and Grad-CAM interpretability. A dataset comprising 1328 regions of interest (ROIs) extracted from 78 field-acquired photographs was organized into five categories: healthy young and mature cladodes (SANV and SANP), early and advanced fertilizer-associated injury (CAT and CAA), and rot and tissue deterioration (PUD). Four convolutional architectures were evaluated using photograph-disjoint partitions and five training repetitions, complemented by ablation experiments, hyperparameter optimization, and statistical comparisons. MobileNetV2 achieved the highest mean accuracy (81.20±1.57%), F1-score (75.84±1.61%), and balanced accuracy (76.15±1.48%). However, photograph-level bootstrap confidence intervals did not establish a clear F1-score advantage over MobileNetV3Small. Ablation experiments demonstrated the importance of pretrained representations and the benefits of online augmentation, whereas Hyperopt did not improve average classification performance. TensorFlow Lite FP16 reduced MobileNetV2 storage requirements to 4.31 MiB while largely preserving predictive performance. On a Samsung SM-A156U smartphone, MobileNetV2 FP16 achieved a median inference latency of 26.59 ms, compared with 8.21 ms for MobileNetV3Small FP16. Grad-CAM provided qualitative visualizations of correct and incorrect predictions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of mobile-assisted visual classification under the evaluated acquisition conditions, while further validation across independent plants, locations, and seasons remains necessary.

title: HTRNet: Hierarchical Temporal-Relation Refinement Network for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting requires modeling both variable-specific temporal patterns and inter-variable relations, including dependencies shared across samples and interactions that vary with the input. In this paper, we propose a Hierarchical Temporal-Relation Refinement Network (HTRNet) for multivariate time series forecasting. HTRNet sequentially learns variable-specific latent representations and models inter-variable relations from the resulting residuals within each refinement layer. The framework supports both single-layer and multi-layer configurations; when multiple layers are used, the updated residual representations are propagated to subsequent layers for further refinement. In addition, a Learnable Static Relation Matrix (LSRM) learns sample-independent relation weights among variables, while a Dynamic Compensation Module (DCM) uses sample-specific inter-variable interactions to enhance the final residual representation and generate a compensation prediction. The final forecast combines the layer-wise predictions with the DCM output. Extensive experiments are conducted on widely used benchmark datasets, including ETT, Weather, Electricity, Traffic, and Solar-Energy, across multiple forecasting horizons. Averaging the relative reductions against the best baseline for each dataset and metric yields improvements of 2.01% in MSE and 4.83% in MAE. These gains vary across datasets and forecasting horizons. On Traffic, HTRNet achieves the lowest average MAE but has a higher average MSE than DeepBooTS, iTransformer, and CASA.

title: Stochastic Chance-Constrained Bilevel Optimization for Electric Vehicle Charging Station Integration and Reserve Provision: A Framework for Smart Energy Management
abstract: This paper proposes a stochastic chance-constrained bilevel optimization framework for electric vehicle charging station (EVCS) integration and reserve provision, using a single-bus equivalent of a smart distribution system for coordinated day-ahead energy and reserve-capacity scheduling. The upper level minimizes the distribution system operator’s (DSO) operating cost, while the lower level minimizes the parking lot operator’s (PLO) own net operating cost by scheduling EV-fleet charging, discharging, and reserve-capacity provision under uncertainty in response to given economic signals from the DSO. The framework jointly considers renewable-generation forecast errors, uncertain load demand, and the time-varying availability of a heterogeneous electric vehicle (EV) fleet. Renewable forecast errors contribute to reserve requirements, while normally distributed arrival and departure times determine hourly connection probabilities for each vehicle category. The aggregation of vehicle connection states within each category motivates a Gaussian approximation of category availability. Conservative availability is calculated for each vehicle category at the prescribed confidence level and aggregated to derive time-varying EVCS power and energy limits and the reserve margin associated with EV availability. A load demand chance constraint yields the corresponding risk-adjusted demand and associated load uncertainty margin. The operating-cost objective also accounts for battery degradation. The bilevel model is transformed into a mathematical program with equilibrium constraints (MPEC) using the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions and subsequently reformulated as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) through Big-M linearization. The framework is evaluated over a 24 h horizon on three test systems comprising 3 to 80 distributed generators and 260 to 1100 EVs. Across the examined confidence levels, EVCS reserve provision reduces operating cost by 1.7 to 7.7%, while higher confidence levels increase scheduling costs.

title: Proteomics Reveals Stress-Related Proteins in the Embryonic Axis of Chickpea Sprouts Grown Under Green and Red LED Light
abstract: Stress-related proteins are overexpressed in plants under adverse growth conditions, helping them to survive. The identification and quantification of these proteins are limited in non-model organisms. Furthermore, the high concentration of storage proteins commonly found in seeds increases the difficulty of studying them. Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) is one of the most consumed legumes worldwide. Nevertheless, the proteins implicated in stress response have not been explored sufficiently in this organism. Light-emitting diode (LED) light has been used to improve crop quality for a long time; however, the stress-related proteins produced under different light wavelengths remain a major gap. This study aimed to identify how the proteins of the chickpea embryonic axis grown under green and red light at 275 µmol·m−2·s−1 are affected. Stress-related differentially expressed proteins (DEPs; |log2 fold change (FC)| > 1 and Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted p-value < 0.05) under green high (GH) and red high (RH) light were identified using proteomics along with deep learning. Two controls were used, control sun (CS) and control dark (CD). Cysteine was the most enriched amino acid under CD and GH (not significant under RH). Moreover, the FTIR amide I profile of the alkali-extracted protein fraction showed significant differences between treatments only in the intermolecular β-sheet, α-helix and high-frequency β components. Twenty stress-related DEPs were identified among the proteins identified at a false discovery rate (FDR) ≤ 1% at both precursor and protein levels; the highest concentration of them was found under red light, while the lowest was under control sun (CS). Proteins were classified into antioxidant defense, protein folding, chaperones and heat shock proteins (HSPs), dehydrins and late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins, redox homeostasis, and other stress-related proteins. These results suggest that red and green LED light modulate stress-related proteins in the embryonic axis of chickpea sprouts; however, their relevance to nutritional quality remains to be evaluated.

title: From Microdata to Macro Forecasts: A Comparative Study of Aggregation Strategies and Benchmark Models in Social Protection Spending
abstract: Does access to transaction-level records affect which forecasting method public-finance analysts should choose? To answer this question, we compare four aggregation strategies and a structural one applied to a short, highly seasonal time series of child-benefit payments: direct-aggregate, bottom-up, data-enrichment, and minimum-trace reconciliation. Our application concerns monthly child-benefit expenditure in Republika Srpska (Bosnia and Herzegovina), where we have approximately a hundred observations of total payments, but more than a million observations of individual payments. We also consider four different ways to deal with the recurring near-zero observations typical of administrative payment data. Under an expanding-window design, where each model can only use information available at the time of each forecast origin, exponential smoothing attains the lowest error across every treatment, though once the overlapping blocks and multiple testing are accounted for, it is statistically indistinguishable from minimum-trace reconciliation and several other benchmarks. Enrichment with microdata-derived features offers no advantage once those features are restricted to information known in advance, and machine-learning methods do not outperform the benchmarks; the treatment of the near-zero observations is as consequential for measured accuracy as the choice of forecasting method. The administrative microdata nonetheless prove valuable in a different way: an entitlement-basis (accrual) series reconstructed from them is far smoother than the cash series, suggesting that their main contribution may lie in defining what is measured rather than in feeding machine-learning models; we examine this accrual view, and its limitations, in an appendix. Overall, on short, strongly seasonal public-finance series, well-established benchmarks remain hard to beat, and additional data changes which object is measured rather than improving the cash forecast itself, unless it carries genuinely forward-looking information.

title: Systems Biology and Network Modeling of Lipid Metabolism in Brassica juncea: A Roadmap for Precision Oil Engineering
abstract: Brassica juncea (Indian mustard) is an economically important oilseed crop, but high erucic acid in traditional seed oils and elevated glucosinolates in seed meal remain important quality-improvement targets. Its allotetraploid genome, developmental regulation, and environmental responses complicate the prediction and engineering of lipid-related traits. This narrative review synthesizes experimentally supported findings on fatty acid biosynthesis, triacylglycerol assembly, and genetic regulation in B. juncea, and distinguishes these findings from evidence transferred from Arabidopsis thaliana, Brassica napus, and soybean. We examine available genomic and multi-omics resources, gene co-expression and regulatory network inference, constraint-based metabolic modeling, and strategies for combining these approaches with genome editing and genomic prediction. Although individual lipid-associated genes and seed traits have been characterized, a comprehensively validated, seed-specific, genome-scale lipid metabolic model for B. juncea remains unavailable. We therefore propose a staged roadmap encompassing developmental multi-omics sampling, homoeolog-aware network reconstruction, model calibration, independent validation, targeted perturbation, and multi-environment field testing. This evidence-led framework could help prioritize robust targets for improving fatty acid composition and seed oil performance without assuming that computationally inferred interactions are experimentally established.

title: An Altitude-Conditioned Spectral–Spatial Transformer for Reliable Cross-Altitude Crop Classification from Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Hyperspectral Imagery
abstract: Crop maps from unmanned aerial vehicle hyperspectral imagery increasingly guide site-specific field decisions, yet the classifiers behind them are almost always trained and evaluated at a single flight altitude. Because operational height varies with weather, battery and airspace limits, the ground sampling distance changes and map accuracy silently degrades at unseen heights, an error rarely measured before maps are trusted. We quantify this cross-altitude reliability gap and identify which design choices contain. Using a public open-field archive of three vegetable crops (tomato, cabbage and eggplant) imaged at six nominal heights (20–100 m), we build a reproducible protocol that trains at 30 m and evaluates at five withheld heights; because trustworthy labels exist only at 30 m, evaluation uses spectral-angle pseudo-labels together with chance-corrected metrics and an independent manual-validation set. We propose an altitude-conditioned spectral–spatial transformer with resolution augmentation and self-supervised pretraining, and compare it against convolutional, transformer and domain-adversarial baselines over five seeds. The proposed model gives the most reliable transfer, reaching a Cohen's kappa of 0.21 against 0.11–0.14 for the baselines, the best result on every chance-corrected metric and across all five seeds, with the firm evidence resting on the 25–50 m band. This advantage is relative and chance-corrected rather than absolute. Because the archive carries no ground truth, evaluation is referenced to Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM) pseudo-labels, so the species-level model ranking is SAM-consistent and awaits field-plot confirmation. An adversarial invariance component leaves flight height fully decodable, so informing the model of the altitude, not enforcing invariance, drives the gain, and no model exceeds a majority-class predictor in overall accuracy. Altitude-robust monitoring cannot yet be assumed: surveys should fly at consistent, documented heights and report chance-corrected accuracy. We release the protocol, pseudo-labeling pipeline, manual-validation set and all code.

title: Decision support system for new student selection at railako vocational technical school using the TOPSIS method
abstract: The student admission selection process is a crucial stage in ensuring the quality of education, yet it is often conducted manually, leading to inefficiency and subjectivity. This study aims to develop a Decision Support System (DSS) for new student selection at Railako Vocational Technical School using the TOPSIS method. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and literature study, while system development employed the SDLC Waterfall model with PHP and MySQL implementation. The system evaluates candidates based on multiple criteria, including academic test scores, interview results, distance, and age. The results show that the TOPSIS method successfully ranks candidates objectively, with preference values of 0.625 (A2), 0.509 (A1), and 0.034 (A3), where A2 is identified as the best alternative. The system improves selection efficiency and reduces subjectivity compared to manual methods. This study contributes by integrating TOPSIS into a web-based system and demonstrating its effectiveness in real-case student selection scenarios.

title: INTEGRATION OF INTELLIGENT AI AGENTS AND CRM SYSTEMS FOR PROACTIVE CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT IN TRANSPORT AND LOGISTICS
journal: ZBORNIK RADOVA ČETRDESET ČETVRTOG SIMPOZIJUMA O NOVIM TEHNOLOGIJAMA U POŠTANSKOM I TELEKOMUNIKACIONOM SAOBRAĆAJU – POSTEL 2026

title: AI in Agricultural Pest Management: A Critical Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence is widely promoted as a solution for automating pest monitoring and reducing crop losses, but many models fail when moved from laboratory conditions to real farms. This review critically examines AI application across three sensing platforms i.e., retrofitted sticky traps with computer vision, drones and rovers for distinguishing mite damage from drought stress and acoustic sensors for detecting wood borers hidden inside trees. This review highlights that while deep learning reliably counts whiteflies and codling moths in controlled settings, performance collapses under variable lighting, dust, dew and occlusion. The core problems are rarely discussed in the literature; for instance, training datasets are often labeled by non-specialists, leading to systematic misclassification, models suffer from domain shift over a single growing season and the black box nature of neural networks erodes trust among farmers and regulators. False positives drive unnecessary pesticide use while false negatives cause crop loss. To the best of current knowledge, AI systems generally struggle to recognize a novel invasive pest in its first year of arrival. Through case studies from China, California and Brazil, it is demonstrated that trust depends on explainability and field validation, not on benchmark accuracy. This study proposes a tiered integration into existing IPM workflows. AI-only alerts, remote human checks and field visits. Unlike previous reviews that focus on model accuracy, this review critically examines why most AI fails in the field and proposes a tiered, human-centered integration pathway.

title: From Smart Hives to Artificial Intelligence: A Bibliometric Analysis of Digital Beekeeping Research (2006–2026)
abstract: Digital technologies allow modern beekeepers to continuously and non-invasively monitor honey bee colonies. The integration of sensors, Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and smart hives has contributed to the rapid evolution of precision beekeeping as a new research area. However, a detailed evolution of the scientific evolution of beekeeping and its development themes is lacking. This study aimed to examine the global research landscape of digital beekeeping using bibliometric and scientific mapping approaches. Bibliographic records published between 2006 and 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and analyzed using Bibliometrix and VOSviewer. The analyses covered publication trends, leading countries, institutions, and authors, prolific journals, highly cited publications, keyword co-occurrence patterns, and thematic evolution. A total of 114 publications from 64 sources were identified, with scientific output reaching its highest level in 2025 after a strong increase after 2020. The USA, Latvia, and China were the most productive countries, with Latvia University of Life Sciences and Technologies being the most productive institution. Keyword and thematic analyses identified prominent themes related to precision beekeeping, IoT, machine learning, monitoring systems, and honey bees. Thematic evolution showed a gradual transition from conventional honey bee biology and environmental monitoring to AI-driven hive management, computer vision applications, acoustic monitoring, and intelligent high-level decision-support systems. Collectively, digital beekeeping has developed as a multidisciplinary field integrating apiculture, engineering, data science, and artificial intelligence, with increasing emphasis on predictive analytics, automated monitoring, and intelligent decision-support systems for sustainable colony management.
