title: Ordered Physics Mamba: A State–space Model for Vehicle Flow Field and Aerodynamic Force Prediction
abstract: The rapid and accurate prediction of vehicle flow field distributions and aerodynamic force coefficients is of great importance in aerodynamic design scenarios. The current deep learning-based surrogate models face three major challenges when handling large-scale irregular meshes: low computational efficiency, the absence of physics priors that are aligned with the dominant flow direction, and the tendency to lose high-frequency geometric details on the surface of the target body. Considering the above issues, the ordered physics Mamba (OP-Mamba) flow field prediction model is proposed in this work based on selective state–space sequence modeling. First, OP-Mamba clusters discrete point clouds into a compact set of physics-aware slices through adaptive soft assignment, thereby reducing the imposed computational burden. A spatial sorting mechanism based on the weighted geometric centroids of these slices is then introduced to reorder them along the principal flow axis. Second, combined with this reordering scheme, bidirectional Mamba scanning not only captures the downstream convective evolution process but also provides a direct backward path for incorporating the nonlocal pressure effects that are associated with the downstream wake structures, thereby efficiently extracting long-range dependencies. Finally, OP-Mamba uses a point cloud-domain residual compensation scheme in which feature mappings and skip connections are implemented in the original discrete space, thus mitigating the high-frequency geometric feature attenuation that is caused by slice-level dimensionality reduction. Extensive experiments conducted on three-dimensional (3D) industrial vehicle datasets (including Baidu CIKM and ShapeNet-Car) and the two-dimensional (2D) airfoil dataset (AirfRANS) demonstrate that OP-Mamba achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in both flow field reconstruction and macroscopic aerodynamic force prediction tasks. Additionally, it maintains competitive performance under physical-field noise augmentation during the training procedure and demonstrates its applicability to both 3D vehicle and 2D airfoil settings.

title: Score-Based Stochastic Closure Modeling via Offline Indirect Learning and Online Data Assimilation
abstract: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical deterministic closures. However, learning stochastic closures typically requires closure data that are difficult to obtain from measurements or often prohibitively expensive to compute using first-principles simulations. In this work, we develop a stochastic closure modeling framework that builds on score-based diffusion models, leveraging indirect offline training and online data assimilation without requiring the direct data of closures. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional turbulent flows demonstrate that indirect offline learning captures key closure statistics and improves predictions of system state. In addition, combining the learned closure with known physical dynamics leads to better generalization capability across different regimes than purely data-driven models that directly predict system state. Compared to standard data assimilation methods with a Gaussian assumption, the posterior-score assimilation better represents non-Gaussian features of the learned closure, and its combination with state-level data assimilation further improves prediction of the system state. The proposed framework enables stochastic closure modeling in realistic and challenging scenarios of complex dynamical systems in mechanics and engineering problems, where non-Gaussian statistics of model-form uncertainties are non-negligible (e.g., due to the nonlinearities of the system dynamics and/or the observations) and true closure data are not available, for both offline learning and online assimilation.

title: SPIKE-Accelerated Split-Bregman/ADMM Methods for Obstacle Problems and American Option Pricing under Jump-Diffusion Models
abstract: This paper presents a parallel split Bregman/alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) \cite{goldstein,tran} for obstacle problems and for the linear complementarity problems (LCPs) that arise in the pricing of American options under the Black--Scholes and Merton jump-diffusion \cite{merton} models. The auxiliary variable of ADMM decouples the inequality constraint from the differential operator, so that every iteration consists of a linear solve with a fixed banded matrix and a pointwise projection. The matrix is factorized once by the SPIKE algorithm \cite{spike}, as in the parallel direct approach of \cite{singh}, and reused in all iterations and time steps in a Fortran~90 MPI implementation. Convergence is proved by a Lyapunov functional for every positive augmentation parameter, for the symmetric obstacle problem and the non-symmetric option LCP alike, and the iterates do not depend on the number of processes. The method therefore needs a single factorization, no tuned relaxation parameter and only pointwise, perfectly parallel updates. One- and two-dimensional obstacle problems, the Black--Scholes call and American put, and European and American options under Merton's model are computed and compared with exact, closed-form, binomial and published values. In two dimension a speed-up of $3.92$ on four processes is obtained. It is also shown that the augmentation parameter has to be scaled to the diagonal of the time-stepping matrix when only a few inner iterations are used.

title: Exploration of Reinforcement Learning in Generative Recommendation Models
abstract: Traditional cascaded recommender systems balance accuracy and efficiency over large item spaces, but misaligned stage-wise objectives hinder end-to-end optimization. Generative recommendation unifies these stages in an autoregressive framework, providing a natural interface for reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize the entire generation process. However, directly applying RL often leads to unstable optimization and degraded recommendation quality. We revisit Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and other ratio-based objectives through a unified logit-gradient view. We identify three issues: (i) clipped surrogates create dead-gradient regions, under-utilizing samples; (ii) negative-advantage updates can become effectively unbounded as importance ratios grow, allowing a small subset of negatives to dominate optimization; and (iii) ratio-based control lacks sensitivity to absolute policy confidence, so updates on high-confidence cases may fail to vanish. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose \emph{Gradient-Bounded Policy Optimization} (GBPO), a simple objective with stop-gradient normalization that is simultaneously (a) fully gradient-active, (b) sign-symmetrically bounded for both positive and negative updates, and (c) explicitly confidence-weighted under current policy probabilities. This ensures that updates gracefully vanish for $π\!\to\!1$ positives and $π\!\to\!0$ negatives. Across the evaluated settings, GBPO achieves competitive recommendation performance with more stable training than competing RL methods.

title: Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Auroral Precipitations with Neural Fields
abstract: Auroras provide remote optical observations of energetic electrons precipitating into the upper atmosphere, and whose energy distribution encodes key information about large scale magnetospheric processes. Recovering the underlying electron precipitation field from ground-based camera images of auroras remains a challenging inverse problem. Existing auroral tomography techniques are often limited to simplified static settings, discrete spatial and energy grids, or strong assumptions on the electron energy spectrum. We propose to model the dynamic auroral electron precipitation field via a temporally conditioned neural network. The state of the precipitation field at each frame is represented by a per-frame latent code driven by learned discrete dynamics. A shared decoder maps horizontal positions and latent states to electron energy spectra. The predicted flux is converted to multi-wavelength volume emission rates and rendered into camera images accounting for delayed emissions. We evaluate the method on synthetic dynamic auroral sequences and real multi-view auroral videos, showing that the proposed representation produces temporally coherent precipitation reconstructions and image projections consistent with the observations.

title: Read Before You Fit: Text-Derived Constraints for Discovering Differential Equations from Noisy Biological Data
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used for scientific equation discovery. However, most existing methods are strongly data-driven and assume sufficiently clean and representative observations. This assumption is problematic in biological systems, where individual-level measurements are often sparse, noisy, heterogeneous, and expensive to obtain. While the underlying mechanisms are extensively described in scientific text, they are not explicitly used for the LLM based modeling of such systems. We introduce P2C, an agentic framework that translates textual descriptions of biological systems into a typed set of formal constraints, and use these constraints to restrict candidate ordinary differential equation (ODE) structures before numerical fitting. P2C consists of five stages: Text2Constraint extraction, ODE discovery, symbolic verification, parameter fitting, and model scoring. We evaluate P2C on four published ODE systems of acute inflammation and immune regulation, under clean and noisy observations. By progressively degrading the numerical evidence, we isolate when textual domain knowledge contributes beyond regression alone. Across the four systems, adding Text2Constraint reduces the worst form error from 1.397 to 0.499 on clean data and from 13.096 to 1.095 for data perturbed with Gaussian noise of $σ=0.1$; P2C also achieves lower form error and trajectory error than several LLM-based baselines over the tested noise range.

title: IANN: A Unified Framework for Equivariant InterAtomic Neural Networks with User-Friendly Implementation
abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy at a fraction of its cost, but the practical benefit is limited by software fragmentation: each state-of-the-art architecture is released as a separate codebase, with its own data format, configuration system, training loop and molecular-dynamics interface. Comparing two architectures on the same dataset, or moving a trained model into a production simulation, therefore requires substantial re-engineering. We introduce IANN (InterAtomic Neural Network), an open-source PyTorch framework that reimplements equivariant graph neural networks - PaiNN, NequIP, MACE, Allegro, EquiformerV2, EquiformerV3 and UMA - behind a unified data object, a unified trainer and a single deployment route, so that the architecture is a one-word change in a configuration dictionary. Forces, stresses and virials are obtained for every architecture from one analytic differentiation of the energy with respect to the edge vectors of the atomic graph, exact under periodic boundary conditions. Distributed training is configured automatically from the SLURM, PBS or MPI environment, so the same script runs unchanged from a workstation to a multi-node GPU allocation. Self-describing checkpoints serve directly as ASE calculators, as ensembles reporting uncertainties, or as TorchScript models run inside LAMMPS through bundled C++ pair styles with single- and multi-GPU inference. Trained on a common dataset of millions of structures, the architectures can be compared under identical conditions. We further release PaiNN foundation models trained on 41.9 million curated DFT structures from MPtrj, Alexandria, OMat24, MatPES, OC20, OC22, OC25, MPr2SCAN and MatPESr2SCAN, spanning the PBE, RPBE and r2SCAN functionals. Additionally, IANN provides an agent interface to facilitate integration with autonomous agents.

title: MAPS: A Multimodal Agentic Framework for POI Data Production Based on Crowdsourced Street-view Imagery
abstract: Point-of-interest (POI) databases support location-based services, yet urban changes quickly make their records stale and manual maintenance is costly. Crowdsourced street-view images provide timely visual evidence, but converting them into database actions requires separating multiple POIs and irrelevant text in each image, then resolving incomplete observations against ambiguous records. We study Street-view Image-based POI Data Production and propose MAPS, the first framework to integrate structured POI extraction with database maintenance from such imagery. MAPS contains two cascaded modules. SPICE progressively adapts a lightweight vision-language model to reconstruct and filter text, group entries belonging to the same POI, and classify their semantics and completeness. RIMA retrieves candidate records, performs evidence-grounded POI matching and attribute-level reasoning, and selectively acquires complementary visual, geospatial, or external-source evidence when necessary. In human-reviewed full-task evaluation, MAPS outperforms the strongest baseline by 21.8\%. MAPS has also been deployed in Kuaishou's large-scale POI production pipeline, reducing average processing time by 76.9\% relative to manual annotation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and practical value of MAPS for scalable POI maintenance.

title: Reasoning in the loop: antibody lead optimization by probing mechanism and measurement
abstract: Lab-in-the-loop systems, in which a model proposes molecules, automated assays measure their properties and the results retrain the model, are a popular approach to antibody lead optimization. These systems optimize for a specification defined with metrics computed from instrument signals, so their success depends on how well those metrics serve as proxies for the properties a drug candidate needs. When a metric is a poor proxy, neither a better model nor more data will fix it, and identifying the problem usually requires expert review. We report two campaigns run on BigHat Biosciences' Milliner platform, one on an anti-albumin nanobody (VHH) and one on an anti-mesothelin single-chain variable fragment (scFv), in which a research team and a general-purpose AI agent, Claude, brought scientific reasoning into the loop. Over seven rounds and about 1,010 design variants we built libraries from antibody lineage, structure and biophysics, and found from the raw curves that on each scaffold one thermal metric did not measure what its name implied. The libraries were built as controlled comparisons, so the results also show what each mutation contributes to each property. We fit a physical model of the curves, used it to choose metrics suited to each scaffold, and changed the experimental protocol, varying protein concentration and heating rate, to test the model against pre-registered predictions. Both leads improve on their parents in affinity, thermal stability and aggregation while improving or maintaining yield and purity.

title: Asking the right question is key to AI discovery in a chain of hypotheses
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) scientists pursue discovery through a chain of hypotheses, fitting candidate models to existing observations and often choosing experiments where those models disagree most. Yet when early data miss a narrow feature, model selection favors simple curves that agree across the unmea- sured gap, so disagreement-guided search has no reason to look where the new phenomenon lies. When we tested two frontier AI scientists, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1-Sol, across 32 closed-loop trials with a narrow peak omitted from the starting data, both sampled inside the peak region less often than random search. Surprisingly, the agent that followed model disagreement more closely missed the peak in all 32 trials, whereas discovery succeeded when experiments probed the unmeasured gap early and followed up across the anomaly. Asking the right question, rather than testing only where current models disagree, is therefore key to AI discovery in a chain of hypotheses.

title: Indication of demographic and epidemiological data on early-stage risks and long-term epidemic burden
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between age-specific cumulative infection burden and the probability of triggering a major outbreak in heterogeneous populations. We develop two modeling frameworks that incorporate empirical age-stratified contact matrices: a deterministic framework for deriving the final size relation and a stochastic framework based on a Continuous-time Markov chain epidemic model, for which a multi-type branching-process approximation is used to characterize early-stage outbreak risk. The framework is illustrated using empirical social contact data from Guangzhou, Foshan, and Zhuhai, China, under two disease-motivated scenarios representing COVID-19 and hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD). The illustrative analyses indicate that the relationship between cumulative infection burden and early-stage outbreak risk depends on both epidemiological characteristics and population contact patterns. In particular, age groups with the highest final attack rates do not necessarily have the highest probability of triggering a major outbreak. These findings highlight the complementary nature of the two measures and the value of considering both when assessing age-specific epidemic risks in practice.

title: When Facts Change, Which Decisions Break? Dependency-Aware Context Graphs for Agents
abstract: When an observed fact changes, an agent must identify and repair the decisions that depend on it while preserving unaffected outputs. We investigate the reliability-cost trade-off of field-level dependency graphs extracted from actual agent read traces. A controlled benchmark spans three executable workflow domains and four successive updates, with independent imperative and expression-based references. Across 120 workflows, two models and two repeated runs, we compare full recomputation, rolling summary memory, lexical retrieval, trace-extracted dependencies and verified dependency upper bounds. Trace-derived graphs reduce reviewed decisions and estimated total cost, but omitted alternative supports and missing repair context can reduce complete-plan correctness. Paired ablations isolate the effects of edge deletion, spurious edges, transitive propagation and context scope. An exploratory enhancement supplies the existing record ID/field directory during extraction without revealing unread values or reference edges. We evaluate this enhancement on 60 fresh workflows with two repeats per model. On this fresh set, the directory-aware graph matches observed full-context complete-plan correctness for gpt-6.1-sol (100%) with an estimated 4.0% total-cost reduction, but reaches only 84.8% versus 99.6% for gpt-6-luna. The results distinguish potential dependency impact from actual decision invalidity and show why selective repair must be evaluated with both executable correctness and full memory-processing cost. The evidence concerns explicit procedural workflows; broad real-world agent-memory generalization remains untested.

title: HBF-EventLab: A Discrete-Event Simulator for Studying Host-Device Coordination in High Bandwidth Flash
abstract: High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) combines NAND flash density with high-bandwidth accelerator connectivity, offering additional memory capacity for large language model inference. However, limited hardware availability makes it difficult to evaluate how host behavior and device resource constraints jointly affect HBF request processing. We present HBF-EventLab, an open-source, transaction-level discrete-event simulator based on the Open Compute Project HBF specification. HBF-EventLab connects host request dispatch, command admission, fragmented write assembly, read dispatch, NAND execution, and completion feedback within a shared event loop. It explicitly models distinct resource lifetimes and separates configurable scheduling policies from ordering and resource constraints, enabling controlled exploration of host-device coordination. Experiments show how resource limits, address interleaving, fragment arrival patterns, and scheduling policies affect write completion and request latency. The results highlight the need to consider resource limits and scheduling policies jointly, accounting for their interactions with write assembly and read eligibility. We also integrate HBF-EventLab with real GPU execution of Qwen3-0.6B, combining profiled GPU activity durations with simulated weight-access delays to estimate time to first token and time per output token, with logits and output tokens remaining bitwise identical to those from native GPU execution. HBF-EventLab provides a configurable foundation for studying HBF mechanisms, exploring scheduling policies, and assessing how HBF access delays affect application-level timing. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/sjtu-epcc/HBF-EventLab.

title: Illusion of Explainability: A Sanity Check for Spectral Band Attribution in Satellite Time-Series Crop Classification
abstract: Attribution methods are commonly validated through convergence across methods and consistency with domain knowledge, yet neither criterion establishes whether identified features are necessary for a task. This limitation is particularly relevant in multispectral remote sensing, where overlapping spectral information makes individual bands potentially substitutable. We investigate this gap in crop-type classification using GradientSHAP, Shapley sampling, and Occlusion on a U-TAE segmentation model trained on Sentinel-2 time series from the PASTIS benchmark. All three methods identify vegetation-sensitive spectral regions consistent with domain knowledge, while Shapley and Occlusion exhibit strong ordering sensitivity in deletion and insertion tests. However, these properties do not reliably predict retraining performance. Aggregate attribution consensus masks substantial per-class disagreement, with pairwise mean Spearman correlations ranging from 0.09 to 0.79. Models retrained from scratch using the five lowest-ranked bands perform comparably to or better than those using the five highest-ranked bands. Furthermore, attribution rankings from an independently trained model with identical configuration and seed identify a different top-five subset that yields better retraining performance. Analysis of all 252 five-band subsets reveals consistently low effective dimensionality (1.35 to 2.62), suggesting substantial spectral redundancy. These findings demonstrate that plausible and apparently faithful attribution rankings do not necessarily identify task-relevant bands for improved retrained performance, highlighting the limitations of band-level feature attribution in spectrally redundant input spaces.

title: HIVE-ECIA: Identity-Aware Historical Evidence Acquisition for Bandwidth-Efficient Multi-Object Tracking
abstract: Panoramic multi-object tracking (MOT) requires reliable identity association across a 360{\deg} field of view, yet bandwidth-constrained operation forces a trade-off between low-resolution (LR) identity ambiguity and costly high-resolution (HR) transmission. We propose HIVE-ECIA, an identity-aware framework that selectively retrieves historical HR evidence to recover fragmented identities without modifying detection boxes or the underlying tracker. An ECIA Base-Guided query policy determines when additional HR evidence is warranted; HIVE ranks historical LR observations to select an informative retrieval timestamp; and ECIA Full integrates the retrieved HR crop through learned gated fusion and conservative identity safeguards. We further introduce DualPano-MOT, a real-world dual-fisheye panoramic evaluation dataset featuring controlled pedestrian interactions, panorama-seam challenges, and occlusions, with model-assisted, manually verified tracking annotations. On held-out QuadTrack sequences and zero-shot DualPano-MOT, HIVE-ECIA improves identity association across four MOT trackers without tracker-specific retraining. Across these trackers, identity switches decrease by up to 21.8% and 23.4%, while the largest IDF1 gains reach 3.81 and 6.74 percentage points, respectively. Under an offline JPEG-based acquisition model, our framework reduces encoded data volume by 89.2% and 79.3% relative to continuous Full-HR acquisition.

title: Attribute or Abstain: Evaluating Evidence-Grounded Retrieval on the Low-Resource African Business Web
abstract: Retrieval-augmented systems that research companies are judged by how much they find, yet in markets where public evidence is sparse, a confident answer without support costs more than no answer. We introduce AfriBizClaims, a benchmark of 150 company-research queries across six African markets in English, French and Portuguese, including queries about fictitious companies that a correct system must decline. Each claim a system makes is judged against the page it cites by an AI judge, checked against a second AI judge from another model family and against two human annotators, and abstentions are scored against answerability labels. We compare BM25 over a pooled corpus, standard web retrieval-augmented generation, and a multi-step agent pipeline (Konexium V1), all using the same language model. The two simple baselines are well attributed: 98% of their judged claims are supported by the page they cite, and they decline every field of every fictitious company. Counting claims about a company other than the one asked about as errors, the agent pipeline's per-query precision is 68%, and it never answers a question about a named company correctly: it substitutes other firms, including for 5 of the 24 fictitious names, and it is the least stable between runs and the most expensive. In the pipeline we evaluated, more steps between the query and the evidence did not buy more grounded answers. We will release the queries, system outputs, labels and short evidence excerpts.

title: "Don't Leave the Task Unfinished": Persistence-Driven Violations under Quiet Oversight
abstract: LLM agents are increasingly given long, multi-step tasks to carry out, with the user reviewing little of what happens in between. Persistence, the tendency to keep working until a task is complete, is installed on purpose to improve performance on long tasks. Long-horizon tasks are typically complex, and the user's instruction can fall short of what the work actually requires, or conflict with the constraints the agent encounters in the task. We study what persistence does on long-horizon operations tasks that cannot be solved without breaking a documented constraint. We find that the agent pursues completion to the point of violating the constraint, and that a critically engaged user lowers the violation rate. Persistence takes violations from 29.2% to 58.3% across four models. Violations stay high wherever oversight goes quiet, whether the user is silent, assenting, or delegating with expressed trust. Only a questioning user, who asks for the basis of each action before allowing the next, brings the rate back to roughly the level measured without persistence. Practitioners should treat high persistence as a setting that carries a safety cost, and should recognize that the cost appears when oversight goes quiet. Safety here is better cast as a property of the human-AI pair than of the model alone. Project page: https://francis21c.github.io/quiet-oversight/

title: Equal Dose, Different Coverage:Tracing Rate and Duration in Image Editing
abstract: Benchmarks for scientific image editing test whether a model draws the outcome of a described process, leaving open which representations carry its errors and whether correcting them yields the right quantity. We study this question with an airbrush of fixed deposition profile, under which exchanging rate and duration preserves the dose and should preserve the endpoint, yet changes the edited coverage. Matched-norm activation patches across text positions and denoising stages show that, in distilled FLUX with Chinese prompts, representations at unchanged text positions (context) carry this discrepancy: early context transfers 3.51 of the 3.98 percentage-point (pp) signed route difference, against 0.09 pp for equal-norm updates at the two changed digits. Early image latents transmit native (unpatched) route differences across two FLUX configurations and OmniGen, while text-position effects depend on configuration. The trace predicts an intervention: share early context between routes while each retains its own digits. On independent English layouts, this reduces the distilled-FLUX absolute route gap from 1.13 to 0.60 pp, outperforms early digit sharing, and improves agreement more than in base FLUX under directly paired tests. Calibrated evaluation, which prescribes an area for each dose, separates this gain from accuracy: sharing the full prompt encoding produces identical route images with target errors of 8-16 pp, and stating the target percentage directly retains a compressed area response. Localization predicts a consistency gain on new layouts, and calibration measures the quantity error that agreement leaves unresolved.

title: Evaluating Near-Perfect Accuracy Claims in Machine-Learning-Based Leak Detection for Two-Phase Pipelines: A Condition-Blocked Audit
abstract: Reliable leak detection in gas-liquid two-phase pipelines is important for process safety, yet machine-learning studies frequently report near-perfect performance using evaluation protocols that may not represent deployment to unseen operating conditions. This study audits a pressure-based leak-detection model using condition-blocked leave-one-condition-out validation, in which the classifier is tested on a flow condition excluded from training. Accuracy decreased from 93.3% under within-condition evaluation to 59.1% across fifteen unseen-condition tests. Ablation analysis showed that most of this difference arose from the data-splitting protocol, with a smaller contribution from encoding operating conditions as model inputs. Under condition-blocked evaluation, the false-alarm and missed-detection rates increased to 34.1% and 10.2%, respectively, demonstrating that near-perfect reported accuracy did not translate into reliable operation at unseen flow conditions. The reduction persisted across all evaluated classifiers, indicating that it was caused by the evaluation design rather than a particular model architecture. Grouped evaluation of an independent acoustic pipeline dataset produced a comparable reduction toward chance-level performance. These findings show that validation units must represent the conditions encountered during deployment. Condition-blocked evaluation and explicit reporting of operational error rates are therefore necessary before machine-learning leak detectors can support process-safety decisions.

title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling
abstract: Day-ahead load forecasts set balancing reserves, including the energy a pumped-storage plant holds against forecast errors. Both depend on three effects that are usually modeled separately, namely the thermal inertia of buildings, which makes load lag temperature, structural breaks, which shift demand, and the long memory of forecast errors, which keeps them from cancelling out. We prove that averaging building responses over Cole-Cole distributed time constants yields a fractional temperature kernel with nonnegative weights exactly when its order is at most one. A Bayesian information criterion that ignores long memory selects spurious breaks with probability tending to one, so breaks and memory are estimated jointly, and an online break detector keeps its false-alarm rate below any prescribed level. Long memory also makes the required storage energy grow faster than the square root of the horizon, so a second-order cone program schedules reserves from the joint distribution of hourly errors. On New England and Mid-Atlantic data including the 2020 pandemic, the proposed framework improves on the best of ten benchmarks by 15.7% and 10.3% in mean absolute percentage error. Its reserves breach the storage energy limit on 4.1% and 8.5% of days, against 36.7% and 57.5% with error correlations ignored.

title: Autonomous Multi-modal Agents for ITOps Observability
abstract: ITOps observability products must integrate data from different tools and systems. We present ITOps Observability Studio, a multi-modal multi-agent system that orchestrates observability workflows through collaborative AI agents. Its three-tier architecture features inter-agent communication, specialized LLM-powered agents for data access, schema operations and visualization, and unified tool integration. The system supports natural language to GraphQL translation, GraphQL schema generation, schema mapping, trace data lifecycle management and multi-tool workflows for reliability engineering. Its agents are instrumented with agent analytics, so that their model and tool calls can be traced. We evaluate each agent on its own benchmark, scored against gold answers where they exist and by a model judge for schema mapping and chart quality. Query generation on a public benchmark and routing work well with a current open model, and the data lifecycle management agent solves most of its scenarios. The evaluation exposed defects that only appear when prompts, parsers and serving stacks are tested together, and we report them together with their fixes.

title: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
abstract: Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our extrapolation method bridges the 10-Hz visual estimation with 50-Hz controller, enabling asynchronous visual processing and policy execution. Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. Project page: https://movicproject.github.io/ .

title: Offline-First Quantized AI: Design and Evaluation of an On-Device Maternal-Health Assistant for Low-Connectivity Environments
abstract: Offline language models could extend access to maternal-health information where internet connectivity is unreliable, but deployment requires both clinically appropriate responses and feasible local execution. This study presents an offline Android assistant integrating ready-made quantized language models, a clinically validated local knowledge package, conversational context, and model-initiated local retrieval. Gemma 4 E2B and Qwen3.5 0.8B were compared across 45 conversations and 312 turns per configuration, including a dedicated offline agentic benchmark. Gemma achieved higher response-quality, context-retention, and safety scores; Qwen offered faster generation and lower memory use. Clinician assessment of 150 Gemma responses across nine clinical domains yielded a mean quality score of 3.80/4, with 147 responses meeting the acceptance criterion. A paired RAG-on/off experiment evaluated 74 questions: retrieval improved 11 responses, left 56 neutral, produced four adverse response changes, and left three pairs unassessable. RAG-on had descriptively higher mean usefulness, safety, correctness, and actionability in the conditional 70-pair subset excluding the four flagged pairs from both conditions. Physical-device testing demonstrated offline responses on a 6 GB Android handset, with a 14.3 s median latency, alongside successful reconnection synchronization in the integrated application. Together, the findings document clinical response quality and practical performance of the integrated offline maternal-health assistant.

title: Physics-Spawned Neural Integration of Rotating Shallow-Water Dynamics
abstract: Equation-derived neural integration can execute prescribed dynamics without training, while informative ensemble learning can estimate uncertain parameters and identify governing interactions without requiring differentiability. Together, these approaches motivate Physics-Spawned Informative Networks ($Φ$SpIN), a framework for prescribed and adaptive hybrid dynamical systems. As a first step toward flood modeling applications, we present $Φ$SpIN-SW, its prescribed-physics realization for the rotating shallow-water equations. Compatible C-grid operators on spherical Voronoi meshes define a computational graph that retains non-polynomial operations and advances the state through recurrent neural integration compiled with JAX. Analytical benchmarks characterize numerical errors, and global and coastal experiments closely reproduce reference solutions generated using the Model Prediction Across Scales (MPAS) model. At approximately 14~km global resolution, A100, H200 and B200 GPUs attain 9-, 19- and 34-fold higher timestep throughput than a 96-core MPAS-SW CPU reference under matched workloads. These results extend training-free neural integration beyond polynomial dynamics to complex geophysical simulation, establishing a computational foundation for subsequent adjoint-free ensemble estimation of physical and neural parameters and informative adaptation of operator structure.

title: The Silent Cost of Conversation History in LLM Reasoning
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in multi-turn information systems accumulate their own earlier replies and a growing task state. We asked whether this conversation history lowers accuracy, and whether process-level quality metrics warn before it does. Each analysis was fixed before its outcomes were computed. In Study 1, on 48 sharded math tasks, retaining its replies lowered final success by 0.21 for GPT-4o-mini and 0.29 for Mistral-7B (Holm-adjusted p = 0.026 and 0.004); Llama-4 Scout showed the same direction, not significant. Study 2 introduces CDR-Stream, 100-turn state-tracking dialogues with an exact answer per turn and per-model difficulty calibration. With the full history, accuracy fell from about 0.6 to 0.1 within twenty turns at matched difficulty, whereas a solver-verified state summary kept it 0.52-0.59 higher (Holm-adjusted p less than 0.001). Consistency and logical coherence fell far less than accuracy, and stability rose. None of these metrics, a paired readiness measure or calibrated single-stream drift detectors gave robust, model-general early warning, although in Study 2 the repeat-based metrics were complete only for GPT-4o-mini. In the monitors we tested, a single 100-turn stream had power only for very large drops. Systems built on LLMs should keep task state outside the transcript and monitor across sessions.

title: Trading Parameters for Accuracy in MambaVision for Chest Radiograph Classification
abstract: MambaVision, a hybrid state-space and attention backbone, places most of its parameters in its widest, fourth stage. We quantified what that stage contributes to multi-label chest radiograph classification. The fourth stage was replaced with lighter single-scan state-space blocks adapted from Spatial-Mamba, with multi-scale dilated depthwise convolutions applied to the scan output; the first three stages were retained. Tiny, Small, and Base models were evaluated across nine dataset-scale combinations drawn from two source cohorts: the National Institutes of Health ChestX-ray14 archive (full ChestMNIST and a high-resolution subset) and Indiana University Open-i. At the Tiny scale, replacement reduced parameter count by 35.7% and increased graphics processing unit throughput by 19.3%; the savings came from the stage's dense projections, not from removing quadratic attention. Without distillation, the mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve on ChestMNIST was 0.004 lower than the baseline (95% bootstrap confidence interval, 0.002 to 0.006), and 0.003 to 0.006 lower across all nine combinations. Knowledge distillation from an unreplaced teacher narrowed the gap to the undistilled baseline to 0.001-0.002 and met the equivalence criterion on ChestMNIST, but distilling the baseline with the same recipe improved it by 0.001-0.003, so a gap of 0.002-0.005 persisted under symmetric training. At the Base scale, the unreplaced Small model was both smaller and more accurate. Fourth-stage replacement is a useful trade-off only for Tiny and Small models. These measurements let developers of chest radiograph screening tools weigh model size and speed against a quantified loss of diagnostic discrimination.

title: A plug-in energy-balance freezing module for transformer frost nowcasting without leaf-sensor inputs
abstract: Frost protection requires local warnings where leaf-sensor inputs are unavailable. In the frost literature we surveyed, physics entered machine-learning models through inputs, numerical-model coupling, or losses, rather than model structure. We develop a transformer-compatible module that embeds leaf energy-balance physics in freezing-probability forecasts: an energy-balance temperature reference and a learned residual predict leaf temperature, which drives a multiplicative gate imposing a temperature-dependent probability cap. We mathematically prove conditional monotonicity and an alarm boundary, and test whether placing the same information in the output pathway or in attention yields different benefits. We evaluated 12 hourly leads at 19 Korean stations over five frost seasons, with and without leaf-sensor inputs. In the 2025-2026 hold-out season without these inputs, our time-token transformer (PET-E) achieved a lead-mean critical success index (CSI) of 0.516 versus 0.478 for fixed-configuration, joint-lead LightGBM, with significant gains at all 12 leads, and the fraction of alarms at observed leaf temperatures of at least 2 degrees C fell from 0.087 to 0.051 relative to the unmodified backbone. Across the hold-out and a retrospective 2024-2025 evaluation, the module reduced Brier scores and warm-surface alarm fractions in both the time-token transformer and iTransformer, with no significant CSI decrease at any lead. At held-out stations without static or leaf-sensor inputs, both module-equipped backbones exceeded LightGBM at all 12 leads (CSI 0.468 and 0.467 versus 0.437). In the time-token backbone, the temperature pathway reduced this alarm fraction in all four settings, whereas the attention prior increased CSI in three. These findings link an explicit temperature-dependent probability cap to improved forecasts and distinguish output-side from attention-based embedding.

title: Aerial Person Detection under Edge Constraints: Held-Out Evaluation and Edge-Ground Verification
abstract: A search drone sees a missing person as a few pixels, carries a small computer, and shares a narrow radio link. We study person detection under those limits; the primary evaluations were declared before they ran, and later analyses are marked exploratory. In an exploratory comparison, holding out recording blocks inferred from thermal frame identifiers cut recall at a fixed false-alarm target from 32.7% to 12.3%. With nothing tuned on test blocks, a 46,000-parameter detector gated by a contrast cue finds 10.4% of people against 5.7% for the same network applied everywhere. A standard detector, YOLO11n, trained under the same folds finds 54.5% at a similar false-alarm rate for about eleven times the arithmetic, and on our 4K field footage at 117 m has a walking person among its top 16 detections in up to 92% of frames against 74% for our board. Run alone, YOLO11n's thresholds set at one location overshot their false-alarm target 1.7 to 3.4 times at new locations, and its best configuration at altitude cost 4 to 24 standard passes per frame. Re-scoring its 16 best crops (154 KB per frame) with an 842,000-parameter ground model, thresholds frozen on a validation location, raised recall from 44.9% to 53.7% against the same 16 crops with YOLO's own scores; in a post hoc paired analysis over 15 test locations the gain was +8.8 points [+2.4, +12.5]. Pooled false detections fell from 0.86 to 0.64 per frame, but that paired change was not distinguishable from zero. Coverage of a still person in earth tones was very low for both detectors in the clips we flew.

title: The mass density slope of early-type galaxies: newest results from the redshift distribution of strong gravitational lenses
abstract: The mass distribution of early-type galaxies (ETGs) encodes key information about baryonic processes and dark-matter assembly. In this paper, we propose a new framework to investigate the mass-density profiles of ETGs and their evolution with redshift, based on the redshift distribution of strong gravitational lenses. We compile 200 galaxy-scale strong lensing systems with complete information, including lens and source redshifts, Einstein radii, and spectroscopic velocity dispersions. To account for the heterogeneous construction of the compiled sample, we model a lens-redshift-dependent selection function for each survey category. By combining the lens-redshift distribution with velocity dispersion function (VDF) and spherical Jeans-based mapping, we obtain population-level constraints on the total mass-density slope gamma in three lens-redshift intervals, marginalizing over the luminosity-density slope delta and the stellar orbital anisotropy beta. We find that the total mass density of ETGs remains close to isothermal at low and intermediate redshifts ($γ=2.00^{+0.07}_{-0.15}$ at 0 < z_l < 0.5 and $γ=1.96^{+0.16}_{-0.26}$ at 0.5 < z_l < 0.6), with a shallower effective slope at higher redshift ($γ=1.81^{+0.17}_{-0.21}$ at $0.6<z_l\lesssim1.0$). The marginalized posteriors of delta and beta remain broad, consistent with $δ\simeq2$ and with isotropic orbits in all three redshift intervals. These results are consistent with the redshift trend predicted by Horizon-AGN simulations, in which active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback, together with stellar assembly and merging, contributes to the structural evolution of ETGs. Applied to the much larger lens samples expected from future missions such as the Chinese Space Station Telescope (CSST), this method will enable tighter tests of density-slope evolution and its connection to galaxy formation processes.

title: HEAMS: Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems
abstract: Memory systems allow AI agents to persist information across interactions, making them more personalized and more capable on long-horizon tasks. This persistence introduces new risks: stored information can be disclosed in inappropriate contexts, resist correction or deletion, be retained beyond what users desire, or be poisoned to influence later agent behaviour. Yet memory systems are typically evaluated on task performance and efficiency alone. We argue that a memory system should instead be understood as the custodian of its user's persistent information, with responsibilities that extend beyond helping an agent complete its tasks, and that it should be evaluated holistically against all such responsibilities. We present Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems (HEAMS), an open-source framework for evaluating agent memory systems in this way. First, we state the responsibilities of agent memory systems as explicit behavioural desiderata spanning performance, efficiency, security, privacy, and user sovereignty. Second, we assemble a benchmark suite that covers these desiderata and acknowledge the gaps that remain. Third, we develop MilaMem, a prototype memory system, and a governance layer that can wrap any memory system, enabling controlled study of memory system design choices. Fourth, we compare memory systems across the full HEAMS benchmark suite. We find that no memory system leads every performance benchmark, and strong performance scores may coexist with poor privacy, user-sovereignty, and security scores. Governance strongly influences results: recall policies can reduce inappropriate disclosure at a cost in helpfulness, while both recall and retention policies improve poisoning resistance. Performance and efficiency benchmarks alone therefore cannot reveal how well a memory system meets its responsibilities. Code: https://github.com/milatechtransfer/heams

title: Analytic Model for Transient Plateau Filling in Vibrational Distributions of Periodically Driven Plasmas
abstract: In periodically driven molecular plasmas, the vibrational distribution function is governed by the competition between vibration--vibration (V-V) up-pumping along the anharmonic ladder and vibration--translation (V-T) relaxation, producing the Treanor--Gordiets distribution. When vibrational energy accumulates across cycles faster than V-V exchange can populate the upper levels, the Gordiets plateau remains transiently depleted. Existing algebraic models assume a quasi-steady plateau, whereas exact transient solutions of the nonlinear V-V diffusion equation require the elapsed time since excitation and the source strength, which are unavailable in multidimensional simulations that track only local macroscopic variables. Here, elapsed time is replaced by a local vibrational energy timescale formed from the vibrational energy per molecule and its period-averaged rate of change. This reduces the diffusion equation in level space to an ordinary differential equation solved in closed form without linearization, yielding a level-dependent correction to the steady plateau governed by a single dimensionless group: the number of V-V collisions per energy timescale weighted by the plateau amplitude at the Treanor minimum. The distribution front advances as the square root of this group, and the steady distribution is recovered as the group grows large. Compared with state-to-state master-equation calculations for N$_2$ under nanosecond pulse trains spanning 300-1500 K, 0.041-1 atm, and 1-100 kHz (1440 sampled states), the model reduces the 90th-percentile error in level populations from 1.88 decades for the steady model and 1.32 decades for an adapted self-similar solution to 0.53 decades, at essentially the evaluation cost of the steady model.

title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Double-source-plane lens candidates
abstract: Strong gravitational-lensing systems with multiple source planes are powerful tools for probing the stellar and dark matter content of galaxies. Lens modelling can measure the relative Einstein radii of the two source planes, which encode a ratio of angular-diameter distances determined by the lens and source redshifts and the dark energy equation of state, independently of the Hubble constant. Galaxy-scale double-source-plane lenses (DSPLs) are extremely rare. We present a sample of 84 galaxy-scale DSPL candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), of which 80 are newly identified. These systems were selected using machine-learning lens-finding models followed by visual inspection by citizen scientists and experts. We then used lens modelling to test the DSPL interpretation. Among our lens candidates, 11 form the 'Gold' sample: each shows two sets of multiple images at different radii, and the observed configuration is reproduced by a DSPL lens model. The remaining 73 'Silver' candidates have at least two lensed arcs from visual inspection, but either lack multiple images for at least one arc, have a best-fitting DSPL distance ratio close to the single-source-plane limit, remain compatible with a single-plane model with multiple sources, or have not yet been modelled. Even if all 84 candidates are DSPLs, the sample falls below the approximately 90 systems expected from extrapolating the Euclid Quick Data Release 1 (Q1) yield and the approximately 200 obtained by scaling the LensPop forecast to the DR1 area, indicating that many DSPLs remain undetected in DR1. Spectroscopy or higher-resolution imaging is required before we can be confident that the Silver candidates are DSPLs.
