title: GeoReVis: Learning Selective Revision and Evidence Consolidation for Remote Sensing Segmentation
abstract: Recent methods try to inspect and revise masks to mitigate referential ambiguity and localization errors caused by complex spatial relations in language-guided remote sensing segmentation. However, these solutions often lead to Revision Degradation: revising missing regions may introduce errors into previously correct ones. Even a globally better mask can omit correct regions found in inferior masks. We term this Evidence Fragmentation: correct target evidence is scattered across imperfect masks. All masks generated by the model at this time are suboptimal. We propose GeoReVis, which unifies revision guided by execution feedback, Candidate Selection, and Cross-Mask Evidence Consolidation. It learns fine-grained revision from real actions that improve segmentation when executed and learns to select a better mask through quality comparisons between actual candidates, reducing the risk of degradation during revision. The selected whole mask can still discard useful regions. GeoReVis therefore retains all candidates across rounds, partitions their spatial disagreements into composable regions, and jointly reconstructs regions conditioned on the full instruction and context. This makes complementary and fragmentary evidence reusable regardless of its source candidate's overall quality, yielding improved segmentation. We further build a data pipeline to generate fine-grained multi-round segmentation trajectories and derive supervision for revision actions, candidate selection, and region composition from the model's own outputs, extending training beyond whole-mask IoU supervision. We also propose ReVis-Eval, a benchmark protocol evaluating multi-round revision and cross-round evidence consolidation accuracy. Experiments on ReVis-Eval and 5 benchmarks for remote sensing reasoning and referring segmentation demonstrate the effectiveness of GeoReVis.

title: Automated Left Ventricle Strain Analysis from DENSE MRI
abstract: Background: Quantifying myocardial strains from Displacement ENcoding with Stimulated Echoes (DENSE) MRI provides insight into left ventricular performance, but current data processing pipelines remain limited in automation, robustness, and full left ventricle coverage. Methods: We present a fully automated framework for voxel-wise displacement and strain analysis of the left ventricle from DENSE MRI. Our method integrates a multi-channel nnU-Net model trained on both magnitude and phase images for segmentation, an automated phase unwrapping approach, an adaptation of the regularized spatiotemporal least squares (RSTLS) formulation for displacement computation, and strain calculations based on radial basis function interpolation. The proposed framework enables the estimation of displacements and strains across the left ventricle from a full stack of short-axis images. Results: Validation using a computational phantom shows the framework's overall resilience to data noise. Following computational phantom evaluation, the proposed framework is applied to analyze DENSE MRI short-axis slices acquired in forty-seven (N=47) healthy volunteers and covering the full left ventricle. Circumferential, longitudinal, and radial strains are presented throughout the cardiac cycle and at peak systole, showcasing the performance of the proposed framework. Results show that circumferential and longitudinal strains are computed accurately. However, challenges persist when estimating radial strain, especially in the subendocardial layer. A group-wise strain comparison is also performed based on volunteers' sex and age showing a significant effect of sex on circumferential and longitudinal strains. Conclusions: Overall, the proposed framework provides an automated and modular pipeline to compute displacements and strains from DENSE MR images that can be scaled and generalized toward clinical applications.

title: Ocular Recognition: Interoperability, Multi-Resolution, and Spectrum Challenges
abstract: Ocular recognition is typically developed under controlled acquisition conditions, limiting its use in semi-controlled and on-the-move scenarios. A key obstacle is the lack of representative data spanning real-world capture conditions. At a border checkpoint, for example, images may range from low-resolution visible-light periocular crops (RGB) to high-resolution near-infrared iris images (NIR). Using this heterogeneous evidence raises three questions: whether resolution-specific processing improves recognition, how to compare templates from different processing routes, and how to allocate training data across resolution specialists. We investigate resolution-specific processing and parameter sharing using three AdaFace-based architecture families: fixed-resolution specialists; Independent Backbones with Shared Heads (IBSH); and models with resolution-specific front-ends for 40x40, 80x80, and 160x160 inputs, followed by a shared identity trunk and embedding projection. We evaluate each architecture with route-specific training subsets and with a full-pool strategy, in which every specialist uses the complete selected training set. Results reveal a trade-off among same-resolution specialization, cross-resolution interoperability, and common-route re-extraction. Route-specific training produces distinct performance profiles across routes, whereas full-pool training makes route performance more uniform and primarily benefits the 160x160 route. Thus, adding training data does not improve all resolution routes equally.

title: From XR Sketches to CAD: Preserving Design Intent with AI
abstract: Extended reality (XR) allows designers to sketch shapes directly in 3D, but converting these sketches into editable, feature-based CAD requires interpreting their intent. A sketch may contain drawing errors, intended features, and design choices that remain open. Correcting every irregularity risks erasing intended features, while automatic completion may impose choices the designer has not made. We argue that AI should add precision without overriding design intent, considering both the resulting shape and how the CAD model behaves during later edits. To guide this process, we propose a conceptual framework that distinguishes errors from intentions in individual sketch properties and relates them to correction, preservation, and exploration in editable CAD. We also outline five research directions for sketch interpretation, CAD construction, and evaluation, with testable hypotheses for selected questions.

title: Contraction Analysis and Control of Polynomial Dynamical Systems
abstract: Contraction analysis has found broad applications in synchronization, tracking, observer design, and nonlinear feedback control. However, establishing contraction conditions for polynomial dynamical systems remains challenging due to their state-dependent Jacobians. In this article, we develop a tensor-based framework for contraction analysis of polynomial dynamical systems by exploiting the structure of orthogonally decomposable (odeco) coefficient tensors. By transforming the dynamics into modal coordinates, we derive necessary and sufficient semicontraction conditions and characterize state-dependent semimetrics. We establish fundamental limitations on exponential contraction and prove polynomial decay of differential displacements on forward-invariant regions. To accommodate more general polynomial dynamical systems, we extend the framework to include linear dynamics and non-odeco tensor perturbations, deriving computationally tractable contraction certificates with explicit robustness guarantees. We further develop convex feedback synthesis conditions based on linear matrix inequalities for general input matrices. We demonstrate the effectiveness and computational scalability of the proposed framework through numerical experiments on both synthetic systems and nonlinear elastic relaxation models.

title: Microfitting: Continual Learning via Cached Test-Time Training
abstract: Continual learning is a promising approach to specialize language models to an organization's private data. However, current methods exhibit a number of drawbacks including catastrophic forgetting, where new training updates overwrite prior knowledge. We present microfitting, which trains and caches a small adapter for each document. Each adapter is trained once, offline, on synthetic questions targeted at demonstrated base-model shortcomings and reused whenever that document is queried. This method borrows from test-time learning literature and sidesteps the problem of continual learning through parameter isolation, allowing the system to specialize on new data without overwriting prior knowledge. The process that generates adapter training data also improves over time, revising its recipe from previous outcomes and fresh examples of the target workload. On DeepSeek V4 Flash, microfitting substantially improves accuracy over the base model. In Enterprise Document Operations (EDO), an open-book Q&A environment over real-world enterprise documents, our method achieves a 38.2% relative improvement over base-model performance. Microfitting makes continual specialization practical and cost-efficient: a frozen model can adapt to an evolving private corpus overnight on local hardware, without modifying the base model or previously cached adapters.

title: Self-supervised learning for zebrafish embryo phenotype evaluation: Systematic comparison of algorithms, label-efficient classification, and transfer learning
abstract: Zebrafish embryos are a prominent model organism for image-based phenotyping and especially suited for large-scale imaging studies, for which machine learning (ML) models can automate evaluation. However, training ML models usually requires large labeled datasets, and differences in imaging conditions often impede reuse across laboratories. Self-supervised learning (SSL) addresses both constraints by learning transferable representations from unlabeled images. Yet central aspects like the choice of algorithm remain underexplored for domain-specific applications. To close this gap, we benchmark popular SSL algorithms on the public EmbryoNet dataset, explore label-efficient learning, and test transfer to an unseen setting. Using representations from our strongest model, a ResNet50 network trained with SwAV, a simple linear classifier reaches 86.4% accuracy and a non-linear classifier 87.1%, rivaling the fully supervised EmbryoNet model (87.1%). The SwAV model decisively outperforms supervised training from scratch when labels are scarce (70.2% vs. 45.7% accuracy with 5% of labels). On a three-class problem (normal, dead, falsely cropped) with a small, previously unseen zebrafish toxicity dataset, recorded in a different setting, our model reaches 81.3% accuracy without retraining, while EmbryoNet achieves 75.9%. Overall, self-supervised models for zebrafish embryos seem to mostly facilitate label-efficiency and transfer to new settings rather than improving supervised results.

title: The Manifold-Index Model: provably and efficiently avoiding the statistical and computational curse of dimensionality
abstract: We study vector-valued regression with predictors filling a tube around an unknown $m$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal{M}$ in $\mathbb{R}^D$. In the Manifold-Index Model, the mean response is $F=f\circΠ_{\mathcal{M}}$, where $Π_{\mathcal{M}}$ is the nearest-point projection onto $\mathcal{M}$ and $f:\mathcal{M}\to\mathbb{R}^p$ is a possibly non-injective link function. Multiscale ANisotropic lOcal Regression (MANOR) estimates tangent planes by multiscale PCA of predictors with similar responses, then refines them by pooling outer products of local slopes. The neighborhoods narrow tangentially while retaining complete normal fibers. We assume a Lipschitz link differential and bounded response noise. For $p\ge m$, under our geometric and sampling conditions, $n$ independent observations give mean tangent-space error of order $n^{-2/(m+4)}$ and integrated squared prediction error at the $m$-dimensional nonparametric rate $n^{-4/(m+4)}$, up to logarithmic factors. In a scaling regime with fixed intrinsic dimension, model and scale parameters, and ratio of manifold volume to the $m$-th power of its reach, the required sample size grows polynomially in $D+p$, and computation is polynomial in $n$, $D$ and $p$. Numerical experiments on curves with non-monotone links and surfaces with vector-valued responses compare observed convergence rates with the theoretical bounds; a Langevin dynamics example tests prediction of hitting probabilities under an approximate manifold-index model.

title: Multi-seed information diffusion with varying reproduction
abstract: We define the $S_hR_k$-process that generalizes the notion of Hamiltonicity through the lense of information diffusion. We say that a graph is $S_hR_k$-infectable if it can be fully infected by transmission trees seeded by at most $h$ initial infections in which each infection leads to at most $k$ others; or, equivalently, if it can be exactly vertex-covered by at most $h$ trees of degree at most $k$. While determining $S_hR_k$ infectability is NP-hard in general, we argue fixed-parameter tractability when parameterised by treewidth. Additionally, we give computational experimental results comparing the performance of several natural heuristics for minimising the number of initial infections required to an optimal LP-based approach on several standard complex network models. We find that a uniformly random approach outperforms greedy heuristics based on degree or clustering.

title: Causal Discovery for Resiliency-Prioritized Transmission Expansion Planning in Power Systems with Grid-Forming Inverter-Based Resources
abstract: Transmission planners at regional transmission organizations (RTOs), independent system operators (ISOs), and NERC-registered entities have limited analytical resources for exploring expansion options that improve resiliency for withstanding and recovering from fault conditions in electric power systems that are dominated by grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) inverter-based resources (IBRs). Conventional existing TPL-001 contingency analysis will assess if a performance benchmark is violated. However, it will not identify which dynamic states and inputs caused the violation, nor how much a protective action will avoid propagation into a cascading outage. This paper proposes an analytical method that combines time-series causal discovery using the Peter and Clark Momentary Conditional Independence (PCMCI) algorithm with right/left eigenvector participation-factor analysis of validated small-signal state-space models. Synthetic data are generated from linearized models derived from substation phasor measurement unit (PMU) data. This includes node-breaker topologies under alternative transmission switching configurations. GFM and GFL inverter controls including phase-locked loops (PLLs) and fault ride-through logic. A planning index referred to as the Resiliency Causal Contribution Index (RCCI) is defined that weights PCMCI-derived causal effects on a TPL benchmark quantity by modal participation. The planning procedure iterates contingency categories, measures margins to RTO/ISO benchmarks for transient voltage recovery, oscillatory damping, inverter ride-through, and TPL-008-1 extreme temperature. The process infers automatic protective actions and repeats until a cascade is ruled out or confirmed. A simplified case study illustrates the entire process for considering the options in transmission expansion planning.

title: Reliable Mining of Heterogeneous AI Coding-Agent Data: Context-Aware Prediction and Resource-Aware Ranking
abstract: Operational records from AI coding agents differ across agents, repositories, tasks, and workflows. We study 71,677 pull requests (PRs) from six agents and show that pooling these records can reverse descriptive and predictive conclusions. PRs carrying a co-authorship trailer have a 55.6% merge rate, compared with 77.5% without the trailer, but removing the dominant agent flips this -21.8 percentage-point gap to +23.7 points. We treat this Simpson-type reversal as a data-veracity problem and represent source, environment, and workflow context in a feature cascade. Gradient-boosting merge-prediction AUC increases from 0.774 to 0.832; the advantage persists under temporal evaluation (0.801) and unseen repositories (0.807). The co-authorship coefficient changes from -1.09 to +1.44 after conditioning, whereas repository-clustered AIPW intervals show no stable adjusted trailer association. A strict PR-creation-time model reaches 0.741 AUC in standard evaluation and 0.710 on unseen repositories, although its temporal AUC falls to 0.641. Finally, a separately cross-fitted analysis of an observed-mode functional estimates a +12.3-point doubly robust gain at a 30% allocation budget on the non-Codex population, only 0.5 points above risk ranking. This last result is retrospective decision support over metadata states, not a causal effect of assigning human review.

title: Soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge for generative AI: numerical algorithms and approximation guarantees
abstract: We study a soft-constrained formulation of the Schrödinger bridge problem, in which the terminal distribution constraint is relaxed into a penalty on the discrepancy between the terminal law of the controlled process and a target distribution. This leads to an unconstrained McKean--Vlasov stochastic control problem, where the interaction enters only through the terminal cost. We characterize the optimizer via a McKean--Vlasov forward-backward stochastic differential equation and establish well-posedness under very mild assumptions. We also analyze two approximation regimes relevant to data-driven computation: approximation of the target law by empirical samples, and finite-particle approximation of the McKean--Vlasov control problem. For both, we derive convergence results and error estimates. Finally, building on the well-posedness and approximation results, we investigate two neural numerical methods: one based on the forward-backward system and the other on direct control optimization. Both methods are tested on state-of-the-art generative tasks. Our results provide both an algorithmic foundation and its theoretical guarentee for soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge problems in sample-based generative modeling.

title: FCP: Formal Context Protocol for Verifying LLM-Generated Artifacts
abstract: When a language model writes both an artifact and the tests meant to check it, a passing test is weak evidence: one misreading of the request yields a faulty artifact and a check that accepts it. We present the Formal Context Protocol (FCP), which checks AI-generated artifacts against the request itself. FCP separates conformance (does the artifact satisfy a formal reading of a requirement?), which model checkers and SMT solvers decide, from fidelity (does the reading mean what the prose means?), which has no decision procedure but is refutable by a concrete witness. Eight ways a proof can falsely certify a requirement each become a mechanical check that returns a witness, and what no machine can settle becomes concrete questions for the request's author. Adapters place hardware, text, agents and code on the same engines. On four hardware designs, trusting AI-written assertions certified 23% of violated requirements, and FCP certified none. On ten code tasks, code from three language models passed its own tests and violated the request every time. Trusting the tests certified all 33 violations, and FCP certified three. Agreement among models, readings or tests did not imply correctness.

title: A Differential Theory of Quality-Resource Trade-offs for AI Model Selection: The Multiresource Frontier and Its Minimax Price
abstract: Comparing AI models across resource budgets yields quality-resource frontiers relating error to latency, parameter count, training compute, and energy. Offset power laws summarize such frontiers, but their fitted parameters reveal neither the price-independent geometry nor the manner in which trade-offs extend across several resource channels. This paper addresses both gaps by developing a differential theory in which this structure is made explicit. Each frontier admits a price-independent plane-curve representation relating the effective number of active resource channels, $N_{\mathrm{eff}} = s^2/κ$ (squared slope over curvature), to the remaining log-error depth, $ΔS = \ln(\varepsilon/\varepsilon_{\infty})$. This representation separates intrinsic shape from the scale and origin of the resource axis. Complete monotonicity and divisibility yield differential inequalities and frontier bounds. When each of $N$ resources contributes one active channel, the theory gives the parameter-free operating rule $N_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1$ in delivered units and derives minimax resource prices $λ^{\star}_i = α_i/(N+1)$ with an exact worst-case regret of $\ln(N+1)$ nats. The results make it possible to interpret measured frontiers and compare resource costs without hand-chosen exchange rates. The theory is evaluated on 117 published frontiers and implemented in the open-source package nn-rank, which derives prices from measured quality and cost, ranks candidates, and reports supported choices and minimax regret: https://github.com/ABrain-One/nn-rank

title: Modelling Solar Radiation for Mangan District of Sikkim, India Using Random Forest Technique
abstract: Solar radiation is one of the most crucial meteorological parameters in crop cultivation as it affects different metabolic processes in plants, and thus influences crop growth. However, the non-availability of long-term and high temporal-resolution solar radiation data is a major limitation, particularly in the northeastern region of India, mainly due to scarce instrumental monitoring of solar radiation. Knowledge about the spatial and temporal distribution of solar radiation along with its trend and future availability is essential for its better utilization in agriculture. Therefore, this study modelled hourly solar radiation for the 2017-2020 period in the Mangan district of Sikkim, India using random forest (RF) method. Data of solar radiation, air temperature, relative humidity and wind speed were collected from an automatic weather station. The results indicated that temperature had the highest correlation with solar radiation (correlation coefficient, r = 0.52), and therefore, it was used as an input variable in the model. In addition to temperature, cyclically encoded temporal variables, namely hour of the day and day of the year, were also included as input features for modelling hourly solar radiation. The developed model was satisfactorily validated using widely used performance parameters such as mean absolute error (33.16 W m-2, root mean square error (12.8% to 21.3%), Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (0.884) and coefficient of determination (R2 = 0.87). The developed RF model can help in estimating solar radiation value for different uses related to solar energy planning, including agriculture for developing crop-growth models, testing the adaptability of solar-operated pumps, and protected cultivation systems.

title: Forecasting Respiratory Syncytial Virus Activity Using Seasonal ARIMA Models: Evidence from CDC Weekly Surveillance Data
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) imposes seasonal operational pressure on paediatric care and hospital healthcare systems. This study evaluates whether weekly RSV test percent positivity data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) can support short-term forecasting of RSV transmission activity. The national weekly surveillance dataset spanning 3 January 2015 to 27 June 2020 was analyzed with four forecasting approaches: seasonal autoreggressive integrated moving average (SARIMA), non-seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), exponential smoothing (ETS), and a seasonal naive benchmark model. Model predictive performance was validated via a 52-week chronological holdout sample and rolling-origin forecasts for 1–4 week ahead horizons. Multiple evaluation metrics were adopted, including root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), symmetric mean absolute percentage error (sMAPE), directional accuracy, and peak-timing error. Exploratory time-series analyses verified prominent annual seasonality and short-term serial dependence embedded in RSV percent positivity time series. Among all candidate models, SARIMA yielded the smallest RMSE and MAE on the holdout dataset, and exhibited relatively robust performance as the forecast window extended. The overall findings demonstrate that surveillance-driven SARIMA forecasting can facilitate early epidemic warning and advance healthcare resource planning. Nevertheless, further external validation using post-pandemic and regional RSV surveillance datasets is required, as the sample only covers the pre-pandemic and early coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19 ) period.
journal: International Journal of Biology and Life Sciences

title: Applications of Deep Learning Algorithms in Protein Structure Prediction and Design
abstract: The three-dimensional configuration of a protein is important for its biological function, which is crucial in biological study and drug development. The progress of deep learning has greatly improved the prediction of protein structures. Especially, the AlphaFold series has increased the prediction precision and extended its use in the simulation of biomolecular complexes and drug discovery. This paper describes the latest progress in protein structure prediction and antibody design based on deep learning. The emphasis is on the enhancement and efficiency of the template-based method and the AlphaFold series. Furthermore, the practical applications of these methods in antibody engineering and drug discovery are illustrated by considering specific examples such as AbEgDiffuser for simultaneous sequence and structure design, and AlphaFold3 for the choice of covalent ligands. Experimental data indicate that deep learning can precisely forecast the protein structures and effectively improve the design and screening of potential substances, thereby offering new possibilities for rational drug design. In the future, more research should concentrate on predicting the conformational changes of proteins, designing novel antibody frameworks from scratch, and obtaining multiple drug-like properties at the same time.

title: Conceptual foundations for forming a system of factors in the spatial and sectoral development of the agro industrial complex
abstract: The spatial and sectoral development of the Russian agro-industrial complex is characterized by the increasing complexity of the interactions between economic, institutional, digital, and natural-climatic factors, necessitating the development of new methodological approaches to their comprehensive assessment. The objective of this study is to develop a scientifically grounded system of factors for the spatial and sectoral development of the agro-industrial complex, providing a comprehensive reflection of the current operating conditions of the agricultural sector and creating a methodological basis for the subsequent integrated assessment of regions. The methodological basis of the study consists of systems and spatial approaches, comparative analysis, expert selection of indicators, statistical diagnostics, and data standardization. As a result of the study, a proprietary system of factors for the spatial and sectoral development of the agro-industrial complex was developed, including twenty statistical indicators grouped into four interconnected thematic blocks: institutional environment, digital maturity, climate adaptability, and economic efficiency. Criteria for selecting statistical indicators and a multi level architecture for organizing them have been proposed. A statistical analysis of the resulting database was conducted, confirming its representativeness for interregional analysis. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the development of conceptual foundations for forming a system of factors for the spatial and sectoral development of the agro industrial complex, which combines economic, digital, institutional, and climatic indicators into a single system. The practical significance of the results lies in the use of the system of factors for interregional comparisons, scenario modeling, and the development of mechanisms for the sustainable development of the agro industrial complex.

title: Digitalisation of Russian Federationn agriculture: the divergence between growing expenditure and the declining share of users of artificial intelligence technologies
abstract: The aim of the study is to reveal the substance of the divergence between the growth of digital technology expenditure of Russian Federation agricultural organizations and the decline in the share of users of artificial intelligence technologies over 2021–2024, drawing on the first Rosstat data for the economic activity «crop and animal production». The methods include grouping of technologies into three layers (infrastructure, data and analytics, production automation), structural analysis of expenditure by purpose and source of financing, and comparison with the economy-wide results of the federal statistical observation. Expenditure grew from 6.84 to 9.40 billion rubles, or by 37%, whereas the share of users of artificial intelligence technologies declined from 3.1 to 1.9%, and from 2.2 to 1.9% over the methodologically comparable period 2023–2024, the share of users of big data technologies from 22.9 to 7.2% and of the Internet of things from 15.2 to 11.3%, while geographic information systems and digital platforms expanded from 16.2 to 24.3% and from 10.1 to 19.7% respectively. External expenditure grew 2.7 times, investment in cross-cutting digital technologies dropped from 72.6 to 9.4 million rubles, budget financing from 1,029.4 to 98.8 million rubles, and the share of own funds in internal expenditure rose from 81.7 to 97.5%. The sector’s lag behind the economy as a whole in the share of users of artificial intelligence technologies widened from 1.6 to 2.2 times. The divergence is explained by the service-and-infrastructure character of digitalization, in which growing outlays serve information exchange channels and do not create the layer of analytical and production automation. The restoration of targeted financing of cross-cutting technologies and the introduction of indicators of the depth of artificial intelligence use in production processes into the program of federal observation are proposed.

title: Theoretical and methodological approaches to spatial analysis of small agribusiness development
abstract: Comprehensive development of the agro-food complex, economy and social sphere of rural areas involves the creation of agricultural ecosystems, including infrastructure development, implementation of digital solutions and artificial intelligence technologies, as well as establishment of direct links between producers and consumers. The importance of achieving national development goals determines the importance of active involvement of all economic entities of the agro-food complex. Spatial development of small businesses should be consistent with the multi-level economic system of the agro-industrial complex and requires strengthening the institutional structure to reveal the territorial potential of small agricultural enterprises. The study focuses on the importance of improving the methodological tools for spatial analysis and territorial planning when placing agro-industrial enterprises of various scales. Insufficient study of the issue of harmonious combination of agricultural enterprises of various scales when placing them is emphasized. An analysis of the current regulatory framework of the state socio-economic and technological policy in relation to the spatial development of the agro-food complex is carried out. The importance of adaptation to the bioclimatic and resource potential of rural areas is noted. The prerequisites for decentralization within the framework of the country's spatial development are identified, which creates advantages for the development of small agribusiness. A retrospective analysis of theoretical concepts of the spatial development of small agribusiness is carried out. A wide range of research problems that can be solved by spatial analysis is described. An approach to state support for small agribusiness is presented based on taking into account the differentiation of the level of development of territories. Ensuring a balance between agricultural production of different scales is the task of the state agrarian policy, which can be achieved through state regulation based on scientifically based approaches to the territorial placement of agricultural enterprises in order to ensure food security of the country and the integrated development of rural areas. It is assumed that one of the results of the spatial development of small agribusiness will be an improvement in the performance indicators of the agro-food complex due to a scientifically based regional policy aimed at developing small enterprises of the agro-industrial complex.

title: Determination of agricultural land micro-relief using satellite geodetic measurements
abstract: Determining the micro-relief of terrain plays a crucial role in modern geodesy and agriculture, particularly within the framework of precision farming. Field surface topography significantly influences the distribution of surface and subsurface water, erosion processes, and the spatial variability of crop yields and soil properties. This study aims to determine the micro-relief of agricultural land using satellite geodetic measurements (conducted at the experimental field of the Agrarian Institute, University of Tyumen) to plan the rational use of the arable area. The article examines the process of determining terrain micro-relief via satellite geodetic measurements; a 3D digital model of the site was generated to provide a clear visualization of the micro-relief's spatial structure and to facilitate the identification of closed depressions (areas of contrasting elevation). Analysis of the data revealed that, while the site's topography does not fall into the category of critically degraded land, localized depressions and pronounced surface micro-irregularities were observed. These morphometric features negatively impact the area's agro-ecological condition, necessitating timely measures to mitigate these adverse factors. To support effective land use within the studied arable area, and based on the generated cartographic materials and the site's intended use, an adaptive system for the differentiated placement of crops is proposed, taking into account the micro-zonal characteristics of the relief and soil cover. Implementing this approach will optimize the land-use structure within the study area. Smoothing out meso-relief irregularities will help minimize spatial moisture heterogeneity, create favorable conditions for high-performance mechanized tillage, and increase crop productivity by homogenizing the distribution of fertilizers and soil moisture reserves. The developed project measures can serve as a basis for preparing technical documentation governing restoration work and agro-technical land improvement at the experimental site.

title: Financial sustainability of the agricultural sector in the Russian Far East under varying capital intensity of production
abstract: The relevance of this study stems from the fact that an expanding agricultural capital base does not necessarily improve the financial position of organizations. In the Russian Far East, differences in production specialization and the size of the organizational sector limit the usefulness of uniform investment targets. The study aims to establish whether fixed asset renewal is associated with the prevalence of profitable organizations and to develop a diagnostic framework incorporating capital intensity and operating performance. Published Rosstat data for 2020–2024 cover fixed asset values, renewal and depreciation, the share of profitable organizations, financial results, and profitability in crop and livestock production. Output structure is examined for 2023–2024. Methods comprise ratio analysis, regional classification, rank correlation, and panel regression with region and year effects. A panel of 50 observations is constructed for 10 regions. Standard errors are clustered by region, and inference is checked using a wild cluster bootstrap. The methodological contribution is a two-stage diagnosis that supplements asset renewal and the prevalence of profitability with a mandatory assessment of recurring operating losses that aggregate averages may conceal. Fixed assets in the district increased from RUB 90.9 billion to RUB 154.2 billion, while the share of profitable organizations changed from 59.5% to 62.7%. The coefficient on asset renewal is −0.399, with p = 0.443; a statistically significant positive association is not detected. In Yakutia and Chukotka, average profitability prevalence exceeds 73%, although livestock sales profitability remains negative in all 5 years. Amur Oblast exhibits the most consistent combination of renewal and positive financial outcomes. The resulting framework distinguishes capital expansion, widespread profitability, and operating sustainability, supporting differentiated renewal and profitability policies. Findings concern the observed organizational sector, do not identify causal investment effects, and cannot replace balance-sheet assessments of individual organizations.

title: Non-relational soil property databases for digital soil science and agriculture
abstract: The aim of the study was to compare relational and non-relational architectures for storing soil information and to justify a document-oriented regional database model for digital soil science and agriculture. Russian and international soil information systems were examined using comparative and structural-functional analysis, together with the capabilities of PostgreSQL/PostGIS, JSONB, materialized views, and MongoDB. Based on project materials for Tula Oblast, an architecturally described prototype is proposed in which the basic storage unit is a georeferenced soil observation object. Each document combines laboratory results, morphological features, digital soil mapping covariates, meteorological characteristics, remote sensing data, measurement status, and data provenance. Validation rules are proposed to distinguish a missing measurement, a value below the detection limit, a measured zero, and results obtained by different analytical methods. The document model is shown to be particularly suitable for integrating sparse and multimodal data, extending the set of indicators, and preparing reproducible training datasets while preserving analytical methods, units, quality flags, and data provenance. For regulatory registries, strict transactional integrity, advanced spatial analysis, and compact long-term storage, a relational or hybrid architecture remains preferable. The proposed solution should therefore be regarded as an operational analytical layer that complements existing relational sources and requires subsequent empirical performance testing.

title: Selection of classification methods and quantification of changes in extent of mangrove forests over 6 years (2019 - 2025) in Ninh Binh province
abstract: Mangrove forests in Ninh Binh Province, a key part of the Red River Delta, provide important ecological services but face significant mapping challenges due to complex land use and tidal dynamics. This study evaluates four classification methods—Traditional RGB, NDVI thresholding, CMRI thresholding, and an Integrated Approach combining spectral bands with vegetation and water indices—using Sentinel-2 imageries (2019–2025) on the Google Earth Engine platform for a coastal area of 23,871.55 ha. Classification performance was assessed using User’s Accuracy, Producer’s Accuracy, Overall Accuracy (OA), the Kappa coefficient and the F1-Score. Findings indicate that the Integrated Approach, powered by a Random Forest algorithm, is the most robust, achieving an OA of 86.27–92.74%, Kappa coefficients of 0.78–0.88 and F1-Scores for the mangrove class of 91.16–99.50%. Unlike single-index methods (NDVI), which are sensitive to tidal submergence and underestimated the mangrove extent at only 2,576.23 ha in 2025, or RGB approaches that misclassify inland crops and overestimated the mangrove extent at up to 7,026.36 ha, the Integrated Approach effectively mitigates spectral confusion and spatial noise. Spatiotemporal analysis identified a stable core mangrove area of 3,750.05 ha out of 4,387.66 ha mapped in 2019, together with approximately 1,344.97 ha gained from non-mangrove areas, reflecting local restoration efforts. These findings underscore the necessity of multi-feature fusion (incorporating CMRI and MNDWI) for accurate coastal monitoring, providing a reliable framework for the sustainable management of Ninh Binh’s mangrove ecosystems.
journal: Journal of Forestry Science and Technology

title: Growing Degree Days to Estimate Crop Development Coefficient in Potato at North Mexico
abstract: Air temperature has increased due to global warming, growing degree days (GDD) use the air temperature for its estimation. Among the methods for estimating GDD, the exponential, physiological, residual, and modified sine methods are significantly similar, but the gradual method is the best option to estimate GDD. Climate variation prompts us to have climate-based models that use GDD to create crop development model. With five agroclimatic stations in locations were sowing potato. With agroclimatic stations estimate Eto is the reference evapotranspiration mm/day and ETr is the crop water consumption in the soil with water content sensor in kPa, gravimetric water content (Pw), with soil’s bulk density to obtain the volumetric content (θ) with the depth of soil water sensor at two depths (15 and 30 cm) to estimate daily consumption in mm/day. If kc = Etr/Eto, the kc is related daily to GDD, the best model estimated was third-degree models with R2 values greater than 0.90, the estimation of GDD with the models are highly significant. This contribution will allow us to estimate the crop coefficient (kc) by measuring temperature and relating it to the reference evapotranspiration (ETo) from agroclimatic stations, in order to determine the water consumption of the potato crop. Therefore, the models for every agroclimatic stations are suitable for climate variation.

title: பாசுரத்திலிருந்து புனிதப் புவியியலுக்கு திருமங்கையாழ்வாரின் பெரிய திருமொழியில் திவ்யதேசங்களின் எண்ணிம வரைபட ஆய்வு
abstract: In Tirumangai Alvar's Periya Tirumozhi, the sacred site is not only the place where the Lord dwells but also a space in which nature, memory, bodily experience and worship come together. This article subjects twelve pasurams relating to six Divya Desams—Tiruvenkatam, Tirukkadalmallai, Tiruvarangam, Tirunaraiyur, Tirukkannapuram and Tiruppullani—to close reading and digital coding. Four elements—place name, local water body, description of nature and the form of the deity—are encoded as data and compared by linking them with present-day geographic coordinates. Rather than treating every geographic word in a pasuram as the setting of the site, the study keeps apart local description, metaphor, mythological place and reference to another site. In the selected sample, local water references occur in three pasurams and local plant or agricultural description in five. At Tiruvarangam the flow of water and human life come together; at Tiruppullani the seashore and the memory of separation are linked; at Tirukkannapuram similes for the form of the deity are prominent. These results apply only to the twelve pasurams studied. The central argument is that sacred geography must be understood by reading the location of a place together with the semantic structure of the text. The digital map serves as a tool for testing this reading.
journal: KALANJIYAM - International Journal of Tamil Studies

title: Dynamic Stability and Neural Residual Forecasting of an Inverse Lomax Autoregressive Model with Application to NSPO Stock Prices
abstract: This study investigates an inverse-Lomax smooth-transition autoregressive (ILAR) model integrated with neural residual forecasting, using 319 weekly NSPO stock-price observations. The ILAR(1) map has a positive deterministic fixed point of 2.3507 and local spectral radius of 0.9345, but its derivative is 1.0193. The fitted deterministic map does not satisfy the sufficient global-contraction condition over the examined state interval. The estimated transition-shape parameter reaches its imposed upper bound ( ) and remains boundary-constrained when the bound is extended to 8. ADF and Phillips–Perron tests do not reject the unit-root null for price levels at 5%. The initial single-run ILAR-TCNA evaluation yielded an RMSE of 0.1427, compared with 0.1474 for the naive benchmark. A separate 20-seed experiment with trainable four-head attention produced mean test RMSE 0.1513 (SD 0.0063) and mean MAE 0.1215 (SD 0.0050). The validation procedure selected zero residual weight in 16 runs; the seed-4 Diebold–Mariano tests did not reject equal predictive accuracy against the naive and AR(1) forecasts. Penalized transition-parameter profiles also support weak identification. These findings indicate local deterministic stability but neither stochastic stationarity nor a reproducible neural forecasting advantage.

title: Weighting the weeks that matter: entropic tilting for epidemic forecast evaluation
abstract: The performance of infectious disease forecasting models is commonly calculated under the implicit assumption that forecast accuracy is equally important across time. This approach may obscure or under-weight differences in model performance during the epidemic periods that matter most for public-health decisions. Here, we introduce the weighted prequential score (WPS), a forecast evaluation framework that can emphasize epidemic periods of interest. The WPS is a weighted average of scores over time, where weights are constructed through entropic tilting which up-weights priority periods while keeping the WPS as close as possible to the arithmetic average. We demonstrate the WPS on forecasts of incident hospitalizations submitted to the CDC FluSight challenge, focusing on two priority periods: weeks of rapid growth in incidence and weeks near the seasonal peak. Across season-location-horizon pairs, doubling the weight assigned to priority periods changes the top-ranked model in 10%-26% of eligible settings, while the top-ranked model remains unchanged regardless of the amount of weight assigned in 37%-68% of settings. We demonstrate that for suitable weights, the models favored by the WPS yield an average gain in accuracy during priority periods that is at least as large as the average accuracy lost during the remaining weeks. Because weights can be defined using observed outcomes, the WPS is not a proper scoring rule. Hence, we recommend using the WPS as a retrospective evaluation diagnostic. The WPS can guide public-health practitioners in selecting models that perform well during periods most relevant to their decisions, while encouraging forecasting teams to improve accuracy during these critical weeks.

title: LabARIA: A Multi-Agent System for Integrative Analytics in Clinical Laboratories
abstract: Background Laboratory medicine underpins clinical decision-making across nearly every care setting. Clinical laboratory errors and delays can compromise diagnostic reliability and patient care. However, laboratory quality and operational data are commonly reviewed through separate manual workflows, limiting timely recognition of emerging problems across complementary data sources. Methods We developed and evaluated LabARIA (Laboratory Agentic Reasoning and Integrative Analytics), a multi-agent AI system for coordinated surveillance of specimen workflows, analytical quality control, and laboratory operations. We conducted a single-center retrospective system development and evaluation at NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell Medical Center using laboratory data collected from May 1 through June 18, 2026, including 177,480 specimen-panel records, 75,103 internal quality-control (IQC) measurements, 633 proficiency-testing challenges, and 422 recalibration or maintenance actions. Forecasting agents were evaluated using patient-result streams with controlled perturbations, and synthetic staffing and inventory data. We assessed specimen rejection, cancellation, and turnaround-time patterns; warning recall and lead time before documented laboratory actions; assay-specific patient-based real-time quality control (PBRTQC) performance; and exploratory operational forecasting discrimination. Findings LabARIA characterized specimen and workflow patterns across clinical units and time periods, including hemolysis-related potassium rejections in the intensive care unit during early morning hours (49 of 367 tests [13.3%]). For analytical quality monitoring, the IQC agent generated warnings before 407 of 422 recorded QC actions (recall, 0.964 [95% CI, 0.942-0.978]), with a median lead time of 5.40 days (95% CI, 3.75-6.07). PBRTQC agent selected different monitoring strategies across 35 analytes. In a separate analysis, adding PBRTQC increased action recall from 0.964 to 0.993 (95% CI, 0.979-0.998). A dashboard presented tiered alerts for human review, and an accompanying chatbot supported interactive exploration of the summaries. For the operational forecasting module, areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve for 7-day inventory and staffing risk forecasting were 0.800 (95% CI, 0.696-0.881) and 0.877 (95% CI, 0.778-0.950), respectively. Interpretation LabARIA demonstrated the feasibility of coordinating laboratory quality surveillance across heterogeneous data sources, providing a foundation for intelligent clinical laboratories. Prospective studies are warranted to determine whether this approach improves monitoring beyond conventional methods, supports laboratory decisions, and benefits patient care without excessive alert burden.

title: Professionally oriented digital tasks in developing information and communication competence of future master’s students in agricultural engineering
abstract: The article addresses the design of professionally oriented digital tasks for future master’s students in agricultural engineering. Its aim is to substantiate a task structure that connects engineering data analysis, digital modelling, verification of a proposed solution, and communication with a professional audience within one learning cycle. The study uses conceptual analysis of digital competence frameworks, alignment of learning outcomes with learning activities and assessment, and methodological modelling of agricultural engineering situations. A task specification is proposed that identifies a professional problem and its intended recipient, the provenance and limitations of data, available tools, the procedure for independent verification, and the required digital and communicative outputs. Observable evidence is mapped to four components of information and communication competence: information analysis, practical digital work, professional communication, and reflective and ethical judgement. A teaching case on selecting a machinery operating mode illustrates how students check input data, compare alternatives, test assumptions, prepare a technical recommendation, and defend it. Two additional task types concern variable-rate application and equipment condition monitoring. The paper further explains how an analytic rubric, a versioned electronic portfolio, and actionable feedback can support assessment and revision. Accessibility, responsible use of generative AI, and protection of personal and operational data are treated as design requirements. The outcome is a methodological model that may be adapted to courses in an agricultural engineering programme. The paper does not report an implemented intervention or empirical evidence of effectiveness; such evidence requires a separate, documented evaluation.

title: OPERATIONALIZATION OF THE INTEGRAL MODEL OF HEALTH IN THE HUMAN-ENVIRONMENT ECOSYSTEM: CRITERIA, VALIDATION, AND DIGITAL BOUNDARIES
abstract: The underlying integral model defines health as a dynamic state of integral human existence in interaction with the environment. This study aims to develop a conceptually coherent architecture for operationalizing this definition and a program for its subsequent empirical validation. A conceptual integrative synthesis was conducted across biopsychosocial, salutogenic, functional, capability-based, socio-ecological, humanities-based, public policy, and digital ethics approaches. The unit of analysis is the human-environment system, with the person as the primary agent in assessment and decision-making. Six interrelated criteria were developed: integrity and coherent interaction among dimensions; adaptability; maintenance and restoration of individual balance; functional capacity and agency; viability, self-realization, and generativity; and distributed responsibility. For each criterion, constructs, candidate indicators, data sources, levels of assessment, and risks of misinterpretation were identified. An operational chain linking definition, criterion, construct, indicator, data, assessment, decision, and feedback, together with a six-stage validation program, is proposed. Within this architecture, the healthcare professional acts as a clinical expert, interpreter, partner in shared decision-making, coordinator, and guarantor of safety, without holding exclusive authority over the definition of health. Economic productivity is regarded as an important, but not exhaustive, manifestation of human capacity. The framework establishes requirements for future digital and AI solutions while preserving human judgment.

title: Continuous indices improve on‐farm dairy soil health assessment compared with management categories
abstract: Quantifying management impacts on soil health often relies on categorical classifications that lack regional consistency and fail to capture temporal variability in management intensity. We evaluated whether continuous indices of cropping‐system management better explained variation in soil health indicators than categorical management (tilled vs. reduced tillage) in dairy forage fields in New York and Wisconsin. Models using living‐root index (LRI) and reduced‐disturbance index (RDI) were compared with categorical models for soil organic carbon (SOC), aggregate stability, carbon mineralization potential (Cmin), and available water‐holding capacity (AWHC). Model sensitivity was tested across 1‐ to 4‐year history windows using arithmetic and exponential‐decay‐weighted means. Continuous indices explained the most additional variation for Cmin across regions, with region‐dependent improvements for aggregate stability and AWHC, and little improvement for SOC. Model performance increased generally with the history window length. Exponential‐decay weighting did not improve model performance, suggesting this fixed weighting added little information beyond arithmetic means.

title: Integrating Biotechnology and Artificial Intelligence for Circular Food Systems: A Critical Review of Evidence, Trade‐offs, and Research Priorities
abstract: Food systems remain largely linear, generating large amounts of food loss and waste and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while being increasingly exposed to climatic, geopolitical, and economic shocks. Biotechnology and artificial intelligence (AI) are supported circular food systems (CFS), but their combined benefits remain unclear. This narrative review, based on a structured search of five bibliographic databases, examines how biotechnological conversion routes (fermentation, enzyme‐assisted extraction, engineered microbial cell factories, crop biotechnology, and bio‐based packaging) and AI tools (machine learning, computer vision, soft sensors, and predictive models) interact across production, processing, packaging, and distribution. A four‐level integration framework is proposed, covering organism and enzyme design, bioprocess operation, feedstock and supply‐chain logistics, and product quality and traceability, and the maturity of the supporting evidence is assessed for each level. Most reported gains derive from laboratory‐ or pilot‐scale studies and from AI models validated on limited, single‐site datasets; techno‐economic and life‐cycle evidence for integrated bio‐digital systems is scarce, and trade‐offs in energy, water, cost and food safety are rarely quantified. Research priorities include open and representative datasets, externally validated and interpretable models, harmonized circularity indicators coupled with life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno‐economic analysis (TEA), and pilot‐scale demonstrations under realistic regulatory conditions.

title: Scalp high-frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. Biomarkers derived from routine EEG may aid identification of neonates with seizures. We investigated whether scalp high-frequency oscillation (HFO) rates derived from the first eligible routine EEG (1) differentiate neonates with HIE with and without seizures; and (2) contribute to seizure classification alongside established clinical, neurophysiological, and imaging biomarkers. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed routine scalp EEG recordings from 33 term neonates with HIE (17 with seizures, 16 without), obtained at a mean postnatal age of 4 ± 3 days. The mean analyzed EEG duration was 38 ± 14 min in neonates with seizures and 36 ± 20 min in those without. HFO rates in sleep segments were quantified using a validated automated detector. RESULTS Scalp HFO rates were significantly higher in neonates with seizures than in those without (.12 ± .11 vs. .03 ± .02 HFOs/min/channel, adjusted p = .02). An HFO rate threshold of .07 HFOs/min/channel optimally discriminated neonates who had seizures from those who did not (area under the curve [AUC] = .81). HFO rates did not differ significantly according to HIE severity, therapeutic hypothermia, antiseizure medication response, EEG background activity, or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities. Multivariable models incorporating HFO rate, EEG background activity, and MRI findings showed discrimination (AUC = .92, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .69-1.00 for logistic regression; AUC = 1.00, 95% CI = .75-1.00 for random forest), with HFO rate as the strongest contributor to seizure classification. SIGNIFICANCE These findings support scalp HFO rate as a potential electrophysiological biomarker of seizure occurrence in neonatal HIE, complementary to EEG background assessment and MRI findings. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether HFOs can predict subsequent seizures.

title: Inferring geographic origin in genebank accessions from genome-wide SNP variation: A barley case study.
abstract: Accurate geographic metadata are essential for using genebank accessions in spatial analyses, but many historical records lack precise coordinates or contain uncertain location information. We developed SNP2GPS, a plant-genomics workflow for inferring geographic origin from genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphism data and supporting passport metadata curation in barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) collections. SNP2GPS integrates genotype preprocessing, neural network-based coordinate prediction, repeated model training, uncertainty estimation, spatial consistency checks, visualization, and extraction of approximate coordinates from free-text locality descriptors. Models were trained on curated passport coordinates from the Leibniz Institute of Plant Genetics and Crop Plant Research barley collection and applied to accessions lacking precise geolocation data. On an independent test set of 200 withheld accessions, the base model achieved a mean prediction error of 383 km and a median error of 58 km; an augmented model using additional country-centroid labels achieved a mean error of 427 km and a median error of 56 km. Country-centroid augmentation increased geographic coverage in undersampled regions, though at the cost of reduced robustness for some samples. SNP2GPS also identified accessions with large discrepancies between recorded and predicted locations, flagging candidates for metadata review. Prediction uncertainty was lower in wild barley than in domesticated material, consistent with a stronger coupling between genetic structure and geography in wild populations. SNP2GPS provides an open, uncertainty-aware framework for imputing incomplete geolocation metadata, identifying inconsistent passport records, and delivering reusable predicted coordinates through downloadable outputs and web-based visualization.

Dedifferentiation stabilizes stem cell lineages: from stochastic models to diffusion theory and thresholds
abstract: We study stem–terminally differentiated (TD) lineages in small niches where demographic noise from discrete division and death events is non-negligible. Starting from a mechanistic five-channel (symmetric self-renewal, symmetric differentiation, asymmetric division, dedifferentiation, TD death), density-dependent continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC), we derive its mean-field limit and functional central limit theorem (FCLT), which motivate a mechanism-consistent chemical Langevin diffusion approximation. Within this diffusion approximation we remove the dedifferentiation flux and obtain a sharp dichotomy: in subcritical regimes the stem coordinate becomes extinct asymptotically almost surely, whereas in supercritical regimes polynomial moments diverge exponentially. This identifies, at the diffusion level, a structural failure mode of strictly hierarchical lineages under demographic fluctuations and clarifies how a cyclic return flux can rescue homeostasis. For interpretation we also derive an exact total ordinary differential equation (ODE) backbone and obtain two steady-state constraints (ratio and equalization laws) linking compartment ratios to turnover and balancing dedifferentiation against fate bias. Genetic diversity and core SNP marker development for dragon fruit (Selenicereus spp.) germplasm identification and breeding
abstract: Dragon fruit (Selenicereus spp.) is a nutritious and economically important tropical and subtropical fruit crop, mainly cultivated in Central America, Southeast Asia and East Asia. However, the molecular basis of flesh color variation remains poorly understood. Traditional germplasm classification mainly relies on phenotypic traits such as fruit skin and flesh color and stem morphology, which often leads to misclassification due to phenotypic similarity and frequent interspecific hybridization, thus hindering efficient breeding and germplasm utilization. In this study, we used SLAF-seq (Specific-Locus Amplified Fragment Sequencing) to develop SNP (Single Nucleotide Polymorphism) markers and perform genetic characterization on 45 dragon fruit accessions, and obtained 1,206,498 high-quality SNPs after strict filtering. Genetic diversity analysis showed that the diversity levels of the three main taxa were significantly higher than the overall level. Population structure and phylogenetic analyses clearly distinguished three genetic groups and corrected several misclassified accessions. Furthermore, we constructed a hierarchical core SNP marker set, among which the 10-SNP ultra-core panel showed optimal discrimination ability with 100% accuracy in independent germplasm validation. This panel effectively overcame the misleading effect of flesh color phenotype caused by hybrid germplasm. This study clarified the genetic diversity and population structure of cultivated dragon fruit, resolved germplasm classification confusion, and developed a set of efficient and diagnostic SNP markers. Furthermore, through phenotype-driven SNP screening and transcriptomic analysis, we identified four candidate genes (bHLH, CYP450, POD12, and MATE transporter) that show strong co-expression with key betalain biosynthesis genes (CYP76AD1-1 and DODA1), providing molecular insights into flesh color regulation. These results provide a solid foundation for germplasm management, parental selection and molecular-assisted breeding of dragon fruit, and will promote the genetic improvement and sustainable development of this important horticultural crop.

Uncoupling traits, colonization, and benefits: genotype-dependent growth promotion by endophytic bacteria in Poaceae, including perennial Kernza
abstract: Thinopyrum intermedium (Kernza) is a perennial Poaceae crop with potential benefits for soil health and contributes to climate change mitigation. In this study, we investigated whether bacterial functional traits and abundance predict growth responses across different Poaceae species. From 21 investigated bacterial strains representing endophytic and rhizosphere strains, five endophytes (Labedella endophytica FR-P-L-64, Pseudomonas lini FR-P-R2-32, Pantoea sp. GT2-2-ED1, Pseudomonas stutzeri ISE-12, Streptomyces phaeochromogenes ISE-4) were selected based on their plant-growth promoting (PGP) traits related to phytohormone production, nutrient assimilation, and stress alleviation. Phenotypic profiling revealed substantial metabolic diversity among the selected strains: P. lini FR-P-R2-32 showed the broadest spectrum of substrate utilization, while S. phaeochromogenes ISE-4 utilized only 10 of the 94 substrates. The strains were evaluated for their ability to promote plant growth in different Poaceae hosts, including two wheat cultivars, two perennial ryegrass varieties, and the perennial grain crop Kernza. Plant responses to inoculation were genotype-dependent: only S. phaeochromogenes ISE-4 increased shoot and root dry weight in Kernza and wheat cv. Euforia, whereas the remaining strains produced neutral or negative effects. Strain-specific quantitative PCR targeting the 16 S rRNA gene revealed distinct colonization patterns in shoots and roots including systemic, organ-specific, and limited colonization. Regression models indicated that post-inoculation endophyte abundance was positively or negatively associated with plant biomass, depending on the plant genotype. These findings highlight the importance of host genotype in determining the effectiveness of bacterial bioinoculants. This study provides the first functional characterization of bacterial endophytes isolated from T. intermedium.

AI and the Responsibility-Bearing Status of Authorship
abstract: Generative AI has sharpened an old question: who, or what, can be an author? The central aim of this paper is to reconstruct the conception of authorship already implicit in copyright law. I argue that copyright encodes authorship as a responsibility-bearing status, constituted by a cluster of conditions: intentional agency, guided control, and relational expression (ACE). The paper’s contribution is to make that conception explicit, to show that the human-authorship rule is best understood as a proxy for those capacities, not a species predicate, and to explain why this generates a tension with recognizing current generative AI systems as authors unless one is prepared to attribute to them the thicker agential capacities ACE requires. On that basis, the paper also clarifies why AI-assisted works may still be human-authored, while some AI-generated outputs give rise to genuine authorship gaps.

Comparison of the neuroprotective effects of tryptamide and ibuprofen in cellular Parkinson's disease models: cell damage type- and cell phenotype-dependent effects.
abstract: BACKGROUND Tryptamide (TRP) is an experimental anti-inflammatory and analgesic drug with a favourable safety profile even at high doses. Since neuroinflammation is a significant contributor to the pathogenesis of various neurodegenerative diseases, in this study we screened for the potential direct neuroprotective effect of TRP in comparison to the classical anti-inflammatory compound, ibuprofen (Ibu), in cellular models of Parkinson's disease. METHODS We compared the effectiveness of TRP (1-300 µM) with Ibu (10-300 µM) against cell damage induced by oxidative stress inducers (H2O2 and 6-hydroxydopamine, 6-OHDA), dopaminergic neurotoxin 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium ion (MPP(+)), and pro-apoptotic factors, staurosporine (St) and doxorubicin (Dox) in undifferentiated (UN-) and retinoic acid (RA)-differentiated human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells. The neuroprotective effects were evidenced by biochemical assays (MTT reduction and LDH release tests), morphology (microscopic evaluation), and caspase-3 activity, as well as validated in mouse primary mesencephalic neurons. RESULTS We demonstrated that TRP and Ibu at concentrations up to 100 µM, when given for 24 and 48 h, did not evoke any detrimental effects in UN- and RA-SH-SY5Y cells, but induced some cytotoxicity at the highest concentration tested (300 µM) in UN-SH-SY5Y cells. TRP significantly attenuated the cytotoxic effect of MPP(+) in UN- and RA-SH-SY5Y cells and was protective against H2O2, St, and Dox only in differentiated cells, however, it did not attenuate the 6-OHDA-induced cell death in both cell phenotypes. Moreover, the protection of TRP against MPP(+) and St, but not against Dox, was associated with inhibition of caspase-3 activity. Ibu did not show any protection in either of the tested cell models or cell phenotypes, with the exception of minor protection (10 µM) against St in UN-SH-SY5Y cells. The effects of TRP were orthogonally confirmed by high-content imaging of Calcein AM/Hoechst 33,342-stained RA-SH-SY5Y cells exposed to MPP(+) and of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-immunostained mouse primary mesencephalic neurons exposed to MPP(+) or 6-OHDA. CONCLUSIONS Our results evidenced a neuroprotective potential of TRP against various cell-damaging factors, with its higher effectiveness in RA-SH-SY5Y cells in apoptotic, rather than oxidative stress-based neuronal cell damage models, which was also confirmed in primary mesencephalic neurons. TRP effects on RA-differentiated neurons were further validated by energy metabolism profile and high-content imaging in the MPP(+) model. Thus, TRP has neuroprotective potential, worth further investigation.

title: Insect-resistant rice and Metarhizium anisopliae sustain the brown planthopper susceptibility through AMPK-mediated lipid redistribution
abstract: The brown planthopper (BPH), Nilaparvata lugens , rapidly overcomes host resistance and develops insecticide resistance, undermining sustainable rice pest control. Here, we show that combining insect-resistant rice IR36 with the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium anisopliae CQMa421 provides durable suppression of BPH under laboratory conditions. Across multiple generations, chemical insecticides drove resistance and host adaptation, whereas M. anisopliae maintained susceptibility. Combined exposure redistributed lipids by reducing diacylglycerol (DAG) and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in the fat body and ovary while increasing DAG in the hemolymph, thereby prioritizing humoral immunity. This redistribution was mediated by AMPK activation in the fat body, which inhibited insulin signaling and lipid catabolism while limiting detoxification and reproduction. AMPK-mediated energy reallocation sustained BPH sensitivity to both resistant rice and fungal infection. Integrating plant resistance with microbial biocontrol therefore suppresses host adaptation and delays resistance evolution, offering a sustainable pest management strategy.

title: Soft computing evaluation of luffa oil epoxide development using luffa fiber catalyst
abstract: Epoxidation of luffa oil was performed using a heterogeneous catalyst developed from calcined luffa fibres. Although luffa oil has previously been epoxidized for biopolymer and polyol production, no study has reported the use of luffa fibre as a catalyst for epoxidation reactions, presenting a clear research gap. Additionally, existing studies lack comprehensive comparative modeling using soft-computing techniques. The fibres were initially washed, dried, pulverized with a ball mill, and sieved to a particle size of 300 μm. They were then treated with 0.5 M sulphuric acid and calcined at 700 °C for four hours to introduce active sites. Characterization using FTIR, SEM, XRD, BET surface analysis, and XRF confirmed that --SO₃H functional groups were successfully incorporated onto the catalyst surface. Process optimization was carried out using catalyst loading, reaction duration, and temperature as the key input factors, while the oxirane value was taken as the output response. Increasing these operational variables led to a notable rise in oxirane yield. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was used to identify the best reaction conditions, and the resulting quadratic model was validated through ANOVA, which produced R² = 0.9927, adjusted R² = 0.9833, and predicted R² = 0.8828 indicating strong model performance. Three-dimensional surface plots further highlighted the significant effects of the variables on oxirane formation. Model accuracy was assessed using R² and mean square error (MSE). The highest oxirane yield (3.34 mol) was obtained at a catalyst loading of 1.62 wt%, reaction time of 6.81 h, and temperature of 57.34 °C. Additional predictive analyses using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) showed that ANFIS provided superior predictive reliability, achieving R² = 0.9969 and MSE = 6.7 × 10⁻⁷, compared with ANN results (R² = 0.9378, MSE = 0.060991). FTIR and GC-MS examination of the resulting epoxide confirmed the formation of oxirane functional groups. The dual utilization of the luffa plant—employing its oil as feedstock and its fibre as catalyst—represents a novel, sustainable approach that enhances the industrial value of this non-edible crop. The findings demonstrate that soft-computing techniques, particularly ANFIS, offer robust predictive capabilities for optimizing bioepoxide production, providing a framework for developing cost-effective, environmentally benign catalysts and reducing dependence on petrochemical-derived epoxides.
