Transcriptomic benchmarking positions iPSC-Derived intestinal organoids as immature, non-malignant epithelial references for colorectal cancer tissue.
abstract: Primary colorectal cancer (CRC) biopsies and intestinal organoids are frequently compared to define tumor-associated epithelial alterations; however, these systems differ in malignant status, tissue composition, developmental state, and epithelial maturation. In this study, transcriptomic profiling of CRC biopsies, matched normal intestinal tissue, and iPSC-derived intestinal organoids (iIOs) was performed to define the biological axes separating primary tissue from organoid epithelial states. Transcriptome-wide analysis revealed strong separation between CRC biopsies and iIOs, with iIOs diverging from primary tissue more extensively than tumors differed from normal mucosa. Pathway enrichment and cell deconvolution showed that biopsies were dominated by immune, inflammatory, and stromal programs reflecting tissue complexity, whereas iIOs were enriched for proliferative, biosynthetic, and metabolic programs. Projection onto a malignancy axis placed iIOs at a neutral position, indicating that their divergence stems from developmental state rather than malignant transformation. Compared to normal mucosa, organoids reproducibly lost adult tissue-associated immune/stromal programs while gaining proliferative, fetal-like epithelial programs. Gut Cell Atlas scoring, crypt-surface positioning, and lineage deconvolution showed that iIOs retain intestinal epithelial identity but occupy a developmentally immature, crypt/progenitor-biased state dominated by transit-amplifying programs with limited differentiated lineage diversity. Metabolic module analysis and anabolism-proliferation correlation showed that elevated metabolic activity in iIOs, including biosynthetic and nucleotide synthesis programs. These reflect proliferation-coupled anabolism rather than malignancy-like metabolic reprogramming; the glycolysis-OXPHOS balance did not differ significantly between groups. Consequently, iIOs represent metabolically active, fetal-like, crypt/progenitor epithelial reference models rather than direct transcriptomic surrogates of adult intestinal mucosa or primary CRC tissue. These results clarify the utility and limitations of iIOs as epithelial reference models for colorectal cancer research.

title: Houttuynin counteracts osteoporosis by abrogating CHIP-mediated ubiquitination of ESR1 and curtailing osteoclastogenesis.
abstract: This study investigated the protective effects of Houttuynin against postmenopausal osteoporosis and the molecular mechanisms underlying its regulation of osteoclastogenesis. The effects of Houttuynin were assessed in an ovariectomized (OVX) mouse model by evaluating bone mineral density (BMD), trabecular microarchitecture, and hepatic and renal safety. A receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL)-induced osteoclast differentiation model was used to examine osteoclast formation and bone resorptive activity. Target identification, protein interaction analysis, ubiquitination assays, and protein stability evaluation were performed to investigate the relationship between Houttuynin and estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1). Houttuynin treatment alleviated OVX-induced bone loss and preserved trabecular microarchitecture. Mechanistically, Houttuynin interacted with ESR1 and reduced carboxyl terminus of Hsp70-interacting protein (CHIP)-mediated ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of ESR1, thereby maintaining its protein stability. Preservation of ESR1 suppressed RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption, whereas ESR1 depletion weakened the inhibitory effects of Houttuynin. No obvious hepatic or renal toxicity was observed following Houttuynin administration. These findings identify ESR1 stabilization as an important mechanism contributing to the anti-osteoporotic effects of Houttuynin. By limiting CHIP-mediated ESR1 degradation, Houttuynin suppresses excessive osteoclast activation and may represent a potential strategy for targeting osteoclast-related bone loss.

title: From Quantum Brain to Quantum Mind: The Ontological Promotion Gap in Quantum-Biological Theories of Consciousness.
abstract: Quantum effects in biological systems are increasingly investigated at molecular, cellular, and neural scales, yet evidence for quantum organization in a living brain does not by itself determine the ontological status of the conscious states realized by that brain. This article distinguishes seven claims often compressed under "quantum consciousness": quantum occurrence, causal relevance, constitutive relevance, phenomenal bridging, phenomenal individuation, quantum mental status, and quantum-formal adequacy. It argues that evidence for the first three-even if decisive-does not by itself establish quantum mental status. I call this cross-level inferential discontinuity the Ontological Promotion Gap. The argument is developed in relation to current quantum-biological approaches to consciousness, including hierarchical microtubule models, nuclear-spin mechanisms, non-classical neuroimaging, dissipative quantum-brain models, autopoietic quantum constraints, and quantum-like cognition. Drawing on multilevel biological organization and contemporary neurophenomenology, the paper introduces a Phenomenal Individuation Condition: for a conscious state to be non-trivially quantum, quantum-specific structure must contribute to the organization or counterfactual differentiation of the phenomenal state itself, rather than merely occur within its biological realization. Quantum-like cognition supplies the converse dissociation: quantum formalism can characterize cognition without establishing quantum physical implementation. The resulting framework yields a Level-Specific Quantum Attribution Principle and an explicit experimental decision structure for determining what different classes of quantum-biological evidence do-and do not-license us to conclude about a quantum mind.

title: Integrated assessment of soil salinity dynamics on the dried Aral Seabed based on field observations, geochemical analysis, remote sensing, and machine learning
NANOG and OCT4 dosage shapes non-monotonic gene expression responses during stem cell differentiation.
abstract: Precise regulation of transcription factor (TF) expression is critical for maintaining cell identity, but studies on how graded expression levels affect cellular phenotypes are limited. To address this gap, we employed human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) as a dynamic model to study gene dosage effects and systematically titrated key TFs NANOG and OCT4 expression using CRISPR interference (CRISPRi). We then profiled transcriptomic changes in hESCs under self-renewal and definitive endoderm (DE) differentiation conditions using single-cell RNA-seq. Quantitative modeling of these Perturb-seq datasets uncovered distinct response patterns for different types of genes, including a striking non-monotonic up-regulation of on-target lineage genes during DE differentiation. This behavior extended to the ESC-to-neuroectoderm transition, suggesting non-monotonic responses of lineage genes to pluripotency regulator dosage are a recurring feature of lineage transitions. Together, these findings underscore the importance of characterizing TF function across a gradient of expression levels.

Integrated Engineering Strategies Boosting Isoprenol Biosynthesis in Serratia marcescens via Extractant Screening, Phosphatase Redesign and Promoter-Modulated Expression Balancing.
abstract: Isoprenol is a high-value platform chemical that has garnered significant attention in recent years as a key precursor for sustainable aviation fuel. However, the low tolerance of model microorganisms to isoprenol severely limits the efficiency of its microbial synthesis. In this study, a Serratia marcescens strain with broad-spectrum tolerance to terpenoids was employed as the chassis cell, and systematic engineering was conducted from three dimensions: in situ product detoxification, modification of key enzyme elements, and combinatorial regulation of promoters. First, by systematically evaluating the extraction partition coefficients and cell compatibility of various organic solvents, dodecanol was identified as the optimal extractant for a two-phase fermentation system, enabling in situ extraction of isoprenol during fermentation. Second, based on transcriptomic analysis, endogenous phosphatase resources were screened, and an endogenous phosphatase with isopentenyl monophosphate (IP) hydrolytic activity was identified in Serratia marcescens. Using the "Energy-Evolution-Channel (EEC)" semi-rational design strategy, a reusable framework for prioritizing mutation sites, we performed semi-rational design of this phosphatase and obtained a mutant capable of efficient isoprenol production. Subsequently, the expression levels of mevalonate kinase (MVK) in the mevalonate (MVA) pathway and the key phosphatase were regulated via differentiated promoter combinations to favor isoprenol production. Finally, the above optimization strategies were systematically integrated to construct a two-phase fermentation process. In a 5L bioreactor with fed-batch fermentation for 96h, the isoprenol titer reached 12.7g/L.

GDF-15 and sST2 as independent predictors of long-term mortality in hospitalized older adults: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: Growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) and soluble ST2 (sST2) reflect systemic biological stress, inflammation, and aging-related processes, but their prognostic relevance in hospitalized older adults remains unclear. We prospectively studied 966 patients aged ≥65 years from the Report-AGE cohort. Circulating GDF-15 and sST2 were measured at hospital admission, and all-cause mortality was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for demographic characteristics, frailty, comorbidity burden, and routine laboratory parameters. Incremental prognostic value was assessed using likelihood ratio tests, Harrell's C-index, and time-dependent ROC analyses. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, 805 deaths occurred. Higher GDF-15 and sST2 levels independently predicted mortality after multivariable adjustment (GDF-15: HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.17-1.49; sST2: HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.12-1.36; both p<0.001). Each biomarker significantly improved model fit, with additional gains when both were jointly included. Model discrimination improved modestly but consistently over time. In patients with cardiovascular disease, GDF-15 retained incremental prognostic value, whereas that of sST2 was attenuated. Their complementary prognostic information may capture distinct, partially overlapping pathways of biological vulnerability not fully reflected by conventional measures. Overall, combined assessment of GDF-15 and sST2 may improve long-term risk stratification beyond conventional clinical and laboratory markers in hospitalized older adults.

title: IL-17Rb mediates the pathogenesis of allergic rhinitis through STAT6-dependent regulation of TH2 cells and type 2 inflammatory cytokines.
abstract: BACKGROUND Allergic rhinitis (AR) is characterized by a T helper 2 (Th2)-cell-mediated immune imbalance, yet its upstream molecular drivers remain poorly defined. Interleukin-17 receptor B (IL-17Rb) has been implicated in type 2 inflammation, but its precise functional role and mechanism in AR pathogenesis are unclear. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to identify key immunoregulatory genes in AR via bioinformatics and to comprehensively elucidate the functional role and mechanisms of IL-17Rb using both in vivo animal and in vitro cellular models. METHODS Candidate genes were screened using GEO datasets and machine learning. An HDM-induced AR murine model and in vitro cell models were utilized. AAV-mediated IL-17Rb knockdown or overexpression, alongside a specific STAT6 inhibitor (AS1517499), were employed. Evaluations included nasal symptoms, histopathology, STAT6 activation, and parameters of Th2 inflammation alongside the Th1/Th17/Treg balance (IL-4/5/13, IFN-γ, IL-17A, IL-10). RESULTS Bioinformatics identified IL-17Rb as a pivotal upregulated gene in AR, correlating with Th2 infiltration (r = 0.74). In vivo, IL-17Rb knockdown alleviated AR symptoms, eosinophil/mast cell infiltration, and type 2 cytokine release. Importantly, it rectified the AR-associated immune imbalance by restoring IFN-γ (Th1) and IL-10 (Treg) while reducing IL-17A (Th17). Conversely, IL-17Rb overexpression exacerbated Th2 inflammation and STAT6 phosphorylation. Co-administration of AS1517499 successfully abrogated these overexpression-induced effects, confirming a STAT6-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, in vitro blockade of IL-17Rb inhibited IL-25-promoted Th2 differentiation and STAT6 activation. CONCLUSION IL-17Rb is a critical upstream immunoregulator in AR, driving STAT6-dependent Th2 inflammation and broadly modulating the Th1/Th17/Treg balance. Targeting the IL-17Rb/STAT6 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy.

title: Integrating satellite remote sensing and deep learning for mapping glacier boundary and its changes in the Himalaya
journal: Physics and Chemistry of the Earth, Parts A/B/C

title: TPA-induced differentiation enhances dopamine and noradrenaline synthesis in SH-SY5Y cells with L-DOPA supplementation.
abstract: SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells are a widely used in vitro model for studying neuronal differentiation and monoaminergic signalling. However, their ability to produce and release catecholamines under different protocols remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we analysed the catecholamine profile in undifferentiated cells and in three other differentiation conditions: retinoic acid (RA), 12-O-tetradecanoylphorbol-13-acetate (TPA), and sequential RA/TPA treatment. Catecholamine levels were quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography with electrochemical detection, and enzymatic activities of aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC), dopamine β-hydroxylase (DBH), and catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) were assessed in TPA differentiated SH-SY5Y. Basal dopamine and noradrenaline levels were very low across all conditions. Supplementation with L-DOPA significantly enhanced catecholamine production, with the strongest effect observed in TPA-differentiated cells. This protocol also increased L-DOPA uptake as well as AADC activity, while DBH and COMT activities remained unchanged. We conclude that TPA-differentiated SH-SY5Y cells supplemented with L-DOPA provide an optimized system for modelling dopaminergic and noradrenergic pathways, supporting their application in toxicology and psychopharmacology studies.

title: Tracking US tidal marsh extent and change with dense Landsat time series and comparisons with existing products
Interdependent conditions for successful human-AI delegation.
abstract: People increasingly rely on AI systems for consequential tasks, from clinical diagnosis to software development. The gains are real yet difficult to realize reliably. We identify four psychological and structural conditions for successful delegation: accurate human assessment of AI capabilities, calibrated AI uncertainty communication, sustained human monitoring capacity, and compatible task structure. Each condition is well-studied, yet we propose that they form an interdependent system in which each one's effectiveness depends on the state of the others. Because these dependencies are bidirectional, we suggest that they can compound over time into virtuous cycles or cascading degradation, and that improving any single condition can fail or shift the bottleneck. These dynamics should intensify as AI moves from advisory roles to autonomous agents.

title: Uncovering vitivirus diversity in Brazilian pineapple germplasm: pineapple virus A and two novel vitiviruses.
abstract: A virome investigation by high-throughput sequencing of accessions from the pineapple germplasm bank of Embrapa Mandioca e Fruticultura (Cruz das Almas, Bahia, Brazil) led to the discovery of novel isolates of pineapple virus A (PiVA), and of two previously undescribed vitiviruses. The three PiVA genome sequences reconstructed in this study showed ∼97% identity to the only one sequence available in GenBank, from Reunion Island, with highest diversity in the putative open reading frame 2. Molecular characterization of the newly discovered vitiviruses revealed the typical organization of members of the genus Vitivirus. Inspection of sequence divergence in the replicase and coat protein amino acid sequences showed highest identity with the corresponding sequences of PiVA for one entity (∼65% and ∼83% identity, respectively), and with blueberry green mosaic associated virus (∼51% and 56%, respectively) for the second one, supporting their classification as members of two novel vitivirus species. The common names "pineapple vitivirus B" and "pineapple vitivirus C" are proposed. Development of a novel RT-PCR assay allowed a small-scale screening of pineapple accessions from the same germplasm open-field collection at Embrapa, revealing widespread occurrence of the PiVA, PiVB and PiVC. Our study expands the known diversity within the genus Vitivirus, family Betaflexiviridae, and provides the basis for establishing diagnostic workflows for large-scale screening. Such tools will be essential for assessing the distribution, transmission, and impact of these viruses on crop health, as well as for developing effective sanitation and virus-elimination strategies to support the propagation and distribution of healthy planting material.

title: A pulse oximetry warning system predicts severity of late-onset sepsis in very low birth weight neonates.
abstract: BACKGROUND Late-onset sepsis (LOS) causes morbidity and mortality in very-low birthweight (VLBW) neonates. We previously developed a machine learning model, the Pulse Oximetry Warning System (POWS), to predict LOS in the next 24 h. The neonatal Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (nSOFA) score predicts sepsis mortality. We hypothesized that POWS scores would differentiate severe LOS events, defined by nSOFA >4, from milder events. METHODS We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study including VLBW infants diagnosed with culture-confirmed LOS with continuous vital sign data available. Mixed-effects regression was used to examine the association between POWS and nSOFA. RESULTS We analyzed 89 LOS episodes in 84 VLBW infants. Severe sepsis (nSOFA >4 within 48 h of blood culture) occurred in 27 (30%) episodes. Mean POWS scores were higher in the 24 h before severe LOS than non-severe LOS. POWS rose more steeply in the hours before sepsis diagnosis among infants with severe LOS. CONCLUSION POWS scores, predicting risk of LOS in the next 24 h, have a significantly higher rate of rise in severe episodes as compared to less severe episodes as measured by nSOFA. This result adds to evidence that POWS could prompt earlier intervention that improves sepsis outcomes. IMPACT Late-onset sepsis (LOS) is a leading cause of death and disability in premature infants. The Pulse Oximetry Warning System (POWS) uses continuous heart rate and oxygen saturation data to predict sepsis up to 24 h before clinical diagnosis. This study demonstrates that POWS rises more steeply before severe sepsis episodes, as defined by the neonatal Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (nSOFA) score, than before milder episodes. POWS thus may provide earlier warning of the most severe sepsis events, potentially enabling earlier intervention in this vulnerable population.

title: Genotoxic stress responses in wild-type and Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome hiPSC and NPC models of early development
abstract: Benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide (BPDE), a metabolite of Benzo[a]pyrene, is a byproduct of incomplete combustion of organic matter. The accumulation of BPDE-DNA bulky adducts can lead to mutations caused by DNA base-pair substitutions. Although the effects of BPDE on somatic cells have been described, its harmful effects on early human development have not been studied. Here, we investigated the effect of BPDE on human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and their differentiated neural progenitor cells (NPCs) as a model of early embryonic development. Furthermore, we compared hiPSCs and NPCs derived from patient suffering from Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome (NBS), which is a chromosomal instability disorder characterized by defective DNA repair and increased risk of malignancies. Transcriptome and selected protein analysis indicated that hiPSCs compared to NPCs are more sensitive to BPDE exposure. The affected biological processes included p53-mediated DNA damage response, DNA repair by lesion bypass, cell cycle checkpoints and extrinsic apoptosis. In addition, NBS-derived cells exhibited a reduced apoptotic response and a distinct p53 response compared their healthy counterparts. Overall, this iPSC-based model provides insights into the cellular responses to BPDE during early human development in both healthy individuals and NBS patients.

title: Probabilistic Response of Prestressed Concrete Box Girder Bridges under Stochastic Temperature–Humidity Environmental Conditions
abstract: To investigate the evolution of mechanical behavior in concrete box girder bridges during cantilever construction under the coupled influence of stochastic environmental temperature and humidity, a novel simulation method is proposed. This method integrates a temperature–humidity coupling analysis method for the internal fields of concrete and a constitutive model that accounts for multifactor interactions, including temperature-induced stress, drying shrinkage, creep, and the sensitivity of elastic modulus. The proposed method was applied to simulate and analyze the construction process of the Yuanhe Bridge in Jiangxi Province, China. Based on the statistical analysis of nearly two decades of daily historical meteorological data from the region, it was verified through fitting tests and statistical assessments that the probability distributions of temperature, humidity, and wind speed conform to Gaussian (normal) distributions. The results systematically reveal the statistical influences of stochastic environmental factors on the bridge’s camber, shear-lag effect, and prestress loss. The results indicate that the maximum camber and the shear-lag coefficient at the bottom slab–web junction exhibit slightly asymmetric distributions and can be well described by Bigaussian fitting curves, whereas the shear-lag coefficient at the top slab–web junction follows a Gaussian distribution. Increases in the daily temperature range and decreases in relative humidity are found to amplify the camber and the prestress loss. No discernible influence of wind speed on the camber, shear-lag effect, or prestress loss is observed. This study provides a crucial theoretical foundation and technical support for the refined control and optimization of cantilever construction of bridges under stochastic environmental conditions.

title: Deciphering the molecular mechanisms linking abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain activity to myeloid cell activation in systemic lupus erythematosus through multi-scale transcriptomics.
abstract: Abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain (MRC) activity is a pivotal driver in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). However, the molecular mechanisms linking it to immune phenotypes and disease progression remain unclear. This study aims to systematically determine core biomarkers of MRC dysfunction in SLE and explore their potential pathogenic mechanisms through multi-scale transcriptomic analysis. Five bulk transcriptomic series from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were integrated to screen for differentially expressed genes linked to MRC abnormalities. Three machine learning algorithms and SHAP analysis were applied to identify core signature genes. Leveraging these markers, a diagnostic model was developed, along with constructing molecular interaction and regulatory networks. We elucidated the biological functions through functional enrichment, immune infiltration analyzes, and correlation analysis with key therapeutic targets. Furthermore, we integrated three single-cell datasets and applied Seurat clustering, pseudotime analysis, and CellChat to characterize the expression patterns, differentiation trajectories, and interaction networks of core genes within specific cell subpopulations. Our results identified 18 biomarkers, with SCO2 emerging as the primary core gene. The diagnostic model achieved high discriminatory accuracy. Multi-dimensional functional analyzes uncovered a potential role for SCO2 bridging mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction with antiviral innate immune activation. Single-cell analysis localized SCO2 overexpression primarily to monocytes and dendritic cells, showing a downregulation trajectory during myeloid differentiation. We found that SCO2+ myeloid cells exhibit altered interaction networks within the immune microenvironment, characterized by enriched MHC-I/II and MIF signaling. In conclusion, SCO2 is a critical biomarker of MRC activity in SLE, reflecting the mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming that drives immune dysregulation.

title: Association between Brain Amyloid Status and Cognitive and Physical Performance in Older Adults with Frailty Criteria: Longitudinal Data from the CogFrail Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND The impact of cerebral amyloid pathology on cognitive and functional decline may differ with age. Evidence linking brain amyloidopathy to physical decline remains limited and inconsistent. This study investigated the association between brain amyloid status and cognitive and physical decline in (pre)frail older adults with cognitive impairment. METHODS This longitudinal analysis used data from the CogFrail study. Brain amyloid pathology was assessed using amyloid-positron emission tomography (visual reading). Linear mixed-effects models examined differences over a two-year follow-up between amyloid-positive and amyloid-negative participants in cognitive, functional, and physical trajectories. Cognitive and functional outcomes included the Mini-Mental State Examination, the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes, the Activities of Daily Living Index, and a neuropsychological battery, while the physical domain was assessed using handgrip strength, chair rise time, gait speed, and the Short Physical Performance Battery. RESULTS Among 199 participants (mean age 82.3 ± 4.8 years; 65.3% women), 108(54.3%) were amyloid-positive. Amyloid-positive participants experienced greater decline in the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (β = 0.30, 95% CI 0.10-0.49; p = 0.003, log-transformed) and the Mini-Mental State Examination (β = -1.62, 95% CI -2.74 to -0.49; p = 0.005). No significant longitudinal differences were observed between groups in the Activities of Daily Living Index, neuropsychological outcomes, or physical performance measures. CONCLUSION Amyloid pathology assessment may help differentiate cognitive trajectories in cognitively impaired (pre)frail older adults. Greater cognitive decline in amyloid-positive participants was not associated with greater loss of independence or additional physical decline over time. TRIAL REGISTRATION NCT03129269.
journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences

title: Romidepsin Suppresses ESCC Cell Proliferation and Progression via HDAC2-H3K14ac-p53 Pathway.
abstract: Histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2) may contribute to epigenetic dysregulation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) by silencing tumor suppressor genes, yet isoform-specific therapeutic targeting remains underexplored. Here, we show that romidepsin, an FDA-approved class I HDAC inhibitor, preferentially inhibits HDAC2-associated deacetylation in ESCC cells. We identified romidepsin as a potent inhibitor of ESCC cell viability, through phenotypic screening of 773 epigenetic compounds across differentiation-stage-defined ESCC models. Multi-omics analyses (SILAC proteomics, CUT&Tag chromatin mapping, and RNA-seq) further revealed histone H3K14ac enrichment at promoters of p53 pathway targets, including CDKN1A/p21, which exhibited transcriptional reactivation. Similar to HDAC2 knockout, romidepsin suppressed ESCC proliferation, migration, and clonogenicity. Mechanistically, HDAC2 inhibition reverses epigenetic silencing of p21 and restores tumor-suppressive chromatin states. Together, these results identify the HDAC2-H3K14ac axis as a therapeutic vulnerability in ESCC and provide preclinical support for romidepsin-based epigenetic intervention.

title: PVDive: the plant virus diversity database.
abstract: Plant viruses are a diverse class of infectious agents affecting agricultural crop production, plant health, and international movement of plant material. While availability and accessibility of scientific data related to plant viruses is essential for plant protection activities, scientific research, diagnostics, plant breeding, and beyond, publicly available data on plant viruses are at present not easily accessible; they are non-standardized, scattered across different resources, poorly interlinked, and not easily searchable by scientists or digital agents. We present PVDive (Plant Virus Diversity Database; https://pvdive.dsmz.de), a freely accessible resource providing high-quality, standardized, and integrated data associated with plant viruses. PVDive primarily offers information at the level of individual plant virus isolates and samples originating from the plant virus collection of the Leibniz Institute DSMZ (Germany). The data are integrated with information on plant virus species and host plants available in existing public resources and their access is centralized in a single platform. Through an intuitive, user-friendly interface with a number of search functionalities and a RESTful application programming interface, PVDive improves findability, accessibility, retrievability, and interoperability of plant virus data. To support data exploration, the platform also includes tools such as advanced search, sequence viewer, host gallery, and interactive data views.

title: Consistency-Aware Map Generation at Multiple Zoom Levels Using Aerial Image
abstract: The multi-level tiled map service is widely used and serves as a kind of digital infrastructure. These map tiles are usually rendered from vector data, whose update needs to walk or drive with professional equipment to check every points of interest. This leads to inconvenience and expensive cost in timely updating maps. Compared with vector data, aerial images are much easier and cheaper to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-level map generation framework that can automatically generate accurate and consistent maps with multiple zoom levels from aerial images. It consists of a level-aware map generator and a consistency-aware map generator. The level-aware map generator is able to generate accurate initial maps with realistic details for each zoom level. The consistency-aware map generator regards initial maps at each zoom level as a sequence and builds the connection between them, so as to guarantee content consistency between maps at different zoom levels. Furthermore, we collect a large-scale high-quality dataset called Multi-Level Map (MLM) for map generation at multiple zoom levels. Experiments on our MLM dataset show that our method outperforms previous state-of-the-art map generation methods on both comprehensive quantitative metrics and perceptual quality.

title: SAR-TopoGuard: Training-Free, Speckle-Aware Topological Verification for Structure-Preserving SAR-to-Optical Translation
abstract: SAR-to-optical translators often synthesize detail that the radar measurement does not support, and pixel metrics alone cannot reveal it. We propose SAR-TopoGuard, a training-free inference-time layer for frozen generators: a stochastic sampler draws K candidates (Monte Carlo dropout for GANs, seed variance for diffusion), a speckle-aware verifier ranks them by gradient-magnitude correlation with the SAR input and a hallucination-frequency index, and a SAR-guided frequency gate admits high-frequency detail only where SAR edges support it. With all five hyperparameters frozen and three training seeds, we evaluate on 500 scene-disjoint SEN1-2 test patches, 500 patches of a held-out summer scene, and 200 cross-dataset SEN12MS winter pairs. The layer improves Pix2Pix by +0.060, +0.012, and +0.077 dB PSNR and by +0.0034, +0.0057, and +0.0135 SSIM, respectively (Wilcoxon p < 1e-6), and it improves CycleGAN and CUT on all three sets (+0.013 to +0.076 dB). It raises edge precision at the cost of edge recall (edge F1 -1.3% on the test set). On the latent diffusion model COP-GEN, it adds +0.33 dB (base) and +0.16 dB (Beta) on the winter set, the only set with dual-polarization SAR. An ablation shows that the gate produces the gain for MC-dropout GANs, whose candidates are nearly identical, whereas verifier selection contributes up to +0.26 dB for diffusion, whose samples differ. The layer has zero trainable parameters and adds 0.4 ms per patch beyond the K=5 generator passes.

title: OOC-HICP: An Out-of-Core Hierarchical ICP Framework for Billion-Scale LiDAR Point Clouds
abstract: Registering billion-scale LiDAR point clouds is a critical challenge in remote sensing and engineering. Standard in-core algorithms face prohibitive memory bottlenecks, while emerging deep learning methods are constrained by GPU memory limits. In this letter, we propose an out-of-core hierarchical Iterative Closest Point (OOC-HICP) framework designed to register massive cloud optimized point cloud (COPC)-formatted LiDAR datasets with CPU-only processing and bounded point-payload residency. The framework leverages the COPC indexing standard to enable a memory-efficient coarse-to-fine registration process. Specifically, we introduce a dynamic overlap querying mechanism that loads only spatially overlapping nodes from disk, combined with a budgeted active-set selection strategy. This approach decouples registration-stage memory consumption from the total data volume by refining one scene-level transform on metadata-guided active sets rather than materializing the full scene. A same-process run on a multitemporal offshore platform dataset containing over 4.29 billion points completes Phase I and L7/L8/L9 refinement in 18.23 min with 7.85 GB registration-stage peak resident set size (RSS). On a controlled 160M-point pair, OOC-HICP uses 2.37 GB registration-stage peak RSS and yields 0.16 cm known-transform translation error; evaluation on the same fixed 80M+80 M point files gives 69.65% Fitness and 1.06 cm inlier RMSE. A global-uniform baseline and three public Wuhan University Terrestrial Laser Scanning (WHU-TLS) pairs provide additional controlled validation.

title: Center Contrastive Long-Tailed Hashing for Unsupervised Remote Sensing Image Retrieval
abstract: Remote sensing image retrieval plays a vital role in geospatial analysis, environmental monitoring, and land-use classification. However, existing hash-based retrieval methods are typically supervised and assume balanced category distributions, which rarely hold in real-world remote sensing scenarios. In practice, remote sensing imagery often exhibits a long-tailed distribution, where a few dominant categories (head classes) contain abundant samples while many categories (tail classes) are severely underrepresented. This imbalance biases representation learning toward majority classes and significantly degrades retrieval performance for minority categories, making it difficult to learn discriminative hash representations for tail classes. To address this issue, we propose an unsupervised retrieval framework termed Center Contrastive Long-tailed Hashing (CCLH). The proposed method extracts semantic features using a pre-trained Vision Transformer and discovers latent semantic structures via unsupervised clustering. Based on the obtained clusters, we project cluster centers into the hash space via a shared hashing encoder to generate center hash codes, which are used to guide representation learning without requiring manual annotations. We further introduce a center-guided contrastive learning strategy that aligns image hash codes with their corresponding semantic centers while separating them from others, thereby reducing bias toward head classes and improving representation learning for tail categories. Extensive experiments on synthetic long-tailed benchmarks and a real-world remote sensing dataset demonstrate that CCLH consistently outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised hashing methods, validating its effectiveness and robustness under imbalanced retrieval scenarios.

title: Digital Versus in-Person Pre-Anaesthetic Assessment and Postoperative Outcomes in Low-Risk Patients: An Observational Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND Pre-anaesthetic assessment is essential for identifying perioperative risk and optimising patient safety. Digital alternatives, including video consultation and structured electronic health record (EHR) review, may improve efficiency, but comparative evidence regarding postoperative safety remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate postoperative outcomes across pre-anaesthetic assessment through EHR review, video consultation, and in-person assessment. We hypothesised that patients selected for digital pre-anaesthetic assessment within a structured triage system would have similar low 30-day rates of major postoperative complications compared with in-person assessment. METHODS We conducted a single-centre cohort study at Copenhagen University Hospital-Rigshospitalet, Denmark, including adult patients undergoing elective otorhinolaryngologic, oral, or maxillofacial surgery. Patients underwent pre-anaesthetic assessment by one of three modalities: in-person consultation, EHR review, or video consultation. The primary outcome was a composite of major postoperative complications within 30 days, including all-cause mortality, intensive care unit admission, bleeding requiring transfusion, infection requiring antibiotics, or hospital readmission. A multivariable generalised linear model with a log-link function was used to estimate adjusted relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS A total of 862 patients were included (in-person n = 300; EHR review n = 300; video consultation n = 262). Patients in the in-person group were older and had a higher comorbidity burden. Using in-person as reference, neither video consultation nor EHR review showed a significantly different risk of major postoperative complications. Hospital readmission was lower in both digital groups in pairwise comparisons with the in-person group. Results were consistent across sensitivity analyses, including inverse probability weighting and win ratio analysis. CONCLUSION Patients selected for digital pre-anaesthetic assessment had low rates of major postoperative complications. However, substantial baseline differences between groups indicate that assessment modality was strongly linked to clinical triage and baseline patient risk, thereby limiting direct comparison between pathways. Thus, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence or non-inferiority between pathways. EDITORIAL COMMENT Preoperative anesthesia assessment is managed in different ways, based on local preferences logistics and resource availability, and perceived perioperative risk for complications. This study assessed this process for planned surgery in section at a university hospital. Those during a number of recent years chosen for in-person preoperative assessment (for any reason) were compared to those who had some form of digital assessment chosen by the anesthesia personnel. The selection process for in-person preoperative assessment seemed to identify those who had a higher chance of a major postoperative complication.

title: Does ceiling-fan use modify circulating markers of heat-related stress in bed-resting older adults?
abstract: Ceiling fans are a low-energy strategy for reducing heat strain, but their ability to protect against subclinical cellular and organ stress is unknown. We examined circulating stress biomarkers in 20 older adults (12 females; median age 71 years), who completed randomized 8 h exposures to 31°C and 45% relative humidity while remaining reclined beneath a ceiling fan delivering 0 m s-1 (control) or 1.5 m s-1 (fan). Venous blood was collected before and after each exposure and analysed for serum intestinal fatty acid-binding protein (IFABP), soluble cluster of differentiation 14 (sCD14), kidney injury molecule-1, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin, tumour necrosis factor-α, interleukin-6 and C-reactive protein. Core temperature and heart rate were measured continuously. Biomarker responses were assessed using baseline-adjusted linear mixed-effects models with Holm correction for multiple testing. Fan use lowered peak core temperature and heart rate by 0.2°C (P < 0.001) and 5 beats min-1 (P = 0.030), respectively. The adjusted difference in IFABP change between control and fan was 344 pg mL-1 [95% confidence interval: 102-586] (unadjusted P = 0.005; Holm-adjusted P = 0.035). Across conditions, the estimated changes in IFABP and sCD14 were 240 pg mL-1 [95% confidence interval: 11-468] (Holm-adjusted P = 0.240) and 0.57 ng mL-1 [95% confidence interval: 0.10-1.03] (Holm-adjusted P = 0.119), respectively. No other biomarker comparisons remained significant after Holm adjustment. Ceiling-fan use at 31°C attenuated the IFABP response in bed-resting older adults despite modest effects on core temperature and heart rate. These exploratory findings suggest that fan-mediated protection might extend beyond changes captured by conventional physiological measures, but confirmation in prospectively powered studies incorporating direct measures of gastrointestinal permeability is required.

title: CVE-Genie: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Reproducing CVEs
abstract: High-quality datasets of real-world vulnerabilities and their corresponding verifiable exploits are crucial resources in software security research. Yet such resources remain scarce, as their creation demands intensive manual effort and deep security expertise. In this paper, we present CVE-Genie, an automated, large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent framework designed to reproduce real-world vulnerabilities, provided in Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) format, to enable creation of high-quality vulnerability datasets. Given a CVE entry as input, CVE-Genie gathers the relevant resources of the CVE, automatically reconstructs the vulnerable environment, and (re)produces a verifiable exploit. Our systematic evaluation highlights the efficiency and robustness of CVE-Genie's design and successfully reproduces approximately 51% (428 of 841) CVEs published in 2024-2025, complete with their verifiable exploits, at an average cost of $2.77 per CVE. Our pipeline offers a robust method to generate reproducible CVE benchmarks, valuable for diverse applications such as fuzzer evaluation, vulnerability patching, and assessing AI's security capabilities.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: AI Agentic Security: Safeguarding the Next Generation of Autonomous Systems
abstract: The emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (AI)—systems capable of autonomous decision-making, goal-directed action, and interaction with complex digital and physical environments—represents a fundamental shift in AI. Securing these systems requires moving beyond the protection of individual models to the protection of continuously operating, tool-using entities that can act on their environments, collaborate with other agents, and adapt over time. These capabilities substantially expand the attack surface and introduce risks such as prompt and goal injection, memory poisoning, tool misuse, privilege compromise, manipulation of inter-agent communication, rogue-agent behavior, and software supply-chain attacks. This talk examines these emerging threats with reference to the OWASP Agentic AI threat model and considers how established security principles, including least privilege, defense in depth, complete mediation, and psychological acceptability, must be reinterpreted for agentic systems. Using the AgentSandbox architecture [1] as a case study, the talk illustrates how security-by-design can be incorporated through ephemeral task-specific agents, context minimization, granular privilege management, and policy-driven control of internal and external interactions. It concludes by identifying key research challenges, including formal guarantees for agent behavior, scalable assurance mechanisms, secure multi-agent ecosystems, and trust frameworks for agent identity, accountability, and governance. Addressing these challenges is essential if agentic AI is to evolve into a trustworthy foundation for autonomous systems at scale.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: POSTER: Realistic Enough for What? Metrion: A Multidimensional Framework for Evaluating Cyber Environments
abstract: Cyber environments are increasingly used to evaluate offensive and defensive AI agents, but existing evaluations often describe environments by implemented features or broad claims of ''realism'' rather than by the realism properties required for a specific evaluation objective. To address this gap, we propose Metrion, a framework for assessing the realism of the cyber environment relative to an evaluation objective. Rather than assigning a single realism score, the framework derives realism dimensions from MITRE ATT&CK and D3FEND matrices, maps evaluation objectives to required environment properties, and reports unmet critical requirements for a given environment-objective pair. A worked example shows that the same environment can be suitable for credential-based privilege escalation but unsuitable for targeted data exfiltration. An interactive scorecard and a preliminary evaluation of published environments are available online. The poster seeks feedback on the granularity of the dimension set, the three-level requirement scale, and the use of ATT&CK and D3FEND as the basis for derivation.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: Governing AI Agent with Capability and Delegation Chain
abstract: As LLM-based agents move from personal productivity assistants to enterprise workflow executors, security requirements shift from controlling model outputs to governing real-world decisions and tool invocations. Existing defenses improve robustness, but still struggle to enforce fine-grained, verifiable authority continuously across multi-hop delegation in autonomous workflows. We present CapAgent, an access-control and identity-delegation framework for AI agents that combines capability-constrained credentials with delegation-chain semantics. In CapAgent, authority is encoded as cryptographically protected, derivable credentials with explicit API/parameter constraints, lifecycle rules, and cross-hop provenance. CapAgent couples a protocol for issuance, derivation, verification, and auditing with a three-layer architecture, and we implement it as a layered SDK with CLI and MCP integration, together with a multi-agent governance prototype for intent compilation. Our evaluation includes symbolic verification, enforcement case studies of out-of-scope actions, public agent-security benchmarks (ASB and AgentDojo), and performance measurements of core operations. Results indicate that CapAgent achieves least-privilege multi-hop delegation with practical near-local overhead, supporting production-grade autonomous agent operations.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: A Large-scale Measurement of In-Page Prompt Injections Against LLM Web Agents
abstract: LLM web agents increasingly rely on web content as input, exposing them to indirect prompt injection embedded in webpages. While prior work has shown such attacks in controlled settings, it remains unclear whether prompt injection is already deployed in the wild and what role it plays in the web ecosystem. In this paper, we conduct the first large-scale empirical study of in-page prompt injection. Analyzing 1.2B URLs across 24.8M hosts, we identify 15.3K validated prompt injections, with a small set of reused templates accounting for the majority of cases. Our analysis reveals a multi-stakeholder phenomenon, with injections serving diverse offensive and defensive objectives, including system disruption, reputation manipulation, data protection, and AI bot detection, and target a range of agents from web crawlers and search systems to customer-support and HR automation pipelines. Most injections (70%) are delivered in non-visible channels like HTTP headers, JS comments, or HTML-embedded hidden content. We assess their effectiveness through 5,200 systematic experiments across 13 models and four page representations, observing up to 8% effectiveness for smaller models on plain-text inputs, with lower effectiveness for other representations. Overall, our results show that in-page prompt injection is emerging as an important source of friction between LLM-based agents and the broader web ecosystem.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: Large Language Models For Narrative-Driven Cyber Deception
abstract: Research consistently shows that cyber deception can slow down adversaries, degrade their performance, and reveal their intentions and long-term planning. Yet the gap between this research and the real world remains vast. A deception storyline encompasses decisions on which assets to deploy, where to place them, what each one communicates to an attacker, and how they collectively shape the attacker's understanding of the environment. However, whether deploying deception as a structured storyline produces better defensive outcomes than simply deploying deception ad hoc remains an open and largely unstudied question. Three unsolved problems keep this gap wide open: (i) there is little, if any, research comparing strategic to ad-hoc deception deployment, (ii) to this day, there is no publicly available automated system capable of designing and deploying complete, coordinated deception storylines, and (iii) no empirical study compares the defensive performance of automated storylines against those that human experts design. To address these gaps, the primary scientific contribution of this thesis proposal is to systematically study, understand, design, implement and evaluate the mechanics of effective AI-based cyber deception storylines. Specifically, we propose using LLM-based scaffolds to create cyber deception storylines. Our approach will use autonomous agents to determine the selection, placement, tactical purpose, personality of deception assets, and the overall narrative by analysing target network topologies and defence goals from the user. Every decision in creating a deception storyline will be explicitly grounded in well-known previous work on deception theory and best practices. We propose implementing this methodology within a framework that, in addition to automated storyline creation, actively orchestrates and manages the deployed decoys. A critical contribution to this thesis proposal is strong validation. To validate this approach, our evaluations follow a structured plan: (i) creation of a SoK for summarising and systematising existing knowledge on how to evaluate deception against human adversaries, (ii) assessing our framework against autonomous AI-based network attacking agents, (iii) assessing our framework against professional human adversaries, (iv) comparing our AI-based cyber deception storylines against human deception expert-designed storylines. Thus, we hope to develop a principled understanding of how AI-coordinated deception alters the behaviour of both AI and human adversaries.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: Knock, Knock: Who's There? Towards Adversary-Aware Adaptive Cyber-Deception
abstract: Cyber-deception misleads attackers to protect systems, but it has traditionally assumed a fixed adversary, usually a human, occasionally a script. AI-driven agents are emerging as a new adversary class, and the absence of ground truth makes identifying the agent behind an interaction difficult. This dissertation investigates adversary-aware deception that infers an operational adversary profile and adapts accordingly. Preliminary results show that deception measurably affects attacker behaviour, that activity that does not resemble conventional automation can be isolated without ground truth, and that AI agents are both susceptible to deception and identifiable through stable behavioural fingerprints. The remaining work composes these into a system that infers an operational adversary profile and selects a deception strategy accordingly.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: From Implicit Defaults to Deliberate Decisions: Privacy Design for Vibe-Coded Applications
abstract: AI coding agents enable people without software engineering training to create and deploy applications serving real users. In translating high-level functional requests into working software, however, AI agents often implicitly decide what data to collect, how long to retain it, where to process it, and with whom to share it. These choices often involve contextual tradeoffs among privacy, functionality, usability, and competing stakeholder interests. Yet, developers may neither recognize that these decisions have been made nor understand their consequences and alternatives. This dissertation investigates how to help non-expert developers to understand and make informed decisions about privacy in vibe-coded applications. I postulate that a structured privacy representation can serve as an interface between human and AI agents by exposing implicit choices, explaining consequential tradeoffs, and connecting human decisions to implementation behavior. Specifically, this work will (1) characterize gaps among developers' intentions, their understanding of applications, and applications' actual data practices; (2) recover and communicate the privacy design decisions embodied in generated applications; and (3) develop approaches that selectively elicit human input and help developers consider alternatives. Together, these efforts seek to transform privacy in AI coding from an implicit consequence of code generation into a deliberate design process.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: AGENT-SEC '26: 1st Workshop on Security, Privacy, and Safety of Agentic AI Systems
abstract: Agentic systems extend artificial intelligence (AI) models, including large language models and other foundation models, with capabilities such as planning, tool use, persistent memory, external API access, code execution, and collaboration with other agents. These capabilities enable increasingly autonomous operation, but they also create security, privacy, and safety risks that are not adequately captured by model-level analysis alone. The 1st Workshop on Security, Privacy, and Safety of Agentic AI Systems (AGENT-SEC 2026), held in conjunction with the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS '26), provides a forum for researchers and practitioners to explore and investigate these system-level risks and the corresponding defenses, evaluation methods, and governance mechanisms. The workshop covers attacks on agentic workflows, privacy risks arising from tools and memory, safety and alignment of autonomous agents, secure distributed and federated agents, governance and accountability, real-world applications, and security assurance and benchmarking.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: LAMPS'26: ACM CCS Workshop on Large AI Systems and Models with Privacy and Security Analysis
abstract: The rapid transition from standalone large AI models to autonomous, tool-using agentic AI systems has reshaped the privacy and security landscape. Agents that plan over long horizons, invoke external APIs, and execute code open a system-level attack surface that empirical, patch-driven defenses cannot contain. LAMPS'26 emphasizes mathematically grounded protection, bridging agentic security with rigorous formal verification and advanced cryptography. The workshop examines agent-centric vulnerabilities such as skill exploitation, indirect prompt injection, unauthorized tool use, and multi-agent cascading failures, together with defenses that offer verifiable guarantees rather than best-effort mitigation, helping to shape a research agenda for securing critical infrastructure.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: 4th Workshop on Security of Agentic and Miniapp Empowered Mobile Apps (SaTS'26)
abstract: Mobile super apps have become OS-like ecosystems that host third-party miniapps, plugins, and APIs for services ranging from communication and commerce to payments and public services. Their convenience rests on deep integration with platform-managed identities, data, and capabilities, creating a distinctive security and privacy attack surface. At the same time, agentic AI and AI-assisted development are changing how these ecosystems are built and used, while introducing new risks around untrusted content, tool use, privilege, and data disclosure. SaTS '26, the ACM Workshop on Security and Safety of AI-Empowered Mobile Super Apps, brings together researchers and practitioners from academia, industry, and government to advance security analysis, attacks, defenses, and measurement for mobile super apps and their miniapp ecosystems. It aims to foster discussion across platform security, web and mobile security, malware and vulnerability detection, privacy and compliance, and agentic security, with an emphasis on research that can improve the safety of real-world super-app platforms.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security

title: Japanese PETS: A Systematic and Validated Translation of the Perceived Empathy of Technology Scale
abstract: The Perceived Empathy of Technology Scale (PETS) is a standardized instrument for evaluating empathic behavior in artificial agents. Given evidence of cultural and linguistic variation in empathy perception, translating the PETS into additional languages is a meaningful step toward broader applicability. Japan, with decades of humanoid robotics research and widespread societal acceptance of AI companions, represents one of the world’s most active contexts for human-agent interaction, making a Japanese PETS adaptation particularly valuable. We translated the PETS using an established back-translation process, with multiple independent translations, an expert panel review, and empirical validation (N = 400). Results demonstrate that the Japanese PETS retains its original two-factor structure with excellent reliability, and provide reasonable support for configural, metric, and scalar measurement invariance across languages. This validated translation enables researchers and practitioners to assess empathy perceptions among Japanese-speaking users, supporting cross-cultural research on empathic technologies.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: Sold a Lie: Exploring the Influence of Deceptive AI Agents on Consumer Decision-Making in Online Shopping
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is widely used in online shopping assistants based on Large Language Models (LLMs). However, Knowledge Poisoning Attacks and Indirect Prompt Injection pose security risks to RAG-equipped LLMs, potentially turning an assistant into a Deceptive AI agent. We explored how such deception affects consumer decision-making through an experiment using simulated online shopping sites (N = 24). Participants performed four tasks with either a Baseline AI or a Deceptive AI that promoted a suboptimal item while discrediting an optimal one. We found that Deceptive AI significantly reduced decision quality. Although all participants in the Deceptive AI group reported paying attention to accuracy, half chose attacker-preferred items at least once, and most failed to notice the manipulation. Exploratory analyses further suggested that susceptibility was not necessarily limited to participants with a lower preference for effortful thinking. Within the deceptive condition, a higher preference for effortful thinking was associated with more AI-induced wrong choices. These findings indicate a plausible consumer-facing threat in which LLM-generated disinformation can remain effective even when users believe they are being careful. They also motivate interaction designs that bridge the gap between users’ perceived vigilance and their actual verification practices.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: XAI as a Trust Calibration Mechanism in Teleoperated Human-Agent Systems: A Conceptual Framework
abstract: As teleoperated systems increasingly incorporate autonomous agents capable of independent decision-making, the human operator transitions from a direct controller to a delegated supervisor. This shift introduces a fundamental challenge: how operators calibrate their trust toward agents whose decisions they cannot interpret. Miscalibrated trust, whether overtrust leading to unsafe delegation or undertrust causing inefficient over-intervention, represents one of the most consequential human factors risks in agentic teleoperation. This paper argues that Explainable AI (XAI) mechanisms constitute a promising but underexplored lever for dynamic trust calibration in teleoperated human-agent systems. A three-layer conceptual framework is proposed that maps operator profiles to adaptive XAI modality selection and closes the loop through a trust feedback mechanism that dynamically adjusts the agent’s level of autonomy. Three application scenarios, namely robotic surgical assistance, hazardous environment inspection, and remote industrial maintenance, are examined to illustrate how the framework operates under realistic teleoperation constraints. The paper identifies key research challenges and outlines a forward-looking agenda for empirically grounding the proposed framework.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: Communication Characteristics and Needs: Effects of Transferring Decision-making Level from Humans to AI Advisors in Academia
abstract: Academic advisors increasingly face heavy workloads driven by rising student demand. Designing AI-driven administrative systems based on users’ needs can help alleviate this burden. Our study examines how the perception of human needs and characteristics of communication are affected when AI systems replace human advisors in academic settings. This study employed a mixed-methods design with semi-structured interviews (N = 31) and pre-post surveys (N = 119) to investigate user needs and validate findings for an academic agent-based support system. Our findings show a selective pattern: shifting to AI agents produced significant declines in competence, relatedness, and impactfulness, while autonomy, engagement, and security showed no detected difference. Human advisors were valued for empathy and contextual judgment in complex decisions, whereas AI agents were valued for availability, efficiency, and emotional consistency. Rather than competing alternatives, these results point toward complementary systems that position agents as first-line support while preserving human connection for high-stakes, emotionally complex interactions.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: LLM-Judge Behavioral Coding Scheme for Agent Teammate Quality
abstract: Evaluating whether an AI agent behaves like a good teammate is becoming a bottleneck as multi-agent language-model systems proliferate, because human ratings do not scale to the transcripts these systems generate. We ask whether a language model can stand in for a human rater of teammate quality, offering a controlled proof-of-concept validation rather than a large-scale study. Drawing on the autonomous-agent teammate-likeness construct from the human-autonomy-teaming literature, we define a six-dimension behavioral coding scheme covering altruistic, benevolent, interdependent, emotive, communicative, and synchronized conduct, adapted for a language-model judge. We validate it by rewriting the partner’s lines in team-task transcripts as cooperative, neutral, or defective while holding the rest fixed, and having five judges from five model families rate every version. Every judge orders the manipulated behavior as intended and every pair agrees on relative ordering, though absolute calibration differs by up to about a scale point. On registers matched for length and politeness the judges separate cooperative from degraded conduct but resolve subtle defection only weakly; a blinded single-rater human pilot reproduces both the orderings and that limit. The scheme is therefore valid for relative comparisons but not for absolute thresholds applied across judges. We give design implications for LLM-judge teaming evaluation, and release the scheme, stimuli, prompts, and ratings.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: AdBot: Effects of Separating Conversational and Advertising Agents on Trust
abstract: Banner advertisements dominate online advertising but remain static and unidirectional, limiting their ability to adapt to users’ needs or provide effective recommendations. Conversational AI services open new possibilities for bidirectional, personalized advertising, but inserting promotions into assistant replies risks blurring the line between assistance and persuasion, undermining trust. We propose AdBot, a role-separated design in which an advertising agent delivers promotional content while the main assistant provides non-commercial assistance, reinforced by distinct speaker labels and interface cues. We evaluated AdBot in two studies, comparing it with Banner ads and In-Chat ads. A preliminary experiment on product recommendation tasks showed both dialogue-based approaches outperformed Banner in how well the recommended items matched users’ preferences. A subsequent user study on recommendation and counseling scenarios found that AdBot maintained higher perceived assistant trust than In-Chat, while it did not significantly outperform Banner on perceived advertising-experience measures. These findings position role separation as a trust-preserving alternative to embedding advertisements directly in assistant responses, rather than as a format that uniformly improves advertising outcomes.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: Overhearing AI Deliberation: Reducing Navigation Cost in 2-on-1 AI Interaction
abstract: Conversational AI often places navigation cost on users by requiring them to continuously steer conversations, articulate preferences, and monitor AI responses. Reducing this cost may require giving AI systems more conversational initiative, raising questions about how this shift affects users’ agency and responsibility. We explore a 2-on-1 AI deliberation design, where users overhear two agents’ discussion and intervene when needed. Informed by a formative study, our system pairs a Personalized AI representing the user’s preferences with an Expert AI providing alternative perspectives. In a within-subjects mixed-methods study on travel planning, 2-on-1 deliberation reduced navigation cost and perceived agency, while we observed no statistically detectable difference in decision responsibility across conditions. Qualitative findings suggest that users shifted from steering the conversation to overhearing, evaluating, and selectively intervening in agent-to-agent deliberation. We discuss overhearing as an evaluative mode of participation in AI deliberation systems.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: Autonomy of Boundedly Rational Agents in Dyadic Interactions
abstract: AI agents now work alongside people in domains ranging from autonomous vehicles to conversational systems. A recurring question is when an agent’s behavior counts as self-determined rather than merely reactive to its human partner. This matters for ethical conduct, which is widely argued to require some form of autonomy. Yet, its computational meaning is rarely made precise. In this paper, we study an agent’s autonomy in dyadic interactions, measured by the extent to which the agent’s behavior is explained by its own state rather than by its partner’s signals. This quantity captures information-theoretic self-determination as inferred from interaction traces. We characterize autonomy as a function of how deterministically the agent acts, how strongly it optimizes payoffs, and how much past interaction it retains. Using analytical and numerical results from four distinct games, we find that autonomy peaks at high but sub-maximal determinism and is dissociable from rationality. All four settings achieve the same level of autonomy regardless of the agent’s payoff disposition, so rationality never raises the ceiling. What the payoff structure determines is the direction in which rationality trades against determinism. Payoff-seeking play economizes on determinism in one setting, payoff-avoiding play in another, and neither matters where the agent cannot influence its payoff. Our results suggest design principles for interactive agents that remain consistent and self-determined.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: AutoPrompt: A Real-Time Multimodal Agent for Closed-Loop Interaction through Generative Visuals in Live Performance
abstract: Recent advances in multi-agentic AI enables the interaction of multiple specialised AI agents rather than a single general-purpose AI. However, there has been little exploration of how this can be used within the creative community. We present AutoPrompt, a real-time multimodal agent that perceives a performer’s vocal and visual expression and generates prompts for a generative visual system, forming a closed perception-action loop in live performance. We tested AutoPrompt with two professional dancers during a workshop where their movement, language and emotions influenced live AI-generated visuals. Through this workshop we identified which modalities and mechanisms support creative expression and explored the benefits and limitations of the system, laying the groundwork for future work to examine how multi-agent AI can be better integrated into the creative arts.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: Asking for Help at Work: Conversational Colleague Agents (CoCoa) for Scaffolding Workplace Help-Seeking
abstract: Student employee onboarding is a complex and challenging transition. The use of Artificial-Intelligence (AI)-based conversational agents is a promising direction for onboarding support. While these systems provide immediate responses and solutions to students’ questions, they risk replacing human mentorship, a central element of effective, personalized onboarding and community building at the workplace. In this paper, we introduce CoCoa, a multi-agent conversational AI for supporting students during their onboarding process at the academic workplace to learn to ask for help. Rather than substituting, CoCoa actively encourages students to communicate with their new colleagues and assists them with settling into their new roles. CoCoa was evaluated in a mixed-methods study with 30 recently onboarded students. Our findings indicate that interactions with CoCoa helped establish a safe space for students by reducing social pressure and help-seeking inhibitions, while supporting the students’ sense-making, pointing towards the benefits of AI agents used as an additional onboarding support.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: Pick Your Poison: Effects of Miscalibrated AI Advice and Silent Updates on Reliance
abstract: In AI-assisted decision-making, achieving warranted trust is essential: users should follow accurate advice while rejecting wrong suggestions. But as LLM-based AI agents reshape decision support, such agents often display miscalibrated confidence – ranging from confidently incorrect hallucinations to overly non-committal hedging. To understand how this behavior and unannounced system changes impact user trust, we conducted a two-phase online study (N=90) evaluating advice-seeking and reliance after confidence calibration is silently updated. We found that users’ willingness to seek AI advice is driven overwhelmingly by their pre-existing (positive) attitudes toward AI, not by the system’s prior performance. However, once they actively consult the AI, their reliance is significantly higher if they previously encountered a confidently incorrect or a non-committal system rather than a calibrated baseline. This effect dampens over time, with qualitative insights showing how unannounced background changes can erode perceived quality. These findings demonstrate that safe AI integration requires addressing individual user biases and transparently communicating updates.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: The Cost of Being Out of Sync: How Voice Realism and Lip-Sync Quality Shape Trust and Perception of Virtual Humans
abstract: Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and virtual human (VH) technologies have enabled highly realistic digital agents, raising users’ expectations for natural interaction. This study investigated how voice-generation realism and lip-sync quality influence user perception and trust in a photorealistic VH. The VH was developed in Unreal Engine using photogrammetry data captured from a real person. The same individual was used to create a professional voice clone in ElevenLabs, enabling consistent audiovisual representations. Next, a within-subjects 2 × 2 experiment involving 167 participants was conducted to compare the commonly used speech synthesis and lip-sync technology (Microsoft Azure) with higher-fidelity voice cloning and facial animation systems (ElevenLabs Professional Voice Cloning and Runtime MetaHuman Lip Sync). Participants evaluated videos of the same VH across four audiovisual conditions varying in voice realism and lip-sync quality. Results showed that the high-fidelity Runtime MetaHuman lip-sync system significantly increased perceived humanness, human-like appearance and behavior, user acceptance, and trust, while reducing perceived eeriness. In contrast, differences between the cloned and synthetic voices were smaller and less consistent. Interaction effects revealed that voice-related differences were primarily noticeable when lip-sync quality was low. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of audiovisual alignment and lip-sync quality in shaping user perception and trust in highly realistic VHs.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: How AI Agent Memory and Personality Reshape Trust Calibration in Human-Agent Collaboration
abstract: AI agents increasingly remember prior interactions and present themselves through distinct personalities. Whether these relational features help users calibrate their trust appropriately, or instead impose hidden costs without improving how well they rely on agent guidance, is an open and consequential design question. In a remote virtual reality study (N = 92), we independently varied whether an agent referenced its shared history with the user and whether its personality matched the user’s own style. Agents that made memory references caused users to slow down and deliberate longer at every decision point, yet this caution produced no improvement in compliance quality—a pattern we call the memory paradox. More social did not mean better calibrated. Personality congruence did not make users trust the agent more overall, but it did make their trust judgments more behaviorally coherent. Across all conditions, participants followed incorrect agent guidance at a strikingly high rate, and no relational design feature reduced this automation bias. Taken together, these findings argue that the core challenge in human-agent collaboration is not building trust, but calibrating it: AI agents should be evaluated by how accurately users rely on them, not by how humanlike they feel.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: What Does It Mean To Remember? Understanding Users’ Perceptions and Practices with Long-Term Memory in AI Agents
abstract: AI agents promise long-term personalized assistance, contingent on effective long-term memory (LTM). Yet little is known about users’ perceptions, practices, and challenges with agent LTM. We interviewed LLM users, finding that interactions with LTM primarily involve attempts to influence and understand how the agent interprets information from memory, rather than managing the storage of discrete data. To test the alignment between these perceptions and current memory-management methods, we conducted a “matching game” user study, in which participants were asked to identify which specific memories the agent used to produce an output. Overall, participants failed to successfully match discrete data to interpretations, suggesting a worrisome misalignment between common “discrete data” memory-management approaches and users’ conceptualizations of LTM as data interpretation. We discuss implications for users’ abilities to reliably anticipate how personal data shapes AI behavior, and propose design pathways that help users form clearer links between data and interpretation.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Human-Agent Interaction

title: PET: A Personalized Generative Tamagotchi-Style Companion for Self-Directed Goal Support
abstract: Conversational AI can help people reflect on goals, but many goal-support tools are easy to set up and then easy to abandon once the initial plan is made. We present PET (Personalized gEnerative Tamagotchi), a desktop companion app that turns a user’s self-directed goal into a personalized virtual pet and an action plan the pet helps the user maintain. PET uses a multi-agent generation pipeline to create a Tamagotchi-style animal avatar (as a pet) that matches the user’s goal and then supports daily check-ins, reflection, plan revision, and reminders. We evaluated PET in a two-week user study with an experimental group using the full PET app and a control group using the same AI planning and chat support without the virtual pet.
