After that, DH-BPR jointly designs and records an application plan for valid candidates, before finally yielding a redesigned BPMN model and an updated resource model (the way resources execute the process). Evaluation based on simulation using a synthetic benchmark and two real-world event logs shows that the framework's redesign reduces the mean case completion time by up to 61.5%.

title: When AI Agents Should Repair, Replan, or Abandon: A Threshold Theory of Plan Commitment
abstract: AI agents often discover mid-execution that their plan is broken, for example when an action fails or a tool is withdrawn. Deployed systems use conventions such as retry loops or "always replan," and a recent benchmark finds no fixed strategy dominates. This paper derives the optimal policy. In the model, a disruption destroys the causal support of part of a plan; repair is a partial reset that preserves the plan's structure, replanning is a full reset, and changing a plan is costly because others have conditioned on it. The optimal policy is a threshold in effective disruption depth: repair shallow damage, replan after deep damage, and abandon the goal when even a fresh plan is not worth its cost. Depth depends on plan structure. In expectation, a single broken action forces 1+R(G)/n actions to be revalidated, where R(G) counts the pairs of actions joined by a dependency path; to first order, a fully serial plan switches to replanning at raw damage about w times smaller than a plan of w parallel chains. A closed-form stability-price threshold determines when a worse repaired plan should be kept over a better fresh one. As language-model planners push replanning costs toward zero, the stability price becomes the only force sustaining plan commitment. Under repeated disruptions, revision frictions make commitment hysteresis optimal: the agent keeps executing a plan it would never choose fresh, and each repair adds patch debt until the debt outweighs repair's cost advantage and the agent rebuilds. A value-of-diagnosis result states when measuring damage is worth its compute and shows that "always replan" is optimal when damage is predictably deep and replanning is the better fallback. A separately implemented numerical checker tests each proposition (zero violations; 1.6 million static-model evaluations), and the model's regime map reproduces that benchmark's regime flips qualitatively.

title: MRASLive: An online parameter estimation toolbox for time-dependent PDEs
abstract: We present MRASLive, a toolbox for online parameter identification in time-dependent partial differential equations based on a model reference adaptive system (MRAS). Building on the MRAS proposed by Kaltenbacher and Nguyen (Inverse Problems 37(5) 2021) and its first numerical realization by the authors (Applied Mathematics for Modern Challenges 8 2026), the toolbox is designed for ease of use, utilising the user's weak form specification to prepare the data, the discretized MRAS and its solvers, and to verify the assumptions of MRAS's convergence theory semi-automatically.

title: Comparative Study of a Biomass-Derived Activated Carbon Catalyst and a Synthetic Silica–Alumina Catalyst on the Heat Transfer Rate Characteristics of Coconut Oil Droplet Combustion
abstract: This study compares the effect of a biomass-derived catalyst (areca-husk activated carbon, hereafter termed the biocatalyst) and a synthetic catalyst (silica–alumina) on the combustion characteristics and heat transfer rate of crude coconut oil (CCO) droplets, a renewable fuel that is difficult to burn because of its high viscosity. Each catalyst was blended into CCO at 1, 2, and 3 ppm, and 0.001 mL droplets suspended at a K-type thermocouple junction were ignited by a Ni–Cr wire heated at 12 V. Flame evolution was recorded with a digital camera and temperature–time data with a data logger, with five repetitions per condition; the heat transfer rate was estimated from the measured temperature using Newton's law of cooling. The biocatalyst blends burned for 1.68–2.00 s and reached peak flame temperatures of about 700–720 °C and peak heat transfer rates of 0.94–0.96 W, whereas the synthetic-catalyst blends burned longer (1.92–2.16 s) but peaked lower, at about 650–665 °C and 0.87–0.88 W. The biocatalyst blends also had a lower kinematic viscosity (27.37–27.46 cSt) than the synthetic-catalyst blends (30.54–32.52 cSt). Within the range tested, the biocatalyst mainly accelerates and intensifies heat release, with 2 ppm giving its longest flame (2.00 s), while silica–alumina mainly prolongs and stabilises combustion, with 3 ppm giving the longest flame of all blends (2.16 s). These findings indicate that low-cost activated carbon from agricultural waste can be used to improve the ignitability of raw vegetable-oil fuels in burners and small-scale combustion systems, whereas silica–alumina is better suited where a steady, sustained flame is required.
journal: Scientific Experiences in Energy and Thermal Engineering

title: A Review on Mustard Aphid: Incidence, Dynamics and Management
abstract: Mustard aphid, Lipaphis erysimi (Kaltenbach) (Hemiptera: Aphididae), is a major sap-sucking pest of rapeseed–mustard and can cause substantial reductions in crop vigour, seed yield and oil content under severe infestation. This review synthesises the supplied literature and selected verified supporting studies on incidence, seasonal population dynamics, weather relationships, crop and host effects, natural enemies, yield consequences and management. Across Indian agro-ecosystems, mustard aphid activity generally occurs during the Rabi season, with peak abundance frequently reported from the 6th to 9th standard meteorological weeks, although the exact peak varies with location, sowing date, cultivar, crop stage and weather. Representative studies have reported peak densities ranging from 250-300 aphids per 10 cm central twig under different environments and sowing schedules. Weather relationships are not uniform: temperature may be positively associated with build-up in some phases and locations but negatively associated during population decline or under warmer conditions; relative humidity and rainfall likewise show variable relationships. Natural enemies, particularly Coccinella septempunctata, Cheilomenes sexmaculata, syrphid larvae and Diaeretiella rapae, contribute to ecological regulation. The review therefore supports an integrated strategy combining timely sowing, balanced crop nutrition, host-plant resistance, conservation biological control, monitoring-based botanical/biorational interventions and selective insecticide use. Forecasting based on weather and crop variables has already been demonstrated for oilseed Brassicas, and current opportunities include smartphone imaging, machine learning and decision-support systems.

title: Spatiotemporal Weather Variability Modelling for Mango Yield Forecasting Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: This study developed and evaluated a machine-learning framework for forecasting mango yield in two mango-growing areas of Tamil Nadu, India: Periyakulam (Theni district) and Krishnagiri district. Annual rainfall, minimum and maximum temperature, relative humidity and mango-yield observations were compiled for 2010–2023 in Periyakulam and 2015–2023 in Krishnagiri. The resulting dataset included 114 district–variety–year observations covering six mango varieties. Descriptive assessments of inter-annual weather variability were combined with Pearson correlation analysis, analysis of variance (ANOVA) and a lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) regression model. Model performance was assessed using a 70:30 training–validation split and five-fold cross-validation, with Random Forest, Support Vector Regression and multiple linear regression as comparators. Yield differed significantly among varieties (F = 10.465, p < 0.001), whereas the district main effect was not significant (F = 0.406, p = 0.525). Validation root mean square error (RMSE) ranged from 3.12 to 3.94 kg/tree in Periyakulam and from 2.98 to 4.01 kg/tree in Krishnagiri. Across the two districts, validation correlations ranged from 88.65% to 95.64%. In the reported cross-validation comparison, the 1D-CNN yielded an RMSE of 3.42 kg/tree and a correlation of 91.8%, outperforming the baseline models. These findings suggest potential for weather-informed, district- and variety-specific mango-yield forecasting, although broader temporal and geographical validation is required.

title: Inclusive Agribusiness Models for Smallholder Farmers: Value Creation, Market Integration and Equitable Benefit Sharing
abstract: Inclusive agribusiness is increasingly proposed as a means of connecting smallholder farmers to remunerative markets while improving the distribution of benefits within agricultural value chains. Yet participation, commercial upgrading and equity are analytically distinct outcomes, and improvements in one do not reliably secure the others. This critical narrative review examines the institutional designs, value-creation mechanisms and distributional consequences of contract farming, producer organisations, coordinated value chains, sustainability certification and digitally mediated market services. Peer-reviewed theoretical, observational, quasi-experimental, experimental and review evidence was assessed with attention to selection, counterfactual validity, contract governance, heterogeneity and geographical transferability. The evidence indicates that coordinated marketing can reduce transaction costs, support quality upgrading and improve access to inputs or information. Nevertheless, observed income gains are contingent on crop characteristics, procurement reliability, bargaining conditions and who is able to enter and remain in a scheme. Stronger causal evidence exists for particular contractual and information interventions than for the broader claim that inclusive business models routinely reduce inequality. Commercial standards may provide price or market advantages while excluding farmers unable to finance compliance. Cooperatives can improve coordination but may reproduce unequal membership and representation. Gendered work, payment arrangements, dependency on powerful buyers and governance of farmers' digital data remain insufficiently captured by conventional farm-income evaluations. This review develops a four-gate analytical perspective that distinguishes access, contractual terms, effective voice and durable benefits, and argues for evaluating the distribution of value and risk across participants and those excluded. Research priorities include longitudinal and experimental comparisons of governance features, disaggregated welfare and labour measures, transparent accounting of value captured along chains, and assessment of resilience under buyer withdrawal or climatic disruption. Inclusiveness should therefore be treated as a verifiable property of institutions and outcomes, not as a label attached to market participation.

title: Comparative Analysis of the Chemical Reactivity and Physicochemical Properties of Selective and Non-selective Herbicides
abstract: This study compared electronic reactivity and selected physicochemical properties of eight herbicides classified as selective or non-selective: glyphosate, butachlor, clethodim, fluazifop, fosamine, glufosinate, paraquat and propanil. Molecular geometries were optimised using density functional theory at the CAM-B3LYP/6-31G level. Frontier molecular orbitals, global reactivity descriptors and condensed Fukui indices were examined, while EPI Suite provided structure-based estimates of lipophilicity, water solubility, bioconcentration, bioaccumulation and persistence. The reported HOMO–LUMO energy gaps ranged from 2.933 to 9.081 eV. Clethodim exhibited the smallest gap and highest tabulated electrophilicity index, whereas glyphosate had the largest gap and greatest chemical hardness. The local reactivity indices suggested variation in preferred atomic sites across the molecular structures, with carbon atoms predominating in the reported assignments. Estimated lipophilicity, solubility and bioaccumulation-related descriptors also differed among the compounds. However, these results describe molecular and model-based properties rather than experimentally measured herbicidal activity, crop selectivity or environmental risk. Interpretation is constrained by the assumptions of the DFT approach and the applicability of the EPI Suite prediction models, particularly for ionisable structures. Furthermore, the software inputs and derivation of persistence values were incompletely specified, and some reported physicochemical results require reconciliation with the original outputs. The analysis therefore provides a comparative theoretical framework for the selected herbicides and identifies the need for computational verification and experimental assessment before broader biological or environmental conclusions are drawn.

title: Spectral similarity shapes species discrimination of herbarium specimens in a taxonomically challenging group.
abstract: PREMISE Supervised machine learning models trained on reflectance spectra are emerging as powerful tools for assisting taxonomic identification of herbarium specimens. However, it is unclear how species composition in model training affects performance. We used the genus Vitis to test how classification errors are driven by spectral similarities among species and whether prediction probabilities decline when classifying species not included in training. METHODS We trained a global partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) on foliar herbarium hyperspectral data from 18 Vitis species. We then ran 18 reduced versions of the global model, where each reduced model omitted one species from training but was tested on all 18 species. We calculated pairwise changes in per-species sensitivity ( ∆ sensitivity ) between the global and reduced models, tested whether ∆ sensitivity correlated with pairwise spectral similarity, and evaluated whether prediction probabilities were lowest when classifying species omitted from training. RESULTS The global PLS-DA had 74.1% accuracy. Across reduced models, sensitivity significantly increased for 31 unique species pairs and significantly decreased for three. Sensitivity improvements were greatest when the focal and omitted species had high spectral similarity and declined nonlinearly with increasing spectral differentiation. Prediction probabilities were highest for correct predictions, intermediate for misclassifications, and lowest for species omitted from training. CONCLUSIONS Our results demonstrate a nonlinear relationship between classification accuracy and spectral similarity, suggesting limits of spectral separability among intrageneric species. Prediction probability may be a useful metric for evaluating the likelihood that a specimen represents a species not included in training.

title: Assessment of cover crop species suitability and water dynamics in hop ( Humulus lupulus L.)
abstract: Hop ( Humulus lupulus L.) is a perennial crop used in brewing, with most US production centered in the semiarid Yakima Valley of Washington State. Growers are interested in cover crops, but limited guidance exists on which species can establish and persist in this high‐traffic, low‐moisture environment. To address this, 19 cover crop species, including annuals, perennials, warm‐ and cool‐season grasses, forbs, and winter‐ and spring‐seeded species, plus a fallow control, were evaluated over 3 years in an experimental hop yard in Prosser, WA. No supplemental irrigation was applied to cover crops beyond water delivered to hop rows, and species performance was assessed through establishment, percent cover, height, and biomass. Soil moisture in the top 20 cm declined by mid‐May, limiting establishment and growth of warm‐season species. Winter‐seeded crops generally achieved higher establishment, cover, and biomass, except for early spring‐seeded mustard ( Brassica napus L.). Drip irrigation applied to hop rows influenced moisture availability in the alleys; in the second year, increased irrigation raised volumetric water content in fallow plots, especially below 75 cm, and species with deeper root systems accessed this moisture. Among annuals, triticale (× Triticosecale Wittmack), cereal rye ( Secale cereale L.), and mustard ( B. napus L.) showed the highest establishment, cover, and biomass. Of the perennials, intermediate wheatgrass ( Thinopyrum intermedium ) and crested wheatgrass ( Agropyron cristatum L.) established in the first year and produced adequate biomass in the second. These results provide initial guidance on species selection and planting timing to improve cover crop performance without supplemental irrigation in hop production systems.

title: Hybrid Forecasting Model for Carbon Price: Integrating Chronological and Weekday‐Structured Temporal Representations
abstract: Accurate carbon price forecasts support allowance trading, compliance planning and market supervision. This study examines whether two temporal representations of the same carbon price series—the original chronological sequence (horizontal dimension) and five weekday‐structured subsequences (vertical dimension) obtained by regrouping Monday‐to‐Friday observations—contain complementary predictive information. Both representations are modeled within a common decomposition‐reconstruction‐forecasting framework: Dynamic time warping (DTW) diagnoses the correspondence between them, complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) and sample entropy (SE) decompose and reconstruct each series, and a leaky‐integrator echo state network (LiESN) generates the forecasts. The weekday‐specific forecasts are restored to chronological order and fused with the horizontal forecast by least squares (LS), and kernel density estimation (KDE) is used to construct prediction intervals. In the Hubei carbon market, the proposed model achieves an MAE of 0.365, a MAPE of 0.800%, an RMSE of 0.538 and an R 2 of 0.949 in the test period, reducing the MAE, MAPE, and RMSE of the chronological‐only benchmark by 2.41%, 2.20%, and 2.89%, respectively, and the Wilcoxon signed‐rank test indicates that its improvements over all benchmark models are significant at the 5% level. The model also attains the highest or tied‐highest interval coverage and the highest composite interval score. Additional experiments on the Shenzhen and Chongqing carbon markets show that the incremental gain is modest, and its statistical significance is market‐dependent: It is significant in Chongqing but not in Shenzhen. These results support the view that weekday‐structured forecasts can provide complementary predictive information beyond adjacent‐day chronological dependence, without treating the weekday sequences as independent multivariate variables or claiming a newly discovered weekday anomaly.

title: Drivers and Impacts of Postharvest Losses in Mango Production for Poverty Reduction Among Smallholder Farmers in Kintampo North Municipality, Ghana.
abstract: Mango is a key export crop that contributes to Ghana's economic growth. However, postharvest losses threaten the industry and the livelihoods of smallholder farmers and traders. Moreover, limited empirical studies assess the extent, constraints, and impact of these losses. The aim of this study was to quantify the amount of mango fruit wasted at the farm level, identify the causes of these losses, and assess their impact on farm income. Using a structured questionnaire, data was solicited from 297 mango producers from Kintampo North municipality in the transitional agroecological zone of Ghana. Disaggregating mango postharvest losses into quantitative and qualitative losses, the data show that approximately 137 kg (2.74 of 50 kg boxes) and 85 kg (1.7 of 50 kg boxes) are wasted per hectare respectively. In terms of economic value, the overall quantity of mango lost at the farm level translates into excess of Gh¢334 (US$32). Results from the Seemingly Unrelated Regression (SUR) model indicate that qualitative mango postharvest losses are significantly influenced by factors such as age, landownership, farm size, and credit access, whereas quantitative losses are associated with gender, family size, farm size, credit access, and type of laborer. Generalized propensity score matching (GPSM) analysis reveals that higher mango postharvest losses significantly reduce farm profitability, with increasing losses leading to declining profit margins. These findings highlight the need for targeted interventions, including improved credit access, farmer training, and postharvest management technologies, to reduce losses and enhance farmers' income. The study also contributes to addressing postharvest losses in ways that align with key Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including SDG 1 (no poverty), SDG 2 (zero hunger), SDG 12 (responsible consumption and production), and SDG 13 (climate action).

title: Dual‑Functionalized Mesoporous Bioactive Glass Integrating BMP‑2 and Apt19S for Outstanding MSC Recruitment and Osteogenesis.
abstract: Insufficient osteoinductive capacity and deficient mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) remain major challenges for artificial bone materials in treating critical-sized bone defects. To alleviate these limitations, we engineered mesoporous bioactive glass (MBG) nanoparticles with superior osteogenic activity via loading of bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) and exceptional MSC recruitment capacity by covalent grafting of nucleic acid aptamer Apt19S. The BMP-2-immobilized MBG (MBG-BMP-2) exhibited sustained release of BMP-2, primarily attributed to the confinement effects of size-matched mesopores. The Apt19S-modified MBG (MBG-Apt19S) effectively recruited bone marrow MSCs (BMSCs) in vitro and efficiently promoted migration of targeted MSCs in vivo. MBG-BMP-2 effectively promoted osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs in vitro and enhanced new bone formation in a rat cranial defect model. In contrast, while MBG-Apt19S showed less direct osteogenic stimulation to BMSCs in vitro, it elicited a substantially greater bone regeneration response in vivo, outperforming even MBG-BMP-2. Notably, MBG co-immobilized with BMP-2 and Apt19S (MBG-BA) produced the most robust osteogenic outcomes. Mechanistically, this superior performance was ascribed to the concurrent activation of the Smad1/5/8 and ERK1/2 signaling axes. This study elucidates the outstanding effects of osteoinductivity and MSC recruitment by MBG-BA, which could offer valuable insights for the development of multifunctional artificial bone materials.

title: Optimized Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Photovoltaic Soiling in Arid Desert Climates
abstract: Soiling is a major source of photovoltaic (PV) energy loss in desert environments, where day‐to‐day dust accumulation alternates between steady deposition, rapid storm‐driven degradation, and rare rain‐driven recovery. This study evaluates a light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM [LGBM]) quantile‐regression framework (Q‐LGBM) that issues 72‐h soiling‐ratio forecasts, comprising a conditional median, an 80% prediction interval, and a directional signal, for an outdoor test facility in Doha, Qatar. Inputs combine weather forecasts, air‐quality metrics, solar irradiance, and autoregressive soiling‐ratio lags. Expanding‐window cross‐validation and a sequential temporal holdout are benchmarked against linear‐decay and persistence baselines. Without rain postprocessing, Q‐LGBM reaches a holdout RMSE of 0.0092, statistically indistinguishable from linear decay (Diebold–Mariano p = 0.951), but detects soiling recovery markedly better (upward recall 0.773 vs. 0.227). Under cooler, dustier holdout inputs, the 80% interval widened from 0.040 to 0.060, and empirical coverage rose from 83.3% to 96.2%. Distribution shift diagnostics across inputs, soiling ratios (SRs), and calibration metrics show that input shift coincided with this interval widening, suggesting a candidate trigger for hyperparameter retuning. A supplementary rain‐reset rule yields the lowest cross‐validation RMSE (0.0083) but degrades on the holdout (0.0160) because of numerical precipitation forecast false alarms and subcleaning rainfall.

title: Population structure and ecotype-associated genomic differentiation in Bangladeshi rice germplasm (Oryza sativa L.).
abstract: In Bangladeshi rice (Oryza sativa L.) germplasm, cultivars or landraces are traditionally classified into four principal ecotypes based on seasonal moisture regimes: Boro, Aman, Aus, and Jhum. The relationships among ecotype differentiation, genomic ancestry, and population structure remain poorly understood. We investigated the genetic diversity and population structure of 333 Bangladeshi rice accessions with respect to their ecotype classification. We identified a total of 25,994 single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers across the whole genome of this panel. From the SNP data and discriminant analysis of principal components, STRUCTURE analysis, genetic diversity analysis, and neighbor-joining analyses, we identified three groups, corresponding to Aromatic, Indica, and Aus. They differed in both genetic ancestry and degree of ecotype-associated differentiation. Aus consisted of all four ecotypes and showed clear ecotype-associated differentiation, suggesting adaptation to distinct ecological environments. Aromatic accessions shared a common genetic background and maintained partial ecotype-associated differentiation between Aman and Boro. Indica showed reduced genetic diversity and weak ecotype differentiation, reflecting intensive crop improvement and ecotype admixture. The genomic population structure of Bangladeshi rice germplasm was therefore shaped by both ecological adaptation and human-mediated selection across distinct ancestry groups. Our findings provide deeper insights into the genetic and ecological foundations of this germplasm, supporting its future use in genome-wide association studies and genomic prediction and its exploitation for rice improvement in Bangladesh and beyond.

title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
abstract: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and generation to the reader's distinct position in the text. The system integrates a hybrid retrieval architecture, combining vector similarity, BM25, and summary embeddings, to ensure high fidelity to the reader's current context. We evaluate the system across classical English books using both quantitative comprehension metrics and qualitative LLM-based independent judging. The results identify a quality-latency frontier, showing that mid-sized local models (2b-4b) can achieve comprehension parity with larger counterparts (5b+) while maintaining acceptable response quality. Importantly, the proposed progress-aware boundary mechanism is shown to prevent future content leakage without compromising retrieval quality and correctness. These findings suggest that a localized, privacy-centric approach can augment, rather than replace, the digital reading experience, offering a good alternative to cloud-dependent services. Therein, there remains a lack of amalgamate systems which combine progress-aware, privacy-preserving, and narrative eBook reading with AI support. It is in this very gap that the development of MeReader came to be; synthesizing said strands into an offline, book-constrained assistant focused on enhancing comprehension without compromising narrative continuity or user privacy.

Establishment and characterisation of primary human oesophageal organoids as a versatile epithelial model
abstract: Human patient-derived oesophageal epithelial models are limited, and organoid cultures often have short passaging lifespans, restricting studies of tissue homeostasis and disease. We aimed to establish and characterise primary oesophageal organoids from non-pathologic epithelium as a renewable epithelial source and adaptable modelling platform. Primary oesophageal tissues were obtained from endoscopic biopsies and surgical resections. Basal epithelial cells were isolated and cultured under optimised conditions to establish long-term three-dimensional organoids. Organoid-derived cells were expanded as two-dimensional monolayers and re-seeded into 3D culture. Epithelial identity and differentiation were assessed by immunostaining and RT-qPCR (reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction) analysis of markers. Primary organoids were established and maintained while preserving epithelial markers. Expression of KRT14, involucrin, loricrin and filaggrin confirmed the oesophageal phenotype. Larger, multilayered primary organoids showed increased expression of differentiation-associated markers relative to 2D monolayers and re-seeded small organoids, indicating culture configuration influences epithelial differentiation while maintaining lineage identity. We established a robust and reproducible protocol for generating and maintaining oesophageal organoids across culture formats. These models retained epithelial features while exhibiting culture-dependent differentiation. This platform enables complementary 2D and 3D investigation of oesophageal epithelial biology and supports future comparison of healthy and disease-derived tissues for patient-specific modelling and mechanistic studies.

title: A UAV-based real-time detection system of flowering nectar plants using a lightweight deep learning model
abstract: Timely knowledge of flowering status and peak blooming periods in transferred areas is crucial for migratory beekeepers to make informed management decisions. Traditional manual field surveys are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Current monitoring approaches using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) rely on offline processing and require complex data analysis by specialists, making them impractical for beekeepers to implement in apicultural settings. Given the short time window for capturing flowering events, especially for species with short florescence periods, an accurate, fast monitoring solution is needed. We developed a UAV-based real-time investigation prototype leveraging edge-intelligence computing for nectar flower detection of Rhus chinensis in complex mountainous field conditions. An improved, high-precision, and lightweight deep learning model based on YOLOv5s was proposed. The model was optimized with acceleration strategies during deployment to reduce inference time. Experimental results showed that the proposed model for flower detection achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 89.5 and an inference speed of 56 frames per second (FPS). After applying acceleration strategies during model deployment on the edge computing device, the processing throughput reached 192 FPS with a mAP of 89.2; a 3.1% increase in mAP and approximately a 5.6 times improvement in FPS compared to the original YOLOv5s. These results demonstrate that the proposed lightweight model and acceleration strategies effectively balance high accuracy with high-throughput onboard image processing. The developed UAV-edge computing system provides a promising prototype for future efficient nectar flowering status monitoring, with potential applications in smart apiculture. First UAV-based real-time counting system for mountainous nectar flowers. Propose an improved high-precision and lightweight DL model for UAV edge computing platform. Achieved 89.5% mAP in complex environment, a 3.4% improvement over original YOLOv5s. Provides a potential prototype for flowering assessment to support timely decision-making in smart apiculture. By integrating UAV-based imaging, accelerated deep learning, and edge computing, this study developed a real-time UAV-edge prototype for nectar flower detection in Rhus chinensis, a nectar plant, under complex mountainous field conditions. The proposed system enables efficient and timely monitoring of nectar plant flowering, providing a foundation for the development of practical decision-support tools for precision apiculture. By facilitating rapid flowering assessment during short blooming periods and supporting timely management decisions, this approach contributes to improved spatial-temporal management and more efficient resource allocation in precision agriculture.

Ghana’s national innovation system and the governance readiness gap for artificial intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding across Ghanaian finance, health, agriculture, public administration and digital services, while the institutions responsible for governing its risks are still developing the capacity, coordination and authority required for implementation. This study examines Ghana’s National Innovation System (NIS) as an institutional setting for AI governance. Using a qualitative, multi-technique design, we conducted 32 purposively sampled interviews across universities and research institutes, firms, government agencies, financial institutions, intermediaries and boundary-spanning actors. Vignette-based interviewing, triadic elicitation and the Critical Incident Technique (CIT) were analysed through reflexive thematic analysis and interpreted using Technological Innovation Systems (TIS) functions and UNESCO/African Union governance benchmarks. Four recurrent failure mechanisms were identified: capability, connectivity, legitimacy and resource failures. The evidence also revealed relative strengths, including a growing research base, emerging public-sector policy direction and boundary-spanning relationships that occasionally enabled knowledge transfer. We therefore characterise Ghana’s condition as a system-wide but uneven governance readiness gap rather than a total governance deficit. The paper develops the Governance Readiness Paradox: AI activity and policy ambition can expand faster than the institutional capacity to translate knowledge into enforceable, accountable and inclusive governance. The study presents a Ghana AI Governance Readiness Matrix and eight sequenced policy recommendations for strengthening research-to-policy translation and implementation capacity.

title: Forward programming of human pluripotent stem cells to endothelial cells utilizing ETV2-mRNA delivery with ionizable lipid nanoparticles.
abstract: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) represent a scalable source of cells for off-the-shelf therapeutics and advanced in vitro tissue models. However, their translational utility is constrained by inefficient differentiation protocols that rely on small molecules, cytokines, or genomic modification. Here, we describe a non-integrating approach that utilizes ionizable lipid nanoparticles (iLNPs) to deliver mRNA encoding the ETV2 transcription factor to efficiently forward reprogram hPSCs to endothelial cells (ECs). This platform achieved transfection efficiencies exceeding 97%, with robust expression of functional mRNA cargo. ETV2 delivery induced rapid endothelial conversion, generating cell populations with average purities greater than 90% based on expression of canonical endothelial surface markers Pecam-1 (CD31) and VE-Cadherin (CD144). Forward programming efficiency depended upon culture parameters including initial seeding density, mRNA dosage, and time after transfection. Functionally, iLNP-ETV2-derived ECs exhibited hallmark endothelial behaviors, including angiogenic network formation in vitro, uptake of acetylated low-density lipoprotein, and inflammatory cytokine responsiveness. Collectively, these findings establish iLNP-mediated ETV2 mRNA delivery as an efficient and non-genome-integrating strategy for forward programming hPSCs to ECs, facilitating their use in tissue engineering, disease modeling, and cell-based therapy applications. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Human pluripotent stem cells are a promising source of cells for regenerative medicine and tissue engineering, but existing differentiation methods often produce low yields and require extensive optimization. In this study, we demonstrate that ionizable lipid nanoparticles can achieve highly efficient mRNA delivery to pluripotent stem cells and enable efficient, non-integrating forward programming to endothelial cells through transient expression of the transcription factor ETV2. This approach generated highly pure endothelial populations that retained key endothelial functions and remained stable during long-term expansion. Importantly, endothelial conversion was maintained across broad ranges of cell seeding densities and mRNA doses, suggesting a robust and scalable manufacturing process. These findings establish a versatile platform for mRNA based cell engineering and stem cell differentiation.

Monitoring ecosystem biodiversity and interaction after forest wildfire: An environmental-DNA-satellite-data-driven artificial intelligence modeling framework.
abstract: Wildfire is an escalating threat to forest ecosystem health, yet post-fire management still lacks the timely and systematic consideration of biodiversity loss and biotic disruption. Here, we present an integrative eDNA-satellite-AI monitoring framework that combines environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, satellite-derived burn-severity mapping, and explainable AI (XAI) to quantify post-fire ecosystem changes. Using Sentinel-2 imagery, we first quantitatively assessed the wildfire severity at study sites differentiated by the extent of fire damage (control, damaged, and extremely damaged). eDNA was then collected from water basins installed at these sites and subjected to eDNA metabarcoding, sequencing, and bioinformatic analyses to characterize a wide range of forest eukaryotic groups (e.g., vertebrates, invertebrates, and other microeukaryotes). Ten supervised machine learning (ML) models were subsequently trained to predict burn severity using eDNA features. Systematic optimization of the ML models based on model selection, feature selection, and hyperparameter tuning achieved a high prediction performance (R2 = 0.76), suggesting eDNA data is reflective of post-fire consequences. XAI and co-occurrence network analysis identified the orders Stylommatophora (land snails and slugs), Rodentia (rodents), and Caudata (amphibians) as the taxonomic groups that were most sensitive to wildfire intensity, with eDNA metabarcoding providing phylogenetic and evolutionary information on these groups that is infeasible to obtain at comparable scale and throughput using traditional field surveys. The proposed eDNA-satellite-data-driven AI modeling framework integrates molecular ecology with remote sensing and XAI, thus advancing forest ecosystem monitoring beyond the passive, descriptive characterization of biota inventories towards predictive, explanatory, and risk-based digital ecosystem assessment.
