title: Paradigm shift from linear discharge to closed-loop cycling: A synergistic phosphorus resource recovery strategy based on waste-treating-waste.
abstract: In the face of the dual challenges posed by the non-renewable crisis of phosphorus resources and the problem of water eutrophication, there is a pressing need to break free from the traditional linear economic model of extraction-use-discharge. Therefore, constructing a resource cycling system based on removal-recovery-reuse has become an essential mission for global sustainable development. This study focused on phosphorus resource recovery and reuse path using lotus leaves-derived biochar (LBC). Through further systematic characterization of surface properties and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the key role of oxygen-containing functional groups (e.g., hydroxyl and carboxyl) in phosphate adsorption was elucidated. In the continuous phosphorus enrichment experiment, the FCDI system concentrated phosphorus from a lower concentration influent solution (20 mg/L) into the electrolyte solution, achieving a high concentration of 185.7 mg/L. Finally, a closed-loop resource chain from waste to functional electrode to phosphorus fertilizer was established. This was achieved through differentiated resource utilization: phosphorus-saturated biochar was directly used in agricultural cultivation, and the concentrated electrolyte was converted into struvite. This study presents a lab-scale proof of concept for continuous phosphorus enrichment and dual-pathway recovery, linking wastewater treatment with resource recycling.

title: Mapping resource dependence across industries and regions for environmental governance: A meso-scale analysis for energy resources in the Yellow River Basin.
abstract: Resource dependence poses a critical challenge for environmental governance in resource-based regions, yet existing assessments often lack a meso-scale perspective that captures heterogeneity across industries and regions. This gap hinders the precise identification of regional resource-dependent industries and the design of differentiated transition policies. Integrating the Pressure-State-Response (PSR) logic and the Multi-regional Input-output (MRIO) model, this study develops an assessment framework for industrial resource dependence (IRD) that captures its multidimensional dependence conditions rather than treating it as a uniformly undesirable outcome. Using the energy-intensive Yellow River Basin as a case study, we assessed the IRD of 42 industries across nine provinces for two major energy resource types-Coal and Oil&Gas in 2017. The results reveal substantial heterogeneity in IRD across provinces, industries, and resource types. Inter-provincial differences were primarily shaped by dominant industrial structures and resource endowments, with Henan exhibiting the highest dependence on Coal and Shandong the highest on Oil&Gas. At the industry level, Coal IRD was mainly associated with electricity and heat production and coal-based processing, whereas Oil&Gas IRD was dominated by petroleum processing and chemical manufacturing. Regarding the multidimensional structure of IRD, while the two resource types shared similarities in consumption scale and intensity, they diverged significantly in resource endowment conditions and adaptive response characteristics. By distinguishing dependence patterns across regions and industries, this study provides a diagnostic tool for identifying highly resource-dependent industries and informing differentiated environmental governance strategies, while offering a transferable framework for application in other resource-dependent regions.

title: Miao medicine Xinlikang capsule attenuates acute erythroleukemia through immune regulation and FLI1-PI3K axis-mediated cell cycle arrest.
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE Acute erythroleukemia (AEL) is an aggressive subtype of acute myeloid leukemia characterized by impaired erythroid differentiation, uncontrolled expansion of erythroid progenitors, and immune dysfunction. Owing to its poor prognosis and lack of specific therapeutic options, effective alternative strategies are urgently needed. Xinlikang capsules (XLK), a Miao medicine formula approved in China, have been clinically used as an adjuvant therapy for malignant tumors. However, its therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms in AEL remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY To evaluate the anti-AEL effects of XLK and clarify its pharmacodynamic material basis and molecular mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS An AEL mouse model was established by F-MuLV infection and treated with XLK for 5 weeks. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed by serum biochemical indicators, organ indices, histopathological examination, immune cell profiling, erythroid differentiation markers, and survival analysis. The chemical compositions of XLK and XLK-containing serum (XLKs) were identified by UPLC-MS/MS. The anti-proliferative effects of XLKs and its absorbed constituents were evaluated in HEL cells using MTT assays and flow cytometry. Network pharmacology, RNA-seq, Western blotting, and Fli1 shRNA knockdown were used to investigate the underlying mechanisms. This integrated approach evaluates in vivo therapeutic efficacy, defines the pharmacodynamic material basis, and dissects the molecular mechanism, providing a multi-layered analytical framework for understanding the anti-AEL effects of XLK. RESULTS XLK markedly reduced splenomegaly and hepatomegaly, improved spleen and liver histopathological damage, normalized serum ALT and AST levels, and prolonged the survival of F-MuLV-induced AEL mice (p<0.001). XLK promoted erythroid maturation by increasing mature erythroid cells and reducing erythroid precursor accumulation. It also restored immune homeostasis, as evidenced by increased CD3+ T cells (by 50%), CD11b+ cells (by 10%), and B220+ B cells (by 46%), together with a normalized CD4+/CD8a+ ratio in the spleen. UPLC-MS/MS identified nine absorbed constituents in XLKs, among which tomentic acid, tanshinone IIA, cryptotanshinone, and apigenin exhibited notable inhibitory effects on HEL cell proliferation. XLKs suppressed HEL cell proliferation (27.69% inhibition at 72 h with 20% XLKs) and induced S-phase arrest in a time- and concentration-dependent manner. Network pharmacology and RNA-seq analyses indicated that the PI3K signaling pathway and cell cycle regulation were key pathways involved in the anti-AEL effects of XLK. Mechanistically, XLKs downregulated FLI1 and inhibited PI3K pathway activation in HEL cells, accompanied by decreased CDK2 and Cyclin B1 expression and increased Cyclin A2 (1.9-fold) and p-CDC25C (1.7-fold) expression. Furthermore, Fli1 knockdown reduced p-PI3K and attenuated the anti-proliferative effect of XLKs (8.51% reduction at 72 h), supporting a key role of FLI1-mediated PI3K signaling in XLK-induced cell cycle arrest. Among the absorbed constituents, cryptotanshinone recapitulated the downregulation of FLI1, p-PI3K, and p-mTOR, supporting its role in XLK-induced cell cycle arrest. CONCLUSIONS These findings suggest that XLK exerts therapeutic effects in F-MuLV-induced AEL. Mechanistically, XLK alleviated spleen and liver injury, promoted erythroid differentiation, restored immune homeostasis, and suppressed erythroleukemia cell proliferation by inducing cell-cycle arrest through modulation of the FLI1-PI3K signaling pathway, thereby exerting a therapeutic effect on AEL.

title: Land use, common agricultural policy subsidies, and farm economic exposure under planetary health diet scenarios in Europe: a physical input-output modelling analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Animal-sourced food (ASF) production dominates agricultural land use in the EU and attracts a large share of public fiscal support. Although shifts away from ASFs have broad implications for land use, public spending, and farming livelihoods, the distributional effects across regions and supply chains remain largely unquantified. This study aims to quantify these effects and identify regional differences in the economic implications of transitioning towards plant-rich diets. METHODS We assessed the effects of adopting the planetary health diet (PHD) and its variants across the EU+UK relative to a 2020 baseline. Using the multiregional food and agriculture biomass input-output model, we linked farm income and labour accounts to agricultural supply, use, and trade to trace feed-animal-food linkages through supply chains. We summarised regional heterogeneity using six transition archetypes defined by sectoral composition, profitability excluding subsidies, and reliance on livestock. FINDINGS Adopting the PHD would release 58-78 million hectares of agricultural land in the EU+UK and free up €28-36 billion per year of common agricultural policy (CAP) subsidies under increasingly plant-rich variants of the PHD. Correspondingly, EU+UK farm employment would decline by 37-40% and farm profits excluding CAP subsidies would decrease by 15% (PHD) to 3% (PHD-vegan). These effects varied across regions: in places where livestock production was loss-making at baseline (excluding CAP subsidies), reduced ASF demand could eliminate these losses and increase regional profits; in contrast, profits declined in regions where livestock production was profitable. INTERPRETATION Dietary change creates substantial scope for land and fiscal repurposing; however, transition costs are concentrated geographically and across production systems. The diversity in regional archetypes will require differentiated support to achieve a plant-rich and just food transition, which could be partly financed via repurposed CAP resources. FUNDING KR Foundation, British Academy, REAPRA, Horizon Europe 2020 Framework GreenGrocer project, Dutch National Research Agenda.

title: The role of cellular signaling pathways in the therapeutic effects of sonodynamic therapy against periodontitis: A narrative review.
abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by dysbiotic subgingival biofilms and driven by a dysregulated host response that destroys the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone. Mechanical debridement remains the cornerstone of therapy, but biofilm tolerance, anatomically inaccessible niches, and the limited action of antimicrobials on host-mediated tissue destruction leave clinically relevant gaps. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) uses low-intensity ultrasound to activate sonosensitizers and generate reactive oxygen species (ROS), offering deeper tissue reach than light-based approaches and a route to site-specific, non-antibiotic adjunctive care. Beyond microbial killing, ROS and co-released mediators may reshape host signaling. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on signaling pathways modulated by SDT and grades it by proximity to periodontitis. Direct evidence from periodontal or jawbone-infection studies concerns NF-κB, NLRP3/caspase-1, Toll-like receptor (TLR) and NOD-like receptor signaling, IL-17 signaling, osteoclast differentiation, M1-to-M2 macrophage polarization, and AMPK and PI3K/Akt-associated osteogenesis. Mechanistic precedents from non-periodontal models concern ROS-PPARγ-NF-κB, Nrf2/ARE, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR-autophagy signaling. Direct periodontal evidence is limited to a small number of preclinical studies, pathway-level claims rest mainly on transcript- or protein-level associations, and the anti-inflammatory and pro-osteogenic effects of some platforms are attributable to co-delivered nitric oxide or metal ions rather than to sonodynamic ROS. We therefore distinguish SDT-dependent from platform-dependent effects, discuss dental translational issues (delivery, ultrasound source and dosimetry, safety, peri-implantitis, systemic comorbidity), and propose research priorities: pathway-specific validation, standardized ultrasound reporting, and controlled clinical trials of SDT as an adjunct to subgingival instrumentation.

title: Stromal Immune Niches in Transplantation: Signaling Circuits and Therapeutic Targets beyond Lymphoid Organs.
abstract: Stromal cells, the extracellular matrix (ECM), and vascular and lymphatic networks are increasingly recognized as organizers of local immune responses in solid organ grafts. However, transplant immunology remains centered largely on immune cells and lymphoid tissues. Here we propose the graft stromal immune niche as an operational concept: a spatially restricted microenvironment in which local stromal, vascular, lymphatic, or matrix-derived cues are associated with measurable changes in immune-cell localization, persistence, differentiation, or function. Synthesizing evidence from kidney, heart, lung, and liver grafts, we describe three recurring spatial contexts-perivascular, interface-associated, and perilymphatic/egress-associated-and discuss how early injury, ECM mechanics, and stromal programming may shape niche behavior over time. Building on current evidence, we propose a three-state model encompassing rejection-prone, tolerance-permissive, and fibrotic niches; delineate established knowledge and remaining evidence gaps; and critically evaluate pharmacological interventions at different stages of clinical development. This framework is intended to guide the interpretation of spatial datasets and the design of niche-directed strategies.

title: Hyperspectral remote sensing of cover crop traits for decision support in precision nitrogen management
Spatiotemporal variability in seasonal and interannual InSAR-derived excess ground ice content retrievals using Sentinel-1
Estimating the red-to-far-red chlorophyll fluorescence ratio with RGB imagery
RepliCore: An execution model for deterministic observable-state progression in browser-based parallel simulation
abstract: Browser-based simulations execute over asynchronous runtime mechanisms including event loops, rendering callbacks, and independently scheduled Web Workers, causing simulation progression to depend on runtime timing and callback scheduling behavior. RepliCore addresses this problem by separating asynchronous runtime progression from externally observable logical-state visibility. Runtime-visible simulation states are exposed only after logical-state progression becomes externally stable, preventing asynchronous runtime activities from observing partially updated simulation progression. The framework prevents rendering callbacks and asynchronous runtime tasks from observing transient intermediate logical states during parallel progression. This organization maintains consistency between parallel and sequential execution. Based on this model, we implement RepliCore, a browser-oriented deterministic parallel simulation framework for reproducible large-scale simulation under asynchronous browser runtimes. Experiments in real browser environments produce bitwise-identical outputs across varying worker configurations, scheduling conditions, and rendering frequencies while remaining practical for large-scale browser-oriented workloads. Additional ablation experiments show systematic state divergence after relaxing key execution constraints. These results indicate that reproducible asynchronous parallel simulation can be achieved through controlled logical-state visibility stabilization without relying on execution replay or explicit schedule control.

title: Reviewing digital gaming and gambling addiction: A dark intersection of technology, psychology, and sociology

Preadipocyte-Derived Decellularized Extracellular Matrix-Functionalized Three Dimensionally Printed Scaffolds Regulate Vascularized Adipose Tissue Regeneration via Modulation of Selected Paracrine Factors.
abstract: The clinical efficacy of soft tissue reconstruction is severely hindered by unpredictable graft resorption and inadequate vascularization. Traditional synthetic implant scaffolds offer mechanical support, with limited bioactivity for adipose tissue regeneration. In this study, we developed a "three-in-one" bioinstructive platform (dPCL) integrating structural support, signal induction, and immunomodulation by functionalizing a 3D-printed polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) derived from 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. The obtained dECM-functionalized scaffold provided essential biochemical cues. In vitro assays demonstrated that dPCL significantly enhanced preadipocyte adhesion and adipogenic differentiation. Besides, the dECM-functionalized scaffold was found to modulate the secretion of selected paracrine factors, markedly upregulating the secretion of adiponectin, VEGF, and IL-10, which facilitated cell differentiation and robust endothelial network formation. In vivo evaluation in a murine subcutaneous model confirmed that dPCL scaffolds effectively supported the formation of stable, well-vascularized adipose tissue. Furthermore, the dECM-functionalized scaffold enhanced the recruitment and accumulation of proregenerative M2 macrophages, maintaining an M2-dominant tissue microenvironment that facilitated graft integration. In summary, current findings demonstrate that integrating cell-specific dECM with 3D-printed scaffolds creates a multifaceted bioactive platform that overcomes the critical barriers of vascularization and metabolic integration, presenting a highly promising strategy for functional soft tissue regeneration.

title: Loading-Dependent Osteogenic Performance of Core-Shell Nanocomposite-Reinforced Poly(ε-caprolactone) Scaffolds for Bone Regeneration.
abstract: Bone defect repair remains challenging due to the complex biological processes involving inflammation, angiogenesis, and osteogenesis. Although therapeutic ions and natural antioxidants have been individually investigated for bone regeneration, the biological performance of scaffolds incorporating multiple functional components at different loading contents remains to be fully explored. In this study, we designed a core-shell nanocomposite (GaTe-MBG@Cur-ZIF-8) consisting of Ga/Te-codoped mesoporous bioactive glass (GaTe-MBG) as the core and curcumin-loaded ZIF-8 as the shell. The nanocomposite was incorporated into poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) at different contents (0, 5, 10, and 15 wt %) to fabricate three-dimensional (3D)-printed composite scaffolds. The designed scaffolds were intended to provide a multifunctional platform integrating curcumin with Ga, Te, Zn, Si, and Ca ions. Among the investigated formulations, the scaffold containing 10% GaTe-MBG@Cur-ZIF-8 (by weight) exhibited the most favorable overall biological performance, including antioxidant activity, favorable inflammation-associated responses, enhanced osteogenic differentiation, and angiogenesis-related effects. In a rat cranial defect model, the 10% scaffold demonstrated improved bone regeneration compared to the other groups. RNA sequencing analysis revealed differential gene expression and enrichment of inflammation- and osteogenesis-related pathways, including IL-17, TNF, and MAPK signaling, suggesting potential associations between the scaffold-induced cellular responses and these signaling pathways. Collectively, these findings highlight the potential of the combined GaTe-MBG@Cur-ZIF-8 nanocomposite for bone tissue engineering and identify 10% as a favorable loading content within the investigated range, providing insights into the design of multifunctional composite scaffolds for bone regeneration.

title: Hierarchical Composite Scaffold That Synergistically Combines Orderly Active Factor Release with Scaffold Degradation for Enhanced Bone Repair.
abstract: Effective bone regeneration requires biodegradable scaffolds to provide temporary mechanical support while progressively creating space and delivering bioactive cues in step with tissue healing. However, achieving synergy between orderly active particle release and scaffold degradation remains a major challenge. This study aimed to develop a hierarchical scaffold for sustained bioactive-ion delivery and bone-defect repair. The scaffold consisted of a 3D-printed poly(p-dioxanone) (PPDO) framework and a freeze-dried gelatin network. Magnesium oxide-coated chitosan microspheres (MgO@CS) were incorporated into gelatin to support early cell recruitment and angiogenesis, whereas citrate-functionalized amorphous calcium phosphate (Cit-ACP) was embedded in PPDO to provide sustained osteogenic stimulation. During in vitro degradation, gelatin was largely removed within 5 weeks, progressively opening space for tissue infiltration. PPDO fibers showed morphological erosion at weeks 7-8 but persisted as the principal structural framework. The scaffold continuously released Mg2+, Ca2+, and citrate during the 14-day observation period. Cell experiments demonstrated enhanced cellular recruitment, vascularization, and osteogenic differentiation. In a rat calvarial defect model, the scaffold enhanced bone formation and improved BV/TV. These results demonstrate that coupling stage-matched scaffold degradation with compartmentalized bioactive-ion delivery provides a promising strategy for coordinating vascularized bone regeneration.

title: Multidimensional Protein-Based Antimicrobial Materials: Construction, Mechanisms, and Applications.
abstract: Bacterial contamination and associated infections remain persistent threats to global public health. Proteins, as renewable biomacromolecules with diverse functional groups, programmable hierarchical structures, and favorable biocompatibility, have emerged as versatile building blocks for antimicrobial materials. Through self-assembly, amyloid-like aggregation, interfacial engineering, and chemical or physical functionalization, proteins can be constructed into zero-dimensional (0D) micro/nanoparticles, one-dimensional (1D) fibers, two-dimensional (2D) films and coatings, and three-dimensional (3D) hydrogels, aerogels, and sponge scaffolds. Dimensional architecture extends beyond morphological classification: it governs active-site exposure, interfacial contact, mass transport, mechanical properties, and antimicrobial-agent retention and release, thereby determining bactericidal activity, resistance to bacterial adhesion, and antibiofilm performance. Nevertheless, the relationships connecting dimensional construction, interfacial structure, antimicrobial mechanism, and application-specific performance remain fragmented. This review therefore adopts dimensionality as the central framework for critically examining the structural design, assembly, and functionalization of protein-based antimicrobial materials across 0D-3D architectures. Particular emphasis is placed on how dimensional features regulate the antimicrobial mechanisms involving membrane disruption, cell-wall hydrolysis, reactive oxygen species generation, physical bacterial trapping, controlled antimicrobial release, and resistance to bacterial adhesion. Recent advances in the applications of these antimicrobial materials, categorized by their dimensional architectures, are further evaluated across biomedicine, food preservation, functional textiles, and agriculture in relation to their operating environments and functional requirements. Finally, challenges concerning mechanistic validation, long-term stability, scalable manufacturing, biological safety, and application-specific evaluation are critically discussed to identify barriers to practical implementation and future directions for technological translation. Emerging opportunities in AI-assisted protein and peptide design, precise interfacial engineering, and multifunctional integration are further highlighted to guide the rational development of next-generation protein-based antimicrobial materials.

title: Genome-wide analysis reveals altitude-associated divergence in a colour-polymorphic insect.
High-Efficiency Combustion Mode in Three-Strut Scramjet Combustor via Clustering Analysis
abstract: This study investigates the influence of five design parameters on the combustion characteristics of a three-strut combustion chamber through single-factor analysis, clarifying their relationship with combustion efficiency and resistance. A Halton sequence with mean squared error–based infill sampling was employed to generate a sample set, and an accurate surrogate model was developed using Gaussian process regression. The Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) was then applied to optimize the chamber geometry with the objectives of improving combustion efficiency and reducing resistance. Through clustering analysis, two distinct high-efficiency combustion modes were identified: a multizone violent combustion mode and a blended mild combustion mode. In the former, the rapid combustion of pilot fuel creates favorable conditions for subsequent fuel combustion, increasing the combustion efficiency from 73% to 93% compared with the baseline case; however, due to excessively abrupt flow field changes, the reduction in resistance is not significant. In the latter, the flame fronts merge and develop smoothly, and although it only improves combustion efficiency to 85% compared with the baseline case, it substantially reduces resistance from − 7,762 newtons (N) to − 8303 N . This work provides enhanced design flexibility for high-performance scramjet combustors.

title: Efficient Synergistic Design Framework for Electric Aircraft Integrating Co-Flow Jet
abstract: Flow control technologies such as the Co-Flow Jet (CFJ) have demonstrated significant potential for improving aerodynamic performance. However, most existing studies treat CFJ parameters as fixed during aircraft conceptual design, limiting the ability to evaluate their system-level impact on aircraft performance. To address this limitation, this study proposes an efficient multidisciplinary design framework that integrates key CFJ design parameters into the conceptual design process of CFJ electric aircraft. The framework combines a quasi-three-dimensional aerodynamic analysis method with energy consumption and weight estimation models of the jet system, enabling rapid evaluation of aerodynamic performance, propulsion power consumption, and aircraft weight within a unified framework. Based on the proposed methodology, a multidisciplinary design optimization problem is formulated to improve aircraft cruise performance. The framework is applied to a representative aircraft configuration, and the predicted aerodynamic performance is validated against computational fluid dynamics simulations. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can efficiently capture the coupled effects of CFJ aerodynamic benefits, jet system energy consumption, and additional structural weight. Parametric studies further reveal the sensitivity of optimal CFJ configuration to cruise velocity and fan efficiency, providing useful guidance for the preliminary design of CFJ electric aircraft.

title: FRGB3D: Fast Reliability-Weighted Gaussian Background Modeling for Roadside LiDAR Traffic Monitoring
abstract: Intelligent transportation systems rely on accurate perception technologies for traffic monitoring, with light detection and ranging (LiDAR) emerging as a critical sensing modality. However, effective background–foreground separation is challenging due to the varying measurement reliability across point clouds caused by distance, reflectivity, and atmospheric conditions. This paper presents fast reliability-weighted Gaussian background modeling for 3D LiDAR traffic monitoring (FRGB3D), a novel unsupervised approach for LiDAR point cloud background modeling and foreground detection that explicitly incorporates physics-based reliability assessment with adaptive learning mechanisms. The key contributions include (1) a physics-based reliability metric that quantifies measurement quality using range and reflectivity characteristics, (2) a reliability-weighted adaptive learning approach for Gaussian background modeling that dynamically adjusts learning rates based on point reliability, and (3) an adaptive thresholding mechanism that incorporates both measurement reliability and learned model uncertainty. Through comprehensive experiments using both the Car Learning to Act (CARLA) simulator and real-world LiDAR data collected in Lowell, Massachusetts, we demonstrate that FRGB3D achieves superior foreground detection performance compared with baseline methods. FRGB3D achieved F1-scores of 0.84, 0.68, and 0.77 across base, adverse-weather, and high-density traffic scenarios, respectively, consistently outperforming simple difference, moving average, and standard Gaussian background modeling approaches. Real-world experiments demonstrated competitive object-level performance average precision (AP) (AP@0.5 = 0.48) while maintaining real-time processing capabilities with 19.1 frames per second (FPS), making it suitable for practical traffic monitoring applications.
journal: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering

title: Comparative Analysis of Two Approaches for Improved Site Safety: Domain Approach versus General End-to-End Compliance Reasoning
abstract: Field compliance checking seeks to automate the process of extracting safety requirements, capturing site information, identifying violations, and generating documentation for different responsible parties to improve construction site safety. However, existing safety checking methods are typically limited in their ability to employ domain knowledge and multimodal data, and they often lack generalizability and scalability. There is also limited effort to automatically generate natural-language descriptions of compliance-checking results for documentation purposes. Aimed toward addressing these gaps, this paper studies and compares two approaches for automated safety checking: a domain approach and an end-to-end approach. The domain approach integrates existing domain-specific information extraction, site visual information detection, and knowledge graph–based compliance reasoning methods. The end-to-end approach relies on multimodal foundation models. The comparative analysis evaluates the information extraction and compliance reasoning capabilities of both approaches in terms of performance, errors, and limitations. The results showed that the domain approach achieved strong performance with good potential for generalizability and adaptability. In contrast, the end-to-end approach requires additional fine-tuning to achieve comparable results.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: A Review of Human-Centric Construction Manufacturing: Current Practices and Research Opportunities
abstract: The industrialization of the construction industry has transformed traditional practices by streamlining construction processes in controlled, factory-based environments through construction manufacturing production systems, in which building components are produced in factories and assembled on-site. Beyond improvements in efficiency and environmental performance, this production paradigm establishes long-term relationships between workers and management, creating an opportunity for human-centric construction manufacturing that prioritizes workers’ well-being as a core element of production within the Industry 5.0 paradigm. Human-centric construction manufacturing offers a practical means of integrating worker well-being, safety, mental health, inclusiveness, and skill development into construction production systems. Despite growing interest in human-centric considerations, existing research remains fragmented, loosely defined, and predominantly technology-driven. To address these gaps, this paper presents a scoping review on human-centric construction manufacturing that synthesizes key research themes, enabling technologies, emerging trends, research gaps, and future research directions within construction production systems. A total of 54 articles were included in the review, spanning three research areas examined from a human-centric perspective, i.e., ergonomics, safety, and workforce planning, each further categorized into subresearch areas. Workers’ mental health, equity, diversity, inclusion, and holistic well-being in the construction manufacturing paradigm remain significant and underexplored research opportunities. Among the most prominent technologies were simulation, virtual reality, optimization, sensing technologies, and 3D modeling, while computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and digital twins were less frequently applied, despite their strong potential to support human-centric construction manufacturing. Overall, this review establishes a comprehensive foundation for understanding the current state of human-centric construction manufacturing, identifies critical research needs, and provides guidance for future efforts toward developing safer, healthier, and more productive factory environments that support resilient construction manufacturing systems.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Revisiting the Dunne Diagram: Seasonal Variation and Spatial Pattern of Runoff Components
abstract: The classic Dunne Diagram qualitatively illustrates how atmospheric conditions, soil, and topography shape runoff generation mechanisms under long-term average conditions. This study revisits the diagram using a novel theoretical framework that unifies infiltration excess and saturation excess runoff into a continuous scheme governed by dynamic soil moisture variations across catchments. The framework captures the spatial and temporal transitions between runoff mechanisms. Using observational data from 600 natural catchments across diverse US atmospheric conditions and landscapes, we develop a data-driven, quantitative reinterpretation of the Dunne Diagram based on multiannual catchment behavior, and further examine runoff generation mechanisms at seasonal timescale. At the mean annual scale, saturation excess runoff dominates the West Coast and Eastern United States, infiltration excess runoff prevails in central regions, and baseflow dominates the Western interior and Appalachian areas. In the western United States, both saturation- and infiltration-excess runoff exhibit strong seasonality, closely following the precipitation patterns along the West Coast. Individual catchments show seasonal switching and coexistence of dominant runoff generation mechanisms. The Unified Scheme for Modeling Saturation and Infiltration Excess Runoff (URSSIE) model broadly reproduces the general pattern of the Dunne Diagram and provides quantitative support for the Dunne Diagram. This approach enhances the understanding of runoff processes and improves hydrologic modeling at catchment scales, with important implications for flood forecasting and water resource management in complex or changing hydrologic regimes.

title: Real-Time Monitoring of Vacuum Leaks in Condenser Pipes Using Ultrasonic Acoustic Signals
abstract: Vacuums in air-cooled condensers (ACCs) are essential for maintaining the efficient operation of thermal power plants. Air ingress caused by vacuum leaks increases condenser pressure, degrades heat transfer performance, raises turbine back pressure, and ultimately reduces plant efficiency. Previous research has primarily focused on leak detection in pressurized pipeline systems, whereas vacuum leak detection in ACCs remains largely unexplored due to the limitations of existing techniques and harsh industrial operating conditions. This paper proposes a portable real-time ultrasonic leak detection (RULD) system for detecting air ingress into vacuum-operated condenser pipes using ultrasonic acoustic signals. The proposed system employs three ultrasonic microphones to acquire leak-generated acoustic signals and processes them using the root mean square (RMS) method with adaptive noise-based thresholds. Leakage is identified when the RMS values of at least two microphones exceed their respective thresholds. Experimental investigations were conducted on four irregular leak geometries (hydraulic diameters 1.19–1.43 mm) under a 0.5-bar vacuum, considering microphone distances of 5–20 cm and angles of 0°–90°. The results showed that the 20–40-kHz ultrasonic frequency band provides the highest sensitivity for leak detection. The 0° microphone orientation produced the maximum RMS response, which decreased with increasing microphone angle, while reliable detection was achieved up to 10–15 cm from the leak source. The developed RULD system processed each 1-s acoustic data segment in 0.0009 ms, enabling real-time leak detection without interrupting subsequent data acquisition. The proposed system was further validated on condenser pipes and a prototype ACC model, demonstrating its suitability for real-time monitoring of vacuum-operated condenser systems.
journal: Journal of Pipeline Systems Engineering and Practice

title: Physiologic and pharmacologic role of the glucocorticoid receptor in germinal center B cells and plasmacytic differentiation.
abstract: In diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL), a malignancy derived from germinal center (GC) B cells, somatic hypermutation aberrantly targets glucocorticoid receptor (GR) binding sequences in the super-enhancer (SE) of multiple oncogenes. These events abrogate GR binding and deregulate the expression of the SE-linked gene, suggesting an important role of GR in normal and transformed GC B cells. Using a GC-specific Nr3c1 knockout mouse model and multi-omics analyses in murine and human GC B cells, here we show that, under physiological conditions, GR constitutively localizes to the nucleus, where it transcriptionally modulates signaling pathways implicated in GC homeostasis and plasmablast differentiation in part by antagonizing the repressive function of BCL6 on the plasma cell master regulators IRF4 and PRDM1. While loss of baseline GR activity led to mild GC hyperplasia and impaired plasmacytic differentiation, pharmacologic doses of glucocorticoids, a key component of DLBCL chemo-immunotherapy, were preferentially toxic to GC in a GC B cell-autonomous manner. These findings uncover a physiological role for GR in the GC reaction as well as in promoting plasmablast/plasma cell formation and provide insights into the specific activity of glucocorticoids in the treatment of DLBCL.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Pulmonary Ionocytes Regulate CFTR-Mediated Chloride Transport in Human iPSC-Derived Epithelium.
abstract: RATIONALE Pulmonary ionocytes, representing approximately 1% of airway epithelial cells, exhibit high CFTR expression and unique transcriptional markers, including FOXI1, ASCL3, and V-ATPase. Their exact role in human airway physiology is incompletely understood. OBJECTIVE This study employs induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived airway epithelial models (iPSC-airways) to elucidate the role of FOXI1 in pulmonary ionocyte differentiation and function. METHODS CRISPR-Cas9 was used to generate FOXI1-knockout iPSCs, into which a doxycycline-inducible FOXI1-overexpression cassette was introduced. Edited and control lines were differentiated into airway epithelia to evaluate ionocyte formation, epithelial composition, and ion transport. Rescue studies assessed the effects of FOXI1 re-expression in a FOXI1-KO background, and the addition of inducible WT-CFTR ionocytes to F508del/F508del cystic fibrosis (CF) cultures on restoring chloride transport. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS FOXI1 deletion abolishes ionocyte formation and alters airway epithelial composition, with increased mucus-secreting goblet cells and decreased ciliated cells. Functional assays confirmed ionocytes as key regulators of chloride homeostasis, with FOXI1-deficient airways displaying diminished ion transport. Induction of FOXI1-overexpression restored CFTR-mediated chloride transport. Introduction of WT ionocytes into CF airway models rescued chloride transport deficits, with no rescue observed in vehicle-treated controls lacking ionocyte induction. CONCLUSIONS These findings highlight FOXI1's essential role in pulmonary ionocyte development, airway cell composition, and airway chloride transport. We present a fully manipulable, gene-edited iPSC-derived system that enables investigation of ionocyte biology and function within a human airway context, highlighting them as promising therapeutic targets for respiratory disorders.
journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology

title: Environmental epimutagens, epigenetic memory, and cancer latency.
abstract: Environmental exposures can cause cancer through DNA damage and mutations, but whether they can also leave durable, cancer-relevant changes in gene regulation is less clear. Chromatin helps maintain cell identity, differentiation state, and plasticity, providing a route by which non-genetic effects of exposure could persist after exposure. We define environmental epimutagens as agents or conditions that perturb chromatin regulation, and examine how such perturbations may influence cancer initiation and latency. Exposures can reach chromatin through altered metabolite or cofactor availability, interference with chromatin-regulating proteins, and direct chemical modification. Most resulting changes are transient, adaptive, or secondary. The central question is which become biologically embedded in long-lived cell populations, remain silent during latency, and alter responses to later genetic, inflammatory, or tissue-level pressures. Studies of inflammatory memory and transient disruption of chromatin repression show that short-lived perturbations can durably reprogram cellular potential, lower the threshold for tumor initiation, or generate tumorigenic states. Exposures may also influence the later selection of primed cells. Establishing causality will require physiologically realistic exposure models, longitudinal and lineage-resolved analyses, and functional tests distinguishing biomarkers of exposure from persistent mediators of cancer susceptibility. Such work may identify preventable exposures, informative biomarkers, and opportunities for cancer interception.

title: GhNAC029 reduces cotton drought tolerance by negatively regulating NCED1-mediated ABA synthesis.
abstract: Cotton (Gossypium hirsutism) is an important economic crop, accounting for 39% of natural fiber production. NAC transcription factors represent one of the largest transcription factor families and play an important role in plant responses to drought stress. However, most studies have been conducted in model plants such as Arabidopsis thaliana, while the regulatory mechanism in cotton require further investigation. Previous studies on genes associated with drought tolerance have predominantly focused on positive regulatory genes, with relatively few reports addressing negative regulatory genes. In this study, we analyzed the transcriptome differences between the drought-sensitive genotype XLZ8 (S) and the drought-tolerant genotype G95079 (G) at various time points during drought stress, identifying the key NAC transcription factor that negatively regulate the cotton drought tolerance gene GhNAC029 (Gh_A03G0887). Through virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) and the transgenic lines, we demonstrated that GhNAC029 negatively regulated the cotton drought tolerance. Further investigation of GhNAC029 downstream regulated genes by transcription and CUT&Tag, we found GhNCED1, a crucial gene involved in abscisic acid (ABA) synthesis, which was down-regulated by GhNAC029. Additionally, exogenous ABA spraying, GhNAC029 was found to increase ABA sensitivity and reduce ABA biosynthesis. Therefore, we infer that GhNAC029 inhibits the expression of GhNCED1, leading to a decrease in ABA biosynthesis in cotton, which consequently weakens the cotton drought tolerance.

title: Crop Management and Seasonal Soil Health Dynamics Are Associated With Soybean Cyst Nematode Reproduction.
abstract: Soybean cyst nematode (SCN) remains the most economically damaging soybean pathogen in North America. While its relationship with soil texture is well documented, less is known about how soil health properties and crop management practices are related to SCN population dynamics under field conditions. This study evaluated SCN reproductive factor (RF) in relation to: 1) soil texture and its interaction with crop management, 2) key soil physicochemical properties and their seasonal changes, and 3) the predictive performance of individual soil properties versus the Comprehensive Assessment of Soil Health (CASH) soil health indices. In 2023 and 2024, soil samples from 185 Ohio fields were collected during spring and fall. Hierarchical modeling and zero-inflated negative binomial regression were used to evaluate relationships among soil texture, management practices, and SCN RF. Soil texture explained little variation in SCN RF, whereas crop rotation with non-host crop was the strongest management factor, with non-host crops associated with a 79% reduction in RF. Seven variables were significantly associated with increased or decreased SCN RF, including seasonal changes in permanganate oxidizable carbon (POXC), pH, and macroaggregates, spring measurements of potassium, pH, and POXC, and the presence of a non-host crop. The final individual soil property model (RF6) explained 2.8 times more variation in SCN RF than the best-performing model based on composite CASH indices. These findings reinforce the importance of crop rotation with non-host crop, and continued SCN monitoring as part of integrated management strategies for soybean production systems, and suggest that seasonal changes in soil properties merit further study as indicators of SCN dynamics.

title: Stock market prediction and trading strategy optimization with S4-integrated deep learning architectures: a comparative study of hybrid fusion mechanisms
abstract: The accurate prediction of stock market movements remains a challenging task due to the non-stationary, noisy and highly volatile nature of financial time series. While deep learning models such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Transformer have demonstrated promising results, they often struggle to capture both long-term dependencies and short-term fluctuations efficiently. To address these limitations, this paper introduces al hybrid framework that integrates the Structured State Space Sequence (S4) model with three fundamental deep learning architectures via tailored fusion mechanisms. Specifically, we propose (1) LSTM-S4, a parallel architecture with attention-based fusion and skip connections; (2) MLP-S4, a serial embedding model that enables temporal modeling for MLP; and (3) Transformer-S4, a tandem structure that combines global attention with local temporal pattern extraction. Extensive experiments are conducted based on real-world data from six Chinese stocks covering diverse sectors and market conditions. The results demonstrate that the S4-integrated hybrid models outperform their base counterparts and existing baseline models in terms of predictive accuracy measured by RMSE, MSE, MAE and $Rˆ2$, as well as simulated investment returns. Notably, we design a practical trading strategy and verify its effectiveness through statistical testing. Paired-sample t-tests confirm that the improvement in returns is statistically significant. Compared to their base counterparts, the LSTM-S4, MLP-S4 and Transformer-S4 models yield t-statistics of −3.72, −3.96 and −2.97, respectively, with all p-values below 0.05 and the minimum p-value reaching 0.01. This conclusion confirms that after incorporating the S4 module, the three models not only enhance prediction performance but also enable the adoption of more profitable trading methods, effectively capturing complex patterns in financial time series. This underscores the significant potential of S4 to enhance temporal feature extraction in financial time series forecasting, offering a valuable tool for practical market prediction.
journal: International Journal of Intelligent Computing and Cybernetics

title: Balancing competitiveness and inclusion: a systematic review of smallholder integration models within Sub-Saharan African cashew value chains
abstract: This study aims to synthesise rigorous evidence on smallholder integration models in Sub-Saharan African cashew value chains and assess whether they simultaneously deliver commercial competitiveness and inclusive development for approximately three million smallholder farmers. A PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review searched Scopus and Google Scholar. After eligibility screening and quality appraisal (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool), we retained 39 empirical studies from eight Sub-Saharan African countries for narrative synthesis. We identified seven integration model types across 23 studies; the remaining 16 examined production, land use or welfare without documenting a discrete arrangement. Contract farming alone showed consistently positive competitiveness findings but also the most consistently adverse gender findings. Of 11 studies reporting productivity, four were positive, three negative and three null. Participation barriers (15 studies) and governance inclusion (6) were uniformly adverse. The evidence base is concentrated in Ghana (53.8% of studies); Côte d'Ivoire, the world's largest raw cashew producer, is represented by only one study. Designs are predominantly cross-sectional and outcome-associational rather than causal. Future research should prioritise longitudinal designs, governance-focused enquiry and underrepresented countries. This is among the first PRISMA-compliant systematic reviews of smallholder integration in SSA cashew value chains. Its main contribution is showing that the competitiveness–inclusion tension remains largely unaddressed: only four of 39 studies examine it within a discrete arrangement, while 12 address cash crop versus food crop allocation.
journal: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies

title: From academic excellence to market attractiveness: explaining the transformation gap in higher education institutions
abstract: This study examines why academic performance does not necessarily translate directly into market attractiveness in higher education institutions. Drawing on capability, institutional and signaling perspectives, it frames this disconnect as a transformation gap: an explanatory condition in which internally generated academic value requires strategic and relational mechanisms to become externally recognized market value. The transformation gap is not treated as a separate latent construct. A quantitative explanatory design was used with 300 strategic-level academic and administrative respondents in Indonesian higher education. Four reflective constructs – academic performance (AP), strategic positioning (SP), relational signaling (RS) and market attractiveness (MA) – were assessed using Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The reported evaluation includes reliability and convergent validity, heterotrait–monotrait ratio (HTMT), collinearity, R2, Q2, f2 and bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples. Academic performance was not significantly related to market attractiveness directly (β = 0.07, t = 1.12, p > 0.05), so H1 was not supported. Academic performance was positively related to strategic positioning (β = 0.41, t = 6.85, p < 0.001) and relational signaling (β = 0.38, t = 6.10, p < 0.001). Strategic positioning (β = 0.46, t = 7.92, p < 0.001) and relational signaling (β = 0.24, t = 4.25, p < 0.001) were positively related to market attractiveness. The indirect effects through strategic positioning (β = 0.19, t = 5.80, p < 0.001) and relational signaling (β = 0.09, t = 3.95, p < 0.01) were significant, indicating an indirect-only mediation pattern, traditionally described as full mediation. The study is limited by its cross-sectional, single-source survey design, which restricts causal inference and does not eliminate potential common method bias. The purposive sampling approach and focus on Indonesian private higher education institutions may also limit generalizability across institutional and national contexts. Moreover, market attractiveness was measured perceptually rather than through objective market outcomes. Future research should employ longitudinal, multi-source and cross-national designs and incorporate objective indicators such as enrollment, retention, graduate employability, employer evaluations and institutional sustainability to further examine the transformation-gap perspective. The findings suggest that university leaders should complement academic excellence with deliberate strategic positioning and relational signaling. Institutions can translate academic strengths into market attractiveness by differentiating program value, aligning offerings with stakeholder needs, strengthening industry and alumni partnerships and communicating credible evidence of academic achievements and graduate outcomes. Managers should therefore monitor not only internal academic performance but also how effectively these achievements are converted into relevant and visible market signals. Importantly, such strategies should complement, rather than substitute for, sustained academic quality. The findings suggest that translating academic strengths into credible and accessible external signals can help prospective students and other stakeholders make better-informed educational choices. Stronger university–industry and stakeholder relationships may also improve the alignment of academic programs with societal and employment needs. However, efforts to enhance market attractiveness should remain consistent with educational access, inclusion, academic quality and institutional social missions. Thus, strategic positioning and relational signaling should support not only institutional visibility but also broader contributions to employability, stakeholder engagement and social development. The contribution lies in distinguishing academic value creation from external value recognition and in specifying two complementary conversion mechanisms. Strategic positioning makes academic value relevant and differentiated, whereas relational signaling makes that value visible and credible. The findings are consistent with a transformation-gap interpretation without claiming validation of a new psychometric construct.
journal: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education

title: From green commitment to sustainable harvest: how digital capabilities and institutional pressure power agricultural sustainability
abstract: The objective of this study is to examine whether, and through which mechanisms, green corporate social responsibility (GCSR) integration improves sustainable farm performance in a climate-vulnerable emerging economy. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and institutional theory, the study analyses the mediating roles of green supply chain dynamic capabilities, sustainable agricultural innovation and digital technology capability, and the first-stage moderating role of coercive institutional pressure. A cross-sectional survey of 420 farmers and agribusiness managers, purposively selected through agricultural extension offices in 30 districts across four Pakistani provinces, was conducted. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 10,000 bootstrap resamples was used to estimate the model, which contains three parallel mediators and three interaction terms. Measurement and structural model quality, predictive relevance, common-method bias, nonresponse bias and endogeneity were assessed through standard procedures. GCSR integration has a significant direct effect on sustainable farm performance, but most of its effect is transmitted through capability building. Digital technology capability carries the largest indirect effect, followed by green supply chain dynamic capabilities and sustainable agricultural innovation. Coercive institutional pressure strengthens the conversion of GCSR into all three capabilities, the moderation is largest for digital capability, but the three moderation effects are not statistically distinguishable. The study concludes that green commitments improve farm sustainability only when they are converted into organizational capabilities, and that regulatory pressure accelerates this conversion. The cross-sectional, self-reported and purposive design limits causal inference and statistical generalization. Future studies should use longitudinal, multi-source and objective farm data and test normative and mimetic pressures. Policymakers should pair environmental regulation with digital monitoring requirements, extension training and affordable digital infrastructure, while farm managers should treat GCSR as a capability-building program rather than a symbolic commitment. The study differentiates three capability pathways through which GCSR becomes farm-level sustainability and treats coercive pressure as a first-stage condition of capability formation rather than a background constraint. It also provides farm-level evidence from a smallholder-dominated emerging economy, where prior work has focused on manufacturing and listed firms.

title: 3DMS-CTR: A Click-Through Rate Prediction Model Based on Feature Extraction Across Frequency, Topology, and Temporal Dimensions
abstract: Feature extraction and representation play a crucial role in click-through rate(CTR) prediction tasks. This work is inspired by multi-scale feature fusion techniques in computer vision. By integrating and fusing features extracted at different scales, richer and more comprehensive information can be captured, leading to more generalized feature representations. This helps to improve the accuracy of predictions and the performance of the model. Inspired by this, we propose a multiscale feature fusion model for click-through rate prediction(3DMS-CTR). First, we propose a multi-dimensional multi-scale feature extraction algorithm, called 3DMSF. It extracts features across temporal, topological, and frequency dimensions using different scale methods to perform hierarchical feature extraction on low-order, high-order, and interest features, ensuring multigranularity in feature learning. Then, we employ a multi-scale feature fusion method based on an improved attention mechanism, called MS2F. During the multi-scale feature fusion process, the weights of different features are dynamically adjusted, thereby enhancing the effectiveness and robustness of feature representations. Finally, inspired by collaborative filtering techniques, we propose a low-order, high-order, and interest feature-based collaborative graph-enhanced embedding method, called LHI2gra. This method addresses the issues of feature sparsity and missing features. Experiments show that this model effectively extracts multi-scale features. On three public datasets, our model outperforms the baseline.

title: In-Storage Heterogeneous Acceleration For Scalable Long-Read Mapping
abstract: Near-data processing accelerates data-intensive applications by moving computation closer to data, reducing data movement overhead and improving performance and efficiency. This paradigm is particularly promising in genome analysis, where read mapping, a critical step for aligning DNA sequences to reference genomes, poses substantial challenges due to the sheer volume and complexity of the data. Traditional software solutions and high-performance computing (HPC) clusters struggle with the rapid growth of genomic datasets, while specialized hardware accelerators remain limited by data movement. In this paper, we present Mendel, a heterogeneous near-storage architecture for end-to-end long-read mapping that combines storage-side, memory-side, and FPGA-based acceleration within an SSD-centered design. Mendel features a superscalar chunk-based pipeline and a chunk-aware filtering heuristic, specifically designed to handle long DNA sequences. Under our modeling-, simulation-, and synthesis-based evaluation, Mendel outperforms the long-read hardware mapper Darwin by up to 2.97 ${\boldsymbol{\times}}$ × in performance and 17.97 ${\boldsymbol{\times}}$ × in energy efficiency. Compared with Darwin enhanced with GenStore-style in-storage filtering, Mendel also provides higher projected performance and lower projected energy consumption in our evaluated setting.

title: Beyond Side-by-Side Comparison: A Unified Evaluation Framework for Model Selection in Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Time series forecasting is a fundamental task in data mining, yet model evaluation remains methodologically underdeveloped. Current practice reports predictive accuracy and computational efficiency as separate indicators, leaving decision makers with ambiguous trade-offs when models show opposing strengths. This paper introduces Efficiency–Precision Equilibrium Coefficient (EPEC), a unified framework that integrates normalized error and training time into a single interpretable ranking. EPEC provides a structured, reproducible aggregation rule that transforms two-dimensional comparisons into a clear, rankable score. Extensive experiments across five domains including transportation, energy, finance, meteorology, and public health demonstrate that EPEC yields stable, discriminative rankings that systematically differ from side-by-side comparisons. The framework shows strong alignment with pragmatic decision heuristics and is robust to parameter variations, multi-seed randomness, and task sampling. By contributing a generalizable methodology for performance aggregation in predictive analytics, EPEC serves as an efficient training-stage model screening and benchmarking tool, bridging the gap between experimental evaluation and reproducible model selection.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering

title: The GIVE Database: Acoustic and Perceptual Characteristics of Infant Emotional Vocalizations in the First Year of Life.
abstract: Infants communicate their affective states through a rich repertoire of preverbal vocalizations that support early social interaction and guide caregiver responsiveness. However, research on emotional infant vocalizations is limited by the lack of standardized, comprehensive, and perceptually validated datasets. To address this need, the Geneva Infant Vocalization of Emotion (GIVE) database includes 360 annotated vocalizations from infants aged 0-12 months across positive, neutral, and negative valences. Vocalizations were extracted from naturalistic parent-infant interactions, manually segmented, and annotated based on the emotional valence of the vocalization and its auditory interactional context. Acoustic features were characterized using the eGeMAPS parameter set, and a large-scale adult perceptual validation provided ratings of valence, cuteness, and aversiveness for each sound. As an example of an individual-level factor, we also examined how parenthood influences adults' perception of infant vocal emotional cues. Results reveal clear perceptual distinctions across valence categories, with acoustic properties contributing to evaluations of emotional valence, cuteness, and aversiveness. Ratings of cuteness and aversiveness further differentiated vocalization categories, while age-related variation in responses to vocalizations produced by infants of different ages, alongside differences associated with parental status, illustrates GIVE's potential for investigating developmental and experiential influences on the interpretation of infant vocalizations. A subset of 120 experimentally validated vocalizations, representative of the full set, was selected and acoustically characterized, providing a resource for research on early emotional communication, parental sensitivity, neuroimaging, and computational modeling of infant vocal behavior.

title: Drought May Alter the Flux of Essential Omega‐3 Fatty Acids From Streams to Terrestrial Ecosystems
abstract: Stream and riparian food webs are connected via cross‐ecosystem subsidies, including essential nutrients like omega‐3 fatty acids that originate in the aquatic environment (microalgae) but support terrestrial consumers. Although global change stressors could be disrupting these linkages, most research to date has focused on subsidy quantity rather than quality. Here, we reviewed the literature on omega‐3 long‐chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (ω3 LC‐PUFA) in streams and other freshwaters, and we examined how drought‐related stress may influence their production, accumulation, and trophic transfer. Although direct evidence linking drought conditions to changes in stream ω3 LC‐PUFA dynamics is limited, existing studies point to several disruptive mechanisms: warming‐ and drying‐induced shifts in basal resource composition and primary production, altered consumer community composition and emergence phenology, and reduced capacity for ω3 LC‐PUFA bioconversion. ω3 LC‐PUFA accumulation in organisms is driven primarily by species identity and further shaped by life‐history traits such as drought adaptations (e.g., resistance and resilience strategies), temporal integration of diet, and feeding ecology. We explored these mechanisms via a case study on intermittent stream invertebrates at Pinnacles National Park, California, and found largely taxon‐specific patterns rather than consistent responses to hydrology. Finally, we identified key challenges and recommendations for advancing ω3 LC‐PUFA research. These include (i) explicitly considering organismal life histories; (ii) improving sampling design to strengthen inference; (iii) considering underground ecological processes; (iv) advancing research on consumer fitness responses to ω3 LC‐PUFA limitation and on “upgrading”; (v) measuring rates and fluxes; and (vi) scaling up and forecasting fatty acid flux under increasingly dry futures by integrating models of hydrology, organismal biology, and community dynamics. We contend that the disruption of cross‐ecosystem linkages, not just in resource magnitude but also in quality, is a “blind spot” of global change ecology that demands immediate attention.

title: Belowground Productivity in Grasslands and Savannas Depends on Shifting Fire and Herbivory Regimes
abstract: In grasslands and savannas, most plant biomass and net primary productivity is belowground. How shifts in disturbance regimes, such as fire or large herbivore activity, impact belowground net primary productivity (BNPP) is unclear across climate‐driven productivity gradients. We tested the hypothesis that altered fire and herbivory regimes impact BNPP by changing the relative biomass of herbaceous and woody plants, which differ in their relative allocation to BNPP, and that climate constrains how much disturbance shifts this herbaceous–woody balance. We measured BNPP and aboveground vegetation across seven African and North American grasslands and savannas, with three long‐term fire manipulation levels (high frequency, intermediate frequency, and suppressed) and, at six sites, two long‐term herbivory levels (large herbivores excluded or open to large herbivores). Sites spanned an aridity index (mean annual precipitation [mm]/potential evapotranspiration [mm]) gradient—and associated woody thickening potential—from 0.21 to 0.71. BNPP increased with water availability. Fire and herbivory increased BNPP, with greater effects in wetter sites. In the wettest sites, BNPP gains under disturbance correlated with herbaceous biomass gains, as herbivory and frequent fire reduced woody plant cover relative to disturbance exclusion plots. BNPP responses were also predicted by root biomass, explaining why wetter sites and frequently disturbed plots within sites had higher BNPP. Climate determined how much the positive response of root biomass offset fire and grazing reductions in aboveground plant stocks, largely because water availability constrained the total aboveground plant biomass achieved without disturbance. Therefore, disturbances stimulated BNPP in wet savannas, largely by limiting woody thickening and promoting herbaceous growth with higher BNPP rates, whereas BNPP in drier and mesic sites tended to be resilient. Our findings show that belowground processes in grasslands and savannas fundamentally depend on disturbance regimes, climate‐driven productivity gradients, and their interactions, with important implications for understanding global carbon storage.

title: Somatic cell reprogramming to totipotency: molecular logic, emerging models, and future perspectives.
abstract: Plant regeneration depends on the capacity of differentiated somatic cells to regain plasticity and acquire totipotency. Although somatic embryogenesis has long been explored, the molecular logic by which a somatic cell converts into an embryo-forming founder cell remains incompletely understood. Classical studies established the developmental and hormonal basis of regeneration, whereas recent multi-omics studies have revealed that regeneration is not a simple process of dedifferentiation. Instead, totipotency emerges through ordered reprogramming events involving cell-type-specific competence, suppression or redirection of pre-existing trajectory, activation of embryogenic transcriptional networks, hormonal rewiring, and epigenetic remodeling. We summarize major findings in plant somatic cell reprogramming, discuss the conceptual transition from dedifferentiation to developmental trajectory rewiring, and highlight future directions for engineering totipotency in recalcitrant crops.

title: Analysis of RGB and thermal images for plants dehydration classification
abstract: In modern agriculture, it is necessary to monitor crops to achieve sustainable usage of the water. However, in the state of Guanajuato, the use of optical techniques in agriculture has been largely unexplored, relying instead on traditional techniques that damage the plants. In this paper, we explore different artificial intelligence and computer vision algorithms applied to RGB and infrared images to classify different levels of plants’ dehydration, offering a non-invasive and fast approach. The methodology consists of capturing RGB and infrared (8–14 µm) images using control plants with different levels of dehydration. Top-down images will be taken to capture the entire plant to obtain a significant measurement of its state. The acquired images are preprocessed to extract the region of interest, corresponding exclusively to the plants’ leaves, are segmented. Based on this, features of interest are calculated and from the extracted data, a dataset is created to apply machine learning algorithms to achieve precise classification. The findings demonstrate that while RGB imagery alone achieved strong classification accuracy (up to 79%), combining RGB and thermal signatures yielded the highest performance (81%), enabling fast and precise estimation of sample hydration states.
journal: Remote Sensing for Agriculture, Ecosystems, and Hydrology XXVIII

title: Early-season crop emergence estimation utilizing time series-based deep learning with multi-sensor remote sensing data
abstract: Early-season crop emergence estimation provides crucial information for monitoring seasonal crop growth and predicting crop yield in supporting food security worldwide. In remote sensing practices for agriculture, it is technically challenging to perform early-season prediction mainly due to factors such as partial crop coverage on soil ground and limited availability of remote sensing data. In this study, we propose a deep learning approach that can effectively utilize all available time series features of satellite images captured by various sensors (RCM, Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2) in early-season for crop emergence estimation. Satellite data are pre-processed and resampled to 20m spatial resolution and temporally aligned as a time series. Various polarimetric features from SAR images and vegetation index features from Sentinel-2 images are also generated to increase the depth of training features for performance improvement. Various machine learning and deep learning algorithms such as XGBoost, CNN and LSTM, are evaluated for their performance in terms of prediction error and computational complexity. The proposed approach is evaluated in Carman MB study site for both 2020 and 2021 seasons based on 48 available ground fields using available early-season images from June 10 to June 30. The cross-validation results show that the best LSTM algorithm can achieve early-season crop emergence date within 4 days across all fields at the end of June. In particular, the LSTM algorithm can achieve the mean absolute difference within around 2 days for wheat, 3 days for canola, soybean, and corn.
journal: Remote Sensing for Agriculture, Ecosystems, and Hydrology XXVIII

title: Toward the integration of water-leaving radiance attenuation and digital surface models for storage-volume characterization in hill reservoirs
abstract: This study proposes a methodological approach to determine the bottom width of small hill reservoirs using remote sensing techniques, specifically 3-m resolution PlanetScope satellite imagery. The objective is to estimate reservoir depth using the radiative transfer equation, focusing on the exponential attenuation of the water‑leaving radiance with depth. Under the assumptions of a flat reservoir bottom with homogeneous reflectance and an optically uniform water column, the bottom reflectance remains constant as long as the water depth allows the substrate to contribute to the emergent radiance, that is, when the water column cannot be considered optically infinitely deep. The case study concerns a set of hill reservoirs located in Sicily. The analysis shows that the best performance in estimating bottom width is obtained using the green band of the satellite imagery. Optimal conditions occur when the water level is at its seasonal minimum, typically during summer, when reduced depth enhances the discrimination of bottom features. Preliminary results, evaluated against reference data, indicate an average determination coefficient of 0.9 in estimating the geometric parameters investigated, with an average underestimation of 20%. This confirms the reliability of the proposed method and its potential for applications in monitoring and managing water resources in hilly environments. Integrating information on bottom width, surface width, and bank slope enables the calculation of the reservoir’s storage volume. The resulting estimates were compared with a recently acquired reference dataset from the competent regional authorities to assess accuracy.
journal: Remote Sensing for Agriculture, Ecosystems, and Hydrology XXVIII

title: Vineyard detection using Sentinel-2 time series and machine learning: a boundary-guided framework for multi-year vineyard mapping
abstract: Accurate, temporally consistent and geographically reliable mapping of vineyards at the block level using remote sensing remains challenging because of seasonal differences in grape varieties, management practices affecting canopy cover and field appearance, and spectral similarity between vineyards and other perennial vegetation. Detection of the vineyard boundaries is an important, but non-trivial task, and models trained for a single growing season or geographic region may have limited transferability. This study presents a boundary-guided framework for transferable vineyard mapping that combines multitemporal Sentinel-2 observations, Random Forest (RF) classification, and externally derived agricultural crop field boundaries (Fields of the World, FTW) to support block-level mapping under limited training data conditions. The experiment was conducted in the Barossa Valley, South Australia, using Sentinel-2 images (10, 20 and 60 m resolution) during the peak-flowering and harvest periods in 2022 and 2025. The RF model achieved an F1 score of 0.8496 in 2022. Direct temporal transfer to 2025 without target-year adaptation showed a significant reduction in performance with F1 score decreasing to 0.6182. Adding a limited set of data from 2025 substantially increased F1 score for 2025 to 0.8551. Additionally, when external field boundaries provide corresponding spatial constraints for scalability, the resulting RF+FTW approach achieved F1 score of 0.8146 and 0.7785 for the years of 2022 and 2025 respectively. The results demonstrated that limited target-year adaptation can substantially improve temporal transferability, while standardized external agricultural field boundaries could provide limited, but useful spatial constraints for scalable vineyard mapping. Further experiments with FTW generation parameters may improve boundary accuracy and, potentially, the performance of boundary-guided vineyard mapping.
journal: Remote Sensing for Agriculture, Ecosystems, and Hydrology XXVIII

title: Noncanonical enhancers control gene expression and cell fate in human pluripotent stem cells
abstract: Enhancers are key gene regulatory elements that ensure the precise spatiotemporal execution of developmental gene expression programs. However, recent findings indicate that current approaches to identify enhancers may not capture the full repertoire of active enhancers in mammalian genomes. Here, we combine massively parallel enhancer assays with chromatin structure and transcriptome profiling to functionally annotate enhancers genome-wide in human induced pluripotent stem cells. We find that a substantial fraction (∼40%) of accessible chromatin regions with enhancer function lack key features associated with active enhancers, including the active enhancer mark histone H3 lysine-27 acetylation and enhancer-associated RNAs. Perturbation of this class of noncanonical enhancers by CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing or deletion results in decreased levels of target gene expression and, in one instance, loss of pluripotent stem cell characteristics. Collectively, our data demonstrate enhancer activity for a class of gene regulatory elements that had, until now, only been associated with a neutral or inactive status, challenging current models of enhancer function.

title: Microscale patchiness controls resource acquisition in populations of foraging bacteria
abstract: Chemotaxis, the ability of cells to detect and respond to chemical gradients, allows them to acquire nutrients, seek hosts, or escape toxins. However, directly measuring bacterial foraging in spatially structured nutrient environments has proven elusive. We developed a new approach to investigate bacterial foraging, on timescales from milliseconds to hours, when exposed to nutrient fluctuations and microscale patchiness mimicking realistic ocean conditions. We generated dynamic, patchy, nutrient landscapes in a large microfluidic arena and simultaneously tracked individual cells of the marine bacterium Vibrio anguillarum . Analyzing single-cell nutrient exposure for tens of thousands of cells revealed that the nutrient exposure and distribution of exposure among bacteria depend strongly on the spatiotemporal characteristics of the patchy landscape. Furthermore, bacterial trajectories revealed a progressive decrease of swimming speed counter-balanced by an increase in chemotactic precision, resulting in stable nutrient exposure over time. This work furthers our understanding of bacterial foraging strategies under ecologically relevant conditions.
