title: CARMA report WP1: Catalogue of available carbon technologies and instruments for scenario building
abstract: Carbon sources are important to green fuels production as well as to CCUS strategies. CARMA takes a holistic approach to ensure cross-sectorial carbon balance for all carbon demanding sectors within the limits of sustainable use of sources integrated with PtX pathways. CARMA is a cross-mission project, which bridges between the Innomissions of Green Fuels, CCUS and AgriFoodTure by developing crosscutting society system analysis of the carbon balance across all sectors of agriculture, forestry, energy, transport, industry, buildings, waste management, and materials. CARMA has the following objectives: To further develop existing theoretical understanding on the concept of sustainable biomass To coordinate the use of novel solutions to negative emissions (carbon storage solutions) To develop crosscutting society system analysis methodologies, tools, and models allowing for an overarching holistic co-optimization of the carbon balance To use these models on the assessment and development of a sustainable co-optimized carbon management strategy for green fuels in the green transition of Denmark To create an understanding of sustainable biomass availability and of the holistic carbon balance of a net zero society on the global scale CARMA results: A cross-cutting and cross-Innomission understanding of the concept of sustainable biomass with GHG neutrality when applied with a holistic integration across the sectors of agriculture, forestry, energy, transport, industry, buildings, waste management, and materials. An assessment and development of a sustainable carbon management strategy for green fuels in the green transition of Denmark including the prioritization and synergy between photosynthetic carbon capture in agriculture and forestry, point source capture of CO2, and direct air capture of CO2. An understanding of sustainable biomass availability and of the holistic carbon balance of a net zero society on the global scale to understand the geographical dependency of the global competitiveness of green fuel production Nøgleresultater This project will contribute with the following results outlining the potential future development of sustainable use of biomass in the fully decarbonized society: Potential quantities of additional agricultural and forest biomass that can be produced sustainably within Denmark under different scenario conditions Optimized use of forest biomass, integrating temporal aspects of the allocation of carbon to the forest ecosystem, materials, energy products and permanent underground storage Which other policies and ecosystem services can be supported by a transition of Danish agriculture and forestry facilitated by an integration with the energy, material, and carbon markets Technology scenarios for the best utilisation of our biomass resources into various materials, energy products and carbon storage via cascade utilisation Perspectives for achieving a greening of Danish agriculture from conversion into a higher share of crop cover across the landscape and over time, with a utilisation of the new crops for biorefinin

title: The model of strengthening social capital for social protection of poor households in rural areas in optimizing food security
abstract: Purposes of the study are to describe the forms of social capital and the strategies for strengthening social capital for the social protection of poor rural households in optimizing food security. This study uses a qualitative method with a case study approach. The informant selection technique used purposive sampling. Data collection techniques using in-depth interviews, observation and document study. The forms of capital for the social protection of poor rural households in optimizing food security are mutual cooperation, trust, social networks, social norms and accessibility of social services. The strategies for strengthening social capital for the social protection of poor rural households in optimizing food security are increasing discipline in gardening, rice and secondary crops; increasing farmers' incentives according to the government purchasing price; improving the functionality of Food Security Council; create policies in the form of regional regulations concerning Regional Food Security and increasing the role of mothers in providing food intake to their children.
journal: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships

title: AI Smart Agriculture System
abstract: This paper presents an AI-based application that brings several common agricultural support tasks into one place. The system combines plant disease identification from images, crop prediction from soil and weather-related values, fertilizer suggestions, soil fertility assessment and a question-answering assistant. It is built with Python and Stream lit. A MobileNetV2-based convolutional neural network is used for plant-image classification, while a Random Forest model predicts suitable crops from nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, temperature, humidity, pH and rainfall values. Fertilizer and soil-fertility outputs are generated using predefined rules. An Ollama-powered assistant provides general responses to farming questions. The project report records approximate accuracies of85–90% for disease detection and 88–92% for crop prediction. These figures are presented as project-reported results and need further testing with varied field data. The application is intended to support farmers’ decisions, not replace expert advice or laboratory soil analysis
journal: International Journal of Science, Strategic Management and Technology

title: Crypto - currency Mining and Student Performance: Perspectives of Lecturers at Adamawa State College of Agriculture, Nigeria
abstract: The abstract of the study "Crypto-currency Mining and Student Performance: Perspectives of Lecturers at Adamawa State College of Agriculture, Nigeria" outlines a quantitative investigation conducted among lecturers from the Department of Computer Science at Adamawa State College of Agriculture, Ganye. It aims to explore how cryptocurrency mining impacts student performance, specifically focusing on student engagement, critical thinking skills, and attitudes toward financial innovation. Findings indicate that cryptocurrency mining activities enhance student engagement and critical thinking, fostering positive attitudes toward financial innovation. Despite benefits, challenges such as technical complexity and resource limitations were identified. Recommendations include improving educational resources and supporting faculty to effectively integrate cryptocurrency education into curricula, thereby preparing students for emerging technological fields. The study contributes to the discourse on digital currency education in higher education contexts
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory

title: Assessing Agricultural Land and Determining Crop Suitability for Optimum Yield using Machine Learning Approach
abstract: Machine Learning has developed rapidly and increasingly becoming significant in agricultural domain as there is need of efficient logical practice for detecting new and valuable information in agricultural domain. Agriculture serves as the primary economic driver and major employment provider for the majority of the population in Nigeria. However, the sector is vulnerable to challenges stemming from inadequate agronomic practices. This study built an Agricultural land assessment model that predict optimum yield using logistic regression model and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers using Python and VScode. Comparing Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classifying crops based on their nutrient content and yield, both algorithms exhibit high overall accuracy of around 87%. However, SVM stands out due to its consistently high precision, recall, and F1-scores across various crops. This indicates that SVM provides a more balanced and robust performance, vital for accurate agricultural predictions. The study also introduces a novel application of machine learning techniques to the field of agriculture and bridges the gap between traditional agricultural practices and modern data analytics, fostering innovation and improving agricultural efficiency and sustainability. The study can further enhance its impact on agricultural productivity and sustainability by Incorporate Internet of Things (IoT) devices to collect real-time data on soil moisture, temperature, and other environmental factors, promote improving the accuracy of crop suitability predictions. Also to extend the model to include a wider variety of crops and explore its applicability to different climatic and geographical regions, ensuring broader relevance and utility

title: Knowledge Discovery Model for Predicting Optimal Climatic Conditions for Maize Crop Productivity
abstract: This research presents an integrated approach to forecasting the impact of climate on maize output in Nigeria, emphasizing the critical role of predictive modeling and data mining techniques. The study acknowledges the profound influence of climate conditions, particularly temperature, rainfall, soil moisture and humidity, on maize development and yield in agriculture. By examining historical climatic data and its correlation with agricultural outcomes, the research aims to develop a predictive model, the "Maize Yield Predictive Model," tailored to Nigeria's agricultural landscape. Leveraging data mining techniques, such as Linear Regression, Decision Trees, Support Vector Machine and K-Nearest Neighbor, the study analyzes meteorological data collected over a Five-year period to predict future climatic conditions and their effects on Maize output. Through meticulous data preprocessing and experimentation with classification algorithms, the optimal predictive model is identified, facilitating strategic planning and decisionmaking for farmers. The significance of the research lies in its potential to enhance agricultural productivity, profitability, and resilience in the face of climate variability, thereby contributing to the socioeconomic development of Nigeria. From the result of the study: Based on the given metrics, KNN (K-Nearest Neighbors) is the best algorithm for this task due to its lowest RMSPE and high CC, indicating good prediction accuracy despite its longer training time withTime: 0.19 (highest), CC: 0.8604 (second highest), RMSPE: 0.0687 (lowest). Additionally, the study adds to the body of literature on the application of data mining techniques in predicting climate effects on agriculture and on maize yield, paving the way for further empirical research in this domain. Despite its scope limitations, focusing on selected cereal crop and sub-variables, the study provides valuable insights into the intersection of climate science, data analytics, and agricultural sustainability. It is recommended from the study that further research should center on enhancing selected classification techniques to boost the efficiency of predictive models by maximizing the utilization of all available options (parameters) for each classifier.
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory

title: Trend Analysis of Financial Intermediation Nexus: Catalyst for Sustainable Development in Nigeria
abstract: This study examined trend analysis of financial intermediation nexus: Catalyst for sustainable development in Nigeria from 1990 to 2025. Time series data were collected from secondary sources such as Central Bank of Nigeria statistical bulletin to proxy bank intermediation nexus: bank customer deposit, credit allocation, private sector credit, credit to core private sector, loan to deposit ratio, credit to agricultural sector and credit to manufacturing sector. The study found that movement in financial intermediation variables are in line with fluctuation in monetary policy variables. The study employed descriptive research analysis to explain the relationship between financial intermediation variables. The study concludes that monetary policy variables determine the fluctuation in financial intermediation variables within the periods under review. The study concludes that monetary and macroeconomic policies determine fluctuation of financial intermediation variables within the time scope of this study. The implication is that financial intermediation nexus can serve as a catalyst for sustainable development when savings and credit are channeled towards productive enterprises infrastructure, agriculture, renewable energy. Health, and other activities that generate employment reduce poverty and strength sustainable development. The study recommends strengthening financial inclusion, expanding productive sector lending, and deepening digital finance
journal: JOURNAL OF ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT

title: A Deep Feature–Based Dynamic Hand Gesture Recognition Framework for Word and Sentence Formation Using Mediapipe
abstract: Individuals who are deaf or experience difficulties with hearing and speech predominantly rely on sign language as their medium to communicate, which is not universally comprehended leading to obstacles in achieving effective communication. Advances in deep learning technologies in recent years have enabled the development of systems intended to autonomously interpret gestures in sign language and translate them into spoken language. This paper introduces a system built on deep learning methodologies for recognizing sign language. It uses long short-term memory (LSTM) architecture to distinguish and classify hand gestures which are static and dynamic. The system is divided into three primary components, including dataset collection, neural network assessment, and sign detection component that encompasses hand gesture extraction and sign language classification. The project was divided into two major phases: Static Sign Recognition and Dynamic Sign Recognition. During the static phase, a fully original dataset comprising 120,000 images was created for 24 alphabets (A–Z excluding J and Z). Each image was then treated through two custom-designed filters: silhouette extraction and finger detection, carried out using MediaPipe for precise annotation and cropping on its own. The training of the static model happened with custom-designed CNN applied on the data to achieve accuracies of 94% (finger detection), 89% (silhouette), and 91% (combined). In the dynamic phase, signs with movement were captured using MediaPipe landmarks and registered as NumPy arrays (CSV and .NPY) files. Hand and facial keypoints were stored at every frame for temporal learning. This phase included one-hand, two-hand, and hand-with-face categories. The whole system achieved 15–20 FPS real-time inference on CPU alone. While the static signs and single-handed dynamic signs were performing very well, the accuracy of complex two-handed and face-assisted gestures suffered due to scarcity and noise in the data. The results provide a very good baseline to improve upon for the future using deep temporal networks like LSTM or 3D CNNs.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Decision Support Systems for Enhancing Sustainable Crop Productivity
abstract: Climate variability, pressure on available resources and increasing demands on food further erode efficacious agricultural systems that require intelligent and adaptive decision-making systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an offering with potential to complement all types of information to integrate into actionable insights (data-driven agricultural management). In this research, empirical research and analytical modeling are applied to discuss the importance of AI-driven decision support systems (DSS) in enhancing the sustainable crop productivity. The study utilizes multi-season field observations, agro- meteorolog data, soil health metrics, remote sensing data, and management records of farmers in the variety of agro-climatic regions. The machine learning models were used to assist with the key farming decisions in terms of forecasting yields, when to irrigate, identifying pests and diseases, and optimization of nutrients. The traditional standard statistical measures of accuracy were to determine model performance, whereas the sustainability performance was measured in terms of the stability of yields, water-use efficiency, and input optimization measures. The findings indicate that AI-powered DSS are associated with a high level of accuracy in decision-making in comparison to traditional methods of advisory, which results in better performance of crops, less wastage of resources, and environmental stress reduction. The results also indicate that the situational calibration, the trustworthiness of the data and the participation of farmers are significant parameters determining whether the systems will work or not. This work can add to the existing literature on AI-based decision frameworks and on the agronomic and sustainability advantages of AI-supported frameworks by empirically showing these benefits. The study highlights the future of AI-based DSS as a strategic mechanism of promoting resilient, resource-efficient, and sustainable agricultural production systems.

title: Explainable Vision Transformers for Early Crop Disease Localization in Smart Farming
abstract: Early detection and localization of crop diseases are critical for improving agricultural productivity and ensuring foodsecurity. This study introduces a novel Centroid Entropy Localization Explainable Vision Transformer (CEL-EViT)framework designed for accurate and interpretable identification of plant diseases in smart farming applications. The proposed approach integrates the classification capabilities of Vision Transformers (ViTs) with a Centroid Entropy Localization (CEL) module, which highlights disease-affected regions, providing explainable visual insights alongside predictions. The model divides input leaf images into patches, extracts deep feature representations, and employs attention-based mechanisms to capture subtle disease patterns. The CEL module computes entropy-weighted centroids to precisely localize diseased areas, enabling both high accuracy and interpretability. Experiments conducted on multiple crops—including tomato, mango, papaya, and maize—demonstrate that CEL-EViT significantly outperforms baseline models such as CNN, ResNet50, and hybrid ViT-CNN. The proposed model achieves an average classification accuracy of 96.6%, Intersection over Union (IoU) of 87.9%, and explainability score of 87.1%, along with high localization consistency and minimal centroid distance errors. These results confirm that CEL-EViT effectively identifies early disease symptoms while providing reliable visual explanations for the affected regions. The framework offers a scalable and practical solution for deployment in real-time precision agriculture systems, including drones and edge devices, facilitating timely interventions, reducing crop losses, and supporting sustainable farming practices. Overall, the proposed method demonstrates the potential of combining deep learning and explainable attention mechanisms for robust, interpretable, and early crop disease management.

title: BEYOND SUBSIDY VOLUME: INSTITUTIONAL QUALITY AS THE TRANSMISSION INFRASTRUCTURE OF SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL TRANSFORMATION. A CRITICAL MECHANISTIC REVIEW
abstract: Public agricultural support is often evaluated by expenditure, coverage, or average treatment effects, yet similar instruments generate sharply different productivity, welfare, and environmental outcomes across agricultural systems. This critical mechanistic review asks where that divergence is produced. Synthesizing recent peer-reviewed empirical studies, meta-analyses, systematic reviews, and comparative policy research, we conceptualize institutional quality as the transmission infrastructure linking policy design to targeting, delivery, complementary services, farmer response, and multidimensional outcomes. Five mechanisms recur across settings: administrative capability and accountability; land and property institutions; market and financial coordination; knowledge, extension, and digital systems; and collective organizations. Evidence from input-support programmes in sub-Saharan Africa, the European Union’s agricultural support architecture, and emerging-economy reforms shows that institutions do not merely add to subsidy effects; they alter targeting, additionality, investment horizons, technology uptake, market participation, and environmental leakage. The synthesis also rejects a simple ‘strong institutions equal good outcomes’ interpretation: capable administrations can efficiently implement incentives that remain environmentally misaligned, while land formalization, credit, or digital tools can underperform when complementary constraints bind. We propose a policy-transmission framework with observable failure signatures for diagnosing where support loses effectiveness and identify mechanism-specific priorities for future causal research.

title: Digitalization of Recruitment in Nigerian Public Establishments: Difficulties and Potentials at the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security
abstract: Background: Digitalization has greatly transformed HRM all over the world, especially in the field of recruitment. However, Nigerian Public Institutions still experience difficulties in the adoption and implementation of digital recruitment systems. Objective: This study explored the challenges and opportunities of digitalization in the recruitment process in the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, Nigeria. Method: A quantitative case study was used, and data were collected from 30 human resource managers, information technology officers, and recruitment staff using a structured questionnaire given via Google Forms. The questionnaire included technical challenges, human factors, organizational factors, perceived potentials, and digital recruitment effectiveness measured on a 5-point Likert scale. Results: Descriptive results revealed moderate technical, human, and organizational challenges, while perceived potentials of digital recruitment showed higher mean scores ranging from 4.10 to 4.32, particularly for efficiency, transparency, and access to talent. Technical challenges (r = ?0.42) and human factors (r = ?0.35) were negatively correlated with digital recruitment effectiveness, whereas perceived potentials showed the strongest positive relationship (r = 0.85). Regression analysis revealed that perceived potentials had a significant positive effect (? = 0.78, p < 0.001), while technical challenges had a significant negative effect (? = ?0.35, p = 0.007). Conclusion: The findings highlight the need to improve technical infrastructure and strengthen the potential benefits of digital recruitment to facilitate more effective recruitment practices in Nigerian public institutions.
journal: Journal of Law and Social Politics

title: Antibody design across observed and forecasted antigenic evolution
abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of antibodies is often limited by the evolution of their targets. Designing or eliciting antibodies that withstand such evolution is challenging as their binding interfaces must accommodate antigenic variation. Here, we introduce Germinal Multi, a computational framework for de novo antibody design and rescue that jointly optimizes a single paratope against multiple antigenic variants. We applied Germinal Multi to cancer and viral antigens, targeting both observed antigenic variation and prospective antibody escape. Multi-target optimization yielded antibodies that bound resistance-associated EGFR variants or that neutralized antigenically distinct historical SARS-CoV-2 variants, with recognition extending to variants withheld from the design process. Beyond acting on observed evolution, we redesigned the broadly neutralizing antibody BD55-1205 to restore neutralization of a prospective escape variant engineered with guidance from an evolutionary forecasting model, while preserving activity against the parental variant. Successful candidates were identified after screening tens of designs per campaign. Together, these results establish multi-target computational design as a strategy for generating antibody breadth across observed antigenic variation and demonstrate the potential of evolutionary forecasting to guide antibody redesign against prospective escape.

title: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy
abstract: Importance: Leg dystonia affects 50-80% of children with cerebral palsy (CP), but severity assessment remains subjective and time-consuming. Objective tools are urgently needed to quantify leg dystonia severity in clinical care and clinical trials. Objective: To develop and validate a deep neural network (DxToniaNet) for leg dystonia severity estimation using 2D clinical video recordings. Design, Setting, and Participants: We retrospectively analyzed video recordings of 298 children with cerebral palsy undergoing a seated hand open-close task as part of routine clinical care (Center 1: 193 videos, 720p/30fps; Center 2: 105 videos, 4K/60fps). Videos were rated for leg dystonia severity by a group of 7 experts using the Global Dystonia Rating Scale (GDRS) leg subscore (range 0-40) which has a minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 4 points. Videos displaying leg dystonia (median expert GDRS score [≥]1) were used to develop and test a machine learning model (DxToniaNet) for estimating leg dystonia severity. Open-source software (OpenPose) estimated bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates, normalized for height and camera positioning, and 69 variance and amplitude features were calculated based on established expert-cited features of leg dystonia. A neural network, DxToniaNet, was developed, trained and validated using 5-fold cross-validation on Center 1 videos before final testing on independent Center 2 videos. Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s): Mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and accuracy in differentiating between videos with clinically meaningful differences in GDRS scores were calculated relative to experts' median GDRS scores. Results: When estimating experts' leg GDRS scores in testing data, the proposed machine learning (ML) model yielded a MAE of 1.71 {+/-} 1.68 and RMSE of 2.21 {+/-} 0.34 (significantly less than the GDRS MCID of 4), and 90-94% accuracy in differentiating between videos with greater than a 4-point difference in the GDRS. Conclusions and Relevance: We have demonstrated that DxToniaNet can accurately estimate leg dystonia severity compared to experts' assessments with a small (clinically insignificant) error margin. Our methodology supports generalizability since DxToniaNet was developed and tested using independent videos datasets from different centers, recorded under different conditions. In the future, DxToniaNet may help facilitate standardized leg dystonia severity estimation in clinical care and clinical trials.

title: Enrollees and Early Lessons from an Agentic Healthcare Platform with Physicians in the Loop
abstract: Agentic healthcare platforms that combine large language models with physician oversight are growing quickly, but little is known about who uses them. We characterized 3,223 enrollees of Lotus AI, a free, physician-supervised agentic platform, who completed onboarding, messaged the agent, and had a linked health record between February and July 2026, and compared them with national benchmarks. Median age was 51 years and 62% were male. Chronic condition prevalence exceeded 2024 National Health Interview Survey estimates in every age band by 4 to 7 percentage points; 18% had a functional or symptom-defined disorder; among the 30% with four or more ambulatory visits in the prior year, care was spread across nearly five providers, with 44% meeting a threshold for high fragmentation. Users with functional disorders generated 1.8 times as many physician escalations and 2.6 times as many laboratory orders as other users, but no more prescriptions. This profile differs from the younger, predominantly female populations reported for direct-to-consumer telemedicine. It moves chronic disease management, functional disorder pathways, and care coordination from aspirations to design requirements, and we argue that deployed AI care platforms should characterize their populations against national benchmarks early.

title: Regional Signals Matter: Rethinking Global Pooling for mRNA Foundation Models
abstract: RNA foundation models with diverse architectures have shown promise for learning representations of messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences. However, existing benchmarks commonly reduce token-level embeddings to transcript-level representations through global mean pooling before fitting a downstream probe. This aggregation does not explicitly preserve the identities of biologically distinct mRNA regions. Consequently, signals associated with short regulatory regions may be diluted, confounding assessments of representation quality with the information preserved by the readout. We introduce an architecture-agnostic, region-aware readout that separately averages embeddings within the 5$'$ untranslated region (UTR), coding sequence, and 3$'$ UTR and concatenates the resulting representations for linear probing. We reproduce mRNABench evaluations for 20 frozen models from 18 families, with a median absolute score difference of 0.0009 across 380 model--dataset--target evaluations published for 19 models, and construct a region-aware benchmark using the same models, tasks, and splits. Relative to global mean pooling, region-aware pooling increases Pearson correlation, averaged across the 20 models, by 11--25\% on translation and stability tasks, with no statistically significant decreases detected for any model on the regression tasks. On classification tasks, relative changes in the area under the precision--recall curve range from $-3\%$ to $+11\%$. Boundary randomization and displacement generally reduce performance, while dimensionality-matched and sequence-composition controls indicate that the gains are not explained solely by increased feature dimensionality, region length, or guanine--cytosine (GC) content. Learned attention pooling approaches region-aware performance only when supplied with one query per region. In silico perturbations reveal stronger sensitivity to upstream AUGs (uAUGs) and their Kozak context, while analyses of endogenous transcripts show approximately threefold greater recovery of length- and GC-adjusted uAUG-associated differences than global-mean probes. Both readouts capture codon optimality. Model rankings averaged over the regression tasks remain largely stable, while within a task models move by several places. Our region-aware benchmark therefore provides a biologically structured and complementary evaluation of mRNA foundation models, revealing regulatory information that is less accessible to linear probes after global mean pooling. The code is available at \url{https://github.com/Sanford-Labs/rnaregionpooling

title: Применение искусственного интеллекта для прогнозирования урожайности кормовых культур и решения проблем кормообеспечения в животноводстве
abstract: An economic model of a web platform for forecasting forage crop yields is proposed. The forecast is linked to herd requirements, the dry matter balance and purchasing costs. Using a hypothetical example, an annual effect of 1.50 million tenge and the break-even point of the service were determined; the consequences of forecast errors were examined. The calculation serves as a basis for subsequent verification using farm data.

title: Qişloq xöjaligini yaşil iqtisodiyot asosida barqaror rivojlantirişda innovatsion yeçimlari
abstract: This scientific paper comprehensively examines the theoretical, methodological and practical aspects of the sustainable development of the agricultural sector based on the tenets and principles of the green economy. In the current period, when global climate change, water scarcity, soil degradation and environmental problems are intensifying, the mechanisms of greening the agricultural sector, introducing resource-saving digital and biological technologies, using renewable energy sources and attracting “green investments” are analyzed. In addition, the reforms being implemented in agriculture within the framework of the Strategy for the Transition to a Green Economy until 2030 in the Republic of Uzbekistan and their economic and environmental efficiency are scientifically substantiated.

title: Стратегическая модернизация аграрного сектора Узбекистана: механизация, финансы и цифровые технологии
abstract: The document examines the comprehensive development of the agricultural sector as the foundation of food security, economic independence and competitiveness of the state. Successful examples of the Netherlands, New Zealand and Brazil are given. For Uzbekistan, the key growth points are described: diversification of sown areas, deep processing, water-saving technologies, greenhouse farms, export logistics, certification and digitalization. The turning point of the reforms since 2017 is noted: liberalization, abolition of the state order and development of clusters. Particular attention is paid to the mechanization of agriculture: the current level of mechanization (81% overall, 52% in cotton harvesting), plans to purchase machinery (800 cotton harvesters and 6000 units of other machinery in 2026), and leasing on preferential terms (up to 10 years, 18% per annum with 8% compensated from the budget). Tasks are set to increase the production of domestic machinery 5-fold and to raise localization to 30–65% by 2028. Financial support measures are considered: subsidizing 15% of the cost of machinery (660 billion soums), lending through Agrobank (growth from 1.6 to 3.9 trillion soums in 2026), automation of loan issuance (from three days to three hours), and the creation of agro-service zones with agricultural agents. Pilot projects using artificial intelligence in livestock farming, horticulture and water management are noted, as well as the creation of a venture company with a capital of 100 billion soums to finance startups.
journal: Partner conferences of the International Scientific Journal Research Focus

title: Suv va yer resurslaridan samarali foydalaniş va iqlimga moslaşiş
abstract: This paper analyzes the economic, environmental, and social aspects of the sustainable development of agriculture. Under conditions of water scarcity, declining soil fertility, climate change, and rising production costs, the introduction of resource-saving technologies, crop diversification, digital monitoring, and the improvement of farmers’ knowledge are substantiated as important directions. Practical recommendations that can be implemented in the conditions of Uzbekistan, including the Republic of Karakalpakstan, are provided.
journal: Partner conferences of the International Scientific Journal Research Focus

title: Agrar sektorda raqamli texnologiyalar va innovatsiyalarni joriy etiş imkoniyatlari
abstract: This scientific thesis comprehensively examines the theoretical and practical opportunities, organizational and economic mechanisms, and economic efficiency of introducing digital technologies and modern innovative solutions in the agricultural sector. The study analyzes the mechanisms for introducing smart agriculture, the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), big data and drone technologies into the agricultural sector. In addition, scientifically substantiated proposals and practical recommendations have been developed for automating agricultural production processes, increasing resource saving and ensuring food security under the conditions of climate change.
journal: Partner conferences of the International Scientific Journal Research Focus

title: JAX-WAVE: A Differentiable Physics-Supervised Framework for Inverse Wave Design in Heterogeneous Media
abstract: Designing a prescribed wave field in a heterogeneous medium requires an initial pressure distribution that compensates for the medium's propagation response. Repeated numerical inversion solves this task afresh for each target and environment. We introduce JAX-WAVE for amortized inverse wave design: a shared neural network maps desired terminal fields and known wave-speed maps directly to bounded initial pressures. Training through a differentiable finite-difference time-domain solver uses the physical design objective without requiring optimized control labels. Linear propagation and symmetric pressure bounds imply an exact sign-reversal relation for the regularized optimum. A shared-weight projection enforces this relation, preserves feasibility, and satisfies an exact identity for the paired-sign objective. We characterize the discrete propagator and its weighted adjoint to connect learning, numerical inversion, and optimality assessment. On an independent confirmation set, three trained models achieve unseen-material errors of 25.24% for geometric targets and 4.77% for reachable targets. Matched-capacity comparisons show improved reconstruction with the sign parameterization. Within a 5 ms median online budget, the learned map reduces mean error by 45% relative to accelerated numerical inversion on the heterogeneous benchmark; longer numerical solves recover greater accuracy. The results establish a reusable inverse-design procedure and show how its accuracy and computational value depend on target structure and query workload.

title: AN ANALYSIS OF METHODS FOR DEVELOPING THE FOOD MARKET AND IMPROVING ITS EFFICIENCY IN UZBEKISTAN
abstract: This article analyses the development of Uzbekistan’s food market in 2020–2025 on the basis of official statistical data. Five priority methods of market management are compared through a multi-criteria expert assessment: market intervention from state reserves, tariff regulation, exchange and wholesale-logistics infrastructure, clusters and vertical integration, and digital monitoring. The analysis shows that agricultural output grew from 261.9 trillion soums in 2020 to 538.9 trillion soums in 2025, that fruit and vegetable exports reached USD 2.1 billion, and that food price growth slowed to 5.4%. According to the assessment, methods based on infrastructure and integration perform best in terms of long-term effectiveness, whereas intervention methods perform best in terms of rapid price stabilisation. Proposals for applying the methods in combination are developed.
journal: Zamonaviy dunyoda ijtimoiy fanlar, Vol. 5, No. 33 (2026)

title: Association of intensity-based walking steps and incident falls: a population-based cohort study.
abstract: Background Falls are the leading cause of morbidity and mortality, yet they are largely preventable. While walking has well-established health benefits, its role in falls remains unclear. We aimed to examine the association between walking and fall risk. Methods Walking steps were defined as purposeful walking steps (≥40 steps/min) and incidental walking steps (<40 steps/min), differentiated by walking intensity. We estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for incident falls using Cox proportional hazards models across the four walking step categories. Risk ratios (RRs) for the number of falls were estimated using Poisson regression. We also estimated the association between walking steps and the risk of incident hip fracture as the secondary outcome. Results We included 94,422 participants aged 42-78 years from the UK Biobank, with a median follow-up of 6.87 years. We adjusted multivariable models for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates. Compared with the lowest purposeful waking group (≤3999 steps/day), the second (HR = 0.75; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.60, 0.92), third (HR = 0.65; 95% CI = 0.52, 0.82), and fourth (HR = 0.68; 95% CI = 0.54, 0.86) group had lower risks of incident falls. Also, the RRs for the second (RR = 0.78; 95% CI = 0.68, 0.90), third (RR = 0.74; 95% CI = 0.64, 0.85), and fourth (RR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.62, 0.84) group showed similar results. We also observed an inverse association between purposeful walking steps and hip fracture risk, while incidental walking steps showed no significant association. Conclusions Higher purposeful walking steps were associated with a lower risk of incident falls, number of falls, and incident hip fracture, although residual confounding cannot be ruled out in this observational study. These findings may help inform future step-based recommendations for fall prevention.

title: From the Return of Water to Composite Risk: Hazards, Damage and Vulnerability in the Southern Korama Valley (Zinder, Niger)
abstract: Background: The southern Korama Valley of Niger is an endorheic basin where the accumulation and persistence of surface water in interdunal depressions create challenges for rural communities. The interaction of groundwater rise, prolonged flooding and seasonal salt concentration poses potential risks to agricultural production, household infrastructure, vegetation and local livelihoods. Understanding these interconnected hazards is essential for assessing the spatial distribution of damage and socio-economic vulnerability in the affected communes. Aims: To show that the return of rainfall in the endorheic southern Korama valley produces a composite risk of linked climate, hydrological and hydrochemical hazards acting on vulnerable households. Study Design: Mixed-methods case study combining climate series, remote sensing, groundwater records, in situ water measurements, a household survey and focus groups. Place and Duration of Study: Rural communes of Kwaya, Bandé and Dungass, Zinder Region, Niger; fieldwork from September 2024 to April 2026. Methodology: We analysed rainfall (1950-2024) and temperature (1994-2024) records at Magaria using the Mann-Kendall, Sen and Pettitt tests; Landsat classifications (1975-2025); a Sentinel-1/2 inventory of cuvettes (2020-2025); groundwater records from 23 piezometers (2014-2023); electrical conductivity (EC) and pH measurements at 20 cuvettes in January and April 2026, summarised using a salinisation risk index mapped for each cuvette; a survey of 293 households; and a count of 504 woody plants. A socio-economic vulnerability index (SVI) was computed by commune. Results: Annual rainfall showed no significant trend (P = .65), but six of the seven seasons from 2018 to 2024 were in surplus and minimum temperature rose by 0.63 °C per decade (P < .001). Water surfaces rose from 847 ha (2000) to 5,223 ha (2025). The water table was less than 2.6 m deep at 8 of 12 piezometers and rose at 4. Mean EC doubled between January and April (from 2.2 to 4.4 dS/m) and exceeded 5 dS/m in seven cuvettes, all in Bandé, while groundwater EC stayed at 0.12 dS/m. Overall, 95% of households reported at least one building collapse, 97% reported crop losses, and 15.5% had sold a field; 45% of woody plants were dead. Dungass had the highest SVI (0.61). Conclusion: The risk works as a chain from rainfall to land loss. It is mainly perceived in Kwaya, contrasted and dynamic in Bandé and moderate in Dungass, calling for groundwater and water-quality monitoring and household-level measures.
journal: International Journal of Environment and Climate Change

title: Calibration and Validation of the CERES-Wheat Crop Simulation Model for Phenology, Leaf Area Dynamics and Yield of Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) under Varying Sowing Dates, Irrigation Schedules and Nitrogen Levels in a Subtropical Agro-Ecosystem of the Vin
abstract: Aims: To calibrate and validate the CERES-Wheat model of the Decision Support System for Agrotechnology Transfer (DSSAT v4.7) to simulate phenology, leaf area index (LAI), grain yield and biological yield of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) cultivar HD 2967 under varying sowing dates, irrigation schedules and nitrogen levels. Study Design: Split-plot field experiment with three replications and 18 treatment combinations of sowing date (main plot), irrigation and nitrogen. Place and Duration of Study: Crop Research Farm, Sam Higginbottom University of Agriculture, Technology and Sciences, Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, India, during the rabi (winter) seasons of 2019–20 and 2020–21. Methodology: Wheat was sown on 20 November and 20 December, with two, three or four irrigations and nitrogen rates of 80, 120 or 160 kg N ha⁻¹. Genetic coefficients were calibrated using 2019–20 data and validated against data from an independent season (2020–21) using mean bias error (MBE), root mean square error (RMSE), normalised RMSE (nRMSE), and Willmott’s index of agreement (d-stat). Results: Anthesis and maturity were simulated with nRMSE below 6% in both seasons, although maturity was predicted 3.5–7.5 days early in the warmer 2020–21 season. Grain yield was simulated with acceptable accuracy in calibration (nRMSE 1.9–20.4%) but less accurately in validation (6.7–27.6%), when it was overpredicted under timely sowing. The model underestimated biological yield in both seasons (nRMSE 6.7–31.0% and 14.2–28.6% in calibration and validation, respectively), and harvest index was overestimated. Maximum LAI was underestimated in calibration (nRMSE 21.2–40.8%) but was simulated accurately in validation (11.1–14.0%). Conclusion: The calibrated genetic coefficients captured the phenology and grain-yield levels of HD 2967 reasonably well, but the underestimation of biomass and canopy growth and the early maturity in the warmer season show that they need refinement with multi-season data before the model is used for management optimisation or yield forecasting in the Vindhyan zone.
journal: International Journal of Environment and Climate Change

title: Transforming Rural Youth Learning through AI-Driven Agricultural Extension: A Conceptual Framework and Proposed Evaluation Protocol
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a means of supporting rural youth in accessing agricultural knowledge, public services, education, and livelihood opportunities. However, access to a smartphone or internet connection does not necessarily provide the ability to locate reliable information, evaluate digital advice, communicate safely, or use online services independently. This paper develops a design-oriented conceptual framework for integrating AI-supported learning into agricultural extension to strengthen these practical digital competencies among rural youth. The framework combines baseline task-based assessment, adaptive learning recommendations, local-language microlearning, agricultural task-based exercises, peer support, and human facilitation by extension workers. The manuscript is conceptual and protocol-oriented; no primary dataset was supplied, no field intervention was conducted, and no empirical outcomes are claimed. The framework is informed by literature on digital competence, digital agricultural extension, and AI adoption in extension services. It also specifies a proposed mixed-method evaluation protocol involving baseline and post-intervention tasks, follow-up assessment, learner interviews, and subgroup analysis where feasible. The paper outlines implementation components, measurable indicators, ethical safeguards, and priorities for future field validation. It argues that AI may help personalise and extend agricultural learning, but equitable and trustworthy implementation requires local-language design, accessible infrastructure, human verification, privacy protection, and continued face-to-face support.
journal: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

title: Designed phenotyping for genomic selection.
abstract: Genomic selection (GS) is increasingly used in plant breeding to predict genetic merit using genome-wide molecular markers. While advances in high-throughput genotyping and statistical modeling, including machine learning, have made GS operational across many crop species, realized prediction accuracy continues to vary substantially among traits, environments, and breeding programs. Much of the GS literature has focused on markers and models, whereas comparatively less attention has been devoted to the design of the phenotyping systems that generate the information required for model training. In this perspective, we argue that GS is built on an information-generation system in which breeding and phenotyping generate information, whereas genotyping and modeling capture, utilize, and propagate that information. We propose the concept of designed phenotyping, in which genomic prediction accuracy is constrained by two complementary factors: phenotypic information quality and information transferability. Multi-environment trial design primarily determines phenotypic information quality through its effects on entry-mean heritability, whereas training population design influences both information quality and transferability through its effects on genetic variability, connectivity, relatedness, and relevance. Together, these factors define the practical upper limit of genomic prediction accuracy. We further argue that phenotyping for GS should not be viewed as a one-time activity but as a continuous investment in the information-generation system underlying future genetic gain. Consequently, designed phenotyping represents a strategic framework for integrating trial design and training population design to sustain long-term breeding progress.

title: Does investment in digital infrastructure increase incomes in rural regions? Evidence from the Broadband China pilot
Phosphogypsum as a soil amendment: mechanisms, applications, and environmental risks
abstract: Phosphogypsum (PG) is a calcium sulfate-rich by-product of phosphoric acid production. Agricultural reuse can recover calcium and sulfur and improve soils constrained by sodicity, subsoil acidity, or nutrient deficiency. This review examines PG characteristics, soil interactions, agronomic responses, and environmental risks. Structured literature screening, evidence classification, bibliometric analysis, and critical narrative synthesis were combined. Phosphogypsum supplies Ca2+ for sodium displacement and clay flocculation in saline-sodic soils and can improve subsoil calcium availability and reduce aluminum toxicity in acid soils. Responses depend on material composition, soil properties, application rate, water management, climate, and crop requirements. Evidence for greenhouse gas mitigation is concentrated in flooded rice systems, with limited validation in upland agriculture. Residual acidity, soluble salts, fluorine, potentially toxic elements, and naturally occurring radionuclides require assessment through contaminant speciation, leachability, cumulative loading, crop uptake, and exposure pathways. Inconsistent material characterization, short experimental durations, and limited long-term field, regulatory, and economic assessments constrain the transfer of published results to practice. Agricultural use requires source-specific quality control, rates matched to soil requirements and environmental limits, long-term monitoring, and economic comparison with conventional amendments and other PG management options.

title: Dominant core bacterial taxa show stronger associations with rhizosphere soil multifunctionality than core rare taxa in Pinus tabuliformis planted forests along a Loess Plateau aridity gradient
abstract: Drought intensification threatens ecosystem functioning of Pinus tabuliformis planted forests on the Loess Plateau. Soil multifunctionality integrates key processes, including nutrient cycling, organic matter transformation, and enzyme activities, thereby supporting planted forests ecosystem functions. Rhizosphere core microorganisms regulate these processes and influence soil multifunctionality. However, core microbial communities are not homogeneous, and how abundance-based ecological differentiation affects their drought responses and contributions to soil multifunctionality remains unclear. Along a natural aridity gradient, rhizosphere soils were collected from mature P. tabuliformis planted forests across three regions of the Loess Plateau. Core bacterial taxa were classified into dominant core and core rare taxa based on 16S rRNA sequencing, prevalence, and relative abundance. We evaluated their ecological differentiation in terms of diversity, niche breadth, drought responses, co-occurrence network topology, and associations with soil multifunctionality. Dominant core and core rare taxa exhibited contrasting community characteristics and drought response patterns. Dominant core taxa showed higher α-diversity, broader niche breadth, and lower compositional variation, whereas core rare taxa displayed higher β-diversity and stronger species turnover. With increasing aridity (decreasing aridity index), diversity increased in both groups, but core rare taxa diversity was more strongly associated with the aridity gradient (R2 = 0.81, P 0.5) and high explanatory power (R2 > 0.6), suggesting a higher prevalence of aridity responses among core rare taxa and stronger abundance-based responses in dominant core taxa. Co-occurrence network analyses revealed distinct topological roles for the two groups. Dominant core taxa formed the main network framework because of their higher abundance and node representation, whereas core rare taxa included a higher proportion of keystone nodes involved in network organization. Dominant core networks exhibited higher global connectivity, while core rare networks showed stronger local clustering and modularity. With increasing aridity, dominant core network complexity decreased significantly (P 0.05). More importantly, dominant core-associated traits independently explained 33.4% of the variation in soil multifunctionality, exceeding the contribution of core rare taxa (6.3%), with network complexity exhibiting the highest relative importance (32.54%). Piecewise structural equation modeling further indicated that dominant core network complexity potentially links aridity variation to soil multifunctionality. Overall, this study reveals abundance-based ecological differentiation within the core microbiome and provides new insights into microbial contributions to ecosystem functioning under increasing aridity.

title: Deep learning for learning outcome prediction and evaluation in Wushu physical education
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: The teaching quality assessment of college Wushu (martial arts) courses has traditionally relied on instructor-based evaluation and individual skill-test indicators, making it difficult to comprehensively characterize students’ learning outcomes across multiple dimensions such as skill, physical fitness, theoretical knowledge, and classroom behavior, and equally difficult to provide early warning for students with lagging learning outcomes. To address this, this paper proposes a multi-branch deep learning framework for quantitative physical education data, MartialSense-Net, which simultaneously performs classification prediction of students’ learning performance levels and regression prediction of their overall performance scores. The framework first partitions the original heterogeneous quantitative features – physical fitness, skill, theory, and classroom behavior – into four semantic branches, and learns low-dimensional representations for each branch independently through a Multi-Branch Feature Extraction (MBFE) module; it then introduces a Cross Feature Attention Fusion (CFAF) module, which models the interactions among the different branches based on a multi-head self-attention mechanism; finally, a multilayer perceptron encoder and multi-task prediction heads are used to output the classification and regression results. The framework is evaluated as a proof of concept on a publicly available general physical education performance benchmark containing 500 student records and 20 original attributes, from which 16 original predictor variables are selected. Because this dataset contains no Wushu-specific measures of routine precision, force expression, rhythm, or posture, the present experiment evaluates the modeling architecture and does not constitute external validation in authentic Wushu courses. The study systematically compares the framework with random forest, XGBoost, support vector machine, and multilayer perceptron baselines using 5-fold stratified cross-validation, and conducts ablation experiments targeting the attention mechanism and multi-branch structure. The reproducible five-fold rerun shows that MartialSense-Net achieves a Macro-F1 score of 0.545, exceeding the plain MLP and the NoMBFE variant but not the NoAttention variant; however, the overall classification performance of the proposed model has not yet surpassed tree-based baselines such as random forest and XGBoost, and the coefficient of determination (R2) for the regression task is negative, indicating that precise regression of the overall performance score remains challenging under the current data scale and feature conditions. This paper further analyzes the limitations of deep learning-based educational assessment under small-scale and class-imbalanced tabular data conditions (samples of “High Performers” account for only 2.4%), and honestly reports all experimental results without any exaggeration of model performance. The findings therefore support MartialSense-Net only as an initial methodological benchmark for structured physical education data. Demonstrating Wushu-specific effectiveness will require multi-institutional records from authentic Wushu courses, direct Wushu skill indicators, and external validation across instructors, course levels, and student cohorts.

title: Quantile temporal graph convolutional networks and Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal models for crime risk forecasting and hotspot identification
abstract: Granular spatio-temporal forecasting of socioeconomic risks, particularly regional crime dynamics, is crucial for formulating targeted public policies and optimizing resource allocation under fiscal constraints. This study presents a comparative framework that benchmarks deep probabilistic graph architectures against Bayesian hierarchical models across 52 administrative districts in South Africa, leveraging a unique multi-year dataset from the Governance, Public Safety, and Justice Survey (GPSJS) spanning 2018/19 to 2023/24. Specifically, we evaluate a novel Quantile Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (Quantile TGCN), which integrates spatio-temporal graph convolutions with pinball-loss optimization to generate distribution-free, calibrated prediction intervals. This model is contrasted with a deterministic Standard TGCN baseline and Bayesian spatio-temporal models fitted via Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA), incorporating Besag-York-Mollié (BYM2) spatial priors under both Gamma and log-normal observation models. The evaluation criteria include out-of-sample point forecast accuracy, residual bias profiles, prediction interval calibration, and the ability to rank high-risk spatial hotspots under strict allocation constraints. Contrary to expectations that more complex architectures would yield superior predictive performance, the Bayesian INLA specifications, particularly the log-normal BYM2 model, demonstrated lower out-of-sample errors and stronger discrimination of high-risk districts. Notably, the Quantile TGCN excels in producing well-calibrated, distribution-free prediction intervals, thus offering valuable insights for granular risk monitoring and evidence-based governance in emerging economies. This comparative approach contributes to the development of robust diagnostic tools for socioeconomic risk assessment and intervention planning.

title: Effects of adopting improved bread wheat varieties on smallholder farmers’ yields: a case study of Duna District, Central Ethiopia
abstract: Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) is a key food and cash crop for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia, yet national yields remain low. Adoption of improved bread wheat varieties is widely promoted to boost productivity, but institutional, socioeconomic, and demographic constraints limit uptake. This study examines the determinants of adoption of improved bread wheat varieties and their association with smallholder yields in Duna District, Hadiya Zone. A multistage sampling procedure selected 264 farm households, including 119 adopters (45.1% of the sample) and 145 non-adopters. Data were analyzed using a binary logit model to identify factors influencing adoption, propensity score matching (PSM) to estimate yield effects, and descriptive statistics. The logit results show that sex of the household head, landholding size, livestock ownership, extension contact, education level, training participation, and cooperative membership were positively and significantly associated with adoption (all effects reported in percentage points of predicted probability, not percent). Access to credit had a significant negative association. Using kernel (Epanechnikov) matching with a bandwidth of 0.01, PSM findings indicate that the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) corresponds to a 15.5% relative difference in wheat yield between matched adopters and non-adopters (5.59 quintals ha⁻¹, equivalent to about 18.4% relative to the matched control group’s yield); this difference is conditional on the observable covariates included in the matching model, and its robustness to potential unobserved confounding is examined through a Rosenbaum bounds sensitivity analysis. The study recommends policies that empower female-headed households, strengthen education and literacy, expand extension services, and promote training and cooperative participation. Improving livestock productivity, land management, and further investigation of the credit-adoption relationship can inform future interventions. These findings are specific to Duna District and should be interpreted with appropriate caution when generalizing to other agroecological or institutional settings; broader claims about food security and rural livelihoods would require additional evidence beyond wheat yield alone.

title: Linking soil taxonomic characterization with GIS–AHP modelling for groundnut land suitability assessment in southern India
abstract: Groundnut cultivation in seasonally dry tropical landscapes is strongly influenced by soil heterogeneity, landscape position and management constraints, requiring crop-specific land evaluation for sustainable production. In this study, detailed field pedology and USDA Soil Taxonomy were used to characterize and interpret soil variability, while GIS–Analytical Hierarchy Process (GIS–AHP) modelling was used separately to weight and combine crop-suitability criteria for the Puttur division of Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh, India. Twenty representative pedons spanning major geomorphic positions were described and 85 horizon-wise samples were analysed. The soils were classified as Alfisols, Inceptisols and Entisols under ustic moisture and isohyperthermic temperature regimes. The AHP matrix assigned the greatest weights to drainage (21.03%), exchangeable Ca (16.08%), texture (15.88%) and effective rooting depth (11.76%); λmax = 11.3782, CI = 0.0378 and CR = 0.0250 indicated acceptable internal consistency of the pairwise judgements. Suitability patterns were governed mainly by drainage, Ca status, texture, rooting depth and slope, with low organic carbon and suboptimal soil reaction acting as additional local constraints. Soil Taxonomy was not used as an AHP criterion; rather, taxonomic and pedogenic information was used to interpret why constraints differed among pedons. The GIS–AHP output is therefore presented as a relative spatial screening framework, and independent yield validation is identified as a requirement for further model testing.

title: Unprecedented but understudied: A brief review of climate-induced forest decline in Central Chile
abstract: Mediterranean-type ecosystems (MTEs) are among the most biodiverse and climate-vulnerable ecosystems globally. Rising temperatures, combined with more frequent and intense droughts, have driven widespread forest decline across all five MTE regions, accounting for 48% of globally documented forest mortality events. Among these, Central Chile has experienced the most severe climatic anomalies, including a persistent megadrought since 2010, two hyperdroughts in 2019 and 2021 with precipitation deficits exceeding 75%, and recurrent spring and summer heatwaves. These unprecedented conditions position Central Chile as a potential worst-case scenario for the future of MTEs worldwide. This review synthesises current knowledge on climate-induced forest decline in Central Chile, summarising recent research conducted across multiple spatial and ecological scales. Emerging evidence reveals a regional forest decline characterised by reduced productivity, radial growth declines, impaired seedling establishment, and widespread canopy browning. While these responses are comparable to those observed in other MTEs, the ecological implications of hyperdroughts and regional warming for forest resilience remain poorly understood. Despite growing research efforts, critical knowledge gaps persist regarding forest mortality rates, regeneration dynamics, and the physiological mechanisms underlying tree survival and mortality. We identify key research priorities, including the need for quantified mortality data, mechanistic understanding of decline processes, assessment of post-disturbance ecological dynamics, and integrative approaches that link plot-based observations with remote sensing and modelling. Addressing these gaps is essential to evaluate changes in productivity, species composition, and the long-term trajectory of Chilean MTEs, while contributing to a broader predictive understanding of forest resilience in Mediterranean-type ecosystems globally.

Optimization of siderophore production by Westiellopsis sp. KM1 and evaluation of its biomass wet extract for rice growth under metal stress: An integrated response surface methodology and Machine learning approach.
abstract: The present study isolated a siderophore-producing cyanobacterium, Westiellopsis sp. KM1 (GenBank accession no. PQ435491), from the Palk Strait region, investigated its siderophore production, and separately evaluated the effects of its biomass wet extract (BWE) on Oryza sativa growth under excess Fe and Cu stress. Qualitative and quantitative assays demonstrated siderophore production. Response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to optimize siderophore production, achieving a maximum of 86 PSU under optimized conditions. An integrated machine learning framework comprising Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Gaussian Process Regression, and Artificial Neural Networks was further evaluated using repeated five-fold cross-validation with ten repetitions (50 resampling iterations). Among the tested models, XGBoost showed the best numerical predictive performance (R2 = 0.594, RMSE = 9.664) indicating moderate predictive ability. The model predicted an optimum siderophore production of 78.65 PSU; however, this prediction was not experimentally verified. SHAP analysis and Differential Evolution-based optimization were used to interpret model predictions and explore cultivation conditions. Based on FT-IR, GC-MS, and NMR analyses, the siderophore was tentatively classified as carboxylate-type. Pot experiments showed BWE from KM1 significantly enhanced seedling growth and increased biomass, protein, carbohydrate, and chlorophyll contents in O. sativa exposed to experimentally imposed excess Fe and Cu. These effects were associated with BWE application and cannot be specifically attributed to siderophore-mediated metal chelation. Overall, this study reports a coastal backwater Westiellopsis strain producing a tentative carboxylate-type siderophore and highlights the potential of cyanobacterial BWE and data-driven optimization for crop improvement under excess metal stress.

Enhancing inherent soil productivity to support sustainable wheat production in China's wheat-growing regions.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Improving soil fertility is essential for securing food production. Inherent soil productivity (ISP) is an integrated indicator of soil fertility, reflecting the nutrient supply capacity and sustainability of soil. However, the regional differences of ISP, its dominant limiting factors, and its impacts on grain production remain poorly quantified at large scales. OBJECTIVES This study aims to quantify the regional differences of ISP, identify its dominant limiting factors, and evaluate the potential for ISP improvement and its implications for grain production. METHODS Using 12,737 fertilization field experiments across China's wheat-growing regions, we first quantified the regional differences of ISP, and then employed a random forest model combined with a multi-start optimization framework to identify its dominant limiting factors, and to assess its improvement potential and impacts on crop productivity and nitrogen efficiency. RESULTS Our results show that the average ISP of wheat fields in China is 3.73 Mg ha-1, and the relative contribution of ISP to yield under the medium N treatment (ISPC) averaged 61%. ISP in the North China Plain and Northwest regions are significantly higher than that in Northeast, the Yangtze River Plain, and Southwest regions. At the national scale, soil available nitrogen and phosphorus are the primary limiting factors of ISP, while irrigation, precipitation, and frost-free period also play important roles. However, the relative importance of these factors varies among regions. Coordinated soil-property improvement showed a model-based upper-bound potential to increase ISP by 0.42 Mg ha-1, with associated national-scale potential gains of 5% in yield and 4% in NUE, and a 4% potential reduction in N surplus, although the magnitude of these benefits varied considerably among regions. CONCLUSION These findings highlight the critical role of ISP in sustaining wheat production and improving N efficiency, and suggest that targeted soil fertility improvement can support sustainable wheat production by enhancing soil-derived yield potential and reducing dependence on further fertilizer intensification.

title: Copper transport to mitochondria by SLC25A3 contributes to skeletal myoblast differentiation and is required for survival of differentiated myotubes.
abstract: Differentiation of skeletal muscle is associated with increased mitochondrial biogenesis and reliance on oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). The terminal enzyme complex in the electron transport chain, cytochrome c oxidase (COX), requires copper for its assembly and activity, and copper delivery to mitochondria is essential for OXPHOS. However, when mitochondrial copper becomes essential during skeletal myoblast differentiation is not known. Here, we show that inducing genetic deficiency of the mitochondrial copper and phosphate carrier SLC25A3 prior to myoblast differentiation leads to the formation of smaller myotubes, but SLC25A3 deficiency induced in mature myotubes leads to cell death and detachment. Both phenotypes are recapitulated upon genetic knockdown of COX17, a key chaperone for COX copper cofactor assembly, and by chemical inhibition of COX. Importantly, myotube death caused by SLC25A3 deficiency is reversed by copper supplementation. Expression of an SLC25A3 isoform A variant that is equivalent to a variant in isoform B that exclusively transports copper also rescues myotube viability. Taken together these data support a model wherein SLC25A3 is critical for survival in mature myotubes, likely due to its role in providing copper to COX.

title: A lightweight edge-based wild boar detection framework for wildlife monitoring and decision support in agroecosystems.
abstract: Wild boar (Sus scrofa) intrusions in agricultural environments cause severe crop damage and economic losses and have become an increasingly prominent human-wildlife conflict. Effective wildlife monitoring is therefore essential for sustainable agricultural ecosystem management. However, wild boar detection in real-world scenarios remains challenging due to frequent occlusion and complex backgrounds. Meanwhile, edge devices deployed in farmland environments typically have limited computational resources, imposing strict requirements on lightweight model design and inference efficiency. To address these challenges, this study proposes HED-YOLOv11, a lightweight wildlife object detection framework with three targeted architectural optimizations. First, the backbone network is reconstructed using HGNetv2 to enhance multi-scale feature extraction capability. Second, a novel C2EPSA module is designed to strengthen discriminative feature representation and suppress background interference in complex farmland scenes. Third, the DySample module is introduced into the neck network to improve feature reconstruction in challenging scenes involving occlusion. Furthermore, to facilitate potential deployment in field monitoring systems, a collaborative model compression strategy combining LAMP-based channel pruning and knowledge distillation is proposed, reducing computational overhead while maintaining detection performance. Experimental results show that HED-YOLOv11 achieves 92.6% precision and 92.2% mAP@0.50, with 2.37M parameters. After model compression, the parameters is reduced to 1.27M. The compressed model achieves an inference speed of 30.7 FPS on the RK3568 edge device. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed framework for edge-based wild boar detection and its potential to support wildlife monitoring and management decision-making in agricultural ecosystems.

title: MAPK signaling in plant metabolic control: integrating phytohormones with primary and secondary metabolism.
abstract: Mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascades are conserved signaling modules that integrate environmental and developmental cues to regulate plant metabolism. This review synthesizes current understanding of how MAPKKK-MAPKK-MAPK cascades coordinate primary metabolism, secondary metabolism, and phytohormone biosynthesis. MAPK cascades regulate photosynthetic capacity, nitrogen fixation and assimilation, and carbon flux through phosphorylation of key metabolic enzymes and transcription factors that balance growth with stress responses. In secondary metabolism, MAPK cascades converge on downstream transcription factors to regulate camalexin, indole glucosinolate, phenylpropanoid, flavonoid, lignin, terpenoid, and alkaloid biosynthesis. We further summarize how MAPKs are involved in the biosynthesis and signaling of ethylene, jasmonic acid, salicylic acid, auxin, and abscisic acid, revealing extensive crosstalk between kinase cascades and hormonal networks. We propose an integrative model in which MAPK cascades function as signaling hubs funneling upstream cues into three coordinated arms: transcription factor phosphorylation, direct modulation of structural enzymes, and phytohormone crosstalk. Future research should address key knowledge gaps, including incomplete MAPK cascades, limited understanding of MAPK substrates and their specificity in metabolic regulation, feedback mechanisms preventing metabolic overactivation, and the conservation of these principles across crop species. Understanding MAPK-mediated metabolic control holds promise for engineering stress-resilient, pathogen-resistant, and high-yield crops.
