title: Soil strength characterization using remote sensing for vehicle mobility assessment: a near-real-time approach
CmWRKY7 and CmMYBL1 directly activate CmP5CS1 to promote proline accumulation and cold tolerance in melon (Cucumis melo L.).
abstract: Melon (Cucumis melo L.) is a typical cold-sensitive crop that is highly susceptible to cold stress, which severely limits yield and quality. Proline accumulation is an important physiological strategy against abiotic stress, but its transcriptional regulation in melon remains unclear. In this study, transcriptome analysis, qRT-PCR, VIGS, yeast one-hybrid, GUS staining, and dual-luciferase assays were used to dissect the mechanism. Low temperature induced proline accumulation in 82.9% of tested melon materials. Key gene of proline synthase CmP5CS1 was specifically upregulated, whereas CmP5CS2 was repressed. Silencing CmP5CS1 reduced proline accumulation by 22.3% and decreased Fv/Fm by 19.0%, indicating that CmP5CS1 is a core gene for cold-induced proline synthesis. The CmP5CS1 promoter contains three W-box and seven MYB binding sites. Yeast one-hybrid, GUS staining, and dual-luciferase assays confirmed that CmWRKY7 and CmMYBL1 directly bind and activate the CmP5CS1 promoter. CmMYBL1 showed higher activation efficiency (LUC/REN, 2.8-fold) than CmWRKY7 (1.5-fold). Silencing CmWRKY7 or CmMYBL1 inhibited cold-induced CmP5CS1 expression, reduced proline accumulation by 28.8% and 27.8%, and decreased Fv/Fm by 22.1% and 22.5%, respectively, with severe wilting and reduced cold tolerance. These results establish a regulatory model in which cold signaling activates CmWRKY7 and CmMYBL1, which directly target the CmP5CS1 promoter to drive proline synthesis and enhance cold tolerance. It reveals a new model in which WRKY and MYB transcription factors coordinately regulate proline accumulation, providing key gene resources and a theoretical basis for molecular breeding of cold-tolerant melon.
journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology

title: ScrewSense: Mapping the Invisible - Anomaly Detection and Error Classification in Screwdriving Processes
abstract: The growing volume of process data generated by screwdriving systems, combined with advancements in computing power, data storage, and algorithms, is facilitating the application of artificial intelligence in this field. Accurately detecting and classifying screwdriving errors is crucial for ensuring product quality, avoiding costly rework in manufacturing, and supporting sustainability by facilitating the maintenance, reuse, and recycling of screw-connected products. In this context, machine learning approaches offer a promising alternative to traditional monitoring techniques, such as window-based methods or envelope curves. This study examines the use of deep learning techniques for anomaly detection and error classification in screwdriving processes. The data corpus consists of multivariate time series capturing process parameters, such as torque and rotation angle. For anomaly detection, the embedding space of a vector quantized variational autoencoder was analyzed. In terms of error classification, four different model architectures were evaluated. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of anomaly detection and confirm that deep learning models can distinguish between multiple error categories beyond traditional binary classification. This extends the capabilities of conventional monitoring approaches, achieving accuracies of up to 100%. Additionally, real-world data material was examined in order to further demonstrate model robustness. Overall the results indicate strong generalization capability and highlight the practical potential of the developed models for use in industrial screwdriving processes, eliminating the need for expert knowledge in error identification and significantly reducing manual effort and analysis time.

Diet-induced chromatin states influence intestinal stem cell behavior.
abstract: Intestinal stem cells (ISCs) integrate dietary cues through metabolic-transcriptional programs, but whether these signals produce lasting changes in chromatin organization remains unclear. We investigated diet-induced chromatin adaptations in ISCs, using a high-fat Western diet (HFD) mouse model. HFD broadly remodels chromatin accessibility, altering pre-existing open regulatory regions. Differentially accessible regions (DARs) reside outside canonical stem cell loci despite functional changes in ISC behavior. Many HFD-induced DARs persist through transient amplifying cell (TAC) differentiation and remain in ISCs following diet normalization regardless of phenotypic reversion. Re-exposure to HFD enhances ISC self-renewal and adenoma growth relative to naive controls, demonstrating a heightened response to dietary re-challenge. The HFD-induced chromatin remodeling requires Ppar-d/a nuclear receptors but is independent of their transcriptional targets. A subset of HFD-induced DARs is maintained following Apc loss, although extensive chromatin alterations largely override diet-dependent differences in Lgr5+ ISCs. Together, these findings reveal that ISCs retain chromatin accessibility features after dietary fat exposure, concordant with altered responses to subsequent dietary challenge.

title: In vitro cell model to assess human erythro-megakaryocytic lineage- and stage-specific toxicity of new antitumoral metallic complexes.
abstract: Early preclinical assessment of hematotoxicity is essential to minimize extensive ex vivo and in vivo experimentation during antitumoral drug development. The erythroid and megakaryocytic lineages are particularly sensitive to chemotherapeutic agents, and reductions in red blood cells or platelets often require treatment interruption or dose adjustment. Therefore, reliable in vitro models capable of detecting lineage-specific toxicity across different stages of maturation can be highly valuable. We developed a in vitro model based on the human cell lines K562 and HEL, which phenotypically resemble bipotential erythro-megakaryocytic progenitors and can be induced to undergo erythroid or megakaryocytic differentiation using defined agents. Cells were characterized in progenitor and differentiated states by viability assays, flow cytometric analysis of DNA content, immunophenotyping, and morphological assessment. Prototype metal-based compounds developed by our group (iodido‑platinum, phosphine‑platinum, and thiosemicarbazone‑copper complexes) were tested at different stages of differentiation. The model discriminated between erythroid and megakaryocytic toxicity among different compounds, lineages, and maturation stages. Differential sensitivity was observed depending on both the drug tested and the differentiation stage. Toxicity could be assessed in single cultures or co-culture conditions. This simple and cost-effective in vitro cell platform enables rapid and reliable detection of erythro-megakaryocytic toxicity in novel antitumoral agents and may help optimize preclinical drug evaluation strategies.

title: Study on the toxic effects of benzopyrene exposure on umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells and the mitigating effects of folic acid.
abstract: Benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) is a potent mutagen and human carcinogen. BaP has been shown to cause a variety of cytotoxicities. Human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (HUC-MSCs) play important roles in tissue regeneration and the treatment of various diseases because of their pluripotent differentiation and self-renewal abilities, immunomodulatory effects, and long-term proliferation in vitro. However, to date, no specific studies have investigated the toxic effects of BaP on HUC-MSCs. Folic acid (FA) participates in one‑carbon metabolism in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes, mediating the transfer of one‑carbon units and playing a crucial role in nucleotide synthesis, methylation, and amino acid balance. Folic acid has been demonstrated to inhibit the toxicity of BaP both in vivo and in vitro. Therefore, we selected human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (HUC-MSCs) as our research model to investigate the effects of benzo[a]pyrene exposure on cultured human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells and the reparative effects of folic acid against benzo[a]pyrene exposure. We aimed to evaluate these effects through CCK-8 assays, comet assays, γH2AX immunofluorescence staining, reactive oxygen species (ROS) detection, FITC-luciferase coupled Annexin-V double staining, alizarin red staining, oil red O staining, and RT-qPCR to evaluate BaP's toxic effects on cell viability, DNA damage, oxidative stress, apoptosis, osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation, as well as folic acid's reparative effects against these toxicities. Results demonstrated that BaP exposure significantly reduced HUC-MSC survival rates, exacerbated DNA damage and oxidative stress levels, induced apoptosis, caused abnormalities in osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation, and disrupted the normal differentiation process of HUC-MSCs. Conversely, FA mitigated BaP-induced DNA damage and oxidative stress in HUC-MSCs, enhanced the expression of antioxidant-related genes, suppressed apoptosis, and alleviated the abnormal osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation, but failed to reverse the BaP-induced upregulation of apoptosis-related genes. In a word, our findings provide crucial experimental evidence for exploring the mechanism of benzo[a]pyrene's toxicity on human umbilical cord blood mesenchymal stem cells, thereby offering a basis for developing BaP prevention strategies.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of adoptively transferred stem-like CD8+ T cells in the tumor microenvironment following vaccination.
abstract: Adoptive cell therapy (ACT) of tumor-specific T cells can improve survival in a subset of cancer patients. Current ACT approaches may be limited by using highly differentiated T cells, which can be inhibited by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Here, we developed an approach to optimize ACT and used spatial transcriptomics to show how stem-like and effector CD8+ T cells differentially mediate tumor control following vaccination. Spatial transcriptomic profiling of the TME showed that ACT with stem-like T cells followed by intravenous vaccination prevented immune exclusion, increased infiltration of pro-inflammatory macrophages, and reprogrammed tumor cells to upregulate type I and type II IFN signaling gene programs, which were shown to be required for tumor control. The protective transcriptomic signature of the TME in this ACT model contained overlapping biomarkers with patients who responded to ACT therapy. This approach demonstrates synergy between transferred stem-like T cells and intravenous vaccination to transcriptionally remodel the TME and enhance tumor control.

title: Near-Real-Time Mapping of Seamless All-Hour Aerosol Optical Depth in China
abstract: Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is central to assessing aerosol climate forcing and air quality, yet persistent cloud cover and the absence of nighttime satellite retrievals preclude seamless, all-hour monitoring. Here, we develop an automated machine-learning framework that fuses a newly available gridded visibility data set with forecast AOD and spatiotemporal covariates to reconstruct AOD over China at an hourly 5 km resolution in near-real-time. Trained on geostationary satellite observations, the model achieves robust performance (Pearson correlation coefficient R = 0.95 in cross-validation) and outperforms reanalysis and forecast products while filling cloud- and darkness-induced gaps. Independent validation against MODIS and ground-based nighttime Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) measurements yields consistent accuracy (MODIS R = 0.61 and AERONET R = 0.76), confirming physical generalizability. The resulting seamless record exposes a pronounced diurnal cycle with a midday minimum and an early morning maximum, and documents a consistent year-on-year decline from 2020 to 2022 that aligns with China’s clean-air actions and COVID-19 lockdowns. During a record-breaking dust storm, the framework tracks aerosol dynamics during cloud-obscured and nocturnal phases, capturing an uninterrupted process-level account of the event. By delivering the day–night aerosol continuum at high resolution and low latency, this work bridges a critical observational gap in air-quality response, data assimilation, and diurnal aerosol-climate research.

title: Template Mineralized, Decellularized Matrix-Alginate-Based Bioink Provides Structural Reinforcement in Caprine Ex Vivo Bone Defect Model.
abstract: Clinical management of critical-sized bone defects (CSDs) remains a significant surgical problem. Current bioinks fail to support initial loading on bone tissue. In this study, goat-derived decellularized matrix (DCM) was used as a template for controlled mineralization, while alginate improved the printability and cellular viability. DCM proteins acted as a natural template for hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal nucleation and growth, mimicking bone nanocomposite chemistry while enhancing structural reinforcement. HA formation on DCM template was visualized by atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis, characteristic phosphate (PO43-) peaks in attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), and the HA-specific (211) diffraction peak in X-ray diffraction (XRD). Mineralized DCM was blended with alginate to formulate printable bioinks. Rheological analysis showed dominant elastic behavior (G' > G″), shear-thinning flow, and rapid post-shear recovery. Mechanical testing further demonstrated enhanced compressive strength in HA-DCM-alginate constructs. Bioprinting with osteoblast cells demonstrated higher cellular viability in the mineralized ink while enhancing osteogenic differentiation, via both biochemical and biophysical signaling from the mineralized-DCM ink. In an ex vivo defect model, the HA-DCM-alginate system significantly increased the compressive properties of the defect construct, providing immediate structural reinforcement at the defect site. Overall, the current mineralized bioink can provide both mechanical support and bone regeneration and holds promising potential for surgical application.

title: Peptide-DNA Hybrid Selection for Chemical Functionality Recognition across Diverse Material Interfaces.
abstract: Sequence-defined affinity ligands are powerful tools for molecular recognition, yet their selection has largely focused on defined molecular targets rather than shared chemical functionalities. Extending sequence-based recognition to a chemical moiety presents a distinct challenge because the same functionality must be recognized across structurally and chemically diverse molecular and material contexts. Here, we demonstrate that in vitro selection of peptide-DNA hybrids can generate an affinity ligand that recognizes a shared chemical functionality across distinct molecular and material interfaces. Using carboxylates as a model functionality, we selected a peptide-DNA hybrid library against a carboxylated material surface and identified R8rank1, whose enhanced binding depended on the selected DNA sequence functioning within the peptide-DNA hybrid architecture. R8rank1 hybrid preferentially recognized carboxylate-containing polymers with distinct molecular backbones over polymers bearing other functionalities, including an anionic sulfonate-containing polymer, and retained its recognition behavior across chemically distinct gold and silica nanoparticle interfaces presenting surface carboxylates. Fluorescently labeled R8rank1 further distinguished carboxylated from hydroxylated silica nanoparticles with an approximately eightfold difference in fluorescence and exhibited an apparent Kd of approximately 390 nM for the carboxylated surface, whereas the two surfaces were not significantly differentiated by zeta-potential measurements. This affinity-based readout provides chemical-functionality information complementary to conventional surface charge characterization. These findings extend sequence-based affinity selection from defined molecular targets to shared chemical functionalities and establish peptide-DNA hybrids as a selectable molecular recognition platform for identifying chemical functionalities across diverse material interfaces.

title: Differentiation hierarchy in adult B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia at clonal resolution.
abstract: While a differentiation hierarchy with leukemia-initiating stem cells (LICs) at the apex is well documented for acute myeloid leukemia, the existence of LICs and their trajectories in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) are debated. This study aims to investigate the hierarchical landscape of two B-ALL cases by combining barcoding and multiome single-cell data to unveil the differentiation architecture and temporal dynamics of leukemic differentiation at clonal and single-cell resolution in vivo. Single-cell transcriptome and AbSeq analysis of lentiviral barcoded and transplanted patient-derived B-ALL cells revealed interconnected subpopulations, which could be prospectively isolated via surface markers and exhibited distinct leukemogenicity. Barcode tracking demonstrated the ability of cells to differentiate from a source cluster into differentiated progeny. Using machine learning, we identified expression patterns predicting the differentiation potential of each barcoded cell within the immature cell compartment. To determine the dynamical properties of clones, we developed a mathematical model that simulates the development of these subpopulations from a clonally diverse stem cell compartment. The model confirmed the most likely cluster of origin, supporting our functional data, and revealed the variability in dynamical properties between clones, while largely excluding plasticity. Hence, our work demonstrates unidirectional differentiation in selected B-ALL cases.

title: Latitude modulates climate-driven maize yield gains across the central U.S. “warming hole”
abstract: Maize yield responses to climate change differ seasonally and regionally, with both positive and negative impacts shaped by local climate trends and management decisions. Here, using a phenology-aligned moving crop-season framework and the Hybrid-Maize model (1991–2024) across five U.S. Corn Belt states, we quantify climate-driven yield contributions and show that they transition from southern declines to northern gains, reflecting the persistent influence of the central U.S. summer warming hole characterized by cooling maximum temperatures and increasing rainfall. A systematic thermal mismatch between environmental heat availability and hybrid growing degree day requirements is observed, particularly south of 42°N, where thermal matching declined despite favorable thermal conditions. Contrasting trends in thermal matching and reproductive duration help explain the latitude-dependent structure of climate-driven yield contributions. Our findings highlight how hybrid selection modulates the impacts of temperature, precipitation, vapor pressure deficit, and radiation trends on maize yield gains across the U.S. Corn Belt.

title: argosim : A differentiable framework for radio interferometric simulation and array optimisation
abstract: We present , a lightweight and modular Python framework for radio interferometric simulation based on the JAX numerical computing library. In addition to providing accelerated simulation on CPUs and GPUs, implements a differentiable interferometric forward model, enabling the gradient-based optimisation of antenna configurations and interferometric point spread functions (PSFs). We describe the main components of the simulation pipeline, from antenna layouts and uv sampling to visibility generation, image reconstruction, and PSF characterisation. We demonstrate the computational performance of the framework and its automatic differentiation capabilities through an antenna-layout optimisation problem in which the interferometric PSF is shaped towards a target response while accounting for physical constraints. The package is a fully open-source project, and its code is publicly available on GitHub. argosim argosim

title: Reservoir Flood Storage Capacity as an Indicator of Potential Forecast-Informed Prerelease Effectiveness
abstract: The operation of multipurpose reservoirs for which flood risk management (FRM) is a primary or key purpose may be improved by the use of Forecast-Informed Reservoir Operations (FIRO). The ability to screen a portfolio of dams to assess FIRO viability allows for more-efficient use of time and funding than individual detailed analyses for several dams. In this study, screening criteria were used to evaluate the potential effectiveness of FIRO prestore and prerelease (PS-PR) and basic operation prerelease (BO-PR) methods using a large data set (58 dams) and along three lines of inquiry. A regression model was used to assess system characteristics and identify the reservoirs for which reservoir filling is most sensitive to changes in flood storage capacity. Historic flood events provided insight into the feasibility of FIRO based on seasonality and storm characteristics. Physical and policy constraints were studied to assess the feasibility of FIRO at or near top of conservation pool and to provide an initial input to the screening framework. A four-parameter equation to predict reservoir-filling frequency had an R 2 value of 0.67, and flood storage capacity was significant at a 99% confidence level. Review of historic reservoir-filling events showed a median 3-day flood storage of 23% and a 7-day flood storage of 38%. Policy and physical release constraints yielded maximum daily drawdown estimates for each reservoir and indicated a median of 2% of average annual inflow evacuation per day. A case study of five dams was used to assess viability of using the storage-based regression as a criterion for prerelease screening. The presented screening approach utilizes an estimate of maximum prerelease drawdown and the regression equations to provide high estimates for potential FIRO effectiveness (with uncertainty); actual applicability depends on forecast skill and available lead time, which are not evaluated in this study.
journal: Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management

title: From field trials to meta-analysis: A practical guide for agricultural synthesis
abstract: Agricultural field experiments often produce context-dependent results because treatment effects vary across crop systems, soil properties, climate conditions, management practices, experimental durations, and measurement methods. Meta-analysis offers a powerful way to synthesize such evidence, increase statistical power, and identify the conditions under which agricultural practices are effective. However, agricultural meta-analysis involves a series of practical decisions that are not always fully addressed in general methodological guidelines. These decisions include framing field-relevant research questions, developing reproducible search strategies, extracting data from heterogeneous reports, defining independent records, selecting appropriate effect-size metrics, handling missing variance information, accounting for dependent effect sizes, modeling heterogeneity, and interpreting results in agronomic terms. This review presents a field-trial-to-meta-analysis framework for agricultural research, emphasizing common pitfalls and agriculture-specific considerations. We highlight the importance of defining research questions around crop or soil system, management practice, comparator, outcome, and context; extracting both core statistics and agronomic moderator variables; choosing effect-size metrics that match the outcome and intended interpretation; and using model structures that reflect heterogeneity and dependence in agricultural datasets. We also provide practical guidance for transparent reporting, sensitivity analysis, and interpretation of statistical results in relation to field relevance, trade-offs, and management implications. By linking general meta-analytic principles with the realities of agricultural field research, this guide aims to support syntheses that are statistically robust, reproducible, and agronomically meaningful.

title: Intellectual property rights and the global exchange of molecular plant technologies.
abstract: The global intellectual property regime for plants is structurally misaligned with the molecular tools on which climate-resilient agriculture now depends. As gene editing, synthetic biology, and Digital Sequence Information (DSI) become central to breeding drought-, heat-, and salinity-tolerant crops, these same technologies are increasingly enclosed within dense patent thickets, trade rules that go beyond the minimum standards of the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS), commonly called TRIPS-plus rules, and costly regulatory requirements. Using doctrinal legal analysis, a patent-landscape review, and product-level case studies, we show how this architecture generates a "Market Power Effect," whereby a small group of firms can set prices, stack royalties, and control access to enabling technologies, effectively sidelining public breeders, small laboratories, and climate-vulnerable states. We develop the concept of "legal resilience" to capture the idea that molecular resilience in biotech crops is meaningless without legal structures that allow rapid, equitable diffusion of adaptive traits. Empirically, we link rising CRISPR-related patents, escalating licensing and compliance costs, and corporate concentration to stagnant yield growth, persistent human undernourishment, and an emerging form of digital biopiracy that existing access and benefit-sharing instruments cannot contain. We also examine the position of large middle-income innovators, China in particular, which do not fit the conventional North-South division and whose domestic policy choices are pushing toward stronger rather than weaker protection. On this basis, we propose a polycentric reform package: a climate-utility model tier for incremental local adaptations; a multilateral DSI benefit-sharing fund financed by small levies on commercial seed sales; compulsory humanitarian patent pools for abiotic stress-resistance technologies; regional molecular hubs that pair laboratories with pro-bono freedom-to-operate support; and sustained support for the existing network of genebanks and community seed systems as a practical counterweight to the hazard of genetic uniformity. Our central claim is that genetic resilience must be treated as an essential facility for human food security, not merely as a tradable private asset.

title: Wound atlas of Atlantic salmon skin.
abstract: The process of wound healing offers a window into how cells coordinate to maintain tissue integrity, repair damage, and restore tissue function. Wound healing in Atlantic salmon, a species of considerable ecological and economic importance, is a tightly coordinated process involving multiple cellular programmes that eventually lead to scarless repair. Here, we present the first single-nucleus atlas of healing salmon skin wounds, providing a comprehensive view of its cellular organisation over multiple timepoints. We have profiled 29,706 nuclei from uninjured skin, 2 days post-wounding (dpw; inflammatory phase), and 14 dpw (proliferative phase), identifying 44 transcriptionally distinct cell clusters. Integration with previously published spatial transcriptomics dataset further enabled the localisation of these populations within the wound microenvironment. We have identified distinct spatial-temporal association for erythrocytes, thrombocytes, macrophages, differentiating muscle cells, fibroblasts, and tenocytes, highlighting their potential contributions to tissue repair. Furthermore, transcriptomic and histological analyses support a previously under-appreciated role for the myosepta in coordinating wound and muscle repair. By linking cellular transcriptional state to the tissue architecture, this spatially resolved wound atlas provides a framework for understanding the repair of cutaneous wounds in Atlantic salmon and establishes a valuable resource for studies of fish health. By exploring wound healing for insights on tissue function, this atlas also offers broader insights into the scarless wound healing biology in non-model organism vertebrates. Data visualisation of the single-nuclei RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics analysis is available on our web portal at https://bshihlab-salmonwoundatlas.share.connect.posit.cloud/.

title: The impact of socio-economic transformation on forest fragmentation: a case study of the Wuling Mountain Area
abstract: The aim of this paper is to examine the impacts of socio-economic transformation on forest fragmentation and to reveal the mediating transmission mechanisms of labor out-migration, agricultural productivity improvement and energy structure transition in this process, providing empirical evidence for achieving synergistic development and conservation in impoverished regions. Based on panel data from 71 counties in the Wuling Mountain Area spanning 2003–2023, this research establishes a socio-economic transformation indicator framework encompassing four dimensions: economic development foundation, industrial structure modification, social advancement and green development. Using fixed effects models and mediation effect models, the study systematically investigates the impacts of socio-economic transformation on forest fragmentation and its transmission mechanisms. First, socio-economic transformation exerts a considerable mitigating effect on forest fragmentation in the Wuling Mountain Area. Second, labor out-migration, agricultural productivity improvement and energy structure transition represent three key mediating pathways through which transformation alleviates forest fragmentation. Third, the mitigating effect of socio-economic transformation demonstrates notable heterogeneity. This study introduces the perspective of socio-economic transformation into forest fragmentation research. Using the Wuling Mountain Area, a contiguous poverty-stricken region in China, as a case study, it broadens the analytical framework of Forest Transition Theory by integrating wider socio-economic transformation processes into the elucidation of forest fragmentation dynamics.

title: Integrating TPB and NAM to explain organic aquaculture transition intentions: evidence from Thanh Hoa, Vietnam
abstract: This study examines aquaculture households' intentions to transition to organic aquaculture in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam. Building on the theory of planned behavior (TPB) and the norm activation model (NAM), the study distinguishes perceived benefits into economic and non-economic dimensions, incorporates moral norm as an internal moral consideration and examines the moderating role of subjective norm in the relationship between moral norm and transition intention. A quantitative research design was employed using survey data collected from 323 aquaculture households in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine the hypothesized direct, indirect and moderating relationships. Perceived economic benefits, perceived non-economic benefits, subjective norm, perceived behavioral control and moral norm are positively associated with transition intention, with moral norm showing the strongest association. Moral norm is positively associated with perceived non-economic benefits but not with perceived economic benefits, indicating a distinction between the two dimensions of perceived benefits. In addition, the interaction between subjective norm and moral norm is positive and statistically significant, indicating that the positive relationship between moral norm and transition intention becomes stronger as subjective norm increases. This study is limited by its cross-sectional design and its focus on transition intention rather than actual behavior. The model also does not fully account for socio-demographic, structural and institutional factors that may affect the intention–behavior gap. Future research should use longitudinal data, incorporate these external constraints, examine mechanisms that may bridge the intention–behavior gap and test the model across different geographical contexts. This study extends behavioral research on organic aquaculture in three respects. First, it distinguishes perceived economic and non-economic benefits to provide a more differentiated understanding of benefit-related considerations associated with transition intention. Second, building on TPB and NAM, it examines subjective norm not only as a direct predictor of intention but also as a moderator of the relationship between moral norm and transition intention. Third, by applying this framework to aquaculture households in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam, the study provides context-specific insights for policymakers, extension agencies and other stakeholders in designing policies and support programs for organic aquaculture transition.
journal: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies

title: Customer-oriented marketing and Gen Z behaviour: combining PLS-SEM and necessary condition analysis
abstract: Based on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) model, this research aims to investigate the impact of customer-oriented marketing (CoM) on the post-purchase behaviour (PPB) of Generation Z hotel customers in Egypt. It further investigates the mediating roles of customer delight and customer well-being and tests whether customer delight enhances customer well-being as a sequential psychological mechanism linking CoM to behavioural outcomes. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed using an online questionnaire distributed to Generation Z hotel customers in Egypt. Of 500 surveys, 362 valid responses were analysed. The authors tested the proposed model using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), complemented by necessary condition analysis (NCA) and importance–necessity scatter mapping. CoM was operationalised as a multidimensional construct reflected by five foci: product, customer relationship, innovation, digitalisation and technology. PPB was measured through purchase intention, word of mouth and customer loyalty. Consistent with S–O–R theory, CoM positively influences PPB both directly and indirectly through customer delight and customer well-being, confirming the proposed sequential mechanism. NCA results further show that digitalisation is a statistically significant necessary condition for achieving high delight, well-being and PPB. The scatter maps reinforce that digitalisation represents the strongest high-importance/high-necessity dimension, whereas innovation and technology function mainly as value-adding enhancers. The descriptive findings show that Gen Z customers value digital convenience and experience quality; use search engines, social media and online travel agencies to evaluate hotels; and share experiences on social media and online review platforms. The post-purchase outcomes for Gen Z customers can be improved by hotels through customer-focused marketing that increases delight and well-being. However, digitalisation should be treated as a baseline requirement, while innovation and technology can be leveraged as differentiators once this foundation is secured. This study conceptualises CoM as a multidimensional stimulus within S–O–R and advances hospitality marketing research by integrating PLS-SEM with NCA and scatter mapping. The findings demonstrate that CoM dimensions differ not only in their net effects but also in their necessity role, highlighting digitalisation as a minimum condition for high Gen Z outcomes in an emerging market context.

title: Algorithmic cognitive programmes: observing ambient architectures of attention with social systems theory
abstract: This paper extends Luhmann's concept of programmes – decision premises specifying the conditions under which a system's binary code is operatively assigned – into the domain of algorithmically mediated communication. It conceptualises recommendation systems, ranking algorithms and feedback architectures as ambient cognitive programmes: recursive, probabilistic selectors that perturb the structural coupling between social and psychic systems, and examines the constitutional implications of their opacity and transfunctional reach. The study develops a systemic–cybernetic model grounded in Luhmann's social systems theory and the epistemology of autopoietic cognition, integrating Teubner's theory of societal constitutionalism to address the normative dimensions of algorithmic mediation. Analytical illustrations from Facebook and TikTok contrast two recommendation architectures – affinity-based cascading and behavioural-similarity propagation – to demonstrate how the model applies across distinct platform logics. Algorithmic cognitive programmes operate as meta-programmes that reconfigure multiple forms of social differentiation simultaneously, enacting a binary operational distinction of visibility/invisibility through engagement metrics. Their colonisation of communicative environments – by economic imperatives and, as the analysis argues, by the autonomous logic of technical mediation – becomes a constitutional pathology where its effects cannot be contested or corrected, requiring internal self-limiting mechanisms that render operative selection criteria observable to affected systems. The paper advances a novel theoretical category – ambient cognitive programmes – that extends Luhmann's organisational typology by identifying a configuration it does not explicitly address: a purpose programme without a terminal goal state that continuously revises the conditional programmes it governs. It connects this analytical framework to Teubner's societal constitutionalism, proposing constitutional observability as a structural condition for the compatibility between algorithmic regimes and communicative pluralism.

title: A psychometric evaluation of the anti-mattering scale: internalized and experiential dimensions in U.S. College students and patients with chronic illness
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the psychometric properties of the anti-mattering scale (AMS) in two U.S. samples, including its factor structure, measurement invariance across race, gender and sexual orientation, construct validity and reliability. Cross-sectional data were collected from 956 college students and 346 patients with chronic illness. Confirmatory factor analyses supported a two-factor model distinguishing internalized (i.e. stable, self-beliefs of anti-mattering) and experiential (i.e. interpersonal experiences of insignificance) dimensions. Both demonstrated strong validity. The AMS predicted suicidal ideation beyond related constructs, with experiential anti-mattering showing more consistent predictive utility, especially among patients with chronic illness. The AMS may serve as a brief multidimensional tool for identifying risk for depressive symptoms and suicide ideation. Differentiating its dimensions may improve assessment precision and inform targeted interventions across educational and healthcare settings. Findings support a multidimensional conceptualization of anti-mattering and highlight the importance of distinguishing internalized and experiential components.

title: Deep learning-based detection and classification of urban traffic infrastructure degradation
abstract: This paper proposes an automated system for the detection and classification of traffic infrastructure degradations to partly automate and improve the efficiency of the inspection process. For this purpose, three cameras are mounted onto an inspection vehicle which record the road infrastructure. The recorded videos are analyzed offline using a processing pipeline consisting of YOLO-World as object detector, MedianFlow as object tracker and QWEN3-VL for final classification and damage assessment. These algorithms are chosen because no dedicated training is performed before inference for the inspection task. Identified damaged objects are reported in the form of GPS coordinates and a corresponding image crop. Experimental results are evaluated against actual traffic intersections and show an overall F1 score of 90.9% for object detection and a damage classification accuracy of 98.6 %.
journal: Earth Resources and Environmental Remote Sensing/GIS Applications XVII

title: Identifying the biophysical manifold: why boundary-based models outperform transformers for pixel-level crop yield prediction in site-specific small-data regimes
abstract: In pixel-level crop yield prediction using remote sensing, high-capacity sequence models are often limited by the scarcity of location-specific ground-truth data. This creates a challenging small-data regime where models must resolve complex biophysical patterns from limited site-specific growing seasons. This study evaluates efficient modelling strategies under data-constrained conditions by comparing deep sequence models against kernel-based and ensemble approaches for winter wheat yield prediction using Sentinel-2 imagery. We benchmark five architectures (Transformer, Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), Decision Tree (DT), Support Vector Machine (SVM)) and compare three temporal selection strategies: full measurements, expert-defined phenological windows, and a model-driven greedy search. Using the full temporal sequence, RF (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.7991) and XGBoost (R<sup>2</sup>= 0.8084) achieved significantly higher predictive fidelity than the Transformer (R<sup>2</sup>= 0.7888, p = 0.002 and p < 0.001 respectively). Under the expert-defined window, SVM achieved its highest fidelity (R<sup>2</sup>= 0.8088). The model-driven greedy strategy achieved highly competitive error rates while using fewer timestamps, even modestly reducing RMSE for the RF ensemble (0.6507 vs 0.6523 under Strategy 1). Although this temporal reduction incurred a modest cost to overall predictive variance (R<sup>2</sup>), the sustained low error rates demonstrate that temporal relevance can effectively offset the loss of sequence completeness in data-scarce settings. Furthermore, dimensionality reduction (PCA and t-SNE) reveals a structured, yield-stratified feature space. These findings suggest that, for this application, yield prediction in site-specific small-data regimes is primarily a problem of non-linear manifold separation, and that boundary-partitioning models outperform attention mechanisms when training data is insufficient to resolve complex sequence structures.
journal: Artificial Intelligence and Image and Signal Processing for Remote Sensing XXXII

title: Combining model inversion defenses to mitigate white‑box membership inference attacks
abstract: Despite recent progress, machine learning models remain vulnerable to powerful white-box post-training privacy attacks. Two prominent threats are membership inference attacks (MIAs), which aim to determine whether specific samples were included in the training data, and model inversion (MI) attacks, which attempt to reconstruct sensitive training samples. Existing defenses typically address these attack classes in isolation, leaving models exposed when adversaries target multiple privacy leakage channels. In this work, we systematically study whether the combination of defenses designed for MI can also strengthen robustness against state-of-the-art MIAs. We consider three representative defenses: transfer learning (TL) and Bilateral Dependency Optimization (BiDO), originally proposed to mitigate model inversion, and random cropping (RC), a strong defense against membership inference. We evaluate each defense individually, in pairwise combinations and in a full stacked configuration, with parameters tuned to preserve utility. We assess privacy leakage using LiRA, a state-of-the-art white-box membership inference attack, against both defended and undefended image classification models. Our results show that while each defense individually reduces MIA effectiveness, the combined configuration (TL-DMI + BiDO + RC) consistently provides the strongest mitigation, reducing attack success—particularly in the low false-positive regime—without notable degradation in model accuracy. Furthermore, the combined defense substantially increases the attacker cost while incurring only moderate overhead for the defender. These findings suggest that carefully combining complementary defenses offers a practical blueprint for mitigating white-box membership inference attacks and moves toward unified protection against multiple post-training privacy threats.

title: An image enhancement algorithm based on mixed fractional differential
abstract: To advance the efficacy of fractional differentiation in image sharpening, this paper proposes a mixed enhancement algorithm that integrates the Riemann–Liouville (R–L) fractional derivative with an extended Laplacian operator. The conventional Laplacian template is first generalized to a fractional-order formulation. A mixed enhancement model is then formulated via weighted fusion of the extended Laplacian and the R–L fractional differential template. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm markedly improves edge acuity and fine-detail contrast while preserving structural integrity, achieving balanced enhancement of global contrast and brightness. The resultant images exhibit quantitatively sharper edges, higher texture fidelity, artifact-free intensity transitions, and superior objective visual quality.

title: Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids
abstract: Electron hydrodynamics is an emerging framework that describes dynamics of interacting electron systems as conventional fluids. Although evidence for hydrodynamic-like transport has been reported in a variety of two-dimensional materials, precise quantitative measurement of the core parameter, electron viscosity, remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate that magnetoresistance in Corbino-shaped graphene devices offers a simultaneous ohmmeter and viscosometer capability, allowing us to disentangle the individual ohmic and viscous contributions to transport, even near viscous-ohmic crossover. In both monolayer and bilayer graphene, the effective electron-electron scattering rate scales linearly with temperature, deviating markedly from the T 2 dependence expected in conventional Fermi liquids. Instead, it is consistent with a recently identified tomographic fluid regime, theoretically predicted to be generic for two-dimensional electron systems.

title: Carbon dioxide and amorphous water ices in the debris disk around β Pictoris
abstract: The star β Pictoris is orbited by a dusty debris disk, within which planet formation is occurring. The outer disk is sufficiently far from the star that volatile molecules are expected to freeze into solid ices. We observed the β Pictoris disk in the near-infrared using the James Webb Space Telescope. The spectrum shows features due to amorphous water ice (<7% crystallinity) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) ice in both the 12 CO 2 and 13 CO 2 isotopologues. We infer that the CO 2 ice is intimately mixed with the water ice at a ratio of 1:10. This implies that the ices formed in cold conditions, likely in the interstellar medium. Frequent collisions within the debris disk are required to explain the observed uniform distribution of icy dust grains.

title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4 + T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer
abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: Strongly correlated and topological phases in moiré materials are exquisitely sensitive to lattice geometry at both atomic and superlattice length scales. Twist angle, pressure, and strain directly modify the lattice and thus act as highly effective tuning parameters. Here, we examined electrical transport in twisted bilayer graphene subjected to continuous uniaxial strain. Near the magic angle (≈1.1°), devices exhibited a pronounced elastoresistance that depended on band filling and temperature, with a gauge factor more than two orders of magnitude larger than that of conventional metals. In selected doping regimes, the elastoresistance exhibited a Curie-Weiss–like temperature divergence. We discuss possible microscopic origins, including nematic fluctuations and enhanced electronic entropy from fluctuating isospin moments. Our work establishes uniaxial strain as a versatile probe of correlated physics in a moiré material.

title: Atmospheric O 2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990
abstract: The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen (O 2 ) and CO 2 observations, we find that the ocean carbon sink increased by 0.63 ± 0.19 petagrams of carbon per year per decade (Pg C year −1 decade −1 ) (a mean of 2.8 ± 0.4 Pg C year −1 ), accounting for 35% of fossil emissions between 1990 and 2019. The net land sink shows no robust trend (with a mean of 1.0 ± 0.5 Pg C year −1 , accounting for 13% of fossil emissions), despite large decadal variability. These results challenge many process-based model simulations of the land and ocean sinks, questioning their ability to accurately predict future climate states.

title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability
abstract: Whether genomic data can be used to effectively predict adaptation in natural populations is unknown. Here, we tested the efficacy of genomic prediction of complex trait evolution by monitoring genome-wide allele frequencies and pigmentation variation in genetically diverse populations of Drosophila melanogaster during evolution in both field mesocosms and a controlled, lab-based setting. At two points during trait evolution, we produced a high-powered, well-resolved genotype-phenotype map that exhibited marked stability across independent populations. Although we were able to use this map to correctly infer the direction of pigmentation evolution in both the lab and field settings, the particular loci responding to selection were largely unpredictable based on the direction of trait evolution itself. Our results hold implications for the promise, and limitations, of genomic prediction.

title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly
abstract: Innate immune systems of living organisms are essential for host defense. Central to these systems is the Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, an evolutionarily conserved module. From antiphage systems in prokaryotes to innate immune systems in plants, TIR domains have catalytic activity. However, TIR domains within animal innate immune receptors, such as Toll-like receptors (TLRs), have been considered as scaffolds for adaptor recruitment. We report that the TLR4 TIR domain possesses an allosterically activated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) hydrolase (NADase) activity that operates in a single-turnover manner. Its product, adenosine diphosphate ribose, is not released but entrapped as a “molecular glue,” stabilizing a composite catalytic pocket with adaptor TIR domain–containing adaptor protein (TIRAP) to nucleate signalosome assembly. This “produce-and-trap” mechanism represents a signaling mode that integrates enzymatic activity with adaptor function to drive downstream signaling.

title: A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment
abstract: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. We analyzed 854,911 cells from 159 patients by single cell RNA sequencing and 39 samples by spatial transcriptomics, which identified 9 cell types and 60 cell states. Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

title: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space
abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants
abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
abstract: Submarine landslides threaten seabed infrastructure and trigger the transport of globally important amounts of sediment, carbon, and pollutants to deep-sea environments. However, fully submarine landslides have never been directly monitored in nature. Past hypotheses for their failure mechanism and dynamics therefore remain unvalidated for natural settings, including that prolonged upslope-migrating failures (breaching) occur in sandy seafloor environments. In this work, we present direct underwater monitoring of fully submarine landslides at Homathko Delta in western Canada that retrogress slowly upslope, indicating breaching-type failure. Their prolonged rather than instantaneous nature has important implications for the stress that seabed structures must be designed to withstand. Prolonged landslides also initiate sustained sediment flows (turbidity currents) that efficiently transport sediment, carbon, and pollutants further offshore.

title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
abstract: After the African origin of Homo sapiens , multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on ‘Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi ), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.

title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs
abstract: Nitrate pollution is widely perceived as a signature of human inputs. Here we show, with machine-learning reconstructed global maps, that climate aridity is also a dominant driver, systematically elevating nitrate concentrations across land-use gradients and creating unexpected hotspots beyond major agricultural and urban centers. Across ~2.9 million river segments worldwide, nitrate concentrations exceed ecological and health thresholds across ~33 and 2% of global land area, affecting ~5.6 billion (73%) and 0.5 billion (6%) people, respectively. Ecological threshold exceedance occurs mostly in headwaters, and about half of the health threshold exceedance occurs in middle-income countries and sparsely populated landscapes. These findings cast nitrate pollution as an aridity-amplified risk, suggesting that aridification may increase nitrate exposure even without additional human inputs. They call for regulatory standards that reflect risks across broad concentration ranges.

title: The genetic landscape of canine tumors: Insights from the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA)
abstract: The Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA, https://caninecancergenomeatlas.org/ ) is an open, accessible comparative oncology resource that harmonizes whole-exome data across 10 canine tumor histotypes. It aggregates 667 tumor-normal pairs with curated single-nucleotide variants, insertions and deletions, structural variants, and copy number aberrations. Cohort-depth stratification distinguished primary, exploratory, and descriptive analyses. Selection analyses identified 39 cancer drivers, including recurrent TP53 , PIK3CA , PTEN , SETD2 , MAP3K14 , and FAT4 alterations; copy number events included MYC amplifications and PTEN deletions. Direct comparison with matched human cancers revealed conserved and species-enriched oncogenic mechanisms, pathways, and therapeutic contexts. The CCGA standardizes alignment, variant calling, and annotation through consensus pipelines and provides downloadable data and interactive analyses. This reusable framework advances precision veterinary oncology and strengthens translational bridges to human cancer, supporting comparative and translational research.

title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca 2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes
abstract: Lysosomal Ca 2+ release from acidic stores is critical for lysosomal function, yet the molecular identity of the Ca 2+ uptake conduit has remained elusive. We used a Ca 2+ -imaging–based genetic screen of the lysosomal membrane proteome to identify TMEM184 family proteins as lysosomal Ca 2+ transporters (LyCaTs) essential for Ca 2+ uptake and refilling. TMEM184 selectively transported Ca 2+ while excluding monovalent cations. Loss of TMEM184B/C depleted lysosomal Ca 2+ stores, diminished Ca 2+ release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human TMEM184B mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca 2+ transport, and Tmem184b -deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca 2+ uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.

title: Geodetic observations in West Antarctica reveal geodynamically consistent 3D mantle viscosity
abstract: The rapid ice loss in West Antarctica since the 1990s has led to substantial ice surface lowering, regional bedrock uplift, and gravity reduction, as measured by geodetic observations. The bedrock (crustal) motions and gravity changes result from glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA), a process controlled by Earth’s viscoelastic properties and deglaciation history. In this study, we present GIA models with geodynamically consistent three-dimensional mantle viscoelastic structures and reconstructed ice history for Antarctica from 1900 to 2020, which explain both the observed Global Navigation Satellite System crustal motions and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment gravity changes in West Antarctica. This study demonstrates that a mantle rheology including a weak asthenosphere and temperature-dependent viscosity is consistent with both mantle convection at million-year timescales and ongoing decadal GIA occurring in West Antarctica.

title: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome outbreak linked to cruise ship travel in April–May 2026
abstract: In April 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. ANDV genome sequences were obtained for 10 of the 13 identified cases during a cross-country investigation established to share initial raw data for joint analysis with reciprocal quality control. The genomic data, symptom onsets, and plausible contact patterns strongly support a tightly linked outbreak cluster compatible with a single or very few zoonotic spillover events prior to embarkment followed by human-to-human transmission onboard. The outbreak represents the international displacement of a virus already known to be capable, under specific conditions, to transmit among humans, and does not suggest emergence of a unusual viral strain.

title: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak
abstract: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.

title: Early epidemiological and spatial assessment of the Bundibugyo virus outbreak 2026
abstract: A Bundibugyo virus outbreak was first reported on May 15th, 2026 in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with multiple cases reported across health zones during the early phase of the outbreak and suggestions of circulation weeks prior to detection. We pair highly resolved case and testing records with human mobility data to investigate the early outbreak dynamics of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD). We show that human movement was a principle driver of early spatial expansion between May 10th and June 1st when the number of health zones and health areas reporting positive cases increased by 12 and 49, respectively. The early doubling time was estimated at ~10 days. Our work shows the rapid spatial expansion and growth of BVD with implications for intervention strategies.

title: ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering drive extracellular vesicle budding from cilia
abstract: Cilia-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate cell-cell communication and remove signaling molecules from cilia. The Hedgehog receptor Smoothened (SMO) is selected for packaging into ciliary EVs by ubiquitin chains, but how cargo selection is coupled to EV budding remains unknown. In this work, working in mouse kidney cells, we found that the ubiquitin reader endosomal sorting complex required for transport–0 (ESCRT-0) orchestrates both cargo selection and EV biogenesis. Unlike the conventional ESCRT pathway, SMO secretion did not require the ESCRT-III membrane scission machinery. Instead, ESCRT-0 condensed at the ciliary tip, where it clustered ubiquitinated SMO to drive EV biogenesis. Disrupting ESCRT-0 condensation blocked SMO secretion, and combining forced recruitment of ESCRT-0 with optogenetic clustering of SMO was sufficient to reconstitute EV budding. Thus, ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering constitute a minimal module for ESCRT-III–independent reverse-topology budding.

title: Tracking danger on the peaks
abstract: The Earth is warming, but not all regions are warming equally. In high mountain areas, temperatures are generally increasing by 1.5 to 2 times the global average, sometimes with devastating consequences. A small or gradual change in the mountain cryosphere—perhaps progressive thawing of frozen ground or a flood from a small glacial lake—can suddenly turn into a cascade of catastrophes with enormous ramifications. Monitoring systems for the cryosphere in high mountain areas have traditionally been designed to look at individual components and changes. What are the temperature and depth of the permafrost, or how much area is covered by snow, and what is the related avalanche danger? Many of the monitoring and warning systems were designed for historical patterns of snowfall or rainfall, and a river gauge may no longer be adequate if there is greater flow in the rainy season, or increased sediment that could damage the gauge.

title: AI Can Do Your Homework. Now What-: Developing a Taxonomy of Computing Assessments That Accommodate GenAI Use
abstract: For decades, computing instructors have given students a specification, asked them to translate it into code, and evaluated the result against the specification. Coding agents can now complete most of these assessments with only a small number of prompts. Students who use AI this way learn neither what the assessment was meant to teach nor how to collaborate with AI effectively. Meanwhile, the rapid adoption of coding agents by developers is reshaping how technology is created. Working with them multiplies individual productivity, accelerates teams, and expands what computing can build. Agentic development is an important new skill. Students must learn it. Updated assessments are needed to teach it. This working group will map how computing educators are responding. In July 2026, we organized a public workshop convening computing educators to discuss how they intended to redesign assessments in response to AI and prepared a public report from those discussions. Then, we will survey computing educators to identify assessments that have been redesigned, replaced, or deliberately preserved, along with the rationale behind each choice. Finally, we will assemble what we discover into a taxonomy that can help future computing education researchers and practitioners design assessments that resist AI delegation and assessments that teach students to direct it.
journal: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Virtual Global Computing Education Conference V.2

title: Teaching Vibecoding: An Open Curriculum for AI-Assisted Software Development
abstract: Vibecoding, building software by stating intent to an AI in natural language instead of hand-coding it, is spreading quickly through industry and entrepreneurship. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 84% of developers reported using or planning to use AI coding tools, and Y Combinator, a startup accelerator, disclosed in early 2025 that a quarter of its most recent startup batch participants had codebases that were roughly 95% AI-generated. As the workforce moves in this direction, graduates need skills that conventional curricula, still built around writing code by hand, seldom teach directly, such as writing precise specifications, supervising AI coding agents, and verifying code that looks plausible but may be wrong or insecure. In a 2024 Cengage survey, 70% of recent graduates said training in generative AI should be integrated into coursework. We present Vibecoding: Introduction to Applied AI, an openly licensed curriculum, released early and still under active development. It comprises a textbook, lecture slides, a syllabus, and a hands-on lab for every chapter. The coursework runs from specification writing through building full-stack applications to critically evaluating AI-generated output. It is sequenced in this way so that students build competence with AI tools before confronting the shortcomings and limitations of such tools. We describe the curriculum's design and rationale while outlining our plan to pilot and evaluate it in the classroom.
journal: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Virtual Global Computing Education Conference V.2

title: ProseSpark: Preserving Student Agency in Computing Writing with an Agentic AI Companion
abstract: Computing students experience challenges with negative perceptions toward writing and communicating technical ideas. While generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) writing tools provide immediate support, they often generate complete written content, which may reduce students' active participation and sense of ownership. ProseSpark is introduced as a consent-based agentic AI writing companion designed to support computing students without writing on their behalf. ProseSpark is grounded in human-centered AI and self-regulated learning theory to maintain student autonomy and encourage active engagement throughout the writing process. This poster presents ProseSpark's design principles, platform, and responsible-AI safeguards. Future evaluation will examine how workflow-oriented AI support influences computing students' motivation, engagement, and writing self-efficacy.
journal: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Virtual Global Computing Education Conference V.2

title: A Competency Framework for Assessing AI-Assisted Programming Work
abstract: AI coding assistants have moved from autocomplete to agents that generate, run, and revise whole programs. As a result, software is increasingly being built by stating intent rather than writing code by hand. Furthermore, students are using these tools in their coursework. In an introductory course, 84 percent of students stated they used ChatGPT for their assignments, exposing a gap in assessment when these tools are at play. When an LLM writes the code, passing test suites alone does not show how well the student works with AI, because there are other expertise-revealing aspects of software development, like security. What separates a strong student (when AI is permitted) is how well they specify a task, direct an agent, and catch bad output. We present a competency framework that scores AI-assisted programming work along five competencies (problem solving, planning, prompting, verification, and agentic workflow) with an assessment design that offers three levels of AI availability. The framework runs in an online assessment platform we built and operate, and it reports interpretable results for each competency backed by evidence, though it is in early development and not yet widely used or validated. We describe the framework and its rationale while outlining a planned evaluation.
journal: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Virtual Global Computing Education Conference V.2

title: Embodied Conversational Agents as Rehearsal Partners for Developing Music Business Students' A&R Skills
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in higher education for assessment, tutoring, learning analytics, resource production and academic administration. An emerging area is the use of generative systems for music business education. Artists and Repertoire (A&R) professionals play a central role in finding new musical talent, shaping artistic direction, and connecting artists with songwriters and music producers. Preparing music business students for this role typically requires them to engage with real world artists, with whom they can develop their interviewing and other A&R skills. Using role play during the early stages of teaching can support students with developing their skills before they work with real artists. In this study, Ama, a fictional R&B and neo-soul musician realised through an embodied conversational agent, underwent preliminary design and formative evaluation. The agent was developed as an interactive rehearsal partner for students learning about the artists and repertoire process. Development involved using a combination of generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Copilot, Kling AI, Suno, Nano Banana, and Adobe Firefly, to develop the artist's lyrics and supporting media, thereby visualising the artist. Her profile was extended into a knowledge base, configuring the agent and refining its responses. The evaluation identified issues relating to response length, answer format, conversational naturalness, generative improvisation and latency. The study presents a prototype developed through iterative design, providing preliminary results and a foundation for further research with students using embodied conversational agents in the classroom.
journal: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Virtual Global Computing Education Conference V.2

title: Promoting Critical AI Literacy in the K–5 Computing Classroom
abstract: As many young children are already active users of AI tools, including voice assistants, building a critical understanding of how these tools work is an emerging goal for AI literacy. Yet, research in K–5 contexts is notably scarce. We use conversational agents (or 'chatbots') as an accessible, real-world context for exploring AI system design and anthropomorphism. In this paper, we describe a design-based study in which a three-lesson computing unit was co-designed with teachers to explore relevant AI concepts, including (i) rule-based vs (ii) data-driven systems and (iii) anthropomorphism as a design feature. We report preliminary findings from classroom observations and teacher interviews during the first design cycle and discuss their implications for the next cycle.
journal: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Virtual Global Computing Education Conference V.2

title: Exploring the Usability of Personality-Aware Conversational Agents in Intelligent Tutoring System
abstract: AI-driven adaptive learning environments are transforming per- sonalized education, yet most tutoring systems lack personality- aware feedback tailored to individual learning preferences. This paper presents a usability study evaluating Casey, an AI-powered conversational agent that dynamically assesses students' Big Five personality traits and adapts instructional support accordingly. Us- ing a mixed-methods approach (including interaction metrics and qualitative feedback), user engagement, perceived usability, and the impact of personality-based adaptation in coding education are analyzed. Findings reveal that personalized feedback may enhance engagement but also introduces usability challenges, particularly in balancing real-time guidance, cognitive load, and user auton- omy. The results provide actionable insights for improving adaptive tutoring systems by optimizing feedback clarity, navigation, and learner control. This work contributes to the field of AI-driven edu- cation by informing the design of intelligent tutoring systems that can enhance both engagement and usability at scale.

abstract: Respire 2.0 is an immersive VR artwork that transforms breathing into a spatial, sensory act. Using a respiration sensor, a Quest VR headset, and an AI musical agent, the installation translates internal rhythms into live generative audio and sculpture animation. The sound layer provides a co-breathing acoustic presence, shifting textures to mirror the participant's internal rhythms and reinforcing the sense of inhabiting a breathing organism.
