abstract: This course introduces the emerging paradigm of world foundation models (WFMs) and their role in enabling real-world physical AI systems. Those WFMs learn structured, multimodal representations of physical environments, supporting perception, prediction, and decision-making from a shared representation that spans vision, language, and action. The course connects foundation model concepts to dynamic visual environments, simulation, synthetic data generation, robotics, and sim-to-real deployment.

title: Artificial Intelligence Models to Predict Recurrence in Patients with Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: A PROBAST + AI Systematic Review of Clinical Applicability.
abstract: BACKGROUND Differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) generally carries an excellent prognosis, yet recurrence occurs in up to 8-9% of patients. Artificial intelligence (AI) models are increasingly proposed to predict DTC recurrence; however, their methodological quality and clinical readiness are poorly defined. We conducted a systematic review to evaluate the methodological quality, risk of bias, and applicability of these models using the PROBAST + AI framework. METHODS We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane databases, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to July 13, 2026. Eligible studies included original research developing or validating AI models for recurrence in DTC. Model quality (for development), risk of bias (for evaluation), and applicability were assessed using the PROBAST + AI framework, with a focus on discrimination, calibration, and validation strategies (PROSPERO; registration number [CRD420251004644]). RESULTS Of 673 records screened, 34 studies were included (21 unique datasets and 13 UCI-derived publications), encompassing 21,267 patients with a recurrence rate of 7.8%. Most were developed in Asian cohorts (17 of 21 datasets) and were structured clinical/tabular variables (82.4%), including demographic, clinical, laboratory, and pathological data, whereas the remaining models incorporated multimodal inputs such as imaging-derived or radiomic features. Notably, nearly one quarter of included studies (13 of 34, 38%) represented reanalysis of a single dataset. Discrimination was reported in 22 of 34 studies (64.7%) (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.67-1.00), though only 10 studies assessed calibration, none with standardized metrics. The PROBAST + AI assessment revealed high overall quality concerns in 26 of 34 (76.5%) development studies due to reliance on single-center cohorts, inadequate handling of missing data, and absence of external validation. Only 6 of 34 included studies (17.6%) were judged to have low overall quality concern, whereas 17 of 34 (50.0%) were rated as having low applicability concern. CONCLUSIONS AI models for predicting DTC recurrence show promising discriminatory performance but have substantial methodological shortcomings in development, and a lack of calibration and external validation necessary for clinical use. Given the guidelines' emphasis on risk-adapted de-escalation of therapy, the development of robust, validated, and clinically calibrated AI tools is a priority. Current evidence remains insufficient to support routine clinical use.

Environmental suitability for cultivation of sweetleaf, Stevia rebaudiana (Asteraceae, Eupatorieae), in South America: an ensemble species distribution modelling approach using bioclimatic and soil variables
abstract: Stevia rebaudiana (Bertoni) Bertoni is a South American crop of increasing agronomic relevance because its leaves accumulate steviol glycosides, high-intensity natural sweeteners used as low-calorie alternatives to sucrose. Although the species is native to Paraguay and adjacent regions, its cultivation has expanded beyond its native range, making the identification of suitable growing areas relevant for agricultural planning under climate change. Here, we modelled the current and future environmental suitability for S. rebaudiana cultivation in South America using cultivation records, bioclimatic variables, and soil predictors. We hypothesized that the main suitability core in southeastern South America would persist under mid-century climate change, with gains and losses concentrated primarily along its margins. A total of 142 georeferenced outdoor cultivation records were compiled from GBIF, iNaturalist, speciesLink, herbarium specimens, and specialized literature. After correlation filtering and exploratory variable selection, 13 predictors were retained, including eight bioclimatic and five edaphic variables. Models were calibrated under current environmental conditions using GLM, MaxEnt, and Random Forest within an ensemble species distribution modelling framework. Because GLM and MaxEnt showed the best balance between AUC and TSS, final current–future projections were based on these algorithms. Future suitability was projected for 2041-2060 under SSP245 and SSP585 using HadGEM3-GC31-LL, GISS-E2-1-G, and MIROC6 climate models combined with present-day soil predictors. Current suitability was highest in Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, Uruguay, and southern to southeastern Brazil. The main predictors were related to seasonal precipitation, annual temperature, and soil conditions. Future projections were consistent with this hypothesis, showing broad persistence of the main suitability core under both SSP245 and SSP585, with gains and losses concentrated mainly in marginal and transitional areas. Suitability gains exceeded losses under both scenarios, resulting in net increases in predicted suitable area of 14.15% and 10.92%, respectively. These results provide a spatial framework for identifying candidate regions for stevia cultivation and for prioritizing field validation under current and future environmental conditions.

title: Green Technological Innovation, Spatial Spillovers, and the Green Transformation of High-Tech Manufacturing in China
abstract: Green technological innovation is widely regarded as a key driver of sustainable industrial transformation, yet most existing research focuses on local effects and neglects spatial interdependence. Using panel data for 30 Chinese provinces from 2010 to 2024, this study measures green transformation performance (GTP) in high-tech manufacturing by integrating a network slacks-based measure (SBM) model with the Global Malmquist–Luenberger (GML) productivity index and estimates spatial Durbin models under multiple spatial weight matrices. The results show that green technological innovation significantly improves local GTP: the baseline coefficients of lagged green patents are positive and statistically significant across all specifications, ranging from 0.0216 to 0.0247, and the decomposed direct effects are consistently positive at approximately 0.025. The spatially lagged green innovation terms are also positive and significant under the three baseline matrices, and the decomposed indirect effects range from 0.051 to 0.129, while total effects range from 0.076 to 0.154, indicating positive but matrix-sensitive spatial spillovers. Heterogeneity analyses reveal pronounced differences between inland and coastal provinces and between regions with different manufacturing foundations: significant total effects are concentrated in coastal provinces and in regions with a high manufacturing foundation, whereas inland provinces show insignificant effects and low-manufacturing-foundation regions exhibit weaker or even negative effects under some matrices. These findings highlight that green transformation is shaped by both local innovation capacity and spatially mediated knowledge diffusion, and underscore the need for coordinated, regionally differentiated policies.

title: Lexico-syntactic complexity in human and AI-generated outputs across interpreting and translation: a paired-corpus study
abstract: This study examines differences in lexico-syntactic complexity between human translation outputs and AI-generated texts under interpreting and translation conditions, with implications for computer-assisted language learning (CALL) and translator/interpreter education. The dataset comprises 60 source segments and their corresponding human and AI outputs, yielding 120 texts. Human and AI texts were source-paired within each mode, while cross-mode comparisons were conducted using quasi-comparable corpora. Five lexical and eight syntactic complexity measures were analyzed to examine mode-related and agent-related differences. The results show dimension-specific mode dependence: AI-human differences in lexical complexity varied significantly across modes, whereas syntactic differences did not. Under the interpreting condition, AI-generated texts showed higher values on all five lexical measures, whereas human interpreting showed higher values on five syntactic measures. Under the translation condition, AI-human differences were reduced and confined to lexical density and sophistication, with no statistically significant differences on the eight syntactic measures. These findings suggest that AI-generated texts tend to display greater lexical concentration and written-like features, while human interpreting reflects characteristics of online language production and structural extension. Source-paired human and AI texts can serve as comparative resources for CALL and translator/interpreter training, helping learners critically evaluate AI outputs through linguistic features, textual evidence, and production conditions. Overall, AI-human complexity differences are not fixed properties of translation agents but vary according to complexity dimensions and production contexts.

title: Prognostic Factors in Lenvatinib-Treated Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: A Real-World Study with Extended Follow-Up.
abstract: BACKGROUND Lenvatinib is a standard first-line treatment for progressive radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (RAI-R DTC), but real-world outcomes over extended follow-up and prognostic factors remain insufficiently characterized. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed 97 patients with progressive RAI-R DTC treated with lenvatinib at a single institution between 2015 and 2024. Patients with anaplastic or medullary thyroid carcinoma and those treated for less than six months were excluded. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and prognostic factors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS Median age at treatment initiation was 68 years, and 38% of patients had bone metastases. With a median follow-up of 36 months, median PFS and OS were 25 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 21-31) and 59 months (95% CI, 45-82), respectively. The objective response rate was 58%, and the disease control rate was 97%. Multivariate analysis identified older age as an independent predictor of shorter PFS (Hazard ratio [HR] 1.34 per decade of age, p<0.01) and OS (HR 1.63 per decade of age, p<0.005). Bone metastasis was independently associated with worse OS (HR 2.25, p<0.05) but not PFS. Receiver operating characteristic analyses suggested age cutoffs of approximately 70 years. Bone metastasis was associated with significantly poorer OS among older patients. CONCLUSIONS Lenvatinib provided durable disease control in patients with RAI-R DTC. Older age at treatment initiation and bone metastasis were independent determinants of survival and may help guide risk stratification and treatment timing in clinical practice.

title: Soil fertility response to land-use changes in agroforestry and silvopastoral systems of the Ecuadorian Amazon: A multivariate and stratification ratio approach
abstract: Conversion of Amazonian forests to pastures and crops threatens soil fertility, but whether tree-based land uses conserve it remains poorly quantified in the Ecuadorian Amazon. We compared a secondary forest (SF, reference) with a cacao agroforestry system (AFC), two silvopastoral systems (Axonopus scoparius and Paspalum dilatatum pastures with trees; GGWT, DGWT) and the same pastures without trees (GGWIT, DGWIT) in Napo and Pastaza provinces. Each land use comprised three plots (5 – 7 sampling points each) sampled at 0 – 10 and 10 – 30 cm (184 samples). Land-use effects were tested with linear mixed models with plot as a random effect. In the topsoil, land use affected aeration porosity (AP; 11.4 % in AFC to 19.2 % in SF), soil organic matter (SOM; 8.5 % in GGWIT to 17.9 % in GGWT) and exchangeable K+ (0.09 cmolc/kg in AFC vs. 0.22 – 0.28 cmolc/kg in GGWT, DGWT and DGWIT), whereas bulk density, pH, total N, available P, Ca2+ and Mg2+ did not differ significantly. Relative to SF, AP decreased by 15 % – 41 % in all land uses, SOM by 47 % in GGWIT and K+ by 43 % in AFC. Most nutrients were concentrated in the topsoil. Stocks in the 0 – 30 cm layer of exchangeable K+ (53 – 102 kg/ha) and, except in DGWT, of available P (6.5 – 22.2 kg/ha) were below forest-maintenance thresholds, whereas NH4+ stocks were highest in treeless pastures and lowest in AFC. Multivariate analyses isolated AFC and grouped the silvopastoral systems with SF. Retaining trees in pastures and replenishing K and P in cacao agroforestry systems are recommended.

title: Serum circFUT8 in gastric cancer: Diagnostic performance and clinicopathological associations.
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality, and biomarkers that complement current diagnostic approaches are needed. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are promising biomarker candidates because of their stability. We characterized circFUT8 and evaluated its potential as an auxiliary serum biomarker for GC. Its circular structure and stability were assessed by back-splice junction validation, freeze-thaw and room-temperature stability assays, actinomycin D treatment, and ribonuclease R (RNase R) digestion. Real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was used to measure circFUT8 expression in 45 pairs of GC and adjacent non-tumor tissues and in serum from 102 patients with GC, 32 patients with gastritis, and 78 healthy controls. CircFUT8 was generated by back-splicing of exons 3-6 of FUT8 and showed a distinct back-splice junction, stability under the tested conditions, and resistance to RNase R digestion. CircFUT8 expression was increased in GC tissues and serum. Serum circFUT8 distinguished GC from healthy controls, gastritis, and pooled non-GC controls, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.725, 0.756, and 0.734, respectively. Combining circFUT8 with carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and CA19-9 yielded the highest apparent AUC of 0.765 against healthy controls (optimism-corrected AUC, 0.756). However, the combined models did not significantly outperform circFUT8 alone. Higher serum circFUT8 levels, analyzed as a continuous variable, were associated with poorly differentiated or undifferentiated histology, lymph node metastasis, higher T stages, and advanced tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) stages. CircFUT8 also showed modest discriminatory performance for T1 and TNM stage I-II disease in exploratory analyses. These findings support serum circFUT8 as a candidate auxiliary biomarker for GC, pending validation in larger, independent cohorts.

title: Lightweight Attention-Enhanced DeepLabV3+ for Agricultural Land Segmentation and AI-Assisted Decision-Making Using Remote Sensing Images
abstract: The detection involves correctly categorizing the smishing message and Accurate agricultural land-cover segmentation can provide a spatial evidence layer for land-use assessment and agricultural planning, but image heterogeneity, class ambiguity and the cost of high-resolution inference complicate its use. This study evaluates a lightweight DeepLabV3+ segmentation configuration with an ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 encoder and a post-decoder Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention module. The framework was assessed on the DeepGlobe Land Cover Classification dataset using an existing crop-based evaluation protocol. The reported experiments yield an Agriculture-class Intersection over Union (IoU) of 77.68%, a six-class mean IoU (mIoU) of 69.42%, overall accuracy of 94.05%, and approximately 14 million model parameters. Relative to the reported ResNet50-based DeepLabV3+ configuration (approximately 41 million parameters), the proposed configuration has about 65.9% fewer parameters. Beyond the segmentation contribution, this study specifies a conceptual, human-supervised decision-support pathway in which predicted agricultural masks could inform land-cover summaries, spatial review and field-verification priorities. That pathway is an interpretation of the existing segmentation outputs, not an experimentally implemented or validated decision-support system. The findings support the potential relevance of a compact segmentation model to agricultural information workflows, subject to confirmation of evaluation-set reporting, uncertainty handling, georeferencing and operational decision utility.

title: A Comprehensive Review of the Physics Involved in Modelling Transport Phenomena Associated with Extrusion-Deposition Additive Manufacturing Process
abstract: The dilemma of most upcoming researchers in the field of fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) composite processing is not the lack or accessibility to relevant background literature but rather their comprehensive nature, or their applicability to the specific needs of the researcher. Most existing literature either target just a specific modeling aspect or present high-level overview of the overall FRP process which lacks necessary underlying physics, coupling across hierarchical physics scales and computational techniques needed to improve on existing process simulation tools without necessarily reinventing the wheel. The current review article presents detailed understanding of the overall FRP composite process, the relevant transport phenomena and underlying physics across various scales and current trends in computational solution techniques used to predict FRP composite melt-flow phenomena in order to develop well equipped process-structure-property (PSP) maps for improved process monitoring and optimized print properties and performance. The overall position of potential research opportunities from survey of existing simulation efforts includes (i) the refinement of existing and development of new quantitative and qualitative multiscale models for predicting transport phenomena, (ii) development of new closed-form tensor evolution equations and constitutive relations with new information of the bulk fiber and melt-flow field states, and (iii) proper model benchmarking with experimental observation from in-situ process monitoring, and development of machine learning tools for the creation of a robust PSP map.

title: Estimand-Relative Validity and Context-Driven Instability of Shapley Explanations for Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Shapley explanations for tabular foundation models depend on a removal operator that determines how predictions are evaluated when features are absent. Although different operators induce different cooperative games, their effects on attribution validity and stability in in-context tabular models remain insufficiently understood. We compare five removal operators for TabPFN v2 and TabICL v2 using exact Shapley enumeration, controlled synthetic data with known or high-precision reference attributions, real-world tabular datasets, and a preregistered factorial design. Operator performance was strongly estimand-dependent. Mean imputation and missing-value encoding most closely approximated interventional attributions, whereas recontextualisation and conditional estimation through in-context learning yielded the lowest errors for the conditional estimand; these rankings also varied with feature dependence. Across nuisance configurations, attribution variability was dominated by the sampled in-context examples, while column order, label coding, and model seed contributed little. A planted-null-feature control further showed that both models frequently changed their predictions in response to features constructed to contain no label information. The analysis is limited to two binary-classification foundation models and exact enumeration in low-dimensional settings, so the observed rankings should not be extrapolated to larger feature spaces or other model families. These findings show that Shapley explanations for tabular foundation models are not interpretable without specifying both the removal operator and the intended estimand, and that context sensitivity should be reported as part of explanation reliability.

title: Incentive-Responsive Agents: A Principal-Agent Framework, Metric Suite, and Runtime Architecture for Long-Lived Personal AI Agents
abstract: Personal AI agents now persist: they hold accounts, mailboxes, long-term memory, and open-ended task streams, yet the dominant way to improve them remains capability-side: prompt engineering, larger models, longer thinking, and retrieval. We argue that long-lived agents are missing an incentive layer. We formalize an incentive not as text in a prompt but as a runtime contract over the agent's operating point (model tier, test-time compute, memory budget, tool authority, task priority, verification, and compensation) that the agent's policy must causally consume. We develop a principal-agent model with hidden effort, a contractible operating point, and costly verification. We derive (i) a non-consumption invariance principle separating genuine incentives from prompt-level persuasion, (ii) a persistence-as-discount theorem making identity continuity a precondition for sustained effort, (iii) an incentive-capability exchange-rate frontier yielding a per-task routing rule, and (iv) a Goodhart bound for multi-channel verification, plus a three-channel decomposition of mechanism gains (allocation, verification, continuation). A 240-run real-LLM experiment with two models and 60 verifiable tasks shows that prompt-level incentive framing has no detectable effect (p = 0.62), whereas runtime allocation raises success on the hardest task family from 0.60 to 1.00 (p = 0.008) at 4.8x price-weighted cost; the exchange-rate theorem predicts the break-even baseline at 0.21. A 20-seed, 3,000-task simulation shows resource ROI rising from 7.09 to 16.67 and gaming falling from 0.333 to 0.115. Code, simulator, and all results are released; live deployment remains future work.

title: Bone Marrow Stem Cells Augmented with Tendon Tissue Lysate Promote Enhanced Achilles Tendon Healing.
abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE Tendon injuries, particularly of the Achilles tendon, are common in both athletic and aging populations. Conventional repair strategies often result in suboptimal healing due to the inherent avascularity and limited regenerative potential of tendon tissue. For tendon regeneration, stem cells have become a promising treatment option. Preconditioning Bone Marrow- Derived Stem Cells (BMSCs) with Tendon Tissue Lysate (TTL), a heterogeneous tissue-derived preparation, may influence tenogenic differentiation. The objective of the study was to evaluate the effect of tendon tissue lysate preconditioning on Bone Marrow-Derived Stem Cells (BMSCs) viability and tenogenic biomarker expression in a rat model of Achilles tendon injury. METHODS Both in vitro and in vivo evaluations were performed. Bone Marrow-Derived Stem Cells (BMSCs) were isolated from rats, cultured, and treated with Tendon Tissue Lysate (TTL). Cell viability was assessed using MTT, crystal violet, and trypan blue assays. Tenogenic differentiation was evaluated via ELISA for Tenomodulin and TGF-β1. For in vivo assessment, forty Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly divided into four groups (n=10/group): (1) healthy control, (2) tendon injury only, (3) injury treated with BMSCs, and (4) tendon injury treated with BMSCs preconditioned with TTL. Achilles tendon injury was induced in groups 2-4, followed by treatments via direct injection into the injury site in groups 3 and 4, except group 2. Serum biomarkers (CRP, IL-6, TGF-β1, TNMD) were quantified, and further tendon healing was evaluated histologically. RESULTS TTL did not significantly affect viability. Morphology and ELISA indicated a favorable tenogenic response at 100 μg/mL. In vivo, rats treated with TTL-preconditioned BMSCs demonstrated more organized tendon histology, increased TNMD and TGF-β1 levels, and reduced CRP and IL-6 compared to other groups. DISCUSSION The results suggest that Tendon Tissue Lysate (TTL) may support tenogenic differentiation of BMSCs. TTL may provide an optimum microenvironment that supports tendon repair. Increased levels of TNMD and TGF-β1 are consistent with tendon maturation and extracellular remodeling. Histological analysis shows improvement in collagen alignment. CONCLUSION Overall, preconditioning of BMSCs with tendon tissue lysate was associated with favorable tenogenic, inflammatory, and histological changes related to tendon repair. TTL represents a promising biological adjunct for optimizing stem cell-based therapies in tendon tissue engineering.

title: An online-learned eddy parameterization in a differentiable shallow water model
abstract: Ocean general circulation models rely on parameterizations to approximate subgrid-scale processes. While parameterizations are traditionally physics-based, machine learning has recently provided an alternative, data-driven approach for developing parameterizations. However, most machine learning-based parameterizations are learned offline due to the lack of differentiable general circulation models. Here, we train an eddy momentum parameterization represented by a neural network online in an idealized barotropic gyre model. We develop the model as fully differentiable in Julia with the automatic differentiation tool Enzyme. The network weights are trained using a loss function that has the same form as in adjoint-based data assimilation, with synthetic observations generated by a fine-resolution simulation. A range of diagnostics evaluate the performance of the parameterized coarse-resolution model. We find improved energetics, physically realistic dynamics, and numerical stability for multi-decadal roll-outs. Importantly, the online-learned parameterization absorbs artifacts from the numerical discretization, such as the time-stepping scheme used, which is invisible to offline-learned parameterizations. We suggest that this is key to improved numerical stability of machine-learned parameterizations. Our research suggests that online-trained neural network parameterizations can be an effective solution to the subgrid-scale parameterization and model calibration problem.

title: Beyond Scarce Labels: Foundation Models for Mapping Oil, Gas, and Power Infrastructure
abstract: Foundation models recognize objects in overhead imagery, but operational Earth observation must also discover unfamiliar assets, separate facilities from equipment, localize them across scales, and explain each conclusion. Industry-specific geospatial datasets are scarce: energy taxonomies are specialized, labels are geographically uneven, and expert annotation is slow and costly. We present a training-free workflow with a provider-agnostic interface that organizes pretrained vision-language, open-vocabulary detection, and segmentation models as a structured geospatial observer. A scene model proposes candidate asset types, counts, and expected patterns. A bounded evidence policy decides where to look more closely, and a typed evidence graph consolidates proposals, preserves facility-equipment relations, arbitrates duplicates, and gates local geometry for dense or repeated structures. Each output is a record with confidence, provenance, processing cost, and explicit uncertainty. Evaluation uses frozen protocols, paired controls, and predeclared claim boundaries. On 300 external aerial images of wind infrastructure, processed without any benchmark taxonomy in the prompts, target-discovery F1 is 0.966 (95% CI 0.943–0.985) versus 0.816 for a fixed-vocabulary open-vocabulary detector, while box localization is weaker (F1 0.209 versus 0.316). On 300 label-blind French aerial images, it raises 11 false alarms on 167 rooftops without solar panels versus 111 for OWLv2, at lower recall (0.52 versus 0.95). On 60 site-disjoint energy sites (well pads, pumpjacks, refineries, terminals, compressor and processing sites, substations, power plants), processed with the benchmark taxonomy declared, entity-center F1 (0.553) far exceeds strict box F1 (0.255): assets are often found but their extent is mis-drawn. The full workflow improves strict F1 by 0.034 over flat fusion of the same primary proposals, and graph-gated local geometry recovers dense repeated objects on DIOR (+0.037 strict F1). Rare-energy scene classification does not outperform a matched vision-language baseline. The workflow can shift scarce expert effort from exhaustive annotation toward verification. Facility extent and open-taxonomy discovery remain the main limitations.

title: Reproduction of land resources in the agricultural sector of a region’s agro-industrial complex: process analysis and management prospects
abstract: The state of agricultural land resources and its impact on economic results are analyzed. The material is presented in three sections. The first of them analyzes the state, dynamics and factors of reproduction and management of the most important component of land resources – soil fertility, its role in increasing the economic efficiency of land use. The problems are highlighted, and the need to find new scientifically sound methods and technologies in the agricultural sector is pointed out. There are some negative phenomena. In the light of the problems of managing the reproduction of land resources (second section), this process is considered as the interaction and development of internal and external factors, including scientific and technological progress, ensuring high efficiency of agricultural production. The economic section discusses the issues of land use efficiency. The results of land use in different soil-climatic zones and microzones are compared. In conclusion, it is pointed out the need to adapt modern agriculture to new developments in government policy, including in connection with the development of a unified digital platform for the agro-industrial and fisheries complexes of the country.

title: What should AI agents know? Explicit knowledge for trustworthy, sustainable materials research
abstract: Artificial intelligence can propose materials, interpret measurements and increasingly coordinate experiments. Yet reliable scientific autonomy requires more than capable models: research systems must preserve what is known, where evidence came from and which actions are justified. We argue that machine-actionable scientific knowledge is essential for trustworthy autonomous research, and that ontologygrounded knowledge graphs are a particularly powerful way of achieving it when scientific meaning must be shared across disciplines, systems and scales. Using The World Avatar (TWA) as a case study, we examine how ontologies, dynamic knowledge graphs and software agents connect models, literature, experiments and laboratory assets, and how ontology-derived tools can constrain large language model (LLM) actions. A reported design-to-synthesis study of a new metal–organic polyhedron demonstrates the integration of previously separate tasks, but not yet an environmental benefit or fully autonomous discovery. A material-passport example further shows how shared semantics can support industrial circularity assessment. We distinguish structural validation from scientific verification, and circularity indicators from demonstrated environmental benefits. The priority is not to create a universal platform but to build evidence-preserving research infrastructure whose scientific and sustainability benefits can be tested.

title: MULTIMODAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR EARLY PLANT STRESS PREDICTION: A REVIEW
abstract: Plant stress is one of the primary limitations to crop growth, yield, and quality and can result from various abiotic and biotic stresses, including drought, extreme temperatures, salinity, nutrient imbalance, pathogens, and insect pests. Early detection of plant stress is crucial for enabling timely intervention and preventing potential crop losses. In recent years, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for automated plant health assessment has gained increasing attention through image-based deep learning and sensor-based machine learning techniques. However, single-modality approaches may have limited capability to capture the complex relationships between plant visual characteristics and environmental conditions. Multimodal AI can address this limitation by integrating complementary information from visual modalities, such as RGB, thermal, multispectral, and hyperspectral imaging, with environmental indicators, including temperature, humidity, soil moisture, light intensity, and weather conditions. In AI-based plant stress assessment, with a particular focus on multimodal data fusion and early stress prediction. AI architectures, data fusion methods, datasets, sensing modalities, and explainable AI (XAI) techniques are examined in detail. Furthermore, key challenges associated with multimodal dataset collection, sensor synchronization, environmental variability, model generalization, computational requirements, and real-world deployment are discussed. Finally, promising research directions, including temporal multimodal learning, edge AI, explainable multimodal models, low-cost sensing technologies, and foundation models for plant science, are highlighted.
journal: SARPS: Journal of Advanced Research in Plant Science

title: Total-Body 18F-FAPI PET/CT for Assessment of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Pilot Study.
abstract: Liver biopsy remains the gold standard for fibrosis assessment; however, its invasiveness limits its suitability for routine clinical use. The rising prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) as a leading cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma underscores the need for reliable noninvasive assessment. Current noninvasive imaging methods provide surrogate measures of fibrosis but do not directly assess fibrogenic activity. In contrast, fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET enables molecular imaging of activated fibroblasts, a key driver of fibrosis. This study evaluates dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET imaging to assess hepatic fibrogenic activity in MASLD. Methods: In this prospective pilot study, 10 subjects (3 healthy volunteers, 4 patients with mild-moderate fibrosis, and 3 patients with advanced fibrosis) underwent 60-min dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET/CT. SUV and blood-normalized SUV ratio (SUVR) were quantified across time frames, and the net influx rate was derived from dynamic data. MR elastography-derived liver stiffness values were obtained for comparison. Correlations with histologic fibrosis scoring of biopsy tissue were assessed using Spearman analysis. Results: At 5 min postinjection, SUVR correlated strongly with histologic fibrosis score (ρ = 0.95; 95% CI, 0.75-1.00; P = 1.89 × 10-5), followed by SUV (ρ = 0.78; 95% CI, 0.23-0.98; P = 0.0077) and net influx rate from kinetic modeling (ρ = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.41-0.98; P = 0.0022). SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval allowed clearer differentiation among healthy volunteers, patients with mild fibrosis, and patients with advanced fibrosis. Conclusion: Dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET enables quantitative visualization of hepatic fibroblast activation in MASLD. SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval correlates more strongly with fibrosis severity, supporting 18F-FAPI-74 PET as a promising molecular biomarker for assessing and potentially monitoring metabolic fibrosis.
journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine

title: Designing AI-Agents with Personalities: A Psychometric Approach
abstract: We introduce a methodology for assigning quantifiable and psychometrically validated personalities to AI-Agents using the Big Five framework. Across three studies, we evaluate its feasibility and limitations. In Study 1, we show that large language models (LLMs) capture semantic similarities among Big Five measures, providing a basis for personality assignment. In Study 2, we create AI-Agents using prompts designed based on the Big Five Inventory-2 (BFI-2) in different format, and find that AI-Agents powered by new models align more closely with human responses on the Mini-Markers test, although the finer pattern of results (e.g., factor loading patterns) were sometimes inconsistent. In Study 3, we validate our AI-Agents on risk-taking and moral dilemma vignettes, finding that models prompted with the BFI-2-Expanded format most closely reproduce human personality-decision associations, while safety-aligned models generally inflate ‘moral’ ratings. Overall, our results show that AI-Agents align with humans in correlations between input Big Five traits and output responses and may serve as useful tools for preliminary research. Nevertheless, discrepancies in finer response patterns indicate that AI-Agents cannot (yet) fully substitute for human participants in precision or high-stakes projects.

title: Forecasting Cohort Fertility with a Simple Neural Network
abstract: Forecasting completed cohort fertility (CCF) helps resolve ambiguities in total fertility rate (TFR) trends, yet conventional cohort forecasting methods perform little better than a freeze-rate baseline (Bohk-Ewald et al., 2018). Inspired by deep learning advances in mortality forecasting, this paper tests whether an untuned ensemble of Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs), named CCF-Net, can improve cohort fertility forecasts. Using data from the Human Fertility Database and the models and evaluation criteria of Bohk-Ewald et al. (2018), CCF-Net ranks first among established methods. On average across jump-off years 1985–2013, CCF-Net forecasts higher CCF than other methods; it appears to better capture rises in fertility among some cohorts born in the late 1970s and early 1980s. However, its accuracy varies considerably across jump-off years, and it falls behind other methods in 2006–2011. When trained on data through 2019, CCF-Net forecasts substantially and perhaps unrealistically lower CCF than all benchmarks, which raises doubts about whether its historical performance will continue.
