title: Revenue Management Practices and Its Impact on Hotel Performance in Nepal
abstract: Revenue management (RM) is now an essential strategic instrument in the competitive and price conscious hotel industry of Nepal. Nevertheless, there is still a lack of empirical data to support the claim that particular RM practices are correlated with quantifiable hotel performance indicators within Nepal context. Thus, this study aims to investigate the effect of five revenue management practices such as dynamic pricing, demand forecasting, market segmentation, channel management, and inventory control on hotel performance among the three-, four-, and five-star hotels of Kathmandu, Pokhara, and Chitwan. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design, which is guided by the Yield Management Theory. 121 hotel managers and operational personnel were used as the sample to complete a structured questionnaire used for the data collection. The SPSS 20 analysis of multiple regression demonstrated that all the five RM practices have a significant and positive effect on hotel performance (R² = 0.537, F = 47.806, p < 0.001), distribution channel management (β = 0.277), inventory control (β = 0.250), and dynamic pricing (β = 0.226) were found to be the strongest predictors. The study findings are that the implementation of revenue management has a positive and significant impact on the hotel performance in Nepal. The three dimensions of RM practices that were the most strongly associated with hotel performance were distribution channel management, inventory control and dynamic pricing. The results revealed that the systematic implementation of revenue management practices can facilitate the hotels in Nepal to achieve high occupancy, revenue generation, pricing efficiency and overall operational performance. So, the study highlights the need of integrated and data-driven revenue management strategies in the Nepalese hospitality sector.
journal: Techspire Journal of Innovation, Technology and Management

title: Soil reclamation induced salinity decline is associated with shifts in bacterial, fungal and protistan communities and higher wheat yield in saline-alkali fields
abstract: Soil reclamation is widely practiced in saline–alkali land areas. However, limited research has focused on how reclamation duration regulates soil microbial communities and crop yield via modifying soil environmental conditions. In this study, high-throughput sequencing, ecological network analysis, and soil physicochemical characterization were integrated to investigate variations in soil properties, microbial community composition, and crop yield across saline–alkali fields with different reclamation durations (1, 5, and 10 years). The results showed that prolonged reclamation significantly reduced soil salinity and increased soil nutrient contents as well as wheat yield. The richness of fungi and protists increased with the extension of reclamation durations, whereas bacterial richness exhibited an opposite trend. Network-associated key taxa of bacteria, fungi and protists were significantly correlated with wheat yield, soil salinity, soil organic matter (SOM), total nitrogen (TN), as well as the activities of leucine aminopeptidase (LAP) and β-glucosidase (Glu). Structural equation modeling (SEM) further revealed that soil salinity was associated with soil physicochemical traits, network-associated key taxa and enzyme activities, altered the soil microecological environment, and ultimately affected wheat yield. In conclusion, reclamation durations mitigated soil salinity, which drove the screening of microbial taxa by soil microhabitats and reconstructed the overall microbial community structure, thereby influencing wheat productivity. These findings provide theoretical and technical support for the sustainable reclamation of saline–alkali land, health management of farmland soil, and stable improvement of grain productivity.

title: Multimodal brain lesion classification approach through MRI radiomics and OCR-recovered MRS metabolites with explainable AI
abstract: This work presents a multimodal machine learning pipeline for brain lesion classification, fusing structural radiomic features from multi-sequence MRI (T2-FLAIR, T1-contrast) with metabolic features recovered from Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (MRS) screenshots via a custom Optical Character Recognition (OCR) pipeline. The study draws on a clinical cohort of 55 patients (17 non-neoplastic, 38 neoplastic). MRI radiomics span first-order intensity statistics, Grey-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture, morphological shape, and contrast-enhancement ratios, while MRS metabolites (Cho, Cr, NAA, and their ratios) are lifted from rendered spectra through Tesseract OCR with multi-region cropping and Lanczos upsampling. Features are evaluated under a leakage-controlled Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV) protocol with in-fold imputation, feature selection and normalization, using the classifier’s default decision threshold. The primary, bias-corrected performance estimate comes from nested LOOCV, in which classifier family and feature count are chosen using training data only: the multimodal pipeline reaches 82.0% accuracy. The best fixed configuration (Random Forest, k = 3) reaches 85.5% accuracy (47/55) and AUC = 0.82, but because it is selected on the same data it is scored on, it is reported as an exploratory, optimistic figure. The comparison model, which uses MRI-derived features without OCR-recovered metabolites, reaches 78.2% at its own best configuration, so the best-configuration gain is +7.3 percentage points and the nested estimate exceeds that baseline by +3.8 points. The two strongest discriminators are log NAA ( F = 16.01) and log Cho ( F = 12.89). The best-configuration result holds under 1,000-permutation testing (random-label mean 55.0%) and McNemar’s exact test ( p = 0.05, borderline). At N = 55, and with diagnostic labels that themselves drew on MRS, these results stand as proof-of-concept: OCR-recovered MRS metabolites are informative for reproducing expert diagnostic judgment beyond what MRI-derived features supply alone.

title: The theoretical and applied implications of self-compassion in the Career Construction Model of Adaptation
abstract: Emotional processes underlying career adaptability remain underexplored. The Career Construction Model of Adaptation (CCMA) asserts that psychological resources of concern, curiosity, control, and confidence promote successful career transitions. This conceptual paper proposes a potential fifth adaptive resource, self-compassion, within the Career Construction Model of Adaptation. Self-compassion adds novelty to the model by theorizing an emotional mechanism that may promote successful career transitions. The proposed theoretical framework differentiates self-compassion from the original adaptive resources and uses a fictional vignette to illustrate clinical application. Limitations of the proposed model are acknowledged. Research, clinical, educational, and organizational implications are discussed.

title: MVMamba-Seg: a precise multimodal segmentation method for tomato disease monitoring via efficient Vision Mamba
abstract: Accurate segmentation of tomato leaf lesions is essential for disease diagnosis, severity assessment, and precision crop protection, yet field images contain complex backgrounds, diverse lesion appearances, irregular boundaries, and confusing foreground-background transitions. We propose MVMamba-Seg, a text-guided multimodal Vision Mamba network that couples CNN and Vision Mamba streams with BERT-encoded expert descriptions for efficient global modeling. Dynamic Difference-Driven Feature Enhancement (DDFE) explicitly models foreground, background, and uncertainty branches, while the SSM Spatial Reweighting Attention Module (SSM-SRAM) refines skip connections and suppresses background noise. On a self-built dataset, MVMamba-Seg achieves 94.32% Dice and 89.26% mIoU using expert text; in cross-domain evaluation on PlantVillage, it achieves 81.82% Dice and 69.24% mIoU with 21.89M parameters. Compared with a Transformer-based counterpart, the Vision Mamba variant reduces parameters by approximately 31%, FLOPs by 42.8%, and improves inference speed by 60.1%. Through efficient global modeling with Mamba and the integration of expert disease descriptions with visual features, the framework delineates lesion contours and spatial distributions to support tomato disease monitoring and targeted crop protection.

title: Beyond affective coping and use frequency: academic rumination, generative AI dependency, and two dimensions of perceived cognitive debt
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support learning and emotion regulation, yet frequent or coping-oriented use does not necessarily constitute difficult-to-regulate dependency. It remains unclear how academic rumination and affective coping are positioned relative to dependency and whether dependency is differentially associated with perceived costs to knowledge internalization and independent reasoning. This study examined these distinctions within a single educational psychology model. A cross-sectional survey included 611 current GenAI users recruited through university settings in Tianjin, China (91.7% first-year students). Dependency was a continuous, nonclinical tendency. Ordinal CFA and WLSMV SEM evaluated a prespecified partial association model. Covariate adjustment, four alternative measurement specifications, an AR-score hybrid, and observed-score regressions assessed sensitivity. In the reference model, academic rumination was associated with affective coping (β = 0.283), and both were associated with dependency (β = 0.187 and 0.555). Dependency was associated with perceived internalization/memory debt (β = 0.550) and independent-reasoning debt (β = 0.644); their standardized difference was 0.095 (95% Monte Carlo CI [0.032, 0.157]). The corresponding observed-score coefficients were 0.413 and 0.518, with a difference of 0.105 (95% bootstrap CI [0.035, 0.175]). Both serial coefficient products remained positive, but the negative conditional coping-internalization association was not sustained in the observed-score analysis. Reported frequency had no unique association in the combined adjusted model. Alternative measurement models retained robust RMSEA of 0.090–0.097; robust hybrid indices were unavailable. The results provide tentative evidence of differentiated self-reported associations among coping, frequency, dependency, and cognitive concerns. Measurement misfit remains unresolved, and the coping-outcome coefficients were sensitive to construct representation. Observed-score consistency for dependency and serial products does not validate the latent structure or establish temporal or causal mediation. These predominantly first-year, Tianjin-based cross-sectional data do not establish objective cognitive decline or generality across student populations.

title: Preliminary diagnostic performance of the MOXO continuous performance test in young adults undergoing ADHD assessment
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) diagnosis in young adults is often challenging due to symptom overlap with affective disorders and the inherent subjectivity of clinical evaluations. While Continuous Performance Tests (CPTs) provide objective metrics, their preliminary diagnostic performance and concordance with clinical evaluations relative to self-report questionnaires require evaluation in clinical settings. This study explored the diagnostic performance of the MOXO-CPT and formally examined its incremental predictive value beyond commonly used self-report measures in young adults assessed for ADHD. A total of 118 young adults (aged 18–25 years) consecutively referred with attention-related complaints completed the MOXO-CPT and self-report scales (ASRS, WURS-25, STAI, RRS-SF). ADHD diagnoses were established via comprehensive semi-structured clinical interviews based on DSM-5 criteria by an experienced psychiatrist blinded to test and questionnaire scores. Multivariable logistic regression and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analyses evaluated independent predictors and discriminative performance relative to this clinical reference standard. ADHD was diagnosed in 58.5% (n=69) of the cohort, while the remaining 41.5% (n=49) comprised a clinical comparison group predominantly presenting with alternative psychiatric conditions (63.3%). Participants with ADHD showed poorer performance across all MOXO-CPT indices (attention, timing, impulsivity, and hyperactivity) compared to the non-ADHD clinical comparison group. In multivariable modeling, average or above-average performance on the attention and hyperactivity indices was independently associated with a lower likelihood of ADHD diagnosis. ROC analysis indicated that the MOXO-CPT attention index demonstrated favorable discriminative capacity relative to the clinical diagnosis (AUC = 0.87, sensitivity = 81.2%, specificity = 85.7%), whereas other indices showed acceptable-to-poor discriminative performance. In this help-seeking sample of young adults, the MOXO-CPT attention index demonstrated promising discriminative ability in differentiating ADHD from a non-ADHD clinical comparison group predominantly presenting with anxiety and depressive disorders. These preliminary findings suggest that distractor-embedded continuous performance testing may serve as a useful objective adjunct for distinguishing ADHD from common psychiatric mimics in outpatient settings, rather than a stand-alone tool or a general screening instrument for healthy populations.

title: Computational fluid dynamics for active solar drying of tuber crops: a critical narrative review of modelling, validation and optimisation evidence and its transferability
abstract: Cassava ( Manihot esculenta ), yam ( Dioscorea spp.) and sweet potato ( Ipomoea batatas ) are highly perishable after harvest, and active (forced-convection) solar drying can reduce losses with little external energy. Dryer performance is governed by coupled airflow, heat transfer and moisture transport, which computational fluid dynamics (CFD) can resolve in principle. This critical narrative review appraises how far CFD and complementary models currently support the design, validation and optimisation of active solar dryers for tuber crops. A documented, non-exhaustive search of Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar (to 30 September 2026), supplemented by citation chaining, was used. Evidence was classified into four tiers: direct tuber CFD; tuber-specific non-CFD numerical models; tuber experimental and kinetic studies; and transferable CFD or multiphysics studies of solar dryers for other products. Studies were compared on governing equations, turbulence and radiation treatment, product and moisture representation, numerical verification and validation error. The review is not systematic and does not report a PRISMA flow diagram or pooled estimates. Of the 41 sources cited, 14 are primary studies. Only one study applied CFD with a tuber product explicitly represented: a sweet-potato dryer in which the loaded racks were modelled as porous thermal media without moisture transport. In that study, CFD and a lumped-capacitance model both predicted a steady chamber temperature rise of about 40 °C, and fitting the rack heat-transfer coefficients reduced the root-mean-square deviation between the two models to 1.8 °C (lower rack) and 0.9 °C (upper rack); this was a model-to-model comparison, not experimental validation. No CFD study of cassava or yam drying was identified. The only validated cassava heat-and-mass-transfer model was a non-CFD, natural-convection model, with moisture-content differences below 0.2 kg/kg. Guidance on turbulence closure, porous-bed resistance, vapour transport, mesh verification and optimisation was therefore transferred from paddy, fruit, herb and empty-chamber studies, where reported validation errors ranged from 4.3 °C in chamber temperature to below 7.33% in CFD outputs. CFD for tuber drying remains largely an inferred rather than demonstrated capability. A decision-driven multiscale framework is proposed that couples loaded-chamber CFD two ways with tuber-specific heat and moisture models, gated by verification, validation and uncertainty analysis; it has not yet been demonstrated on a tuber dryer. Research should prioritise moisture-coupled, experimentally validated tuber CFD and openly shared benchmark data.
journal: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology

title: Effects of digital literacy on rural labor allocation and income inequality
abstract: Rural prosperity depends in part on whether rural households can access more productive employment and income opportunities. The transfer of rural labor to non-agricultural sectors represents an important pathway for improving rural household income. In the digital era, digital literacy has become an increasingly important dimension of human capital that may shape rural labor allocation and the distribution of economic gains. Using data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), this study examines the relationship between digital literacy and rural household labor allocation and further investigates its associations with household income and income inequality. The results show that higher digital literacy is associated with greater labor allocation to non-agricultural activities and less labor allocated to agricultural self-employment. Broader access to information and general human-capital accumulation emerge as two important empirical transmission channels. Heterogeneity analysis further indicates that these labor-allocation patterns vary across households with different baseline human-capital levels and across household-head age and gender groups. Digital literacy is also associated with higher rural household income but greater income inequality, with the distributional association particularly evident in wage income. Labor reallocation represents an additional empirical pathway linking digital literacy to household income outcomes. These findings highlight the dual role of digital literacy in rural prosperity: it may expand employment and income opportunities, but the resulting gains are not necessarily shared equally across rural households.

title: SDE-YOLO: An Improved YOLOv8 Algorithm for Weed Detection in Crop Fields
abstract: Sesame is an important oilseed crop, but weed infestation can adversely affect its growth and yield. Missed weed detections may compromise subsequent control operations, making reliable and comprehensive weed detection essential for precision agriculture. To reduce missed detections while maintaining low model complexity, this study proposes SDE-YOLO, a lightweight detector based on YOLOv8n. First, C2f_Star modules are introduced into the backbone to enhance feature representation while reducing model complexity. Second, DASI modules are incorporated into the neck to improve multiscale feature fusion and strengthen the representation of targets under complex field conditions. Finally, EIoU is adopted for bounding-box regression to provide more effective geometric optimization. Experiments on the Crop and Weed Detection Data with Bounding Boxes dataset show that SDE-YOLO achieves a recall of 78.60% and an mAP@0.5 of 84.40%, outperforming YOLOv8n by 6.00 and 2.40 percentage points, respectively. Meanwhile, the parameter count and GFLOPs are reduced by 18.60% and 3.70%, resulting in only 2.45 M parameters and 7.80 GFLOPs. Additionally, generalization experiments were conducted on two independent datasets, UAV-PDD2023 and WeedCrop Image, to further evaluate the applicability of the proposed SDE-YOLO model beyond the primary dataset. These results indicate that SDE-YOLO improves detection completeness and overall detection performance while retaining a compact model structure, making it a promising solution for precision weed management.

title: Multi-Sensor Wharf Yard Settlement Forecasting via SSA-PCA Sensor Fusion and Heterogeneous Gradient Boosting
abstract: Accurate prediction of wharf yard settlement is difficult because monitoring records combine long-term drift, nonlinear load responses, sensor noise, and redundant exogenous variables. This study presents a three-stage framework that integrates multi-sensor data, separates trend and residual components, and combines heterogeneous learners. An ARIMA model first extracts the linear settlement trend. Singular spectrum analysis then denoises temperature and stress signals, principal component analysis reduces their dimension, and explicit temporal encodings represent daily, weekly, and long-term patterns. A sliding window joins the historical residuals with the exogenous and temporal features. XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost predict the residual correction on complementary feature subsets, with hyperparameters tuned independently for each library, and their out-of-fold predictions are combined by non-negative least squares (NNLS) weights estimated separately for each monitoring station. The trend and residual predictions are finally combined. Tests on 60 days of hourly data from 15 monitoring stations yield an MSE of 1.0098, and an R2 of 0.9492. The method outperforms the LSTM, Prophet-XGBoost, and other evaluated baselines.

title: Terahertz Sensing for Agricultural Engineering: Applications and Intelligent Data Analysis
abstract: The growing demand for rapid and nondestructive sensing in precision and smart agriculture, particularly for continuous crop monitoring in controlled environment agriculture (CEA), has stimulated interest in terahertz (THz) technologies. Owing to their sensitivity to water, low-frequency molecular vibrations, and dielectric properties, THz waves provide a promising approach for probing agricultural materials. This review summarizes advances in THz sensing for agricultural engineering. The principles and characteristics of THz time-domain spectroscopy, frequency-domain spectroscopy, and imaging are first introduced, together with the major interaction mechanisms between THz waves and agricultural materials. Advances in THz data analysis are then discussed, focusing on model selection, reliability under small-sample conditions, multi-source information fusion, and mechanism-informed analysis. Applications are subsequently reviewed in seed quality and germplasm identification, soil property assessment and contaminant detection, crop water-status monitoring, stress and disease detection, and agricultural product quality and safety assessment. Key challenges include complex-matrix interference, weak target responses, limited model generalization across scenarios, and system integration. Future research should emphasize high-sensitivity sensing, mechanism-data-integrated modeling, and miniaturized online detection systems to facilitate the practical deployment of THz technologies in agriculture, including greenhouses and other controlled production environments.

title: Moisture-Dependent Airflow Resistance and Predictive Modeling of Bulk Camelina Seeds for Drying and Aeration Design
abstract: Reliable airflow-resistance data are essential for designing efficient drying, aeration, and storage systems for bulk seeds. However, airflow resistance of camelina remains largely unknown despite its growing importance as an oilseed crop for biofuel production. This study evaluated the effects of airflow rate, bed depth, filling method, and moisture content on pressure drop through bulk camelina seeds and assessed established airflow-resistance models. Seeds were conditioned to 6, 8, 11, and 14% moisture content (w.b.) and tested at airflow rates of 0.02–0.50 m3 s−1 m−2 across five bed depths under loose- and dense-fill conditions. Ergun, Hukill and Ives, and Shedd models were applied to the experimental data. Results indicated that pressure drop increased significantly (p < 0.05) with airflow rate and bed depth, was greater under dense-fill conditions, and decreased with increasing moisture content. All models adequately described the experimental data (R2 = 0.981–0.989), with the Shedd model providing the best overall performance. A moisture-dependent modified Shedd model was developed to incorporate moisture effects and described the observed pressure-drop trends (R2 = 0.975; RMSE = 54.87 Pa m−1). This model was calibrated and evaluated using the same experimental dataset and has not yet been validated with independent data. The results provide crop-specific parameters for predicting airflow resistance and support fan sizing, energy-efficient aeration, and drying-system design for camelina seeds.

title: Non-Destructive Techniques for the Analysis and Evaluation of Strawberry Quality: A Review
abstract: Strawberry is a high-value horticultural crop whose soft and perishable nature makes rapid and reliable quality evaluation essential throughout production, storage, and postharvest handling. Conventional sensory and destructive physicochemical analyses are often unsuitable for high-throughput and automated applications, driving increasing interest in nondestructive quality assessment and prediction technologies. This review summarizes recent advances in four major approaches: vision-based imaging, spectroscopy-based detection, sensor-based detection, and crop model-based prediction. Vision-based methods have evolved from handcrafted image features and conventional machine learning toward deep learning, object detection, instance segmentation, and three-dimensional analysis for evaluating maturity, color, morphology, defects, and diseases. Spectroscopic techniques, particularly near-infrared spectroscopy and hyperspectral imaging, enable nondestructive estimation of internal quality attributes such as soluble solids content, firmness, acidity, and moisture. Sensor-based approaches, especially electronic noses, characterize changes in volatile organic compounds to assess freshness, maturity, mechanical damage, and storage-related deterioration. Crop models, exemplified by DSSAT CSM-CROPGRO-Strawberry, provide a process-based framework for predicting fruit development and quality dynamics in response to environmental conditions. Collectively, advances in machine learning, deep learning, sensing technologies, and process-based modeling are shifting strawberry quality evaluation from static measurement toward automated and dynamic prediction. Future research should prioritize model robustness and cross-cultivar generalizability, lightweight algorithms, multimodal data fusion, integration of crop models with nondestructive sensing, and online detection systems to facilitate practical deployment in precision production and postharvest management.

title: From Technology Acceptance to Actual Use: Determinants of Agricultural Drone Adoption for Digital Agriculture and Crop Monitoring in Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor
abstract: Agricultural drones are increasingly important for digital agriculture and crop monitoring; however, behavioral intention to use the technology does not necessarily translate into actual use. This study developed and empirically tested an integrated model combining the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) to examine agricultural drone adoption in Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) and the surrounding agricultural area of Prachin Buri. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 400 farmers and agricultural practitioners across four provinces using quota sampling. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5000 bootstrap resamples. Seven of the nine hypothesized relationships were supported. Perceived usefulness positively influenced attitude and behavioral intention, while perceived ease of use positively influenced attitude but did not have a significant direct effect on behavioral intention. Attitude positively influenced both behavioral intention and actual use, and behavioral intention positively influenced actual use. Facilitating conditions significantly influenced actual use but did not significantly influence behavioral intention. The model explained 65.0% of the variance in attitude, 63.0% in behavioral intention, and 74.9% in actual use. Positive Q2_predict values and statistically significant cross-validated predictive ability test (CVPAT) results further supported the model’s predictive relevance and predictive performance relative to the indicator-average benchmark. These findings highlight that the factors associated with behavioral intention and actual agricultural drone use are not necessarily identical, emphasizing the importance of distinguishing psychological acceptance from practical implementation conditions. The findings suggest that agricultural drone promotion should demonstrate practical benefits while also addressing technical support, infrastructure, operational knowledge, and access to necessary resources. The findings should be interpreted in light of the study’s regional scope, non-probability quota-sampling approach, self-reported measure of actual use, and cross-sectional design.

title: From Prompting to Multi-Agent AI: Controlled Generation of CEFR-Specific Language Learning Content
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to support content creation in digital language-learning environments; however, generating educational materials that consistently reflect different proficiency levels remains a challenge. This study investigates an orchestrated multi-agent AI architecture for generating language-learning content targeting different CEFR proficiency levels. The proposed architecture employs an orchestrator that routes content-generation requests to independently configured, level-specialized agents operating under predefined lexical, structural, and instructional requirements, without inter-agent collaboration or deliberation. To distinguish the effects of explicit level-specific constraints from those associated with agent-based orchestration, a controlled experiment compared three generation conditions using the same underlying large language model: conventional prompt-based (PB) generation, constrained prompting (CP), and multi-agent (MA) generation. CP incorporated the same core level-specific requirements and vocabulary resources as MA without employing agent-based orchestration. The three conditions were evaluated using 100 matched tasks across five intended CEFR levels (A1–C1), resulting in 300 generated stories. The outputs were assessed in terms of text length, lexical diversity, syntactic characteristics, and adherence to predefined generation constraints. Within MA, all six continuous linguistic measures showed significant differences across intended proficiency levels, although adjacent-level differentiation varied across linguistic dimensions. Across the three conditions, PB differed from CP and MA on several linguistic measures, whereas CP and MA exhibited greater similarity, with statistically significant differences in 12 of 30 planned comparisons. Both CP and MA achieved 100% adherence to the evaluated story-length, target-vocabulary-count, and comprehension-question-count requirements in the analyzed outputs. Overall, the findings suggest that explicit constraints and vocabulary resources contribute substantially to controlled proficiency-targeted generation, while the orchestrated multi-agent architecture provides modular organization and is associated with selected level-dependent linguistic differences rather than consistent superiority over CP. The study therefore focuses on controlled linguistic differentiation and operational constraint adherence, rather than independent validation of CEFR proficiency levels.

title: Building Information Modeling in Civil Engineering: Methods, Applications, and Perspectives for Rural Constructions
abstract: Building Information Modeling (BIM) can contribute to the design of rural civil engineering structures beyond geometric design by relating building elements to productive activities and environmental constraints. This narrative review brings together BIM, Geographic Information Systems (GISs), farm management, process simulation, and Digital Twin literature to assess their relevance to agricultural buildings. A conceptual Unified Modeling Language (UML) diagram relates building- and performance assessment-related entities and attributes. Software environments are described in relation to their principal design or coordination functions and potential rural applications. A previously published solar-barn dryer study is discussed as an example of linking a parametric BIM representation with reduced-order airflow-network simulation. The synthesis identifies three principal requirements: representing production processes within building information structures; connecting building-scale data to farm and territorial information; and distinguishing offline design simulation from sensor-informed operational Digital Twins. Key research needs concern interoperable agricultural information models, context-dependent implementation costs, and validation against observations from functioning facilities.

title: Geoheritage, Sedimentary Controls and Shoreline Change in the Somone Lagoon–Estuary Complex (Senegal): Remote-Sensing and Machine-Learning Projections to 2050
abstract: Lagoon–estuary complexes are dynamic sedimentary archives in which shoreline mobility and human pressure affect both coastal function and geoheritage. We integrate 14 sediment cores, a quantitative assessment of seven geosites (Brilha method), eight Landsat and Sentinel-2 shorelines (1984–2025) analyzed with the Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS), and a Gradient Boosting machine-learning model for the Somone lagoon–estuary complex, Senegal. Four compartments were distinguished: sector A (southern coastal spit) shows accretion, sector B (tidal inlet and main-channel margins) critical erosion, sector C (mangrove-fringed lagoon banks) rates within measurement uncertainty, and sector D (northern open coast at Guéréo), moderate erosion. The model, validated by five-fold cross-validation grouped by transect, yields a mean absolute error of 0.59 m yr−1 and a coefficient of determination of 0.54. Its 2025–2050 baseline projects continued accretion in sector A and retreat in sectors B and D, with sector B the main retreat hotspot. A sea-level sensitivity layer based on Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP2-4.5, SSP5-8.5) and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change Sixth Assessment Report (IPCC AR6) provides conditional screening, not deterministic forecasts. Shoreline exposure, degradation risk and anthropogenic pressure are kept separate, to support geosite conservation planning.

title: Diagnostic Spectrum and Temporal Trends of Necrotic and Inflammatory Jawbone Lesions: A 22-Year Retrospective Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ), osteoradionecrosis (ORN), and osteomyelitis exhibit overlapping histopathological features, making clinical context essential for etiological differentiation. This study aimed to evaluate the clinicopathological characteristics and temporal distribution of four diagnostic categories of necrotic and inflammatory jawbone lesions over a 22-year period. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study reviewed 25,133 oral and maxillofacial pathology reports from 2004 to 2025. A total of 650 patients were included and categorized using clinicopathological diagnoses and available medication history. Demographic, clinical, anatomical, and temporal characteristics were analyzed, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with MRONJ. Results: MRONJ was the most frequent diagnosis (51.5%), followed by osteomyelitis (39.2%), ORN (4.9%), and sclerosing osteomyelitis (4.3%). The proportion of MRONJ increased from 24.7% in 2004–2010 to 61.7% in 2018–2025, whereas osteomyelitis declined from 58.1% to 30.0% (p < 0.001). Calendar year was associated with MRONJ classification in the linear regression model (adjusted odds ratio = 1.114; 95% CI: 1.079–1.149; p < 0.001), although sensitivity analyses indicated a nonlinear temporal association. Among MRONJ patients with documented underlying disease, 37.5% had osteoporosis. The number of recorded osteoporosis-associated MRONJ cases increased from 3 in 2004–2010 to 75 in 2018–2025. Conclusions: The distribution of recorded clinicopathological diagnoses of jawbone lesions has shifted substantially, with MRONJ becoming increasingly prominent, including among patients treated for osteoporosis. These findings highlight the importance of integrating biopsy findings with clinical history and medication exposure for etiological differentiation. Changes in diagnostic recognition, terminology, referral patterns, and biopsy practices may have influenced these trends, which do not establish changes in disease incidence.

title: Calibration and Cross-Dataset Behavior in Malaria Microscopy with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: A Matched LoRA–PiSSA Evaluation
abstract: Background/Objectives: Reliable evaluation of deep-learning methods for malaria microscopy requires assessing both classification performance and the quality of predicted infection probabilities across datasets. We compared low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and principal singular values and singular vectors adaptation (PiSSA) under matched parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). Methods: An ImageNet-pretrained vision transformer (ViT-B/16) was adapted at ranks 2, 4, 8, and 16 using 27,558 National Institutes of Health (NIH) malaria cell images. One NIH grouped partition was held fixed across paired training seeds 42, 123, and 456. Models were evaluated on the NIH test split and, without target-domain adaptation, on BBBC041 P. vivax cell crops. The analysis was also replicated in invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) histopathology. External probability and threshold-transfer analyses were post hoc. Results: Across LoRA and PiSSA configurations, NIH area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC–AUC) ranged from 0.9960 to 0.9970. PiSSA had lower rank-level mean Brier scores and expected calibration error (ECE) at every evaluated rank in NIH and IDC, although paired-run differences varied. On BBBC041, PiSSA-r16 achieved the highest PEFT ROC–AUC (0.8451) and area under the precision–recall curve (PR–AUC, 0.1588), while fully trained reference models performed better. Across all 12 matched external comparisons, PiSSA had lower overall Brier scores and ECE but higher infected-cell Brier scores. PiSSA had lower sensitivity at NIH-derived thresholds in 11 of 12 comparisons. All PEFT models overpredicted infection relative to the observed 2.70% prevalence. Conclusions: Nearly identical internal discrimination concealed differences in external probability behavior and class-specific errors. PiSSA reduced overprediction, but neither adapter achieved adequate external calibration.

title: CNN-Based Temporal Fusion of UAV and Sentinel-2 Imagery for Crop Monitoring
abstract: The use of Sentinel-2 satellite imagery for crop monitoring is constrained by its native spatial resolution. To address this limitation, data fusion-based super-resolution techniques have emerged as a promising approach for generating imagery with enhanced spatial detail. In this study, we propose TVDSR, a Sentinel-2 and UAV image fusion model that integrates temporal and spectral information through a Bidirectional ConvLSTM-based architecture. The images used for super-resolution were constructed from spectral compositions of five vegetation indices. Model performance was evaluated using 15 acquisition dates, including 11 Sentinel-2 images acquired in 2024 and 4 acquired in 2025. Two independent dates were reserved for validation using reconstruction quality metrics. The proposed model was compared against three state-of-the-art reference models: S3-ESRGAN, DeepSent, and UAV-Net. UAV-Net achieved the best performance for the 2024 validation image (RMSE = 0.128, MAE = 0.10, PSNR = 24.06 dB, and SSIM = 0.86). However, TVDSR obtained the best results for the 2025 evaluation image (RMSE = 0.149, MAE = 0.115, PSNR = 22.60 dB, and SSIM = 0.85) and exhibited the lowest performance degradation across acquisition dates, indicating superior temporal generalization capability. Furthermore, TVDSR more consistently preserved the derived vegetation indices, reflecting a better retention of spectral information associated with crop condition, while producing reconstructions that were visually closer to the reference UAV imagery. The joint integration of temporal and spectral information constitutes an effective strategy for improving the robustness and generalization capability of Sentinel-2 image super-resolution for crop monitoring, precision agriculture, crop condition assessment, and agricultural management applications.

title: Parameter-Level Attribution of Uncertainty in Electricity Carbon Footprint Factors: A Case Study of Coal-Fired and Hydropower Plants in a Chinese Province
abstract: Provincial carbon footprint factors of electricity underpin product carbon footprints, green certificate trading, and carbon border adjustment, yet their uncertainty is usually reported as one aggregate interval that does not show which part better measurement could reduce and which part an accounting convention fixes. This case study examines eight plants in one Chinese province with original 2025 accounting workbooks (four coal-fired, four hydropower). Each is rebuilt into a normalized parametric model reproducing the original total. Measurable quantities are propagated by Monte Carlo sampling and apportioned with variance-based sensitivity indices; database choices and accounting conventions are enumerated as discrete scenarios and compared with, rather than added to, the probabilistic interval. For the coal-fired plants, the measurement-driven 95% interval is about −11% to +12%, dominated by coal input; the background database shifts the factor by a comparable amount, whereas every accounting convention shifts it by less than 30% of the interval half-width. For the hydropower plants, the interval is wider, yet harmonizing the amortization horizon of civil works alone moves the factor by 1.5 to 2.8 times that half-width. The findings are specific to the sample and suggest differentiating data collection and factor publication by generation type.

title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Dividend-Increase Behavior from Corporate Financial Indicators and Its Application to Portfolio Management
abstract: This study examines whether corporate information supplements management dividend forecasts in predicting dividend increases and whether the predictions improve stock selection in Japan. Using financial and market indicators, management forecasts, and dividend histories available at each prediction date, we develop machine learning models for Tokyo Stock Exchange firms with March fiscal year-ends, excluding banks. A rolling training, validation, and retraining procedure produces out-of-sample predictions for 2013–2023, with portfolio evaluation from June 2013 to May 2024. We compare forecast-based benchmarks and multivariate models. Then, we combine predicted probabilities with forecast dividend yields. Multivariate eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) achieves a mean annual area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.86, compared with 0.77 for XGBoost using only the forecast dividend yield change. The combined long–short strategy achieves an annualized Sharpe ratio of 1.26 and a positive alpha under the Fama–French three-factor model (t = 4.12, p < 0.001). Its arithmetic cumulative spread return remains positive under the examined transaction cost scenarios. These findings suggest that dividend increase predictions can complement forecast dividend yields in stock selection, whereas practical implementation requires consideration of borrowing costs and other trading constraints not separately assessed here.

title: Genome-Wide Identification and Characterization of the Bromodomain Gene Family in Olive (Olea europaea) and Its Association with Salt Stress Responses
abstract: Bromodomain (BRD) proteins are evolutionarily conserved epigenetic readers that bind acetylated lysine residues on histone tails, linking chromatin remodeling to transcriptional regulation and abiotic stress adaptation. Although salinity is among the most economically damaging abiotic stresses worldwide, the bromodomain-level epigenetic mechanisms underlying salt tolerance in the perennial crop olive (Olea europaea L.) remain unstudied. This study aimed to identify and characterize the complete Olea europaea bromodomain (OeBRD) gene family in olive, resolve its evolutionary relationships with Arabidopsis thaliana, and identify candidate genes potentially associated with salt-stress responses. Genome-wide identification, physicochemical characterization, promoter cis-regulatory element analysis, phylogenetic reconstruction, orthogroup clustering, conserved-motif and gene-structure analysis, AlphaFold3 structural modeling, RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data (BioProject PRJNA841838) from control, primed (75 → 150 mM NaCl) and non-primed (150 mM NaCl) plants, and Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING)-based protein–protein interaction (PPI) and Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analyses were performed. Twenty-one non-redundant OeBRD genes were identified in the O. europaea genome (GCF_002742605.1), with molecular weights of 43,076–242,620 Da, isoelectric points of 5.05–9.67, and universally negative grand average of hydropathicity (GRAVY) values. Phylogenetic analysis resolved four clades, including olive-specific paralog groups, and orthogroup clustering against A. thaliana identified 16 orthogroups, eight of which are strict 1:1 orthologs, five show copy-number differences between the two species (more copies in olive in three groups, including OeBRD6a/6b/6c, and more copies in Arabidopsis in two), one is a balanced 2:2 group and two contain only Arabidopsis genes. Multiple Em for Motif Elicitation (MEME) analysis identified 10 conserved motifs. Promoter analysis revealed abundant abscisic acid (ABA)-, myeloblastosis (MYB)/myelocytomatosis (MYC)- and jasmonate-responsive cis-elements. DESeq2 differential expression analysis of primed (75→150 mM NaCl) and non-primed (150 mM NaCl) plants relative to untreated controls identified four of the 21 OeBRD genes as significantly differentially expressed (adjusted p < 0.05): OeBRD6b, OeBRD6c, OeBRD10 and OeBRD26 were up-regulated in primed roots, OeBRD26 was also up-regulated in non-primed roots and non-primed leaves, and no gene was significant in primed leaves; STRING PPI analysis identified OeBRD24 and OeBRD13 as the most connected nodes in a network inferred from Arabidopsis orthologues, with chromatin, chromatin remodeling and histone acetyltransferase activity among the most significantly enriched GO terms. Ten proteins—OeBRD26, OeBRD6c, OeBRD6b, OeBRD10, OeBRD13, OeBRD24, OeBRD11, OeBRD16, OeBRD28 and OeBRD29—were prioritized as candidates for future experimental validation of a possible role in salt-stress responses in olive.

title: Genome-Wide Identification and Population-Based Genetic Dissection of Amino Acid Transporter (AAT) Gene Family in Maize
abstract: Long-term yield-oriented breeding reduces maize kernel protein content, whereas excessive nitrogen fertilization raises cultivation costs and causes environmental pollution. Amino acid transporters (AATs) are key regulators of plant nitrogen allocation, governing crop nitrogen-use efficiency and grain quality. Here, we systematically identified 98 ZmAAT genes from the latest B73 RefGen_v5 maize genome and classified them into 12 subfamilies. Furthermore, pangenome-wide analysis across 26 diverse maize inbred lines and 8 wild relatives revealed extensive structural polymorphisms, presence/absence variations (PAVs), and core–shell–cloud orthogroup classifications. Segmental duplication primarily drove AAT superfamily expansion; pangenome-level duplication and selection pressure analyses confirmed that all duplicated paralogs experienced strong purifying selection to preserve conserved amino-acid-transport functions. Using metabolite-based genome-wide association study (mGWAS) on 378 diverse maize inbred lines, we uncovered a major pleiotropic hotspot on chromosome 5 containing ZmCAT7 and ZmCAT8 as key candidate genes. Their natural variations are significantly associated with accumulations of glutamine, phenylalanine, and glutamic-acid derivatives. These results highlight ZmCAT7 and ZmCAT8 as promising targets for future functional validation and potential genetic improvement of maize grain quality.

title: Cultivation Duration Reshapes Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi and Soil Aggregation in Relation to Ginseng Growth and Quality
abstract: Understanding how prolonged cultivation reorganizes belowground biological and structural processes is critical for maintaining the productivity and quality of perennial medicinal crops. However, the linkages among arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF), glomalin-related soil protein (GRSP), soil aggregation, and plant performance across cultivation durations remain poorly resolved. We hypothesized that increasing ginseng cultivation duration would alter soil physicochemical properties and AMF functional attributes, thereby affecting soil aggregate stability and ginseng growth and quality. Here, we investigated garden-cultivated Panax ginseng across four cultivation durations (1–4 years) to determine how changes in soil conditions were associated with AMF functional attributes, GRSP fractions, aggregate stability, and ginseng performance. AMF spore density and root colonization exhibited cultivation-duration-dependent variation, whereas GRSP fractions showed contrasting temporal patterns, indicating a decoupling between current AMF functional status and the accumulated soil GRSP pool. Soil aggregate-size distribution and stability also shifted markedly across cultivation durations. Correlation and Mantel analyses further revealed close associations among soil environmental variables, AMF functional attributes, GRSP, aggregate properties, and ginseng traits. Structural equation modeling further revealed distinct pathways linking cultivation duration to ginseng biomass and medicinal quality. Cultivation duration was positively associated with soil environmental conditions and aggregate properties, while soil environmental variation was strongly associated with AMF functional traits. Ginseng weight was positively associated with cultivation duration but negatively associated with aggregate properties, whereas total ginsenoside content was positively associated with aggregate properties and showed no significant direct association with cultivation duration. The direct pathway from AMF functional traits to aggregate properties was not significant, suggesting that AMF responses to cultivation-induced environmental variation did not translate into an independent effect on soil aggregation within the fitted model. Collectively, these findings reveal that prolonged ginseng cultivation reorganizes belowground environmental, mycorrhizal, and structural components in distinct ways and that soil aggregate properties represent an important interface linking cultivation-associated belowground changes with ginseng biomass and medicinal quality.

title: Machine Learning-Based Land-Cover and Crop Types Classification Using Multi-Temporal Sentinel-1 SAR Imagery in Hyper-Arid Environments
abstract: Egypt’s New Delta mega-project represents the largest horizontal agricultural expansion in modern Egyptian history, creating an urgent need for cost-effective land-cover and crop monitoring systems capable of operating under hyper-arid conditions. This study evaluates the operational feasibility of machine learning (ML)-based land-cover and crop classification using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery in the El-Daba Development Corridor, Egypt, a hyper-arid component of newly irrigated desert land. Sentinel-1 Ground Range Detected (GRD) data (vertical-vertical (VV) and vertical-horizontal (VH) polarizations) acquired from January to December 2025 were processed within Google Earth Engine (GEE). Monthly composite images were generated to capture phenological development, from which backscatter features, polarization ratios and differences, statistical descriptors, the Radar Vegetation Index (RVI), and Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture features were extracted. K-Means clustering (K = 10) provided an initial stratification of the feature space, while Random Forest (RF) classification was trained on 840 samples (70%) and validated on 358 independent samples (30%). Temporal backscatter analysis revealed distinct phenological signatures: wheat and sugar beet peaked in March (VV = −7 dB), maize reached maximum backscatter in July (VH = −12 dB, RVI = 0.70), and perennial crops maintained stable signatures year-round. Feature importance analysis identified VH in July (8.7%), VV in March (7.9%), and RVI in July (7.2%) as the most discriminative variables, confirming that combining observations from multiple phenological periods substantially enhances crop separability. The RF classifier achieved 90.5% overall accuracy with a Kappa coefficient of 0.895, with per-class accuracies ranging from 77.8% (vegetables) to 100% (non-agricultural classes). Optimal discrimination windows were identified as February-March for winter cereals, June-July for summer maize, and January/May-June for potato. These results demonstrate that SAR-only land-cover and crop mapping can deliver operationally useful accuracy in hyper-arid environments where optical imagery is constrained, providing a scalable foundation for agricultural monitoring in Egypt’s desert reclamation frontiers and comparable arid systems globally.

title: Analysis of Influencing Factors of Black Soil Protection
abstract: Holistically considering the systemic function of multi-dimensional factors and accurately identifying core elements within black soil conservation are essential for dynamically adjusting conservation strategies and consolidating the foundation of national food security. This study innovatively adapts Hayami’s social development model for the domain of black soil conservation and employs the revised model as its macro-analytical framework. Based on 224 qualitative textual documents collected from four typical pilot counties in Northeast China during 2022–2024, this study adopts a grounded theory approach to unpack micro-level interaction mechanisms in black soil conservation practices. The results demonstrate that black soil conservation constitutes a complex comprehensive system covering technology, talent, institutions, resources, and industry, which shows high consistency with the logic of the social development model. The talent–technology subsystem acts as a critical bridging hub connecting the institutional and the resource–industry subsystems and undertakes core driving functions in conservation practice. Five core interactive influencing mechanisms are identified: technology supply, multi-stakeholder co-governance, institutional normalization, resource allocation, and industrial integration. This study reveals the socioeconomic interaction process of black soil conservation and provides differentiated empirical references for formulating locally adapted governance strategies for pilot areas and similar black soil regions.

title: String Stability of Learned Car-Following Models: Audit, Differentiable Penalties, a Certified Hybrid and Corridor-Level Validation
abstract: Trajectory accuracy does not establish whether learned car-following laws remain stable in a closed loop. We evaluate six neural or hybrid architectures and a nearest-neighbour baseline trained on 12,512 highway events, combining a pre-specified core protocol with exploratory extensions: anchored equilibrium audits, platoon tests and 1445 corridor simulations of two NGSIM sites against macroscopic ground truth. Five unconstrained networks beat the Intelligent Driver Model by 8–33% in trajectory error yet have 84–95% string-unstable equilibria. Jacobian regularisation stabilises the memoryless models with little accuracy loss; standard rollout-based penalties leave the recurrent models unstable, and a longer-window pilot helps but leaves the hypothesis open. For a hybrid with a margin-constrained core and a Lipschitz-bounded residual, a sufficient condition for local linear string stability is verified over gaps at grid speeds and rechecked after fine-tuning. In the baseline corridor configuration, this hybrid has the lowest macro error of the thirteen protocol laws, with no or rare contacts, while the networks that win on trajectory error collide on the unseen site; the certificate is a local linear statement at the verified speeds, and the corridor claims concern the two reconstructed sites, one of them in sample for the fine-tuned laws. A controlled component ablation finds a lower macro error with the derivative budget than without it, although both pass the equilibrium audit. Trajectory accuracy, equilibrium stability, collision behaviour and corridor fidelity require separate assessment.

title: Topology-Triggered Bond-Based Peridynamics with Source-Connected Fracture-Path Reconstruction for Rock Hydraulic Fracturing
abstract: A quasi-static bond-based peridynamic framework combines source-connected fracture-path reconstruction with topology-triggered hydraulic loading. Local failed-bond evidence determines candidate path extensions, while source connectivity and two-sided support govern their acceptance. Each accepted extension updates the pressure-loaded boundary before mechanical equilibrium is restored. At the finest tested spacing, the computed crack openings agree with the Sneddon solution and independent finite-element solutions to within 4.3% for two orientations. Initiation-pressure errors relative to linear elastic fracture mechanics remain below 9%. The directional hydraulic-fracturing validation compares the predicted initiation pressure with the experimental value and the predicted path direction with that given by a mixed-mode criterion. The damage band widens more slowly than the connected path extends. A cavity–tunnel application isolates the role of pressure on newly formed surfaces. At a common cavity pressure, updating the loaded path produces a 40.45 mm pre-intersection equilibrium path, compared with 10.62 mm when fracture pressure is confined to the initial defect. The two loading treatments have the same initiation pressure but markedly different subsequent growth. Characterizing subsequent rock-bridge degradation therefore requires accounting for both initiation pressure and the evolving pressure-loaded boundary.

title: Characterizing Correspondence Coverage Collapse in UAV RGB–TIR Registration
abstract: Registration quality in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB and thermal infrared (TIR) imagery is often assessed using reprojection error, although low residuals at the correspondences used for estimation do not necessarily indicate reliable alignment across the common image footprint. This study investigates Correspondence Coverage Collapse as a diagnostic pattern in which low in-sample error coexists with concentrated correspondences, limited spatial support, and poorer held-out performance. Seventeen RGB–TIR image pairs were analyzed using a two-stage common-footprint normalization and a fixed full-inlier correspondence pool generated by SuperPoint–SuperGlue. Clustered, Random, and Balanced subsets were compared under equal correspondence budgets, with common held-out correspondences used for generalization assessment. At N=80, Clustered selection achieved the lowest selected-point RMSE but showed the highest held-out RMSE, lowest spatial coverage, and largest reference-grid deviation. Confidence-ranked selection showed a similar but weaker pattern at lower correspondence budgets. Continuous analyses further showed that lower coverage and greater distance-to-support were associated with higher held-out error and global transformation deviation. These results indicate that reprojection error alone does not characterize spatial support or held-out performance within the evaluated correspondence pool.

title: STC-PFTF-Net: Structure-Guided Prior Fusion for Cover-Crop Canopy Delineation in Residue-Rich UAV Imagery
abstract: Delineating early cover-crop vegetation in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery requires preserving slender leaves amid cast shadows, desiccated residue, and heterogeneous soil. Weak foliage contrast and leaf-like background edges make appearance and geometry jointly important. We propose the Shadow, Topology, and Chromatic-aware Prior Feature Topology Fusion Network (STC-PFTF-Net), which integrates structure-guided reconstruction with complementary appearance representations. A coherence-guided tangent–normal decomposition preserves tangential sampling displacement and attenuates displacement across local structures. Chromatic–photometric encoding, directional wavelet filtering, and local connectivity refinement support this reconstruction throughout the feature hierarchy. On the 32 validation tiles of the Residue-rich Cover-Crop UAV Dataset, drawn from an area spatially separated from training, STC-PFTF-Net achieves 77.71% foreground intersection over union (IoU), 50.88% Boundary IoU, 83.84% centerline Dice (clDice), and 87.35% F1. At a common decision threshold, the complete model also exceeds the comparison architectures in all four measures. Spatial analyses associate its higher boundary recall with vegetation–background transitions and identify low-greenness foliage as a distinct source of omission. These findings show the value of combining appearance information with explicit reconstruction geometry for fine-scale canopy delineation. With 2.12 million parameters, the model offers a compact representation for UAV-derived vegetation mapping and subsequent canopy-cover assessment.

title: Training-Informed Differentiable Bayesian Inference with PROSPECT for Leaf Trait Retrieval and Uncertainty Analysis
abstract: Leaf radiative transfer models provide a physical basis for leaf trait retrieval, but compensating parameter effects and measurement discrepancies constrain estimation accuracy and uncertainty characterization. This study proposes Training-Informed Differentiable Bayesian Inference (TI-DBI). This method integrates training-derived joint lognormal priors, wavelength-specific spectral biases, and residual scales into a differentiable PROSPECT-D model, enabling joint parameter inference via the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS). Evaluated on multi-source datasets, TI-DBI yields relative root mean square errors (rRMSEs) of 27.31%, 33.72%, 16.22%, and 37.66% for chlorophyll (Cab), carotenoids (Car), equivalent water thickness (Cw), and leaf dry mass per area (Cm). Outperforming an uncalibrated Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) baseline for all traits and partial least squares regression (PLSR) for Cab, Car, and Cw, these results confirm the specific value of the data-informed probabilistic framework. Beyond point-estimation, TI-DBI substantially improves uncertainty characterization. It yields narrower interval widths and lower interval scores than the uncalibrated baseline, with prediction interval coverage probability (PICP) of the 95% highest density intervals (HDIs) reaching 93.14%, 96.46%, 89.62%, and 86.22% for Cab, Car, Cw, and Cm, respectively. Ablation and sensitivity studies confirm that both the learned priors and spectral error calibration drive these performance gains across varying training fractions and spectral configurations. TI-DBI strictly preserves the forward model’s physical structure while providing a robust, practical framework for jointly evaluating trait estimation accuracy and posterior uncertainty.

title: Spatially Aware Uncertainty Feedback for Hard Region Learning in Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Remote sensing semantic segmentation often produces spatially concentrated errors around object boundaries, small targets, shadowed areas, and ambiguous land-cover transitions. This study investigates whether learned spatial uncertainty can guide additional supervision of such difficult pixels. We propose Spatially Aware Uncertainty Feedback for Hard Region Learning (SUF-HRL), which refines a maximum-softmax-probability prior through a residual uncertainty branch attached to a SegFormer backbone. Local alignment and boundary concentration objectives encourage a task-adaptive spatial difficulty map; after a warm-up stage, its highest-scoring pixels receive additional cross-entropy supervision. Experiments use the Potsdam and Vaihingen benchmarks of the International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing and the LoveDA land-cover dataset. Under the controlled SegFormer-B2 protocol, mean intersection over union (mIoU) increases by 0.69, 1.14, and 1.01 percentage points, respectively. Averaging boundary-region mIoU over 3-, 5-, and 7-pixel bands gives gains of approximately 1.44, 1.32, and 1.32 percentage points. Component ablations support contributions from both spatial objectives. Learned uncertainty improves the reported spatial uncertainty criteria on Vaihingen, although it does not achieve the best precision–recall or calibration score. On Potsdam, training time per iteration increases by approximately 68.5% while the reported parameter totals remain nearly unchanged. The additional inference latency is small in the tested configuration. These results support learned spatial uncertainty as a useful training signal for hard-region segmentation.

title: TSD-LitePT: Transition-Sensitive Detail Enhancement for UAV LiDAR Transmission-Corridor Segmentation
abstract: UAV-borne LiDAR segmentation of transmission corridors is hindered by the anisotropic geometry of elongated conductors, semantic ambiguity near component junctions, and the loss of sparse insulator evidence during hierarchical sampling. To address these challenges, we propose TSD-LitePT, a three-stage extension of LitePT. First, Learnable Axial Rotary Position Encoding learns independent scales for the x-, y-, and z-axis rotary phases, adapting positional sensitivity to corridor geometry. Second, Transition-Modulated Semantic Refinement derives a segmentation-driven point-wise response from decoded features and uses it to gate semantic residuals, refining ambiguous representations without boundary annotations. Third, Sparse-Target Detail Calibration uses decoded semantics, normalized coordinates, and transition context to calibrate shallow high-resolution features, then aggregates serialized-neighborhood evidence into an insulator prior. A bounded, confidence-aware residual injects this prior into the insulator logit while suppressing changes at confident non-target points. Across three runs on the original five-class corridor dataset, TSD-LitePT achieved an mIoU of 0.9200±0.0003 and an insulator IoU of 0.7236±0.0016 (mean ± standard deviation), compared with 0.8818±0.0061 and 0.5548±0.0435, respectively, for LitePT. After separate retraining on an independent transmission corridor, TSD-LitePT achieved an mIoU of 0.8909, compared with 0.8653 for LitePT. The largest improvement occurred for insulators, while power-line and ground performance remained close to the baseline. These results show that coordinating positional adaptation, semantic refinement, and controlled detail recovery improves minority-component segmentation without disturbing dominant classes.

title: Monthly Multi-Source Remote Sensing Reveals Seasonal Pulses, Bundle Transitions, and Differentiated Management of Ecosystem Services in the Yongding River Basin
abstract: Seasonal basin management requires knowing when ecosystem services coincide and how their configurations differ among subbasins, information that annual summaries can obscure. We integrated monthly remote sensing, meteorological, soil, and terrain data to estimate carbon fixation (CF), water conservation (WC), soil retention (SR), and wind erosion prevention (WEP) in 18 Yongding River subbasins in 2018, 2020, and 2023. Seasonal association networks and a self-organizing map characterized 648 subbasin–month service profiles and their bundle histories. Of 648 monthly bundle labels, 237 (36.6%) differed from the label of the corresponding annual mean service vector. The high-CF–WC–SR bundle occurred in 26 monthly profiles, including 19 of 54 July observations, whereas subbasin 4 retained a WEP-oriented bundle in 30 of 36 sampled months. In the three-year mean seasonal profiles, 12 of 18 subbasins shared a summer CF-enhanced pathway; the other six followed alternative pathways. CF, WC, and SR were generally higher in summer, while WEP peaked in April and was more prominent in western and southwestern subbasins. Seasonal networks showed the strongest screened association for winter SR–WC, while the summer WC–WEP confidence interval crossed zero. Together, monthly bundle histories and seasonal association networks identify shared summer assessment windows and subbasin-specific priorities for spring wind exposure and service-bundle transition monitoring, providing spatially and temporally explicit evidence for differentiated seasonal management in the Yongding River Basin.
