The framework integrates established components: maximum mean discrepancy-based domain adaptation to reduce simulation-to-experiment discrepancies, a convolutional neural network with a spectral-normalized neural Gaussian process (CNN--SNGP) for predictive uncertainty estimation, and replay with knowledge distillation for sequential model updating. We evaluate the framework using simulated and previously-collected experimental data for crystal structure classification of single-phase body-centered cubic, face-centered cubic, and hexagonal close-packed patterns. Data are organized into predefined sequential blocks to assess adaptation and retention of previously learned knowledge. Within this setting, the results show accurate classification across simulated and experimental data, improved alignment between the two domains, and reduced forgetting compared with naïve fine-tuning. Predictive uncertainty is also evaluated on unfamiliar and noisy inputs. The contribution is the integration and evaluation of these capabilities for sequential XRD interpretation. The framework provides a basis for future integration into autonomous experimentation systems, with experimental planning, instrument control, and closed-loop deployment remaining areas for future development.

title: Talk to Act: A Synthetic Multi-Turn Dialogue Benchmark for Human Intent Extraction and Action Planning in Robotics
abstract: Multi-turn conversational human-robot interaction (HRI) continues to be a challenging problem in robotics, as many existing systems rely on rigid, command-driven interfaces that can be unintuitive for users. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) provide a promising direction, given their ability to process natural language, generate structured outputs, and support tool-based reasoning, all of which are relevant for interpreting user intent in robotic settings. However, progress in this area is constrained by the limited availability of datasets and benchmarks that capture the nuances of real-world human communication, such as multi-turn dialogue, ambiguity, and context-dependent requests. In this work, we present a synthetically generated multi-turn dialogue dataset for HRI, annotated with action intents, object references, and task plans across a range of scenarios and user personas. Our primary focus is on evaluating the capability of small, open-weight language models for robotic tasks, particularly in settings where local deployment and efficiency are important. To this end, we frame intent extraction as a tool-calling problem where each predicted action corresponds to a structured function call with arguments grounded in the dialogue and benchmark models ranging from 270M to 8B parameters on their ability to perform intent extraction and action planning without task-specific fine-tuning. Our results show that these models can achieve reasonable performance on the task even at relatively small scales and without any task-specific fine-tuning. This suggests that compact, locally deployable models already provide a useful baseline for conversational robotic systems. We expect that task-specific fine-tuning and more realistic training data will enhance performance further and make such models increasingly suitable for real-world robotic applications.

title: Online Allocation with Differential Privacy
abstract: We study private online allocation problems, where allocation decisions must satisfy differential privacy (DP) to protect sensitive user information while optimizing performance under limited resources. We first formalize differential privacy notions suited to different privacy requirements in online allocation and establish the fundamental performance limits of any algorithm under these definitions. Based on these insights, we propose PPOA, a privacy-preserving meta algorithm for online allocation, and establish sufficient conditions under which PPOA preserves Joint DP (JDP) or Local DP (LDP) while achieving asymptotically near-optimal performance. Building on these conditions, PPOA can be instantiated into a variety of concrete algorithms. In particular, we present the specific designs, which include PPOA-DMD that preserves JDP and LDP and PPOA-FTRL that preserves JDP. We analyze their performance under both adversarial and stochastic settings and characterize the fundamental trade-offs between DP and allocation performance. Finally, we demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed algorithms via numerical experiments on AI model routing in battery-powered edge systems.

title: Generative Design with Real-time Physics Explainability: Towards Product Definition in the Age of AI
abstract: In this article, we explore opportunities from using generative AI in mechanical engineering. On the one hand, generative methods based on invertible neural networks have been recently proposed for the solution of inverse design problems, allowing to infer design parameters from performance labels. On the other hand, generative AI models have shown that they can act as real time capable surrogates for physics based simulations. Here we suggest that these two streams should be combined in a unified framework, where INN are used to control the design process from the customer requirements perspective and the generative simulation of the systems physics adds a layer of explainability, why the proposed design fulfils the requirements. As generative design is prone to hallucinations, we propose uncertainty quantification to fend off physically infeasible requests. Finally, validation with classical tools is a requirement for generative design process. To demonstrate the capabilities of our novel generative design paradigm, we develop two interactive environments, one for airfoil design based on simulator data and one for the combustor design space exploration based on measured data.

title: AI-Voyager: A Public-Interest System for Human-AI Civic Reasoning to Contest and Shape the Rules That Govern AI
abstract: Governments are writing rules for artificial intelligence that decide what counts as an automated decision or a harm, often before the people they affect have a chance to question them. We introduce AI-Voyager, a public-interest system for human-AI civic reasoning, in which people and AI work together to understand, contest and shape the rules that govern AI. A resident can find their city's rules on AI in hiring or upload their country's AI strategy, read it as an affected worker would, open the passage behind any answer, and draft a revision. Its architecture turns 3,653 governance documents from city, state, federal and national governments into passages that keep their page and edition, and retrieves evidence through bounded agentic search that verifies each statement. On 360 new questions that require finding the relevant documents, it reached 83.0% macro recall, against 80.5% for the strongest baseline, 73.7% without iterative search and 99.1% on a benchmark with fixed documents. In a study with 24 participants new to two AI bills, most proposed changes asked how provisions would apply. Participants chose lenses for the kind of explanation they wanted, and citations signaled grounding but rarely led them to check the source. By binding AI assistance to the exact text of public documents, this work introduces a grammar of operations and a design space that inform how such systems are designed and evaluated, and how people take part in governing AI.

title: Agri-MRAG: Parameter-Enhanced Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Agricultural Visual Question Answering
abstract: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) has shown promise for Agricultural Visual Question Answering (Agri-VQA), but existing methods still face challenges in retrieving relevant knowledge while avoiding redundancy and in integrating retrieved evidence beyond simple prompt concatenation. To address these issues, we propose Agri-MRAG, a multimodal retrieval-augmented framework for agricultural VQA. Specifically, we first introduce a semantic-consistency-guided clustering mechanism that combines multimodal clustering and weighted relevance scoring to select high-confidence knowledge subsets and adaptively determine the retrieval size $k$. We then design a parameterized knowledge injection strategy, where retrieved agricultural knowledge is encoded into LoRA adapters and merged into the feed-forward network (FFN) layers of the MLLM, allowing external knowledge to influence generation through parameter-level adaptation. In addition, a perplexity-guided (PPL-guided) routing mechanism is employed to switch between implicit parametric reasoning and explicit retrieval-assisted generation according to model uncertainty, balancing inference efficiency and answer reliability. For evaluation, we use PlantVillageVQA as a broad agricultural benchmark and construct PlantVQA, a region-specific forestry and fruit crop VQA dataset containing 7,514 images and 15,028 expert-verified question-answer pairs. Experiments show that Agri-MRAG achieves ROUGE-L scores of 41.21 and 46.58 on the two datasets, outperforming mRAG by 11.70 and 4.51 points, and VisRAG by 8.80 and 3.39 points, respectively.

title: Setting Optimal Reserve Prices using Fine-Tuned Language Models
abstract: Online auction houses must set reserve prices for highly differentiated products whose unstructured descriptions contain valuable demand information. Existing approaches generally require managers to specify product attributes in advance. We ask whether a language model can instead learn from listing descriptions and historical bids to set item-specific reserve prices before bidding begins. We fine-tune a pretrained text embedding language model using the structural likelihood of auction bids as its training objective. This directs representation learning toward the valuation distribution that determines the reserve decision. We show that consecutive upper bids identify the tail information needed to set an optimal reserve without observing or modeling the number of potential bidders. A split-sample estimator learns the representation on one half of the data and conducts structural estimation and inference conditional on that representation on the other. We apply the method to approximately 65,800 online used-vehicle auctions. With seller values calibrated to match the sale rate among listings, the model implies a counterfactual net increase of $165.8 million, representing a 14.6% increase above the incumbent reserve policy. The framework translates a listing description and a seller's value into an item-specific reserve recommendation without constructing a product taxonomy or requiring a bid history for the item being priced. It provides an approach to adapting language models for operational decisions in marketplaces where products are heterogeneous and demand-relevant information is recorded in text.

title: Enhancing Preference Detection using Eye Movement Cascade and Multilayer Combinatorial Fusion
abstract: Understanding how visual attention influences human preference formation is a fundamental problem in consumer behavior and cognitive science. In this work, we investigate how eye movement patterns can be used to predict preference decisions when subjects compare two alternatives. To address this problem, we analyze an eye-tracking dataset, where subjects view pairs of face images and their gaze behavior is recorded throughout the decision process. We model this problem using multiple machine learning classifiers and apply the Multi-layer Combinatorial Fusion (MCF) framework to iteratively combine diverse models. The MCF framework expands models to a large pool of model fusions and then reduces them based on cognitive diversity, repeating this process across layers until diversity diminishes. Experimental results show that MCF significantly improves performance over individual models. The best single model achieves a Pre@k of 0.90, which is improved to 0.9143 after the first layer of MCF, and further increased to 0.9286 in the second layer. This progression demonstrates that the second layer not only surpasses the performance of the first layer but also outperforms the best individual model, highlighting the effectiveness of leveraging diversity through multi-layer fusion.

title: ANALYSIS OF SOME MORPHOLOGICAL AND PRODUCTIVITY PARAMETERS IN Myrtus communis L. UNDER POT CROP CONDITIONS
abstract: The study evaluated morphological and productivity parameters of Myrtus communis L. plants. The experiment was conducted within the “Atmosfera Verde” Nursery in the area of the University of Life Sciences “King Mihai I” from Timisoara. The myrtle plants were cultivated in pots with a volume of 10 dm3 , in a substrate of horticultural peat (80 %) and perlite (20 %). The plants were 4 years old at the time of experimental observations, November 2025. Plant height (PH) showed low variability (CV = 7.62), mean stem number (MSN) showed moderate variability (CV = 27.13), and fruits number on plant (FNP) showed high variability (CV = 40.54). Polynomial mathematical models and graphical models (3D model, and isoquants) described the variation of FNP in relation to PH and MSN, in statistical safety conditions.
journal: ANNALS OF THE UNIVERSITY OF CRAIOVA, Biology, Horticulture, Food products processing technology, Environmental engineering

title: 3D Printing in Landscape Scale Model-Making: A Curriculum Reform Case
abstract: Traditional landscape scale model-making courses often emphasize manual fabrication and final-product assessment, leaving limited room for digital modeling, iterative prototyping, and process-oriented evaluation. This paper reports a descriptive curriculum reform case integrating 3D printing into a 32-hour elective Landscape Scale Model-Making course at a public agricultural and forestry institution in northern China. The course involved 110 students from undergraduate and vocational programs and combined manual craft, SketchUp-based digital modeling, desktop FDM 3D printing, role-based teamwork, staged instructor guidance, and process-oriented assessment. A 1:300 campus landscape site model served as the central practical project. Evidence was drawn from course implementation records, an end-of-course questionnaire containing six closed-ended items and four open-ended prompts, instructor reflection, and student work. Closed-ended responses were summarized using counts and percentages, while open-ended responses were examined through content analysis. Course records indicated a shorter calendar project cycle and fewer component failures or major rework episodes in the integrated workflow. Students also reported positive perceptions of digital modeling, 3D printer operation, the realization of design ideas, collaboration, and material use. Content analysis identified the ability to produce complex forms and improved dimensional control as prominent benefits, while modeling difficulties, slicing and printer-operation challenges, uneven workload, and limited equipment access remained important constraints. These findings provide implementation evidence from one institutional setting rather than causal proof of learning gains. The case suggests that 3D printing is most educationally useful when embedded in a scaffolded physical-digital workflow rather than treated as a substitute for manual model-making.

title: Methods of Intelligent Automation of Software System Analysis Using AI Agents in the Development and Operation of Web Applications
abstract: AI agents built on large language models now take part in the analysis of software systems, yet evidence on their use across the life cycle of web applications remains scattered among benchmark reports and separate field studies. This article aims to systematize methods of agent-based analysis in the development and operation of web applications and to substantiate a model for assigning agent autonomy. The study combines a structured review of 25 sources published from 2020 to 2026, comparative analysis of benchmark results, content analysis of field studies, and a qualitative case study of two web products from the author's practice. The synthesis suggests that the strength of the verification oracle may be a more stable basis for assigning autonomy than benchmark capability scores; a direct comparative test of this hypothesis remains necessary. The article proposes an oracle-gated model with four layers, a matrix of four autonomy modes, and five monitoring indicators. The conclusions support staged adoption that begins with tasks backed by executable checks. The findings will interest web developers, game developers, engineering managers, and researchers in software engineering.

title: Myrmecocystus honeypot ants have a species-specific resident gut microbiome
abstract: Myrmecocystus honeypot ants rely on specialized workers, known as repletes, to store dissolved carbohydrates in their crops. The repletes store this liquid for many months at a time without spoilage. When resources are scarce, repletes redistribute the stored nutrients to their colony members via trophallaxis. While we suspect that the gut microbiome of honeypot ants may aid in spoilage prevention, we must first characterize it. Here, we used 16S rRNA gene sequencing to determine the microbial community composition across six Myrmecocystus honeypot ant species, sampling multiple colonies, castes, and organs across four years. We found microbiome community composition was strongly shaped by species, with variation between colonies in M. arenarius, M. depilis, and M. mexicanus. Differences between forager and replete castes were observed in M. arenarius, M. flaviceps, and M. mexicanus. Organ-level differences were observed in the crop and midgut in M. mexicanus. Replete crops of M. mexicanus and M. depilis were enriched in Fructilactobacillus, other lactic acid bacteria, and acetic acid bacteria. These bacteria turn sugars into organic acids that lower pH and can inhibit other microbes. Halophiles were prominent in the guts of M. flaviceps and M. wheeleri, which may reflect the high osmotic stress of concentrated sugars in stored fluids. In this study, we demonstrate that Myrmecocystus ants host species-specific gut microbiomes. While much work remains to understand the relationship between the host ant and its gut microbiome, the repeated presence of acid-producing and stress-tolerant bacteria suggests honeypot ants’ gut microbiome could potentially keep crop contents stable. Importance Previous work showed that fluid stored by Australian honeypot ants has antimicrobial activity, likely influenced by the ants’ gut microbiome. Our study is the first to characterize the gut microbiome of North American honeypot ant species in the genus Myrmecocystus. Our work shows that microbiome composition varies substantially between species, with distinct enrichments of lactic acid bacteria, acetic acid bacteria, or halophiles. These findings suggest that host ecology and environmental conditions, such as diet and the crop’s unique storage environment, can help structure microbial communities. This system provides a framework to examine how host-associated environments shape microbiome composition and function. Understanding microbiome variation in honeypot ants creates opportunities for future work to investigate how microbial communities contribute to the long-term preservation of nutrient-rich resources, analogous to human food preservation and fermentation processes. Our work establishes Myrmecocystus as a model for studying host-microbe symbiosis in extreme nutritional environments, enabling future hypothesis-driven research into microbial function, community assembly, and the evolutionary dynamics of host-associated microbiomes.

title: Discrete dynamic survival analysis of epidemic case line lists
abstract: Case line lists, which record dates of onset, recovery, and hospitalisation, are among the most granular data in infectious disease epidemiology and can provide insights into transmission dynamics. Dynamic survival analysis (DSA) fits a deterministic, differential-equation-based model to line lists to estimate parameters such as infectivity and the infectious period. Infectious periods are usually not exponential, and incorporating this into mechanistic models for line-list data often requires partial differential equation (PDE) schemes that can be difficult to implement and must be customised for each model, which may limit their use. Here, we propose Discrete Dynamic Survival Analysis (DDSA), a discrete-time DSA for case line lists based on difference equations. It matches calendar-day data directly without interpolation, and its log-likelihood is differentiable via forward-mode automatic differentiation, enabling off-the-shelf gradient-based samplers without model-specific numerical infrastructure. Non-exponential infectious periods are accommodated through a boxcar model or a discrete analogue of the "device of stages". We apply the DDSA method to three historical outbreaks of influenza A(H1N1), Ebola, and measles. DDSA estimates of transmission parameters were close to published analyses where these were available, an agreement that partly reflects shared modelling choices, and the method handles incomplete line lists with missing onset or recovery dates. Synthetic experiments show that recovery intervals identify the infectious period, while infection times and final size constrain R0 when the population at risk is known. Discrete DSA provides a simple, extensible framework for simulation and inference of infectious disease dynamics.

title: INFLUÊNCIA DE DIFERENTES PONTAS DE APLICAÇÃO DE BIOINSUMOS E POPULAÇÕES DE PLANTAS NA DEPOSIÇÃO DE GOTAS NA CULTURA DA SOJA (GLYCINE MAX L.)
abstract: The efficiency of bioinput application in soybean is directly related to spray application technology, particularly nozzle characteristics, crop growth stage, and canopy architecture. This study aimed to evaluate the quality of bioinput application at different soybean growth stages, considering spray nozzles, plant populations, and deposition positions within the canopy. The experiment was arranged in a randomized complete block design with a split-split-plot scheme: two plant populations (160,000 and 240,000 plants ha⁻¹) in the main plots; four flat-fan nozzles (TT110.04, TT110.015, TT110.02, and TT110.03) in the subplots; and two sampling positions (upper and lower canopy) and three growth stages (V10, R1, and R5) in the sub-subplots, evaluated as repeated measures. The number of droplets, spray coverage, volume median diameter (VMD), relative span, and deposited spray volume were determined on water-sensitive papers using Gotas® software. Data were analyzed using a Gamma generalized linear model, and means were compared by Fisher’s least significant difference (LSD) test (p ≤ 0.05). The number of droplets was affected by the nozzle × plant population × growth stage interaction. The TT110.02 nozzle provided the highest deposition, coverage, and spray volume at V10 and R5, whereas the TT110.015 stood out for the number of droplets at R1. Deposition and coverage were higher in the upper canopy, indicating reduced droplet penetration at more advanced growth stages. The TT110.04 showed the highest VMD and span values, without resulting in greater deposition. In conclusion, application efficiency depends on the interaction among nozzle, growth stage, and canopy architecture, with the TT110.02 standing out at V10 and R5 and the TT110.015 at R1.

title: PSYCHOMETRIC OPERATIONALIZATION OF FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN AUTONOMOUS MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS BASED ON PERSONAMATRIX: AN AI TRANSITIONAL FIELD FRAMEWORK
abstract: Background: Autonomous LLM agents increasingly operate in shared environments where behavior depends on interaction history, role allocation, local norms, authority, and group structure. Objective: This conceptual methods paper develops a psychometric operationalization of dynamic functional roles in autonomous multi-agent systems using PersonaMatrix-derived measurement principles without attributing human psychological ontology to AI. Methods: A targeted evidence synthesis (2019–2026) was conducted across AI psychometrics, dynamic multi-agent roles, collective-field modeling, norm emergence, trajectory prediction, and anthropomorphism. Peer-reviewed sources were prioritized, while current OpenAI, METR/Redwood, Anthropic, and Moltbook materials were used as primary or emerging evidence for recent agent ecosystems. Results: The framework separates output-level stability (RSI, IDS, RCS) from role-level and field-level constructs. It proposes the Functional Role Consistency Index, Role Transition Index, Agent–Field Differentiation Index, Collective Utility Index, Norm Conflict Index, Regulatory Closure Index, and Field Role Composition Vector. Three falsifiable hypotheses test whether role variables add out-of-sample predictive value for agent behavior, role transitions, and future field states. Conclusion: PersonaMatrix is positioned as a measurement architecture rather than an AI personality diagnosis. The archetypal-role hypothesis is supported only if role coding is reliable, improves prediction beyond non-archetypal baselines, and generalizes to unseen agents and independent multi-agent environments.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in Agricultural University Libraries: Current Trends, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: Agricultural university libraries support the research, teaching and extension mission of agricultural higher education, yet the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into their services has not been systematically theorised or evidenced. This integrative review critically synthesises peer-reviewed articles, conference papers and authoritative institutional reports published between 2015 and 2026 on AI adoption and digital transformation in agricultural and allied academic libraries. Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, AGRIS and CAB Abstracts and were supplemented by Google Scholar, citation chasing and the repositories of FAO, IFLA and UNESCO. Records were screened in two stages against explicit eligibility criteria, and the 64 sources synthesised were appraised by type and strength of evidence. The literature is structured along five application areas: intelligent discovery and semantic search based on agricultural vocabularies such as AGROVOC; automated metadata creation and cataloguing; conversational and virtual reference services, including generative AI assistants; research data management and institutional repositories; and AI-enabled knowledge transfer to extension professionals and farming communities. The synthesis indicates that adoption is uneven and largely experimental, limited less by the availability of technology than by infrastructural gaps, unstable funding, limited AI literacy among library professionals, unresolved privacy and copyright concerns, and the risk of inaccurate or fabricated AI outputs informing high-stakes agricultural decisions. Only seven of the sources deal specifically with agricultural libraries or their information infrastructure, and only two of these report primary empirical data, so evidence from India and other Global South contexts remains very limited. The review proposes a conceptual framework linking institutional readiness, responsible AI governance, librarian capacity development and equitable access to service outcomes for researchers, educators, students and extension personnel working in crop science, climate-resilient agriculture, biodiversity and food security. It offers a domain-specific synthesis largely absent from the library and information science literature, recasts agricultural university libraries as active intermediaries in agricultural knowledge and innovation systems rather than passive repositories, and outlines a prioritised agenda for empirical research, policy and practice.

title: Drivers of Maize Farmers’ Participation in the Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus (Ng-Cares) Programme in Kano and Jigawa States, Nigeria
abstract: Background: The Nigeria Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus (NG-CARES) programme supports smallholder farmers, but evidence on factors associated with maize farmers’ participation in Kano and Jigawa States remains limited. This study examined the socioeconomic and financial characteristics associated with participation. Methods: A multistage sampling technique selected 260 beneficiaries and 260 non-beneficiaries (n = 520) from six Local Government Areas. Questionnaire data were analysed using descriptive statistics and a binary logistic regression model. Results: Beneficiaries had a pooled mean age of 49.70 years, mean household size of 12.67 persons and mean farm size of 1.45 hectares. Corresponding non-beneficiary values were 47.18 years, 13.15 persons and 1.51 hectares. Men accounted for 85.4% of beneficiaries and 95.0% of non-beneficiaries. Participation was positively associated with age (β = 0.0841; p < 0.001), marital status (β = 1.2570; p < 0.001), access to credit (β = 2.9670; p < 0.001) and source of credit (β = 2.0670; p < 0.001). Educational level showed a negative association (β = −0.2538; p = 0.014), while household size showed a weaker negative association (β = −0.0355; p = 0.090). Farm size, major crop grown, major income source, farming experience and access to basic amenities were not statistically significant. Conclusion: The findings indicate that demographic and credit-related characteristics were associated with NG-CARES participation. Programme administrators may strengthen inclusive communication, transparent registration and access to appropriate financing.

title: Farmers’ Knowledge of the Striga Genus and the Impact of Striga [Striga hermonthica (Del.) Benth] on Sorghum [Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench] Productivity in Burkina Faso
abstract: The genus Striga comprises parasitic plants that cause significant crop damage. Despite control strategies, Striga remains the primary biotic constraint for farmers in Burkina Faso. This study used a two-pronged approach to document farmers’ perceptions and knowledge of Striga and assess the impact of S. hermonthica on sorghum productivity. The study combined a survey with a field assessment across five administrative regions of Burkina Faso (Goulmou, Guiriko, Nazinon, Kadiogo, and Oubri). A survey of 385 farmers assessed their knowledge of Striga. The impact of infestation was evaluated in 75 fields across six yield plots measuring 1 m2 per field, comprising three infested and three uninfested plots per field. The data were analysed using univariate and multivariate approaches, as well as linear mixed models. The survey showed that S. hermonthica and S. gesnerioides were the species most familiar to farmers, recognised by 100% and 91.17% of participants, respectively. Striga management relied primarily on mechanical control, with reported frequencies ranging from 37% to 48.4% across sites. Despite its harmful effects, farmers reported using Striga as fodder (8% in Oubri), medicinal products (9% in Goulmou), and veterinary products (10% in Oubri). The field assessment on smallholder farms indicated a negative association between Striga infestation and agronomic traits. Analysis of variance revealed a highly significant effect of the treatment on the variables studied, with F values ranging from 340.11 to 1,038.49 (p < 0.001). Infestation reduced plant height by 17 to 41 percent and grain yield by 59 to 72 percent. These results show that Striga is a major constraint on sorghum production in Burkina Faso and underscore the need to strengthen its management.

title: An Analysis of Market Types and Price Behaviour of Gram (Cicer arietinum L.) in Hanumangarh District of Rajasthan, India
abstract: Background: Gram (chickpea) production and marketing are important to farm households in Hanumangarh district, Rajasthan. Evidence jointly addressing crop growth, seasonal prices, growers’ perceptions of price factors and marketing channels at district level remains limited. Aims: To estimate growth in the area, production and productivity of gram, to study and forecast its price behaviour, to rank the factors affecting its price, and to examine the relationship between market types and price in Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan, India. Study Design: A descriptive-cum-analytical design combining a primary cross-sectional farm survey with secondary time-series data. Place and Duration of Study: Nohar and Bhadra blocks of Hanumangarh district, Rajasthan; the primary survey was conducted during the 2024–25 rabi marketing season, with secondary data for 2004–05 to 2023–24 (area, production, productivity) and 2013–2025 (monthly modal prices). Methodology: A total of 120-gram growers were selected by multistage sampling and interviewed using a structured, pre-tested schedule. The Compound Growth Rate (CGR) and seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) models were used for growth analysis and price forecasting, the Weighted Mean Score (WMS) for ranking price-determining factors, and Pearson’s correlation for the market-type–price relationship. Results: Area, production and productivity grew at 3.46%, 5.99% and 2.45% per annum (P < .001). Prices showed a rising trend with marked seasonality (trough in February–April, peak in August–September); the SARIMA (1,1,2) (0,1,2) ₁₂ model forecast prices of ₹5,668–₹6,520 per quintal (MAPE 2.40%). Arrivals (WMS 4.37), quality (4.32) and demand–supply (4.22) were the most influential factors. Market organisation correlated strongly and positively with price (r = 0.769, n = 210, P < .001), explaining about 59% of price variation, with the regulated mandi and e-NAM giving the highest prices. Conclusion: The type of market significantly determines gram price realisation; promoting organised marketing channels, strengthening storage to exploit the seasonal pattern, and improving grading and market information can raise growers’ incomes.

title: Improving Energy Price Forecasts: Autometrics With Indicator Saturation
abstract: In this study, we evaluate Autometrics, an automated model selection method with controls for outliers and location shifts, against artificial neural networks (ANN) and random forests for six monthly energy price series (WTI, Brent, Dubai, US and Russian gas, Australian coal) from IMF data. Autometrics generally delivers lower RMSE/MAPE and higher directional accuracy than the ANN and random forest specifications considered here, particularly in the more volatile oil and coal markets. Autometrics also has the benefit of being interpretable in a familiar regression context as opposed to more “blackbox” machine learning. The CARDt method often delivers predictive accuracy which is not statistically different from Autometrics, but there is some evidence that simple model averaging of the two with intercept‐corrected Autometrics yields further gains relative to either alone.

title: miR-486-3p knockdown induces testicular ferroptosis by upregulating Acsl4 in mice: a novel molecular target for non-lethal fertility control of rodent pests.
abstract: BACKGROUND Rodent population outbreaks pose serious threats to public health and agricultural production. Traditional lethal rodenticides can cause environmental contamination and poisoning of nontarget organisms, while raising animal welfare concerns, creating an urgent demand for environmentally friendly, nonlethal control strategies. Fertility control through intervention at key molecular targets enables population regulation while preserving ecological integrity, making it a promising nonlethal alternative. Ferroptosis-mediated impairment of testicular function provides a theoretical basis for male fertility control. Nevertheless, key regulatory targets in this pathway remain poorly defined. Here, we used mice as a model to investigate a potential molecular target for inducing male reproductive impairment, laying the foundation for future applications in rodent pest population control. RESULTS We found that miR-486-3p targets the ferroptosis-associated gene encoding acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (Acsl4) and inhibits its expression. miR-486-3p overexpression alleviated peroxide accumulation induced by RAS selective lethal 3 in Sertoli cells and testicular tissue, reducing sensitivity to ferroptosis and indicating that miR-486-3p plays a critical role in regulating ferroptosis. Local knockdown of miR-486-3p in the testis induced peroxide accumulation and ferroptosis, disrupted the seminiferous tubule structure, and caused a 10.8% reduction in testicular weight and a 78.2% reduction in epididymal sperm count. CONCLUSION Our results suggest that miR-486-3p knockdown induces ferroptosis-associated testicular damage by upregulating Acsl4, providing a candidate target for developing nonlethal interventions for rodent pest population management via male fertility control. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Direct and indirect impacts of elephants differentially shape distinct tolerance indicators.
abstract: Human-wildlife coexistence depends on the willingness of people to tolerate the risks posed by wild animals. We analyzed data from a large-scale questionnaire on human-elephant interactions in northern Tanzania to examine three tolerance indicators: willingness to coexist with elephants, support for government-led culling, and attitudes toward poaching. Using Bayesian mixed-effects models and leave-one-out cross-validation, we evaluated how direct impacts of elephants on economic and physical security and indirect effects on well-being were associated with each outcome. Emotional responses (fear and stress) were most strongly associated with unwillingness to coexist with elephants, whereas material costs (crop and property damage) were more strongly associated with support for government-led culling. Attitudes toward poaching were weakly associated with elephant impacts. These findings show that tolerance indicators are not interchangeable or directly comparable, as different wildlife impacts are associated with distinct conservation-relevant responses. Human-wildlife coexistence studies should therefore carefully consider how tolerance is measured.

title: Efficient hybrid quantum-classical neural networks generation for crop yield prediction using sequential satellite images
abstract: A novel approach is introduced that enables the automatic generation of hybrid quantum-classical neural networks using a two-step optimization process, combining multiobjective genetic algorithms specifically designed for time series on satellite images with a subsequent continuous refinement stage of the circuit’s parameters. This strategy provides models with low prediction error and low complexity in terms of trainable parameters. The application of this methodology focuses on using Sentinel-2 satellite images to forecast future values of the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), which holds great significance in agriculture since it is used as an indicator of crop health and yield. The hybrid model is evaluated on random validation pixels and full images, and compared against tuned classical baselines to assess its performance.

Geospatial multi-indicator assessment of flood risk in a wetland ecosystem, using a PCA-weighted risk framework
abstract: Flood risk in wetland ecosystems is increasing due to hydro-climatic variability, land-use changes, and socio-economic vulnerability, particularly in low-lying regions of South Asia. This study presents a geospatial multi-indicator framework to assess flood risk in the Chalan Beel, one of the largest freshwater wetland ecosystems in Bangladesh. The assessment integrates four major risk components (hazard, exposure, vulnerability, and capacity) using the analytical relationship. A total of 23 spatial indicators derived from satellite data, digital elevation models, socio-economic datasets, and open geospatial sources were incorporated. All variables were normalized and resampled to ensure spatial consistency. Indicator weights were determined using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), allowing integration of multi-dimensional variables. Results indicate that 22.85% of the study area falls in the moderate hazard class, while 20.74% and 16.93% fall in the high and very high hazard classes, respectively, under quantile classification. Each exposure class covers approximately 19 to 21% of the area, which is a consequence of the equal-count property of quantile classification and not evidence of a balanced spatial distribution. Elevation (23% weight) and unemployment rate (18%) received the largest exposure weights. Children and elderly population densities received the highest PCA weights (27% each) and therefore contributed most to the spatial variance of the vulnerability component. These weights describe statistical contribution to spatial differentiation and not causal importance. Capacity indicators reveal limited adaptive infrastructure in several locations, and distance to flood shelter (39%) received the largest capacity weight. The integrated assessment places 23.47% of the study area in the relatively high flood risk class and 21.01% in the relatively moderate class. These are relative rankings within the study area under quantile classification and not absolute risk levels, and they indicate spatial heterogeneity in relative risk. Comparison with observed inundation maps of the Bangladesh Water Development Board for 2022 to 2024 gave an area under the ROC curve of 0.84, and the index was compared with alternative weighting and aggregation schemes. Areas characterized by low elevation, proximity to rivers and beels, and higher population sensitivity fall in the relatively highest risk classes. The findings provide a spatially explicit framework to support wetland-focused disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation planning, and sustainable management of wetland ecosystems in Bangladesh.

Thrombolysis and thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: A RAND/UCLA consensus.
abstract: INTRODUCTION The treatment of acute ischemic stroke in the pediatric population involves considerable uncertainty due to the limited evidence on intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. The objective was to assess the contribution of different scenario variables to the appropriateness of thrombolysis and thrombectomy in children and adolescents, as an aid to clinical decision-making. MATERIALS AND METHODS The RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method was applied. A multidisciplinary panel assessed theoretical clinical scenarios, differentiating two age groups: ≥30 days to 2 years, and >2 to 2 to <18 years. The models showed a good overall fit, with Nagelkerke pseudo-R2 values of 0.833 and 0.784, respectively, which allowed summarizing the criteria in the form of decision trees. CONCLUSIONS Appropriateness criteria were established to support decision-making regarding thrombolysis and thrombectomy in pediatric ischemic stroke. Lesion location and symptom onset were the variables that contributed most to model fit, depending on the age group. These criteria may support decision-making in contexts of clinical uncertainty, although they cannot replace clinical judgment.

title: Elastin-based polypeptide-Fc fusion for extended subcutaneous exposure and sustained thrombopoietic activity.
abstract: Immune thrombocytopenia is characterized by increased platelet destruction and impaired platelet production. Thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs) stimulate megakaryopoiesis, but the influence of elastin-based polypeptide (EBP) length on the hydrodynamic properties and platelet responses of Fc-fused TPO-RAs remains unclear. We generated three EBP-Fc fusion TPO-RAs-NT-202 G3, G6, and G12-and evaluated their physicochemical properties, biological activity, and platelet responses; G12 was also examined in an exploratory pharmacokinetic study. The variants, produced in Expi293 cells, differed only in EBP length; all remained soluble at 37°C in phosphate-buffered saline, and hydrodynamic size increased with EBP length. Binding was detected in BaF3/hMPL cells expressing the human thrombopoietin receptor but was minimal in parental BaF3 cells. The variants induced M-07e cell proliferation, JAK2-STAT signaling, and megakaryocytic differentiation of human CD34+ cells. After a single subcutaneous dose of 500 µg/kg in normal mice, platelet elevation persisted longest with NT-202 G12. At 2000 µg/kg, NT-202 G12 peaked at 72 h and remained quantifiable through 336 h. Because the pharmacokinetic study lacked an intravenous arm, used a different dose from the platelet-response studies, and relied on composite mean profiles, it was interpreted descriptively and could not distinguish absorption from elimination or establish an exposure-response relationship. In an anti-CD41 antibody-induced acute thrombocytopenia model, NT-202 G12 and romiplostim, an Fc-peptide TPO-RA, increased platelet counts without a significant between-group difference on day 9. Overall, this exploratory proof-of-concept study suggests that EBP block length is a genetically encoded design variable associated with hydrodynamic size and platelet-response duration.

title: Comprehensive Immunoprofiling and Multi-Omics Modeling Reveal Key Immune Features Associated with Disease Progression and Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Comprehensive profiling of peripheral immune cells has shown prognostic and disease-monitoring value across multiple cancers, but its clinical relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), particularly unresectable HCC, remains insufficiently defined. To address this gap, we performed integrated peripheral immunoprofiling combining T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing, flow cytometry-based T-cell phenotyping, bulk RNA sequencing, and public single-cell RNA-seq analysis in healthy donors, resectable HCC patients, and unresectable HCC patients. This design enabled characterization of HCC-associated and stage-associated peripheral immune alterations and identification of immunotherapy-relevant features in unresectable HCC. Single-cell analysis and flow cytometry revealed remodeling of circulating T-cell states in unresectable HCC, including reduced naïve-like compartments, enrichment of Treg-like cells, and increased memory/effector differentiation. TCR repertoire analysis showed reduced diversity, increased clonal dominance, altered V-J gene usage, decreased interindividual sharing, and convergent motif-level alterations, with early CD4+ TCR perturbations in resectable HCC and more pronounced CD8+ repertoire restriction in unresectable disease. Exploratory GLIPH-based motif analysis, HLA inference, and peptide-HLA binding prediction suggested candidate motif-HLA antigen associations involving hepatitis virus-derived antigens and recurrent HCC mutation-derived candidate neoantigens, although experimental validation is required. Bulk RNA-seq of peripheral CD8+ T cells revealed higher Activation/Effector function, Exhaustion, and Anergy signature scores in both resectable and unresectable HCC than in HDs, with no significant differences between the two HCC groups, whereas the Chemokine/Chemokine receptor signature was specifically increased in unresectable HCC. The overall IFN-response signature did not differ significantly among the three groups. Integrative machine-learning models were then developed using 818 peripheral immune-related features. Among them, the random forest (RF) model effectively distinguished healthy donors, resectable HCC patients, and unresectable HCC patients, with consistently high sensitivity and area under the curve (AUC) in both cross-validation and an independent validation cohort. In unresectable HCC patients receiving immunotherapy, four features derived from TCR-seq and T-cell subset profiling discriminated responders (CR/PR) from non-responders (SD/PD) in univariate analyses, while multivariate prioritization further highlighted ULBP1 as a consistently prioritized response-associated feature that requires validation in an independent cohort. Overall, this study supports comprehensive peripheral immune profiling as an exploratory framework for identifying stage-associated immune alterations and candidate biomarkers to inform personalized immunotherapy strategies in HCC.

DiffSOMNet: A deep model with differentiable soft self-organizing maps and temporal rate-coded integration for waste classification
abstract: Accurate waste classification is vital for achieving sustainable waste management and reducing the environmental footprint of urbanization. Misclassification of recyclable materials contributes to landfill accumulation, inefficient recycling, and increased greenhouse gas emissions. To address these issues, this study introduces HybridSOMSpikeNet, a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates convolutional feature extraction, differentiable self-organization, and spiking-inspired temporal processing to enable intelligent and energy-efficient waste classification. The proposed model employs a pre-trained ResNet-152 backbone to extract deep spatial representations, followed by a Differentiable Soft Self-Organizing Map (Soft-SOM) that enhances topological clustering and interpretability. A spiking neural head accumulates temporal activations over discrete time steps, improving robustness and generalization. Trained on a ten-class waste dataset, HybridSOMSpikeNet achieved a test accuracy of 97.39%, outperforming several state-of-the-art architectures while maintaining a lightweight computational profile suitable for real-world deployment. Beyond its technical innovations, the framework provides tangible environmental benefits. By enabling precise and automated waste segregation, it supports higher recycling efficiency, reduces contamination in recyclable streams, and minimizes the ecological and operational costs of waste processing. The approach aligns with global sustainability priorities, particularly the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 11 and SDG 12), by contributing to cleaner cities, circular economy initiatives, and intelligent environmental management systems.

title: Diagnosing urban ecosystem service flow dynamics under supply-demand mismatch: A coupled social-ecological network and gravity modeling approach with evidence from Wuhan.
abstract: Rapid urbanization intensifies spatial mismatches between ecosystem service supply and demand (ESSD), yet existing studies rarely quantify supply-demand relationships, extract spatial pathways, and estimate flow volumes for multiple services within a single analytical architecture. To address this gap, we coupled social-ecological networks with the gravity model to construct an integrated analytical framework that simultaneously characterizes ESSD patterns, service-specific transmission pathways, and distance-decay flow allocation. Using Wuhan (2005-2025) as a case study, we examined five ecosystem services: crop production (CP), water yield (WY), carbon storage (CS), biodiversity support (BS), and recreation (RE). Three findings emerge. First, all five ESSD patterns exhibit a persistent "central deficits versus peripheral surpluses" spatial configuration, with deficit zones expanding outward over time except for CS. Second, network metrics varied by service type without consistent structural reorganization. CP had the highest connectivity, whereas WY had the lowest (mean 1.44%). Among infrastructure-dependent services, weighted degree was higher for CP and RE than for WY, while CS and BS showed uniformly low values because their edge weights were set to 1. CS and BS had the highest clustering coefficients (0.265 and 0.263), while WY had the lowest (0.056) and the shortest average path length (2.13). Average path length did not decline consistently: it decreased slightly for CP and BS, increased for RE, and remained nearly stable for CS. Core nodes contributed disproportionately to network connectivity relative to peripheral nodes. As supply-demand deficit zones expanded outward from the urban core, virtual flow pathways increased accordingly, whereas actual pathways for CP, WY, BS, and RE shifted from inner suburb-core to outer suburb-inner suburb configurations; those for CS remained stable. Third, flow volumes declined for CP (-68.9%) and CS (-21.3%) but increased for RE (+11.6%), with WY showing the largest interannual fluctuations. These trends were associated with intensifying ESSD mismatches and heterogeneous transmission media. The framework is subject to uncertainties from closed-boundary constraints, neighborhood-priority matching, and isotropic distance decay, which may bias cross-boundary and omnidirectional flows. By enabling unified characterization of ESSD relationships, spatial pathways, and flow processes, the proposed framework provides a replicable toolkit for urban-scale ESF quantification and spatial network analysis. Our findings highlight a sustainability dilemma in rapidly urbanizing regions, characterized by ecological supply contraction, escalating anthropogenic demand, and persistent spatial mismatches, and provide a scientific foundation for ecological space optimization and trans-regional compensation design.

title: Vertical homogenization and legacy sinks of phthalate esters in arid artificial oasis agricultural soils: Implications for long-term management.
abstract: Intensive plastic mulching and agrochemical use in arid oasis agroecosystems exacerbate phthalate ester (PAEs) pollution. However, conventional topsoil monitoring (e.g., 0-20 cm) systematically underestimates deeper soil burdens. This study investigated the occurrence, source apportionment, and health risks of nine PAEs across the 0-60 cm soil profile at 107 agricultural sites in Northwest China. Σ9PAEs exhibited consistent vertical homogenization (averaging 154-159 μg/kg) across the 0-60 cm profile, dominated by di-n-butyl phthalate (DBP) and di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP). Regional practices like deep tillage and mulched drip irrigation likely facilitate this downward migration, which may contribute to a deep-profile legacy sink. Linear mixed-effects modeling revealed strong within-site clustering across the profile (ICC = 0.83), with substantially greater variation among sites than among depth layers within a site; although current single-season mulching was associated with a detectable concentration elevation (P 99.9% of the total estimated risk under the deterministic BAF-based framework. These findings indicate that while halting plastic film usage is indispensable for preventing new inputs, it must be paired with deep-soil remediation strategies to effectively mitigate the entrenched legacy burden. A paradigm shift from topsoil monitoring to comprehensive deep-profile regulation and long-term source reduction is imperative to safeguard agricultural sustainability in arid regions.

From deterministic selection to stochastic drift: Salinity-associated patterns of bacterial community assembly and predicted functional potential in the Pearl River estuarine sediments.
abstract: Salinity gradients in estuaries strongly shape microbial communities and biogeochemical processes, but the links between salinity-driven shifts in bacterial diversity, community assembly, ecological networks, and functional potential remain to be incompletely understood. Here, we investigated bacterial community dynamics across a natural salinity gradient in surface sediments of the Pearl River Estuary, using 16S rRNA gene sequencing combined with neutral community modeling (NCM), β-nearest taxon index (βNTI), infer Community Assembly Mechanisms by Phylogenetic-bin-based null model (iCAMP), co-occurrence network analysis, and functional prediction. Bacterial richness followed a unimodal pattern, peaking at intermediate salinity. Salinity was the primary driver of community variation, explaining 35.9% of the variation, followed by NH4+ at 13.4%. Community assembly shifted from stronger deterministic selection under low and intermediate salinity to increased stochasticity under high salinity, supported by higher neutral model fits and enhanced ecological drift detected by iCAMP. High-salinity communities formed simpler networks, mainly characterized by weakened taxon associations rather than reduced taxonomic participation. Predicted functional profiles showed greater representation of heterotrophic carbon processing and denitrification at low salinity and sulfur-related respiration at high salinity. Overall, our findings indicate that salinity gradients regulate estuarine sediment bacterial communities through coordinated effects on species turnover, community assembly, network structure, and functional differentiation, offering a baseline perspective that may help inform potential microbial community responses under future hydrological variability and seawater intrusion.

title: Adhesive hydrogel-mediated spatiotemporal delivery of garlic-derived nanovesicles reprograms immunometabolism to rescue periodontal bone regeneration.
abstract: The core challenge in regenerating inflammatory bone defects, such as periodontitis-related bone resorption, lies in the dysregulation of the immune-metabolic microenvironment, which required implanted materials to simultaneously possess tissue sealing properties, sustained immune modulation capacity and metabolic intervention functions. Herein, garlic-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (GaELNs), exhibiting anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities, are embedded in an injectable, tissue-adhesive polyethylene glycol hydrogel (GaE-PEG) to meet the challenges. The hydrogel exhibited favorable tissue adhesion and sustained release of GaELN-associated protein in vitro. GaE-PEG promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated periodontal ligament stem cells, GaE-PEG alleviated mitochondrial oxidative stress, restored oxidative phosphorylation, suppressed excessive glycolysis, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses linked these effects to mitochondrial metabolic regulation, while oligomycin treatment attenuated the osteogenic response, supporting a contribution of oxidative phosphorylation. In a rat model of periodontitis-related bone defects, GaE-PEG reduced local inflammation and promoted alveolar bone regeneration, with improved regenerative outcomes compared with a single local injection of free GaELNs at an equivalent dose and Bio-Gide™/Bio-Oss™ treatment. These findings support an adhesive hydrogel strategy integrating local nanovesicle delivery with immunomodulation and metabolic regulation to promote bone regeneration under inflammatory conditions.

Unraveling Yb3+-mediated temperature-dependent upconversion luminescence in Er3+-activated fluoride under 1550 nm excitation.
abstract: Thermoresponsive upconversion luminescent materials can convert thermal variations into visually distinguishable optical signals, offering potential for noncontact temperature sensing, temperature visualization, information encryption, and anti-counterfeiting. However, it remains challenging for current thermochromic upconversion materials to achieve pronounced temperature-induced color variation under single near-infrared excitation. Herein, NaYbF4:Er3+ nanoparticles with a dense Yb sublattice were employed as a model system, exhibiting a thermochromic evolution from green through yellow and orange to red under 1550 nm excitation. By progressively substituting Yb3+ with optically inert Y3+ to dilute the Yb sublattice and further constructing an inert shell structure to suppress surface-related energy loss, the distinct roles of ErYb back energy transfer, YbYb energy migration, and migration-assisted surface dissipation were differentiated. The distinct thermal responses of the red and green emissions arise from different Yb sublattice-mediated surface energy dissipation mainly affecting the red emission and back energy transfer together with nonradiative processes governing the green emission. Benefiting from the pronounced temperature-induced color evolution, temperature-driven dynamic digital information switching and a flame-shaped temperature-visualization label were demonstrated. These results reveal the nonconventional regulatory role of the Yb sublattice under direct Er3+ excitation and provide a mechanistic basis for designing thermochromic upconversion materials for visual thermal information readout and optical information encoding.

Endothelial small extracellular vesicle-derived lncDLX1 facilitates bone repair by recruiting RBMX to activate Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
abstract: Interface integration failure after implanting bone repair material is a core challenge in treating bone defects. This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanism by which endothelial cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (EC-sEVs) deliver lncRNA DLX1 (lncDLX1) to regulate the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs through both in vitro and in vivo experiments. The results showed that lncDLX1 expression was significantly downregulated in an inflammatory microenvironment and that overexpression of lncDLX1 promoted BMSC osteogenic differentiation while inhibiting inflammatory responses. Mechanistic studies revealed that lncDLX1 binds to RBMX, which then transcriptionally activates β-catenin expression and enhances its mRNA stability by binding to the CTNNB1 promoter region, thereby activating the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. Functional experiments confirmed that EC-sEVscould be effectively taken up by BMSCs and functionally deliver lncDLX1, and GW4869 treatment attenuated this regulatory effect, supporting the involvement of sEVs. In vivo experiments showed that hydroxyapatite materials loaded with lncDLX1-overexpressing BMSCs significantly promoted bone repair in a rat femoral defect model. In summary, this study reveals the central role of the EC-sEVs/lncDLX1/RBMX/Wnt/β-catenin signaling axis in bone repair, providing a new theoretical basis for the development of sEV-based lncRNA bone repair strategies.

title: A pH-Responsive and Cofactor-Self-Sufficient DNAzyme@ZIF-8 Probe for Imaging APE1 Activity in Tumor Metastasis and Oxidative Stress.
abstract: Human apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1) exhibits aberrant expression and distribution as cells acquire metastatic potential. However, the complex intracellular environment often limits the recognition accuracy of probes based on a single target. Leveraging pathophysiology-associated microenvironmental conditions as endogenous triggers enables the spatial control of molecular imaging signals, thereby enhancing the differentiation between cancerous and non-cancerous cells. Herein, we developed a pH-responsive, cofactor-self-sufficient probe for APE1 activity imaging based on the acid-responsiveness of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) and Zn2+-dependent deoxyribozyme (DNAzyme) signal amplification. ZIF-8 not only effectively delivers DNA probes into cancer cells but also provides the essential cofactor (Zn2+) for signal amplification. This probe distinguishes cancer cells from normal cells in both cell lysates and living cells, demonstrating its potential application in the precision diagnosis of malignant tumors. Further investigations revealed that APE1 promoted the epithelial-mesenchymal transition in the TGF-β-induced model. In the hydrogen peroxide-induced oxidative stress model, moderate oxidative stress elevated APE1 activity and enhanced cell proliferation and migration, while excessive stress showed the opposite effect. These results establish the relationship between APE1 activity and cell behaviors in tumor metastasis and under oxidative stress and suggest that oxidative stress plays a complex role in the regulation of tumor metastasis.

title: Systematic Discrepancies Should Be Addressed Before Effective Parameter Learning: Insights From Soil Moisture Simulations Using Differentiable Process‐Based Models
abstract: Differentiable hydrologic models combining neural networks with process‐based backbones—fully implemented or approximated by surrogate models—offer highly competitive accuracy and improved interpretability compared to either model type used alone. However, the impacts of surrogate model fidelity (accurate sensitivity of relationships compared to the original model) and systematic discrepancies between models and observations on parameter learning effectiveness remain underexplored. This study evaluates optimization performance of the differentiable HBV model ( δ HBV) and its surrogate variants in simulating soil moisture across the contiguous United States. Results show that high‐fidelity surrogate models can support effective differentiable parameter learning once systematic discrepancies are addressed. In contrast, unresolved systematic discrepancies degrade optimization performance, with particularly severe deterioration when low‐fidelity surrogates are used. These findings provide one possible explanation for the modest improvements reported in recent surrogate‐based differentiable parameter learning (dPL) applications. Linear correction partially mitigates these systematic discrepancies, improves optimization performance, and reduces compensatory parameter adjustment, although it does not resolve the underlying model–observation mismatch. Structural refinement remains a physically grounded long‐term direction, while pragmatic correction modules can provide useful partial mitigation when such refinement is not yet available. In addition, fully implementing differentiable process‐based models or using a rigorously trained surrogate can improve gradient fidelity and reduce amplified deterioration associated with surrogate infidelity.
