title: Hybrid attention and learning mechanism-based deep learning model for crop yield prediction
abstract: An accurate crop yield prediction is necessary for augmenting farming practices and guaranteeing the security of food. Several approaches have been developed to predict the yield of crops. The conventional approaches were incapable of discovering non-linear relationship amid the data, and they exhibit several drawbacks, such as computational overhead, false errors, overfitting issues, limited resources, poor generalizability and computational complexity, which lead to inaccurate predictions. To overcome these limitations, the research proposed a Multi-Attention and Distilled Task Learning enabled Weighted Decision tree based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (MA-DTL-WDBiLSTM) model to predict the crop yield accurately. The model’s performance in forecasting the crop yield is enhanced due to the incorporation of multi attention mechanism and Distilled Task Learning, which distilled the gained knowledge from the teacher model to the student model and split the tasks into subtasks, respectively. Additionally, the integration of the weighted decision tree in the Bi-LSTM model offers an improved prediction accuracy by handling the intricate data and concentrating on the relevant features. The model is evaluated using the Crop yield prediction dataset and the Agricultural Crop Yield in Indian States Dataset, which enhances the interpretability and better generalizability. Specifically, the proposed MA-DTL-WDBiLSTM model achieved a minimum correlation of 0.884, MAE of 1.759, MSE of 6.536, and RMSE of 2.556 using the Agricultural Crop Yield in Indian States Dataset, showcasing high performance in crop yield prediction and outperforming other existing models.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Metabolic signature combined with changes in proteome and transcriptome shape respiratory syncytial virus infection and response to vaccination in a bovine model.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major respiratory disease in infants leading to long-term morbidity. Bovine RSV (bRSV) serves as a clinically translatable large animal model to understand host responses in neonates to vaccination and re-infection enabling straightforward and accessible sample collection not often possible in human infants. This study probes clinically relevant bovine biointerfaces by combining Raman spectroscopy-based metabolic profiling with proteomics and gene expression in nasal fluid, serum, and lung tissues collected from 11 vaccinated (V) and 11 non-vaccinated (NV) neonatal calves following bRSV rechallenge. The analyses showed at Day 7 post-challenge, 16 significant Raman metabolite peaks in nasal fluid, 17 peaks in sera, and 17 peaks in lesioned lung tissue differentiated V from NV calves including features associated with glucose, lipids and fatty acids, and phenylalanine among others. We find that in NV calves systemic metabolic changes were greater than in the V group, and in an exploratory proteomic analysis of a subset of animals (n = 4/group), we identified a complement and innate immune protein signature in NV calves that aligned with metabolic features. In lesioned lung tissue, immune engagement between V and NV calves differed with changes observed in multiple metabolites that tightly correlated with gene expression and showed higher inflammatory cytokine gene expression (IL17A, IL6, IFNγ, IFNβ, IL8) in NV calves. Collectively, our data show an integrative approach enables a comprehensive molecular view of translationally relevant biointerfaces to understand vaccination and reinfection-associated host response. The outcomes of this study can be leveraged in the long-term to understand treatment response in human RSV.

title: How Human–AI Interaction Reshapes Construction Workers’ Safety Behaviors: Insights from Agent-Based Modeling
abstract: The complex nature of human–artificial intelligence (AI) interaction (HAI) introduces new challenges for worker safety. While ensuring human well-being in HAI has become a shared objective, the lack of quantifiable approaches limits our ability to capture its nuanced effects on workers. To address this gap, the present study develops an agent-based modeling framework grounded in stimulus-organism-response (SOR) theory. The model simulates workers’ interactions with AI systems and peers within a bounded two-dimensional space, tracking the resulting cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses. It comprises three components: worker-agent design, SOR process modeling, and an interaction rule base. Experiments were conducted under three scenarios: (1) repeated simulations with balanced parameter settings, (2) batch simulations with varying parameter settings, and (3) empirical validation at a real smart construction site. Results demonstrate that workers’ safety behavior progressively deteriorates as HAI deepens, with extra-role safety behavior exhibiting the most pronounced decline. This study extends the application of SOR theory to the construction industry and deepens the understanding of HAI in the context of construction safety. Practically, it underscores the cumulative cognitive and emotional effects of HAI on workers, providing both a managerial basis for defining human–AI boundaries and a quantifiable tool for long-term safety decision-making.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Quantitative Evaluation and Machine Learning–Based Diagnostic Warning Method for Multilayer Heterogeneous Reservoir Development: A Case Study from Z Oilfield, Dongpu Depression, China
abstract: Rational evaluation and warning-oriented diagnosis of development performance are essential for efficient management of multilayer heterogeneous reservoirs because they support timely identification of underperforming development units. In this study, a quantitative fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method and a machine learning–based diagnostic warning framework are proposed. First, 10 evaluation indicators integrating geological, development, and economic factors were selected from 68 candidate parameters across eight key aspects. Second, the index weight set was calculated by combining the criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC) method, coefficient of variation (COV) method, and analytic hierarchy process (AHP), and the trichotomy method was used to determine the classification boundaries of good, medium, and poor. Based on the established quantitative evaluation method, 52 development units of the Z Oilfield, a mature multilayer heterogeneous fault-block waterflooding oilfield in the Dongpu Depression, China, were quantitatively evaluated. Third, a diagnostic warning model was developed by comparing multiple regression models, including linear regression, ridge regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and back-propagation (BP) neural network. The 52 development units were divided into training and independent testing subsets at a ratio of 70:30, and fivefold cross-validation was performed within the training subset for model assessment. The results show that gradient boosting achieved the best testing performance among the tested models, with a test coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.737, root-mean square error (RMSE) of 5.940, and mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.884. Finally, the selected model was applied to 10 representative development units, and the results indicated that M82 requires particular attention, and several medium-level units should be continuously monitored. The proposed method provides a practical tool for quantitative evaluation, diagnostic warning, and refined management of multilayer heterogeneous reservoirs.

title: Mechanism Construction and Combustion Characteristics Analysis of Diesel Fuel Blended with Nano-CeO 2
abstract: The catalytic influence of CeO 2 nanoparticles on diesel combustion was investigated through detailed kinetic modeling. A diesel surrogate consisting of n - dodecane ( NC 12 H 26 ) and p-xylene ( C 8 H 10 ) was adopted to represent the major chemical characteristics of real diesel fuel. A catalytic reaction mechanism describing the redox behavior of cerium dioxide ( CeO 2 ) was incorporated into the base fuel mechanism to construct a simplified kinetic framework for CeO 2 nanofuels. Combustion simulations were performed under various initial temperatures and pressures to evaluate the influence of CeO 2 nanoparticles on ignition behavior and combustion reactivity. The results indicate that the addition of CeO 2 significantly promotes the formation of OH and H 2 O 2 radicals at relatively low temperatures, leading to shorter ignition delay and enhanced heat release rates. At higher temperatures, combustion is dominated by rapid thermal decomposition of fuel molecules, which reduces the dependence of the system on catalytic radical generation and weakens the catalytic influence of CeO 2 . Furthermore, CeO 2 nanoparticles accelerate hydrocarbon oxidation and CO conversion while also enhancing nitrogen oxides ( NO x ) reduction reactions. Reaction pathway analysis shows that the primary oxidation pathways of the base fuel remain unchanged, whereas the catalytic reactions mainly affect radical formation and intermediate oxidation processes. These findings provide insight into the catalytic combustion mechanism of CeO 2 nanofuels and their potential for improving diesel combustion performance.

title: Risk Assessment of Earth-Rock Dams: A Data-Knowledge Dual-Driven Approach Using IAHP-CRITIC and Two-Dimensional Cloud Model
abstract: This paper proposes a novel data-knowledge dual-driven risk assessment methodology, addressing the limitations of traditional approaches, such as excessive subjectivity, incomplete weighting allocation, and reliance on a single evaluation dimension. The method is based on the improved analytic hierarchy process-criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (IAHP-CRITIC) combined weighting method and two-dimensional cloud model (TDCM). It innovatively constructs a new scoring method for the factor layer of the evaluation index system by utilizing quantitative indexes such as anomaly rate, aging components, change amplitude, and development trend from monitoring data. First, risk probability and consequence are adopted as assessment dimensions to construct a risk assessment system for earth-rock dams, incorporating key monitoring elements such as environmental factors, deformation, seepage, and stress–strain. By analyzing indexes including anomaly rate, aging component, change amplitude, and development trend, the scores for each evaluation index at the factor layer for both risk probability and consequence are determined, and the corresponding cloud digital characteristics are subsequently computed. Second, the IAHP-CRITIC combined weighting method is employed to determine the weights of evaluation indexes within the TDCM framework. Finally, by integrating the risk cloud map and the proximity concept, the risk level is evaluated intuitively and precisely regarding risk probability and consequence. The method is applied to the risk assessment of a concrete-faced rockfill dam in Xinjiang, China. The results indicate strong agreement with the inspection conclusions of the project. Compared with the one-dimensional cloud model (ODCM), the proposed TDCM better captures multidimensional and random uncertainties, offering an effective and rapid tool for the quantitative assessment of dam safety risks.

title: Host and anatomical filters prevent microbiome convergence in avian scavengers.
abstract: How host-associated microbiomes assemble under intense environmental microbial exposure remains a central question in microbial ecology. Vultures represent a unique natural system because these species differ markedly in feeding ecology and carcass use. We characterized bacterial communities across four anatomical niches (facial, buccal, tracheal, and cloacal) in 155 individuals spanning all four European obligate vulture species (subfamily Gypaetinae: Gypaetus barbatus, Neophron percnopterus, and Aegypiinae: Aegypius monachus and Gyps fulvus) and the facultative scavenger Milvus milvus. Microbiome composition was jointly structured by host species and anatomical niche, with host identity explaining more variation than anatomical compartment and a significant interaction indicating that interspecific differentiation depended on body site. Each niche supported distinct bacterial assemblages and core microbiomes: Cloacal communities were enriched in anaerobic gut-associated taxa, whereas facial and tracheal communities contained more environmental and respiratory-associated bacteria. Host-specific taxonomic signatures persisted within anatomical niches despite recurrent exposure to the same carrion-associated microbial pool. Age further influenced community composition, whereas sex had little detectable effect. The facultative scavenger showed the same broad anatomical compartmentalization observed in obligate scavengers, although taxonomic signatures differed among species. Thus, sustained exposure to a shared, microbially rich resource was insufficient to produce a common scavenger microbiome. Instead, microbiome assembly reflected hierarchical filtering by host identity, anatomical environment, and ontogeny. These findings distinguish microbial exposure from microbial persistence, establishing avian scavengers as a natural model for understanding how host-associated communities remain differentiated, despite recurrent exposure to shared environmental microbial reservoirs across ecological and anatomical scales in vertebrate hosts.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Coevolution of social network structure and life history in toothed whales.
abstract: Toothed whales offer a 34 My-long natural experiment for the evolution of complex mammalian societies. However, quantitative comparative analyses of social structure in these species are lacking. Here, we draw on existing social network analyses to compare social structure across toothed whales. We consider published measures of two social network traits across all toothed whales: modularity ([Formula: see text]), which captures divisions or "cliques" in a social community, and social differentiation ([Formula: see text]), which estimates how much whales vary in their relationships-whether they associate equally with others or form special bonds with specific individuals. Combining these with a recently published database of life history traits, we applied phylogenetic multilevel models with the objective of exploring the origins of social network structure. We identified 98 measures of modularity and 89 measures of social differentiation from 23 toothed whale species. Social network structure was more similar among closely related species (showing strong phylogenetic signal), despite substantial intraspecific variability. Toothed whales with longer lifespans and larger bodies tended to form more modular social networks, as did those where males were proportionally larger than females. Similar but weaker patterns were found between life history traits and social differentiation. Results from causal coevolutionary models provide preliminary evidence that social structure has been both a leader and follower of changes in life history. Our findings reveal the correlated evolution of social network structure and life history traits in toothed whales, shedding new light on the origins of social relationships.

title: Effects of Hydroxytyrosol at graded doses on neuroinflammation and the NF-κB pathway are associated with ameliorated cognitive decline in a rat model of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH) is a key factor in vascular cognitive impairment, and persistent neuroinflammation plays a central role in its development. Studies suggested that the Mediterranean diet, which features extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) as the primary source of fat, can significantly improve cognitive function. Hydroxytyrosol (HT), a polyphenol found in EVOO, plays a crucial role in protecting cognitive function. The present study aims to investigate the effects of HT on cognition in CCH rats and the underlying mechanisms. METHODS The rat CCH model was established by permanent bilateral common carotid artery ligation. Dl-3-n-butylphthalide (NBP) served as the positive control. HT was administered at three dose levels. Cognitive function was assessed and pathological changes in the hippocampus were examined. Levels of apoptosis, neuroinflammation, and myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88) /NF-κB pathway activity were evaluated via immunofluorescence, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and western blotting. RESULTS CCH induced cognitive impairment and increased hippocampal neuronal apoptosis, as well as neuroinflammation and activation of the MyD88/NF-κB pathway in rats. These effects were partially reversed by supplementation with NBP or HT. Notably, the medium dose of HT produced the most favorable results, while the high dose did not demonstrate superior efficacy. CONCLUSIONS HT treatment is associated with reduced neuroinflammation and inhibition of the MyD88/NF-κB pathway, which may contribute to the alleviation of CCH-induced cognitive impairment. The optimal effect is observed at the medium dose rather than the high dose.

title: Differentiable quantum-trajectory simulation of Lindblad dynamics for QGP transport-coefficient inference
abstract: We study parameter estimation for the transport coefficients of the quark-gluon plasma by differentiating open-quantum-system-based Monte Carlo simulations of quarkonium suppression. The underlying simulator requires solving a Lindblad equation in a large Hilbert space, which makes parameter estimation computationally expensive. We approach the problem using gradient-based optimization. Specifically, we apply the score-function gradient estimator to differentiate through discrete jump sampling in the Monte Carlo wave-function algorithm used to solve the Lindblad equation. The resulting stochastic gradient estimator exhibits sufficiently low variance and can still be estimated in an embarrassingly parallel manner, enabling efficient scaling of the simulations. We implement this gradient estimator in the existing open-source quarkonium suppression code QTraj. To demonstrate its utility for parameter estimation, we infer the two transport coefficients κ and γ using gradient-based optimization on synthetic nuclear modification factor data.

title: Insight discordance differentiates behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia from false positives.
abstract: Behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) can present with behavioural symptoms similar to psychiatric mimics of the disease (sometimes termed 'phenocopies'). Despite this overlap, loss of insight is a cardinal feature of bvFTD unlike most psychiatric disorders. This study tested whether insight could be quantified to improve diagnostic accuracy in distinguishing these conditions, and examined neuroimaging correlates of impaired insight. In this prospective cohort study, 27 patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) presenting as the bvFTD phenotype and 25 false-positives of bvFTD who ultimately had a psychiatric disorder underwent patient, informant, and clinician symptom ratings on a modified Frontal Behavioural Inventory (FBI). Discrepancy scores were calculated, diagnostic discrimination was evaluated by area under the curve (AUC) with leave-one-out cross-validation, alongside a neuroimaging analysis of network-level associations of insight in bvFTD. Patients with bvFTD endorsed fewer symptoms than false-positives (FBI 6.62 ± 8.80 vs 15.36 ± 8.42, P < 0.001), whereas clinician observations were markedly greater in bvFTD (27.67 ± 8.35 vs 5.64 ± 3.85, P < 0.001). Informant ratings did not differ between groups (25.15 ± 11.11 vs 21.32 ± 12.61, P = 0.14), even though bvFTD informants had more knowledge of the disease (FTD Knowledge Scale 16.20 ± 6.68 vs 9.41 ± 8.19, P = 0.003). A model incorporating patient-clinician and informant-clinician discrepancy showed excellent cross-validated discrimination (AUC 0.99, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.97-1.00). A model independent of expert clinician ratings, the patient-informant discrepancy, showed fair cross-validated discrimination across the full cohort (AUC 0.71, 95% CI 0.56-0.85) and good discrimination in those who did not develop another FTLD syndrome on follow-up ('pure bvFTD'; AUC 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.94). In bvFTD, reduced insight was associated with salience and semantic appraisal network degeneration but not control frontotemporal regions. BvFTD, false-positives, and their informants demonstrated opposing patterns of symptom endorsement. Symptom under-endorsement (lack of insight) by patients relative to clinician and informant observation supports neurodegeneration, whereas informant and patient over-endorsement without clinician-observed disturbance suggests a false-positive. Unfamiliarity with bvFTD may contribute to over-reporting. Though the clinician-dependent findings may not translate to non-expert settings, the patient-informant model retained good discrimination. Formal quantification of discrepancy patterns in behaviour may reduce misdiagnosis in bvFTD. The neuroimaging findings support salience and semantic appraisal networks as the neuroanatomical basis for insight in bvFTD. Future studies should validate the FBI clinician version and examine factors underlying over-reporting by false-positives and their informants.

title: Beyond grades to learning enhancement: development, implementation and evaluation of a conversational AI agent in medical education
abstract: The integration of conversational artificial intelligence (AI) in medical education shows promise but lacks empirical evidence of effectiveness. This study evaluated a customized generative pre-trained transformer (GPT)-4-based conversational agent designed explicitly for a pharmacology block in undergraduate medical education. A mixed-methods sequential explanatory design was employed in a four-week elective pharmacology block at the College of Medicine, Sulaiman Al-Rajhi University. Phase 1 involved a cross-sectional survey of enrolled students (n = 58) who used the AI tool, with a comparative analysis of their academic performance against historical cohorts without access to AI (2022–2023: n = 33; 2023–2024: n = 37). Academic performance was measured through mid-block quizzes, end-of-block examinations, and total block score. Phase 2 comprised semi-structured interviews (n = 9), transcribed and analyzed thematically. The survey response rate was 89.6% (52/58), and 98.1% (51/52) reported using the tool. Among users, 74.5% engaged with the GPT tool daily. Students reported exceptionally high satisfaction: 92.2% found it more effective than traditional methods, 94.1% felt it made learning more engaging, and the likelihood of recommending it averaged 4.65 ± 0.73 (on a 5-point scale). Frequency of use was significantly associated with perceived improvement in learning (χ2 = 15.84, p 0.05), with pass rates improving from 92.9% to 98.3% (p > 0.05). Qualitative analysis revealed six themes: learning support and academic enhancement; efficiency and accessibility; GPT's supplementary role in learning; perceived strengths and unique features; limitations and challenges; and suggestions for improvement. The disconnect between exceptional user engagement and minimal performance improvements challenges traditional evaluation paradigms. While conversational AI may not directly enhance examination scores, students' accounts suggest it may support metacognitive development, reduce cognitive load, and foster critical-thinking skills essential for modern medical practice, thereby necessitating multidimensional assessment frameworks.

title: From western frameworks to epistemically plural governance: a knowledge governance typology for regenerative agricultural supply chains in Africa
abstract: The paper develops a knowledge governance model for regenerative agricultural supply chains in Africa. Existing frameworks assume formal institutions, codified scientific knowledge, and reliable digital infrastructure. African settings, where indigenous ecological norms serve as protective ecological infrastructure operating near irreversibility thresholds, require a different starting point. The paper follows a three-stage theory-building approach. Stage 1 reviews existing knowledge governance models and their limits in African settings. Stage 2 draws on published African case studies to specify recurring challenges. Stage 3 combines typological and prescriptive theorising to produce a 2 × 2 matrix of governance contexts, paired with if-then guidance. The model organises knowledge governance contexts along two dimensions: (1) epistemic-cultural complexity, the challenge of integrating multiple knowledge traditions while respecting culturally specific norms around authority, access and sharing and (2) institutional-infrastructural risk, the vulnerabilities arising where formal governance infrastructure is absent or weak. Crossing them yields four archetypes: Ubuntu-grounded knowledge platforms, community-embedded knowledge stewardship, epistemically just knowledge partnerships and resilient knowledge networks, each with design rules for sharing norms, governance structures, justice safeguards and coordination mechanisms. The paper makes three contributions. It introduces epistemic-cultural complexity as a core knowledge governance dimension in African supply chains; it reconceptualises knowledge polycentrism through Ubuntu, Ujamaa and Ọ̀mọ̀lúwabí while integrating the protective-ecological function of indigenous norms, showing that knowledge governance and ecological protection form a single coordinated problem; and it specifies a prescriptive typology assigning differentiated catalytic responsibilities to downstream supply chain actors.
journal: The International Journal of Logistics Management

title: DRLCI: Dual-view Representation Learning Framework for Predicting Drug-Gene Interactions via Causal Intervention.
abstract: Investigating drug-gene interactions is essential for advancing personalized medicine and therapeutic innovation. In recent years, Graph Neural Network-based approaches have demonstrated significant potential for this task by utilizing diverse strategies, such as subgraph extraction and hypergraph modeling. However, these associative paradigms remain confined to observational statistics, primarily identifying superficial correlations rather than underlying causal mechanisms. Drug-gene prediction tasks are frequently hindered by hard negative samples acting as confounders, which lead existing methods to overweight biologically irrelevant nodes and introduce substantial noise. Moreover, relying solely on a single topological view restricts the prediction framework to a closed loop of established connections, impeding the discovery of novel interaction patterns. Addressing these deficiencies, we propose a dual-view representation learning framework. Initially, Relation-Aware graph convolution adaptively quantifies the differentiated contributions of neighboring nodes via an attention mechanism to capture key interaction patterns. To refine this procedure, we incorporate a causal intervention mask and a causally-debiased contrastive loss into the feature extraction stage, thereby optimizing the representation space and suppressing confounding effects. Finally, external medical prior knowledge is integrated into the prediction pipeline through a textual modality governed by a gated fusion mechanism. Comprehensive benchmark evaluations demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DrugBank and DGIdb datasets.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

title: Indole-3-lactic acid ameliorates thrombocytopenia in primary immune thrombocytopenia by modulating the differentiation of Th17 and Tregs.
abstract: Although some patients with primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) benefit from current treatments, there are still some refractory patients. Our previous research showed that the imbalance of the intestinal microbiota is associated with ITP. Indole-3-lactic acid (ILA) may act as a communication channel between the gut microbiota and the immune system. This study aimed to assess the ILA metabolism and the role in ITP. Plasma metabolites were measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Flow cytometry was used to analyse T-cell subsets and Fc gamma receptors on macrophages. Cytokine mRNA expression and plasma levels were detected by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) and a multiplex assay kit. An ITP mouse model was used to explore the effect of ILA on immune homeostasis. Newly diagnosed and refractory ITP patients with a deficiency of ILA and an imbalance of T helper cell type 17 (Th17)/regulatory T cells (Tregs). ILA alleviated thrombocytopenia in ITP mice by inhibiting Th17 differentiation and the expression of interleukin (IL)-1β, tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interferon-γ (IFN-γ) and IL-12/IL-23p40, and by promoting Tregs differentiation. ILA reduced Th17 cells, increased the Treg/Th17 ratio, downregulated IL17A and TNFα mRNA, and upregulated IL10 mRNA in refractory ITP patients. ILA ameliorates thrombocytopenia in ITP by modulating Th17/Tregs differentiation and suppressing TNF-α expression. Targeting ILA metabolism could be a promising therapeutic strategy for ITP.

title: Hormonal Regulation and the Mechanistic Basis of a Sex-Limited Color Polymorphism.
abstract: The presence of multiple discrete color patterns within a species has captivated evolutionary biologists for more than a century, including cases in which the polymorphism is confined to one sex. The brown anole Anolis sagrei exhibits a female-limited polymorphism in dorsal patterning, which is controlled by allelic variation at the autosomal CCDC170 locus. Here, we present and test a threshold model that can explain why the polymorphism is female-limited. We hypothesize that the hormonal environment determines whether allelic variation at the morph-associated locus is phenotypically manifested, potentially through estrogen-dependent regulation of CCDC170 and its neighboring gene ESR1, which are more highly expressed in female than male embryos. By manipulating embryonic estradiol levels, we show that genetic males can be induced to express the polymorphism according to allelic variation at the CCDC170 locus, which is naturally masked in males. Inversely, treating genetic females with fadrozole, which depletes estradiol, leads to monomorphic patterns irrespective of genotype, as in natural males. Using RT-qPCR on sexual organs, we demonstrate that these effects are accompanied by changes in gene expression levels of CCDC170 and ESR1 in response to estradiol and fadrozole, lending support to the threshold model. Our results suggest that the CCDC170-ESR1-locus is part of a mechanistic link between the morph-determining and the sex differentiation systems, and provide a causal explanation for the developmental origin of a sex-limited color polymorphism.

title: Intensive Agriculture and Erosion Affect Composition of Soil Organic Matter
abstract: Land‐use changes induced by human activities usually accelerate soil erosion, leading to losses of soil organic matter (SOM). The mechanisms by which cultivation‐associated degradation affects SOM composition via changes of content and quality of particulate (POM), mineral‐associated (MAOM), dissolved organic matter (DOM), and microbial biomass are not elucidated. We investigated the C:N stoichiometry of these fractions, and erosion (using 137 Cs activity) along a chronosequence of cultivation‐associated degradation (0–114 years) in Mollisols. Two‐pool and Bayesian three‐source mixing models estimated contributions of microbial biomass, DOM, and POM to MAOM to the total SOM. Erosion intensity ranged locally from 440 to 4800 t km −2 year −1 , resulting in cumulative soil losses of 11,000 to 320,000 t km −2 over 114 years of cultivation. As cultivation duration and eroded amounts increased, the C/N ratios of POM, MAOM, and DOM declined owing to (i) the faster loss of C than N, (ii) a decrease in C/N with soil depth involved in tillage horizon, and (iii) N input by fertilization. These higher C than N losses reflect that erosion is not the sole process leading to the decline of C stocks, but intensive cultivation also accelerates organic matter mineralization and CO 2 release to the atmosphere. As the C/N ratios of POM and MAOM declined but microbial C/N increased, the estimated contribution of microbial inputs to MAOM increased from 6% to 32%. The Bayesian model partitioned MAOM sources into DOM (8%), microbial (11%), and POM (81%), reinforcing that POM dominates MAOM formation in croplands. Cultivation‐associated degradation led to SOC losses by reducing POM‐C/N and MAOM‐C/N ratios, while erosion strongly accelerated these effects. Furthermore, cultivation‐associated degradation is also based on the limited inputs of organic C as the precursors for MAOM formation by depleting POM. These results from a > 100‐year chronosequence indicate that cultivation‐induced degradation reduces SOM content, while also shifting the MAOM composition progressively towards a greater contribution of microbial C.

title: Mineral‐Associated Carbon Accrual Masks Labile Particulate Carbon Loss in Permafrost Region on the Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Permafrost regions store vast quantities of soil organic carbon (SOC), yet the future trajectories of functionally distinct SOC fractions across soil depths remain poorly constrained. Integrating depth‐explicit soil fractionation data from 104 sites across the Tibetan permafrost region with a process‐based SOC model, we project century‐scale dynamics of particulate (POC) and mineral‐associated organic carbon (MAOC) under three emission scenarios. We show that MAOC currently comprises 56.5% of regional total SOC stock and remains far from saturation throughout the profile. Consistent with this large stabilization capacity, total SOC was projected to increase over the 21st century under all scenarios, with the largest gains under SSP5‐8.5. However, this positive net gain masked a significant restructuring of SOC fractions. MAOC accumulated across all depths and scenarios, and heavy POC remained comparatively buffered, whereas light POC declined under SSP5‐8.5. The strongest relative light POC losses occurred in the 10–30 cm layers, where warming‐driven decomposition remained strong while plant‐C input compensation weakened. These divergent trajectories indicate a shift toward a “carbon‐rich yet energy‐poor” state, where mineral‐bound carbon increases while the labile particulate pool supporting microbial activity is depleted. Our findings reveal SOC vulnerability in permafrost region is governed by both fraction identity and soil depth, and that net SOC gains can conceal the loss of metabolically active carbon. Incorporating measurable, depth‐resolved SOC fractions into Earth system models is therefore essential for constraining permafrost–climate feedbacks.

title: Three‐Phase Mobilization of Organic Phosphorus Sustains Phosphorus Bioavailability Under Long‐Term Nitrogen Addition in a Subtropical Plantation
abstract: Nitrogen (N) input is expected to intensify phosphorus (P) limitation in tropical and subtropical forests. However, how soil and microbial processes mobilize P from poorly available pools to sustain soil P bioavailability remains unclear. We conducted a nine‐year experiment with low (20 kg N ha −1 year −1 ) and high (80 kg N ha −1 year −1 ) N addition treatments in a subtropical Moso bamboo ( Phyllostachys edulis ) plantation. We quantified soil P fractions, P‐cycling functional genes, phosphatase activity, P sorption capacity (PSC), iron and aluminum oxides, and plant properties throughout the experiment. Our results reveal three distinct stages in the regulation of soil bioavailable P with prolonged N addition. Phase I: N addition reduces P bioavailability, and labile organic P decomposition becomes the main source of bioavailable P, associated with increased phosphatase activity. Phase II: when labile organic P becomes insufficient to meet P demand, bioavailable P is replenished through the depletion of moderately labile organic P; this is related to decreased PSC and enhanced acid phosphomonoesterases activity. Phase III: stable organic P decreases significantly, jointly sustaining bioavailable P with the depletion of other organic P fractions, alongside a further decrease in PSC and enriched microbial organic acid‐ and phosphatase‐related genes. This study uncovers a novel “three‐phased P supply” model revealed through long‐term observations. These mechanistic insights reveal the pathways of soil P mobilization under continuous N input in a subtropical forest and establish a framework for predicting the buffering capacity of soil P pools in P‐limited ecosystems under global change scenarios.

title: Seasonal variation of immature mosquitoes in rice fields and their association with water quality and crop growth stages in a peri-urban area of Hanoi, Vietnam.
abstract: Rice agroecosystems are among the most productive mosquito habitats in Asia, but the ways in which crop phenology and urbanisation-driven environmental changes shape immature mosquito vector populations remain poorly understood. We quantified mosquito larvae and pupae dynamics across two crop seasons in a rice field located in a peri-urban area of Hanoi, Vietnam, using generalised linear models with appropriate error distributions. A total of 3196 immature mosquitoes representing six species were collected. Overall mosquito abundance was significantly higher in spring than in autumn and peaked during the vegetative stage. Species richness did not vary between seasons but declined significantly at later crop stages. Larval-stage structure varied with both season and crop phenology. Early instars were more prevalent in spring and during the reproductive stage, whereas late instars dominated in autumn and declined during the ripening stage. The proportion of pupae decreased during the reproductive stage. Among dominant taxa, Culex tritaeniorhynchus and Anopheles barbirostris showed strong seasonal responses, whereas Cx. quinquefasciatus exhibited no significant temporal variation. Environmental drivers differed among species. Culex tritaeniorhynchus was positively associated with water depth, pH and dissolved oxygen, but negatively associated with conductivity. In contrast, Cx. quinquefasciatus was strongly associated with higher conductivity, while An. barbirostris showed negative associations with temperature and conductivity. These findings indicate that mosquito development in rice fields is jointly structured by crop seasonality and agronomic water management, with early crop stages creating favourable conditions for larval proliferation. The dominance of vector species of epidemiological concern underscores the need to integrate phenology-based habitat management into nuisance and mosquito vector control strategies in Hanoi and similar peri-urban rice-growing landscapes.

title: Experiential Learning and Technology Acceptance: Agrotechnology Students’ Readiness to Adopt Industrial Internet of Things in Smart Fertigation
abstract: The integration of digital technologies into agricultural education is increasingly important for preparing graduates for Agriculture 4.0. Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technologies offer opportunities for automated monitoring, remote management and data-driven agricultural production. This study examined agrotechnology students’ knowledge, perceptions and acceptance of IIoT following structured experiential exposure to an IIoT-enabled fertigation system. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 100 undergraduate students at Universiti Malaysia Kelantan, Malaysia. Students participated in face-to-face technology knowledge-transfer activities involving theoretical instruction and practical exposure at a fertigation site. A structured questionnaire comprising 47 closed-ended items was administered using a five-point Likert scale, and data were analysed using descriptive statistics and reliability analysis in SPSS version 26.0. The findings indicated high levels of knowledge and understanding of IIoT applications in agriculture (M = 4.34, SD = 0.80), positive perceptions and willingness towards IIoT (M = 4.35, SD = 0.62), and favourable attitudes, acceptance and readiness (M = 4.44, SD = 0.79). Thus, students showed a significant desire to use the technology in agricultural activities and take part in IIoT-related training. However, they highlighted the importance of skilled operators, technical guidance, affordability and service availability. The findings suggest that structured experiential exposure provides a relevant educational context for developing students’ understanding and readiness towards IIoT and supports the integration of practical, industry-linked digital technology competencies into agricultural education curricula.

title: Basin-scale changes in net primary production from the biogeochemical-Argo array
abstract: Marine net primary production is expected to be affected by climate change. Although remote sensing offers broad spatial and temporal coverage, it is limited to surface observations and cannot capture subsurface variability. Autonomous profiling floats provide critical depth-resolved measurements that help bridge this gap. Here, we use data from the biogeochemical-Argo array to estimate basin-scale change in net primary production using the carbon-based production algorithm. We find statistically significant negative trends across the Atlantic and Southern Oceans and positive trends in the Pacific Ocean. These changes, if occurring in response to climate forcing, raise concern due to the key role of phytoplankton productivity in sustaining marine ecosystems. These trends typically agree in direction and magnitude with those from satellites. Our findings highlight the value of the biogeochemical-Argo array in detecting change in ocean productivity, demonstrating its potential for sustained monitoring. These results underscore the need for integrated observing systems to capture the full extent of changing marine productivity.

title: A TROP2-targeting aptamer enables selective drug delivery and potent antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to treat, highlighting the need for strategies that selectively deliver cytotoxic agents to tumor cells. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2) has been proposed as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC, but non-antibody-based delivery formats remain underexplored. Using protein-SELEX, we identified T17, a high-affinity aptamer that specifically binds to TROP2, and conjugated it to monomethyl auristatin E through an MC-Val-Cit-PAB linker to generate the aptamer-drug conjugate T17-M. Preclinical evaluation in cellular and animal models showed that T17-M retained TROP2-dependent binding, underwent clathrin-mediated internalization and lysosomal processing, and suppressed tumor growth in cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts. T17-M also reduced liver metastasis and induced calreticulin exposure, ATP release, and HMGB1 secretion, consistent with immunogenic cell death. In immunocompetent models, T17-M promoted dendritic-cell activation and CD8 + T cell infiltration, while its combination with PD-1 blockade further enhanced tumor control and prolonged survival. These findings provide preclinical proof-of-concept for T17-M as an alternative TROP2-targeted drug-delivery strategy for PDAC.

title: Nonlinear cooling and control of a mechanical quantum harmonic oscillator
abstract: Nonlinearities are a key feature allowing nonclassical control of quantum harmonic oscillators. However, when nonlinearities are strong, designing protocols for control is often difficult, placing a barrier to exploiting these properties fully. In this work, using a single trapped-ion oscillator operated in the strongly nonlinear regime of the atom-light interaction, we show how to generate localized multi (two, three, four, and five)–component Schrödinger’s cat manifolds using a novel form of nonlinear reservoir engineering. We then specifically select Hamiltonians which allow us to perform measurements on these state manifolds. Our work demonstrates the experimental use of high-order nonlinear processes for control of nonclassical states of a quantum harmonic oscillator, opening up a new toolbox which can be applied to bosonic quantum error correction, computation, and sensing.

title: Superoxide dismutase shapes manganese stoichiometry in Southern Ocean diatoms
abstract: Quantifying the elemental stoichiometry of marine phytoplankton biomass is crucial for projections of primary production. In many cases, the mechanistic underpinnings of biomass stoichiometry are unclear. We combined metaproteomics, Bayesian statistical modeling, and geochemical measurements to quantify the contribution of superoxide dismutases to metal stoichiometry in natural populations of Southern Ocean diatoms. Our analyses indicate that a substantial amount of manganese (Mn) in diatoms in an Antarctic polynya can be attributed to superoxide dismutases (∼0.7 micromoles of Mn:moles of carbon; ∼20% of the total cellular Mn quota). We then used proteomic profiles of polar diatom cultures to identify environmental controls on superoxide dismutases and found that Mn limitation induces the depletion of Mn superoxide dismutases and an accompanying increase in nickel superoxide dismutase. Overall, we combined metaproteomic approaches to quantify proteome composition and connected these measurements to metal-to-carbon ratios and their responses to metal availability. Our approach provides a mechanism for directly parameterizing ecosystem-scale models with molecular measurements.

title: Mechanical forces enable human stem cell modeling of protein aggregation cardiomyopathy
abstract: Inherited cardiomyopathies are the leading cause of heart failure in young adults, with limited therapeutic options. Desmin-related cardiomyopathy (DRM), caused by mutations to cytoskeletal proteins and their chaperones, exemplifies this challenge: Here, protein quality control is compromised, leading to toxic protein aggregates that destroy cardiomyocyte contractile machinery. One of the deadliest DRM mutations in the chaperone protein αB crystallin (CRYAB-R120G) lacks a genetically matched preclinical model: Mouse models require massive overexpression of mutant CRYAB, raising questions about physiological relevance. Here, we establish a human model of CRYAB -linked DRM, using induced pluripotent stem cells expressing CRYAB-R120G at near-endogenous levels. We show that three-dimensional mechanical loading, but not fatty acid–based metabolic maturation media, is essential for expressing Desmin, whose aggregation defines DRM. Using microengineered heart tissues, we found that contractile deficits are associated with impaired calcium handling, pointing to electromechanical uncoupling in DRM. Treatment with the Janus kinase 1 inhibitor itacitinib partially rescued contractility, providing a functional validation of this emerging therapeutic strategy.

title: Dual-action small-molecule VSP-51-2 ameliorates polycystic ovary syndrome via PPARγ modulation and AKR1C3 inhibition
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent multifactorial endocrine disorder, is inadequately managed by current therapies that fail to concurrently target its core metabolic (insulin resistance) and reproductive (hyperandrogenism) pathologies. We report VSP-51-2, a dual-target lead compound initially engineered as a selective PPARγ modulator that unexpectedly exerts potent uncompetitive inhibition of the androgen-synthesizing enzyme AKR1C3 through a putative allosteric mechanism. In preclinical PCOS models, VSP-51-2 restored regular estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian follicular morphology, enhanced systemic insulin sensitivity, suppressed hyperandrogenism, and did not significantly perturb measured hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis hormonal parameters. Mechanistically, it blocks PPARγ phosphorylation at Ser 273 , thereby enhancing adiponectin secretion and GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake, and is predicted to bind a putative allosteric pocket of AKR1C3 to constrain androgen biosynthesis. These findings support VSP-51-2 as a preclinical proof-of-concept compound for a dual-target strategy that addresses metabolic dysfunction and androgen excess through a unified molecular scaffold.

title: Reprogramming electron transfer at single-atom Pt sites to break the interference barrier in uric acid detection
abstract: Uric acid (UA) serves as a key biomarker for gout, cardiovascular disease, and kidney dysfunction, yet conventional detection methods relying on H 2 O 2 generation suffer from signal instability and interference from reductive species. Here, we report a uricase-like platinum-nitrogen-carbon nanozyme (Pt-N-C-NH 3 ) that redirects UA oxidation from a two-electron pathway toward a four-electron pathway. By decreasing graphitic nitrogen content, the local electronic microenvironment of platinum sites is modulated, which is associated with a lower calculated free-energy change for the rate-determining absorbed oxygen to absorbed hydroxyl transformation from 1.25 to 0.62 electron volts and thereby promoting oxygen reduction to water. Integrated into a microneedle sensing platform, UA is converted to allantoin for chemiluminescent readout. The sensor exhibits a wide linear range of 50.00 to 1000.00 μM and a detection limit of 15.86 μM, while maintaining 97.57% signal stability against reductive interferents. This work demonstrates that atomic-level coordination engineering enables programmable control over reaction pathways in artificial enzyme systems, thereby facilitating robust biosensing in complex biological environments.

title: Asymmetric cell division is predictive of human T cell vaccine responses
abstract: Vaccine-induced protection relies on the generation and maintenance of stem-like memory B and T cells, a process sustained by two conserved mechanisms: asymmetric cell division (ACD) and autophagy. In T cells, ACD enables them to produce progeny with the same T cell receptor but with divergent metabolic and functional fates upon antigen encounter through the unequal inheritance of cellular cargoes. Autophagy recycles cellular components, provides metabolic substrates essential for sustaining energy demands, and is relevant for the maintenance of T cell memory. Direct evidence of how these processes synergize and affect human immunity is still lacking. Here, we show that mitotic human CD8 + T cells asymmetrically segregate autophagy-related organelles, including autophagosomes and lysosomes. Furthermore, we show that ACD drives divergent transcriptional and functional fates in daughter cells. Extending these findings to an influenza vaccine trial, we demonstrate that autophagic flux follows the dynamics of clonal expansion and contraction of antigen-specific T cells. Notably, individuals with enhanced ACD capacity, especially with increased LC3B asymmetry, exhibit better vaccine responses, linking early cellular segregation events to long-term immune fitness. Last, transient use of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibitor rapamycin improved memory survival, which was associated with improved ACD, measured by the asymmetric inheritance of both CD8 and LC3B. Together, these findings highlight that the asymmetric inheritance of the autophagy machinery represents another layer of human adaptive immunity and offers a potential therapeutic target to enhance vaccine outcomes.

title: A fully hydrogel implantable patch for in situ ultrasonic monitoring of gastric leakage
abstract: Gastric leakage is a common and life-threatening postoperative complication, while delayed detection often leads to severe abdominal organ damage. Current radiological imaging modalities are limited in their ability to provide timely detection of gastric leakage, while the mechanical mismatch and long-term persistence of conventional electronic sensors limit their implantable applications. In this work, we developed a fully hydrogel-based ultrasonic metagel patch (USMP) for direct, real-time monitoring of gastric leakage via ultrasound imaging. The USMP incorporates a tree-ring air cell array, in which densely distributed air cells arranged in concentric rings create a strong back-scattering effect, thereby producing distinctive and stable ultrasound imaging signatures for rapid and sensitive detection. The air cells are encapsulated within biocompatible, hydrolytically degradable pH-responsive hydrogels, forming a fully hydrogel sensing architecture. The potential of the USMP for gastric leakage monitoring up to 7 days postimplantation is validated in the live rabbit model.

title: Does government-assisted relocation help households
abstract: Climate change is intensifying floods and storms, leading governments to consider relocating households away from high-risk areas. Yet, there is little evidence on whether such programs reduce risk or improve household well-being. I evaluate the US Federal Emergency Management Agency’s property acquisition (“buyout”) program using nationwide longitudinal records that track households before and after approval. By comparing households facing similar mapped flood risks, I estimate the program’s effects on relocation, residence in high-risk flood areas, and financial outcomes. Households that participate are more likely to relocate outside Federal Emergency Management Agency–designated flood hazard areas and experience short-term reductions in debt and improvements in neighborhood socioeconomic conditions. However, these benefits are concentrated among participants from wealthier and predominantly white neighborhoods, who relocate more quickly and achieve larger reductions in risk. A benefit-cost analysis shows that the program value depends on implementation costs and realized reductions in flood-risk exposure, with benefit-cost ratios ranging from 0.84 to 1.28 across three scenarios. These results show that government-assisted relocation can be an effective adaptation tool, but its social and economic benefits remain unevenly distributed.

title: Segmented projection image translation for large-area, high-resolution vat photopolymerization
abstract: High-resolution projection-based vat photopolymerization (VP) 3D printing enables rapid fabrication of highly detailed polymeric structures. However, expanding the build area traditionally compromises resolution, creating a fundamental trade-off between projected pixel size and printable area due to fixed digital micromirror device (DMD) pixel counts. Herein, we introduce segmented projection image translation (SPIN), a simple implementation strategy that expands the effective projection area by applying controlled orbital translation to an off-axis objective lens within the optical infinity space. In this work, we demonstrate a projection-based VP printer implemented with SPIN that expands the effective build area by 4.8-fold, from a native field of 60.4 square millimeters to an expanded domain of 290.5 square millimeters. The SPIN-enabled printer produces isolated line features as thin as 9.8 ± 2.2 micrometers and fabricates intricate three-dimensional truss structures with features as small as 30 micrometers. These results validate a practical route for extending microscale projection-based VP printing to larger build areas while preserving feature fidelity across stitched exposure fields.

title: Real-time complex-valued RF blind source separation via in-physics computing
abstract: The rise of edge-centric 6G networks demands real-time intelligent processing of heterogeneous radio-frequency (RF) signals. Complex-valued blind source separation (CV-BSS) provides a physical-layer capability, enabling the blind extraction of source components from overlapping RF signals. Here, we demonstrate an integrated photonic vector processor (IPVP) that implements real-time CV-BSS via in-physics computation directly on raw RF signals. The IPVP operates across multiple RF bands up to 24 GHz and achieves blind, in-hardware adaptation to unknown sources and channels via in situ learning. Experiments demonstrate the efficacy of IPVP in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications and multi-band radar interference suppression. The IPVP reduces the EVMs of the two recovered signals from over 50% to 6.18% and 5.3%, respectively, while enhancing the SIR by up to 26 dB. This work demonstrates, to our knowledge, the first photonic processor capable of real-time CV-BSS at RF, highlighting the potential of integrated photonic hardware for ultralow-latency, edge-intelligent signal processing.

title: A primordial heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system
abstract: The oxygen (O) isotopic composition of outer solar system ices is believed to be enriched in heavy O isotopes owing to photochemical processes, but evidence for this O reservoir is exceedingly rare in meteorites. Hydrated interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) collected in Earth’s stratosphere that display high densities of solar energetic particle tracks originate from Edgeworth-Kuiper belt objects. Their mineralogy is dominated by hydrated minerals that formed by alteration of anhydrous precursor minerals at low temperatures through reactions with water (H 2 O)–carbon dioxide fluids. The O isotopic compositions of track-rich hydrated IDPs implicate 17,18 O-rich ices as the source of H 2 O involved in their alteration, providing compelling evidence for the presence of a major heavy water reservoir beyond the orbits of the gas giant planets that was largely isolated from inner solar system materials.

title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ( M ≳ 2 M ⊙ ) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period P ≈ 1218 ± 3 days and a comparatively low eccentricity e ≈ 0.09 ± 0.01 (with 1σ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from Gaia DR2 and DR3 catalogs, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle i ≈ 73 ∘ ± 11 ∘ . The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8 to 2.8 M ⊙ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of 2.20 − 0.13 + 0.14 M ⊙ . This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

title: The role of network connectivity and transcriptomic vulnerability in shaping gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis
abstract: Clinical progression is strongly linked to gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis (MS), detectable early on MRI and progressing nonrandomly across the brain. However, the mechanisms driving its spatiotemporal progression and individual variability remain unclear. Using MRIs from 2187 participants, alongside normative data, we systematically investigated network-based mechanisms underlying MS-related atrophy. Regional atrophy was associated with functional cortical hubness, supporting the nodal stress hypothesis, and was constrained by anatomical and functional connections, consistent with transneuronal degeneration. Lesional disconnection and transcriptomic vulnerability played marginal roles. Patient- and subgroup-level analyses revealed that network-based mechanisms are specifically linked to MS-related neurodegeneration and may operate differently in distinct subtypes or disease phases. Atrophy patterns were anchored to the connectivity profiles of disease epicenters involving the visual, sensorimotor, and temporal cortices, as well as the hippocampi, amygdalae, and thalami. Network-based measures enhanced the explanation of future atrophy progression in people with MS, providing a mechanistic framework to understand neurodegeneration in MS.

title: Tracing Neanderthal ancestry patterns through successive population expansions in Europe
abstract: During their expansion from Africa, modern humans interbred with Neanderthals, resulting in introgression of Neanderthal DNA into their genomes. This process contributed to a Southeast-to-Northwest gradient of Neanderthal ancestry across Europe. We investigate the population dynamics underlying the emergence and persistence of this gradient through two successive human range expansions. We developed a three-population, layered, spatially explicit simulation framework to track the spatiotemporal evolution of Neanderthal ancestry under a model of interactions among Neanderthals, pre-Neolithic hunter-gatherers, and Neolithic farmers. Our results indicate that the ancestry cline emerged from the interplay between the direction of the initial hunter-gatherer expansion, the northern limit of the Neanderthal range, and strong reproductive isolation, without requiring natural selection. The similar direction of the subsequent Neolithic expansion explains the cline’s persistence and Neanderthal ancestry differences between hunter-gatherers and farmers. These findings demonstrate how spatiotemporal patterns in ancient DNA provide insights into past population dynamics.

title: Inhibition of aberrant astrocyte activity restores auditory sensorimotor function in zebrafish spen mutants
abstract: Sensorimotor deficits can profoundly affect the life quality of patients with neurological disorders, yet our understanding of central dysfunction at the cellular or circuit level is limited. Using a forward genetic approach to generate loss of auditory function in zebrafish larvae, we identified a recessive mutation in split ends ( spen ), which encodes a transcription factor implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders in humans. We found that auditory sensorimotor deficits in spen mutants are associated with chronically elevated calcium levels in hindbrain radial astrocytes. Astrocytes have been previously implicated in the integration of neuronal inputs that alter arousal states and sensorimotor behavior. Inhibition of noradrenergic receptors, which are expressed in astrocytes, lowered calcium levels in mutant radial astrocytes and, notably, restored behavioral responses to sound in spen mutants. Our study highlights a role for noradrenergic signaling in spen -related disease and points to potential therapeutic approaches for pediatric patients.

title: Brown carbon in biomass burning aerosol enhances HONO production
abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is an important source of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). •OH drives ozone and aerosol formation, affecting air quality, health, and climate. Elevated HONO concentrations have been observed in biomass burning (BB) plumes. However, the mechanism remains unclear, hindering parameterization and quantification of the impacts. Here, we conducted flow tube experiments with BB aerosol samples and proxies to investigate renoxification, a process that converts nitrate into HONO and NO x (NO and NO 2 ). Our results reveal that renoxification in BB aerosol is enhanced by brown carbon (BrC) through electron transfer to nitrate as an alternative to surface-enhanced nitrate photolysis. We develop parameterization to assess the potential global impacts of BrC-enhanced renoxification, which suggests that BrC enhances surface-level HONO production by up to one order of magnitude in BB-affected regions, with surface HONO production exceeding 1 part per trillion per hour in regions with high aerosol nitrate. These impacts are expected to worsen as BB intensifies in a warming climate.

title: Input-specific deployment of the active zone scaffold RIM tunes synaptic release probability and plasticity
abstract: The multidomain scaffold RIM (Rab3-interacting molecule) is widely viewed as a broadly required organizer of the presynaptic active zone, clustering voltage-gated Ca 2+ (Ca v 2) channels, priming synaptic vesicles, and supporting neurotransmitter release. Whether this reliance is uniform across synapses with distinct release probabilities, however, has been difficult to resolve at convergent inputs. Here, using neurotoxin-based silencing to isolate transmission at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction, we show that the requirement for RIM is highly input-specific: RIM is essential to empower transmission at a high–release probability phasic synapse, yet is largely dispensable at a neighboring low–release probability tonic synapse. This specificity extends to plasticity: RIM is required for acute homeostatic potentiation at the phasic input, but not for chronic potentiation at the tonic input. Super-resolution imaging reveals that RIM is positioned closer to Ca v 2 channels at phasic synapses and, during acute plasticity, coordinates their nanoscale reorganization to drive the rapid expansion of the readily releasable pool.

title: The transcription factors OsIDD and OsSHR jointly regulate ground tissue patterning and differentiation in rice roots
abstract: Rice roots have a distinctive ground tissue architecture with multiple cortical layers and a single endodermal layer concentrically surrounding the stele. This architecture promotes aerenchyma formation and adaptability to waterlogged environments, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unexplored. Here, we identified the INDETERMINATE DOMAIN (IDD) and SHORTROOT (SHR) families as key regulators of ground tissue development in rice. OsIDD2/3/6/8 govern cortical radial symmetry by coordinating cortical organization and auxin distribution independently of OsSHR1/2/3/4/5. Quadruple knockout of OsIDD2/3/6/8 caused cortical asymmetry without affecting apoplastic barrier integrity or mineral uptake but reduced shoot-directed ion transport. OsIDD8 also controls the number of cortical cell layers and endodermal cells, whereas OsSHR1/2/3/4/5 redundantly promote periclinal divisions of the cortical cells, which require OsIDD8 activity. Moreover, OsIDD and OsSHR members coordinate endodermal differentiation by regulating localization of Casparian strip membrane domain protein OsCASP1 and lignin/suberin deposition. These findings establish a genetic framework underlying the spatial organization and functional differentiation of ground tissue in rice roots.

title: The ZmJAZ14–ZmMYC2 module regulates anthesis–silking synchrony in maize
abstract: The evolution of traits can increase yield potential but may create physiological constraints. Jasmonic acid (JA) signaling regulates sex determination in male (tassel) and female (ear) inflorescences in maize. Although the formation of ears laid the foundation for high yields, the asynchronous development of the tassel and the ear prolongs the anthesis-silking interval (ASI), threatening reproductive success and reducing yield. Whether JA signaling coordinates ear and tassel development remains unclear. Here, we show that the core JA signaling module, ZmJAZ14-ZmMYC2a/b, orchestrates the expression of SPL29 for reproductive transition, BA1 for female inflorescence initiation, and EXPA5 for silk elongation. Coordination of these physiological processes underpins synchronous growth of the tassel and ears, whereas disruption of ZmMYC2a/b or accumulation of the repressor ZmJAZ14 prolongs ASI. Our work suggests that the repurposing of JA signaling to coordinate ear and tassel development may represent a lineage-specific evolutionary burden in maize. Deciphering the link between gains and unforeseen costs of evolution could further improve yields.

title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage
abstract: Far-field optical imaging inevitably involves low-pass spatial filtering, limiting the resolution. Moreover, conventional imaging suppresses high spatial frequency components close to the cutoff, making them invisible under noise—particularly the shot noise arising from discrete and random nature of quantum light. Here, we propose and implement a method for reducing the effect of this noise by optically preprocessing the incoming light before detection, thereby optimizing the quantum measurement performed on it. Our scheme, termed Fourier domain division (FDD), partitions the Fourier plane into multiple regions for independent detection and subsequent post-processing for image reconstruction. By analyzing the quantum and classical Fisher information, we show that our method is advantageous with respect to direct imaging for high spatial-frequency components. As a result, the number of photons required to achieve a certain signal-to-noise ratio in the Fourier domain is reduced, thus enhancing the overall resolution in the photon-starved regime. We demonstrate our method in microscopy, achieving fivefold improvement of Fisher information on high spatial frequency components. Unlike active super-resolution methods, FDD is passive, making it broadly applicable in microscopy and other imaging scenarios, where active illumination is impractical, including astronomy and remote sensing, in the photon-starved regime. Our work establishes a general strategy for designing quantum optimized superresolution imaging systems, bridging fundamental quantum limits, practical image analysis, and computer vision applications.

title: Phototropin-mediated blue light signaling orients the asymmetry of Marchantia polymorpha spores
abstract: Multicellular organisms produced by sexual reproduction develop from single cells, and the asymmetry of these cells can define the orientation of the earliest developmental axes. The haploid multicellular stage of the plant, Marchantia polymorpha, develops from a single cell—the spore—that divides asymmetrically, producing an apical germ cell that generates the plant body and a smaller basal cell that differentiates as an anchoring germ rhizoid cell. We show that the orientation of this asymmetric cell division is controlled by an external environmental cue—blue light—that is perceived by the photoreceptor phototropin. This process requires the NCH1 (NRL PROTEIN FOR CHLOROPLAST MOVEMENT 1) protein for downstream signaling. Together, these findings define core elements of the mechanism by which a directional environmental signal orients cell division, which, in turn, orients the first axis of symmetry.

title: Electronic hair: Transforming hair into a scalable bioelectronic interface
abstract: In electroencephalography, hair remains a major barrier to electrode-skin contact, limiting signal quality. Here, we introduce electronic hair (eHAIR), a strategy that converts hair into a bioelectronic interface using mixed ionic-electronic conductive polymer dyes. Hair, a keratinized filament anchored within the skin, provides a stable and naturally distributed platform for interfacing. Two complementary approaches based on polythiophene derivatives enable rapid, washable functionalization of hair bundles or semipermanent coating of individual strands. The resulting eHAIR forms conformal, low-impedance interfaces that support electrophysiological recordings with increased signal amplitude and spectral power while preserving the underlying neural dynamics without gels or rigid hardware. Beyond passive sensing, eHAIR-based organic electrochemical transistors enable local signal amplification, with gain defined by hair geometry. By repurposing hair as an active bioelectronic interface, eHAIR establishes a wearable and biointegrated platform that can be implemented from individual hairs to larger hair-covered regions.

title: Cell adhesion molecule–related proteins signal to promote cytoneme elongation from Sonic Hedgehog–producing cells
abstract: Tissue morphogenesis and postdevelopmental homeostasis rely on efficient information exchange between communicating cells. Cytonemes are actin-based protrusions that contribute to precise information flow by facilitating contact-mediated directional transport of diverse signaling cargoes. How pathway-specific cytonemes are formed is poorly understood, as are the molecular mechanisms promoting actin organization for elongation and stability of the dynamic cellular extensions. We investigated biogenesis of Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) cytonemes, revealing functional repurposing of cell adhesion molecule-related proteins Brother of CDON (BOC) and Cell adhesion molecule-related, Down-regulated by Oncogenes (CDON) into recruiters of actin regulators FARP1 and Cdc42 for cytoneme elongation. Loss of BOC and CDON function blunts protrusion-localized Cdc42 activity, reducing cytoneme lengths and occurrence in SHH-expressing cells. Live imaging of developing murine spinal cords reveals that CDON loss in SHH-expressing cells reduces the frequency of neuroepithelial cytonemes and alters neuronal cell fate specification. These results inform a model whereby SHH-binding proteins promote ligand transport through stimulating formation of long cytonemes.

title: Multimodal switches exploiting electromechanical snap-through for versatile robotic information processing
abstract: It is highly desirable to design and engineer lightweight, low-power-consumption, and rapid physical intelligence (PI) structures that couple with multiple robotic functions. Here, we present a multimodal electromechanical switch (mEMS), consisting of a stretchable droplet-amplified electrostatic zipping structure, a convex bump, and a pair of electrical contacts, that can be used to achieve the widely used mechanical momentary, mechanical latching, and electrically actuated switching modes by simply tuning the applied voltage and using the same structure. We theoretically investigate the snap-through behavior of the elastic zipping membrane, which can be used to endow the mEMS with voltage-dependent memory, and the theoretical considerations are experimentally validated. As a result, we can apply the mEMS array for robotic memory, such as information writing and erasing; robotic communication by reprogrammable information encrypting, decrypting, and display; robotic computation by electrically reprogrammable logic gates; and reprogrammable binary information transferring. The mEMS represents a comprehensive PI structure for next-generation autonomous machines that can better adapt in unstructured and complex real-world environments.

title: Cocrystals for sequestering and separating large PAHs
abstract: Highly adaptive boroxine organic assemblies (BOAs) derived from a boronic acid and a linear alkene function as a first-generation constitutional dynamic library (CDL) to sequester and separate large polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in form of cocrystals. Configurational and conformational isomerism of the organoboroxines in host-guest assemblies is induced by electronic properties, shape and size of the PAHs through a “shrink-wrap” process/mechanism, which reveals a templating role of the PAH during the CDL assembly. The CDL was applied to separate up to three different PAHs. The cocrystals exhibit tunable electronic properties. The CDL afforded a cocrystal wherein alkenes of two different BOAs undergo [2 + 2] photocycloaddition in the same solid.

title: Dynamic plasmonic imaging of electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for charge-resolved multiplex biosensing
abstract: Multiplexed profiling of diverse biomarkers is essential for precision diagnostics, but remains challenging for label-free sensors because signals typically scale with analyte mass. Here, we present a dynamic plasmonic imaging platform based on electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for multiplexed, label-free quantification of nucleic acids, proteins, and small molecules within a unified sensing architecture. Size-encoded nanoparticles tethered to a plasmonic surface are electrically actuated to oscillate vertically within the evanescent field and tracked by distance-resolved surface plasmon resonance imaging. Molecular binding alters the effective surface charge of each nano-oscillator, modulating the electrostatic-driven forces and changing oscillation amplitude. This charge-to-motion transduction mechanism reduces dependence on molecular mass and enhances sensitivity for low–molecular weight analytes. This platform simultaneously detects microRNAs, proteins, and small molecules spanning a ∼300-fold molecular weight range within a single field of view. We further demonstrate multiplexed profiling of tumor-associated microRNAs in pretreated supernatants from patient-derived breast cancer cells across 24 clinical samples. Dynamic plasmonic nano-oscillators provide a scalable architecture for multiplex molecular diagnostics.

title: Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury
abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body–irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.
