title: Controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D photonic crystals
abstract: The fabrication of visible-spectrum three-dimensional (3D) photonic crystals (PhCs) remains highly challenging, because existing manufacturing techniques cannot simultaneously achieve high processing precision and sufficient geometric freedom. Here, we propose a suspended pyrolysis-assisted two-photon polymerization (SP-TPP) printing strategy, achieving the controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D PhCs. The resulting 3D diamond PhCs exhibit a remarkable lattice-period standard deviation of only 5.75 nm, approximately 1/45 of that achieved without suspended pyrolysis. Microscopic reflection spectra confirm these PhCs possess uniform optical responses across all spatial positions. By tuning the lattice period and structural duty cycle, the PhCs operating at diverse wavelengths are systematically realized. Moreover, through the demonstration of PhC prototype structures and in situ arrayed fabrication, the SP-TPP printing strategy paves the way for applications in photonic microcavities, 3D optical waveguides, optical splitters, and integrated micro-optical systems.

title: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
abstract: Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch + selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H + . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.

title: Weak adsorption, strong consequences: How trace gases control ice growth and quasi-liquid-layer structure
abstract: Gases in the atmosphere are often treated as passive background species in cold environments, yet their molecular roles at icy interfaces remain poorly understood. Here, we show how hydrophobic and hydrophilic trace gases can actively reorganize the ice interface and regulate freezing through interfacial stabilization. We find these gases can actively modulate both the kinetics and thermodynamics of the water-ice interface. Using molecular simulations, we find that all gases examined retard ice-front propagation relative to pure water to different extents. This slowing arises from weak but preferential adsorption at the water-ice interface, where gases occupy water-dense interfacial layers and locally suppress ice-like ordering. After freezing is complete, gases do not distribute uniformly across the frozen surface, but partition selectively among multiple adsorption regions across the ice–quasi-liquid-layer (QLL)–air interfacial landscape. Relatively hydrophobic gases exhibit a three-region adsorption pattern, whereas relatively hydrophilic gases occupy only two dominant adsorption regions. Despite these differences, both classes preferentially accumulate near the QLL-air boundary and its immediate outer region rather than the ice-QLL interface. There, gases pair with and compensate for dangling surface bonds (through a surface-passivating effect reminiscent of ligand stabilization), reducing the thermodynamic driving force for premelting and thereby thinning the QLL. These results establish a unified molecular picture in which atmospheric gases are active interfacial modulators of both ice growth and ice structure, with implications for freezing, ice-cloud microphysics, and heterogeneous atmospheric chemistry.

title: Arbitrarily cuttable and ultrathin MXene structural colors for customizable and wearable multispectral information management
abstract: Structural colors based on natural and artificial microstructures show promising light manipulation. As atomically thick building blocks, Ti 3 C 2 T x sheets have been successfully assembled into the ultrathin, flexible, arbitrarily cuttable, large-size structural colors by the simple and low-cost spray methods based on the lossy thin-film interference. By ordered stacking atomically thick Ti 3 C 2 T x layer by layer at well-organized low–surface tension semidry assemble state, rich colors from yellow to gray with the thickness from ∼22 to ∼154 nanometers of uniform Ti 3 C 2 T x colors are obtained, having the thinnest framework among solution-processed flexible structural colors with similar optical performance. Low-infrared emissivity from room to 300°C temperature and region-selective patterns make highly information-fused and complex visible-infrared (VIS-IR) Ti 3 C 2 T x colors camouflage. Without conventional dielectric layer between Ti 3 C 2 T x and substrate, automated spraying system can produce meter-scale films that can be cut and sewn into VIS-IR concealment “camouflage cloaks” easily, promising ultrathin multifunctional information systems and beyond.

title: Single-cell profiling of the duodenum during chronic human norovirus infection
abstract: Human noroviruses are a major cause of diarrheal disease, yet their pathogenesis remains poorly defined. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of duodenal biopsies and matched stem cell–derived enteroids from immunodeficient individuals with chronic norovirus infection. Norovirus RNA was detected primarily in enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, and macrophages, with the highest proportion of viral RNA-positive cells observed among M2 macrophages, followed by late enterocytes. Despite this distribution, late enterocytes produced higher viral yields than differentiated M2 macrophages in vitro. Norovirus infection was associated with the up-regulation of MHC class I-related genes and IL15 in duodenal macrophages and late enterocytes, together with increased IFNG expression by CD8 T cells. Macrophages and late enterocytes up-regulated CXCL9 and CXCL10/11 , respectively, consistent with CD8 and CD4 T cell recruitment to the duodenum. These findings show that noroviruses infect and persist across multiple permissive cell types during chronic infection, resulting in marked dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses that may drive pathogenesis.

title: Incomplete synaptic vesicle priming functionally disconnects CA1 pyramidal cells
abstract: The hippocampal CA1 area is perceived as a nonrecurrent neuronal network, i.e., CA1 pyramidal cells (CA1PCs) within the CA1 area innervate mainly γ-aminobutyric acid–releasing interneurons but not each other. Here, we performed an unbiased examination of the functional properties of local CA1PC output synapses using in vitro two-photon glutamate imaging. Fluorescent transients measured with iGluSnFR3 in individual boutons displayed extraordinary heterogeneity in their amplitudes and short-term plasticity patterns upon a complex train of presynaptic action potential firing. Post hoc electron microscopy of the imaged boutons demonstrated that distinct postsynaptic structure-innervating boutons display different functional properties. Approximately 25% of the boutons innervate CA1PC spines, which either release glutamate with very low release probability or completely fail to release. Phorbol 12,13-dibutyrate and elevated calcium (2+) concentration, manipulations that enhance synaptic vesicle priming and fusion, convert these silent into properly functioning synapses. Our results provide evidence that CA1PCs are interconnected with structurally and molecularly intact glutamatergic synapses, but incomplete synaptic vesicle (SV) priming precludes SV release.

title: A LiDAR-based reconstruction reveals increasing Arctic phytoplankton production during low-light winter-shoulder period
abstract: Arctic marine productivity is traditionally considered concentrated in the sunlit season, yet low-light winter-shoulder periods remain poorly constrained because passive ocean color observations require sufficient solar illumination. Here, we use 2.39 million spaceborne LiDAR profiles from CALIOP (2006–2023) to reconstruct Arctic net primary production (NPP) and evaluate how active-sensor observations reduce this seasonal blind spot. The bio-optical retrieval model was trained using MODIS-constrained observations under illuminated conditions; accordingly, low-light estimates represent physically constrained extrapolations beyond the primary MODIS-observable training domain rather than direct NPP measurements. Within this framework, LiDAR increases winter half-year observational coverage from ∼20 to 30% to ∼70 to 75% and reveals widespread low-light winter-shoulder production across marginal seas and seasonal ice-edge regions. Pan-Arctic NPP integrated over this period increased at an estimated rate of 0.75 Tg C year −1 during 2007–2023, whereas the corresponding passive-sensor signal was negligible. Accounting for this component raises annual Arctic NPP estimates by ∼13.3% indicating that passive sensor-based assessments may underrepresent the magnitude and seasonal structure of Arctic productivity. Associations with declining sea ice and surface warming suggest this underrepresented production is consistent with ongoing seasonal reorganization of Arctic carbon fixation. Uncertainties from model parameterization, low-light extrapolation, and limited in situ validation are largest in the lowest-light and highest-latitude regimes. These findings do not imply photosynthesis during absolute polar night, but show that active LiDAR observations with explicit light constraints and transparent extrapolation limits can test how unresolved low-light winter-shoulder production may alter Arctic NPP seasonality under continuing sea-ice loss.

title: Structural insights into light harvesting and photosystem II evolution in the basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride
abstract: The basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride represents a critical evolutionary transition toward land plants, yet the molecular basis of its ancestral light-harvesting strategy remains elusive. Here, we present a 2.25-angstrom resolution cryo-EM structure of the M. viride PSII-LHCII-LHCP supercomplex, revealing a unique C 2 S 2 M p2 L p2 -type architecture. Our structure reveals a nearly complete set of conserved PSII core subunits, indicating that much of the PSII structural framework found in terrestrial plants was established early in the streptophyte lineage. At the periphery, the complex features a specialized antenna module in which two ancestral LHCP monomers flank CP29. These ancestral antenna proteins bind an unusually high number of carotenoids, with seven carotenoids per subunit, and extensively incorporate marine-type keto carotenoids, siphonaxanthin, and siphonein, throughout the complex, thereby broadening absorption in the blue-green region. The canonical LHCII trimer exhibits a distinctive chlorophyll b macrocluster and a 96-femtosecond ultrafast energy transfer component. Together, these findings provide a high-resolution molecular framework for an evolutionary intermediate that combines high-capacity aquatic light harvesting with structural features potentially relevant to photoprotection during the transition toward terrestrial life.

title: Piezoelectrically actuated magnetic dipole twisting resonators enable miniaturized low-frequency antennas
abstract: Miniaturized low-frequency antennas are essential for underwater, underground, and biomedical communications, yet their performance is constrained by the fundamental size-efficiency trade-off, a long-standing physical bottleneck. Here, we introduce a radiation mechanism that circumvents this constraint by replacing the time-varying currents in conventional antennas with the mechanical twisting oscillation of a magnetic dipole. Using piezoelectrically actuated, biomimetic twisting resonators with ultrahigh mechanical quality factors, we demonstrate that low-frequency antennas operating at 15.4 and 668 hertz can be miniaturized to centimeter- and millimeter-scale, respectively, with radiation efficiencies exceeding those of size-matched loop antennas by factors of 49,000 and 5000, respectively. This electromechanical-magnetic transduction enables underwater cross-medium communication over 115 meters with only milliwatt-level power consumption, using 99.9% less power than loop antennas. It also supports implantable wireless devices that achieve a fourfold increase in communication range at identical power consumption, opening a route to long-range, low-power wireless systems capable of operating in some of the most demanding environments.

title: Evolutionarily reinforced GC-rich motif enables non-AUG translation in mammals under eIF1/5MP-mediated fidelity control
abstract: Non-AUG translation contributes to proteome diversity, but its regulatory principles remain unclear. Here, we show that a GCC-rich upstream extension, termed the NAT1 motif, acts as a potent enhancer of near-cognate initiation in mammals. Cell-free and reporter assays revealed that eIF1 and 5MP act as conserved inhibitors of non-AUG initiation across mammals and plants, while the NAT1 motif enables enhanced initiation within this fidelity framework. Mutational analysis identified −6 and −7 positions within the GCC repeat as key determinants of motif activity. Genome-wide analyses uncovered evolutionary depletion of NAT1 -type non-AUG codons in human 5′UTRs, suggesting purifying selection against excessive initiation. Nevertheless, more than a hundred retained sites are associated with genes involved in cell proliferation and migration, suggesting that regulated non-AUG initiation may contribute to disease-relevant translational programs. The motif’s enrichment within GCC repeats further suggests a mechanistic link to repeat-associated non-AUG translation.

title: STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages
abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a pleiotropic cytokine that drives macrophage functions ranging from tissue homeostasis to inflammation, yet how STAT3 specifies these divergent outcomes remains unclear. By integrating transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling with selective STAT3 degradation, we show that STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages. Graded STAT3 chromatin recruitment scales with locus-specific H3K27ac deposition and transcriptional output across homeostatic and inflammatory programs. STAT3 degradation permits STAT1 recruitment at a subset of regulatory regions and engages a delayed amplification loop that is partially dependent on STING and type I IFN signaling. In severe COVID-19, monocytes exhibit exaggerated STAT3-associated inflammatory signatures together with attenuated STAT1-associated interferon responses, consistent with a skewed STAT3-STAT1 balance. These findings define a framework in which STAT3 calibrates IL-6–induced chromatin output while maintaining pathway fidelity by limiting STAT1 cross-talk.

title: Integrating biomass production platform and identification approach for stereochemical assignment of super-carbon-chain compounds
abstract: Super-carbon-chain compounds (SCCCs), marine long-carbon-chain polyketides featuring numerous carbon stereocenters, fall into untapped chemical space in between drug-like small molecules and biopolymers. Due to mass-material unavailability and flexible-structure complexity, the reliable stereochemical assignment of SCCCs has long remained stagnant. In this work, a modern microalgal biomass production-platform is created for pilot-scale cultivation of marine dinoflagellates to produce over 100 milligrams of minor SCCCs. The modular fragment-based identification (MFBI) approach is successfully employed to establish the relative and absolute configurations of SCCCs. As an example, 157.7 mg of a minor SCCC, named amphidiketol A, featuring a highly-flexible C 76 -linear carbon backbone and thirty-three carbon stereocenters, is obtained from Amphidinium sp. in our platform. Its hybrid architecture contains eleven‌ distinct modular fragments. Its relative and absolute configurations are successfully established by the MFBI approach. Collectively, an undescribed paradigm for stereochemical assignment of SCCCs is presented. Nine senescence-associated protein targets of amphidiketol A in lung cancer A549 cells are identified.

title: Integrated physiological and multiomic analyses reveal the multilayered aluminum tolerance mechanisms of acidophilic alga Coccomyxa sp. A2.
abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) is a pervasive global environmental challenge, and algal-based bioremediation represents one of the most robust strategies for its treatment. However, the mechanisms by which algae survive in metal-rich AMD remain largely unclear. Here, we integrated physiological, transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses to explore the tolerance mechanisms of the acidophilic alga Coccomyxa sp. A2 to aluminum (Al), a metal prevalent in AMD. The results demonstrated that A2 exhibited substantially higher Al tolerance than the model alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii under their respective optimal pH conditions. Upon Al exposure, A2 significantly increased the extracellular levels of three strong organic acids (oxalic, citric, and tartaric acids), thereby facilitating chelation of free Al3+ present in the acidic environment. In the near-neutral cytosol, A2 accumulated a broader array of organic acids at higher concentrations to sequester Al despite severe extracellular H+ stress. To restrict Al influx, A2 enhanced the synthesis of cellulose, hemicellulose, and proteins across the distinct layers of its cell wall, increasing cell wall dry weight by 66%. This remodeling was probably supported by starch degradation, enhanced gluconeogenesis, and Calvin cycle activation, which together supplied sufficient monosaccharide precursors for polysaccharide synthesis. Concurrently, the upregulation of glycosyltransferases facilitated rapid polysaccharide chain elongation. To scavenge ROS, the alga likely initiated a temporally coordinated, biphasic antioxidant response, in which non-enzymatic ascorbic acid pools compensated for lagging superoxide dismutase activity during the early acute phase of stress. Calcium, abscisic acid, and jasmonic acid coordinated these defense mechanisms, with calcium serving as the primary signaling hub. IMPORTANCE The conventional treatment method for acid mine drainage (AMD) involves neutralization with lime, which is costly and generates large amounts of sludge that is difficult to manage. The application of sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) presents a promising alternative by eliminating secondary pollution and enabling metal sulfide recovery. However, a key challenge of this approach is ensuring an affordable and sustainable organic carbon source for SRB since AMD is oligotrophic. A potential solution is the in-situ cultivation of acidophilic algae. Given the high metal concentrations in AMD, investigating the metal tolerance mechanisms of acidophilic algae is vital for producing sufficient biomass to support SRB. Meanwhile, about 40% of the world’s arable soils are acidic, and these soils typically contain high concentrations of aluminum (Al), which is a major factor limiting crop production. Therefore, research on the exceptional Al tolerance mechanisms of acidophilic algae can provide insights into improving crop metal resistance through genetic engineering techniques. title: A human sensory neuron model for varicella-zoster virus latency and reactivation in vitro.
abstract: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) is a ubiquitous human neurotropic alphaherpesvirus that establishes lifelong latency in sensory ganglionic neurons. Subsequent viral reactivation causes herpes zoster, a morbid disease often complicated by neuropathic pain. Mechanisms underlying VZV latency and reactivation are not understood, mostly due to the lack of permissive animal models and challenges of current in vitro latency modeling. Here, we evaluated HD10.6 cells, a simplified and easily expandable human sensory neuron line to model VZV latency and reactivation. Differentiated HD10.6 (dHD10.6) neurons supported productive VZV infection, viral DNA replication, production of infectious progeny, and viral spread in cultures. VZV infection was associated with limited cytopathic effects and ultrastructural changes. Infecting dHD10.6 neurons with cell-free VZV in the presence of antivirals resulted in a quiescent-persistent state, characterized by persistent VZV genomes with restricted VZV gene expression and absence of infectious virus. Importantly, VZV could be reactivated by treatment with capsaicin, as evidenced by increased lytic viral transcription and virus spread. In conclusion, this study establishes human HD10.6 neurons as a novel and expandable in vitro model for studying VZV latency and reactivation to identify virus and host factors governing latency that may serve as therapeutic targets to restrict VZV reactivation. IMPORTANCE Most individuals carry latent varicella-zoster virus (VZV) in their dorsal root ganglia (DRG), which can reactivate to cause shingles and chronic pain. The mechanisms by which VZV establishes latency and triggers of reactivation are incompletely understood. Current platforms for the study of VZV latency do not easily support functional experiments (ganglia) or are difficult to expand and complicated by mixed neuronal populations (stem cell-derived neurons). Here, we demonstrate that differentiated HD10.6 cells derived from immortalized human DRG-derived neurons provide a clonal and easy-to-expand platform for studying lytic, latent, and reactivated VZV infection in sensory neurons. We propose that the HD10.6 platform could provide the basis to conduct studies on the viral latent state that have hitherto not been possible. title: Agricultural Information Networks, Information Needs and Risk Management Strategies among Smallholder Farmers in Southeast Nigeria
abstract: This study examined agricultural information networks, information needs, and risk management strategies among smallholder farmers in Southeast Nigeria using the Diffusion of Innovation Theory. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS Version 21 with descriptive statistics including means, frequencies, rankings, and standard deviations, while qualitative data from focus group discussions were examined thematically using Braun and Clarke’s six-step framework. Findings show dominance of farmer-to-farmer networks, traditional knowledge systems, and kinship ties as the most trusted sources of agricultural information, while institutional and digital platforms were least utilized. Major information needs centred on disease and pest management, climate-related risks, fertilizer use, and improved seed varieties, reflecting farmers’ vulnerability to environmental and production uncertainties. Within Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovation Theory, interpersonal communication channels such as peer networks significantly influenced awareness and adoption of agricultural practices. The study concludes that strengthening farmer-led networks and improving access to credible institutional information sources can enhance risk management and innovation adoption among smallholders in the region. Implications suggest that extension agencies and development actors should leverage existing social structures, enhance participatory communication strategies, and integrate indigenous knowledge with formal agricultural advisory services to improve resilience, reduce information asymmetry, and support sustainable adoption of innovations in line with diffusion processes in rural farming communities. Furthermore, the study contributes to the understanding of agricultural information behaviour in developing contexts and highlights the need for improved digital infrastructure, policy support, and capacity building to strengthen inclusive rural information ecosystems development.

journal: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Virtual Global Computing Education Conference V.2
abstract: AI agents are increasingly used by professional software developers to support tasks such as planning, coding, debugging, refactoring, and drafting documentation. Unlike basic chat models, AI agents work more autonomously toward a broader goal: breaking tasks into steps, taking actions, using tools, and iterating on their own output. Based on our experiences, similar agent-based workflows can be used to assist educators in generating and refining learning materials. In this hands-on tutorial, we will introduce participants to practical ways of using AI agents to support the development of computing education resources, including lecture slides, online textbook materials, programming exercises, explanations, analogies, and visualizations. We will compare different types of tools, including general-purpose AI systems and coding-focused agentic tools, and discuss when each may be useful for educational material generation. Participants will explore agent-based workflows through hands-on activities in which they create, revise, and adapt learning materials for their own teaching contexts. Throughout the tutorial, we will emphasize both the opportunities and limitations of these tools. We will also discuss ethical and practical issues, including copyright, citations, attribution, transparency, and responsible use. Drawing on the organizers' experiences, the tutorial will provide participants with concrete workflows, examples, and strategies for incorporating AI agents into the creation of learning materials in computing education.

title: An Experience Report on Teaching Students to Evaluate AI Agent Skills as Authorization Decisions
abstract: Cultivating a security mindset has long been a goal of computing education, and students now need it when deciding whether to trust an AI agent skill. Skills are add-ons that can shape an agent's behavior through natural language instructions and configuration settings, not just executable code. To prepare students to evaluate skills as authorization decisions, we designed a classroom activity and taught it in a senior undergraduate and a graduate cybersecurity-focused course. Students inspected three example skills, each pairing a real workflow task with one agent-specific authority, such as acting without asking for user consent before each action. The activity guided them to make initial authorization recommendations and then use a static security scanner to test and revise their recommendations. We observed in class that students needed guidance to extend their security review from a skill's code to what they would be authorizing the agent to do through the skill. Pre/post surveys from 11 volunteer respondents in this preliminary pilot showed greater self-reported confidence in evaluating skills, and post-activity responses placed more emphasis on the authority that skills carry. We release all activity materials for reuse.

title: Motion-Informed Neural Network Towards Diastolic Mechanics in Takotsubo Syndrome.
abstract: BACKGROUND The pathophysiology of Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) remains perplexing. We developed a motion-informed neural network (MiNN-Echo) using echocardiograms to elucidate the diastolic mechanics of TTS. METHODS We trained and validated MiNN-Echo, a deep convolutional neural network (2D+t) echocardiographic prediction model using multi-vendor echocardiograms from 1142 patients (596 TTS and 546 anterior myocardial infarction) in a multi-institutional cohort. A total of 68 expert echocardiographic readers performed human interpretation. The network's dual-branch architecture independently learns spatial and temporal features, using 2-dimensional image frames for spatial representation and segmentation, and optical flow with sinusoidal phase encoding for temporal dynamics. The MiNN-Echo model integrates static cardiac anatomic changes with motion details from 2-dimensional echocardiographic videos to produce interpretable disease predictions. RESULTS The MiNN-Echo model achieved an area under the curve of 0.77, compared with 0.69 among human readers in differentiating TTS from acute myocardial infarction. Myocardial motion features during diastole contributed more (≈71%) to the differential diagnosis than those during systole. Compared with patients with acute myocardial infarction, TTS patients showed increased isovolumic relaxation time (112.5 [interquartile range (IQR), 68.75-165.94] ms versus 87.5 [IQR, 54.17-140] ms, P<0.001; 28% versus 19% of diastolic time, P<0.001), decreased passive ventricular filling (before atrial contraction) time (176.04 [IQR, 114.2-248.12] ms versus 258.62 [IQR, 199.89-331.9] ms, P<0.001; 44% versus 54% of diastolic time, P<0.001), and a different mitral-annulus motion trajectory: lower pixel-wise myocardial displacement in the isovolumic relaxation (0.35 [IQR, 0.26-0.47] versus 0.38 [IQR, 0.28-0.51]; P=0.006), passive (0.45 [IQR, 0.33-0.58] versus 0.50 [IQR, 0.38-0.68]; P<0.001), and active ventricular filling (0.43 [IQR, 0.32-0.56] versus 0.48 [IQR, 0.35-0.63]; P=0.001) phases, and altered rotation angles (away from the horizontal A-V plane) in the passive ventricular filling phase (-70.19 [IQR, -89.62 to -41.33] versus -60.34 [IQR, -87.07 to -30.84]; P=0.020). CONCLUSIONS MiNN-Echo in echocardiograms elucidates unique myocardial relaxation kinematics to characterize TTS-associated diastolic mechanics.

title: Prediction of antioxidant compounds in water spinach ( Ipomoea aquatica Forsk.) across peri-urban food value chains in Indonesia using near infrared spectroscopy
abstract: Water spinach or “ kangkung ” ( Ipomoea aquatica Forsk.) is a semi-aquatic leafy vegetable belonging to the family Convolvulaceae. This plant is widely used in tropical and sub-tropical regions of Southeast Asia, grow well in moist soils and aquatic environments, making it a valuable crop for lowland and wetland agriculture. This species has long been cultivated and consumed across Asia for its nutritional value and its role in traditional medicine. The aim of this study was to evaluate the use of near infrared (NIR) spectroscopy to predict phenolic compounds, β-carotene and total chlorophyll of I. aquatica obtained from four diverse geographical locations of Indonesia representing peri-urban areas near Greater Jakarta, Bandung, Yogyakarta, and Surabaya given their critical position to link between rural agricultural production and urban consumption and food systems. The coefficient of determination in cross validation (r 2 CV ) and the standard error in cross validation (SECV) were 0.68 (SECV: 2.4 mg gallic acid equivalents (GAE)/g dry weight (DW)), 0.65 (SECV: 42.4 µmol Fe 2+ equivalents/g DW), 0.56 (SECV: 25.8 μmol Trolox equivalents (TE)/g DW), 0.25 (SECV: 15.1 mg/100 g DW) and 0.68 (SECV: 0.23 mg/g DW) for total phenolic compounds (TPC), corresponding to ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP), 2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) ABTS, β-carotene and total chlorophyll, respectively. The RPD values ranged between 1.1 and 2.1 indicating that the cross-validation models are adequate for screening purposes. The standard errors of prediction (SEP) were 2 mg GAE/g DW, 44.4 µmol Fe 2+ equivalents/g DW, 30.5 μmol TE/g DW, and 0.21 mg/g DW for TPC, FRAP, ABTS, and total chlorophyll, respectively. No satisfactory prediction results were obtained for β-carotene. The development and implementation of rapid analytical methods such as those based on the utilization of NIR spectroscopy, provide with tools that can be used for early dietary interventions, to monitor bioactive compounds, ensuring food authenticity and security, and supporting nutrition-sensitive and sustainable agriculture.

title: Model cards are not primary artifacts: stereochemistry in the MoLFormer and SMI-TED chemical foundation models
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: Pretrained chemical language models are selected, embedded with, and fine tuned on the basis of what their documentation says they are. We report that the released model card for MoLFormer, one of the most widely used chemical foundation models, states that isomeric information was removed from its training data, and that this statement is contradicted by artifacts distributed in the model's own repository. The shipped token frequency table records the tetrahedral stereocentre token [C@H] occurring 669,642,207 times, making it the twelfth most frequent token in a corpus of 47.2 billion tokens, ahead of fluorine, and stereochemical tokens account for 3.17% of all token occurrences. The described stripping is real but occurs at a different pipeline stage: isomeric = False is hardcoded into the fine tuning scripts and applied to downstream benchmark data, not to pretraining. We find a related divergence in SMI-TED, whose released vocabulary contains 2,393 tokens rather than the 2,988 reported, and whose shipped frequency table is identical to MoLFormer's, byte for byte, across all 2,357 shared tokens, despite the paper describing a different corpus. We release the extracted frequency table and an audit tool, and recommend that chemical model cards state stereochemistry handling separately for pretraining, fine tuning, and inference.

title: GLP-1/GLP-1R signalling in infectious diseases: basic biology, immunometabolic mechanisms, and therapeutic translation
abstract: Infectious diseases remain a major global health burden, and metabolic disorders such as diabetes and obesity further increase susceptibility to infection and adverse outcomes. These intersecting metabolic and infectious risks have prompted growing interest in the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)/GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) axis beyond its established role in glycaemic regulation. GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) modulate systemic metabolism, neuroimmune signalling, vascular and epithelial homeostasis, and inflammatory responses. Whether their infection-related effects arise from direct immune-cell GLP-1R signalling, improved pathogen control, or indirect host protection remains unresolved. This narrative review critically evaluates GLP-1/GLP-1R signalling in infection. It distinguishes live-pathogen models from endotoxin and sterile-injury models, host resistance from host tolerance, and direct receptor-dependent actions from indirect systemic effects. It also differentiates chronic pre-infection exposure from treatment initiated after infection onset. Across selected preclinical models, GLP-1RAs more consistently attenuate inflammation and tissue injury while preserving organ function, whereas their effects on pathogen burden and clearance remain variable. Receptor-specific evidence for immune-cell-intrinsic GLP-1R signalling remains limited, and many reported immune phenotypes may instead reflect metabolic improvement, neuroimmune regulation, or barrier protection. Human evidence is derived mainly from observational studies and secondary analyses of chronic GLP-1RA exposure, with limited evidence from trials initiating treatment during acute infection. Future translation will require cell-specific receptor validation, live-pathogen models with post-infection treatment, parallel assessment of pathogen control and host protection, clinically relevant standard-of-care comparators, and infection-specific safety evaluation. GLP-1RAs are therefore best regarded as candidate host-directed adjuncts. Current evidence does not establish them as direct anti-infective therapies.

title: Climate-Related Health Challenges and Digital Health Needs among Women Agricultural Workers in Limpopo, South Africa: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Background Climate change is intensifying heat exposure in agricultural and agro-processing work across southern Africa. Women face intersecting reproductive, occupational and caregiving burdens that are often overlooked by occupational health systems. Digital health offers potential adaptation strategies, but its suitability for women farm workers remains underexplored. Aim To explore climate-related health challenges and digital health needs among women working at a selected mango atchaar agro-processing farm outside Tzaneen, Limpopo Province, South Africa. Methods A qualitative, exploratory and descriptive design was employed. Purposive sampling recruited 25 women workers and two key informants (the farm manager and safety officer). Data were collected on 18 June 2026 through five focus group discussions and two semi-structured interviews. Tesch’s eight-step open-coding approach was used for analysis, guided by the socio-ecological model (SEM). Lincoln and Guba’s criteria ensured trustworthiness. Results Twenty-seven participants contributed to five themes: climate-related health experiences; occupational conditions and safety risks; healthcare access and support; digital health use, barriers and opportunities; and workplace and community strategies for improving women’s health. Among the women, 19 (76%) were aged 46 years or older. Heat-related experiences included fatigue, headaches, dizziness, swelling, raised blood pressure and lower-abdominal discomfort, potentially overlapping with menopausal symptoms. Prolonged standing, heavy loads and spice-dust exposure compounded these challenges. Women relied largely on family and peer support. Digital health access was constrained by workplace phone restrictions, data costs, management-only Wi-Fi and limited digital literacy. Conclusion Women’s climate-related occupational health risks reflect interacting individual, interpersonal, workplace and policy-level factors. Digital health interventions should be accessible, context-sensitive and integrated with workplace-based primary healthcare. Such interventions must complement, not replace, employers’ occupational health and safety responsibilities and regulatory enforcement. Multilevel strategies are essential to strengthen occupational protection and timely healthcare access.

title: AgriTech: Foundations, Emerging Technologies, System Architectures, and Deployment Readiness—A Comprehensive Survey
abstract: Agricultural technology (AgriTech) is transforming agricultural production through advances in artificial intelligence, Internet of Things, robotics, remote sensing, digital twins, and intelligent decision-support systems. Despite these developments, the transition from technological innovation to effective agricultural deployment remains constrained by technical, operational, economic, and institutional challenges. Existing research frequently emphasizes individual technologies, applications, or performance indicators, providing limited integration of system architectures, operational reliability, affordability, interoperability, and deployment readiness. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of AgriTech foundations, enabling technologies, architectural approaches, agricultural applications, and performance evaluation methods. It examines centralized, distributed, cloud, edge, and hybrid architectures alongside intelligent agricultural systems and autonomous technologies. A comparative analysis identifies their capabilities, limitations, infrastructure requirements, and operational trade-offs. The survey further investigates agricultural data quality, environmental variability, cybersecurity, maintenance, financial sustainability, digital inclusion, and governance challenges affecting practical implementation. Building on this synthesis, the paper proposes the Integrated AgriTech Effectiveness and Deployment Readiness Framework (IAEDRF), which connects agricultural requirements, technology selection, system integration, performance validation, economic feasibility, organizational preparedness, and responsible governance. The framework introduces context-dependent assessment criteria, mandatory deployment requirements, and continuous operational reassessment. Its proposed suitability model remains conceptual and requires empirical validation. Finally, the survey identifies research priorities involving generalizable agricultural AI, interoperable infrastructures, affordable technologies, real-world benchmarking, and sustainable scaling. The findings emphasize that AgriTech effectiveness depends not only on technological capability but also on reliable, affordable, interoperable, and context-appropriate deployment. The survey provides an integrated foundation for future research, technology development, and evidence-based agricultural implementation.

title: Pepti-DrugPhAI: Multimodal AI-evaluator for functional pharmacokinetics and toxicity of peptides.
abstract: Peptide drugs exhibit exceptional selectivity for biological targets and high functional activity making them among the most promising therapeutic agents. However, unsatisfactory pharmacokinetic characteristics remain a critical barrier to their implementation. They often become the primary reason for the failure of promising candidates in preclinical and clinical trials. To address this issue, we present Pepti-DrugPhAI - a comprehensive algorithm for the precise prediction of the pharmacokinetics and toxicity of a wide range of peptide compounds. Unlike many existing solutions, the proposed algorithm is multimodal and can simultaneously process both SMILES representations of chemical structures and amino acid sequences. This ensures efficient processing not only of canonical peptides but also of non-canonical modifications, cyclic structures, and peptide-like small molecules. We also created an original dataset for model training integrating data from public databases and relevant scientific publications. The algorithm simultaneously predicts key parameters including membrane permeability (Caco-2 and PAMPA penetration), distribution and excretion (half-life, clearance, volume of distribution), as well as general and specific toxicity profiles (neurotoxicity, hemolytic activity). A key innovation of the study is the integration of functional pharmacokinetic scoring. The model not only predicts ADMET values but also calculates an adaptive suitability rating for a compound in the context of its specific biological activity. We have conducted a comparative analysis of various data encoding strategies implementing a stack of models ranging from classical machine learning methods to modern transformers and language models in classification modes. Results from testing on independent test sets demonstrate high prediction accuracy and interpretability of features making Pepti-DrugPhAI a powerful tool for more robust selection of promising peptide drug candidates. All data and the code are available in the GitHub repository at https://github.com/EABogdanova/Pepti-DrugPhAI.

title: Comparative Study of Neural Networks and Support Vector Regression for Final Project Duration Prediction using Simulated Scheduling Scenarios
abstract: The prediction of the duration of a construction project is a highly complex task influenced by multiple factors. To tackle the heterogeneity and noise of historical datasets, this paper proposes the use of a highly controlled, simulation-generated dataset comprising 157 realistic schedules of school construction projects. The schedules were generated using six core planning variables. A distinctive contribution of this research is the systematic evaluation of the combinatorial performance between data normalization techniques (Min-Max and Z-score) and learning algorithms (Support Vector Regression and Artificial Neural Networks). The models were globally optimized using cross-validation to prevent data leakage. Comparison between the results of the SVR model with an RBF kernel under Min-Max normalization, and a compact ANN with one hidden layer using the Levenberg-Marquardt training function, demonstrated high theoretical accuracy within the simulated boundaries. The results indicate that SVR yields superior generalization accuracy across the analyzed scenarios. Furthermore, a conceptual reliability-aware framework, ScheduleRelia, is introduced. ScheduleRelia serves as a proof-of-concept application designed to estimate project duration and assess schedule health using critical path metrics. While broad generalization requires future external validation with real-world inputs, this study establishes a rigorous baseline for algorithm selection and data formatting in schedule forecasting.

title: Peculiarities of Selection for Yield and Yield Components in Segregating Populations of Spring Soft Wheat
BCAT: A Block Causal Transformer for PDE Foundation Models for Fluid Dynamics
abstract: Background: Foundation models have demonstrated remarkable generalization in vision and language, but their accurate use for scientific computing remains challenging. For two-dimensional fluid-dynamics prediction, current transformer-based models are often hindered by limited context and rigid causality information, as they typically map fixed windows to the next step. Objectives: We aim to develop a unified architecture for heterogeneous fluid-dynamics families. The goal is to better capture the complex spatio-temporal dependencies inherent in nonlinear fluid dynamics. Methods: We introduce BCAT, a block-causal transformer for autoregressive prediction of two-dimensional fluid-dynamics solutions. Our approach adapts block-causal attention to next-frame prediction, leveraging previous frames as contextual priors. The model is trained on 69K trajectory sequences from PDEBench, PDEArena, and CFDBench using the Muon optimizer. Results: BCAT achieved an average relative 𝐿 2 error of 1.18% across the six evaluated fluid families, reducing error by 45% relative to a 3.4-times-larger baseline. In ablations, next-frame prediction was 3.5x more accurate than the corresponding nexttoken variant. A five-seed analysis, noisy-input stress test, long-rollout analysis, and physics diagnostics further characterize the model. Conclusions: The block-causal framework captures spatial interactions within frames while enforcing temporal causality across frames. BCAT provides an accurate and computationally efficient model for the two-dimensional fluid-dynamics benchmarks considered here.

title: LSTM Network Architecture based on Programmable Logic Controllers
abstract: The article is devoted to the problem of short-term forecasting of technological parameters at the level of a programmable logic controller (PLC). Real-time analysis of process signals is infeasible due to latency in the network infrastructure between industrial control system (ICS) levels, as well as delays in measurement channels. The paper proposes implementing an LSTM neural network model at the PLC level, which makes it possible to optimize data handling time and promptly detect deviations from normal operating modes. An implementation of the LSTM model architecture on a PLC is presented for forecasting time series of process parameters. The LSTM model, developed in the high-level Python language, was trained on 110 hours of historical data sampled at one-minute intervals. Training yielded weight coefficients and neuron bias values that were used to generate forecasts on the PLC. An LSTM model library was developed in Structured Text (ST) as defined by the IEC 61131-3 standard. For the obtained results, forecast metrics were computed — both on the upper-level server and on the PLC — against the test data, and forecasting performance indicators are reported. The results demonstrate the feasibility of implementing neural network models, in particular LSTM, at the PLC level without adversely affecting system performance.

title: EQUALITY BEFORE THE LAW IN THE SPHERE OF DIGITAL PROPERTY (THE CORRELATION BETWEEN THE CONSTITUTIONAL PRINCIPLE OF EQUALITY AND DIFFERENTIATION OF THE LEGAL REGIME OF SUBJECTS IN THE SPHERE OF DIGITAL PROPERTY)
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of the problem of the correlation between the principle of equality before the law and differentiation of the legal regime of subjects in the sphere of digital property. Based on the analysis of doctrinal approaches, new laws and judicial practice, a model of a balanced legal regime is substantiated, combining a unified basic status of digital property as an object of civil rights with targeted differentiated restrictions for certain categories of participants. Criteria for permissible differentiationare proposed, ensuring compliance with the constitutional principles of equality and proportionality.

title: The Personal Fund as a Mechanism for Family Business Succession in Russia
abstract: The article studies the impact of the personal fund structure on ensuring family business succession and transforming traditional approaches to succession planning. The conclusion is substantiated that transferring key assets to an independent legal entity enables the founder, during their lifetime, to establish a stable governance model for the family business, define the procedures for asset utilization, and secure the financial interests of family members after their death. The significance of a personal fund is examined in terms of preserving unified corporate control, preventing the fragmentation of ownership interests and shares among heirs, mitigating the risk of inheritance and corporate disputes, and maintaining the continuity of a family business. Particular attention is paid to separating the functions of business management from the receipt of economic benefits: heirs and other family members can act as beneficiaries of a personal fund without being directly involved in managing the company. The article analyzes the specific features of the legal status of beneficiaries and separately examines the property qualification of 100 million rubles established by the civil law which is required for the creation of a lifetime personal fund. The conclusion is made that the high qualification amount limits the accessibility of this structure for small and medium-sized enterprises, even though they are also exposed to the risks of inheritance disputes and business fragmentation. Proposals are formulated regarding the possible differentiation of the legal regulation of personal funds established specifically for managing family businesses. In conclusion, the need to align the articles of association and terms and conditions for personal fund management with the founder’s prenuptial agreement, divorce settlement agreement, and testamentary dispositions is emphasized.

title: The Relationship Between Types of Proceedings and Other Procedures for Case Hearings in Civil Proceedings
abstract: The article examines the relationship between a type of proceeding and other case consideration procedures in civil procedure. The author views civil procedure as a four-level system of case examination procedures, the levels of which are: type of judicial proceedings, type of proceeding, features of the examination of individual categories of cases, and the legal case. Each level represents a differentiation of the civil procedural form to varying degrees. The constructed model allows for an examination of the dynamics of case examination procedures — their emergence and transition from one level to another.

title: AI and precision agriculture for food security and rural livelihoods in developing countries: A systematic review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and precision agriculture technologies are increasingly promoted as tools for addressing food insecurity and improving rural livelihoods in developing countries, but the evidence on their developmental outcomes and governance implications is fragmented across disciplines. This study conducted a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review of peer-reviewed journal articles and scholarly book chapters published between 1 January 2012 and 15 January 2026 and retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ). Of 412 records identified, 52 studies met the inclusion criteria. Empirical studies were appraised at the study level with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT 2018), while reviews and conceptual papers were used for context. Studies were coded against an a priori framework of four governance mechanisms (targeting and allocation; delivery and service provision; monitoring and evaluation; accountability and participation) and synthesised thematically across six domains. The strongest evidence concerns the technical performance of AI models for crop and food-insecurity prediction and for pest and disease detection. Evidence that these tools improve farm incomes, food security or livelihood resilience in practice is limited: few studies measured livelihood or food-security outcomes, were longitudinal, or disaggregated results by gender or farm size. Recurrent constraints include infrastructure deficits, low digital literacy, unrepresentative training data, weak institutional capacity and regulatory gaps. The study contributes a framework that links AI applications to food-security and livelihood outcomes through governance mechanisms and identifies where evidence is strong, emerging or absent. Potential benefits should be regarded as plausible but not yet demonstrated at scale. Priorities include impact evaluations with livelihood endpoints, gender-disaggregated and distributional analysis, and comparative studies of the institutional conditions under which AI-enabled agriculture benefits smallholders.
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Education and Society

title: AI Agents and Agentic AI in Medicine: An Autonomy-Centred Scoping Review and Research Agenda
abstract: Artificial intelligence agents—software systems that perceive, reason, plan and act over multiple steps with limited human intervention—are moving from research prototypes towards clinical deployment. Recent reviews map what has been built; this one asks what would have to hold for such systems to be deployed safely. We conducted a scoping review reported according to the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews, searching eight bibliographic sources from January 2017 to June 2026, admitting foundational computer science and regulatory literature alongside clinical applications. Five architectural paradigms recur—tool-augmented large language model agents, multi-agent systems, offline reinforcement learning agents, embodied robotic agents and autonomous monitoring agents—nearly all sharing a common four-layer stack. We introduce a six-level scale of clinical agent autonomy that grades systems by where human judgement enters relative to the reasoning, and by whether the resulting action remains reversible. The scale exposes an inversion in the evidence base: demonstrated patient benefit concentrates at high autonomy in narrow, bounded domains, whereas research effort concentrates at intermediate autonomy, where prospective outcome evidence is absent and automation bias is the dominant risk. We further propose seven evaluation dimensions specific to agency, a mapping of evaluation requirements to autonomy level, and a ten-item failure mode taxonomy assigned to the architectural layer at which each is addressable. Deploying agentic systems safely requires prospective multi-site validation, reporting standards adapted to agency, equity-aware design, and regulatory obligations indexed to autonomy rather than algorithm class. We conclude with an eight-point research agenda.

title: Explainable EEG Foundation Models for Schizophrenia Detection Across Independent Datasets
abstract: Schizophrenia is a complex psychiatric disorder associated with altered brain electrophysiology. EEG foundation models provide promising approaches for learning transferable neural representations; however, their effectiveness and interpretability for schizophrenia detection remain insufficiently investigated. Three pretrained EEG foundation models, EEGMamba, EEGPT, and BIOT, were systematically evaluated for schizophrenia classification, with Simple Mamba included as an additional comparison. Two independent resting-state EEG datasets were analyzed: ASEEG, comprising 51 individuals with schizophrenia (SZ) and 50 healthy controls (HC), and Warsaw, comprising 14 SZ and 14 HC participants. Subject-wise cross-validation was employed. Integrated Gradients (IG) and channel occlusion were used to investigate spatial importance and explanation consistency. EEGMamba achieved the strongest performance on both datasets. On ASEEG, it obtained 79.18 ± 8.00% accuracy, 82.33 ± 12.54% sensitivity, an F1-score of 0.79 ± 0.10, and ROC-AUC of 0.83 ± 0.09. On Warsaw, EEGMamba achieved 78.33 ± 24.90% accuracy and 80.00 ± 14.21% sensitivity. XAI revealed model- and dataset-dependent patterns involving frontal/frontopolar, central, temporal, and parietal regions, with recurrent importance of C3, C4, Cz, Fp1/Fp2, and P3/P4. On Warsaw, BIOT demonstrated strong agreement between IG and occlusion (ρ = 0.744, p < 0.001). EEG foundation models show potential for subject-independent schizophrenia detection, with EEGMamba providing the strongest predictive performance. Complementary XAI analyses revealed spatially distributed discriminative information and highlighted the importance of jointly evaluating predictive performance and interpretability across independent datasets.

title: In silico perturbation as an adversarial attack: combinatorial searchover cell states in single-cell foundation models
abstract: Background: Identifying which genes to perturb in order to drive a cell towards a desired state is a common problem in biology, and the answer is often a combination of genes. Single-cell foundation models can predict the effect of forcing a gene on without an experiment, but in silico perturbation has been confined to single genes or to a few hundred enumerated combinations. In token-based models, choosing which genes to force on is formally the same optimization problem as a discrete adversarial attack on a language model. We therefore investigated whether Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG), a search developed for such attacks, can be used to find combinations of genes. Results: Our results suggest that GCG is useful for finding combinations of genes. In Geneformer, the effect of a set was well below the sum of the individual effects of its members, which suggests that assembling combinations from single-gene effects is not a promising approach. GCG exceeded forward-selection greedy search at equal cost in two models (Geneformer and scGPT) and at every set size. Against published reprogramming protocols, GCG recovered the reported factors at a rate well above chance and higher than the random-pool and all-gene greedy searches at equal cost, although ranking genes by their individual effect gave a higher recovery rate. Recovery corresponded to whether a search used the embedding gradient, which suggests that the gradient is useful for narrowing the search, whereas stronger optimization of the objective did not raise recovery, which suggests that the similarity induced by the model does not fully reflect the regulatory logic of genes. Conclusions: These results are obtained within the constraints of the foundation models; nevertheless, searching for combinations of factors with foundation models extends in silico perturbation beyond single genes, reveals a property of the induced objective that single-gene evaluation does not, and points to a new direction for using and evaluating the models.

title: Enhanced rock weathering increases crop yield: a global meta-analysis
abstract: Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) is increasingly considered for CO₂ removal on agricultural land, yet its effects on crop productivity remain uncertain across crops, soils and amendment practices. This work is the first global meta-analysis of experimental evidence published between 1983 and 2026, comprising 7,236 treatment-control comparisons from 113 publications. Of these, 2,086 comparisons from 52 publications were eligible for multilevel random-effects meta-analysis with publication-clustered robust inference. ERW increased harvested yield by 29.0% (95% CI: 8.7–53.1%; 22 publications, 91 comparisons), shoot dry biomass by 16.1% (95% CI: 8.6–24.2%) and aboveground potassium uptake by 36.5% (95% CI: 26.7–47.0%). However, the publication-balanced median harvested-yield increase was 14.8% across the broader evidence base, and substantial heterogeneity produced a wide prediction interval (-43.4% to + 194.0%). Crop-specific responses varied, while exploratory moderator analyses did not establish reliable predictors of agronomic effectiveness across soil conditions, climates, rock materials or application practices. Strictly matched experimental responses revealed a positive association between potassium uptake and harvested yield (Spearman's ρ = 0.905; adjusted q = 0.008), although the limited evidence and potential mathematical coupling preclude causal interpretation. Overall, ERW can improve agricultural productivity, but the magnitude and consistency of these benefits remain context-dependent. Agronomic performance should therefore be evaluated independently of CO₂ removal, with greater emphasis on replicated field experiments and concurrent measurements of crop productivity, nutrient acquisition and soil conditions.
