title: Bank rate surprises, quantitative easing regimes and volatility connectedness in UK financial markets
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study examines how conventional Bank Rate surprises and quantitative easing (QE) regimes relate to volatility connectedness across UK gilts, equities, sterling and oil. Monthly realized-volatility proxies for the 10-year gilt yield, FTSE 100, GBP/USD and Brent are constructed from public daily data for 2010–2025. A vector autoregression with generalized forecast error variance decomposition estimates total, directional, and net connectedness. Inference uses 2,000 bootstrap replications that re-estimate the decomposition and a moving-block bootstrap for policy regressions. Total connectedness is 39.65%, and corrected total connectedness is 52.87%. The FTSE 100 is the dominant net transmitter at 42.11 (95% interval 35.48 to 53.31), followed by gilts at 13.25 (4.62 to 24.19). Brent is a net receiver at –54.00 (–70.10 to –51.20); sterling, at –1.36 (–5.71 to 7.05), is indistinguishable from zero. Narrow-window Bank Rate surprises do not predict connectedness across five monthly lags, with robustness across alternative identifications and rolling windows and at 59 of 64 specification-grid points. A close-to-close two-year gilt proxy shares only 31% of its variance with the identified surprise and produces significant coefficients under Newey-West errors, but moving-block bootstrap inference removes them. None of the fifteen QE-active minus QE-inactive differences is distinguishable from zero, and the aggregate difference changes sign with crisis exclusions. Neither policy instrument shows a measurable monthly association with volatility allocation after accounting for surprise identification and estimation uncertainty.

title: Estimation of evaporation rates in arid regions using an improved inverse analysis method.
abstract: Arid regions cover approximately 41% of the Earth's land surface, and water scarcity is a critical challenge for the populations living in these regions. Evaporation is an important component of crop water requirements and plays a significant role in ground surface energy exchange and climate change. This study improves a previously proposed inverse analysis method for estimating evaporation in arid regions by considering the distinct locations of sensible and latent heat transfer. In arid environments, sensible heat is transferred at the ground surface, whereas latent heat transfer associated with evaporation occurs below the ground surface. To represent this difference, a new relationship, CE = BeCH (CH: bulk transfer coefficient for sensible heat, CE: bulk transfer coefficient for latent heat, Be: evaporation efficiency), was incorporated into the model. The proposed method was evaluated using FLUXNET2015 data from four sites in the U.S.A. and three sites in Australia at hourly, daily, monthly, and annual time scales. The results generally showed good agreement between the estimated and observed evaporation values across all time scales, demonstrating the applicability of the proposed inverse analysis method to arid regions. The introduction of Be provides a physically meaningful representation of the reduced efficiency of evaporation under dryland conditions and offers a new perspective for evaporation estimation in arid environments.
journal: Proceedings of the Japan Academy. Series B, Physical and biological sciences

title: Predicción de emisiones de CO2 en países de la OCDE mediante redes neuronales e indicadores demográficos, económicos y de economía circular
abstract: Introduction: Mitigating climate change requires accurate monitoring and prediction of CO2 emissions, particularly in OECD countries, where industrialization and economic growth have historically driven high emission levels.Objective: To predict CO2 emissions in OECD countries using a neural network approach that incorporates demographic and economic indicators, circular economy legislation, and plastics trade data.Methods: A quantitative, longitudinal and predictive design was applied to a panel of 32 OECD countries (1960–2023; 2,048 country-year observations). GRU networks with one-, three- and five-year windows were optimized with Optuna, trained with a temporal split (training up to 2018, validation 2019–2021, test 2022–2023), and complemented by post-hoc calibration and Kernel SHAP. Results were compared with persistence, fixed-effects panel, Random Forest and LSTM benchmarks and checked across five random seeds.Results: Optimization and calibration raised the test R² from 0.053 for the non-optimized network to 0.968 for the calibrated three-step model (MAE = 83.7 MtCO2). This model was the most stable across seeds (MAE = 86.7 ± 4.3 MtCO2), and window length did not yield consistent differences. Simple benchmarks, however, achieved lower errors: persistence (MAE = 11.0) and Random Forest (MAE = 45.8). Plastics trade, likely acting as a proxy for economic size, and labor force were the most influential variables, whereas circular economy laws had the weakest contribution.Conclusions: Calibrated GRU networks provide an interpretable framework that links CO2 emissions to structural demographic, economic, trade and regulatory indicators without using past emissions as inputs. However, they do not outperform simple benchmarks for short-term forecasting. Their value lies in explanation and scenario analysis rather than in point prediction.

title: DELINEATION OF AGRICULTURAL FIELD BOUNDARIES USING MACHINE LEARNING: BASED ON THE CASE OF THE ZHETYSAI DISTRICT, KAZAKHSTAN
abstract: Accurate delineation of agricultural field boundaries is essential for agro-production monitoring, irrigation management, and sustainable land use planning. Manual digitization is labour-intensive and poorly scalable, while conventional segmentation algorithms are sensitive to spectral heterogeneity and weak inter-field contrast. The Zhetysai district of southern Kazakhstan – where approximately 45-50% of irrigated farmland exhibits salinization – exemplifies the urgent demand for automated field mapping. This study evaluates the Meta AI Segment Anything Model (SAM) with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning as a parameter-efficient, scalable approach to automated field boundary delineation. High-resolution Esri World Imagery served as the primary data source. A training dataset of 705 manually digitized field polygons was prepared in ArcGIS Pro and exported as classified tiles. SAM – pre-trained on over one billion masks – was fine-tuned via the SAMLoRA architecture, which freezes the Vision Transformer encoder and trains only lightweight adapter layers, enabling efficient domain adaptation from limited annotations. The model was trained on a CUDA GPU with early stopping, then applied district-wide to generate a pixel classification raster, which was vectorized into closed field polygons and validated through expert visual inspection. Fine-tuning achieved 91% overall pixel accuracy on the validation subset. Applied to the full study area, the model delineated 4,060 field polygons covering 809.76 km2 . Expert verification confirmed high boundary correspondence and negligible false positives. The results demonstrate that a foundation model can be effectively adapted to a new agrolandscape with minimal labelled data, yielding a reproducible and scalable geospatial workflow suitable for precision irrigation management, sown area assessment, and land resource governance across irrigated regions.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL SATISFACTION AS A MODERATOR IN THE HARNESSING OF COMMUNITY-BASED TOURISM FOR SUSTAINABLE GROWTH
abstract: Community-based tourism (CBT) has come up as a viable solution towards development of sustainable tourism. Against the conventional tourism models, CBT focuses on the active participation and empowerment of the local communities in the planning, management, and decision-making processes in tourism. Through prioritization of local ownership, cultural preservation and environmental conservation, the CBT seeks to achieve more equitable distribution of tourism benefits and minimizing negative impacts. This is more so applicable in developing areas where tourism can be used as a trigger in bringing about socio-economic development provided it is done in a responsible manner This study aims to investigate how communitybased tourism (CBT), with its three dimensions (economic, social, and environmental), affects long-term tourism growth and explores the moderating role of environmental satisfaction in the relationship between (CBT) factors and sustainable growth (SG). An online survey was conducted, involving 402 participants from the local community, representatives of the tourism sector, and visitors to the Dhofar tourism destination. A two-step quantitative approach was employed, utilizing structural equation modelling (SEM) using WarpPLS software. The findings demonstrated that the economic factor had a positive influence on sustainable growth, whereas the social factor exerted a negative influence, and the environmental factor exhibited no effect. Environmental satisfaction serves as a crucial moderator, amplifying the positive effects of social and environmental factors on tourism sustainability. CBT is a model of tourism that places local communities at the center of tourism management, development, and operation. This approach not only prioritizes environmental and cultural conservation but also enhances local livelihoods, making it a powerful tool for fostering sustainable tourism development. This study represents one of the limited investigations within the Sultanate of Oman in this context. The findings may assist the tourism industry in comprehending the potential advantages and challenges of (CBT) as well as how to employ it in their specific fields.

title: SPATIAL DISPARITIES IN CULTURAL TOURISM: A MULTIDIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS OF MUSEUM ATTENDANCE DYNAMICS IN BULGARIA
abstract: This study aims to identify and analyse spatial disparities and structural stratification of regional museum activity in Bulgaria over a 13-year period (2012-2024). The primary objective is to evaluate the stability, growth trajectory, and resilience of regional cultural supply models in response to external and macroeconomic shifts, specifically the COVID-19 pandemic. A multidimensional statistical analysis was applied to panel data from the National Statistical Institute and the Institute for Market Economics, encompassing all 28 administrative districts in Bulgaria. Quartile grouping (based on visits per 1000 inhabitants) was utilized to differentiate clusters, while long-term dynamics and crisis resilience were assessed through specific indicators: Coefficient of Variation (CV), Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR), Sensitivity Index (SI), and Recovery Index (RI). Through this approach, the districts were categorized into three distinct performance tiers: Highlevel (Leaders), Mid-level, and Low-level. The analysis reveals significant structural imbalances and high systemic volatility across all clusters, indicating a critical dependence on incidental tourist flows. A “scale paradox” was identified, whereby districts with moderate attendance volumes and a developed local product demonstrate considerably higher post-crisis adaptability compared to traditional leaders. Although all groups exhibit coefficients of variation exceeding 40%, the Mid-level segment achieves the highest annual growth (4.95%) and positive recovery (17.15%), outperforming the top-tier districts, which record slower growth (1.62%) and negative post-pandemic recovery (-12.08%). Empirical profiles highlight stable cores (Veliko Tarnovo, Gabrovo), strategic event legacies (Plovdiv), and nature-integrated recovery (Smolyan), contrasting with transitdependent declines (Vidin). The high structural volatility underscores an urgent need for a conceptual shift in regional cultural policies. Strategic management should pivot towards active audience development and integrated regional tourism products, linking public subsidies to institutional flexibility and proven post-crisis resilience rather than merely static volumes.

title: Activity-based excavation modelling in total Lagrangian SPH with pressure-dependent plasticity
abstract: We present an activity-based excavation model for underground mining simulations implemented within the total Lagrangian Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (TLSPH) framework of SoliDualSPHysics. The model introduces three key features: (1) a smooth cosine-based activity transition that gradually reduces the stiffness, mass, and gravitational loading of excavated particles; (2) a Drucker-Prager plasticity model with closed-form return mapping for pressure-dependent geomaterial behaviour; and (3) a stress diffusion stabilisation term that damps dynamic oscillations in the explicit time integration. The model is validated against the FEM code TOCHNOG using J2 and Drucker-Prager plasticity. For J2, the maximum equivalent plastic strain agrees within 10%. For Drucker-Prager, qualitative agreement is observed with quantitative overprediction attributed to the lower yield threshold at low confining pressure and the inherent dynamic overshoot of explicit time integration.

title: Histogram Analysis of IVIM MRI Parameters for Distinguishing Pseudo-progression and True Progression in High-Grade Gliomas.
abstract: Background Differentiating pseudoprogression (PsP) from true progression (TP) in high-grade gliomas (HGGs) is challenging, as conventional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) lacks sufficient specificity. Intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) MRI, may improve diagnostic performance by providing insights into tumor microstructure. Objective To evaluate the diagnostic performance of IVIM MRI derived parameters histogram in distinguishing PsP from TP in HGG patients. Material and Methods In a prospective study, 30 patients with WHO grade III or IV gliomas, previously treated with standard therapy, underwent IVIM MRI. Parametric maps (D, D*, f, and Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC)) were normalized to contralateral white matter, and histogram features were extracted from enhancing lesions. Univariate analysis identified significant features, and multivariate logistic regression assessed their combined diagnostic performance. The model's diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, with Area Under Curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Results Histogram analysis revealed significant differences in most histogram features of the D-ratio, D*-ratio, and ADC-ratio between PsP and TP groups. The 50th percentile of the D-ratio and the 99th percentile of the D*-ratio were identified as independent predictors in the final model, with AUC values of 0.79 and 0.728, respectively. The final model achieved an AUC of 0.853, demonstrating high sensitivity (93.8%), specificity (64.3%), and overall accuracy (80%), outperforming individual parameters. Conclusion The 50v percentile of the D-ratio and the 99th percentile of the D*-ratio demonstrated significant discrimination power between PsP and TP. Their combination further enhanced diagnostic accuracy, making them valuable metrics for clinical decision-making in HGG management.

title: Integrated reclamation of unused agricultural land in Tver oblast
abstract: The article examines structural changes in crop production in the Tver Region and the dynamics of the stock of unused agricultural land in comparison with the Central Federal District over the period 2007–2024. It has been established that the growth in gross output of major crops in the region during the 2020s was driven by higher yields and the increasing role of intensive production factors rather than by the expansion of sown areas. At the same time, the Tver Region is among the regions with a high concentration of unused agricultural land: by 2023, it accounted for more than 25% of all abandoned agricultural land in the Central Federal District, while the actual use of the available reclaimed land fund did not exceed 43%. The economically efficient incorporation of fallow and degraded lands of the Non-Chernozem zone into agricultural use is possible only through a transition from an extensive plowing model to integrated land reclamation, including the restoration of water regulation infrastructure and the improvement of soil agrophysical properties

title: Quantitative image-based assessment of biofilm-induced surface stabilization in saline soils
abstract: Soil degradation and erosion are major threats to agricultural productivity and ecosystem stability in arid environments, yet the early-stage stabilization of saline soil surfaces by biocrust-forming cyanobacteria has rarely been quantified using a non-destructive approach. To address this gap, we developed a quantitative image-based framework to track micro-topographical changes in field plots inoculated with native cyanobacteria under two salinity levels, low salinity (EC = 6.5 dS m −1 ) and high salinity (EC = 15.4 dS m −1 ), using a completely randomized design with two independent replicates per treatment. After 50 days, standardized digital images of the soil surface were analyzed in MATLAB through grayscale conversion and local texture processing, including pixel standard deviation (SD), image entropy, and moving-window SD/entropy filtering, to capture spatial heterogeneity associated with roughness, cracks, and surface disorder. The inoculated plots showed visibly smoother and more cohesive surfaces than the controls, with significant reductions in pixel variability (14% and 37.36% under low and high salinity, respectively; P 0.01). These results indicate that cyanobacterial inoculation can improve soil surface organization, but its effectiveness declines under stronger salinity stress, likely because osmotic and ionic constraints suppress metabolic activity, limit extracellular polymeric substance secretion, and restrict formation of the filamentous network needed for particle binding and crust development. The study demonstrates that non-destructive image analysis can sensitively detect early biocrust formation and that cyanobacterial inoculation is a promising bioengineering strategy for stabilizing saline soil surfaces when salinity does not exceed physiological tolerance thresholds.

title: An IoT-enabled environmental informatics framework for real-time crop disease detection using attention-driven deep learning
abstract: Introduction Crop diseases are a major challenge in agriculture because their early and accurate identification is essential for reducing crop losses and improving productivity. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) with deep learning provides an effective approach for automated crop disease monitoring by enabling the collection and analysis of environmental parameters such as soil moisture, temperature, and humidity. However, accurate fine-grained disease identification remains challenging because of variations in disease symptoms, environmental conditions, and visual characteristics. Methods This study proposes an IoT-enabled deep learning framework for automated crop disease detection and classification. The collected crop images are pre-processed using scaling, normalization, and data augmentation techniques to improve image quality and model generalization. For efficient disease detection, a lightweight attention-driven convolutional neural network-based object detection approach, termed YOLO10-YSTs (You Only Look Once 10-Yield Surveillance Technology), is employed. The framework integrates the real-time detection capability of YOLO10 with an attention mechanism to emphasize disease-relevant regions and a stigmergy-based encoding strategy to enhance feature representation and extraction. In addition, a novel DBGU-LSTM (Dual-Bi-Gated Recurrent Unit with Long Short-Term Memory) architecture is developed for fine-grained crop disease classification. Results The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides effective disease detection, discriminative feature representation, and fine-grained classification. The DBGU-LSTM architecture achieves improved classification performance and training stability compared with the conventional deep learning models considered in the study. Overall, the proposed approach achieves a classification accuracy of 97.99%, demonstrating its effectiveness for automated crop disease recognition. Discussion and conclusion The results indicate that combining IoT-based environmental monitoring with attention-driven deep learning and recurrent feature-learning mechanisms can provide an effective solution for intelligent crop disease detection. The proposed framework enables accurate identification of disease patterns while supporting efficient and automated agricultural monitoring. Therefore, the approach has potential to assist farmers in early disease diagnosis, reduce crop losses, and improve agricultural productivity.

title: Edge-deployable cotton–weed pose estimation for growth-point localization in mechanical weeding
abstract: Precision mechanical weeding requires not only reliable crop–weed recognition but also an explicit image-plane target for each weed, because bounding boxes and segmentation masks do not directly indicate where a mechanical end effector should act. This study aimed to develop an edge-deployable method that jointly recognizes cotton and five weed species and directly predicts one visually defined growth-point keypoint for each plant instance. We propose WGPose, a lightweight pose-estimation network that represents each plant using its class, bounding box, and a single growth-point keypoint; only growth-point keypoints associated with weed instances are retained as candidate references for subsequent mechanical positioning. To reduce inference cost while preserving local plant structures, the explicit multiscale neck of YOLO11n-Pose was removed, backbone features were connected to a shared lightweight prediction head, and detail-preserving downsampling, high-level feature regulation, and multiscale channel-wise knowledge distillation were incorporated. The model was evaluated using 2,177 cotton-field images containing 2,830 annotated plant instances. WGPose + CWD achieved a Pose mAP50–95 of 94.30 ± 0.57% across three independent training runs using random seeds 42, 43, and 44, with 1.17 million parameters and 3.91 GFLOPs. Compared with YOLO11n-Pose (92.42 ± 0.65%), the mean Pose mAP50–95 increased by 1.88 percentage points, while the parameter count and GFLOPs decreased by 56.02% and 40.40%, respectively. Relative to non-distilled WGPose (92.96 ± 1.02%), CWD improved the mean Pose mAP50–95 by 1.34 percentage points without increasing inference complexity. In a separate single-checkpoint coordinate-level evaluation, the mean normalized distance error decreased from 0.0562 to 0.0468, and PCK@0.05 increased from 59.46% to 70.30%. In a three-run offline RGB-image benchmark on the Jetson AGX Orin, the TensorRT prediction pipeline achieved a mean latency of 20.59 ± 0.08 ms per image, corresponding to 48.57 ± 0.18 FPS. These results demonstrate that directly predicting instance-level growth-point keypoints can provide compact and explicit visual references for weed-specific positioning while maintaining localization accuracy and edge-deployment efficiency.

title: Quality-consistent purification and structure-conditioned diffusion augmentation with ConvSwin feature fusion for multiclass wheat leaf disease classification
abstract: Food security and sustainable crop production are essential for meeting the demands of a growing global population. Among staple crops, wheat is the second most consumed grain worldwide, and its sustainable production is essential for global food demand. The production of wheat is significantly influenced by foliar diseases, which may lead to lower yields of the crop, hence impacting sustainable production. Therefore, this work focuses on the classification of nine major wheat leaf diseases and one healthy leaf class. The multiclass nature of the problem is challenging, as several disease classes exhibit high visual similarity with only minor distinguishing features. A diffusion-augmented ConvSwin Feature Fusion framework is developed for ten-class wheat leaf disease classification. The architecture fine-tunes a pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone and refines its spatial feature representation using a lightweight two-block Swin-style self-attention module before MLP-based feature fusion. The dataset comprised 10,641 images, of which 1,000 original images were reserved for validation and another 1,000 for testing. Of the remaining 8,641 training images, 5,839 were retained after the complete VQC-PS purification process. The purified training subset had a maximum class-count ratio of approximately 3.59:1 and was subsequently standardized to 1,000 images per class using structure-conditioned diffusion synthesis and controlled downsampling. The resulting VQC-PS ConvSwin-FF framework combines quality-aware training-data preparation, diffusion-based class balancing, convolutional feature extraction, transformer-based spatial refinement, and MLP-based feature fusion within a unified classification pipeline. The results are further interpreted using XAI-based techniques to enhance model transparency. Across five independent runs, the proposed framework achieved a mean test accuracy of 93.40 ± 1.25% and a macro-F1 score of 93.24 ± 1.39%, with the best run attaining 94.50% accuracy. These results indicate consistent performance across different random initializations and competitive performance relative to the evaluated baseline architectures under the adopted experimental protocol.

title: A complementary two-resolution assessment of ratoon rice suitability using agroclimatic predictors and satellite embeddings in central and southern China
abstract: Ratoon rice can increase annual rice production, but regional agroclimatic conditions and local landscape heterogeneity complicate suitability assessment. We developed a complementary two-resolution framework for central and southern China. Phase I used 1 km maximum entropy (MaxEnt) models combining 1981–2010 climate normals, terrain, soil, and seasonal thermal-exposure proxies under alternative early- and late-window scenarios. Phase II independently used the 2024 Google Satellite Embedding V1 Annual product at 30 m, comparing random forest (RF) feature selection with principal component analysis (PCA). Fully nested four-fold spatial validation confined feature adaptation, screening, and tuning to outer-training data, using 618 occurrences and 9,937 background points. Topography had the greatest permutation importance, while climatic associations differed between seasonal windows. The two 1 km baselines averaged an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.685, a continuous Boyce index (CBI) of 0.877, and an omission rate at the 10th-percentile training-presence threshold (OR10) of 0.147. PCA achieved AUC = 0.829, CBI = 0.912, and OR10 = 0.113; RF achieved AUC = 0.828, CBI = 0.929, and OR10 = 0.109. The embedding pathways showed similar discrimination, with RF providing numerically stronger ranking consistency and omission control. Historical agroclimatic baselines and contemporary satellite representations provide complementary spatial evidence. The 30 m embedding models outperformed the tested 1 km environmental baselines, but their latent dimensions do not measure crop physiology. Temporal mismatch among occurrence records, climate normals, and 2024 imagery limits inference about current cultivation and extreme-weather exposure. The maps support field-survey prioritization rather than estimates of planted area, yield, profitability, or expansion capacity.

title: Compactness-aware proposal refinement for foundation model-assisted maize instance annotation in complex field environments
abstract: Instance segmentation in complex field scenes depends on accurate pixel-level labels, but tracing every plant is slow and limits the scale of agricultural vision datasets. We examined a less studied source of error in automated annotation: the spatial uncertainty of open-vocabulary detection boxes used as prompts for a foundation segmentation model. The resulting workflow combines Grounding DINO, Compactness-Aware Proposal Refinement (CAPR), SAM2, and manual refinement. Experiments used 695 field images with 6,269 manually annotated maize instances. Among 4,680 valid proposal-GT-mask triplets, Proposal Box IoU was positively associated with SAM2 Mask IoU (Spearman rho = 0.380, p< 0.001). Within 239 non-duplicated GT-level pairs, the better-localized proposal also produced the better mask in 234 cases (97.9%), with a mean Mask IoU difference of 8.86 percentage points. A controlled perturbation analysis using one maize instance from each of the 695 images further showed that box expansion and contraction produced opposite Precision–Recall responses, confirming the sensitivity of SAM2 output to box-prompt geometry. CAPR re-ranks locally overlapping proposals by combining detection confidence with relative compactness. Of 69 valid cases in which CAPR and Standard NMS selected different proposals for the same GT instance, CAPR chose the box with higher IoU in 65 (94.2%) and the linked SAM2 mask with higher IoU in 63 (91.3%). YOLO26n-seg trained on CAPR + SAM2 labels reached 81.10% Mask mAP50 and 43.52% Mask mAP50–95. Manual refinement increased these values to 91.94% and 52.93%, close to 93.16% and 53.84% with Manual GT. In a single-annotator comparison, human operation time fell from 275 to 85 s per image, a reduction of 69.09% and a 3.24-fold increase in annotation throughput per unit of human time. Proposal geometry influences the quality of SAM2 prompts for seedling maize. Combining selective proposal refinement with human review reduced annotation effort and retained much of the downstream training value of Manual GT.

title: Temporal instability of genotype adaptation limits environment targeting in dryland foxtail millet production systems
abstract: Genotype adaptation in dryland cropping systems is frequently challenged by environmental variability across both space and time. However, whether geographically defined testing environments provide repeatable information for genotype selection remains poorly understood. We evaluated grain yield adaptation of foxtail millet (Setaria italica (L.) P. Beauv.) using replicated trials conducted at 20 locations across northern China during two growing seasons (2023–2024). A connected panel of 13 common genotypes evaluated across 40 site-year environments (1,560 plot observations) was used to quantify repeatable and non-static genotype-by-environment interactions (G×E). Heterogeneous-residual mixed models, reduced-rank covariance modelling, and environmental characterization were applied. Genotype-related variation was mainly attributable to genotype × location × year (50.3%), genotype × location (34.6%), and genotype × year (15.1%) interactions, with these percentages representing components of genotype-related rather than total phenotypic variance. The mean pairwise genotypic correlation across the 40 site-year environments was 0.037, and 48.7% of correlations were negative. The mean same-location cross-year genotypic correlation was only 0.027, with negative correlations at 12 of the 20 locations. Long-term climatic characteristics, soil properties, and seasonal anomalies showed limited correspondence with latent genotype-response dimensions. Genotypes differed in their environmental responsiveness despite relatively stable rankings for broad performance. These results indicate substantial season-specific genotype responses and limited evidence for consistently transferable location-specific selection information within the sampled two-year network. Multi-year testing and environmentally representative sampling are therefore important for improving genotype selection and deployment in variable dryland production systems.

title: Low-carbon city pilot policy, carbon emission reduction effect of agricultural inputs, and transmission pathways: evidence from a quasi-natural experiment at the prefecture level in China based on multi-period DID
abstract: Low-carbon city pilot policies constitute an important institutional practice for advancing the green and low-carbon transition of agriculture and achieving the “Dual-Carbon” goals. Scientific assessment of the agricultural emission-reduction effects of this policy is critical for land and food security. Based on prefecture-level panel data of China spanning 2005–2024, this paper adopts a multi-period staggered Difference-in-Differences (DID) model to systematically examine the impacts of low-carbon city pilot policies on carbon emissions associated with agricultural inputs, and provides associational evidence on the transmission mechanisms. Given that the conventional two-way fixed-effect multi-period DID may yield potential bias under strong heterogeneity, this study further employs the Callaway-Sant’Anna staggered DID (CS-DID) to estimate the dynamic treatment effects for different cohorts. Multiple robustness strategies including PSM and placebo tests are also applied to validate regression results and improve the credibility of causal inference. The study finds that low-carbon city pilot policies significantly reduce regional Agricultural input-related carbon emissions mainly through three pathways: optimizing agricultural factor allocation, forcing the low-carbon transformation of agricultural industrial structure, and improving agricultural energy-use efficiency. Heterogeneity exists in policy effects: western cities achieve the strongest emission-reduction outcomes, provincial-capital cities show substantially stronger carbon-mitigation effects than ordinary prefecture-level cities (significant only at the 10% level in the heterogeneity test), and cities included in the pilot program at an earlier stage deliver greater carbon-reduction efforts for agriculture. This paper effectively identifies the net agricultural emission reduction effect of the progressive low-carbon policy, supplements empirical evidence on the governance of agricultural non-point source carbon emissions by low-carbon policies, and provides empirical support and decision-making references by region and city administrative level for the national low-carbon transformation of agriculture and the optimization and implementation of differentiated low-carbon policies.

title: How does building climate-resilient cities affect food production: evidence from pilot policies in China
abstract: Ensuring food security is a crucial foundation for macroeconomic stability and social welfare. Against the backdrop of intensifying climate change, frequent extreme weather events, and rising uncertainty in agricultural production, identifying systematic and forward-looking adaptation pathways has become increasingly important. This paper examines whether the Climate-Resilient Cities Policy (CRCP) is associated with changes in the spillover effects of food production at the city level in China. Using city-level panel data from China for 2005–2024, the study treats the rollout of the pilot policy as a quasi-natural experiment and employs a multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) framework to estimate the policy’s impact on per capita food production. The results indicate that CRCP is positively associated with increases in per capita grain production in pilot areas, and this finding remains robust after parallel trends tests, placebo tests, PSM-DID estimates, substitution of dependent variables, and control for contemporaneous policies. Mechanism tests suggest that the policy may operate by enhancing agricultural technological innovation, expanding new digital infrastructure, and improving traditional infrastructure conditions. Since these channel analyses are primarily based on city-level indicators rather than direct household-level evidence of intermediation, the findings should be interpreted as potential mechanisms rather than a complete decomposition of causal pathways. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the policy effects are stronger in prefecture-level cities along the Hu Huanyong Line and in resource-based cities. This paper provides new evidence on the cross-sectoral benefits of urban climate adaptation policies and offers policy implications for integrating climate governance, urban resilience, and food security.

title: Regional Crop Diversity and Crop-Specific Productivity Following Wildfire Exposure: Evidence from Portuguese Agricultural Regions
abstract: Crop diversification is widely proposed as a resilience strategy, but whether regional crop diversity buffers crop-specific productivity after wildfire exposure remains uncertain. This study examines seven Portuguese agricultural regions using exposure years 2012–2024 and crop-specific productivity at t + 1. The primary sample comprises 972 Region × Crop × Year observations nested in 91 Region × Year cells. Pre-fire diversity is measured by a one-year-lagged Shannon index based on 11 crop groups. Models include Region × Crop and Year fixed effects, a lagged crop-area control, and few-cluster inference based on null-imposed wild cluster restricted bootstrap tests with Webb weights. Neither wildfire exposure nor crop diversity shows a statistically supported main association with subsequent productivity. The wildfire × diversity interaction is positive but unsupported at t + 1 (β = 0.0931; p = 0.491), t + 2 (β = 0.0623; p = 0.699), and t + 3 (β = 0.0348; p = 0.778). The interaction changes sign in a supplementary region-specific linear-trend specification (β = −0.0410), indicating sensitivity to regional trajectories; none of the preferred hypothesis tests support the proposed buffering mechanism. The results do not establish regional crop diversity as a wildfire-specific buffer for crop-specific productivity in this design, while remaining consistent with potential diversification benefits for other outcomes and spatial scales.

title: Comparison of Time-Series Encoding Methods for Rice Crop System Mapping Using Sentinel-2 EVI Time Series and Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Rice is one of the world’s most important staple crops, sustaining food security and rural livelihoods across many tropical countries. Accurate mapping of rice crop systems is therefore essential for monitoring agricultural production, supporting irrigation management, and assessing seasonal cultivation patterns. Reliable discrimination between crop systems depends not only on the quality of satellite observations but also on the time-series representation’s ability to preserve crop phenological characteristics. This study compares representative image encodings for rice crop system classification using Sentinel-2 Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) time series over Suphan Buri province, Thailand. The EVI profiles were reconstructed into daily observations using a Savitzky–Golay filter and encoded as images by the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), Synchrosqueezing Transform (SST), Gramian Angular Field (GAF), Markov Transition Field (MTF), Recurrence Plot (RP), and Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), with the unencoded one-dimensional (1D) series as the baseline. To ensure a fair comparison, all representations were classified using the same convolutional neural network architecture and identical training samples, and evaluated on 200 independent ground truth points (with 50 samples per class). Overall accuracy ranged from 0.788 to 0.899 across the seven representations. STFT was the most accurate at 0.899, followed by CWT at 0.871, with a statistically significant difference between them. Confusion between the two most intensive systems accounted for about seven-tenths of the difference in accuracy between the best encoding and the baseline. Encoding alone was insufficient, since CWT did not significantly exceed the baseline, and SST, RP, GAF, and MTF fell below it. Encodings that preserve the interval between growth cycles are therefore preferable when classes are defined by cycle count rather than by signal amplitude.

title: Phenology-Aligned Pineapple Mapping Using Dynamic Temporal Windows from Sentinel-2 Time Series
abstract: Pineapple is an economically important tropical fruit crop that contributes substantially to agricultural production, international trade, and rural livelihoods in tropical regions. Pineapple can be planted throughout the year under favorable climatic conditions, resulting in strong phenological asynchrony among fields and reducing the effectiveness of conventional fixed-window classification. To address this challenge, this study proposes a phenology-guided dynamic temporal window approach for pineapple mapping using Sentinel-2 time-series observations. A continuous normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) time series was reconstructed to identify the start of the growing season (SOS) for individual fields, which was then used as a temporal reference to define a key phenological window 12–14 months after the SOS, corresponding to the inflorescence emergence and flowering stages. Nine multispectral bands and seven vegetation indices within this window were summarized and used to train a random forest classifier. Experiments in Xuwen County, China, showed that the proposed method achieved an overall accuracy of 91.67% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.8329, with pineapple producer’s accuracy, user’s accuracy, and F1-score of 90.44%, 92.04%, and 91.23%, respectively. Compared with a conventional fixed-window approach, overall accuracy increased from 85.83% to 91.67%, demonstrating the benefit of phenological alignment. Shortwave-infrared bands and moisture-related indices contributed most strongly to classification. Regional application produced a pineapple distribution map broadly consistent with known planting patterns. These results demonstrate that aligning asynchronously planted fields to comparable phenological stages can improve spectral feature consistency and support accurate regional pineapple mapping.

title: Crop Yield Responses to No-Tillage Versus Rotary Tillage Across China: Drivers and Spatial Heterogeneity
abstract: Rotary tillage (RT) is the predominant soil management practice in China’s croplands, but long-term intensive use may compromise soil structure. No-tillage (NT) is promoted as an alternative, yet whether it maintains productivity relative to RT is uncertain. We synthesized 383 paired NT–RT comparisons from 94 publications across China with a multilevel meta-analysis clustered by publication. Relative to RT, NT reduced grain yield by 4.28% (95% CI −6.13% to −2.39%), an estimate that remained between −3.90% and −4.94% across six weighting and aggregation schemes. The reduction was associated with a 5.22% decline in spike number, partly offset by a small and non-significant increase in grain number per spike (+2.17%). Bulk density increased by 3.44%, whereas soil organic carbon (+4.62%) and total nitrogen (+3.45%) did not change significantly. Nitrogen application rate, available potassium and NT duration carried the highest cumulative Akaike weights and were the dominant predictors of yield responses. Structural equation modelling indicated that increased bulk density was negatively associated with 1000-grain weight (β = −0.21), whereas nutrient status was positively associated with grain filling (β = 0.92); these are associations, not identified causal mechanisms. Machine learning was integrated with georeferenced soil and climate data to conduct national-scale spatial prediction of crop-yield responses to NT relative to RT. Across the six major agricultural regions, the predicted yield response to NT relative to RT for all crops was least negative in Northeast China (−0.88%) and most negative in North China (−4.02%).The resulting spatial predictions revealed substantial crop-specific and regional variation in yield responses across China’s croplands. NT therefore carries a consistent, context-dependent yield cost in China, and soil physical degradation accompanies rather than offsets it.

title: Crop-Season-Matched Climate Risks to Wheat and Maize Production in Henan Province, China: Evidence from a 29-Year Two-Way Fixed-Effects Panel
abstract: Aligning climate exposures with crop calendars is essential for credible climate-risk assessment in double-cropping systems. We quantified crop-season-matched precipitation and temperature effects on wheat and maize yields across 18 cities in Henan Province, China’s leading grain province, using a balanced panel of 522 city-year observations (1996–2024) and two-way fixed-effects models. Because winter wheat is harvested in early June and summer maize is sown in late June, wheat is modelled only against spring (March–May) climate and maize only against summer (June–August) climate. Spring precipitation significantly reduced wheat yield (elasticity −0.0299), and spring warming was associated with lower yield by 3.4% per °C once trends and province-wide shocks were removed; the apparent positive raw temperature correlation (+0.283) proved artefactual. Summer climate effects on maize were insignificant at the seasonal scale, consistent with irrigation buffering, but July heat and August rainfall revealed emerging vulnerabilities. Three documented extremes—2003 summer flood, July 2021 extreme rainfall, and 2023 harvest rain—were consistent with the panel mechanisms, with city-level yields falling 52–70%, up to 64%, and 11–16% below trend, respectively. K-means clustering identified three agro-climatic zones (robust to excluding yield variables), supporting spatially differentiated adaptation. Sensitivity analyses confirm that results hold when the wheat window is extended to March–June or when growing degree days replace mean temperature. Climate-risk assessment must be crop-, season-, and zone-specific.

title: Virus-Induced Plant Genome Editing: Four Delivery Architectures and Their Trade-Offs
abstract: Plant genome editing has been limited by the difficulty of delivering CRISPR (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats) reagents to germline-competent cells without stable transgene integration. Viral vectors address this by exploiting endogenous replication, cell-to-cell movement and phloem transport, but cargo capacity and germline access have so far traded against each other. We classify virus-induced genome editing (VIGE) systems along two binary design choices: whether the vector itself encodes the nuclease and whether an engineered mobility mechanism carries the editing reagents to the germline. These two axes define four delivery architectures: (a) guide-only without a mobility element, in which guides are delivered into a nuclease-expressing host; (b) guide-only with a mobile RNA element that carries the guide into meristematic cells, yielding heritable edits without tissue culture; (c) nuclease-encoding without a route to the germline, achieved by shrinking the nuclease or enlarging the vector; and (d) nuclease-encoding with a mobility element, reaching the germline directly. We evaluate all four architectures against three persistent constraints. These are off-target risks from viral amplification of the editing reagents, the host range of the available vectors, and the gap between model-system demonstrations and breeding pipelines. Finally, we propose that combining engineered compact nucleases, mobile RNA signals, and morphogenic regulators could enable a single-vector pipeline for producing edited seeds. This would extend genome editing to refractory crop species and reduce reliance on tissue-culture-based transformation.

title: High-Dimensional Memristive Hyperchaos and RNA Rule Chains for Robust Color Image Encryption
abstract: This article presents a novel six-dimensional (6D) ideal flux-controlled memristive hyperchaotic system and its application to secure color image encryption. The proposed system extends a five-dimensional hyperchaotic system by incorporating a cosine-type memductance into its dynamics. Numerical simulations show that the proposed 6D memristive system substantially reduces the severe amplitude disparity present in the original system. Equilibrium and dissipativity analyses establish the system’s mathematical foundation, while phase portraits, Poincaré sections, and Lyapunov exponent spectra confirm its hyperchaotic dynamics. Furthermore, the system exhibits greater dynamical complexity, achieving a Lyapunov dimension of 4.2824, which exceeds that of the base model and other selected comparison systems. Based on these properties, a plaintext-dependent color image encryption scheme is developed using the SHA-512 hash of the full plaintext byte sequence, a 512-bit external secret key, and six secret offset parameters to generate sensitive initial conditions. The algorithm combines a 3D chaotic rule-chain RNA scrambling mechanism with adaptive RNA diffusion incorporating pixel-wise feedback. Evaluations demonstrate near-ideal entropy, near-zero adjacent-pixel correlations, NPCR and UACI values close to theoretical ideals, and exact lossless decryption. The scheme achieves a nominal key space of 2830, passes NIST SP 800-22 tests, and successfully resists chosen-plaintext and known-plaintext attacks. Furthermore, cropping and noise experiments demonstrate robustness against data loss and transmission corruption. Ultimately, the proposed memristive hyperchaotic system and its associated encryption scheme offer a promising solution for secure color image communication.

title: Soil Microbiome Restructuring Associated with Potassium Conversion Following Compound Bacillus Biofertilizer Application Under Continuous Cropping of Tomato
abstract: Greenhouse tomato continuous cropping obstacles stem primarily from soil microecological imbalance and potassium fixation. While K-solubilizing bacteria are widely studied, how compound Bacillus biofertilizer drives cascading K bioactivation and absolute microbial community shifts under long-term protected tomato cropping remains unclear. Using spike-in absolute quantitative sequencing, this study offers novel insights into the linkage between compound Bacillus biofertilizer-driven microbial restructuring and soil K availability. A field trial was conducted in a 27-year continuous tomato cropping system with three fertilizer doses (0, 300, and 500 L/mu). We measured soil physicochemical properties, microbial community composition and metabolism, and root architecture and fruit yield and explored hypothesized path relationships to associate yield- and fruit-quality traits with soil K availability and root traits. The biofertilizer was associated with increased available K consistent with bioactivation rather than expanding the total K pool. At 500 L/mu, available K and microbial biomass K increased by 1383.96 mg/kg and 127.17 mg/kg, respectively, with unchanged total K, confirming that this pattern is consistent with activation of native potassium reserves. Soil macroaggregate content and stability improved with dose; the 500 L/mu treatment increased estimated bacterial 16S rRNA gene abundance by 21.6%, enriched putative beneficial taxa (Sphingomonas, Paenibacillus) and reduced Fusarium abundance. Potassium-solubilizing taxa were coupled with TCA cycle and organic acid synthesis. Single-fruit weight rose from 140.00 to 272.00 g. Structural equation modeling supported a hypothesized indirect yield-associated cascade: soil improvement → K transformation → root growth → yield. Compound Bacillus biofertilizer is consistent with a multi-level cascading regulation framework, providing a promising green strategy for mitigating continuous cropping obstacles.

title: Measurand-Aware Inter-Platform Consistency Assessment of GOES Land Surface Temperature Harmonization
abstract: Cross-platform land surface temperature (LST) harmonization is often evaluated by agreement of individual observations, although urban analyses commonly rely on spatial differences and temporal changes. We investigated whether improving agreement in urban-core and surrounding-ring LST also improves their core–ring contrast and pre-to-post-sunset transition. Using Advanced Baseline Imager observations from Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES)-16, -17, -18, and -19 over western North American cities during 2019–2026, we evaluated five cohorts using established mean-squared-error (MSE) decomposition and cross-validated model selection at each measurand. Component root-mean-squared error (RMSE) decreased by 29.3–59.7%, whereas core–ring contrast RMSE ranged from an 11.5% reduction to a 13.1% increase. Loss of residual covariance offset 94.6–114.0% of gross variance-plus-bias gains. In the post hoc 2026 temporal evaluation of the same 75 cities used for 2025 calibration, core and ring RMSE declined by 59.7% and 56.1%, but contrast RMSE reduction was −0.14% (95% crossed city–interval bootstrap interval, −6.75% to +6.48%, with cities and intervals resampled independently). The historical 2021 evaluation likewise showed only a small, uncertain contrast improvement (2.9%; 95% interval, −4.3% to +9.8%). Calibration-based selection retained raw contrasts and transitions, while a residual interval rule withheld uncertain transition direction claims. Independent three-station radiometric comparisons assessed raw satellite products at station scale rather than the complete urban workflow. These findings demonstrate why harmonization performance should be evaluated at the derived scientific quantity, with processing decisions based on its observed cross-platform consistency.

title: PMA-SAM2: Prior-Memory Adapted Framework for Automatic Remote Sensing Water Body Extraction
abstract: SAM2 has great potential for remote sensing water body extraction due to its strong feature representation capability. However, when directly applied to the water body segmentation task, SAM2 still faces several challenges, including domain discrepancy, spectral confusion between water bodies and shadow-like objects, significant intra-class variations, and dependence on manual prompts. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the PMA-SAM2, which integrates domain prior injection, prototype memory calibration, and automatic prompt guidance for robust water body extraction. First, a Multi-level Prior Adaptation Module is designed to inject spatial geometric information and texture features into the SAM2 encoder, enabling effective alignment between general visual representations and remote sensing domain features. Then, a Prototype Memory Calibration Module is introduced to dynamically accumulate water feature prototypes under different geographical environments and imaging conditions, improving the model’s robustness to intra-class variations and inter-class spectral ambiguity. Furthermore, an Automatic Prompt Decoder is proposed to transform prototype-retrieved similarity maps into dense prompts, replacing manual prompts and enabling fully automatic water body segmentation. Experimental results on four datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior water body extraction accuracy compared with mainstream segmentation methods, verifying its strong generalization capability and scene adaptability.
