Based on these findings, a psychological intervention program was proposed to strengthen self-differentiation, promote attachment security, and develop adaptive emotion regulation skills, thereby enhancing the psychological well-being and interpersonal functioning of undergraduate nursing students.
journal: International Journal of Research Studies in Education

title: Pedon-Scale Characterization and Classification of Soils at the Teaching and Research Farm, Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, Nigeria
abstract: The Teaching and Research Farm of the Faculty of Agriculture, Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, is a source of crop trials, teaching and soil science research, but the horizon-level information of its soils is lacking. This study characterized and provisionally classified three pedons (P1, P2 and P3) selected across the farm’s soil–landscape units. The profiles were described according to the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) guidelines and samples from each horizon were analysed for physical and chemical properties. The profile depths varied from 83 to 150 cm with the A–AB–Bt field-horizon sequences. The particle-size results indicated predominantly sandy-loam textures with the reported sand contents of 572–712 g kg⁻¹ and clay contents of 108–208 g kg⁻¹. However, the reported particle-size fractions for P1 Bt2 sum to 1,060 g kg⁻¹ and need to be verified. The bulk density varied from 1.19 to 1.76 Mg m⁻³, and pH in water from 5.44 to 6.10. Available phosphorus ranged from 0.96 to 4.27 mg kg⁻¹; the reported organic carbon and total nitrogen values and units need to be confirmed against the laboratory records. Effective cation exchange capacity ranged from 3.08 to 5.33 cmol(+) kg⁻¹, while ECEC-based base saturation was 65–84%, aluminum saturation 9.2–28.3%, and exchangeable sodium percentage below 4%. The low-chroma matrices and red mottles in the lower horizons of P1 and P3 suggest periodic redox conditions. Provisionally, P1 and P3 were considered possible Hapludults (Ultisols) and Acrisols in the World Reference Base (WRB), while P2 was considered an Inceptisol and Cambisol candidate. These placements are not definitive since the diagnostic-horizon criteria and classification-specific chemical data were not fully confirmed. The findings provide pedon-scale baseline information and identify priorities for verifying the soil data and assessing the nutrient, subsoil-strength and drainage constraints.
journal: International Journal of Horticulture and Agriculture Research

title: From Symbolic Recognition to Operational Resilience: Local Knowledge, Social Transformation, and Disaster Governance in Sembalun, Indonesia
abstract: Recognising local traditions does not necessarily mean that they continue to organise disaster preparedness. This study examines how cultural knowledge, livelihood transformation, and changing information networks intersect in two communities in Sembalun, East Lombok, Indonesia. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design combines a purposive-quota survey of 106 residents in Sembalun Bumbung and Sembalun Lawang with focus group discussions, semi-structured interviews, ethnographic observation, and documentary analysis. The survey is reported descriptively; qualitative materials are interpreted thematically and integrated through cross-case comparison and joint displays. More than 60% of respondents reportedly recognised Ngayu-ayu, although only a minority articulated its social-ecological functions; approximately 40–50% understood the ecological role of the Pemangku, while more than half did not know or only vaguely recognised Nyampang. Older residents, agricultural households, and respondents in Bumbung generally reported greater functional familiarity than younger and tourism-oriented groups. Qualitative evidence associates these patterns with the ceremonialisation of customary authority, disrupted intergenerational learning, livelihood differentiation, and changing collective labour. Yet young people and tourism actors also contribute digital communication capacity. We interpret these findings through a symbolic–operational gap and propose a Sembalun Hybrid Resilience Framework linking cultural, informational, and social resources through inclusive knowledge co-production, institutional coordination, and scientifically verified warning protocols. The framework is a conceptual synthesis rather than a validated predictive model. Community resilience requires more than preserving the names of traditions: it requires credible authority, opportunities for practice, equitable participation, and connections between customary and formal disaster governance.

title: Unsupervised Clustering Enables Cohort-Specific Variant Recalibration in Crops
abstract: Trait discovery in crops require reliable marker datasets, yet variant discovery remains constrained by the lack of standardised, high-confidence reference resources. Publicly available plant genomic resources often rely on outdated reference genomes, heterogenous pipelines, and generic variant hard-filtering thresholds derived from human studies. Consequently, applying the Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) Best Practices framework, particularly machine learning-based variant quality score recalibration (VQSR), remains challenging in crops lacking suitable training resources. Here, we present an unsupervised approach for variant quality assessment and generating cohort-specific training resources, enabling integration of VQSR into established GATK workflows without predefined high-confidence training variant sets. Using Brassica napus as a model, we use the Illumina 60k Brassica SNP array to establish a reference-specific truth set for base quality score recalibration (BQSR) and independent benchmarking. Gaussian mixture model (GMM)-based clustering of multidimensional variant annotation profiles identifies high-, intermediate-, and low-quality variant classes, which provide flexible training resources without requiring labelled training data. We further validate the approach in diploid Brassica oleracea and hexaploid wheat (Triticum aestivum), representing contrasting population characteristics and genome architectures. Across all three species, GMM-based clustering consistently identifies informative quality classes and enables cohort-specific recalibration of both SNPs and insertion-deletions (INDELs). Comparison with conventional hard filtering reveals discordant pass/fail classifications for up to 46.4% of SNPs and 37.8% of INDELs across evaluated cohorts, demonstrating that the approaches capture distinct aspects of variant quality. Our results establish unsupervised variant classification as transferable strategy for generating cohort-specific VQSR resources, extending established GATK workflows to crops lacking comprehensive genomic resources.

title: Comparative cryo-EM studies reveal structural aspects of host specificity for tobamoviruses
abstract: Tobamoviruses are a group of economically important plant viruses exhibiting extreme stability and persistence. Despite high morphological similarity, they show extensive host-family specificity, induce a wide range of symptoms, and inflict significant global yield losses in fruit and vegetable crops. Composed of a rod-shaped helical assembly of identical coat proteins encasing a single-stranded RNA, tobamoviruses have long served as fundamental models for understanding helical assemblies. Here we report the cryo-EM structures of two viruses from this genus, cucumber green mottle mosaic virus (CGMMV) and tomato mottle mosaic virus (ToMMV), at 2.86 Å and 2.71 Å resolution, respectively, revealing divergent packing strategies within the virion assembly. Whereas the solanaceous-infecting ToMMV closely mirrors genetically-similar canonical tobacco mosaic virus (TMV), CGMMV employs a specialized hydrophobic packing strategy based at the solvent-exposed inner loop lining the solvent-exposed central canal. Comparative biophysical and molecular dynamics analyses from the reconstructed structures reveal more stable and compact protein packing for CGMMV at both the subunit and assembly levels. Furthermore, we identify a conserved electrostatic pentapeptide motif (residues 113–117) on the lower radial alpha helix that serves as an additional RNA-stabilizing region, harbouring a clade-defining Lys113 synapomorphy in cucurbit-infecting tobamoviruses. Together, our findings elucidate how subtle electrostatic tuning and divergent hydrophobic packing strategies drive differential virion stability and host-family adaptation within a strictly conserved helical scaffold. Significance statement Understanding how plant viruses adapt to diverse host species while maintaining physical stability is crucial for combating crop loss. Tobamoviruses are hyper-stable, rod-shaped plant viruses with highly conserved structures, yet they infect vastly different host families. By solving high-resolution cryo-EM structures of two representative tobamoviruses and comparing them with existing structural information, we show that despite near-identical overall shapes, these viruses employ distinct internal packing mechanisms and electrostatic strategies to stabilize their viral RNA. This work reveals how subtle sequence variations tune internal hydrophobic and electrostatic networks, providing fundamental insights into the evolutionary principles that allow these viruses to drive host diversification without altering their overarching structural architecture.

title: Drought Response and Recovery in Wild, Feral, and Domesticated Brassica rapa: Implications for Crop Climate Resilience
abstract: Drought poses a serious threat to agricultural production and food security. Wild relatives of crops, including pre-domesticated and feral varieties, contain genetic diversity that can serve as a breeding resource for increasing desirable crop traits such as drought resilience, but little is known about the relative ability of wild varieties to cope with climate change in most species. In this study, we investigated the drought response of wild, feral, and domesticated varieties of Brassica rapa, an important crop and model species. Twenty-five accessions were subjected to experimental drought and recovery, and variation in traits such as biomass retention, photosynthetic rate, and water use efficiency were quantified. We found several wild accessions of B. rapa had high biomass retention under drought and full recovery of maximum assimilation rate after rewatering, challenging the assumption that feralization produces stress-resilient phenotypes and suggesting that populations of wild crop progenitors are especially promising reservoirs of drought-response diversity. Our results also showed taproot biomass was positively associated with water use efficiency. Our findings provide candidate traits and genotypes for agricultural breeding aimed at increasing drought resilience in domesticated B. rapa cultivars and give insights into evolution under domestication and feralization in the context of climate change. Highlight Drought-resilient traits and genotypes were identified in wild, feral, and domesticated accessions of Brassica rapa, providing insight into evolution under domestication and feralization in the context of climate change.

title: Illuminating duckweed: hyperspectral reflectance highlights a predictive ceiling for accurate determination of biomass
abstract: Duckweed is a fast-growing aquatic plant with strong potential as a sustainable, high protein crop that can be produced without expanding agricultural land. However, substantial trait variation necessitates rapid selection proxies to identify genotypes with high growth, biomass and pigment content while simultaneously suited to low input, controlled environments. Although hyperspectral reflectance phenotyping is widely applied in conventional crops, its utility for duckweed remains unexplored. We assessed 133 UK accessions from six species grown under ambient light, quantifying growth, pigment composition, photosynthetic performance and spectral reflectance. A second panel with contrasting light tolerance strategies, including growth and photosynthetic acclimation, was used to test whether hyperspectral reflectance could detect photoprotective mechanisms associated with high light resilience. Duckweed accessions displayed extensive variation across all traits. However, vegetation indices (VIs) commonly used in arable crops demonstrated only limited predictive accuracy for total chlorophyll (R2 =0.34, p<0.005) and maximum photosystem II (PSII) quantum yield (Fv/Fm) (R2 =0.25, p<0.0001), with poor performance for other traits. Under high light, VIs moderately differentiated tolerant accessions, including those maintaining higher Fv/Fm, ΦPSII operating efficiency and carotenoid:chlorophyll ratios. Partial least squares regression (PLSR) modelling improved predictive performance, providing reliable estimates of chlorophyll content (R2 =0.5, RMSE =2.05 mg/g freeze dry weight) maximum non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) (R2 =0.5, RMSE =0.57) and NPQ efficiency of PSII (R2 =0.53, RMSE =0.04). Although predictions of biomass and growth rate remained weak, green and red edge spectral regions were strongly associated with pigment contents and photosynthesis and indirectly linked to biomass. This study provides the first comprehensive evaluation of spectral phenotyping for duckweed crop development. Our findings indicate that broad spectrum modelling approaches, integrated with other high throughput phenotyping tools, may support selection of high vigour varieties and monitoring of commercial duckweed production systems.

title: BryoCAD: Extending Plant DNA Foundation Models Beyond Flowering Plants
abstract: Bryophytes exhibit diverse genome architectures and gene repertoires, yet their functional interpretation remains constrained by incomplete genomic annotations and limited experimental resources. Although DNA foundation models offer promising solutions, their applicability to evolutionarily divergent bryophytes remains largely unexplored. Here, we introduce BryoCAD, a DNA language model developed through continued pre-training of the angiosperm-specific PlantCAD2 model on 17 bryophyte genomes spanning hornworts, liverworts, and mosses. Across three representative bryophyte genomes and four gene-boundary motif recovery tasks, BryoCAD-Small improved mean zero-shot accuracy from 45.7% to 57.0%, a 24.8% relative increase over PlantCAD2-Small, while the over 200-fold larger Evo2-20B achieved a mean accuracy of only 39.3%. Remarkably, BryoCAD-Small outperformed PlantCAD2-Large in 11 of 12 motif-recovery comparisons across the three bryophytes, highlighting the benefits of lineage-specific adaptation over model scaling alone. These improvements extended to all six tested algal species, increasing mean accuracy from 26.3% to 37.5%, although performance varied across ferns and gymnosperms. BryoCAD also enhanced gene structure annotation: replacing PlantCAD2-Small with BryoCAD-Small increased transcript-level F1 scores from 0.578 to 0.625 in Marchantia polymorpha and from 0.485 to 0.530 in Physcomitrium patens . Together, our findings demonstrate that lineage- specific continued pre-training enhances genomic sequence interpretation and gene annotation across bryophytes, providing a transferable framework for extending DNA foundation models to evolutionarily diverse, understudied plant lineages.

title: Development of an Integrated Web-Based Partnership Management Information System for PHRI Bekasi City
abstract: Professional associations require integrated information systems to improve administrative efficiency and support digital transformation. However, the Indonesian Hotel and Restaurant Association (PHRI) Bekasi City still manages membership administration, membership fee payments, organizational information dissemination, and hotel occupancy reporting through separate and predominantly manual processes, resulting in inefficient data management and delayed administrative services. This study aims to develop an integrated web-based Partnership Management Information System to streamline administrative processes and enhance organizational services. The project was governed using the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK) framework for initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, and closing, while the Waterfall model guided sequential software development. Laravel was employed as the web application framework, MySQL as the database management system, Bootstrap for the user interface, and the Midtrans payment gateway for digital membership fee transactions. Functional evaluation was conducted through User Acceptance Testing (UAT) with the PHRI Bekasi City management board, while technical performance was evaluated using Google PageSpeed Insights. The developed system successfully integrated membership management, digital membership cards, digital payment processing, organizational information management, and hotel occupancy reporting into a single platform. UAT results showed very good scores across functionality (93%), performance (92.5%), interface (91%), and efficiency (97%), while Performance Testing indicated strong results on desktop and good results on mobile devices. These findings demonstrate that the proposed system effectively supports the digital transformation of partnership management and provides a practical reference for implementing integrated information systems in similar professional organizations.
journal: Journal of Engineering Technology and Science Integration (JETSI)

title: Pengembangan Mesin Pertanian Hemat Energi untuk Mendukung Produktivitas dan Keberlanjutan Pertanian
abstract: The development of energy-efficient agricultural machinery is increasingly important for improving agricultural productivity while supporting the sustainability of agricultural systems. Conventional agricultural machinery continues to face challenges related to fuel consumption, operational costs, and environmental emissions. This study aims to examine technological developments in energy-efficient agricultural machinery, identify innovations and operational factors that support energy efficiency, and develop a conceptual framework to support agricultural productivity and sustainability. A qualitative approach was employed through a narrative-conceptual literature study using relevant scientific publications from 2020 to 2026 retrieved from Scopus and Google Scholar. The literature was analyzed descriptively, comparatively, and thematically based on four dimensions: technological innovation, energy optimization, operational performance and productivity, and environmental sustainability. The findings indicate that agricultural machinery efficiency can be supported through the optimization of conventional machinery, electrification, hybrid propulsion systems, and digital technologies for operational control and monitoring. This study proposes a conceptual framework integrating these four dimensions as a foundation for developing energy-efficient agricultural machinery. The framework is expected to provide a reference for further research and the development of more efficient, adaptive, and sustainable agricultural mechanization technologies. Empirical validation is still required to examine its applicability under different agricultural conditions.
journal: INOMATEC: Jurnal Inovasi dan Kajian Multidisipliner Kontemporer

title: Cropping Pattern Dynamics, Climatic Trends and Rice Water Use in Thiruvarur District, Tamil Nadu, India: An Economic Analysis
abstract: Rice-based agriculture in the lower Cauvery Delta is subject to climatic variability and water-management pressures. This study integrates district crop-area indices for 2013–2014 to 2023–2024, annual meteorological trend statistics, contextual vulnerability indicators, two seasonal rice-water scenarios and stochastic-frontier estimates for 120 rice farms in Thiruvarur district. The composite entropy index decreased from 0.409 to 0.118, with fluctuations and a pronounced decline in 2023–2024. A 10-state Markov matrix implies conditional stationary shares of 0.246 for cotton and 0.105 for rice, rather than observed crop substitutions. The minimum-temperature Sen slope was +0.0216 °C/year (nominal p = 0.0257), and the wind-speed slope was −0.0082 m/s/year (nominal p = 0.0020); after Holm adjustment for five tests, only wind speed remained significant at 0.05. Exposure, sensitivity and adaptive-capacity indicator means were 0.650, 0.750 and 0.475, but inconsistent score direction and absent validation preclude a district vulnerability classification. Using stated seasonal water depths, yields and nitrogen assumptions, green, blue-evapotranspiration and grey footprints were approximately 570, 593 and 205 m³/t for Kuruvai rice and 697, 558 and 212 m³/t for Samba rice. Their composite unweighted seasonal mean was 1,417 m³/t, not a measured district-wide footprint. The frontier's reported inefficiency variance fraction was 0.0031, although insufficient information is available for causal attribution. The illustrative gross-output-to-irrigation ratio was ₹10.19/m³. The findings characterise crop-area variability and conditional water-use indicators; independent validation of underlying time series and fitted models is still necessary.
journal: International Journal of Environment and Climate Change

title: Navigating relational agency in AI feedback musicianship: a diffractive dialogue
abstract: Musical AI systems behave in non-linear, dynamic ways that exceed the tool-oriented framings inherited from earlier instrument design. Existing frames of control and ensemble interaction do not articulate the entangled, relational agency that emerges when performers work with AI feedback instruments over time. We examine a duet practice with two AI-enabled feedback instruments, S\`u and Agentier, in which feedback operates at the inner level of the AI's recurrent processes and the outer loop of musical interaction between performer, instrument, and co-performer. Our work draws on agential realism and a diffractive dialogue methodology to read our independent reflections through one another across five performances, examining how agency is enacted between performers and AI instruments. We find that control and agency are relational and shift across performances; musical textures enact feedback moments of control with performers; reaching a productive feedback environment is itself a shared exploratory act; and performers maintain their instruments through funnelling and injection, developing the skill of navigating agency along a continuous spectrum. Feedback musicianship with AI instruments demands navigation of this relational agency, displacing the leading-versus-responding binary that initially framed our reflections. This work contributes a materially-grounded vocabulary for AI feedback musicianship and a model of human-AI creative collaboration in which mutual agency is worked for through practice rather than designed in.

title: A Coaxial Bioprinted Hydrogel With Semipermeable Sheath and Pro-Chondrogenic Core for Articular Cartilage Repair.
abstract: Stem cell-laden hydrogels represent a promising strategy for the functional repair of articular cartilage defects. However, the pathological joint microenvironment is often characterized by persistently elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, which severely compromise transplanted cell survival and impair their chondrogenic differentiation potential. Inspired by the hierarchical mechanical gradient of native cartilage, we developed a sheath-core biomimetic hydrogel (SCGAE) via embedded coaxial bioprinting, featuring a robust poly(ethylene glycol)-alginate (PA) sheath that spatially integrates mechanical support and immunoprotection around a soft, bioactive gelatin methacryloyl-alginate-decellularized extracellular matrix (GAE) core. The dense PA sheath provides immediate mechanical support and functions as a size-selective diffusion barrier, permitting nutrient and oxygen permeation while effectively blocking inflammatory cytokines (>40 kDa). This protective niche enables the pericellular matrix-mimicking GAE core to maintain stem cell viability >89% under pro-inflammatory conditions and support robust chondrogenic differentiation. In a rabbit osteochondral defect model, bone marrow stromal cell-laden SCGAE constructs promoted substantial cartilage repair, achieving defect filling, host integration, and regeneration of glycosaminoglycan-rich hyaline-like cartilage. This sheath-core architecture design spatially integrates structural, mechanical, and immunoprotection functions, presenting a promising platform for the regeneration of load-bearing articular cartilage.

title: EZpred: Improving Deep Learning‐Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs
abstract: Features extracted from sequence homologs significantly enhance the accuracy of deep learning‐based protein structure prediction. Indeed, homolog‐aware models such as AlphaFold generally produce more accurate protein structures compared to single sequence‐based methods like ESMfold. In contrast, features from sequence homologs are seldom employed for deep learning‐based prediction of the biological functions of a protein, such as Gene Ontology terms or Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. Although a small number of models also incorporate function labels from sequence homologs, they cannot utilize features extracted from homologs that lack function labels. To address this gap, we developed EZpred, which is the first deep learning model to use sequence homologs by extracting their sequence features while ignoring any function labels. Starting with the target sequence and homologs identified by MMseqs2, EZpred extracts sequence features using the ESM‐C protein language model. These features are then fed into a deep learning model to predict the EC numbers of the target protein. For test enzymes with < 30% sequence identity to any training proteins, the F1‐score of EZpred EC number prediction is at least 34% higher than state‐of‐the‐art EC number prediction models. These results demonstrate the strong positive impact of sequence homologs in deep learning‐based enzyme function prediction.

title: Biochemical basis of cervical remodeling in preterm and term labor revealed by Raman spectroscopy
abstract: Preterm birth (PTB), affecting approximately 15 million infants annually, is the leading cause of neonatal mortality. However, the underlying mechanisms driving preterm labor (PTL) remain poorly understood. Early detection of biomolecular changes associated with both term and PTL is critical but challenging with current methods. Here, we utilize in vivo Raman spectroscopy (RS) to non‐invasively investigate cervical remodeling in mouse models of PTL induced by inflammatory (lipopolysaccharide ‘LPS’) and hormonal (RU486) pathways, compared with term labor (TL). In vivo RS results revealed etiology‐specific biochemical differences associated with cervical remodeling. LPS‐induced PTL exhibited increased carbohydrate‐associated spectral features, whereas the RU486 model exhibited a distinct protein remodeling pattern that diverged from both LPS‐induced PTL and TL. These biochemical signatures aligned with ex vivo imaging and biomechanical assessments of collagen, elastin, and vascularity. RS differentiated PTL from TL with 86% accuracy, outperforming existing techniques. Collectively, these results demonstrate that PTL is not a single biochemical process but comprises distinct remodeling trajectories that can be detected in vivo prior to labor onset. This work establishes a translational framework for Raman‐based cervical phenotyping, supporting the future development of non‐invasive tools for early PTL detection, etiological stratification, and targeted clinical intervention, to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes.

title: The Pie Theory of Plant Breeding: A systems framework
abstract: Plant breeding has achieved remarkable success through concepts and approaches including yield‐component analysis, ideotype breeding, heterosis, genotype‐by‐environment interaction (GE), genomic selection, multi‐trait selection, and the breeder's eye. Although each illuminates an important aspect of crop improvement, these concepts are often considered separately. This article proposes the “Pie Theory of Plant Breeding” as a systems framework that integrates established and emerging breeding concepts within a common perspective of optimization, expansion, prediction, adaptation, and validation. Optimization seeks the best‐performing combination of competing traits within available biological capacity, whereas expansion shifts the biological boundary and enlarges the space of possibilities available for subsequent optimization. The two processes are interdependent: expansion creates new opportunities for optimization, while optimization realizes the value of expansion and reveals constraints that may require further expansion. Within this framework, competing traits determine how biological capacity is converted into cultivar value, whereas enabling genes, gene combinations, traits, and environmental inputs create, preserve, protect, or expand that capacity. The framework applies across pure‐line and hybrid breeding: parent selection creates possibilities through merit and complementation, while heterozygosity expands the range of selectable genetic states without necessarily guaranteeing heterosis. The breeder's eye and genomic selection are interpreted as complementary G + GE (GGE)‐based prediction systems operating on different sources of information, while formal multi‐location, multi‐year, and multi‐trait GGE integration validates whether predicted optimization and expansion have translated into adaptation and agricultural value. Plant breeding is therefore viewed as a recursive process in which biological possibilities are created, optimized, predicted, filtered, and ultimately validated through whole‐system performance.

title: Choroid plexus biomarkers capture neuroinflammatory processes associated with amyloid and neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease
abstract: INTRODUCTION The amyloid/tau/neurodegeneration (ATN) framework characterizes Alzheimer's disease (AD) biomarkers but does not fully capture neuroinflammation. The choroid plexus (CP), a critical blood–cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) barrier component, has emerged as a neuroinflammatory imaging marker whose relationship to established AD biomarkers remains unclear. METHODS We analyzed multimodal data from 641 Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative participants using magnetic resonance imaging, amyloid/tau positron emission tomography, CSF/plasma biomarkers, and cognitive measures. Associations were examined via correlations, amyloid‐stratified analyses, and structural equation modeling (SEM). RESULTS CP volume was consistently associated with hippocampal atrophy but did not differentiate amyloid‐positive from amyloid‐negative individuals. Plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein showed the strongest association with CP volume, particularly in amyloid‐positive participants. SEM linked CP volume and entorhinal tau to hippocampal atrophy, with amyloid contributing indirectly through tau. DISCUSSION CP volume reflects neuroinflammatory processes more closely tied to neurodegeneration than to amyloid or tau pathology, supporting its role as a complementary biomarker within the ATN framework.
journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia : Diagnosis, Assessment & Disease Monitoring

title: Crop‐light constrained circular‐energy optimization of a semitransparent photovoltaic greenhouse
abstract: Greenhouse cultivation faces the fundamental challenge of balancing energy supply, crop growth requirements, and environmental sustainability within a single production system. This study develops a deterministic linear optimization model that simultaneously coordinates photovoltaic generation, heat pumping, electrical and thermal storage, supplemental lighting, drainage reuse, reverse osmosis, freshwater consumption, sodium quality, greenhouse gas emissions, and nutrient discharge in a 1000 m 2 semitransparent photovoltaic tomato greenhouse located in Çanakkale, Türkiye. The model is formulated as a multi‐objective ε‐constraint problem with 10,620 continuous decision variables, solved over 366 days divided into day and night periods, and evaluated across twelve scenarios, including reference, cost‐optimal, environmentally constrained, and technology‐ablation cases. A balanced solution based on the case‐study weather data achieved simultaneous reductions of 20% in greenhouse gas emissions, 25% in freshwater use, and 96% in nitrogen and phosphorus discharges, with only a 0.74% increase in annual cost compared with the fossil fuel‐based reference system. This solution selected 418.40 kWp of photovoltaic capacity, 502.99 kW th of heat pump capacity, 2.13 MWh of thermal storage capacity, and 2.90 m 3 /d of reverse osmosis capacity, while setting the battery capacity to 0. The results demonstrated that crop‐light and water‐quality constraints materially affect renewable energy design; carbon‐only optimization fails to deliver comparable improvements in water and nutrient quality; removing thermal storage increases costs by 3.58%; and removing photovoltaic, heat pump, or reverse osmosis renders the joint environmental targets infeasible. The model developed in this study provides a reproducible pre‐feasibility framework for integrated greenhouse energy‐water‐environment management.

title: A Homozygous FOXA1 Variant Links Choreoathetosis, Bronchiectasis, and Anorectal-Axial Anomalies.
abstract: BACKGROUND FOXA1 encodes a forkhead-box pioneer transcription factor involved in chromatin accessibility, epithelial and endodermal lineage specification, pulmonary epithelial differentiation, and selected neurodevelopmental programs. Although somatic FOXA1 alterations are well recognized in cancer, a germline FOXA1-associated Mendelian disorder has not been defined. OBJECTIVES To delineate the clinical and genetic features of a syndromic neuropulmonary phenotype associated with a homozygous FOXA1 variant. METHODS We evaluated three affected individuals from an extended consanguineous Turkish family with childhood-onset action-induced hyperkinetic/choreoathetoid movement disorder, bronchiectatic lung disease, anorectal abnormalities, axial skeletal defects, and neurobehavioral features. Whole-exome sequencing with copy-number variant analysis, homozygosity mapping, and segregation analysis were performed. RESULTS Exome-based analysis did not identify diagnostic variants in known disease genes relevant to the combined neurological, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, and skeletal phenotype. Homozygosity mapping identified a 16.8-Mb shared homozygous interval on chromosome 14 encompassing FOXA1. All three affected individuals carried the same homozygous FOXA1 c.623G>C, p.(Arg208Pro) variant, which segregated with the phenotype under an autosomal recessive model. The variant affects a conserved residue within the DNA-binding forkhead domain and was absent in the homozygous state from population databases. The clinical pattern partially overlaps with NKX2-1-related brain-lung disease but appears distinct, with preserved thyroid function and prominent bronchiectatic airway, anorectal, and axial skeletal involvement. CONCLUSION These findings support FOXA1 as a plausible candidate disease gene for an emerging autosomal recessive syndromic neuropulmonary disorder with anorectal and axial skeletal involvement. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.
journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society

title: TaPYL-mediated chemical activation of ABA signaling in wheat enhances water productivity and reinforces carbohydrate reserves
abstract: Chemical activation of ABA signaling via synthetic agonists provides a reversible, high-precision strategy to optimize wheat water-use efficiency by coupling persistent antitranspirant effects with the metabolic reinforcement of carbohydrate reserves. The phytohormone abscisic acid (ABA) and its PYR/PYL/RCAR receptors are central targets for improving crop drought tolerance. In hexaploid wheat (Triticum aestivum), the actual number of ABA receptors (TaPYLs) has been a matter of debate, ranging from 26 to 38. This study refines this classification, demonstrating that 12 putative TaPYLs belong to the Bet v/START/Polyketide cyclase superfamily, but lack key structural features of functional ABA receptors. Indeed, structural and bioinformatic analyses confirm that their ligand-binding cavities cannot accommodate ABA and lack key residues for ABA binding. As a result, whereas TaPYL1, TaPYL4, and TaPYL6 mediate ABA-dependent inhibition of PP2Cs, the TraesCS3B02G160200 putative receptor does not. Therefore, wheat has only 26 potential TaPYL ABA receptors. Given the biotechnological potential of the ABA pathway, we investigated its chemical activation using the synthetic receptor agonist iSB09. This compound is perceived by highly expressed TaPYLs and induces a more persistent antitranspirant effect than exogenous ABA. Plants treated with iSB09 consumed approximately 25% less water over 15 days without incurring a biomass penalty, resulting in significantly higher water productivity. Beyond regulating transpiration, agonist treatment increased fructan and starch levels compared with controls. A short-term RNA-seq experiment revealed that ABA treatment triggers a coordinated reprogramming of carbohydrate metabolism genes, including the upregulation of genes involved in the biosynthesis of protective osmolytes (fructans and raffinose) and starch, coupled with the downregulation of genes involved in starch mobilization. In summary, this work provides a clarified census of the wheat TaPYL family, establishes chemical activation of ABA signaling as an effective strategy to boost water-use efficiency, and suggests that the reinforcement of reserve and protective carbohydrate pathways is a key metabolic mechanism linked to ABA signaling.

title: Mapping the potential harvestable productivity of wild edible mushrooms by integrating expert knowledge and forest inventory data
abstract: Wild edible mushrooms are valuable non-wood forest products with ecological, cultural and economic relevance, but their integration into forest resource assessment and planning is constrained by scarce large-scale productivity data. We developed a spatially explicit, expert-based framework to estimate and map the potential harvestable productivity of socio-economically important edible mushroom taxa under favourable fruiting conditions. Using Aragón, Spain, as a case study, we modelled 15 target taxa in Spanish Forest Map units characterized by habitat class, stand structure, edaphic substrate, and topography. In two independent elicitation sessions, 30 experienced mushroom pickers estimated habitat-specific productivity, harvesting-effort parameters and taxon-specific correction coefficients. These estimates were converted into annualized estimates of potential harvestable productivity using taxon-specific peak-week production fractions informed by historical production patterns. The model revealed strong taxon–habitat differentiation and spatial heterogeneity, with the highest values concentrated in Pyrenean forests and the Iberian System. Model-estimated regional potential harvestable production under favourable conditions was 15,940 t·yr⁻¹; Lactarius group deliciosus (42.2%), Morchella sp. (17.4%) and the Boletus edulis commercial group (12.2%) jointly accounted for 71.8%, while all remaining taxa accounted for 28.2%. The framework provides an operational approach for mapping the potential harvestable productivity of wild mushrooms in data-limited regions and supporting forest resource assessment, multifunctional forest planning, sustainable harvesting, and mycotourism.

The qualitative TOL: integrating trees, networks, and organismal biology
abstract: The tree of life (TOL) was, for almost 150 years, conceived as the representation of the history of life. Since the discovery of lateral gene transfer (LGT) and its relevant evolutionary implications, the TOL has been questioned as a correct representation and several researchers have proposed networks of life as a suitable replacement. Nevertheless, these depictions pose important epistemological problems, such as historicity and resolutions levels. This paper problematizes on such subject and sustains that both representations, the TOL and networks, necessarily collide and correspond to different types of inheritance that require distinct levels of resolution. I argue in favor of doing such a differentiation for understanding and modeling diverse biological processes. I analyze here different representations of the history of life, their meanings, and several inherent problems to some of them. Substituting the TOL by networks of life as the correct representations, or sustaining the TOL notwithstanding the amount of LGT evidence, obliterates important data. This paper proposes a qualitative TOL, a TOL produced by core and essential genes and organismic information, that serves as a necessary scaffolding for anchoring LGT networks and pivotal for providing a historical dimension in our representations. An important part of the paper is the historical parameter of the different representations. An argument about why networks without the TOL fail to retrieve historicity is made. Finally, the qualitative TOL serves as a tool that gives orientation through the entangled data in order to understand the webbed history of life.

title: Grapevine red blotch disease: a temperate pathosystem and its relevance to tropical and subtropical viticulture

Comparative effectiveness of soil and foliar application of different silicon sources on wheat productivity in coastal soils of the Ganges delta
abstract: Silicon (Si) has emerged as a beneficial nutrient element for increasing crop resilience under various stresses; however, limited information is available regarding the comparative performance of different application methods and sources for wheat production in coastal areas of the Ganges delta. A field experiment was conducted during two consecutive winter seasons of 2024–25 and 2025–26 in Patuakhali district of Bangladesh, to examine the effects of different Si sources and application methods on growth, yield, Si uptake and economic performance of wheat in coastal soil. The experiment was laid out in a randomized complete block design with three replications comprising seven treatments: control, soil application of calcium (Ca) silicate, sodium (Na) meta-silicate, and Si dioxide (80 kg Si ha−1), and foliar spraying in the morning four times of the same sources as 0.3% Si solution (total 30 kg Si ha−1). Data were statistically analysed following two-way ANOVA model where year and Si treatments were the factors. Si supplementation significantly increased plant height, tillers m−2, spike length, grains spike−1, 1000 grain weight, grain yield, straw yield, straw Si content and straw Si uptake. Among treatments, foliar Si dioxide provided the highest grain yield (4.47 t ha−1), representing a 21.8% increase over control (3.67 t ha−1) which was statistically similar with foliar Na meta-silicate (4.21 t ha−1) and soil applied Si dioxide (4.17 t ha−1). Foliar Si dioxide also resulted in the highest grains spike−1 (31.9) and straw yield (5.99 t ha−1). The Si uptake efficiency and economic efficiency (MBCR) of foliar applied Si was much better than the soil application, and among the sources Si dioxide was the greatest. Overall, the results endorse that Si dioxide both in foliar spray or soil application was the best-performing treatment under tested single-site conditions and requires multi-location validation.

Minds, machines, and medicine: AI technologies across health domains.
abstract: Patients' psychological responses to artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare depend on the functions it performs and how they interpret its assistance. This review examines how four forms of AI may engage different psychological mechanisms across physical, mental, and social health. Generative AI may facilitate cognitive offloading and foster perceived responsiveness, but risks leaving patients vulnerable to unsound medical advice or emotional isolation. Predictive AI engages risk appraisal and can validate or destabilize patients' health beliefs, while anticipated stigma may paradoxically discourage engagement with predictive AI. Agentic AI holds the potential to restore perceived control over poorly coordinated care; however, patients' sense of agency may erode when they are excluded from consequential decisions, and attributions of responsibility following AI failures risk undermining trust in both the AI system and clinical oversight. Embodied AI supports self-efficacy through guided practice in physical rehabilitation, but attributing success to the robot rather than oneself can impede independent functioning, while anthropomorphism may generate unexpected relational obligations. Across these forms of AI, uniqueness neglect and subjective understanding emerge as cross-cutting mechanisms that shape acceptance. We argue that the psychological viability of medical AI hinges not merely on technical performance, but on how assistance is interpreted, and we outline critical directions for future research.

Forecasting hourly size-resolved ambient ultrafine particles with size-specific historical windows.
abstract: Ultrafine particles (UFPs; diameter ≤100 nm) vary rapidly in number concentration, but the history length associated with the lowest hourly prediction error may differ among particle sizes. We measured eight nominal size bins (10, 14, 19, 27, 37, 52, 72, and 100 nm) using a Mini-Wide-Range Aerosol Spectrometer (Mini-WRAS) at an urban site in Shenzhen, China (September 2023-June 2025), obtaining 8,982 quality-controlled hourly observations (89.6% of acquired monitoring hours) for analysis. We compared multiple linear regression (MLR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), long short-term memory (LSTM), and bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) across six historical windows (1, 2, 4, 6, 12, and 24 h) for one-hour-ahead prediction of each bin and their sum. All 270 model-window-target configurations were evaluated on the same 533 observed testing hours using normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) as the primary metric. The lowest NRMSE values were 60.2% at 10 nm and 22.1% at 14 nm versus 13.4-14.8% at 19-100 nm. A 2 h history yielded the lowest or co-lowest NRMSE at 10-19 nm, compared with 4 h at 27-100 nm. Multiple model classes shared the lowest NRMSE for several prediction targets. For total selected-channel UFPs, defined as the sum of the eight bins spanning approximately 8.8-118 nm, the lowest NRMSE was 13.7% at 12 h. The contrast between errors for the summed concentration and smallest bins highlights the importance of size-resolved forecasting evaluation.

title: Lymphoid malignancies and agricultural exposures: Assessing subtype-specific risks in the AGRICAN prospective cohort.
abstract: Farming, particularly pesticide use, has been associated with increased risks of non-Hodgkin lymphoma and multiple myeloma (MM). However, evidence regarding links between specific farming activities and lymphoid malignancies (LM) subtypes remains limited. We investigated these associations in the AGRICAN cohort. Among 155,173 AGRICAN participants, incident LM cases were identified through linkage with population-based cancer registries from enrollment (2005-2007) until 2017. Cox models with attained age as the underlying time scale were used to estimate the risk of 8 major subtypes associated with self-reported lifetime exposure information collected at enrollment (18 types of farming and related tasks) considering ever exposure, duration and size. During follow-up, 1,654 incident LM cases were identified. In men, cattle farming would increase the risk of lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenström macroglobulinemia (LL/WM) (HR=1.97, 95%CI=0.95-4.10) and marginal zone lymphoma (MZL) (HR=1.95, 95%CI=0.77-4.91), particularly among farmers involved in chemical use, animal care, or milking. In winegrowing, indirect pesticide exposure increased risks for chronic lymphoid leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (HR=1.69, 95%CI=1.08-2.64) and diffuse large-B cell lymphoma (HR=1.84, 95%CI=1.08-3.15), and probably LL/WM (HR=1.85, 95% CI=0.78-4.38) and MZL (HR=1.52, 95%CI=0.86-2.66). In women, suggested elevated risks were observed for most subtypes in animal farming, notably cattle farming (MZL: HR=2.82, 95%CI=0.86-9.27) and in some crops (MM and MZL). Analyses adjusting for BMI, height, smoking status, and history of hay fever or eczema yielded similar results. Our results suggest that both animal and crop farming increase the risks of specific LM subtypes, with a key role for (i) indirect exposure to pesticides in winegrowing, (ii) use of chemical products in animal farming, and (iii) animal contact. These findings point to several potentially complementary etiological pathways implicated in LM subtypes in farming populations.

title: Reduced and layered fertilization improves soil water and nutrient availability for dryland wheat during the critical grain formation stage on the semi-arid Loess Plateau of China
Earth accreted increasingly oxidized material as it grew constraining Theia to be small and relatively oxidized
abstract: Many different Solar System formation scenarios successfully reproduce the main astrophysical properties of the inner Solar System. Here, we use the chemistry of Earth's mantle to determine whether proposed Solar System formation scenarios can produce Earth and to constrain the characteristics of both the Proto-Earth and the Moon-forming impactor, Theia. To do this, we use a coupled N-body accretion and core-mantle differentiation model (Rubie et al., 2011, 2015b) applied to a range of proposed formation scenarios (Classical, Annulus, and Grand Tack scenarios). This model calculates the mantle chemistry of Earth-like planets in Solar System formation simulations and adjusts the initial redox state of the building blocks in a synthetic protoplanetary disk until the mantle of the simulated Earth closely matches the bulk silicate Earth. We find that a strong oxidizing gradient among the initial solids of the protoplanetary disk is favored to reproduce the chemistry of Earth's mantle, in agreement with Rubie et al. (2015b). The Solar System formation scenarios examined here successfully reproduce the composition of Earth if two related conditions are met: 1) there is a strong positive oxidation gradient with distance in the inner protoplanetary disk and 2) Earth accretes increasingly more oxidized material (on average) as it grows. Furthermore, in simulations that successfully reproduce Earth's composition, Proto-Earth and Theia may possess a wide range of mantle compositions and mass ratios. However, because late accretion is oxidizing across all proposed Solar System formation scenarios, Theia and Proto-Earth cannot both possess mantles that are more oxidized than the present-day Earth's mantle. Similarly, Theia's mantle may be significantly more oxidized than present-day Earth's mantle, but only if it is relatively small compared to the Proto-Earth.

title: RANKL exacerbates atopic dermatitis by amplifying keratinocyte barrier dysfunction and allergic skin inflammation.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease driven by epidermal barrier dysfunction and immune dysregulation. Although receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappa B ligand (RANKL) is known to modulate mucosal allergies, its specific impact on skin barrier differentiation and inflammatory pathways remains unclear. This study aimed to identify RANKL as a pathological amplifier of epidermal barrier dysfunction and Th2-mediated inflammation in atopic dermatitis (AD), and to elucidate its downstream intracellular signaling mechanisms. Serum RANKL levels were quantified in AD patients. The functional impact of RANKL was evaluated in a 2,4-dinitrofluorobenzene (DNFB)-induced mouse model using siRNA-mediated silencing and recombinant RANKL (rRANKL) administration. In HaCaT cells, the direct effects of RANKL on barrier markers and inflammatory mediators were assessed. Serum RANKL levels were significantly elevated in AD patients and positively correlated with thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) and IgE. In mice, RANKL inhibition attenuated skin lesions, suppressed Th2 cytokines, pro-inflammatory mediator, and alarmins, and reduced caspase-1 activity. Conversely, rRANKL exacerbated AD symptoms and increased caspase-1 activity. In vitro, RANKL stimulation directly impaired the expression of skin barrier proteins while upregulating pro-inflammatory cytokines. Mechanistically, rRANKL activated p38 and extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) phosphorylation, whereas pretreatment with p38 or ERK inhibitors suppressed the induction of inflammatory cytokines. Conclusion, RANKL serves as a context-dependent amplifier in established AD that exacerbates skin barrier impairment and allergic inflammation.

title: Selective ORgan-targeting lipid nanoparticles deliver SMAD7 mRNA to fibrotic lungs and attenuate pulmonary fibrosis.
abstract: Fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts drive excessive extracellular matrix deposition and irreversible scarring in pulmonary fibrosis, such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), underscoring the need for therapies that directly target fibroblast activation. Here, we apply engineered lung-targeting Selective ORgan-Targeting (SORT) lipid nanoparticles for intravenous RNA delivery to fibrotic lungs. In a preclinical model of pulmonary fibrosis, engineered SORT LNPs achieved functional mRNA delivery in approximately 20% of CD45-CD31-EpCAM-Thy1.2+ mesenchymal cells in fibrotic lungs. Mechanistic studies further supported a contributory role of the vitronectin (Vtn)/vitronectin receptor (VtnR) axis in 1A7B13 Lung SORT LNP uptake. Therapeutic delivery of SMAD7 mRNA inhibited fibroblast activation in human lung fibroblast cultures and attenuated pulmonary fibrosis in vivo, resulting in an approximately 40% reduction in histological collagen deposition and a significant reduction in lung hydroxyproline content. Together, these findings establish engineered lung-enriched SORT LNPs as a platform for systemic RNA delivery to fibrotic lungs, including disease-relevant mesenchymal populations, and demonstrate their potential for RNA-based anti-fibrotic therapy.

title: Maternal mortality in the Americas, 2000-2023: an ecological study of temporal trends, socioeconomic inequalities, and progress towards 2030 targets.
abstract: Background Maternal mortality rose sharply during 2019-2021, coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic, against a backdrop of already fragile progress in maternal survival across the Americas. We assessed whether the subsequent decline restored sufficient and equitable progress towards the 2030 regional benchmark. Methods We conducted an ecological country-year observational analysis using Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (MMEIG) estimates for 36 countries and territories, together with the regional series for the Americas, from 2000 to 2023. Temporal trends were assessed using continuous log-linear models with zero to four joinpoints. Social inequalities were quantified using the slope index of inequality (SII), relative index of inequality (RII), and health concentration index (CIx). We also estimated the annual rate of reduction required for each country and territory to reach a maternal mortality ratio (MMR) of 30 per 100,000 live births by 2030. As the principal external comparison of the pandemic-period signal, country-year MMRs officially reported to the Pan American Health Organization were compared with the corresponding MMEIG estimates. Findings Regional maternal deaths averaged 9408 annually during 2000-2019, peaked at 14,498 in 2021, and declined to 7813 in 2023. The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) decreased from 70.4 in 2000 to 58.5 in 2023, despite rising from 58.9 in 2019 to 106.8 in 2021. Joinpoints occurred in 2014, 2019, and 2021; the 2000-2023 average annual percentage change was -0.9%. Reaching an MMR of 30 by 2030 would require a 9.6% annual regional reduction. In 2023, the SII was -123.6 (95% CI -181.7 to -65.6), the RII was 9.9 (4.4-22.5), and the CIx was -39.6% (-52.4 to -15.3). These measures describe concentration of MMEIG-estimated mortality among countries at the lower end of the GDP distribution and are not interpreted as independent effects of GDP. Interpretation The post-2021 decline is consistent with recovery, but it did not restore an adequate or equitable long-term trajectory. The pandemic-period rise was also evident in many independently reported country series, although its magnitude and timing varied and causal attribution cannot be established from this ecological analysis. Reaching the 2030 benchmark requires sustained acceleration, differentiated country support based on mortality and target gaps, stronger maternal-death surveillance and response, and equitable access to high-quality care. Funding This study received no specific funding.

title: RSP1141, a reversible non-covalent BTK inhibitor, suppresses GPVI-mediated platelet activation.
abstract: AIMS The glycoprotein VI (GPVI)-Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) axis drives collagen-induced platelet activation and arterial thrombosis. Approved BTK inhibitors act irreversibly on Cys481, raising concerns over off-target kinase inhibition, C481S resistance, and bleeding. We aimed to identify a non-covalent, reversible BTK inhibitor with antiplatelet activity and to define quantitatively its selectivity within the platelet GPVI cascade. MATERIALS AND METHODS Fifty-five imidazo[4,5-b]pyridine derivatives were screened using a BTK enzymatic assay and CRP-XL-induced aggregation of washed human platelets. The lead compound, RSP1141, was characterized by concentration-response immunoblotting of GPVI signaling nodes, Ca2+ mobilization, functional assays, drug washout, 370-kinase profiling, C481S enzymatic assay, molecular docking, and a murine FeCl₃-induced arterial thrombosis and tail-bleeding model. KEY FINDINGS RSP1141 inhibited BTK (IC₅₀ 27.9 nM) and CRP-XL-induced aggregation (IC₅₀ 173.6 nM). In intact platelets, RSP1141 inhibited BTK-pY223 (IC₅₀ 0.316 μM) and PLCγ2-pY753 (0.325 μM) at essentially identical concentrations, whereas SYK-pY525/526 (2.88 μM) and Src-family kinase-pY416 (3.96 μM) required 9.1- and 12.5-fold higher concentrations. Downstream PKC, Ca2+, granule secretion, integrin, and spreading responses were suppressed. RSP1141 retained activity against C481S BTK (IC₅₀ 141 nM), docking predicted no covalent Cys481 engagement, and platelet aggregation and BTK-PLCγ2 signaling recovered after washout. In mice, oral RSP1141 delayed FeCl₃-induced carotid occlusion at 10 mg/kg, whereas tail bleeding time was not detectably prolonged. SIGNIFICANCE RSP1141 engages the BTK-PLCγ2 node with approximately 10-fold cellular selectivity over proximal GPVI kinases, inhibits reversibly, and is antithrombotic in vivo without detectable bleeding prolongation, providing a mechanistically differentiated antiplatelet lead.

title: DTC1225, a novel benzothiazole-based compound, ameliorates MASLD by restoring metabolic-redox homeostasis and promoting hepatic lipid remodeling.
abstract: BACKGROUND Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a highly prevalent chronic liver disorder for which effective pharmacotherapies remain limited. Autophagy is a fundamental intracellular degradation and recycling process that maintains hepatic homeostasis by regulating lipid metabolism and mitigating lipid-induced cellular stress, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for MASLD. APPROACH AND RESULTS Through an in vitro reporter-based screening of a chemical compound library, DTC1225, a novel benzothiazole-derived compound was identified as an autophagy activator that inhibited mTORC1 signaling, promoted transcription factor EB nuclear translocation, activated the autophagy-lysosome pathway, and enhanced autophagic flux. Functionally, DTC1225 reduced lipid droplet accumulation in steatotic HepG2 cells and differentiated 3 T3-L1 adipocytes, accompanied by alterations in autophagy-related markers and gene expression, and attenuation of MASLD-associated cellular injury. In a 4-month fructose, palmitate, and cholesterol diet-induced mouse model of MASLD, DTC1225 alleviated hepatic injury, modulated autophagic machinery, improved lipid metabolic profiles, restored redox homeostasis, and attenuated early-stage hepatic fibrosis. Hepatic lipidomics analysis further revealed that DTC1225 induced selective structural lipid remodeling, shifting the lipidome toward longer-chain and more unsaturated species, with a preferential enrichment of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids-containing lipids, which may contribute to attenuated lipotoxicity and modulation of membrane fluidity. CONCLUSIONS DTC1225 ameliorates MASLD-associated hepatic pathology through multifaceted mechanisms involving coordinated modulation of autophagy-related pathways, lipid metabolism, and redox homeostasis, accompanied by favorable hepatic lipid remodeling. These findings provide a critical rationale for further development of DTC1225 as an innovative therapeutic candidate for MASLD and its associated complications.

title: Neuronal and mitochondrial phenotypes in iPSC-derived bipolar disorder models with and without a family history of mitochondrial disease.
abstract: Psychiatric disorders frequently accompany primary mitochondrial diseases (PMDs), suggesting shared biological pathways between mitochondrial function and psychiatric vulnerability. In this exploratory study, we investigated whether bipolar disorder (BD) occurring in the context of a family history of primary mitochondrial disease is associated with differences in neuronal and mitochondrial phenotypes. We generated induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), neural progenitor cells (NPCs), and cortical neurons (CNs) from three non-psychiatric controls, three individuals with BD without a family history of mitochondrial disease, and three individuals with BD who did not themselves have mitochondrial disease but had relatives with clinically diagnosed mitochondrial (BD-FHMD). Our primary endpoints were distinguished network activity and cytosolic and mitochondrial Ca2+ dynamics, complemented by measurements of mitochondrial and cellular function and metabolomic profiles across differentiation. Across neurodifferentiation, we assessed neuronal network activity, calcium dynamics, mitochondrial and cellular health, and metabolomic signatures. BD neurons exhibited sustained hyperexcitability with increased firing and burst activity. In contrast, BD-FHMD neurons showed lower network activity with enhanced cytosolic calcium responses and prolonged mitochondrial calcium transients. BD-FHMD also exhibited stage-dependent mitochondrial alterations, while BD and BD-FHMD showed distinct developmental metabolic signatures. Together, these findings identify two distinct mitochondrial-associated phenotypes within BD. BD is characterized by a hyperexcitable neuronal phenotype associated with altered developmental metabolic programming, whereas BD-FHMD exhibits calcium dysregulation and altered mitochondrial developmental trajectories consistent with increased bioenergetic vulnerability. These findings suggest that BD occurring in the context of a family history of primary mitochondrial disease may be characterized by a distinct pattern of neuronal and mitochondrial dysfunction. Replication in larger, independently characterized cohorts will be important to determine whether this family-history-defined phenotype can contribute to biologically informed subtyping and therapeutic approaches in BD.
