An Integrated Framework to Develop and Deliver Salt-Tolerant Rice Varieties for Coastal Ecologies.
abstract: Cultivated rice (Oryza sativa) is intrinsically salt-sensitive, with yield declining sharply once soil electrical conductivity (EC) exceeds ∼4 dS m-1. Although mechanistic understanding of salinity tolerance has advanced considerably, its translation into farmer-adopted varieties remains limited. Genetic gains in rice salinity breeding programs remain critically low, at 0.10-0.33% per year, far below the ≥1.5-2% annual rates required for meaningful varietal impact. Three constraints recur: a narrow donor base, an over-reliance on single-gene approaches to a polygenic trait, and phenotypic screening in controlled environments that correlates only modestly with field performance. Here we outline an integrated breeding strategy that combines realistic field-based phenotyping in saline hotspots, the Connected Breeding framework for systematic polygenic introgression, and the Transition from Trait to Environment (TTE) approach-using the target saline environment itself as the selection background to implement genomic selection alongside modern breeding tools as a pragmatic framework for developing the next generation of salinity-tolerant varieties. Using a stochastic breeding simulation in which grain yield is modelled as an additive polygenic trait-without salinity-specific tolerance, genotype-by-salinity interaction, or stage-specific effects-we show that CB sustains a higher late-horizon rate of genetic gain than closed-pool genomic selection while retaining 2.2 times more of the allelic diversity on which further gain depends. In the baseline comparison, which grants CB greater genotyping and phenotyping resources and immediate bridge-line availability, CB also finished the 60-year horizon +1.26 t ha-1 ahead (P < 0.0001); this cumulative-yield advantage was not retained once resource and time costs were equalised, whereas the rate and diversity effects persisted under every constraint tested. The simulation therefore addresses the population-genetic logic of CB rather than salinity tolerance itself, and it does not evaluate the TTE design, whose value must be established empirically. We then situate this framework within a Technology-Investment-Partnership-Scaling (TIPs) roadmap to translate improved genotypes into farmer-ready rice products. The approach is, in principle, transferable to other abiotic stresses and crops.

title: FusioBERT: A Task-Adapted Peptide Language Modeling Framework for Anti- Fusarium Peptide Discovery
abstract: Fusarium pathogens cause substantial crop losses, motivating targeted antifungal peptide discovery. We developed FusioBERT, a 7.52-million-parameter peptide language model incorporating fixed sinusoidal positional encoding, learnable relative position bias, RMSNorm, and SwiGLU. It was pretrained on 19.18 million short sequences and 12,616 candidates mined from 232 Trichoderma genomes. The curated benchmark comprised 210 labeled peptides; evaluation used five balanced 178-sequence subsets with three-seed 5-fold cross-validation. FusioBERT achieved an MCC of 0.948 ± 0.058 and generated continuously differentiated genome-scale rankings, whereas physicochemical classifiers exhibited score saturation. Across nine external peptide tasks, FusioBERT obtained a mean MCC of 0.685, compared with 0.666 for PepBERT-large and 0.654 for ESM2. Fixed-seed residue-order shuffling reduced MCC from 0.947 to 0.874, providing preliminary evidence of sequence-order sensitivity beyond bulk composition. Among the three evaluated prioritization strategies, FusioBERT-only ranking yielded the most favorable descriptive wet-laboratory outcomes, including the strongest broad-spectrum candidates, SR1403–2 and SR1403–3. Their Hill-logistic EC50 values ranged from 1.62 to 7.07 μM; observed MIC end points were 8–32 μM. Physicochemical fusion, docking, and molecular dynamics were treated as auxiliary analyses. FusioBERT supports model-first prioritization but does not directly establish activity probabilities, candidate safety, or universal homology-independent generalization.
journal: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Mitochondrial antiviral signalling protein (MAVS) in cardiovascular diseases (CVD): a novel pharmacological target.
abstract: Mitochondrial antiviral signalling protein (MAVS), also known as interferon-β (IFN-β) promoter stimulator 1 (IPS-1), virus-induced signalling adaptor (VISA), and CARD adaptor inducing IFN-β (CARDIF), has emerged as a regulatory node linking mitochondrial stress, innate immune signalling, and cardiovascular disease (CVD) pathogenesis. In the cardiovascular system, MAVS is activated not only by viral RNA sensors such as retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) and melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5), but also by endogenous danger signals. This activation promotes transcription of NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) and pro-inflammatory cytokines, and facilitates NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and cytokine maturation, processes implicated in myocardial inflammation, remodelling, and dysfunction in conditions such as myocardial hypertrophy, atherosclerosis, and cardiomyopathy. Beyond inflammasome activation, MAVS intersects with multiple cell death and homeostatic pathways relevant to CVD, including apoptosis, autophagy, and, potentially, ferroptosis. Preclinical studies show that genetic ablation of MAVS, or pharmacological interventions that limit mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS), mitochondrial double-stranded RNA (mtdsRNA) release, or downstream innate immune signalling, can attenuate MAVS-associated inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic remodelling, thereby slowing disease progression in experimental cardiovascular models. MAVS, however, also performs essential protective functions, particularly in antiviral defence and maintenance of cardiac homeostasis, underscoring the need for context-specific, cell-type-restricted, or pathway-selective modulation rather than indiscriminate inhibition. Collectively, these findings position MAVS as a promising therapeutic target in CVD, warranting further investigation into MAVS-associated signalling pathways and their modulation in cardiovascular contexts.

title: Prediction of the self-association of the nuclear inhibitor of DNA-binding and differentiation proteins
abstract: The inhibitor of DNA binding and differentiation (ID) proteins (ID1–ID4) are members of the helix-loop-helix (HLH) family of transcriptional regulators that play a critical role in regulating cell cycle progression and cell differentiation. Their overexpression in various cancer types makes them promising therapeutic targets. It has been reported that ID4 acts as a tumor suppressor, as ID4 heterodimerizes with ID-1, -2, and -3 and promotes bHLH DNA binding, essentially acting as an inhibitor of inhibitors of differentiation proteins. In this work, we utilize advanced computational biophysics and bioinformatics tools to map the structural foundations of ID protein self-association. High-resolution models were generated and subjected to 100 ns Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations to capture their conformational dynamics in physiological environments. Through protein–protein docking (HADDOCK) and interface analysis, aiming to characterize the binding hotspots of both homodimers and heterodimers, facilitating the development of inhibitors that can disrupt its pathological interactions. Results revealed that ID1 can self-dimerize and form a stable dimer with ID4. The dimerization is exerted by the HLH domain, and the dimers are stable compared to the monomeric isoforms. The ID1-ID4 dimer formation has an important role in lowering their concentration in the nucleus and hence affecting their function. Hence, the identified interaction pattern may have important implications for regulating their activity.

title: Toxicity of immunosuppressive drugs on human fetal kidney development ex vivo
abstract: Immunosuppressants, including calcineurin inhibitors and corticosteroids, are used during pregnancy to treat autoimmune diseases and prevent transplant rejection. Their use requires balancing maternal benefits against potential fetal toxicity, as calcineurin inhibitors are nephrotoxic in adults and cross the placenta. This study investigated whether immunosuppressants induce toxicity or affect early differentiation of the human fetal kidney. Human fetal kidneys (7–14 weeks of development) obtained following elective abortions were analyzed for gene expression patterns. Kidney fragments were exposed for seven days to increasing concentrations of immunosuppressants, alone or in combination. Toxicity and developmental effects were evaluated by flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, and quantitative PCR. We first characterized the expression of genes encoding proteins of the calcineurin signaling pathway by in situ hybridization. Although expression signatures differed, most genes were detected in interstitial cells. High concentrations of cyclosporine impaired cell viability, proliferation, differentiation, glomerular density, and depleted renin-positive cells. Tacrolimus and prednisone, alone or combined, produced subtler effects, mainly on differentiation. Their combination slightly decreased proliferation and glomerular density. Overall, immunosuppressants did not induce acute toxicity at biologically relevant concentrations. However, the sensitivity of renin-positive cells warrants further investigation, including cardiovascular and renal follow-up in experimental models and mother–child cohorts.

title: Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
abstract: Agricultural nitrogen (N) surplus (the residual of total N inputs after harvest removal, plant-tissue storage, runoff and atmospheric losses) is a leading cause of groundwater and other environmental contamination in intensive food-producing regions, yet N surplus estimates often depend on inconsistent fertilizer, harvest and manure datasets in an N balance. Using California’s Central Valley as a data-rich test case, we propagate expert, survey-based, regulatory and county-level datasets through a fixed crop-specific N surplus framework to generate 24 cases. Holding model structure and land use constant, we quantify the large divergence in estimated N surplus arising from data choice, especially for manure-treated field crops. The uncertainty about N surplus is consequential: it can reorder which crops, regions and pathways receive priority for groundwater protection. The resulting spread among N surplus outcomes is large enough to alter hotspot rankings, mitigation priorities and screening-level estimates of economic burden. Credible nitrogen assessment at farm to global scales therefore requires explicit propagation of agricultural data source uncertainty, which can materially affect resulting N surplus estimates. Absent specific local data, the uncertainty magnitudes reported here may guide N surplus uncertainty assessment in other regional, national and global analyses.

title: Smart red berry-derived carbon nanofiber-polyethylene imine beads for controlled urea release, amoxicillin encapsulation and digital image colorimetry in soil by fast microwave method
abstract: A novel dual-mode optical sensor and controlled-delivery hydrogel system (CNF-PEI-AMX-Urea) was successfully engineered using biomass-derived carbon nanofibers (CNFs) decorated with active functional groups and co-entrapped with urea and amoxicillin (AMX). Morphological and structural evaluations confirmed an interconnected fibrous network with ultrafine widths ranging tightly between 2.40–4.76 nm and an amorphous-to-nanocrystalline sp2-hybridized graphitic framework. FTIR spectroscopy verified an intensely hydrophilic boundary layer rich in amine (3471 cm−1), hydroxyl (3372 cm−1), carbonyl (1669 cm−1), and graphitic carbon (1408 cm−1) functional groups, achieving a high operational degree of substitution of 0.52. The fabricated platform demonstrated striking dual-mode optical performance, functioning simultaneously as a daylight halochromic sensor exhibiting pronounced color difference (ΔE) values reaching 4.50 at pH 3 and 8.08 at pH 9 for blank beads, and 2.54 (pH 3) and 3.15 (pH 9) for the urea-loaded test system and as a pH-responsive fluorogenic probe under UV illumination with distinct emission shifts across acidic, neutral, and alkaline conditions. Furthermore, in vitro release studies conducted at a simulated soil pH of 6 demonstrated a slow, sustained, and diffusion-controlled delivery profile governed closely by the Higuchi model (R2 = 0.9747 for urea, R2 = 0.9811 for AMX), avoiding burst release and achieving 24-hour cumulative releases of 4.08% for urea and 15.58% for AMX. Overall, this multifunctional hybrid platform successfully unifies smart optical pH sensing with regulated agricultural delivery, presenting exceptional potential for intelligent real-time environmental monitoring and sustainable agricultural applications.

title: Automatic Gravel Road Dust Monitoring Analysis Using Deep Learning Models and Small Uncrewed Aircraft Systems
abstract: Gravel, unsurfaced, or unpaved road networks account for 35% of the total roadways in the US, with some states such as Iowa having about 60% of their roadways unpaved, and regular monitoring is required to maintain and extend their service life. Among the major types of gravel road distress, dust clouds from passing traffic can cause significant environmental problems, impair visibility, and pose health risks to human respiratory systems. Popular technical manual for unsurfaced road maintenance management typically recommend assessment of dust-severity levels based on the severity of a dust cloud produced by a vehicle driving at 40 km / h ( 25 mi / h ). Because this method exposes assessors to unsafe conditions, its use is impractical for long road networks and high-dust severity conditions, so there is a need to explore automated and remote-sensing techniques for rating dust severity. Although previous studies have employed image-processing techniques to assess dust levels from images captured by vehicle-mounted cameras, dust accumulation on windshields and unstable camera attachments have reduced the reliability of such data collection. To address these limitations, this paper investigates the application of small uncrewed aircraft systems (sUAS) in rating dust clouds generated by traffic at various speeds. For this experiment, we collected dust data using sUAS from three gravel roads in Iowa and applied deep-learning models, specifically You Only Look Once version 8 large (YOLOv8l), to detect the truck driven for dust activation and residual network (ResNet) models to classify the level of dust severity in each sUAS video frame. The ResNet-152 classification model achieved the best result on the test data set with a weighted F1-score of 0.9867, highlighting a promising outcome for adoption of sUAS for dust monitoring.

title: Utilization of Copper Tailings in Structural Ceramsite: Processing Optimization, Mechanical Performance, and Sustainability Assessment
abstract: The accumulation of copper tailings (CTs) has become a serious environmental challenge, and their recycling into building materials offers a practical way to reduce waste and support sustainable construction. This study examines the preparation of ceramsite from copper tailings, fly ash, and bentonite. The work aims to produce aggregates with high strength suitable for concrete applications. A uniform experimental design was used to explore how raw material ratios, sintering temperature, and sintering time influence the properties of ceramsite, while data analysis and process optimization were supported by regression-based modeling and numerical optimization techniques. The optimized ceramsite exhibited high compressive strength and very low water absorption. It had a dense matrix, contributing to its strength and durability. Microstructural investigations using X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive spectroscopy revealed the presence of quartz, feldspars, mullite, and corundum, with mullite and corundum playing a key role in improving strength. To evaluate practical performance, concrete specimens were prepared with varying volumetric replacement ratios of ceramsite and tested for their mechanical properties. Results demonstrated that replacing ordinary crushed stone with ceramsite significantly enhanced both compressive and flexural strength. The greatest improvements appeared at moderate replacement levels, and overall performance still surpassed conventional concrete even at higher ratios. In addition, carbon emission assessments confirmed that producing ceramsite from CTs generated substantially lower emissions compared with traditional aggregates, supporting its role as a green material. Overall, this work demonstrates a promising pathway for recycling industrial waste into high-quality construction materials, providing both environmental and engineering benefits.
journal: Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering

title: Multidimensional Urban–Rural Integration Based on Factor Flows and Its Effects on Landscape Patterns: A Case Study of Nanjing, China
abstract: Urban–rural integration (URI) refers to coordinated development between cities and rural areas. While existing research addresses URI quantification, effects, and optimization, gaps remain in quantifying URI from the perspective of factor flows, analyzing its distribution across urban–fringe–rural regions, and examining URI’s impact on landscape patterns. This study analyzed Nanjing, which is a typical metropolitan city of China, using a machine learning method to identify urban, fringe, and rural areas, quantifying URI from economic, social, and spatial dimensions, and applied a Random Forest regression model combined with Shapley additive explanations analysis to examine URI’s influence on landscapes. Findings include the following: (1) Nanjing’s urban, fringe, and rural areas occupied 18.3%, 29.0%, and 52.7% in 2022, respectively. (2) Urban area had the highest URI estimations of all dimensions. Fringe area held the medium values, with lower social and spatial integration. URI in rural areas was the weakest. (3) URI showed significant effects in fringe and rural areas. In fringe zones, ecological land division was positively correlated with spatial integration, while construction land patterns were influenced by multidimensional URI dynamics. In rural zones, construction land connectivity was shaped by the synergy of spatial and social integration and service facility distribution. (4) Based on these findings, a differentiated zoning strategy was proposed to guide region-specific integration and landscape optimization. This study provides a new perspective on understanding URI, offering both theoretical and practical implications for landscape optimization.

title: Rock Discontinuity Parameter Generation Based on Differentiated WGAN-GP Models: Heterogeneous-Architecture Ensemble and Source-Wise Reconstruction
abstract: The generation of rock discontinuity parameters constitutes a fundamental prerequisite for equivalent rock mass construction and rock engineering stability analysis. Conventional Monte Carlo (MC) independent sampling fails to reproduce the correlation structure among parameters. Building upon heterogeneous Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) models, this study proposes a heterogeneous-architecture ensemble method and a source-wise reconstruction method. The heterogeneous-architecture ensemble method performs row-level weighted combination of samples generated by distinct individual models. The source-wise reconstruction method restores marginal distributions and the linear dependence structure through parameter-column-wise source selection, empirical-quantile calibration, and Iman–Conover rank reordering. Using 122 measured discontinuities from an open-pit mine slope, the proposed methods were evaluated using three metrics: the mean KS statistic across four parameters, the normalized Wasserstein distance, and the mean absolute error of six Pearson correlation coefficients. The results show that the source-wise reconstruction method achieved the lowest mean KS statistic (0.168) and normalized Wasserstein distance (0.046) among the six methods. The heterogeneous architecture ensemble reduced the correlation error from the individual-model mean of 0.264 to 0.248. Both methods outperformed the Monte Carlo method, which yielded a correlation error of 0.326. Ablation experiments indicated that the performance improvement mainly resulted from quantile calibration and rank reordering. The proposed methods preserve the linear correlations among parameters while maintaining accurate marginal distribution fits, providing a feasible approach for generating discontinuity parameters.

title: Genotype-Environment Association and Climate Change Vulnerability of the Economically Important Crop Wild Relative Agave Angustifolia Haw.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS Crop wild relatives (CWR) are an important source for crop improvement, but they are often threatened by overharvesting and habitat fragmentation. This is the case for Agave angustifolia, one of the most important CWRs of cultivated agave species in the tequila and mezcal industries. Despite its cultural and economic importance, no range-wide genomic assessments exist for this species. METHODS We analyzed double-digest genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) data from 215 wild individuals from 67 populations spanning the entire Mexican distribution range of A. angustifolia. We combined newly generated data (97 individuals) with previously published sequences (118 individuals). We combined genomic data with species distribution models for past and future climatic scenarios, performed environmental association and genomic offset analyses, and tested spatial versus environmental drivers of differentiation. KEY RESULTS In terms of climate and genomic offset, we found that although some populations-especially coastal ones-are expected to experience a considerable challenge adapting to changing environments, the species as a whole is likely to benefit from the warmer, drier conditions predicted by climate change projections. We identified specific wild populations that harbour climate-adapted alleles and are best positioned for persistence and crop improvement. While contemporary populations showed moderate-to-high genomic diversity, recent demographic impacts from wild harvest and local cultivation may not yet be detectable due to the species' long generation time and vegetative propagation. Genome-wide divergence among A. angustifolia populations was driven by Pleistocene climate oscillations and isolation-by-environment. CONCLUSIONS Our study highlights both resilience and risk across the range of A. angustifolia, providing a comprehensive genetic framework for conserving its adaptive potential in the face of environmental change.

title: Injectable Polyleucine Hydrogel for Local Amino Acid Supplementation Drives Muscle Regeneration through mTOR-Associated Metabolic Reprogramming
abstract: Skeletal muscle regeneration following volumetric muscle loss (VML) is hindered by impaired regenerative capacity and excessive fibrosis, which are associated with aberrant metabolism in the microenvironment of damaged tissue. Although dietary amino acids effectively promote muscle protein synthesis and myogenesis, their in situ supplementation to correct metabolic dysregulation remains a substantial challenge. Therefore, this study aimed to identify critical amino acid metabolites that drive myogenesis and to develop a local supplementation strategy that promotes muscle regeneration through metabolic reprogramming. Targeted metabolomics was performed on differentiating C2C12 myoblasts, and L-leucine was identified as a key promoter of myogenic differentiation. An injectable poly(L-leucine) hydrogel (PEG-Leugel) was formed by self-assembly of the polyethylene glycol–polyleucine copolymer (PEG-Leu), which was synthesized by ring-opening polymerization. Its mechanical properties, degradability, and biocompatibility were systematically evaluated. The effects of PEG-Leugel on myoblast differentiation, mitochondrial metabolism, and mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signalling were assessed in C2C12 cells. The hydrogel was further loaded with interleukin-4 (IL-4), and its effects on macrophages were evaluated. Therapeutic efficacy was further assessed in a VML rat model using ultrasonography, gait analysis, histological staining, biochemical assays, and transcriptomic analysis. PEG-Leugel exhibited shear-thinning behaviour, injectability, a porous microstructure, and sustained degradation. In vitro, PEG-Leugel promoted myoblast differentiation by increasing mitochondrial metabolism and the energy supply through activation of the mTOR signalling pathway. Furthermore, PEG-Leugel also served as a carrier for the loading and subsequent sustained release of therapeutic agents such as IL-4, thereby promoting M2 macrophage polarization. In a rat VML model, PEG-Leugel reduced the defect area and fibrosis by restoring metabolic enzyme activity and inhibiting protein degradation. These effects were augmented by IL-4-modulated pro-reparative immune responses. The injectable leucine-based polypeptide hydrogel system effectively promoted muscle regeneration through the in situ regulation of bioenergetic metabolism. These findings provide proof-of-concept that local amino acid supplementation via a biodegradable polypeptide hydrogel can reprogram the bioenergetic metabolism of the injured muscle microenvironment and promote functional regeneration in a VML model.

title: What do we really know about human immunometabolism in inflammatory disease?
abstract: Cellular metabolism is now recognised as an active regulator of immune cell activation, differentiation, and function. However, much of this conceptual framework derives from in vitro systems and animal models that may not fully reproduce human physiology or disease. Many studies of human immune metabolism are constrained by artificial culture conditions, tissue dissociation, limited pathway coverage, and a reliance on static measurements that do not directly quantify metabolic flux in vivo. Interpretation is further complicated by the use of blood samples as a surrogate for diseases that arise in specialised tissues, such as synovium, gut, and skin, and by the influence of systemic physiology, including hepatic substrate regulation, adipose tissue, endocrine and neuronal signalling, and the gut microbiota. In this review, we examine what current experimental approaches can infer about immune metabolism in humans, with a focus on immune-mediated inflammatory diseases. Oncology provides a valuable methodological precedent through its use of tissue sampling, spatial profiling, and stable isotope tracing, while also illustrating the challenges of assigning metabolic activity to individual cell populations within heterogeneous tissues. We propose five priorities for the field: move beyond blood to inflammatory tissue; complement static abundance with dynamic, stable isotope flux analysis; integrate single cell, spatial, and imaging modalities; incorporate carefully designed human metabolic perturbations; and account for the wider systemic and pre-analytical context. The next phase of human immunometabolism should move from pathway annotation in reductionist models towards dynamic, tissue-resolved, and clinically anchored studies of immune cell metabolism in vivo.

title: A RARγ-SMARCA5 chromatin-remodeling axis stabilizes AR luminal programs and opposes lineage plasticity in prostate cancer.
abstract: In prostate cancer (PCa), epigenomic mechanisms drive resistance to androgen receptor (AR) signaling inhibitors, such as enzalutamide (enza). We tested whether retinoic acid receptor gamma (RARγ) shapes the epigenome to direct AR transcription, promote luminal identity, and limit enza resistance. RARγ restoration in enza-resistant 22Rv1 cells induced a large RARγ complex containing its coactivator TACC1 and the chromatin remodeler ISWI ATPase SMARCA5. RARγ restoration expanded and redistributed the AR cistrome toward active promoters, enhancers, and unique super-enhancers and increased the overlap with H3K27ac. RARγ restoration also increased SMARCA5 promoter-proximal binding that overlapped with G2/M-enriched AR cistrome, linking AR redistribution to cell cycle-associated chromatin engagement, including at luminal genes. In 22Rv1 and LNCaP C4-2 (also enza-resistant), RARγ restoration directed the AR transcriptome toward luminal differentiation. A miR-96 antagomir (targeting RARγ) mirrored the impact of RARγ restoration. RARγ antagonized the actions of the master lineage regulator ONECUT2 at the cistrome and transcriptome level and these antagonized genes were significantly associated with alternative lineages in murine PCa models of lineage plasticity and enza responsiveness and lineage plasticity in human PCa cohorts. These findings identify RARγ as a regulator of a chromatin remodeling mechanism that sustains luminal AR programs and opposes therapeutic resistance.

title: First report of Stemphylium eturmiunum causing leaf spot on Eucalyptus tricarpa in Australian native vegetation.
abstract: Eucalyptus spp. dominate Australia's most environmentally and economically significant ecosystems due to their ecological resilience (through post-fire epicormic regeneration), and widespread occurrence in remnant vegetation adjacent to agricultural crops, where they can influence disease dynamics and biosecurity risk (Keane et al. 2000). In March 2025, leaves from epicormic growth of two mature Eucalyptus tricarpa trees exhibiting concolorous 35 mm2 (15% leaf area) asymmetrical brown, sunken necrotic lesions with dark margins were collected from native vegetation near Anglesea, Victoria (38°22'27" S, 144°14'43" E). Approximately 10% of epicormic leaves of adjacent E. tricarpa within a 100 m radius of the site displayed similar lesions. The leaves were surface sterilized (80% ethanol) and sections from lesion margins were cultured (25°C, one week). Hyphal tips were subcultured onto Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA). One lesion yielded three morphologically distinct isolates, including Alternaria sp., Allelochaeta sp., and Stemphylium sp., the second lesion yielded a further two distinct isolates, including Readeriella sp., and Neofusiccocum eucalypticola. All species isolated are known Eucalyptus pathogens (Crous et al. 2018; Keane et al. 2000), except Stemphylium sp. (UOM26001), which was examined further. This genus comprises important agricultural pathogens but are unknown from Australian native vegetation (Vaghefi et al. 2020). Two week-old PDA cultures had pale salmon mycelium and brown sporulation rings. Microscopic examination revealed hyaline few-septate hyphae, and mid-brown vertically and transversely 2-4-septate globose conidia 23.6 ± 3.38 x 17.6 ± 2.59 µm (21.0 - 30.9 x 12.3 - 22.8 µm), n=16, consistent with Stemphylium spp. (Simmons 2001). DNA was extracted via a modified Qiagen Plant MiniKit protocol (Vaghefi et al. 2024), and PCR and Sanger sequencing was performed for the internal transcribed spacer region and intervening 5.8S (ITS), calmodulin and gapdh with primers ITS1/ITS4 (White et al. 1990), caldf1/caldr2 (Carbone and Kohn 1999), and Gpd1/Gpd2 (Berbee et al. 1999). Sequences were deposited in GenBank as PZ054204 (ITS), PZ055902 (cal), PZ055903 (gapdh). BLAST showed all sequences were identical to Stemphylium eturmiunum reference sequences, including ex-holotype (CBS 109845). Multi-locus phylogenetic analysis was performed using RaxML v8.2.11 and MrBayes v3.2.6 (GTR model and 10 000 bootstrap replicates). UOM26001 clustered with S. eturmiunum isolates, with bootstrap and posterior probability values of 96 and 1.00, respectively. To assess pathogenicity, detached leaf assays were conducted due to constraints in sourcing whole trees for representative in planta assays, and biosecurity restrictions for trials external to a laboratory space. Therefore, following a standard method for Eucalyptus spp. bioassays (Alcova et al. 2026) sprigs of E. tricarpa epicormic growth each had 2 leaves surface sterilized (1% NaClO) and inoculated with 1 mm2 plugs of one week old UOM26001 via wounding (abrasions with sterile scalpel) (n = 6) and non-wounding (n = 6) methods. Negative controls (n = 6) were sterilized, wounded, and inoculated with clean PDA. Sprigs were placed in water and incubated for two weeks (12 - 20°C, 90% humidity, 12hr photoperiod), pathogenicity assays were repeated 3 times, for a total of 6 replicates of each inoculation method, including the control. After 14 days, 3/6 wounded, and 2/6 non-wounded inoculated leaves displayed pale brown necrotic lesions, similar but not identical to the original lesion due to the field symptoms being caused by a disease complex rather than UOM26001 alone. Negative controls were symptom free. Sections from lesion margins were plated onto PDA and incubated for one week at 25°C. Colonies re-isolated from all inoculated symptomatic leaf lesions were identified as S. eturmiunum based on culture and conidia morphology, confirming pathogenicity. Stemphylium eturmiunum is known in Australia and globally as a pathogen of agricultural crops (Vaghefi et al. 2020), but this is the first report on native Eastern Australian vegetation, and on E. tricarpa globally. This suggests S. eturmiunum may threaten post-fire regeneration of native trees by destroying new photosynthetic surfaces. And while this report cannot fully confirm significance for E. tricarpa due to only a single isolate being recovered, the detection in native vegetation expands the host range of S. eturmiunum, indicating E. tricarpa remnant vegetation could act as a pathogen reservoir, facilitating crop infection in Australian agricultural settings.

title: Occurrence of Leaf Spot on Solidago canadensis caused by Colletotrichum aenigma in China
abstract: Solidago canadensis is a rhizomatous perennial plant native to North America that has invaded eastern China and continues to spread northward and westward (Uzelac et al. 2025). In June 2025, leaf spot on S. canadensis was obsered in Chibi (29.811199° N, 113.577812° E), Xianning City, Hubei Province, China. The disease incidence reached 10% across surveyed fields covering 100 square meters. Initially, small necrotic spots appeared, which rapidly expanded into irregular grayish-brown lesions with a reddish-brown outer ring. Collected leaf samples were used to isolate the pathogen by single-spore isolation method (Choi et al. 1999). The isolates grown on potato dextrose agar (PDA) plates at 25°C in the dark for 5 to 7 days of incubation with similar morphology, and two representative isolates, QM-1 and QM-2 were used for further study. The colony surface presents a circular, white, cottony morphology and undergoes a brownish-gary discoloration. Conidia were unicellular, oval, and hyaline, usually in size from 10.47 to 21.16 × 3.14 to 6.98 μm in size (n = 50). The morphological characteristics were consistent with published descriptions of the Colletotrichum sp. (Liu et al. 2022). For accurate classification, genomic DNA of two representative isolates was extracted from mycelia using a DNA extraction kit (TSINGKE Biotech Co., Ltd.). For molecular identification, the regions of actin ( ACT ), glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase ( GAPDH ), and ribosomal internal transcribed spacer (ITS) (Weir et al. 2012) were amplified and sequenced. The obtained sequences were deposited in GenBank (ACT: PZ213906, PZ213907; GAPDH: PZ213908, PZ213909; ITS: PZ658286, PZ658287. BLASTn results revealed that the sequences of ACT, GAPDH , and ITS were identical to C. aenigma ICMP 18608 (JX009443, JX010044, JX010244). A phylogenetic tree was constructed using the neighbor-joining method in MEGA 7 (Kumar et al. 2016). The two isolates fell into the clade of C. aenigma , supported by bootstrap value of 96%. Pathogenicity tests were conducted using three healthy S. canadensis plants. Conidia were collected and re-suspended in sterilized distilled water (1×106 conidia/mL). Five leaves per seedling were selected for inoculation, each of conidial suspension was inoculated on two sites near midrib and sterile water was used as controls. All the treated plants were covered with plastic bags to maintain high humidity and placed in a greenhouse at 25°C with a photoperiod of 12 h. Grayish-brown lesions similar to those in the field appeared on leaves 5 days after inoculation. While no symptoms were observed on the control leaves. The same fungus was reisolated from the diseased leaves based on morphological characterization and sequence analyses but not from the healthy controls, which fulfilled Koch’s postulates. The same treatment was repeated for three times. Previous studies have reported that C. aenigma can cause anthracnose on the leaves of various economic crops in China, such as apple, tree peonies, mulberry, and walnut (Wang et al. 2021; Wang et al. 2023; Zhang et al. 2021). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of C. aenigma causing anthracnose on S. canadensis in China, which can lay a theoretical foundation for disease diagnosis, epidemic dynamics, and the development of effective management strategies.

title: The architecture of Responsible Autonomy in biological and artificial systems: the Distributed Adaptive Control of volition and agency
abstract: This paper proposes the Distributed Adaptive Control theory of volition and agency (DACva), which parses biological and artificial free will into six capacities that close the agency gap between a reflex and an act: active decoupling, endogenous drive, leeway, normative self-governance, diachronic integrity and experiential ownership. Together they constitute Responsible Autonomy. The DACva architecture spans five layers, somatic to reflective, coordinated by a decoupled model-predictive controller, the compression–expansion–selection–projection (CESP) cascade. It constructs, rather than presupposes, the causal models counterfactual control requires, under the evolutionary pressure of survival in social worlds pervaded by hidden intentional states. The computational principles and neurobiological substrate of DACva are specified in a 12-equation formalism, with an assay and a refutation condition for each capacity. The formalism closes on one equation, the CESP cascade, and yields an explicit definition of freedom: the degree to which an act is the committed trajectory of the agent's own cascade, read on six conditions, one per capacity. From this follows the Evaluation Suite for Responsible Autonomy (ESRA), a perturbational test of architectural competence rather than mimicry, proposed to replace the imitation game; ESRA-S assesses the safety constraints a deployer of AI must impose. DACva argues that the architecture of Responsible Autonomy is the architecture of mind. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue ‘From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self’.
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

title: From rest to task: temporal mechanisms of self-association
abstract: Our self is characterized by both ongoing, long-lasting intrinsic self-representation in spontaneous brain activity and short-term, transient self-association with extrinsic stimuli during task-related activity. However, how these two dimensions of the self are related remains unclear. How do they interact when extrinsic stimuli become associated with one's self-representation? Addressing this gap in our knowledge is the goal of our paper. We propose three temporal mechanisms that may connect spontaneous and task-related activity during sequential self-processing stages: (i) temporal matching of spontaneous activity's intrinsic self-representation with extrinsic stimuli through the brain's scale-free dynamics; (ii) temporal integration of the shorter extrinsic stimulus duration within the longer temporal windows of the spontaneous, intrinsic self-representation using the brain's intrinsic neural timescales; and (iii) temporal differentiation by which the self-specificity of extrinsic stimuli is distinguished from intrinsic self-representation via transient suppression and compression of ongoing spontaneous activity. Together, these three temporal mechanisms may shed light on the nature of self–stimulus associations by explicating the interaction between intrinsic self-representation and task-related extrinsic stimulus processing. This novel temporal framework extends current theories by proposing a hierarchical temporal model of self embedded within a dynamic layer model of the brain. This framework may have major implications for an artificial self in current artificial intelligence technologies. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue ‘From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self’.
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

title: The six capacities of responsible autonomy: naturalizing free will in biological and artificial systems
abstract: The rapid integration of agentic AI is intensifying disputes about artificial autonomy, widening an agency schism between normative frameworks that presuppose agency and a scientific ontology that denies it. This paper proposes a revisionary naturalization: free will designates the control interface that embodied agents evolved to navigate social worlds pervaded by hidden intentional states, not a metaphysical ornament. The antinomy between determinism and libertarian freedom is dissolved by analysing free will from the perspective of control mechanisms. Diagnosing the philosophical record and systems neuroscience, I specify six capacities that naturalize free will as Responsible Autonomy: Active Decoupling, Endogenous Drive, Leeway, Normative Self-Governance, Diachronic Integrity and Experiential Ownership. These are proposed as control constraints on any responsible agent, and hence as design constraints for model construction and as a checklist for evaluating responsible agency in biological and artificial systems. A companion paper maps each capacity to the Distributed Adaptive Control theory of volition and agency, its neurobiological substrates and the Evaluation Suite for Responsible Autonomy (ESRA) test, supplying, in Carnap's terms, the precision and predictive power that complete the explication. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue ‘From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self’.
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

title: Climate change adaptation practices in fruit-irrigated agriculture: the role of nudging in farmers’ adoption decisions
abstract: This study analyses farmers’ responses to economic incentives and behavioural nudges for promoting adoption of water and soil conservation practices, identifying which are most effective. A discrete choice experiment was conducted with irrigated fruit farmers, focusing on three climate change adaptation agricultural practices (subsurface irrigation, regulated deficit irrigation and cover crops) combined with a monetary incentive (framed as subsidy or discount) and additional services replicating the most common characteristics of nudges. Four categories of nudges are evaluated: facilitators (advisory mobile apps), confrontational (apps showcasing the negative effects of not adopting the water-saving practices), social norms (apps benchmarking individual performance against peers) and reinforcement (public recognition and certifications). The analysis incorporates preference heterogeneity based on farmers’ attitudes to nudging. Results show that both monetary incentives and nudges increase farmers’ willingness to adopt subsurface irrigation, regulated deficit irrigation and cover crops. Apps tackling behavioural biases can reduce the need for compensation. Confrontational nudges are most effective; facilitation nudges show heterogeneous response and social influence and signalling nudges generate undefined responses. Therefore, there is potential to reduce the overall cost of promoting biodiversity and water-saving technology adoption by farmers by combining economic incentives with tailored nudges. The study focuses on irrigated fruit farmers in the Region of Murcia, Spain, which may limit the generalisation of the findings to other agricultural systems and geographical contexts. Moreover, stated preferences derived from a discrete choice experiment may differ from actual adoption behaviour. Future research could test these behavioural interventions in real-world settings and examine their effectiveness across different farmer profiles, agricultural sectors and regions. Financial incentives remain important for encouraging farmers to adopt climate change adaptation practices, but behavioural interventions can complement them and potentially reduce the level of financial support required. Policymakers, irrigation associations and advisory services could use digital tools providing personalised information on the environmental consequences of farming practices. For example, irrigation-scheduling and climate-risk dashboards could provide tailored recommendations based on environmental conditions and local water availability, combining behavioural information with technical guidance according to farmer profiles. Promoting climate change adaptation practices can contribute to more sustainable water and soil management in water-scarce agricultural regions. By making the environmental consequences of farming decisions more visible, behavioural interventions may strengthen farmers’ awareness of climate-related risks and encourage more sustainable resource use. Tailoring these interventions to farmers’ environmental attitudes and risk perceptions may also improve their effectiveness and support broader collective efforts towards climate-resilient agriculture. This study explores how combining economic incentives and nudges can facilitate the adoption of climate change adaptation farming practices. The combined economic and behavioural analysis provides novel evidence to inform the design of more climate-resilient agricultural policies.

title: When AI takes control, who takes responsibility? Structural analysis of agentic AI risks in supply chains
abstract: Agentic AI systems execute procurement decisions, reroute shipments and renegotiate supplier contracts at speeds that preclude real-time human review. The existing literature offers limited analytical attention to the risks that arise when decision authority is delegated to agents. This paper develops a risk taxonomy for agentic AI in supply chains and traces the hierarchical dependencies and influence magnitudes among the identified risks. A systematic review of literature, analyzed through theories–characteristics–contexts–methods framework, produces the risk taxonomy. A hybrid modified total interpretive structural modeling and fuzzy decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory methodology is then applied to structured expert judgments to establish the causal hierarchy and quantify inter-risk influence. Three risks, namely workforce skill gap, data quality and reliability and ethical misalignment occupy the deepest level of the causal hierarchy. Lack of accountability and governance and data privacy emerge as terminal outcomes. All three analytical methods converge on a conclusion: agentic AI risks originate at the institutional layer, with technical risks acting as transmission mechanisms. The findings indicate that effective governance requires that workforce capability, data integrity and objective-function alignment are addressed before deployment. The stratified agentic AI governance framework is proposed that translates hierarchical structure into a sequenced intervention architecture, providing practitioners with governance priorities organized by risk-propagation logic. This paper contributes a systematically derived risk taxonomy and a causally weighted governance map for agentic AI risks in supply chains. Five propositions are derived from the causal structure and are advanced as a testable research agenda.

title: Commercial coconut farming as agribusiness investment in sub-Saharan Africa: empirical evidence of financial viability from Ghana’s Jomoro district
abstract: Perennial tropical cash crops in Sub-Saharan Africa attract significant policy interest yet suffer from a systematic absence of formal investment appraisal evidence. This study evaluates the financial viability and risk profile of establishing a 100-acre commercial coconut farm in Ghana’s Jomoro District, the country’s preeminent coconut-producing zone, generating replicable evidence to inform investment decisions, development finance targeting and agricultural sector policy across emerging economies. A mixed-methods investment appraisal framework integrates primary data from 23 structured key informant interviews, spanning farmers, input suppliers, equipment dealers and export agents with secondary macroeconomic data from the Ghana Statistical Service, Bank of Ghana, Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Ghana Commodity Exchange. Five analytical techniques are applied: net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR), benefit–cost ratio (BCR), simple and discounted payback period, and multi-scenario sensitivity analysis across revenue and cost perturbations of ±10% and ±20%. At a 25% discount rate, the project yields a positive NPV of GH₵5.07 million, an IRR of 38% and a profitability index (BCR) of 1.66, all substantially exceeding the cost-of-capital hurdle. The simple payback period is 5.3 years (discounted: 6.3 years). Despite cumulative pre-production losses of GH₵6.10 million during the four-year moratorium, the farm transitions to sustained profitability from Year 1, with net margins rising from 39% to 56% by Year 5. Sensitivity analysis identifies revenue volatility, not cost escalation, as the dominant risk driver. The analysis is grounded in 2025 price levels for a single agro-ecological zone. Future research should extend this framework to smallholder scales and across Ghana’s multiple coconut belts, and should incorporate climate risk modelling and longer-horizon projections that capture the full productive life of the palm. The 100-acre commercial farm model generates an estimated 31 permanent and 50 seasonal farm-level jobs, derived from the labour cost parameters in the financial model. The intercrop system further supports commodity exchange market participation. The study provides a financial foundation for designing inclusive investment models, including outgrower schemes and cooperatives that extend these benefits to smallholder households. Based on a systematic review of the perennial crop investment appraisal literature, this study addresses a critical regional evidence gap by providing the first comprehensive formal investment appraisal of commercial-scale coconut farming in West Africa. The concurrent treatment of debt service dynamics, intercrop revenue modelling, year-by-year moratorium discounting and multi-scenario sensitivity analysis under Ghanaian macroeconomic conditions constitutes a methodological contribution directly transferable to comparable perennial crop investment contexts across Sub-Saharan Africa.
journal: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies

title: Weighted technical and scale efficiency of Greek public general hospitals grouped by bed capacity: a DEA analysis (2019–2023)
abstract: Purpose This study examines the weighted technical efficiency and scale efficiency of Greek public general hospitals within the National Health System during the period 2019–2023, grouping hospitals by capacity size (small ≤ 200 beds, medium 201–400 beds, large ≥ 401 beds). The analysis investigates efficiency differentials across hospital size categories and the evolution of operational performance before and after the COVID-19 pandemic in a context of sustained fiscal pressure on public health systems. Design/methodology/approach Efficiency is assessed using Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA), applying Constant Returns to Scale (CRS) and Variable Returns to Scale (VRS) models. Indicators of technical efficiency, pure technical efficiency and scale efficiency (SE = CRS/VRS) are estimated using the MaxDEA Lite software. Weighted annual efficiency scores are calculated by hospital size group, enabling consistent intertemporal comparisons and a clearer interpretation of structural performance differences across hospital categories. Findings The results reveal variations in technical and scale efficiency across hospital size groups and differences in operational performance during the study period. Overall, efficiency shows a gradual post-pandemic improvement, indicating enhanced managerial adaptability and more effective resource utilisation, although structural differences between hospital size categories remain evident. Research limitations/implications The study is subject to certain limitations. First, the analysis relies on administrative input–output data and does not incorporate indicators of quality of care, case severity, or clinical outcomes. Second, the results may be influenced by the exceptional conditions of the COVID-19 pandemic, which affected hospital operations and demand patterns. Third, spatial and demographic factors are not explicitly captured in the model, potentially affecting efficiency estimates. Future research could incorporate quality indicators, extend the analysis to other contexts, and apply complementary methodologies for a more comprehensive evaluation. Practical implications The findings provide actionable insights for policymakers and hospital administrators by highlighting the need for differentiated strategies based on hospital size and scale efficiency. Large hospitals operating under decreasing returns to scale may benefit from service reorganization and improved internal coordination, while smaller and medium-sized hospitals require targeted investments in infrastructure and human resources. The results also support the adoption of performance monitoring systems, benchmarking practices, and digital health technologies to enhance efficiency, transparency, and long-term sustainability within the Greek public health system. Social implications The findings highlight disparities in efficiency across hospital size groups, particularly affecting smaller and remote hospitals, which may affect equitable access to healthcare services. Strengthening these units through targeted support and collaborative arrangements can help reduce regional inequalities and improve service availability. Enhancing operational efficiency and resource allocation contributes to better quality of care and supports the long-term sustainability of the public health system. Originality/value The study provides empirical evidence on hospital efficiency in Greece and demonstrates the usefulness of weighted DEA for analysing heterogeneous hospital systems. The findings support targeted resource allocation, strengthened collaboration among hospital units and the development of benchmarking mechanisms to improve operational efficiency and long-term system sustainability.
journal: Journal of Health Organization and Management

title: Unpacking the relationship between overall ESG performance and employee satisfaction: evidence of differentiated effects
abstract: This study aims to examine whether overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance is uniformly associated with employee satisfaction or produces differentiated effects across distinct satisfaction facets. It further investigates whether organizational consensus conditions these relationships, thereby clarifying when objective ESG performance translates into more favorable employee evaluations. The study combines firm-level ESG ratings from the Korea Corporate Governance Service with 26,072 employee reviews from JobPlanet across 117 South Korean listed firms from 2018 to 2022. Multilevel models examine the association between overall ESG performance and six employee satisfaction facets. Additional analyses test organizational consensus and visibility as firm-level moderators, together with lagged models, firm-size analyses and an alternative consensus measure based on former-employee reviews. Overall ESG performance is positively associated with overall satisfaction, compensation and benefits and career advancement, but shows no average association with work-life balance, company culture or management quality. However, these relationships are contingent on organizational consensus. The ESG–satisfaction association becomes more favorable when employees hold more convergent organizational evaluations, while several relationships become negative under low consensus. Thus, the apparent null effects for some satisfaction facets conceal opposing conditional relationships. This study moves beyond the assumption that ESG uniformly improves employee attitudes by demonstrating both facet specificity and perceptual contingency in the ESG–employee satisfaction relationship. It refines social exchange theory by showing that reciprocal responses depend on the type of employee outcome considered and the organizational perceptual context. By distinguishing the interpretive role of signaling theory from the reciprocity mechanism of social exchange theory, the study provides a more nuanced explanation of how objective ESG performance translates into employee outcomes.

title: Does Digital Technology Enhance New Quality Agricultural Productivity? A Quantitative Meta‐Analysis
abstract: This study employs meta‐analysis to assess the effect of digital technology on new quality agricultural productivity, defined as a systemic construct driven by technological innovation and factor reallocation and encompassing output, efficiency, and green performance. Based on 853 estimates from 48 studies, all effect sizes are converted into partial correlation coefficients. The results show a small positive average effect that remains robust across publication‐bias and sensitivity tests. The positive effect does not vary significantly across digital technology types, productivity measures, transmission mechanisms, region, or analytical scales, but is influenced by climate and environmental risks, temporal contexts, and econometric methods. Climate risk significantly strengthens the contribution of digital technology, particularly in the 2010s, whereas this effect was relatively weak in the 1990s. No significant differences emerge across technology types under climate risk, suggesting that coordinated digital systems may enhance agricultural climate resilience more effectively than individual technologies. This study integrates fragmented microlevel, regional, and cross‐country evidence within a comparable framework, distinguishes average from conditional effects, and incorporates climate risk into research on new quality agricultural productivity.

title: APOBEC3 antagonism fully explains HIV-1 Vif essentiality in THP-1 cells under interferon and differentiation conditions.
abstract: HIV-1 virion infectivity factor (Vif) counteracts APOBEC3 (A3) proteins by targeting them for proteasomal degradation, thereby preventing lethal G-to-A mutations and loss of infectivity. However, Vif also degrades additional cellular proteins, raising the possibility that its essential role in infectious virion production may extend beyond A3 antagonism, particularly under inflammatory or differentiation conditions. Whether such conditions reveal additional essential Vif targets remains unresolved. Here, using interferon (IFN)-stimulated or phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-differentiated THP-1 monocytic cells, we directly addressed this question. Although type I IFN and PMA markedly suppressed viral production through Vif-independent mechanisms, ΔVif viruses produced from stimulated parental cells exhibited severely reduced infectivity. In contrast, disruption of A3A-A3G fully restored ΔVif infectivity to wild-type levels under all conditions tested. G-to-A mutations were attributable exclusively to A3 proteins under both IFN and PMA stimulation, whereas IFN-induced, A3-independent blocks to reverse transcription were not antagonized by Vif. Moreover, Vif-mediated degradation of the non-A3 targets PPP2R5 family proteins did not measurably contribute to virion infectivity under these conditions. Across diverse HIV-1 strains, the requirement for Vif in this experimental system was strictly dependent on A3 family proteins. These findings indicate that, under the conditions examined here, the essential role of Vif is fully explained by antagonism of A3-mediated restriction. Our results further suggest that counteracting A3-mediated restriction and mutagenesis represents a major evolutionary pressure shaping Vif. IMPORTANCE A3 proteins are potent intrinsic antiviral factors that restrict HIV-1 by inducing lethal mutations and impairing reverse transcription. The viral protein Vif counteracts A3-mediated restriction, yet it also targets additional host proteins, raising questions about whether its essential role extends beyond A3 antagonism under inflammatory conditions. Myeloid cells mount interferon (IFN) responses and undergo transcriptional reprogramming upon differentiation, environments in which additional Vif functions could emerge. Using an A3A-A3G-null monocytic cell model, we show that even under IFN stimulation or phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-induced differentiation, the requirement for Vif in maintaining HIV-1 infectivity is due to A3 proteins. In contrast, Vif does not counteract IFN-induced, A3-independent restriction pathways, highlighting functional specificity. These findings establish the A3-Vif axis as the central determinant of Vif dependency and suggest that counteracting A3-mediated restriction and mutagenesis represents a major evolutionary pressure shaping Vif. Targeting Vif may therefore expose HIV-1 to intrinsic inactivation, even in inflammatory environments.
