title: SENTRA: Privacy-Preserving Training in Outsourced Cloud Environments
abstract: Training machine learning models in untrusted clouds requires strong guarantees of confidentiality, integrity, and correctness, while remaining scalable and resilient to node churn. These challenges are further amplified in emerging agentic AI systems, where autonomous and distributed learning components require trustworthy coordination and secure state management across heterogeneous cloud environments. Existing Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) lack scalability and remain vulnerable to side-channel attacks for large workloads, while pure secure multi-party computation (MPC) approaches incur prohibitive overhead in practice. SENTRA (Secure ENclave-based TRaining Architecture) addresses these challenges through a hybrid architecture that combines TEEs, secret sharing, and communication-efficient MPC with system-level mechanisms that secure the entire training lifecycle. SENTRA introduces a scalable collective attestation protocol that verifies all participating enclaves and enforces hardware exclusivity before any node may store or process secret shares. Training data and model parameters are stored as secret shares in a versioned enclave-backed key–value store (KVS), providing rollback resistance and consistent state under the stated threat model. SENTRA further supports dynamic, fault-tolerant membership management, rollback resistance, and recovery from node failures. Evaluation of a prototype implementation shows that SENTRA achieves up to 8.89 samples/s throughput in software-only mode. In hardware-enclave mode, SENTRA provides memory-isolated confidentiality, fault-tolerant membership management, rollback resistance under the stated threat model, and recovery from node failures in approximately 8 seconds.
journal: Proceedings of the 19th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security

title: Ghost Approvals: Approval-Provenance Failure in Agentic AI Frameworks
abstract: Agentic AI systems increasingly execute actions for users, including transfers, deployments, account changes, and data release. Human approval gates are meant to prevent these actions from running until a reviewer has inspected the proposed action and issued a decision. Because approval can arrive after a delay, frameworks often persist workflow state and resume later. The resume path therefore becomes a security boundary: it must distinguish evidence that a human approved from approval-shaped values stored in mutable state. We define Approval-Provenance Failure as a condition in which a workflow resume path treats mutable approval-relevant state as evidence that a trusted human approval path produced a decision. Our adversary can write approval-relevant workflow state, but cannot use the approval path, change the model, modify tool code, invoke the tool directly, write the business database, mint a valid approval artifact, or access the approval issuer key. We evaluate 18 agent frameworks with human approval, interruption, or pause-resume behavior. Thirteen are exposed, three are resistant, and two are non-applicable. In exposed cases, state-only approval forgery causes gated action execution after a negative control blocks ordinary resume. The failure also forges the evidence of human oversight itself: across 500 paired audit traces, genuine and forged records are statistically indistinguishable, with exact-match rate 1.0 and AUC 0.5 under the tested native audit-field projection, while provenance evidence separates them with AUC 1.0. Finally, we evaluate a provenance-bound approval artifact that authenticates the decision with a MAC or digital signature and is verified at resume time. The full artifact check blocks 13 adversarial variants on five representative targets with microsecond-scale verification cost.
journal: Proceedings of the 19th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security

title: LEASH: Zero-Trust Containment for AI Agent Swarms
abstract: Autonomous AI agents increasingly spawn sub-agent swarms that carry derived credentials to APIs, databases, and production infrastructure. When an operator kills a misbehaving orchestrator, its descendants keep exercising valid credentials for minutes to hours, since every deployed revocation mechanism needs network connectivity to a central authority, unavailable precisely when the network is degraded or adversarial. This paper presents LEASH - Liveness-Enforced Authorization for Swarm Hierarchies, which applies the zero-trust principle of continuous verification to a delegation hierarchy without a reachable authority. A parent emits a signed, epoch-indexed liveness beacon every Δh seconds, where Δh is the beacon interval, and each child staples a fresh beacon into every authentication proof, and the enforcement point checks freshness using only cached public keys and a local clock. Revocation happens by omission: when beacons stop, all descendants fail closed within a bounded zombie window Wz ≤ Wmax + Δh + ϵ , where Wmax is the maximum beacon age and ϵ is the clock skew. Immediate-parent verification at O(1) and full-chain verification at O(d), where d is the hierarchy depth, extend this bound against compromised intermediates. We evaluate LEASH with real GPT-4o-mini agent swarms: 0.71% tool-call overhead, cascading revocation across a 49-agent four-level hierarchy within bound, and 295 × less credential-theft exposure versus OAuth 2.0. Under prompt injection that bypasses application-layer guardrails, LEASH denies every post-revocation tool call, since enforcement sits below the LLM.
journal: Proceedings of the 19th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security

title: Emergence-Driven Security of LLM Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are no longer limited to text generators, but they can also plan, call tools, delegate tasks to other agents, act within external environments, and change states in response to their actions. In Anthropic’s recent report on an AI-orchestrated cyber-espionage campaign involving Claude Code, individual subtasks appeared legitimate when evaluated in isolation but became malicious when combined into an autonomous attack sequence. Consequently, the security of such complex LLM-based agentic systems may fail even when each component appears secure in isolation. This position and open-problem paper argues that LLM agent security should be studied as emergence-driven security: the analysis of security properties that arise from the interactions among agents and its components over time. We define emergence-driven security and provide a conceptual taxonomy to classify emergent security-related phenomena in LLM agents, covering both beneficial and harmful forms of emergence. Based on these insights, we propose EASE, an Emergence-Aware Security Evaluation framework that provides a systematic process for assessing how interactions among agents combine over time to produce harmful or beneficial system-level security outcomes. Finally, we conclude by outlining open problems for studying emergent behavior in LLM agents in the context of security. The paper is intended to provide a foundation for examining how the emerging capabilities and operational needs of LLM agents may shape security evaluations that go beyond static, model-level testing.
journal: Proceedings of the 19th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security

title: Effect of Prestorage Treatments and Zero‐Energy Cooling Chamber Storage on the Physicochemical Quality and Shelf Life of Orange‐Fleshed Sweet Potato Tubers
abstract: Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is a key tuber crop, second in size and seventh in global food production. It faces significant postharvest losses, with quality declining by 45%–69% due to improper handling, including respiration, moisture loss, sprouting, and disease. This study examined how prestorage treatments and storage in a zero‐energy cooling chamber affect the storage and nutritional quality of OFSP tubers. The experimental design featured a three‐factor full factorial model, including prestorage treatments (CaCl2 dip, hot water, and a control), storage conditions in a zero‐energy cooling chamber, and storage times (Days 8, 15, 22, and 29). CaCl2‐treated OFSP tubers had the lowest weight loss (9.17%) and highest marketability (63.93%) after 29 days in a cooling chamber. On Day 29 in a zero‐energy cooling chamber, CaCl2‐treated sweet potato samples maintained the highest levels of crude protein (5.85%), crude fiber (2.36%), ash (3.24%), and fat (0.92%), with intermediate moisture content (72.3%) and carbohydrates (80.41%). They had the highest levels of beta‐carotene at 53.27 mg per 100 g and vitamin C at 7.15 mg per 100 g. Treating orange‐fleshed sweet potato tubers with CaCl2 and using ZECC storage can extend their storage life for farmers and processors.

title: Engineered stem cell-derived CD16-enhanced universal NKT cells improve monoclonal antibody-based cancer immunotherapy.
abstract: Monoclonal antibody (mAb)-based therapies have revolutionized cancer treatment; however, their clinical efficacy is often limited by insufficient antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), tumor antigen escape, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). To overcome these limitations, we developed an allogeneic stem cell-derived invariant natural killer T (NKT) cell platform engineered to express a high-affinity non-cleavable CD16 receptor (CD16HSC-NKT) for broad enhancement of mAb-based immunotherapy. Using a clinically guided differentiation platform, we generated highly pure and scalable CD16HSC-NKT cells exhibiting robust expression of NK receptors, potent cytotoxic machinery, and a Th1-biased cytokine profile. CD16HSC-NKT cells demonstrated potent intrinsic antitumor activity and potently enhanced the efficacy of multiple therapeutic antibodies, including Trastuzumab, Tafasitamab, Rituximab, Daratumumab, and Cusatuzumab, across diverse hematologic and solid tumor models. In vivo, combination therapy induced durable tumor eradication and prolonged survival in xenograft models, outperforming the clinically approved antibody-drug conjugate trastuzumab deruxtecan. Mechanistically, therapeutic antibodies promoted the expansion, persistence, and activation of CD16HSC-NKT cells within tumors. CD16HSC-NKT uniquely remodeled the TME by selectively depleting CD1d-expressing tumor-associated macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. CD16HSC-NKT cells also exhibited minimal alloreactivity, no graft-versus-host disease, and no detectable systemic toxicity. Collectively, these findings establish CD16HSC-NKT cells as a safe, off-the-shelf cellular platform capable of broadly enhancing monoclonal antibody therapy through sustained ADCC, multimodal tumor targeting, and TME remodeling.

title: Smart Agricultural Intensity and Income—Carbon Nexus Among Wheat Smallholders in China’s Yellow River Basin
abstract: Agricultural digitalization could help reconcile farm-income growth with emissions reduction, but evidence on how the depth of smart-technology application shapes these outcomes among smallholders remains limited. Using field-survey data from 243 wheat-growing households in Neihuang, Lintong and Lingwu along China’s Yellow River, we construct a smart agricultural technology application-intensity index covering planting, irrigation and fertilization, crop protection and harvesting. We combine regression analysis with a coupling-coordination model to examine effects on per-mu net income and carbon emissions, and to assess the moderating roles of farmer education and green planting practices. Greater technology application is associated with higher per-mu net income and lower per-mu carbon emissions: the estimated coefficients are 0.0341 and −0.0979, respectively. Farmer education strengthens the income effect, whereas green planting practices weaken it in the short term. Overall, the coupling between emissions reduction and income growth is at an intermediate level, with coordination highest in Lintong, followed by Neihuang and Lingwu. These findings indicate that smart agriculture generates economic and environmental benefits when technology depth is supported by human capital, technical services and market institutions. Policies that integrate digital-skills training, production-stage services, green incentives and agricultural value-chain development could improve the alignment between farmer prosperity and low-carbon agricultural transformation.

title: Nuclear Receptor Nur77 Orchestrates Hematopoietic Lineage Commitment to Avert Anemia in Diabetes.
abstract: Anemia is a prevalent but poorly understood complication of diabetes mellitus. Here, we identify orphan nuclear receptor Nur77 as a critical suppressor of diabetic anemia. Nur77 expression was downregulated in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) from diabetic patients with anemia. In multiple diabetic mouse models, knockout of Nur77 induced anemia, a phenotype recapitulated by bone marrow transplantation. Mechanistically, Nur77 functioned as a transcriptional repressor in HSPCs, whose deficiency, together with diabetes-associated epigenetic modifications, enhanced chromatin accessibility and expression of genes involved in myeloid leukocyte differentiation. Consequently, this led to myeloid leukocyte-biased differentiation of HSPCs at the expense of erythroid lineage. Pharmacological upregulation of Nur77 with its agonist cytosporone B (Csn-B) effectively prevented anemia in diabetic mice. Clinically, Nur77 levels in HSPCs of diabetic patient negatively correlated with anemia occurrence. Collectively, our findings reveal a novel Nur77-mediated pathway in diabetic anemia pathogenesis and propose Nur77 as a new therapeutic target.

title: Match Exposure and Estimated Travel Before ACL Injury in Professional Women’s Football: An Exploratory Within-Player Case-Crossover Study
abstract: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries are a substantial concern in professional women’s football and involve a complex interplay of intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Pre-injury match exposure and match-related travel may represent relevant contextual factors; however, their relationship with ACL injury occurrence remains unclear. To quantify and compare pre-injury match exposure and estimated travel distance between ACL injury seasons and matched preceding-season periods using a within-player design. This retrospective, within-player case-crossover study included professional women’s football players (Tier 3–5) with publicly reported ACL injuries between 2022 and 2024. For each player, match exposure and estimated travel distance before injury were compared with the corresponding calendar window 365 days earlier. Match minutes, appearances, and matches started were assessed across 30-, 60- and 90-day pre-injury windows, whilst estimated travel distance was assessed over 30 days. Paired tests and Cohen’s d quantified the differences. Mixed-effects logistic regression models examined whether exposure variables differentiated injury-season from control-season observations, and Spearman’s correlations assessed associations between the corresponding between-season differences in match exposure and estimated travel distance. Data from 375 players were analysed. Match minutes, appearances and matches started were greater during injury seasons across all observation windows, with small effect sizes (d = 0.21–0.37). Estimated travel distance during the 30 days preceding injury was significantly greater in injury seasons (2724 ± 4821 km vs 2194 ± 4625 km, p < 0.001), though variability was substantial and the effect size was negligible (d = 0.106). In both mixed-effects logistic regression models, no travel was associated with lower odds that an observation belonged to the injury-season period (OR = 0.43–0.53, p ≤ 0.024). Match exposure was moderately correlated with travel distance (ρ = 0.399–0.556, p < 0.001); this was most evident amongst players transitioning from Tier 3 to Tier 4 or competing at Tier 5. Injury season periods were characterised by slightly greater match exposure and estimated travel distance than matched control periods from the preceding year. However, effect sizes were small and between-player variability was substantial. These exploratory findings do not establish causality but identify contextual exposure patterns that warrant further prospective investigation.

title: The synergistic effects of reflective sheets and photovoltaic panels in agrivoltaics: a study on taro
abstract: Agrivoltaics involves a trade-off between the negative impact on shade-intolerant crop growth caused by panel shading and the positive impact of electricity generation. Although taro is known as a shade-tolerant crop, the effect of shade from the panels on reducing soil temperature and the effect of installing reflective sheets to increase bilateral photovoltaic power generation and reduce soil temperature have not been verified. This study used an experimental field with wooden panels that shade solar radiation and reflective sheets that strongly reflect solar radiation and examined the effects of shade and reflective sheets. It shows that the land equivalent ratio (LER) can be significantly greater than one in high shade plots (GCR, ground cover 29%). The reflective sheets not only estimated to increase the amount of electricity generated by approximately 20%, but also improved taro yield by lowering soil temperature. For panels with a GCR of 29%, the LER improves from 1.65 to 2.12 in 2021 and from 1.90 to 1.94 in 2023 due to the reflective sheets. Even under a lower GCR of 14% without reflective sheets, the LER exceeded 1.0, reaching 1.42 in 2025. Box–Cox-transformed random-intercept linear mixed-effects models showed significant associations of quantitative GCR, reflective-sheet treatment, and experimental year with taro yield, together with a strong reflective-sheet × year interaction. The findings indicate that shade has the positive effect of reducing midsummer soil temperature, demonstrating that shade has an additional positive effect on the yields of shade-tolerant crops. Agrivoltaics of taro using reflective sheets has shown promise as a system that can sustainably produce both crops and electricity.

title: RE-AIM evaluation of the national scale-up of community-based index case HIV testing in Guinea: Successes and challenges
abstract: In Guinea, an estimated 36% of people living with HIV remain unaware of their status, hindering progress toward the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets (95% of people living with HIV to know their HIV status, 95% of those diagnosed with HIV to receive sustained antiretroviral therapy, and 95% of those receiving antiretroviral therapy to achieve viral suppression). This study evaluated the effectiveness, implementation fidelity, and sustainability of the community-based index case testing (ICT) strategy using the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance (RE-AIM) framework. We conducted a retrospective mixed-methods evaluation (2021–2024) across 17 districts supported by 26 community-based organizations (CBOs). Quantitative analyses included mixed-effects models, district-stratified descriptive analyses, and Spearman correlations. In parallel, 28 semi-structured interviews with key stakeholders were thematically analyzed in NVivo, guided by the five RE-AIM dimensions. Among 50,609 individuals reached, 8,112 underwent HIV testing, yielding a positivity rate of 8.4% (95% CI: 7.8 to 9.0), with 84.9% (95% CI: 81.9 to 87.6) successfully linked to care. Linkage to care was substantially higher among women (93.6%) and children (90.2%) than among men (14.1%). Adoption expanded from 3 to 17 districts between 2021 and 2023, while cascade performance displayed notable inter-district heterogeneity. Qualitative findings identified strong PMTCT mentorship, community trust, and counseling continuity as key facilitators, contrasted by recurrent challenges including commodity stockouts, financial dependency, and intrahousehold disclosure barriers. The ICT strategy was associated with expanding testing uptake and high linkage to care levels under routine programmatic conditions. Maintenance findings suggest that strengthening institutional integration of CBOs, reinforcing supply chain stability, and improving financing continuity may enhance programme sustainability. These findings provide context-sensitive operational evidence that may inform the adaptation of differentiated community-based testing strategies in comparable implementation settings.

title: Ecological insights and societal impacts: Unveiling the relationship between outdoor sports and mental well-being among college students
abstract: This study develops and empirically validates a College Sports Ecological Risk Assessment (CSERA) model grounded in Bronfenbrenner’s multi-level social ecosystem theory to address the prevalent unidimensional limitations of conventional sports risk evaluation instruments. The proposed CSERA model encompasses four standardized risk domains—teaching risk, student personal risk, competition risk, and sports equipment risk—systematically mapped onto the micro-, meso-, and macro-system nested ecological layers of campus sports systems. Drawing on stratified probability-proportional-to-size (PPS) cluster survey data from 330 full-time undergraduates across 10 universities in Shanghai, this study adopts confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), kernel density estimation, and the Ti algorithm to test three predefined hypotheses concerning risk perception heterogeneity, the mediating role of mental well-being, and model predictive efficacy. Consistent with the results of multi-group ANOVA and bootstrap mediation analyses, teaching risk (42%) and student personal risk (35%) serve as dominant negative correlates of college outdoor sports participation. Distinct grade-based heterogeneity is identified in risk perception: freshmen demonstrate greater susceptibility to micro-system personal sports risk, whereas upper-grade students prioritize meso-system teaching risk concerns. Mental well-being exerts a statistically robust partial mediating effect on the focal association (indirect effect = 0.23, 95% CI [0.15, 0.31], 5000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples). Cross-model MSE comparison results suggest that the CSERA model (MSE = 0.02) achieves substantially better predictive performance than hierarchical regression, risk matrix, and BP neural network models (MSE = 0.08), with its empirical stability validated via three complementary robustness tests. All observed associations are correlational given the cross-sectional self-reported design. These findings are based on undergraduates from resource-sufficient universities in Shanghai and may not be directly generalizable to institutions with limited sports infrastructure or other geographic regions. This study offers a replicable quantitative assessment tool for campus sports risk governance and provides tentative directional references for grade-differentiated physical education design that may inform campus sports safety management considerations.

title: Machine Learning Models in Precision Agriculture for Classification of Diseases
abstract: The bond between machine learning models and the agriculture field is becoming stronger with each passing day. The pre-trained AlexNet, ResNet, VggNet, and GoogleNet models commonly support various tasks in the precision agriculture field, such as disease detection, nitrogen status estimation, leaf area index identification, nutrient status measuring, finding pesticide requirements, measuring growth, etc. These tasks involve a huge amount of data, such as simple cell phone images, satellite imagery data, vegetation index data, images from UAVs, and sensor data from various soil and water sensors. Analyzing and finding insight from such data is a complex task. In this article, a framework is proposed using the transfer learning method for disease classification using manual CNN model along with the pre-trained AlexNet, ResNet, and GoogleNet. The 5450-image dataset,, is considered that includes four wheat disease labels and a healthy wheat label, is used, which was constructed from publicly available datasets. The fine-tuned models are compared for the disease prediction task using the parameters such as accuracy, F1 score, recall and precision. Transfer learning ResNet50 gives promising results once fine-tuned, having the accuracy of 93% compared with other transfer learning models, which ranges from 61 % to 78%. The framework proposed can identify diseases for various crops in agriculture field.
journal: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

title: Weather-based modelling of individual and joint effects on rice yield in Varanasi district, Uttar Pradesh
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is the primary staple crop of Uttar Pradesh, occupying approximately 36.5 % of the state's total agricultural area. Reliable pre-harvest yield forecasting is essential for agricultural planning, food security management and climate-resilient decision-making. This study aimed to develop pre-harvest forecasting models for rice yield in Varanasi district by assessing the individual, joint and composite effects of weather variables using statistical modelling. Long-term rice yield time series spanning 38 years (1986–2023) were used along with weekly weather parameters such as maximum and minimum temperature, rainfall and wind velocity-covering standard meteorological data from weeks 24–42 every year. Weather indices (weighted and unweighted) and their relationships were generated using correlation-based methods. Stepwise multiple regression was applied to fit models incorporating a temporal trend (T) to account for technological advancements. Among individual weather variables, rainfall had the strongest explanatory power (R² = 41.47 %), followed by maximum temperature (R² = 29.53 %), wind velocity (R² = 22.81 %) and minimum temperature (R² = 19.88 %). Joint effect models improved explanatory power, with the maximum temperature–rainfall combination achieving the highest R² (44.43 %). The composite model, combining individual indices and interaction terms, explained 44.08 % of yield variation. The T was consistently positive and significant across all models, reflecting the contributions of improved crop varieties and management practices. Combining meteorological indices with stepwise regression modelling provides a reliable approach for pre-harvest rice yield forecasting.

title: Determinants and Constraints of Rural Youth Participation in Agriculture: Implications for Extension Support in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa
abstract: Rural youth represent a vital resource for agricultural growth and rural transformation in South Africa; however, their participation in agricultural activities remains limited. This study examined the socioeconomic factors and constraints influencing youth involvement in agrarian livelihood activities across five municipalities in the Eastern Cape Province. Data were collected from 104 respondents and analysed using SPSS version 28. Descriptive statistics, including frequencies and percentages, and inferential statistics (at p < 0.05) were used to identify patterns and relationships between demographic characteristics and participation levels. The results indicated that most respondents were male (59.6%), aged 30–35 years (53.8%) and had attained secondary education (52.9%). Youth participation was higher in crop production (54%) than in livestock farming. However, productivity was constrained by insecure land tenure, high input costs, low returns, and limited access to credit, markets, and agricultural extension services. Significant associations were observed between age, farming experience, and levels of participation, suggesting that maturity and exposure enhance youth engagement in agricultural livelihoods. These findings highlight the need for youth-responsive extension approaches that improve access to land, financial resources, and technical training. Strengthening participatory and digital extension models may further enhance the reach of advisory services and facilitate the adoption of innovative agricultural practices. Overall, the study provides empirical insights to support the effective implementation of South Africa’s Extension Recovery Plan and the youth employment and rural development objectives of the National Development Plan (NDP) 2030.
journal: South African Journal of Agricultural Extension (SAJAE)

title: Engineering Enterprise AI Platforms: Integrating Large Language Models, AI Agents, and Intelligent Decision Ecosystems
abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), autonomous AI agents, multimodal foundation models, and enterprise-scale Artificial Intelligence has fundamentally transformed the technological capabilities available to modern organizations. Contemporary enterprises increasingly deploy conversational assistants, intelligent workflow automation, retrieval-augmented generation systems, specialized AI agents, predictive analytics, and generative Artificial Intelligence across nearly every business function. Despite this remarkable technological progress, many organizations continue to experience a fundamental limitation: intelligent applications frequently operate as isolated computational services rather than as coordinated organizational capabilities. As a result, enterprises often accumulate numerous AI-enabled systems while failing to establish enterprise-wide intelligence capable of supporting coherent organizational decision-making. This paper argues that the next stage of Enterprise Artificial Intelligence should not be defined by deploying additional Large Language Models or autonomous AI agents. Instead, it should be characterized by engineering integrated Enterprise AI Platforms capable of coordinating heterogeneous cognitive resources—including foundation models, specialized AI agents, enterprise knowledge, organizational governance, analytical services, business processes, and human expertise—within a unified intelligent decision ecosystem. Rather than positioning Large Language Models as the center of enterprise architecture, the proposed framework conceptualizes them as cognitive components operating within a broader organizational intelligence infrastructure. To address this challenge, the study introduces an Enterprise AI Platform Architecture (EAPA) that extends conventional enterprise software engineering beyond application integration toward intelligence orchestration. The proposed architecture distinguishes between application intelligence, platform intelligence, and enterprise intelligence. Application intelligence describes the analytical capability of individual AI-enabled systems. Platform intelligence concerns the coordinated interaction among heterogeneous intelligent services operating within a shared enterprise environment. Enterprise intelligence ultimately measures whether this coordinated cognitive capability continuously improves organizational reasoning, strategic decision-making, operational effectiveness, and organizational learning. This distinction represents one of the principal theoretical contributions of the paper. A second contribution is the introduction of the Enterprise Intelligence Orchestration Layer, an architectural component responsible for coordinating interactions among AI agents, Large Language Models, enterprise knowledge, governance mechanisms, analytical services, operational workflows, and human decision-makers. Unlike conventional workflow orchestration, which primarily coordinates procedural execution, Enterprise Intelligence Orchestration coordinates organizational reasoning itself. The architecture dynamically determines which intelligent components should participate in particular decisions, how knowledge should be exchanged, how governance policies should be enforced, and how organizational objectives should guide collaborative reasoning across the enterprise. The conceptual framework is further supported by recurring engineering observations obtained through professional implementations addressing complementary aspects of enterprise Artificial Intelligence. AI-supported decision systems designed to organize heterogeneous analytical evidence around business decisions demonstrated that enterprise value is generated when intelligence is coordinated around organizational objectives rather than around isolated analytical models. Complementary infrastructure implementations addressing centralized model access, governance, usage control, and policy enforcement demonstrated that Large Language Models should function as governed enterprise resources rather than as independent architectural centers. Together, these professional implementations provide practical foundations for the Enterprise AI Platform Architecture proposed in this paper. The study concludes that future enterprise competitiveness will increasingly depend upon an organization's ability to engineer coordinated intelligence ecosystems rather than to deploy increasingly sophisticated AI technologies independently. Enterprise Artificial Intelligence therefore evolves from collections of disconnected intelligent applications toward adaptive organizational intelligence platforms capable of continuously integrating computational reasoning, enterprise knowledge, governance, human expertise, and organizational learning. Within this perspective, the fundamental engineering challenge shifts from building intelligent applications to engineering intelligent enterprises.
journal: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science

title: A Novel Hardware-Aware Multi-Objective Evolutionary Neural Architecture for Crop-Disease Classification on Edge Devices
abstract: Crop disease detection plays a pivotal role in improving yields and quality, thereby supporting the efficient utilization of agricultural resources. Conventional detection methods suffer from limited scalability, subjective detection, and reduced reliability under varying environmental conditions. Machine learning and deep learning-based approaches have demonstrated their strong capabilities for efficient crop disease classification from versatile field and plant images. However, non-scalable architectures of these existing models consume large amounts of parameters, computational overhead, memory, and high latency. To address the aforementioned challenge, this research paper proposes hardware-aware, multi-objective, evolutionary search-based neural architectures for efficient crop detection on low-power edge devices. The proposed framework utilizes an EfficientNet-Lite model as the main component, whose parameters are optimized by the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to achieve high classification performance, low inference latency, and limited computational parameters. In the proposed optimization, the framework predicts the performance of learning networks and estimates their execution time on the target edge hardware without testing each model directly. It then identifies a set of efficient architectures with varying accuracy, latency, and energy trade-offs, enabling the selection of the most suitable model based on the target device's requirements. Extensive Experimentation is carried out using PlantVillage datasets, and performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, latency, and computational parameters are calculated. Results illustrates the suggested framework has achieved the accuracy of 0.98, precision of 0.9734, recall of 0.973 with latency and parameters on different edge architectures. Compared with EfficientNet-B0 and MobileNetV3, it is [A]× faster and [B]× smaller, with accuracy within [C]%. These results show that hardware-aware evolutionary search can produce compact and accurate models for real-time plant disease monitoring in the field

title: Fail-Closed Authorization for Tool-Using AI Agents: A Capability Contract and Case Study
abstract: For tool-using LLM agents the decisive question is whether a concrete tool call is authorized before it executes. We describe the Agent Security Contract (ASC), a deny-by-default, pre-execution gate for agent and MCP tool calls. An ASC policy pins a SHA-256 digest of the approved tool catalog, declares per-agent tool allowlists with argument constraints, marks high-impact tools that require out-of-band approval, and bounds call rates; each decision (ALLOW, BLOCK, REQUIRE_APPROVAL) is emitted as an integrity-checked (unkeyed) JSON evidence envelope, and every error path we enumerate and test resolves to BLOCK. We evaluate the open-source implementation on static, recorded tool-call traces only; no live agent is run. Bypasses of the v0.1.0 demo policy found in review were fixed in v0.2.0; on a 60-case adversarial probe, allowed attacks fall from 32 to 1 (a policy gap), at the cost of 3 new benign over-blocks. On the author-constructed 66-scenario v0.2.1 corpus, designed around these checks, ASC returns the expected verdict in 66/66 cases; tool-name RBAC (Python and OPA/Rego) admits 30 of its 33 attacks by construction, and mutation testing shows the corpus exercises few policy constraints (8 of 62 single-constraint mutants killed). As a held-out check we replay 132 AgentDojo v1.2 ground-truth traces under policies frozen beforehand. With tool-level approval policies, 25 of 26 non-empty attack traces but also 60 of 97 benign tasks are held for approval. v0.2.0's strict-argument rule makes these unadapted policies block 94 of 97 benign tasks. Policies derived mechanically from AgentDojo's tool signatures first hit v0.2.0's lack of optional arguments (31 benign blocks); with v0.2.1 they reproduce the tool-level verdicts on all 132 traces, with no blocks and no newly admitted attack, so type-only declarations add no protection here. Median in-process latency is about 38 us per trace.
