title: Cotransplantation With Human AAT-MSCs Enhances Human Islet Graft Survival in Humanized Mice by Modulating B- and T-Cell Responses.
abstract: Immune-mediated rejection remains a major barrier to long-term success of islet/stem cell-derived islet transplantation for type 1 diabetes. We evaluated whether cotransplantation of human islets with human α-1 antitrypsin-overexpressing mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (AAT-MSCs) improves islet graft survival by modulating human immune responses in a humanized diabetic mouse model. Humanized NOD/SCID/IL2Rγ-/- (NSG) mice were generated by irradiation and transfer of human CD34+ hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells, resulting in stable T- and B-cell reconstitution. Diabetes was induced by multiple doses of low-dose streptozotocin (STZ), after which mice received intrahepatic transplants of human islets alone or together with AAT-MSCs and were monitored for 100 days. Cotransplantation with AAT-MSCs markedly improved glycemic control, prolonged graft survival, and reduced the risk of rejection. These beneficial effects were associated with lower serum IgM levels, which inversely correlated with graft rejection, and with expansion of regulatory B cells (Bregs), followed by durable suppression of T helper 1, T helper 17, and cytotoxic T cell responses. Cotransplant grafts showed improved insulin preservation and enrichment of interleukin (IL) 10+ cells within islets. In vitro, AAT-MSCs promoted Breg differentiation, shifted cytokine production toward IL-10 over IL-6, and attenuated activated B cell-mediated cytotoxicity against human islets. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that AAT-MSC cotransplantation promotes immune tolerance and human islet graft function, supporting its translational potential to reduce reliance on systemic immunosuppression in the clinic. ARTICLE HIGHLIGHTS Immune-mediated rejection limits the long-term success of islet and stem cell-derived islet transplantation in type 1 diabetes, and strategies that protect the graft without systemic immunosuppression are needed. We asked whether cotransplanting human islets with α-1 antitrypsin-overexpressing mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (AAT-MSCs) improves graft outcomes in humanized mice, and how human immune responses are affected. AAT-MSC cotransplantation improved glycemic control, prolonged graft survival, and shifted immune responses toward a more regulatory, less inflammatory profile. These findings support further development of AAT-MSCs as an adjunct to reduce reliance on systemic immunosuppression in islet transplantation.

title: Autonomous drilling and blasting operations in open-pit mining: automation of the process cycle, drilling accuracy and management of blast fragmentation of rocks
abstract: Drilling and blasting is a basic stage of open-pit mining that governs the particle-size distribution in the muck pile and, consequently, the costs of excavation, haulage and processing. Blasting accounts for 20–35% of the mining cost and up to 90% of the rock breaking by volume. Manual operations cause drilling inaccuracy, excessive consumption of explosives, an increased oversize yield, higher seismicity and risks to personnel. The paper systematizes directions of drilling and blasting robotization across the following five process stages: drilling, pattern and charge design, charging, initiation and fragmentation diagnostics. It also introduces a unified five-level automation-maturity scale, i.e. manual → mechanized → automated → robotic → autonomous operations. An integral robotization efficiency index is proposed, with process weights normalized by their contribution to the effects. Fragmentation forecast is made using the Kuznetsov–Rammler model and the Swebrec function. The median fragment size shifts from 420 to 350 mm and the oversize yield drops from 7.8 to 2.9% for a model block (250 mm hole diameter). Industry effects of automation are generalized including a 50–75% reduction in the hole deviation, a 40–65% drop in oversize, a 5–12% decrease in the specific explosive consumption, a 10–20% gain in the drilling productivity and a 15–30% reduction in seismicity. In the typical and target scenarios the integral index equals 56% and 88%. Implementation barriers and a roadmap for drilling and blasting robotization within the process-control system and the digital twin of the pit are outlined.

title: BIG DATA ANALYSIS AND ANALYTICS TO SUPPORT THE ACCELERATION OF INNOVATIVE BUSINESS PROJECTS IN THE MODERN DYNAMIC CONDITIONS OF UNCERTAINTY, TURBULENCE AND SYSTEMIC RISKS OF THE GLOBAL ENVIRONMENT
abstract: Purpose of the work. The study is devoted to the theoretical and methodological substantiation and development of a conceptual model for the application of intelligent Big Data analysis & analytics – as a strategic tool for accelerating innovative business projects. The work is aimed at resolving the fundamental scientific contradiction between the need for forced commercialization of innovations and the avalanche-like growth of entropy, uncertainty and systemic environmental risks in the conditions of permanent macrosystemic transit of the global economy. Methodology. The methodological basis of the work was the systemic, comparative and evolutionary analysis of macroecological paradigms, as well as the conceptual modeling of complex socio-economic systems. The instrumental and analytical basis is formed by Data Mining methods, machine learning technologies, artificial intelligence, neural network architectures of natural language processing and graph-based modeling. The approaches of predictive, management and cognitive analytics, principles of digital twins, knowledge graphs and intelligent decision support systems are used. Scientific novelty. The work conceptualizes for the first time the cumulative nature of the genesis of global macroenvironments, consistently traces the transit from the VUCA and TUNA models to the fragile nonlinearity of BANI, the chaotic fragmentation of SHIVA markets and the geoeconomic hostility of the WARMI environment. The complete incapacity of classical management based on retrospective diagnostics in the conditions of SHIVA and WARMI environments is proven. The conceptual five-level model of analytical maturity of innovative business projects in the conditions of macrodynamics VUCA → WARMI has been developed, which is distinguished by a synergistic combination of technologies of digital twins of projects and ecosystem of knowledge graphs. The author’s model of the four-level architecture of the intelligent acceleration platform (including the levels of Data Ingestion/Collection, Data Ingestion, Data Processing & Cleansing, Data Analysis & Analytics, intelligent DSS in real-time mode) has been developed, which transforms uncertainty and chaos in the external environment into a formalized matrix of uncertainties (probabilities for mass events and fuzzyness for individual projects/cases). Conclusions. It is established that Big Data analytics provides a transition from reactive management to proactive business resilience. The essence of innovation acceleration is redefined as the system’s ability to high-speed pivoting of business models based on the detection of weak market signals. It is proven that the implementation of the proposed platform minimizes the risks of startups passing through the “valley of death”, optimizes resource allocation and reduces decision-making time from weeks to minutes. The results obtained are applicable in the design of digital innovation management platforms, corporate analytical systems, accelerators and venture ecosystems. The practical significance of the work lies in the possibility of applying its provisions for the design of startup accelerators, digital innovation management platforms, corporate analytical systems and venture funds. Promising areas of future research related to the use of multi-agent systems, large language models, generative AI and cognitive modeling of complex systems are highlighted.
journal: Information Technology: Computer Science, Software Engineering and Cyber Security

title: Comparative Evaluation of Classical Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Crop Type Classification From Sentinel-2 Ndvi Time Series
abstract: Accurate crop type classification from satellite imagery underpins food security monitoring, subsidy verification, and precision agriculture. The objective of this study is to establish which classification paradigm – classical machine learning or deep learning – provides higher accuracy and better cross-domain transferability for crop type mapping from Sentinel-2 NDVI time series, focusing on the underrepresented conditions of Ukrainian agriculture. Nine classifiers – six classical (Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM, KNN, Gradient Boosting) and three deep-learning-based (Temporal CNN, Bidirectional LSTM, Transformer encoder) – are evaluated on the multi-country AgriSen-COG benchmark and independently tested on a Ukrainian farm dataset (Krynychanska community, Dnipro region; four crops, 2025 season, 38,867 samples). Performance is assessed through overall accuracy (OA), balanced accuracy, weighted/ macro F1, Cohen’s kappa, Matthews correlation coefficient, ROC AUC, and per-class F1. The scientific novelty lies in: (a) the first unified nine-model comparison under identical protocols on a standardized European benchmark with simultaneous cross-domain transfer evaluation on independent Ukrainian field data; (b) quantification of the domain gap between Western-European benchmark and Ukrainian agricultural conditions for both classical and deep learning methods. Results show that deep learning models outperform classical classifiers on the benchmark, with TempCNN achieving the highest OA (0.839) – 3.2 % above the best classical model (XGBoost, 0.813). Upon cross-domain transfer, accuracy degrades substantially across all models (mean ΔOA = -56.4 %), yet deep learning retains a relative advantage: DL models lose on average 52.1 % vs. 58.5 % for classical ML, and TempCNN transfers best (OA = 0.441, +34.9 % relative to the best classical transfer). Per-class analysis reveals that only maize transfers reliably (F1 ≥ 0.82), while rapeseed and sunflower require domain adaptation. Conclusions. The practical significance of the results consists in providing evidence-based guidelines for selecting classification methods in operational crop monitoring systems, demonstrating that TempCNN is the preferred model for both in-domain accuracy and cross-domain robustness, and confirming that domain adaptation is essential before deploying benchmark-trained classifiers in Ukrainian agriculture.
journal: Information Technology: Computer Science, Software Engineering and Cyber Security

title: Personality without a person: measuring personality in generative AI
abstract: Personality describes relatively stable styles of thinking, feeling, and acting when interacting with the physical and social environment. The stability and reliability of these individual styles plays an important role in our daily lives as we team with various individuals at work and home. Generative AI agents (LLMs) are new additions to our lives, quickly assuming roles that might otherwise have been given to humans though there is little known about the stability and reliability of LLM “thinking” styles or actions. We have been investigating whether LLMs can be thought of as having personality out of the box along with the creation and measurement of AI agents with distinct and reliable personalities. In this study four LLMs were assessed with both self-report and newer gamified behavioral measures of personality under an Out-of-the-Box condition and with three prompt-based personas. Contrary to previous studies, LLMs showed very high test-retest reliability. Personality scores varied predictably following persona prompting, while agreement between assessment types varied across models and persona conditions.

title: Investigating the biomarkers associated with pathogenicity and colonization of lower respiratory tract pathogens through analysis of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid
abstract: This study aims to ascertain the optimal volume and procedural protocol for bronchoscopic bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) in patients with lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI), improve diagnostic yield, and identify cell-component-based biomarkers in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) that can distinguish active infection from microbial colonization. This study is comprised of two distinct phases. In Part 1, a cohort of 130 patients was enrolled, including 96 individuals with confirmed LRTI and 34 without LRTI. Under bronchoscopic guidance, two sequential 60 mL aliquots of normal saline (total volume, 120 mL) were instilled into the target segment. BALF was collected separately after each 60 mL instillation. The microbial yield and cellular composition of each aliquot were analyzed to ascertain the optimal volume and procedural protocol for BAL in patients with LRTI. In Part 2, of these 130 patients, 110 with suspected LRTI were further classified based on clinical and microbiological criteria: 96 were identified as having a pathogenic infection, while 14 were determined to have microbial colonization. BAL was performed using the optimal volume and method established in Part 1. The BALF obtained was analyzed to identify cellular biomarkers capable of distinguishing active infection from microbial colonization. The diagnostic efficacy of these biomarkers was assessed. In Part 1, patients with LRTI exhibited elevated peripheral blood neutrophil counts and higher CRP and IL-6 levels. Large-volume BALF (60-120mL) revealed a greater number of significantly different parameters (9 in Large-volume vs 8 in Small-volume;P<0.05). In Part 2, the pathogenic group had higher serum IL-6 levels than the colonized group. Analysis of BALF showed higher neutrophils and polymorphonuclear cells, whereas macrophages, CD206 + HLA-DR + macrophages (tissue-resident macrophages), mononuclear cells, and tissue-resident macrophages to CD14 low CD16 + monocytes ratio (TRMMR) were lower (P<0.05). The AUCs for predicting infection were 0.668 for CD16 + CD24 + neutrophils, 0.673 for polymorphonuclear cells, and 0.693 for the combined model. The AUCs for predicting colonization were 0.682 for macrophages, 0.687 for CD206 + HLA-DR + macrophages, 0.676 for TRMMR, and 0.681 for mononuclear cells. Large-volume BALF is optimal for cellular analysis in LRTI. Elevated proportions of neutrophils and polymorphonuclear cells may indicate infection, whereas increased proportions of macrophages (particularly CD206 + HLA-DR + subset), mononuclear cells, and TRMMR were associated with colonization. These cellular indices may serve as valuable biomarkers for differentiating infection from colonization.

title: A machine learning-based model for predicting 5-year conditional survival in patients with colon cancer: a development and validation study
abstract: Most prognostic models for colon cancer are not tailored to the Chinese population or implemented clinically. This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for five-year conditional survival and compare conventional logistic regression with machine learning models to develop an optimal predictive model. This retrospective study included 430 newly diagnosed colon cancer patients from Suzhou Municipal Hospital (2015–2022). Clinicopathological data and dynamic tumor markers—carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9)—were collected. Patients were randomly split 70:30 into training (n=301) and validation (n=129) sets. This study employed a dual feature selection strategy combining the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and Boruta algorithms. One conventional logistic regression model and six machine learning models (including XGBoost) were built. Performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier score, and F1 score, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) employed for model interpretability. Nine core predictors were selected: clinical stage, differentiation, distant metastasis, surgery, targeted therapy, and baseline and 12-month CEA and CA19–9 levels. The XGBoost model performed best, achieving an AUC of 0.955, the highest F1 score (0.904), and the lowest Brier score (0.085). SHAP analysis revealed that 12-month post-treatment CEA is the crucial predictor for survival prognosis. The XGBoost and Random Forest models demonstrated superior predictive performance over conventional logistic regression. XGBoost was ultimately selected as the primary model due to its optimal balance of discrimination, calibration, and compatibility with the SHAP framework. SHAP provided quantitative, individualized risk interpretation, demonstrating the value of dynamic monitoring in disease assessment and management for colon cancer patients. Meanwhile, the SHAP interpretability framework was employed to provide interpretation of the risk factors and individualized risk prediction methods for the model, demonstrating the important value of dynamic monitoring in individualized disease assessment.

title: Reactive oxygen species and secondary metabolite nexus in plant-microbe dialogues
abstract: Plants interact continuously with diverse microbial communities ranging from mutualists to pathogens. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) and secondary metabolites (SMs) are central regulators of these interactions, functioning as interconnected signaling and defense components. ROS coordinate pattern-triggered immunity (PTI), effector-triggered immunity (ETI), systemic signaling, and cellular reprogramming, whereas SMs such as phenolics, terpenoids, and alkaloids contribute to antimicrobial defense, signaling, and plant–microbe specificity. In this tightly interconnected nexus, ROS regulate SM biosynthetic pathways, while SMs modulate ROS homeostasis through antioxidant and signaling functions. This bidirectional crosstalk therefore helps determine interaction outcomes by balancing defense activation, metabolic cost, and symbiotic compatibility. Furthermore, microbial modulation of ROS–SM networks is highly context-dependent. Pathogens may suppress or detoxify early immune-associated ROS to facilitate colonization, whereas some later exploit ROS accumulation and host cell death depending on trophic lifestyle and infection stage. Beneficial microbes can likewise induce, attenuate, or spatially regulate ROS and SM responses during colonization, accommodation, and immune priming. Thus, the outcome of plant–microbe interactions depends on microbial identity and lifestyle together with the magnitude, duration, and localization of host redox responses. This review synthesizes current knowledge of ROS–SM crosstalk in plant–microbe interactions, emphasizing biochemical sources, regulatory networks, microbial manipulation, and systemic functions. We also highlight emerging insights from multi-omics, spatial biology, and systems modeling, and discuss opportunities to harness ROS–SM networks for sustainable crop protection, microbiome engineering, and climate-resilient agriculture.

title: Psychometric evaluation of the child and youth resilience measure across migration background groups among adolescents in Norway
abstract: Resilience is conceptualized as a dynamic ecological process, yet its assessment across diverse populations remains a methodological challenge. Although the Child and Youth Resilience Measure (CYRM-28) has been evaluated across cultural settings, its psychometric properties have not been examined among adolescents in Norway or across migration background groups. This cross-sectional study included 829 adolescents aged 15–18 years from Norwegian upper secondary schools. Confirmatory factor analysis and measurement invariance testing were conducted across adolescents without an immigrant background, first-generation immigrant adolescents, and second-generation immigrant adolescents. The original three-factor model showed suboptimal fit, while an adapted model with five theoretically interpretable correlated residuals showed improved fit. Measurement invariance analyses supported comparable thresholds and factor loadings across groups based on changes in approximate fit indices, with partial intercept invariance supported after allowing the intercept of item 9 to vary. Relational resources showed the most consistent measurement properties, whereas the contextual domain showed lower reliability and weaker performance of religion-related items. Strong correlations between individual and contextual resources further indicated limited differentiation between these domains. Overall, the findings provide qualified support for the CYRM-28 while highlighting aspects requiring careful linguistic, cultural, and contextual interpretation.

title: From cognitive relief to motivational enhancement: associations between perceived Agentic AI Capability and student engagement in systems development courses
abstract: Generative AI agents are increasingly emerging as important learning partners for supporting complex problem-solving in higher education; however, the psychological processes associated with student engagement remain insufficiently understood. Grounded in Cognitive Load Theory and Social Cognitive Theory, this study examines how perceived Agentic AI Capability is associated with students' extraneous cognitive load, academic self-efficacy, and overall student engagement in systems development courses. An empirical study was conducted among undergraduate students majoring in e-commerce who participated in systems development-related courses. The results indicate that perceived Agentic AI Capability is negatively associated with extraneous cognitive load and positively associated with academic self-efficacy. Extraneous cognitive load is negatively associated with academic self-efficacy and student engagement, whereas academic self-efficacy is positively associated with student engagement. The indirect associations through academic self-efficacy and the sequential pathway are statistically significant. The findings provide evidence on cognitive and motivational correlates of AI-supported learning while, given the cross-sectional design, not establishing causal or temporal relationships. This study extends the application of Cognitive Load Theory and Social Cognitive Theory to human–AI collaborative learning environments and provides theoretical insights and practical implications for integrating generative AI into systems development education.

title: A hybrid framework with quantum-inspired feature selection and hyperparameter optimization for rice price forecasting
abstract: Rice price volatility in India is driven by temporal dependence, climatic variability and supply-side uncertainties, creating continuous challenges for farmers, traders and policymakers. This study proposes a hybrid forecasting framework for rice price prediction that combines quantum-inspired feature selection and hyperparameter optimization with time-series decomposition. A unified dataset was constructed by integrating daily rice market prices (2001-2023) with climatic variables, agricultural supply metrics and spatial information from 23 Indian states and 602 districts. Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) split the price series into trend, seasonal and residual components to capture the structure of price variations. An eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model forecast the trend, and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network modeled the seasonal-residual components. A Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA) performed feature selection, and Quantum Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO) tuned hyperparameters (Hybrid QGA-QPSO). Forecast accuracy was assessed with the Diebold-Mariano (DM) test, residual diagnostics and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). QGA reduced the original 47 variables to 11 optimal predictors, and QPSO ensured stable hyperparameter convergence. The Hybrid QGA-QPSO model achieved RMSEs of 164.57, 242.59 and 294.07 Rs./qtl, with R 2 of 0.9662, 0.9250 and 0.8866 at 1-week, 4-week and 12-week horizons, respectively. It recorded the lowest RMSE at all three horizons among QGA-configured models, with a relative R 2 decline of 8.24% across horizons. Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) recorded the lowest 1-week RMSE (236.27 Rs./qtl) among full-feature models. The DM test confirmed a statistically significant improvement of the hybrid model over the baseline (DM = 5.0108, p < 0.001). Ljung-Box and Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity-Lagrange Multiplier (ARCH-LM) tests showed that forecast errors were free of autocorrelation and heteroscedasticity. SHAP analysis identified price lags as the strongest predictors, with climate influencing prices indirectly through crop supply. No single model dominates across all horizons and metrics. The proposed framework provided competitive and interpretable multi-horizon forecasts and can support market monitoring, procurement planning and post-harvest decision-making for paddy farmers in Indian rice markets.

title: Can rural e-commerce policies enhance the total factor productivity of agricultural enterprises? Causal inference based on dual machine learning models
abstract: Rural e-commerce policies, as an important component of the digital economy, are profoundly reshaping the agricultural value chain and food supply chain, and are of great significance for enhancing the economic efficiency of the grain industry. Based on the panel data of 231 A-share agricultural listed enterprises in China from 2010 to 2024, this paper takes the comprehensive demonstration policy of e-commerce entering rural areas in China as the standard natural experiment, constructs A dual machine learning model, and systematically examines the impact of rural e-commerce policies (RECP) on the total factor productivity (TFP) of agricultural enterprises and its mechanism of action. The research findings are as follows: (1) RECP significantly enhanced the TFP of agricultural enterprises. After introducing high-dimensional fixed effects, replacing machine learning algorithms, and using instrumental variable methods to alleviate potential endogeneity, the conclusion remained robust. (2) Mechanism analysis indicates that RECP mainly promotes the improvement of TFP in agricultural enterprises by reducing information asymmetry, increasing R&D investment and optimizing the human capital structure. (3) Heterogeneity analysis shows that this promoting effect is more significant in enterprises in the growth stage, those with lower financing constraints, those engaged in agricultural product processing, and large listed agricultural enterprises. The research conclusion provides new empirical evidence for understanding the micro-mechanism by which the digital economy empowers the productivity improvement of listed agricultural enterprises, and offers policy implications for enhancing the supporting digital ecosystem of listed agricultural enterprises.

title: Identifying and validating suitable strategies for promoting ICT-based agro-advisory services: an expert consensus study in Eastern Uttar Pradesh, India
abstract: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)-based agro-advisory services can expand the timeliness, reach and responsiveness of agricultural extension, but their sustained use depends on strategies that are locally relevant, operationally feasible and institutionally scalable. This study identified and expert-validated strategies for promoting ICT-based agro-advisory services through a three-round Delphi design incorporating Fuzzy Delphi principles. A purposive panel of 75 experts drawn from agricultural universities, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) institutes, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs; Farm Science Centers) and allied professional institutions participated in the process. Literature-derived domains provided the initial structure, while Round I expert inputs generated and refined candidate strategies. Twenty-eight strategies entered Rounds II and III. Round-II ratings were summarized as normalized relevance weights and represented through triangular fuzzy numbers; final retention was decided after Round III using pre-specified consensus criteria (mean and median >= 3.50, |median-mode| <= 1 and interquartile range <= 1.50). Twenty-four strategies (85.7%) were retained. Digital content in regional languages (mean = 4.89), ICT-enabled Quick Response Teams (4.82), ICT-based FAQ repositories (4.74), digital claim-processing systems (4.74) and digital knowledge libraries (4.70) received the strongest support. Four strategies were rejected because their interquartile range was 2, indicating insufficient consensus despite moderate-to-high central ratings. The accepted strategies formed five domains: digital knowledge management, decision-support and advisory services, communication and farmer engagement, digital infrastructure and institutional collaboration, and governance and service facilitation. The results support an ecosystem perspective in which effective digital extension combines localized content, real-time decision support, two-way communication, interoperable infrastructure and service-linked governance. The framework offers a practical basis for program design and monitoring while requiring field validation with farmers and service providers before use as a standardized evaluation instrument.

title: Nitrogen Surplus in Croplands and Its Key Driving Factors in Intensive Agricultural Areas
abstract: Intensive agricultural areas across China suffer severe nitrogen surplus, yet its spatiotemporal drivers remain unclear. Using the nutrient balance method, this study quantified cropland nitrogen surplus and its intensity in 47 prefecture-level cities in Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei Province, Shandong Province, and Henan Province from 2010 to 2022. The Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression (GTWR) model was applied to analyze six driving factors. Nitrogen surplus decreased from 6.71 million t to 4.11 million t, representing a reduction of 38.7%, with a marked decline occurring after 2016. Surplus intensity dropped by 30.7% from 29.13 t/km2 to 20.20 t/km2, and nitrogen use efficiency rose from 46% to 60%. The GTWR model proved to perform well (R2 = 0.749). Both the multiple cropping index and the agricultural industrial structure shifted from positive to negative effects. Specifically, the effect of the multiple cropping index declined from 0.325 to −0.183, showing the largest absolute average annual change. Urbanization rate, agricultural mechanization level, and per capita cropland area exerted negative effects, whereas the agricultural planting structure varied among regions. The multiple cropping index was the most critical factor. Therefore, optimizing cropping systems is an effective pathway to reduce nitrogen surplus. Future research should focus on incorporating climate factors and exploring the interactive effects among driving factors at finer spatial scales (e.g., county level), to achieve more precise nitrogen management.

title: Biochar–Dolomite Co-Application Alleviates Soil Functional Decline Under Continuous Ganoderma lingzhi Cropping and Promotes Quality Formation
abstract: Soil degradation caused by continuous cropping has become a major constraint on stable Ganoderma lingzhi production, while biochar–mineral amendments are commonly used to restore degraded soils. However, the specific effects of continuous cropping on Ganoderma lingzhi production and soil functions, as well as the potential of co-application to restore its yield and quality, remain unclear. A Ganoderma lingzhi microcosm system was established with first-cropping, continuous-cropping, and different biochar–dolomite treatments. Soil physicochemical properties, enzyme activities, microbial communities, yield, quality traits, and heavy metals were evaluated. Continuous cropping significantly reduced soil pH, organic carbon, total nitrogen, available nutrients, microbial diversity, and Ganoderma lingzhi yield. Fruiting-body dry weight and triterpenoid content declined by 20.09% and 24.62%, respectively. Biochar–dolomite co-application effectively alleviated the adverse effects of continuous cropping. Compared with other co-application treatments, the 30% biochar + 70% dolomite treatment showed strong overall recovery capacity. Compared with continuous cropping, this treatment increased fruiting-body biomass by up to 54.81% and triterpenes by up to 75.57%. Different co-application ratios produced distinct ecological regulation patterns: the dolomite treatment favored soil pH elevation, available nutrient and S-NPH accumulation, and sporulation; the biochar treatment showed advantages in S-UE activity and heavy metal control; and the 70% biochar + 30% dolomite and 50% biochar + 50% dolomite treatments regulated carbon transformation processes and microbial community recovery, respectively. Co-application also increased microbial richness and diversity and reshaped community structure. Structural equation modeling indicated that the amendments strengthened positive links among soil nutrients, the ionic environment, microorganisms, enzyme activities, and Ganoderma lingzhi quality, revealing a potential nutrient and ionic environment-microorganism-enzyme-Ganoderma lingzhi quality pathway. In summary, biochar–dolomite co-application alleviates the continuous cropping obstacle of Ganoderma lingzhi and improves its yield and functional quality by improving the soil physicochemical environment, promoting humus accumulation, and reshaping microbial community structure, providing a theoretical basis for quality improvement of medicinal fungi and soil ecological regulation under continuous cropping.

title: Organic and Biofertilizer Substitution Enhances Maize/Soybean Intercropping Productivity Through Improved Growth Dynamics and Interspecific Interaction Analysis
abstract: Maize/soybean intercropping systems improve resource use efficiency through interspecific complementarity. However, the regulatory mechanisms by which the partial replacement of chemical nitrogen fertilizer by organic fertilizer and biofertilizer affects crop growth and productivity in maize/soybean systems remain unclear. A two-year field experiment (2024–2025) was conducted in the Hexi oasis irrigation district of Zhangye, Northwest China. The main plots were assigned to fertilization regimes (conventional nitrogen, N1; reduced nitrogen, N2; organic substitution, ON2; and biofertilizer substitution, BN2), and the subplots were assigned to cropping systems (maize monoculture, soybean monoculture, and maize/soybean intercropping). A logistic growth model was used to simulate dry matter accumulation, and the land equivalent ratio (LER), net effect (NE), complementarity effect (CE), and selection effect (SE) were employed to evaluate intercropping advantage. Mantel analysis was applied to analyze relationships between crop growth parameters and system grain yield. Study results showed that cropping system fertilization regime, year, and their multiple interactions had significant effects on maize, soybean, and system grain yields (p BN2 > N1 > N2. Mantel tests further revealed that maize maximum biomass potential (Ymax) was highly significantly and positively correlated with system grain yield (p < 0.01), and maximum growth rate (Imax) was significantly positively correlated (p < 0.05), whereas soybean growth parameters showed no significant correlation with system yield. Overall, partial substitution of chemical fertilizer with organic fertilizer enhances maize biomass accumulation and fosters positive interspecific interactions, thereby increasing grain yield in maize/soybean intercropping. These findings provide a practical basis for reducing chemical fertilizer use while maintaining productive and sustainable cropping systems.

title: Forecasting the Cost of the Basic Family Food Basket in the Districts of Panama and San Miguelito: A Comparative Analysis of Statistical and Machine Learning Models
abstract: Forecasting food costs is an important tool for food security planning and management. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the performance of statistical and machine learning models for forecasting the monthly cost of the Basic Family Food Basket (BFFB) in Panama and San Miguelito. Monthly data from 2009 to 2024 were chronologically divided into training and test sets. A Naïve model was used as a benchmark, while ARIMA, Holt, Random Forest and XGBoost models were evaluated using MAE, RMSE and MAPE. The main evaluation used a fixed-origin multi-step forecasting scheme, complemented by a rolling-origin evaluation. Predictive accuracy was also assessed using the Diebold–Mariano test with Holm correction for multiple comparisons. Random Forest yielded the lowest test-set errors (MAE = 13.82, RMSE = 17.23, MAPE = 3.92%), followed by XGBoost (MAE = 15.84, RMSE = 18.14, MAPE = 4.53%). The rolling-origin evaluation also showed favorable performance for both machine learning models, while the Diebold–Mariano test identified statistically significant differences in four of the ten pairwise comparisons based on the Holm p-values, all involving XGBoost. These results highlight the potential of machine learning models for BFFB cost forecasting and support their usefulness as tools for food security-related monitoring and planning.

title: Terrain-Modulated Meteorological Conditions and Rime Accretion at a Mountain Transmission Tower in Southern Hunan, China
abstract: Rime accretion on transmission lines in mountainous terrain is strongly influenced by local airflow and the availability of supercooled liquid water. This study combined nested Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations, tower observations, and the Makkonen ice-accretion model to investigate a rime-icing event at Tower No. 117 in southern Hunan, China, during 1–3 January 2026. Regional analysis revealed persistent low-level cold-air advection, warm and moist airflow aloft, and a pronounced temperature inversion near the tower, indicating a cold and stably stratified environment favourable for rime formation. At the local scale, simulated airflow and model-derived liquid water content (LWC) showed patterns consistent with terrain channelling and windward-slope ascent. During both active ice-growth stages, wind speed, LWC, and a diagnostic liquid-water transport metric were higher at the tower than in a nearby reference area. During the subsequent weakening phase, air temperature remained below freezing and wind speed remained relatively high, whereas model-derived LWC and the transport metric decreased to 18.8% and 16.9% of their first-stage values, respectively. This contrast indicates that weakened rime growth was more closely associated with reduced liquid-water availability than with temperature or wind speed changes alone. The 300 m WRF configuration yielded end-of-stage ice thicknesses closer to observations than the 1.5 km configuration. Sensitivity experiments showed that quantitative ice-accretion estimates remained sensitive to model initialisation, meteorological forcing, and icing-model assumptions. Overall, the results highlight the importance of representing terrain-modulated airflow and liquid-water variability in tower-scale icing assessments over mountainous terrain.

title: Convolutional Neural Network-Based Deep Learning Models for Diagnosis of Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Oral Potentially Malignant Disorders: A Scoping Review
abstract: Background/Objectives: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) represents the most common oral malignancy, accounting for over 90% of cases, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 50%. Oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) carry an inherent risk of malignant transformation to OSCC, yet early and accurate diagnosis of both conditions remains challenging in clinical practice, owing to lesion heterogeneity and inter-observer variability in histopathological interpretation. While existing reviews have addressed artificial intelligence (AI) models’ diagnostic performance in oral oncology, these have typically combined varied model types and have not restricted inclusion to studies based on a held-out test set. This scoping review maps convolutional neural network (CNN)-based models applied with explicit diagnostic intent primarily to OSCC, with exploratory coverage of OPMDs, across histopathological and clinical photographic imaging, limited to studies reporting performance on held-out test data separate from model development. Methods: Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in August 2025 across Scopus, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library. Studies were included if they applied CNN-based models with explicit diagnostic intent for OPMDs and/or OSCC using histopathological or clinical photographic images and reported quantitative diagnostic performance on a held-out test set. Extracted data included model architecture, imaging modality, dataset characteristics, and performance metrics comprising accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve). Results: Thirty studies published between 2020 and 2025 were included. CNN-based models reported generally favorable diagnostic performance, particularly with histopathological images, with accuracy frequently exceeding 90%. Models utilizing clinical photographic images demonstrated greater variability, with accuracy ranging from approximately 76% to 97.5%, in the seven of 13 studies that reported it. Across both modalities, binary classification tasks generally outperformed multi-class differentiation. Inconsistent metric reporting, reliance on small single-institution datasets, and near-absent reporting of external validation were observed as recurring methodological limitations. Conclusions: CNN-based models reported high diagnostic performance for OSCC, particularly in histopathological binary classification settings, although evidence for OPMD subtypes remains limited. However, translating this into clinical practice will require investment in large shared data repositories, standardized reporting of performance metrics, rigorous benchmarking against human experts, and external and prospective clinical validation.

title: Protecting Critical Energy Infrastructure in the Baltic Sea: Energy Security Challenges After 2022
abstract: Energy security after 2022 increasingly depends on maintaining services despite offshore infrastructure disruption. This integrative review examines policy documents, technical studies and four Baltic disruption episodes involving three systems: Nord Stream, Balticconnector and EstLink 2. The observation window is September 2022–December 2025; the two EstLink 2 episodes are within-asset observations, not independent replications. Asset unavailability means loss of a component’s intended function; service interruption means a break in the specified energy service; service failure means the inability of the assessed system to maintain the required service despite available substitutes. The comparison separates reported evidence, interpretations and untested propositions. Operating baselines, substitute supply and confirmed restoration explain why physical damage need not produce system-level service failure. An episode-level matrix links documented disruptions to institutional concern and protective responses without assigning hostile intent to every event. Public records document disruption and recovery sequences and the protection of EstLink 1 after the damage to EstLink 2. They do not establish resulting insurance premiums, financing losses or transition delays. Governance instruments and monitoring capabilities have distinct scopes and evidential limits. The contribution is a two-path framework with differentiated documentary support, not a statistically validated causal model or a representative inventory of Baltic infrastructure failures.

title: From Location-Based Services to Agentic Location-Integrated Social-Spatial Services: A Scoping Review of Agentic AI in Location-Based Services
abstract: Location-based services (LBS) have traditionally helped users answer questions such as where to go or what is nearby. With the emergence of large language model (LLM)-based agents, LBS are beginning to move toward understanding open-ended goals, coordinating spatial tasks, and supporting decisions about what to do and how to do it. This review refers to LBS that integrate such agentic capabilities into location-dependent service processes as Agentic LBS. To systematically characterize the current state of Agentic LBS and identify directions for future research, we conducted a scoping review and proposed an Autonomy–Innovation–Experience (A-I-E) framework as its analytical lens. Following the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), we searched the ACM Digital Library, Web of Science, and Scopus for peer-reviewed, English-language journal articles and conference papers published between 2021 and 2026. The search identified 228 records. After removing 21 duplicates, 207 records underwent screening, and 27 studies were included in the final review. The included studies were systematically charted and analyzed through descriptive mapping and qualitative coding to characterize their application directions, autonomy levels, innovation patterns, and user-experience implications. The results show that: (1) Agentic LBS research remains concentrated at lower autonomy levels, with 23 of the 27 studies (85.18%) classified as L1–L2 and four as L3; nevertheless, the emergence of L3 systems indicates a gradual movement toward more complex task planning and coordination. (2) LLM-based agents are expanding LBS beyond location-based information retrieval toward more personalized, context-aware, and task-oriented service delivery. (3) Reported user-experience benefits are concentrated in usability, accessibility, personalization, and task efficiency, whereas evidence concerning trust, user control, privacy, safety, and long-term use remains limited. (4) By synthesizing these findings across autonomy, innovation, and experience, this review proposes a future-oriented conceptual framework for understanding the emerging trajectory of Agentic LBS.

title: From Setpoints to System Dynamics: Integrating Light, CO2 and Fertigation in Controlled-Environment Agriculture
abstract: Controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) allows growers to regulate temperature, humidity, light, nutrients and root-zone parameters with high precision. However, precision alone does not guarantee improved performance when each control variable is interpreted in isolation, because plants respond to these inputs as an integrated system. Light controls both photosynthetic activity and photomorphogenic signalling. CO2 changes carbon assimilation, stomatal behaviour, water use and source-sink relations. Fertigation variables such as individual macro- and microelement concentrations, electrical conductivity (EC), pH, and nutrient solution flow rate determine nutrient availability, plant development, osmotic status, oxygen delivery and root-zone signalling. In plants, these inputs converge on shared physiological and molecular processes, including carbon–nitrogen balance, transpiration-driven nutrient delivery, nitrate and phosphate uptake, H+-ATPase activity, hormone signalling, root architecture, and sink development. This narrative review proposes a qualitative, conceptual systems-dynamics framework; it does not present a calibrated simulation or validated control model. The central proposition is that plant growth, yield and fruit quality emerge from feedback loops among carbon capture, nutrient acquisition, hydraulic function and developmental sink strength. In crops such as cucumber, tomato, lettuce, strawberry, pepper and basil, the same environmental input can improve one trait whilst weakening another, depending on developmental stage, cultivar, sink demand, and root-zone conditions. A system-dynamics framework is therefore essential for designing production strategies that synchronise light settings, CO2 schedules and fertigation regimes with plant physiological stages. For compact cucurbits and other commercial CEA crops, this approach can help optimise productivity per unit volume whilst maintaining nutrient status, water-use efficiency and fruit quality. These insights also apply to CEA for long-term space, Moon and Mars missions.

title: Drebrin Links Actin Organization to MRTFA–SRF Signaling During Skeletal Myogenesis
abstract: Drebrin is an F-actin side-binding protein previously implicated in myoblast differentiation, but the signaling mechanisms linking drebrin-dependent actin organization to myogenic state transitions remain unclear. Here, we combined transcriptomic prioritization with C2C12 loss-of-function analyses. Drebrin knockdown reduced phalloidin fluorescence and increased DNase I-Alexa Fluor 488 median fluorescence intensity, shifting actin-associated readouts toward a more monomeric state. This was accompanied by increased cytoplasmic MRTFA, reduced nuclear MRTFA and SRF, lower CArG-dependent SMYD1 reporter activity, and decreased expression of SRF-responsive genes. Drebrin knockdown also altered YAP1 abundance and phosphorylation, reduced EdU incorporation and cell-cycle protein expression, increased G0/G1 accumulation, and resulted in approximately 25% fewer cells at 72 h. During differentiation, drebrin knockdown attenuated MyoD, MyoG, and sarcomeric myosin heavy chain (MyHC) expression and impaired myotube formation. Public skeletal-muscle datasets associated DBN1 preferentially with a myogenic transcriptional program, although DBN1/Dbn1 regulation varied across aging and muscle-wasting contexts. These findings support a working model in which drebrin-dependent actin organization contributes to MRTFA–SRF transcriptional competence during myogenic progression. These findings provide a basis for testing the proposed mechanism and for investigating whether drebrin contributes to muscle atrophy in appropriate experimental models.

title: Cross-Session Memory Poisoning of AI Agents in Connected-Vehicle Security: Write-Time Filtering Costs Adaptation Under Concept Drift
abstract: Persistent AI agents increasingly triage security alerts by retrieving precedents from earlier sessions. This creates an attack surface separated in time from its effect: an adversary writing a few false precedents alters a later decision while being absent when it occurs. Defences screen new memory at write time, rejecting entries that contradict what is stored, and are reported as highly effective. Existing assessments hold the correct answer fixed, so any contradicting assertion is adversarial by construction. Real environments are not stationary, and when the world legitimately changes, a correct update and a poisoning attempt are indistinguishable on content alone: rejecting contradiction also rejects learning. We evaluate defences on real vehicle traffic, where a fleet refresh shifts the alert distribution, and a synthetic control, where the correct label itself changes. Write-time screening is effective and free when the environment is fixed yet substantially impairs adaptation under both kinds of change. Provisional trust, which admits new records at reduced influence until outcomes corroborate them, recovers more safety without a detectable adaptation cost; on a language model agent, its gain is significant with frozen memory but not with persistent memory. Ablation credits the provisional weighting. Memory defences cannot be assessed in a stationary setting.

title: Evaluating Large Language Model Platforms for Medical Nutrition Therapy in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Quality, Guideline Concordance, Readability, and Hallucinations
abstract: Background/Objectives: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) commonly experience feeding- and nutrition-related problems, while families increasingly encounter large language model (LLM)-based tools as sources of health information. Evidence on the reliability of these tools for ASD-specific medical nutrition therapy (MNT) remains limited. The aim of this study is to compare the responses of four publicly available LLM-based platform configurations to nutrition questions related to ASD in terms of quality, guideline compliance, readability, and hallucination. Methods: In this cross-sectional comparative benchmark study, 60 standardized, unbiased informational questions across five MNT domains (12 per domain) were each submitted once in separate sessions to four LLM-based platform configurations: ChatGPT, ChatGPT Plus, Microsoft Copilot, and Google Gemini, yielding 240 responses. Only one response was evaluated for each question-platform combination, and variability between repeated productions was not measured. Four nutrition and dietetics experts, blinded to platform identity, assessed response quality using Medical Artificial Intelligence Quality Analysis (QAMAI) and Global Quality Score (GQS), and reviewed compliance with NICE guidelines and the American Academy of Pediatrics clinical report, and evaluated readability and binary hallucination classifications. QAMAI, GQS, and guideline-concordance scores were compared using generalized estimating equations with a Gamma distribution and a log link. Results: Platform, domain (D), and platform × domain effects were significant for QAMAI, GQS, and guideline concordance (all omnibus p < 0.05). ChatGPT Plus had the highest overall mean QAMAI, GQS, and guideline-concordance scores. Gemini showed relatively high quality ratings but the lowest overall concordance with guidelines. In the analyzed response set, no hallucinations were detected in either the ChatGPT or ChatGPT Plus configurations (0/60 each; 0%). Hallucinations were detected in 21/60 (35.0%) of the Copilot responses and in 38/60 (63.3%) of the Gemini responses. Overall platform comparisons of hallucination classifications across the five domains were significant in all five domains after false discovery rate correction; pairwise differences remained significant in D1, D2, and D5, but not in D3 or D4. Mean Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level scores ranged from 14.62 to 18.87 across platforms. Conclusions: In this standardized single-generation comparison, overall response quality, guideline compliance, readability, and findings on hallucinations did not always coincide. Observed hallucination rates are limited to the response set examined. The observation of zero events in two ChatGPT configurations does not indicate the absence of hallucination risk, nor does it provide a basis for differentiating the configurations or concluding that they are equivalent in this respect. The binary hallucination rates did not reflect error severity and therefore should not be used to compare the clinical risks of the platforms. The findings are limited to a controlled set of questions and cannot be generalized to emotional, directive, or multi-round caregiver interactions. The ASD nutritional information generated by the LLM should be evaluated multidimensionally and subjected to expert validation. Studies involving repeated independent response generation in each question-platform combination are necessary for comparing hallucination tendencies.

title: Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Sets Framework with a Digital Twin Prototype for Simulation-Supported Supplier Selection Under Industry 5.0
abstract: Supplier selection is a critical strategic decision in supply chain management, with a direct impact on operational performance, competitiveness, and long-term sustainability. The contemporary business environment, characterised by globalisation, climate change, and increasingly stringent regulatory requirements, necessitates an expanded supplier evaluation framework that encompasses the dimensions of resilience and sustainability. Industry 5.0 and digital twins (DT) are advanced concepts that enable improvements in the supplier selection process through the integration of advanced technologies and human knowledge. Using a five-member expert panel from different departments, both criterion importance and the qualitative supplier ratings were assessed individually by each expert; quantitative criteria were derived from a preliminary DT prototype running documented scenario simulations, in the case of an agricultural company operating in south-eastern Bosnia and Herzegovina. Interval type-2 fuzzy sets (IT2FS) were applied, with asymmetric fuzzy numbers used in the membership function. The results obtained using IT2FS Simple Weight Calculation (SiWeC) showed that total costs, recovery capability following disruptive events, and product and service quality were the most important criteria. Qualitative supplier ratings were aggregated by unweighted arithmetic mean, while criterion importance was determined through IT2FS SiWeC. The six selected suppliers were ranked using IT2FS Multi-Attributive Border Approximation Area Comparison (MABAC), which demonstrated that supplier SUPP1 achieved the best results according to the expert assessments and the DT-based scenario simulations. These findings were additionally confirmed through comparative and sensitivity analyses. This study contributes practical guidance regarding the criteria and suppliers that agricultural enterprises should select in order to improve the procurement process and reduce supply chain risks. This research presents a framework for supplier selection based on aggregated DT output data. The DT prototype used in this study is a preliminary, uncalibrated simulation system whose outputs are treated as simulation-based estimates rather than validated real-time measurements. This limitation is stated explicitly, and the calibration of the DT against actual supplier performance is identified as a direction for future research. This framework can be extended to real-time dynamic updating, which is a direction for future research.

title: Integrated Scheduling of Wind Power and Pumped Hydroelectric Storage Based on an MILP Model
abstract: In this article, we develop a tractable mixed-integer linear programming framework for the annual scheduling of a hybrid offshore wind and pumped hydroelectric energy storage system. The proposed formulation uses McCormick envelopes to relax the non-convex hydraulic power relations while embedding generation dispatch within a direct current optimal power flow model. In particular, we incorporate a cumulative storage incentive into the objective function to capture the trade-off between net electricity-market revenue and intra-horizon water availability, examining its weighting multiplier through a systematic sensitivity analysis. We illustrate the performance of the proposed formulation applied to (i) a modified PJM five-bus benchmark and (ii) an IEEE 30-bus network hosting two hybrid installations, driven by historical wind profiles from Tamaulipas and locational marginal prices from the Mexican wholesale electricity market. Moreover, we assess the selected binary operating-mode sequences ex post by re-optimizing the continuous dispatch under the exact bilinear hydraulic equations. The numerical results demonstrate that coordinated dispatch enhances energy arbitrage and dynamic grid interaction. In the five-bus case, the reference cumulative storage incentive raises the average upper-reservoir elevation relative to scheduling without the incentive, but both schedules end at the minimum operating level. Thus, the incentive improves water availability within the annual horizon without preventing terminal depletion or guaranteeing long-term water reserves.

title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Polymer Drag Reduction: Bridging Laboratory Turbulent Pipe Flow and Field-Scale Crude Oil Pipeline Operation
abstract: Polymeric drag-reducing agents (DRAs) can significantly suppress turbulent friction in crude oil pipelines. However, the design of field dosing strategies still relies on empirical rules because laboratory-scale drag-reduction (DR) measurements fail to transfer quantitatively to industrial diameters, fluids, and shear histories. In this study, we present an integrated laboratory–field–machine-learning framework that closes this gap. Systematic recirculating-loop experiments (Reynolds number of 2 × 104–1.2 × 105, four pipe diameters, 3–200 ppmw of a polyalphaolefin DRA in a model oil) established concentration–Reynolds response surfaces, first-order mechanical degradation kinetics with a wall-shear-scaling rate constant kd ∝ τw1.25, and a normalized scale-up correlation validated over an eight-fold range of controlled laboratory diameters (12.7–102.0 mm) and, after a two-parameter transfer calibration, applicable to a 711 mm trunk line. A 90-day campaign on a 720 km, 711 mm crude oil trunk line (129,600 SCADA records) yielded a mean field DR of 22.9% and a mean pumping-energy saving of 22.9%. A gradient-boosting model trained jointly on laboratory and field data predicts DR with an R2 = 0.984 and an RMSE = 0.89 percentage points, while SHAP analysis ranks Reynolds number, concentration, and pipe diameter as the variables with the largest marginal contribution. A physics-informed hybrid network constrained by the Virk maximum-drag-reduction asymptote reduces extrapolation error by 34% relative to a purely data-driven network, and a sequence-to-one LSTM forecasts field DR 24 h ahead with an RMSE ≈ 1.4 points, outperforming persistence by more than a factor of two. Bayesian multi-objective optimization of the trained surrogate identifies dosing schedules that add two to three percentage points of energy savings per DRA-treated segment, corresponding to a modeled net benefit of 1.85 M US$ yr−1 and 17.7 kt CO2 yr−1. The framework demonstrates that physics-constrained machine learning can convert routine laboratory rheometry and SCADA streams into quantitatively predictive, economically deployable drag-reduction engineering.

title: Climatic Controls of Interannual Variability in Forest Land Surface Phenology Across Poland
abstract: Understanding how consistently forest phenology responds from year to year is important for characterizing vegetation responses to climatic variability, yet most studies have focused on long-term phenological trends. Here, we assessed the spatial patterns and environmental controls of detrended interannual variability in the start (SOS) and end (EOS) of the growing season across Polish forests during 2003–2025. SOS and EOS were derived from MODIS NDVI time series, while climatic controls were evaluated using variable-specific preseason windows. Generalized additive models were used to relate phenological variability to long-term climatic conditions, interannual climate variability, aridity, and topography. SOS and EOS variability showed distinct spatial patterns and contrasting climatic sensitivities. SOS was most strongly associated with temperature during the 30-day preseason, whereas EOS showed weaker and more variable climatic relationships. The relevant preseason periods differed among climatic variables and between SOS and EOS. Environmental relationships were predominantly nonlinear, with important effects of temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, solar radiation, aridity, and elevation. The models explained 35.2% and 51.6% of the deviance in SOS and EOS variability, respectively. These findings demonstrate that interannual variability provides complementary information to long-term phenological trends and that SOS and EOS respond differently to climatic and environmental conditions.

title: Subpixel Low-Intensity Fire Detection in Wide-Swath Remote Sensing: Dual-Scale Thermal Background Adaptation and Spatiotemporal Semantic Constraints
abstract: Subpixel low-intensity fires are difficult to detect in wide-swath imagery because mixed pixels weaken their thermal signals, whereas industrial facilities and photovoltaic panels can generate false alarms. We propose a dual-scale adaptive thermal background thresholding method based on spatiotemporal semantic constraints and conduct experiments using the detection of crop straw burning in China as a specific application scenario. The method combines scene-wide thermal state classification with local neighborhood statistics to adjust the above-background threshold and recover additional weak fire candidates. Farmland support, a persistent heat source prior derived from long-term VIIRS observations, and candidate-to-source proximity are then applied to newly added candidates to suppress non-target anomalies while preserving strong thermal detections. Experiments using 36 Wide Swath Imager scenes, near-contemporaneous Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite observations, field surveys in Anhui Province, and 260 Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer scenes support the method’s use for weak fire candidate screening under heterogeneous thermal backgrounds. Targeted field surveys found fresh crop residue burn marks at 10 of 12 selected T0 candidate sites (83.3%). This proportion applies only to the surveyed candidate set and does not represent an estimate of overall detection accuracy. In the MODIS transfer experiment, detections near industrial facilities decreased from 45.17% for the official products to 7.92% with the transferred method. The proposed framework supports the regional screening of low-intensity fire candidates and targeted field verification, with persistent heat source information providing contextual constraints.

title: Joint Assimilation of FY-3E Microwave Sounding and Ground-Based Microwave Radiometer Observations Incorporating AI-Based Cloudy-Sky Profile Retrievals over Complex Terrain on the Eastern Margin of the Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Forecasting convective precipitation over complex terrain requires accurate thermodynamic initialization. We developed a WRFDA 3D-Var framework combining nominally clear-sky FY-3E MWTS-3/MWHS-2 radiances, artificial-neural-network (ANN)-retrieved cloudy-sky thermodynamic profiles, and ground-based microwave radiometer (MWR) profiles. In a 5–15 July 2024 inner-domain sample, cloud routing assigned 66.1% of MWTS-3 and 66.9% of MWHS-2 fields of view to the cloudy-sky pathway. Independent radiosonde validation yielded RMSEs of 2.537 K for land temperature and 1.071 g kg−1 for bias-corrected land specific humidity, although a −1.748 K cold bias remained in temperature. Principal precipitation comparisons of four experiments (CTRL, FY, MWR, and FY-MWR) used a common CV7 background-error covariance configuration across nine daily forecasts over Chongqing during 7–15 July. During the principal 10–11 July event, MWR performed comparatively well at selected light-to-moderate precipitation thresholds, whereas FY-MWR had the highest TS at the highest 24 h thresholds. In pooled nine-day verification, CTRL retained the highest threat scores at 0.1–50 mm, while FY-MWR had the highest point estimate at 100 mm (0.083 versus 0.048 for CTRL); however, the paired bootstrap confidence interval for the FY-MWR-minus-CTRL difference included zero. Instability, convective inhibition, moisture-flux convergence, and vertical-motion diagnostics showed time-dependent relationships with precipitation differences. The results therefore indicate event- and intensity-dependent forecast responses rather than uniformly improved forecasts.

title: Quality-Gated Integration of Predicted Fields for Maize–Soybean Mapping with AlphaEarth Foundations
abstract: Timely field-level crop mapping remains difficult where current labels and reliable parcel boundaries are scarce. This study examined whether 2024 AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) annual embeddings could support maize–soybean mapping through unsupervised clustering followed by label-assisted semantic assignment and whether Fields of the World (FTW) predictions could convert pixel clusters into reliable parcel-level maps. The 64-dimensional AEF features at 10 m resolution were clustered without crop labels in an agricultural region of northern Northeast China. After the cluster solution was fixed, the field observations were used for semantic assignment and spatially blocked assessment. At the 652 route-based reference points collected in this study, direct AEF clustering yielded F1-scores of 0.944 for maize and 0.942 for soybean, with a macro-F1 of 0.943 for binary maize–soybean retrieval. Unconditional parcel assignment increased spatial regularity but reduced agreement with the reference observations. A quality gate based on pixel support, within-field purity, and under-segmentation risk retained a macro-F1 of 0.936 while reducing small patches by 31.0%. Selective use of predicted fields reduced fragmentation while preserving most of the sample-based accuracy of direct AEF clustering, offering a way to control the loss of pixel-level crop information during parcel aggregation.

title: Orientation-Aware Feature Flow Network for Oriented Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Remote sensing oriented object detection faces the challenge of maintaining consistent rotational geometric information throughout feature representation, cross-scale propagation, and bounding-box localization. To address this issue, this paper proposes a direction–scale collaborative optimization method for oriented object detection. A frozen DINOv3 encoder is adopted as the semantic feature source to enhance target discrimination in complex backgrounds through global semantic modeling and dense feature representation. Rotation-Oriented Space-to-Depth Convolution (ROSPD) is introduced to preserve fine-grained spatial structures and local directional-response cues during downsampling. In addition, a Rotation-Aware Residual Fusion (RARF) module estimates local axial agreement between adjacent feature levels and uses it to condition residual multi-scale fusion. A ProbIoU–NWD joint loss with deterministic target-size-adaptive weighting is further constructed: it emphasizes NWD supervision for small objects and gradually returns to ProbIoU as target size increases, thereby improving localization stability under low-overlap conditions. Experiments on DIOR-R and DOTA-v1.5 demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves the detection and localization performance of multi-scale oriented objects in complex remote sensing scenes.

title: A Spectral–Spatial Fusion Network for Hyperspectral Small Water Body Extraction
abstract: In hyperspectral imagery, small water bodies are often difficult to delineate due to their limited spatial extent, irregular shapes, and spectral similarity to surrounding land-cover types, which can lead to missed detections and fragmented boundaries. To address these challenges, this study proposes a spectral–spatial fusion network with parallel 3D CNN and ResNet-50 branches to extract complementary spectral–spatial and hierarchical spatial features. A progressive gated spectral–spatial fusion (PGSSF) module integrates these features across successive scales to help preserve weak water-body features and reduce background interference. The fused features are further processed by a scale-adaptive local–global (SALG) module, which combines local spatial details with broader contextual information to better characterize narrow watercourses and their continuity. Experiments were conducted using hyperspectral imagery from the Dongting Lake region, with comparisons against the normalized difference water index (NDWI), U-Net, Swin Transformer, and WaterFormer. The proposed method achieved a Water IoU of 80.68%, a recall of 90.33%, and an F1-score of 89.31%, with Water IoU exceeding that of WaterFormer by 4.76 percentage points. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed method for regional small-water-body mapping and surface-water monitoring.
