title: A first application of split conformal prediction for dose prediction in knowledge-based radiotherapy planning
abstract: Radiation therapy treatment planning is a labour-intensive process prone to inter-expert variability. Deep learning (DL) dose prediction can accelerate this process, but most DL models do not quantify their reliability. In this study, we construct prediction intervals for DL-based radiotherapy dose prediction using split conformal prediction (CP), a model-agnostic and distribution-free method for uncertainty quantification that provides finite-sample coverage guarantees. We propose patient-level nonconformity scores obtained by aggregating voxelwise scores. Specifically, we formulate a maximum aggregation construction, which guarantees simultaneous coverage of the true dose in all voxels of a future patient with at least a user-defined probability, and a quantile-based construction, which guarantees, with the same probability lower bound, that a future patient attains a prescribed minimum level of voxel coverage. We also investigate groupwise calibration for region-specific guarantees and predictive uncertainty scaling for locally adaptive prediction intervals. The methods are evaluated on head-and-neck cases using a deep ensemble model. The proposed constructions achieved empirical coverage consistent with the nominal levels. Maximum aggregation led to conservative prediction intervals, whereas quantile aggregation produced narrower intervals. Groupwise calibration and uncertainty scaling reduced interval widths in some anatomical regions, while providing region-specific guarantees and local adaptivity. This is the first application of split CP to radiotherapy dose prediction. The explicit patient-level coverage guarantees offer a more interpretable characterisation of prediction reliability than raw uncertainty estimates. Split CP could help clinicians assess the reliability of model predictions and identify cases requiring further review.

title: C$^2$-Routing: Complementary Cropping and Compression for Efficient Vision-Language Inference
abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) imposes substantial computational overhead on vision-language models (VLMs), motivating model-agnostic input reduction methods that can be readily applied across diverse VLMs, including in black-box settings. Simply enforcing a visual-token cap reduces computation, but it can discard information needed to answer the question. A single reduction strategy also struggles to accommodate different scenarios. Our key observation is that cropping and compression are complementary: cropping highlights small targets and local details, whereas whole-image compression better preserves context for large targets or distributed evidence. Based on this observation, we propose C$^2$-Routing, which adaptively selects cropping or compression according to the input image and question. Since both strategies may still discard key information, we further design a safety gate that uses the predicted joint correctness distribution under original and reduced inputs to guide fallback and protect accuracy. To accommodate consumer GPU resource constraints, all training and evaluation experiments run on RTX 3090 GPUs. To measure gains beyond token capping, we use full-image baselines with the same cap of 1,024 visual tokens. We conduct extensive evaluation on three VLMs and 18 datasets spanning local details, global scenes, scene text, and documents. With the visual budget already capped, C$^2$-Routing further reduces end-to-end FLOPs by 36.53% and visual tokens by 42.36% on average, with a mean relative task-score decrease of only 0.77%.

title: TanCRAFT: Context-Reasoned Anticipatory Feedback for Assembly Tasks
abstract: Preventing human error in physical assembly tasks requires assistance systems that can intervene before mistakes are made. This is especially challenging in settings where users are free to choose the construction order and correctness depends on the evolving assembly rather than a fixed next step. We present TanCRAFT, a four-stage real-time predictive assistance system that tracks the scene state, reasons about the current partial assembly, forecasts the near-future motion of manipulated pieces, and intervenes when the predicted placement is incompatible with the target. We instantiate our framework and confirm its effectiveness in a controlled tangram assembly task through offline benchmarks and a within-subject user study. Our findings show that the predictive feedback significantly reduces mistakes relative to unguided and reactive sessions, while yielding the lowest mean perceived workload and shortest mean completion time. Overall, these results demonstrate the value of predictive feedback for error prevention and provide a step toward cost-aware assistance for automation and human-robot workcells.

title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
abstract: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. Yet existing evaluations obscure this search process, making it difficult to understand how LLMs explore the space of research ideas and what limits their progress. We introduce Re-Search, which adapts the format of Twenty Questions to research ideation: given only the research problem of a published paper, a model must rediscover the paper's core idea by asking yes-or-no questions. Built from 200 ICML 2026 papers, Re-Search tracks how a model's idea evolves as it asks questions and receives binary oracle feedback, isolating ideation from execution. Across six recent LLMs, nearly all progress happens within the first 30 of 100 questions, which largely decide how the game ends; after that, most models plateau. Through controlled interventions on the candidate questions and the hypothesis space, we find that the bottleneck is generation, not judgment: models recognize a good idea or a good question when one is offered, but often cannot produce it on their own. We further analyze the ideation traces and find that models fail by either over-exploiting one direction or over-exploring too many. These findings point to concrete design principles for autoresearch systems: since models can judge candidates they cannot produce, enriching the search with externally sourced ideas and questions may be more effective than improving any single model's generation ability.

title: RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval
abstract: Cross-sensor remote sensing image retrieval aims to find scenes with the same content across heterogeneous sensors, such as SAR and optical or panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) imagery, without manual labels. Existing self-supervised methods either reconstruct sensor-specific pixel detail, align each image only with its co-registered twin, or rely on large transformers with 118-173M parameters (and up to 398M). We introduce RS-JEPA, a compact joint-embedding predictive framework built on a Vision Mamba encoder shared by both sensors. Since a state-space encoder reads an image as an ordered sequence of patches, we propose scan-path views, which treat two reading orders of the same image as two views with identical pixels and predict the hidden patches in one order from the visible patches in the other.To keep this prediction challenging, we propose Adversarial View Coupling (AVC), which learns the hardest split of the visible patches, and a neighbourhood consensus loss that aligns the scene similarities of both sensors. Extensive experiments on SAR-optical (BEN-14K, CBRSIR-VS) and PAN-MS (DSRSID) benchmarks demonstrate that RS-JEPA achieves the highest F1@5 among twelve re-implemented methods (72.92, 80.35 and 94.43) with a retrieval network of only 3.88M parameters (14.57M in training, 8-16times fewer than prior JEPA retrievers). Like prior methods, RS-JEPA trains on co-registered pairs. Our results highlight reading order as a source of self-supervised views. code: https://github.com/Tanishq251/RSJEPA.

title: Measuring Robustness and Efficiency in a Connectome-Constrained Fly Visual System Model: Linking an Adversarial and a Perceptual Illusion
abstract: Biological visual systems compute reliably under tight metabolic and wiring constraints, whereas artificial vision systems consume far more energy and can be sensitive to adversarial perturbations. Whether networks with brain-like wiring are more robust at lower computational cost is unclear. We address this by benchmarking a task-optimized, continuous-time recurrent neural network of the fly visual system constrained by its synaptic connectome (FlyNet) against artificial neural networks. We compare it against CNNs, RAFT, and continuous-time recurrent neural networks without detailed connectome constraints (sCTRNN, CTRNN) on a collision-detection task within a differentiable 3D rendering pipeline. FlyNet is adversarially vulnerable but, relative to its compute, more robust to common video corruptions than RAFT, while using up to five orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs. The CTRNNs remain more robust than FlyNet across almost all tested perturbations, suggesting that connectome constraints benefit efficiency, through their low edge count, over robustness. Recurrence improves robustness to white-box attacks in RAFT and temporal context improves robustness to common corruptions. FlyNet's position and velocity representations degrade under adversarial textures but recover under counterfactual textures that restore correct classification while staying equally far from training, ruling out unfamiliar textures as the cause of failure. The reverse-phi illusion similarly disrupts these representations and inverts the same low-level motion statistic as the adversarial textures. Optimizing this input statistic alone, without access to the network, suffices to induce classification failure, attributing both perturbations to the same circuit vulnerability. Connectome-constrained models can thus surface adversarial failure mechanisms as testable hypotheses about biological perceptual vulnerabilities.

title: Annular Counterexamples and Skew-Shape Block Identities
abstract: We establish four connected results on weighted order ideals, cluster coefficients, and block-statistic enumerators. First, we give a counterexample to Theorem 14 of Kang, Lee and Lim (European Journal of Combinatorics, 2026): in the rank-two annular cluster model, a single bridging-lamination coefficient row produces $1+q^2$, contradicting the asserted unimodality. We identify the unsupported initial case in their published induction. Second, we refute their log-concavity Conjecture 1: the same gap example violates log-concavity, and a further single-curve computation gives the full-support polynomial $1+2q+7q^2+10q^3+9q^4+4q^5+q^6$, which also fails log-concavity. Third, we establish the skew-shape block-statistic identity proposed in Kahane's Conjecture 4.4 (arXiv:2607.11225v1) for arbitrary finite skew Young diagrams, under an explicitly specified root-exclusion convention. Its proof combines commuting tableau-transfer matrices, a connected-block inverse kernel, and finite polynomial differential equations; the corresponding mathematical statements have Lean 4/Mathlib formalizations. Fourth, we derive a bivariate block refinement whose coefficients are nonnegative after shifting the order parameter by one and, when necessary, multiplying by a monomial in the weight parameter. We specify the correction to the printed root convention, confirmed by Kahane in correspondence, and the geometric sign and specialization conventions clarified by the relevant authors for the annular examples.

title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
abstract: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls. These agents achieve up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, exceeding observed expert performance. LLM-guided feature discovery generally outperforms direct reasoning, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves open-weight models, enabling them to match or surpass closed-source frontier models in our evaluations. These results establish Pyrite as a challenging test of pose-ranking ability and highlight LLM-guided feature discovery as a promising approach to interpret and combine the outputs of computational chemistry tools.

title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
abstract: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes. The results illustrate where this generality remains computationally practical and where overhead is substantial. Library is available on GitHub at https://github.com/alexshtf/torchcurves.

title: When Evaluators of AI Agents Disagree: An Empirical Study of Native Scoring, LLM Judges, and Commit-Boundary Checks on tau2-bench
abstract: Agentic workflows, in which a large language model (LLM) calls tools to read and write data, are evaluated in two ways. Benchmarks compare the final state against a gold answer. Deployed services have none; an LLM judge reads the transcript and decides. Practice treats the two as interchangeable. This paper measures whether they are. We ran 2,160 episodes in tau2-bench's airline and retail domains and recorded every database write. We scored each episode four ways: native scoring against gold state, an LLM judge, that judge given the policy document, and the boundary evaluator, a minimal rule-based check of whether a write was expected against whether one occurred in the trace. Two annotators independently labeled 120 episodes for task correctness, policy compliance, and commitment correctness. The judge repeated its verdict 98.2% of the time but agreed with native scoring on 56.2%. In 11 episodes the agent executed a forbidden write. The judge passed 10 to 11, with or without the policy or transcript. A stronger judge still passed 6. The boundary evaluator, with no model call, caught all 11; no judge significantly exceeded it on human labels. Forbidden writes occurred in 11.1% of episodes without gates. Verification, correction, and safe-termination gates did not reduce them significantly. The traces show a candidate cause: the gates' evidence digest dropped the order status and customer authentication, so valid requests were rejected. The choice of evaluator decides the conclusion; the minimal check exposes failures the judges miss. Traces, code, prompts, and labels are released.

title: An Asynchronous Federated Learning Platform for Lung Adenocarcinoma Grading via Foundation Models and Structural Pruning
abstract: Classification of lung adenocarcinoma into poorly differentiated (PD) and well-to-moderately differentiated (WMD) subtypes plays an important role in patient survival; however, consistent classification is difficult due to inter-observer variability among pathologists. Collecting data from multiple hospitals is also challenging due to patient privacy concerns. This study proposes a web-based federated learning system that shares only locally trained model weights without sharing patient data between institutions. The UNI2 foundation model and CLAM-SB were used to classify pathological whole slide images. A four-client federated learning system was constructed, and the NLST cohort was reserved exclusively for external validation. In centralized evaluation, joint training with CPTAC and TCGA outperformed single-institution training on external validation, confirming the necessity of multi-institutional data integration. FedAvg, FedProx, FedBN, and FedNova were compared as federated learning algorithms under identical experimental conditions. Test AUC ranked as FedBN, FedProx, FedNova, and FedAvg. FedNova showed the most balanced classification performance between PD and WMD. L1-norm structural pruning at 20%, 30%, and 40% sparsity was applied to reduce model transmission size. FedAvg, FedProx, and FedBN showed a tendency of decreasing Test AUC under pruning, while FedNova achieved improved Test AUC across all sparsity levels. A web-based application was developed supporting slide upload, local training, AI classification, and attention heatmap-based visualization. The combination of FedNova and 40% pruning was confirmed as a practical approach that improves communication efficiency and classification performance while protecting patient privacy.

title: galpy with differentiable, accelerated backends: galactic dynamics in jax and PyTorch
abstract: We describe an extension of galpy, the Python library for galactic dynamics, that adds jax and PyTorch as computational backends alongside its existing numpy and C implementation. With it, galpy's gravitational potentials, orbit integration, action-angle transformations and their inverses, and distribution functions, including those for tidal streams, run on GPUs, can be compiled as part of a user's program, and can be differentiated with respect to their inputs and parameters, from the force at a point to the samples drawn from a distribution function. The user-facing design is kept simple: the active backend follows from the type of the arrays that are passed in, the galpy interface is unchanged, and the numpy path gives the same results as before. We describe the design of the backend framework and its implementation in each of galpy's modules, with examples of use, and we discuss its limitations. On a GPU, batches of orbits, samples from distribution functions, and stream models run one to five orders of magnitude faster than on a single CPU core. To illustrate the new capabilities, we present simple examples of fitting the Galactic potential with a hypervelocity star and of learning the inverse action-angle transformation with a neural network trained through galpy. An AI coding agent wrote essentially all of the code under the detailed direction and review of the human author, and we describe how we organized this work and how we established the correctness of the result. This work is the start of galpy's version 2, which is available at https://github.com/jobovy/galpy and documented at https://docs.galpy.org/en/v2/ .

title: AI-assisted search for self-compressing gigawatt subcycle field waveforms
abstract: We explore the physics behind pulse self-compression to high-power subcycle field waveforms and search for the optimal regimes of such compression over the parameter space as laid out by multimode nonlinear dynamics of ultrashort laser pulses in gas-filled hollow fibers. With the pertinent physical criteria for pulse contrast and no pulse breakup formalized as operational stopping rules, a radical speedup of such search is achieved by delegating its tedious preliminary stages to generative pretrained transformer models. The precise adjustment of self-compression dynamics vis-a-vis the desired compressed pulse output is, however, not yet delegable to AI agents, as the criteria for such search are still largely subjective, operating with fine aspects of subcycle field structure, not yet formalizable as clear search-stopping instructions. An ultimate precision in such subcycle field engineering is attainable via a management of field-phase-sensitive nonlinear processes, enabling pulse self-compression to high-power subcycle field waveforms and opening paths toward fiber-optic attosecond lightwave engineering.

title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
abstract: Today's AI workloads are rapidly changing: new models are released more often, model architectures are increasingly diverse, and traffic distributions change frequently. The challenge we face at Together AI is continual optimization for these changing workloads. Compiling a deployment into an optimized forward pass is a challenge that is well-suited for agent hill-climbing. Existing systems struggle with continual compilation due to a tradeoff between measurement throughput and fidelity. Many systems use agents to optimize individual kernels from the inference forward pass using offline benchmarks, but timings are low-fidelity because of data-dependent behavior in primitives like mixture-of-experts (MoE). On the other hand, systems use agents to directly optimize end-to-end engines but suffer from slow engine launch times. To address these challenges, we build Together Compiler (TKCC), the first truly continual agent loop designed for AI inference optimization. To address the throughput-fidelity tradeoff, we propose: (1) a Tiered Persistent Engine that decouples engine launch overheads from forward pass computation; (2) a cost model to select the parallelism configurations that seed the optimization process. We also conduct extensive ablations on agent context management and present our insights on deploying TKCC in production. TKCC outperforms highly-optimized hand-written Megakernels on the Llama 1B workhorse workload by up to 1.7x and the best open source engines on the latest frontier models (Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, DeepSeek v4.1 Flash) across hardware platforms by up to 2.6x higher TPS on the InferenceX benchmark. TKCC also sets the state-of-the-art performance at batch size 1, with 1111 TPS on M3.1 Flash and 1205 TPS on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash. Finally, TKCC generalizes beyond frontier language model inference. TKCC serves trillions of tokens across our production fleet.

title: What Entropy-Based View Selection Cannot See: An Audit of Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-language models such as CLIP can classify images into categories they were never explicitly trained to recognize, but accuracy degrades when test images differ in style or source from their training data. A common remedy generates randomly cropped and flipped copies of each test image, called views, and combines their predictions. Since some views miss the object, methods must identify which views to trust. The dominant approach uses prediction entropy to measure confidence and retains the most certain views. Other methods use signals such as embedding typicality. Despite repeated refinements of these scoring functions, the information they rely on, the model's own response to each view, remains largely unexamined. We investigate this choice while holding other pipeline stages fixed. First, we show that view selection, rather than the gradient update, accounts for almost all accuracy gains. We then examine whether entropy identifies useful views when predictions are wrong, despite at least one view predicting the correct class. In these cases, entropy ranks correct views above incorrect ones no better than chance, recovering only about one-twentieth of the accuracy recovered by an oracle over the same views. This finding holds across two image encoders and under a control ruling out an obvious statistical artifact. An exact analysis explains this limitation: entropy measures confidence but not which class a view favors. We identify an unused signal already available in the augmentation pipeline: the fraction of the original image retained by each crop. Ranking views by this quantity improves accuracy on 14 of 15 benchmark datasets over entropy and on 11 of 15 over the strongest scoring function tested. A pre-method measurement also predicts which datasets benefit.

title: Deep Unrolling of Lanczos-based Laplacian Eigensolver for Crop Classification in Satellite Images
abstract: Per-pixel crop classification in satellite images is an important pre-processing step in remote crop monitoring. Leveraging progress in signed graph signal processing, we build an interpretable and lightweight neural network for binary crop classification (e.g., corn versus non-corn) in two stages: i) learn a signed graph from data, and ii) unroll a Lanczos-based eigensolver to compute the eigenvector $\u_1$ associated with the smallest eigenvalue of a hybrid graph Laplacian $\cL$ for spectral clustering. Specifically, we first construct a near-balanced signed graph $\cG^s$, where signed edge weights $w_{i,j}\in(-1,1)$ are computed from learned feature distances $d_{i,j}$ via a hyperbolic tangent mapping. Given $\cG^s$, we estimate $\u_1$ by unrolling the Lanczos algorithm and use $\mathrm{sign}(\u_1)$ for binary classification. Mathematically, we develop a theorem establishing conditions under which $\u_1$ can be well approximated after finite Lanczos iterations. Motivated by this theorem, we relax the classical Lanczos orthogonality constraints during unrolling and optimize end-to-end classification performance while promoting the derived conditions for accurate eigenvector approximation. Experiments on real-world Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel imagery show classification performance comparable to state-of-the-art deep learning models while reducing parameters by up to two orders of magnitude.

title: Martingale posteriors for flexible regression via recursive least squares
abstract: Predictive Bayes quantifies uncertainty by specifying a sequence of one-step-ahead predictive distributions, inducing a martingale posterior without an explicit prior. Existing parametric constructions rely on stochastic-gradient updates and have seen limited development for flexible regression. We propose a predictive Bayes framework based on recursive least squares, whose martingale posterior has an explicit representation: given future covariates, it is the law of the posterior mean plus a weighted series of independent draws from the standardized predictive distribution. The posterior mean is a penalized least squares estimator, available in closed form and invariant to data ordering, whereas the predictive distribution, for example heavy tailed, is chosen separately without changing the estimator or algorithm. We derive the exact posterior variance under a known design and an asymptotically Gaussian approximation, and obtain the martingale posterior in closed form for Gaussian predictive distributions. Posterior draws are independent by construction, with a known truncation error, and require no Markov chain Monte Carlo. The construction extends to additive, mixed and Gaussian process models. In simulations and an analysis of NHANES triglyceride data, the method attains accuracy comparable to that of a fully Bayesian model with the same response distribution at a fraction of its computational cost.

title: Don't Match the Noise: Distribution Matching under Unknown Measurement Error with an Audit Sample
abstract: Real-world machine learning systems often operate on imperfect measurements: sensors are noisy, annotations are produced by non-experts, and scientific observations are often indirect. In these settings, classic distribution comparison tools such as maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) can be systematically biased, matching artifacts of the measurement process rather than the underlying mechanisms of interest. We study a practical regime in which noisy observations are abundant, but only a small audited subset contains ground-truth measurements. We propose measurement-error-corrected MMD (MEC-MMD), an audit-based estimator that debiases kernel evaluations without requiring a noise model. MEC-MMD is exactly unbiased for the oracle MMD under simple random auditing, admits an explicit variance decomposition, and is consistent for the population MMD, achieving the standard $O_p(N^{-1/2})$ rate when the audit size scales with the dataset. We demonstrate the utility of distributional matching with MEC-MMD loss for both parameter estimation and unsupervised applications, showing that MEC-MMD consistently outperforms MMD and alternative methods. These results provide a principled foundation for robust distribution comparison, simulation-based inference, and learning in noisy real-world machine learning pipelines.

title: RECALL: Real-Time Recalibration of Multi-Camera Rigs via Learned OEM-Anchored Residuals
abstract: Multi-camera rigs ship pre-calibrated from the manufacturer, but their calibration goes stale each time the rig is repositioned, and drifts continuously through wear, thermal cycling, and vibration. Recovering it on-the-fly is hard: classical bundle adjustment needs a fresh multi-view capture and a global optimization whose cost grows with the rig, ruling out real-time use. In this paper we present RECALL, a feed-forward method that recalibrates a movable multi-camera rig in a single pass. From the nominal OEM calibration as an anchor and a brief observation of a known object, it predicts each camera's current intrinsics and extrinsics, written as a shared global rotation of the rig composed with a small per-camera drift. Instead of regressing the calibration in one shot, RECALL refines its estimate with a learned, rig-coupled recurrent operator that reprojects through a differentiable projection and applies attention across the cameras at each step, and solves for the shared rotational gauge in-network with a learned Gauss-Newton step rather than regressing it. Because the ground truth is synthesizable, we train entirely on data generated on-the-fly and need no captured dataset. On a synthetic 10-camera benchmark, RECALL is more accurate than per-camera and rig-coupled joint bundle adjustment ($0.26^\circ$ vs $0.47^\circ$ rotation, $5.4$ vs $8.9$ px focal) and runs about $10^5\times$ faster at about $0.12$ ms per rig. On real data (TotalCapture, CMU Panoptic) it matches or beats offline rig-coupled bundle adjustment on absolute and relative rotation while running four-to-five orders of magnitude faster, and on the Panoptic surround rig it also matches the strongest image-only foundation models (VGGT, VGGT-$Ω$, $π^3$) on relative pose while staying metric and about $15\times$ more accurate in focal length. Code: https://github.com/theICTlab/RECALL-multicam

authors.name: Mario Alberto Tapia de la Cruz

title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
abstract: All social interactions are situated in time. Previous studies have shown that humans are able to use implicit temporal cues, such as the duration of a pause, to infer others' mental states. But how do humans use temporal cues for dynamic, fine-grained social coordination? And can AI systems do the same, without ``experiencing'' continuous real-time as humans do? We study these questions using a cooperative card game task called The Mind, which requires players to achieve a shared goal across repeated interactions but forbids explicit communication: the only available signal is the passage of time. We evaluate 150 humans, and two classes of AI models which reflect different ways of operationalizing time in artificial systems: computer-use agents (CUAs), and standard text-prompted LLMs. We find that human behavior is best captured by a Bayesian strategy that infers a partner's belief from their timing---and similarly for frontier models. However, unlike humans, none of the tested models seem to efficiently adapt their behaviors to their partners' over the course of the game. From a cognitive perspective, our findings suggest that humans perform implicit probabilistic reasoning about continuous-time signals in dynamic social settings, and that such reasoning mechanisms may emerge without real-time experience. Practically, our study highlights new challenges for AI systems to coordinate efficiently with other agents by learning to interpret and adapt to their implicit signals in dynamic settings.

title: From Classification to Generation: Vision-Language Models for Roman Imperial Coin Description
abstract: Cataloguing a Roman Imperial coin involves reading its legends and identifying its imagery in order to match it to an entry in the standard reference catalogue. Previous work has automated individual parts of this process, such as identifying the issuer or recognizing reverse motifs, by formulating each part as a classification task over a predefined set of labels. We instead formulate coin description as image-to-text generation and adapt an open-weight vision-language model (VLM), Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, to four tasks: transcribing the obverse and reverse legends, and describing the obverse and reverse imagery. To obtain training data, we convert approximately 30,000 auction records into structured image-text pairs. We separate the two sides of each coin, extract and normalize legends and descriptions, and standardize obverse descriptions against a bust-type taxonomy. We then train a separate low-rank adapter for each task on a single 20GB GPU, and evaluate each task with metrics that we define to capture the key components of numismatic descriptions. The adapted models outperform both the unadapted base model and GPT-4.1 on all four tasks, reducing the normalized edit distance of legend transcriptions by over 40% relative to GPT-4.1. The improvement is smaller, but still present, on legends absent from the training data.

title: Locating Debunkers for Rumor Mitigation in Directed Networks
abstract: Rumors can spread widely through social networks, making the selection of a limited number of debunkers to disseminate corrective information important. Existing centrality-based methods only consider the individual influence of a node on spreading processes. Those individually influential nodes often have heavily overlapping influence ranges, resulting in a limited number of users they can cover. To address this problem, we propose the so-called Hybrid Marginal Influence (HMI) framework, which combines node centrality with additional audience coverage provided by each candidate and adaptively balances these two factors through a greedy selection procedure. We further develop the Debunker-Augmented SIR (DA-SIR) model for the propagation of rumors and corrective information. Experiments on ten real-world directed networks show that HMI generally selects debunkers with broader audience coverage than conventional centrality-based methods, accompanied by a lower final cumulative fraction of users who repost the rumor.

title: Open Challenges and Opportunities in Human-Agent Systems
abstract: Agentic AI systems increasingly undertake extended tasks and act on people's behalf, making human-agent interaction central to their effectiveness. Successful interaction requires understanding human perspectives, coordinating complementary capabilities, and maintaining productive relationships within socio-technical environments. This paper examines how foundations developed by the Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems (AAMAS) community inform these demands. We consider interactions ranging from individual human-agent partnerships to teams and larger groups, where participants differ in their roles, decision authority, capabilities, and objectives. We organize computational approaches around the connected challenges of understanding others and deciding how to interact with them. Theory of Mind, belief-desire-intention architectures, goal and plan recognition, inverse planning, and recursive reasoning provide mechanisms for representing and inferring partially observable mental states. Observer-aware planning, model reconciliation, and decision-theoretic communication connect these inferences to action, explanation, and information exchange. Together with shared autonomy, argumentation, and cooperative inverse reinforcement learning, these approaches offer foundations for agentic systems that account for evolving human knowledge, intentions, and expectations. We argue that progress requires treating human interaction as an ongoing decision problem shaped by uncertainty, interdependence, and potentially conflicting objectives.

title: Tideway: Phase-Aware Tiered Memory Management for MoE Inference on Consumer Devices
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly becoming a dominant paradigm for AI applications. Recently, there is a growing demand to deploy large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models locally on consumer PCs to balance data privacy, API costs, and inference efficiency. However, unlike datacenter servers with abundant DRAM, consumer devices are tightly constrained in both GPU VRAM and host RAM, forcing massive MoE weights to spill across VRAM, host RAM, and SSD. Under such spilling, we observe that existing systems fail to fully utilize this memory hierarchy, treating the tiers as independent caches and thrashing in inference. We present TIDEWAY, a system for efficient inference of large MoE models on memory-constrained consumer devices. Our core insight is to manage host RAM and GPU VRAM as a unified memory pool. Within this pool, TIDEWAY couples phase-aware memory layouts, which adapt to the distinct access patterns of prefill and decode, with an execution engine that optimizes CUDA Graph execution under expert paging. Our evaluations on representative consumer hardware with frontier MoE models demonstrate that TIDEWAY significantly outperforms state-of-the-art systems. On average, TIDEWAY achieves speedups of 1.97x in end-to-end latency and 2.40x in Time-to-First-Token (TTFT), along with 1.61x higher decode throughput against the fastest baseline. Our source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Afterglow231/Tideway .

title: Generalize Then Personalize: Wearable-Based Heart Rate Forecasting Under Scarce Ruck-March Data
abstract: Heart rate (HR) forecasting may provide advance information about near-future cardiovascular response, potentially supporting physiological monitoring and workload-management decisions during ruck marching. However, robust model development is constrained by the difficulty of collecting large-scale ruck-march datasets, creating a scarce-data problem in which models must generalize across participants while adapting to individuals from limited personal data. To address this problem, we benchmark population-only training (POT), personalized-from-scratch training (PFST), and population-pretrained fine-tuning (PPFT) for HR forecasting during loaded ruck marching using data from eight active-duty U.S. Army medics across thirteen sessions. LSTM, Attention-LSTM, and CNN-LSTM backbones were evaluated against a persistence baseline at 30 s and 60 s horizons. Across all neural architectures and horizons, PPFT yielded lower mean MAE, RMSE, and endpoint MAE than both POT and PFST. Participant-level paired analysis after averaging across three training seeds showed that, relative to PFST, PPFT reduced trajectory MAE by 2.22-4.30 bpm and endpoint MAE by 1.24-2.88 bpm. All six trajectory-MAE comparisons remained significant after Holm adjustment ($p_{adj}$ = 0.0469), while four of six endpoint-MAE comparisons remained significant after adjustment. At 30 s, persistence achieved the lowest MAE (3.555 $\pm$ 1.274 bpm), while CNN-LSTM PPFT achieved the lowest RMSE (4.669 $\pm$ 1.916 bpm); LSTM PPFT achieved the lowest endpoint MAE (5.093 $\pm$ 2.365 bpm). At 60 s, Attention-LSTM PPFT achieved the lowest MAE (5.573 $\pm$ 1.939 bpm) and RMSE (7.134 $\pm$ 2.260 bpm), while CNN-LSTM PPFT achieved the lowest endpoint MAE (7.553 $\pm$ 2.357 bpm). These results suggest that population pretraining followed by participant-specific fine-tuning may provide a practical strategy for scarce-data wearable HR forecasting.

title: Fumigador UAV (vehículo aéreo no tripulado) para 1 hectárea
abstract: Precision agriculture has emerged as a technological strategy to enhance the efficiency of agricultural systems through the integration of digital tools and automated processes. In this context, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have gained increasing relevance due to their ability to optimize agrochemical application, reduce operational costs, and minimize environmental impacts. The objective of this research was to conceptually design a zeppelin-type unmanned aerial vehicle for spraying corn crops covering areas of up to one hectare. The study adopted an applied research approach with a descriptive scope and a non-experimental research design, supported by a comprehensive documentary review and the application of the Jenkins methodology for the systematic development of the proposed prototype. Key design variables included payload capacity, flight endurance, spraying coverage, aerodynamic stability, and operational efficiency, while also considering applicable aeronautical regulations. The proposed design demonstrates potential advantages over conventional spraying methods by reducing application time, improving the efficiency of agrochemical use, decreasing operator exposure to hazardous substances, and increasing agricultural productivity. It is concluded that the incorporation of a zeppelin-type UAV constitutes a viable technological alternative to strengthen precision agriculture, promote sustainable farming practices, and support the modernization of agricultural activities, particularly for small-scale producers.
journal: Desarrollo sustentable, Negocios, Emprendimiento y Educación

title: Explicit numerical simulations of hailstorm seeding with a three–moment microphysics cloud–resolving model: a comparison of two operational methodologies for hail suppression
abstract: Increasing economic losses from hailstorms sustain the relevance of hail suppression as a weather modification technique. However, quantifying operational cloud seeding effectiveness remains challenging due to the inherent nonlinearity and complexity of convective processes. In this study, we use the 3D numerical model ARPS (Advanced Regional Prediction System), featuring a three-moment microphysical scheme, to simulate supercell seeding. The model was enhanced by implementing two-moment aerosol microphysics accounting for all known scavenging processes and parameterizations of all four ice-nucleating modes. Prognostic equations for aerosol mixing ratio and number concentration in air and each hydrometeor category were calculated. Simulations ran at high spatial resolution (500 m horizontal, 250 m vertical) over a 3 h evolution period. This approach enables detailed simulation of processes associated with cloud seeding. Two operational seeding strategies were investigated: RHSS (Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia, 2023) and AB23 (Abshaev et al., 2023). Results indicate that both strategies modify surface hail characteristics by reducing kinetic energy, potentially mitigating crop damage. Total surface hail kinetic energy decreased by 27 % (RHSS) and 17.9 % (AB23). Notably, moderate-energy surface areas (KE flux >100 J m −2 ) decreased by 36.6 % and 38.6 %, while high-intensity areas (KE flux >300 J m −2 ) dropped by 66 % and 88 %, respectively. Nonparametric Wilcoxon signed-rank testing verified that both methods cause statistically significant changes ( p <0.05 and p <0.01) in surface hail diameter and kinetic energy flux throughout the storm lifecycle.

title: Solarspitzengesetz: Potentials for Energy Optimization of Multi Use Battery Storages
abstract: This paper analyses the operational and economic impacts of the MiSpeL regulation (status 10/2025) on residential PV battery systems. It models and compares the two new accounting options introduced by §19 EEG: the Abgrenzungsoption (differentiation option) and the Pauschaloption (flat‑rate option). A MILP approach is used to represent the regulatory rules and to optimize arbitrage and self‑consumption strategies. The two options create distinct operational incentives. The Abgrenzungsoption increases storage-grid-interaction that may produce distinct power peaks. In contrast, the Pauschaloption decouples storage dispatch from local generation and reacts primarily to national price signals. Economic outcomes depend strongly on storage size; small storages favour the Pauschaloption, while very large storages may benefit more from the Abgrenzungsoption. In all simulations the new accounting options outrun the already existing exclusivity option. The complex structure of the new regulation however emphasizes that simulation tools are recommended to support regulatory design.

title: Significant Nameplate Overrating of Current PV-Modules and Their Impacts
abstract: Global PV deployment is surging, with Germany adding ~18 GWp in 2024 and 2025 and total capacity reaching ~118 GWp by end-2025. Worldwide, DC nameplate capacity rose from ~1,620 to ~2,760 GWp between 2023 and 2025 amid a rapid shift from PERC to TOPCon and intense cost pressure. While degradation is acknowledged, we focus on discrepancies between module nameplate ratings and delivered power, and on a pragmatic, cost-effective measurement approach to reduce uncertainty, minimizing financial risks, and therefore improving bankability. Manufacturers typically declare positive binning (+5/−0 W) and ±3% tolerances; laboratories report ~±2% measurement uncertainty (MU). Measuring sets of modules and cross-validating a subset in a second, independently calibrated laboratory can reduce effective MU by ~40% (±2% to ~±1.2%). Despite literature indicating average overrating of ~1.3%, our multi-laboratory tests on Tier‑1 batches show underperformance of ~3% or more relative to nameplate - beyond MU and financially acceptable return expectations of 5 to 7%. We tested 10-30 modules per batch using LED AAA (Lab 1) and Xenon A+A+A+ (Lab 2) flashers. TOPCon hysteresis or dark storage effects were mitigated, if necessary, via multi-flash and brief light exposure, however, dark-storage effects were negligible (<0.1%). EL imaging revealed no severe defects (per VDE‑SPEC 90031). Manufacturer flasher lists matched binning, yet both labs measured ~3% lower power; inter-lab agreement was within 1%, reinforcing the validity of the offset. Aggregated 2024 to 2026 results show small within-batch dispersion but batch-to-batch shifts, including bimodal distributions; some outliers exhibited up to 10% overrating and then also often EL anomalies. Because DC underperformance is a persistent offset, a 3% shortfall raises LCOE by ~3%. Financially such increases, or the other way around, lower incomes will make such PV investments risky to not bankable. Systematic two-laboratory quality control reduces uncertainty, improves energy yield forecasts, and strengthens contractual claims for missing “Watt-peak”.

title: Preface
abstract: For more than 40 years, the PV Symposium held in Bad Staffelstein has been the central meeting place for expertise and networking in applied research and development in solar technology. With the 2026 claim "Rethinking Energy Supply: PV, Grids, Storage, and Sector Coupling," it focuses on the latest technical developments, current regulatory and political trends, and advances in research and application. As one of the most important drivers of innovation and the further development of a sustainable energy supply, the PV Symposium shapes the future of the photovoltaic industry. Two terawatts of PV capacity have already been installed worldwide. To achieve complete defossilization of all energy sectors, we need between 70 and 100 terawatts of PV capacity. This vision must be translated quickly and efficiently into future markets. This results in new tasks and challenges: On the one hand, it involves improving technical components and developing integrated photovoltaic solutions for optimal land use, as well as quality assurance in production and operation. On the other hand, the grid-supportive use of solar power – including grid stability, optimized self-consumption, storage integration, and more precise yield forecasts – is becoming increasingly important. In the future, solar power can no longer be considered in isolation but must be holistically integrated into the energy system. This requires functioning sector coupling. Energy storage systems such as batteries of all sizes, heat pumps, and e-mobility must be considered together and integrated systemically. This holistic approach is the key to innovation and new solutions. The PV Symposium is dedicated precisely to these system solutions and system technology. This industry gathering offers the ideal platform to discuss current issues, exchange knowledge, and present the latest developments. By publishing these proceedings, we ensure that the valuable knowledge exchanged during the conference reaches a wider audience, contributing to the ongoing dialogue and collaboration necessary to tackle the challenges faced by the photovoltaics sector. This documentation not only highlights the key results from the conference but also serves as a reference point for future work and a foundation for further collaboration between research, industry and policymaking In this context, the proceedings volume plays a particularly important role. It not only documents the thematic breadth and scientific depth of the symposium, it contributes to the visibility and long-term impact of the presented work and enable informed knowledge exchange well beyond the event itself.

title: Assessment of surface soil loss on erosion prone slopes
abstract: The study was conducted to comparatively assess quantitative soil loss, calculated using field data and mathematical models. The work was conducted from 1985 to 2026 on erosion-prone slopes of a watershed used in a contour-reclamation farming experiment in the Kursk region. The soil cover consists of typical chernozems and leached heavy loamy soils. A mathematical model of water erosion was used to predict average long-term soil loss. The second assessment method was geoinformation, with calculations based on a universal equation for soil loss due to erosion and coefficients established for the Central Black Earth Region. The calculations were based on a digital elevation model of the studied watershed. Field data on soil loss were obtained at runoff sites and calculated using the water-based method. An increase in the share of continuous winter crops in the cropped area structure contributed to a reduction in soil loss due to runoff in the spring. Based on field studies, soil erosion losses in the study area averaged 3.79 t/ha from 1985 to 2005, with a peak of 21.7 t/ha. In 2006-2026, the respective figures were 1.89 t/ha and 16.3 t/ha. Calculations using a mathematical model indicate higher losses (4.9 ± 0.2 t/ha), indicating an overestimation of these figures. A water erosion model-based forecast of probable average annual soil loss, taking into account the changed structure of cropped areas for the catchment area as a whole, revealed a trend toward an increasing contribution of rainfall to total soil loss compared to snowmelt runoff. This is consistent with field survey results and does not exceed the permissible erosive soil loss (3 t/ha).
journal: Achievements of Science and Technology in Agro-Industrial Complex

title: Development and testing of an online model for corn seed quality analysis using deep learning
abstract: The study was aimed to develop and test an online model based on YOLOv8n for detecting mechanical and biological damage to corn seeds based on RGB images, adapted for mobile applications. The work was carried out in 2025 in laboratory (artificial lighting with 4000 K fluorescent lamps) and field (natural daylight) conditions of the Cis-Ural forest-steppe zone of the Republic of Bashkortostan. The object was seeds of the Ross 190 MV and Ross 199 MV corn hybrids; shooting was taken with the main camera of a smartphone (64 MP, f / 1.7), 600 JPEG images with a resolution of 3000 × 4000 pixels were obtained. The dataset is annotated into two classes (healthy and damaged seeds) in Roboflow and divided into training (70 %), validation (15 %) and test (15 %) sets; the following augmentation was used: rotation of ±30°, change of brightness and contrast, scaling, reflection. The YOLOv8n model was trained for 150 epochs (batch 16, AdamW optimiser, initial learning rate of 0.001) on the Roboflow cloud platform. On the test set (90 images), the mAP@0.5 indicator was equal to 0.95; the detection accuracy of healthy seeds was 97.0 %, damaged ones – 93.0 %; recall for damaged ones was 87.5 %, accuracy – 85.4 %. The inference time via Roboflow Inference API was 150-300 ms with stable Wi-Fi (>50 Mbps) and up to 1-2 s with unstable cellular communication (3G/4G). The developed model ensures high accuracy and acceptable analysis speed, and is suitable for express quality control of seeds at storage and reception sites. Limitations include errors due to suboptimal lighting and seed overlap. The approach is scalable to other crops without changing the architecture.
journal: Achievements of Science and Technology in Agro-Industrial Complex

title: Glucocorticoid-Mediated Regulation of BDNF and Autophagy in Dentate Gyrus Neurons
abstract: Chronic stress is an important risk factor for depression and is associated with sutained glucocorticoid signaling and impaired hippocampal function. Prolonged exposure to corticosterone, a major glucocorticoid, can distrpt adult hippocampal neurogenesis (AHN) in the dentate gyrus (DG) and reduce brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), which contributes to the differentiation and maturation of adult-born neurons through TrkB signaling. This review focuses on the studies showing that chronic CORT exposure increases neuronal autophagy in the DG and reduces BDNF levels, and disccus the current evidence linking CORT-induced neural autophagy to BDNF loss. While inhibition of autophagy can restore BDNF and partially rescue impaired AHN, whether GR mediates CORT-induced autophagy in DG neurons remain unanswered. In addition, GR signaling may influence BDNF through autophagy-independent mechanisms, including direct regulation of BDNF transcription. Together, the current studies supports a potential model in which GR-mediated autophay coontributes to intracellular BDNF loss following chornic CORT. This propsoed mechanism provides a direction for further examing how prolonged glucocorticoid signaling participates in impaired AHN.

title: Substitution Boundaries of AI Agents in Team Collaboration: An Empirical Analysis Based on Front-Line Employees' Perceptions
abstract: With AI agents increasingly involved in teamwork, whether AI can substitute human collaboration has become a heated topic in academia. Large-model-driven agents are now capable of participating in team brainstorming, task coordination, and collaborative problem-solving, and knowledge-intensive industries are beginning to form a large number of human-machine hybrid teams. Existing research mostly relies on theoretical reasoning and lacks empirical perceptual data from front-line practitioners. Drawing on a questionnaire survey of 158 employees with cross-industry teamwork experience, this paper explores practitioners' perceptions regarding the substitution of human collaborative behaviors by AI. The results show that AI can only partially substitute procedural and rule-oriented collaborative tasks, whereas social-emotional communication, conflict mediation and value judgment remain irreplaceable human strengths. Position, work experience and AI familiarity jointly shape individual perceptions of the substitution boundary. Most practitioners regard AI as an auxiliary tool rather than a leader of team collaboration. This study provides a practical reference for enterprises applying AI collaboration tools.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Research on the Impact of Digital Inclusive Finance on Corporate Financing Cost: Theoretical Mechanism and Empirical Test
abstract: Based on the data of A-share non-financial listed companies from 2011 to 2023, this paper matches the Peking University prefecture-level city digital inclusive finance index with corporate financial data, and empirically examines the impact of digital inclusive finance on corporate financing cost and its mechanism of action. Financing cost is measured by the financial expense ratio, and the industry and year fixed effects model is used for estimation. The study finds that the increase of the regional digital inclusive finance development level significantly reduces corporate financing cost; the mechanism analysis shows that digital inclusive finance plays its role by improving the external information environment of enterprises and raising analyst following and research report coverage. The heterogeneity analysis shows that this effect is more obvious in non-state-owned enterprises, the eastern region and larger-scale enterprises. The study provides an empirical basis for improving digital financial infrastructure, optimizing corporate credit information governance and differentiated credit pricing.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: ESG Rating Disagreement and Stock Price Crash Risk: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Companies
abstract: Environmental, social and governance (ESG) ratings issued by different agencies frequently point in opposite directions, yet it remains unsettled whether such disagreement helps market participants or confuses them. Drawing on a panel of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2018 to 2024, we measure rating disagreement as the dispersion among three domestic raters—Huazheng, Wind, and SynTao Green Finance—and relate it to subsequent crash risk. Pooled two-way fixed effects estimates yield no significant average relation, indicating that the noise channel and the information channel embedded in disagreement counterbalance each other. Tests based on stock price synchronicity do not detect an information channel at the aggregate level. Splitting the sample by analyst forecast dispersion, however, uncovers a sharp boundary condition: disagreement is followed by significantly lower crash risk only among firms whose information environment is relatively transparent, and the contrast between groups is significant at the 5% level. Disagreement therefore behaves as information where investors are able to verify it and as noise where they are not. Implications for rating-market regulation, disclosure policy, and rating users are discussed.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Effect of Digital Extension and E-Learning Intervention and Adoption Among Cassava and Fish Farmers in Bayelsa State
abstract: This research investigated the effects of digital extension and e-learning intervention and adoption among cassava and fish farmers in Bayelsa State. A quasi-experimental design incorporating pre test and post-test assessments was employed, involving 240 active smallholder farmers selected from Yenagoa, Ogbia and Sagbama Local Government Areas. Agricultural advisory content was delivered through WhatsApp groups, Interactive Voice Response (IVR) and YouTube videos over a twelve-week period. The data obtained were subjected to descriptive and inferential statistical analyses. The results indicated that farmers’ technical knowledge improved after the interventions. Cassava and fish farmers acknowledged the positive contributions of the interventions, with fish farmers expressing greater perceived benefits. The interventions also shaped production decisions and farm management practices, particularly in fertiliser and feed application, input selection, disease control and weed management. Technology adoption emerged as a significant predictor of changes in farmers’ practices after the interventions. Nevertheless, inconsistent mobile network connectivity, expensive data subscriptions, unreliable electricity and inadequate digital literacy limited effective engagement. The research concluded that digital extension and e-learning interventions offer opportunities for enhancing agricultural knowledge dissemination and improving farming practices. It recommended the establishment of public–private partnerships to improve rural network infrastructure and provide subsidised data packages for farmers.

title: Mitigating Revenue Leakage: An AI Framework for Connecticut Healthcare Organizations
abstract: This paper examined the impact of AI framework for mitigating revenue leakage in Connecticut Healthcare Organizations as a result of thin margins, strict state cost benchmarks, and complex regional payer dynamics that cause severe financial strain for the organizations. The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) served as the theoretical roadmap for the review. Using a qualitative, non-empirical conceptual review framework and thematic synthesis, this review analyzed and synthesized healthcare literature from 2019 to 2026 across major databases. The methodology mapped data pipelines across the care continuum to isolate technical friction and deployment barriers. The review indicated that integrated AI frameworks deliver substantial financial protection across regional health networks. Specifically, clinical-grade NLP optimizes comorbidity capture from unstructured documentation, predictive analytics compute pre-bill risk scores to intercept billing errors, autonomous multi-agent systems execute closed loop denial remediation, and the Patient Prism framework activates front-end appointment recovery within a 60-second window. It was concluded that AI protects revenue, but only if it fits daily workflows and protects data security. It was recommended that to lower alert fatigue, executives should use AI systems tailored to local health insurance data alongside simple, user friendly dashboards. Also, hospitals should connect separate software systems using standard APIs. This removes manual workarounds, protects data, and keeps information flowing smoothly. Next-gen AI must use self-correcting networks that audit billing and automatically adapt to new regulations.
journal: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT

title: Assessing the Role of Agroforestry in Mitigating Climate Change and Enhancing Food Security in Nigeria
abstract: Climate change poses significant challenges to agriculture in Nigeria, threatening food security and livelihoods. This research assesses the role of agroforestry in mitigating climate change impacts and enhancing food security in Nigeria. Through a systematic literature review and analysis of case studies, the study explores the diverse applications and benefits of agroforestry practices across different agroecological zones in Nigeria. Findings reveal that agroforestry systems offer sustainable solutions by sequestering carbon, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and improving soil fertility. Case studies illustrate successful agroforestry initiatives, including alley cropping, agro-silvopastoral systems, home gardens, and agroforestry parklands, showcasing enhanced agricultural productivity, resilience, and food security. Recommendations are provided to promote the adoption of agroforestry practices, including policy support, capacity building, research, community engagement, partnerships, monitoring, and scaling up successful models. Implementing these recommendations can harness the potential of agroforestry to address climate change and food insecurity, fostering sustainable agricultural development in Nigeria.
journal: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT

title: Spatial Pattern of Landuse/Landcover and Flood Management Strategies by Vulnerable Communities in Kogi State, Nigeria
abstract: Flood is among the most recurring and devastating natural hazards causing colossal loss of lives and severe economic damages throughout the world. Kogi State in Nigeria, because of its confluence nature, experiences perennial flooding which this study seeks to examine. The objectives of this study includes to: identify and map landuse/land cover dynamics as they accelerate flooding, identify and examine the effects of flood risk on vulnerable communities, and examine the flood management practices in Kogi State. LandSat satellite images obtained from USGS Global Land Cover Facility website of different epochs (2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2024) were used to model the variations in the spatial pattern of landues/landcover (LULC) changes. ENVI Remote Sensing Software was used to carry out digital image processing of the images and then classify the images into Crop, Settlement, Water and Island. ASTER elevation image data (DEM) of 30m Resolution was used to create terrain model of Kogi State to show regions of low lands that easily get flooded. The ArcGIS 10.5 was used to create the map layouts. The vulnerable communities to flood were geo-tagged using the Garmin 72+ handheld GPS. Using simple random sampling technique, a total of 418 copies of questionnaire sampled across the three senatorial zones of Kogi State: Kogi East - 197 (44.94%), Kogi West - 112 (27.89%), and Kogi Central - 109 (27.16%)) were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including graph and tables. 418 copies of questionnaires administered to residents were used to examine the impact of flooding on vulnerable communities at risk of flooding. The study reveals that the 2020 and 2024 images had scan and cloud cover errors; hence, they were excluded from further analyses. LULC change was considered to be partly responsible for flood in the vulnerable communities as most crop lands had been converted to settlements. The identified major vulnerable communities include Lokoja, Gadumo, Ganaja, Koton Karfe, Adankolo and Natako. These settlements fall within the lowlands of Kogi State. Flood impact on the communities includes loss of human lives (21%), loss of property (17%), displacement of people (13%), health risk (12%), disruption of economic activities (14%) and food insecurity (23%) during flood disaster in Kogi State. The identified flood management practices include flood vulnerability management (21%), flood plain management (20%), natural flood control system (19%), construction of flood barriers (15%), and early warning system (25%). This means that in most cases, before rainy season, early warning on flood vulnerability are received from relevant MDAs like NIHSA, NIMET and FEMA. The study, therefore, recommends, as a matter of urgency, the creation of Emergency evacuation route, emergency evacuation/health centers, support coastal communities with fishing tools, timely and adequately response to flood affected communities to save lives, ensure public and environmental safety, and ecological security
journal: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT

title: Impact and Implications of Optimizing Productivity of the Nigerian Economy Under Existing Paradigm
abstract: Low productivity constrains an economy’s long-term potential, leading to stagnant wages, reduced global competitiveness, higher inflation, and slower Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth. National productivity was derived as nominal income divided by labour compensation while labor productivity as nominal income divided by the employed workforce. Labour compensation is the total package of benefits accruable to the worker for their contribution to production and includes wages and salaries, health care, pension, etc. The aim of this study is to analyze the impact and implications of attempting to optimize the productivity of the Nigerian economy under the extant paradigm, with a view to determine the needed policy interventions and developmental strategies that are required in order to proceed to mitigate the challenges posed by low productivity. The result indicated that to attempt to optimize productivity in Nigeria under the existing state of affairs of the Nigerian economy without first fixing the entire economy as well as the citizens, will be counter-productive and self-defeating; as this will only promote and fuel corruption, inflation and poverty in Nigeria. Tackling Nigeria's low productivity requires aggressive investments in critical infrastructure (such as reliable power and transportation networks), widespread human capital development through vocational and digital skills training, and economic reforms that support SMEs, modernize agriculture, and promote regional trade. In addition, Nigeria needs a paradigm shift and the citizens’ reorientation and attitudinal change. In addition, the country needs a good, honest and decisive leader, who is bold, courageous and pragmatic in his leadership and who has the political will to implement the range of recommendations emanating from thisstudy, including a deliberate attempt to minimize corruption and indiscipline as well as ensuring good governance, amongst others.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH

title: Forensiq - Intelligent Security Operations & Investigation Platform
abstract: Security Operations Centers process security alerts from many different systems. Analysts must match events gather evidence add data and evaluate risk before deciding. Forensiq is a platform that uses AI agents to help with these tasks. It works inside Splunk. Handles alert ingestion, event exploration, alert triage, threat-intelligence enrichment of indicators of compromise, mapping to MITRE ATT&CK correlating events calculating risk reasoning through investigations checking claims with facts and producing reports for analysts. A multi-agent design splits the work into tasks but the original data stays for analysts to check. Tests will look at how alerts are sorted how well ATT&CK mapping works how much threat data is added, how well evidence supports claims how many unsupported claims appear, how good event correlation is, how efficient investigations become, how good reports are and how the system scales. The final test will compare the Forensiq workflow to a baseline under the same data. Forensiq is meant to help analysts; the system gives reasoning support. Does not replace human checking and response decisions.
journal: International Journal of Innovative Research in Engineering

title: SMARTKISAAN: An AI-Driven, IoT-Based Smart Irrigation Monitoring System for Small and Marginal Farmers
abstract: Small and marginal farmers often irrigate by observation and fixed schedules, which can lead to over-irrigation, under-irrigation, and wasted water. This paper describes SmartKisaan, a low-cost, solar-powered smart irrigation prototype that combines an ESP32 microcontroller, soil-moisture, temperature-humidity, rain, and water-tank sensors, Firebase Realtime Database, a Random Forest irrigation model served through a Flask API, and a Flutter mobile application with weather-based scheduling, leaf-image disease screening, and an English and Kannada voice-enabled assistant. Every pump command passes through a layered safety hierarchy that is also implemented in the ESP32 firmware. On a held-out test set of 700 records, the Random Forest achieved 99.00% accuracy and an F1-score of 97.73%. However, the 3,500 records used for training were generated by simulation from agronomic rules, so these results show that the model learns the intended irrigation policy and do not represent measured performance in a real field. Four of five hardware bench tests passed and one failure was recorded; all 12 automated decision-logic tests passed. These checks do not establish water savings, crop-yield improvement, or long-term field reliability. SmartKisaan is a decision-support prototype and not a validated commercial irrigation controller.
journal: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology

title: Farm Market: A Review of Digital Agricultural Marketing, Crop-Price Prediction and Transparent Offer Scoring with an Implemented Farmer Decision-Support Prototype
abstract: Small farmers frequently make selling decisions without reliable information about market prices, buyer dependability or transport costs. Digital marketplaces and machine-learning models may help address this information gap. This review examines 14 published studies from 2007–2025 and one government-commissioned report covering mobile-phone market information, India’s electronic National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), and statistical, machine-learning and deep-learning approaches to crop-price forecasting. Forecasting results vary with the commodity, prediction horizon, dataset and evaluation method; in some cases, simple baselines perform competitively. A single score therefore cannot establish whether a model suits a particular mandi. The paper also analyses the supplied FarmMarket project: a React/TypeScript interface with farmer, dealer, transporter and administrator workflows, a five-factor dealer-offer score, a net-return calculation, a rule-based crop-price estimator, a PHP/MySQL API and a scikit-learn ridge-regression script. The code contains these components, but the front end currently stores data in browser localStorage and is not connected to the API. The front end and back end also use different scoring formulas, while the price model relies on a 21-row demonstration dataset. The quoted accuracy figures cannot therefore be independently verified, and neither predictive performance nor practical benefit has yet been established.
journal: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology

title: Reliability-Aware Active Crowdsourcing and Ontology-Constrained Multi-Evidence Clustering for Agricultural Multimedia Knowledge-Base Construction
abstract: Constructing agricultural multimedia knowledge bases is complicated by heterogeneous evidence, noisy crowdsourced annotations, variations in sample difficulty, and inadequate integration of multisource information. Using tomato disease and pest data, this study proposes a unified framework comprising Multi-evidence Reliability-Aware Active Crowdsourcing (MRAC) and Ontology-Constrained Multi-Evidence Clustering and Refinement (OMCR). MRAC jointly models annotator reliability, sample difficulty, content-evidence quality, and evidence availability. It selects sample-annotator pairs according to the expected information gain per unit cost and produces calibrated soft-label posteriors. OMCR integrates frozen visual features, crowdsourcing posteriors, and agricultural ontology constraints, and uses class prototypes, pairwise constraints, and risk scores for sample clustering, mislabeled-instance detection, and label refinement. Under 30% synthetic annotation noise, MRAC achieved an Accuracy of 0.9732 and a Macro-F1 of 0.9676. MRAC-EIG achieved the highest mean Macro-F1 (0.9631) and the lowest mean relative annotation cost (1.0080) among the evaluated policies. The complete OMCR model achieved ACC, NMI, and ARI values of 0.9708, 0.9293, and 0.9500, respectively. The unified framework achieved Precision@5, Precision@10, and nDCG@10 values of 0.9251, 0.9223, and 0.9233, respectively, with a 14.97% relative improvement in nDCG@10 over visual-only retrieval. These results show that the proposed framework improves noisy-label aggregation, multi-evidence knowledge organization, and retrieval ranking while controlling annotation costs, offering a practical route to reliable agricultural multimedia knowledge-base construction.
