title: Benchmarking Large Language AI Models Against Human Doctors Using an Emergency Medicine Simulation Approach
abstract: Background: Proper adoption of AI in emergency medicine necessitate thorough and rigorous appraisal. Classic benchmarks, which rely heavily on basic question-and-answer formats, though dominating the benchmarking field of LLM usage in medicine, have proven inadequate in assessing the full spectrum of skills incumbent upon an agent in healthcare. Methods: We propose an intricate benchmarking scheme in which the skill set required of an emergency physician is tested and quantified. Our benchmarking structure is 3-fold: skills such as history taking, diagnostic accuracy, treatment plan, and empathy are evaluated by an emergency medicine expert, while the same expertise is scored by an intern from the perspective of a patient, through what we call a simulated emergency room visit. A comprehensive written examination is also utilized to measure general emergency medicine knowledge. Results: Eight LLMs were benchmarked against each other and in contrast to nine emergency medical doctors. Our findings indicate that the AI models significantly outperformed human physicians across several key domains, including history taking, investigation, diagnostic accuracy, and treatment planning. Furthermore, the models demonstrated superior performance in comprehensibility, credibility, and empathy. When comparing AI models against each other, performance advantages were marginal during simulated emergency room visits and were mostly pronounced during the written examination. Conclusion: AI models demonstrate a clear advantage over human physicians across a diverse range of emergency medicine competencies. The proposed benchmarking scheme provides a comprehensive metric for a thorough evaluation of medical skill set, furthering validation, adaptation, and utilization of AI in emergency medicine.

title: Behavioral Orientations and Self-Rated Performance Among University Employees in Vietnam
abstract: University work increasingly combines professional discretion with digital change, accountability demands, and cross-unit coordination. This cross-sectional study examined associations among five work-related behavioral orientations responsibility, discipline, engagement, cooperation, and adaptability and four domains of self-rated performance among 450 university employees in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. A four-point questionnaire was analyzed using a reflective composite-based PLS path model with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Reliability and convergent validity were strong across the nine constructs, although several conceptually adjacent constructs showed high HTMT values and were therefore interpreted cautiously. All five orientations showed positive bivariate relationships with performance, but their unique multivariable associations were uneven. Adaptability and cooperation showed the most consistent unique associations across the four performance domains, whereas several responsibility, discipline, and engagement paths were small or nonsignificant after shared variance was considered. Discipline was strongly associated with responsibility, engagement, cooperation, and adaptability, and several model-based indirect associations with performance were observed. These findings support a differentiated but interconnected view of work behavior rather than a single generic positive attitude. Because predictors and outcomes were measured concurrently from the same respondents, the results do not establish temporal mediation or causal effects.

title: Operator-Splitting Architectures for Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
abstract: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs) replace the discrete layer stack of a residual network by a continuous-time vector field parameterised by a neural network. This reformulation opens a dialogue with classical numerical analysis: every time integrator can be read as a particular network architecture. We study operator splitting as an architectural principle and apply it. The vector field is decomposed into two sub-networks, typically a linear part advanced exactly by the matrix exponential and a nonlinear part advanced by a Runge–Kutta solver, which are composed by Lie–Trotter or Strang splitting (LT-NODE and S-NODE). We prove that the local splitting error is O(τ3)for Lie–Trotter and O(τ3) for Strang splitting, with the corresponding global convergence; that splitting preserves the contraction rate μA + μB of one-sided Lipschitz sub-fields for every step size; and we derive and verify a split adjoint for gradient computation. In our experimental studies with five independent seeds, validation-based model selection and baselines including GRU, ODE-RNN, unsplit additive Neural ODEs and Neural CDEs (six UEA datasets, four missing-data rates, a synthetic system, a spiral benchmark and a stiff reaction–diffusion system), we show differentiated pictures. At least splitting does not improve accuracy by itself relative to an unsplit model with the same additive structure, and it is not universally cheaper. It pays off when one part of the dynamics is stiff and can be integrated exactly, for example for a reaction–diffusion system with known diffusion, S-NODE, we reach the accuracy of the unsplit hybrid model with 19 times fewer function evaluations and 23 times shorter training. We also included a report of an encoder defect that caused the chance-level spiral result.
journal: Journal of Algorithms in Complex Systems

title: Integrating Digital Tools into Agricultural Science Instruction in Secondary Schools: Opportunities and Challenges for Curriculum Developers in Delta State
From Responsible AI Governance to Competitive Advantage: Examining the Role of AI Governance Capability in Driving Innovation and Organizational Performance in Nigerian Organizations
abstract: Artificial intelligence creates opportunities for organizational innovation while introducing accountability, fairness, privacy, and oversight challenges. Existing research explains AI resources and business value more extensively than the organizational capability required to govern AI responsibly and translate governance into strategic outcomes. This conceptual paper develops a framework connecting AI governance capability, innovation capability, organizational performance, and competitive advantage in Nigerian organizations. A purposive, integrative synthesis of 20 journal articles informs construct differentiation and the development of seven hypotheses. Drawing on resource-based and dynamic capability perspectives, the paper conceptualizes AI governance capability through strategic accountability, data and model lifecycle governance, ethical assurance, human oversight, and adaptive monitoring. Innovation capability is proposed as a mechanism linking governance capability to two distinct organizational ou

authors.name: Afeniforo Ayodele Augustine Afeniforo Ayodele Augustine

journal: Journal of Business Practice and Academic Research

title: Digital Transformation of Uzbekistan’s Agricultural Sector: The Role of Human Capital in Ensuring Sustainable Development
abstract: This article examines the key directions of digital transformation in Uzbekistan’s agricultural sector and the role of human capital in its implementation. Based on data from the National Statistics Committee and government programs, the study analyzes the role of agriculture in the national economy and the outcomes of introducing water-saving technologies and digital platforms. The findings indicate that the predominance of small-scale dehkan farms makes the digital competencies of agricultural producers a crucial prerequisite for the widespread adoption of modern technologies. The article proposes measures to develop human capital in rural areas to ensure the sustainable development of the agricultural sector.

title: The Role of the Food Industry in Uzbekistan’s Industrial Development: Trends, Structural Changes and Statistical Assessment
abstract: This study analyzes the development trends and economic role of the food industry in Uzbekistan using official statistical data for 2000–2025. The research examines production dynamics, the industry's share in manufacturing and consumer goods, and per capita production indicators. The results indicate that the food industry has achieved stable growth through modernization, increased processing of agricultural raw materials, and structural economic reforms. Despite a declining share in manufacturing, the industry remains a strategic contributor to food security, industrial competitiveness, and sustainable economic development. Recommendations are proposed to support digitalization, innovation, and deeper processing of agricultural products.

title: Viabilidade econômica do uso de drones na agricultura de precisão aplicada à cultura da cana-de-açúcar em propriedades rurais de médio porte.
abstract: The integration of digital technologies into agriculture has encouraged the use of drones as tools for precision farming, with the potential to reduce operating costs and improve processes. This study aims to assess the economic viability of using drones in sugarcane cultivation on medium-sized farms. It is a qualitative, descriptive study based on a literature review of scientific and institutional sources, primarily published between 2016 and 2025. The analysis considers acquisition and operating costs, potential productivity gains, and financial indicators such as payback, Net Present Value (NPV), and Internal Rate of Return (IRR). The reviewed literature suggests potential savings in inputs and labor, as well as more accurate monitoring and pesticide application. The scenarios presented suggest that investment returns may be more favorable on farms larger than 150 hectares, depending on the assumptions adopted. The study concludes that drones may be economically viable in the medium term, particularly when integrated into data-driven management, provided that credit access, technical training, and operational planning are considered.

title: The Care Plan Compiler as an Agentic AI Framework for Translating Clinical Recommendations into Feasible Patient-Centered Care
abstract: A clinical recommendation becomes care after someone confirms coverage, finds a facility that provides the service, arranges language support and transportation, books an appointment, and verifies that the visit took place. When no organization owns this work, it falls to the patient, and a missed service is recorded as nonadherence, even when the failure occurred within the health system. The review examines five adjacent fields, each addressing part of this problem, and develops the Care Plan Compiler, an agentic AI framework that treats the clinician-approved recommendation as a protected source specification and compiles it into a graph of tasks with named owners. A deterministic readiness checker releases a task once all prerequisites hold and classifies any unknown coverage, capacity, or accessibility as unresolved. Feasible plans are compared across a multidimensional burden vector, and a change in context triggers recompilation of the dependent tasks. A synthetic case of diabetic retinal screening illustrates the compilation, and a four-stage evaluation program sets a screening completed within the approved window and verified within 90 days of referral approval as its primary endpoint. The framework moves responsibility for missed care to the system layer where the failure occurs.
journal: Universal Library of Innovative Research and Studies

title: Mapping Environmental Degradation and Climate Vulnerability using GIS and Remote Sensing
abstract: Environmental degradation and climate vulnerability pose significant threats to the stability of ecosystems, agriculture, water supply, and humans’ well-being. The use of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and remote sensing can prove beneficial in detecting spatial patterns of environmental changes, detecting signs of land degradation, and assessing regions’ vulnerability to climate threats. In this study, a geospatial framework is suggested to map environmental degradation and climate vulnerability through satellite imagery analysis, vegetation indexes, land use and land cover classification, land surface temperature, precipitation, terrain properties, and socioeconomic factors. Landsat imagery, Sentinel-2 imagery, digital elevation models, and climate gridded data will be combined in GIS to assess changes in vegetation cover, urbanization, bare lands, land surface temperature, and drought. To do that, NDVI, NDBI, LST, and precipitation anomalies will be used to derive indicators of environmental degradation. Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI) will be created using weighted overlay models with environmental exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity indicators. The accuracy of classification will be measured using independent reference data sets, whereas temporal variations will be evaluated via post-classification assessment. As illustrated in the figure below, a conceptual example of the application of the framework is shown by partitioning a study site into different vulnerability zones (low, medium, high, and very high), wherein 35% of the study site has been assigned to high and very high vulnerability zones. The values are purely illustrative and are not obtained from any satellite processing. This framework can contribute to environmental monitoring, climate adaptation strategy, land management, and identification of vulnerable sites.
journal: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF A METHODOLOGY FOR ASSESSING THE POTENTIAL EROSION HAZARD OF RELIEF ON THE EXAMPLE OF A MUNICIPAL FORMATION IN TAMBOV OBLAST
abstract: For the plain landscapes of the chernozem zone of Russia, where extensive agricultural exploitation of land has led to large-scale degradation of the most fertile soils, assessing the contribution of relief to the development of erosion processes is one of the most important tasks of environmentally sustainable land use. This paper describes the author’s methodology for assessing the potential erosion hazard of relief. The methodology relies on the morphometric analysis of a digital elevation model using GIS applications. The lowest-tier municipal formations were adopted as the operational territorial units. For each territorial unit, four morphometric criteria were calculated: the weighted average LS-factor, the depth of relief dissection, the fluvial network density, and the share of land with a steepness of >7° in the total area. An integral indicator of the potential erosion hazard of relief for each territorial unit was calculated as the geometric mean of the values of these criteria, scaled to a comparable order of magnitude using scale factors. The assessment scale for land typification includes six types of lands differing in their erosion potential of relief. The upper limit of the scale was empirically calibrated using reference areas with high erosional dissection within the forest-steppe and steppe zones of the East European Plain. Testing of the methodology was carried out on the example of the Sosnovsky Municipal District of Tambov Oblast, located within the Oka-Don Lowland. According to the assessment results, lands of three types were identified in the district: with minimal (Type II), low (Type III) and moderate erosion potential of relief (Type IV). Two territorial divisions in the northern and north-western parts of the district, classified as Type IV lands, are considered a priority zone for the development of erosion control land management based on comprehensive soil-erosion surveys. The methodology is presumably applicable to agricultural landscapes of the steppe and forest-steppe zones of the East European Plain, where Chernozems dominate the soil cover structure of agricultural lands.
journal: Soil erosion and river channel processes

title: TRANSFORMATION OF RADIOACTIVE CONTAMINATION OF AGRICULTURAL LAND IN THE UPA RIVER BASIN DUE TO EROSION PROCESSES
abstract: This study evaluates long-term changes (up to 2050) in 137 Cs contamination levels across agricultural lands within the Upa River basin (Tula Region, Russia). Following the 1986 Chernobyl disaster, this river basin remains one of the most heavily contaminated areas in the Central Russian Upland. Developing mid- and long-term predictive contamination maps is a critical environmental task. It requires accounting for all processes beyond radioactive decay that significantly influence radionuclide density. Due to the chemical properties of radiocesium, its lateral migration occurs primarily bound to fine sediments within sediment yield. Consequently, assessing soil erosion dynamics on arable lands is essential for accurate environmental forecasting. However, existing publicly available contamination atlases omitted the erosion factor due to the small scale of their mapping materials. In this study, we verified the radioactive contamination map using past field observations and refined the forecast of contamination density changes on agricultural lands by incorporating long- term average erosion rates modelled with the WaTEM/SEDEM model. Radioactive decay remains the dominant factor driving contamination density reduction across most of the studied area. However, identifying local hotspots of severe erosion and associated 137 Cs inventory redistribution serves as a key predictor of secondary environmental risks linked to the accumulation of legacy sediments and bound radionuclides within the fluvial network.
journal: Soil erosion and river channel processes

title: Optimised YOLO and MobileNet SSD models for animal intrusion detection in agriculture
abstract: Animal intrusion detection is critical for mitigating agricultural losses, yet real-world deployments remain challenging due to high computational demands and suboptimal hyperparameter configurations. This study presents a robust, multi-class detection framework optimised for real-world agricultural environments. The lightweight SSD Lite MobileNetV3 is benchmarked against the state-of-the-art YOLOv11 family (Nano, Small, and Medium) using a comprehensive, field-collected dataset. To overcome the performance bottlenecks with the default configuration, the framework uses Bayesian Optimisation with Hyperband (BOHB) for compute-efficient hyperparameter tuning. Experimental evaluation shows that BOHB enhances the performance. The optimised models achieved an exceptional F1-score of 0.90 for You Only Look Once version 11 medium (YOLO11m), 0.88 for You Only Look Once version 11 (YOLO11), 0.83 for You Only Look Once version 11 nano (YOLO11n), and 0.68 for Single Shot Detector Lite with MobileNetV3 (SSDLite MobileNetV3). The results show that the proposed framework delivers reliable detection, providing a scalable smart-farming solution to safeguard crops and reduce human-wildlife conflict.

title: Marketing Efficiency and Determinants of e-NAM Adoption in Tomato Marketing: Evidence from Dharmapuri District, Tamil Nadu, India
abstract: Tomato is an important commercial vegetable crop in India, but its perishable nature and frequent price fluctuations make efficient marketing essential for improving farmers’ income. The Electronic National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) aims to strengthen agricultural marketing through digital trading, wider market access and transparent price discovery. This study analysed tomato marketing channels, price spread and marketing efficiency, and examined the factors influencing farmers’ adoption of e-NAM in Dharmapuri district of Tamil Nadu. Primary data were collected from 120 tomato growers, comprising 60 e-NAM users and 60 non-users, along with 25 market intermediaries. Price spread analysis, producer’s share in the consumer’s rupee, Acharya’s modified marketing efficiency measure and a binary logit model were employed. The results showed that the e-NAM channel recorded the highest producer’s share (80.47 per cent) and marketing efficiency (4.33), compared with conventional channels. Awareness of e-NAM, literacy and trust in government policies had a positive and significant influence on adoption, while distance to the regulated market had a negative and significant influence. The findings indicate that e-NAM has the potential to improve price realisation and marketing efficiency for tomato farmers. Strengthening awareness, digital literacy and market infrastructure could further encourage farmers’ participation in the platform.

title: Factors Affecting Adoption of Climate-Smart Agricultural Innovations among Smallholder Sorghum Farmers in Soin Sigowet Sub County, Kericho County
abstract: Drought has substantially affected agricultural productivity in Kenya. For example, farmers experience income losses due to reduced crop yields, deterioration in crop quality, insect infestations, including recent locust outbreaks in Kenya, high irrigation costs, plant diseases and a reduction in productive, arable land. Persistent drought in parts of Kenya has created a need for coping strategies, including growing alternative crops and the adoption of Climate-Smart Agricultural (CSA) innovations. KALRO has been promoting Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) innovations in sorghum production in Kericho County to increase production and alleviate food insecurity among small-scale farmers. However, despite these efforts, production levels have remained low. The study hypothesised that limited adoption of CSA innovations among farmers may be a contributing factor. The study examined the socioeconomic and institutional factors that influence the adoption of these CSA innovations among smallholder sorghum farmers in Soin Sigowet Sub-County, Kericho County. A descriptive survey research design was used, and a multistage sampling procedure was employed to select 239 respondents from a population of 629. Both structured and unstructured questionnaires were used in data collection. A binary logistic regression model was analysed to determine the factors affecting the adoption of CSAs. Data were analysed using SPSS version 25. The results indicated that land size (p =0.000, β =1.237), years of schooling (p =0.000, β =1.877) and household size (p =0.007|β =0.319) significantly and positively influenced the adoption of CSA innovations. However, the age of the household head (p =0.002, β =-0.15) significantly and negatively influenced the adoption of CSA innovations. The study recommends that more farmers receive training in the use of CSA interventions. Furthermore, policymakers should develop policy directives that encourage intensification of farm production that could increase agricultural production and incomes among small-scale farmer households.
journal: Asian Journal of Agricultural and Horticultural Research

title: Structural Breaks and Comparative Time-Series Forecasting of Kenya’s Mobile Money Ecosystem
abstract: Background: Kenya’s mobile money ecosystem has expanded substantially, but changes in its underlying growth rate and the forecasting implications of those changes warrant examination. Problem: Policy-associated movements in the aggregate series may reflect longer-running structural changes rather than effects attributable to a particular intervention. Aim: To detect structural breaks, assess the March 2020 emergency period and compare transaction-volume forecasts across horizons. Methods: Monthly Central Bank of Kenya statistics covering July 2009–April 2026 (202 observations) were analysed. Chow, sup-F, dynamic-programming, CUSUM and variance-break tests examined stability. Seasonal ARIMA intervention models estimated adjusted period associations. Eight forecasting models were compared using expanding-window rolling-origin evaluation at 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month horizons. Results: Transaction-volume growth changed in May 2017 (sup-F = 13.72, P = .001), declining from approximately 2.2% to 0.5% monthly. CUSUM crossed its lower bound in June 2018; no robust variance break was identified. During March–December 2020, volume was 4.8% below its model-implied path (P = .006). The April–May 2020 window yielded a 13.1% reduction. Value and ticket-size effects were not statistically significant. Damped-trend exponential smoothing had the lowest forecast errors at every horizon (MAPE approximately 2.3%–3.1%). Conclusion: Transaction-volume growth slowed before the 2018 policy changes, precluding attribution of the earlier break to those measures. The 2020 contraction was temporary, and forecast accuracy depended on accommodating trend deceleration.
journal: Asian Journal of Probability and Statistics

title: The Dual Role of Nitrogen in Plant Health: A Critical Review of Crop Growth, Disease Resistance and Susceptibility
abstract: Nitrogen is essential for crop growth and yield. However, its influence on plant health extends beyond its role as a nutrient source. Nitrogen availability can affect plant physiology, defence metabolism, tissue composition and interactions with pathogenic and beneficial microorganisms. Thus, nitrogen fertilisation may increase resistance to some diseases while making plants more susceptible to others. These contrasting effects complicate the optimisation of nitrogen management for sustainable agricultural production. This critical analysis examines the relationships among nitrogen nutrition, crop development, plant defence mechanisms and disease progression. It focuses on nitrogen availability, chemical form, application rate and environmental conditions. It evaluates the physiological, biochemical and ecological processes by which nitrogen influences plant–pathogen interactions and distinguishes between soil-borne and foliar diseases. The analysis also explores why reported disease responses to nitrogen fertilisation vary, highlighting the roles of host physiology, pathogen behaviour, soil characteristics, microbial populations and experimental design. A central conclusion is that nitrogen cannot be categorically classified as either disease-promoting or disease-suppressing. This is because its effects depend on interactions among the crop, pathogen and cultivation environment. Current studies are further limited by inconsistent disease assessments and insufficient integration of nitrogen use efficiency, disease intensity, crop productivity and environmental impacts within individual experiments. Future research should prioritize mechanistic field studies, standardised disease evaluations and forecasting models that account for the interaction between nitrogen management and disease susceptibility. Integrating plant nutrition with disease control may improve crop yields while minimising excessive fertiliser application and its associated environmental impacts.
journal: Asian Journal of Soil Science and Plant Nutrition

title: Artificial Intelligence and Smart Surveillance in Agricultural Entomology: Computer Vision, Sensing and Predictive Pest Monitoring
abstract: Agricultural pest surveillance is shifting from periodic manual inspection towards digitally mediated observation, combining automated traps, computer vision, environmental sensors and statistical or machine-learning forecasts. The technological literature reports increasingly sophisticated species recognition, remote counting and near-real-time data transmission. Whether these capabilities generate reliable estimates of pest pressure or improve integrated pest management, however, depends on ecological sampling, field validation and decisions taken after an alert. This critical narrative review evaluates the measurement-to-decision pathway rather than treating classification accuracy as evidence of agronomic benefit. Peer-reviewed research and relevant methodological literature were identified through accessible scholarly sources, with thematic emphasis on camera-equipped pheromone, light and adhesive traps; image-recognition architectures; optical, acoustic and environmental sensing; predictive modelling; and operational evaluation. The synthesis indicates that instrumented traps and image-processing methods can reduce some observation burdens and produce useful within-system temporal information. Their reported performance is nevertheless strongly conditioned by trap selectivity, target species, illumination, specimen overlap, annotation quality, seasonal distribution shifts and the choice of validation dataset. Forecasting approaches can exploit temperature, phenology and historical trap catches, but retrospective fit does not establish transferable warning value. Ecological inference also requires distinguishing insect activity, trap catches, abundance, crop injury and economic risk. The most consequential weaknesses are limited independent multi-site prospective testing, incomplete uncertainty reporting, insufficient comparison with manual scouting, and few controlled evaluations of management consequences. A deployment-oriented framework is proposed in which measurement validity, calibration, forecast skill, decision thresholds, costs and non-target effects are appraised as connected requirements. Progress will depend less on marginal improvements in benchmark detection scores than on prospective, locally calibrated studies that measure timeliness, intervention quality, labour, pesticide use, yield and biodiversity outcomes.

title: Patterns and Determinants of Library Usage Behaviour among Undergraduate Students in Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, India
abstract: Background & Aims: Understanding why undergraduate students use university libraries can inform the design of physical and digital services. This study examined the associations between performance expectancy, effort expectancy, library anxiety, the physical library environment, technological infrastructure and library usage behaviour among undergraduates at Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore. Methods: An ex-post facto research design was adopted. From eligible undergraduate library users across four academic years, 250 students were selected following purposive identification of the study population. Responses were collected through a structured 25-item questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. The six reflective constructs were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4.0. Reliability, convergent and discriminant validity, collinearity and model fit were assessed, and hypotheses were tested using 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Results: The model explained 77.0% of the variance in library usage behaviour (R² = 0.770). Performance expectancy (β = 0.371), the physical library environment (β = 0.252), technological infrastructure (β = 0.240) and effort expectancy (β = 0.200) were positively associated with usage behaviour, whereas library anxiety was negatively associated with usage behaviour (β = −0.209). All five associations were statistically significant (P < .001). Conclusion: Students are more likely to use the library when they perceive a clear academic benefit and when technological support is dependable. Orientation and information literacy programmes, sustained investment in digital infrastructure, and user-friendly library services are recommended to promote continued library use.
journal: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

title: Defined Matrices Reveal Epithelial- and Mesenchymal-Specific Responses to Stiffness and Adhesion in Human iPSC-Derived Intestinal Organoids.
abstract: Human intestinal organoids (hIOs) are powerful models for studying development and disease, yet dissecting how physical and matrix cues shape epithelial and mesenchymal responses remains challenging due to reliance on ill-defined matrices. Here, a fully defined hIO workflow was developed in which Matrigel was replaced by recombinant human substrates during pluripotent stem cell differentiation and by polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogels during 3D culture, while maintaining organoid viability and epithelial cytodifferentiation. Transcriptomic analyses show that both PEG- and Matrigel-cultured hIO epithelial cells are most similar to human duodenal reference populations, and have greater transcriptional similarity to fetal than adult duodenal references. Despite this overall similarity, PEG culture is associated with subtle shifts in epithelial differentiation-associated gene expression, together with altered mesenchymal ECM-remodelling and integrin-associated programs. Increasing matrix stiffness produces modest effects in epithelial cells, including increased MUC2-positive cells, whereas mesenchymal transcriptional responses to stiffness are limited. Together, these findings establish a fully defined hIO platform that retains responsiveness to inflammatory stimulation while enabling controlled investigation of how matrix composition and stiffness shape epithelial and mesenchymal cell states in models of intestinal development and fibrosis.

title: Low-Intensity Focused Ultrasound Enables Temporal Modulation of Human Midbrain Organoid Differentiation.
abstract: Controlling the precise timing of biosignaling cues in complex 3D models such as organoids is critical for guiding cellular differentiation and functional maturation. Ultrasound stimulation, a next‐generation neuromodulation modality, offers unique advantages due to its target specificity, ability to elicit mechanosensitive responses, and high spatial resolution. However, there is still a lack of precision stimulation platforms and comprehensive biomarker assays for selective control of organoid development. Here, we introduce a modular piezoelectric ultrasound stimulation platform that integrates seamlessly with conventional multi‐well plates, enabling selective neuromodulation of midbrain organoids (mBOs). We demonstrate that ultrasound can specifically modulate cellular differentiation by promoting dopaminergic progenitor markers while delaying terminal differentiation. Importantly, ultrasound stimulation did not induce cellular damage, as confirmed by the absence of apoptosis and DNA damage markers. This work demonstrates the potential of focused ultrasound as a safe, non‐invasive, and tunable biophysical cue for temporal regulation of organoid differentiation.

title: Do Information and Communication Technologies Promote Climate‐Smart Irrigation in Sub‐Saharan Africa?
abstract: Irrigation is vital for climate resilience and food security in Sub‐Saharan Africa (SSA), yet its expansion remains constrained by climatic and structural barriers. Although information and communication technologies (ICTs) offer opportunities for climate‐smart irrigation, evidence across diverse SSA remains limited. Using panel data from 20 SSA countries (2000–2023), this study employs fixed‐effects (FE) and dynamic system–GMM (Generalized Method of Moments) estimators to examine the ICT–irrigation relationship, accounting for persistence and potential endogeneity. The findings reveal that ICT effects vary by technology and income level. Internet access consistently promotes irrigation development, particularly in low‐ and upper‐middle‐income economies, potentially by reducing information gaps and improving water management. Conversely, mobile phone penetration does not automatically generate irrigation gains and is negatively associated with irrigation development in lower‐middle‐income economies. Complementary conditions are also crucial: Electricity access and agricultural capital support irrigation development, whereas higher rainfall is associated with lower irrigation intensity, reflecting reduced reliance on irrigation. These findings reveal a development gradient in digital benefits, demonstrating that connectivity alone cannot drive irrigation expansion. Policies should therefore prioritize rural internet access alongside electrification, irrigation infrastructure and agricultural finance, supported by context‐specific digital agriculture strategies to advance climate resilience and sustainable agriculture across SSA.

title: Diagnostic Value of Serum GREM1 Levels in Differentiating Benign and Malignant Subsolid Pulmonary Nodules: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: To evaluate the diagnostic value of serum gremlin 1 (GREM1) levels in differentiating benign from malignant subsolid pulmonary nodules, a clinically challenging CT phenotype, this prospective observational cohort study included 183 patients with subsolid (ground-glass) pulmonary nodules identified by thin-section chest CT and 100 age- and sex-matched healthy volunteers between January and December 2025. Patients were followed through the standard diagnostic pathway, and the final diagnosis was confirmed histopathologically. Serum GREM1 levels were quantified using ELISA. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and multivariable binary logistic regression were used to evaluate diagnostic performance and factors associated with malignancy. Serum GREM1 levels increased stepwise from the healthy control group to the benign and malignant groups (all p < 0.05). The AUC of GREM1 for differentiating malignant nodules from benign nodules was 0.859, and the combined GREM1 and CYFRA21-1 model achieved an AUC of 0.918. Multivariable analysis revealed maximum nodule diameter, serum GREM1 level, and CYFRA21-1 level as independent risk factors associated with malignant nodules. Serum GREM1, particularly in combination with CYFRA21-1, may improve differentiation between benign and malignant subsolid pulmonary nodules. Further studies with larger samples and external validation are needed.
journal: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences

title: Global threat of Fusarium head blight to wheat production: Projecting host‐pathogen overlap under climate change
abstract: Wheat is one of the world's most important staple crops, but its production is increasingly threatened by Fusarium head blight, a disease that reduces yield and grain quality. We mapped where wheat and its major disease‐causing fungi are likely to overlap now and under future climate change. Our results show that several major wheat‐producing regions may remain or become persistently vulnerable, including parts of North America, South America, Europe, East Asia, Australia, and New Zealand. These findings can help guide disease monitoring, resistant cultivar deployment and climate‐adaptive crop protection strategies to support global food security. Fusarium head blight (FHB) is a major fungal disease threatening global wheat ( Triticum aestivum ) production and food security. Because climate change may alter the distributions of both wheat and its causal pathogens, this study aimed to assess current and future global FHB risk by identifying areas where host and pathogen suitability overlap. We modeled the potential distributions of wheat and two major FHB pathogens, Fusarium graminearum and F. asiaticum , using an ensemble framework integrating MaxEnt and random forest algorithms. Future projections were generated for 2050 and 2090 under two climate scenarios, SSP2‐4.5 and SSP5‐8.5, using multiple general circulation models. Fusarium graminearum was projected to remain globally widespread, with pronounced northward expansion in the Northern Hemisphere, whereas F. asiaticum was projected to expand further northward in Northeast Asia. Wheat suitability also showed a poleward shift, increasing spatial convergence between host and pathogen distributions. Persistently high‐risk regions were identified in the eastern United States, southeastern South America, Europe, East Asia, southeastern Australia, and New Zealand. These findings indicate that climate change may broaden and intensify global FHB risk by increasing the spatial alignment between wheat and major Fusarium pathogens. The study provides a scientific basis for proactive disease surveillance, targeted deployment of resistant cultivars, and climate‐adaptive management strategies to safeguard wheat production and global food security.

title: 1-Deoxynojirimycin Alleviates Osteoporosis via Promoting LRP5 Signaling in Osteoblasts and BMSCs.
abstract: Osteoporosis is the most common bone disease worldwide, and natural bioactive products that promote osteogenesis are a therapeutic strategy to prevent osteoporosis. 1-Deoxynojirimycin (DNJ) is the major bioactive small molecule in mulberry with anti-diabetic properties, but its effect on osteoporosis treatment remains largely unexplored. This study aims to investigate the effects and underlying mechanisms of DNJ on osteoporosis, with a particular emphasis on its ability to promote osteogenesis pathways. We investigated the bone anabolic ability of DNJ in two well-recognized osteoporosis models: ovariectomy-induced and high-fat diet (HFD)-induced osteoporosis. DNJ prevented estrogen deficiency and HFD-induced bone loss, resulting in increased osteoblast number and inhibited osteoclast number, supporting its therapeutic potential for osteoporosis. Consistent with these in vivo results, in vitro experiments showed that DNJ promoted osteogenic differentiation and matrix mineralization of primary BMSCs and osteoblasts without affecting primary osteoclast differentiation. Mechanistic studies revealed that DNJ increased osteoblastic mineralization by directly binding to the extracellular domain of the transmembrane protein LRP5, thus promoting the Wnt/β-catenin signaling axis to activate the transcription of osteogenesis-related genes in osteoblasts. Taken together, our study demonstrated that DNJ plays a critical role in activating the LRP5/β-catenin pathway, suggesting its potential as a candidate for osteoporosis prevention and treatment.

title: Oxyberberine Ameliorates Type 2 Diabetic Osteoporosis Through Sirtuin 3-Associated Regulation of Autophagy and Ferroptosis in Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cells.
abstract: Type 2 diabetic osteoporosis (T2DOP) is characterized by impaired bone formation and dysfunction of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) under persistent metabolic stress. This study investigated the osteoprotective effects of Oxyberberine (OBB) and the involvement of sirtuin 3 (Sirt3)-associated autophagy and ferroptosis. A high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced T2DOP mouse model and high-glucose-treated BMSCs were used. Integrated omics, UHPLC-HRMS, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and cellular thermal shift assays were used for compound and target evaluation. Osteogenesis, autophagy, oxidative stress, and ferroptosis were assessed using histological, biochemical, fluorescence, and molecular assays. Sirt3 was suppressed using shRNA in BMSCs and systemic adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown in mice. Ferrostatin-1 was used as a ferroptosis inhibitor. OBB improved trabecular bone microarchitecture and osteogenic indices in T2DOP mice. In high-glucose-treated BMSCs, OBB enhanced osteogenic differentiation and autophagy-associated activity while reducing reactive oxygen species, Fe2+ accumulation, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial abnormalities. OBB also decreased Ac-SOD2/SOD2 and Ac-FoxO3a/FoxO3a ratios. Autophagy inhibition weakened the anti-ferroptotic effects of OBB, whereas Ferrostatin-1 partially reproduced its anti-ferroptotic and pro-osteogenic effects. Sirt3 knockdown attenuated OBB-associated protective effects in vitro and reduced skeletal protection in vivo. OBB ameliorates diabetic bone deterioration and high-glucose-induced BMSC dysfunction, with Sirt3-associated regulation of autophagy, redox homeostasis, and ferroptosis contributing to its effects. These findings support further evaluation of OBB as a potential pharmacological candidate for T2DOP.

title: Innovations and emerging trends in applied machine intelligence
abstract: The article presents selected insights from the tenth Dagstuhl Workshop on Applied Machine Intelligence, highlighting recent advances in generative, knowledge‑based, and hybrid AI. It discusses how generative AI is reshaping creative and editorial workflows. The workshop also examined the limitations of LLMs in explanation tasks and quality assurance, emphasising the need for trustworthy, domain‑sensitive and hybrid approaches that combine neural and symbolic methods. Further contributions explore agentic AI as an emerging paradigm for business information systems and revisit abductive reasoning to better integrate formal inference with human‑centred modelling. Together, these perspectives illustrate how hybrid AI can address current shortcomings and support reliable, transparent and domain‑aligned applications across sectors.

A taste for what should not be wanted: generative AI and transgressive fantasy
abstract: With generative AI, everyone can materialize whatever fantasy they can conjure up in their imagination, including transgressive ones. The ‘orthodox’ view on the moral status of fantasies, even of materialized ones, is that such content is outside the scope of morality, since fantasies are quarantined from the agent’s real-world beliefs and desires. In this paper, we challenge this view by arguing that even if we grant that that is the case, repeated engagement with fantasies can contribute to the cultivation of various affective dispositions, or tastes, that can themselves be morally criticizable. We then argue that generative AI allows users to enter a ‘co-creative feedback loop’, a near-instantaneous cycle of prompting, viewing, and refining one’s fantasy, which makes sustained engagement with the transgressive representations very easy. Our claim is that such repeated and focused engagement with transgressive content can contribute to the cultivation of a taste or sensibility for what is morally problematic in those fantasies. If such tastes are morally criticizable, then engaging in practices that cultivate them is also open to moral criticism, even when no one is directly harmed.

Metal–Ligand Design of Co(II), Ni(II), Cu(II), and VO(II) Azo–Schiff Base Complexes: Structural Elucidation, DFT Insights, Promising Biological Activities and DNA Interactions
abstract: A new azo-Schiff base ligand, 2-ethoxy-4-(phenyldiazenyl)− 6-[(phenylimino)methyl]phenol (HL), was synthesized as a bidentate scaffold, giving rise to a new family of VO(II) (VOL), Co(II) (CoL), Ni(II) (NiL), and Cu(II) (CuL) complexes, then comprehensively characterized by CHN analysis, FT-IR, 1 H NMR, UV–Vis, magnetic characterization, TGA, mass spectroscopy, and powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD). From FT-IR data the shift of the azomethine ν(C=N) band from 1618 cm⁻ 1 in HL to 1633–1669 cm⁻ 1 in the complexes, together with the appearance of M–N and M–O vibrations, suggest bidentate coordination of the ligand through the azomethine nitrogen and deprotonated phenolic oxygen atoms. Magnetic susceptibility measurements gave μ eff values of 1.75, 3.92, 2.93, and 1.91 B.M. for VOL, CoL, NiL, and CuL, respectively, consistent with the proposed square-pyramidal geometry of VOL and distorted octahedral geometries of the CoL, NiL, and CuL complexes. CuL complex exhibit the smallest crystallite sizes (27.08 nm). Frontier molecular orbital analysis revealed that metal coordination reduced the energy gap of HL (ΔE = 5.93 eV). Among the complexes, VOL exhibited the lowest energy gap (ΔE = 2.78 eV) and higher softness (σ = 0.72 eV⁻ 1 ). The complexes displayed promising biological activities; CoL was the most active antimicrobial agent against Pseudomonas aeruginosa (AI = 183.3%) and Candida tropicalis (AI = 254.5%). NiL and VOL showed high radical scavenging efficiencies of 96.94% and 95.75%, and VOL exhibited the highest anti-inflammatory activity (IC₅₀ = 41.84 µg/mL), with CT-DNA binding affinity (K b = 2.28 × 10 5 M⁻ 1 ). Molecular docking against COX-2 enzyme showed that VOL complex displays the highest binding affinity (− 8.90 kcal/mol).

title: Integrating spectral and texture indices from Jilin-1 imagery with soil and fertilization data to predict plot-level sugarcane yield, millable stalk population and Brix
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the potential of high spatial resolution Jilin-1 satellite imagery for plot-level prediction of sugarcane yield, millable stalk population (MSP), and Brix, and to assess whether integrating spectral, image texture, soil, and fertilization information (FI) could improve prediction performance for precision sugarcane management. Jilin-1 satellite images covering four sugarcane growth stages (from seedling to maturity) were used to calculate vegetation indices (VIs) and satellite image texture indices (TIs). Representative VIs adopted include the Green Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (GNDVI), Chlorophyll Vegetation Index (CVI), and Green Difference Vegetation Index (GDVI). The three TIs are the normalized difference texture index (NDTI), enhanced vegetation texture index (EVTI), and the newly constructed double-difference ratio texture index (DDRTI). Soil chemical properties (SCPs) and fertilization information were further incorporated with the remotely sensed variables. Machine learning models, including ridge regression (RR), gaussian process regression (GPR), support vector regression (SVR), and categorical boosting (CatBoost) were used for plot-level prediction of sugarcane traits across plant cane and first ratoon cane, and texture window size was optimized to improve TI extraction and model performance. For yield, the combination of VIs and TIs outperformed VIs alone at the tillering stage (R2CV = 0.65, RMSECV = 15.06 t/ha, RPDCV = 1.68). Adding SCPs and FI further improved yield prediction across plant cane and first ratoon cane (R2CV = 0.66, RMSECV = 14.74 t/ha, RPDCV = 1.72). MSP was best predicted at the maturation stage by VIs and TIs, achieving the best performance (R2CV = 0.63, RMSECV = 6602 stalks/ha, RPDCV = 1.66). The best Brix model integrated VIs, TIs, SCPs, and FI at the maturation stage (R2CV = 0.44, RMSECV = 0.53 °Bx, RPDCV = 1.33). SHAP analysis identified VIs as the dominant features for sugarcane traits prediction. And, DDRTI contributed more than NDTI and EVTI in yield and Brix prediction. It is concluded that integrating spectral and texture information from high spatial resolution imagery with soil, and fertilization data is a promising approach for improving plot-level prediction of key sugarcane traits.

Empowering Digital Twins with Generative AI: Applications, Case Studies, and Limitations
abstract: The rise of the Generative Pre-Trained Transformer(GPT) language model, more commonly used as ChatGPT, has brought a spotlight on the ever-developing field of Generative AI (GAI). With current advancements in graphics processing units (GPUs), training and using deep generative models have become easier. Similarly, the developments in edge computing have made it possible to make the most of GAI’s potential for numerous use cases. One such use case involves its integration with Digital Twin technology, offering new possibilities for enhanced simulations, predictive analytics, and real-time decision-making. This paper explores the prospects of combining GAI with Digital Twin technology to create innovative solutions for applications like healthcare, manufacturing, agriculture, cybersecurity, etc. It also discusses how GAI can train Digital Twins by simulating various scenarios and providing different data sets, enabling predictive maintenance. It also delves into the real-world scenarios in which the technology has been implemented. The paper concludes with the limitations of GAI technology for Digital Twin applications, which can be worked upon in the future.

title: Who am I really talking to? Authenticity, transparency, and the case for “AI ticks” in AI-mediated communication
abstract: The growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into everyday messaging systems is transforming the conditions under which interpersonal communication takes place. As AI-mediated communication (AI-MC) becomes increasingly seamless and context-sensitive, it blurs the boundary between human expression and algorithmic assistance. This development raises fundamental questions about potential challenges to authenticity in personal relationships and possible strategies to address them. In this regard, we make three main contributions. First, we offer a technically grounded analysis of emerging AI-MC architectures, distinguishing between external prompting, keyboard-level assistance, and fully integrated in-app co-authoring systems. Second, we develop a normative account of authenticity in AI-MC, understood as a second-person, relationship-sensitive notion, drawing on analytic theories of endorsement, relational normativity, and socially situated self-expression. On this basis, we argue that authenticity cannot be directly engineered by design, since it depends on reflective agency and context-dependent interpersonal obligations. Third, we advance a design-oriented proposal aimed at mitigating authenticity-related concerns without resorting to paternalistic restrictions: the introduction of optional and granular disclosure mechanisms (“AI ticks”) that allow users to signal the presence and degree of AI assistance in a context-sensitive manner. We argue that such forms of transparency function not as a substitute for authenticity, but as a pro-ethical condition that enables agents to negotiate authenticity-based obligations within their relationships. The analysis contributes to current debates on the ethics of AI-mediated communication and the conditions of responsible human–AI interaction.

title: A hybrid negative sampling strategy for landslide susceptibility assessment in mining area
abstract: Reliable delineation of non-landslide samples remains a challenge in data-driven landslide susceptibility assessment, particularly where landslide inventories are incomplete. This study proposes a hybrid negative sampling (HNS) strategy that integrates frequency ratio (FR)-based susceptibility pre-screening with SPY-based positive–unlabeled (PU) learning and differentiated instance weighting. Specifically, an initial pool of fuzzy negatives was derived from frequency ratio-based susceptibility indices, followed by the SPY algorithm to identify relatively high-confidence negative candidates. The integration of these two sources allows candidate negatives with different screening confidence levels to contribute to model training through distinct weights. Applied to Jiaokou County, a loess mining area in China (157 inventory-positive geological hazard records, 1,914 slope units), the methodology was evaluated using a common five-fold spatial holdout validation protocol with XGBoost and SVM, four baseline sampling strategies, and positive-to-negative ratios of 1:1 and 1:2. HNS achieved the highest mean ROC-AUC across all four classifier–ratio configurations, including 0.812 ± 0.041 for XGBoost and 0.797 ± 0.055 for SVM at 1:2, although its improvements over baseline strategies were modest and not statistically significant. Sensitivity and ablation analyses indicated that differentiated weighting primarily influenced the trade-offs among Recall, Precision, and Specificity, without consistently improving overall discrimination or area-based capture performance. Furthermore, SHAP analysis identified fractional vegetation cover (FVC), nighttime lights (NTL), and lithology as the leading contributors to model predictions rather than direct causal factors. Overall, HNS provides a structured approach to incorporating candidate negatives with different screening confidence levels, offering competitive predictive performance with application-dependent benefits and trade-offs.

title: A stock-and-flow model of biofuels and carbon
abstract: The climate benefit of biofuels depends on how well their production offsets the biogenic carbon emitted by their use. It is commonly assumed that carbon uptake during feedstock growth renders biofuels carbon neutral aside from ancillary fossil carbon and other production-related greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. This assumption of a feedstock offset is retained in the lifecycle assessment (LCA) models adopted by policymakers for renewable fuels. However, consideration of land-use change (LUC) and other economically induced effects has revealed carbon flow changes more complex than those of a feedstock offset. This paper presents a relatively simple stock-and-flow model that offers a conceptual understanding of the carbon-related dynamics of biofuel use. The model focuses only on key carbon exchanges, omitting the ancillary emissions while capturing the economic impacts of increased crop yields, cropland expansion with LUC, decreased food demand and petroleum market rebound. Applied to a stylized scenario of corn ethanol use, the model transparently depicts effects and trade-offs previously characterized by LCA and other complex methods. It reframes biofuel carbon neutrality in terms of distinct market-mediated mechanisms of net uptake that can offset the biogenic carbon emitted from biofuel use while highlighting the dynamics of the atmospheric carbon response. As a complement to LCA, stock-and-flow analysis can be informative for policymakers and valuable for educational purposes.

A preliminary characterization of humoral markers and immune gene expression of rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) subjected to emerging Lactococcus petauri infection.
abstract: Lactococcus petauri is an emerging causative agent of lactococcosis in farmed rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) yet host immune responses to this pathogen remain entirely uncharacterized. This study provides a preliminary description of innate immune dynamics following intraperitoneal challenge with 100 CFU/fish of L. petauri strain TURK72 in two genetically selected trout lines, resistant (R) and susceptible (S) to lactococcosis, differentiated by a single nucleotide polymorphism (C>T) at position 140 of the mhc-iiβ gene. No mortality or clinical signs were observed, suggesting the development of a possible subclinical infection model. Leukocyte differential counts, five selected non-specific humoral immune parameters, and RT-qPCR expression of 12 immune-related genes (il-8, mhc-ii, saa, ptx, cox-2, cath-1, cath-2, hepcidin, c3, c5, casp3, casp8) were assessed in head kidney and spleen at 1 and 7 days post-infection (dpi). Among the humoral parameters, only serum lysozyme activity differed significantly, increasing from ∼1,000 U/mL at 1 dpi to ∼2,500-2,700 U/mL at 7 dpi. Gene expression analysis revealed significant time-dependent changes, predominantly in the head kidney at 1 dpi (il-8, mhc-ii, saa, ptx, hepcidin, c5) and in the spleen at 7 dpi (casp3, casp8). These results represent initial immune reference for L. petauri-challenged rainbow trout and highlight areas requiring further investigation.

PING: Physics-informed graph neural network for advection–diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
abstract: Advection-diffusion plays an essential role in transport phenomena such as atmospheric and cloud dynamics. Improved forecasting of cloud motion, in turn, enhances solar power production forecasts and facilitates the integration of additional photovoltaic (PV) sources into the power grid. However, both classical numerical models and emerging deep learning approaches face challenges when applied to spatially irregular sensor networks such as those formed by weather stations. In this work, we adopt a graph signal processing perspective and model advection-diffusion particles as signals on a graph to capture the dynamics of these processes. We introduce a Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PING) for forecasting future advection-diffusion particle concentrations on irregular grids. The model incorporates a discretized advection-diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the loss function to guide learning toward physically consistent solutions. This model is on par with state of the art models on synthetic and real transport phenomena datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index datasets. Furthermore, the PING model is successfully coupled with models for forecasting PV power production. This hybrid approach leverages data fusion from ground-based sensors at PV stations and satellite images with cloud concentration to improve the accuracy of intra-day PV power production.

The role of emotion dysregulation and trait aggression in suicide ideation and attempts: A cross-sectional mediation analysis in a sample of undergraduate students.
abstract: Suicide remains a leading cause of death in the United States, yet factors differentiating suicidal ideation (SI) from suicide attempts (SA) remain insufficiently understood. Although trait aggression and emotion dysregulation are associated with suicidal thoughts and behaviors, no studies have examined aggression as a mediator between emotion dysregulation and SA. Participants consisted of 5229 undergraduates who completed self-report measures of SI/SA history (Suicide Behaviors Questionnaire-Revised), trait aggression (Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire) and emotion dysregulation (Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale [DERS]). Participants were classified into three groups: SA+ (one or more lifetime suicide attempts), SI+ (lifetime suicidal ideation without a suicide attempt), and SI/SA- (no lifetime history of suicidal ideation or attempts). Multinomial logistic regressions examined associations of aggression and emotion dysregulation with SI/SA group membership, and mediation models tested whether aggression mediated associations between emotion dysregulation and SI/SA group membership. Higher trait aggression and emotion dysregulation scores were associated with greater odds of both SI+ and SA+ relative to SI/SA-, as well as greater odds of SA+ relative to SI+. Trait aggression partially mediated associations between emotion dysregulation and SI/SA group membership. Exploratory analyses showed that five of six DERS subscales were associated with both SI+ and SA+ relative to SI/SA-, and three subscales (Nonacceptance, Impulse Control, and Access to Strategies) differentiated SA+ from SI+. These findings suggest that trait aggression and emotion dysregulation are relevant to both SI and SA and that aggression may help account for the association between emotion dysregulation and SA.

title: GPCRAgent: an intelligent multi-agent platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models for GPCR-targeted drug discovery.
abstract: INTRODUCTION G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are major therapeutic targets in drug discovery. However, systematic characterization of GPCR functions and ligand interactions remains constrained by the high cost and complexity of experimental approaches. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance in biomedical question answering, their direct application to GPCR research is limited by insufficient integration of structured domain knowledge and poor interpretability of generated inferences. OBJECTIVES This study aimed to develop an interpretable artificial intelligence framework for automated and traceable analysis of complex GPCR-related problems, and to evaluate its utility in GPCR knowledge reasoning, structural property interpretation, disease target prioritization and ligand recommendation. METHODS We developed GPCRAgent, a multi-agent artificial intelligence framework enabled by VecKG-CoReason, which integrates vector-based semantic retrieval with knowledge graph-guided collaborative reasoning. GPCRAgent was evaluated on benchmark tasks covering GPCR knowledge question answering, multiple-choice reasoning and structural property interpretation. Its practical utility was further assessed in an idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis case study, in which prioritized targets and ligand candidates were supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. RESULTS GPCRAgent achieved accuracies of 85 % in GPCR knowledge question answering, 90 % in multiple-choice reasoning and 83 % in structural property interpretation, outperforming general-purpose LLMs across benchmark tasks. In an idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis case study, GPCRAgent identified LPAR1 as the top candidate and prioritized potential ligands. In a separate renal fibrosis study, experimental evaluation of the optimized LPAR1 ligand in kidney organoids showed suppressed fibrosis-associated marker induction during IL-1β-induced fibrosis. These results illustrate how the platform integrates evidence for target prioritization and structure-based ligand assessment. To facilitate broader adoption, an online platform (https://cbcb.cdutcm.edu.cn/GPCRAgent/) was developed to support GPCR-related drug discovery. CONCLUSION By integrating structured knowledge retrieval with collaborative multi-agent reasoning, GPCRAgent provides an interpretable AI framework for evidence-based GPCR target prioritization, ligand recommendation, and decision support.
