title: Cultivating Resilience: Urban Agriculture and Vertical Farming for Food, Health, and Environment – A Systematic Review
abstract: Background Urbanization and climate change pressure urban food systems. Urban agriculture and vertical farming integrate biological systems, smart technologies, architectural design, food engineering, and environmental management to enhance food security, public health, and environmental sustainability. However, the literature remains fragmented, and no synthesis has examined how these domains interact within a food, health, and environment nexus. Methods This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020. Scopus was searched using a four-block string covering urban agriculture, smart technologies, architecture and biology, and food, health, and environment. From 1,207 documents, after filtering (2016–2026, research articles, English, open access) and screening, 38 studies were included. Data extraction used a standardized form. Quality was assessed with MMAT, JBI, CASP, and ISO 14040/14044. Thematic synthesis addressed eight research questions. Results The 38 studies spanned Architecture (n = 14), IT/Computational Science (n = 8), PSDAL (n = 14), Breeding (n = 7), Biology (n = 7), Public Health (n = 5), and Food Science (n = 4). Quality assessment: 27 low risk, 11 moderate, none high. Key findings: 156% food self-sufficiency; 13.5–20.2% energy savings; 57.14% water savings; 14.1% CO2 reduction; 28.1% VOC reduction; 20.9% PM2.5 reduction; 7.8°C PET reduction; GWP 0.86 kg CO2-eq/MJ; NER 3.7. CRISPR crops, arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, and microalgae improved crop architecture, nutrient uptake, and resource recovery. IoT, AI, digital twins, and robotics enabled precision monitoring and control. Green façades, BIPV, agrivoltaics, and green roofs created multifunctional envelopes. Conclusions Urban agriculture and vertical farming yield synergistic benefits across food, health, and environment. Evidence supports integration into sustainable urban development. Gaps remain: multi-climate validation, economic analysis, policy fragmentation, data standardisation, and social acceptance. Future research should prioritise multi-site validation, economic assessment, regulatory frameworks, data interoperability, and AI-driven optimisation. Cultivating resilience requires integrated, evidence-based approaches aligning biological potential, technological capability, and architectural design.

title: A Computational Brainsphere Model for the Simulation of Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: Nowadays, there are different medical imaging techniques to collect data about the progression of Alzhei\-mer's disease in a patient's brain. These data describe different phenomena which are still not understood from a biological point of view. How can these data sets be combined in a mathematical model to simulate the evolution of such a neurodegenerative disease in a computer? In this snapshot, we present one possible approach to address this task with the help of graph theory and partial differential equations.

title: Dexamethasone restores odontogenic differentiation in lipopolysaccharide-inflamed human dental pulp stem cells
abstract: Pulpitis caused by bacterial infection compromises dental pulp regeneration. This study investigated whether dexamethasone (Dex) could restore odontogenic differentiation in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-inflamed human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs) and examined the involvement of TLR4/NF-κB signaling. hDPSCs isolated from healthy third molars were characterized by flow cytometry, and Cell Counting Kit-8 assays were used to identify noncytotoxic concentrations of LPS (2 μg/mL) and Dex (10−8 mol/L). In an LPS-induced inflammatory model, with or without Dex pretreatment, the expression and secretion of proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β) were quantified by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). TLR4/NF-κB activation was evaluated by qRT-PCR and western blotting, including measurement of total and phosphorylated p65. Odontogenic differentiation was assessed using alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity and Alizarin Red S (ARS) mineralization assays. Data were analyzed by one-way analysis of variance followed by Tukey’s post hoc test. LPS markedly increased cytokine expression and secretion, upregulated TLR4, increased the p-p65/p65 ratio, and reduced ALP activity and mineralized nodule formation. Dex pretreatment significantly attenuated cytokine induction, reduced TLR4 expression and p65 phosphorylation, and restored ALP activity and mineralization relative to LPS alone. Low-dose Dex attenuated LPS-induced inflammation in hDPSCs by suppressing the TLR4/NF-κB axis and restored odontogenic differentiation. These findings support further investigation of localized Dex delivery as an adjunct to vital pulp therapy.

title: Impact of built environment in mountainous aging communities on spatiotemporal behavioural differentiation among older persons: a geospatial analysis
abstract: As demographic aging deepens, the conflict between efficiency of public space resource allocation in mountainous communities and the diverse needs of older persons becomes more prominent. Understanding the adaptability between space and behaviour is crucial for identifying the built environment characteristics associated with the older persons’ outdoor activities for targeted environmental interventions. This study focuses on 42 public spaces in Chongqing, a typical mountainous city in China. From the perspectives of spatial layout and design, it establishes a connection between the public space environment and the characteristics of the older persons’ outdoor activities. Spatial clustering is used to explore the spatiotemporal aggregation of the older persons’ activities, and multiple linear regression models are employed to quantify the associations between environmental factors and the older persons’ behaviours. The results aim to match spatial environments with the activity requirements of older persons, providing evidence for optimising age-friendly built environment upgrades.
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Urban Design and Planning

title: Shift-Aware Group-Calibrated Crop Recommendation with Conformal Uncertainty and Selective Abstention for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Objectives: Crop-recommendation benchmarks are now showing near ceiling classification accuracy, but a high top-1 score provides little guarantee when soil or climate or sensor conditions deviate from the training distribution. The objective of this study is to design a crop recommendation system that is more reliable and that provides more useful predictions even in the presence of distribution shift while avoiding giving strong recommendations when evidence is weak. Method: The primary benchmark contains 2,200 balanced observations, 22 crop classes and seven core agro-climatic variables. CatBoost was used as the probability engine. The reliability layer combines temperature scaling, training-derived agronomic groups, density-ratio screening, group-weighted conformal prediction sets, Mahalanobis out-of-distribution screening and a group-specific empirical-risk operating threshold. Predictive stability, dose-response sensitivity and reliability baselines were evaluated over 10 stratified 80:20 splits using seeds 42–132. Component ablation was repeated over five seeds. Controlled sensitivity tests varied temperature, humidity, rainfall reduction, sensor noise, missingness and their combined severity. Max-softmax, predictive entropy, standard split conformal Adaptive Prediction Sets (APS) and unweighted Regularized Adaptive Prediction Sets (RAPS) were compared at matched acceptance. Findings: Across 10 seeds, CatBoost achieved 99.39 ± 0.37% accuracy (95% CI 99.16–99.62%) and 99.38% macro-F1. The seven-feature and 22-feature CatBoost configurations had the same mean accuracy (99.39%), while the seven-feature model had lower log loss (0.0288 vs 0.0357) and ECE (0.0186 vs 0.0242). Dose-response analysis showed progressive degradation: rainfall reductions of 10–40% reduced mean forced accuracy from 97.70% to 84.20% and 5–20% missingness reduced it from 94.64% to 78.23%. At matched acceptance, simple confidence thresholds and unweighted RAPS achieved higher selective accuracy than the full framework under moderate and severe combined stress. Ablation nevertheless showed that density-ratio screening substantially reduced false-definitive decisions, from 4.23% to 1.77% under moderate combined stress and from 8.82% to 2.05% under severe combined stress, at the cost of increased abstention. Novelty: Group-dependent calibration, conformal candidate sets, explicit distribution-shift screening and selective abstention are all combined in a single pipeline. The primary advantage is that the framework will reduce the number of unsafe definitive recommendations if the data no longer match the training environment. Keywords: Crop Recommendation, Conformal Prediction, Distribution Shift, Precision Agriculture, Selective Abstention, Uncertainty Calibration
journal: Indian Journal Of Science And Technology

title: The Dual Return, Humanitarian and Fiscal, of Investing in Anticipatory Action
abstract: Droughts, floods, and storms are increasingly forecastable days or weeks in advance, yet governments across Latin America and the Caribbean continue to finance them as fiscal surprises. Post-disaster response is costly in three compounding ways: emergency procurement carries a 30 to 50 percent scarcity premium, output and tax revenue contract by 1 to 2 percent, and the resulting gap is closed through expensive borrowing or cuts to health, education, and infrastructure, raising debt service by roughly 2.5 percentage points of GDP. The humanitarian returns of anticipatory action are well established; whether it also protects public budgets has not been. This report develops a deliberately conservative fiscal model, counting only direct emergency spending the government would otherwise incur, and applies it to eleven country-hazard cases. In Honduras, the only case with country-specific data for every parameter, an anticipatory drought programme costing 8 million dollars per year yields a benefit-cost ratio of 1.69 when financing frictions are included and 1.21 on direct costs alone, breaking even if it avoids just 12 percent of emergency spending. Returns are strongest for droughts, where most spending is avoidable, and weaker for floods and storms, where reconstruction dominates. A forty-year simulation shows that a government investing about 0.8 percent of GDP annually in anticipatory action sustains GDP roughly 24 percent higher and a lower debt ratio than one that only reacts. Data gaps limit precision but not direction. The report proposes eight reforms for governments, multilateral development banks, and humanitarian agencies to reframe anticipatory action as a fiscal investment with a dual return.

title: Agronomic feasibility of biostimulant products in dryland wheat crops in Minas Gerais, Brazil
abstract: Fungi and bacteria are among the most widely used biological agents in Brazilian agricultural practices. However, their application in wheat under rainfed tropical conditions remains limited. This study was developed to evaluate the feasibility of applying biological products as inoculants in rainfed wheat cultivation in the southern region of Minas Gerais state. Field trials were carried out over two crop seasons (2021 and 2022) at two and three locations, respectively. Four biological products and a control were tested in this study. The experimental design was a randomized complete block design with four replicates. Seven agronomic traits, such as thousand grain weight and grain yield per hectare, were evaluated. Statistical analyses included combined mixed model analysis, followed by the multilocation GGE biplot and AMMI analysis and a principal components (PCA) multi-trait analysis, using R software. No significant differences were observed among treatments, likely influenced by suboptimal environmental conditions during the study periods. As an initial assessment under field conditions, it was observed that the biological products did not significantly enhance rainfed wheat productivity.

title: Climate footprint in arid Tunisia: cropping systems, crop pattern and crop water productivity
abstract: Tunisia is recognized as vulnerable to climate change impact, ranked 64th out of 187 countries in the 2022 ND-GAIN Index. With less than 150 mm mean annual rainfall, irrigation becomes essential in arid regions. Additional water supply was estimated between 2970 and 9730 m 3 /ha. Crop water productivity (CWP) was high in mulberry and pomegranate (CWP > 1.5 kg/m3), while low values were recorded in species like pistachio, olives and date palm (CWP ≤ 0.5 kg/m3). In palm groves, appropriate water management systems could save until 620 m 3 /ha by a 10% increase in CWP. For olive tree, CWP can be amplified by creation of medium- to high-density orchards, reducing tree spacing within the row. Warm temperatures during the chilling period of dormancy led to the limitation of suitable land for pome fruits’ growing and accentuating alternate bearing in some nut crops. Scion/rootstock combinations are under test for better growth and yield performances. The national strategy should focus on cultivating crops with low chill needs and reduced water consumption. Biodiversity in-situ should be enhanced to promote sustainability and resilience of fruit cropping systems in dry lands.

title: Warp-Geo: Differentiable Geometry Representation for Dynamic-Boundary Simulation and Shape Optimization
abstract: Modern inverse problems and adaptive simulations require efficient and differentiable representations of complex geometries that can be updated frequently for gradient-based optimization. Existing methods cannot simultaneously achieve both. We present Warp-Geo, a differentiable GPU-accelerated framework for reconstructing signed distance fields and evaluating surface normals from point clouds of complex 3D geometries. Warp-Geo combines uniform grids for GPU parallelism with implicit differentiation through the Poisson solve, enabling frequent geometry recomputation while maintaining full differentiability. We demonstrate Warp-Geo on forward SDF reconstruction, dynamic fluid--structure interaction with moving boundaries, and inverse shape optimization via automatic differentiation with gradient validation. GPU scalability analysis confirms practical feasibility for frequent geometry updates. The framework, implemented in Warp and JAX, enables seamless integration with differentiable physics solvers for end-to-end shape optimization.

title: Modeling and simulation methods used in the maritime industry: evolution, applications and future perspectives
abstract: Modeling and simulation (M&S) techniques have evolved from optional engineering tools to indispensable pillars of modern maritime practice. This article presents a comprehensive systematic review of the most important modeling and simulation methodologies applied to maritime industry processes, including workflows for ship design, shipyard fabrication and construction, port and terminal operations, vessel traffic management, maintenance scheduling, supply chain logistics, and risk management procedures. The study demonstrates that M&S techniques enable safer, more efficient, and more environmentally sustainable operations, validated by scientific standards. The COVID-19 pandemic served as a critical catalyst, consolidating the strategic value of M&S as a central component of maritime resilience and innovation. This research traces the evolution of M&S adoption from 2010 to 2025, identifying four dominant research directions: maritime simulators, computational fluid dynamics (CFD)/finite element analysis (FEA), digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based methods. The analysis reveals that while traditional approaches dominated the 2010-2020 period, emerging technologies—particularly digital twins and AI-based methods—have accelerated exponentially since 2020, reflecting the maritime industry's accelerated digitalization. Forward projections through 2035 indicate that AI-based methodologies will experience the highest growth rate at approximately 329%, followed by digital twins at 147%, underscoring the fundamental transformation of maritime research and practice. The integration of these advanced modeling approaches offers optimal equilibrium between physical precision and computational efficiency for addressing complex maritime challenges.

title: Staging, workup, neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapy, and treatment options for cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is the second most common skin cancer worldwide and represents a growing source of morbidity and mortality. Incidence continues to rise globally, driven by an aging population, cumulative ultraviolet exposure, and increasing prevalence of high-risk patient populations. While most cSCCs follow an indolent course, a clinically meaningful subset can demonstrate aggressive behavior, highlighting the need for accurate risk stratification and individualized management strategies. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the clinical presentation, tumor biology, diagnostic evaluation, staging systems, and treatment paradigms for cSCC with emphasis on emerging prognostic tools shaping future care. We summarize key clinical and histopathologic features associated with adverse outcomes, including depth of invasion, differentiation, and perineural involvement, and review current imaging and nodal assessment strategies. Staging frameworks, including American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC), Brigham and Women's Hospital (BWH), and evolving stages of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) systems, are discussed alongside newer models such as risk-integrated squamous cell carcinoma staging, which aim to improve outcome discrimination. Treatment approaches encompassing surgery, radiation therapy, and systemic immunotherapy are reviewed, with particular attention to risk-adapted use of Mohs micrographic surgery, adjuvant radiation therapy (ART), and neoadjuvant or definitive programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) blockade for advanced disease. Finally, we examine emerging molecular prognostic assays, including gene expression profiling (GEP), that offer biologic insight beyond traditional clinicopathologic factors and may refine decisions regarding surveillance and treatment escalation. As the burden of cSCC continues to expand, integrated frameworks incorporating clinical, histopathologic, and molecular data will be essential for optimizing outcomes while minimizing patient and system-level burdens, particularly for identifying tumors requiring treatment escalation.
journal: Italian journal of dermatology and venereology

title: Effect of Prepared Skills and Tools on AI Agent Performance in Power System Steady-State Analysis
DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander
abstract: Soft powered descent landings are becoming evermore important in the field of space exploration and scientific advancement, because of their ability to deliver mission critical payloads, both highly accurately and safely. The high efficiency restriction on planetary landings due to the severely limited fuel supply results in the need for optimal guidance trajectories and control. Model based reinforcement learning is proving to be an important tool in simplifying the highly complex process of generating optimal guidance trajectories and control. In this work, we present DreamLander, a state of the art model based reinforcement learning algorithm based on DreamerV3, to generate optimal guidance and control for a realistic 6 degree of freedom entry descent landing problem. The model based approach creates a sample efficient and highly generalizable model that can be applied to a variety of scenarios whilst maintaining a high degree of accuracy, landing within 2 meters of the designated landing zone, and with velocity norm less than 0.3 meters per second. DreamLander makes use of state sensor observations, making progress toward End-to-End solutions of the Entry Descent Landing problem.

title: Differentiable Search of Compositionally Complex Alloys
abstract: Identifying solid-solution compositions in multicomponent alloys requires exploring a highdimensional design space while accounting for competing phases. We present a differentiable search framework that uses composition gradients of a thermodynamic objective to identify promising alloy regions without exhaustive grid enumeration. In the present implementation, an alchemical machine-learning interatomic potential and ideal configurational entropy provide a differentiable free-energy approximation for random solid solutions. Gradient-based optimization is combined with metadynamics biasing to explore multiple basins, and a tangent-plane criterion screens candidates against precipitation of competing compounds. Applied to the Mg–Al–Sc–Ti–V–Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni system on fcc, bcc, and hcp lattices at 1000 and 1600 K, the search recovers compositionally complex alloy (CCA) families supported by literature. The dominant Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni candidate region expands at 1600 K to include V-containing families and six-principal-element compositions. Screened compositions show substantial departures from equimolarity, highlighting the value of continuous composition optimization. The search also identifies the less-explored Mg–Sc–Ti system, for which preliminary CALPHAD calculations suggest extended high-temperature bcc solid-solution fields under suitable pressure conditions. These results demonstrate a framework for efficient search of CCAs and illustrate how differentiable materials models can serve directly as tools for materials design.

title: MobileNetV2 Optimization with Enhanced Classification Head and Progressive Fine-Tuning Strategy for Banana Leaf Disease Classification
abstract: Banana plants are important horticultural commodities that contribute to food security and economic growth in tropical regions. However, their productivity is often affected by leaf diseases such as sigatoka, cordana, and pestalotiopsis. Manual disease identification has several limitations, including subjectivity, longer processing time, and the risk of misclassification. Therefore, this study proposes an optimized MobileNetV2 model with a fine-tuning strategy for image-based banana leaf disease classification using deep learning. The dataset consists of 1,600 images, divided into 80% training data, 10% validation data, and 10% testing data. Data augmentation techniques, including gaussian blur, horizontal flip, linear contrast, cropping, and rotational shear, were applied to improve model performance. The results show that the proposed model achieved 95.82% accuracy, 95.67% precision, 95.74% recall, and a 95.70% F1-score. These results indicate that the model has good generalization capability and stable performance in classifying each disease category. Compared to previous studies, the proposed approach provides competitive and more optimal results. Therefore, the optimization of MobileNetV2 through a fine-tuning strategy is effective and has strong potential for early detection of banana leaf diseases.

title: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning and Gradient Boosting for Student Dropout Prediction on OULAD
abstract: Student dropout in e-learning remains a persistent problem, and the belief that deep learning outperforms conventional methods has rarely been tested on large, real data. This study compares five models: Random Forest, XGBoost, a convolutional neural network (CNN), a long short-term memory (LSTM) network, and a hybrid CNN-LSTM, for dropout prediction on the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD), covering 32,593 students with 21 aggregated features shared by all models. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied within each fold of a 5-fold stratified cross-validation, and the best model was explained with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and converted into a three-tier Early Warning System (EWS). XGBoost reached the highest accuracy (86.77%) and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9442, ahead of the hybrid CNN-LSTM (accuracy 85.36%, AUC 0.9328). The gap had a large effect size (Cohen's dz = -1.06) but was not significant (p = 0.077). SHAP identified active span as the strongest predictor, and the EWS flagged 10,180 students as high-risk. External validation on an independent public dataset reproduced the ranking (XGBoost AUC 0.923; deep models mean AUC 0.879). Interpretable gradient boosting therefore matches or exceeds deep learning on tabular data.

title: The Language of Local Wisdom: Participatory Communication and Knowledge Conversion in Tourism Villages
abstract: Cultural heritage is sustained not simply by what communities preserve but by how they narrate, explain, and collectively enact what they know. Yet research rarely explains how participatory communication links indigenous knowledge governance with the conversion of tacit cultural expertise into shared resources. This study examines that relationship by integrating the Indigenous Knowledge Management (IKM) cycle with the Socialisation, Externalisation, Combination, and Internalisation (SECI) model in Wukirsari and Kebonagung, two tourism villages in Bantul, Indonesia. Guided by a constructivist multiple-case design, the study drew on semi-structured interviews, participant observation, focus group discussions, and documentary analysis, interpreted through NVivo-assisted thematic coding and cross-case comparison. Findings show that oral explanation, cultural storytelling, guided demonstration, and collaborative learning enable artisans and farmers to communicate batik and agricultural knowledge across generations and audiences. Knowledge identification and transformation were prominent IKM activities, while experiential internalisation featured strongly in SECI processes. Lexical patterns further situated local wisdom within interconnected discussions of community actors, cultural practice, tourism, and collective organisation. However, incomplete digital documentation and uneven access to tourism benefits constrained knowledge continuity and inclusive participation. By positioning participatory communication as the connective practice between knowledge management and conversion, the proposed IKM–SECI synthesis extends language and communication scholarship beyond promotional storytelling towards socially situated knowledge-making. It supports community-controlled documentation, intergenerational learning, and equitable cultural governance as foundations for sustainable rural development.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Crop Yields Across Sixteen Crops in Nigeria
abstract: Accurate crop yield prediction supports agricultural planning, food security and the scheduling of harvest-related resources. This study compared machine learning models for predicting the yields of sixteen major crops in Nigeria, using secondary agricultural and climatic data for 2015–2019 from the Agricultural Performance Survey of Nigeria (National Agricultural Extension and Research Liaison Services and Federal Department of Agricultural Extension) and the Nigerian Meteorological Agency. After preprocessing and the removal of 25 extreme yield observations, 1,962 crop–state–year records were analysed. Five approaches were evaluated: Random Forest; XGBoost; CatBoost; Ridge Regression; and a stacked ensemble combining the three tree-based models with a Ridge Regression meta-learner. XGBoost and CatBoost were run with their original libraries. Performance was assessed with crop-specific five-fold cross-validation, repeated three times, using R², RMSE, MSE and MAE. Under the random, record-level With-State design, in which state was an input and almost all test states also appeared in the training data, CatBoost achieved the highest mean R² (0.357; RMSE = 1.031 t/ha; MAE = 0.754 t/ha), followed by XGBoost (0.331) and Random Forest (0.315); its advantage over Random Forest (0.042; 95% CI 0.018 to 0.067) and XGBoost (0.026; 95% CI 0.003 to 0.049) was small relative to differences among crops. Crop-level R² was highest for yam (0.720), soybean (0.549), onion (0.542) and tomato (0.524) and low for groundnut, ginger, benniseed and okra. The stacked ensemble (mean R² = 0.281) did not outperform the strongest individual models and was below the best individual model in 14 of 16 crops

title: Multi-crop disease classification using a Dilateformer-MobileNetV2 dual-branch fusion network
abstract: Multi-crop disease classification requires discrimination among visually similar symptoms. This study evaluates late feature fusion of Dilateformer and MobileNetV2 for 45-class image classification. The two pooled representations are concatenated before classification. The original experiment achieved 97.21% Top-1 accuracy and 96.63% macro F1 on a 59,905-image benchmark. During revision, PlantDoc-derived samples were added to the existing collection to broaden image diversity. On this expanded 68,682-sample dataset, the selected fusion checkpoint achieved 95.45% accuracy and 93.63% macro F1 on 6,550 test samples, compared with 95.48% accuracy for MobileNetV2. These results belong to distinct data and implementation versions. Dataset provenance, parameter accounting and branch-specific gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) support interpretation of the revision-stage results. The findings demonstrate useful multi-crop classification performance, while showing that simple feature concatenation does not guarantee improvement over a single branch. Independent field generalization remains to be established.

title: The growth period and earliness of cotton (Gossypium spp.): phenological architecture, environmental and genetic regulation, and breeding perspectives
abstract: The growth period of cotton ( Gossypium spp.), spanning emergence to boll opening, is a highly complex quantitative trait governed by genetic potential, thermal accumulation, photoperiodic sensing, resource availability, and agronomic management. Optimizing developmental duration and enhancing earliness are essential for mitigating grain-cotton land competition, enabling mechanized harvesting, and strengthening climate resilience. This review synthesizes current advances in cotton phenology, earliness genetics, and developmental regulation across six key domains. We first detail principal phenological stages and standardized BBCH staging systems based on a systematic literature synthesis following PRISMA principles. Next, we examine thermal and environmental drivers, focusing on growing degree days, photoperiodic responses, and resource dynamics highlighting subgenome-biased expression. We then outline the genetic architecture of earliness, integrating two decades of bi-parental QTL mapping, fine-mapping, meta-QTL analyses, and multi-environment GWAS alongside structural variants predominantly on chromosomes D03, D08, and A10, such as pericentric inversions revealed by telomere-to-telomere assemblies. Furthermore, we delineate the multi-layered molecular and epigenetic networks governing floral induction, centered on the FT-FD-14-3-3 florigen activation complex (FAC), upstream miR157-SPL and HD-Zip I regulators, and histone and DNA methylation dynamics, while establishing rigorous distinctions between true physiological earliness and premature senescence. We also deliberate agronomic management and chemical regulation levers alongside physiological source-sink trade-offs. Finally, we critically assess prospective biotechnological tools, including CRISPR/Cas promoter fine-tuning, genomic selection (GS), high-throughput phenomics, and crop simulation modeling to overcome traditional yield-quality penalties and break linkage drag.

title: Fine-grained sugarcane varietal classification using high-resolution PRSS-1 satellite imagery: a field-validated dataset and a spatial context-aware deep learning framework
abstract: Precise mapping of sugarcane varieties is crucial for precision agriculture, yield evaluation, protection of breeders’ rights, efficient supply chain management and policy formulation. Previous studies highlighted that remote sensing techniques suffered issues such as low spatial resolution and inadequate field-validated ground truth data. Literature review reported usage of statistical analysis methods and machine learning approaches in classification of sugarcane varieties, while constraining the use of deep learning techniques, primarily due to low quality and insufficient dataset size. Furthermore, the literature highlights the scarcity of high spatial resolution datasets that could be attributed to employment of open-source hyper-spectral and low spatial resolution remote sensing data. To the best of our knowledge, neither any industrial solution exists nor any research study is conducted on sugarcane varietal classification in Pakistan. In this study, we made an endeavor to prepare a high-resolution dataset of Pakistani sugarcane varieties (CPF-253 & SL-284) based on field-validated ground truth dataset using Pakistan Remote Sensing Satellite-1 (PRSS-1) single date imagery. We also included non crop classes like urban, water and road as well. Pan-sharpening is employed to enhance the spatial resolution of multispectral bands and retaining the original spectral characteristics, by aligning the 3 m bands to the 1 m panchromatic grid and then injecting the panchromatic residual. The dataset was prepared based on field-validated ground truth collection duly verified by sugarcane scientist, a farmer and research team to make the approach efficient and reliable. The study performed a random pixel split strategy as well as polygon-based experiments; the polygon split is the primary protocol so that a field is not shared across train and test. We proposed a Spatial Context Aware Transformer that includes the spatial context from neighboring pixels, resulting in an enhanced feature space. Specifically, our proposed model is characterized by a unique pixel feature augmentation approach, thus significantly increasing the size of the spectral feature space and making it possible to account for local neighborhood spectral context. We experimented with benchmark machine learning approaches such as support vector machine and random forest on our dataset to evaluate their potential as well. Moreover, we also evaluated deep learning methods suggested by previous studies like CNN and transformer architectures. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed spatial context-aware transformer performed better than other architectures on the polygon-based test set (accuracy 95.2%, macro F1 0.92), compared with SVM 90.5%, Random Forest 92.5%, 1-D CNN 93.0% and the Tabular Transformer 93.4% (gains of 4.7% and 1.8% in accuracy versus SVM and the Tabular-Transformer). On the same 3x3 pixels, a center-only Transformer scored 94.2%; the 3x3 Transformer 95.2%; and 3x3 MLP, CNN and RF scored 93.48%, 93.75% and 92.96%, showing that the neighborhood pixels spectral context along with attention mechanism account for the classification results. We also conducted a binary classification experiment employing CNN, Tabular Transformer, Centre-pixel only Transformer (1x1) and proposed Transformer (3x3). The results demonstrated that Center-pixel only Transformer achieved highest overall accuracy of 88.59%, followed by Tabular Transformer (87.63%), 1D-CNN (87.10%) and proposed Transformer (3x3) (86.99%). The feature significance analysis identified the Green Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and the red spectral band as the most discriminative features for sugarcane varieties classification. The study recommends that future research should incorporate time-series, multi-seasonal and multi-region imagery analysis including non-image information such as climate and production environment for highly precise sugarcane varieties classification in real-world conditions. precise sugarcane varieties classification in real-world conditions.

title: Multi-criteria decision-making and geospatial techniques for groundwater quality mapping in eastern India
abstract: Groundwater is vital for drinking, agriculture and industrial uses. Ensuring its quality through assessment is essential to meet health standards, prevent waterborne diseases and ensure safe consumption. Agriculture in the region heavily depends on groundwater for irrigation, and poor water quality can damage crops, reduce productivity, and harm soil health, leading to economic losses and food security challenges. This study assesses the suitability of groundwater for human use and irrigation by analyzing water quality parameters and calculating the groundwater quality index (GWQI) of Odisha state of India. The evaluation integrates Geographic Information System (GIS) technology with the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), Frequency Ratio (FR), and Shannon’s Entropy (SE) methods. The research encompasses nine thematic layers for assessing irrigation water quality and eleven for drinking water quality. Each thematic layer was assigned a specific weight, and different methodologies were employed for each of the three techniques. The thematic maps were then converted into raster format and integrated within the ArcGIS Environment. To compute the Groundwater Quality Index (GWQI) for each method, a weighted overlay analysis technique was utilized. GWQI maps revealed that 70% of the irrigation areas were rated good by AHP, 63% moderate by FR, and 76% good by SE. For drinking water, 52% of the areas were classified as good by AHP, 75% good by FR, and 66% good by SE. Coastal areas of the state is affected by highly saline groundwater and magnesium contamination. The significant portion of the state experienced hard or very hard groundwater conditions whereas 24.03% of area affected by alkaline water. The outcomes of the three techniques were validated using the error matrix method with data from the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB). The Validation indicated the AHP model was the most accurate, with 78.7% accuracy for irrigation and 80% for drinking water. The study highlights the need for treatment and protection of groundwater in areas with poor quality.

title: Can agricultural green development policies improve the carbon performance of enterprises? Empirical evidence from listed agricultural enterprises in China
abstract: Carbon management in agricultural enterprises is deeply embedded in the agricultural industrial ecosystem. The policy of green development in agriculture provides a key path to solve the predicament of carbon reduction in agriculture. This paper, based on the microdata of 245 listed agricultural enterprises in China from 2011 to 2024, uses a dual machine learning model to investigate the impact of agricultural green development policies on the carbon performance (CP) of agricultural enterprises and its mechanism of action. The research findings are as follows: First, the green development policy for agriculture has significantly enhanced the CP of agricultural enterprises. Second, mechanism tests have shown that promoting green technological innovation, alleviating financing constraints, and increasing external media attention are the three core paths for agricultural green development policies to enhance the CP of agricultural enterprises. Thirdly, heterogeneity analysis indicates that this policy has a more significant effect on enhancing CP for agricultural enterprises located in the second batch of pilot zones, regions with strong environmental regulations, and those with lower digitalization levels. Fourth, an expansive analysis reveals that there is a significant synergy between the agricultural green development policy and the green finance reform and innovation pilot zone policy in enhancing the CP of agricultural enterprises, and the implementation effect of the compound policy is superior to that of a single policy. This article expands the research on the environmental effects of agricultural green development policies from the perspective of micro enterprises, providing empirical evidence and policy inspirations for optimizing the policy system of agricultural green development, strengthening policy coordination, and promoting the green and low-carbon transformation of agricultural enterprises.

title: Access, not ability: gender disparities in access to smartphone-based AI advisory tools for banana disease management among smallholder farmers in Rwanda
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered decision support tools can strengthen crop disease management, but their benefits reach farmers only when access is equitable. This study investigated how gender shapes access to smartphone-based AI advisory tools for banana disease management among smallholder farmers in Rwanda, using Tumaini, an AI-powered banana disease detection app, as a case. Using a mixed-method design, we combined a survey of 357 smallholder farmers across three districts, 12 focus groups, interviews with 61 farmers, and 12-month WhatsApp monitoring of 40 smartphone owners. Men had significantly greater smartphone ownership than women, and gender remained a significant predictor after controlling for education, income, and electricity access. However, among smartphone users, no significant gender differences were observed in digital literacy. Decision-making power was significantly lower among married women than married men. Despite high willingness to adopt, post-training use remained limited, with women significantly less likely to use the app than men. Men interacted with the app on significantly more days than women, though engagement per active day was comparable. Gender disparities in AI-tool use are associated with unequal access to devices and enabling conditions rather than with differences in technical capability. Addressing them requires gender-responsive interventions prioritizing equitable access, localized design (local-language and voice-guided interfaces), and structured group-based support. Such gender-responsive efforts are essential for women farmers to benefit equally from improved banana disease management and sustainable banana production, and for inclusive digital transformation in agriculture.

title: An exploratory classification-tree analysis of crop residue allocation trade-offs in crop-livestock systems in Malawi
abstract: Background Crop residues are a critical resource in crop-livestock systems, serving competing functions as livestock feed and soil-management inputs. However, limited residue availability often creates trade-offs between supporting livestock productivity and maintaining soil fertility, making allocation decisions a persistent challenge in integrated farming systems. Understanding the factors that influence these decisions is important for promoting sustainable intensification and improving resource-use efficiency. Therefore, this study sought to identify the behavioral, socioeconomic, and human-capital factors associated with crop-residue allocation decisions among three participant groups engaged in integrated crop-livestock systems in Malawi. Groups A and B, comprising younger highly educated students and graduates/community youth with mixed livelihood activities, respectively, participated in a structured experiential-learning intervention and served as treatment groups, while Group C, consisting predominantly of older farmers, served as the comparison group. Methods An exploratory Classification and Regression Tree (CART) analysis was conducted using nine group-year observations derived from three investor groups observed over three production cycles. Residue allocation was classified into two categories: livestock feed and land management. Candidate predictor variables included risk tolerance, group income, education level, occupation, marital status, livestock ownership, and exposure to crop-livestock systems (CLS) training. Model performance was evaluated using confusion matrices, classification accuracy, precision, recall, F1-scores, and cross-validation procedures. Results The CART model identified risk tolerance, group income, and education level as the principal factors associated with residue-allocation decisions, with risk tolerance emerging as the root node and strongest discriminator among candidate predictors. Of the nine group-year observations, 55.6% were allocated to land management and 44.4% to livestock feed. Group A allocated residue to land management during the first two production cycles before shifting to livestock feed in the third year, Group B consistently allocated residues to livestock feed across all 3 years, and Group C consistently allocated residues to land management. These patterns suggest that differences in residue-allocation behavior were associated with variation in behavioral, economic, and educational characteristics across the groups. The model achieved perfect classification of the training data and a cross-validated accuracy of 77.8%. Class-specific performance metrics indicated comparable classification performance across allocation categories, with precision, recall, and F1-scores of 0.80 for land management and 0.75 for livestock feed, and macro-average and weighted-average scores of 0.78. Occupation, marital status, livestock ownership, and CLS training were not retained in the final tree structure. Conclusion The findings suggest that residue-allocation decisions within crop-livestock systems are associated primarily with behavioral, economic, and human-capital characteristics, particularly risk tolerance, income, and education. Differences observed among Groups A, B, and C appear to reflect variation in these characteristics rather than group membership itself. However, given the small sample size and exploratory nature of the analysis, the identified decision pathways should be interpreted as indicative patterns rather than robust predictive relationships. Future research using larger datasets and direct measures of learning and behavioral change is needed to validate these findings and strengthen understanding of residue-allocation decision-making in integrated crop-livestock systems.

title: Research Applications and Advances in Threshing and Cleaning Devices for Grain Harvesters
abstract: Against the backdrop of increasing demand for intelligent, high-efficiency, and low-loss harvesting, the operational performance of threshing and cleaning devices directly affects the loss rate, grain quality, and operational efficiency of grain combine harvesters. However, continuous variations in crop type, moisture content, feed rate, and material composition make the threshing and cleaning processes highly complex. Existing devices still encounter problems such as grain breakage, threshing losses, cleaning losses, and increased impurity content under high loads and complex operating conditions. This paper systematically reviews the current research status and development progress of threshing and cleaning devices for grain harvesters and analyzes the structural composition and working principles of threshing and cleaning systems. In terms of threshing, particular attention is given to research progress on tangential-flow, axial-flow, and combined tangential- and longitudinal-flow cylinders, as well as fixed, variable-clearance, rotary, and load-adaptive concave structures. The applications of the discrete element method (DEM) and its coupling with multibody dynamics in analyzing material motion and forces and optimizing parameters are also examined. In terms of cleaning, approaches to structural improvement are summarized with respect to vibrating screen structures, fan and air duct configurations, and related aspects. The applications of DEM, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and coupled CFD–DEM simulations in studies of particle stratification, passage through screen openings, and gas–solid motion are analyzed. Existing cleaning airflow designs have gradually shifted from single-variable airflow rate adjustment toward zoned and multi-source air supply to accommodate material loads in different screen sections. In addition, this paper further reviews technologies for feed rate and operational load sensing, online detection of threshing and cleaning quality, and coordinated control of multiple parameters. Issues concerning material state coupling, simulation model credibility and transferability, and sensing delays are also discussed. Finally, it is proposed that threshing and cleaning devices should evolve from the optimization of individual structures and parameters toward the integration of structural design, numerical simulation, state sensing, and coordinated regulation and control. This review provides a theoretical and technical reference for the low-loss, high-efficiency, and intelligent design of threshing and cleaning devices for grain combine harvesters.

title: Research on the Impact of Demographic Structure Transition on Rural Economic Resilience: Empirical Evidence from China
abstract: Enhancing rural economic resilience is a critical pathway for unleashing endogenous momentum in rural development, safeguarding national food security, and ensuring macroeconomic stability. Employing panel data from 31 Chinese provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities) spanning 2008–2023, this study employs the FAHP–Entropy Weight–TOPSIS composite method to measure the levels of rural demographic structure transition and rural economic resilience. We systematically integrate two-way fixed effects models, mediation-moderation models, and Spatial Durbin Models to identify the mechanisms, transmission pathways, and spatial spillover characteristics through which rural demographic structure transition affects rural economic resilience. The findings indicate that: ① The spatiotemporal evolution of China’s rural economic resilience is characterized by “stage-differentiated growth, synergistic evolution across dimensions, and regional pattern divergence,” and it currently displays a pronounced “core–periphery” structure. ② Rural demographic structure transition exerts a significant and robust negative effect on rural economic resilience. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that this inhibitory effect is only significant in major grain-producing areas and the central region, primarily weakening the resistance-recovery and innovation-reconfiguration capabilities of the rural economy. ③ The mechanism analysis reveals that the mediating effect of agricultural technological progress is not empirically supported, while the scale of cultivated land operations and rural digital infrastructure further amplify this negative effect. From a spatial perspective, changes in rural population structure significantly inhibit the development of rural economic resilience in the local region while generating a significant positive spillover effect on rural economic resilience in neighboring regions. However, the estimated total effects are highly sensitive to the specification of the spatial weight matrix. These findings should therefore be interpreted with caution. ④ Based on these findings, this paper constructs optimization pathways encompassing differentiated talent cultivation, industrial technology empowerment, scale operation adaptation, digital literacy enhancement, and cross-regional agricultural synergy, providing theoretical reference and policy references for hierarchically enhancing rural economic resilience and promoting high-quality agricultural development in the context of demographic structural transformation in the new era.

title: Nitrogen Supply Regulates Productivity, Forage Quality, and Interspecific Interactions in a Silage Maize–Sweet Sorghum Intercropping System in an Arid Irrigated Region
abstract: To clarify the effects of nitrogen application rates on production performance, nutritional quality, and nitrogen use efficiency in a silage maize/sweet sorghum intercropping system, this study established a 3:3 intercropping treatment (B), a silage maize monoculture (S), sweet sorghum monoculture (T)—as well as six nitrogen application rates: 0 (N0), 120 (N1), 180 (N2), 240 (N3), 300 (N4), and 360 kg ha−1 (N5). The results showed that both the cropping system and nitrogen application rate significantly influenced crop growth and yield formation. The N4 (300 kg ha−1) treatment yielded the best results, promoting plant height and dry matter accumulation in both crops. Under intercropping conditions, the biomass of silage maize at the milky stage was significantly higher than that under the N0 treatment. Excessive nitrogen application (N5) did not further promote crop growth and, instead, weakened the complementary benefits of intercropping. The 3:3 intercropping combination with the N4 nitrogen application rate yielded higher forage yields and Feed Value; hay yield and crude protein yield increased by 37.86% and 52.04%, respectively, compared to N0, while crude protein content increased by 10.70%, resulting in a comprehensive production advantage over monoculture. At the same time, the N4 treatment offered a higher return on nitrogen fertilizer investment and helped maintain total nitrogen levels in the 0–40 cm soil layer. In summary, a 3:3 intercropping system of silage maize and sweet sorghum, combined with the application of 300 kg ha−1 of nitrogen fertilizer, is the optimal cultivation model under the conditions of this experiment and can serve as a preliminary recommendation for optimizing nitrogen fertilizer management in grass forage intercropping systems in arid irrigation areas.

title: Selection of Advanced Soybean Lines for Grain Yield and Seed Composition Using Genetic Parameters, a Z Selection Index, and Random Forest Classification
abstract: This study aimed to identify promising soybean lines by combining genetic parameter estimates, simultaneous selection for grain yield and oil content, and a complementary multivariate classification of already phenotyped materials. Four soybean populations were evaluated in Jaboticabal, São Paulo, Brazil, across three agricultural years corresponding to the F5:6, F5:7, and F5:8 generations. The breeding populations comprised 142 advanced lines, whereas the augmented-block field experiment contained 281 plot-level experimental records in each agricultural year because the complete layout also included the repeated check plots required by the design. Population-based analyses were conducted using REML/BLUP, likelihood-ratio tests, and a standardized Z selection index for grain yield and oil content. The Z index identified the highest-ranked lines within each population, including genotypes 19, 42, 38, and 27 in populations A, B, C, and D, respectively. A complementary Random Forest analysis was used as a decision-support classification procedure applied to observed phenotypic information, rather than as a model for forecasting future performance or estimating unknown oil or protein values. The procedure organized the phenotypic profiles into oil-based, protein-based, and combined oil-plus-protein groups. For the combined scenario, the classification criterion rewarded high standardized values for both seed-composition traits while penalizing imbalance between them. Out-of-fold classification results showed high agreement with the predefined operational groups, with overall accuracy rates of 0.99, 1.00, and 0.98 for the oil, protein, and combined scenarios, respectively. Principal component analysis described the multivariate structure of the same phenotypic dataset. Because generation and crop year coincide, changes in genetic parameter estimates across successive evaluations cannot be attributed exclusively to selection. Overall, the results support the use of mixed models and the Z index for line selection, while Random Forest provides a complementary framework for organizing already measured materials according to contrasting and combined seed-composition objectives.

title: DTW-kNN and Sentinel-2 NDVI Time Series for Field-Scale Maize Identification and Multi-Crop Classification in an African Smallholder Landscape
abstract: Mapping crops at the field scale supports agricultural planning, production monitoring and resource allocation. However, this remains difficult in smallholder landscapes, where planting dates vary among farms, ground-reference data are limited, and fields are small, fragmented and irregularly shaped. This study evaluated Sentinel-2 Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) time series combined with Dynamic Time Warping k-nearest neighbour (DTW-kNN) for maize identification and multi-crop classification in the O.R. Tambo District Municipality, South Africa.. A maize reference trajectory was first developed from known maize fields and then assessed against independent maize validation fields and candidate unknown fields. Known maize fields produced low DTW distances to the maize reference trajectory, while Days After Planting alignment showed a clear maize phenological pattern, with NDVI increasing after planting, peaking between approximately 90 and 120 DAP, and declining thereafter. For multi-crop classification, a simple mean-reference DTW baseline achieved 80.0% accuracy on independent validation fields. Retaining individual reference-field trajectories (DTW-kNN) instead of a single mean reference improved on this baseline. Training-only cross-validation selected DTW-kNN with k = 1 and a one-composite warping window; this configuration achieved 92.9% independent validation accuracy, comparable to benchmark Random Forest and Support Vector Machine classifiers (95.7%). DTW-kNN remained competitive while retaining direct temporal-similarity interpretation. When applied to 128 unlabelled fields, the selected DTW-kNN classifier predicted 106 fields as maize and 22 as soybean, with 65.6% of predictions classified with high confidence. The findings show that Sentinel-2 NDVI time series combined with DTW-kNN can support interpretable field-level crop classification in fragmented smallholder farming systems.

title: GDF15 Mediates the Anti-Obesity Effects of Ursolic Acid via Coordinated Regulation of Lipid Metabolism
abstract: Obesity is a metabolic syndrome characterized by the excessive accumulation of adipose tissue. Ursolic acid (UA) modulates diverse metabolic processes, including the amelioration of metabolic syndrome and attenuation of hepatic steatosis. However, the specific effects and underlying mechanisms by which UA ameliorates high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity and associated metabolic disorders remain to be elucidated. In this study, we investigated the ameliorative effects of UA on obesity using an HFD-induced obese mouse model and a sodium oleate-induced HepG2 cell model. Our results demonstrated that UA supplementation significantly reduced HFD-induced weight gain and visceral fat mass, lowered serum and hepatic total cholesterol (TC), triglyceride (TG), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels while increasing high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels, attenuated hepatic steatosis with a marked reduction in hepatic TG content, and suppressed inflammation with decreased serum and hepatic interleukin-18 (IL-18) and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) levels. Correspondingly, in HepG2 cells, UA mitigated sodium oleate-induced TG and TC accumulation, decreased intracellular ROS, and lowered IL-18 and IL-1β secretion. Additionally, UA upregulated the lipolytic enzymes adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) and hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) at both protein and mRNA levels, downregulated the lipogenic factors sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1c (SREBP1c) and stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1 (SCD-1), and suppressed absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2) and apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD (ASC) expression. Notably, we identified growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) as a critical upstream mediator of UA’s multifaceted effects. UA robustly upregulated GDF15 expression both in vivo and in vitro, and siRNA-mediated knockdown of GDF15 completely abolished UA’s beneficial actions, including its regulation of lipolysis/lipogenesis, inhibition of the AIM2 inflammasome, reduction in oxidative stress, and attenuation of lipid accumulation. In summary, our findings reveal that UA ameliorates obesity-related metabolic disorders and inflammation by modulating GDF15 expression, which in turn coordinately regulates lipid catabolism/anabolism pathways and AIM2 inflammasome activation. These results establish the UA-GDF15 axis as a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of obesity and its metabolic complications.

title: Low-Power FPGA-Based Differentiable Mesh Rendering for On-Device Dense Photometric Pose Refinement
abstract: Differentiable rasterization enables image inversion by providing gradients of image-based losses with respect to camera and scene parameters, and has become a practical foundation for inverse graphics and photometric estimation on GPUs. However, the real-time deployment of differentiable rendering in embedded perception remains challenging due to the high cost of per-pixel sampling and gradient computation. In this work, we present an nvdiffrast-inspired differentiable rasterization engine implemented on FPGA and demonstrate its use in a simplified dense photometric pose-refinement task. Our design follows the modular philosophy of nvdiffrast while specializing it for deterministic, low-latency hardware execution. We implement point-sampled triangle rasterization with hard z-buffer visibility, perspective-correct interpolation, and an analytic antialiasing stage that yields stable, non-zero gradients at silhouettes and occlusion boundaries. Unlike GPU pipelines where texturing behavior may be hardware defined, our FPGA implementation controls the texture sampler, enabling a fused rasterize–interpolate–texture operator with a matched backward pass. Beyond pixelwise gradients, we introduce an on-device accumulation scheme that directly forms Gauss–Newton normal-equation terms, enabling second-order pose updates with substantially fewer iterations than gradient descent. We validate forward rendering and derivatives against a GLSL reference implementation, and report FPGA resource utilization and runtime. The core rasterization and analytic antialiasing pipeline achieves 2.5 ms per frame, while the full textured keyframe-projection operator runs in 8 ms per frame on an AMD Kria KV260. In a dense photometric pose-refinement evaluation on synthetic and real sequences, the proposed Jacobian accumulation reduces the number of optimization iterations required for convergence, improving time-to-solution despite the added cost of texturing. Together with a post-implementation on-chip power estimate of 3.662 W and an estimated 29.3 mJ per full-resolution differentiable rendering iteration, these results provide an implementation-level estimate of the accelerator’s power envelope for real-time photometric tracking and refinement.

title: ECG-Based Arrhythmia Analysis and Short-Term Ventricular Event Prediction Using Deep Learning
abstract: Early prediction and characterization of ventricular arrhythmias are important for reducing the risk of sudden cardiac death, a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Conventional ECG analysis commonly relies on full waveform processing, which can be computationally intensive and may provide limited interpretability at the individual-beat level. In this study, we propose a lightweight Hybrid CNN framework for beat-level ECG analysis and short-term prediction of ventricular arrhythmic events. ECG signals are segmented into individual heartbeats, and eleven statistical, temporal, and morphological features, namely the mean, standard deviation, maximum, minimum, RR interval, RR ratio, QRS amplitude, QRS width, energy, skewness, and kurtosis, are extracted from each beat. At each prediction time point, a sequence containing up to 300 consecutive heartbeats is organized as the input to the proposed Hybrid CNN, with a minimum sequence length of 20 beats. The primary task is binary prediction of the occurrence of a ventricular arrhythmic event within the subsequent five-minute window, where a ventricular event is defined by a “V” annotation in the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. To assess the reliability and reproducibility of the proposed framework, the experimental analysis includes annotation-parser validation, explicit definition of ventricular event labels, automatic R-peak detection, feature ablation analysis, quantitative explainability, and confusion-matrix-based performance evaluation. The current implementation uses offline preprocessing, and its suitability for strictly causal real-time prediction requires further investigation. Experiments conducted on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database demonstrate that the proposed Hybrid CNN achieves a sensitivity of 90.22% and a specificity of 89.55% for short-term ventricular event prediction. The ablation further evaluates the contribution and temporal robustness of the proposed beat-level representation. Overall, the proposed framework provides an integrated and lightweight solution for beat-level ECG representation, arrhythmia characterization, and short-term ventricular event prediction, with potential applicability to real-time wearable and edge-AI ECG monitoring systems.

title: MeteoFormer: The Accuracy–Faithfulness Trade-Off of Built-In Attention in Meteorological Forecasting
abstract: Built-in attention is often presented as a free explanation of what a forecasting transformer relies on, but the claim is rarely tested. We test it on MeteoFormer, a patch-based transformer with single-head variable and temporal attention that forecasts four weather variables 24 h ahead from 96 h of hourly input on the Jena and Beijing PRSA datasets. Against ten baselines trained under one protocol with five seeds, MeteoFormer has the lowest mean absolute error on Jena (3.025 against 3.107 for Crossformer, Diebold–Mariano p < 0.05 against every baseline after Holm correction) and is level with Crossformer on Beijing (4.151 against 4.138, p = 0.72), while Crossformer has the lower squared error, a difference traced to humidity. The model depends heavily on the latest observations: losing the last 16 h raises its Jena error by 73% and drops it from first to sixth place. The explanation claim fails. The fidelity of the variable attention does not differ from zero (0.012 on Jena, 0.046 on Beijing), far below SHAP on the same model; the temporal attention is almost uniform although the forecast depends mainly on the last 16 h; and the configuration selected for accuracy has the least faithful attention (0.012 against 0.181 with instance normalization, p = 0.001), but the more faithful configuration is less accurate (Jena MAE 3.195 against 3.025) and its attention remains below SHAP.

title: Sedimentary Reorganization at the Day River Mouth (Southern Red River Delta, Vietnam) Following Coastal Infrastructure Development: Evidence from EMMA and Grain-Size Trend Analysis
abstract: Grain-size distributions of surface sediments provide indicators of sediment provenance and transport, and their comparison through time can reveal changes in the sedimentary organization at river mouths. This study analyzes 113 surface-sediment samples collected in April 2016 and April 2025 from the Day River mouth, southern Red River Delta, Vietnam, under the same seasonal regime at the end of the northeast monsoon. The datasets were collected before and after the construction of a mainland–Con Noi sandbar sea-crossing road and bridge and the subsequent appearance of a T-shaped spur dike system. Grain-size distributions were jointly analyzed using End-member Modelling Analysis (EMMA) and Grain-Size Trend Analysis (GSTA). Three end-members were consistently resolved in both datasets, explaining 86% and 91% of the total variance: EM1, medium silt (10.1–11.6 μm); EM2, very fine sand (88–101 μm); and EM3, fine sand (133–175 μm). EM1 is concentrated along the river channel, river mouth and northern nearshore zone, whereas EM3 is mainly distributed in the southern to southeastern offshore sector and EM2 occupies transitional zones. GSTA identifies two co-existing trends, FB- associated with finer-grained sediment trends and CB+ associated with the relative redistribution and accumulation of coarser material. Between 2016 and 2025, EM1 displayed a higher variance contribution in the 2025 dataset (43%) than in 2016 (35%), whereas EM3 displayed the opposite tendency (35% versus 45%); EM2 remained broadly similar (20–22%). However, statistical comparisons performed on paired stations and within the common sampling domain did not detect significant differences in the overall proportions of the end-members. In contrast, mapped distributions of the end-members revealed descriptive differences in their spatial organization between surveys. The FB- XOR CB+ representation further highlights a more spatially differentiated pattern in 2025, particularly around Con Noi and the southeastern offshore sector. These results suggest that the principal decadal evolution was expressed as a spatial reorganization of persistent sediment components and associated grain-size trend patterns, rather than as a statistically demonstrable change in their overall proportions or the emergence of a new sedimentary regime. The observed patterns are consistent with the combined influence of the fluvial sediment supply, tidal and wave processes, and southward residual longshore sediment transport. Coastal infrastructure constructed between the two surveys may have contributed to local sedimentary reorganization at the Day River mouth.

title: Calibrated and Explainable Temporal Forecasting of Psychoemotional Risk from Longitudinal Mobile-Health Data
abstract: Mobile-health systems generate repeated, time-stamped observations, but future-risk forecasts must be reliable rather than merely discriminative. We evaluate Temporal Calibrated Explainable Risk Forecasting (T-CERF) for irregular ecological momentary assessment histories. Study A used 5726 forecasting examples from 542 Corona Health participants, a 56-day history window, and a 28-day primary horizon. On the fixed participant-independent test set, T-CERF achieved a PR-AUC of 0.867, ROC-AUC of 0.946, and Brier score of 0.083. Random Forest matched its ROC-AUC (0.947 versus 0.946), while the Persistence baseline yielded a higher F1-score (0.786 versus 0.761). The PR-AUC difference from the matched current-only model was +0.023, but its paired participant-level bootstrap interval included zero. Across five additional participant-level splits, ΔPR-AUC averaged +0.0106 (SD 0.0262; range −0.0298 to +0.0399), with one split favoring the current-only model. Thus, a consistent discriminative benefit from temporal history was not established. Temperature Scaling improved calibration, while ensemble uncertainty supported selective prediction. A separate HBSC Kazakhstan analysis remains exploratory. T-CERF is therefore presented as a calibrated, uncertainty-aware mobile-health forecasting framework rather than as a hardware or network-level IoT implementation.

title: A Multi-Source Data Fusion and PSO-Transformer Decision Support System for Gold Price Volatility Forecasting and Risk Warning
abstract: Gold volatility responds to shocks and sentiment, yet the two are rarely fused, and forecasts seldom become actionable. We link a multi-source fusion subsystem to a risk-warning layer through a Transformer whose three pre-registered hyperparameters are searched by particle swarm optimization (PSO-Transformer). It fuses video sentiment, headline scoring and market factors screened to 20 of 21 candidates; the decision side maps the predicted realized variance RVt/Mt (bp2, non-annualized) into three traffic-light tiers of a calibrated predictive distribution. On 5-min spot gold data (January–June 2025, 126 trading days), the PSO-Transformer attains a one-step MAE of 8.038, a 36.5% average improvement over seven baselines under protocol P1, where selection and evaluation share one window; under the leak-free protocol P2, the same pipeline attains 10.16 against 8.82 for the GRU, so the first place reflects the P1 design, not an independent out-of-sample comparison. Diebold–Mariano gains over GARCH, SVM and XGBoost survive a Holm correction. Walk-forward backtesting over 59 origins with persistence-anchored alerts yields 67.8% tier accuracy, 78.8% high-risk precision and 92.9% recall, with the neural engine fed into the same rule attaining 45.5% against 61.4%. One instrument, six months: a documented architecture, not a demonstrated transfer.

title: Design of Auxetic Metamaterials via Adaptive Body-Fitted Mesh-Based Bi-Directional Evolutionary Structural Optimization
abstract: Fixed-grid topology optimization is widely used for auxetic metamaterial design, but its discretization-dependent boundaries may require substantial refinement or post-processing, potentially altering slender ligaments and the resulting deformation mechanisms. This study develops an adaptive body-fitted bi-directional evolutionary structural optimization (BESO) framework for two-dimensional periodic auxetic metamaterials. The topology is persistently represented by an implicit field on a fixed background grid, while a geometry-conforming T6 finite-element mesh is regenerated for periodic homogenization at each iteration. Mutual-energy sensitivities are normalized by element area and transferred from the nonuniform analysis mesh back to the background design field, enabling stable evolutionary updates under repeated remeshing. The adaptive workflow reconstructs the boundary within the optimization loop, avoiding a separate post-optimization B-spline smoothing step; in the fixed-grid Q4 comparison, this smoothing reduces the magnitude of the Poisson’s ratio. The mesh-parameter study shows how the adaptive mesh-size ratio affects computational time and the optimized auxetic response. In the tested comparison, the adaptive workflow shows closer agreement between the optimized and independently verified Poisson’s ratios.
