title: A time-resolved image-environment dataset for tatsoi growth monitoring and intelligent phytoprotection benchmarking
abstract: Image-based crop monitoring is now widely used in sustainable plant production, but public datasets that combine visual canopy appearance with synchronized local environmental measurements remain scarce. As a result, models are difficult to evaluate under field variation that must operate under field variation, including changes in plant growth, microclimate, soil conditions, pest pressure, illumination, and acquisition date. We present a time-resolved tatsoi ( Brassica campestris L. ssp. chinensis var. rosularis Tsen) image-environment dataset collected during winter cultivation from 12 November 2025 to 28 February 2026. The dataset contains 3456 plant-level images from 128 repeatedly imaged plants across 27 acquisition dates. Each image is linked to Labelme polygon annotations of the tatsoi canopy, derived bounding boxes and segmentation masks, plant identity, acquisition date, seven phenotype or condition labels, and synchronized field solar insecticidal lamp Internet of Things (SIL-IoT) records. The sensor-derived metadata used in the baseline analyses include air temperature and humidity, illumination, rain-status records, device-level pest-signal counts, soil moisture and temperature, wind speed, and wind direction. These metadata are provided as nearest sensor readings and as 1 h, 6 h, and 24 h pre-capture aggregates. Standardized random, temporal, and plant-holdout splits are provided to support reproducible evaluation. Baseline benchmarks showed that the resource can be reused for canopy detection, canopy segmentation, and image-environment trait recognition. Under the plant-holdout split, YOLOv8n reached a box mAP50–95 of 0.887, RetinaNet-R50 reached a box mAP50–95 of 0.826 among torchvision detectors, and Swin-T with environmental features reached a mean macro-F1 of 0.819 across plant-level traits. The dataset provides a reusable resource for multimodal crop phenotyping, field-condition visual benchmarking, and intelligent phytoprotection research.

title: Terminal Cooperative Guidance Based on LOS Geometry and Optimal Control for TAD Engagement
abstract: Some existing three-body cooperative guidance methods for terminal interception rely on the attacker’s future-maneuver prediction or explicit forecasting of its future maneuver and may require high overload demand. Therefore, this paper presents an improved terminal cooperative guidance law, referred to as LOS-OCG (LOS-based Optimal Cooperative Guidance), by integrating modified line-of-sight (LOS) geometry and optimal control. An optimal performance index with terminal soft objectives on miss distance, LOS angle and target velocity direction is constructed to solve the cooperative control equation. Geometric sign heuristic analysis is employed to qualitatively examine the convergence trend and to calculate the rough initial aiming, followed by multi-condition comparison, Monte Carlo verification and batch simulations. Under the engagement conditions selected in this paper, Monte Carlo robustness tests with 18,000 runs across nine engagement configurations yield narrow 95% confidence intervals. Among the 6427 successful trajectories of 6435-trajectory batch grid, the defender’s peak overload remains below 6 g for 80.82%, below 9 g for 95.49%, and 97.15% achieve a defender maneuver effort no greater than 30% of the attacker’s. The proposed method features closed-form analytical gains within the single-cycle frozen framework, propagates a frozen surrogate of the current maneuver to the terminal time, and requires neither an identified attacker guidance law nor explicit multi-step maneuver forecasting. It exhibits acceptable robustness and presents a viable planar research concept for terminal cooperative interception.

title: Vision–Language–Action Model for Agricultural Fresh Produce Handling with a Humanoid Robot
abstract: Reaching, grasping, and placing delicate fresh produce are among the most labor-intensive operations in agricultural production, yet most robotic solutions remain task-specific, single-crop systems that generalize poorly across the morphological diversity of fresh produce. This study investigates whether a large, pre-trained Vision–Language–Action (VLA) model can be adapted with only modest demonstration data to serve as a flexible language-conditioned produce-handling policy on a humanoid robotic platform. The NVIDIA GR00T N1.7-3B foundation model is fine-tuned for a standard 23-degree-of-freedom Unitree G1 humanoid robot fitted with two Dex3-1 three-finger dexterous hands, whose arm and hand joint streams form a 24-dimensional combined manipulation command space. This study also compared the π0.5 VLA model. Demonstrations were collected through a Meta Quest 3 extended-reality teleoperation pipeline augmented with a multi-label recording mode that embeds a natural-language goal in each episode, yielding 605 language-conditioned demonstrations (261,724 synchronized frames) across four produce categories (lemon, peach, pear, and tomato). A dual-camera design paired a wide-angle head camera for global scene context with a wrist-mounted camera for close-range grasp feedback. The results show that the fine-tuned policy achieved a 96.25% individual-trial success rate and 85% on mixed-scene trials requiring retrieval of the language-specified item. However, adapting the π0.5 VLA model to the same data achieved 68.75% individual-trial success. Furthermore, a controlled ablation isolated the role of close-range perception. Without wrist-camera input, the policy reached every target in single-item trials but failed to secure a single grasp, resulting in 0% pick-and-place success despite comparable training loss. Therefore, close-range wrist perception was a precondition for contact in this setting. Together, these results demonstrate that VLA fine-tuning can transform a pre-trained humanoid foundation model into a reliable, data-efficient policy for multi-category fresh produce handling. This work provides a practical step toward flexible humanoid robotic systems for agricultural pick-and-place, sorting, and postharvest automation.

title: Statistical Descriptors of β-Variational Autoencoder Latent Feature Maps for Image-Based Blueberry Canopy-Size Phenotyping
abstract: Plant-level canopy-size assessment is important for precision agriculture applications, including crop monitoring and variable-rate fertilization, but trait-specific annotation remains costly. This study investigates whether unsupervised β-Variational Autoencoder (β-VAE) latent maps from an image reconstruction model encode canopy-size information recoverable through compact statistical descriptors. A β-VAE was trained on the designated training partitions of a dataset of 2043 field-acquired RGB images of individual blueberry plants, without canopy-size labels. The encoder generated spatial posterior mean (μ) and log-variance (logσ2) maps, from which per-location Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence maps were also computed. These maps were summarized into five descriptor configurations and evaluated using a separate classifier. The 300-feature reference configuration, which combined μ, logσ2, and KL descriptors, achieved 73.11% accuracy, 73.54% balanced accuracy, and 73.42% macro-F1 under a stratified-random split. Independent retraining of the complete pipeline for three acquisition session-held-out evaluations yielded 63.04 ± 4.54% balanced accuracy and 60.92 ± 6.68% macro-F1. Corresponding balanced accuracies were 78.77 ± 7.24% for ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B0 and 54.13 ± 4.95% for a radial basis function support vector machine using 22 image descriptors; summaries are unweighted means ± sample standard deviations across sessions. These findings support a compact and modular framework for image-based blueberry canopy-size phenotyping, in which unsupervised representation learning is separated from downstream supervised classification, although performance remained below supervised transfer learning. The reference trait measures image-relative canopy extent, not physically calibrated plant size.

title: Deep Percolation Risk and Optimal Irrigation Threshold for Sunflower Under Mulched Drip Irrigation: A HYDRUS-2D Modeling Study
abstract: Deep percolation induced by excessive irrigation represents a critical bottleneck limiting water use efficiency in sunflower fields under mulched drip irrigation in arid regions. However, systematic understanding of stage-specific allocation of water losses remains limited. This study conducted a field experiment on oilseed sunflower with three irrigation levels (300, 450, and 600 mm) in Shihezi, Xinjiang. The two-dimensional finite-element software, version 2.05 (HYDRUS-2D model) was calibrated and validated to simulate water balance components in the 0–60 cm soil profile across growth stages. The model demonstrated satisfactory performance, with coefficient of determination (R2) ≥ 0.70, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.025–0.039 cm3 cm−3 and Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) of 0.574–0.822. Results showed that evaporation responded weakly to irrigation amount (increasing by only 1.3 mm from 300 to 600 mm), while deep percolation increased nonlinearly, with the high-irrigation treatment exhibiting a percolation rate approximately five times that of the low-irrigation treatment. Crop water consumption exhibited pronounced stage-specific differences: during the seedling stage, evapotranspiration (92.29 mm) was derived almost entirely from soil evaporation; and from budding to filling (S2–S5), cumulative root water uptake accounted for 75–78% of seasonal total, while percolation losses during this period represented 91.5–96.3% of total deep percolation. An irrigation amount of 450 mm optimized the trade-off between grain yield and water use efficiency. A “small and frequent” irrigation strategy during S2–S5 is recommended to minimize deep percolation and enhance irrigation water use efficiency.

title: A BeiDou-Based Intelligent Monitoring System and Multi-Level Trajectory Fusion Framework for Operational Area Estimation: A Case Study on Large-Scale Automated Transplanting
abstract: Accurate estimation of the effective operational area of automatic transplanters is essential for evaluating machinery productivity, improving field management efficiency, and supporting digital agricultural applications. However, operational-area estimation based on low-cost BeiDou trajectories remains challenging because raw trajectories are often affected by positioning uncertainty, trajectory discontinuities, and non-productive machine movements, including headland turning, road transportation, empty transfer, and seedling loading/unloading operations. Directly using all recorded trajectories may therefore introduce considerable area overestimation, whereas excessive trajectory filtering may remove valid productive operations. This study proposes a state-aware hierarchical trajectory fusion framework coupled with a low-cost BeiDou-based monitoring system for automatic operation-state recognition and operational-area estimation of transplanters. Unlike conventional trajectory-processing approaches that mainly focus on geometric smoothing or spatial clustering, the proposed framework jointly considers positioning reliability, motion consistency, spatiotemporal continuity, and operational semantics to extract productive transplanting trajectories from noisy GNSS observations. Three field datasets containing more than 49,000 trajectory points (approximately 30,000 valid records after preprocessing) were collected from automatic transplanters operating in Xinjiang, China. The proposed framework integrated adaptive trajectory filtering, motion-consistency screening, spatiotemporal continuity optimization, and operation-state recognition to classify five operation states, including field transplanting, headland turning, empty transfer, road travel, and seedling loading/unloading. After productive transplanting trajectories were identified, coordinate transformation was applied to convert the retained trajectories into a local coordinate system for operational-area estimation using the effective working width of 1.2 m obtained from overlap and pass-spacing correction of the nominal 1.4 m width. The estimated operational areas were validated against RTK-derived reference measurements. Across the three datasets, the proposed framework achieved F1-scores ranging from 0.94 to 0.95, trajectory continuity rates of 94.2–96.5%, and effective trajectory-length retention above 99.5%. The estimated operational-area bias was limited to 0.9–1.5%, compared with 12.8–18.4% obtained from direct calculation using raw trajectories. These results demonstrate that integrating motion consistency, spatiotemporal continuity, and operational-state recognition can effectively reduce operational-area overestimation caused by non-productive trajectories. The proposed framework provides a low-cost and interpretable approach for agricultural machinery operational monitoring and operational-area estimation. Although low-cost GNSS positioning alone cannot satisfy centimeter-level autonomous navigation requirements, the proposed approach provides a practical foundation for future integration with multi-sensor perception, edge-intelligent processing, and digital agricultural management systems.

title: Mineral Fertilization of Maize Under Contrasting Organic Backgrounds on a Post-Mining Anthropogenic Protosol at Husnicioara, Romania: A Historical Reanalysis of Soil Fertility and P–K Balances
abstract: Post-mining agricultural reclamation requires crop productivity to be rebuilt without exhausting nutrient reserves or destabilizing soil chemistry. We reanalyzed a three-year maize study at Husnicioara, Romania, using the original doctoral thesis as the primary provenance source. Baseline soil measurements were made in 2000 and final measurements in 2003. The archive documents two parallel experiments: one on a single 25 t ha−1 well-fermented manure background and one without manure, each containing seven mineral treatments (N0, N40, N80, N120, N160, N160P80, and N160P80K80) in four replicates. Because a common randomized factorial layout was not recovered, model-based tests were limited to within-experiment treatment-associated soil changes; between-background differences were descriptive. Change-score ANOVA identified strong treatment-associated differences in pH decline, mobile P, and mobile K in both experiments (all p < 0.001), whereas the humus response was not robust. Cumulative yield, available only as treatment totals, reached 7.416 t ha−1 without manure and 13.806 t ha−1 on the manure background. P80 was associated with higher extractable P, and K80 with higher extractable K. Historical P–K residuals are interpreted as soil-test balance diagnostics rather than closed nutrient budgets. The study supports staged, monitored reclamation management and a new randomized validation trial, not a current economic optimum.

title: Tabular Foundation Models Versus Established Tabular Learners: A Regime-Stratified Critical Review
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are pretrained once across many tables and applied to a new table by conditioning on its labelled rows, with no training on that table. They challenge gradient-boosted decision trees, the long-standing default for tabular prediction, but the published comparisons are hard to interpret, because studies differ in data regime, split design, baseline tuning, and metric. This review assesses the evidence regime by regime. From 76 peer-reviewed works selected under a documented protocol, it defines TFMs by reusable cross-table pretraining, organises them by pretraining data, context mechanism, scale, modality, and task interface, and compares them with tree ensembles, deep tabular networks, and tabular-to-image methods. Seven recurring claims are graded on peer review, evaluator independence, split match, baseline strength, and replication, with all scores published. One claim is strongly supported: on small-to-medium independent and identically distributed tables, TFMs match or exceed tuned tree ensembles without per-dataset tuning. Tuned tree-based and deep models remain as strong or stronger on temporal, feature-engineered data; above 10,000 rows the evidence is developer-reported except for one independent clinical benchmark; and no eligible study tests a frozen TFM under a grouped split or beyond its feature envelope. Tabular-to-image methods win only on small or very high-dimensional tables. Among the comparison-bearing studies, about one in ten use a deployment-matched split, none of them an independent evaluation of a TFM, and more than half of those evaluating a pretrained model report no contamination check. A reporting checklist, an evidence ladder, and seven research directions turn these findings into practice.

title: Machine Learning and SHAP for Morphological Feature Identification of Longjing Tea Straightness
abstract: The sensory evaluation of Longjing tea quality relies predominantly on subjective human judgment. Straightness is a critical sensory descriptor in the morphological quality assessment of Longjing tea, which lacks objective and quantifiable criteria. To objectively quantify this descriptor from a morphological perspective, this study developed an interpretable machine learning framework that integrates computer vision and SHAP analysis to digitally characterize the sensory attribute of straightness. Nine morphological features were extracted from Longjing tea samples collected across major production regions, including six contour-based and three skeleton-based descriptors. Three classification models, namely random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and support vector machine (SVM), were constructed and compared based on morphological features. SHAP analysis was employed to interpret model decisions, identifying three core morphological determinants, length ratio (lr), standard deviation (sd) and rectangularity (R), which consistently ranked highest in both univariate effect sizes and cross-model feature importance, with Cliff’s δ of 0.93, 0.81 and −0.78, respectively. By establishing a quantitative link between morphological features and sensory terminology, this study offers an interpretable tool for automated tea quality evaluation, with broader implications for digital standardization in quality evaluation of agricultural products.

title: Forecasting Post-Pandemic Tourism Recovery: Counterfactual Benchmarks, Intervention Models and Value–Volume Asymmetry in Greece
abstract: Whether tourism has recovered from the COVID-19 shock depends on the benchmark used. This study combines interrupted time-series models, structural-break detection, an event-study specification and counterfactual forecasts to quantify the shock and recovery of Greek tourism using 132 monthly observations for 2015–2025. A counterfactual path is forecast from a trend–seasonal model estimated on pre-pandemic data, validated out of sample against seasonal-naïve, exponential-smoothing and SARIMA benchmarks, and compared with SARIMA, damped-trend ETS and growth-scenario alternatives; a sieve bootstrap quantifies the uncertainty of shortfalls and recovery dates. Travel receipts, inbound traveler flows and receipts per traveler are compared. Receipts and arrivals contracted by approximately 83%, a finding that was robust across intervention dates, HAC bandwidths and serially correlated-error specifications, whereas a single constant recovery slope is not supported. Both indicators regained their 2019 levels in April 2023 under all rules. Relative to the counterfactual, receipts met a three-month criterion in February 2024 while arrivals had not by end-2025; receipts cross first with probability 0.64, but the dates depend on the run-length rule and the assumed pre-pandemic growth, and in real terms the post-2022 lead of receipts reflects prices, not higher spending per traveler. Domestic accommodation demand resisted the shock better; foreign demand rebounded faster.

title: Primary Post-Traumatic Aspergillus fumigatus Soft-Tissue Infection of the Hand Requiring Digital Amputation and Reconstruction: A Case Report
abstract: Background: Primary post-traumatic aspergillosis is an uncommon fungal infection resulting from direct inoculation of Aspergillus species into disrupted skin and soft tissue. Although it is more frequently encountered in immunocompromised patients, severe localized infection may also occur after traumatic inoculation, particularly in the presence of previously unrecognized predisposing conditions. Involvement of the hand is rare. Case Presentation: A 68-year-old man was referred to our department with a progressive necrotizing infection of the right hand following an occupational agricultural injury. The initial injury had been surgically treated at another institution. On presentation, extensive necrosis involved the palmar aspect of the hand; the index, middle, and ring fingers; and the hypothenar region. The patient had no known systemic condition predisposing him to fungal infection at presentation. During hospitalization, however, persistent hyperglycemia led to the diagnosis of previously unrecognized and uncontrolled diabetes mellitus. Surgical exploration revealed extensive soft-tissue necrosis, thrombosed vessels, poorly perfused and friable tendinous structures, and exposed bony structures of the middle and ring fingers. Aspergillus fumigatus was repeatedly isolated from wound and deep-tissue specimens. Antifungal therapy was initially started with amphotericin B but was discontinued because of a severe allergic reaction and replaced with voriconazole. Three sequential surgical debridements were performed. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated extensive soft-tissue involvement without evidence of osteomyelitis. A fourth operation combined further debridement with amputation of the irreversibly damaged middle and ring fingers and immediate reconstruction of the resulting defect with local flap coverage. Subsequent cultures were negative, and the postoperative course was uncomplicated. Conclusions: Post-traumatic A. fumigatus infection of the hand is rare but may lead to extensive soft-tissue destruction. An invasive fungal infection should be considered in progressive necrotizing wounds following contaminated trauma, particularly when the clinical course is atypical or refractory to conventional antibacterial treatment. Early microbiological diagnosis, systemic antifungal therapy, repeated surgical debridement, and recognition of underlying predisposing conditions are essential for successful management.

title: From E-Commerce to AI Commerce: Rethinking the Consumer Journey in the Era of AI Agents
abstract: The emergence of increasingly autonomous Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents is reshaping how consumers search for information, evaluate alternatives, and make purchasing decisions. While existing consumer journey models have incorporated AI primarily as a decision-support technology, they provide limited conceptual guidance for understanding situations in which AI agents perform purchasing activities on consumers’ behalf. Drawing on consumer journey theory, AI-enabled commerce, and human–AI collaboration research, this conceptual paper adopts a theory-adaptation approach to examine how established frameworks may be extended to account for emerging forms of delegated decision-making. We propose the Human–AI Collaborative Consumer Journey, a framework that conceptualizes purchasing as a collaborative process involving consumers and consumer-authorized AI agents across different stages of the journey. Its central contribution is the concept of Delegated Consumer Agency (DCA), defined as the configuration of authority consumers grant AI agents to perform cognitive or operational purchasing activities within predefined goals and constraints. The framework highlights how human and AI participation may vary across purchasing contexts and identifies implications for consumer autonomy, decision-making, and e-commerce management. Finally, six research propositions and a future research agenda are presented to guide empirical investigation.

title: YT93-159: A High-Yield and Early-Maturing Sugarcane Variety with Superior Agronomic Traits
abstract: Sugarcane is an essential global industrial cash crop for sugar and bioenergy production, and breeding superior varieties is critical to improving industrial benefits and adapting to changing climatic environments. This review synthesizes the published breeding history, agronomic trial records, juice-quality evaluations, and transcriptomic analyses of the elite sugarcane variety YT93-159, and uses this variety as a model case to discuss the achievements and challenges of sugarcane breeding in South China. YT93-159 was bred through artificial hybridization using YN73-204 as the female parent and CP72-1210 as the male parent. Data compiled from variety-registration archives, peer-reviewed studies, and the authors’ previously published transcriptomic analyses indicate that YT93-159 integrates excellent parental advantages, with prominent early sugar accumulation, high yield, stable stress resistance, and wide adaptability. On the basis of differentially expressed genes identified in published transcriptomic datasets, its superior comprehensive traits may be co-regulated by candidate pathways including carbon fixation, sucrose metabolism, and plant hormone signal transduction; however, several pathway members showed the opposite expression changes, and these mechanisms should be regarded as hypotheses requiring further functional validation. This variety has achieved large-scale popularization in China and possesses excellent functional nutritional values. By clarifying the phenotypic and proposed molecular basis of YT93-159′s superior traits, this review provides a valuable germplasm resource profile and theoretical reference for sugarcane genetic improvement and sustainable industrial development.

title: Self-Compatibility Alleviates Inbreeding Depression and Maintains Yield and Quality in Winter Turnip Rape (Brassica rapa L.)
abstract: Winter turnip rape (Brassica rapa L.) is an important winter oilseed crop in the arid and cold regions of northern China due to its strong cold tolerance and wide adaptability. However, its prevalent self-incompatibility readily causes inbreeding depression, leading to declines in yield and quality and creating difficulties for cultivar breeding and pure-line propagation. To clarify how self-compatibility affects growth, yield, quality, and physiological traits, highly self-compatible (HSC), self-compatible (SC), and self-incompatible (SI) lines were compared under self-pollination and open pollination, and leaf antioxidant enzyme activities and endogenous hormone contents were measured. The results showed that the effects of selfing on seedling vegetative growth, agronomic traits, quality, and biomass were far smaller in HSC and SC lines than in SI lines, with inbreeding depression markedly alleviated. The mean inbreeding depression rates (IDRs) of major traits in HSC, SC, and SI lines were 4.32%, 8.14%, and 20.05%, respectively, the IDRs of effective silique number per plant were 3.03%, 5.22%, and 20.53%, and those of seed yield were 4.69%, 9.39%, and 27.90%. Line-level ANOVA and Tukey tests (three lines per group) confirmed that the IDRs of SI lines were significantly higher than those of HSC lines for all six core traits, with SC lines intermediate. Physiological and biochemical analyses indicated that HSC lines maintained higher SOD activity, and the contents of growth-promoting hormones, such as gibberellin (GA), cytokinin (CTK), and auxin (IAA), were generally higher than in SI lines, whereas CAT activity did not show a consistent advantage: in HSC lines CAT did not differ significantly between SP and OP (the two shared a significance group), and under open pollination SI-OP was grouped with HSC-OP and SC-OP. In contrast, after selfing, SI lines accumulated more abscisic acid (ABA), whereas the ethylene (ETH) differences were not consistently significant and the coordination of their antioxidant enzymes was altered rather than disrupted. Correlation analysis showed that the contents of growth-promoting hormones (GA, CTK, IAA, and BR) were significantly or highly significantly positively correlated with yield traits, such as seed yield per plant, effective silique number per plant, and thousand-seed weight, whereas ABA and ETH contents were highly significantly negatively correlated. A structural equation model, based on composite scores of hormones, enzymes, growth, and yield and quality, indicated that the hormone composite was strongly associated with the growth composite (standardized path coefficients of hormone → growth and growth → yield and quality were 0.816 and 0.535, respectively), whereas the enzyme composite was directly associated with yield and quality (0.291). These paths reflect statistical associations among the composite scores rather than confirming the specific underlying mechanisms, and vegetative growth was the main mediator linking the hormone composite to yield and quality. To our knowledge, self-compatibility in winter turnip rape can maintain relatively stable plant growth and development as well as yield and quality by alleviating inbreeding depression and maintaining physiological metabolism and hormone homeostasis. This study provides a theoretical basis for the screening and utilization of self-compatible germplasm and for high-yield breeding of winter turnip rape; because stress tolerance was not directly measured, any extrapolation to stress-resistant breeding requires dedicated stress-tolerance experiments in future work.

title: Growing-Season Drought and Gross Revenue Losses in Maize Production in the Colombian Caribbean
abstract: Drought limits maize production in regions exposed to climate variability; however, estimates of agricultural and economic impacts depend on the precipitation data used to characterize drought. This study evaluates the relationship between growing-season drought and historical maize yields and estimates corresponding losses in production and gross income in the Colombian Caribbean. Municipal-level data from 191 municipalities across different agricultural cycles were analyzed using the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) at 3- and 6-month accumulation scales, derived from the CHIRPS v3.0, GPCC v2025, and MSWEP v2.8 precipitation products. Fixed-effects panel models estimated yield responses, accounting for municipality, cycle, year, and department-specific temporal trends. Drought severity, derived from SPEI03 during the growing season, was negatively associated with maize yield in the CHIRPS and GPCC models (estimated coefficients of −0.042 and −0.039, respectively), while the MSWEP estimate was close to zero. The corresponding cumulative production losses, calculated using the models, were 76.2 thousand metric tons for CHIRPS and 71.6 thousand metric tons for GPCC, equating to estimated gross revenue losses of 115,550 million COP and 106,500 million COP, respectively, at constant 2024 prices. In contrast, the MSWEP model yielded much lower estimates: 2400 metric tons and 3.76 billion COP, with confidence intervals that included zero for both results. The negative associations between yield and precipitation under the CHIRPS and GPCC frameworks generally persisted across several alternative drought definitions, although they weakened when the growing season was shifted one month later. These results show how sensitive estimated drought-related agricultural losses are to crop choice and precipitation data, and support presenting crop-specific estimates and uncertainty when assessing climate-related risks to traditional maize production.

title: Machine Learning-Based Bias Correction Scheme for FY-4A AGRI Radiance Assimilation and Its Impact on Typhoon Forecasting
abstract: Data assimilation generally assumes that observation-minus-background (OMB) departures follow an unbiased Gaussian distribution. Therefore, bias correction (BC) is essential for the effective assimilation of satellite radiances. This study applies four machine learning (ML) approaches to reduce systematic biases in clear-sky observations from the water-vapor-sensitive channels 9 and 10 of the Fengyun-4A (FY-4A) Advanced Geosynchronous Radiation Imager (AGRI). These methods include random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), multilayer perceptron (MLP), and the Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN). The machine-learning-based bias correction (MLBC) methods are evaluated for Typhoon In-Fa (2021) using the Weather Research and Forecasting Data Assimilation (WRFDA) system. Experiments without BC and with conventional variational bias correction (VarBC) are designed for comparison. Compared with VARBC, the four MLBC methods better capture nonlinear OMB biases and improve the statistical distributions of the departures. They produce more symmetric OMB distributions for channel 9 and distributions closer to the Gaussian distribution for channel 10, with smaller OMB STDVs and RMSEs than VARBC over both land and ocean for channel 10. After assimilation, KANBC produces the smallest OMA STDV and RMSE for both channels. For the Typhoon In-Fa case examined here, KANBC yields the smallest track errors among the experiments. In particular, KAN-based BC reduces the anomalously strong positive 500 hPa geopotential height increments over the continental high pressure and western North Pacific subtropical high pressure. The resulting initial conditions improve the environmental steering flow and reduce the northwestward track bias. Channel sensitivity experiments were further conducted for water-vapor-sensitive channels 9 and 10 of the FY-4A AGRI using the KAN-based BC method. The results show that single-channel assimilation performs better than dual-channel assimilation. Assimilating channel 10 alone produces the smallest track errors and lower analysis RMSEs relative to ERA5 than assimilating both channels.

title: An Investigation into Land Surface Temperature-Based Climate Indices
abstract: Monitoring climate change is crucial to society, industry, and the environment to assess their vulnerability to such extreme temperature events and plan adaptation and mitigation strategies. Temperature-based climate indices, which are used for climate monitoring, are usually calculated using near-surface air temperature (NSAT) from weather stations. A limitation of NSAT is the inhomogeneity of station distribution across the globe, with some regions under-sampled. This study evaluates the potential of using land surface temperature (LST) retrieved via satellite to calculate temperature indices, because low Earth-orbiting satellites can observe almost all of the Earth. This work compares indices calculated from NSAT to those produced from LST, and the indices are aggregated by Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change AR6 regions. Results show that there is often moderate to high correlation between indices produced using NSAT and LST. In addition, it is found that monthly to seasonal changes in indices are similar for both variables, particularly in percentile-based indices. Threshold-based indices could not be calculated for some regions due to low data availability, and therefore this work also applies “relative” indices, where indices are normalised relative to the amount of data available. These generally also demonstrate high correlations between NSAT and LST and can better show when events, such as heatwaves, occur. Lastly, this work presents the potential of an LST-based temperature indices dataset and how uncertainties could be evaluated.

title: SparseHSR: From RGB Guidance to Sparse Visible–NIR Sensing for Full-Range Hyperspectral Super-Resolution
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) super-resolution often uses RGB or RGB-like high-resolution guidance, which provides no direct high-resolution observation in the near-infrared (NIR). Keeping the low-resolution HSI spectrally complete, we first add one high-resolution NIR band near 801 nm to RGB. For abundance-Gram reconstruction, this reduces full-spectrum mean per-band RMSE by 92.2% on Chikusei and 75.5% on ICVL. We then replace RGB with only one to four high-resolution narrowbands spanning the visible and NIR. A few strategically distributed bands support strong full-spectrum reconstruction while substantially reducing the high-resolution spectral measurement burden. Using the same sparse observations, abundance-Gram reconstruction is strongly sensitive to wavelength placement, whereas registered HySure-SVD is much less sensitive. A targeted three-seed analysis confirms that the key 549 + 801 nm and four-band spanning designs are highly stable, while some weaker configurations are seed-sensitive. A guide-permutation stress test links the cross-architecture contrast to permutation-invariant global abundance-statistics matching versus registered pixelwise fusion. Sensor-native HySpex Mjolnir imagery reproduces the same crossover. These results support sparse visible-NIR sensing and joint design of high-resolution measurements and reconstruction.

title: Lightweight and Poisoning-Resilient Federated AI Framework for Secure 5G Edge Communications
abstract: With the rapid popularization of 5G edge communication systems, their decentralized architecture and the ultra-large attack surface brought by massive access devices have created severe network security challenges. Although current artificial intelligence-based intrusion detection systems and conventional federated learning schemes can achieve high intrusion detection accuracy, they universally suffer from two major limitations: excessive computational overhead and vulnerability to poisoning attacks, which make them unable to adapt to resource-constrained edge deployment environments. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight anti-poisoning federated learning framework for low-latency secure 5G edge communications, with two core design elements: First, it integrates lightweight GRU/CNN models and a trust-aware aggregation mechanism to weaken the negative impact of malicious model updates; second, it introduces a deviation-based poisoning detection strategy to identify and filter adversarial updates during the federated learning process. We used the public CICIDS2017 dataset to complete tests in a simulated 5G edge environment equipped with 100 to 1000 edge devices, covering multiple scenarios including DDoS, MITM, and poisoning attacks. The results show that compared with existing similar schemes, the proposed framework reaches a maximum detection accuracy of 98.3\%, reduces communication latency by 30-35\%, cuts computational overhead by 40-60\%, and sees only a negligible drop in accuracy under poisoning attacks. It can support a wide range of real-time 5G edge applications such as intelligent transportation, smart cities, and the industrial Internet of Things.
journal: International Journal of Mechatronics, Robotics, and Artificial Intelligence

title: The role of the international FinTech market in shaping investment support for global food security
abstract: The article aims to substantiate the role of the international FinTech market in shaping investment provision for global food security and to identify the channels through which digital financial technologies can transform access to capital in the agri-food sector. The research uses systems analysis, scientific generalization, comparison, classification, structural and logical analysis, and conceptual modeling. The study establishes that digital payment systems, digital lending, peer-to-peer financing, crowdfunding, digital investment platforms, InsurTech, artificial intelligence, big data, distributed ledger technologies, and RegTech can expand financial inclusion, diversify sources of investment capital, reduce selected transaction costs and information asymmetry, improve risk assessment and insurance, and facilitate cross-border financial flows. It is demonstrated that the impact of FinTech on global food security is predominantly indirect and is realized through an investment channel: the development of the international FinTech market creates new financing opportunities; these opportunities are transformed into investments in agricultural production, processing, storage, logistics, digitalization, climate adaptation and risk management; such investments enhance the productivity and resilience of agri-food systems and contribute to the physical and economic accessibility and stability of food supply. The scientific novelty lies in the substantiation of an integrated mechanism “FinTech – investment – agri-food system – food security”, which combines financial accessibility, capital mobilization, productive investment and the resulting parameters of food-system resilience within a single causal framework. The practical significance of the findings lies in their potential use by public authorities, financial institutions, international organizations, investors, and agri-food enterprises when designing investment instruments and programs to improve access to finance and strengthen food-system resilience. Particular attention is paid to the constraints of digital inequality, cybersecurity risks, regulatory fragmentation, and differences in institutional capacity. Further research should quantitatively assess the relationship between FinTech development, international investment flows, and food-security indicators, and test the proposed mechanism across countries with different levels of digital and financial development. Keywords: FinTech, international FinTech market, investment provision, global food security, agri-food sector, digital financial technologies, international investment.
journal: Actual problems of innovative economy and law

title: The Role and Significance of Agritourism in the Post-War Development of Rural Areas in Ukraine
abstract: This article examines the theoretical and practical aspects of developing agritourism as an effective catalyst for the socio-economic recovery of rural areas in Ukraine during the post-war period. It demonstrates that the traditional agricultural paradigm—focused on large-scale commercial production—fails to address challenges related to employment and population retention. In contrast, agritourism enables rural households to diversify income sources, boosts local budget revenues, and generates added value directly within territorial communities. A three-tiered typology of rural areas, categorized by security criteria, is proposed: de-occupied rear-area communities (suitable for full-scale commercial business); de-occupied frontline zones subject to shelling and landmine threats (suitable for specialized, small-scale initiatives such as educational, volunteer-based, or gastronomic projects); and areas of active combat (where development is currently in a “deferred start” phase, supported by the digitalization of resources). A formal calculation model incorporates direct and indirect employment effects, a local expenditure multiplier (accounting for capital leakage), and the net present value (NPV) of investments, adjusted for war-related and landmine risks. Through scenario modeling and sensitivity analysis, it is shown that the primary driver of investment attractiveness and the sustainability of agritourism enterprises is not merely an increase in aggregate demand, but rather a systematic reduction in the risk premium—achieved through demining, the construction of shelters, and the implementation of insurance—alongside an increased share of local procurement within the supply chain. State and donor support is most effective when provided as grants for initial capital expenditures, which lower the threshold for achieving a return on investment. We formulated practical recommendations for public administration bodies, including introducing safety profiles for rural tourism establishments, clustering and cooperation among local farmers, developing veteran-focused and rehabilitation tourism programs, and creating institutional conditions to encourage the population’s return to rural areas. Keywords: agritourism, post-war recovery, rural areas, de-occupied territories, multiplier effect, frontline communities, income diversification.
journal: Actual problems of innovative economy and law

title: Adoption and Impact of Climate-Smart Technologies on Agrifood Systems in Vihiga County, Kenya
abstract: Agrifood systems in sub-Saharan Africa face significant challenges from climate change, threatening food security and rural livelihoods. Climate-smart technologies (CSTs) offer a viable way to strengthen resilience, productivity, and sustainability in smallholder farming systems. This study examines the adoption and impact of CSTs in Vihiga County, a high-potential agricultural region in western Kenya with small landholdings and high vulnerability to climate variability. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study assesses the extent of CST adoption, key drivers and barriers, and socio-economic benefits among smallholder farmers. Primary data were collected through household surveys (n=383), focus group discussions (n=5), and key informant interviews (n=15) with farmers, extension officers, and policymakers. Findings indicate that practices such as conservation agriculture (25%), agroforestry (15%), drought-resistant crop varieties (60%), and integrated soil fertility management have contributed to improved yields, reduced greenhouse gas emissions, and enhanced climate adaptation. However, adoption remains constrained by limited access to finance, inadequate extension services, and fragmented land ownership. The study highlights the role of policy support, capacity building, and public-private partnerships in scaling up CSTs for sustainable agrifood transformation. By aligning local practices with Kenya's Climate-Smart Agriculture Strategy, Vihiga County can serve as a model for climate-resilient development in similar agro-ecological zones. The research underscores the need for context-specific, farmer-centred approaches to ensure equitable and sustainable adoption of CSTs in sub-Saharan Africa's agrifood systems.
journal: African Journal of Climate Change and Resource Sustainability

title: Crop Prospects and Food Situation
Category-Aware Transformer for Automotive Spare Parts Demand Forecasting
abstract: In the modeling process, existing auto parts demand forecasting methods often fail to clearly distinguish structural differences at the demand-frequency level, which results in limited adaptability in real scenarios characterized by sparse demand and a complex category structure. In response to the above problems, this paper proposes a category-aware Transformer framework for auto parts demand forecasting. To explicitly represent demand differences across frequency-based accessory groups and to reduce training bias caused by long-tail sample imbalance, the framework first constructs frequency categories based on statistical demand characteristics and incorporates them into the model as embedding-based structural priors. It then designs a category-perception attention mechanism within the Transformer to guide differentiated modeling of category-related temporal dependencies. At the same time, in order to improve the expression ability of sparse and nonlinear disturbances, this paper introduces a nonlinear mapping module at the prediction end and uses a weighted loss function based on sample distribution to constrain the training target. Experimental results on three real auto-parts demand datasets from Dongfeng Automobile Co., Ltd. show that the proposed method outperforms five benchmark models in terms of RMSE and MAE, with especially strong performance in predicting intermediate-frequency and long-tail parts.

title: Identifying Structural Drivers of Crime Using Statistical Inference and Machine Learning Models
abstract: This study identifies structural socio-economic correlates of crime investigation activity in Kazakhstan and examines how interpretable composite indicators relate to it. The dependent variable is the annual volume of pre-trial investigations recorded in the Unified Register of Pre-Trial Investigations over 2015–2025. It is modeled against 70 explanatory factors that span socio-economic, demographic, institutional, legal, healthcare, education, agriculture, and digitalization domains. The analysis combines Pearson correlation, one-way analysis of variance, simple and multivariate linear regression, and regularized ensemble machine learning (Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, Ridge, Support Vector Machine). A category-based dimensionality reduction then aggregates the 70 factors into 8, and subsequently 10, standardized composite indices. Because only about 10 aggregated annual observations are available, findings are reported in associational rather than causal terms. The strongly negative cross-validated R2 of the ensemble models is flagged as direct evidence of overfitting in this small-n, high-dimensional setting. Digitalization, education, poverty, and healthcare indicators emerge as the leading correlates of crime. A parsimonious regression on the composite indices accounts for 97.6% of insample crime variance while improving interpretability and stability. Interpretable index-based models therefore appear better suited than high-capacity learners for policy-relevant inference in this setting.
