title: Enacting effectuation in scarcity: a symbiotic model driven by bricolage and socio-cultural networks in Moroccan SME entrepreneurship
abstract: Effectuation theory (Sarasvathy, 2001) posits a control-oriented logic for entrepreneurial decision-making under uncertainty, yet its enactment in resource-scarce emerging economies remains underexplored, particularly through cultural and recombinative lenses. This study aims to address this gap by examining how Moroccan SME entrepreneurs in artisanal, agricultural and digital sectors navigate Knightian uncertainty via effectuation, moderated by socio-cultural networks and mediated by bricolage, to achieve hybrid effectuation-causation logics and sustained performance. Drawing on a qualitative multiple-case study of five established SMEs, the authors develop a symbiotic model exploring four theoretical propositions. These propositions examine how: (P1) effectuation enables adaptive decision-making through controllable means-based action in volatile contexts; (P2) collectivist networks (el-maârifa) shape the adoption and enactment of effectual principles; (P3) bricolage serves as the operational mechanism transforming bird-in-hand means into value; and (P4) entrepreneurs navigate venture lifecycles through dynamic hybrid logics blending effectual discovery with causal execution. Thematic analysis reveals pervasive effectual principles – affordable loss and crazy quilt – enacted through trust-based recombinations (e.g. waste-to-innovation in ceramics and honey) and context-adaptive ambidexterity. This yields resilience amid pandemics, regulations and climatic risks. While the deep contextual insights are a core contribution, future research could test the transferability of this framework in other emerging economies. Practically, it offers a roadmap for emerging-market entrepreneurs – “build on roots, recombine creatively” – legitimizing adaptive bootstrapping. The study highlights the role of collectivist networks (el-maârifa) in fostering trust-based recombinations and ethical hybridity, promoting collective stewardship and resilience in resource-scarce communities facing socio-economic and environmental challenges. The authors contribute a context-specific theoretical framework: a symbiotic model integrating socio-cultural network embeddedness and ethical hybridity. This elaborates effectuation beyond individualism to collective stewardship in scarcity-driven settings.
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Innovation and Entrepreneurship

title: Research on the impact of vertical fiscal imbalance on the supply of basic public services from the perspective of tax effort
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of vertical fiscal imbalance (VFI) on local public service provision and environmental pollution, and examines the moderating role of fiscal transfers. Using panel data from Chinese prefecture-level cities, we construct econometric models with a VFI index as the key independent variable. Dependent variables include basic public service supply and pollution emissions. Two-way fixed effects and instrumental variable methods are applied. VFI significantly reduces the level of local public services, especially in fiscally weak regions. It also aggravates industrial pollution, suggesting that fiscal pressure may relax environmental regulation. General-purpose transfers mitigate the negative service effect, but earmarked transfers do not. This study extends VFI research to public service and environmental outcomes, provides new empirical evidence from China, and reveals differentiated roles of transfer types, offering policy implications for fiscal reform.

title: Climate transition risk and corporate cash holdings evidence from China's agricultural sector
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the impact of climate transition risk on agricultural firms' cash holdings, and to further explore the underlying mechanisms and economic consequence. This study constructs a panel dataset from the annual reports of Chinese agricultural listed firms using textual analysis, and employs a fixed-effects model to explore the relationship between climate transition risk and cash holdings. This study demonstrates that climate transition risk significantly reduces the cash holdings of agricultural firms. Corporate investment and financing constraints mediate this effect, while customer concentration moderates it. Firms located in western regions, large-scale firms, those with a high degree of digital transformation, and foreign-invested firms are better able to cushion the impact of climate transition risk on cash holdings. The influence of climate transition risk on cash holdings further leads to a reduction in operating profit margins. This study makes a significant contribution to revealing the relationship between climate transition risk and cash holdings in agricultural firms.

title: Understanding CRM–service quality relationships through a multi-theoretical contingency framework: evidence from emerging economy banking
abstract: Although Customer Relationship Management (CRM) is widely regarded as a strategic mechanism for enhancing service quality in retail banking, empirical findings remain inconsistent, particularly within emerging economy contexts. This conceptual paper addresses the persistent CRM–service quality paradox by arguing that the relationship between CRM and service quality is neither universally positive nor linear, but contingent upon customer-level relational conditions, specifically Customer Commitment. The study develops an integrated multi-theoretical framework explaining how distinct CRM dimensions differentially influence perceived service quality and proposes Customer Commitment as a critical moderating mechanism. The paper synthesises insights from Expectancy Disconfirmation Theory, Customer Engagement Theory, and Commitment-Trust Theory within the IDIC (Identify, Differentiate, Interact, Customize) CRM architecture. Building on this integration, the study advances six theoretically grounded propositions linking CRM dimensions to service quality outcomes. To facilitate future empirical validation, a mixed-methods sequential research design is proposed, comprising qualitative interviews with Nigerian retail banking customers, a large-scale survey analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM), and a longitudinal panel design to establish temporal relationships. The paper advances a contingency-based reconceptualization of CRM effectiveness by demonstrating that identical CRM practices may produce divergent service quality outcomes depending on customers' commitment levels. The framework further distinguishes between volitional customer engagement, which enhances service experiences, and forced customer involvement, which may undermine perceived service quality. In doing so, the study extends Commitment-Trust Theory by repositioning Customer Commitment from a relational outcome to a perceptual moderator shaping customers' interpretations of CRM practices. As a conceptual study, the framework requires empirical validation across diverse institutional and cultural settings. Nevertheless, the propositions are theoretically grounded, falsifiable, and intended to provide a robust foundation for future doctoral and scholarly investigations into CRM effectiveness in emerging markets. The study suggests that retail banks in emerging economies should calibrate CRM strategies according to customer commitment profiles rather than applying uniform relationship-management practices. For low-commitment customers, trust-building and relational assurance should precede intensive engagement initiatives. This study has important social implications for how retail banks in emerging economies manage customer relationships in a more equitable and trust-sensitive manner. By highlighting Customer Commitment as a key moderating factor, it shows that customers experience CRM practices differently depending on their relational readiness and trust levels. This reduces the risk of over-engagement or perceived intrusion, which can negatively affect vulnerable or low-commitment customers. The framework encourages banks to adopt more inclusive, ethical, and customer-sensitive relationship strategies that build trust gradually. Ultimately, this supports stronger financial inclusion, improved customer dignity, and more balanced digital banking relationships in sub-Saharan Africa. This paper contributes to CRM and service management scholarship in four important ways. First, it reconceptualizes Customer Commitment as a moderating rather than outcome variable. Second, it distinguishes customer engagement from customer involvement, highlighting the potentially detrimental consequences of excessive participation demands. Third, it advances a contingency perspective of CRM effectiveness by demonstrating that CRM practices may generate both positive and negative service quality outcomes. Finally, the study contextualizes CRM theory within sub-Saharan African banking environments, a significantly underexplored setting in the relationship marketing literature.
journal: International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management

title: When traditional culture meets digital games: pathways and boundary conditions linking cultural identity to purchase intention
abstract: This study aims to examine how cultural identity is associated with purchase intention for paid digital games featuring local cultural elements. In the context of Black Myth: Wukong, it further investigates whether perceived value and immersive experience explain this relationship and whether price sensitivity conditions these associations. Survey data from 1,167 mainland Chinese and international gamers were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) and cross-sample model comparisons were used to examine group differences. Cultural identity was positively associated with purchase intention, with significant indirect effects through perceived value and immersive experience. In the full sample, price sensitivity weakened the links between cultural identity and both mediators and their indirect effects. Mainland Chinese gamers showed higher cultural identity and perceived value, and stronger direct and indirect effects of cultural identity, than international gamers. The moderating effect of price sensitivity was not significant in the international subsample. Managers can strengthen culturally grounded digital products by embedding culturally resonant narratives, symbols and aesthetics into product design, communicating their relevance to target consumers and adopting differentiated value-framing and pricing strategies for consumers with varying levels of price sensitivity. This study applies cultural identity theory to paid digital game consumption by integrating perceived value and immersive experience as two distinct mechanisms linking cultural identity to purchase intention and examining price sensitivity as a boundary condition of these relationships.

title: Student and Educator Perspectives on Embodied AI Agents in Education.
abstract: As AI is beginning to take embodied form in classrooms (e.g., through avatars or immersive companions), it may funda mentally reshape how students learn. However, little is known about how such AI embodied agents might be used, what roles they could take, and what risks they carry. We addressed this gap through a three-phase study: (a) scoping review of Extended Reality educational applications with embodied AI agents; (b) participatory workshops with 23 students and educators; and (c) a workshop with 9 HCI and education experts. Participants envisioned agents as tutors, accessibility companions, and teacher-training partners, with educators being more enthusiastic about adoption while students stressing the irreplaceable value of human teachers; yet both groups agreed that embodied AI should augment rather than replace teaching. These findings suggest that embodiment should be understood not as a technical property solely but as a relational quality that shapes trust, authority, and inclusion in education.
journal: IEEE transactions on visualization and computer graphics

title: Beyond the label 'high-grade': histological heterogeneity as a prognostic marker in Ta non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To evaluate whether the proportion of a high-grade (HG) component within primary non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) influences recurrence and progression outcomes beyond the current World Health Organization (WHO) recommended threshold of ≥5% to designate a tumour as HG. PATIENTS AND METHODS We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients diagnosed with primary pathological T stage (pT)a HG NMIBC. All cases underwent centralised genitourinary pathological re-review to quantify the percentage of the HG component. Patients were stratified using pre-defined HG cut-offs (5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, and 100%). Recurrence-free survival and progression-free survival (PFS) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analyses and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, adjusting for established clinicopathological factors. Subgroup analyses were performed according to intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) treatment. RESULTS From 466 patients identified in our database, 362 underwent centralised pathologic re-review, and a total of 321 patients with confirmed pTa urothelial carcinoma were included in the study. The median follow-up was 61.3 months. The overall incidence of recurrence and progression, defined as progression to pathological stage ≥T1, was 35.5% and 9.4%, respectively. Increasing HG proportion was not significantly associated with recurrence after multivariable adjustment, whereas age and tumour multiplicity independently predicted recurrence risk. In contrast, higher HG percentage thresholds (≥10%, ≥25%, ≥50%, and 100%) were associated with progressively worse PFS, most pronounced in exploratory subgroups without BCG. The 5% threshold did not significantly discriminate outcomes. CONCLUSION The overall burden of HG differentiation seems to provide better prognostic significance than the mere presence of mixed histology in HG pTa tumours. Using higher HG percentage thresholds might improve the identification of patients at risk of progression and enhance risk stratification beyond existing WHO criteria. Prospective studies are needed to confirm if including HG percentage in clinical decision-making can lead to better personalised treatment for NMIBC.

title: Intensification and Spatial Reorganization of Drought Risks for Global Rainfed Crops Under Climate Change
abstract: Rainfed agriculture covers roughly 80% of global cropland and supplies more than half of global food production, yet uncertainty in how meteorological drying propagates into root‐zone water deficits and crop losses impedes robust risk assessment. Here, we establish an integrated, production‐weighted assessment framework coupling SPEI, SSI, and 12 GGCMI3 crop models to trace how meteorological drying propagates into root‐zone deficits and crop losses, explicitly separating affected area, conditional yield loss, and accumulated production loss across rainfed maize, soybean, and wheat. By 2070–2099, opposing‐direction SPEI–SSI change classes occupied 6.8%–28.4% of rainfed area across crops under SSP1‐2.6/default CO 2 and 26.6%–48.2% under SSP5‐8.5/default CO 2 . Comparison with fixed‐2015 CO 2 experiments (7.5%–27.6% and 21.7%–34.9%, respectively) indicates that elevated CO 2 substantially expanded the spatial footprint of this hydrometeorological decoupling. Historically, SSI‐defined drought affected 12–16 million ha year −1 and was associated with annual production losses of 5–12 Mt year −1 (1.6–2.0% year −1 ). Under default CO 2 , affected area increased to 14–21 million ha under SSP1‐2.6 and 19–27 million ha under SSP5‐8.5, with production losses of 6–12 and 9–12 Mt year −1 , respectively. Under SSP5‐8.5, median loss rates were higher under fixed‐2015 than default CO 2 for maize (3.33 vs. 1.96% year −1 ), soybean (4.22 vs. 2.84% year −1 ) and wheat (5.41 vs. 2.90% year −1 ), as elevated CO 2 reduces stomatal water loss and thus mitigates drought impacts, whereas SSP1‐2.6 estimates were similar. Severe drought became the largest loss contributor under both pathways and CO 2 settings. Under default CO 2 , loss increases clustered in Central America, northeastern Brazil, western Europe and southern Africa; fixed‐2015 CO 2 broadened the area of robust grid‐cell loss increases. These results show that drought‐related production losses are spatially uneven and sensitive to the modeled CO 2 response, highlighting the value of crop‐ and region‐specific risk assessment.

title: Plant‐ and Microbial‐Derived Soil Organic Carbon: Global Patterns and Divergent Climatic Associations
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) pools reflect the net balance of plant‐ and microbial‐derived inputs, transformation, and loss, yet a global‐scale assessment of distribution patterns, relative contributions, and hierarchical environmental correlates of microbial necromass carbon (MNC) and plant‐derived carbon (PdC) remains incomplete. Based on 1167 site‐level observations (1235 pool‐level records) across four ecosystem types, we applied variance partitioning, random forest, linear mixed‐effects models, and structural equation modeling to quantify global patterns and associative pathways of the two carbon pools. Unadjusted pooled comparisons showed higher MNC concentration and SOC contribution than PdC. However, covariate‐adjusted linear mixed‐effects models revealed significantly higher PdC. Paired observations showed the same directional trend, although statistical significance was not reached due to limited paired sample size (concentration: p = 0.104; contribution: p = 0.140). The apparent MNC dominance constitutes a Simpson's paradox driven by uneven ecosystem sampling, rather than a consistent within‐ecosystem pattern. Instead, the relative contribution of MNC and PdC was ecosystem‐dependent: MNC was marginally higher in forests, whereas PdC dominated in croplands and wetlands, with no significant difference in grasslands in paired observations. Edaphic variables were the strongest predictors (independent explanatory power: 61.1% for MNC, 47.4% for PdC), with total nitrogen, C:N ratio, pH, and mean annual temperature as key correlates. Our results reveal a hierarchical associative cascade in which geographic factors covary with climate, which in turn correlates with edaphic properties as the strongest direct predictors. Climate shows a weak but significant negative direct association with MNC only. This synthesis provides a hierarchical correlative framework and biome‐specific baseline parameters to support explicit representation of plant‐ and microbial‐mediated SOC pathways in Earth system models.

title: Does it matter if agentic AI is an author? effort and Nigerian Copyright Law
abstract: Agentic AI complicates copyright by unsettling the basis on which authorship is attributed, particularly where effort bears on originality and protection. This article asks what makes effort legally authorial, examining Nigerian copyright law, whose originality threshold requires effort to give a work original character, alongside comparative doctrine. That formulation reflects a common‐law tradition attentive to labour, skill and judgment, distinct from the European emphasis on the author's own intellectual creation and free and creative choices. The article argues that neither the quantity of labour involved in production nor the operational agency attributed to an AI system establishes authorship by itself. What matters is the relation between the claimed effort and the determination of copyright‐relevant expression. This difficulty is especially apparent where systems generate music with limited human intervention. Agentic production thus exposes a broader problem of legal attribution. Copyright may continue to seek an author even where production no longer coheres around one. The article describes the unsettled condition surrounding this shift as nescience, arguing that it counsels legal restraint rather than inaction. Where no qualifying human authorial contribution to the resulting expression can be established, copyright protection should be withheld, leaving fully AI‐generated expression in the public domain.
journal: The Journal of World Intellectual Property

title: The tin granite trade-off: Modeling redox evolution during magmatic processing
abstract: Most primary tin (Sn) deposits are genetically related to Sn-rich, reduced, ilmenite series “tin granites” derived from partial melting of a metasedimentary source. Petrogenetic models for tin granites invoke varying contributions of fractional crystallization, source Sn enrichment, and specific melting conditions. Tin can speciate as either Sn4+, which is compatible in minerals such as biotite, or Sn2+, which is generally incompatible. A key, but poorly constrained, factor in tin metallogeny is how melting and magmatic evolution modify magma redox state (expressed as molar XFe3+ = Fe3+/ Fetotal), and therefore redox-dependent Sn speciation and compatibility. We use phase equilibria modeling to quantify redox evolution during crustal melting and subsequent fractional crystallization. We show that ilmenite series magmas (XFe3+ 90%) cannot produce reduced ilmenite series melts characteristic of tin granites. Instead, our results necessitate Sn “pre-enrichment” during anatexis of a reduced, Sn-rich protolith prior to magmatic differentiation to generate Sn-fertile magmas.

title: Abstract 6408: AI That Builds Better AI: Autonomous Agents for Cardiovascular Model Development and Optimization
abstract: Background: Building high-performing cardiovascular AI models traditionally requires months of expert engineering, spanning experimentation with model architectures, development strategies, and tuning features. Autonomous AI research agents, in which large language models independently propose, train, and evaluate model improvements, could scale this process and uncover designs that human experts would not test. Aim: To test whether autonomous AI research agents, one iterative and one evolutionary, can systematically improve established cardiovascular AI-ECG models for structural heart disease detection, without human input or additional data. Methods: We applied both agents to two validated AI-ECG models for structural heart disease (SHD) - Columbia's EchoNext-mini (train, val, test N = 72,475, 4,626, 5,442) and a Yale composite SHD signal model (N = 261,228, 5,512, 11,023). Each agent proposed, trained, and evaluated model variants on the original code and data, within a fixed compute time and budget, and without human guidance ( Fig 1 ). The Iteration Agent searched sequentially, keeping the best variant at each step and discarding low performers in the autonomous loop. The Evolution Agent searched in parallel across multiple large language models for novel code modifications, and used meta-learning across generations to prioritize high-performing lineages. The agent code is publicly released as a cardiovascular AI development playbook. Results: Both agents consistently improved model discrimination across both AI-ECG families in all validation settings (AUROC gain 0.015 to 0.039; all p<0.001; Fig 2 ). For EchoNext, AUROC rose from 0.817 to 0.838 on held-out testing and from 0.773 to 0.807-0.812 in the external validation set. For the Yale model, AUROC rose from 0.871 to 0.889-0.897 in the test set and from 0.829 to 0.847-0.853 in external validation. Most agent-proposed improvements were architectural (Iteration 49%, Evolution 74%; Fig 3 ); the Iteration Agent prioritized integrating clinical features early, while the Evolution Agent emphasized multi-scale encoders, cross-lead attention, and loss-function changes. Conclusion: Autonomous AI research agents consistently improved cardiovascular AI models across two distinct architectures, without human engineering input. This agentic approach suggests a scalable path for keeping clinical AI tools current as data, populations, and clinical needs evolve. Our agent code is publicly available for the cardiovascular AI community.

title: Local and scientific knowledge of edible and crop-damaging crickets in Kousseri, Far North Region of Cameroon
abstract: This pilot study investigated local knowledge, perceptions, and practices regarding crickets in Kousseri, northern Cameroon, and compared them with entomological observations. Data were collected through household surveys involving 200 respondents, complemented by field and household sampling that identified six cricket species and morphospecies. Results showed that local knowledge was strongly influenced by sociocultural factors. Respondents demonstrated relatively detailed knowledge of cricket habitats, seasonal occurrence, appearance, sexual dimorphism, and associations with crops, although local classification was mainly based on house- and field-associated forms rather than on the full taxonomic diversity recorded. Crickets were perceived both as useful and harmful: 47% of respondents considered them harmful, 39% both useful and harmful, and only 7% exclusively useful. Their perceived benefits included use as food for humans and animals, fishing bait, children’s games, and, to a lesser extent, traditional medicine. Perceived harmful effects were mainly associated with crop damage and household nuisance, including consumption or damage of food and household materials but also noise nuisance. Although 115 respondents identified crickets as crop pests, their perceived economic impact was generally low, with 65.8% reporting yield losses below 5%. These results indicate that local knowledge encompasses multiple ecological, cultural, and socioeconomic dimensions of cricket–human interactions. Further field and household studies are needed to quantify species-specific abundance, crop damage and effects on crop yield, as well as the extent of cricket-related household nuisances in Kousseri.

title: An Application of the Self-Determination Theory Model for AI-Enhanced, Digital Psychosocial Interventions for Pediatric Disabilities.
abstract: BACKGROUND Youth with developmental disabilities (DDs) experience elevated psychosocial challenges, including difficulties with emotion regulation, self-concept, and access to timely mental health support. Pediatric nurses are well-positioned to address these needs; however, time constraints, limited training, and restricted access to specialty services often impede the provision of consistent psychosocial care. Digitally delivered psychosocial interventions enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI) offer new opportunities for individualized, accessible support, but these approaches frequently lack a clear theoretical foundation. PURPOSE This paper applied Self-Determination Theory (SDT), specifically Basic Psychological Needs Theory, to guide pediatric nurses' use of AI-enhanced, digital psychosocial interventions for DDs in practice. METHODS A theory-driven synthesis mapped SDT needs (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) to AI-enabled intervention features: conversational agents, neuro/adaptive feedback, and emotion-recognition tailoring. RESULTS The framework specifies how these features can promote volitional engagement, optimal challenge with timely feedback, and supportive interactions for youth with DDs. It also notes evidence gaps (small, heterogeneous samples; limited comparisons and follow-up) and barriers involving payment/workload, equity and access, and data protection, transparency, and bias. CONCLUSIONS/IMPLICATIONS SDT offers a coherent, testable foundation for designing, evaluating, and integrating AI-enhanced psychosocial supports for pediatric DDs. Nurses can screen for support, coach families, monitor risks, and advocate for ethical deployment and rigorous research.

title: Quantitative imaging–pathology correlation in nodular fasciitis and diagnostic discrimination from sarcoma
abstract: To investigate associations between key magnetic resonance imaging features of nodular fasciitis (NF) and quantitative histopathologic biomarkers, and to evaluate whether their integration provides complementary information for differentiating NF from soft tissue sarcoma (STS) in diagnostically equivocal settings. This retrospective study included 128 patients with NF and 133 with STS who underwent preoperative 3-T MRI between May 2023 and June 2025. Two blinded musculoskeletal radiologists independently evaluated predefined imaging features, including fascial tail sign, T2 heterogeneity score, enhancement pattern, perilesional edema, and mean/minimum apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Histopathology quantified cellular density, collagen content, and myxoid degeneration. Imaging–pathology correlations were assessed using Spearman analysis and multivariable regression. Diagnostic performance of MRI-only, pathology-only, and combined models was evaluated using logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), area under the curve (AUC) analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap validation. T2 heterogeneity correlated positively with myxoid degeneration (ρ = 0.52) and negatively with collagen content (ρ = −0.28) (p < 0.001). Mean ADC correlated inversely with cellular density (ρ = −0.63, p < 0.001). Mean ADC was significantly higher in NF than STS (p < 0.001). The combined model outperformed MRI alone (AUC, 0.96 vs 0.89) and demonstrated greater net clinical benefit. Bootstrap validation confirmed stable performance (mean AUC, 0.960; 95% confidence interval, 0.938–0.978). Imaging features of NF were associated with underlying stromal and cellular substrates. Integrating imaging features with quantitative pathology biomarkers may support radiology–pathology concordance assessment in selected diagnostically equivocal cases. Question How can we improve radiology–pathology concordance and reduce interpretative variability for NF cases presenting with suspicious, diagnostically equivocal magnetic resonance imaging findings? Findings T2 heterogeneity and diffusion measurements are associated with stromal composition and cellularity, while predefined MRI features demonstrated substantial-to-excellent inter-reader agreement. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91–81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

title: Spatiotemporal variations and influencing factors of highly pathogenic avian influenza risk in the Pan-Tibetan Plateau region
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) is a major infectious disease threatening the poultry industry and public health severely. The spatiotemporal patterns and driving forces, however, remain elusive in the Tibetan Plateau and its vicinity, an ecologically critical corridor for migratory birds. This study aims to identify the factors driving these variations and to assess the HPAI risk in wild birds and domestic poultry across this region. Based on HPAI records from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the Official Veterinary Bulletin and 34 potential drivers in the Pan-Tibetan Plateau (PTP), comprising Xizang Autonomous Region (XZ), Qinghai Province (QH), Gansu Province (GS), Sichuan Province (SC), Yunnan Province (YN) and Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region (XJ), this study utilized the MaxEnt models to simulate spatial patterns of HPAI risk of wild birds, domestic poultry, and the integration of both, and identify key risk factors. Performances of models for wild birds and domestic poultry models were robust (both Test AUC values > 0.9). Although the mixed model performed acceptably overall, it significantly underestimated the infection risk in wild birds. High-risk areas of wild birds HPAI were concentrated in XZ, QH, GS and XJ (> 93%), showing a close relationship with natural factors like slope and distance to water sources. Conversely, those for domestic poultry were mainly distributed in YN, SC, GS (about 70%) and the peripheries of provincial capitals, dominated by socioeconomic variables such as gross domestic product and road networks. Moreover, overlapping HPAI risk areas were found in GS, XJ, XZ, and QH, which may be associated with increasing poultry production and fragmented wetland landscape. Additionally, it’s recommended that HPAI risk modeling be stratified by host types, particularly in areas with sparse surveillance data. HPAI risks in wild birds and domestic poultry are dominated by natural factors and socioeconomic conditions respectively, and overlapping high-risk areas require focused attention. This study contributes to the understanding of HPAI transmission mechanisms in different hosts, providing a scientific basis for differentiated surveillance in the PTP.

title: Agri-PIDNet-S: Lightweight semantic segmentation for field-structure and obstacle perception in seedling-stage cotton fields
abstract: Reliable joint perception of crop rows, furrows, and obstacles is essential for autonomous inter-row operations in seedling-stage cotton fields. However, small and sparsely distributed plants, perspective-convergent rows, irregular furrow boundaries, and low obstacle pixel coverage jointly challenge fine-detail preservation, long-range structural modeling, and boundary discrimination under real-time constraints. This study formulated cotton-field perception as a four-class semantic segmentation task and constructed a dataset of 709 pixel-wise annotated images comprising background, crop rows, furrows, and obstacles. We developed Agri-PIDNet-S, a field-specific lightweight network based on PIDNet-S. A coordinate-aware multi-kernel inverted residual module (CA-MKIR) preserves shallow details and small-obstacle contours, a squeeze-and-excitation-enhanced deep-to-token module (SaE-D2T) models long-range row and furrow structures, and a boundary-guided window-attention refinement Bag (BWR-Bag) improves semantic–boundary fusion. The network was trained with a composite loss incorporating auxiliary boundary supervision. On the cotton-field test set, Agri-PIDNet-S achieved 92.37% mean intersection over union (mIoU) and 96.02% mean Dice coefficient (mDice) in the model-comparison experiment, while repeated training with three seeds yielded an mIoU of 92.35 ± 0.03%. Relative to PIDNet-S under the same comparison protocol, mIoU increased by 3.53 percentage points, while obstacle IoU improved from 79.60% to 88.67%. The model contained 8.048 million parameters, required 19.161 GFLOPs, and achieved 155.67 frames per second. Zero-shot external evaluation on tomato, watermelon, and maize fields yielded a structural mIoU of 86.29% for the background, crop-row, and furrow classes. Under the evaluated conditions, the task-oriented modifications achieved higher segmentation point estimates than PIDNet-S while maintaining computational efficiency; the external results provide preliminary evidence of cross-crop structural transfer.
