title: Co-Designing a Website With Young People to Enable the Uptake of Online, Self-Help Single Session Interventions for Mental Health: A Participatory Approach.
abstract: BACKGROUND Evidence-based self-help digital interventions are a promising approach to low-barrier mental health and well-being support. They could be particularly impactful at the early stages of help-seeking and could reach young people who may not otherwise access any help at all. To capitalise on these interventions, they need to be offered in ways that are engaging and easily navigated by the end-user and promote trust and credibility. Co-designing the implementation of these interventions could enable this. METHODS We aimed to co-design a website to host self-help digital interventions aimed at young people in the United Kingdom. We used the Design, Develop, Build and Test model to guide our development process. Over 8 months, we ran a series of participatory virtual co-design workshops with young people as contributors (N = 29, 13-18 years). RESULTS By iteratively moving between the design-development-build phases, we co-created our website, including branding, look and feel, structure, content and functionality. All design decisions were led by what young people told us was most important to them. CONCLUSIONS Young people's input shaped every aspect of the co-designed unlockwellbeing.org.uk website, from branding to functionality, ensuring relevance, credibility and accessibility. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION This descriptive paper presents a practical, experience-informed illustration of how to meaningfully involve young people in the co-design of digital mental health resources. Grounded in both the literature and our own participatory co-design work, we describe the iterative development of a website hosting evidence-based self-help interventions for young people with symptoms of depression. Using the Design, Develop, Build and Test model, we engaged 29 young people aged 13-18 in a series of virtual workshops over 8 months, ensuring that every design decision, from branding to functionality, was led by their input.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

title: Crop‐System Variation in Methyl‐Eugenol‐Responsive Male Bactrocera Assemblages Covaries With Geographic and Landscape Context
abstract: Methyl eugenol trapping is widely used to monitor male Bactrocera , but capture patterns can reflect crop context, geography, elevation and surrounding landscape as well as species biology. We analysed a harmonised dataset from nine apple, nine guava and nine citrus orchards in East Java, Indonesia, using nine traps per orchard in two sampling periods (486 trap‐period observations). Among 16,185 males, Bactrocera carambolae Drew & Hancock represented 57.6% of apple captures, whereas Bactrocera dorsalis (Hendel) represented 71.9% of guava and 94.8% of citrus captures. Repeated‐measures negative‐binomial models showed markedly higher B. carambolae captures in apple than in guava or citrus, while absolute B. dorsalis captures did not differ among crop systems and sampling period had no overall effect. Crop system explained substantial variation in elevation ( R 2 = 0.742), plant age and latitude. Accordingly, the crop association detected by simple PERMANOVA ( R 2 = 0.269, p = 0.0012) weakened after conditioning on broad geography ( p = 0.0618) or elevation ( p = 0.0682). A pre‐specified AICc candidate set identified crop‐only as the highest‐ranked model for B. carambolae , whereas landscape‐configuration models ranked slightly above crop‐only for B. dorsalis and total captures; these rankings were not robust to leave‐one‐orchard‐out and spatial‐covariance sensitivity analyses. Bactrocera umbrosa (Fabricius) occurred in eight of nine guava orchards but was absent from citrus. These results support context‐aware trap surveillance while showing that lure‐based crop associations should not be interpreted as confirmed host use, infestation or crop damage.

title: Risk-Oriented Differentiated Governance for Ambiguous Information.
abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has led to an exponential increase in false information, especially ambiguous information. Hampered by resource constraints, conventional governance approaches fall short of enabling efficient and precise risk management. In response, this paper innovatively proposes a risk-oriented tiered governance framework tailored to ambiguous information. Specifically, we quantify epistemic uncertainty via multi-level semantic features, combine it with network propagation features to determine latent influence scores, and construct a risk function capturing their synergy. Critical and acceptable boundaries are introduced to categorize ambiguous information into discrete risk levels, tier-specific governance strategies are devised, and a propagation throttling (limiting each user's successful forwards per ambiguous information) strategy is innovatively proposed for medium-risk information. Finally, we simulate differentiated governance strategies across risk levels of ambiguous information, systematically assess governance effectiveness, and offer a comparative discussion grounded in fairness and ethics. This study offers an operational analytical framework for refined risk governance of ambiguous information, contributes methodological innovations in risk quantification modeling and tiered governance strategies, and provides theoretical support and practical guidance for risk management authorities in designing differentiated measures.
journal: Risk analysis : an official publication of the Society for Risk Analysis

title: Holographic study of the scalar meson $K_0^*(1430)$ with dynamical longitudinal confinement
abstract: Within the framework of light-front holographic QCD, where transverse confinement is inherently realized through holography, the structure and mass spectrum of the light scalar meson $K_0^{*}(1430)$ are investigated by employing the invariant mass ansatz and enhancing the model with a longitudinal confinement potential (specifically, the 't Hooft equation and the analytically solvable LMZV potential). The combined transverse and longitudinal confinement dynamics lead to more reliable calculations of key observables, including decay constants, parton distribution function, $ξ$-moments, and twist-$2$ and twist-$3$ distribution amplitudes. Transition form factors for the semileptonic decay $B \rightarrow K_0^{*} \ell^+ \ell^-$ are computed from these amplitudes, yielding predictions for differential branching ratios and longitudinal lepton polarization asymmetries as functions of $q^2$. The results are compared with other theoretical models, offering valuable insights into the non-perturbative dynamics of QCD. The predicted observables provide theoretically motivated benchmarks for future experimental investigations of $B\rightarrow K_0^*(1430)\ell^+\ell^-$ decays at LHCb and Belle II.

title: Programming by Teaching: Authoring Agent Workflows through Voice Conversation
abstract: Agent workflow automation is increasingly accessible to users without programming experience, but much of the knowledge needed to author workflows is implicit. Programming by Demonstration captures what users do on screen but not the rules behind their actions. We propose Programming by Teaching, where users teach a task to an AI through real-time voice conversation while navigating the application, as they would teach a colleague. The AI listens, takes notes, and generates an agent workflow. We implemented both modes in the same Chrome extension and compared them in a within-subjects study with 28 participants, primarily non-programmers. Teaching passed held-out edge-case tests at 87.2% compared to 46.7% for demonstration (p =.002). Teaching reduced cognitive load (p =.04), scored higher on both pragmatic and hedonic quality (p ≤.001), and made it easier to incorporate rules not visible in the UI (p =.003). The hardest part of demonstration was not building the workflow but editing it afterward; teaching sidesteps this by front-loading specification into conversation.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Neighborhood: Dynamic Spatial Alignment for Traversable Telepresence Across Remote Spaces
abstract: We propose Neighborhood, a mixed reality (MR) telepresence system that allows users to experience an illusion of walking between local and remote spaces as if they are physically connected. Prior studies transmit either the avatar or the space alone to the remote space. Works that transmit both limit either remote space’s visibility or traversability to specific areas. Our work builds upon prior works by transmitting both the avatar and the space, while also supporting full visibility and traversability of local and remote spaces with user’s activities grounded with their real furniture and objects, distinct from VR traversal. Our system begins with users moving to the specific area they wish to connect. Using the chosen spaces, the optimization function aligns them to initiate Walking In Mode, visualizing a traversable area with remote spaces augmented. If users wish to move to a different area, the system transits to Panning Mode. Here, the moving user’s avatar appears stationary while the background shifts from the observing user’s perspective. We quantitatively measure metrics including the size of the neighborhood and ablate each term to evaluate the optimization function across diverse spatial configurations. We also conducted an exploratory user study with 21 participants, showing that traversing within Neighborhood evokes a compelling sense of real spatial adjoin.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: iRing: Rich Interaction on Smart Ring with Multi-point Capacitive Touch Screen
abstract: Rising interest in smart rings reflects a growing demand for immediate, lightweight interaction. However, prior designs have largely treated rings as input-only interfaces, or devices with limited on-device visualization, fall short in supporting for tightly coupled, direct, and expressive co-located interaction. To bridge this gap, we present iRing, a lightweight (6.4 g), low-cost ($46.43), open-source, and reproducible smart ring platform centered on a capacitive multi-touch display. We design a compact, multi-touch interface using accessible components that fit the ring’s tight form factor. It further integrates a flexible OLED display, BLE micro-controller, IMU, and PPG sensor, supporting both local and remote interaction. To bridge hardware touch sensing and interaction events, we introduce nano interactions—a compact vocabulary that adapts familiar touch primitives for direct, co-located input and visual output on ultra-small, curved surfaces. Nano interactions allow interaction within a single glance–touch cycle, supporting one-handed, low-attention use under motion. We implement a set of applications to explore the design space enabled by multi-touch on a ring. A user study with 12 participants demonstrates reliable touch interaction and provides positive short-term assessments of usability, comfort, and social acceptability, highlighting opportunities for compact interaction surfaces supporting glanceable and on-the-go interaction.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: PrejSense: Non-intrusive Gaze-Informed Prediction of Implicit Prejudice Against Machine for Proactive Interface Adaptation
abstract: Implicit prejudice against machine can critically undermine the effectiveness of human-AI collaboration by limiting trust, cooperation, and system acceptance. Despite its significance, such prejudice is rarely addressed in real world usage and is often assessed retrospectively through self-report measures or implicit association test, lacking automated and adaptive interface essential for responsive system design. Drawn from dual process theory, we propose and test PrejSense, a proof-of-concept adaptive interface loop that uses non-intrusive gaze signals to predict users’ prejudice states and adapt interface support accordingly. First, we develop interpretable deep learning models to predict prejudice from gaze features. Second, we develop adaptive interface using LLM agents to dynamically respond to estimated prejudice states, with expert-informed refinement. Third, we build a full-stack system for automated prejudice prediction and adaptive interaction, enabling non-intrusive integration into collaborative AI systems. We conduct a user testing experiment to evaluate the effectiveness of PrejSense. Compared with baseline, PrejSense significantly enhanced emotional trust and showed marginal positive effects on cognitive trust and WOA. These results provide preliminary evidence for state-contingent prejudice-aware adaptation in a low-risk decision-support task. By combining gaze-informed prejudice prediction with adaptive interaction design, this work opens a design space for prejudice-aware adaptive interfaces while highlighting the need for larger-scale validation.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Priors of U: Dynamic Preference Learning for Embodied Interaction
abstract: People have their own habits; from how they organize their workspace, over which mug they reach for in the morning, to how they prepare for cooking. Such preferences are context-dependent, dynamic, and often difficult to articulate. As embodied AI agents, such as robots, enter personal spaces, effective interaction requires understanding these implicit and evolving preferences; otherwise, such systems risk being more hindering than helpful. We propose an architecture that learns user preferences from real-world behavioral observation without requiring explicit instruction or feedback. We introduce a factor-graph-based user model that captures preferences across spatial arrangement, tool selection, and workflow, and continuously adapts as tasks and contexts change. The model expands with new observations, enabling open-ended, in situ learning of user-specific preference patterns. Our evaluation shows accurate, calibrated predictions across domains and robust adaptation over time. We demonstrate personalized robot assistance scenarios illustrating seamless and context-aware human–agent interaction.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: CARVid: Content-Aware Retargeting of Videos with On-Screen Graphics
abstract: Video editors routinely reframe landscape videos containing on-screen graphics, such as lower thirds or scoreboards, to portrait aspect ratios for sharing on social media. Existing methods often crop, shrink, or distort these graphics, reducing readability and disrupting their original design. Manual redesign is also slow and frustrating due to the difficulty of dealing with layered compositions or flattened videos with graphics that lack editable layers. We present CARVid, a content-aware retargeting tool for adapting on-screen graphics in videos to new aspect ratios while preserving readability and original design intent. CARVid leverages recent advances in foundation vision and segmentation models, together with a novel graphics-processing algorithm guided by a VLM critic, to detect graphical overlays, extract them from their underlying videos, and apply content-aware retargeting operations to adapt them to new aspect ratios. Our human-in-the-loop approach combines text-aware scaling, layout-aware horizontal and vertical segmentation, and content-aware space removal to support both automatic and user-directed retargeting of on-screen graphics. We conducted a technical evaluation using a custom dataset of 60 in-the-wild videos from popular internet sources that contain on-screen graphics. Results provide evidence of CARVid’s technical feasibility across a wide range of videos.
journal: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: BrewSense: A Mobile Water Quality Monitoring Platform using Laser Reflection near Brewster Angle
abstract: BrewSense is a mobile water-quality monitoring platform for realtime, large-scale detection of inland water pollution beyond the reach of grab sampling and remote sensing, whose alternatives are invasive, expensive, or limited to narrow classes of solutes and controlled environments. BrewSense leverages laser reflection near Brewster's angle to remotely infer the refractive index of surface water, which varies approximately linearly with the concentration of both ionic and organic solutes. It combines a beam-splitter and orthogonal-polarizer front-end that strongly suppresses ambient light, synchronized electrodynamic indexers with magnetic angle sensing, and hierarchical angular sampling, Gaussian spot filtering, and derivative-based Brewster-angle fitting that stabilize measurements under platform motion, waves, turbidity, and temperature variations. Implemented on a UAV, BrewSense operates at meter-scale standoff distances and achieves sub-10-4 refractive-index resolution under controlled conditions. Controlled and real-lake-water tank experiments evaluate inorganic salts (NaCl, NH4Cl) and organic solutes (glucose, urea), and a UAV deployment validates end-to-end operation in a NaCl-dominated field setting. BrewSense achieves up to 3.2× lower error than prior UWB and vibration-based systems and an approximately 8% mean relative concentration-estimation error across 20 UAV field sites.
journal: Proceedings of the Twenty-seventh International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Poster: When Safer AI Makes the System Less Safe: Inference Reuse and Systemic Risk in Networked Autonomy
abstract: Network-assisted inference can improve the decisions of autonomous agents, while reusing inference results can avoid repeated computation. However, when multiple agents reuse the same inference result, their failures become more coupled. We show that beyond a simple threshold, simultaneous failure can become more likely even though every agent is individually more accurate. We then characterize when the resource savings from reuse justify this added shared-failure risk.
journal: Proceedings of the Twenty-seventh International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Ripple: Coordination-Free Message Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows at the IoT Edge
abstract: Distributed intelligence in IoT and edge systems increasingly runs as agentic AI: production large language model (LLM) applications execute as workflows—directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of agents and tools that exchange prompts, retrieved context, and tool outputs across end devices, edge servers, and the cloud. When many such workflows share a capacity-limited link, such as an edge gateway uplink or a regional aggregation point, that link rather than the GPU gates the communication phase, and a message that unblocks an idle agent may wait behind an unrelated bulk transfer. A dependency-aware link scheduler can mitigate this, but a scheduler that ranks messages by whole-workflow remaining work and downstream critical path requires a global, continuously updated view of every concurrent workflow, that is, a central coordinator that heterogeneous and dynamic IoT edge deployments typically lack. This paper presents Ripple, a coordination-free link scheduler in which each agent ranks only its own outgoing messages, using a local rule that prioritizes downstream criticality per unit transmission cost and applies an age credit to curb long waits. The required downstream-criticality signal is a bounded scalar initialized with the source's task descriptor, so no runtime node maintains the global graph. In an event-driven, flow-level evaluation on a shared 100 Mbps link with heavy-tailed messages (median 419 KB, 99th-percentile about 30 MB) and four DAG shapes, network waiting accounts for 46% of the mean workflow completion time (WCT) under fair sharing at offered load ρ=0.88. Ripple reduces mean and 99th-percentile WCT by 24% and 38% relative to fair sharing, and attains 9% lower mean and 27% lower tail WCT than a global-view reference heuristic while using no global state. A knowledge-horizon analysis shows that performance saturates at a one-hop view, and an ablation finds that message size and age drive most of the aggregate gain. The results use an idealized flow-level priority model; a DSCP/eBPF realization that needs no coordinator and no change to the LLM runtime is proposed but not yet evaluated.
journal: Proceedings of the Twenty-seventh International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: An Agentic AI Architecture for Zero-Touch IoT Device Onboarding and Interoperability
abstract: The heterogeneity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices remains a major barrier to scalable deployment, automated onboarding, and cross-platform interoperability. Device-specific protocols, software dependencies, telemetry formats, and runtime constraints often require manual configuration and ad-hoc integration logic. This paper proposes an agentic AI architecture for zero-touch IoT device onboarding, where a large language model is used as an autonomous configuration agent capable of generating device-side software, installing dependencies, validating runtime behavior, and recursively correcting failures until convergence is achieved. The proposed architecture introduces a closed-loop workflow that combines device inspection, AI-based runtime generation, remote deployment, telemetry validation, and self-correction. Interoperability is addressed through a normalized telemetry contract that abstracts device-specific behavior into a common telemetry representation. We evaluate the approach on a real IoT device by benchmarking multiple AI models under clean installation conditions in two campaigns: the original pipeline and a second pipeline assisted by a locally trained semantic context optimizer. The comparison covers convergence time, correction cycles, recursive iterations, and prompt tokens. The optimizer-assisted campaign reduced prompt redundancy and recursive recovery effort while preserving successful onboarding across all tested models. Overall, the results show that agentic AI can support zero-touch onboarding while exposing measurable differences among models in reliability, efficiency, and runtime convergence.
journal: Proceedings of the Twenty-seventh International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Air pollution in the context of building structure and density in selected Polish cities
abstract: The aim of the study was to determine the differentiation of mean annual concentrations of particulate matter PM2.5 and PM10, benzo(a)pyrene (BaP), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), and benzene (C₆H₆) in 2018–2024 in the context of the structure and intensity of development in Gdańsk, Kraków, and Łódź. The analysis also account - ed for reported pollutant emissions and mean annual wind speed. Data from GIOŚ, KOBiZE, and IMGW-PIB, as well as building data from BDOT10k were used. The highest mean annual concentrations of all analysed pollutants were recorded in Kraków, where the share of built-up area was 49%, and the lowest in Gdańsk, where this share was 30%. After accounting for differences between cities, significant positive correlations between reported emissions and concentration were found for BaP (ρ = 0.90), NO₂ (ρ = 0.60), and PM10 ( ρ = 0.55). However, in the models accounting for the city effect, reported emissions were not significantly associated with the concentration of any of the analysed pollutants. The mean annual wind speed was highest in Gdańsk (3.98 m/s) and lowest in Kraków (3.08 m/s). The height structure of buildings differed between cities, but did not directly correspond to the observed differences in concentrations. The results indicate that the differentiation of mean annual air pollutant concentrations between cities co-occurs with differences in building intensity and wind speed. Due to the limited number of cities analysed, these relationships should not be interpreted as causal.

title: Reactive dyes adsorption by chestnut shells coated with nanoparticles of zinc oxide: Characterization, isotherm and kinetic studies
abstract: This investigation employed a new adsorbent composed of chestnut shell powder and covered with ZnO nanoparticles. Coated chestnut shell (CCS) was examined to assess the adsorption of Reactive Blue-19 Dye and Red Reac - tive-2 from a water-based mixture. Considerable increases in the capability of adsorption of the chestnut shell were recognized following the coating of the powder particles with ZnO nanoparticles. The adsorbent was analyzed using surface area analysis, FTIR, SEM, and XRD to verify its structural and morphological properties. Batch adsorption Research was done to ascertain the optimum Situations, including the solution pH, adsorbent dosage, contact period, speed of shaking, and initial dye concentration, all conducted at room temperature, which is 25 °C. Both the Freundlich and Langmuir isotherm models were used to describe the equilibrium information on adsorption. As a result revealed that the process of adsorption followed Langmuir’s isotherm model, using correlation values (R²) of 0.9886 for Reactive Red-2 and 0.9955 for Reactive Blue-19, demonstrating monolayer adsorption onto a uniform surface. The greatest CCS adsorption capacity was observed for Reactive Blue-19 (172.413 mg/g), followed by Reactive Red-2 (114.942 mg/g). Kinetic information was correlated using both pseudo-first-order and pseudo-second-order models. The findings demonstrated that the model of pseudo-second order gave greater results compared to the pseudo-first order model, considering correlation coefficients (R²) of 0.9951 for Reactive Red-2 and 0.9975for Reactive Blue-19, demonstrating that the process of chemisorption step that limits the rate of adsorption mechanism. Thus, these results show that CCS is among the best and most efficient adsorbents for getting rid of wastewater tainted with reactive dye residues.

title: Digital Transformation in South American Soybean Production: A Systematic Review of Drivers and Barriers to Agricultural Technology Adoption
journal: Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção

title: When Actors Stop Participating: Delegated Participation and Representative-Centered Organizing
abstract: Organizational theories usually treat participation as actor-bound: the actors whose interests are at stake are expected to occupy the interactions through which outcomes are produced. Agentic artificial intelligence and other autonomous representatives weaken that correspondence. This conceptual article develops a theory of delegated participation, defined as the authorized transfer of communicative, evaluative, coordinative, or exchange-related participation from a principal to a representative. The argument moves beyond treating participation delegation as merely another agency relationship. When representatives operate on multiple sides of an exchange, they form an interaction system that can persist without direct principal participation, reshape the alternatives reaching principals, and separate participation from accountability. The model identifies activity conditions, capability–structure alignment, and authorization as antecedents; bilateral representation and interaction displacement as mechanisms; and symbolic concentration and representative-centered organizing as organizational consequences. The framework contributes by challenging the actor-bound conception of participation, identifying bilateral representation as a discontinuity in organizing, and explaining why declining principal participation may coexist with persistent principal accountability and increasingly consequential symbolic appearances. The article concludes with managerial implications and an empirical research agenda focused on recruitment, procurement, customer service, and AI-mediated negotiation.

title: Deep Learning-Based Multimodal Urban Air Quality Prediction
journal: De Gruyter Handbook of Disruptive Urban Technologies and Society

title: Towards Fine-grained and Robust Detection of Human-AI Co-authorship
abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) is reshaping how textual content is produced, complicating text provenance, and raising concerns for misinformation, plagiarism, and intellectual property. While prior work on AI-generated text detection has progressed, one-dimensional human-AI co-authorship scores lack signals directly relevant to ``AI involvement''. It remains unclear how adversarial paraphrasing distorts detection signals. In this work, we formulate a discrete-class text provenance detection framework. This framework allows an abstraction of realistic co-authorship scenarios into distinct degrees of AI involvement, differentiating the AI polishing on the surface level from the AI updating the discourse structures. This framework reveals the mechanisms of how adversarial paraphrasing blurs the decision boundaries for co-authorship detectors. To improve robustness of the detectors, we augment training data with adversarial paraphrases generated by the state-of-the-art paraphrasing attack model, exposing detectors to challenging meaning-preserving rewrites. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and generation models demonstrate that adversarial paraphrasing substantially degrades detectors trained only on benign data, while adversarial data augmentation leads to consistent robustness gains and good cross-generator transferability. Overall, our findings highlight the value of discrete-class formulation and principled data augmentation for building reliable detectors of human-AI co-authorship.

title: Integrating Agricultural Yield Variability and Financial Failure Risk Assessment Through Production and Financial Indicators for Data-Informed Farm Management Decisions
abstract: Variations in agricultural production may affect farm performance, the use of resources and potential farm financial vulnerability, and integrated analyses are essential to make data-informed decisions. This study aimed to analyse the production characteristics at farm level and to create a production-based vulnerability framework based on the FLAME database. A secondary quantitative analytical design was used for 59,171 farms and other crop/livestock-level data was utilized to describe agricultural structure and production. Farm size, estimated output, output per hectare, crop diversity and livestock indicators were assessed using descriptive statistics and Spearman correlation analysis, along with group comparisons and vulnerability classification. Median farm area was 50.36 ha with a median estimated production of 125.98 tonnes. Total estimated crop production was led by winter wheat, potato and beet. Farm area was highly correlated with total production (ρ = 0.722, p < 0.001) and production was highly correlated with production per hectare (ρ = 0.783, p < 0.001). The highly vulnerable farms were identified based on low production, low production intensity and limited crop diversity and accounted for 24.05% of all the farms. High vulnerability farms significantly had less farm area, production, production intensity and crop diversity compared with low vulnerability farms. While production indicators cannot directly be used to identify financially failed farms since these variables were not available in this study, the results show how production indicators can be used to identify potentially vulnerable farm profiles as well as to support data-driven farm management.
journal: Computer and Decision Making: An International Journal

title: Explainable Hybrid Deep Learning for Tomato Leaf Disease Classification: Comparative Performance and Agricultural Decision-Support Implications
abstract: Timely identification of tomato leaf disease can be helpful for crop monitoring and agricultural assessment; however, the similar symptoms of different diseases hinder the automated recognition and interpretation. This study proposes an explainable hybrid deep learning model which fuses the MobileNetV3Large and EfficientNetB4 at the feature level, followed by multiclass classification and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). The model was tested on 30,609 images of ten tomato leaf classes and five stand-alone CNN models. The proposed hybrid obtained a training accuracy of 97.31%, a validation accuracy of 96.57%, and a test accuracy of 96.61% along with macro-averaged precision, recall and F1-score of 96.67%, 96.63% and 96.62% respectively. It achieved a test accuracy of more than 0.78 percentage points higher than the best standalone architecture, MobileNetV3Large (95.83%). In addition to the overall accuracy, the assessment also reveals the differences in recognition of the disease, including those between visually similar classes. Qualitative indications of image regions associated with predictions are provided by grad-CAM maps. Based on these findings, the classifier can be considered as an explainable information component for human supervised agricultural assessment. Experimental evaluation of decision policies, field-level management outcomes and improvements in agricultural decision quality were not conducted.
journal: Computer and Decision Making: An International Journal

title: PIPNet EA for Robust and Explainable Crop Weed Classification Using Enhanced Prototype Evidence Aggregation
abstract: Deep learning models can achieve high accuracy on clean crop–weed images but often lose performance when field images are affected by noise, blur, poor illumination, motion, or compression. This study presents PIPNet-EA, an enhanced prototype-based interpretable prediction framework that combines top-κ spatial evidence aggregation with confidence-weighted prototype reasoning. Five deep learning architectures—ResNet50, ResNet101, ViT-B/16, PIPNet-R50, and PIPNet-R101—were evaluated on two crop–weed image datasets under seven common image corruptions at three severity levels: mild, moderate, and severe. The evaluation generated 210 model–corruption–severity accuracy measurements, while the accuracy retention rate (ARR) was used to quantify the proportion of clean-image performance preserved under degradation. PIPNet-R50 showed the strongest overall robustness. On the challenging field dataset, its mean accuracy was 0.641, 0.568, and 0.437 under mild, moderate, and severe corruption, respectively, compared with 0.594, 0.525, and 0.391 for ResNet50. It retained 98.9%, 87.7%, and 67.5% of its clean performance across the three severity levels, exceeding the corresponding retention of ResNet50. Prototype activation maps remained focused on meaningful plant structures, including leaf tips, midribs, and petiole regions, even under moderate degradation. By combining evidence from multiple spatial locations rather than relying on a single dominant activation, PIPNet-EA reduces the effect of local image corruption while maintaining interpretable predictions. These findings support prototype-based evidence aggregation as a practical approach for developing robust and explainable crop–weed classification systems for precision agriculture.

title: Evaluation of Seedling-stage Salt Tolerance in USDA Spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.) Accessions
abstract: Soil salinity is a major constraint on crop production, and improving salt tolerance requires phenotyping methods that capture multiple components of the plant stress response. Salt tolerance was evaluated in 150 US Department of Agriculture spinach ( Spinacia oleracea L.) accessions at the seedling stage under 300 mM NaCl and a nonsaltwater control (no added NaCl) using a completely randomized design with three replications. Visual leaf injury, leaf chlorophyll content, and seedling height were measured, and both absolute and proportional stress indices were calculated. Salt-tolerant accessions were defined as those that maintained lower leaf injury, retained more leaf chlorophyll, and showed less reduction in seedling height under salt stress relative to the control. Genotypic effects were significant for all traits ( P < 0.0001), and broad-sense heritability was high, ranging from 89.70% to 99.12%. Leaf injury score correlated moderately with chlorophyll reduction ( r = 0.70), whereas no statistically significant correlation was detected between chlorophyll reduction traits and seedling height reduction traits. These results indicate that visual injury, chlorophyll reduction, and growth inhibition provide complementary information for evaluating seedling salt tolerance. An average salt-tolerance rank (ASR) integrating the leaf injury score (LIS), absolute decrease in chlorophyll (AD_C), inhibition index of chlorophyll (II_C), absolute decrease in seedling height (AD_SH), and inhibition index of seedling height (II_SH) identified PI 177082 as the most tolerant accession and PI 648962 as the most sensitive accession. PI 177082 had an ASR of 11.50, with an LIS of 1.67, an AD_C of 8.67 soil plant analysis development units, an II_C of 26.94%, an AD_SH of 7.33 cm, and an II_SH of 26.51%. Hierarchical clustering broadly supported the ASR-based classification while showing phenotypic diversity among the tolerant accessions. These findings indicate that seedling salt tolerance in spinach was better characterized by the combined descriptors than by a single trait. The contrasting accessions identified in our study provide a phenotypic resource for future validation, breeding, and association mapping studies aimed at improving salt tolerance in spinach.

title: The Cryptocurrency Trend Factor Revisited: Predictive Information, Portfolio Construction, and Pricing Claims
abstract: We reassess five economic claims about the cryptocurrency trend factor (CTREND): cross-sectional return predictability, high risk-adjusted performance, incremental information beyond market, size, and momentum, the ability to replace momentum in factor models, and robustness among large and liquid coins and after trading costs. Our reconstruction and code audit identify issues in information timing, technical indicators, forecast coverage, portfolio formation, and return accounting. We first correct future-information use and related settlement rules, then implement broader corrections to indicators, forecast availability, and portfolio accounting. Without additional coin exclusions, the first stage changes CTREND's mean weekly gross return from 4.07% to 4.25%, annualized Sharpe ratio from 2.08 to 1.48, and weekly alpha relative to published market, size, and momentum factors from 2.77% to 3.06%. After comprehensive correction, these become 0.05%, 0.01, and -1.38%; the alpha is no longer significant. Replacing momentum with CTREND yields an advantage in maximum squared Sharpe ratios of 0.058 in the original implementation, 0.024 after the first-stage correction, and -0.0185 after comprehensive correction, with a statistically significant overall decline. Mean weekly gross returns for the largest 100 coins change from 2.93% to 3.99% to 1.00%, while mean weekly net returns for the full long-short portfolio under the lowest assumed trading costs change from 2.93% to 3.35% to -0.87%. These findings show that reported performance and factor-substitution gains depend materially on implementation and sample composition. We distinguish predictive information, an independent return premium, and the incremental value of replacing an existing factor as separate economic claims.

title: Managing Reciprocal Partnerships for Continuing Agrotechnology Education of Young Farmers
abstract: This study aims to analyze and develop a strategic management framework for reciprocal partnerships between non-formal education institutions and the Business and Industrial World (DUDI) to develop Continuing Agrotechnology Education (CAE) for young farmers in Jember Regency. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, data were gathered through in-depth interviews and participatory observations in industrial farmland, with key informants including managers of the Jember Vocational Training Center (BLK), agricultural DUDI practitioners, leaders of millennial farmer groups, and educational and agricultural experts. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically and systematically using the latest NVivo software to ensure coding validity and analytical depth. The findings reveal that current non-formal agricultural training remains short-term, fragmented, and poorly aligned with the ongoing digitalization needs of smart farming. This study proposes a framework that develops a CAE management model positioning industry as a co-architect of the curriculum, integrating digital literacy, Internet of Things (IoT) applications, and data-driven farming into non-formal education systems. The study concludes that the empirically grounded reciprocal partnership framework conceptually offers a strategic foundation with the potential to enhance young farmers' dynamic capabilities and functional digital literacy. Consequently, it is recommended that local governments and vocational training providers consider this framework as an operational reference for community empowerment programs in digital agriculture, serving as a basis for empirical validation in future experimental studies.

title: Correlation of Test Load Results of Pile Foundation for Various Selected Models
abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyse the foundation of an automated high - bay warehouse using Continuous Flight Auger (CFA) piles. Data regarding the designed structure, geotechnical conditions, pile loads, and allowable differences in pile settlement were obtained from the detailed design, which included CPT probe tests, geological drilling, and laboratory tests of samples collected during drilling. This provided relatively precise data on the geological conditions in the area under consideration. The tests indicated that the area falls into Geotechnical Category 2, and the ground conditions were considered as complex. Due to the presence of the soft soils, a foundation was designed using cast - in - situ CFA piles, which will meet the requirements for the first (ULS) and, above all, the second (SLS) limit state. The primary purpose of the designed piles is to ensure uniform settlement of the foundation slab on which the self - supporting racks of the planned warehouse are placed. This study focused on determining the load - bearing capacity of piles using various calculation methods. The obtained results were compared with the values obtained from finite element method (FEM). The Midas GTS NX program was used. The results finally were compared with the pile load tests.

title: Climate Change Reshapes Vineyard Disease – Pest Pressure and Grape Yield Losses in Romania
abstract: Climate change is increasingly constraining Romanian viticulture by intensifying biotic stress and destabilizing grape yields . Across Europe, rising temperatures, altered precipitation seasonality, and more frequent extremes are reshaping grapevine – pest – pa thogen interactions: downy and powdery mildews remain dominant phytosanitary threats, while chronic decline syndromes linked to grapevine trunk diseases and the spread of invasive organisms expand risk profiles and management costs. In Romania, producer re ports and surveillance outputs consistently highlight recurrent pressure from Plasmopara viticola (downy mildew), Erysiphe (Uncinula) necator (powdery mildew), Botrytis cinerea (bunch rot), Pseudopeziza spp., and key pests including Lobesia botrana and eriophyid mites (Eriophyes/Colomerus spp.), with implications for yield stability and intervention intensity. Here we propose a reproducible, country - level framework for Romania (2015 – 2025) that integrates three open - data pillars: (i ) official crop statistics for grape production and yield (INSSE/TEMPO and harmonized EU reporting), (ii) publicly posted phytosanitary warning bulletins as an operational proxy for disease – pest pressure, and (iii) reanalysis - based climate descriptors suit able for viticulture risk assessment. A national Warning - Bulletin Pressure Index (WBPI) is constructed by systematically collecting, filtering to vineyard - relevant advisories, removing duplicates, and aggregating annual counts by territory; where possible, WBPI is also normalized to account for reporting effort (e.g., bulletins per issuing unit/year) and tested for sensitivity to changes in bulletin volume. Climate covariates are derived from ERA5 - Land/ERA5 products using standardized growing - season indicat ors aligned with vine phenology (e.g., heat accumulation, hot - day frequency, and precipitation regime metrics including seasonal totals and dry - spell structure), spatially aggregated to the territorial scale used in statistical reporting. We outline an attribution strategy that links interannual production and yield anomalies to climate and WBPI signals using trend – cycle decomposition and regression models with lagged sensitivity windows, emphasizing interpretability for risk management rat her than purely predictive skill. As an empirical anchor, official series indicate that Romania reached approximately 1,069 kt of grapes for wine in 2018 and declined to ~668 kt by 2024 (≈37.5% contraction), underscoring the magnitude of recent volatility and motivating integrated climate - biotic assessments. The resulting pipeline supports rapid annual updates as new statistics and bulletins become available and provides actionable evidence for adaptation planning (cultivar/clone choice, canopy and irrigati on strategy, forecast - informed spray timing, and integrated pest management), while explicitly recognizing that warning bulletins capture both biological pressure and surveillance/reporting intensity.

title: NEUROGENESIS: MECHANISMS, REGULATION, AND IMPLICATIONS FOR BRAIN FUNCTION AND DISEASE
abstract: Adult neurogenesis, the continuous generation of functional neurons from neural stem cells in the mature mammalian brain, represents one of the most remarkable forms of structural plasticity in the central nervous system. Once considered impossible, adult neurogenesis is now recognized as a fundamental process occurring primarily in two canonical neurogenic niches: the subgranular zone (SGZ) of the hippocampal dentate gyrus and the subventricular zone (SVZ) of the lateral ventricles. This review synthesizes current knowledge on adult neurogenesis, covering the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying neural stem cell maintenance and neuronal differentiation, the stages of neurogenesis from proliferation to synaptic integration, the functional contributions of adult-born neurons to learning, memory, and mood regulation, and the modulation of neurogenesis by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. We examine the impact of aging and disease on neurogenesis, with particular emphasis on the ongoing debate regarding adult human neurogenesis. Recent conflicting reports about the extent and persistence of neurogenesis in the adult human brain have highlighted critical methodological challenges and species differences that must be addressed for successful clinical translation. We discuss evidence for and against human adult neurogenesis, the methodological factors contributing to discrepancies, and the implications for understanding human brain function and developing therapeutic strategies. This review also covers therapeutic strategies targeting neurogenic processes, including behavioral interventions, pharmacological approaches, and emerging cell-based therapies. Recent advances in molecular profiling, lineage tracing, and imaging technologies have deepened our understanding while revealing the complexity of neurogenic regulation across species and throughout the lifespan. This review aims to provide researchers, clinicians, and students with an integrative perspective on adult neurogenesis with special attention to translating findings from animal models to human applications.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Driving Business Growth through Adaptive Leadership, Open Innovation, and Market Sensing: The Role of Purple Ocean Strategy in Information Technology Solution Business
abstract: The rapid development of digital technologies and increasing competitive intensity have created significant challenges for information technology (IT) solution businesses seeking sustainable growth. Organizations must continuously adapt to technological changes, customer expectations, and competitive pressures while developing innovative and differentiated solutions. However, limited research has integrated adaptive leadership, open innovation, market sensing capability, purple ocean strategy formulation, and overall business growth within a single research framework. This study aims to investigate the causal factors and relationships among adaptive leadership, open innovation, market sensing capability, purple ocean strategy formulation, and overall business growth in IT solution businesses, and to develop an empirical causal model explaining these relationships. The study employs a quantitative research design supported by qualitative thematic analysis. Data are collected from 400 respondents consisting of business owners, executives, managers, and individuals involved in organizational decision-making. A structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale measures the five major constructs. Descriptive statistics and structural equation modeling (SEM) are employed to assess the measurement model and test the proposed hypotheses. The anticipated results suggest that adaptive leadership positively influences open innovation, market sensing capability, purple ocean strategy formulation, and overall business growth. Open innovation and market sensing capability are expected to positively influence purple ocean strategy formulation and overall business growth. Purple ocean strategy formulation is also expected to contribute positively to organizational growth by strengthening value innovation, customer-centric innovation, competitive differentiation, continuous improvement, and strategic integration. The study is expected to provide theoretical and practical contributions by demonstrating how leadership capabilities, external knowledge, market intelligence, and strategic formulation can be integrated to strengthen the competitiveness and sustainable growth of IT solution businesses.
journal: International Review of Management and Marketing

title: A Hybrid Multi-Objective Optimization Framework for Crop Planting Planning under Digital Economy
abstract: With the deep integration of artificial intelligence and the digital economy in agriculture, traditional crop planting planning still suffers from slow convergence, limited optimization accuracy, and weak adaptability to ecological and market uncertainties. To address these challenges, this study proposes a multi-objective crop planting optimization model that integrates the Multi-Objective Grey Wolf Optimizer (MOGWO), the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II, and proximal policy optimization, enabling dynamic decision-making driven by multi-source data. Experimental results on two authoritative datasets showed that the model achieved Pareto frontier coverage above 90% and stable convergence within 500 iterations. Multi-scenario simulations indicated that peak annual net profit exceeded 1.8 million yuan, and annual carbon reduction potential generally exceeded 150 tons of CO2, while computation time was maintained at approximately 4.8s per 100 iterations. Overall, the proposed model demonstrates strong robustness, ecological effectiveness, and computational efficiency, supporting intelligent agricultural decision-making under the digital economy framework.
journal: Journal of Engineering, Project, and Production Management

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF THE INDEPENDENT CURRICULUM ON STUDENT CREATIVITY IN PJOK LEARNING AT ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of the Merdeka Curriculum implementation on the development of students' creativity in Physical Education, Sports, and Health (PJOK) learning at elementary schools in Gelumbang District. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach with participants consisting of PJOK teachers and six fifth-grade students from SDN 6 and SDN 9 Gelumbang. Data were collected through observation, interviews, questionnaires, and documentation, and analyzed using Miles and Huberman's model through data reduction, data display, and verification. The results indicate that the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum can enhance students’ creativity in the indicators of fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration, with students from SDN 6 achieving 77–91%, higher than SDN 9, which ranged from 61–83%. Supporting factors include school support and students’ learning motivation, while obstacles involve limited facilities and teachers’ understanding of differentiated learning. This study recommends improving infrastructure, providing teacher training, and expanding further research to optimally support the development of students' creativity.

title: Government Extension, Peer Communication, and Digital Technology Adoption Among Family Farms
abstract: Using survey data from 533 grain-growing family farms in Sichuan Province, this study employs a Poisson model to compare the relationships of government extension (GE) and peer communication (PC) with the number of digital technologies adopted, jointly examines cognitive and ability pathways, and conducts bounded-model, instrumental-variable and omitted-variable sensitivity analyses. The results show that PC has a stronger positive association with the adoption count; when the frequencies of the two channels increase from their respective 25th to 75th percentiles, the average predicted adoption count increases by 0.186 and 0.595 technologies, respectively, with a difference of 0.409 technologies. Perceived usefulness (PU) is a shared cognitive pathway for both channels, with a larger coefficient product for GE along this pathway; PC has a larger coefficient product along the pathway of ability to access socialized agricultural services (SA). The study reveals different linkages of the two information channels with technology cognition and service access, providing empirical evidence for connecting systematic technical information with local user experience.

title: Spectral and Physiological Responses of Pisum sativum and Datura stramonium to Light Intensity and Far-Red Radiation Under Controlled Hydroponic Conditions
abstract: Light quantity and spectral quality regulate plant growth and may influence crop–weed interactions by altering plant morphology, biomass allocation, and physiology. This study evaluated the combined effects of photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD) and far-red (FR) radiation on the morphological, biomass, physiological, and hyperspectral responses of Pisum sativum L. and Datura stramonium L. grown separately under controlled hydroponic conditions. A 2 × 2 × 2 factorial experiment was conducted using two species, two PPFD levels, and two FR treatments. Morphological traits, biomass production, root mass fraction, SPAD chlorophyll content, hyperspectral reflectance (350–2500 nm), and vegetation indices were analyzed using multivariate statistics, principal component analysis, and Random Forest classification. Species identity explained most of the variation in morphology, biomass allocation, and spectral characteristics. FR supplementation increased mean shoot height in D. stramonium by 62.5% under high PPFD and 101.2% under low PPFD, whereas shoot height in P. sativum was not significantly affected. Red wavelengths between 649 and 668 nm provided the strongest discriminatory information, while short-wave infrared wavelengths contributed complementary biochemical information. The Random Forest model achieved an overall accuracy of 75.7%, an AUC of 0.839, and a Cohen’s κ of 0.489. These findings demonstrate that D. stramonium exhibits greater FR-induced morphological plasticity than P. sativum and that hyperspectral sensing provides useful, although not yet field-validated, crop–weed discrimination.

title: The Green Productivity Effect of Agricultural New Quality Productive Forces—Evidence from Provincial Panel Data and Farm Household Surveys
abstract: Developing agricultural new quality productive forces (NQP) is an important pathway to promoting the green transformation of agriculture. This study constructs an evaluation indicator system for NQP from three dimensions: new quality workers (NQW), new quality means of labor (NQML), and new quality objects of labor (NQOL). Using panel data from 30 provinces in China for 2011–2023 and survey data from 533 farm households in Sichuan Province in 2024, it employs a two-way fixed effects model, a spatial Durbin model (SDM), and a threshold model to examine the relationships between NQP and agricultural green total factor productivity (AGTFP), and between farm-level new quality productive forces (FNQP) and green production behavior (GB), respectively. The findings show that NQP are significantly positively associated with AGTFP and exhibit certain spatial associations; FNQP are significantly positively associated with GB, indicating that production factor quality is closely associated with farmers’ green production practices; the threshold analysis suggests a stronger positive association between FNQP and GB among farmers with higher digital information analysis ability (DIAA). The study reveals the links between production factor quality and agricultural green development (AGD) at the levels of regional productivity and farmer behavior, providing empirical evidence for coordinating the development of knowledge and skills, technological equipment, and production conditions, and for providing targeted training in information ability.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Longitudinal Trajectory Forecasting in Alzheimer’s Disease with a Multi-Task Transformer
abstract: Accurately predicting the progression of Alzheimer’s disease is crucial for physicians, who need not only to identify the most likely short-term diagnosis but also to understand how the condition will evolve over time and how reliable the prediction is for each patient. However, the heterogeneity of disease expression and the scarcity of longitudinal data make this task challenging. Many current deep learning methods reduce the problem to single-step classification and give little consideration to the role of uncertainty across subsequent visits. We present NeuroTrajectory-Net, a multi-task Transformer that forecasts the future Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) slope, the future Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) slope, and the binary progression risk from a subject’s past visits alone. Using the OASIS-2 dataset of 150 patients (373 visits), we evaluate the model on a single patient-level (subject-disjoint) split of 90, 30, and 30 subjects for training, validation, and testing, so that no subject contributes sequences to more than one partition. On the test set, NeuroTrajectory-Net achieves a forecasting mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.82 MMSE points/year for the future MMSE slope. However, its classification head does not perform as well as single-task models (AUC = 0.51 versus 0.87–0.98). Monte Carlo Dropout yields personalized 95% prediction intervals; however, their empirical coverage on the test set is only 48.8%, so they are under-calibrated and not yet suitable for clinical decision-making. The exact target-generation rule and the handling of zero-padded visits have not yet been re-verified at the code level and are reported as reproducibility limitations; the progression classification results should therefore be regarded as preliminary. This paper introduces a multi-task framework designed to avoid target and split leakage and reports both its strengths and its limitations.

title: Photorespiratory Engineering from an Evolutionary Perspective: A Constraint-Aligned Evaluation and Validation Framework
abstract: More than two billion years of photorespiratory evolution have shaped three sets of constraints: catalytic constraints associated with Rubisco oxygenase activity; compartmental topology constraints arising from compartmental organization, transport processes, and cofactor coupling; and physiological and ecological constraints arising from integration with metabolic and signaling networks. Photorespiratory engineering has emerged as a key strategy for improving photosynthetic efficiency in C3 crops, yet existing studies have not systematically assessed the practical implications of these constraints. Evaluation metrics remain inconsistent, the scope and depth of stability and risk assessments vary, and methodological heterogeneity hinders comparisons across studies. To address these issues, we synthesize the evolutionary history of photorespiration and findings from previous research to develop an evaluation and validation framework aligned with these constraints. This framework comprises eight assessment dimensions defining what to report, a context matrix specifying the conditions under which assessments should be conducted, and a five-tier validation pipeline defining the sequence of validation steps and the criteria for classifying outcomes. Retrospective application to five published case studies demonstrates that the framework enables consistent classification of outcomes and identifies distinct priorities for further improvement across studies involving different crop species, engineering strategies, and evaluation endpoints. By providing a practical evidence structure that can be updated as new findings emerge, this framework supports the transition from empirical exploration to systematic photorespiratory engineering and facilitates cross-study comparisons and the cumulative synthesis of evidence across assessment dimensions, experimental contexts, and outcomes.

title: A Semi-Parametric Dynamic Conditional Correlation Framework for Forecasting Systemic Risk: Evidence from CoVaR and Marginal Expected Shortfall
abstract: Accurate forecasting of systemic risk is crucial for financial stability and regulatory oversight. Traditional parametric models often fail to capture the complex, nonlinear dependence structures in financial markets, particularly during periods of distress. This paper proposes a semi-parametric dynamic conditional correlation (DCC) framework that integrates nonparametric estimation of marginal distributions with a parametric DCC specification to improve the forecasting of systemic risk measures—Conditional Value-at-Risk (CoVaR) and Marginal Expected Shortfall (MES). We employ a kernel-based quantile regression approach for marginal modeling and combine it with a DCC-GARCH structure for capturing time-varying conditional correlations. Empirical results using daily equity returns for a panel of 20 large U.S. financial institutions over the period January 2000 to December 2023, with emphasis on three stress episodes—the 2007–2009 global financial crisis, the 2011 European sovereign debt crisis spillover, and the March 2020 COVID-19 market disruption—demonstrate that the suggested semi-parametric DCC framework yields more accurate and robust one-day-ahead forecasts of CoVaR and MES compared to fully parametric alternatives, with the advantage widening during stress periods. During the 2007–2009 crisis sub-period, the SP-DCC model reduces the Fissler–Ziegel loss for CoVaR by 19.0% relative to the Gaussian-DCC benchmark and by 6.5% relative to the strongest parametric benchmark (skewed-t DCC). Importantly, the SP-DCC specification is the only model in our comparison set for which the null hypotheses of correct unconditional and conditional coverage are not rejected at the 1% significance level during stress periods, whereas the Gaussian-DCC benchmark significantly over-rejects. The model also exhibits improved performance in identifying systemically important institutions and tail interdependencies during stress episodes, with rankings that align more closely with official G-SIB designations and SRISK-based rankings than those implied by Gaussian-DCC benchmarks. Our findings underscore the importance of flexible marginal modeling in systemic risk measurement and provide policymakers with an enhanced toolkit for macroprudential surveillance.
journal: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

title: A Modeling-Based Predictive Regenerative Braking Strategy for a Parallel P2 Hybrid Electric Vehicle
abstract: Regenerative braking control in a hybrid electric vehicle must be evaluated at both the brake and powertrain levels, and additional recovered energy does not necessarily imply lower fuel consumption. This study examines a preview-aware C3 controller for a midsize parallel P2 hybrid electric vehicle against a causal, state-of-power-constrained C2 controller. C3 changes the desired regenerative torque share during braking and modifies the SOC target and power allocation before predicted deceleration. The controllers were evaluated on FTP-75, WLTP Class 3b and US06 using 100 matched realizations of six uncertain factors per cycle (300 C2–C3 pairs). Mean battery-recovered energy increased by 1.751%, 1.420% and 4.083%, while friction braking energy decreased by 5.100%, 4.393% and 11.842%, respectively. All 300 pairs favored C3 on the three braking metrics. Full-cycle factorial ablations attributed the nominal recovery gain primarily to the braking-torque allocation channel. SOC target preparation alone yielded negligible additional recovery at the tested initial SOC. With the stated algebraic terminal-SOC correction, mean fuel effects were −0.171%, −0.439% and +0.118%, respectively, where positive values indicate a reduction. Direct SOC-matched checks preserved the cycle-dependent sign, but the US06 advantage was only about 0.03–0.05%. Thus, the robust braking-energy benefit and the small, cycle-dependent fuel response arise from distinct control mechanisms. Improved recuperation alone does not establish a fuel-economy benefit.

title: Multi-Class Fine-Scale Vegetation Mapping: An Automated Object-Based Workflow for New Mexico Drylands
abstract: Fine-scale vegetation mapping supports habitat management, landscape change monitoring, and local planning. However, fine-scale maps that distinguish a large number of vegetation classes across broad extents remain scarce. Previous classifications using imagery with spatial resolutions of 1 m or finer have generally distinguished only six to ten classes at broad physiognomic levels and relied on training data generated exclusively through image interpretation. This study develops an object-based classification workflow to map vegetation at the Group Level of the United States National Vegetation Classification across two pilot study areas in New Mexico totaling 705,154 hectares, including the montane Jemez Mountains and the semi-arid Sevilleta region. Segmentation was performed using Geographic Object-Based Image Analysis (GEOBIA) at two hierarchical levels with 0.6 m National Agriculture Imagery Program (NAIP) imagery and a LiDAR-derived digital height model. Classification was conducted using a random forest model with 65 predictor variables derived from NAIP imagery, PlanetScope imagery, Sentinel-2 imagery, LiDAR-derived terrain surfaces, and Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) soil moisture. Training and validation data were obtained from a legacy ecological plot database originally collected for purposes other than classification. Of the 34 classes initially targeted for mapping, 27 were ultimately mapped after spectrally inseparable classes were collapsed into coarser hierarchical levels. Mean overall accuracy across 1000 training and validation partitions was 54.8%, with a minimum of 51.2% to a maximum of 65.6%. Phenological variables derived from PlanetScope imagery improved overall accuracy by an average of 6.5 percentage points. Overall classification accuracy varied by 12.7 percentage points across partitions, indicating that overall accuracy estimates based on a single training and validation split may provide a poor representation of expected model performance.

title: Economic Efficiency of Introducing Digital Technologies in The Agriculture of Uzbekistan
abstract: Agriculture remains a fundamental pillar of the economy of Uzbekistan, providing employment for a significant portion of the population and contributing substantially to the gross domestic product (GDP). However, traditional agricultural practices in the region are increasingly challenged by critical water scarcity, land degradation, climate volatility, and fluctuating market demands. This research article comprehensively analyzes the economic efficiency of introducing advanced digital technologies—including Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, automated drip irrigation systems, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), drone-based remote sensing, and Big Data analytics—into Uzbekistan's agricultural matrix. Following the formal IMRAD framework, this study synthesizes empirical field data gathered over a multi-year period from select automated pilot farms in the Fergana and Namangan regions, comparing them against adjacent conventional farms. The empirical findings demonstrate a substantial increase in average crop yields (ranging from 18% to 25% for cotton and wheat), a profound reduction in water consumption (by 30% to 35%), and a noticeable decrease in chemical fertilizer and fuel deployment. Econometric modeling indicates an average Net Present Value (NPV) improvement and a typical payback period of 2.8 to 3.5 years for digital technology capital expenditures. Ultimately, this paper discusses the systemic institutional, technical, and educational barriers to widespread digital adoption, offering actionable policy recommendations for expanding precision agriculture across the Republic.

title: Architectural Design and Internal Working of Health Talk: An Offline-Capable, Multilingual AI Conversational Agent for Clinical Triage and Healthcare Facility Discovery in Regional India
abstract: In developing nations such as India, primary healthcare triage faces acute structural bottlenecks, including severe doctor-to-population deficits in semi-urban and rural agglomerations, fragmented municipal health informatics, and linguistic barriers across heterogeneous regional populations. While modern conversational agents and large language models (LLMs) offer promising interactive capabilities, their direct clinical deployment is severely hampered by pharmaceutical hallucination risks, non-deterministic reasoning trajectories, prohibitive cloud API costs, and an absence of localized Indic language models. To resolve this critical dilemma, this paper presents the complete architectural design, algorithmic foundations, and empirical validation of Health Talk AI—a novel, offline-first, multilingual conversational triage agent specifically engineered for Tier-2 regional healthcare ecosystems such as the Greater Nashik Metropolitan Area in Maharashtra, India. Health Talk decouples clinical urgency categorization from generative text synthesis by introducing an inviolable, deterministic three-tier triage rule engine that executes prior to any natural language parsing. The architecture synthesizes: (1) an emergency finite-state pre-filter for instant red-flag detection; (2) a multilingual Natural Language Processing (NLP) subsystem featuring Devanagari script tokenization, Hindi versus Marathi marker-word frequency ratio disambiguation, and RapidFuzz partial-ratio entity extraction for pain intensity (1–10 scale), temporal duration, and anatomical body parts; (3) an offline-first Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) vector engine utilizing dense multilingual sentence embeddings (paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2) coupled with an inviolable cosine dot-product threshold (tau = 0.45) that mathematically eliminates medical hallucinations; (4) a privacy-preserving geospatial discovery subsystem indexing 347 verified healthcare facilities across Nashik using the spherical Haversine metric with two-decimal-place differential coordinate rounding (~1.1 km); and (5) automated state healthcare entitlement checklists (Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana - MJPJAY) paired with multi-lingual emergency first-aid response cards. Evaluated across 91 rigorous automated unit tests, Health Talk achieves a 100% test pass rate, 100% Top-1 retrieval precision on clinical queries in English, Hindi, and Marathi, and an end-to-end execution latency under 28 ms on commodity quad-core CPUs without GPU hardware. This work establishes an authoritative, open-access, zero-cloud-cost framework for safe, equitable, and privacy-compliant digital clinical triage.

title: Deep Learning Based Crop Health Monitoring Using IoT Sensors
abstract: This paper proposes a smart crop-health monitoring system that combines Internet of Things (IoT) sensors with deep-learning-based image analysis. Crop health is affected by soil moisture, temperature, humidity, light and plant diseases. Periodic manual inspection may delay the identification of crop stress. The proposed approach collects field conditions through low-cost sensors and captures leaf images using a camera. Sensor readings and images are processed by a controller or computer. A trained deep learning model can analyse leaf images for visible symptoms, while sensor readings provide information about growing conditions. The system aims to display crop information and generate alerts to support timely crop-care decisions. This is an introductory project proposal; performance results will be added after implementation and testing

title: Triple bubbles in the hyperbolic plane
abstract: We prove that the standard triple bubble uniquely minimizes perimeter among clusters in the hyperbolic plane with three prescribed positive finite areas. The standard family admits global pressure coordinates, and its volume differential is the negative of a positive definite grounded weighted graph Laplacian. A normalized perimeter excess attains a comparison minimum under a perimeter bound and gives a strict comparison between actual and model pressures. Component relabeling reduces the possible topologies to an all-boundary network or a 4-daisy. Discrete comparisons exclude the 4-daisy; pressure-preserving face deletion reduces the remaining network to the standard tetrahedral configuration.

title: Mathematical modeling to study combination strategies for neural stem cell therapy in glioblastoma
abstract: Neural stem cells (NSCs) are a promising treatment platform due to their ability to cross the restrictive blood-brain barrier and migrate toward damaged regions of the brain. These properties can be leveraged to target brain tumors, as NSCs can infiltrate tumor lesions and deliver therapeutic agents such as drugs, oncolytic viruses, and genetic materials. Despite the advantages of NSCs, translational challenges remain, including patient-specific chemotactic signaling and immune responses, variability in migration and localization at tumor sites, and optimization of delivery strategies. In this work, we focus on intranasal delivery of NSCs and combination strategies for the treatment of brain cancer. To investigate strategies for improving NSC arrival at the tumor site, we developed a hybrid mathematical model of NSC migration that couples an agent-based model with a partial differential equation, where cell motion is guided by the spatial dynamics of chemoattractants. Using data collected from a murine model and our mathematical model, we {investigate treatment-motivated downstream effects associated with three combination strategies:} (1) IL-10 pretreatment, (2) CXCL12 pretreatment, and (3) radiotherapy. We find that IL-10 pretreatment improves NSC arrival numbers at tumor only under the Gaussian chemoattractant profile, whereas CXCL12 pretreatment moderately improves arrival numbers when the tumor is located in the anterior brain. Radiotherapy significantly enhances the tumor arrival under uniform profiles. These simulation studies suggest that both treatment strategies and chemoattractant distribution influence intranasal NSC delivery, and the proposed model can be used to predict how targeted modulation of chemotactic signaling and tissue-guided migration may improve delivery outcomes.

title: A Self-Exploring and Self-Evolving Paradigm for Adaptive Edge AI Development
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit powerful code generation abilities, fostering agentic systems to automate edge AI application development. However, existing agents typically operate via fixed agentic workflows and predefined design spaces, struggling to handle rapidly evolving demands of real-world scenarios (e.g., heterogeneous data modalities, diverse task pipelines). Unlike prior systems that treat LLMs mainly as code generators following rigid workflows, we fully exploit their reasoning capabilities to allow agents to determine their own workflows on the fly. To this end, we propose SE2, a self-exploring and self-evolving paradigm for adaptive edge AI development. Inspired by human learning processes, we distill development into four atomic operations (retrieve, reason, code, test), and empower agents to explore workflows by dynamically and adaptively selecting an appropriate next operation based on the current context. Extensive evaluations show that, with adaptive workflows, the synthesized programs achieve up to 26% higher accuracy and consume 28% lower resources than state-of-the-art baselines, while maintaining superior adaptability to unforeseen edge AI scenarios. This highlights the potential of reasoning-driven adaptive agentic workflow in edge AI development.

title: Toward Executable Multi-framework Front-end Code Generation with Self-Correction
abstract: Generating codes from UI screenshots has recently benefited from MLLMs, yet existing methods centered on HTML targets and transfer poorly to multi-frameworks such as React, Vue, and Angular. However, unlike HTML, which does not entail compilation issues, generating executable code in multi-framework settings is more challenging due to framework-specific differences in syntax and failure modes, as well as the need to maintain global consistency across files. To address this problem, we study executable multi-framework front-end code generation and propose MESCoder, a tree-structured self-corrective generation framework. Our method first extracts a structural scaffold from the screenshot and then constructs sub-trees and assembly relations step by step, transforming large project generation into a sequence of localized decisions. On top of this scaffold, we introduce a unified Project Agent that continuously revises its own partial project under runtime sandbox feedback and dynamically chooses between local repair and cluster level repair.
