Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a key enabler of smart agriculture, supporting crop yield prediction, early plant disease detection, and precision farming interventions. This chapter surveys ML methods and systems across these three pillars. We review data sources—including satellite and drone imagery, IoT soil and weather sensors, and historical farm records—and algorithms ranging from classical ensembles (random forests, gradient boosting) to deep convolutional and sequential models. Comparative analyses illustrate performance trends in yield forecasting and disease classification, as well as the resource-efficiency gains achievable through precision management. Challenges related to data quality, smallholder accessibility, model transferability across agro-climatic zones, and integration with farm machinery are examined. The chapter concludes with open research directions toward scalable, affordable, and climate-resilient agricultural intelligence.

title: Deep Learning-driven Resnet-based Lung Sound Analysis for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Prediction
abstract: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) affects around 300–400 million people worldwide and remains a major global health concern. Early detection is important because timely treatment can improve patient care and disease management. This study introduces a framework called Chronic Lung Analysis via Audio Signal Prediction (CLASP) for the automatic detection of COPD using respiratory audio signals, achieving an accuracy of 97.90%. The method combines advanced signal-processing techniques with deep-learning models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Residual Networks (ResNet), to identify the most effective approach. Among these models, ResNet achieved the best performance, with a precision of 98.72%, recall of 96.86%, and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.9937. The results show that the proposed method performs better than existing approaches and offers a promising non-invasive option for COPD detection. Its use in clinical settings may support earlier diagnosis, improve patient outcomes, and reduce healthcare costs.

title: Explainable and Energy-efficient Deep Learning for Academic Risk Prediction in Higher Education
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence and learning analytics in order to predict academic risk in higher education is increasing. Deep learning can be used to model complex relationships between academic performance, assessment activity, engagement and other educational indicators, but these models can be challenging to interpret for educators, and may require significant computational resources. In this chapter, we propose a conceptual framework for explainable and energy-efficient deep-learning-based academic risk prediction. The framework comprises prescriptive modeling, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), lightweight deep learning, energy-aware computation, and human-centered decision support. Methods of explainability such as SHAP and LIME are proposed as ways to translate the model outputs into information that can be understood and used by educators. To reduce the computational cost, we consider energy-aware techniques, such as pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation, and lightweight inference. An educator-in-the-loop layer retains educator judgment at right decision points. The chapter also proposes a multi-objective evaluation perspective based on predictive performance, explainability, computational efficiency, energy consumption, robustness, and educational usefulness, not only accuracy. This framework provides a basis to develop sustainable and reliable academic early-warning systems especially in resource-constrained educational environments.

title: Crop Classification Using Deep Learning in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Cropping categorization is an important aspect of precision agriculture and has an important role in effective crop monitoring, yield estimation and resource management. With the rapid development of remote sensing technology, such as UAV and high-resolution satellite photography, there are now large amounts of agricultural data available for study. The performance of crop classification systems has been recently improved a lot using powerful models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTMs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), and hybrid models that combine the ability to extract spatial and temporal features. LSTM-based methods exploit the temporal dependencies in time series data for better classification. CNN-based models have been successfully applied to extract spatial patterns from multispectral and hyperspectral pictures. Advances in the field of Vision Transformers have been made by mimicking global contextual interactions in images and hybrid models have been benefited from the strengths of multiple designs to achieve higher accuracy and robustness. This chapter looks back at older studies about using deep learning for crop classification. It focuses on the main methods, the data used, and what those studies found. The chapter also critically examines the pros and cons of current approaches, covering problems like uneven data, complicated calculations, how well models work in new situations, and the need for lots of labeled data. The chapter also identified several research challenges and gaps, including the limited use of multimodal data fusion, a lack of frameworks for real-time use, and scalability issues in several agricultural applications. The use of IoT-based data acquisition, edge computing-enabled real-time processing, explainable artificial intelligence for model interpretation, and development of realistic but compact models for practical use in precision agriculture were all mentioned as areas for future research.

title: Hybrid AI–Quantum Architecture for Sustainable Plant Disease Detection and Pesticide Recommendation
abstract: Plant diseases, pest attacks, and nutrient imbalances significantly affect agricultural productivity and can reduce both yield and quality. Timely and accurate identification of these issues is essential for effective crop management and sustainable farming. Conventional manual inspection methods are often inefficient and inconsistent, while existing deep learning approaches may struggle to differentiate between diseases with similar visual characteristics, leading to inaccurate predictions and suboptimal treatment choices. To overcome these limitations, this work introduces a hybrid classical–quantum framework aimed at improving disease detection and decision-making. The proposed system uses EfficientNet-B0 to learn rich visual representations from plant images, then processes them with a variational quantum circuit to capture complex, nonlinear feature interactions. By integrating classical and quantum techniques, the model enhances classification performance beyond traditional methods. Beyond accurate disease identification, the system provides environmentally conscious pesticide recommendations, supporting responsible chemical use. Overall, this approach serves as an effective intelligent decision-support system, contributing to more precise and sustainable agricultural practices.
journal: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology

title: Calibrated Quantile Transformers for Cost-Aware Inventory Control in Simulated Multi-Echelon Supply Networks
abstract: Accurate demand quantiles do not automatically yield low-cost network inventory decisions. We evaluate a series-aware quantile Transformer linked to a rolling residual correction that shrinks item-specific errors toward pooled calibration residuals. The corrected 0.90 demand quantile drives retailer order-up-to decisions under shared distribution-center supply, with explicit replenishment lead times. To distinguish the value of calibration from forecasting architecture, a LightGBM quantile model and fixed-buffer controls are subjected to the same simulation. 10 independently generated synthetic networks each contain 48 product-store demand series over 176 weeks, and all policies use the same chronological 31-week holdout. Across the networks, the calibrated Transformer lowers average simulated cost by 13.1% relative to static stock and 3.6% relative to its uncalibrated quantiles. The network-paired mean incremental cost reduction is 3.54% with a 95% bootstrap interval [2.33%, 4.78%]. The study isolates decision postprocessing in a controlled simulation rather than making a real-retailer deployment claim.
journal: Academic Journal of Management Science and Engineering

title: Innovative Operation Ideas of Guangxi Agricultural Assistance Platform from a Demand-Side Orientation: A Case Study of "Mang Xiaozhong"
abstract: In recent years, with the deep penetration of the digital economy into rural areas and the rapid development of agricultural e-commerce in Guangxi, the demand-side oriented agricultural assistance model has emerged as an innovative form of agricultural product circulation. In response to problems in the upward distribution of characteristic agricultural products in Guangxi—including disconnection between production and marketing, high loss in circulation links, difficulties in brand transformation, and seasonal capital shortage at the production end—the "Mang Xiaozhong" platform constructs four interconnected operation strategies: customized pre-sale, two-way exchange among production areas, rule-based trust design, and consumer-side pre-purchase crowdfunding. These strategies adapt to the industrial reality of decentralized smallholder production and staggered listing of multiple categories in Guangxi. The research shows that the demand-side oriented, asset-light third-party service model can address the practical bottlenecks of county-level agricultural assistance e-commerce in Guangxi, and has reference value for the construction of similar platforms.

title: Differentiable Spin-Center Diffusion Model Enables DEER-Guided Generative Pipeline of Weighted Protein Ensembles
abstract: Biological function entails the interconversion of a protein between distinct conformations, an equilibrium modulated by ligands and other physicochemical conditions. Double electron-electron resonance (DEER) spectroscopy captures these ensembles as distance distributions, P(r), between spin label pairs. However, the width of P(r) convolves protein conformational heterogeneity with the rotameric flexibility of the label. Because current spin label models overestimate this contribution, translating P(r) into ensembles has remained indirect and predominantly qualitative. Here, we developed spin-center (SC) diffusion, a differentiable model of the spin label with a tunable spin label rotameric width. Coupled to a frozen Boltz-2 structure generator, SC diffusion enables the entire experimental P(r) to guide ensemble generation at inference time. We demonstrate the robustness of this pipeline on synthetic P(r) of known composition, recovering the ensemble populations, including both components of a bimodal profile. Guided by experimental P(r) measured under different biochemical conditions, ensembles of the transporters PfMATE, LmrP, MhsT and P-glycoprotein were modeled and free energy differences derived from the ensembles in a condition-dependent manner. By embedding a differentiable label model in structure generation, our approach interprets DEER distributions as weighted conformational ensembles, adding a missing thermodynamic grounding to generative protein structure prediction methods.

title: An Artificial Intelligence-Driven Predictive Framework for Residential Energy Demand Forecasting in Smart Urban Environments
abstract: Reliable short-term electricity demand forecasting is a critical requirement for the operational efficiency and sustainability of smart city energy infrastructure. Insufficient forecast precision leads to either excess generation capacity, causing fuel wastage and elevated carbon emissions, or supply shortfalls that threaten grid stability. This paper presents a systematic comparison of five forecasting approaches applied to residential electricity demand prediction: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit, Convolutional Neural Network combined with LSTM, Prophet, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Experiments were conducted on the UCI (University of California, Irvine) Individual Household Electric Power Consumption dataset, which contains minute-resolution measurements of electricity usage across eight electrical attributes spanning approximately four years. A chronological 80/20 train-test split was applied throughout to ensure that model evaluation reflected performance on genuinely unseen future data. XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy among the five models, attaining a root mean squared error of 0.024 kWh and a normalised root mean squared error of 2.37%, with substantially lower computational cost than the neural network approaches. Prophet captured seasonal demand patterns effectively and yielded interpretable forecast components suitable for integration with real-time urban energy monitoring systems. Among the deep learning models, Convolutional Neural Network-LSTM outperformed both standalone recurrent architectures, confirming the advantage of combining local feature extraction with sequential modelling. The results demonstrate that gradient-boosted tree ensembles, when combined with well-designed feature engineering, constitute a computationally efficient and highly accurate alternative to deep sequence models for short-term residential energy forecasting and are well-suited to deployment within smart city energy management systems.

title: The Discovery Gap: Why Artificial Intelligence Must Learn to Change Its Mind "Rethinking Human–AI Collaboration from Molecule to Market"
abstract: Scientific discovery requires the revision of belief: giving up a claim when the evidence turns against it, and knowing what else must change with it. Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed research - predicting protein structures, generating molecules, screening billions of candidates - but it does not do this. Autonomous agents traverse the discovery loop end to end without holding the beliefs that loop exists to revise. I use dynamic scientific intelligence for the class of system this requires, one that holds hypotheses as persistent objects with provenance, uncertainty and explicit dependencies. Its distinguishing condition is that a system can identify what supports each commitment and what depends on it, and so revise one without disturbing the rest. Because no architecture can revise beliefs on evidence it never receives, the problem is jointly architectural and infrastructural. Using drug development from molecule to market as the test case, I identify where evidence generated downstream should revise commitments made upstream and does not, and three decision points at which the non-delegable human act is adjudication rather than generation. I propose a revision test - an evaluation distinct in kind from any predictive benchmark - and a minimum reporting standard for claims of AI-assisted discovery. Until AI learns to change its mind well, it will remain a tool rather than an infrastructure in which discovery accumulates.

title: RUNX1-Mediated Hypoxic Signaling Impairs Myogenesis and Promotes Fibrosis in Myopathies.
abstract: Compromised myogenic repair with enhanced fibrosis is common in myopathies, including Wooden Breast (WB) myopathy in broilers, but the underlying mechanism of their co-occurrence remains elusive. Using WB myopathy as a model, we investigated the common pathological origins of these co-occurring features. Our single-nucleus RNA sequencing results showed enhanced oxidative stress and profibrotic remodeling of myofibers, increased proliferation but decreased differentiation of satellite cells (SCs), and aggravated differentiation of fibroblasts (FBs) in WB samples. Differential gene expression and pseudotime trajectory analysis further identified RUNX1 as a key regulator for both SCs and FBs, which was further supported by gene functional studies in respective cell culture models. Moreover, reduced blood flow and oxygen supply may indicate a hypoxic state in WB muscle, which was associated with enhanced RUNX1 expression. Consistently, coordinately enhanced HIF1A and RUNX1 expressions were found in differentiated FBs of human muscles and in muscles with diseases. Collectively, our study found that hypoxia-associated upregulation of RUNX1 disrupted the myogenic progression of SCs and exacerbated fibrotic differentiation of FBs, contributing to pathological degeneration in myopathies. Targeting RUNX1 may therefore represent a potential therapeutic strategy for prevention and treatment, which warrants future in vivo investigations.

title: RTMB: An R Package for Fitting Latent Variable Models With Template Model Builder.
abstract: Hierarchical and latent variable models are fundamental in ecology, fisheries science, and epidemiology, but fitting them efficiently relies on automatic differentiation (AD) combined with approximations such as the Laplace approximation. Template Model Builder (TMB) has become a standard tool for this kind of inference in R, but it requires users to write the objective function in C++, which is a potential obstacle for those unfamiliar with it, slows model iteration through compilation, and complicates debugging and simulation. We present RTMB, an R package that exposes the full power of TMB's AD machinery directly from plain R. Users write the joint negative log-likelihood as an ordinary R function; RTMB traces it onto an AD tape and hands the result to TMB's existing optimization, Laplace approximation, and reporting routines. We describe the design of the package, illustrate its use through a worked example, and provide a side-by-side comparison with the equivalent TMB implementation of a theta-logistic state-space population model. The result is a transparent, debuggable, and pedagogically accessible interface to state-of-the-art latent variable inference, with runtime performance comparable to native TMB.

title: Determinants of Crop Diversification in Boro Rice-Based, Wetland Farming Systems in Bangladesh.
abstract: The haor landscape of Bangladesh is highly reliant on Boro rice cultivation, making farm households vulnerable to recurring floods and climate-related risks. Crop diversification can intensify agricultural resilience and reduce production risks. This study examined the pattern, extent, and determinants of crop diversification using a cross-sectional field survey performed in 2023 among 240 farm households in three purposively selected upazilas (Itna, Mithamoin, and Nikli) of Kishoreganj district. The Simpson Diversification Index (SDI), based on crop-area shares, was used to measure crop diversification, while Censored Tobit and Ordered Probit models were employed to identify its determinants. The results showed that farmers were gradually familiarizing themselves with crops such as maize, mustard, jute, chili, sweet potato, groundnut, potato, pumpkin, black gram, and various vegetables, along with Boro rice. The mean SDI was 0.22, with 58.33% of households falling within the poor diversification category (0-0.24). The Tobit model indicated that household head education, farm size, agricultural training, marketing training, and extension contact positively associated with crop diversification. In contrast, road distance, duration of waterlogging, and agro-ecological location had negative effects. The Ordered Probit results generally confirmed these associations and also revealed a positive relationship between the dependency ratio and the higher category of crop diversification. Marginal effects indicated that agricultural training, marketing training, and extension contact increased the probability of achieving excellent diversification by 6.2, 5.5, and 4.8 percentage points, respectively, while each additional kilometer from a nearby road and each additional month of waterlogging reduced this probability by 5.4 and 3.1 percentage points, respectively. These findings emphasize the importance of improving farmer training, extension services, rural infrastructure, and location-specific waterlogging control to increase crop diversification and resilience in haor farming systems. Given the purposive selection of three upazilas in Kishoreganj district, the findings should be interpreted with caution in other haor regions.

title: Impact of Salinity on Rice Production in Vulnerable Southern Coastal Regions of Bangladesh: A Case Study Through a Cobb-Douglas Stochastic Production Function Model.
abstract: Salinity in coastal areas has a significant effect on the technical efficiency (maximum potential yield utilizing available inputs) of rice production and subsequently reduces food security in developing countries. We examined the salinity status and its impact on overall rice production across seasonal cycles in the southern coastal region of Bangladesh, utilizing data from 464 farmers from vulnerable coastal areas. The estimation from the Cobb-Douglas stochastic production function revealed that salinity has a statistically negative relationship with rice yield. Our study revealed that technical efficiency increased when farmers adopted salt-tolerant rice varieties and special techniques to manage salinity problems. Consequently, the profit per hectare was greater in the low-salinity zone than in the moderate- and high-salinity zones. We also find from binary logistic regression that with a greater possibility of yield loss, rice quality destruction, and salt land, farmers were more likely to migrate from cultivated rice to other crops because of salinity problems. In contrast, higher income, more consultations with extension officers and other farmers, and training knowledge, the likelihood of migrating from rice cultivation is lower. To mitigate salinity problems and ensure a sustainable future, salt-tolerant hybrid rice varieties need to be developed by research institutes, and frequent consultation and training need to be arranged by extension departments in Bangladesh.

title: Modular Biofabrication of Functional Skeletal Muscle Incorporated with Endothelialized Microvascular Seed-Derived Lumenized Microvessels.
abstract: The clinical translation of engineered skeletal muscle (eSM) for volumetric muscle regeneration is hindered by the challenge of establishing a functional vascular network capable of sustaining its high metabolic demand and ensuring graft survival. Here, we present a bottom-up biofabrication strategy to generate a pre-vascularized in vitro eSM model through the modular assembly of independently matured muscle and vascular compartments. C2C12 myoblasts were encapsulated within core-shell fibers using rotary wet-spinning (RoWS), yielding anisotropically aligned, multinucleated, and contractile myofibers expressing myosin heavy chain and sarcomeric α-actinin. In parallel, gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)-based microvascular seeds (µVS), pre-endothelialized with human umbilical vein endothelial cells, were engineered to guide rapid and structurally stable vascular formation while preventing uncontrolled capillary self-organization. Fully endothelialized µVS were incorporated into a pro-angiogenic bioink and processed via RoWS to generate tubular vascular fibers with physiological diameters (100-200 µm) and continuous CD31-positive lumens. After independent maturation, muscle and vascular constructs were bioassembled into a hierarchically organized tissue and co-cultured. By decoupling myogenic and angiogenic differentiation, this strategy overcomes medium incompatibility typical of conventional co-cultures, preserving compartment-specific architecture and function and establishing a versatile platform for muscle-vascular modeling and translational muscle repair.

title: RDAR biofilm formation and in silico analysis of putative amyloid proteins in Azospirillum baldaniorum Sp245
abstract: Azospirillum baldaniorum Sp245 is a plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium (PGPR) whose ability to benefit host crops depends on robust root colonization, a process driven by the transition from a planktonic state to a sessile, biofilm-associated lifestyle. This study investigated the capacity of A. baldaniorum Sp245 to form Red, Dry, and Rough (RDAR) morphotype biofilms. Through macroscopic evaluation and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM), we visualized the presence of exopolysaccharides, putative amyloid proteins, and extracellular DNA (eDNA) within the RDAR biofilm matrix using Calcofluor White (CFW), Thioflavin S (TS), and Propidium Iodide (PI) fluorescent probes, respectively. Furthermore, formic acid treatment of extracellular matrix proteins extracts suggests the presence of resistant, putative amyloid proteins. Because genomic screening revealed the absence of homologs of a canonical curli-dependent amyloid system, we performed a genome-wide in silico analysis to identify genes encoding alternative biofilm-associated proteins. Using the Staphylococcus aureus Biofilm-Associated Protein (Bap protein) as a reference, we identified 20 candidate proteins characterized by extensive domain reiteration and diverse architectures, including bacterial immunoglobulin (Ig-like) domains, VCBS repeats, SWM motifs, DUF4347, PKD domains, and RTX β-roll structures. Three-dimensional modeling indicates that these candidates possess elongated, filament-like conformations with repetitive β-strand motifs typical of amyloid-like assembly and calcium-dependent adhesion. These findings suggest that in the absence of traditional curli machinery, A. baldaniorum Sp245 could be using a diverse, domain-rich repertoire of alternative matrix proteins to facilitate cell surface interactions, coordinate structural stability, and establish the RDAR biofilm morphotype. Ultimately, this study establishes a foundation for understanding the role of amyloid proteins in Azospirillum biofilm matrix formation and offers new insights into the potential mechanisms of bacterial persistence and ecological fitness in the rhizosphere.

title: Precision maize crop height mapping using multispectral and LiDAR data from unmanned aerial system
abstract: Context Spatially explicit and accurate maize crop height maps are essential for supporting site-specific management in precision agriculture. Although low-cost unmanned aerial system (UAS)-based multispectral imagery offers a promising approach for maize crop height estimation, it’s accuracy under varying canopy conditions remains uncertain. Aims In this study, we used 3D point clouds to estimate maize crop height during sparse and dense canopy cover based on UAS-captured multispectral images and compare with light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-based estimates. Methods The 3D point clouds from multispectral images and LiDAR data were processed using a spatially localized grid (SLG) filtering approachto derive digital terrain model (DTM) and canopy surface model (CSM), which were then used to estimate maize crop height.Furthermore, two strategies were explored — (1) grid expansion, and (2) using ground reference derived during sparse canopy aspotential tools to mitigate issues during dense canopy cover for multispectral image-based estimations. Results Results showed that the crop height estimated from multispectral images during sparse canopy cover show comparable accuracy (r = 0.9, nRMSE = 32%) to LiDAR-based estimation (r = 0.81, nRMSE = 17%). The accuracy of multispectral-based estimation, however, significantly declined under dense canopy cover, where no meaningful correlation was observed (r = − 0.1, nRMSE = 61%). In contrast, LiDAR-based estimates show consistent level of accuracy under the same conditions (r = 0.78, nRMSE = 15%). When grid expansion strategy was implemented for multispectral-based estimation during the dense canopy cover, the nRMSE was observed to decrease up to 28%. Meanwhile, with the use of sparse canopy cover ground reference, the nRMSE decreased up to 17%, comparable to the LiDAR-based estimate. Conclusion Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of deriving crop heights cost-effectively using multispectral imaging from UAS. This approach offers a scalable and economically viable alternative to expensive LiDAR systems, enabling wider integration of crop height information into precision agriculture applications.

How Do Soil Properties and Canopy Status Influence Potato Traits while Continuously Monitoring Soil Moisture with Iot-Based Sensors?
abstract: Soil-related properties associated with potato yield and quality are implicitly linked to soil water storage (SWS) determined by soil texture (ST). This soil property also affects the potato canopy, which could be evaluated indirectly using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The objective of this study carried out in 2022 was to define explanatory soil- and canopy state-related properties (NDVI – Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), that determine with the highest extent potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.) traits: total yield (TY), dry matter (DM) content, and average tuber weight (ATW) over a rainfed production field located in central Poland (52°4′ 50.94" N, 21°10′ 6.73" E). Soil water storage was derived from continuously measured volumetric water content (VWC) using moisture sensors installed at three depths (10, 20, and 30 cm), which were connected via the Internet to exchange data (IoT-based sensors). Thus, the second objective of this study was to evaluate how temporal changes in SWS and the duration of periods when SWS falls below the level that limits plant growth affected TY in sampling areas characterized by different ST. Potatoes were grown under a suboptimal water supply during crucial stages for yield formation. More explanatory soil- and canopy state-related properties significantly, and to a greater extent, affected ATW and TY than DM content. SWS, determined between the stages of leaf development and canopy closure, played a more critical role in forming ATW and TY than soil chemical properties. NDVI derived from four out of five UAV images (58–100 days after planting – DAP) showed a very high correlation (r values of 0.79–0.90) with yield and ATW, and this canopy status indicator outperformed all soil-based variables. The model, based on sand and silt content, soil fertility in Cu and Zn, and NDVI measured at the time of fruit development, and soil water storage recorded between leaf development and canopy closure, showed the lowest RMSE of 5.85 t∙ha −1 and 7.98 g for TY and ATW prediction, respectively. A model based solely on NDVI evaluation between canopy closure and the end of flowering, and SWS determined simultaneously, was a strong alternative for forecasting TY (RMSE = 6.67 t∙ha −1 ) and ATW (RMSE = 9.23 g). In the sampling area with the highest TY, characterized by loamy sand ST, the deficit of SWS started at 46 DAP and lasted only for 12 days. In contrast, the sampling area with the lowest TY, with sandy ST, experienced SWS deficit from 34 DAP, and this period of plant-limited growth lasted for 34 days.

A multiagent framework for trustworthy AI financial advisory for displaced Ukrainians in Poland
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer opportunities for scalable financial guidance, but hallucinations, numerical errors, insufficient grounding, and unstable decisions limit their use in high-stakes financial settings. This study develops and evaluates a multiagent AI framework for retirement-oriented financial guidance using synthetic profiles modelled on displaced Ukrainians in Poland. The framework combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), structured profile generation, deterministic budget calculations, and an architecturally separate Evaluator Agent. The primary computational evaluation comprised 500 synthetic advisory cases. Additional experiments included a paired no-RAG ablation on 50 fixed profiles and a repeated-run stability analysis of 100 fixed profiles replayed five times. Under the predefined automated routing criteria, 327 cases were accepted, 170 required review, and 3 were flagged. After the deterministic budget overwrite, a separate deterministic arithmetic check found zero profile-to-answer mismatches. In the paired ablation, the mean final composite score was 8.40 with RAG and 7.08 without RAG. The difference was driven primarily by larger deterministic penalty deductions and grounding-gate failures without RAG, while the mean of the five LLM rubric dimensions did not improve with RAG. In repeated runs, only 14% of profiles retained identical routing across all five replays. The deterministic arithmetic pathway remained invariant, while generation, retrieval, model-based evaluation, and threshold-based routing varied across repeated execution. The framework is therefore interpreted as a controlled computational testbed and quality-assurance architecture rather than a validated autonomous financial advisor.

The Senescent Macrophage as a Central Hub in Skeletal Aging: Mechanisms, Niche Disruption, and Systemic Consequences.
abstract: Bone marrow macrophages (BMMs) coordinate skeletal remodelling, haematopoietic niche function, immune surveillance, and tissue repair. Whether a persistent senescent state in BMMs is a causal driver of skeletal ageing, however, remains unresolved. The central challenge is both definitional and causal: macrophages may be quiescent, terminally differentiated, chronically activated, tolerant, or metabolically dysfunctional, whereas commonly used senescence markers-including p16INK4a, p21CIP1, senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, and individual senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors-lack diagnostic specificity when used in isolation. In this critical Review, we distinguish evidence for senescence in anatomically defined BMMs from observations in aged marrow myeloid cells, broad myeloid perturbations, systemic senolysis, and mechanistic extrapolation from other tissues. We organize the evidence using a five-link causal chain connecting BMM identity and ontogeny, multidimensional validation of senescence, a defined macrophage-derived mediator, a response in an identified recipient cell, and phenotypic rescue after BMM-specific intervention. Current evidence supports age-associated macrophage-state changes that influence osteoblast support, bone repair, haematopoietic regulation, and inflammatory signalling. It does not yet establish that rigorously defined senescent resident BMMs are necessary or sufficient for age-related bone loss. Evidence for BMM-specific control of vascular dysfunction, haematopoietic bias, and distant-organ ageing is weaker still. The most defensible current model is therefore that senescent or persistently dysfunctional BMMs act as context-dependent amplifiers within an ageing marrow network rather than as universally established initiators. Resolving this question will require spatially resolved state validation, intersectional lineage targeting, temporally controlled necessity and sufficiency experiments, mediator-specific rescue, and validation in human bone marrow.

OC-STAMP deficiency limits MMT and ameliorates silicosis by inhibiting macrophage phenotype differentiation.
abstract: Silicosis is a progressive fibrotic lung disease characterized by myofibroblast accumulation and excessive extracellular matrix deposition, for which effective therapeutic interventions remain limited. Macrophage to myofibroblast transition (MMT) has emerged as a critical cellular source of myofibroblasts during silicosis, yet the molecular regulators governing this process are not fully understood. Osteoclast stimulatory transmembrane protein (OC-STAMP) is a multi-transmembrane protein originally identified in osteoclast differentiation, but its role in silicosis remains unexplored. In this study, we investigated the expression and functional involvement of OC-STAMP in silicosis using in vivo and in vitro models. We found that OC-STAMP was significantly upregulated in the lung tissues of silicotic mice and MH-S stimulated by SiO2, and was predominantly localized to macrophages. Macrophage-specific conditional knockout of Ocstamp (Ocstampflox/flox; Lyz2-cre) markedly suppressed M2 macrophage polarization and MMT, and attenuated the progress of silicosis. Mechanistically, Ocstamp knockdown attenuated JAK1/STAT6 signaling, whereas Ocstamp overexpression enhanced it, and pharmacological inhibition of JAK1 with Upadacitinib reversed OC-STAMP-induced MMT and signaling activation. Collectively, these findings identify OC-STAMP as a previously unrecognized regulator of MMT via JAK1/STAT6 signaling, highlighting OC-STAMP as a potential therapeutic target for silicosis and other fibrotic diseases.

Folate-decorated nanoparticles deliver bulleyaconitine A to inflammatory macrophages for rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease driven by synovial inflammatory cell infiltration and progressive joint erosion. Macrophages undergo a pathological shift toward an M1 pro-inflammatory phenotype, which plays a critical role in the progression of the disease. Modulation of M1 macrophages may be a promising therapeutic strategy. Herein, we developed folic acid-functionalized PLGA nanoparticles (FA-PLGA NPs) for targeted delivery of an anti-inflammatory natural compound, bulleyaconitine A (BLA), into M1 macrophages. The nanoparticles exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 151.91 ± 5.41 nm with a polydispersity index of 0.153 ± 0.016, a negative zeta potential (-13.50 ± 0.82 mV), a high encapsulation efficiency of 90.0%, and excellent colloidal stability. In vitro, FA-PLGA NPs were efficiently internalized by M1-polarized RAW264.7 macrophages via folate receptor-mediated endocytosis, and the uptake level was 7.79-fold higher than non-targeted NPs. Exposure to the NPs significantly reduced the population of CD86-positive M1 cells and decreased iNOS expression while increasing Arg-1 expression. Transcriptomic analysis revealed downregulation of pro-inflammatory and tissue-destructive pathways and upregulation of myeloid differentiation and immune regulation genes. In an adjuvant-induced arthritis rat model, FA-PLGA NPs treatment resulted in significant alleviation of paw swelling, joint destruction, and cartilage proteoglycan loss, as well as a decrease in the levels of serum IL-6 and TNF-α. Encouragingly, the nanoparticle formulation exhibited favorable in vivo safety, with no observable adverse effects on major organs. Collectively, FA‑PLGA NPs effectively modulated M1 macrophages and achieved potent anti‑arthritic efficacy with improved safety, demonstrating their potential as a nanotherapeutic for RA management.

title: STPAgent: A Writer-Reviewer multi-agent architecture for AI-assisted Unsafe Control Action identification
Biotin-dependent metabolism controls germinal center fate and vaccine-induced antibody diversification.
abstract: Nutrient availability shapes antibody responses, yet its role in metabolic checkpoints governing germinal center (GC) B-cell differentiation remains incompletely defined. Using heterozygous (HZ) Slc5a6 M60K mice modeling human loss-of-function mutations in the multivitamin transporter SLC5A6, we found that deficient biotin imports impaired mitochondrial metabolism and restricted preGC-to-dark zone progression after vaccination. Single-cell transcriptomics and RNA velocity revealed disrupted GC trajectories, while B-cell receptor repertoire analysis showed impaired class-switch recombination, somatic hypermutation, and vaccine-induced clonal diversity. Spatial multiplexed imaging showed reduced GL7-high GC-associated B-cell regions. Flow cytometric analyses revealed reduced frequencies of RBD-specific B cells and RBD-specific GL7+CD95+ GC B cells in HZ mice, with higher frequencies after biotin supplementation. Pseudovirus assays demonstrated impaired neutralization of Wuhan-Hu-1 and Omicron BA.2. Dietary biotin supplementation restored GC-associated differentiation, antibody diversification, and vaccine-induced humoral responses. These findings identify biotin-dependent mitochondrial metabolism as an important checkpoint linking micronutrient availability to GC B-cell differentiation and vaccine responsiveness.

title: The stimulative effect of Cordyceps sinensis functionalized selenium nanoparticles on bone development in growing mice: involvement of the gut microbiota-bone axis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Achieving optimal peak bone mass (PBM) during adolescence through adequate intake of trace element such as selenium is crucial for reducing osteoporosis risk in later life. We previously developed novel functionalized selenium nanoparticles (Cs4-SeNPs) utilizing polysaccharide-protein complex isolated from Cordyceps sinensis for prevention of osteoporosis. The gut microbiota, functioning as the "second gene pool", plays a crucial role in maintaining bone homeostasis. However, how Cs4-SeNPs regulate bone metabolism via the gut microbiota-bone axis remains unclear. OBJECTIVES To elucidate how the gut microbiota and microbial metabolites mediate the bone-promoting effect of Cs4-SeNPs. METHODS Growing mice model was used to assess the effect of Cs4-SeNPs on bone development. Metagenomics, metabolomics, and proteomics analyses were conducted to uncover the mechanism of action of Cs4-SeNPs. In vitro osteoblast and osteoclast models were employed to validate the effects of key gut microbial metabolites regulated by Cs4-SeNPs on osteogenesis and osteoclastogenesis. Pseudo-germ-free mice model treated with antibiotics was employed to determine the role of gut microbiota in bone-promoting effects of Cs4-SeNPs. RESULTS We found that Cs4-SeNPs significantly enhanced bone mass in growing mice, as evidenced by improved bone microarchitecture and increased expression of bone extracellular matrix-related markers. Notably, antibiotic treatment-induced microbial depletion abolished the effects of Cs4-SeNPs on bone development in growing mice. Increased abundance of beneficial gut bacterial genera, notably Adlercreutzia and Parvibacter, were observed following Cs4-SeNPs administration. Proteomics analysis and subsequent verification experiments demonstrated that Cs4-SeNPs inhibited the TNF-R1/TAB2/NF-κB inflammatory pathway and upregulated the expression of antioxidant proteins including SERPINA3K, GPX1, and SOD in the bone tissue. Metabolomic analysis revealed that Cs4-SeNPs treatment significantly elevated fecal and serum levels of two key metabolites: kynurenic acid and trehalose. Further in vitro studies confirmed that kynurenic acid and trehalose could reproduce the effects of Cs4-SeNPs on osteoblastic and osteoclastic differentiation. CONCLUSIONS Our findings suggest that Cs4-SeNPs optimize PBM and promote bone development in growing mice by improving the osteoblast/osteoclast balance via the modulation of the inflammatory TNF-R1/TAB2/NF-κB axis and the enhancement of antioxidant activity through the elevated levels of gut microbial metabolites kynurenic acid and trehalose in a gut microbiota-dependent manner.

title: Family Risk and Resilience Patterns Differentiate Early Childhood Vulnerability to Intergenerational Transmission of Abdominal Pain.
abstract: Children are at increased risk of developing chronic abdominal pain if a parent has an abdominal pain-related disorder of brain-gut interaction such as irritable bowel syndrome, suggesting family mechanisms of intergenerational pain transmission. However, patterns of family risk and resilience factors that predict children's vulnerability for developing chronic abdominal pain remain unknown. In a sample of parents with an abdominal pain-related disorder of brain-gut interaction and their young child without chronic pain, this cross-sectional study identified subgroups representing different constellations of family risk and resilience factors. It also tested subgroup differences on two vulnerability markers for children's future development of chronic abdominal pain: child emotional functioning and parental protective behavior. Baseline data from 212 parents and their 4-7-year-old child, participating in a randomized controlled trial testing a preventative intervention were included. Latent mixture modeling indicated a 3-group solution: (1) "High Socioeconomic Status, High Functioning" (55%) characterized by lower anxiety and depression and higher family resilience, (2) "Low Socioeconomic Status, High Pain Burden" (13%) characterized by higher pain catastrophizing and gastrointestinal symptoms, and (3) "High Socioeconomic Status, High Distress" (32%) characterized by higher parenting stress. Two of the three groups ("Low Socioeconomic Status, High Pain Burden" and "High Socioeconomic Status, High Distress" groups) showed lower child emotional functioning, and the "Low Socioeconomic Status, High Pain Burden" group also showed higher parental protective behavior, than the "High Socioeconomic Status, High Functioning" group. Results contribute to theoretical models of intergenerational pain transmission and help identify families who could benefit from preventative interventions. PERSPECTIVE: Among families of parents with chronic abdominal pain, low family resilience, low socioeconomic status, high parent pain burden, and high parent psychological distress may make young children more vulnerable to developing chronic abdominal pain in the future. These findings inform targeted interventions to prevent intergenerational transmission of abdominal pain.

Differentiated obesity treatment: Pharmacological CRF2 agonism drives fat loss, skeletal muscle hypertrophy and improved glucose metabolism in preclinical obesity.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Loss of lean mass during weight reduction may compromise metabolic health and physical function. Urocortin 2 (UCN2) activates corticotropin-releasing factor receptor 2 (CRF2) and has been linked to beneficial effects on skeletal muscle and glucose metabolism. We evaluated an acylated UCN2 analogue (acyUCN2), alone or combined with an acylated GLP-1 analogue (acyGLP-1), in preclinical obesity models. METHODS Diet-induced obese (DIO) Sprague Dawley rats and DIO Göttingen Minipigs were treated with vehicle or acyUCN2 (rats, pigs) or acyGLP-1 or combination therapy (rats only). Food intake, body weight (BW), body composition, glucose tolerance and energy expenditure (rats only) were assessed. Histology and RNA-sequencing were used to characterize muscle remodelling and transcriptional responses. RESULTS In rats, acyUCN2 reduced food intake and fat mass, increased lean mass and muscle weight, and improved glucose tolerance despite limited effects on BW. Energy expenditure was not affected. Histology demonstrated hypertrophy across fibre types and a shift from type 2A to type 2X/B fibres. Transcriptomic analyses supported muscle growth and fibre type switch, relative reduced vasculature, regulation of neuromuscular junction-associated genes, and overlap to human acute exercise-response signatures. In obese minipigs, acyUCN2 increased lean mass and improved insulin sensitivity, with modest effects on BW and fat mass, alongside regulation of genes linked to muscle biology and metabolism. CONCLUSIONS Pharmacological CRF2 agonism promotes favourable body composition, muscle hypertrophy, and improved glucose metabolism despite limited weight loss, supporting clinical development of UCN2 analogues as a differentiated obesity treatment, particularly in combination with appetite-regulating therapies and in settings where preservation of functional muscle mass is critical.

title: Integrating GWAS, transcriptomics, and machine learning enables genomic prediction of grain cadmium content in malting barley.
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) contamination in arable land poses a serious threat to the production of malting barley, a cornerstone crop for the brewing industry. Excessive Cd in grains undermines malting quality by disrupting germination evenness and reducing enzymatic activity during mashing. Despite this challenge, effective predictive tools for grain Cd levels are scarce, and the genetic architecture controlling this trait remains largely elusive. Here, we employed an integrated strategy combining genome-wide association study (GWAS), RNA-seq, and machine learning across a panel of 100 barley accessions. We benchmarked five genomic prediction algorithms, performed cis-eQTL mapping, and applied multi-omics integration to nominate high-confidence candidate genes. Our GWAS uncovered 3902 Cd-associated SNPs, and the XGBoost model, trained on merely 1000 markers, achieved the highest overall predictive performance (r = 0.86). Through systematic prioritization, we identified 67 candidate metal transporter genes. Among these, HvACA8a emerged as a likely negative modulator of grain Cd loading, whereas HvAHA9 and HvYSL15 were implicated as positive regulators. Collectively, our findings establish a robust genomic prediction framework for early Cd risk evaluation in malting barley. The identified markers and candidate genes offer tangible targets for breeding low-Cd cultivars, thereby helping to safeguard the quality of raw materials destined for the malting and brewing sectors.

title: Protocol for a phase I/II, open-label, single-arm trial of autologous chemically induced liver progenitor (CLiP) cell transplantation in patients with decompensated cirrhosis.
abstract: Introduction Decompensated cirrhosis is associated with a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options for patients who are not candidates for liver transplantation. Although various cell-based regenerative therapies have been investigated, their clinical benefits are limited. Autologous chemically-induced liver progenitor cells (CLiPs) are expandable progenitor-like cells generated from mature hepatocytes using small-molecule reprogramming and have demonstrated regenerative potential in multiple preclinical models. Because CLiPs are bipotent and can differentiate toward both hepatocytic and biliary epithelial lineages, their lineage fate after transplantation may be influenced by the recipient liver microenvironment, and whether transplanted CLiPs undergo hepatocytic maturation in the human decompensated cirrhotic liver to the extent observed in animal models remains unknown. We describe the rationale and design of the first-in-human clinical trial evaluating autologous CLiP transplantation for decompensated cirrhosis. Setting Autologous CLiP cells (CLP-001) are manufactured from liver tissue obtained by laparoscopic partial hepatectomy and expanded in a certified Cell Processing Center under controlled conditions. Quality and safety assessment includes histopathological examination of the harvested liver tissue, sterility, endotoxin and mycoplasma testing, viable cell count, cell viability, cell-surface marker characterization, copy-number variation (CNV) analysis, and targeted cancer-related gene-panel testing (Table 1). The study is conducted under the Japanese Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine and has been approved by a Certified Special Committee for Regenerative Medicine. Methods This is a first-in-human, single-center, open-label, single-arm phase I/II study. Three adults with Child-Pugh class B decompensated cirrhosis who are not candidates for liver transplantation will be enrolled. Approximately 30 g of liver tissue will be harvested laparoscopically and used for CLiP manufacturing over a 12-16 week period. Following successful quality and safety testing, CLP-001 will be administered into the portal venous system through surgical cannulation of the ileocolic vein. The primary endpoint is safety, defined as adverse events and product-related deficiencies from tissue procurement through 1 month after transplantation. Secondary and exploratory endpoints include safety through 12 months and descriptive changes in liver function, fibrosis-related biomarkers, liver stiffness, and clinical manifestations of cirrhosis. Conclusion This is, to our knowledge, the first clinical evaluation of autologous CLiP transplantation in patients with decompensated cirrhosis. The trial is designed to establish the safety and procedural feasibility of the entire therapeutic workflow, including tissue procurement, cell manufacturing, quality assurance, and portal venous administration. Efficacy-related observations are exploratory, and the lineage fate of transplanted CLiPs cannot be directly established in this study. The findings are expected to provide the first clinical evidence regarding the safety and feasibility of autologous CLiP transplantation and support the future development of CLiP-based regenerative therapy for advanced chronic liver disease. At the time of submission, patient enrollment has commenced, and no participant has yet undergone CLiP transplantation.

Scaffold-based and calcium-silicate biomaterials in vital pulp therapy: a systematic review of current evidence and translational perspectives
abstract: To critically synthesise and appraise the current evidence on scaffold-based regenerative biomaterials and calcium-silicate biomaterials used in vital pulp therapy (VPT), with particular emphasis on the translational challenges associated with achieving biological regeneration of the dentine–pulp complex. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic searches of MEDLINE (via PubMed), Scopus and Web of Science were performed from database inception to March 2025. Studies evaluating scaffold-based regenerative biomaterials or calcium-silicate biomaterials in VPT were included. Human clinical investigations and in vivo animal studies were considered to capture evidence across different stages of translational research. Methodological quality was assessed using study-design-appropriate risk-of-bias tools. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in study design, interventions and outcome measures, findings were synthesised narratively. Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising six clinical investigations evaluating calcium-silicate biomaterials and five preclinical animal studies investigating scaffold-based regenerative approaches. Clinical evidence consistently demonstrated favourable outcomes for calcium-silicate biomaterials in preserving pulpal vitality and promoting reparative dentine formation. Scaffold-based systems demonstrated promising regenerative characteristics, including enhanced angiogenesis, odontogenic differentiation and formation of organised pulp-like tissue under experimental conditions. However, scaffold evidence was limited to preclinical models, and no included study directly compared scaffold-based and calcium-silicate biomaterials within the same experimental or clinical framework. Current evidence supports calcium-silicate biomaterials as the clinical standard for VPT, whereas scaffold-based regenerative biomaterials remain a promising area of translational research. Although experimental findings suggest considerable regenerative potential, the absence of direct comparative clinical evidence precludes conclusions regarding comparative effectiveness. Future well-designed clinical studies are required to determine whether scaffold-based approaches can successfully translate into predictable clinical regeneration of the dentine–pulp complex.

title: Integrating Augmented Reality Sandbox Technology to Enhance Hydrology Education in Civil Engineering: A Pilot Study
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) tools may support hydrology instruction by turning abstract watershed concepts into visible and manipulable processes. This pilot study reports the construction and classroom implementation of an AR sandbox to support basin and watershed understanding in an undergraduate civil engineering hydrology course in Bolivia. The system combines a depth sensor and projector with open-source software to overlay real-time elevation, contour lines, and simulated water on a physical sand surface. The AR sandbox was integrated into one laboratory session within a 20-week course, following a socio-constructivist approach in which students worked in small groups to iteratively model landforms and test hypotheses. The activity was organized around four learning objectives: (1) delineating watershed divides from terrain form; (2) identifying drainage direction and flow accumulation; (3) distinguishing endorheic basins, where water ponds internally, from exorheic basins, where water exits through an outlet; and (4) connecting topographic changes with runoff pathways through simulated rainfall. Student perceptions were collected through a brief postsession questionnaire and complemented by instructor observations. Self-reported responses indicated high engagement and perceived support for understanding key ideas such as watershed boundaries, drainage direction, basin outlets, and the contrast between closed and open hydrologic systems. From an instructional standpoint, instructor observations suggested that the hands-on visualization helped address common misconceptions and supported the transition to subsequent numerical and geographic information system (GIS)–based tasks. While the evidence is preliminary and based on short-term perception measures, the findings suggest that AR sandbox activities may serve as a practical and adaptable supplement to hydrology education, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Future implementations will incorporate performance-based assessment, including pre- and postactivity questions, rubric-based watershed-delineation tasks, and comparisons of student performance on drainage-network and GIS-based exercises.

title: Data-Driven Micromechanical Characterization and Mapping of Shale Rocks Using High-Speed Nanoindentation
abstract: This study investigates the potential of high-speed nanoindentation in collaboration with data analytics and phase volume fractions to achieve micromechanical characterization of heterogeneous rocks. Although micromechanical characterization can be performed using mechanical testing alone, integrating chemical analysis—such as elemental mapping techniques—provides essential phase identification. This enables more accurate interpretation of phase-specific mechanical properties. However, incorporating chemical analysis increases the complexity of the process. Hence, this study proposes data-driven micromechanical characterization and mapping of heterogeneous rocks based primarily on mechanical data and limited dependence on chemical analysis. In this study, Mancos shale rock is analyzed using high-speed nanoindentation with high spatial resolution to determine the mechanical properties at the microscale. Subsequently, a suite of unsupervised statistical learning techniques, such as uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) with k -means clustering, Gaussian mixture model (GMM), Dirichlet process mixture model (DPMM), and density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN), are applied to the nanoindentation data. Additionally, an automated image processing and segmentation technique was developed and tested. The results from each technique have been systematically compared against the conventional chemomechanical approach using two metrics: weighted error, which evaluates how well cluster sizes match actual phase sizes, and spatial error, which quantifies the accuracy of mineral phase assignment at each indentation point. Based on the results, UMAP with k -means clustering is the most appropriate technique (with relatively low weighted and spatial errors of 13.40% and 30.40% for Test 2 grid and 26.74% and 49.20% for Test 3 grid) for micromechanical characterization and mapping of heterogeneous rocks, whereas DBSCAN, DPMM, and image segmentation techniques are more suitable as secondary approaches for cross-checking results from UMAP with k -means. Moreover, a comparison of the application of scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) image volume fractions and chemomechanical grid volume fractions for the phase volume fractions has been performed to derive the influence of chemical analysis on the results. This study demonstrates the capability of high-speed nanoindentation combined with machine learning techniques for micromechanical characterization with reduced analytical complexity and improved workflow efficiency.

title: Design Method for Axially Compressed Members Reinforced with Sleeves
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive investigation into a novel prefabricated sleeved retrofit technique for enhancing the global stability of steel compression members in grid structures that are interconnected through joints, such as space grids, latticed shells, and trusses. The research systematically examines the effects of key parameters, including material constitutive laws, yield strengths, outer sleeve geometries (diameter, wall thickness, and moment of inertia), and initial geometric imperfections, on the buckling behavior of reinforced members. A simplified yet accurate finite element modeling strategy, validated against experimental tests, was employed for parametric analysis. The results demonstrate that the retrofit significantly improves the buckling factor, with enhancement governed primarily by the outer sleeve’s moment of inertia rather than its material strength. Notably, the yield strength of the inner tube has a negligible effect, while the amplitude of initial imperfections significantly influences the postretrofit performance. Based on these findings, a modified column curve is proposed. For welded sleeves, the curve aligns closely with the standard column curve a, enabling straightforward design. Further, a practical and efficient design methodology is established, which determines the required sleeve dimensions by first calculating the target moment of inertia based on load demands, thereby streamlining the engineering design process. This work provides theoretical insight and a practical design framework for the application of this efficient retrofit technique.

title: Placental small-RNA sequencing reveals a distinct microRNA signature and its functional relevance in a preeclampsia rat model.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Despite extensive investigations over the last few decades, molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of preeclampsia remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence suggests that microRNAs (miRNAs) regulate key pathological processes in preeclampsia including endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and oxidative stress. However, a comprehensive profiling of miRNA expression has not been previously carried out. Thus, using reduced uterine perfusion pressure (RUPP) model of preeclampsia, we performed placental miRNA sequencing to identify functional relevance of abnormally expressed miRNAs. METHODS Blood pressure was measured via carotid catheterization on gestational day (GD)19. Placental small-RNA sequencing was performed using Illumina NextSeq2000 sequencer. RESULTS Our analysis identified 142 differentially regulated miRNAs (40 up- and 102 down-regulated) in placenta from RUPP rats. The top upregulated miRNAs included miR-211-3p, miR-628, miR-6324, miR-363-5p, and miR-6329, while miR-3587, miR-29b-3p, miR-3556a, miR-29a-3p, and miR-21-3p were the most downregulated. Functional annotation revealed associations with immune response (miR-363, miR-21, miR-29), B-cell differentiation (miR-628), T-cell activation (miR-21), adipogenesis, and lipid metabolism (miR-211, miR-29, miR-21), and angiogenesis (miR-363, miR-21). Further, gene ontology analysis revealed significant enrichment in biological processes; regulation of transport, cell-cell signaling, and calcium-dependent exocytosis, cellular components; synaptic vesicles, perinuclear cytoplasm, and clathrin-coated vesicles, and molecular functions; glycoprotein binding, protein dimerization, and myosin binding. CONCLUSION These findings suggest that robust miRNA dysregulation in RUPP rats may underlie disease pathogenesis.

title: Blackberry Leaf Blotch Virus, a Novel Emaravirus Infecting Cultivated and Wild Blackberry Plants in Europe.
abstract: A novel emaravirus provisionally named blackberry leaf blotch virus (BLBV), was identified from cultivated and wild blackberry plants (Rubus sp.) exhibiting leaf blotch and vein banding/feathering symptoms. BLBV has been detected in Belgium, France, the Netherlands and Slovenia. The virus is most closely related to raspberry leaf blotch virus (RLBV, Emaravirus idaeobati) infecting raspberry (Rubus idaeus) in Europe, and is distant from blackberry leaf mottle-associated virus (BLMaV, Emaravirus rubi), infecting blackberry in the USA. Up to eight RNA segments were identified in BLBV isolates, including the four core RNA segments present in all emaraviruses and up to four additional non-core RNA segments. Spherical virus-like particles (70-90 nm), morphologically similar to emaravirus virions, were observed in sap from symptomatic blackberry tissue by transmission electron microscopy. The proteins encoded by the core RNA segments were all more than 20% divergent from their closest known emaravirus homologues, supporting the classification of BLBV as a new species. Genetic diversity was found among isolates even at the country level, with some additional RNA segments only detected for some isolates. Eriophyoid mites, known vectors of emaraviruses, were found on several infected plants and molecular barcoding identified the them as Epitrimerus gibbosus, an eriophyoid species previously reported on Rubus spp. in Europe. Transmission bioassays performed with these mites in a greenhouse supported E. gibbosus as a putative vector of BLBV. This discovery raises questions about the impact of BLBV on blackberry crops and the need for virus surveillance in plant propagation material.

title: Icariin Ameliorates Postmenopausal Osteoporosis by Modulating Phosphodiesterase 5A-Mediated RANKL/OPG Signaling.
abstract: To investigate the effects of icariin on postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) and its underlying molecular mechanisms. A PMOP rat model was established by ovariectomy and treated with icariin alone or combined with estrogen. Bone mineral density (BMD), serum estradiol (E2), osteocalcin (OCN), and CTX-I were measured. Bone histomorphology was assessed using HE staining and immunohistochemistry. In vivo safety was evaluated by body weight, organ indices, serum ALT, AST, BUN, CREA, and liver/kidney HE staining. In vitro, a co-culture system of MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts and RAW264.7 osteoclasts was constructed to evaluate icariin's effects on osteogenesis and osteoclastogenesis, with CCK-8 and lactate dehydrogenase assays for safety. Mechanisms were further explored via ALP/ARS staining, molecular docking, RT-qPCR, Western blot, dual-luciferase assays, and PDE5A knockdown/overexpression. Icariin significantly increased BMD, elevated serum E2 and OCN, reduced CTX-I, and improved trabecular microarchitecture in PMOP rats. Icariin promoted osteoblastic differentiation/mineralization while suppressing osteoclast activity in vitro. PDE5A was highly expressed in PMOP; icariin downregulated PDE5A, inhibited RANKL, and upregulated OPG, thereby blocking NF-κB activation, enhancing Runx2 and OCN expression, and reducing cathepsin K and NFATc1. PDE5A overexpression partially reversed icariin's effects. Icariin at high doses showed no hepatorenal or osteoblast toxicity in vivo or in vitro, as per serum, histopathology, and LDH. Icariin promotes osteogenesis and inhibits osteoclastogenesis by downregulating PDE5A and modulating RANKL/OPG signaling, thereby restoring bone metabolic balance and exerting osteoprotective effects against PMOP, with a synergistic action when combined with estrogen and a favorable safety profile both in vivo and in vitro.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. Evaluated across all 62 subjects in the public MASS-SS3 dataset using 31-fold leave-two-subject-out cross-validation, the mixed-precision approach with hybrid quantization maintains 5-class accuracy within 0.15% of the floating-point baseline when optimized for general sleep staging and N3 sensitivity within 0.51% when optimized for deep-sleep detection. The developed techniques are broadly applicable to EEG-based DL workloads.

title: FPGA Acceleration of CNN-BiLSTM for EEG-Based Sleep Staging Featuring FFT-Based Non-Unit Stride Fast Convolution
abstract: Deep learning (DL) models for real-time wearable sleep staging often rely on long-kernel temporal convolutions, a requirement that current accelerators struggle to support efficiently. To overcome this, we present an FPGA-based CNN-BiLSTM accelerator that incorporates several algorithm-hardware co-design techniques to enable efficient edge inference. Central to this design is an FFT-based non-unit stride fast convolution, which performs accumulation in the frequency domain to enable a single IFFT per block, reducing post-processing complexity to $O(N\log N)$. On the target long-kernel convolution layer, this yields a 20.5$\times$ reduction in arithmetic operations. Power-of-two quantization is applied across the pipeline, including FFT-based convolution and BiLSTM activations, with an average accuracy degradation of only 0.11% relative to the floating-point baseline across all subjects on the public MASS-SS3 dataset. Additional optimizations, including block convolution, depth-first execution, and hardware engine reuse minimize memory access and enhance resource utilization. The accelerator, implemented on a Xilinx Zynq-7000 FPGA, operates at 10 MHz and consumes 11 mW of dynamic power including data handling and configuration overhead from a microcontroller. The design achieves a DSP power efficiency of 0.91 GOPS/W/DSP using only 4 DSPs, demonstrating scalable and energy-efficient DL acceleration for sleep staging that can be extended to other wearable applications.

title: The social origins of identity and bias: Language models, accumulated meaning and positioning.
abstract: This paper develops a social psychological interpretation of distributional language models, algorithmically learned representations of natural language. Within these models, words are positioned according to patterns of usage, and the resulting embeddings can be interpreted as maps of cultural associations available for learning. This cultural-learning account explains how patterned meanings become available to individual cognition but leaves open how those meanings are socially produced. Drawing on social identity theory, discursive psychology and a stigmergic-dialogical model of communication, the paper argues that identity and bias emerge through social interaction and the accumulation of linguistic traces. As people take positions, respond to others and circulate formulations, they produce patterns of meaning that locate actors relationally and make alignments and differences recognizable. Bias emerges when this accumulation is uneven, making associations, evaluations and distinctions differentially available across communities. From this perspective, embeddings map patterns accumulated through social activity. Their geometry captures relations through which identities become recognizable and groups distinguishable. The paper extends this approach with speaker landscapes, which locate speakers by their language use and show how groups become differentiated. The result is a framework for studying how meaning, identity, bias and group differentiation are socially produced at scale.
journal: The British journal of social psychology

title: Compliance by Design: Governing AI-Augmented Quantitative Analysis in Clinical and Translational Research.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from promise to routine practice in clinical and translational research, and large language models (LLMs) are now used to scope analyses, draft and debug code, and accelerate the quantitative work that supports clinical and translational decisions. This adoption is outpacing the operational safeguards that keep such work reproducible and auditable, and the central risk is not only erroneous code but the quieter erosion of the analytical discipline on which trustworthy bench-to-bedside decisions depend. In this position paper, we argue that AI can be integrated into regulated quantitative workflows without sacrificing reproducibility, provided it operates inside a compliance-by-design architecture built on two principles: analytical intent must be formally encoded and locked before execution, and the analysis itself must run outside the LLM as specification-verified code in a validated environment. We describe three failure modes that ordinary quality control does not detect, namely context drift, the displacement effect, and implementation drift, and we link each to documented model behavior. For open-ended investigation, these principles are operationalized as a four-step execution firewall; for recurring development studies such as assay validations and animal safety studies, they are operationalized through a governed library of documented, validated agents, supported by fit-for-purpose validation, a clear separation of human and machine roles, and post-deployment monitoring. Both approaches can be implemented with components available today. Used this way, AI enhances rather than replaces quantitative expertise, which now resides less in the code a model produces than in the constraints a scientist defines before it runs.

title: Unified Learning Ensemble for Robust Leaf Disease Detection: Integrating Improved Laplacian of Gaussian (ILoG) and Unified Learning Ensemble Approach
abstract: The world's population mostly obtains its food from plants. Plant diseases, which may be prevented with continuous observation, are a contributing factor in productivity loss. Monitoring plant diseases manually is time-consuming and prone to mistakes. To overcome this problem, this research endeavours to develop an advanced tomato leaf disease detection system, aiming to address the pressing challenge of crop health deterioration. The methodology involves a comprehensive approach, starting with a robust pre-processing pipeline utilizing Non-Local Means (NLM) for image cleaning, standardizing image sizes, and normalizing pixel values to enhance model convergence. A novel Improved Laplacian of Gaussian (ILoG) segmentation algorithm is proposed for precise leaf region extraction, while advanced texture analysis methods such as Gamma Correlation-based Local Phase Quantization (GC-LPQ) and Local Directional Patterns (LDP) are explored for feature extraction. Additionally, colour-based features, including colour moments, and geometric features like leaf area, perimeter, and shape descriptors, are extracted. The research delves into effective feature selection using the Hybrid FoxWheel Optimization Algorithm (HFWOA), a combination of Binary Waterwheel Plant Optimization Algorithm (BWPOA) and FOX-Inspired Optimization Algorithm (FIOA). The Unified Learning Ensemble (ULE) approach integrates Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Neural Networks with weighted voting for accurate leaf disease classification. The methodology's efficacy is evaluated through cross-validation, achieving an accuracy of 99.29% with an 80:20 training-testing split. The implementation is publicly available in a GitHub repository https://github.com/psaranyadevi27-ui/UNIFIED-LEARNING-ENSEMBLE-FORROBUST-LEAF-DISEASE-DETECTION
journal: Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers

title: Multifunctional composite magnetic particles combined with static magnetic field for treating infectious bone defects via SLC2A1-mediated HIF-1 and PI3K/AKT pathways
abstract: Infectious bone defects are a major challenge in orthopedics and stomatology, requiring strategies that eliminate bacteria and promote osteogenesis. Here, we developed a multifunctional composite magnetic particle system (F-Fe3O4) and demonstrate its synergistic combination with a static magnetic field (SMF) for treating infectious bone defects. In vitro, F-Fe3O4 demonstrated good biocompatibility with human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hBMSCs) and facilitated their proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation, while inhibiting the growth of Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Enterococcus faecalis. With the application with SMF, the aforementioned effects are further enhanced. The in vivo studies in the rat model further revealed that F-Fe3O4 combined with SMF can reduce early infection, alleviate inflammation, and accelerate new bone formation. Mechanistically, RNA sequencing and verification experiments revealed that the combination therapy upregulated SLC2A1-mediated glucose uptake and activated HIF-1 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of hBMSCs. In conclusion, this study developed an efficient treatment approach for infectious bone defects by integrating F-Fe3O4 and SMF.
